english_verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
translation_verse: Na kayawi kalɔ kesekɔ ƒui ni, Katɔti údie katɔ ku kalɔ.

english_verse: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
translation_verse: Na kalɔ kammɔ keeebo udu ɔdi. Na lɛla lɛdi lɛnɔ liiibo-ka kemmo, na lɛdisa kani náƒɔ kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui. Na Katɔti Kɔyu kani nkɛ mɔɔví ntu bɔni náƒɔ-ka anumi mmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti údie lɛdi ɔnini, “Bukeye bubo,” na bukeye búbo.

english_verse: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
translation_verse: Na Katɔti ɔ́nu ka bukeye bɔmmɔ bɔdia. Na úle bukeye bɔmmɔ na lɛdisa kudɔ.

english_verse: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
translation_verse: Na bukeye bɔmmɔ na Katɔti ɔ́lɔ ɔnii kadi nwaa, na ɔ́lɔ lɛdisa ɔnii usien. Na useyi údu na kadi kégye na limeyi lideedi lɛ́vi.

english_verse: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti údie lɛdi ɔnini, “Kuƒi kuduo ntu bɔmɛni kemmo, na kule ntu bɔmɛni bɔsiku ɔkpanadi kudɔ.”

english_verse: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
translation_verse: Na kuƒi kɔmmɔ na Katɔti ɔ́lɔ ɔnii kayaa. Na useyi údu na kadi kégye na limeyi linyɔdi lɛ́vi.

english_verse: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti údie lɛdi ɔnini, “Ntu bɔni náƒɔ kayaa kalɔ ni, bɔsala likpo linwi. Na kesii kani nákwii kakɔ kalɛ.” Na úbo úte lɛni.

english_verse: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
translation_verse: Na kesii kani nákwii mmɔ na Katɔti ɔ́lɔ ɔnii, “kalɔ,” na ntu bɔni násala lɛlɔ buwi likpo linwi mmɔ na Katɔti ɔ́lɔ ɔnii, “ɛpu.” Na Katɔti ɔ́nu ka ɔdia.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to produce all kinds of plants, including fruit trees and grain.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na údie lɛdi ɔnini, “Kalɔ kamɛni kakwɛ egyii ku livo lidu lidu ku adingyii lidu lɛnɔ.” Na úbo úte lɛni.

english_verse: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu kalɔ kammɔ kénwini lɛku ku livo ku adingyii lidu lidu. Na Katɔti ɔ́nu ka ɔdia.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
translation_verse: Na useyi údu na kadi kégye na limeyi lɛtɛdi lɛ́vi.

english_verse: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti údie lɛdi ɔnini, “Bukeye lidu libo kayaa na bule usien ku kadi nwaa ntɛ. Na ɔmɛni ɔbla likposela ute uwi ku emeyi ku akwa.

english_verse: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na bukeye lidu lɛmɛni lɛsɔ lɛkya kayaa na buteekeye teewi kalɔ lɛlɔ.” Na úbo úte lɛni.

english_verse: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔ́bla bukeye bonwu akpa anyɔ. Bukeye bunengudi bɔni ndi ɔƒɛ bɔdanku kadi nwaa, na kɔbuli kɔni nsia lɛnɔ kɔdanku usien. Na ɔ́bla ayabi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔ́ya na bukeye lidu lɛmɛni ƒui lɛkya kayaa. Na buukeye teewi kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́ya na bukeye bɔmɛni bɔɔdi kadi nwaa ku usien lɛlɔ, na buule lɛdisa ku bukeye ntɛ. Na Katɔti ɔ́nu ka ɔdia.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
translation_verse: Na useyi údu na kadi kégye na limeyi linedi lɛ́vi.

english_verse: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti údie lɛdi ɔnini, “Kɔbɛ ku kɔkpaku ku ketu kemmo bebuo benengudi lidu lidu bɛƒɔ ntu bɔmmɔ kemmo ƒui. Na lɛla biala lɛni mbo avwi lɛnɔ liteeveyi taavi kayaa.”

english_verse: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Katɔti údie bebweyi benengudi bani nkya ɛpu kemmo ku babambadi bani mɔɔví ntu kemmo ɔdi biala ku nwuna udu. Na údie bani mbo avwi lɛnɔ, ɔdi biala ku nwuna udu. Na Katɔti ɔ́nu ka ɔdia.

english_verse: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Katɔti úte-ma kusɛ kusɛ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bɛwɔ na bimomo na bɛƒɔ ntu bɔmmɔ kemmo ƒui. Na bani mbo avwi lɛnɔ bemomo.”

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
translation_verse: Na useyi údu na kadi kégye na limeyi lɛlɔndi lɛ́vi.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to give life to all kinds of tame animals, wild animals, and reptiles.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti údie lɛdi ɔnini, “Bebuo lidu lidu bɛƒɔ kalɔ kamɛni ƒui lɛlɔ, bebuo benengudi ku bebliidi ku bebweyi lidu lidu ƒui.” Na úbo úte lɛni.

english_verse: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Katɔti ɔ́bla bebuo benengudi ku bebliidi ku bebweyi lidu lidu, na báƒɔ kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Na Katɔti ɔ́nu ka ɔdia.

english_verse: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bɛya na bɔbla ukyuli na ɔlɛ-bu na bula udu kenye kalɛ na utaadi ɛpu ku kalɔ ku kayaa bebweyi ƒui lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Katɔti údie ukyuli na ɔ́lɛ-nwu na nwuna udu kenye. Údie-ma, na badi ɔnana ku uleku.

english_verse: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti úte-ma kusɛ kusɛ, na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛwɔ biyile kalɔ kamɛni ƒui lɛlɔ. Na bɛdi-ka lɛlɔ ku bebweyi bani ƒui nkya-ka kemmo.”

english_verse: I have provided all kinds of fruit and grain for you to eat.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Katɔti ɔ́su bekyuli bammɔ ɔnini, “Binu! Líti livo lidu ku adingyii lidu ƒui líte-mii nnii enwini bina adila.

english_verse: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
translation_verse: Na líti livo líte bebuo bani nkya kalɔ lɛlɔ ku baasɛ ku bebweyi ƒui nnii linwini bana adila.”

english_verse: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔ́nu ala ani ƒui na ɔ́bla na adia-nwu sɔsɔ. Na useyi údu na kadi kégye na limeyi lɛkundi lɛ́vi.

english_verse: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
translation_verse: Lɛni na Katɔti úti ɔ́wɔlɔ katɔ ku kalɔ ku ala ani ƒui nkya-nya kemmo budie.

english_verse: By the seventh day God had finished his work, and so he rested.
translation_verse: Na údie lɛla biala ɔ́wɔlɔ asa na limeyi maatɛdi lídu. Anwuɔsu limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, Katɔti ɔ́da kabla ƒui ɔ́ya na ɔ́nwuna.

english_verse: God blessed the seventh day and made it special, because on that day he rested from his work.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛdanku kusɛ kusɛ na lise kedee ka ɔ́ƒuna-ni úse ɔsu. Ɔsika limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ na ɔ́nwuna ɔni na údie ala ƒui ɔ́wɔlɔ. Adam Ku Hawa Lɛlɔ Kɔtɛ

english_verse: That's how God created the heavens and the earth. The Garden of Eden When the Lord God made the heavens and the earth,
translation_verse: Kalɛ na bédie katɔ ku kalɔ kɔtɛ ndi amɛni. Uwi ɔni na Katɔti údie katɔ ku kalɔ ni,

english_verse: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
translation_verse: edula ku egyiibi adi átakwɛ tɔ na kalɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔsika Unwoti Katɔti útaya na ɔnantu ɔna uwi kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na ukyuli ɔdi lɛnɔ uuubo na utaatuma kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But streams came up from the ground and watered the earth.
translation_verse: Nsu ntukpa buuyi taasi kalɔ kemmo na buute kalɔ kammɔ ntu.

english_verse: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́vɔ ukyuli ɔ́lɛku kalɔ kammɔ lɛti kemmo. Na ɔ́nwuna ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni muute ngba ɔ́kya ukyuli ɔmmɔ enwu kemmo aani ɔyawine.

english_verse: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́bla kemo kadi na kesii kani baalɔ banii Eden na ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na mmɔ ni, úti ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́vɔ mmɔ ɔ́kya.

english_verse: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
translation_verse: Na kemo kammɔ kemmo ni, Katɔti ɔ́ya na egyii ákwɛ enye na adi egyii abuni ani mɔɔdia bɔnu ku edula ani ndia kaduɛ na adia ete ka badi. Na kemo kammɔ ntɛntɛ ni, kugyii kɔni muute ukyuli ngba kunye na kɔni mɔɔyá na ɔɔnu lɛbuni ku likpidi taati lɛnɔ kunye.

english_verse: From Eden a river flowed out to water the garden, then it divided into four rivers.
translation_verse: Na ketu kani muute kemo kammɔ ntu kaagbá taasi Eden mmɔ. Na ketu kammɔ kábwɛ kéle lɛlɔ ntukpa ine.

english_verse: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
translation_verse: Ketu kedeedi lɛnyi ndi Pison. Na kaagbá taavi kalɛkɛ kani baalɔ Hawila kemmo, kesii kani na sika ugyiedi ɔkya.

english_verse: where pure gold, rare perfumes, and precious stones are found.
translation_verse: Kesii kammɔ ni, sika ugyiedi ɔni mɔɔdia bɔnu geen ku atabi ani náƒɔ kuye na baalɔ-nya banii Onis akya.

english_verse: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Na ketu kanyɔdi lɛnyi ndi Gihon na kaagbá taavi kalɛkɛ kani na baalɔ banii Kus mmɔ kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Na ketu katɛdi lɛnyi ndi Hidekel na kaagbá taavi kalɛkɛ kani baalɔ Asiria ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na ketu kenedi lɛnyi ndi Euƒrate.

english_verse: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti Katɔti úti ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́vɔ mmɔ ɔ́kya Eden kemo kammɔ kemmo ka utaabla-ka lɛlɔ kabla na utaanu-ka lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Ebo kuƒi ka adi egyii ani nnye kemo kamɛni kemmo ebi ƒui.

english_verse: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
translation_verse: Nsu kugyii kɔni mɔɔyá na ukyuli ɔɔnu lɛbuni ku likpidi taati aku ni, tadi-ku ebi. Ɔsika si ádi kugyii kɔmmɔ ebi ni, bukpi kani na adubo bukpi.”

english_verse: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Katɔti ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdia si ɔnana lɛti ɔkya. Ndubɔbla ubunkune ɔni námanku-nwu lite-nwu.”

english_verse: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na Adam úduo lɛlɛɛ kemmo úsie ɔgyu geen. Na uwi ɔni na ɔtɛ ɔlɛɛ mmɔ ni, Katɔti údie-nwu ɔƒɛnyi likubi linwi na úti ɔlɔna útile likpo lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti Katɔti úti likubi lɛni na údie ɔ́lɛku ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔƒɛnyi mmɔ ɔ́bla uleku. Na ɔ́kpanku-nwu úboku ɔnana ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Likubi lɛmɛni lɛ́si mina ekubi kemmo. Na ɔlɔna ɔmɛni ɔ́si mina ɔlɔna kemmo. Ndubɔlɔ-nwu nnii uleku. Ɔsika ɔnana kemmo na bédie-nwu bálɛku.”

english_verse: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu na ɔnana ɔdubɔmami ɔti ku uni lɛlɔ na uti lɛlɔ utámana ulekudi lɛlɔ. Na bana inyɔ badubɔbla ɔlɔna unwi.

english_verse: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmɛni kemmo ni, ɔnana ku uleku ɔmmɔ beli kasɔngya ɔni na kɔƒa kɔdi kulekpo-ma.

english_verse: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
translation_verse: Na mmɔ ni, kɔlakpi ndi kebweyi kani mbo lɛkwɛ geen ntulo bebuo bani ƒui na Unwoti Katɔti údie akɔ. Na limeyi lɛdi ni, kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kúsie uleku ɔmmɔ kudɔ na kútéye-nwu kɔnini, “Sɔsɔ geen na Katɔti ɔ́su-ɔ ɔnii, ‘Tadi egyii ammɔ adi biala ebi’?”

english_verse: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Amu na uleku ɔmɛni údie kenye ɔnini, “Bɔkana na bɔdi kugyii biala kɔni nkya kemo kamɛni kemmo ebi.

english_verse: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
translation_verse: Mmomu bɔsu na Katɔti ɔ́su ɔnii butadi kugyii kɔni nnye kemo kamɛni ntɛntɛ mmɔ ebi. Na butetuku-ku lɛnɔ. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, bɔdubo bukpi.”

english_verse: “No, you won't!” the snake replied.
translation_verse: Amu na kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kɔ́su-nwu kɔnini, “Kudii! Ɔɔɔdi bukpi na bɛdubo bukpi.

english_verse: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
translation_verse: Mmomu Katɔti ɔgyi ka si bɛ́di kugyii kɔmmɔ ebi ni, bɛdubo anu bɔda. Na bɛdubo bɔbla aani anwu Katɔti kalɛ. Na bɛdubɔnu lɛbuni ku likpidi lɛnɔ bɛti.”

english_verse: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
translation_verse: Amu ka uleku ɔmɛni ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka kugyii kɔmmɔ ebi adia bɔdi, na aadia bɔnu, na aayá na ukyuli ɔɔdá anu ɔsu ni, úde adi na ɔ́di. Na úde ɔdi úte ɔgyani ɔni nkya mmɔ lɛnɔ na ɔ́di.

english_verse: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bana inyɔ ƒui anumi ébimi na bánu báti ka bakɛ kasɔngya. Anwuɔsu béde kugyii evete bonwu adi básala na béti bábɛla lɛlɔ kasɔngya.

english_verse: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
translation_verse: Amu ka useyi uwi údu ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ ku ulekudi bénu Unwoti Katɔti kɔku uwi ɔni na ɔkɛ ɔɔví kemo kammɔ kemmo. Amu na bátábɛ na egyii akɔ kalɛ na Unwoti Katɔti ulanu-ma.

english_verse: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́kpali ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Wɛ na akya?”

english_verse: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
translation_verse: Amu na údie kenye ɔnini, “Línu-ɔ kɔku na kemo kammɔ kemmo na liƒu lɛ́da-mi, ɔsika nkɛ kasɔngya. Anwuɔsu líkeli ńtábɛ.”

english_verse: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Katɔti úye-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔma násu-ɔ ɔnii akɛ kasɔngya? Munuu kugyii kɔni lɛlɔ ebi na líbo-ɔ ɔda nnii tadi mmɔ ni, aku na átádi?”

english_verse: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔnana ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Uleku ɔni na éti éte-mi ni, anwu néde ebi ammɔ adi úte-mi na lɛ́di.”

english_verse: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti Katɔti úye uleku ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Bi na ábla mɛni?” Amu na uleku ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ nátɔlɔ-mi na lɛ́di.”

english_verse: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Lɛla lɛni na ábla mɛni ɔsu ni, “Ewida adubɔsiaku-ɔ etulo bebuo ku alakpi akɔ bebweyi ƒui. Kaƒɔ lɛlɔ na adubo butaakpɛ. Na lɛti na adubo butaadi ƒula ngba uwi ƒui.

english_verse: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
translation_verse: Na ndubɔya na awɔ ku uleku ɔmɛni binwini bekisine, na ƒula ubi ku uleku ɔmɛni ubi lɛnɔ benwini bekisine. Ɔdubo-ɔ lili bubo bɔbwɛ, na awɔ adu-nwu lɛnikpo.”

english_verse: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “You will suffer terribly when you give birth. But you will still desire your husband, and he will rule over you.”
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔ́su uleku ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Ndubɔya na ebo abi geen uwi ɔni na ada kaƒɔ. Na adubunu ɔlɛ asa na awɔ bebi. Ina amu muedi ni, ƒula anu adubɔsia ƒ'ɔgyani lɛlɔ, na akya-nwu kalɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.

english_verse: The king was good to Abram because of Sarai, and Abram was given sheep, cattle, donkeys, slaves, and camels.
translation_verse: Ɔ́da Abram kaduɛ na Sarai ɔsu na béte-nwu baƒonu ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku bebuo ala betine bagyani ku beledi ku bananabi kabla bablane ku belekubi kabla bablane ku baƒlumu lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Because of Sarai, the Lord struck the king and everyone in his palace with terrible diseases.
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti ɔ́ya na ɔlɛ kpakplaa ɔdi úbo Ƒarao ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli na Abram ulekudi Sarai ɔsu.

english_verse: Finally, the king sent for Abram and said to him, “What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me Sarai was your wife?
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Ƒarao ɔ́tala na bátálɔ Abram béboku-nwu na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi na ɔdi na ábla-bu mɛni, na átasu-mi ka ƒ'ulekudi na ɔdi?

english_verse: Why did you make me believe she was your sister? Now I've married her. Take her and go! She's your wife.”
translation_verse: Na bi ɔsu na ásu-mi anii, ‘Mina ɔnwani ulekubi na ɔdi.’ Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na líti-nwu lísienku mina kaduli ka unwini-mi uleku. Aanu ƒ'ulekudi, ɔƒaani tiku-nwu na biteesie!”

english_verse: So the king told his men to let Abram and Sarai take their possessions and leave.
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒarao úbo nwuna benengu bammɔ ɔda na Abram lɛlɔ na bédie-nwu ulu ku ulekudi ku ala ani ƒui na ubo na bátɔlɔ.

english_verse: Abram and Sarai took everything they owned and went to the Southern Desert. Lot went with them.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Abram ɔ́tɔlɔ Egyipte úti ɔ́kɔ úsie kesii kani baalɔ Negev. Na útiku ulekudi ku ala ani ƒui na ubo. Na Lot lɛnɔ ɔ́siaku-nwu.

english_verse: Abram was very rich. He owned many cattle, sheep, and goats, and had a lot of silver and gold.
translation_verse: Abram úbenwini ɔlakɛne na bebuo bani na ubo ku sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ɔsu.

english_verse: Abram moved from place to place in the Southern Desert. And finally, he went north and set up his tents between Bethel and Ai,
translation_verse: Ka ɔ́si Negev mmɔ ni, úsie ɔ́vi ekpo ekpo laa na úbedu lɛma lɛni ndi Betel ku Ai. Lɛma lɛmɛni ntɛ na ɔ́ka nwuna kevo bɔtu.

english_verse: where he had earlier camped and built an altar. There he worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Na mmɔ na ɔ́ka lɛkpabi bɔtu bute Katɔti. Mmɔ na Abram útaakpali Katɔti lɛnyi teemwi-nwu.

english_verse: Lot, who was traveling with him, also had sheep, goats, and cattle, as well as his own family and slaves.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Lot ɔni lɛnɔ nkɛ ɔsiaku Abram ni, anwu lɛnɔ ubo bebuo lidu lidu na bemomo geen na ɔ́tu nvo pii lɛnɔ.

english_verse: At this time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were still living in the same area, and so there wasn't enough pastureland left for Abram and Lot with all of their animals. Besides this, the men who took care of Abram's animals and the ones who took care of Lot's animals started quarreling.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni úbaya na kadɔ keduo Abram bebuo lɛlɔ banune ku Lot bebuo lɛlɔ banune ntɛ. Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo lɛnɔ ni, Kanaanƒuɔ ku Perisiƒuɔ bakya kalɔ kammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Abram said to Lot, “We are close relatives. We shouldn't argue, and our men shouldn't be fighting one another.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Abram ɔ́su Lot ɔnini, “Taya na kadɔ kakya ami ku-ɔ ntɛ iye ƒula bebuo lɛlɔ banune ku ami badi ntɛ. Ɔsika banwani na bɔdi.

english_verse: There is plenty of land for you to choose from. Let's separate. If you go north, I'll go south; if you go south, I'll go north.”
translation_verse: Aanu ka kalɔ kamɛni ƒui kewi ƒula anumi. Ya na bugyingyaku lɛlɔ. Na si awɔ ésie kɔdianu ni, na ami nteesie kɔmiinu.”

english_verse: This happened before the Lord had destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. And when Lot looked around, he saw there was plenty of water in the Jordan Valley. All the way to Zoar the valley was as green as the garden of the Lord or the land of Egypt.
translation_verse: Amu na ka Lot ɔ́kɔliku anumi na ɔ́nu ɔ́mana ni, ɔ́nu ka Yordan kalɔ kani nwi késela ƒui ni, ntu bɔkya-ka kemmo geen. Na kese aani Katɔti kemo kani na ɔ́bla na Eden. Na kese aani Egyipte kalɔ kani nwi késie ɔma ɔni ndi Soar kakɛ. Na uwi ɔni na ɔɔnu ala amɛni ƒui lɛni ni, ɔdi uwi ɔni na Katɔti útakyula tɔ Sodom ku Gomora kalɔ.

english_verse: So Lot chose the whole Jordan Valley for himself, and as he started out toward the east, he and Abram separated.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu kalɔ kani nwi késie Yordan kakɛ mmɔ na Lot ɔ́ƒuna. Na ɔ́yu ulu úsie ɔƒɛ katukɔ. Mmɔ nkyuli inyɔ bamɛni bégyingyaku lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Abram stayed in the land of Canaan. But Lot settled near the cities of the valley and put up his tents not far from Sodom,
translation_verse: Abram úlie Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na Lot ɔ́tu nwuna nvo na kalɔ ƒiaa ntɛ kesii kani nde Sodom.

english_verse: where the people were evil and sinned terribly against the Lord. Abram Moves to Hebron
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Sodom bekyuli bebo kuli ɔkplu na bátaabla alaekpidi lidu lidu taaƒiɔ Katɔti.

english_verse: After Abram and Lot had gone their separate ways, the Lord said to Abram: Look around to the north, south, east, and west.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, uwi ɔni na Lot ɔ́mami Abram lɛlɔ ni, Katɔti ɔ́su Abram ɔnini, “Talaku ƒula anumi na anu asi kesii kani na enye na anu esie katɔ kakɛ ku kada kakɛ. Na anu esie ɔƒɛ katukɔ ku ɔƒɛ kanukɔ.

english_verse: I will give you and your family all the land you can see. It will be theirs forever!
translation_verse: Na kalɔ kani ƒui na aanu ka kewi mmɔ ni, aka na ndubuti lite-ɔ ku ƒula bawɔ uwi ƒui.

english_verse: I will give you more descendants than there are specks of dust on the earth, and someday it will be easier to count those specks of dust than to count your descendants.
translation_verse: Na ndubɔya na ƒula bawɔ bemomo aani kɔnwinimi. Na si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́kana na ɔka kɔnwinimi kɔmmɔ ni, ɔdubɔkana na ɔka ƒula bawɔ lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Now walk back and forth across the land, because I am going to give it to you.
translation_verse: Sie na atáka amana kalɔ kammɔ ƒui linene ku bɔbɛbɛ, ɔsika aka na liti muute-ɔ.”

english_verse: Abram took down his tents and went to live near the sacred trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Abram ɔ́ta mmɔ ku nwuna ala ƒui na úsie kesii kani na Mamre egyii enengudi enye na Hebron kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na mmɔ na ɔ́tu lɛkpabi úte Katɔti.

english_verse: About this time, King Amraphel of Babylonia, King Arioch of Ellasar, King Chedorlaomer of Elam, and King Tidal of Goiim
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Amraƒel mɔɔdi lɛga na Sinear, na Ariok ɔdi ɔga na Elasar, na Kedorlaomer ɔdi ɔga na Elam, na Tidal ɔdi ɔga na Goyim.

english_verse: attacked King Bera of Sodom, King Birsha of Gomorrah, King Shinab of Admah, King Shemeber of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, a city also known as Zoar.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔmɛni kemmo ni, baga bedeedi bamɛni báta kekpo ku Bera ɔni ndi ɔga na Sodom ku Birsa ɔni ndi ɔga na Gomora ku Sinab ɔni ndi ɔga na Adma ku Semeber ɔni ndi ɔga na Seboim ku Bela, kalɔ kani lɛnɔ baalɔ Soar ɔga lɛlɔ.

english_verse: King Chedorlaomer and his allies had ruled these last five kings for twelve years, but in the thirteenth year the kings rebelled and joined forces in Siddim Valley, which is now covered by the southern part of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Akwa leevu-anyɔ sɔɔn na baga bekplodi bamɛni bakya Ɔga Kedorlaomer kalɔ. Na lɛkwa leevu-lɛtɛdi kemmo ni, baga bamɛni lɛnɔ báta bénye Kedorlaomer lɛlɔ.

english_verse: A year later King Chedorlaomer and his allies attacked and defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth-Karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, and the Emites in Shaveh-Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama na lɛkwa leevu-linedi kemmo ni, Kedorlaomer ku baga bani na anwu ku-ma násala lɛlɔ mmɔ básɔ báta bésie bétékpoku Reƒaiƒuɔ na Asteroƒ Karnaim kalɔ lɛlɔ ku Susiƒuɔ na Ham kalɔ lɛlɔ ku Emiƒuɔ na Sare Kiriataim kalɔ lɛlɔ ku

english_verse: They also defeated the Horites in the hill country of Edom, as far as El-Paran, near the desert.
translation_verse: Horiƒuɔ na Seir abi lɛlɔ. Na ɔkɛ mmɔ útédu kalɔ kani baalɔ El-Paran na ketele kudɔ.

english_verse: They went back to the city of Enmishpat, better known as Kadesh. Then they captured all the land that belonged to the Amalekites, and they defeated the Amorites who were living in Hazazon-Tamar.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na básɔ bénwini bésie En-Misƒat, kesii kani basɔ baalɔ lɛnɔ banii Kades. Na bádi Amalek kalɛkɛ mmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ ku Amoriƒuɔ bani nli Hasason Tamar kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: At Siddim Valley, the armies of the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela fought the armies of King Chedorlaomer of Elam, King Tidal of Goiim, King Amraphel of Babylonia, and King Arioch of Ellasar. The valley
translation_verse: Na békpoku Ɔga Kedorlaomer ɔni mɔɔdi Elam kalɔ lɛlɔ ku Tidal ɔni mɔɔdi lɛga na Goim kalɔ lɛlɔ ku Amraƒel ɔni mɔɔdi lɛga na Sinear ku Ariok ɔni mɔɔdi lɛga na Elasa kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na lɛkpa linwi lɛdi baga ine na beekpóku lɛkpa linyɔdi bani ndi baga ɛlɔ.

english_verse: was full of tar pits, and when the troops from Sodom and Gomorrah started running away, some of them fell into the pits. Others escaped to the hill country.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni Sidim Ɔkwalɛ ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, libu lɛdi lɛkya mmɔ lɛni kemmo na béku nnɔ tonwu mataa kɔni na beewi lilu. Na uwi ɔni na Sodom ku Gomora baga beekeli ni, bana bekyuli badi bánu libu lɛmmɔ kemmo. Na bakladi békeli bésie abi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Their enemies took everything of value from Sodom and Gomorrah, including their food supplies.
translation_verse: Baga ine bammɔ béƒie Sodom ku Gomora bekeline bamɛni ala ku adila ƒui báƒɔ na bátɔlɔ.

english_verse: They also captured Abram's nephew Lot, who lived in Sodom. They took him and his possessions and then left.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bétiku Abram ɔnwani Lot ku nwuna ala lɛnɔ, ɔsika Sodom mmɔ na ɔ́kya.

english_verse: At this time Abram the Hebrew was living near the oaks that belonged to Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers Eshcol and Aner were Abram's friends. Someone who had escaped from the battle told Abram
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔni kani nákana bukeli ni, anwu nébo ubedie litemi lɛmɛni kalɔ úte Abram, Hebrini ɔmmɔ. Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Abram kakyakɔ kedenku Mamre egyii enengudi ammɔ. Na Mamre ɔmɛni ɔdi Amorini ɔni ndi Eskol ku Aner ɔnwani. Na bekyuli bamɛni ƒui ni, ama ku Abram básala lɛlɔ na badi benwi.

english_verse: that his nephew Lot had been taken away. Three hundred and eighteen of Abram's servants were fighting men, so he took them and followed the enemy as far north as the city of Dan.
translation_verse: Amu ka Abram únu ka béƒie ɔnwani Lot bátɔlɔku ni, ɔ́lɔ nwuna kaduli nkyuli eti aku ku leevu-maane (

english_verse: That night, Abram divided up his troops, attacked from all sides, and won a great victory. But some of the enemy escaped to the town of Hobah north of Damascus,
translation_verse: Ka údu usien ni, Abram úle bekpone bamɛni na bétéyu-ma bátu, na békpoku-ma na bágya-ma bálɛku mmɔ ku usi útálɛ Hoba kalɔ lɛlɔ na Damasko katɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: and Abram went after them. He brought back his nephew Lot, together with Lot's possessions and the women and everyone else who had been captured. Abram Is Blessed by Melchizedek
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́ƒɔ Lot ku nwuna ala ani ƒui na béti békeliku mmɔ. Na ɔ́ƒɔ beleku ku bekyuli bamba bani ƒui na bákpanku bátɔlɔku mmɔ.

english_verse: Abram returned after he had defeated King Chedorlaomer and the other kings. Then the king of Sodom went to meet Abram in Shaveh Valley, which is also known as King's Valley.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ka Abram útádi Ɔga Kedorlaomer lɛlɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ ku baga bani na anwu ku-ma badi benwi mmɔ ni, Sodom ɔga úbo úbasiaku-nwu na ɔkwalɛ ɔni baalɔ Save kemmo na basɔ baalɔ mmɔ Ɔga Ɔkwalɛ.

english_verse: King Melchizedek of Salem was a priest of God Most High. He brought out some bread and wine
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔni Ntulo Ƒui ɔkpane ɔni baalɔ Melkisedek na ɔ́si Salem ɔma kemmo ni, údie bodobodo ku ntɛ bɔdi úte Abram.

english_verse: and said to Abram: “I bless you in the name of God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth.
translation_verse: Úvele kusɛ kusɛ úte-nwu ɔnini, “Katɔti Ɔni Ntulo Ƒui na anwu nédie katɔ ku kalɔ ni, ɔdubɔya na nwuna kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku Abram.

english_verse: All praise belongs to God Most High for helping you defeat your enemies.” Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
translation_verse: Na kusɛ kusɛ kani beete Katɔti ɔni Ntulo Ƒui, ɔsika anwu néti ƒula bekisine ɔ́kya-a enu kemmo.” Amu na Abram úti ala ani ƒui na úƒie mmɔ ana lɛkpa leevudi úte ɔkpane ɔmɛni.

english_verse: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “All I want are my people. You can keep everything else.”
translation_verse: Sodom ɔga úvele Abram ɔnini, “Nyonu bekyuli bammɔ te-mi, na eti ala ammɔ ƒui.”

english_verse: Abram answered: The Lord God Most High made the heavens and the earth. And I have promised him
translation_verse: Nsu Abram údie kenye na ɔ́su Sodom ɔga ɔnini, “Katɔti ɔni Ntulo Ƒui na anwu nédie katɔ ku kalɔ ni, anwu na lɛkɔliku mina enu lite. Na lɛ́kpali ala lɛ́lɔ-nwu lɛnyi lɛ́su nnini,

english_verse: that I won't keep anything of yours, not even a sandal strap or a piece of thread. Then you can never say that you are the one who made me rich.
translation_verse: ‘Lɛɛɛdubo lɛla lɛni ndi awɔ lɛdi lɛdi bɔƒɔ ina ƒula lɛgbanvuo kabuli muedi.’ Na alasu anii ami ɔsu na Abram únwini ɔlakɛne.

english_verse: Let my share be the food that my men have eaten. But Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre went with me, so give them their share of what we brought back.
translation_verse: Lɛɛɛdubo lɛla lɛdi bɔƒɔ butulo lɛla lɛni na mina bekyuli bamɛni bádi ku kadikɔ kani ndubuti lite ama bani násiaku-mi. Aka na ndubuti lite Ane ku Eskol ku Mamre bani na ami ku-ma bɔdi benwi.”

english_verse: Later the Lord spoke to Abram in a vision, “Abram, don't be afraid! I will protect you and reward you greatly.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Abram ɔ́nu kɔyu kemmo lɛla lɛdi na Katɔti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Abram, sɔ tayia! Ami ndi ƒula katamikukɔ ku kesii kani na adubɔkɛ ƒula lɛyuƒɔla linengudi.”

english_verse: But Abram answered, “Lord All-Powerful, you have given me everything I could ask for, except children. And when I die, Eliezer of Damascus will get all I own.
translation_verse: Nsu Abram údie kenye ɔnini, “O Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, bi na adubɔkana-mi bute ka liiibo ubi ɔni madi-mi ala muedi? Na Eleasa ɔni nási Damasko kani nkya-mi kudɔ.”

english_verse: You have not given me any children, and this servant of mine will inherit everything.”
translation_verse: Na Abram ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ka étete-mi ubi ɔsu ni, kabla ɔblane ɔni nkya-mi kaduli ɔɔbla-mi kabla ni, anwu ndubo-mi ala bɔdi.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “No, he won't! You will have a son of your own, and everything you have will be his.”
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔ́ya na Abram ɔ́ti ɔnini, “Ukyuli ɔmmɔ udu uladi-ɔ ala. Mmomu awɔ ɔlati kaƒɔ ubi ndubɔdi-ɔ ala.”

english_verse: Then the Lord took Abram outside and said, “Look at the sky and see if you can count the stars. That's how many descendants you will have.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́kpanku-nwu úsienku keyi na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Kɔliku anumi katɔ na anu kayaa na aka ayabi ani na aanu si adubɔkana-nya bɔka.” Amu na Katɔti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ƒula bawɔ lɛnɔ badubo bumomo lɛni kani.”

english_verse: Abram believed the Lord, so the Lord was pleased with him and accepted him. The Lord Makes Another Promise to Abram
translation_verse: Abram ɔ́ƒɔ Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́di, ɔmmɔ ɔsu na Katɔti ɔ́bu-nwu aani ukyuli ɔni nse siin.

english_verse: The Lord said to Abram, “I brought you here from Ur in Chaldea, and I gave you this land.”
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti ɔni nákpanku-ɔ ɔ́siku Ur ɔma kemmo na Kaldea kalɔ lɛlɔ, kalɛ na liti kalɔ kamɛni lite-ɔ na kenwini awɔ kadi.”

english_verse: Abram asked, “Lord God, how can I know the land will be mine?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Abram ɔ́su ɔnini, “Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, dɛ na mabla na mati ka kalɔ kamɛni ƒui kadubunwini ami kadi?”

english_verse: Then the Lord told him, “Bring me a three-year-old cow, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a dove, and a young pigeon.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Téti ɔmantɛ akɔ uledi ku ese ku koƒonu kɔgyani bani náaƒɔ akwa atɛ atɛ boku-mi. Na eboku abloduma ku lɛmangbɛ.”

english_verse: Abram obeyed the Lord. Then he cut the animals in half and laid the two halves of each animal opposite each other on the ground. But he did not cut the doves and pigeons in half.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Abram útéti ala amɛni úboku. Ka ɔ́du-ma ni, úle ɔdi biala kemmo inyɔ na use kɔkɛ kɔmmɔ ɔ́sala. Na baasɛ bammɔ ama ni, útele-ma kemmo lɛni.

english_verse: And when birds came down to eat the animals, Abram chased them away.
translation_verse: Na ka baasɛ bamba béveyi bébo bábadi lɛna lɛmmɔ ni, Abram ɔ́gya-ma.

english_verse: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and everything became dark and frightening.
translation_verse: Ka ɔƒɛ úsela bɔnu ni, Abram úduo lɛlɛɛ kemmo úsie ɔgyu. Na kadi kábla suu na liƒu lɛ́da-nwu geen.

english_verse: Four generations later, your descendants will return here and take this land, because only then will the people who live here be so sinful that they deserve to be punished.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na ƒula bawɔ mmɔ bulie búdu akwa ammɔ ni, badubɔsɔ benwini bebo mɛni. Ɔsika Amoriƒuɔ ekpidi ani baabla ni, étedu tɔ kesii kani na lɛni-ma kɔtu kɔni meduku-ma.”

english_verse: Sometime after sunset, when it was very dark, a smoking cooking pot and a flaming fire passed between the two halves of each animal.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ka ɔƒɛ ɔ́nu na kadi kábla suu ni, libui bonwu lɛdi ku uyɔ lɛni kemmo na ɔgya ɔɔda lɛdi lɛ́da lɛ́lɛ. Libui lɛmɛni lɛkɛ lɛ́vi lɛna lɛmmɔ ƒui ntɛ.

english_verse: At that time the Lord made an agreement with Abram and told him: I will give your descendants the land east of the Shihor River on the border of Egypt as far as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛmmɔ ni, Unwoti únyimi lɛla lɛdi ku Abram. Na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Líti kalɔ kamɛni ƒui muute ƒula bawɔ. Na ɔ́si ketu blii kani nkya Egyipte ɔmii útédu Euƒrate Ketu bonwu líti muute-ma.

english_verse: They will possess the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
translation_verse: Na Keniƒuɔ ku Kenisiƒuɔ kalɔ ku Kadmoniƒuɔ

english_verse: the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaites,
translation_verse: ku Hetiƒuɔ ku Perisiƒuɔ ku Reƒaiƒuɔ

english_verse: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.
translation_verse: ku Amoriƒuɔ ku Kanaanƒuɔ ku Girgasiƒuɔ ku Yebusiƒuɔ kɔlɔ ƒui na líti muute-ma.”

english_verse: Abram's wife Sarai had not been able to have any children. But she owned a young Egyptian slave woman named Hagar,
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Abram ulekudi Sarai útawɔ ubi ɔdi útete-nwu tɔ. Nsu Egyipteni ulekubi ɔdi ɔ́kya-nwu kudɔ útaabla-nwu kabla ɔni baalɔ Hagar.

english_verse: and Sarai said to Abram, “The Lord has not given me any children. Sleep with my slave, and if she has a child, it will be mine.” Abram agreed,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Sarai ɔ́su Abram ɔnini, “Unwoti ɔ́ya na naaawɔ. Anwuɔsu sie mina ulekubi kabla ɔblane kudɔ na bɛtɛ. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ ndubudie kaba bɔsiku nwuna bebi bani na ɔdubɔwɔ kemmo.” Abram lɛnɔ únu lɛla lɛni na Sarai ɔ́su-nwu kalɔ.

english_verse: and Sarai gave him Hagar to be his wife. This happened after Abram had lived in the land of Canaan for ten years.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔni na Abram úulie Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ aani akwa leevu kama ni, ulekudi Sarai úti Hagar nwuna Egyipteni ulekubi kabla ɔblane úte ɔgyani ɔnii uti-nwu aani ulekudi kalɛ.

english_verse: Later, when Hagar knew she was going to have a baby, she became proud and treated Sarai hatefully.
translation_verse: Na ka anwu ku Hagar bátɛ ni, ɔ́da kaƒɔ. Uwi ɔni na Hagar ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka ɔ́ɔda kaƒɔ ni, ɔsɔ ulakpete nwuna kɔduni.

english_verse: Then Sarai said to Abram, “It's all your fault! I gave you my slave woman, but she has been hateful to me ever since she found out she was pregnant. You have done me wrong, and you will have to answer to the Lord for this.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Sarai ɔ́su Abram ɔnini, “Ukyuli tabu ala ani na Hagar ɔɔbla-mi ni, awɔ na lɛ́si. Ami néti mina kaduli kabla ɔblane ulekubi líte-ɔ. Na ka ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka ɔ́ɔda kaƒɔ ɔsu ni, ɔsɔ ulábu-mi. Unwoti kani ndubuye litemi lɛmɛni na ami ku awɔ ntɛ.”

english_verse: Abram said, “All right! She's your slave—do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai began treating Hagar so harshly that she finally ran away.
translation_verse: Amu na Abram ɔ́su Sarai ɔnini, “Ƒula ubi ulekubi na ɔdi ɔsu lɛla lɛni na ánu ka lɛ́manku ni, na ablaku-nwu.” Anwuɔsu Sarai úse kalɔ ɔɔbla-nwu ulikplu ala. Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu ulekubi ɔmmɔ úkeli-nwu kudɔ.

english_verse: Hagar stopped to rest at a spring in the desert on the road to Shur. While she was there, the angel of the Lord came to her
translation_verse: Ka úkeli ni, Katɔti ɔtu ɔdi ɔ́nu Hagar na libiɔ lɛdi kɔtu na ketele kemmo kesii kadi. Na libiɔ lɛmmɔ ndi libiɔ lɛni nkya ulu kudɔ si éti ésela ɔma ɔni baalɔ Sur kemmo.

english_verse: and asked, “Hagar, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She answered, “I'm running away from Sarai, my owner.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́kpali-nwu ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Hagar, Sarai ubi ulekubi, wɛ na ási na wɛ na ésela?” Amu na Hagar údie kenye ɔnini, “Bukeli na nda mina kɔduni Sarai kudɔ.”

english_verse: The angel said, “Go back to Sarai and be her slave.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Sɔ nwini teesie ƒula kɔduni kudɔ na eboku lɛlɔ kalɔ ete-nwu.”

english_verse: I will give you a son, who will be called Ishmael, because I have heard your cry for help. And someday I will give you so many descendants that no one will be able to count them all.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-nwu lɛnɔ ɔnini, “Ada kaƒɔ ɔƒaani, na adubo ɔnanabi bɔwɔ. Na adubo-nwu lɛnyi bɔsia anii Ismael. Ɔsika Unwoti únu ƒula kɔnyana kɔni na eewulo.

english_verse: But your son will live far from his relatives; he will be like a wild donkey, fighting everyone, and everyone fighting him.”
translation_verse: Ɔdubo bɔbla ukyuli gyegyengye ɔni ndubɔkɛ utaavi aani alakpi akɔ ebuo ala utine kalɛ. Bekyuli ala aláyɔ-nwu kaƒɔ na nwuna ala lɛnɔ aláyɔ bekyuli kaƒɔ. Na anwu ku nwuna banwani beléduku na baaadubo bɔsala bulie liku linwi.”

english_verse: Hagar thought, “Have I really seen God and lived to tell about it?” So from then on she called him, “The God Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́sia Unwoti ɔni nátɛmiku-nwu lɛnyi ɔnini, “Awɔ ndi Katɔti ɔni mɔɔnu-mi. Ɔsika ɔƒɛni ni, lɛ́nu awɔ ɔni mɔɔnu-mi.”

english_verse: That's why people call the well between Kadesh and Bered, “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na básia libiɔ lɛmmɔ lɛnyi banii Beer-Lahar-Roi. Na libiɔ lɛmmɔ lɛmu lɛkya Kades ku Bared lɛma ntɛ.

english_verse: I will keep my solemn promise to you and give you more descendants than can be counted.”
translation_verse: Na lɛla lɛni na muunyimiku-ɔ mɛni ni, ndubɔlɛ-ni ugyii lite-ɔ na adubɔwɔ bebi na bemomo kaduɛ.”

english_verse: Abram bowed with his face to the ground, and God said:
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Abram ɔ́yu úbi kalɔ na Katɔti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini,

english_verse: I promise that you will be the father of many nations. So now I'm changing your name from Abram to Abraham.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, basɔ baaadubo-ɔ bɔlɔ banii Abram, ɔni kalɔ ndi Ati ɔni náƒɔ lɛnyi. Mmomu badubɔlɔ-ɔ banii Abraham, ɔsika líti-ɔ lɛ́bla kadi bekyuli pii ɔti.

english_verse: I will give you a lot of descendants, and they will become great nations. Some of them will even be kings.
translation_verse: Na ndubɔya na ƒula bawɔ bemomo na benwini kadi pii bekyuli na badi benwini baga muedi.

english_verse: I will always keep the promise I have made to you and your descendants, because I am your God and their God.
translation_verse: Ndubɔlɛ bunyimi bɔmɛni ugyii. Na amu ndubɔkya ami ku-ɔ ntɛ ku ƒula bawɔ ku kaba bekyuli bani ƒui masia-a kama uwi ƒui. Na ami ndi ƒula Katɔti na madi ama lɛnɔ Katɔti.

english_verse: I will give you and them the land in which you are now a foreigner. I will give the whole land of Canaan to your family forever, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Kanaan kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na adi ɔƒɔ mɛni ni, ndubuti-ka lite awɔ ku ƒula bawɔ na ami ndubɔbla bana Katɔti.”

english_verse: Abraham, you and all future members of your family must promise to obey me.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Katɔti ɔ́su Abraham ɔnini, “Awɔ ni, ɔlɛka adi mina bunyimi lɛlɔ, awɔ ku ƒula bawɔ ku kaba bekyuli bani ƒui masia-a kama.

english_verse: As the sign that you are keeping this promise, you must circumcise every man and boy in your family.
translation_verse: Ago bukulo bɔmmɔ ndubɔtina bunyimi bɔni nkya ami ku-mii ntɛ.

english_verse: Any man who isn't circumcised hasn't kept his part of the promise and cannot be one of my people.
translation_verse: Ɔnana biala na útekulo tɔ lego ni, ɔdubukulo kɔna kɔni nkya anwu ku mina bekyuli ntɛ, ɔsika útadi mina bunyimi lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Abraham, from now on your wife's name will be Sarah instead of Sarai.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Abraham ɔnini, “Ƒ'ulekudi Sarai ni, ɔƒaamu badubɔlɔ-nwu Sara.

english_verse: I will bless her, and you will have a son by her. She will become the mother of nations, and some of her descendants will even be kings.
translation_verse: Ndubute-nwu kusɛ kusɛ. Na ɔdi litemi geen ka anwu ɔlati ɔdubɔwɔ ɔnanabi ute-ɔ. Ndubute-nwu kusɛ kusɛ ɔni na ɔdubɔya na unwini kaba bekyuli pii uni. Na baga bani madi bekyuli lɛlɔ badubɔlɛ basiku-nwu lɛlɔ kemmo.”

english_verse: Then he asked God, “Why not let Ishmael inherit what you have promised me?”
translation_verse: Amu na Abraham ɔ́su Katɔti ɔnini, “Si adubute Ismael kusɛ kusɛ na ulie ngba ni, nka ɔdia!”

english_verse: But God answered: No! You and Sarah will have a son. His name will be Isaac, and I will make an everlasting promise to him and his descendants.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Katɔti ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɛɛn! Nsu ƒ'ulekudi Sara ɔdubɔwɔ ɔnanabi ute-ɔ. Na adubɔsia-nwu lɛnyi anii Isak. Ndubɔlɛ mina bunyimi ugyii ku anwu ɔmmɔ aani bunyimi bɔni makya ami ku-nwu ntɛ usela uwi ƒui ku nwuna bawɔ lɛnɔ ntɛ.

english_verse: However, I have heard what you asked me to do for Ishmael, and so I will also bless him with many descendants. He will be the father of twelve princes, and I will make his family a great nation.
translation_verse: Na Ismael anwu ni, línu lɛla lɛni na éye-mi. Sɔsɔ ni, ndubute-nwu kusɛ kusɛ na lɛya na ɔwɔ bebi pii na bemomo geen. Anwu ndubɔdi lɛlɔ badine leevu-inyɔ ɔti. Na ndubɔya na nwuna kadi bekyuli bakɛ ɔyikun geen.

english_verse: But your son Isaac will be born about this time next year, and the promise I am making to you and your family will be for him and his descendants forever.
translation_verse: Nsu mina bunyimi ni, ami ku Isak bawɔ ntɛ na ndubɔlɛ-mu ugyii. Na anwu ndi ubi ɔni na Sara ɔdubɔwɔ ute-ɔ na lɛkwa lɛni ndubo aani uwi ɔmɛni kalɛ.”

english_verse: God finished speaking to Abraham and then left.
translation_verse: Na ka Katɔti ɔ́wɔlɔ Abraham bɔtɛmiku ni, ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie katɔ.

english_verse: On that same day Abraham obeyed God by circumcising Ishmael. Abraham was also circumcised, and so were all the other men and boys in his household, including his servants and slaves. He was
translation_verse: Na lɛni kani na bananabi bani ƒui nkya Abraham kaduli ku bani mɔɔbla-nwu kabla, anwu ku ama ƒui békulo ago.

english_verse: One hot summer afternoon while Abraham was sitting by the entrance to his tent near the sacred trees of Mamre, the Lord appeared to him.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔdi kama ni, Unwoti údie lɛlɔ ɔ́tina Abraham na Mamre egyii enengudi kudɔ uwi ɔni na ulie nwuna kevo kenye ka kadi kábi ɔsu.

english_verse: Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. He quickly ran to meet them, bowed with his face to the ground,
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Abraham ɔ́talaku anumi na ɔ́nu nkyuli ɛtɛ badi ka benye-nwu kɔmadɔ. Ka ɔ́nu-ma kani na ɔ́babla na ɔ́ta kesii kani na úlie mmɔ útásiaku-ma ulu na úboku lili kalɔ bana anumi.

english_verse: and said, “Please come to my home where I can serve you.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ati, si ánu-mi áti ka lɛ́manku ni, tebo tavi ami ƒula kabla ɔblane.

english_verse: I'll have some water brought, so you can wash your feet, then you can rest under a tree.
translation_verse: Ya na beboku ntu bɔdi na bina ƒui bɛƒɔ lɛgba na bɛnwuna na kugyii kɔmɛni kalɔ.

english_verse: Let me get you some food to give you strength before you leave. I would be honored to serve you.” “Thank you very much,” they answered. “We accept your offer.”
translation_verse: Na aya na lɛwia lɛla lɛdi lite-mii na bɛdi kalɛ na bɛsɔ bɛkɛ ɔlɔkplu na biteesie bina ulu ka ami ƒula kabla ɔblane na bíbeduo.” Amu na ama lɛnɔ banini, “Ƒaa, bla kalɛ na aayɔ́.”

english_verse: Abraham went quickly to his tent and said to Sarah, “Hurry! Get a large sack of flour and make some bread.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Abraham úkeli úsie ulekudi Sara kudɔ na kevo kemmo na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Babla na ama ɔlaaƒɔ lɛɛƒɛɛ ɛtɛ na anwu na eƒi bodobodo ɔdi.”

english_verse: After saying this, he rushed off to his herd of cattle and picked out one of the best calves, which his servant quickly prepared.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, úkeli úsie nwuna bebuo akɔ na útáƒuna ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔkɔdi ɔdi úte nwuna kabla ɔblane ɔnii utádu-nwu na ɔbla-nwu kaduɛ uboku.

english_verse: He then served his guests some yogurt and milk together with the meat. While they were eating, he stood near them under the tree,
translation_verse: Amu na bábla adila adi béboku-ma ku bebuo anyi ntu ku lɛna lɛni bágyi mmɔ na béti béte-ma banii badi. Na uwi ɔni na belie baadi ni, Abraham ɔ́sɔ únye-ma kudɔ mmɔ na kugyii kalɔ.

english_verse: and they asked, “Where's your wife Sarah?” “She is right there in the tent,” Abraham answered.
translation_verse: Amu na béye-nwu banini, “Wɛ na ƒ'ulekudi Sara ɔkya?” Údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔkya kevo kemmo ngye.”

english_verse: Abraham and Sarah were very old, and Sarah was well past the age for having children.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni Abraham ku ulekudi Sara ƒui ni, bana akwa éesie lɛtɔtɔ geen ɔsu báabi. Na Sara lɛnɔ ɔ́ɔvi uwi ɔni na nka ɔkana kaƒɔ bɔda.

english_verse: So she laughed and said to herself, “Now that I am worn out and my husband is old, will I really know such happiness?”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Sara ɔ́ma na ɔ́su lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Ɔni na ami ku mina ɔtɔlati bɔ́ɔbi mɛni ni, ɔƒɛni na bɔdubo ebiti amɛni bɔkɛ?”

english_verse: The Lord asked Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh? Does she doubt that she can have a child in her old age?
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti úye Abraham ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na Sara ɔ́ma na úye ɔnii, ‘Sɔsɔ na ndubɔsɔ lɛkana kaƒɔ bɔda ɔƒɛni?’

english_verse: I am the Lord! There is nothing too difficult for me. I'll come back next year at the time I promised, and Sarah will already have a son.”
translation_verse: Bɛɛkali bɛnii lɛla lɛdi libo ɔkplu litulo Unwoti ka ɔkana bɔbla? Ndubɔsɔ linwini libo-mii kudɔ na uwi ɔni námanku lɛlɔ na lɛkwa lɛni ndubo. Na Sara ɔdubɔwɔ ɔnanabi.”

english_verse: The men turned and started toward Sodom. But the Lord stayed with Abraham.

english_verse: Finally, Abraham said, “Please don't get angry, Lord, if I speak just once more. Suppose you find only
translation_verse: Abraham ɔ́sɔ úvele ɔmmɔ kama ɔnini, “Unwoti, muuvele-ɔ nnii teti kɔnyi takya-mi, ya na lɛsɔ livele lɛla linwi. Si banii nkyuli leevu kani nkya mmɔ nɔɔ?” Unwoti ɔnini, “Na nkyuli leevu ɔsu ni, lɛɛɛdubo mmɔ bɔkyula.”

english_verse: After speaking with Abraham, the Lord left, and Abraham went back home.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Unwoti ɔ́su Abraham ɔmɛni ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔ́tɔlɔ. Na Abraham únwini úsie kaduli.

english_verse: That evening, while Lot was sitting near the city gate, the two angels arrived in Sodom. When Lot saw them, he got up, bowed down low,
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Unwoti batu inyɔ bammɔ bébeduo Sodom useyi uwi. Na Lot ulie ɔma ɔmmɔ kabanye na ɔban ɔmmɔ kayakun. Ka ɔ́nu-ma ni, ɔ́ta útásiaku-ma na úboku lili kalɔ.

translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni asa na badubusie batátɛ ni, Sodom ɔma ɔmmɔ banana, banamu ku benengu ƒui, báasi ɔma ɔmmɔ ekpo ekpo ƒui bábaka bámana kaduli kammɔ.

english_verse: and started shouting, “Where are your visitors? Send them out, so we can have sex with them!”
translation_verse: Amu na bákpali Lot beye-nwu banini, “Ntele bekyuli bani néduo-ɔ. Kpanku-ma boku na abu ku-ma bɔtɛ aani ɔnana ku uleku.”

english_verse: Lot went outside and shut the door behind him.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Lot ɔ́vi ɔlɛ útásiaku-ma na keyi, na ɔ́kalɛ ɔ́da-ma.

english_verse: Then he said, “Friends, please don't do such a terrible thing!
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bakpana, bitabla kalala kamɛni udu.

english_verse: I have two daughters who have never had sex. I'll bring them out, and you can do what you want with them. But don't harm these men. They are guests in my home.”
translation_verse: Bɛnu, mbo belekubi inyɔ bani nétesie tɔ ɔnana ɔdi kudɔ kudii. Bɛya na lɛkpanku-ma liboku-mii na bɛblaku-ma lɛla biala na bɛɛyɔ́. Na bekyuli bamɛni ama ni, bitabla-ma lɛla lɛdi. Ɔsika ami na bébeduo na ɔlɛka lɛgyumana-ma.”

english_verse: “Don't get in our way,” the crowd answered. “You're a foreigner. What right do you have to order us around? We'll do worse things to you than we're going to do to them.” The crowd kept arguing with Lot. Finally, they rushed toward the door to break it down.
translation_verse: Amu na Sodom banana bammɔ básu-nwu banini, “Gyu lɛgba bula anumi.” Na básu lɛnɔ banini, “Ɔƒɔ na Lot ɔmɛni ɔdi na úbeduo-bu, na ɔƒɛni amu úti lɛlɔ ɔ́bla bula litemi ɔtɛne. Bɔdubo awɔ ɔlati ɔmmɔ lɛla lɛdi bɔbla butulo bekyuli bani néduo-ɔ si átanu kaduɛ!” Na bénye-nwu lɛlɔ geen ɔni na baayɔ́ babwɛ kayakun kammɔ beduo ɔtɔ muedi.

english_verse: But the two angels in the house reached out and pulled Lot safely inside.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Lot baƒɔ bammɔ báni Lot béduoku ɔtɔ na bákalɛ.

english_verse: Then they struck blind everyone in the crowd, and none of them could even find the door.
translation_verse: Na báya na ogya ɔdi ɔ́bwɛ bekyuli bani ƒui nnye keyi mmɔ anumi na básɔ bátanu kayakun na beduo ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Lot went to the men who were engaged to his daughters and said, “Hurry up and get out of here! The Lord is going to destroy this city.” But they thought he was joking, and they laughed at him.
translation_verse: Ka básu-nwu lɛni ni, Lot ɔ́ta ɔ́lɛ na útásu nwuna bebi bagya bani néebo bébevele-nwu ka beti nwuna bebi. Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔbabla-mii na bɛvi bɛlɛ ɔma ɔmɛni kemmo pla. Ɔsika Katɔti ɔdubo ɔma ɔmɛni bɔkyula.” Nsu nwuna bebi bagya bamɛni béti lɛla lɛmɛni bákya bɔƒia.

english_verse: Early the next morning the two angels tried to make Lot hurry and leave. They said, “Take your wife and your two daughters and get away from here as fast as you can! If you don't, every one of you will be killed when the Lord destroys the city.”
translation_verse: Amu ka kadi kadubo kegyekɔ ni, batu inyɔ bammɔ básu Lot kpakplaa banini, “Babla na akpanku ƒ'ulekudi ku ƒula bebi belekubi inyɔ bani nkya-a kudɔ mɛni alɛku ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni amii lɛnɔ bɛdubo bɔkywi si Katɔti ɔɔkyula ɔma ɔmmɔ.”

english_verse: At first, Lot just stood there. But the Lord wanted to save him. So the angels took Lot, his wife, and his two daughters by the hand and led them out of the city.
translation_verse: Ka Lot unye ɔɔní litemi lɛmɛni teenene ni, batu bammɔ báda-nwu kɔnu ku ulekudi lɛnɔ enu ku nwuna bebi belekubi inyɔ bammɔ, ɔsika Katɔti ɔɔyɔ́ ka udie-ma na bákpanku-ma bálɛku ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: When they were outside, one of the angels said, “Run for your lives! Don't even look back. And don't stop in the valley. Run to the hills, where you'll be safe.”
translation_verse: Ka bálɛ ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo kani na batu bammɔ kemmo unwi ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔdi biala ukeli momoomo na udie lɛlɔ na ɔgbankpi ɔni ndubo bɔlɛ kemmo. Na ɔdi utenwini utanu kama. Na ɔdi lɛnɔ utasu ɔnii uudí unye na kalɔ ntɛ mmɔ kesii kadi. Bikeli siin biteesie abi lɛlɔ. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni bɛdubo bɔkywi!”

english_verse: Lot answered, “You have done us a great favor, sir. You have saved our lives, but please don't make us go to the hills. That's too far away. The city will be destroyed before we can get there, and we will be killed when it happens.
translation_verse: Ami aani bina kabla ɔblane kalɛ ni, mina ala áƒɔ-mi anu. Na bɛ́nu-mi kɔnyana geen. Na bidie-mi ngba na ɔgbankpi kemmo. Nsu naaakana bukeli busie abi lɛlɔ. Amu ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni ɔdububo ubaka-mi ɔkya na likpi.

english_verse: There's a town near here. It's only a small place, but my family and I will be safe, if you let us go there.”
translation_verse: Bɛɛnu ɔma ɔni baalɔ Soar na nwuna kalɔ ndi ubliidi ka nde mɛni. Buvele, bitakyula-nwu. Bɛya na likeli lisie mmɔ. Munuu ulatɛ?”

english_verse: Hurry! Run! I can't do anything until you are safely there.” The town was later called Zoar because Lot had said it was small. Sodom and Gomorrah Are Destroyed
translation_verse: Mmomu bikeli bisie mmɔ pla, ɔsika naaakana lɛla lɛdi bɔbla wetédu uwi ɔni na bíkeli bísie mmɔ.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na baalɔ ɔma ɔmmɔ banii Soar.

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Lot reached the town of Zoar,
translation_verse: Ka Lot údu Soar ni, ɔƒɛ ɔmmɔ ɔ́ɔkuku geen na mmɔ.

english_verse: He destroyed those cities and everyone who lived in them, as well as their land and the trees and grass that grew there.
translation_verse: Ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na Katɔti ɔ́sia na ɔ́kyula lɛma lɛmmɔ ku bekyuli bani ƒui nli mmɔ ku bana kalɔ ku aku ku edula ƒui.

english_verse: On the way, Lot's wife looked back and was turned into a block of salt.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na ala amɛni aalɛ́ ni, Lot ulekudi únwini ɔ́nu kama. Amu na únwini mma lɛbanta bonwu linye ulu ntɛ.

english_verse: That same morning Abraham got up and went to the place where he had stood and spoken with the Lord.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛni nsia ala amɛni bɔlɛ kama ɔtanta tutuutu ni, Abraham ɔ́ta úténye likpo lɛni na únye Katɔti anumi úvele-nwu na ɔma ɔmɛni lili.

english_verse: He looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and saw smoke rising from all over the land—it was like a flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Únye mmɔ na ɔɔnu kalɛ na uyɔ ɔɔkɔ́ taasi Sodom ku Gomora ku kalɔ kani nwi mmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na uyɔ ɔɔkɔ́ taalɛ ɔgya livongu bonwu na lɛyu bonwu lɛdi kemmo.

english_verse: When God destroyed the cities of the valley where Lot lived, he remembered his promise to Abraham and saved Lot from the terrible destruction. Moab and Ammon
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu uwi ɔni na Katɔti ɔɔkyula lɛma linengudi lɛmɛni ni, únyimo Abraham lɛla lɛni na úvele-nwu. Anwuɔsu údie Lot na ɔgbankpi ɔni na Katɔti ɔ́ya na úbakyula ɔma ɔni kemmo na Lot ulie mmɔ kemmo. Lot Ku Nwuna Bebi Belekubi

english_verse: Lot was afraid to stay on in Zoar. So he took his two daughters and moved to a cave in the hill country.
translation_verse: Na ala amɛni bɔlɛ kama ni, Lot ku nwuna bebi belekubi bátɔlɔ Soar mmɔ bésie bétélie abi lɛlɔ. Ɔsika ɔɔɔgyi kalɛ na welie Soar mmɔ. Na anwu ku nwuna bebi belekubi bammɔ bákya atabi ubu kemmo.

english_verse: One day his older daughter said to her sister, “Our father is old, and there are no men anywhere for us to marry.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, ulekubi unengudi ɔ́su ɔnwani ɔnamudi ɔnini, “Bula ɔti ɔ́ɔbi lɛlɔ na ɔnana ɔdi uuubo mɛni na bulieku-nwu na bula ɔdi kenye.

english_verse: Let's get our father drunk! Then we can sleep with him and have children.”
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, ya na bute bula ɔti ntɛ na ɔni ukpi na lisie ntátɛ-nwu kudɔ kalɛ na bula ɔti kaba kalayii.”

english_verse: That night they got their father drunk, and the older daughter got in bed with him, but he was too drunk even to know she was there.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu usien ɔmmɔ ni, báya na ɔti ɔ́ni ntɛ úkpi na ulekubi unengudi útátɛ ɔti kudɔ. Ɔti útati uwi ɔni na ubidi ulekubi úbatɛ-nwu kudɔ ku uwi ɔni na ɔ́ta ɔ́tɔlɔ.

english_verse: The next day the older daughter said to her sister, “I slept with my father last night. We'll get him drunk again tonight, so you can sleep with him, and we can each have a child.”
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛni nsia ni, ulekubi unengudi ɔ́su ɔnwani ɔnamudi ɔnini, “Usien ɔni návi ni, ńtátɛ bula ɔti kudɔ. Anwuɔsu ya na bɔsɔ bute-nwu ntɛ na ɔ́ni ukpi ɔmwi lɛnɔ na awɔ lɛnɔ esie na atátɛ-nwu kudɔ ɔmwi usien kalɛ na bula ɔti kaba kalayii.”

english_verse: That night they got their father drunk, and this time the younger sister slept with him. But once again he was too drunk even to know she was there.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu béte bana ɔti ntɛ na ɔ́ni-mu úkpi usien ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ. Na ulekubi ɔnamudi lɛnɔ úsie útátɛ bana ɔti kudɔ. Na ɔƒɛni lɛnɔ ni, bana ɔti útati uwi ɔni na ulekubi ɔmmɔ úbatɛ-nwu kudɔ iye ɔ́ta ɔ́tɔlɔ.

english_verse: That's how Lot's two daughters had children.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Lot bebi belekubi inyɔ bammɔ ƒui bábada kaƒɔ béte bana ɔti.

english_verse: The older daughter named her son Moab, and he is the ancestor of the Moabites.
translation_verse: Na ulekubi unengudi úbawɔ ɔnanabi na ɔ́sia-nwu lɛnyi ɔnii Moab, na anwu ndi Moab kadi bekyuli ƒui ɔti.

english_verse: The younger daughter named her son Benammi, and he is the ancestor of the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Na ulekubi ɔnamudi lɛnɔ úbawɔ ɔnanabi na ɔ́sia-nwu lɛnyi ɔnii Ben-Ami na anwu ndi Amon kadi bekyuli bani na bakya ɔmwi ƒui ɔti.

english_verse: he told everyone that his wife Sarah was his sister. So King Abimelech of Gerar had Sarah brought to him.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ka Abraham údie ulekudi Sara ɔ́tina bekyuli bammɔ ni, ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Mina ɔnwani ulekubi na ɔdi.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Abimelek ɔni ndi Gerar ɔma ɔga ɔ́tala na bátákpanku Sara béboku-nwu.

english_verse: But God came to Abimelech in a dream and said, “You have taken a married woman into your home, and for this you will die!”
translation_verse: Nsu Katɔti údie lɛlɔ ɔtina-nwu na kɔna kemmo limeyi lɛdi usien na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Uleku ɔni na áƒɔ eenwíni awɔ ɔdi mɛni ɔsu ni, si ékpi muedi ɔdia-a utulo. Ɔsika uleku ɔni nli kɔgya na ɔdi.”

english_verse: Abimelech said to the Lord, “Don't kill me! I haven't slept with Sarah. Didn't they say they were brother and sister? I am completely innocent.”
translation_verse: Ɔɔɔdi Abraham ɔlati násu-mi ɔnini, ‘Mina ɔnwani ulekubi na ɔdi’? Lɛla lɛni na lɛ́bla ni, mina kayi kaladu-mi kɔtɔ. Na aanu-mi enu na katɔ.”

english_verse: Then God continued: I know you are innocent. That's why I kept you from sleeping with Sarah and doing anything wrong.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔ́su-nwu na kɔna kemmo ɔnini, “Sɔsɔ na ɔdi, ngyi ka lɛla lɛni na ábla ni, ƒula kayi kaladu-ɔ kɔtɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na ńtaya na ablaku-nwu likpidi lɛdi iye etuku-nwu na aƒiɔ-mi.

english_verse: Her husband is a prophet. Let her go back to him, and his prayers will save you from death. But if you don't return her, you and all your people will die.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ni, ya na uleku ɔmmɔ ɔsɔ unwini usie ɔgyani kudɔ, ɔsika Katɔti Kenye Udiene na ɔdi. Na ɔdubɔkpali katɔ na ƒula lili na elie ngba. Nsu si átaya na ulekudi ɔmmɔ ɔsɔ unwini ni, na ati ka awɔ ku ƒula badi ƒui bɛdubo bukpi.”

english_verse: Early the next morning Abimelech sent for his officials, and when he told them what had happened, they were frightened.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛni nsia ɔtanta tutuutu ni, Abimelek ɔ́lɔ nwuna benengu ƒui ɔ́sala. Na ka údie kenye na ɔ́su-ma ala ani ƒui nálɛ ni, báyia geen.

english_verse: Abimelech then called in Abraham and said: Look what you've done to us! What have I ever done to you? Why did you make me and my nation guilty of such a terrible sin?
translation_verse: Amu na Abimelek ɔ́lɔ Abraham úboku na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ndi lɛla lɛni na ábla-bu mɛni? Munuu lɛla lɛdi na lɛ́bla lɛ́ƒiɔ-ɔ ɔsu na áyɔ ka likpidi bonwu lɛmɛni udu libo ami ku mina kadi bekyuli lɛlɔ? Ábla-mi lɛla lɛni na balabla ukyuli.”

english_verse: What were you thinking when you did this?
translation_verse: Na Abimelek úye Abraham ɔnini, “Bi ndi-ɔ kasusu kani ɔsu na ábla lɛla lɛmɛni udu?”

english_verse: Abraham answered: I did it because I didn't think any of you respected God, and I was sure that someone would kill me to get my wife.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Abraham údie kenye ɔnini, “Na mina bɔnu kemmo ni, lɛ́su nnii, ‘Kadi kamɛni bekyuli balayia Katɔti, na ɔƒɛni kalɛ badubo-mi bɔdu na mina uleku ɔsu.’

english_verse: Besides, she is my half sister. We have the same father, but different mothers.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama lɛnɔ ni, mina ɔnwani na ɔdi sɔsɔ na kalɛ na báwɔ-bu kenye. Ɔsika mina ɔti ubi ulekubi na ɔdi, ina ka ɔɔɔdi mina uni náwɔ-nwu.

english_verse: When God made us leave my father's home and start wandering, I told her, “If you really love me, then tell everyone that I am your brother.”
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni uwi ɔni na Katɔti ɔ́ya na lɛ́tɔlɔ mina ɔti kaduli na línwini ukyuli ɔni nkɛ mɔɔví ni, lɛni na lɛ́su mina uleku nnii, ‘Ƒula bɔyɔ bɔni na mɔɔwia ka edie atina-mi ni, amu ndi ka kesii biala na búsie ni, na asu anini, “Ɔnana ɔmɛni ni, mina ɔnwani ɔnanabi na ɔdi.” ’ ”

english_verse: After Abimelech had given Abraham some sheep, cattle, and slaves, he sent Sarah back
translation_verse: Amu na Abimelek úti baƒonu ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku bananabi ku belekubi kabla bablane na uti-ma úte Abraham, na ɔ́sɔku ulekudi Sara lɛnɔ úte-nwu.

english_verse: and told Abraham he could settle anywhere in his country.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Abimelek ɔ́su Abraham ɔnini, “Aanu mina kalɔ nwi késela. Teesie na etélie kesii biala na aayɔ́.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, God had kept Abimelech's wife and slaves from having children. But Abraham prayed, and God let them start having children again.
translation_verse: ɔsika nka Katɔti útile Abimelek ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ƒui kɔwɔ kenye, ɔkɛnku Abraham ulekudi Sara litemi lɛmɛni ɔsu.

english_verse: The Lord was good to Sarah and kept his promise.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́nu Sara kɔnyana aani kalɛ na ɔ́su-nwu úse.

english_verse: Although Abraham was very old, Sarah had a son exactly at the time God had said.
translation_verse: Sara úbada kaƒɔ na ɔ́wɔ ɔnanabi úte Abraham uwi ɔni na ɔ́ɔbi lɛlɔ mmɔ. Na ɔ́wɔ uwi ɔni lɛlɔ na Katɔti ɔ́su úse ka ɔdubɔwɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: and when the boy was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, just as God had commanded.
translation_verse: Na ka ubidi Isak ɔmɛni ɔ́ƒɔ emeyi maane ni, Abraham úkulo-nwu lego aani kalɛ na Katɔti úbo-nwu ɔda.

english_verse: and Sarah said, “God has made me laugh. And now everyone will laugh with me.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Sara ɔ́su ɔnini, “Katɔti ɔ́ya na mina anumi aƒɛnimi ku lɛma. Na ukyuli biala ɔni menu lɛla lɛmɛni ɔdubo bɔma ku-mi ku ebiti.”

english_verse: Who would have dared to tell Abraham that someday I would have a child? But in his old age, I have given him a son.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔma ndubɔkana na nka ɔsu Abraham ɔnini, ami Sara lɛnɔ ndubute ubi lɛnyi na ɔnyimi. Nsu ina ka Abraham ɔ́ɔbi ni, lɛ́wɔ lite-nwu na nwuna linengu uwi.” Abraham Ɔ́nyonu Hagar Ku Ubidi Ismael

english_verse: The time came when Sarah no longer had to nurse Isaac, and on that day Abraham gave a big feast. Hagar and Ishmael Are Sent Away
translation_verse: Isak úbabi lɛlɔ na basɔ belete-nwu lɛnyi. Na uwi ɔmɛni kemmo ni, Abraham ɔ́di limeyi libendi lɛdi.

english_verse: One day, Sarah noticed Hagar's son Ishmael playing, and she said to Abraham, “Get rid of that Egyptian slave woman and her son! I don't want him to inherit anything. It should all go to my son.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔ́su Abraham ɔnini, “Bɔku uleku ɔni mɔɔbla kaduli kabla mmɔ ku ubidi na batɔlɔ kaduli mmɔ, ɔsika uleku ɔni mɔɔbla kaduli kabla ubi ku mina ubi Isak balakana bana ɔti ala bule bɔdi.”

english_verse: Abraham was worried about Ishmael.
translation_verse: Litemi lɛmɛni lɛ́kpulu Abraham kayi, ɔsika lɛdanku ubidi.

english_verse: But God said, “Abraham, don't worry about your slave woman and the boy. Just do what Sarah tells you. Isaac will inherit your family name,
translation_verse: Nsu Katɔti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Awɔ, nu lɛla biala na Sara wasu-ɔ. Na kayi katakpulu-ɔ na ƒ'ubidi ku ƒula kabla ɔblane uleku ɔmɛni lɛlɔ. Ɔsika ɔkɛnku Isak lɛlɔ na adubudie kaba aani kalɛ na lɛ́su-ɔ líse.

english_verse: but the son of the slave woman is also your son, and I will make his descendants into a great nation.”
translation_verse: Na ƒula kabla ɔblane uleku ɔmmɔ ubidi ni, ndubɔya na udie kaba na benwini kadi ka anwu lɛnɔ ɔdi ƒ'ubidi ɔsu.”

english_verse: Early the next morning Abraham gave Hagar an animal skin full of water and some bread. Then he put the boy on her shoulder and sent them away. They wandered around in the desert near Beersheba,
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛni nsia ɔtanta tutuutu ni, Abraham úti adila ku ntu ɔsii ɔdi útile Hagar na údie anwu ku ubidi ɔnanabi ɔmmɔ ulu. Uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́yu ulu na ɔkɛ ɔɔví Beer-Seba ketele kemmo.

english_verse: and after they had run out of water, Hagar put her son under a bush.
translation_verse: Ka ntu búbasa ɔsii ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ɔda ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́kya ɔyuli ɔdi kalɔ.

english_verse: Then she sat down a long way off, because she could not bear to watch him die. And she cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Na anwu ɔ́kpɛ ɔ́lɛ-nwu kudɔ úsie kama blii, ɔsika ɔ́su lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Naaakana bunye bɔnu kalɛ na mina ubi uukpi.” Na ka ulie kesii kammɔ ni, úse kalɔ uuwulo keku geen.

english_verse: When God heard the boy crying, the angel of God called out to Hagar from heaven and said, “Hagar, why are you worried? Don't be afraid. I have heard your son crying.
translation_verse: Katɔti únu ka ubi ɔmmɔ uuwulo. Amu na Katɔti ɔtu ɔdi ɔ́kpali úmene ɔ́si Katɔ na ɔ́su Hagar ɔnini, “Hagar, bi nébo? Tayia! Katɔti únu ka ɔnamu ɔmmɔ uuwulo na kesii kani na ɔtɛ.

english_verse: Help him up and hold his hand, because I will make him the father of a great nation.”
translation_verse: Sie na atáda-nwu kɔnu na ɔta unye, ɔsika ndubɔya na udie kaba na benwini kadi bekyuli bonwu.”

english_verse: Then God let her see a well. So she went to the well and filled the skin with water, then gave some to her son.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Katɔti ɔ́ya na uleku ɔmmɔ anumi ábla nwaa na ɔ́nu libiɔ lɛdi na mmɔ ka ntu buwi. Anwuɔsu úsie na útédu ntu úyile ɔsii ɔmmɔ na úte ubidi na ɔ́ni.

english_verse: God blessed Ishmael, and as the boy grew older, he became an expert at hunting with his bow and arrows. He lived in the Paran Desert, and his mother chose an Egyptian woman for him to marry. A Peace Treaty
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na ɔkya ketele kani baalɔ Paran kemmo mmɔ ni, uni ɔ́wia uleku ɔ́siku Egyipte úte-nwu na úti. Abimelek Ku Abraham Bényimi Lɛla Lɛdi Na Beer-Seba

english_verse: About this time Abimelech and his army commander Phicol said to Abraham, “God blesses everything you do!
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Abimelek ku nwuna bekpone ɔtɔnkune ɔni baalɔ Pikol básu Abraham banini, “Bɔɔnu ka Katɔti uliku-ɔ na ƒula lɛla biala na aabla kemmo.

english_verse: Now I want you to promise in the name of God that you will always be loyal to me and my descendants, just as I have always been loyal to you in this land where you have lived as a foreigner.”
translation_verse: Ɔƒaani ni, mɔɔwia ka ese kenye kadi ete-mi na Katɔti anumi na mɛni ka aaadubo ami iye mina bebi iye bawɔ bɔtɔlɔ. Ka ɔƒɔ na adi na eli kalɔ kamɛni kemmo ɔsu ni, bla lɛbuni lɛni na lɛ́bla líte-ɔ te ami ku mina kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ bekyuli ƒui.”

english_verse: One day, Abraham told Abimelech, “Some of your servants have taken over one of my wells.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Abraham údie lɛla lɛni muukpóku-nwu ɔ́su Abimelek ɔ́si libiɔ ku ntu bɔni na nwuna kabla bablane béƒie báƒɔ-nwu kudɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: “This is the first I've heard about it,” Abimelech replied. “Why haven't you said something before? I don't have any idea who did it.”
translation_verse: Nsu Abimelek ɔ́su ɔnini, “Lɛɛɛgyi ukyuli ɔni nábla lɛla lɛmɛni udu. Na awɔ lɛnɔ átasu-mi ɔmɛni kudii. Na ńtenu lɛla lɛmɛni lɛnɔ kudii si ɔɔɔdi ɔmwi.”

english_verse: Abraham gave Abimelech some sheep and cattle, then the two men made a peace treaty.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Abraham úti baƒonu ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ na úti-ma úte Abimelek na bana inyɔ bényimi lɛlakpa linwi.

english_verse: Abraham separated seven female lambs from his flock of sheep,
translation_verse: Abraham údie baƒonu beledi bakɔdi maatɛ úse kɔmadɔ na bakladi akɔ.

english_verse: Abraham replied, “I want you to accept these seven lambs as proof that I dug this well.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Abraham údie kenye ɔnini, “Mɔɔyɔ́ ka aƒɔ baƒonu maatɛ bamɛni asiku-mi kudɔ aani kenye budie likpose ka ami néku libiɔ lɛmɛni.”

english_verse: So they called the place Beersheba, because they made a treaty there.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu na baalɔ kesii kani na ala ammɔ álɛ banii Beer-Seba. Ɔsika mmɔ na bana inyɔ bákpali ala bényimi lɛla lɛdi bése.

english_verse: When the treaty was completed, Abimelech and his army commander Phicol went back to the land of the Philistines.
translation_verse: Na lɛla lɛmmɔ bunyimi kama na Beer-Seba mmɔ ni, Abimelek ku nwuna bekpone ɔtɔnkune Pikol bénwini bésie Ƒilistiƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba and worshiped the eternal Lord God.
translation_verse: Na Abraham ɔ́lɛ ɔyuli kugyii kɔdi na Beer-Seba mmɔ. Na mmɔ na ɔ́kpali Katɔti lɛnyi ɔnii, Unwoti, Uwi Ƒui Katɔti.

english_verse: Then Abraham lived a long time as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines.
translation_verse: Na Abraham úlie Ƒilistiƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ uwi gyɔlɔɔ.

english_verse: Some years later God decided to test Abraham, so he spoke to him. Abraham answered, “Here I am, Lord.”
translation_verse: Akwa adi kama ni, Katɔti ɔ́kɔku Abraham ɔ́nu na ɔ́kpali-nwu ɔnini, “Abraham!” Na Abraham lɛnɔ ɔ́tuna ɔnini, “Ati, aanu-mi.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Go get Isaac, your only son, the one you dearly love! Take him to the land of Moriah, and I will show you a mountain where you must sacrifice him to me on the fires of an altar.”
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔnini, “Ta na eti ƒ'ubidi Isak unwi pɛ ɔni na aayɔ́ mmɔ, na eteesie Moria kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ. Mmɔ ni, tádu-nwu na akyula-nwu eti abla akpala ete-mi na kɔbi kɔni matina-a lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: So Abraham got up early the next morning and chopped wood for the fire. He put a saddle on his donkey and set out with Isaac and two servants for the place where God had told him to go.
translation_verse: Ka kadi kégye lɛdigye tutuutu ni, Abraham ɔ́ta na útile nwuna ebuo ala utine ala na ɔ́bala-nwu ala kaduɛ. Amu na útiku nwuna kabla bablane inyɔ ku ubidi Isak. Na ka ɔ́yɔ ekyweni pii na edu kalɛ na weti wakyula akpala ammɔ ni, ɔ́yu ulu úsie kesii kani na Katɔti ɔ́tina-nwu mmɔ.

english_verse: Three days later Abraham looked off in the distance and saw the place.
translation_verse: Na ka bákɛ ulu bésela limeyi lɛtɛdi lɛlɔ ni, Abraham ɔ́talaku anumi na ɔ́nu kesii kammɔ úmene.

english_verse: He told his servants, “Stay here with the donkey, while my son and I go over there to worship. We will come back.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su nwuna kabla bablane ɔnini, “Amii bɛsɔ binye mɛni ku ebuo ala utine ɔmmɔ. Na ami ku mina ubi busie butákpa Katɔti na bɔsɔ bunwini bubo.”

english_verse: Abraham put the wood on Isaac's shoulder, but he carried the hot coals and the knife. As the two of them walked along,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Abraham úti ekyweni ammɔ útile ubidi Isak. Na anwu ɔlati ɔda ogya ku kewii. Amu ka bana inyɔ bakɛ bésela ni,

english_verse: Isaac said, “Father, we have the coals and the wood, but where is the lamb for the sacrifice?” “My son,” Abraham answered, “God will provide the lamb.” The two of them walked on, and
translation_verse: Amu na Abraham údie kenye ɔnini, “Ubi, Katɔti ɔlati ndubute-bu koƒonu kɔni na bɔdubuti bɔbla akpala ammɔ.” Ka ɔ́su-nwu lɛni ni, básɔ béti bákɔ bésela.

english_verse: when they reached the place that God had told him about, Abraham built an altar and placed the wood on it. Next, he tied up his son and put him on the wood.
translation_verse: Na ka bédu kesii kani na Katɔti ɔ́tina-nwu mmɔ ni, Abraham ɔ́tu lɛkpabi na ɔ́tɛ ekyweni ammɔ ɔ́sia-ni lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́da ubidi na únyimi-nwu kaduɛ na ɔ́gyu-nwu ɔ́sia lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ na ekyweni ammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: He then took the knife and got ready to kill his son.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na úsienku kɔnu na údie nwuna kewii kalɛ na ɔdu ubidi.

english_verse: But the Lord's angel shouted from heaven, “Abraham! Abraham!” “Here I am!” he answered.
translation_verse: Kɔnakunwi ni, Katɔti ɔtu ɔdi ɔ́kpali ɔ́siku Katɔ ɔnini, “Abraham! Abraham!” Amu na Abraham údie kenye ɔnini, “Aanu-mi mɛni.”

english_verse: “Don't hurt the boy or harm him in any way!” the angel said. “Now I know that you truly obey God, because you were willing to offer him your only son.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́su Abraham ɔnini, “Ƒula kɔnu kutetuku ɔnamu ɔmmɔ. Na tabla-nwu lɛla lɛdi lɛnɔ. Ɔƒɛni na lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka aayia Katɔti sɔsɔ. Ɔsika éteni ka eti ƒ'ubidi ɔni ndi ubi unwi pɛ ɔni na ebo ete-nwu.”

english_verse: Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in the bushes. So he took the ram and sacrificed it instead of his son.
translation_verse: Amu ka Abraham ɔ́talaku anumi ɔɔnu ni, ɔ́nu koƒonu kɔgyani bonwu kɔdi ka kunye na kuna ese ábala kugyii kɔdi kɔgba. Amu na úsie útédie koƒonu kɔmmɔ na úti-ku ɔ́kpa ɔ́bla akpala na ubidi ɔmmɔ kenye.

english_verse: Abraham named that place “The Lord Will Provide.” And even now people say, “On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Abraham ɔ́lɔ kesii kammɔ ɔnii Katɔti Ɔdubute. Na úti úbedu ku ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ ni, ɔdi lɛsugba lɛdi na baasu banii, “Na Unwoti kɔbi lɛlɔ ni, anwu ɔlati ɔdubute lɛla lɛni bɔɔwia.”

english_verse: The Lord's angel called out from heaven a second time:
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Katɔti ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kpali Abraham kunyɔdi.

english_verse: You were willing to offer your only son to the Lord, and so he makes you this solemn promise,
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-nwu ka Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su ɔnini, “Éteni ka eti ƒ'ubidi unwi pɛ akpa ete-mi. Anwuɔsu ni, lɛ́kpali lɛlɔ líse kenye ka

english_verse: “I will bless you and give you such a large family, that someday your descendants will be more numerous than the stars in the sky or the grains of sand along the seashore. They will defeat their enemies and take over the cities where their enemies live.
translation_verse: ndubute-ɔ kusɛ kusɛ na lɛya na ƒula kaba bebi bemomo betulo ayabi. Na badubo bumomo aani ɛpu kɔnwinimi. Na ƒula bawɔ badubo bukpo na baƒɔ bana bekisine lɛma linengudi ƒui.

english_verse: You have obeyed me, and so you and your descendants will be a blessing to all nations on earth.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛ ƒula kaba kemmo ni, ndubute kayawi ƒui bekyuli kusɛ kusɛ. Ɔsika énu-mi litemi na ádi-ni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Abraham and Isaac went back to the servants who had come with him, and they returned to Abraham's home in Beersheba. The Children of Nahor
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Abraham ɔ́sɔ únwini úsie nwuna kabla bablane kudɔ. Na bénwini bésie Beer-Seba. Na Abraham útélie Beer-Seba mmɔ. Bebi Bani Nahor Ɔ́wɔ

english_verse: Nahor also had another wife. Her name was Reumah, and she had four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
translation_verse: Na nwuna ɔsɔnɔ ɔni baalɔ Rehuma lɛnɔ ɔ́wɔ bananabi úte-nwu. Na bebi bammɔ ndi Teba ku Gaham ku Tahas ku Maaka.

english_verse: “I live as a foreigner in your land, and I don't own any property where I can bury my wife. Please let me buy a piece of land.”
translation_verse: “Kadi bamba ukyuli na ndi. Na ndi ɔƒɔ na bina akɔ. Mɔɔyɔ́ ka bibo kabuli kalɔ kadi bite-mi na liye na bina kudɔ mɛni, na liti linwini bekyuli kavakɔ kalɛ na lɛkana na lɛva mina uleku.”

english_verse: “Sir,” they answered, “you are an important man. Choose the best place to bury your wife. None of us would refuse you a resting place for your dead.”
translation_verse: “Ati, kywɛ-bu atu, ɔgadine ɔni na áƒɔ lɛnyi geen na adi na bula akɔ. Anwuɔsu ti ƒula ukpine táva kɔƒiɔtɔ kɔbuni kɔni na béku bése mmɔ akɔ unwi kemmo. Bula akɔ ɔdi biala uléni ka ava ƒula ukpine na nwuna kaƒiɔtɔ kadi kemmo.”

english_verse: and replied, “If you are willing to let me bury my wife here, please ask Zohar's son Ephron
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Si bínu kalɔ ka lɛva mina ukpine ni, amu bɛkywɛ-mi atu na bivele Soha ubidi Eƒron bite-mi.

english_verse: to sell me Machpelah Cave at the end of his field. I'll pay what it's worth, and all of you can be witnesses.”
translation_verse: Na uti Makpela lɛtakpɛ ubu ɔni ndi anwu Eƒron ɔdi na ɔkya nwuna kalɔ kawɔlɔkɔ mmɔ uye ute-mi. Bɛsu-nwu na uye-ka ute-mi na kuye kɔni na ɔ́manku kenye. Na liti mmɔ linwini bekyuli kavakɔ.”

english_verse: Ephron was sitting there near the city gate, when Abraham made this request, and he answered,
translation_verse: Amu na Eƒron, Hitini ɔmmɔ údie kenye na ɔma ɔmmɔ ɔba kenye kesii kani na bása beli mmɔ, na ɔ́su Abraham ɔnini,
