english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Ƒarao úye benengu bammɔ ɔnini, “Wɛ na bɔdubɔkɛ ukyuli bamba ɔdi aani Yoseƒ ɔmɛni kalɛ ɔni na Unwoti Katɔti Kɔyu kɔ́ƒɔ-nwu lɛlɔ kemmo lɛni?”

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ƒarao ɔ́su Yoseƒ ɔnini, “Ka awɔ na Unwoti Katɔti údie ala amɛni ƒui ɔ́tina ni, naaabu nnii ukyuli bamba ɔdi ɔkya na ɔ́da anu na ɔɔnu ala kemmo kaduɛ aani ƒula kalɛ.

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Awɔ ndubo mina lɛga kadikɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ butaanu. Na bekyuli bakladi ƒui badubo ƒula kalɔ bɔkya na bataadi ƒula ɔda bubo lɛlɔ. Na lɛgaboku lɛnyi lɛni na mɔɔdi kani na ami ndubuti litulo-ɔ.” Yoseƒ Ɔɔnu Egyipte Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒarao údie nwuna lɛgadi kakwɛnimi na kɔnu ɔ́kya Yoseƒ kɔnu. Na ɔ́ya na béti awu gyɔlɔɔ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ɔbuni ɔdi bákya-nwu. Na béti sika ugyiedi adala bákya-nwu ɔkwɛ.

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́ya na ɔ́kɔ úduo kɛɛkɛ libi lɛdi kemmo na beekú-nwu taavinku aani ɔgadine kama unyene. Na bekyuli batɔ ku kudu momoomo banini, “Ɔ́si ɔdubo o-o! Bite-nwu ulu na ubavi.” Lɛni na Ƒarao ɔ́bla na úti Egyipte lɛlɔ bɔnu ƒui ɔ́kya Yoseƒ kɔnu.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Ƒarao ɔ́su Yoseƒ ɔnini, “Ami ndi Ƒarao, nsu si ɔɔɔdi awɔ masu anii babla lɛla lɛdi ni, ukyuli ɔdi uledie ɔgba iye ɔtala kɔnu katɔ!”

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni lɛnyi lɛni na Ƒarao ɔ́sia Yoseƒ ndi Saƒnat Panea. Na nwuna kama úte-nwu uleku ɔni baalɔ Asnat na ɔti ndi Potiƒera ɔni nádi bana kadi ɔkpane na ɔma ɔni baalɔ On kemmo. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Egyipte kalɔ ƒui kénwini Yoseƒ kadi na ɔɔka taamana kesii biala.

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Na sɔsɔ akwa maatɛ edeedi ani na ɔ́su ka edula adubɔdia kaduɛɛ mmɔ ni, Egyipteƒuɔ báƒɛ edula geen.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sala edula ebi amɛni aani ɛpu kɔnwinimi esu bonwu ani bɔka muedi na ɔsɔ ulénweni, ɔsika ábɔ étulo bɔkɔku.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Ubidi udeedi baalɔ Manase na nwuna kalɔ ndi Kayiƒala. Na Yoseƒ ɔnini, “Mɔɔlɔ-nwu lɛni, ɔsika Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na lɛ́yiƒala lɛbibo ku mina ɔti kaduli bekyuli.”

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: Na ubidi unyɔdi na baalɔ Eƒraim na nwuna kalɔ ndi ebi bɔnwu. Na anwu lɛnɔ Yoseƒ ɔ́sia-nwu lɛnyi lɛmmɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Kalɔ kani lɛlɔ nli muubó abi ni, Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na lɛ́wɔ.”

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Akwa maatɛ ani kemmo na edula adubɔdia Egyipteƒuɔ mmɔ éedu kawɔlɔkɔ.

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: Na akwa maatɛ ani kemmo na ɔ́su ka kɔka kɔdubo mmɔ ése kalɔ. Kɔlɔ kɔni náka kɔ́mana ƒui kɔka kúbo sɔsɔ ntu Egyipte lɛti kani na adila akya kesii biala.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Egyipteƒuɔ lɛnɔ bése kalɔ beenú kɔka kɔmmɔ ni, mmɔ na bákya animi ku kɔka buwulo taakya Ƒarao ka ute-ma adila. Mmɔ na Ƒarao ɔ́su nwuna kadi bekyuli ɔnini, “Biteesie Yoseƒ kudɔ. Na lɛla biala na ɔ́su-mi ni, na bɛbla bɛsiaku-ni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Na kɔlɔ ƒui bekyuli beebo Yoseƒ kudɔ teebeye edula, ɔsika kɔka kɔmmɔ kɔ́ƒɔ kayawi kesii biala.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Ka Yakob únu ka edula akya Egyipte ni, ɔ́su nwuna bebi bananabi ɔnini, “Bitasɔ bitelie mɛni bitataanu lɛlɔ anumi!

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: Línu ka banii edula akya Egyipte. Anwuɔsu bisie na bitéye na bɔkɛ lɛla lɛni na bɔdi bulie ngba na bulekpi!”

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Amu na Yoseƒ banwani leevu bátɔlɔ bésie Egyipte bétéye edula.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Nsu Yakob útaya na ubidi Benyamin ɔsiaku-ma, ɔsika ɔɔyia ɔnii ɔgbankpi ɔdi watásiaku-nwu.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israel bebi lɛnɔ básiaku bekyuli lisu lɛni nási Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ bésie betéye adila, ɔsika kɔka kɔmmɔ kɔ́ƒɔ Kanaan kalɔ ƒui lɛnɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Na ɔƒɛni ni, Yoseƒ ndi aban ɔgadine unengu ɔni muuyé edula ammɔ teete kadi biala bekyuli. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ka Yoseƒ banwani bammɔ lɛnɔ bébo ni, bábayu bébi kalɔ ku ɔbu na bégyele-nwu.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Na mmɔ ni, Yoseƒ únyimo ana ani na anwu ɔlatidi ɔmmɔ úgye dii úbavi ɔ́siku-ma lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Batu bani mɔɔbɛ́ taawia ala kalɔ taanu na bɛdi. Na bíbo bɛnii bɛɛwia bɛti kesii kani na buuubo ɔyikun na bɛsia mmɔ bɛkɛ-bu.”

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Amu na bédie kenye banini, “Ati, kudii! Edula kani na abu, ƒula kabla bablane, búbo bɔnii bubeye.

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yoseƒ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Kudii! Batu bani mɔɔwia ala kalɔ taanu na bɛdi! Bíbo bɛnii bɛɛwia bɛti kesii kani na buuubo ɔyikun na bɛsia mmɔ na bɛkɛ-bu!”

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Amu na bédie kenye banini, “Abu ƒula kabla bablane ni, nka mbo-bu leevu-inyɔ na bɔdi ɔnana unwi bebi. Na bula ɔti ɔmmɔ ɔkya Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔƒɛni. Na bula ɔnwani ɔnamudi ƒui ɔkya bula ɔti kudɔ, na unwi anwu ɔsɔ uuubo.”

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Ami lɛnɔ ndubo-mii bɔkɔku bɔnu na ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ. Lɛ́kpali ala mɔɔlɔ Ƒarao na nwuna lɛgadi kenye ka si bina ɔnwani ɔnamudi ɔmmɔ útebo mɛni ni, bina akɔ ɔdi ulágyu na kesii kamɛni.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bɛtala bina akɔ unwi na útákpanku bina ɔnwani ɔnamudi ɔmmɔ uboku. Na bina bakladi bani mebu ni, ndubɔya na bakya-mi aban ɔtɔ wetédu uwi ɔni na bɔ́nu bɔ́ti ka litemi geen na bɛɛsu. Na si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, na mɔɔsu-mii na Ƒarao lɛgadi lɛnyi kenye ka batu bani mɔɔwia ala taanu na bɛdi sɔsɔ!”

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Amu na Yoseƒ ɔ́ya na bébo-ma lɛkpu na bagyumanane enu kemmo emeyi atɛ.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Si bɛɛdi litemi geen lɛlɔ ni, bɛya na ukyuli unwi ɔsɔ ɔkya aban ɔtɔ ɔmɛni kemmo. Na bina bakladi bitáƒɔ edula bisienku bina kaduli bekyuli bani na kɔka kɔdaku bɔdu.

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: Mmomu bɛkpanku bina ɔnwani ɔnamudi ɔmmɔ biboku na bɔwia bina etemila kalɔ bɔnu. Na si sɔsɔ geen litemi na bɛda ni, bɛdubulie ngba.” Amu na báta kɔnakunwi bésie bátábla kalɛ na Yoseƒ ɔ́su-ma.

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama básu lɛlɔ banini, “Katuala kadi keeebo ɔmɛni kemmo. Bɔgyi nwaa ka bula ɔnwani ɔni bɔ́bla likpidi ɔsu na buubó abi amɛni udu. Búnyimo kalɛ na ɔ́ƒɛ ɔ́da-nwu uwi ɔni na uuvele-bu ka nka bútabla-nwu lɛla lɛmmɔ udu. Nsu búni na bútanu-nwu kɔnyana. Anwuɔsu na lɛbibo lɛmɛni udu líbo-bu lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Amu Ruben úye nwuna banwani bakladi ɔnini, “Ńtasu-mii nnii bitaya na bɔbla likpidi bɔƒiɔ ɔnamu ɔmɛni, na bítenuku-mi kalɔ? Ɔƒɛni bula ɔti ubi na ɔdi, na bɔdi ubugya unwi. Bɛɛnu ka nwuna ubugya lɛlɔ kɔtu na baaní-bu ɔmwi.”

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: Na ɔmɛni ƒui ni, baaagyi banii Yoseƒ uunú ala ani ƒui na baasu kede kede, ɔsika lɛdi bamba na uutemiku-ma asa na nwuna kenye udiene uudie kalɔ teete-ma.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, ɔ́gyu-ma kudɔ kɔnakunwi na úsie ɔkya uuwulo. Na ka ɔkwɛnu ɔ́da-nwu bukpo ɔ́ya ni, ɔ́sɔ únwini úbo-ma kudɔ ubatɛmiku-ma. Na ɔ́ya na béƒie Simeon na bényimi-nwu na bana anumi.

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Yoseƒ úbo nwuna kabla bablane ɔda ɔnii bakya edula beyile-ma aƒo. Na basɔku bana sika ɔƒualadi ɔni na nka bada badubo bebeye edula mmɔ bakya ɔdi biala koƒo kemmo. Na bete-ma adila bamba kalɛ na baatádi si bakɛ ulu bésela.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Ka ɔƒɛ ɔ́sa-ma na bédu kesii kani na batɛ ni, bana akɔ unwi ɔƒɛnimi nwuna koƒo ɔnii uute nwuna ebuo ala utine adila. Na ka ɔɔnu ni, aanu sika ɔƒualadi ɔni na úti útéye edula mmɔ na básɔku bakya-nwu koƒo kemmo.

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́su nwuna banwani kɔnakunwi ɔnini, “Bɛnu básɔku mina sika ɔƒualadi ɔmmɔ bákya-mi koƒo kemmo, bɛɛnu ka ɔsia edula lɛlɔ mɛni.” Mmɔ kani na bana ƒui bágyini benye. Bénwini bánu lɛlɔ na lɛlɔ lɛɛtɔ́-ma na béye lɛlɔ banini, “Bi na Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́bla-bu mɛni?”

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Amu ka bébeduo ɔma na Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ na bana ɔti Yakob kudɔ ni, básɔku lɛla biala nálɛ mmɔ ƒui básu-nwu. Na bédie kenye banini,

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Na nka bubo banwani leevu-inyɔ na bula ɔti ɔ́wɔ na unwi ɔsɔ uuubo. Na ɔnamudi ƒui ni, anwu nkya bula ɔti kudɔ na Kanaan mɛni.

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: “Amu na kalɔ kammɔ unengu ɔni mɔɔnu-ka lɛlɔ mɛni ɔ́su-bu ɔnini, ‘Ndubɔsia ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ na lɛnu lɛti si sɔsɔ na bɛɛdi litemi geen lɛlɔ. Bɛnyonu bina akɔ unwi bɛkya kama na mina kudɔ mɛni. Na biti adila bitésienku bina kaduli bekyuli bani na kɔka kɔdaku bɔdu.

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: Nsu bɛkpanku bina ɔnwani ɔnamudi biboku-mi na lɛti ka sɔsɔ bɛɛɛdi batu bani mɔɔwia ala kalɔ taanu. Na ndubɔsɔku bina ɔnwani lite-mii. Na ndubɔya na biteebo mɛni taabadi kuye ku bula kalɔ lɛlɔ bekyuli.’ ”

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ka ɔdi biala úwilimi nwuna edula ni, ɔdi biala sika ɔƒualadi ku obo ɔni na nka béti betéye edula mmɔ ɔkya bana aƒo kemmo. Na ka bátina bana ɔti lɛnɔ na ɔ́nu sika lɛbo lɛmɛni ni, bana ƒui báyia.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bana ɔti Yakob ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛ́ya na lɛ́yila mina bebi. Yoseƒ ɔsɔ uuubo. Simeon lɛnɔ na bɛnii béƒie bése ngye. Amu na bɛsɔ bɛkpanku Benyamin lɛnɔ bɛtɔlɔku-mi kudɔ? Bi ɔsu na mina lɛla biala linwini-mi kekuma lɛni?”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ruben ɔ́su ɔti ɔnini, “Si ńtakana na lɛsɔku Benyamin liboku-ɔ ni, akana na adu-mi bebi inyɔ bani nnye-mi. Awɔ, ti-nwu bo ɔda te-mi. Na ndubɔsɔku-nwu liboku.”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yakob ɔ́su Ruben ɔnini, “Mina ubi ulayu ulu ulasiaku-ɔ ulesie mmɔ! Ɔnwani úkpi na anwu lɛti kani nébu. Na si ɔgbankpi ɔdi úsie útásiaku anwu lɛnɔ na ulu ni, agyi anii lɛbibo kemmo na ndubuti mina liliƒuala ntéduo kekpine.”

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu edula ani ƒui na bétéye na Egyipte mmɔ ni, báadi lɛla biala ƒui bédie báwɔlɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bana ɔti Yakob ɔ́lɔ-ma ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bɛsɔ bisie na bitéye edula blii adi biboku.”

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: Na si elénu kalɔ bɔdi ni, abu lɛnɔ bulésie. Ɔsika bɔsu na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Bɛsɔ bitada bitalɛ-mi anumi, amu ntu bɛdanku bina ɔnwani.’ ”

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bana ɔti Israel ɔsu ɔnini, “Dɛ na ɔ́bla na bɛɛsu ɔnana ɔmmɔ bɛnii bibo ɔnwani bamba na bíti lɛbibo lɛmɛni bíboku-mi lɛlɔ?”

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bédie kenye banini, “Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔlati nénye kpakplaa uuye-bu ala ammɔ udu teenu ɔ́si bula bɔwɔ ku kaduli bekyuli lɛlɔ. Ala ani bene na úye-bu adi ndi, ‘Bina ɔti ɔmu uli ngba? Bibo banwani bamba badi?’ Na ala ani na úye-bu kenye kani na búdie. Na bútati bɔnii ɔdubɔsu ɔnini, ‘Bɛkpanku bina ɔnwani buboku mɛni.’ ”

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Amu na Yuda ɔ́su ɔti Israel ɔnini, “Ya na okloƒu ɔmɛni ɔsiaku-bu na bɔyu ulu kɔnakunwi. Na butéye edula adi buboku na bɔkɛ lɛla lɛni na butaadi kalɛ na bulekpi.

english_verse: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
translation_verse: Ami ɔlati líti mina lɛlɔ muunyene kama ka lɛla lɛdi lilálɛku-nwu. Na si ńtasɔku-nwu ńteboku na liti-nwu mbenyene ƒula anumi mɛni ni, ami ndubunye kayu kammɔ kenye mina ngba uwi ƒui.

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: Na kalɛ na use ni, si ɔɔɔdi abu alati nákpɛ kama ni, nka búusie mmɔ bubo kunyɔ muedi.”

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Na biti sika ɔƒualadi ɔni na básɔku bákya-mii aƒo kemmo akpa anyɔ bɛda. Ɔsika ɔlɛka bitáƒɔ kayu kedeedi kammɔ lɛnɔ. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ bɔti na bátati asa na básɔku sika ɔƒualadi ɔmmɔ bákya-mii aƒo kemmo.

english_verse: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
translation_verse: Na bɛkpanku bina ɔnwani bɛda na bɛyu ulu kɔnakunwi biteesie ɔnana ɔmmɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Na muuvele Unwoti Katɔti nnii ɔnu-mii kɔnyana na ɔya na ɔnana ɔmmɔ kayi kayɔ na ɔnyonu Benyamin ku ɔnwani ɔni na úƒie úse, na basiaku-mi na bɛsɔ binwini bibo. Nsu ami amu ni, si kukpi kɔ́du-mi ni, bɔdu na kɔ́du-mi.”

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, nwuna bebi bammɔ béti sika ɔƒualadi ɔmmɔ akpa anyɔ aani kalɛ na ɔ́su-ma. Na béti etela ammɔ lɛnɔ ku Benyamin na bátɔlɔ bésie Egyipte na bétédie lɛlɔ bátina Yoseƒ.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Ka Yoseƒ ɔ́nu Benyamin ku nwuna banwani ni, ɔ́su nwuna kaduli lɛlɔ ɔnune ɔnini, “Kpanku bekyuli bamɛni teesienku mina kaduli. Na adu ebuo ɔdi na anwa adila adi ete-bu. Ɔsika ɔlɛka ami ku-ma bɔdi ɔƒiiwi ɔmɛni.”

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Kaduli lɛlɔ ɔnune ɔmmɔ ɔ́bla aani kalɛ kani na Yoseƒ ɔ́su-nwu.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: Amu uwi ɔni na bákpanku-ma béselaku Yoseƒ kaduli ni, liƒu bonwu lɛdi lɛ́da Yoseƒ banwani bamɛni. Na ɔdi biala ɔ́kali ɔnii, “Sika ɔƒualadi ɔni na básɔku bákya bula aƒo kemmo ɔni na búbo búbavi ɔsu na béti-bu béboku mɛni. Na ɔɔyɔ́ ka úkpoku-bu na ɔdi-bu lɛlɔ na uƒie-bu unwini nwuna kabla bablane, na ɔƒɔ-bu bebuo ala betine.”

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, báni béde kaduli lɛlɔ ɔnune ɔmmɔ asa na badubuduo kaduli kammɔ kemmo na básu-nwu banini,

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: “Ati, buvele búbo mɛni kudeedi uwi ɔdi návi búbeye edula.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Na búti sika ɔƒualadi ɔbambadi lɛnɔ búboku kalɛ na bubeye adila bamba. Na bútati ukyuli ɔni násɔku sika ɔmmɔ ɔkya-bu aƒo kemmo.”

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Yoseƒ kaduli lɛlɔ ɔnune ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Bɛsɔ bitayia. Ɔmmɔ útebile lɛla lɛdi. Bina Katɔti ɔni ndi Unwoti Katɔti úte bina ɔti ni, anwu néti lɛkɛ ɔ́kya bina aƒo kemmo. Ami ndi ukyuli ɔni na bɛ́ƒɔ kayu kammɔ bíte.” Ka ɔ́su-ma lɛni ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, útédie Simeon úboku-ma.

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔkpanku-ma na bétéduo Yoseƒ kaduli kemmo, na úte-ma ntu, na báƒɔ lɛgba. Na ɔ́wia adila úte bana bebuo ala betine.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni Yoseƒ banwani lɛnɔ básala bana etela ani na badanku bése. Na benye bagya Yoseƒ ka ubo, ɔsika básu-ma ka anwu ku-ma ndubo bɔdi ɔƒiiwi ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
translation_verse: Ka Yoseƒ úbeduo kaduli ni, béti etela ani bada béboku mmɔ béte-nwu, na bákya eli kalɔ béte-nwu.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: Na Yoseƒ úye-ma kalɛ na báta. Na úye-ma lɛnɔ ɔnini, “Bina ɔti ɔni na bɛ́su ka ɔ́ɔbi lɛlɔ geen mmɔ ni, ɔmu ɔkya ngba?”

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Amu na bédie kenye banini, “Bula ɔti ɔni ndi ƒula kabla ɔblane ɔmu uli ngba na ubo ɔlɔkplu kaduɛ.” Mmɔ lɛnɔ béboku eli kalɔ na bábu-nwu geen.

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́nu ɔ́ka ɔ́mana na ɔ́nu ɔnwani Benyamin ɔni ndi-nwu unibi geen mmɔ. Na úye-ma ɔnini, “Bina ɔnwani ɔnamudi ƒui ɔni na bɛ́su mmɔ na ɔdi mɛni?” Ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Benyamin ɔnini, “Mina ubi, Unwoti Katɔti lɛƒɔndia lɛsiaku-ɔ uwi biala.”

english_verse: Then, because of his love for Benjamin, he rushed off to his room and cried.
translation_verse: Na ka ɔkwɛnu úkpo-nwu geen ka ɔ́nu ɔnwani ɔsu ni, Yoseƒ ɔ́babla ɔ́lɛ na útábɛ úwulo keku na nwuna ɔtɔ ɔni na údie úse lɛlɔ lɛti pɛ kemmo.

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama údu ntu ɔ́ƒɔ anumi na ɔ́kya kayi na únwini úbo-ma kudɔ. Mmɔ na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bidie adila ammɔ na bɔdi.”

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: Amu na bése-ma kadikɔ bun bun. Yoseƒ uli kakɛ kenwi, na nwuna banwani lɛnɔ beli kakɛ kenwi. Na béte Egyipteƒuɔ lɛnɔ kesii bamba na beli. Bábla lɛni, ɔsika Egyipteƒuɔ beení ka ama ku Hebriƒuɔ badi basala.

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: Nwuna banwani bammɔ ƒui bélie kalɔ na nwuna anumi. Na ɔ́ya na beli atɔ asia ɔ́si ɔtɔnkune úbedu ɔnamudi lɛlɔ. Na ɔmɛni ɔ́bla-ma kalɛ kadi.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Na kesii kani na Yoseƒ uli mmɔ na beele adila taasiku teeboku-ma. Na ani na béte Benyamin ni, abla aani bakladi adi akpa alɔ. Lɛni na anwu ku-ma bádi na báni bákɛ ebiti ku kayi ƒaa.

english_verse: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
translation_verse: Na eti mina sika ɔƒualadi ɔɔƒɛɛ akya ɔnamudi koƒo kemmo ebunku nwuna edula sika ɔƒualadi ɔmmɔ.” Na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́bla aani kalɛ na Yoseƒ ɔ́su-nwu.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: Ka kadi kadubo kegyekɔ ni, bédie-ma ulu ku bana bebuo ala betine.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Yoseƒ banwani bamɛni bétesie tɔ ɔgyu ɔdi na ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kudɔ asa na ɔ́tala nwuna kaduli lɛlɔ ɔnune ɔnii ɔsia-ma kama. Úbo-nwu ɔda ɔnini, “Sie na atábala banana bammɔ kɔnakunwi. Na si átásiaku-ma ni, na eye-ma anini, ‘Bi ɔsu na bíti likpidi bɛ́ƒɔ lɛbuni lɛni na mina ɔtɔlati ɔ́bla-mii kayu?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Ɔɔɔdi mina ɔtɔlati ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔni kemmo na ɔɔní taasiku, na anwu kani kemmo na ɔɔnu ala kemmo taati na bíti bɛtɔlɔku mɛni? Kalala geen kadi na bɛ́bla mɛni!’ ”

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: Ka ɔnana ɔmɛni útasiaku-ma sɔsɔ ni, anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́sɔku ala ammɔ úye-ma lɛni kani.

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: Nsu banana bammɔ bédie kenye banini, “Ati, bi ɔsu na aasu ala amɛni udu taasiku-bu lɛlɔ. Abu ƒula kabla bablane bulakana lɛmɛni udu bɔbla kudii!

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Na sika ɔƒualadi udeedi ɔni na bɔ́ka bɔnu muedi ni, bɔ́sɔku-nwu bɔ́siku Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ búboku. Bi ɔsu na aabu anii bɔdubuyu sika ɔƒualadi iye ugyiedi bɔsiku ƒula ɔtɔlati kesii?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Na si bula akɔ ɔni koƒo kemmo na ánu lɛla lɛmɛni udu ni, na adu-nwu. Na abu bakladi bunwini kabla bablane bute bula Ati.”

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔnana ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔmmɔ ɔdia. Bɔdubuti-nwu lɛni. Anwuɔsu bina akɔ ɔni koƒo kemmo na manu lɛnila lɛmɛni ni, anwu ndubuti lɛbla mina kabla ɔblane. Na bakladi ni, lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-ma.”

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔdi biala ɔ́babla na ɔ́lɛlɛ nwuna etila úse kalɔ na ɔ́ƒɛnimi-nya.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, kaduli lɛlɔ ɔnune ɔmmɔ úse kalɔ na ɔɔnu bana aƒo kemmo taawia ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ. Úse kalɔ ɔ́si bana ɔtɔnkune lɛlɔ na úbawɔlɔ ɔnamudi lɛlɔ. Na ɔnamudi ɔni ndi Benyamin mmɔ koƒo kemmo na ɔ́nu ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: Ka úbo úte lɛni ni, ɔ́bla-ma kɔnyana geen na bana ƒui báni bana lɛwu bábwɛ! Amu na básɔ bágyu ala bétile bana bebuo ala betine na bénwini bésie ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Ka bétéduo ni, Yoseƒ ɔmu ɔkya kaduli asa na Yuda ku nwuna banwani bakladi bábalɛlɛ. Mmɔ na báyu bébi kalɔ na Yoseƒ lɛgba akɔ.

english_verse: who asked them, “What have you done? Didn't you know I could find out?”
translation_verse: Amu na Yoseƒ úye-ma ɔnini, “Bi ɔdi na bɛ́bla mɛni? Bɛɛɛgyi bɛnii ukyuli aani ami bene udu ni, mɔɔkana na mɔɔnu ala na bɔbɛ kemmo?”

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yuda ɔ́ƒɔ na údie kenye ɔnini, “O Ati, bi na bɔdubɔkana na bɔsu ɔƒɛni. Bi geen na bɔdubɔsu na ati ka bɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́ mɛni kemmo lɛla lɛdi? Unwoti Katɔti ɔlati muudie abu, ƒula kabla bablane, likpidi keyi. Ɔƒɛni amu búnwini ƒula kabla bablane ƒui, abu ku ukyuli ɔni koƒo kemmo na bánu ƒula sika ɔƒualadi ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ.”

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Nsu Yoseƒ údie kenye ɔnini, “Kudi kudii! Ɔɔɔdi ami ndubɔbla lɛmmɔ udu. Ukyuli unwi pɛ ɔni kudɔ na bánu ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔmɛni ni, anwu kani na ndubo bɔkpanku na unwini mina kabla ɔblane. Amii bakladi ƒui binwini biteesie bina ɔti kudɔ ku keyi buɛɛ.”

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Yuda ɔ́ni úde-nwu na útévele-nwu ɔnini, “Ati, kɛku-mi kayi na aya na ami, ƒula kabla ɔblane, lɛtɛmiku awɔ, mina Ati. Takɛ kɔnyi takya ami, ƒula kabla ɔblane! Ngyi ka awɔ ku Ɔga Unengudi Ƒarao ni, kavumana keeebo-mi ntɛ ɔdi.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Awɔ ɔni ndi bula Ati ni, éye abu, ƒula kabla bablane, anini, ‘Bibo ɔti iye ɔnwani ɔnamudi ɔdi?’

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na búdie kenye ka ni, ‘Bubo ɔti ɔni náabi lɛlɔ geen. Na ubo ubi ɔni na ɔ́wɔ na nwuna linengu uwi. Ɔnwani ɔni na anwu ku-nwu badi uni unwi bebi úkpi na anwu lɛti kani nébu na uni bebi akɔ. Na ubi ɔmɛni ni, bula ɔti ɔɔyɔ́-nwu geen.’

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: “Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Ati, ásɔ ásu-bu anii, ‘Biti-nwu biboku na ami ɔlati lɛnu-nwu!’

english_verse: We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him.
translation_verse: Ati, mmɔ na bɔ́su-ɔ bɔnini, ‘Bula ɔti ulakana kebii kamɛni bɔnyonu. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni na ɔ́tɔlɔ-nwu kudɔ ni, bula ɔti ɔdubo bukpi.’

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Nsu ásu-bu aani ƒula kabla bablane kalɛ anini, ‘Si bítakpanku bina ɔnwani ɔnamudi ɔmmɔ bíteboku ni, bɛsɔ bitada bitalɛ mina anumi.’

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ka búnwini búsie bula ɔti ɔni ndi ƒula kabla ɔblane kudɔ ni, bɔ́su-nwu lɛla lɛni na awɔ bula Ati ásu-bu.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: “Ɔmmɔ kama ni, bula ɔti ɔ́su-bu ɔnini, ‘Bisie na bitéye adila ammɔ adi bibu.’

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: Nsu bɔ́su-nwu bɔnini, ‘Bulakana busie ntu bɔdanku bula ɔnwani ɔnamudi ɔmmɔ asa na bɔdubusie. Ɔsika bulakana ɔnana ɔmmɔ anumi bɔda bɔlɛ amu ntu bula ɔnwani ɔnamudi ɔsiaku-bu.’

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: “Ƒula kabla ɔblane ɔni ndi bula ɔti údie kenye ɔnini, ‘Bɛgyi ka bebi inyɔ na mina uleku ɔni náwɔ kebii kamɛni ɔ́wɔ úte-mi.

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: Na bana akɔ unwi ɔ́da-mi úse. Na lɛ́su ka ɔƒɛni kalɛ eƒiebuo ɔdi nádu-nwu na ɔ́duli-nwu lɛna lɛni. Na ɔ́si ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, ńsɔ ńtanu-nwu kudii.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Na si bɛ́sɔ bɛ́kpanku ɔmɛni lɛnɔ bɛ́tɔlɔku-mi kudɔ na ɔgbankpi ɔdi útásiaku-nwu mmɔ ni, agyi anii lɛbibo kemmo na ndubuti mina liliƒuala ntéduo kekpine.’

english_verse: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
translation_verse: “Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔƒɛni ni, si ɔnanabi ɔmɛni ɔɔɔsiaku-mi si lɛ́sɔ línwini ńtéduo mina ɔti ɔni ndi ƒula kabla ɔblane kudɔ ni,

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Ami, ƒula kabla ɔblane, líti mina lɛlɔ línyene kama líte mina ɔti ka ubi ɔmɛni ɔdubɔsɔ unwini ubo-nwu kudɔ na lɛla lɛdi lilabla-nwu. Na lɛ́su-nwu nnini, ‘Si ńtasɔku ɔnamu ɔmɛni ńteboku-ɔ ni, ami ndubɔƒɔ kɔtu bɔni bɔmmɔ mina ngba ƒui kemmo.’

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: “Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔƒaani ni, Ati, ya na ami ƒula kabla ɔblane lɛ́sɔ lɛkya-a kudɔ mɛni aani ƒula kabla ɔblane na aya na ɔnamu ɔmmɔ uteesie bula ɔti kudɔ ku nwuna banwani bakladi.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Dɛ na ndubɔkana na lɛsɔ linwini lisie mina ɔti kudɔ si ɔnamu ɔmɛni ɔɔɔsiaku-mi? Ulatɛ! Tadu-mi ku kɔnyana! Naaakana mina ɔti lɛƒɛda lɛni mebo-nwu lɛlɔ bunye bɔnu kunyɔ.”

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Na etemila ammɔ kama ni, Yoseƒ ɔ́sɔ útakana kayi bɔkya na bani nnye ƒui anumi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́va ɔ́su nwuna bebunkune bammɔ ɔnini, “Ɔdi biala ɔvi ɔlɛ!” Na ka bávi bálɛ ni, kébu Yoseƒ ku nwuna banwani lɛti asa na údie lɛlɔ ɔ́tina-ma.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Na úwulo keku momoomo ɔni na Egyipteƒuɔ bani na amadɔ ƒui bénu-nwu kɔku. Na bátásu Ɔga Unengudi Ƒarao kaduli bekyuli lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Amu na Yoseƒ ɔ́su nwuna banwani ɔnini, “Bɛni bide-mi.” Na ka báni béde-nwu ni, ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ami ndi bina ɔnwani Yoseƒ ɔni na bíti bíye, na béti-mi béboku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ!

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: Na ɔƒaani ni, kayi katakpulu-mii. Na biteti kɔnyi lɛnɔ bitakya lɛlɔ na kalɛ na bíti-mi bíye asa na líbo mɛni ɔsu. Ɔsika Unwoti Katɔti ɔɔwia ka lɛƒɔ bekyuli pii ngba lɛlɛku ɔgbankpi kemmo. Anwuɔsu Unwoti Katɔti úti-mi úmene kesii kamɛni ɔnii ngyu ntɔ-mii.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Akwa anyɔ sɔɔn mɛni ka kɔka kúbo kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Na akwa alɔ bamba ani lɛnɔ ndubo ni, ɔdi ulakana edula adi bɔkya na balaƒɛ adi lɛnɔ na kalɔ kammɔ ƒui kemmo.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́tala-mi ɔnii ngyu ntɔ-mi na mbaklibi kama lise lite amii bani lɛnɔ na ɔ́ƒuna úse úte ka ɔƒɔ-mii ngba.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu ɔɔɔdi amii néti-mi bímene kesii kamɛni. Mmomu Unwoti Katɔti nátala-mi mɛni. Anwu nábla-mi kadi ƒui ogyangba ute Ƒarao. Anwuɔsu Ƒarao kaduli bekyuli ƒui baalɔ-mi banii Ati. Na ndi Egyipte kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ ɔdine.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: Ɔƒaani ni, bɛbabla na bisie mina ɔti kudɔ na bitásu-nwu bɛnini, ‘Lɛni na ami ƒ'ubidi Yoseƒ mɔɔsu ka ni, “Unwoti Katɔti úti-mi ɔ́bla ukyuli ɔni na Egyipteƒuɔ ƒui baalɔ Ati. Ɔsu tɔlɔ bo-mi kudɔ na tetu uwi munu munu.

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Na si ébo ni, adubulie kalɛkɛ kani baalɔ banii Gosen lɛlɔ. Na mmɔ udenku-mi kesii kani na nli. Awɔ ku ƒula bebi ku bawɔ ƒui ku ƒula bebuo lidu lidu ƒui na akpanku-ma ada ku ala ani ƒui na ebo.

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Na ndubute-mii ala ani ƒui na bɛɛwia, ɔsika akwa alɔ sɔɔn nsɔ ntɛ anumi adubo ɔni na kɔka kɔmmɔ kenye kaláyɔ tɔ. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, awɔ ku ƒula kaduli bekyuli ku bebuo ƒui bɛdubo udu bɔyii.” ’

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: “Amii alati bɛɛnu-mi taati ka ami Yoseƒ geen na ɔdi. Na mina ɔnwani Benyamin lɛnɔ ɔɔnu-mi taati ka ami mɔɔtɛmiku-mii.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Bɛsu mina ɔti kalɛ ɔnwa na Egyipteƒuɔ ƒui baakya lili kalɔ teete-mi. Na bɛsu-nwu ala ani ƒui na bɛ́nu. Na bɛkpanku mina ɔti biboku mɛni kɔnakunwi.”

english_verse: Joseph and Benjamin hugged each other and started crying.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔ́kya Benyamin kɔgbu na úwulo ebiti keku na Benyamin lɛnɔ úwulo na bébo báda lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Ɔ́kya nwuna banwani bakladi ƒui kɔgbu na úwulo keku ku ebiti ka básɔ bása lɛni. Na batɛmi ɔnwa ku ɔnwa atɛ pii.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Ka kudu kɔmɛni kútédu Ɔga Ƒarao ku nwuna benengu bakladi kudɔ ka Yoseƒ banwani bébo ni, lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ bana ƒui kaduɛ.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Ɔga unengudi Ƒarao ɔ́su Yoseƒ ɔnini, “Su ƒula banwani anii, ‘Bɛbla kalɛ mɔɔsu-mi mɛni. Bitile bina bebuo ala betene ala na binwini bisie Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: Na si bísie ni, na bɛkpanku bina ɔti ku bina lɛlɔ bekyuli ƒui biboku-mi mɛni. Ndubute-mii kalɔ kabuni ƒui na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ na bɛdi kalɔ kammɔ lɛmwi lɛni nkya-ka.’

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: “Su-ma anii ami Ƒarao nnii beti kɛɛkɛ ɔni na bebuo baaní mmɔ ɔdi bada ɔ́si Egyipte mɛni. Nwuna kemmo na bana bebi ku beleku badubo bulieku bina ɔti ƒui na bakpanku-ma beboku.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na ala ani na bebo ni, betekpoku lɛlɔ munu munu na ana lɛlɔ. Ɔsika ala abuni ani ƒui nkya Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ adubunwini bana ɔdi.”

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Israel bebi bénu kalɔ ka babla ala ani na básu-ma mmɔ. Yoseƒ úte-ma kɛɛkɛ aani kalɛ na Ɔga Ƒarao ɔ́su. Na úte-ma ala lidu lidu lɛni na beti bada besie ulu.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: Úte ɔdi biala adala awɔdi na Benyamin anwu ni, úte-nwu adala ammɔ udu akpa alɔ.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Na úti ala ani ndubo mɛni lɛnɔ úmene ɔti. Na ala ammɔ ndi bebuo ala betine leevu bani nti ala abuni lidu lidu ani nkya Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na úte bebuo ala betine bamba beledi leevu bani nti edula ku bodobodo ku adila lidu bamba lɛni na ɔdubuti usie ulu si ɔ́si ɔdubo.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama údie nwuna banwani bammɔ ulu na úbo-ma ɔda ɔnini, “Bitatádɔ na ulu lɛlɔ si bísela.”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu báyu ulu na básia bálɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ na bétéduo bana ɔti Yakob kudɔ na Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: Ka bédu mmɔ ni, básu-nwu banii, “Yoseƒ ɔmu uli ngba. Na geen ni, anwu mɔɔdi Egyipte kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ!” Litemi lɛmɛni lɛ́tua Yakob na ɔ́bla-nwu dɛye dɛye, na útaƒɔ-ma útadi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Nsu ka básɔku ala ani nálɛ ƒui kalɔ bédie béte-nwu ku ala ani na Yoseƒ ɔ́su-ma na ɔ́nu kɛɛkɛ ɔni Yoseƒ úti úmene ka bebeti-nwu beboku ni, ɔ́sɔ únwini úbo lɛlɔ kemmo na anumi ábla-nwu nwaa.

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Israel ɔ́su ɔnini, “Lɛ́ƒɔ lɛ́di sɔsɔ ka mina ubi Yoseƒ uli ngba. Na ndubusie ntánu-nwu asa mekpi.”

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Israel úti ala ani na ubo ƒui na ɔ́yu Egyipte ulu. Na ka útédu Beer-Seba ni, ɔ́bla akpala adi na mmɔ úte Unwoti Katɔti ɔni na ɔti Isak lɛnɔ útaakpa.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Na mmɔ ni, Unwoti Katɔti útemiku Israel na kɔna kemmo usien na ɔ́kpali-nwu ɔnini, “Yakob! Yakob!” Na Yakob lɛnɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Ati, aanu-mi mɛni.”

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ami ndi ƒula Unwoti Katɔti, na ndi ƒ'ɔti lɛnɔ Unwoti Katɔti. Tayia ka esie Egyipte, ɔsika ndubɔya na bimomo na bɛbla kadi bekyuli bani mbo ɔyikun geen na mmɔ.

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: Ndubuliku-ɔ ɔni na ésela Egyipte mɛni. Na ndubutiku-ɔ na asɔ enwini ebo ɔni na kavumana kadi kelebo-nwu kemmo. Na Yoseƒ enu kemmo na adubo bɔyula.”

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families. Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of
translation_verse: Bebi bammɔ na Lea ɔ́wɔ úte Yakob ɔni bákya Mesopotamia kalɔ lɛlɔ na bana ɔnwani ulekubi Dina kama. Na nwuna bebi bananabi ku belekubi bammɔ bumomo bɔdi nkyuli avlaatɛ-ɛtɛ.

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Na si Ƒarao ɔ́lɔ-mii na úye-mii ɔnini, ‘Bi kabla na bɛɛbla?’ ni,

english_verse: Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of
translation_verse: Bebi leevu-ɛku bani anyi na búnu mmɔ ni, Silpa náwɔ-ma úte Yakob. Na Silpa ɔdi Lea kaduli ulekubi kabla ɔblane ɔni na ɔti Laban úte-nwu.

english_verse: Jacob and Bilhah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Rachel, had seven children and grandchildren. Their son Dan took his son Hushim. Their son Naphtali took his sons Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
translation_verse: Bebi maatɛ bani anyi na búnu mmɔ ni, Bilha náwɔ-ma úte Yakob. Na Bilha ɔdi Rahel kaduli ulekubi kabla ɔblane ɔni na ɔti Laban úte-nwu.

english_verse: Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law.
translation_verse: Yakob ku anwu badi bani ƒui nésie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ bebo nkyuli liti ku ɛku. Na nwuna bebi beleku ama baaakɛ.

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: Yoseƒ ɔ́ya na béti nwuna kɛɛkɛ béboku-nwu, na ɔ́klibi lɛlɔ na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Gosen mmɔ útásiaku ɔti Israel. Uwi ɔni na Yoseƒ ɔ́nu ɔ́ti kani na ɔ́tu ɔ́bali-nwu na úwulo keku na uwi útu.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani na Israel ɔ́su Yoseƒ ɔnini, “Ɔƒɛni amu uwi údu ka likpi, ɔsika ami ɔlati lɛ́nu ku mina anumi ka akya ngba sɔsɔ.”

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Amu na Yoseƒ ɔ́su nwuna banwani ku ɔti kaduli bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ɔnini, “Lísela na ntánu Ƒarao na ami ku-nwu bɔtɛmi na lɛsu-nwu nnini, ‘Mina banwani ku mina ɔti kaduli bekyuli bani ƒui nli Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ bátɔlɔ bébo-mi kudɔ mɛni.

english_verse: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bammɔ badi baƒonu badane. Na baanyuɛ bebuo ɔsu badanku bana bebuo lidu lidu ku ala ani ƒui na bebo na mmɔ béboku mɛni.’

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: na bidie kenye bɛnini, ‘Ati, abu ƒula kabla bablane ni, bebuo kani na bɔɔnyuɛ ɔ́si-bu lɛnamu uwi ƒui aani bula bati kalɛ.’ Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na bete-mii kuƒi ka bilie kalɔ kammɔ kemmo na Gosen kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ. Ɔsika bebuo banyuɛne ƒui beesé Egyipte kadi bekyuli ƒui lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Ƒarao úye-ma ɔnini, “Bi kabla na bɛɛbla?” Amu na bédie kenye banini, “Ati, abu ƒula kabla bablane ni, bebuo na bɔɔnyuɛ aani bula bati kalɛ.”

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, básu-nwu banini, “Búbo bɔnii bubakya-a kudɔ na ƒula kalɔ lɛlɔ mɛni uwi blii ɔdi. Kɔka kunengudi kɔni nébo mɛni ni, kuna kenye kebo ɔkplu na Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ na bula bebuo basɔ balakɛ kadikɔ buni kadi. Ɔmɛni ɔsu buuvele-ɔ ka aya na abu ƒula kabla bablane bɔƒɔ lɛlɔ bɔkya Gosen mɛni uwi blii ɔdi.”

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ƒarao ɔ́su Yoseƒ ɔnini, “Ƒ'ɔti ku ƒula banwani bébo-ɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Aanu Egyipte kalɔ lɛnɔ nwi-ɔ anumi késela. Wia-ma keliekɔ na kalɔ kammɔ kesii kani na ánu ka kadia. Ya na belie Gosen mmɔ. Na bana akɔ ɔni na ánu ka ɔgyi bebuo lɛlɔ ala kaduɛ ni, na aya na utaanu mina bebuo lɛnɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Yoseƒ ɔ́ya na ɔti Yakob lɛnɔ úbeduo-ma kudɔ mmɔ na Ƒarao ɔ́nu-nwu. Na Yakob úte-nwu kusɛ kusɛ.

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: Ka Ƒarao ɔ́nu-nwu ni, úye-nwu ɔnini, “Akwa alɛ na áaƒɔ?”

english_verse: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
translation_verse: Na mmɔ ni, Yakob úte Ƒarao kusɛ kusɛ asa na ɔ́vi ɔ́lɛ-nwu kudɔ.

english_verse: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yoseƒ ɔ́ya na ɔti ku nwuna banwani báwia keliekɔ na Egyipte mmɔ, na úse-ma kama ku akɛla ani nkya mmɔ na kabunikɔ ƒui. Mmɔ kakya Rameses kalɛkɛ kesii kani na Ƒarao ɔ́tina.

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Yoseƒ ɔ́ɔƒɔ egulabi ani na bekyuli bebo ƒui na Egyipte ku Kanaan, ɔsika béti béye edula. Na úti egulabi ammɔ ƒui úboku Ɔga Ƒarao kesii.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Ka Kanaan ku Egyipte kadi bekyuli bánu ka egulabi ása-ma ƒui ni, bébo Yoseƒ kudɔ na bábasu-nwu banini, “Alakana-bu bunye bɔnu na bukpi bɔyii udu na ƒula anumi. Buvele, te-bu adila, ɔsika bɔsɔ buuubo egulabi adi lɛnɔ. Bɔ́ɔkpala bula lɛtɔ kemmo ƒui ɔni na lɛla lɛla lɛsɔ liiibo.”

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yoseƒ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Amu biti bina bebuo bibavumanaku adila ammɔ si bɛnii bina egulabi ása.”

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Ka lɛkwa lɛmmɔ lɛ́sa ni, Egyipteƒuɔ bammɔ básɔ bébo-nwu kudɔ lɛkwa lɛni nsia. Na bábasu-nwu banini, “Ati bulakana-a lɛla lɛdi buti bɔbala ka bɔ́sɔ buuubo ku lɛla buuutulo bula ɔlɔna ugyii ɔni nse-bu ku bula kɔlɔ kɔni kani na bubo. Ɔsika bula egulabi ku bebuo bani ƒui na bubo bása na bénwini awɔ badi.

english_verse: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
translation_verse: Na alakana-bu bunye bɔnu na bukpi bɔyii ku udu na ƒula anumi na kalɔ kasɔ kewi ukpludi. Anwuɔsu ni, ye-bu ku bula kɔlɔ na ete-bu adila. Na buti ku bula kɔlɔ ƒui buse ɔkpa bute Ƒarao. Te-bu edula kalɛ na bɔkɛ bɔdi bulie ngba na bulekpi. Na kalɔ kammɔ kalasɔ kelewi ukpludi.”

english_verse: The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Yoseƒ úye bana kɔlɔ kɔni ƒui nkya Egyipte úte Ƒarao. Na béye bana mmo ƒui, ɔsika kɔka kɔmmɔ kenye káyu ɔkplu geen. Na kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ ƒui lɛnɔ kúnwini Ƒarao kɔdi.

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: Nsu bakpane kɔlɔ aku ni, Yoseƒ úteye aku. Ɔsika bakpane bammɔ ama bebo bana kɔdikɔ kɔni na beete-ma uwi biala na adila ammɔ kemmo. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu béteti bana kɔlɔ béteye bátaƒɔ adila adi.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yoseƒ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔƒaani ni, bɛnu bɛti ka líye ami ku bina kɔlɔ ƒui ɔmwi líte Ƒarao. Anwuɔsu ni, bɛɛnu edula ebi ani na bɛdubo bɔkya.

english_verse: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
translation_verse: Nsu si edula ammɔ ábi ni, bíti lɛkpa lɛlɔndi bite Ƒarao. Na akpa ene ani mebu ni, amii alati bɛklibi-nya bise bite amii ku bina bebi ku kaduli bekyuli kalɛ na bɛkɛ bɛdi na bɛkɛ bɛkya lɛkwa bamba.”

english_verse: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na básu Yoseƒ banini, “Áƒɔ-bu lili ngba. Ati, ya na bula lɛlɔ lɛda-a ebiti. Búnu kalɔ ka bɔdubulie ɔkpa bute Ƒarao.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Yoseƒ úti ɔmɛni ɔ́bla ɔda bubo úte-ma ɔkɛnku Egyipte kalɔ kammɔ ala bɔdi lɛlɔ úti úbedu ku ɔmwi kadi. Amu ntu bakpane kalɔ kani naaadi Ƒarao kadi.

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Israel kadi bekyuli béelie kalɔ na Gosen kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ. Na báakɛ lɛkɛ na báawɔ geen lɛnɔ na bemomo.

english_verse: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na ka nwuna ukpiwi ɔ́ni úde ni, ɔ́ya na bálɔ Yoseƒ béte-nwu. Mmɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Si mina lɛlɔ lɛ́da-a ebiti ni, na ete-mi kɔnu na akpali Katɔti ese-mi kenye ka adubɔbla-mi lɛƒɔndia lɛdi. Na adubɔdi-ka lɛlɔ lɛnɔ. Tava-mi na Egyipte mɛni.

english_verse: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Mmomu si lísie ati bene kudɔ ni, na eti-mi ukpine alɛku Egyipte mɛni atáva kesii kani na báva ama lɛnɔ.” Yoseƒ údie kenye kɔnakunwi ɔnini, “Ndubɔbla lɛni.”

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yakob ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Kpali Katɔti na ese-mi kenye ka adubo bɔbla lɛni sɔsɔ.” Yoseƒ lɛnɔ ɔ́kpali Katɔti na ɔ́su-nwu geen ka wabla lɛni. Na Israel ɔ́bu ɔƒa nwuna ugyii ɔdadi lɛlɔ na úmwi Katɔti.

english_verse: Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔdi kama ni, bábasu Yoseƒ banini, “Ƒ'ɔti uuƒi.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́ta na útiku nwuna bebi bananabi inyɔ bani ndi Manase ku Eƒraim na bésie ɔti kudɔ.

english_verse: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
translation_verse: Ka bétéduo ni, ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́su Yakob ɔnini, “Ƒ'ubidi Yoseƒ úbo-ɔ kudɔ.” Mmɔ kani na Israel úkpoku lɛlɔ ɔyikun bɔdi na ɔ́ta úlie nwuna katɛnkɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
translation_verse: Amu na Yakob ɔ́su Yoseƒ ɔnini, “Unwoti Katɔti údie lɛlɔ ɔ́tina-mi na kesii kani baalɔ Lus na Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na mmɔ ni, úte-mi kusɛ kusɛ.

english_verse: and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Ndubɔya na awɔ bebi na bimomo geen na binwini kadi bekyuli pii, na ndubuti kalɔ kamɛni lite-ɔ na kenwini awɔ ku ƒula kaba kemmo bebi kadi uwi ƒui.’

english_verse: Then Jacob went on to say: Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
translation_verse: “Na ɔƒaani ƒula bebi bananabi inyɔ bani na báwɔ béte-ɔ na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ mɛni asa na líbo ni, badubo-ma bɔka ka ami badi badi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Eƒraim ku Manase badubo bunwini ami badi kalɛ kani na Ruben ku Simeon badi ami badi.

english_verse: Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na bebi bani na adubɔsɔ awɔ na bana kama ni, ama na badubɔka aani awɔ badi. Na kadikɔ kani na badubɔkɛ ni, kadubɔsi bana banwani bamɛni lɛnyi kemmo.

english_verse: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na línwini lɛ́si Mesopotamia kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, ḿbasiaku ɔgbankpi. Na uwi ɔni na bɔkɛ ulu na kébu blii na buduo Eƒrata na kesii kani lɛnɔ baalɔ Betlehem na Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, mina uleku Rahel úbekpi na líduo kɔnyana. Anwuɔsu lɛ́va-nwu na kuludɔ mmɔ.”

english_verse: Jacob was very old and almost blind. He did not recognize the two boys, and so he asked Joseph, “Who are these boys?” Joseph answered, “They are my sons. God has given them to me here in Egypt.” “Bring them to me,” Jacob said. “I want to give them my blessing.” Joseph brought the boys to him, and he hugged and kissed them.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Israel bɔnu bɔmmɔ bɔsɔ bulékpi-nwu kaduɛ ka ɔ́ɔbla unengu ɔsu. Nwuna anumi aabla-nwu ƒluƒlu. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Yoseƒ ɔ́kpanku bebi bammɔ na báni béde ɔti na ɔ́kya-ma kɔgbu.

english_verse: Jacob turned to Joseph and told him, “For many years I thought you were dead and that I would never see you again. But now God has even let me live to see your children.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Israel ɔ́su Yoseƒ ɔnini, “Lɛɛɛsia anu nnii nsɔ ndubo-ɔ bɔnu kudii. Na ɔƒaani ni, Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na lɛ́nu-ɔ ku ƒula bebi lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
translation_verse: Ka ɔ́su lɛni ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, Yoseƒ ɔ́da bebi bammɔ na báta Israel lɛgba lɛlɔ na ɔ́yu úbi kalɔ na ɔti anumi mmɔ.

english_verse: After Joseph got up, he brought his two sons over to Jacob again. He led his younger son Ephraim to the left side of Jacob and his older son Manasseh to the right.
translation_verse: Yoseƒ ɔ́ya na Eƒraim úbenye-nwu kɔdianu na Israel kɔmii kakɛ. Na ɔ́ya na Manase úbenye-nwu kɔmii kakɛ na Israel kɔdianu kakɛ. Na ɔ́ya na bana ƒui báni béde ɔti Israel.

english_verse: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Nsu Israel údie nwuna kɔdianu útásia Eƒraim lili ina ka anwu ndi ɔnamu. Na ɔ́vumana nwuna kɔmii útásia Manase lili ina ka anwu ndi ubi unengudi.

english_verse: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
translation_verse: Amu na úte Yoseƒ kusɛ kusɛ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Unwoti Katɔti nátɔnku mina bati bani ndi Abraham ku Isak. Unwoti Katɔti anwu náda-mi na mina ngba emeyi kemmo ƒui aani baƒonu ɔdane kalɛ.

english_verse: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́ya na nwuna ɔtu údie-mi na ɔdi útabla-mi kalala kadi. Muuvele nnii ute bebi bananabi bamɛni kusɛ kusɛ. Mina lɛnyi ku mina bati bani ndi Abraham ku Isak lɛnyi na badubo bɔdi. Na muuvele nnii bawɔ na bemomo na baƒɔ lɛnyi na kayawi.”

english_verse: Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ka Yoseƒ ɔ́nu ka Eƒraim lili na ɔti úti nwuna kɔdianu ɔ́sia ni, útayɔ-nwu kaƒɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, ɔ́da ɔti kɔdianu ɔnii uuti utásia Manase lili.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
translation_verse: Na Yoseƒ ɔ́su ɔti ɔnini, “Ati, oowo! Aanu, ɔmɛni ndi ubi unengudi. Ti ƒula kɔdianu sia-nwu lili.”

english_verse: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
translation_verse: Nsu ɔti úbulo na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ubi, ngyi lɛni. Anwu lɛnɔ ni, kadi bekyuli badubɔsi-nwu kemmo na ɔƒɔ lɛnyi. Nsu nwuna ɔmansiane ni, ɔdubɔƒɔ lɛnyi utulo-nwu. Na nwuna bebi ku bawɔ badubo bunwini kadi bekyuli pii.”

english_verse: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
translation_verse: Úte-ma kusɛ kusɛ limeyi lɛmmɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bina lɛnyi kemmo na Israel kadi bekyuli badubo buvele kusɛ kusɛ bute bekyuli banini, ‘Unwoti Katɔti ute-ɔ kusɛ kusɛ aani Eƒraim ku Manase.’ ” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́ya na Eƒraim únwini lili úte Manase.

english_verse: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Israel ɔ́su Yoseƒ ɔnini, “Uwi údu ka likpi. Nsu Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubulieku-ɔ na ɔsɔku-ɔ usienku ƒ'ɔti bene kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Jacob called his sons together and said: My sons, I am Jacob, your father Israel.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yakob ɔ́lɔ nwuna bebi ƒui ɔnini, “Bibasala na lɛsu-mii ala ani ndubo-mii bɔlɛku na emeyi ani nkpɛ kama adubo kemmo.

english_verse: Reuben, you are my oldest, born at the peak of my powers; you were an honored leader.
translation_verse: “Ruben, awɔ ndi mina ubi unengudi, mina ɔyikun, awɔ ndi mina lɛkloƒu ɔyikun ɔni na lɛ́ka keyi budie. Awɔ na baabu teetulo ƒui. Awɔ mbo ɔyikun ntulo.

english_verse: Uncontrollable as a flood, you slept with my wife and disgraced my bed. And so you no longer deserve the place of honor.
translation_verse: Ƒula udu use aani ntu bɔni mɔɔnwanɛ lɛlɔ. Nsu asɔ eletulo bakladi na lɛla lɛdi kemmo lɛnɔ. Ɔsika ákɔ ƒ'ɔti katɛnkɔ. Na ébile-nwu atɛla.

english_verse: Simeon and Levi, you are brothers, each a gruesome sword.
translation_verse: “Simeon ku Lewi badi banwa. Bana kuwii kɔwia kuwi ubugya kalɔ.

english_verse: I never want to take part in your plans or deeds. You slaughtered people in your anger, and you crippled cattle for no reason.
translation_verse: Naaawia ka liduo bana kasusu ketikɔ iye bana kasalakɔ. Ɔsika bana kɔnyi kɔ́ya na bádu bekyuli na békulo bana bebuo kɔgbama nti na basɔ balakana lɛla lɛdi bɔbla.

english_verse: Now I place a curse on you because of your fierce anger. Your descendants will be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Badubo bɔnuku-ni. Béyi ku kɔnyi kati kati na bebo kalala. Ndubo-ma bugyingya na Yakob badi akɔ. Na lɛgya-ma lɛkya na Israel badi akɔ.

english_verse: Judah, you will be praised by your brothers; they will bow down to you, as you defeat your enemies.
translation_verse: “Yuda, ƒula banwani badubo-ɔ bumwi. Na adubo ƒula bekisine amɔ bɔda. Na ƒ'ɔti bebi badubo-ɔ lili kalɔ bɔkya.

english_verse: My son, you are a lion ready to eat your victim! You are terribly fierce; no one will bother you.
translation_verse: Yuda, gyata ubi na adi. Ebuo keƒiekɔ na ási ébo. Aabɛ́bɛ taayu teebi kalɔ aani gyata uwele. Na ɔma ndubuse kayi ɔnii utágya-a?

english_verse: You will tie your donkey to a choice grapevine and wash your clothes in wine from those grapes.
translation_verse: Adububo ƒula ebuo ala utine ada kɔdingyii lɛlɔ. Na adubɔƒɔ ƒula lɛwu na kɔdingyii kɔmmɔ ebi ntu kemmo. Na adingyii ebi ntu bɔni nse aani ubugya kemmo na badubɔƒɔ ƒula lɛwu gyɔlɔɔ.

english_verse: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
translation_verse: Ƒula anumi aatu anumi. Na ƒula anyi eekeye.

english_verse: Zebulun, you will settle along the seashore and provide safe harbors as far north as Sidon.
translation_verse: “Sebulon ɔdubulie ɛpu kɔtu. Na lɛkɔlɔ libendi lɛdubɔlɛlɛ mmɔ buɛɛ. Na nwuna lɛmii lisie ɔgyu litédu Sidon kakɛ.

english_verse: Dan, you are the tribe that will bring justice to Israel.
translation_verse: “Dan, adubɔbla ala ulu lɛlɔ siin bute ƒula Israelƒuɔ kaba kemmo bekyuli.

english_verse: You are a snake that bites the heel of a horse, making its rider fall.
translation_verse: Adubɔdu ƒula bekisine aani kalɛ na kɔlakpi kɔni ntɛ kuludɔ kɔɔdu ɔpɔnkɔ lɛgba na ɔya na ukyuli ɔni nli-nwu lɛlɔ ɔlɛ utébo kalɔ.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: “O Unwoti, nnye mɔɔnu-ɔ anumi ka aƒɔ-bu ngba!

english_verse: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
translation_verse: “Aser adila adubo-ɔ bɔdia geen, na akɛ adila ani náƒɔ kuye na bete baga muedi.

english_verse: Naphtali, you are a wild deer with lovely fawns.
translation_verse: “Neƒtali, ese aani alakpiakɔ ebuo ɔni nédie atu ɔkɛ lɛku kemmo, na ɔɔwɔ bebi babuni.

english_verse: Joseph, you are a fruitful vine growing near a stream and climbing a wall.
translation_verse: “Yoseƒ, ese aani kɔdingyii kɔni mɔɔnwu ebi pii na libiɔ kɔtu, na ƒula kɔgba kuusé ɔgyu.

english_verse: Enemies attacked with arrows, refusing to show mercy.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani muukisi-ɔ ku ɔdu kati kati badubo-ɔ bukpoku ku atula. Na badubɔtu-nya balɛ-ɔ kalala bɔdi.

english_verse: But you stood your ground, swiftly shooting back with the help of Jacob's God, the All-Powerful One— his name is the Shepherd, Israel's mighty rock.
translation_verse: Nsu ƒula kataminta kalatu kaláƒiɔ. Na ƒula enu ani mbo ɔkplu geen alayuɛ. Ɔsika Yakob Unwoti Ɔyikune kɔnu kɔɔgyumana-a. Na Katɔti ndi Israel ɔdane aani baƒonu ɔdane kalɛ, na use aani lɛtakpɛ ute-nwu.

english_verse: Your help came from the God your father worshiped, from God All-Powerful. God will bless you with rain and streams from the earth; he will bless you with many descendants.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti Katɔti ɔni ndi ƒula bati Katɔti muubunku-ɔ. Na ɔdubute-ɔ ntu bɔsiku katɔ ku kalɔ ƒui. Na ɔdubɔya na beleku bawɔ na bete bebi anyii ntu.

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: Kusɛ kusɛ ɔni na ami, ƒula ɔti, muute-ɔ ni, úbomo utulo ala ani nkya abi enengudi ku abinkpo ani nnye ási kukuuku ƒui kemmo. Ala amɛni ƒui na muuvele ka enwini kusɛ kusɛ ewi awɔ Yoseƒ lili aani ɔga ubi na ƒula banwani bakladi ƒui akɔ.

english_verse: These are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is how Jacob gave each of them their proper blessings. Jacob's Death
translation_verse: Israel kaba kemmo bebi leevu-inyɔ bammɔ mɛni. Na ala ani na búnu mɛni ndi ala ani na ɔ́su-ma uwi ɔni na úte-ma kusɛ kusɛ. Yakob Kukpi Ku Kalɛ Na Báva-nwu

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: Kemo kammɔ ku lɛtabi ubu ɔmmɔ ni, Hetiƒuɔ kudɔ na béye mmɔ básiku.”

english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Ka Yakob úbo nwuna bebi ɔda ɔmɛni ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔ́sɔku lɛgba útásia nwuna atɛla lɛlɔ na ɔ́yula, na úsie ɔti bene kudɔ.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Yoseƒ ɔ́yu úwi ɔti lɛlɔ na úwulo geen na ɔ́kya-nwu kɔgbu.

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for Jacob's body to be embalmed,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yoseƒ ɔ́su bekyuli bani mɔɔklibi ɔnii baklibi ɔti. Anwuɔsu báklibi-nwu

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: Ka emeyi ani na beeti teewulo ukpine ávi ni, Yoseƒ ɔ́su Ƒarao kelisa benengu ɔnini, “Si mina ablala áyɔ-mi kaƒɔ ni, na bitásu Ƒarao bɛnini,

english_verse: Just before my father died, he made me promise to bury him in his burial cave in Canaan. If the king will give me permission to go, I will come back here.”
translation_verse: ‘Mina ɔti ɔ́ya na lɛ́kpali Katɔti líse-nwu kenye ka mabla lɛla lɛni na wasu-mi. Na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Uwi údu ka likpi. Na ɔlɛka ava-mi na kaƒiɔtɔ kani kemmo na ami ɔlati líku líse na Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, bite-mi kuƒi na ntáva mina ɔti ukpine na mmɔ. Na ndubo bunwini bubo na ɔmmɔ kama.’ ”

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ƒarao údie kenye ɔnini, “Sie na atáva ƒ'ɔti aani kalɛ na ɔ́ya-a na ákpali Katɔti ése-nwu kenye ése ka adubo bɔbla.”

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: Ka bédu ɔma ɔni baalɔ Atad na Yordan kudɔ na kesii kani bákwaa bésie na beewiile edula ni, béwulo momoomo geen. Na mmɔ ni, Yoseƒ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla ukpine buwulo ɔdi emeyi maatɛ úte ɔti.

english_verse: The Canaanites saw this and said, “The Egyptians are in great sorrow.” Then they named the place “Egypt in Sorrow.”
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ka Kanaanƒuɔ bani nkya mmɔ bánu buwulo ɔdi ɔni baabla mmɔ ni, Kanaanƒuɔ básu banini, “Egyipteƒuɔ baabla buwulo ɔdi kpakplaa ɔdi.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na baalɔ kesii kani nde Yordan mmɔ banii Abel Misraim.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔda ɔni na Yakob úbo nwuna bebi ni, bábla lɛni kani.

english_verse: They took him to Mamre in Canaan and buried him in Machpelah Cave, the burial place Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite.
translation_verse: Na béti-nwu bésienku Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ na bátáva-nwu na Makpela lɛtabi ubu. Na ude Mamre kesii kani na Abraham úye ka bataava nwuna bekyuli. Na Hitini ɔni baalɔ Eƒron kudɔ na úye kemo kani kemmo na ubu ɔmmɔ ɔkya.

english_verse: After the funeral, Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else returned to Egypt. Joseph's Promise to His Brothers
translation_verse: Ka báva bana ɔti báwɔlɔ ni, Yoseƒ ku nwuna banwani ku bekyuli bani ƒui násiaku-nwu bésie ɔti kavakɔ mmɔ bénwini bésie Egyipte. Yoseƒ Úse Nwuna Banwani Kayi

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Ka Yoseƒ banwani bánu ka bana ɔti úkpi ni, básu banini, “Ɔƒɛni kalɛ Yoseƒ ɔdubo nwuna kɔnyi keyi budie na ɔƒɔ-bu likpidi lɛni na bɔ́bla-nwu kayu.”

english_verse: So they sent this message to Joseph: Before our father died,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bátala ukyuli ɔdi ka usie utásu Yoseƒ ɔnini, “Ƒula banwani banii Ƒ'ɔti ɔ́da kenye kadi úse asa na úkpi ɔnini,

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: ‘Ƒula banwani ekpidi ani ƒui na bábla-a ku ulikplu ni, ti-nya ƒui kyiɛ-ma.’ Anwuɔsu buuvele-ɔ geen ka ƒula bati ƒui Unwoti Katɔti kabla bablane bamɛni ni, ti bana ekpidi kyiɛ-ma.” Ka kenye kamɛni kébedu Yoseƒ ni, úwulo geen.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na nwuna banwani bébo bábayu bébi-nwu lɛgba kudɔ na bévele-nwu básu banini, “Ƒula kabla bablane na bɔdi.”

english_verse: But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided.
translation_verse: Nsu Yoseƒ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bitayia, ɔɔɔdi ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti.

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: Ɔsika bɛ́kali bɛnii bɛɛbla-mi likpidi, nsu Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na lɛbuni nálɛ lɛ́si-nwu kemmo kalɛ na ɔbla nwuna kabla kani bɛɛnu ɔƒɛni. Na ɔƒɔ bekyuli pii ngba.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ni, bitayia. Ndubute amii ku bina bebi ƒui ala ani na bɛdubɔwia.” Na ɔ́sɔ úse-ma kayi na ɔ́tɛmiku-ma na lɛƒɔndia kemmo. Yoseƒ Úkpi

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Yoseƒ úlie Egyipte mmɔ ku ɔti lɛlɔ bekyuli bakladi ƒui. Na ɔ́ƒɔ akwa eti anyɔ ku leevu.

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́nu kaba katɛdi na Eƒraim bebi akɔ. Lɛni kani na ɔ́nu Manase ubidi Makir bebi lɛnɔ na béti-ma bábasia-nwu akɔnkɔ ka báwɔ-ma.

english_verse: Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yoseƒ ɔ́su nwuna banwani ɔnini, “Uwi údu ka likpi. Nsu Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubo-mii bubunku na ɔkpanku-mii ɔlɛku Egyipte kalɔ kamɛni kemmo usienku kalɔ kani na ɔ́su úse ka wete-mii kemmo. Lɛni na úse Abraham ku Isak ku Yakob kenye úse.”

english_verse: Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
translation_verse: Na Yoseƒ ɔ́ya na Israel bebi bákpali Katɔti bése kenye, na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ngyi geen ka Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubo ubebunku-mii. Na ɔdi ka biti mina ekubi bɛtɔlɔku mɛni.”

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his son Joseph was already there. So Jacob took his eleven other sons and their families. They were: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Benjamin, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher. Altogether, Jacob had
translation_verse: Na kaba bekyuli bani nási Yakob kemmo bumomo bɔdi nkyuli liti ku aavlanyɔ. Nsu Yakob ubidi Yoseƒ anwu ɔkya Egyipte kukuuku.

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔdi kama ni, Yoseƒ ku nwuna banwani ku kaba kammɔ bekyuli bakladi bébekpi.

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: Nsu Israel kadi bekyuli bammɔ báwɔ pii geen béyile Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ, na bébo ɔlɔkplu lɛnɔ geen.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Na uwi útetu asa na bése ɔga ɔwɔdi na Egyipte mmɔ. Na ɔga ɔmɛni ɔɔɔgyi Yoseƒ.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmɛni ɔ́su nwuna bekyuli ɔnini, “Bɛnu, Israelƒuɔ bamɛni béemomo bétulo-bu.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Bɛya na bɔwia ulu ɔdi na basɔ belemomo belebu. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni na banii kekpo kadi kébo ɔƒɛni ni, badubo bula bekisine bubunku na bekpo badi-bu lɛlɔ na bekeli balɛ kalɔ kamɛni kemmo.”

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: Amu na Egyipteƒuɔ báwia lɛlɔ badine béte-ma aani bekyuli beƒiedi lɛlɔ banune kalɛ. Bekyuli bamɛni bénye-ma lɛlɔ na baabla kabla kpakplaa, na bátu Pitom ku Rameses lɛma linengudi kesii kani na beesé ala teete bana Ɔga Ƒarao.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Nsu kalɛ kani na baanya Israelƒuɔ bamɛni taamana ni, lɛni kani na beemomo teebu na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu Egyipteƒuɔ bébo baayia Israelƒuɔ bamɛni,

english_verse: and made them work so hard
translation_verse: na beenye-ma lɛlɔ na baabla kabla kpakplaa teetulo lɛlɔ.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: Baanwu lɛti na beekúlo atimbɔ ku katuma lidu bamba lɛnɔ na kemo ɔni na bana ngba keliela káyu-ma ɔdu geen.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Amu na Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ɔmɛni ɔ́su Siƒra ku Pua bani mɔɔƒɔ́ kɔwɔ teete Hebriƒuɔ beleku bammɔ ɔnini,

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: “Si uwi ɔni na bɛɛƒɔ́ Israelni uleku ɔdi kɔwɔ na ubi ɔmmɔ ɔdi ɔnanabi ni, na bɛdu-nwu. Nsu si ulekubi na ɔdi ni, bitadu-nwu.”

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Nsu ka beleku bamɛni baayia Katɔti ɔsu bátabla bátasiaku kalɛ na Ƒarao ɔ́su-ma mmɔ lɛlɔ, mmomu báya na beli ngba.

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Amu na beleku bamɛni bédie kenye banini, “Israelƒuɔ beleku beeese aani Egyipteƒuɔ beleku. Bebo ɔlɔkplu ɔkplu. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu asa na buteenu ni, na báawɔ!”

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Na ka baayia Katɔti ɔsu ni, ɔ́ya na kɔwɔ baƒɔne bammɔ alati lɛnɔ báwɔ.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Ƒarao úbo nwuna bekyuli ɔda ɔnini, “Si bɛ́nu ka Hebrini uleku ɔdi ɔ́wɔ ubi ɔnanabi ɔdi ɔda ni, na bibo-nwu bɛkya Nil Ketu kemmo. Nsu si ulekubi na ɔdi ni, na bɛya na ɔsɔ ɔkya ngba.”

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ɔnana ɔdi ɔ́si Lewi ɔtɔ kemmo na úti uleku ɔdi ɔ́siku ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kani kemmo.

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Na uleku ɔmɛni úbawɔ ɔnanabi úte-nwu. Na kalɛ na ubiwɔ ɔmɛni ɔɔdia bɔnu ɔsu ni, úti-nwu ɔ́bɛla abuli atɛ sɔɔn.
