english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Nsu ka ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka ubiwɔ ɔmɛni ɔsɔ uládia bɔbɛla ni, ɔ́wia kagyigyɛ kadi na ɔ́wia kɔma ɔ́mana-nwu kemmo ku kama kalɛ na ntu bulakana-ka kemmo buduo. Amu na úti ubiwɔ ɔmɛni ɔ́kya kagyigyɛ kamɛni kemmo. Na úti-nwu útákya ketudɔ alakpi adi akɔ na Nil Ketu kɔtu.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Na ubiwɔ ɔmɛni ɔnwani ulekubi ɔ́bɛ unye kesii kadi na unye ɔɔnu lɛla lɛni ndubɔlɛku ubi ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kani na Ɔga Ƒarao ubidi ulekubi úsie ketu mmɔ ɔnii utákpi. Na ka ɔkya ɔɔkpí ni, nwuna bebunkune lɛnɔ bakɛ ketu amadɔ mmɔ. Amu na kɔnakunwi Ƒarao ubidi ɔmɛni ɔ́nu kagyigyɛ kamɛni na livo lɛmmɔ akɔ na ɔ́tala nwuna belekubi kabla bablane bammɔ unwi ka utágyu-ka uboku-nwu.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Ka Ƒarao ubidi úbimi kagyigyɛ kamɛni ni, ɔ́nu ka ubiwɔ ɔdi ɔ́kya-nwu kemmo. Ubiwɔ ɔmɛni úse kalɔ uuwulo na nwuna lɛlɔ lɛ́kywi-nwu kaƒɔ. Mmɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ubiwɔ ɔmɛni ɔdi Hebriƒuɔ bebi akɔ ɔdi.”

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ubiwɔ ɔmɛni ɔnwani ulekubi úsie ɔga ubidi ɔmɛni kudɔ na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Nteesie na ntálɔ Hebrini uleku ɔdi mboku-ɔ na uteete-nwu lɛnyii teete-ɔ?”

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ubidi ɔmɛni údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɛɛn.” Mmɔ na ulekubi ɔmɛni útálɔ ubiwɔ ɔmmɔ uni geen.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ubidi ɔmɛni ɔ́su uleku ɔni bátálɔ mmɔ ɔnini, “Ti ubiwɔ ɔmɛni na eteete-nwu lɛnyii teete-mi, na ndubuteete-ɔ lɛyuƒɔla.” Anwuɔsu uleku ɔmɛni úti ubiwɔ ɔmɛni na uute-nwu lɛnyii.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Amu ka ubiwɔ ɔmɛni ɔ́lɛ lili blii ni, uleku ɔmmɔ úti ɔnamu ɔmmɔ úsienku ɔga ubidi ɔmmɔ, na úti-nwu ɔ́bla ubidi na ɔ́sia-nwu lɛnyi ɔnii Mose lɛni kalɔ ndi “Lídie ubi ɔmɛni lɛ́lɛku ketu kemmo.” Mose Úkeli Úsie Midian Kalɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Mose ɔ́ɔlɛ lili ƒui kama ni, limeyi lɛdi úsie kesii kani na nwuna bekyuli bakya, na ɔ́nu kabla kpakplaa kani na baabla. Mmɔ ni, ɔ́nu ka Egyipteni ɔdi ɔkya uubó Hebrini ɔdi ɔni ndi anwu Mose lɛlɔ ukyuli.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Amu ka Mose ɔ́tɛ anu ɔ́mana ni, ɔ́nu ka ukyuli ɔdi uuude mmɔ. Amu na úƒie Egyipteni ɔni nébo Hebrini ɔmmɔ na úbo-nwu ɔ́du. Na úti-nwu ɔ́bɛla lɛti kemmo.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Na ka kadi kégye ni, Mose ɔ́nu ka Hebriƒuɔ lɛti lɛti badi bakya beekpó. Amu na ɔ́su ɔnwa ɔni náƒiɔ ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na eebó ƒula ɔnwa Hebrini?”

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔnana ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔma nédi-ɔ bula lɛlɔ ɔdine ku bula litemi ɔtɛne? Munuu aayɔ́ ka adu-mi aani kalɛ na ádu Egyipteni ɔmmɔ yoo?” Mmɔ na Mose ɔ́yia na ɔ́su lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Likpidi lɛni na lɛ́bla mɛni ni, bekyuli bánu-ni báti.”

english_verse: When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian. One day, when Moses was sitting by a well,
translation_verse: Amu ka Ƒarao únu litemi lɛmɛni ni, ɔ́wia ulu biala lɛlɔ ka nka ɔdu Mose. Nsu Mose úkeli na útélie Midian kalɔ lɛlɔ na libiɔ lɛdi kɔtu.

english_verse: the seven daughters of Jethro, the priest of Midian, came up to water their father's sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Na ka úsie útélie mmɔ ni, Midian ɔkpane ɔdi bebi begblebi maatɛ bébo libiɔ lɛmmɔ kudɔ banii bebedu ntu na beti betéte bana ɔti baƒonu ku bese.

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Nsu baƒonu lɛlɔ banune badi bébo libiɔ lɛmmɔ kudɔ na bábɔku begblebi bammɔ. Na Mose úkpo ɔ́ƒɔ begblebi bammɔ na údu ntu úte-ma.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Amu ka begblebi bammɔ bénwini bésie bana ɔti Yetro kudɔ ni, úye-ma ɔnini, “Bi nébo ɔsu na ɔmwi bíyile bubo lɛni?”

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Amu na bédie kenye banini, “Egyipteni ɔdi úbo na úbekpo ɔ́ƒɔ-bu na baƒonu lɛlɔ banune bammɔ enu kemmo. Na úbunku na búdu bula ntu muedi búte bula bebuo.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Amu na úye nwuna bebi bammɔ ɔnini, “Wɛ na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔkya? Bi ɔsu na bɛ́ya na ɔtɔlɔ? Bitáwia-nwu biboku na bute-nwu lɛla lɛdi na ɔdi.”

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Mose únu kalɔ ka ɔsɔ ɔkya ɔnana ɔmɛni kudɔ, na ɔnana ɔmmɔ úti ubidi ulekubi Sipora úte-nwu ɔnii uti.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Na Sipora ɔ́wɔ ubi ɔnanabi úte Mose. Na Mose ɔ́sia-nwu lɛnyi ɔnii Gerson ɔni kalɔ ndi ɔnii, “Línwini ɔƒɔ na kalɔ bamba lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Akwa pii adi kama ni, Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga úbekpi. Nsu Israelƒuɔ bamu bakya bana lɛbibo kemmo. Ɔmɛni ɔsu béwulo bévele Katɔti ka ubedie-ma ɔlɛku bana lɛbibo kemmo.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Na Katɔti únu bana budumo na únyimo bunyimi bɔni na únyimi ku Abraham ku Isak ku Yakob.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Katɔti ɔ́nu kalɛ na Israelƒuɔ beebó abi, na litemi lɛmmɔ líkpoku-nwu.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, Mose úti ulekudi ɔti Yetro baƒonu ku bese úsienku kadikɔ na ketele ɔgyu na bédu Katɔti kɔbi kɔni baalɔ Horeb kudɔ.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔtu ɔdi ɔ́da ɔ́lɛ-nwu lɛlɔ aani ogya ɔni mɔɔda na kugyii lɛƒoƒo lɛdi lɛlɔ. Na Mose ɔ́nu ka lɛƒoƒo lɛmmɔ lɛɛda, nsu lɛla biala lilakywi.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose úye lɛlɔ ɔnii, “Bi akɔla adi mɛni? Bi ɔsu na ogya ɔɔda lɛƒoƒo lɛmɛni kemmo, nsu lɛla biala lilakywi? Ndubusie ntánu.”

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Amu ka Unwoti ɔ́nu ka Mose ɔ́kpɛ uudé ogya ɔmmɔ kudɔ ni, údie lɛdi ɔ́lɛku ogya ɔmmɔ kemmo na ɔ́kpali-nwu ɔnii, “Mose! Mose!” Na Mose údie kenye ɔnii, “Ati, aanu-mi mɛni.”

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Da ƒula lɛgbanvuo die! Ɔsika kalɔ kedee lɛlɔ na enye.”

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Ami ndi ƒ'ɔti Katɔti ku Abraham Katɔti ku Isak Katɔti ku Yakob Katɔti.” Na ka Mose ɔɔyia ka wanu Katɔti ɔsu ni, ɔ́bɛla nwuna anumi.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Lɛ́nu kalɛ na Egyipteƒuɔ bakya baanya Israelƒuɔ taakya ku kalɛ báya na beebó abi. Na muunú bana keku kani beewulo taawia ukyuli ɔni mekpo maƒɔ-ma malɛku bana lɛbibo kemmo.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Na ɔmɛni ɔsu na lɛ́yu líbo ka mbedie-ma lɛlɛku Egyipteƒuɔ enu ku bana kalɔ kammɔ kemmo. Na lɛya na betélie kalɔ kani na kana egyiibi ntu bɔɔyu emini aani uwɔ na kana lɛlɔ bebuo baayu anyi ntu pii. Na kalɔ kammɔ na Kanaanƒuɔ ku Hetiƒuɔ ku Amoriƒuɔ ku Perisiƒuɔ ku Hewiƒuɔ ku Yebusiƒuɔ belie.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Geen ni, línu keku kani na Israelƒuɔ beewulo na mɔɔnu kalɛ na Egyipteƒuɔ benye-ma lɛlɔ na baanya-ma taakya.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu mɔɔtala-a ɔƒɛni na eteesie Ɔga Ƒarao kudɔ. Na etédie mina bekyuli bani ndi Israelƒuɔ alɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔsu Katɔti ɔnini, “Ami ndi ɔma, na muusié nténye Ɔga Ƒarao anumi nnii mɔɔkpanku Israelƒuɔ lɛlɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ?”

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti údie Mose kenye ɔnini, “Ndubulie-ku-ɔ. Na likposela lɛni na ndubɔtina-a ka ami nátala-a sɔsɔ ndi ka si ákpanku-ma álɛku mmɔ áwɔlɔ ni, amii Hebriƒuɔ bɛdubo-mi bɔkpa na kɔbi kɔmɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose úye Katɔti ɔnii, “Na si banii lísie ńténye Israelƒuɔ anumi na lɛ́su-ma nnii, ‘Bina bati kuuku Katɔti nátala-mi ɔ́kya-mii’ na béye-mi banii, ‘Dɛ na baalɔ-nwu’ ni, bi na nsu-ma?”

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti ɔ́sɔ ɔsu Mose ɔnini, “Su Israelƒuɔ anini, ‘Bina bati kuuku Abraham Katɔti ku Isak Katɔti ku Yakob Katɔti nátála-mi ɔ́kya-mii.’ Na lɛnyi lɛmɛni na mɔɔdi úsela uwi ƒui na ani na bina bawɔ bawɔ badubuti beteenyimo-mi ɔ́si kaba úsie kaba.”

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnii, “Sie na atálɔ Israel atɔƒi benengu ƒui asala na asu-ma anii, ‘Unwoti ɔni ndi bina bati kuuku Abraham ku Isak ku Yakob Katɔti nédie lɛlɔ ɔ́tina-mi ɔnini, lɛ́nu kalɛ na Egyipteƒuɔ baabla-mii kalala.

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Na líse kenye ka ndubɔda-mii lidie lɛbibo lɛmmɔ kemmo na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ, na liti-mii ntése kalɔ kani kemmo na Kanaanƒuɔ ku Hetiƒuɔ ku Amoriƒuɔ ku Perisiƒuɔ ku Hewiƒuɔ ku Yebusiƒuɔ beli, kesii kani kana egyiibi ntu bɔɔyu emini aani uwɔ na kana lɛlɔ bebuo baayu anyi ntu pii.’

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: “Si ásu-ma etemila amɛni ni, mina bekyuli badubo ƒula litemi buti. Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, na eti Israelƒuɔ benengu bammɔ ada na bisie Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga kudɔ na bɛsu-nwu bɛnini, ‘Unwoti ɔni ndi Hebriƒuɔ Katɔti údie lɛlɔ ɔ́tina-bu. Anwuɔsu te-bu kuƒi na buti emeyi atɛ busie ketele kemmo na butábla akpala bute bula Unwoti Katɔti.’

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Nsu ngyi ka Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ɔɔɔdubo bɔtuna, si ɔyikun ubendi ɔdi útebedi-nwu asa na unu kalɔ.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ndubudie mina kɔnu lɛtina Egyipteƒuɔ na lɛni-ma kɔtu na akɔla lidu lidu budie bɔtina kemmo. Na ɔmmɔ kama ɔdubɔtuna na bɛtɔlɔ.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Na kaduli biala uleku ku bani na beli-ma kudɔ ƒui badubuvele bana liku bekyuli na bete-ma lɛwu ku sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi na beti ala ammɔ bakya bana bebi belekubi ku bananabi. Na lɛni bɛdubɔbla na biti Egyipteƒuɔ akɛla bɛtɔlɔku.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose úye Unwoti ɔnini, “Na si Israelƒuɔ bátaƒɔ-mi bátadi iye bétenu mina litemi na básu banii, ‘Unwoti útedie lɛlɔ biala útatina-a’ ni, dɛ na mabla?”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi na ada mmɔ?” Amu na Mose údie kenye ɔnini, “Ugyii ɔdadi.”

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Bo ugyii ɔmmɔ va kalɔ.” Amu ka Mose úbo-nwu ɔ́va kalɔ ni, kɔnakunwi ugyii ɔmmɔ únwini kɔlakpi. Amu na Mose úkeli úsie kama.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Die kɔnu na agyu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ ɔka kakɛ.” Anwuɔsu Mose údie kɔnu na ɔ́gyu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ ɔka kakɛ. Na ɔ́sɔ únwini ugyii ɔdadi ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Bla ɔmɛni tina-ma, na ɔdubɔya na baƒɔ badi ka ami bana bati kuuku Abraham Katɔti ku Isak Katɔti ku Yakob Katɔti nédie lɛlɔ lɛ́tina-a.”

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Ti ƒula kɔnu kya ƒula awu kemmo.” Amu ka Mose ɔ́bla lɛni ni, ka ɔ́da nwuna kɔnu údie kani na kɔnu kɔmmɔ kɔ́ƒɔ ɔlɛgyie na kɔ́bla ƒututuu aani etubankɛ.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Sɔku kɔnu kɔmmɔ kya ƒula awu kemmo.” Amu ka Mose ɔ́bla lɛni na ɔ́da nwuna kɔnu údie kani kɔnu kɔmmɔ kɔ́sɔ kɔ́yu ɔkplu na kúnwini aani kalɛ na nwuna ɔlɔna use.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Nsu si édie akɔla akpa anyɔ amɛni na bátaƒɔ-nya bátadi iye bétenu ƒula litemi ni, na etédu ntu bɔdi asiku Nil Ketu kemmo na aƒɛ ntu bɔmmɔ ewi kalɔ kani kákwii lɛlɔ. Na ntu bɔni na édu ásiku ketu mmɔ bɔdubunwini ubugya buwi kalɔ mmɔ.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su Unwoti ɔnini, “O Unwoti, ɔ́si mina lɛnamu uwi úti úbedu ɔƒɛni ni, lɛɛɛgyi bɔtɛmi. Na úti úbedu uwi ɔni na aatɛmiku ami ƒula kabla ɔblane mɛni ni, mina bɔtɛmi bulábla nwaa. Na ndi ukyuli ɔni mɔɔwalɛ.”

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔma nédie ukyuli kenye? Na ɔma mɔɔbla ukyuli na ulákana butemi iye ulenu? Na ɔma mɔɔyá na ukyuli ɔɔnu iye ɔɔyá na anumi aabwɛ-nwu si ɔɔɔdi ami Unwoti?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu teesie na ndubo-ɔ bunku na akana bɔtɛmi na ndubɔtina-a lɛla lɛni na adubɔsu.”

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Nsu Mose ɔ́su ɔnini, “O Unwoti, buvele nda-a, wia ukyuli bamba na atala-nwu.”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti úti kɔnyi kati kati ɔ́kya Mose na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Ƒ'ɔnwani Aaron, Lewini ɔmmɔ nɔɔ? Ngyi ka ɔgyi bɔtɛmi, na ɔsia ulu lɛlɔ lɛnɔ ɔdubo ubasiaku-ɔ, na kubiti kɔdubɔƒɔ-nwu kayi kemmo si ɔ́nu-ɔ.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Nsu ti ugyii ɔmmɔ da kɔnu kalɛ na eteeti taabla akɔla budie taatina lidu lidu.” Mose Únwini Úsie Egyipte Kalɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Mose únwini úsie ulekudi ɔti ɔni ndi Yetro kudɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Te-mi kuƒi na linwini lisie mina kadi bekyuli kudɔ na Egyipte na ntánu si ɔdi ɔmu ulie ngba.” Amu na Yetro ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku-ɔ.”

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Mose ɔ́mu ɔkya Midian kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Nwini teesie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ, ɔsika bekyuli bani ƒui nkya mmɔ na baawia-a badu béekpi.”

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose úti ulekudi ku nwuna bebi bananabi na úti-ma ɔ́sia ɔƒlumu kama. Na bátɔlɔ bésie Egyipte. Na úti Katɔti ugyii ɔdadi ɔmmɔ ɔ́da.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Si énwini ésie Egyipte ni, nu ka ábla akɔla budie taatina ammɔ na Ɔga Ƒarao anumi ɔkɛnku ɔyikun ɔni na líte-ɔ kenye. Nsu ndubɔya na Ɔga Ƒarao kayi kayu ɔkplu ɔni na ɔɔɔdubo bɔtuna na Israelƒuɔ batɔlɔ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Mmɔ na adubɔsu ɔga ɔmmɔ anini, ‘Unwoti ɔnii Israel ndi mina ubi udeedi,

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: na lɛ́su-ɔ nnini, “Ya na mina ubi ɔtɔlɔ, kalɛ na usie utábla-mi kabla na ɔkya-mi lili kalɔ.” Nsu éni na étedie-nwu ulu na ɔtɔlɔ, anwuɔsu ndubo ƒula ubi ɔnanabi udeedi bɔdu.’ ”

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Amu ka bakɛ ulu na bétédu keduokɔ kadi ni, Unwoti útásiaku Mose ubidi na ɔ́yɔ ka nka ɔdu-nwu.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Nsu ulekudi Sipora úti lɛtabi lɛni kenye mbo ɔbi na úkulo ubidi lego kenye na úti útuku Mose lɛgba na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Geen ni, ubugya kemmo ɔgya na adi-mi.”

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Unwoti ɔ́sɔ útabla Mose ubidi lɛla lɛdi. Na uwi ɔni na Sipora ɔ́su ka ubugya kemmo ɔgya na ɔdi-nwu mmɔ ni, ɔɔtɛmi taasiku bana lego bukulo ɔdi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Aaron ɔnini, “Ta na eteesie na atásiaku Mose na ketele kemmo.” Anwuɔsu úsie na útásiaku Mose na Katɔti kɔbi lɛlɔ. Na ka ɔ́nu-nwu ni, bákya lɛlɔ kɔgbu.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su Aaron lɛla biala na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu. Na ɔsɔ ɔ́su-nwu akɔla ala budie taatina lidu lidu lɛni na úbo-nwu ɔda ka ɔbla.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Mose ku Aaron bénwini na bésie Egyipte na bátálɔ Israel batɔnkune básala.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Na Aaron ɔ́su batɔnkune bammɔ lɛla biala na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose. Na Mose lɛnɔ ɔ́bla akɔla budie taatina lidu lidu na batɔnkune bammɔ anumi.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Na ka bánu akɔla ala budie taatina ammɔ ni, báƒɔ bádi. Na ka bénu ka Unwoti úbo-ma lɛlɔ kasusu na ɔ́nu kalɛ na bakya beebó abi ni, bana ƒui béboku lɛlɔ kalɔ béte-nwu na bémwi-nwu.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ku Aaron bésie Ƒarao kudɔ na básu-nwu banini, “Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti ɔnini, ‘Te mina bekyuli kuƒi na beteesie ketele kemmo na batádi limeyi bete-mi.’ ”

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒarao úye-ma ɔnini, “Ɔma ndi Unwoti ɔmmɔ na ɔlɛka linu-nwu litemi na lite kuƒi na Israelƒuɔ batɔlɔ? Lɛɛɛgyi Unwoti ɔmmɔ, na lɛɛɛdubo bɔya na batɔlɔ.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ku Aaron bédie kenye banini, “Hebriƒuɔ Katɔti nédie lɛlɔ ɔ́tina-bu. Na ɔƒaani ni, te-bu kuƒi na buti emeyi atɛ busie ketele kemmo na butábla akpala bute bula Unwoti Katɔti. Na si bútabla akpala ammɔ ni, ɔdubɔya na ɔlɛ ubo-bu lɛlɔ na bukpi iye ɔdubɔya na kekpo kadi kebo-bu lɛlɔ na badu-bu kede kede.”

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Amii ɔlati bɛɛnu ka bimomo bitulo Egyipteƒuɔ, bi ɔsu na ɔƒɛni na bɛɛsu-ma na bada kabla bɔbla baya?”

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛmmɔ kani ni, Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga úbo bekyuli bani mɔɔnu Israelƒuɔ kabla bablane lɛlɔ ku bana benengu ɔda ɔnii,

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: “Bɛda keti kani na kabla bablane bammɔ baasála ku lɛti lɛmmɔ bute bɛya na ama alati beteekulo alakpi ammɔ.

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Nsu bitaya na baƒana bana atimbɔ bumomo bɔni na beekúlo kuuku mmɔ. Israelƒuɔ bamɛni bébo kɔkɔsɔ, anwuɔsu na benye-mi lɛlɔ banii nte-ma kuƒi na beteesie batábla akpala bete bana Katɔti.

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bɛya na benye kabla kammɔ lɛlɔ kpakplaa bebu na bada atu bedie bana ɔkɔ etemila ammɔ bene lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛlɔ banune bamɛni ku bana batɔnkune bésie bátásu Israelƒuɔ ka Ɔga Ƒarao ɔnii, “Nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo-mii keti kani biiti teekulo atimbɔ mmɔ bɔwia bute.

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: Amii alati bisie bitáwia ala ammɔ. Na kesii kani na bɛdubo ala ammɔ bɔkɛ ɔkya bina kudɔ. Nsu atimbɔ bumomo bɔni na biikúlo limeyi ɔɔɔdi ka ɔƒana munu munu.”

english_verse: The slaves went all over Egypt, looking for straw.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Israelƒuɔ bákɛ Egyipte kalɔ kesi biala baawia alakpi lidu lidu lɛni beti bekulo atimbɔ ammɔ.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Na lɛlɔ banune bammɔ beenye kabla bablane bammɔ lɛlɔ taasu-ma banini, “Bikulo atimbɔ bumomo bɔni na bɔɔwia aani kudeedi kalɛ!”

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Nsu kawɔlɔkɔ ka bánu ka atimbɔ ammɔ étedu kudeedi adi ni, lɛlɔ banune bammɔ béye-ma banini, “Bi? Bukulo na bítakana atimbɔ bumomo bɔni na bɔɔwia bukulo?” Na bébo-ma kugyiimi kaduɛ.

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Israelƒuɔ kabla bablane batɔnkune bésie Ɔga Ƒarao kudɔ na bétéye-nwu banini, “Bi ɔsu na aaní-bu kɔtu lɛni?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Bétete abu ƒula kabla bablane keti kani na bukulo atimbɔ, nsu benye-bu lɛlɔ banini, ‘Bikulo atimbɔ ammɔ!’ Na beebó-bu, nsu bana kudɔ na ɔ́si.”

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒarao údie kenye ɔnini, “Bakɔsɔne na bɛdi, anwuɔsu na bɛɛbla kɔkɔsɔ ala! Na bɛɛsu taasia kama bɛnii, ‘Bɛya na busie butábla akpala bute Unwoti.’

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Binwini kɔnakunwi biteesie bitátaabla bina kabla. Na mɔɔsu-mii nnii, ukyuli biala ɔɔɔdubo-mii keti kadi bute, nsu ɔlɛka bikulo atimbɔ bumomo bɔni kani na básu-mii kudeedi.”

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Israelƒuɔ kabla bablane batɔnkune bammɔ bánu báti ka béduo ɔgbankpi kemmo na uwi ɔni na básu-ma banini, “Útalɛ ka bɛƒana atimbɔ ammɔ bumomo bɔni na biikúlo limeyi ndi limeyi mmɔ.”

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni bási baalɛ́ Ƒarao kudɔ ni, básiaku Mose ku Aaron na ulu lɛlɔ ka benye bágya-ma.

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: Mmɔ na batɔnkune bammɔ básu-ma banini, “Unwoti ɔdubɔtɛku-mii litemi! Amii néti-bu bínwini bekyuli bani muuƒí Ƒarao ku nwuna benengu livo yayaaya, na utulo ka bɛ́kya-ma kewii kɔnu ka badu-bu muedi.” Mose Ɔ́kpali Unwoti

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Amu na Mose únwini úsie útákpali Unwoti na úye-nwu ɔnini, “O Unwoti, bi ɔsu na éti lɛbibo éboku ƒula bekyuli lɛlɔ lɛni? Ɔmɛni ɔsu na átala-mi?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Ɔ́si uwi ɔni na lísie Ƒarao kudɔ ńtátɛmiku-nwu na ƒula lɛnyi kemmo ni, lɛbibo kani na uuti taasia bekyuli bamɛni lɛlɔ na étedie-ma ɔdi lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Ɔƒɛni na adubo bɔnu lɛla lɛni na ndubo Ƒarao bɔbla. Ɔkɛnku mina ɔyikun kabla lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, ɔdubo Israelƒuɔ ulu budie. Na bɔbɔku na ɔdubo-ma bɔbɔku bɔlɛku nwuna kalɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: My name is the Lord.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Ami ndi Unwoti.

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: Na lídie lɛlɔ lɛ́tina Abraham ku Isak ku Yakob ka ami ndi Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui. Na Unwoti lɛnyi lɛni na mɔɔdi ni, ńtedie-ni keyi ńtatina-ma tɔ?

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: Na bunyimi bɔni na línyimiku-ma ka meti Kanaan kalɔ kesii kani na bélie dii aani baƒɔ mete-ma ni, lɛ́lɛ-mu ugyii.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: Na ɔƒɛni ni, línu Israelƒuɔ budumo na kalɛ na Egyipteƒuɔ baabla-ma kalala ɔsu. Na ɔmɛni ɔ́ya na línyimo mina bunyimi bɔni línyimi ku bina bati kuuku.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu sie na atásu Israelƒuɔ anini, ‘Ami ndi Unwoti, na ndubo-mii budie bɔsiku lɛbibo ugyigba ɔni na Egyipteƒuɔ bétile-mii kalɔ. Na lɛya na bɛkɛ bɔnwuna na bɛsɔ bilabla-ma kabla lɛnɔ. Na ndubudie mina kɔnu na lɛbla ɔyikun ala ebendi na bana akɔ liti lɛtɛku-ma litemi.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Na ndubuti-mii lɛbla aani ami ɔlati mina bekyuli geen na lɛbla bina Katɔti. Na ɔmɛni ɔdubɔya na bɛnu bɛti ka ami Unwoti bina Katɔti nédie-mii lɛ́lɛku lɛbibo kalɔ na Egyipte.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: Na ndubuti-mii lisienku kalɔ kani na lɛ́kɔliku mina kɔnu katɔ líse kenye ka meti mete Abraham ku Isak ku Yakob. Na ndubuti-ka lite-mii na biti-ka bɛbla bina kadikɔ. Ami ndi Unwoti.’ ”

english_verse: When Moses told this to the Israelites, they were too discouraged and mistreated to believe him.
translation_verse: Na ka Mose úsie útásu Israelƒuɔ etemila amɛni ni, bátakpete-nwu. Ɔsika enu áƒɛ-ma na abi ani na beebó mmɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
translation_verse: “Sie na atásu Egyipteƒuɔ Ɔga Ƒarao na udie Israelƒuɔ ulu na balɛ nwuna kalɔ kemmo.”

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Nsu Mose ɔ́su Unwoti ɔnii, “Ka lísie Israelƒuɔ kudɔ na bátakpete-mi ni, Ƒarao ndubo ami ɔni mɔɔwalɛ mɛni bɔkpete?” Mose Ku Aaron Bati Kuuku Anyi

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́tɛmiku Mose ku Aaron ɔ́siku Israelƒuɔ ku Egyipteƒuɔ Ɔga Ƒarao lɛlɔ, na úbo-ma ɔda ɔnii, batákpanku Israelƒuɔ balɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Na bana atɔƒi benengu anyi ndi ani ndubo mɛni. Israel ubidi udeedi ɔni ndi Ruben bebi ndi Hanok ku Palu ku Hesron ku Karmi. Na ama ndi Ruben ɔtɔ bekyuli bammɔ.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Na Simeon bebi ndi Yemuel ku Yamin ku Ohad ku Yakin ku Sohar ku Saul ɔni ndi Kanaanni uleku ɔdi ubidi. Na ama lɛnɔ ndi Simeon ɔtɔ bekyuli bammɔ.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Na Gerson lɛnɔ bebi na adua ammɔ kenye ndi Libni ku Simei.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Na Merari bebi ndi Mahli ku Musi. Na Lewi adua anyi aani kalɛ na bénweni bése na adi mmɔ.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Na Isehar bebi ndi Kora ku Naƒeg ku Sikri.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Na Usiel bebi ndi Misael ku Elsaƒan ku Sitri.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Na Aaron úti Aminadab ubidi ulekubi ɔni baalɔ banii Elisaba ɔni ndi Nahson ɔnwani, na báwɔ Nadab ku Abihu ku Eleasar ku Itamar.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Na Aaron ubidi Eleasar úti Putiel bebi belekubi bammɔ akɔ ɔdi. Na ɔ́wɔ Pinehas úte-nwu. Na bammɔ ndi Lewi atɔƒi ammɔ bati na adua ammɔ kenye.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: Na Aaron ku Mose ndi bekyuli bani na Unwoti ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bisie na bitédie Israelƒuɔ bɛlɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ na adua ammɔ kenye.”

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Ama kani nátɛmiku Egyipteƒuɔ Ɔga Ƒarao ɔ́siku Israelƒuɔ bɔkpanku bɔlɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. Aaron Ɔ́tɛmi Na Mose Kenye

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni uwi ɔni na Unwoti ɔ́tɛmiku Mose na Egyipte ni,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ami ndi Unwoti, anwuɔsu su Egyipteƒuɔ Ɔga Ƒarao lɛla biala na lɛ́su-ɔ.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Nsu Mose udie kenye ɔ́su Unwoti ɔnini, “Kalɛ na mɔɔtɛmi taawalɛ mɛni ni, dɛ na Ƒarao ɔdubo-mi kalɔ bunu?”

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Nu, lɛ́bla-a aani Katɔti líte Ɔga Ƒarao. Na lɛ́bla ƒula ɔnwani Aaron aani ƒula kenye udiene.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Na ɔlɛka asu-ma lɛla biala na líbo-ɔ ɔda nnii su-ma. Na ɔlɛka ƒ'ɔnwani Aaron lɛnɔ ɔsu Ɔga Ƒarao na udie Israelƒuɔ ulu na balɛ nwuna kalɔ kemmo.

english_verse: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
translation_verse: ɔɔɔdubo-ɔ litemi bunu. Mmɔ na ndubɔda Egyipteƒuɔ ƒui kpakplaa, na lɛbla ala enengudi na liti lɛtɛku-ma litemi. Na ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na ndubɔsia na lidie mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ ati ati na bana bule bɔmmɔ kenye lɛlɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: “Si Ƒarao ɔ́su-mii ɔnini, ‘Bɛbla akɔla budie taatina bɔdi’ ni, na asu Aaron na uti nwuna ugyii ɔdadi mmɔ ɔva Ƒarao anumi. Na ugyii ɔmmɔ ɔdubunwini kɔlakpi.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose ku Aaron bésie Ƒarao kudɔ na bábla kalɛ kani na Katɔti úbo-ma ɔda. Na Aaron ɔ́da ugyii ɔmmɔ ɔ́va kalɔ na Ƒarao ku nwuna benengu anumi. Na ugyii ɔmmɔ únwini kɔlakpi kɔnakunwi.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ƒarao lɛnɔ ɔ́lɔ nwuna banundane ku bani muubó like ku bani mɔɔbla akɔla lidu budie taatina na bébo. Na ama lɛnɔ bábla lɛni kani.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmɛni kama ƒui Ƒarao kɔtu kɔ́mu kɔ́yu ɔkplu na ulenu Mose ku Aaron litemi aani kalɛ kani na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ku Aaron úse. Ubugya Ɔgbankpi Úbo Egyipte Kalɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Ƒarao ubo atuɔkplu na ulenu kalɔ na bekyuli bammɔ batɔlɔ.

english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu, sie na atásiaku Ƒarao ɔtanta uwi ɔni na ɔ́ta úsela Nil Ketu kemmo. Na si ésela ni, na eti ƒula ugyii ɔdadi ɔni nénwini kɔlakpi mmɔ ada. Na enye agya Ƒarao na ketudɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: Na si úbo ni, na asu-nwu anini, ‘Unwoti ɔni Ndi Hebriƒuɔ Katɔti ɔ́tala-mi ɔ́kya-a ɔnii, “Ya mina bekyuli beteesie ketele kemmo na batákpa-mi na mmɔ.” Nsu úti úbedu ɔƒɛni ni, elenu kalɔ.

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Unwoti ɔnini, “Ɔkɛnku ɔmɛni lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, adubo bɔnu bɔti ka Ami ndi Unwoti sɔsɔ.” Na ugyii ɔni nkya-mii kɔnu mɛni, ndubuti bɔƒiɛmi Nil Ketu ntu bɔmɛni anumi na ketu kammɔ kenwini ubugya.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Kɔkpaku kɔni ƒui nkya ntu bɔmmɔ kemmo kɔdubukpi. Na ntu bɔmmɔ bɔdubo buteenwenyi ɔni na Egyipteƒuɔ balakana ketu kammɔ ntu bɔni.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Su Aaron na uti ugyii ɔdadi ɔmmɔ na unene ɔtina etukpa ku abiɔ ku lɛba lɛni ƒui nkya Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na ntu bɔmmɔ ƒui bɔdubunwini ubugya. Na ndubɔya na ubugya ɔ́ƒɔ kesii biala. Na ntu bɔni buwi ebui ku atabi kutubui kemmo muedi bɔdubunwini ubugya.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Mose ku Aaron bábla kalɛ na Unwoti ɔ́su-ma pɛpɛɛpɛ. Mose únene nwuna ugyii ɔdadi ɔmmɔ, na úti ɔ́ƒiɛmi Nil ntu anumi na Ƒarao ku nwuna benengu anumi. Na ntu bɔmmɔ búnwini ubugya.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na kɔkpaku kɔni ƒui nkya Nil ntu kemmo kúkpi. Na ɔmɛni ɔ́ya ntu bɔmmɔ buunwenyi kpatii ɔni na Egyipteƒuɔ balakana ntu bɔmmɔ bɔni. Na ubugya ɔ́ƒɔ Egyipte kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒarao akɔla ala bediene lɛnɔ bábla lɛni kani ɔkɛnku bana lɛkwɛ likpidi akɔla ala budie taatina lɛlɔ. Na Ƒarao úsie anumi ɔɔyu kayi ɔkplu teebu aani kalɛ na Unwoti ɔ́su na ulenu-ma litemi.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Mmomu bunwini na Ƒarao únwini úsie nwuna kaduli ɔni na útakpete ala ani nálɛ na ketu kenye mmɔ.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Na ɔmɛni ɔ́ya na Egyipteƒuɔ béku abiɔ béyile Nil amadɔ, ɔsika Nil ntu bɔmmɔ buládia-ma bɔni. Bapɔtɔlɔ Báƒɔ Egyipte Kalɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: Emeyi maatɛ ávi ɔ́si uwi ɔni na Unwoti úti ugyii ɔ́ƒiɛmi Nil ntu bɔmmɔ anumi.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Teesie na atásu Ƒarao anini, ‘Ami Unwoti nnii ya na mina bekyuli batɔlɔ kalɛ na batákpa-mi.

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Na si anii eledie-ma ulu na batɔlɔ ni, ndubɔya na bapɔtɔlɔ baƒɔ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Warn the king that the Nile will be full of frogs, and from there they will spread into the royal palace, including the king's bedroom and even his bed. Frogs will enter the homes of his officials and will find their way into ovens and into the bowls of bread dough.
translation_verse: Na ndubɔya na Nil Ketu keyi ku bapɔtɔlɔ. Na bapɔtɔlɔ bammɔ badubo ƒula kaduli kemmo buduo. Na beduo ƒula katɛnkɔ ku atɛla lɛlɔ. Na beduo ƒula benengu kɔduli ku Egyipteni biala kaduli. Na badubuduo bina bodobodo ayu ku bodobodo ɔlaaƒɔ kɔnwukɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Frogs will be crawling on everyone—the king, his officials, and every citizen of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na badubɔƒulu belie-ɔ lɛlɔ ku ƒula benengu ku ƒula bekyuli ƒui lɛlɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Su Aaron na unene nwuna ugyii ɔdadi ɔmmɔ ɔtina etukpa ku abiɔ, na ɔya na bapɔtɔlɔ balɛ basiku-nya kemmo na bebeyi Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui.”

english_verse: Aaron obeyed, and suddenly frogs were everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Aaron únene ugyii ɔmmɔ na bapɔtɔlɔ bákɔ bálɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui.

english_verse: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
translation_verse: Nsu Ƒarao bevone lɛnɔ bábla akɔla budie taatina na báya na bapɔtɔlɔ bákɔ bálɛ kalɔ kammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒarao ɔ́lɔ Mose ku Aaron na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛkpali Unwoti na ɔya na bapɔtɔlɔ bammɔ ƒui balɛ ami ku mina kalɔ bekyuli ƒui lɛlɔ. Na ndubute bina bekyuli kuƒi na batɔlɔ. Kalɛ na batábla akpala bete Unwoti.”

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su Ƒarao ɔnini, “Ndubɔyɔ ka awɔ ɔlati ete-mi uwi ɔni na aayɔ́ ka libo, na mbevele Unwoti lite-mii na ɔda bapɔtɔlɔ bammɔ udie bina bekyuli ku bina benengu kɔduli, na kebu bani kani nkya Nil Ketu kammɔ kemmo kani.”

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Ƒarao údie kenye ɔnini, “Bo na ebevele Unwoti ete-mi kɔnaadi.” Amu na Mose udie kenye ɔnini, “Línu. Ndubɔbla lɛla lɛni na éye-mi lite-ɔ. Na mmɔ na adubɔnu bɔti ka Katɔti ɔdi uuubo na utulo bula Unwoti Katɔti.

english_verse: and frogs will no longer be found anywhere, except in the Nile.”
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama bapɔtɔlɔ bammɔ ƒui badubɔtɔlɔ mmɔ, nsu Nil Ketu kemmo badi kani ndubɔsɔ bakya. Na ƒula benengu ku ƒula bekyuli bakɛ bɔnwuna.”

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Ka Mose ku Aaron bátɔlɔ Ƒarao kudɔ ni, Mose úsie na útévele Unwoti ka ɔda bapɔtɔlɔ bammɔ udie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Moses, and the frogs died everywhere—in houses, yards, and fields.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti únu Mose bɔ́kpali. Na bapɔtɔlɔ bani ƒui nkya Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ békpi na ekpo ekpo ammɔ ƒui, nsu bani nkya Nil Ketu kemmo kani nétekpi.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Na Egyipteƒuɔ bábuma bapɔtɔlɔ bammɔ bétéwi liku linwi na bébun na beenwenyi geen.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Na ka Ƒarao ɔ́nu ka bapɔtɔlɔ bammɔ ƒui békpi ni, ɔ́sɔ únwini kasusu na úni ɔnii ulenu Mose ku Aaron litemi kalɛ na Unwoti ɔ́su úse. Baƒɔtɔ Báƒɔ Egyipte Kalɔ Ƒui

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Su Aaron na uti ugyii ɔni na ɔda mmɔ ɔƒiɛmi kalɔ, na ɔdubɔya na ɔtumu ɔni malɛ mmɔ uyi Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔtumu ɔmmɔ ɔdubunwini baƒɔtɔ bataadu bekyuli.”

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Aaron úti ugyii ɔmmɔ ɔ́ƒiɛmi kalɔ na ɔtumu uyi Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔtumu ɔmmɔ únwini baƒɔtɔ.

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Nsu ka Ƒarao bevone lɛnɔ banii beedie baƒɔtɔ bammɔ badi ni, bátakana, na Mose badi báƒɔ bekyuli ku bebuo lɛlɔ ƒui.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ƒarao bevone bammɔ báni béde Ƒarao na básu-nwu banini, “Lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́ mɛni lɛ́si Katɔti kudɔ.” Nsu Ƒarao ɔ́mu ɔ́yu kayi ɔkplu na útenu-ma litemi kalɛ kani na Unwoti ɔ́su úse. Balɔlɔ Béyi Egyipte Kalɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Ta kɔnaadi ɔtanta tutuutu na atáni ede Ƒarao si úsela ketu. Na asu-nwu anii, ‘Unwoti ɔnii die mina bekyuli ulu na besie batákpa-mi.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Na si étedie-ma ulu na batɔlɔ ni, ndubɔya na balɔlɔ bebewi awɔ ku ƒula benengu ku ƒula kalɔ bekyuli ƒui lɛlɔ ku kɔduli kemmo na baƒɔ kalɔ kplu kesii biala.

english_verse: “The Lord's people in Goshen won't be bothered by flies, but your people in the rest of the country will be tormented by them. That's how you will know that the Lord is here in Egypt. This miracle will happen tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ndubɔya na kavumana kakya mina bekyuli ku Ƒarao bekyuli ntɛ. Na ndubɔya na akɔla ala budie taatina amɛni alɛ kɔnaadi.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́bla lɛni sɔsɔ na balɔlɔ yuu badi báyu na bétéduo Ƒarao kaduli ku nwuna benengu kɔduli. Na balɔlɔ bamɛni báƒɔ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui kede kede na lɛla biala líbie na kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒarao ɔ́lɔ Mose ku Aaron ɔnii, “Biteesie na bitábla bina akpala bite bina Unwoti na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ mɛni kani.”

english_verse: “That's impossible!” Moses replied. “Any sacrifices we offer to the Lord our God would disgust the Egyptians, and they would stone us to death.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdia ka bɔbla akpala ammɔ na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ, ɔsika si bɔnii bɔɔbla akpala ammɔ na mɛni ni, bula akpala ammɔ adubuse Egyipteƒuɔ lɛlɔ na atu-ma anumi. Na si úbo úte lɛni ni, bubo na baaadubo-bu atabi bubo?

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔlɛka buti emeyi atɛ busie butéduo ketele kemmo na butábla akpala ammɔ na mmɔ aani kalɛ na bula Unwoti Katɔti úbo-bu ɔda.”

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒarao ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ndubute-mii kuƒi na bisie bitákpa bina Unwoti Katɔti na ketele kemmo, nsu bitesie ɔgyu. Na ɔƒaani ni, bɛkpali katɔ na bivele Unwoti na mina lili.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose údie kenye ɔnini, “Si lɛ́nya lɛ́tɔlɔ-ɔ kudɔ ni, ndubo Unwoti buvele bute-ɔ na balɔlɔ bammɔ batɔlɔ awɔ ku ƒula benengu ku ƒula bekyuli lɛlɔ kɔnaadi. Mmomu bulayɔ ka asɔ atɔlɔ-bu lɛnɔ na elete kuƒi na bula bekyuli besie batábla akpala bete Unwoti.”

english_verse: After leaving the palace, Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́tɔlɔ Ƒarao kudɔ na úsie útevele Unwoti.

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: Unwoti únu Mose bɔkpali. Na balɔlɔ bammɔ ƒui bátɔlɔ Ƒarao ku nwuna benengu ku nwuna bekyuli kɔduli, na ina alɔlɔ unwi muedi ɔ́sɔ útebu Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmɛni kama Ƒarao kayi kásɔ kábayu ɔkplu kébu na úbulo Israelƒuɔ ulu budie.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Sie na atásu Ƒarao anini, ‘Lɛni na Unwoti ɔni ndi Hebriƒuɔ Katɔti ɔɔsu, “Te kuƒi na mina bekyuli batɔlɔ na besie batákpa-mi.”

english_verse: he will bring a terrible disease on your horses and donkeys, your camels and cattle, and your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: ndubɔya na ɔlɛ ukpidi ɔdi uduo bina bebuo akɔ na ɔdu bina baƒlumu ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku bapɔnkɔ ku baƒonu ku bese ƒui.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Nsu Israelƒuɔ bebuo ama ni, ami Unwoti ndubɔya na bana akɔ ɔdi ulekpi, na kavumana kakya Egyipteƒuɔ ku Israelƒuɔ ntɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Tomorrow is the day the Lord has set to do this.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti úse limeyi ɔnii, “Kɔnaadi ami Unwoti ndubo ɔmɛni bɔbla na kalɔ kamɛni kemmo.”

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Na sɔsɔ ni, ka kadi kégye ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na bebuo bammɔ ƒui békpi. Nsu Israelƒuɔ ebuo biala útekpi kalɛ kani na ɔ́su úse.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ku Aaron ɔnini, “Bidie ntɔ bɔdi na asi kemmo kɔnu lɛkɔkɔ keyile. Na Mose uƒwi ntɔ bɔmmɔ ɔkya kayaa na Ƒarao anumi.

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: Na ɔdubunwini aani ɔtumu na ɔƒɔ Egyipte kalɔ kayaa ƒui. Na ɔtumu ɔmmɔ ɔdububoku eƒula na aƒɔ bekyuli ku bebuo ƒui lɛlɔ na kalɔ kammɔ kemmo.”

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose ku Aaron bétédie ntɔ bɔmmɔ básiku asi kemmo na beténye Ƒarao anumi. Mmɔ na Mose úƒwi ntɔ bɔmmɔ ɔ́kya kayaa na bekyuli bammɔ ku bebuo ƒui lɛlɔ lɛ́ƒɔ eƒula kede kede.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Ƒarao bevone básɔ bátakana na benye Mose anumi na eƒula ani náƒɔ-ma lɛlɔ mmɔ ku Egyipteƒuɔ bakladi ƒui lɛlɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti ɔ́ya na Ƒarao ɔ́yu kayi ɔkplu na útenu Mose ku Aaron litemi kalɛ kani na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose úse. Etubankɛ Ána Ási Kayaa

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Kɔnaadi lɛdigye ni, sie na atásiaku Ƒarao na asu-nwu anini, ‘Unwoti ɔni ndi Hebriƒuɔ Katɔti ɔnii, Die mina kadi bekyuli ulu na batɔlɔ na besie batákpa-mi,

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, ɔƒɛni na ndubɔya na ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ ubasiaku-mii kpakplaa ku ogya awɔ ku ƒula benengu ku kadi bekyuli ƒui, na mmɔ na adubo bɔnu bɔti ka Unwoti ɔdi uuubo aani ami kalɛ na kalɔ kamɛni ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɔsika úti úbalɛ ɔƒaani ni, lɛkana na nka lidie kɔnu na lɛya na ɔgbankpi ubo bina ƒui bammɔ lɛlɔ na lɛyila-mii udu lidie kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui.

english_verse: But he has kept you alive, just to show you his power and to bring honor to himself everywhere in the world.
translation_verse: Nsu kasusu kamɛni geen ɔsu na líse-ɔ lɛga kalɛ na lɛtina-a mina ɔyikun na bebo-mi lɛnyi kudu bete kayawi bekyuli ƒui.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Nsu ámu énye áda mina bekyuli na anii elete-ma kuƒi na batɔlɔ.

english_verse: All right. At this time tomorrow, he will bring on Egypt the worst hailstorm in its history.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu kɔnaadi ɔƒɛni kalɛ ni, ndubɔya na etubankɛ ku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa ɔni udu nétebo tɔ na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ubekpo.

english_verse: You had better give orders for every person and every animal in Egypt to take shelter. If they don't, they will die.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu bo ƒula bekyuli ƒui ɔda na beti bana lɛla biala ku bana bebuo bani nkya alakpi akɔ bakya ɔtɔ. Ɔsika etubankɛ adubo bɔna na ukyuli iye ebuo biala makya alakpi akɔ ɔdubo bukpi.’ ”

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔda bubo bɔmɛni bɔ́da Ƒarao benengu bammɔ badi liƒu. Anwuɔsu béti bana bekyuli bani mɔɔbla kabla teete-ma ku bana bebuo bátákya ɔtɔ kemmo.

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: Nsu bakladi ama bátakpete Unwoti ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ, mmomu bányonu bana bekyuli bani mɔɔbla kabla teete-ma ku bana bebuo bényene alakpi akɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Kɔliku ƒula ugyii ɔni na ada mmɔ tina katɔ, kalɛ na lɛya na etubankɛ ana ewi bekyuli ku bebuo ku edula ani ƒui nnye Egyipte mmɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: Etubankɛ ammɔ ána lɛni na katɔ kaabwɛ ogya taasia kama ɔni na ɔmɛni udu útalɛ lɛni kudii na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: People, animals, and crops were pounded by the hailstones, and bark was stripped from trees.
translation_verse: Na etubankɛ ɔmmɔ ébile bekyuli ku bebuo bani nkya alakpi akɔ. Na ɔ́ƒɛ egyii ku edula ani ƒui nnye mmɔ.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Na Gosen kalɔ lɛlɔ kesii kani na Israelƒuɔ belie aka etubankɛ ammɔ átana.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒarao ɔ́tala na bálɔ Mose ku Aaron béte-nwu. Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔƒaani lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka lɛ́ƒiɔ geen na líte Unwoti ubo ka ami ku mina bekyuli ɔdi ɔɔɔdia.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu kpali Unwoti na evele-nwu ete-bu, ɔsika etubankɛ ku katɔ budu ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni údu-bu ɔkwɛ. Ndubudie-mii ulu ɔƒɛni amu, ɔsika ɔ́sɔ útalɛka bɛsɔ bɛkya mɛni lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su Ƒarao ɔnini, “Si lɛ́nya lɛ́lɛ ɔma ubendi ɔmɛni kemmo ni, ndubɔkɔliku enu katɔ na livele Unwoti na etubankɛ ku katɔ budu bɔmmɔ ƒui kenye kawɔ, na anu ati ka Unwoti nédie kayawi na anwu mbo-ka.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Nsu mɔɔnu taati ka awɔ ku ƒula benengu bammɔ biláyia Unwoti Katɔti.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: Etubankɛ ammɔ ébile anta edula udu ani náakya ebi mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Nsu ani mɔɔkpɛ kama aani kakpa ku ana udu kani nébu na étebie.

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Amu ka Mose ɔ́nya ɔ́tɔlɔ Ƒarao kaduli na ɔ́lɛ ɔma ubendi ɔmmɔ kemmo kani na ɔ́talaku enu katɔ na ɔ́kpali Unwoti na úvele-nwu. Na mmɔ kani na etubankɛ atakpɛ bonwu ammɔ ƒui ku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ku katɔ budu bɔmmɔ kenye káyɔ.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Nsu ka Ƒarao ɔ́nya ɔ́nu ka lɛla biala lɛ́sɔ lɛ́bla buɛɛ ni, anwu ku nwuna benengu bammɔ básɔ báyu kayi ɔkplu.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Na lɛni kani na ɔdanku kayi ɔkplu ɔmmɔ na ulédie Israelƒuɔ ulu na batɔlɔ kalɛ kani na Unwoti ɔ́su úse.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Teesie na atánu Ƒarao, ɔsika lɛ́ya na anwu ku nwuna benengu báyu kayi ɔkplu kalɛ na ɔdia-mi na lidie akɔla ala budie taatina lidu lidu lɛmɛni lɛtina na bana akɔ.

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔdubɔdia na biti bana litemi bɛtɛmi bina bebi ku bawɔ. Na bɛsu-ma kalɛ ami Unwoti lɛ́bla Egyipteƒuɔ ɔkɛnku akɔla budie taatina lidu lidu lɛmɛni lɛlɔ, na bɛti ka ami ndi Unwoti.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose ku Aaron báta na bésie Ƒarao kaduli na básu-nwu banini, “Hebriƒuɔ Katɔti ɔnii, ‘Kɔlɛ sɔɔn na adubuni ka eboku lɛlɔ kalɔ ete-mi? Ya na mina kadi bekyuli batɔlɔ na batákpa-mi.

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: Si éni-ma ulu budie ni, ndubɔya na baalɔlɔ bani muubile ala baƒɔ ƒula kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ kɔnaadi.

english_verse: that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees.
translation_verse: Badubɔƒɔ kalɔ kammɔ kesi kesii na ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ ulakana lɛla lɛdi bɔnu. Ndubɔya na baalɔlɔ bammɔ bayalɛ edula blii ani nébu evete na etubankɛ atakpɛ ammɔ bɔna kama na egyii ani ƒui mɔɔkwɛ́ bina mmo lɛnɔ bebile-nya.

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: Badubɔƒɔ awɔ Ƒarao ku ƒula benengu ku ƒula bekyuli kɔduli kemmo ƒui tɛtɛɛtɛ. Na ɔmɛni ɔdubɔbla lɛla lɛni na ƒula bati ku bati kuuku bátanu kudii úti ɔ́si uwi ɔni bélie kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ úti úbedu ɔmwi kadi.’ ” Amu ka Mose ɔ́su Ƒarao ala amɛni ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔ́gyu ɔ́tɔlɔ.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Na Ƒarao benengu bammɔ básu-nwu banini, “Bi ɔsu na ɔlɛka bɔya na ɔnana ɔmɛni uteekpoku-bu lɛni? Bɛya bute Israelƒuɔ bamɛni kuƒi na batɔlɔ, na beteesie batákpa bana Unwoti Katɔti. Aanu taati ka Egyipte kalɔ ƒui kadaku udu bɔyii na ama ɔsu?”

english_verse: The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu básɔ bálɔ Mose ku Aaron béboku Ƒarao kaduli na básu-ma banini, “Biteesie na bitákpa bina Unwoti Katɔti.” Amu na béye Mose ku Aaron banini, “Nsu bina ɛlɛ nésela?”

english_verse: “Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose údie kenye ɔnini, “Bɔdubutiku bula banamu ku benengu ku bebi bananabi ku belekubi ku bebuo lidu lidu ƒui, ɔsika limeyi geen na bɔdubo bɔdi bute Unwoti.”

english_verse: The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good.
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒarao ɔ́kpali Unwoti lɛnyi na ɔ́su ɔnii, “Bɛnu lɛlɔ kemmo kaduɛ si bɛnii amii ku bina beleku ku bebi nésela mmɔ, ɔsika bɛɛwia ɔgbankpi teete lɛlɔ, ɔsika bɛda kasusu kekpidi na mɔɔnu.

english_verse: Do you want to worship the Lord? All right, take only the men and go.” Then Moses and Aaron were chased out of the palace.
translation_verse: Oowo! Bɛya na bina banana kani besie batákpa Unwoti, ɔsika lɛni na amii alati bíye bɛ́siku kalɔ kesekɔ.” Ɔmmɔ kama bábɔku Mose ku Aaron bálɛku Ƒarao anumi mmɔ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward Egypt. Swarms of locusts will come and eat everything left by the hail.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Nene ƒula kɔnu tina Egyipte kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ, na baalɔlɔ bani muubile ala badubɔyu baƒɔ kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui na bebile lɛla biala nébu na etubankɛ ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa ɔmmɔ kama na mmo bɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo.”

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose únene kɔnu na úti nwuna ugyii ɔdadi ɔmmɔ ɔ́tina Egyipte kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ, na Unwoti ɔ́ya na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔdi úkpo ɔ́si ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔ́vi kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ limeyi lɛmmɔ ku usien umodi. Na kadi buteegye ni, baalɔlɔ bani muubile ala mmɔ báyu bébewi geen.

english_verse: were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many.
translation_verse: Bébile ala kalɔ kammɔ kemmo ƒui na bakɛ esu esu na béyii Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui kede kede. Na Egyipteƒuɔ bátanu-ma lɛni kudii. Na badi lɛnɔ basɔ baaadubo bɔlɛ lɛni lɛnɔ kudii.

english_verse: The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
translation_verse: Baalɔlɔ bammɔ báƒɔ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ kesii biala na bewi totonto. Na bádi lɛla biala na etubankɛ atakpɛ ammɔ étebile. Na bádi egyiibi ku evete biala. Ɔni na ina livete linwi lítebu lɛɛɛsia kugyii iye edula kugyii kɔdi lɛlɔ na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒarao ɔ́ya na bábabla bálɔ Mose ku Aaron béte-nwu. Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Lɛ́bla likpidi lɛ́ƒiɔ bina Unwoti Katɔti ku amii lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: Na muuvele-mii nnii biti likpidi lɛmmɔ bɛkyiɛ-mi. Na bivele bina Unwoti Katɔti kɔkladi kɔmɛni bite-mi. Na ɔda ɔgbankpi ubendi ɔmɛni udie-mi lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Moses left the palace and prayed.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose únu kalɔ na ɔ́tɔlɔ na útévele Unwoti úte Ƒarao.

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́vumana ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ bukpo na ɔbambadi úkpo kpakplaa ɔ́si ɔƒɛ kanukɔ. Na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmɛni úbo baalɔlɔ bamɛni ƒui útákya Ɛpugyie kemmo. Na baalɔlɔ bammɔ ɔdi biala ɔ́sɔ útebu na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti ɔ́ya na Ƒarao kayi kásɔ káyu ɔkplu na útete kuƒi na ɔya na Israelƒuɔ batɔlɔ. Lɛdisa Bonwu Lɛdi Lɛ́lɛ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Talaku kɔnu na eti atina katɔ na ndubɔya na lɛdisa susuusu bonwu lɛdi libo Egyipte kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose ɔ́talaku kɔnu katɔ ɔ́tina kayaa na lɛdisa bonwu lɛ́ƒɔ Egyipte kalɔ ƒui emeyi atɛ sɔɔn.

english_verse: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
translation_verse: Emeyi atɛ sɔɔn ukyuli ɔdi ulákana na ɔnu ɔkpanadi iye ɔkana na ɔlɛ kesii kani na ɔkya muedi. Nsu Israelƒuɔ keliekɔ aka keekeye uwi biala.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒarao ɔ́lɔ Mose na ɔsu-nwu ɔnini, “Biteesie bitákpa Unwoti na bitiku bina beleku ku bebi muedi ƒaa, nsu bɛda bina bebuo lidu ƒui binyene kama.”

english_verse: “No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God,
translation_verse: Amu na Mose údie kenye ɔnini, “Amu adubɔwia akpala ete-bu ku ani na bɔdubɔkyula bute Unwoti Katɔti lɛnɔ ete-bu.

english_verse: and we won't know which animals we will need until we get there. That's why we can't leave even one of them here.”
translation_verse: Oowo ɔlɛka buti bula bebuo lɛnɔ bɔda. Na ɔdi ɔgbanvuo ulébu kama. Bebuo bammɔ badi na bɔdubuti bɔbla akpala. Na si búteduo tɔ mmɔ ni, buláti bani madia akpala ammɔ bɔbla bute bula Unwoti Katɔti.”

english_verse: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmɛni kama Unwoti ɔ́ya na Ƒarao kayi kásɔ káyu ɔkplu na útete kuƒi na Israelƒuɔ batɔlɔ.

english_verse: that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Ƒarao ɔ́bɔku Mose ɔnini, “Gyu tɔlɔ-mi anumi! Na nsɔ naaayɔ ka lɛsɔ lɛnu-ɔ kudii. Si lɛ́sɔ lɛ́nu-ɔ, adubukpi.”

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su Ƒarao ɔnini, “Línu, ɔdubuse kalɛ kani na ásu, nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo-ɔ bɔnu kudii.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Ndubo Ƒarao ku Egyipteƒuɔ kɔtu kɔkladi bɔni. Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔdubɔya na Israelƒuɔ batɔlɔ, na ɔdubo-mii bɔbɔku muedi.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu kɔ lɛsa na asu Israelƒuɔ ƒui ka bevele sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi basiku bana liku bekyuli kudɔ.”

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́ya na Egyipteƒuɔ beeti ɔbu teete Israelƒuɔ geen. Na sɔsɔ ni, Ƒarao benengu ku Egyipteƒuɔ ƒui baanu Mose ka ɔdi ukyuli ɔni náƒɔ kuye geen.

english_verse: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Amu na Mose útásu Ƒarao ɔnini, “Lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu ɔnii, ‘Ɔmwi usien lɛdibantɛ ni, ndubɔvi Egyipte kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: Na ndubɔya na ukyuli biala ubi udeedi ɔni na ɔ́wɔ ukpi, ɔ́si Ƒarao ubidi udeedi ɔni nlie-nwu lɛgaboku lɛlɔ, úti útédu ulekubi kabla ɔblane ɔni nƒa lɛtabi kukɔ lɛlɔ, ku bebi bedeedi bani na bina bebuo báwɔ lɛnɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Na kɔvanu kɔni udu nátalɛ tɔ dii na Egyipte na kɔsɔ kɔɔɔdubo bɔlɛ kudii lɛnɔ kɔdubɔlɛ limeyi lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Nsu Israelƒuɔ keliekɔ aka ni, akpewe ina unwi muedi ulébo kudu na ukyuli iye ebuo ɔdi ɔsu.’ Na mmɔ na adubo bɔnu bɔti ka ami ɔni ndi Unwoti mɔɔkya kavumana Egyipteƒuɔ ku Israelƒuɔ ntɛ.

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: Ƒula benengu ƒui badubɔlɛ akɔnkɔ na mina anumi na beteevele-mi banii, ‘Awɔ ku bani ƒui nsiaku-ɔ kama biteesie.’ Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, ndubɔtɔlɔ.” Amu na Mose ɔ́tɔlɔ Ƒarao anumi ku kɔnyi.

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti ɔ́su Mose úse ɔnini, “Ƒarao ɔdubo buni na ulénu ƒula litemi na ɔmmɔ ndubo bɔya na mina akɔla budie taatina akɔ katɔ ebu na Egyipte.”

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Na Mose ku Aaron bábla akɔla budie taatina lidu lidu amɛni na Ƒarao anumi, nsu Unwoti ɔ́ya na Ƒarao kayi kayu ɔkplu na útete kuƒi na Israelƒuɔ batɔlɔ.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ku Aaron na Egyipte ɔnini,

english_verse: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
translation_verse: “Kɔbuli kɔni kemmo bɛkya mɛni ndi kɔbuli kudeedi na lɛkwa lɛmɛni kemmo ute-mii.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bibo ɔda ɔmɛni bite Israelƒuɔ ƒui ka ni, kɔbuli kɔmɛni limeyi leevudi lɛlɔ ni, ɔnana biala ɔwia koƒonubi iye ese ubi use ute nwuna kaduli bekyuli.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: “Na bitaanu-ma lɛlɔ kaduɛ útédu kɔbuli limeyi leevu-linedi lɛlɔ useyi uwi asa na ɔdi biala ɔdu nwuna ebuo.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Na biti bebuo bammɔ ubugya bɛkuna biwi bina kɔyakun ligyii lɛtɔdi ku amadɔ lɛdi lɛlɔ na kesii kani na bɛdubo lɛna lɛmmɔ bɔkun mmɔ.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Na usien ɔmmɔ ni, ukyuli biala uƒi nwuna lɛna na ɔkun-ni ku evete ani mbo ɔdu ku bodobodo ɔni kemmo na bɔnyii buuubo.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: Nsu ukyuli biala uteƒulo lɛna lɛmmɔ lɛdi iye ɔkun lɛna lɛmmɔ ɔwɔdi, mmomu biƒi-ni ku lili ku lɛgba ku aƒɔla ammɔ ƒui na bɛkun.

english_verse: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
translation_verse: Na bɛnu ka lɛna lɛmmɔ lɛdi lítebu asa na kadi kégye. Na si ɔdi úbu ni, na bɛkyula-ni ɔtanta ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: “Na bɛda lɛlɔ asa bise kalɔ ku bɔdi, na bɛkya bina lɛwu ku agbanvuo na bɛwia bina ugyii ɔdadi bɛda. Na ɔlɛka bɛdi adila ammɔ pla pla. Ɔsika usien ɔmmɔ ɔdi Unwoti Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: “Ɔsika usien ɔmmɔ ami Unwoti ndubo bɔvi Egyipte kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ na lɛdu ubi udeedi biala na bekyuli ku bebuo ƒui báwɔ. Na ndubɔni Egyipteƒuɔ baƒiɔ ƒui kɔtu. Ami Unwoti mɔɔsu.

english_verse: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni mɔɔní Egyipteƒuɔ kɔtu ni, ubugya ɔni bɛ́kuna bíwi bina kɔyakun ndubɔbla bina likposela ka amii nlie mmɔ. Na si lɛ́nu ubugya ɔmmɔ ni, ndububo lɛvi-mii lɛlɔ, na naaabla-mii lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: Remember this day and celebrate it each year as a festival in my honor.
translation_verse: “Bidie limeyi lɛmɛni bise bitaadi uwi ƒui amii ku bina kaba kemmo bebi ƒui, ɔsika ɔdi lɛla bonwu lɛni na ami Unwoti lɛ́bla líte-mii.

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Biti emeyi maatɛ bɛdi bodobodo ɔni kemmo na bátakya bɔnyii. Na emeyi maatɛ ammɔ limeyi lideedi ni, ukyuli biala na ubo bɔnyii na nwuna kaduli ubo-nwu uwiakun. Na Ukyuli biala madi bodobodo ɔni kemmo na bákya bɔnyii emeyi maatɛ ammɔ kemmo ni, ndubɔda-nwu lidie mina bekyuli akɔ.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lideedi ku maatɛdi ni, bɛsa bɔsa kedee na mina lɛnyi lɛlɔ. Na ukyuli biala utabla kabla kadi emeyi ammɔ kemmo. Nsu bibo kuƒi ka bɛnwa adila bɛdi. Ɔmɛni kani na ɔlɛka bɛbla.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
translation_verse: “Bɛdi Bodobodo Ɔni Néteƒu Limeyi lɛmmɔ, ɔsika limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ geen na lídie-mii lɛ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ na bina adua adua ammɔ kenye. Bɛlɛ limeyi lɛmɛni ugyii na bitaadi-ni amii ku bina kaba kaba bekyuli úsela uwi ƒui.
