english_verse: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
translation_verse: Bɛdi limeyi lɛmɛni úti ɔ́si kɔbuli kudeedi limeyi leevu-linedi useyi lɛlɔ úti útédu limeyi aavlanyɔ-unwi useyi. Na ɔdi utadi bodobodo ɔni kemmo na bɔnyii bɔkya na emeyi ammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Na emeyi maatɛ ammɔ kemmo ɔdi uteti bɔnyii bɔdi utese nwuna kaduli. Na si Israelni iye ɔƒɔ ɔdi ɔ́di bodobodo ɔni bakya bɔnyii ni, ndubɔda-nwu lidie mina bekyuli akɔ.

english_verse: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
translation_verse: Bitadi lɛla biala kemmo na bákya bɔnyii. Bodobodo ɔni néteƒu kani na ɔlɛka bɛdi na kesi kesii na bɛdubɔkya na emeyi bɔdi bɔmmɔ kemmo.” Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi Lideedi

english_verse: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́lɔ Israelƒuɔ benengu ƒui ɔ́sala na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bisie na ɔdi biala utáwia koƒonubi iye esebi na ɔdu, na ɔdi biala kaduli bekyuli beti ebuo ɔmmɔ badi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi.

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Na si bɛ́du bebuo bammɔ ni, na biti bebuo bammɔ ubugya biwi ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔdi kemmo. Na bɛwia libu lɛni baalɔ hisope na biti bitákya ubugya ɔmmɔ kemmo na bɛkuna biwi kɔyaku ligyii lɛmmɔ eli ku amadɔ. Na ukyuli biala utalɛ keyi úti útédu ka kadi kégye.

english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
translation_verse: Kalɛ na si uwi ɔni na Unwoti úbo ɔɔví Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ kalɛ na ɔdu bebi bammɔ na ɔ́nu ubugya ɔmmɔ na ligyii lɛlɔ ni, na uláya na nwuna ɔtu ɔni mɔɔdú bekyuli bammɔ weduo bina kɔduli na ɔdu-mii.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Na si bítéduo kalɔ kani na Unwoti ɔ́su úse ka wete-mii kemmo ni, na bitaadi ɔdi limeyi lɛmɛni.

english_verse: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
translation_verse: Na si bina bebi báta bákɔ na béye-mii banii, ‘Limeyi lɛmani udu bɔdi na bɔdi mɛni?’ ni,

english_verse: And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: na bɛsu-ma bɛnini, ‘Unwoti Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Lɛkpa na bɔdi, ɔsika limeyi lɛmmɔ Unwoti ɔ́via Israelƒuɔ kɔduli na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ na ɔ́du Egyipteƒuɔ, nsu útadu Israelni ɔdi ina unwi muedi.’ ” Amu ka Mose ɔ́su-ma ala amɛni ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ benengu bammɔ bálɛ akɔnkɔ na bémwi Unwoti.

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: Amu na bátɔlɔ bésie bana kɔduli na bátábla lɛla lɛni na Mose ku Aaron básu-ma aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo-ma ɔda. Egyipte Bebi Bedeedi Békpi

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Usien ɔmmɔ lɛdibantɛ kani na Unwoti ɔ́du Egyipteƒuɔ bebi bananabi bedeedi ƒui. Ɔ́du-ma ɔ́siku Ƒarao ubidi udeedi ɔni muulie-nwu kelekɔ úti útédu ukyuli ɔni ntɛ aban ɔtɔ ubidi lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́du bebuo bebi bedeedi bani na báwɔ ƒui lɛnɔ.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Na ka Ƒarao ku nwuna benengu ku Egyipteƒuɔ bekyuli békeyi lɛlɔ bágyinya usien ɔmmɔ ni, ukyuli biala úse kalɔ uuwulo. Ɔsika Egyipte kaduli biala kemmo ni, ukpine ɔtɛ.

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Na usien ɔmmɔ Ƒarao ɔ́ya na bálɔ Mose ku Aaron béte-nwu. Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛgyu bɛtɔlɔ, amii ku bina Israelƒuɔ ƒui! Na naaawia-mi na mina kalɔ lɛlɔ. Biteesie na Bitákpa Unwoti aani kalɛ na bívele-mi ulu.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Na biti bina baƒonu ku bese ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ na bɛtɔlɔ. Na bivele Unwoti kusɛ kusɛ bite-mi asa na bɛtɔlɔ.”

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Amu na Egyipteƒuɔ bénye Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ ka bababla na bagyu batɔlɔ. Na basu-ma banii, “Si bítatɔlɔ pla bula ƒui bɔdubo bukpi.”

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Israelƒuɔ béti bana bodobodo ɔni nátasa tɔ bɔnwu na bátakya tɔ bɔnyii nwuna kemmo bébi-nwu ala bákya bodobodo akyami ammɔ kemmo na béti bákya ala akɔ baƒala bana amangba.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bábla lɛla biala siin aani kalɛ na Mose úbo-ma ɔda. Na bévele Egyipteƒuɔ na béte-ma sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi, na bévele-ma adi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́ya na Egyipteƒuɔ ƒui beeti ɔbu teete Israelƒuɔ kaduɛ. Na ɔmɛni ɔsu ala ani béye-ma ni, béte-ma. Na ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na Israelƒuɔ béti bákɛ akɛla pii básiku Egyipteƒuɔ kudɔ na béti-nya bátɔlɔku. Israelƒuɔ Bálɛ Egyipte Kalɔ Lɛlɔ Bátɔlɔ

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Israelƒuɔ bésie lɛgba ulu bási Rameses bétédu Sukot. Na banana bani nkɛ ulu ɔmmɔ bésela babla mpim eti leevu-inyɔ (

english_verse: of them, not counting women and children.
translation_verse: ). Ɔni na beleku ku banamu bɔka buuubunku.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bamba pii lɛnɔ bebunku-ma akɔ. Na bakɛ bada baƒonu ku bese ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ pii lɛnɔ.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Ka bɔbɔku na bábɔku-ma bálɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, bátakɛ kɔnu na banwa adila adi bada. Mmomu bodobodo ɔni básiku Egyipte na bɔnyii buuubo-nwu kemmo mmɔ na béti béƒi bodobodo wɛlɛ wɛlɛ ɔdi.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Ka Unwoti úlie usien umodi ɔmmɔ na ɔ́nu ka nwuna bekyuli bálɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, úbo Israelƒuɔ ɔda ka bese limeyi lɛmmɔ likpo na beteelie teegye kadi. Ɔda Bubo Na Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Lɛlɔ

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ku Aaron ɔnini, “Ɔda ɔmɛni na muubó-mii na Kukpi Lili Bɔvia lɛlɔ. Ukyuli biala na ɔɔɔdi Israelni utadi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia adila ammɔ adi.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Nsu ukyuli uyedi ɔni na ɔkya-mii akɔ si úkulo nwuna lego ni, ubo kuƒi ka ɔdi adila ammɔ adi.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: “Na Kukpi Lili Bɔvia adila ani na ukyuli biala ɔ́nwa ni, ɔnu ka ɔ́di-nya na nwuna kaduli kani. Ɔdi utabwɛ likubi linwi muedi.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔlɛka Israelƒuɔ ƒui bitaadi limeyi lɛmɛni.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: “Nsu bɛnu ka ukyuli biala na útekulo lego útadi adila ammɔ adi. Na si baƒɔ bani nkya-mii akɔ ɔdi ɔɔwia ka ɔdi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia limeyi lɛmmɔ na uti ɔkɔliku Unwoti lɛnyi katɔ ni, ɔlɛka ɔka nwuna bebi bananabi ƒui ago bukulo. Na ɔmmɔ kama ukyuli ɔmmɔ unwini Israelni na ɔkana na ɔdi limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛdi.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Na ɔda bubo bɔmɛni buse bute Israelni biala ku bani naaadi Israelƒuɔ na bákya-mii akɔ.”

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bábla básia ɔda ɔni na Mose ku Aaron bébo-ma mmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛmmɔ Unwoti ɔ́da Israelƒuɔ ƒui údie Egyipte na bana adua adua kenye.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: “Die ubi ɔnanabi udeedi biala se-mi. Ɔsika Israelni kɔwɔ kudeedi ku bana bebuo ƒui kɔwɔ kudeedi kɔdi mina ɔdi. Na abla-ma sɛsɛɛ ete-mi.” Bodobodo Ɔni Néteƒu Limeyi Bɔdi

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Na si Unwoti úti-mii úduoku Kanaanƒuɔ ku Hetiƒuɔ ku Amoriƒuɔ ku Hewiƒuɔ ku Yebusiƒuɔ kalɔ kamɛni kemmo ni, na bɛsia anu na bitaadi limeyi lɛmɛni na kɔbuli kɔmɛni kemmo. Kalɔ kamɛni na úse kenye úse úte bina bati kuuku ka kana egyiibi ntu bɔɔyu emini aani uwɔ na kana lɛlɔ bebuo baayu anyi ntu pii na aka na ɔdubuti ute-mii na kenwini bina kadikɔ.

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Na bitadi bodobodo ɔni na bɔnyii bɔkya-nwu kemmo emeyi maatɛ. Na limeyi maatɛdi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, na bɛdi limeyi lɛmmɔ biti bɛkɔliku Unwoti lɛnyi katɔ.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Bɛdi bodobodo ɔni néteƒu emeyi maatɛ ammɔ kemmo. Na bɛnu ka lɛla biala kemmo na bɔnyii bɔkya ni, bídie-ni na bina akɔ ku bina amadɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: “Na limeyi bɔdi bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, su ƒ'ubidi anini, ‘Ɔkɛnku lɛla lɛni na mina Unwoti ɔ́bla úte-mi ɔni na lɛ́lɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔsu na mɔɔbla ɔmɛni.’

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Si bɛɛsia limeyi lɛmɛni anu taadi-ni ni, ɔdubunwini aani likposela ɔsia-mii kɔnu iye atɛntɛ ka ɔdi ka Unwoti ɔda bubo bɔsia-mii enyekuli lɛlɔ uwi ndi uwi. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔkɛnku nwuna kɔnu ɔyikun lɛlɔ na udie-mii ɔ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
translation_verse: Na bɛnu ka bɛɛdi limeyi lɛmɛni na nina uwi lɛlɔ lɛkwa biala kemmo.

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: “Si Unwoti úti-mii úduoku Kanaanƒuɔ kalɔ kani na úse kenye úte amii ku bina bati kuuku ka weti wete-mii kemmo ni,

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: na bɛnu ka bíti bina bebi bedeedi bani ndi bananabi ku bebuo bagyani bebi bedeedi bíte-nwu, ɔsika bana ƒui badi Unwoti badi.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Na ebuo ala utine ubi udeedi ɔgyani ni, ti koƒonu ubi ɔgyani ɔkɔdi ƒɔ-nwu lili kayu na edie-nwu ngba. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, ɔdi na aƒɛ-nwu limɔ. Na bebi bananabi bedeedi lɛnɔ ni, ɔlɛka eti koƒonu kɔkɔdi kɔgyani aƒɔ-nwu lili kayu na edie-nwu ngba.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: “Na si ƒ'ubidi ɔnanabi úye-ɔ limeyi lɛdi ɔnini, ‘Lɛla lɛmɛni kalɔ ndi bi’ ni, na asu-nwu anii, ‘Ɔkɛnku Katɔti kɔnu ɔyikun ablala ɔsu na údie-bu ɔ́lɛku bekyuli bamba kabla bɔbla kalɔ na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.’

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Na bɛsu-ma bɛnii, ‘Uwi ɔni na Ɔga Ƒarao ɔ́yu kayi ɔkplu na ɔnii ulatuna na Israelƒuɔ batɔlɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́du ɔnanabi udeedi ku ebuo ubi ɔgyani udeedi biala na báwɔ na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu na buuti bula bebuo bebi bagyani bedeedi taakpa teete Unwoti. Na buuti baƒonu bagyani bakɔdi taaƒɔ́ bula bebi bananabi bedeedi lili kayu teedie-ma ngba.’

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Na ɔmɛni ɔdubɔbla likposela ɔsia-mii kɔnu ku atɛntɛ ka Unwoti ɔkɛnku nwuna kɔnu ɔyikun lɛlɔ údie-bu ɔ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.” Israelƒuɔ Ɛpugyie Bɔvia

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Ƒarao úte kuƒi ka Israelƒuɔ batɔlɔ ni, Katɔti úteti-ma útasiaku Ƒilistiƒuɔ kalɔ kemmo, ina ka mmɔ ulu use klukwii. Mmomu bɔsu na Katɔti ɔ́su ɔnini, “Si bekyuli bamɛni bátásiaku kekpo kadi ni, badubo kasusu bɔvumana ka benwini besie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Katɔti ɔ́tɔnku-ma na bénwini bátásia ketele ulu ɔni ntɛ úsie Ɛpugyie mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na Israelƒuɔ báda lɛlɔ aani bekpone kalɛ asa na bálɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bésela ni, Mose úti Yoseƒ ekubi ɔ́da. Yoseƒ ɔ́ɔya na Israelƒuɔ bése-nwu kenye lɛni, ɔsika ɔ́ɔsu-ma kukuuku ɔnini, “Katɔti ɔdubo-mii kebunku kadi bute uwi ɔdi kemmo. Anwuɔsu si úbo úte lɛni ni, na biti mina ekubi bɛtɔlɔku si bɛɛtɔlɔ.”

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Na ka Israelƒuɔ bátɔlɔ Sukot ni, bátálɛlɛ na Etam ketele kudɔ.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: “Kɔ lɛsa, na asu Israelƒuɔ na benwini kama beteesie batáwia keliekɔ na Pi-Hahirot, na Migdol ku Ɛpu ntɛ. Na basɔ bakya Ɛpu ɔmmɔ kudɔ, na Baal-Seƒon ɔƒɛnyi kakɛ.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Ƒarao ɔdubuti kasusu ɔnini, ‘Ngyi ka Israelƒuɔ bétéƒu bakya ketele kammɔ kemmo baaví susuusu na balati bana kasiakɔ.’

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: Na ami Unwoti ndubɔya na Ƒarao kayi kayu ɔkplu, na lɛya na ɔbi ɔsiaku-ma. Na ndubɔdi Ƒarao ku nwuna bekpone lɛlɔ. Na mmɔ na Egyipteƒuɔ badubɔnu ka ami ndi Unwoti.” Na bábla básiaku lɛni kani.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Amu ka básu Ƒarao ka Israelƒuɔ békeli bátɔlɔ ni, anwu ku nwuna benengu bávumana kasusu na béye lɛlɔ banini, “Bi adɔlɔla adi na bɔ́bla mɛni? Bɔ́ya na Israelƒuɔ békeli bátɔlɔ. Na ɔma bene nsɔ ndubɔbla kabla bete-bu?”

english_verse: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒarao úti nwuna bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ na úbo nwuna bekpone ɔda ka baklibi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: He commanded his officers in charge of his
translation_verse: Amu na úti bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ eti leevu-anyɔ (

english_verse: best chariots and all his other chariots to start after the Israelites.
translation_verse: ) lɛni nkya-nwu kudɔ ku kɛɛkɛ lɛbambadi lɛni nkya Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ku bana bekpone bani ngyi bukpo geen ɔ́da.

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́ya na Ƒarao kayi káyu ɔkplu na báta banii batábi basiaku Israelƒuɔ bani náta báyu ulu bésela ku kayi buse.

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Na Egyipte bekpone ƒui ku bana bapɔnkɔ ku bana bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ƒui ku bana bakane báta na bábi básiaku Israelƒuɔ bamɛni. Na sɔsɔ ni, bátánu-ma na Ɛpugyie kudɔ na Pi-Hahirot, na Baal-Seƒon ɔƒɛnyi, ka bewi mmɔ.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Amu ka Israelƒuɔ bánu bémene ka Ƒarao ku nwuna bekpone basia-ma kama badubo ni, liƒu libendi lɛ́da-ma. Na bése kalɔ baava taakpali Unwoti ka ubebunku-ma.

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: Amu na béye Mose banini, “Bɔkɛ na bɔɔɔdubo bɔkɛ kesii kani na bava-bu na Egyipte ɔsu na ákpanku-bu éboku ketele kemmo mɛni anii bubekpi?

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: Bútasu-ɔ na Egyipte ƒui bɔnini, ‘Nyonu-bu kpoo na bunye butaabla kabla teete Egyipteƒuɔ’? Ɔdia-bu ka bunye butaabla kabla teete-ma utulo ka bubekpi na ketele kemmo mɛni!”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ɔnini, “Liƒu litada-mii. Binye kpakplaa na bɛdubɔnu kalɛ na Unwoti ɔdubukpo ute-mii ɔmwi kadi. Na mɔɔsu-mii ka Egyipteƒuɔ bani na bɛɛnu ɔmwi mɛni ni, bɛsɔ bɛɛɛdubo-ma bɔnu kudii.

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔdubo bukpo bute-mii, amii ɔdi kani ndi ka binye kpoo bitaanu.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti úye Mose ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na bɛɛva taakpali-mi? Su Israelƒuɔ bammɔ na batɔ bana anumi.

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Talaku ƒula ugyii ɔdadi ɔmmɔ katɔ na enene kɔnu atina Ɛpugyie ɔmmɔ na ntu bɔmmɔ bɔbwɛ kemmo inyɔ na Israelƒuɔ basia ɛpu ɔmmɔ kemmo balɛ kalɔ kakwiidi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Na ndubɔya na Egyipteƒuɔ bammɔ kayi kayu ɔkplu na basia-ma kama lɛni kani. Na ɔkɛnku Ƒarao ku nwuna bekpone bammɔ ku bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ku bapɔnkɔ beliene bammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ ɔsu na mina lɛnyi likeye.

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔtu ɔni ntɔnku Israelƒuɔ únwini útákpɛ-ma kama. Na liƒlukutu lɛni ntɔ-ma anumi lɛnɔ línwini lítákpɛ-ma kama

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: na lɛ́kya Egyipteƒuɔ bekpone ku Israelƒuɔ ntɛ. Na usien umodi ɔmmɔ ni, liƒlukutu lɛmmɔ lɛ́ya na lɛdisa líduo kakɛ kadi na kakɛ kadi lɛnɔ bukeye bɔkya mmɔ, na ɔdi utakana ɔkpanadi kudɔ bɔkpɛ bude usien ɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Amu na Mose únene nwuna ugyii ɔdadi ɔmmɔ ɔ́tina Ɛpugyie ɔmmɔ, na Unwoti ɔ́ya na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ bonwu ɔdi úkpo ɔ́si ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmɛni údi ɛpu ntu bɔmɛni úsienku kama na ɔ́ya na kalɔ kakwiidi kálɛ. Ntu bɔmmɔ búle lɛlɔ kemmo inyɔ,

english_verse: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
translation_verse: na Israelƒuɔ bésie bávia ɛpu ɔmmɔ kemmo kalɔ kakwiidi lɛlɔ. Na ntu bɔmmɔ bɔ́bla awodu bonwu bɔ́kya-ma kɔmii ku kɔdianu.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Na asa kadi keteegye ni, Unwoti ɔ́nu Egyipteƒuɔ bekpone bamɛni úmene ɔ́siku nwuna lɛgyavonku ku liƒlukutu bonwu lɛmmɔ kemmo na ɔ́ya na béƒu bábla susuusu.

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́ya na bana bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ lɛmmɔ lɛgba lɛ́ƒɛ na lɛsɔ liládia bɔni. Amu na Egyipteƒuɔ básu lɛlɔ banii, “Unwoti ɔkya uukpóku-bu teete Israelƒuɔ, anwuɔsu bɛya na bɔda-ma bɔnyonu na bɔtɔlɔ-ma kudɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Nene kɔnu tina ɛpu ɔmmɔ na ntu bɔmmɔ bɔbwɛ bubebi Egyipteƒuɔ ku bana kɛɛkɛ ku bana bakane ƒui lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose únene nwuna kɔnu ɔ́tina ɛpu ɔmmɔ, na asa kadi keteegye ni, ntu bɔmmɔ bɔ́sɔ bɔ́sala lɛlɔ na bɔ́gbala Egyipteƒuɔ bammɔ ɔ́sɔku úwi ɛpu ɔmmɔ kemmo ina ka báyɔ ka nka bekeli.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Na ntu bɔmmɔ bɔ́nyina Ƒarao bekpone bani nábi basiaku Israelƒuɔ bɔ́kya ɛpu ɔmmɔ kemmo ku bana kɛɛkɛ ku bana bakane, na ina unwi útakɛ ngba.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Nsu Israelƒuɔ bésie bávi ɛpu ɔmmɔ kemmo kalɔ kakwiidi lɛlɔ, na ntu bɔmmɔ bunye aani awodu na bana kɔmii ku kɔdianu kakɛ ƒui.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛmmɔ Unwoti úkpo ɔ́ƒɔ Israelƒuɔ ɔ́lɛku Egyipteƒuɔ enu kemmo. Na Israelƒuɔ bánu kalɛ Egyipteƒuɔ bamɛni békpi bewi ɛpu kɔtu.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Amu ka bánu kalɛ na Unwoti údie nwuna ɔyikun keyi na Egyipteƒuɔ bamɛni lɛlɔ ni, báyia Unwoti na báƒɔ anwu ku Mose nwuna kabla ɔblane bádi na béti bana anu básia-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ku Israelƒuɔ bátu ɔnu bémwi Unwoti banini, “Ndubɔtu ɔnu limwi Unwoti. Ɔsika Úkpo kekpo kebendi na ɔ́di lɛlɔ Na bapɔnkɔ ku bana bakane ƒui úbo-ma útákya ɛpu kemmo.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: Unwoti ndi mina ɔyikun ɔni ɔsu na mɔɔtu kɔgya. Anwu nénwini mina ɔƒɔne. Na mina Katɔti na ndubumwi, Ɔdi mina Katɔti, mina bati kuuku Katɔti, na ndubɔkɔliku-nwu lɛnyi katɔ.

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔdi ukpone geen. Na nwuna lɛnyi ndi Unwoti.

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: Ƒarao bekpone ku bana kɛɛkɛ ƒui ɔ́nyina-ma ɔ́kya ɛpu kemmo. Ƒarao benengu batɔnkune ƒui bátɛ Ɛpugyie kalɔ.

english_verse: They sank to the bottom just like stones.
translation_verse: Na ɛpu ligyu lɛmmɔ líbi-ma ala kpoo, na báyu bátátɛ-nwu kalɔ aani lɛtabi.

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: “Unwoti, ƒula kɔdianu kɔnu kɔɔtina lɛgadi ɔyikun. Unwoti, ƒula kɔdianu kɔnu nákɔ ukisine ɔmmɔ ɔ́bwɛ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: Na ƒula lɛgadi bubomo kenye na éti ébo bani mɔɔta teenye-ɔ lɛlɔ áƒiɛmi kalɔ. Na ka édie ƒula kɔnyi keyi ni, ɔ́kyula-ma aani kalɛ na alakpi aakywí.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: Ƒula kɔnyi ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni nálɛ-ɔ enwu kemmo ɔ́ya na ntu bɔmmɔ bɔ́sala lɛlɔ. Na ntu bɔni avlɔvɔ mɔɔkɔ́ mmɔ búnye kpakplaa aani awodu. Na ɛpu ntɛ ntu bɔmmɔ bɔ́kwii bɔ́bla kpakplaa.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: “Ukisine ɔmmɔ ɔ́kun lɛmɛnɛ ɔnini, ‘Ndubɔbi bɔsiaku-ma na ntáka-ma lɛkya. Na liƒie-ma ala lɛƒɔ na lile-nya na lɛdi-nya kalɛ biala na mɔɔyɔ́. Ndubɔkpa mina kewii liti lɛyila-ma udu.’

english_verse: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
translation_verse: Nsu ka Unwoti ɔ́nya ɔ́nwuna kunwi pɛ kani na ɛpu ɔmmɔ úti Egyipteƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui. Na bányi ntu kemmo aani lɛbuala lɛni mbo unu.

english_verse: Our Lord, no other gods compare with you— Majestic and holy! Fearsome and glorious! Miracle worker!
translation_verse: “Unwoti, baƒiɔ bamani nse aani ƒula kalɛ? Ɔma nse aani awɔ kalɛ? Ƒula lɛgadi lise kedee, na liikeye ku liƒu na aabla ala ebendi ku akɔla ala budie taatina.

english_verse: The people you rescued were led by your powerful love to your holy place.
translation_verse: “Adubɔtɔnku ƒula bekyuli ka aayɔ́-ma uwi ndi uwi ɔsu. Ƒula bekyuli bani na ékpo áƒɔ. Na ɔkɛnku ƒula ɔyikun lɛlɔ ɔsu adubɔtɔnku-ma etéduoku ƒula kalɔ kedee kemmo.

english_verse: Nations learned of this and trembled— Philistines shook with horror.
translation_verse: Na kadi bekyuli badubunu na liƒu libendi lɛda-ma. Na liƒu ku lɛlɔ bɔtɔ bɔdubɔda Ƒilistiƒuɔ

english_verse: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
translation_verse: Na Edomƒuɔ baga badubo bɔyia geen ku liƒu, na liƒu lɛmmɔ lɛya na lɛlɔ litaatɔ Moabƒuɔ batɔnkune kpakpaakpa. Na enu adubɔƒɛ Kanaanƒuɔ geen na bataayila.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Liƒu ku bɔyia geen ndubo bekyuli bamɛni bɔda. O, Unwoti, ɔkɛnku ƒula ɔyikun ɔsu ni, badubo bɔsinsi bunye aani lɛtakpɛ, úti útédu ka awɔ Unwoti ásia ávi, na ƒula bekyuli bani na édie adanku bávi bátɔlɔ.

english_verse: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Na adubɔkpanku-ma ebenyene kenyekɔ kadi. Kenyekɔ kani ndi ƒula kɔbi lɛlɔ, kesii kani na ábla na kadi ƒula kakyakɔ, na ásia mmɔ kɔnu ése kpakplaa.

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: Unwoti, awɔ kani ndubɔdi lɛga úsela uwi ƒui.” Miriam Údie Kɔgya Úte Unwoti

english_verse: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Israelƒuɔ bésie bávi ɛpu kalɔ aani kalɔ kakwiidi. Nsu uwi ɔni na Egyipteƒuɔ bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ku bana bapɔnkɔ ku bana bakane béduo ɛpu ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Unwoti ɔ́sɔku ntu bɔmmɔ ɔ́sala na búti-ma.

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti Kenye Udiene Miriam ɔni ndi Mose ɔnwani ulekubi úti nwuna kabontobi na Israel beleku básiaku-nwu, na ama lɛnɔ bada bana ɔdi na baakunku na baatɔ́.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Na kɔgya kɔni na Miriam údie ndi, “Bidie kɔgya bite Unwoti, ɔsika úkpo ɔ́di lɛlɔ geen. Bapɔnkɔ ku bana lɛlɔ beliene ƒui úbo-ma útákya ɛpu kemmo.” Mara Ku Elim Ketu

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́tɔnku Israel bekyuli bammɔ ɔsiku Ɛpugyie kɔtu mmɔ útédu ketele kani baalɔ banii Sur kemmo. Na bésie lɛgba emeyi atɛ sɔɔn na ketele kemmo. Nsu bátasiaku ntu bɔdi.

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: Amu na bétédu kesii kani baalɔ banii Mara, nsu ntu bɔni nkya mmɔ bubo ɔdu geen ɔni na bútadia-ma bɔni. Anwuɔsu básia-nwu lɛnyi banii Mara. Na nwuna kalɔ ndi ɔdu.

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli básu Mose kalɛ na ntu bɔmmɔ buse. Na béwulo bákya-nwu banii, “Bi ntu bɔdubo bɔni ɔƒɛni?”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose úwulo ɔ́kpali Unwoti momoomo. Na Unwoti ɔ́tina-nwu ligyiiku lɛdi na úƒwimi ɔ́kya ntu bɔmmɔ kemmo. Na ntu bɔmmɔ bɔ́dia-ma bɔni. Mmɔ na Unwoti úbo-ma ɔda úti ɔ́kɔku-ma ɔ́nu.

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: Ɔnini, “Si biinú ami bina Unwoti Katɔti litemi na bɛɛbla ala ani nse siin na mina anumi na bɛɛdi mina ɔda bubo ƒui lɛlɔ kpakplaa ni, lɛɛɛdubo bɔya na lɛlɛ lidu lidu lɛni na lɛ́ya na líbo Egyipteƒuɔ lɛlɔ ɔdi ubo-mii lɛlɔ kudii. Ɔsika ami ndi bina Unwoti ɔni mɔɔbwi-mii lɛlɛ.”

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui báta bási Elim na bétédu Sin ketele kemmo, na ketele kani nkya Elim ku Sinai ntɛ. Na ka bálɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, na ɔdi kɔbuli kunyɔdi limeyi leevu-lɛlɔndi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Na ketele kemmo mmɔ ni, bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bakya baadɔnku Mose ku Aaron banini,

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: “Si nka bɔdu mmomu na Unwoti ɔ́du-bu na Egyipte nka ɔdia-bu utulo ɔni na búbo bɔkya mɛni. Ɔsika na mmɔ ni, nka bɔɔnwá adila ani bɔɔyɔ́ na bɔɔdi kaduɛ. Nsu bíti-bu bíboku ketele kamɛni kemmo ka bise-bu kɔka bɛdu.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Ndubɔya na adila ataana taasi katɔ teete-mii aani ɔnantu. Na limeyi ndi limeyi ni, ya na bekyuli bammɔ balɛ na batála kalɛ kani medu-ma bɔdi limeyi kenye. Na ɔmɛni ndubuti bɔkɔku-ma bɔnu si badubo mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ bɔdi.

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛkundi lɛlɔ ni, ɔdi biala ɔla kalɛ ndubudu-nwu emeyi anyɔ.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose ku Aaron básu Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui banini, “Ɔmwi useyi ɔmɛni ni, bɛdubɔti ka Unwoti náda-mii údie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: Na si údu ɔtanta ni, bɛdubɔnu Unwoti bukeye bonwu, ɔsika únu bina enyekpi ani ƒui bɛkya bɛɛsu teewi-nwu. Na bi ɔsu na abu na ɔlɛka biti kɔnyi bɛkya?”

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛdubɔti ka anwu ndi Unwoti si uwi ɔni na úte-mii lɛna na bɛ́kun useyi, na úte-mii bodobodo ɔni ƒui na bɛɛwia na bɛ́di ɔtanta, ɔsika únu kalɛ na bíti kɔnyi kemmo bɛɛsu etemila teewi-nwu. Bi na abu bɔdi? Ɔɔɔdi abu na bɛɛdɔnku, mmomu Unwoti.”

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su Aaron ɔnini, “Kɔ lɛsa te Israelƒuɔ ƒui anini, ‘Bibo bibenye Unwoti anumi, ɔsika únu kalɛ na bɛkya bɛɛdɔnku-nwu.’ ”

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Aaron ɔkya ɔɔtɛmi teete bekyuli bammɔ ni, bénwini anumi bátina ketele kammɔ. Mmɔ na Unwoti bukeye bonwu bɔ́bwɛ bɔ́lɛ kɔnakunwi na liƒlukutu kemmo.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: “Su Israelƒuɔ bammɔ anini, línu bana etemila ani bakya baasu teewi-mi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu si úsela useyi uwi ni, badubɔkun lɛna. Na ɔtanta lɛnɔ badubɔkɛ bodobodo ɔni baawia badi. Mmɔ na badubɔnu bɔti ka ami Unwoti ndi bana Katɔti.”

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Useyi ɔmmɔ ni, baasɛ wɛlɛ wɛlɛ badi báyu bébewi bana kakyakɔ mmɔ yuu. Na ɔtanta ni, amii áyu ámana bana kakyakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na amii ammɔ ákwii ni, kɔlɛmii kɔdi nse aani etubankɛ kɔtakɛ áyu ewi ámana ketele mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Ka Israelƒuɔ bánu lɛla lɛmmɔ ni, balati lɛla lɛni lɛdi. Amu na bakya beeye lɛlɔ banii, “Bi na ɔdi mɛni?” Amu na Mose ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔmɛni ndi adila ani na Unwoti úte-mii ka bɛdi.

english_verse: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
translation_verse: Na úbo-mii ɔda ka ɔdi biala ɔla kalɛ kani medu-nwu bɔdi. Anwuɔsu kaduli biala ukyuli biala ɔla kalɛ medu-nwu bɔdi aani kalaku kenwi keyile.”

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ bábla kalɛ kani na Mose ɔ́su-ma. Na badi bála-nwu pii na badi lɛnɔ bála blii suɛ.

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Nsu badi bátadi Mose ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na báda bana adila ammɔ adi bése na kadi kégye-nya lɛlɔ. Na bani náda bana adila bese na kadi kégye ni, beklubi béyii-nya kemmo na eenwenyi geen. Anwuɔsu Mose úti kɔnyi geen ɔ́kya-ma.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Na ɔtanta biala ɔdi biala ɔɔla kalɛ kani wakana bɔdi. Na si ɔƒɛ ɔ́bi ni, ɔni muubú ƒui ɔɔnani na ɔɔyii taakya.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛkundi ni, bála adila ammɔ akpa anyɔ kalɛ na wedu-ma bɔdi emeyi anyɔ, ɔni mabla aani kɔlaku kɔmmɔ inyɔ inyɔ ɔdi biala. Amu na lɛtɔ benengu bammɔ ƒui bésie Mose kudɔ bátásu-nwu lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́.

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Lɛni na Unwoti úbo ɔda ɔnini, ‘Kɔnaadi ɔdi Lɛnwunameyi kedee ute ami Unwoti. Anwuɔsu biƒi lɛla biala na bɛɛyɔ́ ka biƒi, na biƒulo lɛla biala na bɛɛyɔ́ ka biƒulo. Na bɛklibi lɛla biala nébu bise bite kadi kegye.’ ”

english_verse: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu báklibi lɛla biala nébu bése aani kalɛ kani na Mose ɔ́su-ma mmɔ, na beklubi béteduo iye enwenyi.

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛdi adila ammɔ ɔmwi, ɔsika Lɛnwunameyi lɛdi ute Unwoti, na bɛɛɛdubo lɛla biala bɔnu bɔla ɔmwi.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Emeyi aku na bɛdubɔla-nya, nsu limeyi maatɛdi lɛdi Lɛnwunameyi na lɛla biala lilayu.”

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui kama ni, bekyuli badi bálɛ limeyi maatɛdi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ bésie batánu si badubɔkɛ lɛla lɛdi, nsu bátanu lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti úye Mose ɔnini, “Uwi ɛlɛ sɔɔn na amii Hebriƒuɔ bɛdubuni mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ bɔdi bitédu?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Binyimo ka ami Unwoti nédie Lɛnwunameyi lɛmɛni líte-mii. Ɔmɛni ɔsu limeyi lɛkundi biala lɛlɔ ndubute-mii adila ani ndubudu-mii emeyi anyɔ. Na ukyuli biala utalɛ nwuna kaduli utesie kesi kesii limeyi maatɛdi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu bekyuli bammɔ bánwuna limeyi maatɛdi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔsu ɔnini, “Unwoti úbo-bu ɔda ɔnini, ‘Bɛklibi manna ɔmmɔ kalaku keyile bise bite bina bawɔ bawɔ kalɛ na ama lɛnɔ babanu adila ani na líte-mii na bɛ́di na ketele kemmo uwi ɔni na lɛ́ƒɔ-mii lɛ́siku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su Aaron ɔnini, “Wia ɔsii ɔdi na eti manna ɔmmɔ ɔdi aani omar bɔkɔku akya-nwu kemmo. Na eti ese Unwoti anumi. Ɔmɛni ɔdubuse bute bula bawɔ bawɔ.”

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Aaron ɔ́bla kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda mmɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ na úti manna ɔmmɔ ɔdi úse Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ anumi kalɛ na bada bese kama bete bawɔ bammɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites ate manna for
translation_verse: Omar bɔkɔku bɔmɛni mabla aani kalaku kenwi.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui báta bási Sin ketele kemmo na bakɛ beelie taata aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo-ma ɔda. Bátáda keliekɔ na Reƒidim, nsu ntu bɔni na bani buuubo mmɔ.

english_verse: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bammɔ bakya baadɔnku Mose banini, “Te-bu ntu na bɔni.” Mmɔ na Mose údie kenye ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na bɛɛdɔnku-mi? Na bi ɔsu na bɛɛkɔ́ku Unwoti taanu?”

english_verse: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
translation_verse: Nsu ka utukwɛ mɔɔda bekyuli bamɛni ɔsu ni, baadɔnku Mose banini, “Bi ɔsu na ákpanku-bu ásiku Egyipte na áya na utukwɛ ɔdubo abu ku bula bebi ku bebuo ƒui bɔdu?”

english_verse: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Mose ɔ́kpali Unwoti momoomo na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Bi na ndubo bekyuli bamɛni bɔbla ɔƒɛni? Benye kagyumana ka bebo-mi atabi badu.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Tiku Israel batɔnkune bammɔ badi da na bisie lɛtɔtɔ blii. Na si bísela ni, na eti ƒula ugyii ɔdadi ɔni na éti áƒiɛmi Nil ntu anumi mmɔ ada.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
translation_verse: Na ami Unwoti ndubunye-ɔ kudɔ na lɛtakpɛ lɛni nlɛ Horeb kɔbi lili mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na eti ugyii ɔmmɔ aƒiɛmi lɛtakpɛ lɛmmɔ, na ntu bɔdubɔlɛ bɔsiku-ni kemmo na bekyuli bammɔ bani.” Na Mose ɔ́bla kalɛ kani na Unwoti ɔ́tina-nwu na batɔnkune bammɔ anumi.

english_verse: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu básia kesii kani na ntu bɔmmɔ bɔ́lɛ lɛnyi banii Masa, ɔni kalɔ ndi bɔkɔku taanu ku Meriba ɔni lɛnɔ kalɔ ndi Bɔdɔ, ɔsika mmɔ na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ bádɔ na bákɔku Unwoti bánu na béye banini, “Unwoti ɔkya-bu akɔ ɔƒɛni?” Israelƒuɔ Békpoku Amalekƒuɔ

english_verse: When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Amu na Amalekƒuɔ báta ka bébekpoku Israelƒuɔ na Reƒidim.

english_verse: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su Yosua ɔnini, “Tiku banana badi na bitékpoku Amalekƒuɔ. Ndubɔkɔ lisie nténye kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili kɔnaadi na liti Katɔti ugyii ɔdadi ɔmmɔ lɛda.”

english_verse: Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yosua ɔ́ta útékpoku Amalekƒuɔ bammɔ aani kalɛ na Mose úbo-nwu ɔda mmɔ. Na Mose ku Aaron ku Hur bákɔ bésie kɔbi lili.

english_verse: The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni ƒui na Mose enu aƒa katɔ mmɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ baadi kekpo kammɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu si ɔ́nya ɔ́yula enu kalɔ pɛ na Amalekƒuɔ bénwini baadi Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Mose enu aƒa katɔ laa na ɔ́ɔnɔ ni, Aaron ku Hur báwia lɛtabi lɛdi béte Mose na ɔ́sɔ úlie-ni lɛlɔ. Na unwi unye ɔƒɛnyi ɔmɛni na unwi lɛnɔ unye ɔƒɛnyi ɔngye. Na béƒie-nwu enu bada benye na aƒa katɔ laa úti útédu ka ɔƒɛ ɔ́nu.

english_verse: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Nweni kekpo kamɛni lɛlɔ bɔdi etemila kya kakunkɛ kadi kemmo na aya na Yosua unu, na unwini enyimo na uteese, ɔsika ndubo Amalekƒuɔ ƒui udu bɔyila na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ na ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ uleti-ma lɛlɔ kasusu.”

english_verse: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mose ɔ́tu lɛkpabi na ɔ́sia-ni lɛnyi ɔnii, “Unwoti mɔɔyá na mɔɔdi lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_verse: Na Mose údie kalɔ ɔnini, “Ɔsika Unwoti lɛlɔ na líti kama líkpo, nsu uwi ɔni mebo kemmo ni, Unwoti ɔdubukpoku Amalekƒuɔ ɔsia kama ɔ́si kaba úsie kaba.”

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
translation_verse: Na asa badubɔyu ulu ni, ɔ́sia kenye úmene Mose ka anwu ku ulekudi ku nwuna bebi inyɔ bakɛ ulu lɛlɔ badubo.

english_verse: When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose ɔ́ta ɔnii utásiaku nwuna aasi na ulu lɛlɔ. Ka útásiaku-nwu ni, úbo kalɔ úte-nwu na ɔ́kya-nwu kɔgbu. Na bégyele lɛlɔ kaduɛ. Na ɔmmɔ kama bénwini bésie nwuna adi kevo kemmo.

english_verse: where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
translation_verse: Na Mose ɔ́su nwuna aasi ala ani ƒui na Unwoti ɔ́bla Ƒarao ku Egyipteƒuɔ na Israelƒuɔ ɔsu. Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-nwu abi ani bébo na ulu lɛlɔ ku kalɛ na Unwoti ɔ́da-ma údie.

english_verse: Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.”
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka Unwoti utulo benwoti bani ƒui nkya, ɔsika ɔ́bla ala amɛni úti ɔ́ƒɔ bekyuli bani nkya mɔɔbla Israelƒuɔ kalala.”

english_verse: Jethro offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and Israel's leaders came to eat with Jethro there at the place of worship. Judges Are Appointed (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Amu na Mose aasi ɔmɛni úte bebuo ku akpala bamba na béti bákpa béte Katɔti. Na Aaron ku Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune bésie na bátádiku-ma bodobodo na Unwoti anumi. Mose Údie Litemi Batɛne

english_verse: You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔsu-ɔ ka uwi uletu awɔ ku bekyuli bamɛni ƒui lɛlɔ lɛdubo-mii butu geen, ɔsika etila amɛni etulo-ɔ buti, awɔ lɛti.

english_verse: The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening.
translation_verse: Kadi kégye ni, Mose úti nwuna liboku na úse kalɔ ɔɔtɛ etemila. Na ɔ́tɛ etemila ɔ́si ɔtanta laa útédu useyi ɔni na útakɛ kɔnu na ɔnwuna.

english_verse: Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
translation_verse: Amu ka nwuna aasi ɔ́nu kabla kani na Mose ɔkya ɔɔbla teete bekyuli bammɔ ni, úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi kabla udu na awɔ lɛti enye aabla teete bekyuli bamɛni lɛni? Bi ɔsu na awɔ lɛti mɔɔbla ɔmɛni, na bekyuli benye-ɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́si ɔtanta útédu usien ka atɛ bana litemi ete-ma?”

english_verse: Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose údie kenye ɔnini, “Mɔɔbla ɔmɛni, ɔsika bekyuli baawia Katɔti lɛyɔla bati.

english_verse: They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
translation_verse: Na si nkyuli inyɔ bakɛ litemi ni, beebo-mi kudɔ na lɛtɛ-ni lite-ma, na lɛsia ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ lɛtina-ma Katɔti ɔda bubo ala.”

english_verse: Jethro replied: That isn't the best way to do it.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose aasi údie kenye ɔnini, “Eeenye alábla ala ulu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu nu mina litemi ɔƒɛni. Na eti bɔlɛ bɔni mɔɔlɛ-ɔ mɛni. Na Katɔti ɔdubunyeku-ɔ. Awɔ nye Katɔti kenye te bekyuli bammɔ ƒui. Na etemila biala na bebo ka basu ni, ya na beti-nya beboku Katɔti.

english_verse: and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
translation_verse: Na ataatina-ma ɔda bubo etemila ammɔ. Na atina-ma kalɛ na ɔlɛka belie ngba bavinku. Ku kabla kani na ɔlɛka babla.

english_verse: These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bamɛni ndubutaatɛ bekyuli bammɔ ƒui litemi. Nsu si etemila adi akya na étulo-ma ni, na aya beti-nya beboku-ɔ. Na etemila ani neeebo ɔkplu ni, ama alati bakana batɛ-nya. Ɔmɛni ɔdubɔya na ƒula etila abla ƒaaƒaa. Ɔsika badubutiku-ɔ etila ammɔ adi.

english_verse: This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
translation_verse: Na si ábla ɔmɛni aani kalɛ na Katɔti úbo-ɔ ɔda ni, lɛlɔ lɛdubɔkɔsi-ɔ butu. Na bekyuli bani litemi bátɛ badubo bunwini besie bana kɔduli na kaƒɔ kayɔ-ma.”

english_verse: They served as judges, deciding the easy cases themselves, but bringing the more difficult ones to Moses.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bamɛni baatɛ etemila teete Israelƒuɔ uwi ndi uwi. Na beeti etemila ani mbo ɔkplu teete Mose na ɔɔtɛ. Nsu ani neeebo ɔkplu ni, ama alatidi mɔɔtɛ-nya.

english_verse: After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_verse: Amu na Yetro úye ulu ɔ́siku Mose kudɔ, na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie nwuna ɔma.

english_verse: Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
translation_verse: Amu Mose ɔ́kɔ úsie kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili na útasiaku Katɔti. Na mmɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́lɔ Mose na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Tásu Yakob kaduli bekyuli ku Israelƒuɔ anini,

english_verse: You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young.
translation_verse: ‘Amii alati bɛ́nu ku bina anumi lɛla lɛni na lɛ́bla Egyipteƒuɔ ku kalɛ na líti-mii aani kalɛ kɔdigbo aasɛ uuti nwuna bebi taasia nwuna avwi lɛlɔ líboku mɛni.

english_verse: Now if you will faithfully obey me, you will be my very own people. The whole world is mine,
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni si bínu-mi litemi kaduɛ na bɛ́di mina bunyimi lɛlɔ ni, amii ndubɔbla mina bekyuli bani lɛlɔ na mina kayi kadubɔsia na kadi bekyuli ƒui akɔ, ina ka kayawi ƒui kadi mina kadi.

english_verse: but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests. Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
translation_verse: Na bɛdubɔbla bakpane ku kadi kani bekyuli nse kedee bite-mi.’ Etemila ammɔ lɛsa na ɔlɛka akɔ ete Israelƒuɔ.”

english_verse: After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose ɔ́yu úbo kalɔ na ɔ́lɔ Israel batɔnkune ƒui ɔ́sala. Na ɔ́su-ma ɔda ɔni ƒui na Unwoti úbo-nwu.

english_verse: and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
translation_verse: Amu na bana ƒui bédie kenye banini, “Bɔdubɔbla lɛla biala na Unwoti ɔ́su-bu.” Anwuɔsu Mose únwini útásu Unwoti kenye kani bekyuli bammɔ bédie.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Ndubo bɔda bɔlɛ bekyuli bammɔ kudɔ na liƒlukutu bonwu kemmo na benu ka mɔɔtɛmiku-ɔ. Na ɔ́si ɔmmɔ kama ni, badubɔƒɔ-ɔ badi.” Mose ɔ́sɔ únwini ku kenye kammɔ útásu bekyuli bammɔ.

english_verse: Once more the Lord spoke to Moses: Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Sie na atáya na baklibi lɛlɔ bese sɛɛn ɔmwi ku kɔnaadi. Na baƒɔ bana adala.

english_verse: and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
translation_verse: Na baklibi lɛlɔ bese limeyi lɛtɛdi. Ɔsika limeyi lɛtɛdi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ndubɔyu bubo Sinai kɔbi kaƒɔna na ukyuli biala ɔnu-mi.

english_verse: Warn the people that they are forbidden to touch any part of the mountain. Anyone who does will be put to death,
translation_verse: Tina-ma kesii kani na ɔdi biala ubo kuƒi ka unye udu na kɔbi kɔmmɔ kudɔ. Na asu-ma ka ukyuli biala ɔ́nu kaduɛ na utakɔ utebo kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili, iye ɔni ude-ku muedi. Na si ɔdi ɔ́bla unyeƒi na ɔ́via ɔmii ɔmmɔ ni, ɔlɛka badu-nwu.

english_verse: either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Bɛkana na bibo-nwu atabi iye kataminta, nsu ɔdi uteti kɔnu utetuku ukyuli ɔmmɔ udu. Na ɔda bubo bɔmɛni buse bute bekyuli ku bebuo ƒui. Si ɔdi útadi-mu lɛlɔ na badu-nwu. Nsu si bínu kakpɛɛ bɔvwi ni, bekyuli bammɔ bebo kuƒi ka bakɔ besie kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili.”

english_verse: After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́si kɔbi lili mmɔ úsie nwuna bekyuli kudɔ na ɔ́su-ma ka baklibi lɛlɔ bese bete Unwoti bɔsiaku. Anwuɔsu báƒɔ bana adala.

english_verse: He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime. The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Mose ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛklibi lɛlɔ bise bite limeyi lɛtɛdi. Na ɔdi utese ulekudi kudɔ.”

english_verse: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛtɛdi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, kayaa kése kalɔ keedu na kaabwɛ ogya na liƒlukutu bonwu líbaƒɔ kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili. Na kɔnakunwi bénu kakpɛɛ kɔku bonwu kɔdi. Na bani ƒui nkya keliekɔ mmɔ ƒui liƒu bonwu lɛ́da-ma.

english_verse: Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́kpanku-ma ɔlɛku bana keliekɔ usienku kɔbi kɔmmɔ kaƒɔna.

english_verse: Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook.
translation_verse: Na sɔsɔ ni, uyɔ úyi Sinai kɔbi kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ƒui. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́yu úbo kɔbi kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ku ogya. Na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔɔkɔ́ katɔ aani si lɛgyavonku bonwu lɛdi na bákya ogya bálɛ, na kɔbi kɔmmɔ kɔɔkunku na lɛlɔ lɛɛtɔ́-ma kpakpaakpa na bɔyia ɔsu.

english_verse: The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
translation_verse: Na bɔkɔ kani na kakpɛɛ kammɔ kɔku kɔɔkɔ́ katɔ teebu. Amu na Mose ɔ́tɛmi úte Unwoti, na Unwoti údie kenye ku katɔ budun.

english_verse: The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́yu úbo Sinai kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili. Na ɔ́kpali Mose ka ɔkɔ ubo kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili. Amu na Mose ɔ́kɔ úsie mmɔ.

english_verse: Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Yu, na esie atásu bekyuli bammɔ ka batavia ɔmii ɔmmɔ betebo banii baawia Unwoti banu. Na si báyu atuɔkplu ni, bana ketulodikɔ badubo bukpi bɔyii udu.

english_verse: Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
translation_verse: Ina bakpane bani mɔɔní teede-mi ni, ɔlɛka babla lɛlɔ sɛɛn. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ndubo-ma kɔtu bɔni.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “The people cannot come up the mountain. You warned us to stay away because it is holy.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su Unwoti ɔnini, “Bekyuli bammɔ balakana bɔkɔ bubo Sinai kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili. Ɔsika awɔ ɔlati nébo-bu ɔda anii, ‘Sia ɔmii mana kɔbi kɔmmɔ na abla mmɔ sɛsɛɛ kedee ete-mi.’ ”

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti údie Mose kenye ɔnini, “Sɔ yu sie kɔbi kɔmmɔ kalɔ, na atákpanku Aaron eboku. Nsu útalɛka bakpane ku bekyuli bammɔ bavia ɔmii ɔmmɔ, na bakɔ bebo Unwoti kudɔ. Na si báyu atuɔkplu ni, ndubo-ma kɔtu bɔni.”

english_verse: After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́yu úsie bekyuli bammɔ kudɔ na ɔ́su-ma ala ani na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu.

english_verse: God said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́ka ɔda bubo etemila leevu amɛni ɔ́su ɔnini,

english_verse: But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off. Idols and Altars
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmmɔ ƒui kama bekyuli bammɔ bámu benye ɔgyu baanu, na Mose lɛti kani nésie úsela kɔbi suu kɔni kemmo na Unwoti ɔ́kya mmɔ kudɔ. Katɔti Úbo Israelƒuɔ Ɔda Na Lɛƒiɔkpa Lɛlɔ

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
translation_verse: “Ami ndi bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔni nédie-mii ɔ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ kesii kani nka bénye-mii lɛlɔ na bɛɛbla bana kabla.

english_verse: Do not worship any god except me.
translation_verse: Bitese benwoti badi bitebunku-mi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth.
translation_verse: Bitavɔ iye bɛnwi lɛla lɛni nálɛ ala ani nkya kayaa iye kalɔ lɛlɔ iye ntu bɔni na kalɔ kemmo na bitaakpa.

english_verse: But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
translation_verse: Nsu mɔɔbla lɛƒɔndia teete nkyuli ɛlɛ ɛlɛ bani mɔɔyɔ́-mi na baadi mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
translation_verse: Takpali Unwoti ƒula Katɔti lɛnyi keeke. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubɔni ukyuli ɔni mɔɔlɔ-nwu lɛnyi keeke kɔtu.

english_verse: Remember that the Sabbath Day belongs to me.
translation_verse: Se Lɛnwunameyi likpo, na abla-ni kedee.

english_verse: You have six days when you can do your work,
translation_verse: Emeyi aku na ɔlɛka eti abla ƒula kabla.

english_verse: but the seventh day of each week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your slaves, your animals, or the foreigners who live in your towns.
translation_verse: Nsu limeyi maatɛdi ndi ami Unwoti ƒula Katɔti Lɛnwunameyi lɛni kemmo na útalɛ ka abla kabla kadi, awɔ iye ƒula bebi iye ƒula kabla bablane iye ƒula bebuo iye ɔƒɔ ɔni nlie-ɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: In six days I made the sky, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them, but on the seventh day I rested. That's why I made the Sabbath a special day that belongs to me.
translation_verse: Ɔsika emeyi aku kemmo na Unwoti údie katɔ ku kalɔ ku ɛpu ku ala ani nkya-nya kemmo, nsu ɔ́nwuna limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu Unwoti údie Lɛnwunameyi sɛsɛɛ na úte-ni kusɛ kusɛ.

english_verse: Respect your father and your mother, and you will live a long time in the land I am giving you.
translation_verse: Bu ƒ'ɔti ku ƒ'ini na adubulie ngba gyɔlɔɔ, na keyi kayɔku-ɔ na kalɔ lɛlɔ, kalɔ kani na ami Unwoti ƒula Katɔti ndubuti lite-ɔ.

english_verse: Do not murder.
translation_verse: Tadu ukyuli.

english_verse: Be faithful in marriage.
translation_verse: Tadi kɔsɔnɔ.

english_verse: Do not tell lies about others.
translation_verse: Tada ukyuli ɔdi kenye.

english_verse: Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else. The People Are Afraid (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Taya na anumi egyie-ɔ na ƒula ukyulikpana kaduli lɛlɔ. Na taya na anumi egyie-ɔ na ƒula ukyulikpana ulekudi, iye nwuna kabla ɔblane ɔnanabi iye ulekubi, iye nwuna ɔmantɛ bakɔ iye nwuna bebuo ala betine iye nwuna lɛla biala na ubo lɛlɔ.” Liƒu Lɛ́da Israelƒuɔ

english_verse: So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bitese baƒiɔ badi bitebunku-mi, na biteti sika ɔƒualadi iye ugyiedi bitavɔ baƒiɔ badi bitese lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The people trembled with fear when they heard the thunder and the trumpet and saw the lightning and the smoke coming from the mountain. They stood a long way off
translation_verse: Amu ka bekyuli bammɔ bénu kalɛ na katɔ keedu, na kaabwɛ ogya, na kakpɛɛ lɛnɔ kaaku, na bánu kalɛ na uyɔ lɛnɔ ɔ́ƒɔ kɔbi kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, liƒu bonwu lɛ́da-ma. Anwuɔsu báni bésie kama kama.

english_verse: and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
translation_verse: Na básu Mose banini, “Si Unwoti úbo litemi lɛdi na wasu-bu ni, na ɔsu-ɔ na asu-bu. Na bulayɔ ka Unwoti ɔlati ɔtɛmi ute-bu. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni bula ƒui bɔdubo bukpi.”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su bekyuli bammɔ ɔnini, “Liƒu litada-mii. Bubo kani na Unwoti úbo ubakɔku-mii ɔnu kalɛ na bitaadi nwuna ɔda bubo lɛlɔ na bilabla likpidi lɛdi.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel: With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Su Israelƒuɔ anini, ‘Amii alati bínu kalɛ na ami Unwoti lɛ́tɛmiku-mii lɛ́siku katɔ,

english_verse: Build an altar out of earth, and offer on it your sacrifices of sheep, goats, and cattle. Wherever I choose to be worshiped, I will come down to bless you.
translation_verse: “ ‘Biti lɛti bɛtu lɛkpabi bite-mi na biti bina baƒonu ku bese ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ bitaabla bɔkyula akpala ku unwi bɔbla akpala nwuna lɛlɔ teete-mi. Na kesii biala na lɛ́su ka bɛkpa-mi na bɛkɔliku mina lɛnyi katɔ ni, ndubɔyu libo na mbete-mii kusɛ kusɛ.

english_verse: If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship.
translation_verse: Na si bíti atabi bɛɛbla lɛkpabi bite-mi ni, biteti atabi ani na abuala na béti bábuɛ-nya, ɔsika si bíti atabi ammɔ udu bɛ́tu-ni ni, bɛdubɔya na uteese-mi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: And don't build an altar that requires steps; you might expose yourself when you climb up.
translation_verse: Na bitabla akpabi na bɛsia ubili bitédu-nwu kudɔ kalɛ na bilakɔ libili lɛmmɔ na ɔdi wetédie lɛlɔ kasɔngya.’ ”

english_verse: Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.
translation_verse: “Na ukyuli biala maƒiɛmi uni iye ɔti lɛla lɛdi ni, ɔlɛka badu-nwu.

english_verse: Suppose two of you are arguing, and you hit the other with either a rock or your fist, without causing a fatal injury. If the victim has to stay in bed,
translation_verse: “Bɛya bɔsu bɔnii nkyuli inyɔ beekpó na unwi úbeyi ɔkpanadi ɔvu iye ɔ́gyu lɛtabi ɔƒiɛmi-nwu na útekpi. Si ɔ́ƒɔ ɔlɛ na ɔkya ɔtɔ

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses the following laws for his people:
translation_verse: “Na ɔda bubo bɔmɛni na ɔlɛka eti ete Israelƒuɔ. Hebrini Kabla Ɔblane

english_verse: If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must remain your slave for six years. But in the seventh year you must set him free, without cost to him.
translation_verse: “Si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́ƒɔ Hebrini ɔdi ɔkpa ka utaabla kabla teete-nwu ni, ɔkpa ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔlɛka ɔkya-nwu kudɔ akwa aku kani. Na si údu lɛkwa maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka udie-nwu ulu, na utaƒɔ-nwu lɛla biala.

english_verse: If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom.
translation_verse: Si uwi údu ka edie ukyuli ɔmmɔ ulu na uuubo uleku ni, nyonu-nwu na ɔtɔlɔ anwu lɛti. Nsu si ɔdanku uleku ni, na anyonu anwu ku ulekudi na batɔlɔ.

english_verse: If you give him a wife, and they have children, only the man himself must be set free; his wife and children remain the property of his owner.
translation_verse: Na si nwuna unwoti náwia uleku úte-nwu, na anwu ku-nwu báwɔ bebi ni, na uleku ɔmmɔ ku nwuna bebi badi unwoti ɔmmɔ badi.

english_verse: But suppose the slave loves his wife and children and his owner so much that he won't leave them.
translation_verse: “Nsu si ukyuli uyedi ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Mɔɔyɔ́ mina unwoti ku mina uleku ku bebi bammɔ ɔsu naaayɔ ka lɛtɔlɔ’ ni,

english_verse: Then he must stand beside either the door or the doorpost at the place of worship, while his owner punches a small hole through one of his ears with a sharp metal rod. This makes him a slave for life.
translation_verse: na nwuna unwoti ɔkpanku-nwu usienku Katɔti kakpakɔ na Katɔti anumi, na ɔya na uténye kakpakɔ kammɔ kayakun iye nwuna kayakun ugyii lɛlɔ na baƒuaala-nwu kɔtu. Na ɔ́si ɔmmɔ kama ɔdubɔbla ukyuli ɔni ndubutaabla kabla teete-ɔ nwuna akwa ƒui.

english_verse: A young woman who was sold by her father doesn't gain her freedom in the same way that a man does.
translation_verse: “Na si ukyuli ɔdi úti ubidi ulekubi úye ni, anwu uuubo kuƒi ka ɔkɛ bɔnwuna aani kalɛ na baanyonu banana.

english_verse: If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her.
translation_verse: Na si béye uleku ɔdi béte ɔnana ɔdi na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔɔyɔ́ ka uti-nwu, nsu uleku ɔmmɔ útenu kalɔ ni, na ɔlɛka unwoti ɔmmɔ ɔsɔku uleku ɔmmɔ uye ute ɔti. Nsu utalɛka unwoti ɔmmɔ uye uleku ɔmmɔ ute ɔƒɔ ɔdi. Ɔsika ɔbla uleku ɔmmɔ kalala.

english_verse: If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
translation_verse: Na si ɔnana ɔdi úye ulekubi ɔdi úte ubidi ɔnanabi ni, ɔlɛka ɔda ulekubi ɔmmɔ aani ubidi ulekudi kalɛ.

english_verse: If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife.
translation_verse: Na si ɔnana úti uleku unyɔdi ni, utalɛka uni ulekudi udeedi, mmomu ɔlɛka uteete-nwu adila ku adala na uteesie-nwu kudɔ ɔnana ku uleku kalɛ.

english_verse: If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it. Murder and Other Violent Crimes The Lord said:
translation_verse: Na si ulete-nwu alakpa atɛ amɛni ni, uleku ɔmmɔ ɔkana na ɔtɔlɔ na ɔnana ɔmmɔ uuubo kuƒi ka ɔƒɔ uleku ɔmmɔ lɛla lɛdi. Ɔda Bubo Na Likyulikpi Ala Bɔbla Lɛlɔ

english_verse: But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside.
translation_verse: Nsu si útati asa na ɔ́du-nwu, na Katɔti bɔyɔ na bɔdi ni, ubo kuƒi ka ukeli usie kesii kani ndubo-mii bɔtina. Na si úkeli úsie mmɔ ni, batadu-nwu.

english_verse: If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
translation_verse: Nsu si kɔnyi ɔsu na úbo nwuna ɔkpana ɔ́du ni, ɔlɛka badu ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ina úkeli útátamiku mina lɛkpabi.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for kidnapping. If you sell the person you kidnapped, or if you are caught with that person, the penalty is death.
translation_verse: “Na si bina akɔ ɔdi úƒie ukyuli ɔdi ka uti-nwu utéye iye uti-nwu ɔbla nwuna kabla ɔblane ni, ɔlɛka badu-nwu si béƒie-nwu.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
translation_verse: “Ukyuli ɔni mewida ɔti iye uni ɔlɛka badu-nwu.

english_verse: and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
translation_verse: na kama ɔ́ta úsie ɔ́vi kaduli ɔ́mana ni, ɔkpanadi ɔmmɔ kayu kani ndi ka ɔƒɔ lɛla biala na ɔlɛne ɔmmɔ ɔ́yila wetédu ka lɛlɔ lɛ́yu-nwu ɔkplu.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for beating to death any of your slaves.
translation_verse: “Na si ɔdi úti ugyii na ɔ́ƒiɛmi nwuna kabla ɔblane ɔnanabi iye ulekubi na úkpi kɔnakunwi ni, ɔlɛka bani ukyuli ɔmmɔ kɔtu.

english_verse: However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
translation_verse: Nsu si ukyuli uyedi ɔmmɔ útekpi limeyi lɛmmɔ iye kadi kegye ni, utalɛka bani unwoti ɔmmɔ kɔtu. Ɔsika unwoti ɔmmɔ mbo-nwu.

english_verse: Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve.
translation_verse: “Si bekyuli badi beekpó na bétédi ɔƒɔndane ɔdi báƒiɛmi na úbile kaƒɔ, nsu útaƒɔ ɔlɛ kpakplaa bamba ɔdi ni, ɔdi ka ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔƒɔ ɔƒɔndane ɔmmɔ ɔgyani kayu kani na ɔ́kya na litemi batɛne básia kɔnu.

english_verse: But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life,
translation_verse: Nsu si ɔlɛ ɔni na uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́ƒɔ ubo ɔkplu ni, ɔdi ka ukyuli ɔmmɔ kɔtu bɔni bɔyu ɔkplu lɛni kani, ngba na ngba kenye,

english_verse: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
translation_verse: lɛnumi na lɛnumi kenye, kenye lɛnyi na lɛnyi kenye, kɔnu na kɔnu kenye ɔgba na ɔgba kenye.

english_verse: If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free.
translation_verse: “Ɔƒɛni si ɔnana ɔdi úbo nwuna kabla ɔblane ɔnanabi iye ulekubi na ɔ́bwɛ-nwu lɛnumi ni, ɔlɛka udie kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ ulu na ɔtɔlɔ ƒaa aani likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla-nwu ku nwuna buye lili kayu bɔƒɔ.

english_verse: A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
translation_verse: “Si ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔdi ɔ́wɔ ukyuli ese ɔ́du ni, ɔlɛka bebo-nwu atabi badu na ɔdi utakun-nwu lɛna lɛmmɔ. Na ukyuli ɔni ebuo na ɔdi ni, utalɛka bani-nwu kɔtu kɔdi.

english_verse: Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning.
translation_verse: Nsu si ebuo ɔmmɔ ɔɔyɔ́ bekyuli ese bɔwɔ lɛni na béte nwuna ɔlati bɔti na útakya-nwu ɔbuli útada kesii kadi na útádu ukyuli ɔdi ni, ɔdi ka bebo ebuo ɔmmɔ atabi badu na badu ɔlati lɛnɔ.

english_verse: pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
translation_verse: Na mmomu si kayu na bákya-nwu ka ɔƒɔ ni, ɔkana na ɔƒɔ kayu kammɔ na uti udie nwuna ngba.

english_verse: This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter.
translation_verse: “Ɔda bubo bɔmɛni bɔdanku si ebuo ɔmmɔ úbo ubi ɔnanabi iye ulekubi ɔ́du.

english_verse: Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property.
translation_verse: “Ɔƒɛni si ukyuli ɔdi úku ubu na útebi-nwu ala na ɔdi ebuo útánu-nwu kemmo ni,

english_verse: You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
translation_verse: ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔdi ka ɔƒɔ ebuo ɔmmɔ kayu ute ɔlati, na ebuo ukpine ɔmmɔ unwini ubu ɔlati ɔdi.

english_verse: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
translation_verse: “Si ukyuli ɔdi ebuo ɔ́du ɔkpanadi ɔdi ni, beti ebuo ɔni nádu unyɔdi mmɔ béye na beti egulabi ammɔ ku ebuo ɔni nékpi mmɔ bele likeke bete bebuo bammɔ balati inyɔ bammɔ.

english_verse: If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_verse: Nsu si bánu báti ka lɛni na ebuo ɔmmɔ ɔɔbi taasiaku bebuo bamba taawɔ-ma taadu, nsu ɔlati útakya-nwu lɛyu ni, ɔdi ka ɔlati ɔmmɔ ɔƒɔ kayu kammɔ, ebuo na ebuo kenye, na ɔni nékpi mmɔ unwini kayu ɔƒɔne ɔmmɔ ɔdi.”

english_verse: If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep.
translation_verse: “Si ukyuli ɔdi úyu ɔmantɛ akɔ iye koƒonu na ɔ́du-ku iye úti-ku úye ni, ɔlɛka ɔƒɔ ɔmantɛ bakɔ ɛlɔ kayu na akɔ ɔgyani ɔni na úyu lili, na ɔlɛka ɔƒɔ baƒonu ine kayu na koƒonu kɔni na úyu lili.

english_verse: If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
translation_verse: “Si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́kpanku nwuna bebuo úsienku kadikɔ na bebuo bammɔ bávia bétéduo ukyuli bamba kemo na bébile-nwu ala ni, ɔlɛka eti ƒula edula abuni aƒɔ kayu kammɔ na ani na bébile kenye.

english_verse: If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
translation_verse: “Si ɔdi ɔ́kya nwuna kemo ogya na ogya ɔmmɔ ɔ́via útákyula ukyuli bamba edula ani nnye-nwu kemo iye ɔ́kyula-nwu kemo kammɔ ƒui ni, ɔlɛka ukyuli ɔni nákya ogya ɔmmɔ uti kemo kammɔ udu bamba ɔƒɔ ɔni ala na úbile kayu.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double.
translation_verse: “Si ukyuli ɔdi únu kalɔ ka ɔƒɔ ɔkpanadi egulabi ɔda-nwu iye utaanu nwuna akɛla lɛlɔ teete-nwu na egulabi iye akɛla ammɔ abayi na ɔ́nu ukyuli ɔni néyu ala ammɔ ni, ɔlɛka uyune ɔmmɔ ɔƒɔ ala ani náyi mmɔ kayu akpa anyɔ.

english_verse: Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
translation_verse: Na si unyeƒi ɔdi ubo nkyuli inyɔ ntɛ na akɛla adi lɛlɔ aani ɔmantɛ bakɔ iye baƒonu iye adala lɛlɔ iye lɛla biala náyi lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka beti-ma besienku litemi batɛne anumi na ukyuli ɔni na litemi batɛne bammɔ bádu kɔtɔ ɔlɛka ɔƒɔ ala ani lɛlɔ baakya unyeƒi mmɔ kayu kunyɔ ute ukyuli ɔni geen mbo ala ammɔ.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking.
translation_verse: “Si ukyuli ɔdi únu kalɔ ka ɔƒɔ ɔkpanadi ebuo ala utine iye ɔmantɛ akɔ iye koƒonu iye ebuo biala utaatumini, na ebuo ɔmmɔ úbekpi iye nwuna lɛlɔ kesii kadi kaƒɔ ɔlɛ iye bebeyu ebuo ɔmmɔ na ukyuli biala utanu ni,

english_verse: If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough.
translation_verse: ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔlɛka usie utákpali ala use kenye na Katɔti anumi ka ɔɔɔdi anwu néyu ebuo ɔni bete-nwu bɔda mmɔ. Na si ɔɔɔdi buyu na beyu ebuo ɔmmɔ ni, utalɛka ɔƒɔ ukyuli ɔni néte-nwu ebuo bɔtumini mmɔ kayu kadi. Ebuo ɔlati uti-nwu lɛni kani.

english_verse: But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it.
translation_verse: Nsu si buyu na béyu ebuo ɔmmɔ ni, ɔlɛka ɔƒɔ ebuo ɔlati kayu.

english_verse: If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
translation_verse: Na si ebuo ukpidi ɔdi lɛnɔ nádu-nwu ni, ɔlɛka uti ebuo ukpine kakɛ kani nébu ubatina. Na si úbo lɛni ni, utalɛka ebuo ɔdane ɔmmɔ ɔƒɔ kayu kadi ute ebuo ɔlati.

english_verse: Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it.
translation_verse: “Na si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́ƒɔ ɔkpanadi ebuo ɔɔtumini, na nwuna kesii kadi káƒɔ ɔlɛ iye úkpi ɔni ɔlati uuubo asa na ebuo ɔmmɔ úkpi ni, ɔlɛka ebuo ɔdane ɔmmɔ ɔƒɔ ebuo ɔmmɔ kayu ute ebuo ɔlati.
