english_verse: Work for six days and rest on the seventh day, even during the seasons for plowing and harvesting.
translation_verse: “Emeyi aku na ebo kuƒi ka abla kabla biala. Nsu ɔtuma uwi na ɔdi o-o, edula ɔƒɛwi o-o ni, tabla kabla kadi na limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
translation_verse: “Na taadi Edula Ebi Edeedi Bɔƒɛ Limeyi ku Kevo Kemmo Bɔkya Emeyi lɛkwa biala.

english_verse: As you advance, I will force the nations out of your land and enlarge your borders. Then no one will try to take your property when you come to worship me these three times each year.
translation_verse: Na ndubɔbɔku kadi bamba bani nlie mmɔ asa na ésie. Na ndubɔya na ƒula lɛmii lɛbɛbɛ libu. Kɔtɛ na adubɔda bɔlɛ ami Unwoti Katɔti anumi lɛkwa biala. Na ukyuli ɔdi uleti lɛnungyie na waƒɔ ƒula kalɔ kadi.

english_verse: When you sacrifice an animal on the altar, don't offer bread made with yeast. And don't save any part of the Passover meal for the next day.
translation_verse: “Teti akpala ubugya ku lɛla biala kemmo na bɔnyii bɔkya tabla akpala tete-mi. Na akpala ani na ábla na Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi ni, taya na kadi kegye akpala ammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, and you must bring the first part of your harvest to the place of worship. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
translation_verse: “Na eti edula abuni ani na ákɛ ásiku ƒula kalɔ kemmo eboku ami Unwoti Katɔti kaduli. “Na tadu koƒonu iye ese ɔni mɔɔnyimi takun.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to put these laws in writing, as part of his agreement with Israel.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Nweni etemila amɛni ƒui se. Ɔsika etemila amɛni na ndubo buti bɔbla mina bunyimi ku Israel.”

english_verse: Moses came down from Mount Sinai, carrying the Ten Commandments. His face was shining brightly because the Lord had been speaking to him. But Moses did not know at first that his face was shining.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Mose ɔ́yu Sinai kɔbi úbo na ɔda Ɔda Bubo Leevu ni, nwuna anumi eekeye, ɔsika ɔ́kya Unwoti kudɔ na bátɛmi. Nsu na ɔɔɔgyi ɔnii nwuna anumi eekeye lɛni.

english_verse: When Aaron and the others looked at Moses, they saw this, and they were afraid to go near him.
translation_verse: Amu ka Aaron ku bekyuli bammɔ bánu kalɛ na nwuna anumi eekeye ni, ɔdi biala ɔ́yia ka ɔni ude-nwu.

english_verse: Moses called out for Aaron and the leaders to come to him, and he spoke with them.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔ́lɔ-ma ka bebo. Na Aaron ku Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune bésie Mose kudɔ na ɔ́tɛmi úte-ma.

english_verse: Then the rest of the people of Israel gathered around Moses, and he gave them the laws that the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama Israelƒuɔ ƒui báni béde-nwu na báka bamana-nwu. Na Mose ɔ́kɔ lɛsa ɔ́su-ma ɔda bubo etemila ani na Unwoti úti úte-nwu na Sinai kɔbi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The face of Moses kept shining, and after he had spoken with the people, he covered his face with a veil.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Mose ɔ́kɔ lɛsa lɛmmɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, úti lɛla lɛdi úbi anumi.

english_verse: Moses would always remove the veil when he went into the sacred tent to speak with the Lord. And when he came out, he would tell the people everything the Lord had told him to say.
translation_verse: Na uwi biala na Mose wesie Unwoti anumi utátɛmiku-nwu ni, ɔɔda lɛdiku lɛmmɔ teebimi. Na si ɔ́tɔlɔ mmɔ úbo Israelƒuɔ kudɔ úbasu-ma ɔda bubo biala ni,

english_verse: They could see that his face was still shining. So after he had spoken with them, he would put the veil back on and leave it on until the next time he went to speak with the Lord.
translation_verse: bekyuli bammɔ baanu ka nwuna anumi eekeye, na ɔɔsɔku lɛdiku lɛmmɔ teebi anumi útédu uwi ɔni na ɔ́sɔ únwini úsie utátɛmiku Unwoti.

english_verse: You have six days in which to do your work. But the seventh day must be dedicated to me, your Lord, as a day of rest. Whoever works on the Sabbath will be put to death.
translation_verse: Ɔnii bibo emeyi aku ka biti bɛbla bina kabla. Nsu limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, bɛbla-ni kedee bite Unwoti na ɔdi utabla kabla kadi. Na si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́bla kabla kadi lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka badu-nwu.

english_verse: Don't even build a cooking fire at home on the Sabbath. Offerings for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Na ɔdi utasala ogya muedi lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ.” Akpala Buti Busienku Unwoti

english_verse: The women who were good at weaving cloth brought the blue, purple, and red wool and the fine linen they had made.
translation_verse: Na beleku bani lɛnɔ ngyi budi béti bana linwo buluu ku ligyiedi lɛni náƒɔ kuye ku adi kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ béboku.

english_verse: And he has given them all kinds of artistic skills, including the ability to design and embroider with blue, purple, and red wool and to weave fine linen.
translation_verse: Ɔ́ya na nwuna kɔyu kɔ́ƒɔ bekyuli bamɛni lɛlɔ kemmo kalɛ bakana na banwi ala lidu lidu na bataa ala lidu lidu na beti linwo buluu ku ligyiedi lɛni náƒɔ kuye ku adi kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ bedi ala lidu lidu. Na bagyi bana kabla kaduɛ.”

english_verse: If you have any skills, you should use them to help make what I have commanded:
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su bekyuli bani ƒui nda kɔnu kemmo kabla ka bebo na babla kabla kani Katɔti úbo-ma ɔda.

english_verse: and the finely woven priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons. Gifts for the Lord
translation_verse: Na bawia adi na bédi Aaron lɛwu sɛsɛɛ ku nwuna bebi lɛwu lɛni na badubo butaakya taabla bakpane kabla. Israelƒuɔ Béti Bana Akpala Béte

english_verse: Moses told the people of Israel that the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: blue, purple, or red wool; fine linen; goat hair;
translation_verse: ku unwo buluu ku ugyiedi ɔni náƒɔ kuye adi kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ku bese linwini,

english_verse: olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices for the oil of dedication and for the incense; or
translation_verse: ku asogya nnɔmii, ku ugyulo ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni na baakya likpose nnɔmii kemmo ku oloƒui ƒɛƒɛɛ,

english_verse: the sacred chest with its carrying poles, its place of mercy, and the curtain in front of it;
translation_verse: Na bawia ala na batu Bunyimi Adaka ku nwuna ligyii ku likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie libila ku kakpakɔ bule kɔdi kɔni beeti taaƒla-nwu anumi.

english_verse: the table with its carrying poles and all that goes on it, including the sacred bread;
translation_verse: Na babla ala kasiakɔ ku nwuna ligyii lɛni baagyú-nwu ku ala ani na baasia-nwu lɛlɔ ku Katɔti bodobodo kedee ɔni muusé-nwu anumi.

english_verse: the incense altar with its carrying poles and sweet-smelling incense; the ordination oil; the curtain for the entrance to the sacred tent;
translation_verse: Na batu oloƒui bɔkyula lɛbi ku nwuna ligyii ku likpose nnɔmii oloƒui ku kevo kayakun lɛduni.

english_verse: the altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand;
translation_verse: Na beti kugyikɛ na babla bɔkyula lɛkpabi ku ntɔ bɔƒɔ lɛbuala ku nwuna bɔgyu ligyii ku nwuna lɛlɔ ala. Na beti abuala egyiedi babla lɛkyami lɛni kemmo badubo asogya butaaƒɔ ku nina ɔka.

english_verse: the curtains with the posts and stands that go around the courtyard and the curtain at the entrance;
translation_verse: Na babla aduni bete kevo kaduli kammɔ ku kana akpa ku ana ɔka, ku aduni ani na baaƒala kayakun.

english_verse: the pegs and ropes for the tent and the courtyard;
translation_verse: Na bawia ewele ku kɔbuli kɔni ndubɔda kevo ku kaduli kammɔ akpa.

english_verse: Moses finished speaking, and everyone left.
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bammɔ bátɔlɔ Mose kudɔ.

english_verse: Then those who wanted to bring gifts to the Lord, brought them to be used for the sacred tent, the worship services, and the priestly clothes.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala kubiti kɔ́da-nwu. Na bani nátuna ku kaƒɔ ƒaa béti etela bésienku Unwoti ka beti batu Kevo Kasakɔ kammɔ ku akpala lɛlɔ ala ku bakpane lɛwu kedee lɛmmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Men and women came willingly and gave all kinds of gold jewelry such as pins, earrings, rings, and necklaces.
translation_verse: Na banana ku beleku bani mɔɔyɔ́ ni, bédie bana kaƒɔ ƒaa na beti bana sika ugyiedi ala ani baakya ɔkwɛ ku atu ku animi ku ana udu besienku Mose. Na bákɔliku-nya katɔ bátina Katɔti bébo-nya kudu.

english_verse: Everyone brought their blue, purple, and red wool, their fine linen, and their cloth made of goat hair, as well as their ram skins dyed red and their fine leather.
translation_verse: Na bani ƒui na bébo linwo buluu ku ligyiedi lɛni náƒɔ kuye ku adi kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ iye bese linwini iye baƒonu lɛku lɛni békpeyi na bákya-ni kuvogyie iye ɛpu bebuo lɛku ni, béti-ni béboku.

english_verse: Anyone who had silver or bronze or acacia wood brought it as a gift to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na bani mbo sika ɔƒualadi ku abuala egyiedi ku bani mbo akasia kugyikɛ kɔni ndubɔdia bute kabla kammɔ lɛnɔ béti béboku Unwoti.

english_verse: And the women who knew how to make cloth from goat hair were glad to do so.
translation_verse: Na béti bana bese linwini bédi ala lidu béboku.

english_verse: The leaders brought different kinds of jewels to be sewn on the special clothes and the breastpiece for the high priest.
translation_verse: Na batɔnkune bammɔ béboku onis atabi ani náƒɔ kuye ku ana lidu bamba ani na badubɔka bamana ɔkpane unengudi awu kedee ku lɛdiku lɛni muubi-nwu kayi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: They also brought sweet-smelling spices to be mixed with the incense and olive oil that were for the lamps and for ordaining the priests.
translation_verse: Na básɔ béboku nnɔmii kede kede, ku ugyulo ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni na baakya likpose nnɔmii kemmo ku oloƒui ƒɛƒɛɛ.

english_verse: Moses had told the people what the Lord wanted them to do, and many of them decided to bring their gifts. Bezalel and Oholiab (Exodus
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ beleku ku banana bédie kayi ƒaa na béti ala pii bésienku Unwoti ka beti babla kabla kani na Unwoti ɔkɛnku Mose lɛlɔ úbo-ma ɔda mmɔ. Besaleel Ku Oholiab Lɛlɔ Kɔtɛ

english_verse: Moses said to the people of Israel: The Lord has chosen Bezalel of the Judah tribe.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ɔnini, “Unwoti údie Besaleel ɔni ndi Uri ubidi na ɔdi Hura uwɔ ɔni nási Yuda kaba kemmo.

english_verse: The Lord is urging him and Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to teach others.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti úte anwu ku Oholiab ɔni ndi Ahisamak ubidi na ɔ́si Dan kaba kemmo kasusu ka béti ala ani na Unwoti úte-ma mmɔ batina bekyuli bamba.

english_verse: and he gave them the gifts that the people of Israel had donated for building the place of worship. In fact, so much was being given each morning,
translation_verse: Na Mose úti ala ani ƒui na Israelƒuɔ béte ka béti bátu Kevo Kasakɔ kammɔ úte-ma. Na Israelƒuɔ beesiénku etela ani beti batu ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ɔtanta ndi ɔtanta ku kayi ƒaa.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, there is already more than we need for what the Lord has assigned us to do.”
translation_verse: Na bésie bátásu Mose banini, “Bekyuli bammɔ béte ala bétulo kalɛ na Unwoti úbo-ma ɔda ka beti batu Kevo kammɔ.”

english_verse: But there was already more than enough to do what needed to be done. The Curtains and Coverings for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Ɔsika ala ani beti batu Kevo kammɔ éemomo étulo kalɛ na baawia. Kevo Kasakɔ Bɔtu Kalɔ Kesekɔ

english_verse: and they were sewn together to make two curtains with five panels each.
translation_verse: Na báka aduni alɔ básala ɔvi unwi, na báka alɔ lɛnɔ básala ɔvi ɔkladi.

english_verse: These eleven sections were joined to make two panels, one with five and the other with six sections.
translation_verse: Na báka aduni alɔ básala ɔvi unwi na báka ɛku lɛnɔ básala ɔvi unyɔdi.

english_verse: Fifty loops were put along one of the wider sides of each panel,
translation_verse: Amu na báka eƒi kunu kunu liti báda kayakun aduni ammɔ kɔtu ɔvi unwi na bábla lɛni kani ku ɔvi unyɔdi.

english_verse: and the two panels were fastened at the loops with
translation_verse: Na béti abuala egyiedi bánwamana bábla ala abalala liti báda libila lɛdiku lɛmmɔ básala.

english_verse: Two other coverings were made—one with fine leather and the other with ram skins dyed red. The Framework for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Na béti koƒonu ɔku ɔni békpeyi na bákya-nwu kuvogyie báka básala béti bébi Kevo kammɔ katɔ na béti ɛpu kemmo ebuo ɔku lɛnɔ báka básala bébi udeedi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Altogether, along the back wall there were eight frames with two silver stands under each of them.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu eku ammɔ ebo maane ku sika ɔƒualadi agbanvuo leevu-ɛku, na inyɔ bɔkya liku biala kalɔ.

english_verse: Six frames were used for the back wall along the west side
translation_verse: Na bása eku aku bálɛ kaduli kammɔ ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. These corner frames were joined from top to bottom.
translation_verse: Na lɛkɔkɔ ligyii lɛmmɔ básala-ni ɔ́si kalɔ betédu katɔ, na nina inyɔ líduo ɔgbanvuo unwi kemmo.

english_verse: Five crossbars were made for each of the wooden frames, with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall.
translation_verse: Na ɔtagyii ɔni na ntɛntɛ úne ɔ́si ligyii lɛni nnye ntɛ mmɔ ɔvi unwi úsie ɔkladi.

english_verse: The frames and crossbars were covered with gold, and gold rings were attached to the frames to run the crossbars through. The Inside Curtain for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Na béti sika ugyiedi bákwa ligyii lɛni nnye mmɔ lɛlɔ ƒui. Na béti sika ugyiedi kɔkwɛnimi báda lɛtagyii lɛmmɔ na bákwa ani lɛnɔ ku sika ugyiedi.

english_verse: For the entrance to the tent, they used a curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework.
translation_verse: Na kevo kammɔ kayakun ni, béti unwo buluu ku ugyiedi ɔni náƒɔ kuye ku adi kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ na bédi lɛduni. Na bedine babuni nábla kɔlɛmii básia-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: They made the inside curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures.
translation_verse: Na béti unwo buluu ku ugyiedi ɔni náƒɔ kuye ku adi kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ na bédi kakpakɔ bule kɔdi kɔmmɔ, na bédi Kerub bebweyi básia-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: They also made four acacia wood posts and covered them with gold. Then gold rings were fastened to the posts, which were set on silver stands.
translation_verse: Na béti akasia ligyii bábla akpa ene na bakwa-ni lɛlɔ ku sika ugyiedi. Na bábla sika ugyiedi kɔkwɛnimi kɔbaladi ku nina sika ɔƒualadi agbanvuo.

english_verse: They made five posts, covered them completely with gold, and set each of them on a gold-covered bronze stand. Finally, they attached hooks for the curtain.
translation_verse: Bánwi ligyii ɛlɔ ku nina kɔkwɛnimi kɔbaladi, na bákwa-ni ku sika ugyiedi. Na béti abuala egyiedi bábla ligyii lɛmmɔ agbanvuo.

english_verse: He covered it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the top.
translation_verse: Na úti sika ugyiedi ɔ́nwamina úwi-nwu kemmo ku kama, na úti anwu kani ɔ́da-nwu atu ɔ́mana.

english_verse: He made four gold rings and attached one of them to each of the four legs of the chest.
translation_verse: Na úti sika ugyiedi ɔ́bla kɔkwɛnimi ɔ́da adaka ɔmmɔ lɛgba ine bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na ɔƒɛnyi ɔni ku ɔni.

english_verse: Then he made two poles of acacia wood, covered them with gold,
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́nwi akasia ligyii na ɔ́kwa-ni ku sika ugyiedi.

english_verse: The entire lid of the chest, which was made of pure gold, was the place of mercy.
translation_verse: Na úti sika ugyiedi sɔɔn ɔ́bla likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie libila úte Adaka ɔmmɔ. Na libila lɛmmɔ bune bɔdi lɛgba ɛtɛ ku kakɛ na nwuna bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba inyɔ ku kakɛ.

english_verse: On each of the two ends of the chest he made a winged creature of hammered gold. They faced each other, and their wings covered the place of mercy. The Table for the Sacred Bread (Exodus
translation_verse: Na bebweyi bammɔ baanu lɛlɔ na bana avwi étile adaka mmɔ. Bávɔ Lɛla Lɛni Lɛlɔ Badubo Bodobodo Butaasia

english_verse: He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border
translation_verse: Na ɔ́bla eƒi ɔ́kya-nwu ɔ́mana na úti sika ugyiedi ɔ́kya eƒi ammɔ ɔ́mana.

english_verse: He made four gold rings and attached one to each of the legs
translation_verse: Ɔ́bla sika ugyiedi kɔkwɛnimii kɔdi ɔ́kya-nwu lɛkɔkɔ ine bɔmmɔ na kesii kani na lɛgba lɛmmɔ lɛda na atu kakɛ.

english_verse: near the edging. The poles for carrying the table were placed through these rings
translation_verse: Na kɔkwɛnimi kɔmmɔ kemmo na beeti ligyii taakya kalɛ na ɔdia na bagyu-nwu.

english_verse: and were made of acacia wood covered with gold.
translation_verse: Na akasia ligyii na úti ɔ́nwi ligyii lɛni na baagyú-nwu mmɔ na úti sika ugyiedi ɔ́kwa-ni lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Everything that was to be set on the table was made of pure gold—the bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings. The Lampstand (Exodus
translation_verse: Na úti sika ugyiedi na ɔ́kwa akyami ku ebui ku ana udu ku lɛɛƒɛɛ kalɛ beti bataabla ntɛ akpala. Bábla Asogya Kasiakɔ Ligyii

english_verse: Bezalel made a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, was made from a single piece of hammered gold,
translation_verse: Amu na úti sika ugyiedi ugyii na útu-nwu ɔ́bla asogya kasiakɔ ugyii na ubo ɔka ku ugyii ɔni muunye-nwu lɛlɔ. Na úti kugyii anwula aani ɔɔƒɛɛ udu ku nwuna evete ƒui ɔ́bla unwi ɔ́danku lɛlɔ ɔ́mana-nwu lɛlɔ na ɔɔdia bɔnu.

english_verse: There was also a blossom where each pair of branches came out from the stem.
translation_verse: Na kesii biala kani na kɔgba kɔmmɔ kɔdanku ugyii ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, lɛɛƒɛɛ udu anwula ammɔ alɛ.

english_verse: The lamp and its equipment, including the tongs and trays, were made of about
translation_verse: Na sika ugyiedi edula ebi akyami maane ku kakɛ unu na béti bábla ala ammɔ. Bábla Oloƒui Kakyulakɔ Lɛbi

english_verse: He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it.
translation_verse: Na úti sika ugyiedi ɔ́kwa-nwu katɔ ku amadɔ ku ese ammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui ɔ́mana.

english_verse: Then below the edging on opposite sides he attached two gold rings through which he put the poles for carrying the altar.
translation_verse: Na úti sika ugyiedi na ɔ́bla kɔkwɛnimi inyɔ ɔ́da lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ atu kada kakɛ blii na lɛƒɛnyi inyɔ lɛlɔ kalɛ ɔkana ligyii lɛmmɔ bɔda na ɔdia buti.

english_verse: These poles were also made of acacia wood and covered with gold. The Oil for Dedication and the Incense (Exodus
translation_verse: Na úti sika ugyiedi na ɔ́kwa akasia ligyii lɛni badubo kɔkwɛnimi kɔmmɔ kemmo bɔkya.

english_verse: Bezalel mixed the sacred oil for dedication and the pure spices for the sweet-smelling incense.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔ ɔbla ala kewikɔ kesii kani beewi nnɔmii kedee ku oloƒui ɔni muunwenyi ƒɛƒɛɛ na béti ala ƒɛƒɛɛ básala-nwu.

english_verse: Bezalel made a large bowl and a stand out of bronze from the mirrors of the women who helped at the entrance to the sacred tent. The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Amu na úti beleku bani mɔɔbla kabla na kasakɔ kedee kayakun kenye mmɔ abuala egyiedi kanu ɔ́vɔ lɛkyami bonwu lɛdi ku nwuna ɔka. Katɔti Kevo Kaduli

english_verse: and the silver that was collected when the people were counted came to
translation_verse: Na sika ɔƒualadi ɔni na kadi bammɔ bekyuli bani na báka mmɔ béyii ɔdi edula ebi aƒɔ avlaatɛ ku kakɛ unu.

english_verse: Then he attached a bronze ring beneath the ledge at the four corners to put the poles through.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́bla kɔkwɛnimi ine ɔ́da ntɔ lɛƒɔla lɛmmɔ atu ene ammɔ kalɛ na ɔdia na beti ligyii bavinku-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: put them through the rings for carrying the altar, which was shaped like an open box. The Large Bronze Bowl (Exodus
translation_verse: Na úti ɔkya kɔkwɛnimi kɔmmɔ kemmo kalɛ na ɔdia na bataagyu lɛkpabi lɛni bábla ku kugyikɛ na liƒi lɛtɛ-nwu kemmo mmɔ. Bávɔ Lɛlɔ Bɔƒɔ Lɛkyami

english_verse: And it was used to make the stands for the entrance to the tent, the altar and its grating, the equipment for the altar,
translation_verse: Na anwu na béti bábla kalɔ ɔka béte Kevo Kasakɔ kayakun ku abualagyie lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ku nina abualagyie ntɔ kaƒɔkɔ kammɔ ku kana lɛlɔ ablala ƒui

english_verse: For the entrance to the courtyard, Bezalel made a curtain nine meters long, which he hung on four bronze posts that were set on bronze stands. This curtain was
translation_verse: Na ligyii lɛmmɔ libo ine ku nina abuala egyiedi ɔka ine. Na akpa ammɔ eli ku abalala ani nda-nya lɛlɔ adi sika ɔƒualadi.

english_verse: for the west. Then he hung a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods. He placed three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hung a curtain
translation_verse: Na akpa aavlanyɔ ammɔ ku ana aka ƒui adi abuala egyiedi ku sika ɔƒualadi abalala na úti ligyii aavlanyɔ lɛni na úti abuala egyiedi ɔ́kwa-nya lɛlɔ ɔda-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Bezalel had worked closely with Oholiab, who was an expert at designing and engraving, and at embroidering blue, purple, and red wool. The two of them completed the work that the Lord had commanded to be done. Moses put Aaron's son Ithamar in charge of the Levites who kept record of the metals used for the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na ubunkune ɔni baalɔ banii Oholiab ɔni ndi Ahisamak ubidi na ɔ́si Dan kaba kemmo na ɔdi enu kabla lidu ɔblane ni, ɔgyi bɔtaa ku adi buluu ku egyiedi kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ani náƒɔ kuye geen budi.

english_verse: According to the official weights, the amount of gold given was a ton,
translation_verse: Na akpala ani bekyuli bammɔ béte na bákɔliku katɔ bébo kudu béte Unwoti na ɔdi sika ugyiedi bumomo bɔdubɔbla aani edula ebi aƒo leevu unu.

english_verse: Two thousand four hundred and twenty-five kilograms of bronze were given.
translation_verse: Na abuala egyiedi akpala ani bákɔliku katɔ bébo kudu béte Unwoti mmɔ unu ɔdi edula ebi aƒo aavlanyɔ ku kakɛ unu.

english_verse: the stands for the posts that surrounded the courtyard, including those at the entrance to the courtyard, and the pegs for the tent and the courtyard.
translation_verse: ku kaduli kammɔ akpa ammɔ ku kana kaduli kammɔ kayakun ku ewele ani nda kevo ku kaduli kammɔ ámana ƒui. Ligyii lɛni nda ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo ku kama.

english_verse: Beautiful priestly clothes were made of blue, purple, and red wool for Aaron to wear when he performed his duties in the holy place. This was done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
translation_verse: Amu na béti linwo buluu ku ligyiedi lɛni náƒɔ kuye geen na bédi lɛwu lɛni mɔɔdia bɔnu béte bakpane bani ndubo kabla butaabla na Unwoti Adi Kevo kedee kammɔ kemmo. Na bédi ɔkpane awu sɛsɛɛ béte Aaron aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda.

english_verse: and on each of them was engraved the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Na adi atabi leevu-inyɔ ani lɛlɔ na bénweni Yakob bebi leevu-inyɔ bammɔ anyi básia unwi unwi. Na adi ekposela úte Israelƒuɔ kaba leevu-inyɔ bammɔ.

english_verse: The entire priestly vest was made of fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool. Thin sheets of gold were hammered out and cut into threads that were skillfully woven into the vest.
translation_verse: Sika ugyiedi na bétu bábla aani kɔbuli gyɛlɛɛ na bélii-nwu básala ku linwo buluu ku ligyiedi na bedine babuni geen bédi-nwu kaduɛ ku adi kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: Onyx stones were placed in gold settings, and each one was engraved with the name of one of Israel's sons.
translation_verse: Béti atabi anyɔ ani náƒɔ kuye na baalɔ-nya oniks na bénweni Israel bebi anyi básia-nya lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then these were attached to the shoulder straps of the vest, so the Lord would never forget his people. Everything was done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses. The Breastpiece (Exodus
translation_verse: Na báka-nwu bámana awu kedee ɔmmɔ amangba lɛlɔ aani likposela úte Israelƒuɔ aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda. Kayi Lɛbalala Lɛdiku

english_verse: The words “Dedicated to the Lord” were engraved on a narrow strip of pure gold,
translation_verse: Na béti sika ugyiedi na bábla kalɛkɛ blii kadi na bánwi-nwu kemmo na bénweni básia banii, Ɔmɛni Use Sɛsɛɛ Ute Unwoti.

english_verse: a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond were in the second row;
translation_verse: Na ɔgaala unyɔdi atabi adi torkis ku sapir ku smardo.

english_verse: a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst were in the third row;
translation_verse: Na ɔgaala ɔtɛdi atabi adi yiakint ku agate ku ametist.

english_verse: and a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper were in the fourth row. They were mounted in a delicate gold setting,
translation_verse: Na ɔgaala unedi atabi adi krisolit ku oniks ku yaspa. Na lɛni bámana atabi ammɔ na sika ugyiedi asɛɛ ebi eƒi kemmo.

english_verse: Two gold rings were attached to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fastened with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps.
translation_verse: Na sika ugyiedi kɔbuli kɔmmɔ eli anyɔ akladi ni, béti-nya bébo báda awu kedee ɔmmɔ amangba na sika asɛɛ ebi eƒi anyɔ ammɔ kemmo na anumi kakɛ.

english_verse: To keep the breastpiece in place, a blue cord was used to tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses. The Clothes for the Priests (Exodus
translation_verse: Bébo unwo buluu kadii kammɔ báda lɛdiku lɛmmɔ kɔkwɛnimii bábala bádanku awu kedee ɔmmɔ kɔkwɛnimii lɛlɔ. Na kadii kammɔ kasia awu ɔmmɔ kavobi lɛduni lɛni bédi bákya-ni bɔdia mmɔ lɛlɔ kalɛ na ɔda lɛdiku lɛmmɔ use nwuna keliekɔ. Báka Bakpane Bakladi Lɛwu

english_verse: which was fastened to Aaron's turban. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses. The Work Is Completed (Exodus
translation_verse: Na unwo buluu na bényimi bámana kabwa kammɔ anumi aani kalɛ kani na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda. Mose Úsie Útánu Kalɛ Bátu Unwoti Kevo Kammɔ

english_verse: When Moses saw that the people had done everything exactly as the Lord had commanded, he gave them his blessing.
translation_verse: Na ka Mose ɔ́sia ala ammɔ ƒui anu na ɔ́nu ka bábla-nya kalɛ kani na Unwoti úbo-nwu ɔda ni, úte Israelƒuɔ kusɛ kusɛ.

english_verse: with an opening in the center for the head. The material around the collar was bound so as to keep it from wearing out.
translation_verse: Na bédie liƒi kesii kani na lili lɛɛví na kɔdi kɔmmɔ ntɛntɛ na bédie liƒi lɛmmɔ békpo atu kalɛ na uleyile bɔbwɛ.

english_verse: Along the hem of the robe were woven pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a bell of pure gold between each of them. This robe was to be worn by Aaron when he performed his duties.
translation_verse: Na awu gyɔlɔɔ ɔni na baakya taabla lɛkpa mmɔ atu na lɛgba kada ni, béti unwo buluu ku ugyiedi ɔni náƒɔ kuye bédi egyiibi adi udu básia bámana na béti sika ugyiedi lɛdɔn wɛlɛ wɛlɛ báƒala-nwu ntɛ.

english_verse: Everything that Aaron and his sons wore was made of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, including their robes and turbans, their fancy caps and underwear, and even their sashes that were embroidered with needlework.
translation_verse: Na kavobi lɛduni lɛmmɔ ni, béti unwo buluu ku ugyiedi ɔni náƒɔ kuye bédi-nwu na bávili-nwu atu kaduɛ aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda.

english_verse: the sacred chest with its carrying poles and the place of mercy;
translation_verse: Na ɔ́nu Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ ku nwuna ligyii ku likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie libila lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: So the people of Israel finished making everything the Lord had told Moses to make.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Israelƒuɔ báwɔlɔ Unwoti Adi Kevo kani ndi Kevo Kasakɔ kammɔ bɔtu. Na bátu-nwu pɛpɛɛpɛ aani kalɛ kani na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda.

english_verse: Then they brought it all to Moses: the sacred tent and its equipment, including the hooks, the framework and crossbars, and its posts and stands;
translation_verse: Amu na béti Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ atula ammɔ ƒui bátátina Mose na ɔ́nu kalɛ bánwi kɔyakun ku ƒansili kugyikɛ ku lɛtagyii lɛmmɔ ku akpa ku ana kalɔ ɔka ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: the table with all that goes on it, including the sacred bread;
translation_verse: Na ɔ́nu ala kasiakɔ kammɔ ku nwuna lɛlɔ ala ku bodobodo ɔni muusé Unwoti anumi.

english_verse: the lampstand of pure gold, together with its equipment and oil;
translation_verse: Ɔ́nu sika ugyiedi asogya kasiakɔ ligyii ku lɛsogya lɛmmɔ otogyi ƒui ku nina lɛlɔ ala ku lɛsogya nnɔmii bɔmmɔ.

english_verse: the gold-covered incense altar; the ordination oil and the sweet-smelling incense; the curtain for the entrance to the tent;
translation_verse: Na ɔ́nu sika ugyiedi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ku likpose nnɔmii ku oloƒui ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ku kevo kammɔ kayakun aduni ammɔ.

english_verse: the bronze altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand;
translation_verse: Ɔ́nu abuala egyiedi lɛkpabi ku abuala egyiedi ntɔ kaƒɔkɔ kammɔ ku ana ligyii ku kabla ablala ku ɔdi lɛlɔ bɔƒɔ lɛkyami bonwu ku nina ɔka.

english_verse: the curtain with its posts and cords, and its pegs and stands that go around the courtyard; everything needed for the sacred tent;
translation_verse: Ɔ́nu Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kaduli aduni ku kana ligyii ku ɔka ɔni lɛlɔ na liinye ku kaduli kayakun lɛduni ku kana lɛbuli ku ewele ku Unwoti Adi Kevo kani ndi Kevo Kasakɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ala ƒui.

english_verse: and the finely woven priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́nu Aaron lɛwu sɛsɛɛ lɛni bédi ku nwuna bebi lɛwu lɛni na badubo butaakya taabla bakpane kabla.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: Set up my tent on the first day of the year
translation_verse: “Lɛ Adi Kevo kani ndi Kevo Kasakɔ kammɔ na kɔbuli kudeedi kuna limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and put the chest with the Ten Commandments behind the inside curtain.
translation_verse: Na eti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ alɛ-nwu kemmo na eti kakpakɔ bule kɔdi kɔni mɔɔbala adaka ɔmmɔ anumi aƒala.

english_verse: Bring in the table and set on it those things that are made for it. Also bring in the lampstand and attach the lamps to it.
translation_verse: Na alɛ ala kasiakɔ kammɔ na eti ala ani na ɔlɛka beti basia-nwu lɛlɔ asia. Na eti asogya kasiakɔ ugyii ɔmmɔ alɛ na eti lɛsogya lɛmmɔ ƒui asia-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then place the gold altar of incense in front of the sacred chest and hang a curtain at the entrance to the tent.
translation_verse: Na eti oloƒui bɔkyula sika ugyiedi lɛbi lɛmmɔ alɛ Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ anumi na eti kɔdi aƒala kevo kammɔ kayakun.

english_verse: Set the altar for burning sacrifices in front of the entrance to my tent.
translation_verse: “Na eti lɛkpabi lɛni lɛlɔ badubo butaakyula akpala alɛ Unwoti Adi Kevo kani ndi Kevo Kasakɔ ɔmmɔ kayakun.

english_verse: Put the large bronze bowl between the tent and the altar and fill the bowl with water.
translation_verse: Na eti lɛkyami lɛni kemmo badubo enu butaaƒɔ alɛ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ntɛ na edu ntu eyile-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: Surround the tent and the altar with the wall of curtains and hang the curtain that was made for the entrance.
translation_verse: Na alɛ kevo kaduli kammɔ ɔban eku amana na eti kayakun kɔdi aƒala kayakun kammɔ.

english_verse: Use the sacred olive oil to dedicate to me the tent and everything in it.
translation_verse: “Si áwɔlɔ ala ammɔ ƒui bɔbla ni, na eti nnɔmii kedee na akuna ewi kevo kammɔ ku ala ani ƒui nkya-ka kemmo na abla-nya sɛsɛɛ na adubuse kedee.

english_verse: Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent and tell them to wash themselves.
translation_verse: “Na akpanku Aaron ku nwuna bebi bananabi eboku kevo kammɔ kenye na akpila-ma ntu.

english_verse: Dress Aaron in the priestly clothes, then use the sacred olive oil to ordain him and dedicate him to me as my priest.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama na eti ɔkpane awu kedee ɔmmɔ akya Aaron na awɛɛ-nwu nnɔmii kedee bɔmmɔ ese-nwu likpo. Kalɛ wakana na wabla ɔkpane wete-mi.

english_verse: Put the priestly robes on Aaron's sons
translation_verse: Na akpanku Aaron bebi lɛnɔ eboku na akya-ma bana lɛwu lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: Moses followed the Lord's instructions.
translation_verse: Na Mose ɔ́bla ɔsiaku kalɛ kani na Unwoti úbo-nwu ɔda.

english_verse: And on the first day of the first month of the second year, the sacred tent was set up.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bálɛ kevo kammɔ na lɛkwa linyɔdi kɔbuli kudeedi limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ka bálɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The stones with the Ten Commandments written on them were stored in the sacred chest, the place of mercy was put on top of it, and the carrying poles were attached.
translation_verse: Na uti atabi anyɔ ani na ɔda bubo etemila ásia-nwu lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔ́kya Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na úti ligyii ɔ́kya eƒi ammɔ kemmo ɔ́danku adaka ɔmmɔ atu. Na úti likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie libila úbi adaka ɔmmɔ katɔ.

english_verse: The chest was brought into the tent and set behind the curtain in the most holy place. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́ya na béti adaka ɔmmɔ bése Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo na béti kakpakɔ bule kɔdi báƒala. Na ɔ́bɛla Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo-nwu ɔda.

english_verse: The table for the sacred bread was put along the north wall of the holy place,
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́ya na béti ala kasiakɔ kammɔ béduoku ɔtɔ kemmo bétése kasakɔ kevo kani ndi Unwoti Adi Kevo mmɔ kemmo na katɔ kakɛ na kakpakɔ bule kɔdi kɔmmɔ anumi kakɛ.

english_verse: after which the bread was set on the table.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́tɛ Unwoti Bodobodo ɔmmɔ ɔ́sia-nwu lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo-nwu ɔda.

english_verse: then the lamps were attached to it there in the presence of the Lord.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́tu lɛsogya lɛmmɔ ɔ́sia nina kalɛkɔ mmɔ na Unwoti anumi aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo-nwu ɔda.

english_verse: The gold incense altar was set up in front of the curtain,
translation_verse: Na úti sika ugyiedi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔ́lɛ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo na kesii kani kakpakɔ bule kɔdi kɔmmɔ kɔ́ƒa anumi kakɛ.

english_verse: and sweet-smelling incense was burned on it. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́kyula oloƒui ƒɛƒɛɛ aani kalɛ kani na Unwoti úbo-nwu ɔda.

english_verse: The curtain was hung at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na úti kɔdi ɔ́ƒala kevo kammɔ kayakun.

english_verse: Then the altar for offering sacrifices was put in front of the tent, and animal sacrifices and gifts of grain were offered there.
translation_verse: Na úti bɔkyula lɛkpabi ɔ́lɛ úde Unwoti Adi Kevo kani ndi Kevo Kasakɔ mmɔ kayakun na ɔ́kyula akpala na béti edula etela lɛnɔ béboku Unwoti na mmɔ aani kalɛ kani na Unwoti úbo-nwu ɔda.

english_verse: The large bronze bowl was placed between the altar and the entrance to the tent. It was filled with water,
translation_verse: Na úti lɛkyami lɛni kemmo badubo enu butaaƒɔ mmɔ ɔ́lɛ Kevo Kasakɔ ku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ntɛ na ɔ́ya na bédu ntu béwi-ni kemmo kalɛ na bataaƒɔ enu.

english_verse: then Moses and Aaron, together with Aaron's sons, washed their hands and feet.
translation_verse: Na lɛkyami lɛmmɔ kemmo na Mose ku Aaron ku Aaron bebi baaƒɔ enu ku lɛgba.

english_verse: In fact, they washed each time before entering the tent or offering sacrifices at the altar. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
translation_verse: Na uwi biala na badubuduo Kevo Kasakɔ mmɔ ku si báni beedé lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ni, baaƒɔ bana enu ku lɛgba aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda.

english_verse: Suddenly the sacred tent was covered by a thick cloud and filled with the glory of the Lord.
translation_verse: Amu na liƒlukutu lɛdi líbebi Kevo Kasakɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ na Unwoti bukeye bɔ́ƒɔ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: Whenever the cloud moved from the tent, the people would break camp and follow;
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ ulu buse biala kemmo ni, si bánya bánu ka liƒlukutu lɛmmɔ lɛ́ta Adi Kevo kammɔ eli ni, na ɔlɛka ama lɛnɔ basiaku-nwu.

english_verse: then they would set up camp and stay there, until it moved again.
translation_verse: Nsu si liƒlukutu lɛmmɔ lítata tɔ ni, ama lɛnɔ balata tɔ wetédu limeyi lɛni na liƒlukutu lɛmmɔ lɛ́ta.

english_verse: No matter where the people traveled, the Lord was with them. Each day his cloud was over the tent, and each night a fire could be seen in the cloud.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na Israelƒuɔ ulu busie kemmo ƒui ni, Unwoti liƒlukutu lɛmmɔ liibi Adi Kevo kammɔ lɛlɔ na kadi nwaa. Na usien lɛnɔ liinwíni aani lɛgyavonku lɛkpa taatɔnku-ma.

english_verse: Lay your hand on its head, and I will accept the animal as a sacrifice for taking away your sins.
translation_verse: Ɔdi ka ukyuli ɔmmɔ uti kɔnu ɔsia ebuo ɔmmɔ lili, na ɔtina ka ebuo ɔmmɔ na úti uunyene nwuna lɛlɔ kenye kalɛ na lɛƒɔ nwuna akpala bɔkyula ƒui bɔmmɔ na lidie kɔtu bɔni biala na nwuna lɛlɔ.

english_verse: After the bull is killed in my presence, some priests from Aaron's family will offer its blood to me by splattering it against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔdubɔdu ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔgyani ɔmmɔ na Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kayakun kenye. Na Aaron bebi bananabi bani ndi bakpane mmɔ ndubɔkɔliku ubugya ɔmmɔ katɔ batina-mi asa na bakuna-nwu bewi lɛkpabi lɛni nnye Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kayakun kenye mmɔ lɛlɔ bamana.

english_verse: while the priests pile wood on the altar fire to make it start blazing.
translation_verse: Aaron bebi bakpane bammɔ badubo ogya bɔsala na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na bala ekyweni basia-nwu lɛlɔ kaduɛ.

english_verse: Wash the bull's insides and hind legs, so the priests can lay them on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. A priest will then send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti kaƒɔ ala ammɔ ku agyobi ɔkya ntu kemmo na ɔƒɔ kaduɛ na beti basia ogya ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na akywi. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla ogya akpala bɔkyula ƒui ute-mi na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ.

english_verse: Lead the animal to the north side of the altar, where it is to be killed in my presence. Then some of the priests will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Na badubɔdu ebuo ɔmmɔ na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ katɔ kakɛ na Unwoti anumi. Na Aaron bebi, bakpane bammɔ badubuti ubugya ɔmmɔ na bakuna bewi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ bamana.

english_verse: Cut up the animal and wash its insides and hind legs. A priest will put these parts on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. Then he will send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Na agyobi ku kaƒɔ ala ammɔ ni, ɔdubuti-nya ɔkya ntu kemmo na ɔƒɔ kaduɛ. Na bakpane bammɔ beti ana ƒui basia ogya na akywi. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla ogya akpala bɔkyula ƒui ute-mi na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ.

english_verse: If you offer a bird for this kind of sacrifice, it must be a dove or a pigeon.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na si baasɛ na ɔdi úti ubabla bɔkyula ɔdi ɔmmɔ ni, na ɔdi ka ɔƒuna-ma na babloduma iye bamangbɛ akɔ.

english_verse: A priest will take the bird to the bronze altar, where he will wring its neck and put its head on the fire. Then he will drain out its blood on one side of the altar,
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti-nwu uboku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ, na ulii-nwu limɔ ukulo na uti lili lɛmmɔ ɔkya ogya ɔkyula na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ, na ɔya na lɛna lɛkladi ubugya ɔ́yu uwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ amadɔ.

english_verse: remove the bird's craw with what is in it, and throw them on the ash heap at the east side of the altar.
translation_verse: Na udie ala ani nkya nwuna lɛkoolobi koƒo na ɔgya-nwu uwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ kesii kani na beedie ogya ntɔ bɔmmɔ teewi.

english_verse: Finally, he will take the bird by its wings, tear it partially open, and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Na ɔda-nwu avwi na ɔni-nwu kemmo ɔbwɛ, nsu utamamiku lɛlɔ, na uti-nwu ɔsia ogya ku ekyweni ammɔ lɛlɔ na ɔkywi. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla ogya akpala bɔkyula ƒui ute-mi na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ.’

english_verse: When you offer sacrifices to give thanks to me, you must use only your finest flour. Put it in a dish, sprinkle olive oil and incense on the flour,
translation_verse: “ ‘Si ukyuli ɔdi úti edula ebi úboku ɔnii ubabla akpala ni, ɔlɛ ka ɔkɔ ala ammɔ ɔbla ɔlaaƒɔ sɛɛn. Na ɔdi ka uti nnɔ uwi-nwu lili na uti oloƒui ɔsia-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and take it to the priests from Aaron's family. One of them will scoop up the incense together with a handful of the flour and oil. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay this part on the bronze altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama na uti ala ammɔ uboku Aaron bebi bananabi bakpane bammɔ na badubudie ɔlaaƒɔ ɔmmɔ lɛkɔkɔ linwi ku nwuna lɛlɔ nnɔ ku oloƒui ɔmmɔ ƒui. Na badubuti bakyula lɛkpabi lɛlɔ aani enyimo adila bɔsia akpala. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla akpala bɔkyula ƒui ute-mi na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ.

english_verse: The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
translation_verse: Na ɔlaaƒɔ ɔkladi ɔni mebu ɔdi Aaron ku nwuna bebi bananabi ɔdi. Na ɔdi lɛla lɛni na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ na akpala ani na bábla béte-mi kemmo.

english_verse: If you bake bread in an oven for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour, but without any yeast. You may make the flour into a loaf mixed with olive oil, or you may make it into thin wafers and brush them with oil.
translation_verse: “ ‘Si ukyuli ɔdi úti edula ebi etela ani na béƒi bodobodo lɛyu kemmo ɔduboku-mi ni, ɔlɛka ɔnu ka ɔdi ɔlaaƒɔ sɛɛn ɔni na bɔnyii bɔdi buuubo-nwu kemmo. Na uti nnɔ ɔsala-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: If you cook bread in a shallow pan for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour. Mix it with olive oil, but do not use any yeast.
translation_verse: Na si lɛbuala kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ na ɔ́bla lɛla lɛni na úti ɔdubo ubete-mi mmɔ ni, ɔnu ka ɔdi ɔlaaƒɔ sɛɛn ɔni na bɔnyii buuubo-nwu kemmo na ɔ́sala-nwu ku nnɔ.

english_verse: Then break the bread into small pieces and sprinkle them with oil.
translation_verse: Na ɔbwɛ-nwu kɔkɛ kɔkɛ na uwi nnɔ. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdi edula etela akpala.

english_verse: If you cook your bread in a pan with a lid on it, you must also use the finest flour mixed with oil.
translation_verse: Na si etela ani na úti ɔduboku mmɔ adi lɛla lɛni na bánwa na lɛbuala libui lɛkya kemmo ni, ɔnu ka ɔlaaƒɔ ɔmmɔ use sɛɛn na ɔ́sala-nwu ku nnɔ.

english_verse: You may prepare sacrifices to give thanks in any of these three ways. Bring your sacrifice to a priest, and he will take it to the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Ala ani na lɛ́ka mɛni si ana ɔdi biala na éti edula ebi ábla na éti aduboku-mi ni, na eti ete ɔkpane na anwu ɔdubuti usienku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay part of it on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubudie lɛkpabi lɛlɔ enyimo adila ani na ɔdubuti ɔkyula ute-mi na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔdubɔbla akpala bɔkyula ƒui ute-mi na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ.

english_verse: The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
translation_verse: Na ɔkladi ɔni mebu ɔdi Aaron ku bebi bananabi ɔdi aani bana kadikɔ kani bédie bése sɛsɛɛ ɔ́siku akpala ani na béboku-mi kemmo.

english_verse: Yeast and honey must never be burned on the altar, so don't ever mix either of these in a grain sacrifice.
translation_verse: “ ‘Edula ebi etela biala na ɔdi éti aduboku-mi ni, nu ka bɔnyii bɔdi buuubo-nwu kemmo. Ɔsika lɛla lɛni kemmo na bɔnyii bɔkya iye uwɔ ni, utalɛka beti-nwu babla ogya akpala bɔkyula ƒui bete-mi.

english_verse: You may offer either of them separately, when you present the first part of your harvest to me, but they must never be burned on the altar.
translation_verse: Bakana beti ala ammɔ basala ku kemo edula awɔdi ani báka bɔƒɛ beboku-mi aani etela, nsu balakyula-nya aani ogya akpala bɔkyula ƒui na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ.

english_verse: Freshly cut grain, either roasted or coarsely ground, must be used when you offer the first part of your grain harvest.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɔƒɛni lɛnɔ si bíti edula ebi udu biala ani náka bugyie bɛdububoku-mi ni, bɛƒɛ edula aboyo awɔdi ammɔ na biƒi-nwu ɔgya kemmo na bikuo-nwu na ɔbwɛ na biti bibunku bina edula awɔdi bɔƒɛ etela ammɔ.

english_verse: You must mix in some olive oil and put incense on top, because this is a grain sacrifice.
translation_verse: Na biti nnɔ bibunku na biti oloƒui bɛsia. Na ndubɔƒɔ-nwu lite-mii aani edula ebi akpala.

english_verse: A priest will sprinkle all of the incense and some of the grain and oil on the altar and send them up in smoke to show that the whole offering belongs to me.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔkpane ɔdubudie edula ebi aboyo ani na bíƒi na bíkuo-nya bɛ́bwɛ mmɔ enyimo adila ku nwuna lɛlɔ nnɔ ku oloƒui ɔmmɔ ƒui na uti ɔkyula aani akpala bɔkyula ƒui ute-mi.’

english_verse: When you offer sacrifices to ask my blessing, you may offer either a bull or a cow, but there must be nothing wrong with the animal.
translation_verse: “ ‘Si ɔdi úti ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔgyani iye uledi úboku ka ubabla unwi bɔbla akpala ni, ɔlɛ ka ɔƒuna ebuo ɔni nse sɛɛn na útasɔ kesii kadi uboku ami Unwoti anumi.

english_verse: Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay your hand on its head, and have it killed there. A priest from Aaron's family will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Na uti nwuna enu ɔsia ebuo ɔmmɔ lili uti ɔtina ka ɔmmɔ na úti únyene nwuna lɛlɔ kenye. Ɔmmɔ kama na badu ebuo ɔmmɔ na Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kenye. Na Aaron bebi bananabi bakpane bammɔ beti ubugya ɔmmɔ bakuna bewi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ bamana.

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ ubunku akabi ammɔ ku lɛmwi lɛni mma-nwu lɛlɔ ku kasɔma lɛmwi ku akɔ ammɔ kenye kakɛ.

english_verse: Some of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me, together with the sacrifice that is offered to please me.
translation_verse: Na Aaron bebi bananabi bammɔ badubuti basia ekyweni ani mɔɔda mmɔ lɛlɔ na ɔkywi. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla ogya akpala bɔkyula ƒui ute-mi na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ.

english_verse: Instead of a bull or a cow, you may offer any sheep or goat that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: “ ‘Nsu si bese ku baƒonu na ɔdanku úboku ka ubabla unwi bɔbla akpala ɔdi ɔmmɔ ute-mi ni, ɔkana uboku ebuo ɔgyani iye uledi. Nsu ɔnu ka use sɛɛn na útasɔ kesii kadi.

english_verse: If you offer a sheep, you must present it to me at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na si koƒonu ubi na ɔda ɔnii uuti uboku aani nwuna akpala ni, ɔlɛka uti uboku mina anumi.

english_verse: Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Na ɔdubuti enu ɔsia-ku lili na ɔmmɔ kama na ɔdu-nwu na Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kenye. Na Aaron bebi bananabi bammɔ badubuti ubugya ɔmmɔ bakuna bewi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ bamana.

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: Na udie akabi anyɔ ammɔ ku lɛmwi lɛni mma-nwu lɛlɔ ku kasɔma lɛmwi ku akɔ ammɔ kawɔlɔkɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering for me.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔdubuti ala amɛni kakɛ kadi ɔkyula na lɛkpabi lɛlɔ. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla ogya akpala bɔkyula ute-mi na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ aani kalɛ na lɛdila liimó ukyuli.

english_verse: If you offer a goat, you must also present it to me
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɔƒɛni si ese na ɔdanku úboku ubabla akpala ammɔ ni, ɔlɛka uti uboku Unwoti anumi.

english_verse: at the entrance to the sacred tent. Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Na ɔdubuti enu ɔsia-nwu lili. Na nwuna kama na ɔdu-nwu na Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ anumi, na Aaron bebi bananabi bammɔ bakuna ubugya ɔmmɔ bewi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ bamana.

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: na ɔdubudie akabi anyɔ ammɔ ku lɛmwi lɛni mma-nwu lɛlɔ ku kasɔma lɛmwi ku akɔ ammɔ kawɔlɔkɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: One of the priests will put these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering with a smell that pleases me. All fat belongs to me.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔdubuti ala amɛni kakɛ ɔkyula na lɛkpabi lɛlɔ. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla ogya akpala bɔkyula ute-mi na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ aani kalɛ lɛdila liimó ukyuli. Unwoti mbo lɛmwi biala.

english_verse: So you and your descendants must never eat any fat or any blood, not even in the privacy of your own homes. This law will never change.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na ɔmɛni ɔdi ɔda ɔni na muubó-mii úti úsela bina kaba kaba kemmo bawɔ ƒui akɔ. Na kesii biala bɛdubulie ƒui ni, bitadi lɛmwi lɛdi biala iye ubugya biala.’ ”

english_verse: dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain.
translation_verse: Na ɔkya ubugya ɔmmɔ lɛnimi ɔkuna uwi Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kakpakɔ bule kɔdi kɔmmɔ anumi maatɛ.

english_verse: This is a sacrifice for sin. So he will lay his hand on the animal's head, before having it killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti enu ɔsia ketukpa kammɔ lili uti ɔtina ka aka na úti uunyene lɛlɔ kenye. Ɔmmɔ kama na ɔdu-ka na kesii kani na baadú bebuo taakyula teete-mi mmɔ. Na ndubɔƒɔ lite-nwu aani likpidi lili buvele akpala.

english_verse: Then a priest will dip a finger in the blood; he will smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti lɛnimi ɔkya ubugya ɔmmɔ kemmo na uti ususu ese ani nlɛ bɔkyula lɛkpabi lɛlɔ mmɔ na uti ubugya ɔkladi uwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kalɔ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: Offer a sacrifice to ask forgiveness when you sin by accidentally doing something I have told you not to do. When the High Priest Sins The Lord said:
translation_verse: “Tásu Israel kadi bekyuli ƒui anini, ‘Ɔƒɛni kalɛ ɔdi ɔdubɔƒiɔ na tati tati ɔsu na ɔbla ala ani lɛlɔ na líbo-mii ɔda ɔdi.

english_verse: When the high priest sins, he makes everyone else guilty too. And so, he must sacrifice a young bull that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: “ ‘Si ɔkpane ɔni na bése-nwu likpo na ɔdi na úti bɔƒiɔ úboku bekyuli ƒui lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka uti ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔgyani ubete Unwoti. Na ɔlɛka ɔnu ka akɔ ɔmmɔ use sɛɛn na útasɔ kesii kadi asa beti babla likpidi butitaakyiɛ akpala ammɔ na likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla ɔsu.

english_verse: The priest will lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay his hand on its head, and kill it there.
translation_verse: Ɔdubuti ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔgyani ɔmmɔ uboku Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kayakun na Unwoti anumi. Na uti enu ɔsia akɔ ɔmmɔ lili uti ɔtina ka ɔmmɔ na úti unyene nwuna likpidi kenye Na ɔmmɔ kama na badu akɔ ɔmmɔ na Unwoti anumi.

english_verse: He will take a bowl of the blood inside the tent,
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɔƒɛni ɔkpane unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti akɔ ɔmmɔ ubugya ɔdi na uti uboku Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Then, in my presence, he will smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
translation_verse: Na uti ubugya ɔmmɔ ɔdi ususu ebuo ese ani nlɛ oloƒui lɛkpabi lɛni nnye Unwoti anumi na Unwoti Adi Kevo kemmo mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na akɔ ɔmmɔ ubugya ɔkladi ƒui ni, ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti uwi lɛkpabi lɛni nnye Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kayakun kenye mmɔ kalɔ.

english_verse: The priest will remove the fat from the bull, just as he does when he sacrifices a bull to ask my blessing. This includes the fat on the insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. He will then send it all up in smoke.
translation_verse: Na ɔmɛni útavumanaku ekpo ani na beedie na ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔgyani iye uledi lɛlɔ si baabla unwi bɔbla akpala. Na ala amɛni na ɔdi ka ɔkpane uti ɔbla ogya akpala bɔkyula ƒui ute-mi na bɔkyula lɛkpabi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The skin and flesh of the bull, together with its legs, insides, and the food still in its stomach, are to be taken outside the camp and burned on a wood fire near the ash heap. When the Whole Nation Sins The Lord said:
translation_verse: Na ala ani ƒui nébu ni, ɔlɛka balɛku-nya bana keliekɔ mmɔ besienku kama ƒui na kesii kani na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ beewi ala ani na bákyula mmɔ ntɔ. Na mmɔ na badubo ogya ɔbambadi bɔsala na bakyula ala ammɔ ƒui na kesii kani na ntɔ bɔmmɔ buwi mmɔ.

english_verse: When the nation of Israel disobeys me without meaning to, the whole nation is still guilty.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na si ɔƒɛni kalɛ kadi kammɔ ƒui naaagyi asa na bábla lɛla lɛdi na báta bénye Unwoti ɔda bubo bɔdi lɛlɔ ni, ɔdi-ma bɔƒiɔ ina ka bátati asa na bábla-ni.

english_verse: Once you realize what has happened, you must sacrifice a young bull to ask my forgiveness. Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent,
translation_verse: Si bábanu likpidi lɛmmɔ báti ni, na ɔlɛka kadi kammɔ ƒui beti ɔmantɛ akɔ beboku na bababla likpidi butitaakyiɛ akpala. Na ɔdi ka beti-nwu beboku Unwoti Adi Kevo anumi.

english_verse: where your tribal leaders will lay their hands on its head, before having it killed in my presence.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na kadi benengu bammɔ ƒui badubuti bana enu basia akɔ ɔmmɔ lili na Unwoti anumi. Na beti batina ka ɔmmɔ na béti beenyene bana kenye. Ɔmmɔ kama na badu-nwu na Unwoti anumi mmɔ.

english_verse: The priest will take a bowl of the animal's blood inside the sacred tent,
translation_verse: “ ‘Na ɔdi ka ɔkpane unengudi ɔmmɔ uti akɔ ɔmmɔ ubugya ɔdi uboku Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain.
translation_verse: Na uti nwuna lɛnimi ɔkya na ɔkuna uwi kakpakɔ bule kɔdi kɔni nƒa mmɔ kenye na Unwoti anumi maatɛ.

english_verse: Then, in my presence, he must smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
translation_verse: Ɔdubuti ubugya ɔmmɔ ɔdi ususu ese ani nlɛ lɛkpabi lɛni nnye Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo lɛlɔ na Unwoti anumi. Na uti ubugya ɔkladi uwi lɛkpabi lɛni lɛlɔ na baakyula akpala mmɔ lɛlɔ na linye Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kayakun kenye.

english_verse: Any tribal leader who disobeys me without knowing it is still guilty.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na si ɔtɔnkune ɔdi nábla likpidi lɛdi na ɔ́ƒiɔ Unwoti nwuna Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔdi ina útati ni, ɔ́ƒiɔ.

english_verse: As soon as the leader realizes what has happened, he must sacrifice a goat that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: Na si kama na báya na ɔ́ti likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla ni, ɔlɛka uti ketukpa kani nse sɛɛn na kátasɔ uboku aani nwuna akpala etela.

english_verse: The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti lɛnimi ɔ́kya ebuo ɔni na úti úboku ka ubabla likpidi lili buvele akpala mmɔ ubugya kemmo na uti ususu ese ani nlɛ lɛkpabi lɛni lɛlɔ na baakyula bebuo mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na ubugya ɔkladi ni, ɔdubuti uwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kalɔ.

english_verse: Then he must send all of the fat up in smoke, just as he does when a sacrifice is offered to ask my blessing. By this sacrifice the leader's sin will be forgiven. When Ordinary People Sin The Lord said:
translation_verse: Na ebuo ɔmmɔ lɛmwi ƒui ni, ɔdubuti-ni ɔkyula na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ aani kalɛ baakyula unwi bɔbla lɛmwi. Ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔsia na ɔbla likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie akpala na lidie likpidi kɔtu bɔni biala na ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na liti-nya lɛkyiɛ-nwu.

english_verse: When any of you ordinary people disobey me without meaning to, you are still guilty.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɔƒɛni si Israel kadi akɔ ukyuli ɔdi nátati asa na ɔ́bla lɛla lɛdi ɔ́ƒiɔ Unwoti ɔda bubo bɔdi ni, ɔ́ƒiɔ na ɔmmɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: As soon as you realize what you have done, you must sacrifice a female goat that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: Na si ɔdi údie nwuna likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla mmɔ ɔ́tina-nwu ni, na ɔlɛka uti ese uledi ɔni nse sɛɛn na útasɔ uboku na likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla lili.

english_verse: Lead the goat to the north side of the bronze altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed.
translation_verse: Ɔdubuti enu ɔsia ebuo ɔni na úti úbo ubete mmɔ lili. Ɔmmɔ kama na badu ebuo ɔmmɔ na kesii kani na badubo akpala bɔkyula ɔdi ɔmmɔ bɔbla.

english_verse: After this, the priest will remove all of the fat, just as he does when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. The priest will then send the fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. This animal is sacrificed so that I will forgive you ordinary people when you sin.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, ɔdubudie ebuo ɔmmɔ lɛmwi ƒui aani kalɛ na bédie unwi bɔbla akpala ebuo ɔmmɔ lɛmwi. Na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti ɔkyula. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla ogya akpala bɔkyula ƒui ute-mi na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ. Ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na ɔkpane ɔdubɔsia na ɔbla akpala na udie likpidi kɔtu bɔni na ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: If you offer a lamb instead of a goat as a sacrifice for sin, it must be a female that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: “ ‘Nsu si koƒonu ubi na úti úboku ubabla likpidi lili buvele akpala ammɔ ni, ɔlɛka uboku koƒonu kuledi kɔni nse sɛɛn na kútasɔ kesii kadi.

english_verse: Lead the lamb to the altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed.
translation_verse: Ɔdubuti enu ɔsia likpidi bɔkyiɛ ebuo ɔmmɔ lili, na badu-ku na ɔmmɔ kama na beti babla likpidi bɔkyiɛ ɔdi ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti lɛnimi ɔkya ubugya ɔmmɔ kemmo na uti ususu ese ani nlɛ lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na uti ubugya ɔkladi ɔmmɔ ƒui uwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kalɔ.

english_verse: After this, all of the fat must be removed, just as when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. Then the priest will send it up in smoke to me, together with a food offering, and your sin will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama badubudie lɛmwi lɛmmɔ ƒui aani kalɛ na beedie koƒonu ubi ɔni na béti bábabla unwi bɔbla akpala kalɛ. Na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti ɔbla akpala bɔkyula na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla ogya akpala bɔkyula ƒui ute-mi na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ. Ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔsia na ɔbla akpala na udie kɔtu bɔni na ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.’ ”

english_verse: You are guilty and unfit to worship me, if you accidentally touch the dead body of any kind of unclean animal.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na si ɔdi útuku lɛla lɛni muusé lɛlɔ aani ebuo ukpine iye ebuo ɔni na muusé lɛlɔ iye bebweyi bani mɔɔví kalɔ, ina útati ni, ukyuli ɔmmɔ únwini ukyuli ɔni muusé lɛlɔ na ɔ́ƒiɔ.

english_verse: You are guilty if you find out that you have accidentally touched anything unclean that comes from a human body.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na si ukyuli lɛlɔ lɛla lɛdi na útuku na liisé lɛlɔ ni, ina útati na úbati kama ni, ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ únwini lɛla lɛni muusé lɛlɔ na ɔ́ƒiɔ.

english_verse: You are guilty the moment you realize that you have made a hasty promise to do something good or bad.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na si ɔdi útewi lɛlɔ útabla kasusu na ɔ́kpali-mi lɛnyi úse kenye kalɛ kalɛ ka ɔdubɔbla lɛla lɛdi, lɛdia o-o lɛɛɛdia o-o, na údie lɛlɔ atu na útabla útasia na úbati kama kama ni, ɔ́ƒiɔ.

english_verse: As soon as you discover that you have committed any of these sins, you must confess what you have done.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na si ɔdi ɔ́nu ka ɔ́bla likpidi ɔ́ƒiɔ na ala ani ƒui na lɛ́ka lɛ́vi mɛni ɔdi lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka udie lɛla lɛni na ɔbla kalɔ ɔsu nwaa na kadi anumi.

english_verse: Then you must bring a female sheep or goat to me as the price for your sin. A priest will sacrifice the animal, and you will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama na uti nwuna likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie akpala uboku Unwoti anumi na likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla ɔsu. Ɔlɛka uboku koƒonu iye ese uledi ɔsiku nwuna bebuo akɔ ute akpala ammɔ. Na ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na ɔkpane ɔdubɔsia na ɔbla akpala na udie kɔtu bɔni na ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Give both birds to the priest, who will offer one as a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness. He will wring its neck without tearing off its head,
translation_verse: Ɔdubuti ala amɛni uboku ɔkpane. Na ɔni na badubuti babla likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie akpala ni, ɔdubulii-nwu limɔ ɔƒɛ, nsu utekulo-nwu utedie ƒui.

english_verse: splatter some of its blood on one side of the bronze altar, and drain out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Na ɔdubɔkuna nwuna ubugya ɔmmɔ uwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kɔmadɔ. Na ɔya na ubugya ɔkladi ɔkpala uwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kalɔ. Na ndubɔƒɔ lite-nwu aani likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie akpala.

english_verse: If you are so poor that you cannot afford doves or pigeons, you may bring one kilogram of your finest flour. This is a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness, so don't sprinkle olive oil or sweet-smelling incense on it.
translation_verse: “ ‘Nsu si uuubo babloduma inyɔ iye bamangbɛ inyɔ ni, na uti ɔlaaƒɔ ɔni muukeye lɛɛƒɛɛ inyɔ ubabla likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie akpala ammɔ. Na uteti nnɔ iye oloƒui utasia, ɔsika likpidi bɔkyiɛ etela na adi.

english_verse: Give the flour to a priest, who will scoop up a handful and send it up in smoke together with the other offerings. This is a reminder that all of the flour belongs to me.
translation_verse: Ɔdubuti ala ammɔ uboku ɔkpane, na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔma ɔlaaƒɔ ɔmmɔ lɛkɔkɔ linwi buyi aani enyimo adila na uti ɔkyula ubunku akpala bɔkyula ƒui adi na lɛkpabi lɛlɔ na ɔdi likpidi lili buvele akpala.

english_verse: By offering this sacrifice, the priest pays the price for any of these sins you may have committed. The priest gets to keep the rest of the flour, just as he does with grain sacrifices. Sacrifices To Make Things Right (Leviticus
translation_verse: Ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na ɔkpane ɔdubɔsia na ɔbla akpala na udie kɔtu bɔni na ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔlaaƒɔ ɔkladi ɔni mebu ɔdubunwini ɔkpane ɔmmɔ kadikɔ aani kalɛ na baabla edula akpala.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses what the people must do to make things right when they find out they have cheated the Lord without meaning to: If this happens, you must either sacrifice a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay the price of a ram with the official money used by the priests.
translation_verse: “Si ɔƒɛni kalɛ ukyuli ɔdi útadi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ ɔkɛnku ala ani na lɛ́lɛ ugyii líse ka ute-mi ka ese-mi sɛsɛɛ kedee ɔsu ni, ɔ́bla likpidi si ina útati na úbati kama. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔlɛka uti kɔtɔ bukpi akpala uboku Unwoti ani ndi koƒonu kɔgyani kɔni nse sɛɛn na kútasɔ kesii kadi ɔsiku nwuna baƒonu akɔ. Na ɔlɛka kuna kuye kudu sika ɔƒualadi ɔni na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔ́su kenye. Ɔmmɔ na ɔdubuti ɔbla kɔtɔ bukpi akpala ammɔ.

english_verse: The next morning you will dress in your priestly clothes, including your linen underwear. Then clean away the ashes left by the sacrifices and pile them beside the altar.
translation_verse: Ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔka lɛwuku bɔkya use kalɔ asa na ɔkya awu kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ bonwu gyɔlɔɔ ɔsia-nwu katɔ. Na udie ntɔ bɔni na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kalɔ ɔni na ogya ɔmmɔ ɔ́kyula akpala ammɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ uboku asi ammɔ kɔmadɔ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses what the people must do when they commit other sins against the Lord: You have sinned if you rob or cheat someone, if you keep back money or valuables left in your care, or if you find something and claim not to have it.
translation_verse: iye ɔ́kɛ ukyuli ɔdi lɛla lɛdi, nsu útaƒɔ enu ka béye-nwu, mmomu ɔ́nyi ɔkɔ ɔ́kpali ala ka útanu lɛla lɛmmɔ. Ukyuli ɔni nábla ala amɛni ɔdi ɔ́bla likpidi.

english_verse: and told him what sacrifices the priests must offer on the morning and evening of the day they are ordained: It is the same as the regular morning and evening sacrifices—half a kilogram of flour
translation_verse: “Akpala ani ndubo-ɔ bɔtina mɛni ndi akpala ani na Aaron ku nwuna bebi bananabi badubuti beboku-mi na limeyi lɛni lɛlɔ na badubuwi bana ɔdi nnɔmii lili na bese-nwu likpo. Ɔlaaƒɔ sɛɛn ɔni mabla aani antabi lɛkyami linwi na badubuti beboku aani limeyi ndi limeyi etela ani beele kakɛ ɔtanta ku kakɛ useyi uwi.

english_verse: This sacrifice is very holy, and only the priests may have any part of it.
translation_verse: Ɔnanabi biala na bakpane bammɔ akɔ ɔkana na ɔkun lɛna lɛmmɔ ƒaa, ɔsika lise kedee ƒui.

english_verse: If the meat was cooked in a clay pot, the pot must be destroyed, but if it was cooked in a bronze pot, the pot must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
translation_verse: Na avɔbui ani ƒui kemmo na béƒulo lɛna lɛmmɔ ni, ɔdi ka bebo-nya babwɛ. Na si abuala ebui kemmo na béƒulo-ni ni, ɔlɛka bekuo-nya kemmo baƒɔ kaduɛ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to tell Aaron and his sons how to offer the daily sacrifices that are sent up in smoke to please the Lord: You must put the animal for the sacrifice on the altar in the evening and let it stay there all night. But make sure the fire keeps burning.
translation_verse: “Bo Aaron ku nwuna bebi bananabi ɔda anini, ‘Ulu ɔni na ndubo-ma bɔtina mɛni ndi ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na badubo bɔsia butaabla akpala bɔkyula ƒui ɔdi ɔmmɔ. Na muubó-ma ɔda geen na ɔmɛni lɛlɔ, ka akpala ani na baakyula mmɔ ni, ɔlɛka ataasia lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ usien umodi útálɛ ɔtanta. Na útalɛ ka ogya ɔmmɔ uni.

english_verse: The fire must never go out, so put wood on it each morning. After this, you are to lay an animal on the altar next to the fat that you sacrifice to ask my blessing. Then send it all up in smoke to me.
translation_verse: Na ogya ɔni na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka banu ka ɔkya mmɔ uwi mmɔ uwi biala na uteni. Mmomu bakpane bammɔ banu ka bákya ekyweni ogya ɔmmɔ kemmo ɔtanta biala. Na akpala ani na bekyuli beeboku ni, ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔnu ka bákyula-nya ƒui ku lɛmwi lɛni bédie na unwi bɔbla akpala ammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The altar fire must always be kept burning—it must never go out. Sacrifices To Give Thanks to the Lord The Lord said:
translation_verse: Banu ka ogya ɔkya mmɔ uwi ndi uwi na uteni. Edula Ebi Akpala

english_verse: When someone offers a sacrifice to give thanks to me, the priests from Aaron's family must bring it to the front of the bronze altar,
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɔmɛni ndi mina ɔda bubo bɔni nkɛnku edula ebi akpala lɛlɔ. Aaron bebi bananabi badubuti etela ammɔ beboku Unwoti anumi na lɛkpabi anumi.

english_verse: where one of them will scoop up a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the incense on it. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, he will lay all of this on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔma akpala etela ammɔ ɔlaaƒɔ ɔni muukeye lɛkɔkɔ linwi ku nwuna lɛlɔ nnɔ ku oloƒui ɔna ƒui ɔni nsia etela ammɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔdubuti ɔkyula na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ aani lɛkpabi lɛlɔ enyimo likposela adila bɔkyula ƒui akpala na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ.

english_verse: The rest of it is to be baked without yeast and eaten by the priests in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent. This bread is very holy, just like the sacrifices for sin or the sacrifices for making things right, and I have given this part to the priests from what is offered to me on the altar.
translation_verse: Utalɛ ka beƒi-nwu na bɔnyii bɔkya-nwu kemmo. Ami néti lɛla lɛmmɔ líte-ma aani bana kadikɔ ɔ́siku akpala ani na béti bákyula béte-mi kemmo. Na ese kedee aani likpidi bɔkyiɛ ku kɔtɔ bukpi akpala.

english_verse: Only the men in Aaron's family are allowed to eat this bread, and they must go through a ceremony to be made holy before touching it. This law will never change. When Priests Are Ordained
translation_verse: Ɔnana biala na Aaron bebi akɔ ɔkana na ɔdi adila ammɔ. Ɔsika adi bana kadikɔ na ala ani na bákyula béte-mi kemmo úsie bina kaba kaba kemmo bekyuli ƒui akɔ. Na lɛla biala nétuku ala ammɔ adubɔbla kedee. Na ukyuli biala metuku ala ammɔ lɛnɔ ɔ́bla kedee.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord spoke to Moses
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Unwoti ɔsɔ ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: mixed with olive oil and cooked in a shallow pan. The bread must then be crumbled into small pieces and sent up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Badubɔnwu ɔlaaƒɔ ɔmmɔ na beƒi-nwu na lɛbuala kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ na basala-nwu ku nnɔ. Si bátu-nwu bénwini na ɔ́bi kaduɛ ni, badubuti beboku na bedie-nwu unwi unwi kalɛ na béƒi-nwu mmɔ, na báƒɛ-nwu kemmo kɔkɛ kɔkɛ bete-mi aani edula ebi akpala na ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ.

english_verse: Each of Aaron's descendants who is ordained as a priest must perform this ceremony and make sure that the bread is completely burned on the altar. None of it may be eaten! Sacrifices for Sin (Leviticus
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔkpane edula ebi etela udu biala ani na úti úboku ni, ɔdubɔkyula ana ƒui na batadi ɔdi.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: how the priests from Aaron's family were to offer the sacrifice for sin: This sacrifice is very sacred, and the animal must be killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar.
translation_verse: “Tásu Aaron ku nwuna bebi bananabi anini, ‘Ulu ɔni na ndubo-ma bɔtina mɛni lɛlɔ na badubɔsia babla ekpidi bɔkyiɛ akpala. Kesii kani na bádu ebuo ɔni badubuti babla bɔkyula ɔdi ni, mmɔ kani na badubɔdu ekpidi bɔkyiɛ akpala ebuo ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ na Unwoti anumi, ɔsika lɛla lɛni nse kedee na lɛdi.

english_verse: The priest who offers this sacrifice must eat it in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent,
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔni nábla ekpidi bɔkyiɛ akpala ammɔ ubo nwuna kadikɔ. Na kadikɔ kammɔ ni, Unwoti Adi Kevo kaduli kesii kani nse kedee mmɔ na badubɔdi adila ammɔ.

english_verse: and anyone or anything that touches the meat will be holy. If any of the animal's blood is splattered on the clothes of the priest, they must be washed in a holy place.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala ɔni métuku lɛna lɛmmɔ ni, ɔ́bla kedee. Na si ebuo ɔmmɔ ubugya úwi awu ɔdi lɛlɔ ni, ɔdi ka baƒɔ awu ɔmmɔ na kesii kani nse kedee mmɔ.

english_verse: None of the meat may be eaten from the sacrifices for sin that require blood to be brought into the sacred tent. These sacrifices must be completely burned.
translation_verse: Nsu likpidi bɔkyiɛ ebuo biala na béti-nwu ubugya béduoku Unwoti Adi Kevo kesii kani nse kedee mmɔ ka babla akpala na bedie kɔtu bɔni na ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, útalɛ ka ɔdi biala utuku-nwu kenye, mmomu badubɔkyula-nwu ƒui.’ ”

english_verse: One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke to me.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti-nya ɔsia ogya lɛlɔ na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na ndubɔƒɔ-nwu aani kɔtɔ bukpi akpala bɔkyula.

english_verse: Give me one loaf or wafer from each of these four kinds of bread, after which they will belong to the priest who splattered the blood against the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Na ala eƒidi amɛni akɔ ni, ɔdubudie ɔdi biala unwi unwi aani lɛla lɛni na anwu lɛnɔ úti uute Unwoti. Na ala ammɔ adubunwini ɔkpane ɔdi anwu ɔni néti unwi bɔbla akpala ammɔ ubugya ɔ́kuna úwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Don't eat any of the meat that has touched something unclean. Instead, burn it. The rest of the meat may be eaten by anyone who is clean and acceptable to me.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na lɛna biala nétuku lɛla lɛni muusé lɛlɔ ni, lɛsɔ lɛɛɛdia ka ɔdi ɔkun-ni. Mmomu ɔlɛka bakyula-ni kede kede. Na si uwi ɔni na lɛ́mu lise sɛɛn na lítetuku lɛla lɛni muusé lɛlɔ ni, ukyuli ɔni na use sɛɛn kani ndubɔkana na ɔkun-ni.

english_verse: The sacrifice to make things right is very sacred.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɔda bubo bɔmɛni ndanku kɔtɔ bukpi akpala ani ndi lɛla lɛni nse kedee ƒui.

english_verse: The animal must be killed in the same place where the sacrifice to please me is killed, and the animal's blood must be splattered against the four sides of the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Na kesii kani na bádu bɔkyula ƒui akpala ebuo ni, mmɔ kani na ɔlɛka badu kɔtɔ bukpi akpala ebuo ɔmɛni lɛnɔ na beti nwuna ubugya bakuna bewi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ bamana.

english_verse: Offer all of the animal's fat, including the fat on its tail and on its insides,
translation_verse: Na badubuti nwuna lɛmwi ƒui bete-mi. Lɛmwi lɛni ndanku ɔka ku lɛmwi lɛni mma kaƒɔ ala ammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: Akabi anyɔ ammɔ lɛmwi lɛni mma-nwu lɛlɔ ku kasɔma lɛmwi lɛmmɔ ku akɔ ammɔ kenye kammɔ ƒui ɔlɛka uti-nwu ubunku akabi ammɔ.

english_verse: This sacrifice for making things right is very holy. Only the priests may eat it, and they must eat it in a holy place.
translation_verse: Ɔnana biala na bakpane bammɔ akɔ ɔdubɔkana na ɔkun lɛna lɛmmɔ lɛdi na Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kaduli kesii kani na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ na use kedee ƒui mmɔ.

english_verse: The ceremony for this sacrifice and the one for sin are the same, and the meat may be eaten only by the priest who performs this ceremony of forgiveness.
translation_verse: “ ‘Kɔtɔ bukpi akpala ese aani likpidi lili buvele akpala na ɔda bubo bunwi kani ndanku ɔnanyɔ. Na ɔkpane ɔni névele ka bedie kɔtu bɔni na bekyuli bammɔ lɛlɔ ni, anwu mbo lɛna lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: In fact, the priest who offers a sacrifice to please me may keep the skin of the animal,
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔni nábla ebuo bɔdu taakyula akpala ute-mi ni, ebuo ɔku ɔmmɔ ɔdi anwu ɔdi.

english_verse: All other grain sacrifices—with or without olive oil in them—are to be divided equally among the priests of Aaron's family. Sacrifices To Ask the Lord's Blessing The Lord said:
translation_verse: Na lɛkpabi lɛlɔ edula ebi akpala biala na básala ku nnɔ iye ukpludi na ɔdi ni, ɔdi Aaron bebi bananabi ƒui ɔdi likeke.

english_verse: Here are the instructions for offering a sacrifice to ask my blessing:
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɔƒɛni mɔɔwia ka enu ɔda bubo bɔni lɛlɔ na badubɔsia na babla unwi bɔbla akpala ani na badubuti beboku Unwoti anumi.

english_verse: If you offer it to give thanks, you must offer some bread together with it. Use the finest flour to make three kinds of bread without yeast—two in the form of loaves mixed with olive oil and one in the form of thin wafers brushed with oil.
translation_verse: “ ‘Si ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔnii ɔɔbla akpala ammɔ na adanku linugya ni, na ɔlɛka ubunku ɔlaaƒɔ ɔni na bánwu na béƒi-nwu aani bodobodo na bɔnyii buuubo-nwu kemmo, na ɔsala-nwu ku nnɔ, ku bodobodo uƒidi udu bamba ɔni nse bɛbɛɛbɛ kunu kunu na bésusu nnɔ nwuna lɛlɔ. Na edula ebi ɔlaaƒɔ ɔni na bánwu béƒi mɛni ni, banu ka bábaka-nwu kaduɛ ku ɔlaaƒɔ ɔni nse sɛɛn na básala-nwu ku nnɔ.

english_verse: When you offer an animal to ask a blessing from me or to thank me, the meat belongs to you, but it must be eaten the same day.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ebuo ɔni na úti úboku úbo ɔɔbla unwi bɔbla enugya akpala ammɔ ni, limeyi lɛni na bábla akpala ammɔ lɛlɔ kani na ɔlɛka bakun lɛna lɛmmɔ. Na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ulada-ni ulése na kadi kegye kewi-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: It is different with the sacrifices you offer when you make me a promise or voluntarily give me something. The meat from those sacrifices may be kept and eaten the next day,
translation_verse: “ ‘Nsu is akpala ammɔ adi lili budie iye kaƒɔ ƒaa akpala ni, bakana bakun lɛna lɛmmɔ na limeyi lɛmmɔ. Na si lítasa ni, bakana bakun-ni kadi kégye.

english_verse: but any that is left over must be destroyed. If you eat any of it after the second day, your sacrifice will be useless and unacceptable, and you will be both disgusting and guilty.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu si unwi bɔbla akpala ebuo ɔmmɔ lɛna lɛdi líbu limeyi lɛtɛdi na ɔdi ɔ́kun-ni ni, lɛɛɛdubo ukyuli ɔmmɔ bɔƒɔ ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ. Na akpala ammɔ aaadubo kɔsia kɔdi bɔlɛ bute ukyuli ɔmmɔ mmomu ɔdubɔkya-mi kɔnyi geen na ndubɔdu-nwu kɔtɔ geen.

english_verse: But don't eat any of this meat if you have become unclean by touching something unclean from a human or an animal or from any other creature. If you do, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
translation_verse: Si ukyuli ɔdi útuku lɛla lɛni muusé lɛlɔ na ɔdi ukyuli ɔni na lɛla lɛdi lɛda o-o, ebuo na ɔdi o-o, iye lɛla bamba biala na muusé lɛlɔ na nkisi o-o, asa na ɔ́kun unwi bɔbla lɛna lɛni na béti bákpa béte-mi ni, ɔlɛka bekulo kɔna biala nkya anwu ku nwuna badi ntɛ.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: to say to the people: Don't eat the fat of cattle, sheep, or goats.
translation_verse: “Tásu Israel kadi bekyuli anini, ‘Ɔdi utakun ɔmantɛ akɔ lɛmwi iye koƒonu iye ese lɛmwi.

english_verse: If one of your animals dies or is killed by some wild animal, you may do anything with its fat except eat it.
translation_verse: Na ebuo ɔni na úkpi iye ebuo ukpidi ɔdi néƒie-nwu na ɔ́duli-nwu ɔ́va ni, bakana beti lɛmwi babla lɛla bamba biala, nsu betetuku-nwu kenye anwu lo.

english_verse: If you eat the fat of an animal that can be used as a sacrifice to me, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ebuo ɔni na beti básia lɛkpabi lɛlɔ béte-mi ni, ukyuli ɔni makun-nwu lɛmwi lɛmmɔ ndubukulo kɔna kɔni nkya anwu ku anwu badi ntɛ.

english_verse: And no matter where you live, you must not eat the blood of any bird or animal,
translation_verse: Na kesi kesii na bilie ni, útalɛ ka bɛdi ubugya ɔdi. Aasɛ ubugya na ɔdi o-o, ebuo bamba ɔdi ubugya na ɔdi o-o ni, ɔdi utadi.

english_verse: or you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
translation_verse: Ukyuli biala madi ubugya ni, ndubukulo ukyuli ɔmmɔ kɔna kɔni nkya anwu ku anwu badi ntɛ.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord also told Moses
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: If you want to offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, you must bring the part to be burned and lay it on the bronze altar. But you must first lift up the choice ribs with their fat to show that the offering is dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Anwu ɔlati nwuna enu kemmo na ɔdubɔda-nya uboku na babla akpala ammɔ. Na lɛmwi ku ebuo ɔmmɔ kayi ɔvu ni, ɔdubuti uboku na bakɔliku-nwu katɔ batina-mi bebo-ni kudu.

english_verse: A priest from Aaron's family will then send the fat up in smoke, but the ribs belong to the priests.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔdubɔkyula lɛmwi lɛmmɔ, nsu kayi ɔvu ɔmmɔ ni, ɔdi Aaron ku nwuna bebi bananabi ɔdi.

english_verse: The upper joint of the right hind leg is for the priest who offers the blood and the fat of the animal.
translation_verse: Na Aaron bebi akɔ ɔkpane ɔni néti ubugya ɔmmɔ ku unwi bɔbla akpala ammɔ ku lɛmwi úte-mi ni, kɔdianu libuli lɛmmɔ lɛdi nwuna lɛdi aani nwuna kadikɔ.

english_verse: These are the ceremonies for sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessing or his forgiveness, as well as the ceremonies for those sacrifices that demand a payment and for the sacrifices that are offered when priests are ordained.
