english_verse: Then he gave it to Aaron and his sons, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: úte Aaron ku nwuna bebi bananabi kalɛ na Unwoti úbo-nwu ɔda.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ku Aaron ɔnini,

english_verse: The Kohathites will be responsible for carrying the sacred objects used in worship at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: “Kehatƒuɔ bammɔ kabla na Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo ndi ka bataanu ala kedee ani nse mmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: When the Israelites are ready to move their camp, Aaron and his sons will enter the tent and take down the curtain that separates the sacred chest from the rest of the tent. They will cover the chest with this curtain,
translation_verse: Na si úbo úte ka bɛta mmɔ bisie kesii bamba ni, ɔlɛka Aaron ku nwuna bebi bananabi besie na batáƒami kakpakɔ bule kɔdi kɔni mɔɔbala Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ na beti benyimi adaka ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ bamana ƒui.

english_verse: and then with a piece of fine leather, and cover it all with a solid blue cloth. After this they will put the carrying poles in place.
translation_verse: Na beti ketu kemmo bebuo benengudi lɛku buni bebi-nwu eli, na beti kɔdi buluu bebi-nwu lɛlɔ, na beti ligyii lɛni beeti teeti kevo kammɔ bakya-nwu lɛƒɛnyi.

english_verse: Next, Aaron and his sons will use another blue cloth to cover the table for the sacred bread. On the cloth they will place the dishes, the bowls for incense, the cups, the jugs for wine, as well as the bread itself.
translation_verse: “Na ala kasiakɔ kani nlɛ-mi anumi ni, beti kɔdi buluu bewi-nwu lɛlɔ. Na beti akyami eblidi ku enengudi lidu basia. Na beti lɛsii lɛni kemmo na beewi akpala ntɛ ku bodobodo ɔni ndubɔsia mmɔ uwi ndi uwi basia-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: With another blue cloth they will cover the lampstand, along with the lamps, the lamp snuffers, the fire pans, and the jars of oil for the lamps.
translation_verse: “Ɔmmɔ kama na beti kɔdi buluu benyimi asogya kasiakɔ ugyii ɔmmɔ ku lɛla lɛni na beeti teenyene lɛsogya kɔbuli kɔmmɔ ku ntɔ kuwikɔ ku lɛsogya nnɔmii kuwikɔ lɛsii lɛmmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: All of this will then be covered with a piece of fine leather and placed on a carrying frame.
translation_verse: Na benyimi-nya ku ana lɛlɔ kabla ala ƒui bakya ketu kemmo bebuo benengudi lɛku kemmo na beti basia ligyii lɛni lɛlɔ na beeti teeti ala ammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The gold incense altar is to be covered with a blue cloth, and then with a piece of fine leather, before its carrying poles are put in place.
translation_verse: “Na sika ugyiedi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ni, beti kɔdi buluu bebi-nwu lɛlɔ na beti bebuo ɔku bebi kɔdi kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na bakya-nwu ligyii lɛni na baagyú-nwu lɛƒɛnyi.

english_verse: Next, Aaron and his sons will take blue cloth and wrap all the objects used in worship at the sacred tent. These will need to be covered with a piece of fine leather, then placed on a carrying frame.
translation_verse: “Na kakpakɔ kabla lɛlɔ ala ƒui na katɔma kedee kammɔ kemmo ni, benyimi ala ammɔ ƒui bakya kɔdi buluu kemmo, na beti bebuo ɔku bebi-nya lɛlɔ ƒui, na bagyu basia ligyii lɛni lɛlɔ na beeti teeti-nya lɛlɔ.

english_verse: They are to remove the ashes from the bronze altar and cover it with a purple cloth.
translation_verse: “Bedie ntɔ na lɛbualagyie lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kemmo na beti kɔdi kɔni náƒɔ kuye geen bebi-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: On that cloth will be placed the utensils used at the altar, including the fire pans, the meat forks, the shovels, and the sprinkling bowls. All of this will then be covered with a piece of fine leather, before the carrying poles are put in place.
translation_verse: Na beti anwabui ku akyami ani lɛlɔ kabla na baabla na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ basia-nwu lɛlɔ. Ala ammɔ adanku ogya kuwikɔ ku kɔvili kɔni na baatu lɛna ku alakpi kɔlɛkɛ ku akyami bonwu ani kemmo na baakya ntu teewi bekyuli. Beti bebuo lɛku bebi ala amɛni lɛlɔ benyimi na beti ligyii lɛni na beeti taagyu-nwu bakya-nwu lɛƒɛnyi.

english_verse: When the camp is ready to be moved, the Kohathites will be responsible for carrying the sacred objects and the furnishings of the sacred tent. But Aaron and his sons must have already covered those things so the Kohathites won't touch them and die.
translation_verse: “Ɔƒɛni si uwi ɔni na Aaron ku nwuna bebi bananabi báwɔlɔ ala buti teebi Kevo kammɔ, na báwɔlɔ ala kedee ammɔ ku kana kemmo ala ani nse kedee mmɔ ƒui ala bubi, na báwɔlɔ lɛlɔ bɔklibi ƒui ka bata ni, na Kehat bebi bananabi bani na ɔ́lɛka beti ala ammɔ bebo na bebeti-nya. Nsu bana ɔdi kɔnu kutetuku ala ani nse kedee mmɔ amu badubo bukpi. Kehatƒuɔ bammɔ beti ala ani nse Kevo Kasakɔ kemmo mmɔ.

english_verse: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest will be in charge of the oil for the lamps, the sweet-smelling incense, the grain for the sacrifices, and the olive oil used for dedications and ordinations. Eleazar is responsible for seeing that the sacred tent, its furnishings, and the sacred objects are taken care of.
translation_verse: “Aaron ubidi Eleasar ɔni ndi ɔkpane ni, nnɔmii bɔni na beewi asogya ku oloƒui ƒɛƒɛɛ ku limeyi ndi limeyi edula ebi akpala ku likpose nnɔmii ni, nwuna lɛkɔkɔ na ɔ́lɛka akya. Na anwu na ɔlɛka utaanu katɔma kammɔ ku kana lɛlɔ ku kakpakɔ lɛlɔ ala kedee ammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: Find out how many men between the ages of
translation_verse: Ka banana bani náaƒɔ akwa avlaatɛ útédu akwa liti na beebo taababla kabla na Unwoti Kevo Kasakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: the curtains hanging around the courtyard of the tent, and the curtain and ropes for the entrance to the courtyard. The Gershonites are to do whatever needs to be done to take care of these things,
translation_verse: ku aduni ani nƒa kaduli kammɔ ámana Adi Kevo kammɔ ku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ku kayakun kɔdi kɔmmɔ ku kɔbuli kɔmmɔ ku kabla kammɔ lɛlɔ kɔlɛmii ƒui. Na Gersonƒuɔ bammɔ na ɔlɛka babla kabla biala na kadanku ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ala amɛni ƒui.

english_verse: These are the duties of the Gershonites at the sacred tent, and Ithamar son of Aaron will make sure they do their work. The Duties of the Merarite Clans
translation_verse: Gersonƒuɔ bammɔ bana kabla kadi mmɔ na Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo. Na ɔkpane Aaron ubidi Itamar ndubo bana kabla lɛlɔ bɔnu. Merari Kaba Bekyuli Kabla

english_verse: The Merarites will be responsible for carrying the frames of the tent and its other pieces, including the bars, the posts, and the stands,
translation_verse: Na bana kabla ndi ka ama ndubo ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ligyii ku lɛtalagyii ku akpa ammɔ ku ligyii lɛni nda kakpakɔ bule kɔdi ana lɛka ƒui buteeti.

english_verse: as well as the posts that support the courtyard, together with their stands, tent pegs, and ropes. The Merarites are to be told exactly what objects they are to carry,
translation_verse: Na ama kani ndubɔlɛ kaduli kammɔ ƒui ligyii ku akpa ku ana lɛka ku Kevo kammɔ ewele ku kɔbuli ku kevo kammɔ lɛlɔ ala ani ndanku-ka ƒui. Na ete ɔdi biala ku lɛla lɛni na ɔdi ka uti.

english_verse: and Ithamar son of Aaron will make sure they do their work. The Levites Are Counted Again
translation_verse: Kabla kammɔ na Merari adua ammɔ badubo butaabla na Unwoti Adi Kevo mmɔ. Na ɔkpane Aaron ubidi Itamar ndubo kabla kammɔ lɛlɔ bɔnu.” Báka Lewiƒuɔ Bammɔ Bánu

english_verse: Moses, Aaron, and the other Israelite leaders obeyed the Lord and counted the Levi tribe by families and clans, to find out how many men there were between the ages of
translation_verse: Na béte ɔdi biala nwuna lɛla lɛni na ɔdi ka ɔbla iye uti. Lɛni na báka bekyuli bammɔ aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda.

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel, “Put out of the camp everyone who has leprosy or a bodily discharge or who has touched a dead body. Now that I live among my people, their camp must be kept clean.”
translation_verse: Bɛda bekyuli bani muusé lɛlɔ uleku iye ɔnana na ɔdi bidie bina keliekɔ kesii kani na nliku-mii na belebile-ka na keteese lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed the Lord's instructions. The Penalty for Committing a Crime (Leviticus
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israelƒuɔ bése atu na báda balɛne bammɔ ƒui bédie bana kakyakɔ aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda. Kayu Bɔƒɔ Na Bɔƒiɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: If any of you commit a crime against someone, you have sinned against me.
translation_verse: “Sɔ kɔ lɛsa na asu Israelƒuɔ anini, ‘Si ukyuli ɔ́lɛ Unwoti kama na útábla ɔkpanadi likpidi lɛdi ni,

english_verse: You must confess your guilt and pay the victim in full for whatever damage has been done, plus a fine of
translation_verse: Ɔlɛka ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔsu likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla na ɔƒɔ likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla mmɔ kayu ƒui ute ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́ƒiɔ mmɔ. Na ɔsɔ ɔƒɔ kayu kammɔ lɛkpa lɛlɔndi ɔsia kayu kammɔ lɛlɔ ute-nwu.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: If the victim has no relative who can accept this money, it belongs to me and will be paid to the priest. In addition to that payment, you must take a ram for the priest to sacrifice so your sin will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Nsu si ukyuli ɔni na badubɔƒɔ kayu kammɔ bete úkpi na uuubo lɛlɔ ukyuli ɔdi na baƒɔ kayu kammɔ bete-nwu ni, na lɛla lɛni na nka ɔlɛka baƒɔ mmɔ línwini Unwoti ɔdi na ɔlɛka beti bete ɔkpane ku ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔni na béti baabla likpidi lili kayu bɔƒɔ bɔmmɔ na ukyuli ɔni náƒiɔ mmɔ lili.

english_verse: When you make a donation to the sacred tent, that money belongs only to the priest, and each priest will keep what is given to him. A Suspicious Husband
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala etela sɛsɛɛ ammɔ adi ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔlati adi, nsu ani na úti úte ɔkpane adi ɔkpane ɔmmɔ adi.’ ” Batɛku Uleku Ɔni Nálɛ Ɔgyani Kama Litemi

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda ɔnini,

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: Suppose a man becomes jealous and suspects that his wife has been unfaithful, but he has no proof.
translation_verse: Si lɛla lɛdi lɛ́vi uleku ɔmmɔ ɔgyani lɛlɔ na úse kalɔ uukpó kɔgyulo ka ulekudi ɔ́lɛ-nwu kama na uusé lɛlɔ iye ɔƒɛni kalɛ útalɛ-nwu kama na ulese lɛlɔ mmomu bɔkali kani na ɔɔkali lɛni ni,

english_verse: He must take his wife to the priest, together with one kilogram of ground barley as an offering to find out if she is guilty. No olive oil or incense is to be put on that offering.
translation_verse: ɔlɛka ɔkpanku ulekudi usienku ɔkpane kudɔ. Na si úsela ni, ɔlɛka uti bodobodo ɔlaaƒɔ lɛɛƒɛɛ inyɔ ɔda. Na utalɛka uti nnɔ uwi-nwu lɛlɔ iye uti oloƒui ɔsia-nwu lɛlɔ, ɔsika akpala ammɔ adi kɔgyulo edula ebi akpala na adi enyimo kati bute na bɔƒiɔ bɔdi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The priest will lead the woman to my altar and make her stand there.
translation_verse: “ ‘Mmɔ ni, ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na uleku ɔmmɔ ubenye Unwoti anumi.

english_verse: He will then pour sacred water into a clay jar and stir in some dust from the floor of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na udu ntu kedee bɔni buwi libui kemmo mmɔ na ɔma na ɔtumu na Adi Kevo kammɔ kɔmadɔ uwi ntu bɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The priest will write these curses on special paper and wash them off into the bitter water,
translation_verse: “ ‘Mmɔ na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubo ewida etemila ammɔ bunweni bɔsia kakunkɛ kadi lɛlɔ na ɔƒɔ-nya uwi ewida ntu ku ɔdu ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: so that when the woman drinks this water, the curses will enter her body.
translation_verse: Na ɔya na uleku ɔmmɔ ɔni ntu ɔdu ɔdu bɔni nnye nte ewida mmɔ. Na si ɔ́ni ntu bɔmmɔ ni, ɔdubɔya na uleku ɔmmɔ uteebo abi geen.

english_verse: He will take the barley offering from her and lift it up in dedication to me, the Lord. Then he will place it on my altar
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔƒɔ kɔgyulo edula ebi akpala ammɔ ɔsiku uleku ɔmmɔ enu kemmo na ɔkɔliku-nya katɔ ɔtina Unwoti asa na uti-nya usienku lɛkpabi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: If the woman has been unfaithful, the water will immediately make her unable to have children, and she will be a curse among her people.
translation_verse: Na si uleku ɔmmɔ úbile lɛlɔ na ɔ́lɛ ɔgyani kama ni, si báya na ɔ́ni ntu bɔni ndanku ewida mmɔ ni, ɔdubɔya na uteebo abi. Na ɔya na nwuna kaƒɔna keƒu na ɔsɔ ulakana kaƒɔ bɔda na ɔwɔ. Na ɔdubunwini ukyuli ɔni na ewida asiaku-nwu na nwuna badi akɔ.

english_verse: But if she is innocent, her body will not be harmed, and she will still be able to have children.
translation_verse: Nsu si uleku ɔmmɔ útebile lɛlɔ na lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-nwu ka use sɛɛn ɔsu ni, ɔdubɔkana na ɔwɔ bebi.

english_verse: This is the ceremony that must take place at my altar when a husband suspects that his wife has been unfaithful. The priest must tell the woman to stand in my presence and carefully follow these instructions.
translation_verse: iye si lɛla lɛdi liikpóku ɔnana ɔdi na ɔɔbla-nwu aani ulekudi ɔ́di kɔsɔnɔ. Ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na uleku ɔmmɔ ubenye Unwoti anumi na ɔbla-nwu ɔdi ɔni na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔɔtina mɛni.

english_verse: If the husband is wrong, he will not be punished; but if his wife is guilty, she will be punished.
translation_verse: Ɔnana ɔmmɔ útaƒiɔ si ɔ́bla ɔmɛni mmomu uleku ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔkɛ nwuna likpidi kɔtu bɔni biala.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: If any of you want to dedicate yourself to me by vowing to become a Nazirite,
translation_verse: “Kɔ lɛsa na asu Israelƒuɔ anini, ‘Si ɔnana ɔdi iye uleku ɔdi ɔɔyɔ́ ka use kenye kadi na kenye kammɔ kaatina ka ɔɔyɔ́ ka udie lɛlɔ lɛti sɛsɛɛ use ute Unwoti na bataalɔ-nwu banii, Nasareni ni,

english_verse: you must no longer drink any wine or beer or use any kind of vinegar. Don't drink grape juice or eat grapes or raisins—
translation_verse: ɔlɛka ɔda lɛlɔ udie ntɛ bɔni mbo ɔkplu bɔni kemmo. Na utalɛka ɔni egyiibi ntɛ bɔni na bébulo, na utalɛka ɔni lɛla lɛni mɔɔda kenye, iye egyiibi lidu biala ntu bɔni na bámana ebi ammɔ bédie iye ɔdi-nya muedi.

english_verse: The hair of a Nazirite is sacred to me, and as long as you are a Nazirite, you must never cut your hair.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na uwi ɔni na údie lɛlɔ lɛti sɛsɛɛ úse úte Unwoti mɛni ni, utalɛka ukpeyi lili. Ɔlɛka ɔbla kedee ute Unwoti úti útédu ka uwi ɔni na ɔ́su ka wedie lɛlɔ lɛti sɛsɛɛ wetédu mmɔ údu. Na ɔlɛka ɔnyonu nwuna kuli linwini na line gyɔlɔɔ.

english_verse: During the time that you are a Nazirite, you must never go close to a dead body,
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si uwi ɔni na údie lɛlɔ sɛsɛɛ úse úte Unwoti mɛni ni, utalɛka ɔni ude ukpine ɔdi.

english_verse: If someone suddenly dies near you, your hair is no longer sacred, and you must shave it seven days later during the ceremony to make you clean.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na si úbo úte ka ukyuli ɔdi úkpi kɔnakunwi na nwuna anumi na ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu na úbile linwini lɛni na ɔ́bla sɛsɛɛ kedee úte Unwoti mmɔ ni, ɔlɛka ukpeyi kuli kɔmmɔ ƒui na lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi limeyi lɛni ndi limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then on the next day, bring two doves or two pigeons to the priest at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na limeyi maanedi lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka ɔwia babloduma inyɔ iye bamangbɛ inyɔ na uti-ma usienku ɔkpane na Unwoti Adi Kevo kayakun.

english_verse: He will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me. You will then be forgiven for being too near a dead body, and your hair will again become sacred.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti aasɛ unwi ɔbla likpidi lili buvele akpala na uti unyɔdi ɔbla bɔkyula akpala ute Unwoti na nwuna likpidi lili kayu bɔƒɔ. Ɔsika úlie bekyuli bani muuwulo ukpine akɔ ɔsu ɔ́bla likpidi. Na limeyi lɛmmɔ kani lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka ɔsɔ ɔbla nwuna lili linwini kedee sɛsɛɛ use ute Unwoti.

english_verse: But the dead body made you unacceptable, so you must make another vow to become a Nazirite and be dedicated once more. Finally, a year-old ram must be offered as the sacrifice to make things right.
translation_verse: Na ɔlɛka ɔsɔku lɛlɔ ɔbla sɛsɛɛ kedee ute Unwoti na uwi ɔni ɔ́ƒuna ka udie lɛlɔ lɛti use ute Unwoti mmɔ utédu kenye. Na ɔlɛka ɔwia koƒonu ubi kɔni nákɛ lɛkwa linwi uboku na beti-ku babla kɔtɔ bukpi akpala. Na uwi ɔni návi na nka údie lɛlɔ lɛti mmɔ uuubunku, ɔsika uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo na úbile lɛlɔ na uusé lɛlɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: When you have completed your promised time of being a Nazirite, go to the sacred tent
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɔƒɛni Nasareni ɔni nédie lɛlɔ lɛti úse úte Unwoti úte uwi ɔdi na uwi ɔmmɔ údu ni, ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ ndi ka bakpanku-nwu bebenyene Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kayakun.

english_verse: and offer three animals that have nothing wrong with them: a year-old ram as a sacrifice to please me, a year-old female lamb as a sacrifice for sin, and a full-grown ram as a sacrifice to ask my blessing.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, ɔlɛka uti koƒonu kɔkɔdi kɔni nákɛ lɛkwa na kútasɔ kesii kadi uboku na babla bɔkyula akpala, ku koƒonu kuledi kɔni nátasɔ kesii kadi na beti babla likpidi lili buvele akpala ku koƒonu kɔgyani kɔni na kútasɔ kesii kadi na beti babla unwi bɔbla akpala.

english_verse: Wine offerings and grain sacrifices must also be brought with these animals. Finally, you are to bring a basket of bread made with your finest flour and olive oil, but without yeast. Also bring some thin wafers brushed with oil.
translation_verse: Na si ɔdubo ubabla akpala ammɔ ni, ɔlɛka uboku edula ebi ku nwuna lɛlɔ ntɛ akpala ku bodobodo kagyigyɛ ɔni kemmo na bɔnyii buuubo na bábla-nwu ku ɔlaaƒɔ ɔni nse sɛɛn na básala-nwu ku nnɔ ku bodobodo bɛbɛ ɔni na bésusu nnɔ nwuna lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The priest will take these gifts to my altar and offer them, so that I will be pleased and will forgive you.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti ala ammɔ uboku Unwoti anumi mmɔ na uti ɔbla likpidi lili buvele akpala ku bɔkyula akpala ammɔ.

english_verse: After that, you will stand at the entrance to the sacred tent, shave your head, and put the hair in the fire where the priest has offered the sacrifice to ask my blessing.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na Unwoti Adi Kevo kayakun mmɔ ni, Nasareni ɔmmɔ ɔdubo nwuna lili linwini lɛni na ɔ́bla sɛsɛɛ kedee úte Unwoti mmɔ bukpeyi na uti linwini lɛmmɔ ɔkya unwi bɔbla akpala ogya ɔni mɔɔda mmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Once the meat from the ram's shoulder has been boiled, the priest will take it, along with one loaf of bread and one wafer brushed with oil, and give them to you.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na si Nasareni ɔmmɔ úkpeyi nwuna linwini lɛni na ɔ́bla sɛsɛɛ kedee úte Unwoti mmɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti koƒonu kɔmmɔ lɛmangba lɛni béƒulo ɔkya-nwu kɔnu na udie bodobodo geen ku bodobodo bɛbɛɛbɛ na kagyigyɛ kemmo ubunku ute-nwu

english_verse: You will hand them back to the priest, who will lift them up in dedication to me. Then he can eat the meat from the ram's shoulder, its choice ribs, and its hind leg, because this is his share of the sacrifice. After this, you will no longer be a Nazirite, and you will be free to drink wine.
translation_verse: na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔkɔliku ala ammɔ katɔ ɔtina Unwoti ubo-nya kudu na adi ala ani nse kedee na adi ɔkpane adi ku ebuo ɔmmɔ kayi ɔvu kani na ɔ́kɔliku katɔ ɔ́tina Unwoti mmɔ ku nwuna libuli lɛni béti béboku mmɔ. Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Nasareni ɔmmɔ ɔkana na ɔni ntɛ ƒaa.

english_verse: These are the requirements for Nazirites. However, if you can afford to offer more, you must do so. The Blessing for the People
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɔmmɔ ndi ɔda bubo ute Nasareni ɔni nédie lɛlɔ lɛti na ɔ́bla lɛlɔ sɛsɛɛ kede úte Unwoti na úbo uudie lɛlɔ, nsu ɔkana na ute ala bamba utulo amɛni ƒaa na nwuna ɔyikun kenye.’ ” Kalɛ Na Bakpane Beete Kusɛ Kusɛ

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda ɔnini,

english_verse: “When Aaron and his sons bless the people of Israel, they must say:
translation_verse: “Su Aaron ku bebi anini, ‘Bitaasia ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ teete Israelƒuɔ kusɛ kusɛ bɛnini,

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will bless and protect you,
translation_verse: “ ‘Unwoti ute-mii kusɛ kusɛ na ɔda-mii,

english_verse: and that he will show you mercy and kindness.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔya na nwuna anumi eteekeye teewi-mii na ɔnu-mii ku lɛƒɔndia,

english_verse: May the Lord be good to you and give you peace.”
translation_verse: Unwoti unwini nwuna anumi ɔtina-mii na ute-mii keyi buɛɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If Aaron and his sons ask me to bless the Israelites, I will give them my blessing.”
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu badubɔkpali-mi lɛnyi bete Israelƒuɔ kusɛ kusɛ na ɔdububo-nwu kemmo lɛni.”

english_verse: When Moses had finished setting up the sacred tent, he dedicated it to the Lord, together with its furnishings, the altar, and its equipment.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Mose ɔ́wɔlɔ Unwoti kakpakɔ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ bɔlɛ ni, ɔ́kpali katɔ na úti lɛla biala ɔ́kya Unwoti enu kemmo. Na ɔsɔ ɔ́kpali katɔ na úti lɛkpabi ku akyami ani nse mmɔ ƒui ɔ́kya Unwoti enu kemmo.

english_verse: Then the twelve tribal leaders of Israel, the same men who had been in charge of counting the people, came to the tent
translation_verse: Mmɔ na batɔnkune bani bédie bálɛku kaba biala kemmo na báka bekyuli bammɔ béti bana akpala bésienku Unwoti.

english_verse: with gifts for the Lord. They brought six strong carts and twelve oxen—one ox from each leader and a cart from every two.
translation_verse: Na ala ani béti bátábla akpala béte Unwoti mmɔ ndi bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ɛku ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ leevu-inyɔ bani ndubo kɛɛkɛ lɛmmɔ butaani na ɔtɔnkune biala úte unwi na batɔnkune bammɔ inyɔ biala béte ɔpɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ unwi. Ala amɛni na béti bésienku Unwoti Adi Kevo anumi.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: “Accept these gifts, so the Levites can use them here at the sacred tent for carrying the sacred things.”
translation_verse: “Ƒɔ akpala ammɔ siku batɔnkune bammɔ kudɔ na béti bataabla kabla na Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ lɛlɔ ala. Na ele ala ammɔ ete Lewini biala kalɛ na nwuna kabla kámanku.”

english_verse: Then Moses took the carts and oxen and gave them to the Levites,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose úti bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ bammɔ na úti-ma úte Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ,

english_verse: who were under the leadership of Ithamar son of Aaron. Moses gave two carts and four oxen to the Gershonites for their work, and four carts and eight oxen to the Merarites for their work.
translation_verse: na úti bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ine ku bakɔ maane úte Merari bebi na bana kabla kenye. Na bana ƒui bakya ɔkpane Aaron ubidi Itamar lɛlɔ bɔnu kalɔ.

english_verse: But Moses did not give any to the Kohathites, because they were in charge of the sacred objects that had to be carried on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Nsu Mose útete Kehat bebi ama ɔdi, ɔsika bana kabla ndi ka beteeti ala ani nse kedee mmɔ taasia bana amangba.

english_verse: On the day the altar was dedicated, the twelve leaders brought offerings for its dedication.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Mose ɔ́bla lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ sɛsɛɛ kede úte Unwoti ni, batɔnkune bammɔ béti bana akpala béboku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ anumi ka béti babla kabla kammɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Each day one leader is to give his offering for the dedication.”
translation_verse: Ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Limeyi biala ni, ɔtɔnkune unwi ɔlɛka uti nwuna akpala ani na badubuti babla akpala bete lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ bɔbla sɛsɛɛ kedee bete Unwoti uboku.”

english_verse: kilograms, according to the official standards;
translation_verse: ku ketukpa kenwi úte likpidi lili buvele akpala,

english_verse: rams a year old as sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing.
translation_verse: Na limeyi yaalenwidi lɛlɔ ni, Benyamin kaba bekyuli ɔtɔnkune ɔni ndi Gideoni ubidi Abidan úti nwuna akpala úboku.

english_verse: Whenever Moses needed to talk with the Lord, he went into the sacred tent, where he heard the Lord's voice coming from between the two winged creatures above the lid of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni Mose úduo Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo ka anwu ku Unwoti batɛmi ni, mmɔ kani na únu Unwoti lɛdi ɔ́siku ngba bebweyi inyɔ bani nnye bunyimi adaka likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie libila lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Mmɔ na anwu ku-nwu bátɛmi.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: “Tell Aaron to put the seven lamps on the lampstand so they shine toward the front.”
translation_verse: “Su Aaron anini, ‘Si éti lɛsogya maatɛ lɛmmɔ aalɛ ni, na anu ka lɛsogya lɛmmɔ bukeye bɔɔtina anumi kakɛ.’ ”

english_verse: The lampstand was made of hammered gold from its base to the decorative flowers on top, exactly like the pattern the Lord had described to Moses. Instructions for Ordaining the Levites
translation_verse: Ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na básia bábla lɛsogya lɛmmɔ ugyii ɔmmɔ ndi ka bétu sika ugyiedi bávɔ-nwu ɔ́si nwuna ɔka útédu kesii kani na bákya-nwu bɔdia ku egyii anwula. Na bávɔ asogya ugyii ɔmmɔ na ulu ɔni kani lɛlɔ na Unwoti ɔ́tina Mose. Bédie Lewiƒuɔ Bése Sɛsɛɛ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: The Levites must be acceptable to me before they begin working at the sacred tent. So separate them from the rest of the Israelites
translation_verse: “Die Lewiƒuɔ lɛku Israelƒuɔ bammɔ akɔ na abla-ma lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi.

english_verse: and sprinkle them with the water that washes away their sins. Then have them shave their entire bodies and wash their clothes.
translation_verse: Na ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na adubɔsia na abla-ma sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ. Kuna sɛɛn bɔbla ntu bɔmmɔ wi-ma lɛlɔ, na aya na bana ɔdi biala ukpeyi nwuna ɔlɔna linwini ƒui udie lɛlɔ na baƒɔ bana adala ƒui, na bana lɛlɔ lɛdubɔbla sɛɛn.

english_verse: They are to bring a bull and its proper grain sacrifice of flour mixed with olive oil. And they must bring a second bull as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama na beti akɔ ɔkɔdi ku edula ebi ɔlaaƒɔ buni sɛɛn ɔni na básala ku nnɔ, na asɔ aƒɔ akɔ ɔkɔdi bamba ute likpidi lili buvele akpala.

english_verse: Then you, Moses, will call together all the people of Israel and send the Levites to my sacred tent,
translation_verse: Na aya na Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bebenye Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ anumi, na asala Israel kadi bekyuli bammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: where the people will place their hands on them.
translation_verse: Na aya na Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui bebenye Unwoti anumi. Na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ beti bana enu basia-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Aaron will present the Levites to me as a gift from the people, so that the Levites will do my work.
translation_verse: Na Aaron ɔdubuti Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ɔkya Unwoti enu aani kadi bammɔ akpala ani na bákɔliku katɔ bátina-mi bébo-nya kudu.

english_verse: After this, the Levites are to place their hands on the heads of the bulls. Sacrifice one of the bulls for the forgiveness of sin, and the other to make sure that I am pleased. Then the Levites will be acceptable to me.
translation_verse: “Ɔmmɔ kama na Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ béti bana enu basia bakɔ bammɔ eli lɛlɔ. Na edie unwi abla likpidi lili buvele akpala ete Unwoti na eti unyɔdi lɛnɔ abla bɔkyula akpala ute Lewiƒuɔ likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie bana lɛlɔ.

english_verse: They will stand at my altar in front of Aaron and his sons, who will dedicate the Levites to me.
translation_verse: Na aya na Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ benye Aaron ku nwuna bebi anumi na eti-ma akya Unwoti lɛkɔkɔ aani kudu bubo akpala.

english_verse: This ceremony will show that the Levites are different from the other Israelites and belong to me in a special way.
translation_verse: Ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na adubudie Lewiƒuɔ sɛsɛɛ asiku Israelƒuɔ akɔ ete-mi na benwini mina badi.

english_verse: After they have been made acceptable and have been dedicated, they will be allowed to work at my sacred tent.
translation_verse: “Uwi ɔni na ábla-ma sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ áwɔlɔ na éti-ma ákya-mi kɔnu aani kudu bubo akpala kama ni, na aya bebo mina Adi Kevo kemmo babataabla bana kabla.

english_verse: When I killed the oldest sons of the Egyptians, I decided that the first-born sons in each Israelite family would be mine, as well as every first-born male from their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: Israelni ubi ɔnanabi udeedi iye ebuo ubi ɔgyani udeedi ɔni na báwɔ ɔdi mina ɔdi. Ɔsika uwi ɔni na lɛ́du Egyipteni ubi udeedi biala ni, uwi ɔmmɔ na lídie-ma líse líte lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But now I have chosen these Levites as substitutes for the first-born sons,
translation_verse: Na lɛ́ƒɔ Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ muunyene Israelƒuɔ bebi bedeedi bammɔ kenye.

english_verse: and I have given them as gifts to Aaron and his sons to serve at the sacred tent. I will hold them responsible for what happens to anyone who gets too close to the sacred tent. The Levites Are Dedicated to the Lord
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui akɔ na líti Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ muute Aaron ku nwuna bebi aani bana litela ka bataabla kabla na Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui kenye na bataabla akpala ute bana likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie kalɛ na ɔlɛ ukpidi ɔdi ulebo-ma lɛlɔ si uwi ɔni na báni béde Unwoti kakpakɔ kammɔ.”

english_verse: Moses, Aaron, and the other Israelites made sure that the Levites did everything the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Mose ku Aaron ku Israelƒuɔ ƒui ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bábla básiaku kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda mmɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: The Levites sprinkled themselves with the water of forgiveness and washed their clothes. Then Aaron brought them to the altar and offered sacrifices to forgive their sins and make them acceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Lewiƒuɔ bábla lɛlɔ sɛɛn bɔbla ɔdi ɔmmɔ na báƒɔ bana adala. Ɔmmɔ kama Aaron ɔ́kpanku-ma na útéti-ma ɔ́kya Unwoti lɛkɔkɔ aani kudu bubo akpala bana lili úte bana likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie kalɛ na ɔbla-ma sɛɛn.

english_verse: After this, the Levites worked at the sacred tent as assistants to Aaron and his sons, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bésie na bétése bana kabla kalɔ na Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo na Aaron ku nwuna bebi lɛlɔ bɔnu kalɔ. Na béti Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bábla kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda.

english_verse: The Lord also told Moses,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: They may help the other Levites in their duties, but they must no longer be responsible for any work themselves. Remember this when you assign their duties.”
translation_verse: Bebo kuƒi ka bete bana banwani kebunku na Unwoti Adi Kevo mmɔ, nsu utalɛka ama basɔ benye kabla kadi kenye ama alati. Anwuɔsu ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na adubɔsia na ele kabla ete Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ.”

english_verse: During the first month of Israel's second year in the Sinai Desert, the Lord had told Moses
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́tɛmiku Mose na Sinai ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo na lɛkwa linyɔdi kɔbuli kudeedi kemmo ka bálɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. Mmɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini,

english_verse: in the evening of the fourteenth day of this month and do it by following all the regulations.”
translation_verse: Na badi limeyi lɛmmɔ useyi uwi. Na kɔbuli kudeedi limeyi leevu-linedi lɛlɔ. Na badi limeyi lɛmmɔ basiaku kalɛ na líbo-ma ɔda pɛpɛɛpɛ.”

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had said, and they celebrated Passover there in the desert in the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month.
translation_verse: Na sɔsɔ ama lɛnɔ bádi limeyi lɛmmɔ na Sinai ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo na kɔbuli kudeedi limeyi leevu-linedi lɛlɔ useyi uwi. Na Israelƒuɔ bábla básiaku kalɛ kani na Unwoti úbo-ma ɔda.

english_verse: Some people in Israel's camp had touched a dead body and had become unfit to worship the Lord, and they could not celebrate Passover. But they asked Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Nsu bana badi bátakana na badi limeyi lɛmmɔ na bana lɛlɔ ukyuli ɔdi kukpi ɔsu. Ɔmmɔ ɔ́ya na básɔ na basɔ beeese sɛɛn na ukpine ɔmmɔ ɔsu. Anwuɔsu báni béde Mose ku Aaron limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ kani

english_verse: “Even though we have touched a dead body, why can't we celebrate Passover and offer sacrifices to the Lord at the same time as everyone else?”
translation_verse: na básu Mose banini, “Ka bula ukyuli ɔdi úkpi ɔsu ni, bɔ́nu ka buuuse sɛɛn, nsu bi ɔsu na abu bulakana bula akpala buti busienku Unwoti ku bula bakpana na limeyi lɛni na básu bése mmɔ lɛlɔ?”

english_verse: Moses said, “Wait here while I go into the sacred tent and find out what the Lord says about this.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose údie kenye na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛkɛ kayi utédu ka lɛ́tɛmiku Unwoti na bina litemi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord then told Moses
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: If any of you or your descendants touch a dead body and become unfit to worship me, or if you are away on a long journey, you may still celebrate Passover.
translation_verse: “Kɔ lɛsa na asu Israelƒuɔ anini, ‘Si úbo úte ka bina akɔ ɔdi ɔ́sɔ na uuuse sɛɛn ka nwuna lɛlɔ ukyuli ɔdi kukpi ɔsu iye nwuna ulu busie bɔdi ɔsu ni, bamu bebo kuƒi ka badi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi.

english_verse: But it must be done in the second month, in the evening of the fourteenth day. Eat the Passover lamb with thin bread and bitter herbs,
translation_verse: Na ɔlɛka badi limeyi lɛmmɔ na kɔbuli kunyɔdi limeyi leevu-linedi lɛlɔ useyi uwi. Na ɔlɛka bakun koƒonu ubi kɔmmɔ ku bodobodo ɔni na bɔnyii buuubo-nwu kemmo ku evete ani mbo ɔdu.

english_verse: and don't leave any of it until morning or break any of the animal's bones. Be sure to follow these regulations.
translation_verse: Na betebu ala ammɔ lɛdi betese na kadi kegye-ni lɛlɔ iye babwɛ likubi lɛdi lɛnɔ si baadi. Ɔƒɛni si baadi limeyi lɛmɛni ni, badi bunyimi bɔmmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ kaduɛ.

english_verse: But if any of you are fit to worship me, and yet refuse to celebrate Passover when you are not away on a journey, you will no longer belong to my people. You will be punished because you did not offer sacrifices to me at the proper time.
translation_verse: Nsu ukyuli ɔni na use sɛɛn na útesie ulu ɔdi lɛnɔ na úni limeyi lɛmmɔ bɔdi ni, ɔdi ka bedie-nwu nwuna badi akɔ, ɔsika úni nwuna akpala buti busienku Unwoti na uwi ɔni na bése bése lɛlɔ. Na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔlati ɔdubuti anwu ɔlati nwuna ekpidi etila.

english_verse: As soon as the sacred tent was set up, a thick cloud appeared and covered it. The cloud was there each day, and during the night, a fire could be seen in it.
translation_verse: Na lɛni kani úse uwi ƒui. Na liƒlukutu lɛmmɔ lɛ́ƒɔ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ƒui. Na si useyi údu ni, ɔɔda aani ogya kalɛ.

english_verse: whether it was only one night, a few days, a month, or even a year. As long as the cloud remained over the tent, the Israelites stayed where they were. But when the cloud moved, so did the Israelites.
translation_verse: Na si liƒlukutu lɛmmɔ lɛ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ linye ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ eli emeyi anyɔ iye kɔbuli iye lɛkwa ni, Israelƒuɔ bammɔ lɛnɔ badubɔsɔ bɔkya bana keliekɔ mmɔ lɛni kani na balata. Nsu si liƒlukutu lɛmmɔ lɛ́nya lɛ́ta na ama lɛnɔ bata.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: Have someone make two trumpets out of hammered silver. These will be used to call the people together and to give the signal for moving your camp.
translation_verse: “Tu sika ɔƒualadi na eti avɔ kɔkpɛɛ inyɔ, na eteeti-ku taalɔ Israelƒuɔ taasala ku kati bute uwi ɔni na bata bana keliekɔ bayu ulu.

english_verse: If both trumpets are blown, everyone is to meet with you at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Si bávwi kɔkpɛɛ inyɔ bɔmmɔ ni, na Israelƒuɔ ƒui ɔlɛka babasiaku-ɔ na Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ anumi.

english_verse: But if just one is blown, only the twelve tribal leaders need to come together.
translation_verse: Nsu si bávwi kakpɛɛ kenwi ni, na ɔɔtina ka benengu bammɔ ku baduɔti bammɔ ƒui ɔlɛka babasa-a kudɔ na Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ anumi.

english_verse: Give a signal on a trumpet when it is time to break camp. The first blast will be the signal for the tribes camped on the east side, and the second blast will be the signal for those on the south.
translation_verse: Na si básɔ bénu-ka bɔvwi lɛni kani kunyɔdi ni, na adua ani náda keliekɔ na kada kakɛ na ɔlɛka bata bana keliekɔ bayu ulu. Kɔkpɛɛ bɔvi klukwii ɔmɛni ndubɔbla kati bute uwi ɔni na bata bayu ulu.

english_verse: But when you want everyone to come together, sound a different signal on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bɔlɔ bɔsala ni, ɔlɛka kɔkpɛɛ kɔmmɔ bɔvwi bɔvumana ku kati bute kalɛ na bata bayu ulu.

english_verse: The priests of Aaron's family will be the ones to blow the trumpets, and this law will never change.
translation_verse: “Na Aaron bebi bani ndi bakpane ndubo kɔkpɛɛ kɔmmɔ butaavwi. Na ɔda bubo bɔmɛni buse bute-mii uwi ƒui ku bina bawɔ bawɔ.

english_verse: Whenever you go into battle against an enemy attacking your land, give a warning signal on the trumpets. Then I, the Lord, will hear it and rescue you.
translation_verse: Na si bɛ́ta bɛnii biikpóku bina bekisine bani na banii babaƒɔ-mii kalɔ ni, na bɛvwi kakpɛɛ kammɔ kɔnakunwi. Na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubo-mii bunyimo na ukpo ɔƒɔ-mii na bina bekisine enu kemmo.

english_verse: During the celebration of the New Moon Festival and other religious festivals, sound the trumpets while you offer sacrifices. This will be a reminder that I am the Lord your God. The Israelites Begin Their Journey
translation_verse: Na bina lɛlɔyɔ emeyi ku emeyi ani na bɛ́lɛ ugyii bíse aani kɔbuli kɔwɔdi bɔlɛ ku abamba ni, bɛvwi kɔkpɛɛ kɔmmɔ na bɔkyula akpala ku unwi bɔbla akpala ammɔ lili na adubunwini bina lɛlɔ enyimo ete Unwoti na bina lili. Ami ndi bina Unwoti Katɔti.” Israelƒuɔ Báta Sinai Ketele Kemmo Bátɔlɔ

english_verse: On the twentieth day of the second month of that same year, the cloud over the sacred tent moved on.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa linyɔdi kɔbuli kunyɔdi limeyi aavlanyɔdi lɛlɔ ka Israelƒuɔ bálɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, liƒlukutu lɛmmɔ lɛ́sɔ lɛ́ta na Unwoti Adi Kevo lɛlɔ.

english_verse: So the Israelites broke camp and left the Sinai Desert. And some time later, the cloud stopped in the Paran Desert.
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ báta Sinai ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo mmɔ báyu ulu na bávi ekpo ekpo. Na liƒlukutu lɛmmɔ lítáyu lílie Para ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo.

english_verse: This was the first time the Lord had told Moses to command the people of Israel to move on.
translation_verse: Na kudeedi kɔmɛni na báta báyu ulu na Unwoti ɔda bubo kenye ɔkɛnku Mose lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Judah and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out first, carrying their banner. Nahshon son of Amminadab was the leader of the Judah tribe,
translation_verse: Na Yuda kaba bekyuli náka bɔta na bana esu kenye ku bana likposela na Aminadab ubidi Nahason ndi bana ɔtɔnkune.

english_verse: Nethanel son of Zuar was the leader of the Issachar tribe,
translation_verse: Na Suar ubidi Netaneel ɔtɔnku Isakar kaba bekyuli lisu.

english_verse: and Eliab son of Helon was the leader of the Zebulun tribe.
translation_verse: Na Helon ubidi Eliab ɔtɔnku Sebulon kaba bekyuli lisu.

english_verse: The sacred tent had been taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites carried it, marching behind the Judah camp.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama bégyingya Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ na Gerson bebi ku Merari bebi bani nti-ka lɛnɔ báyu ulu.

english_verse: Reuben and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out second, carrying their banner. Elizur son of Shedeur was the leader of the Reuben tribe,
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni Ruben kaba bekyuli násia-ma kama, na bana esu esu kenye, na Seleur ubidi Elisur ɔtɔnku-ma ku bana likposela.

english_verse: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was the leader of the Simeon tribe,
translation_verse: Na Surisadai ubidi Selumiel ɔtɔnku Simeon kaba bekyuli lisu.

english_verse: and Eliasaph son of Deuel was the leader of the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: Na Deuel ubidi Eliasaƒ ɔtɔnku Gad kaba bekyuli lisu.

english_verse: Next were the Kohathites, carrying the objects for the sacred tent, which was to be set up before they arrived at the new camp.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Kehat kaba bekyuli bani nti Unwoti Adi Kevo kemmo ala kedee basia. Na ɔdi ka balɛ Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ asa na ama betédu mmɔ.

english_verse: Ephraim and the tribes that camped alongside it marched next, carrying their banner. Elishama son of Ammihud was the leader of the Ephraim tribe,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Eƒraim kaba bekyuli nsia na bana esu esu kenye, na Amihud ubidi Elisama ɔtɔnku-ma ku bana likpose aƒlaga.

english_verse: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was the leader of the Manasseh tribe,
translation_verse: Na Pedahsur ubidi Gamaliel ɔtɔnku Manase kaba bekyuli lisu.

english_verse: and Abidan son of Gideoni was the leader of the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Na Gideoni ubidi Abidan ɔtɔnku Benyamin kaba bekyuli lisu.

english_verse: Dan and the tribes that camped alongside it were to protect the Israelites against an attack from behind, and so they marched last, carrying their banner. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was the leader of the tribe of Dan,
translation_verse: Amu na kawɔlɔkɔ ƒui ni, Dan kaba bekyuli bakpɛ kama na bana esu kenye aani lisu likplodi. Na Amisadai bidi Ahieser ɔtɔnku-ma ku bana likposela.

english_verse: Pagiel son of Ochran was the leader of the Asher tribe,
translation_verse: Na Okran ubidi Pagiel ɔtɔnku Aser kaba bekyuli lisu.

english_verse: and Ahira son of Enan was the leader of the Naphtali tribe.
translation_verse: Na Enan ubidi Ahira ɔtɔnku Naƒtali kaba bekyuli lisu.

english_verse: This was the order in which the Israelites marched each time they moved their camp.
translation_verse: Na lɛni na Israelƒuɔ kaba bekyuli esu esu ammɔ béti bésie bana ulu ɔmmɔ ka báyu ulu.

english_verse: Hobab the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses, was there. And Moses said to him, “We're leaving for the place the Lord has promised us. He has said that all will go well for us. So come along, and we will make sure that all goes well for you.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su ulekudi ɔti Hobab ɔni ndi Midiani ɔni baalɔ Reuel ubidi ɔnini, “Uwi údu ka buteesie kalɔ kani na Unwoti ɔ́su úse ɔnini, ‘Ndubuti-ka lite-mii,’ mmɔ lɛlɔ. Bo na abasiaku-bu, na bɔdubɔda-a kaduɛ, ɔsika Unwoti úse ala abuni kenye úte Israelƒuɔ.”

english_verse: “No, I won't go,” Hobab answered. “I'm returning home to be with my own people.”
translation_verse: Amu na Hobab údie kenye ɔnini, “Oowo, lɛɛɛdubo mmɔ busie, mmomu línwini lísela mina bati ku beni kalɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: “Please go with us!” Moses said. “You can be our guide because you know the places to camp in the desert.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mose ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Buvele nda-a tatɔlɔ-bu kudɔ. Ɔsika agyi kesii kani búsela bútáda bula keliekɔ na ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo, na adubɔbla ɔtɔnkune ete-bu.

english_verse: Besides that, if you go, we will give you a share of the good things the Lord gives us.”
translation_verse: Na si asiaku-bu ni, ala abuni ani na Unwoti ɔdubute-bu mmɔ ni, abu ku-ɔ ƒui bɔdubule-nya.”

english_verse: The people of Israel began their journey from Mount Sinai. They traveled three days, and the Levites who carried the sacred chest led the way, so the Lord could show them where to camp.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israelƒuɔ báta Sinai kɔbi kedee kaƒɔna mmɔ na bésie emeyi atɛ. Na Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔtɔ-ma emeyi atɛ ammɔ ƒui kalɛ na utáwia keliekɔ kadi ute-ma na banwuna.

english_verse: And the cloud always stayed with them.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti liƒlukutu lɛmmɔ lɛɛƒa-ma katɔ ɔƒiiwi ɔ́si ɔni na báta bakɛ ulu.

english_verse: Each day as the Israelites began their journey, Moses would pray, “Our Lord, defeat your enemies and make them run!”
translation_verse: Na uwi biala na Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ ɔdubo bɔgyu ni, Mose uudie kudu kɔmɛni, “Unwoti ta! Na ƒula bekisine begyingya. Na aya na bani muukisi-ɔ bekeli na ƒula anumi.”

english_verse: And when they stopped to set up camp, he would pray, “Our Lord, stay close to Israel's thousands and thousands of people.”
translation_verse: Na uwi biala na Adaka ɔmmɔ ɔdubo budi bunye na Mose ɔsɔ udie kudu ɔnini, “Unwoti, yu bo, Israelƒuɔ bekyuli mpim mpim akɔ.”

english_verse: One day the Israelites started complaining about their troubles. The Lord heard them and became so angry that he destroyed the outer edges of their camp with fire.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti únu ka Israelƒuɔ bamɛni bésie kalɔ beetemi enyekpi taasiku-nwu lɛlɔ na lɛbibo lɛni baasiáku ɔsu. Na ka Unwoti únu bana etemila ammɔ ni, úti kɔnyi kaduɛ. Na ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́ya na ogya ɔ́si katɔ na úbakyula ala na bana keliekɔ mmɔ amadɔ.

english_verse: When the people begged Moses to help, he prayed, and the fire went out.
translation_verse: Na ka bákpali Mose ni, úvele Unwoti na ogya ɔmmɔ úni.

english_verse: They named the place “Burning,” because in his anger the Lord had set their camp on fire. The People Grumble about Being Hungry
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu básia kesii kani na ogya ɔmmɔ ɔ́kyula mmɔ lɛnyi banii Tabera, na nwuna kalɔ ndi bɔkywi. Ɔsika ogya ɔ́si Unwoti kudɔ úbakyula ala bana akɔ. Unwoti Úte Israelƒuɔ Baasɛ Wɛlɛwɛlɛ Badi

english_verse: One day some foreigners among the Israelites became greedy for food, and even the Israelites themselves began moaning, “We don't have any meat!
translation_verse: Amu na baƒɔ bani nsiaku Israelƒuɔ na ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo ku Israelƒuɔ alati bésie kalɔ baawia adila ani badi. Ɔmɛni ɔsu bése kalɔ baasu banini, “Si nka bɔkɛ lɛna lɛdi nka bɔdubɔkun.

english_verse: In Egypt we could eat all the fish we wanted, and there were cucumbers, melons, all kinds of onions, and garlic.
translation_verse: Buunyimo lɛna lɛni bútaakun uwi ɔni bɔ́kya Egyipte, na lɛna lɛmmɔ lítaƒɔ kuye kɔdi, ku egyiibi, ku alakpi lidu, ku kutu akyala aani abuala ku nwuna udu ani ƒui na bútaadi mmɔ lɛnɔ.

english_verse: But we're starving out here, and the only food we have is this manna.”
translation_verse: Nsu ɔƒɛni bɔsɔ bulakɛ adila bamba biala taadi amu ntu manna ɔmɛni kani, na anwu lɛnɔ úukpi-bu ɔkwɛ.”

english_verse: The manna was like small whitish seeds
translation_verse: Na manna ɔmɛni use aani kakpa kebi ƒuala ƒuala.

english_verse: and tasted like something baked with sweet olive oil. It appeared at night with the dew. In the morning the people would collect the manna, grind or crush it into flour, then boil it and make it into thin wafers.
translation_verse: Na si amii áyu éwi kesii kani na Israelƒuɔ belie mmɔ usien ni, na manna ɔmɛni lɛnɔ ɔ́ɔyu úbewi kalɔ.

english_verse: He prayed: I am your servant, Lord, so why are you doing this to me? What have I done to deserve this? You've made me responsible for all these people,
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mose ɔ́kpali Unwoti ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na éti etila amɛni udu ásia-mi ƒula kabla ɔblane lɛlɔ lɛni? Bi na lɛ́bla-a na útayɔ-ɔ kaƒɔ ɔsu na eti bekyuli bamɛni ƒui etila asia-mi lɛlɔ?

english_verse: but they're not my children. You told me to nurse them along and to carry them to the land you promised their ancestors.
translation_verse: Ami náda bekyuli bamɛni ƒui kaƒɔ, munuu ami náwɔ-ma? Na bi ɔsu na aayɔ́ ka ntaagyu-ma taada enu kemmo aani kalɛ na ukyuli ɔni mɔɔda ubi ɔɔbla, asa na lɛkpanku-ma lisienku kalɔ kani na ése bana bati kuuku kenye ka adubute-ma kemmo?

english_verse: They keep whining for meat, but where can I get meat for them?
translation_verse: Wɛ na ndubo lɛna bɔkɛ bute bekyuli bamɛni? Bakya beewulo kɔnyana taakpali-mi banii ‘Te-bu lɛna lɛdi na bɔkun!’

english_verse: This job is too much for me. How can I take care of all these people by myself?
translation_verse: Kabla kamɛni kétulo-mi na naaakana bekyuli bamɛni ƒui bɔtɔnku ami lɛti.

english_verse: If this is the way you're going to treat me, just kill me now and end my miserable life! Seventy Leaders Are Chosen To Help Moses
translation_verse: Na si lɛni na adubo-mi bɔbla bɔdi ni, si áya-mi na líkpi muedi ɔdia-mi utulo si ɔ́yɔ-ɔ kaƒɔ lɛni, na taya na lisie ntásiaku mina ɔgbankpi ɔdi.”

english_verse: While I am talking with you there, I will give them some of your authority, so they can share responsibility for my people. You will no longer have to care for them by yourself.
translation_verse: Na si bébenye mmɔ ni, ndubɔyu bubo-mii kudɔ na lɛtɛmiku-mii. Na mmɔ ni, ndubɔya na mina kɔyu kɔni nkya-a kemmo kɔdi kɔlɛ na liti ku lɛkya bana kemmo ɔdi. Na ama ndubo-ɔ kebunku buteete. Na betiku-ɔ bekyuli bammɔ etila. Kalɛ na asɔ eleti etila ammɔ awɔ lɛti.

english_verse: As for the Israelites, I have heard them complaining about not having meat and about being better off in Egypt. So tell them to make themselves acceptable to me, because tomorrow they will have meat.
translation_verse: “Su bekyuli bammɔ anini, ‘Bikisi lɛlɔ na bɛbla lɛlɔ sɛɛn bite kɔnaadi limeyi lɛni na bɛdubo lɛna bɔkun. Unwoti únu uwi ɔni na bɛkya biiwulo kɔnya bɛnii, “Si bɔkɛ na bɔkɛ lɛna lɛdi bɔkun nka ɔdia, ɔsika uwi ɔni na bɔ́kya Egyipte ni, ala ádianku-bu étulo ɔmɛni!”

english_verse: Even if we butchered all our sheep and cattle, or caught every fish in the sea, we wouldn't have enough to feed them.”
translation_verse: Na si ina baƒonu ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ ɛlɛ ɛlɛ na bádu béte-ma muedi lɛna lɛmmɔ lɛdubudu-ma? Na si ketu kemmo kɔbɛ ƒui na béƒie béte-ma lɛnɔ nɔɔ ɔdubudu-ma bɔkun?”

english_verse: Eldad and Medad were two leaders who had not gone to the tent. But when the Spirit took control of them, they began shouting like prophets right there in camp.
translation_verse: Nsu banana inyɔ bádi bákya na baalɔ-ma Eldad ku Medad na báƒuna ama lɛnɔ bákya benengu bammɔ akɔ, nsu báƒɔ lɛlɔ bákya bana nvo kemmo mmɔ na bétesie kasakɔ mmɔ, nsu Kɔyu kɔmmɔ kɔ́ƒɔ-ma lɛlɔ kemmo na ama lɛnɔ bákya béteedie Unwoti ablala kenye na bana kakyakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: A boy ran to Moses and told him about Eldad and Medad.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na okloƒu ɔdi úkeli usi na útásu Mose ka Eldad ku Medad lɛnɔ bakya beedie Unwoti ablala kenye bana kakyakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Joshua was there helping Moses, as he had done since he was young. And he said to Moses, “Sir, you must stop them!”
translation_verse: Amu na Nun ubidi ɔni baalɔ banii Yosua na anwu nsiaku Mose kesi kesii na úsela ɔ́si nwuna lɛkloƒu uwi ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Ati, ya na bekyuli bammɔ bada Unwoti ablala kudu bubo baya.”

english_verse: But Moses replied, “Are you concerned what this might do to me? I wish the Lord would give his Spirit to all his people so everyone could be a prophet.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mose údie-nwu kenye ɔnini, “Anumi eegyie-ɔ mina lɛlɔ yoo? Si nka ami lɛti ni, nka Unwoti bekyuli ƒui benwini nwuna kenye bediene na Unwoti ɔya na nwuna kɔyu kɔƒɔ-ma lɛlɔ kemmo!”

english_verse: Some time later the Lord sent a strong wind that blew quails in from the sea until Israel's camp was completely surrounded with birds, piled up about a meter high for many kilometers in every direction.
translation_verse: Kɔnakunwi Unwoti ɔ́ya na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ubendi ɔdi úkpo na ɔ́sala baasɛ wɛlɛ wɛlɛ badi ɔ́siku ɛpu kudɔ. Na bakya beeveyi taavi kalɔ kalɔ. Na bébo bewi bekyuli bammɔ kakyakɔ mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: The people picked up quails for two days—each person filled at least ten large baskets. Then they spread them out to dry.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́si limeyi lɛmmɔ ku kadi kegye usien ku ɔƒɛ bekyuli bammɔ bakya baala baasɛ bamɛni. Na ukyuli biala ɔ́la baasɛ bamɛni aani edula ebi lɛkyami linwi unu. Na bégyingya baasɛ bamɛni béwi ɔƒɛ lɛlɔ kalɛ bakwii.

english_verse: But before the meat could be eaten, the Lord became angry and sent a deadly disease through the camp.
translation_verse: Nsu asa na badubɔkun lɛna lɛmɛni bebweli ni, Unwoti úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya bekyuli bammɔ geen na ɔ́ya na ɔlɛ ukpidi ɔni mɔɔví úduo-ma akɔ.

english_verse: After they had buried the people who had been so greedy for meat, they called the place “Graves for the Greedy.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na baalɔ kesii kammɔ banii Kibrot-Hataawa. Na nwuna kalɔ ndi ɔkwɛ adala kaƒiɔtɔ. Ɔsika mmɔ na báva bekyuli bani nkya muuwulo ka lɛna lɛɛda-ma ɔkwɛ.

english_verse: Israel then broke camp and traveled to Hazeroth.
translation_verse: Ka bekyuli bammɔ báta Kibrot-Hataawa mmɔ ni, bésie bétéli Haserot.

english_verse: and told Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to come to the entrance of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Kɔnakunwi Unwoti ɔ́kpali Mose ku Aaron ku Miriam ɔnini, “Bina ɛtɛ ƒui bɛlɛ bibo Unwoti Adi Kevo mɛni.” Anwuɔsu bana ɛtɛ bammɔ ƒui bálɛ bébo.

english_verse: There the Lord appeared in a cloud and told Aaron and Miriam to come closer.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́yu úbo kalɔ na liƒlukutu bonwu kemmo, na úbenye Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ anumi na ɔ́lɔ Aaron ku Miriam. Ka bálɛ bébo ni,

english_verse: Then after commanding them to listen carefully, he said: “I, the Lord, speak to prophets in visions and dreams.
translation_verse: ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Binu etemila ani ndubo-mii bɔsu mɛni. “Si Unwoti kenye udiene ɔdi ɔkya-mii akɔ ni, muudie lɛlɔ taatina-nwu na kɔyu kemmo ala budie bɔtina kemmo iye kɔna kemmo na mɔɔtɛmiku-nwu.

english_verse: He sees me face to face, and everything I say to him is perfectly clear. You have no right to criticize my servant Moses.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔtɛmi ku anwu anumi ku anumi, na ɔɔɔdi agyolo kemmo, mmomu atɛ nwaa kemmo, na ɔɔnu kalɛ na Unwoti use ku nwuna anumi. Na bi ɔsu na bítayia ka bɛsu lɛla lɛdi na bɛ́ta bínye mina kabla ɔblane Mose lɛlɔ?”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Aaron and Miriam. And after the Lord left
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti kɔnyi kúbakɔ katɔ na Aaron ku Miriam lɛlɔ, na ɔ́gyu-ma kudɔ na ɔ́tɔlɔ.

english_verse: and the cloud disappeared from over the sacred tent, Miriam's skin turned white with leprosy. When Aaron saw what had happened to her,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na liƒlukutu lɛmmɔ lɛ́ta na Adi Kevo ɔmmɔ eli ni, amu na ɔlɛgyie ɔ́lɛ úwi Miriam lɛlɔ, na nwuna ɔlɔna ɔ́ta ɔ́bla ƒututuu aani etubankɛ. Uwi ɔni na Aaron únwini na ɔ́nu ka ɔlɛgyie uwi Miriam lɛlɔ ni,

english_verse: he said to Moses, “Sir, please don't punish us for doing such a foolish thing.
translation_verse: ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Mina ati, buvele nda-a, tenye tanu na kɔdɔlɔ likpidi lɛni bɔ́bla mɛni lɛtuni lɛsiaku-bu.

english_verse: Don't let Miriam's flesh rot away like a child born dead!”
translation_verse: Na taya na Miriam únwini ubi ɔni báwɔ na útata ntu kemmo na nwuna ɔlɔna kakɛ kadi lɛnɔ káyii udu.”

english_verse: But the Lord replied, “Miriam would be disgraced for seven days if her father had punished her by spitting in her face. So make her stay outside the camp for seven days, before coming back.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti údie Mose kenye ɔnini, “Si nka bɔbwɛ na ɔti ɔ́bwɛ lisuo úwi Miriam anumi ni, nka kɔƒa kɔɔɔdubo-nwu bukpo emeyi maatɛ? Anwuɔsu biti-nwu bɛlɛku bina kakyakɔ mmɔ emeyi maatɛ. Na ɔmmɔ kama bɛsɔ bitiku-nwu biboku.”

english_verse: The people of Israel did not move their camp until Miriam returned seven days later.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu báda Miriam bédie bana kakyakɔ mmɔ emeyi maatɛ, na bekyuli bammɔ lɛnɔ básɔ bátata bana keliekɔ mmɔ útédu ka emeyi maatɛ ammɔ édu. Na básɔku-nwu béboku.

english_verse: Then they left Hazeroth and set up camp in the Paran Desert.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama bekyuli bammɔ báta Haserot na bétélie Paran ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: In fact, we saw the Nephilim who are the ancestors of the Anakim. They were so big that we felt as small as grasshoppers.”
translation_verse: Na bɔ́nu bekyuli bani náta katɔ na bási Anak kaba kemmo muedi na mmɔ. Na abu buse na buse aani bakpɔtilikpɔ na bana anumi. Na lɛni na badubo-bu bɔnu.”

english_verse: “Choose a leader from each tribe and send them into Canaan to explore the land I am giving you.”
translation_verse: “Die ukyuli unwi unwi na Israel kaba leevu-anyɔ ammɔ batɔnkune akɔ, na besie batánu Kanaan kalɔ kani na lɛ́su ka meti mete Israelƒuɔ mmɔ kemmo banu kalɛ kalɔ kammɔ kese.”

english_verse: Before Moses sent them into Canaan, he said: After you go through the Southern Desert of Canaan, continue north into the hill country
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Mose ɔ́tala bekyuli bammɔ ɔnii batávi banu Kanaan kalɔ kammɔ ni, ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Si bísela ni, na bɛsia Negev kalɔ kemmo na biti bɛkɔ bisie abi lɛma kalɔ kammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: and find out what those regions are like. Be sure to remember how many people live there, how strong they are,
translation_verse: Na bɛnu kalɛ kalɔ kammɔ kese ku bekyuli bammɔ si badi bekyuli bani mbo ɔlɔkplu iye beeebo ɔlɔkplu, ku si bemomo iye beeemomo.

english_verse: and if they live in open towns or walled cities. See if the land is good for growing crops and find out what kinds of trees grow there. It's time for grapes to ripen, so try to bring back some of the fruit that grows there.
translation_verse: Na kalɔ kammɔ lɛti nɔɔ, dɛ na lise, lɛdia munuu lɛɛɛdia? Na egyii akya kalɔ kammɔ kemmo munuu eeebo? Bɛsia ulu biala lɛlɔ na biti adingyii ebi adi bɛsiku kalɔ kammɔ kemmo biboku si bɛdubo.” Na uwi ɔmmɔ ɔdi adingyii ebi edeedi bugyie uwi.

english_verse: The twelve men left to explore Canaan from the Zin Desert in the south all the way to the town of Rehob near Lebo-Hamath in the north.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu bekyuli bamɛni báyu ulu na bátávi bánu kalɔ kammɔ ɔ́si Sin ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo útédu Rehab, kesii kani baasia teesie Hamat.

english_verse: As they went through the Southern Desert, they came to the town of Hebron, which was seven years older than the Egyptian town of Zoan. In Hebron, they saw the three Anakim clans of Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai.
translation_verse: Na básia Negev kalɔ kemmo na bákɔ bétédu Hebron, kesii kani na Anak kaba kemmo bekyuli bani ndi Ahiman ku Sesai ku Talmai bélie. Báada Hebron ɔma akwa maatɛ kama asa na báda Soan ɔma ɔni nkya Egyipte.

english_verse: the twelve men returned to Kadesh in the Paran Desert and told Moses, Aaron, and the people what they had seen. They showed them the fruit
translation_verse: Amu na batalane bammɔ ƒui bénwini bébo na básala Mose ku Aaron ku Israelƒuɔ ƒui lisu na Paran ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo na Kedes. Mmɔ na básu-ma ala ani bánu na béti egyiibi ani béde na kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ adi bátina-ma.

english_verse: But the people who live there are strong, and their cities are large and walled. We even saw the three Anakim clans.
translation_verse: Nsu bɔɔsu-ɔ ka bekyuli bani nlie mmɔ ni, bebo ɔyikun geen, na bana lɛma linengudi ƒui lɛnɔ bátu awodu bámana-ni. Na mmɔ muedi na bɔ́nu Anak kaba bekyuli.

english_verse: Besides that, the Amalekites live in the Southern Desert; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites are in the hill country; and the Canaanites live along the Mediterranean Sea and the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Amalekƒuɔ belie bésie Negev kalɔ kemmo na Hetiƒuɔ ku Yebusiƒuɔ ku Amoriƒuɔ ama belie abi eli. Na Kanaanƒuɔ belie bésie ɛpu amadɔ na Yordan kakɛ.”

english_verse: Caleb calmed down the crowd and said, “Let's go and take the land. I know we can do it!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Kaleb údie lɛdi na ɔ́ya na bekyuli bammɔ bába lɛsɛ na Mose anumi na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛya na busie butéti kalɔ kammɔ, ɔsika bɔdubɔkana bukpo na bɔdi-ma lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: But the other men replied, “Those people are much too strong for us.”
translation_verse: Nsu bekyuli bani na ama ku Kaleb bésie mmɔ bénye momoomo básu banii, “Bulakana-ma bukpoku, ɔsika bebo ɔyikun betulo-bu.”

english_verse: Then they started spreading rumors and saying, “We won't be able to grow anything in that soil. And the people are like giants.
translation_verse: Na batalane bamɛni bégyingya bana etemila ekpidi amɛni bákya Israelƒuɔ akɔ. Na básu-ma banini, “Kalɔ kammɔ muedi kalákana edula bɔnwu kaduɛ. Na bekyuli bani udu nli kalɔ kammɔ kemmo bákuku na bébomo.

english_verse: and complained to Moses and Aaron, “We wish we had died in Egypt or somewhere out here in the desert!
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu bekyuli bammɔ bákya baadɔnku Mose ku Aaron kalɔ kalɔ. Na baasu banini, “Si bukpi na búkpi bɔ́kya Egyipte iye ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo mmɔ muedi nka ɔdia utulo!

english_verse: Is the Lord leading us into Canaan, just to have us killed and our women and children captured? We'd be better off in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na bi ɔsu na Unwoti úti-bu úboku kalɔ kamɛni kemmo na bubekpi na kewii kenye? Bula bekisine badubo bula beleku ku bebi buƒie bɔtɔlɔku. Ɔɔɔdia-bu uuutulo ka bɔsɔ bunwini buteesie Egyipte mmomu?”

english_verse: Then they said to one another, “Let's choose our own leader and go back.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu básu lɛlɔ ka, “Bɛya na bɔwia ɔtɔnkune na bɔsɔ bunwini buteesie Egyipte.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron bowed down to pray in front of the crowd.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mose ku Aaron báyu bebi kalɔ na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui anumi.

english_verse: and said: We saw the land ourselves, and it's very good.
translation_verse: Na básu Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui banini, “Kalɔ kani kemmo na bútávi bɔnu mmɔ kadia geen sɔsɔ.

english_verse: If we obey the Lord, he will surely give us that land rich with milk and honey.
translation_verse: Na bɔɔsu-mii ka si ɔ́yɔ Unwoti kaƒɔ ni, ɔdubɔtɔnku-bu na butéduo kalɔ kani kana egyiibi ntu bɔɔyu emini aani uwɔ na kana lɛlɔ bebuo baayu anyi ntu pii na kabla bula kadi.

english_verse: So don't rebel. We have no reason to be afraid of the people who live there. The Lord is on our side, and they won't stand a chance against us!
translation_verse: Na bɔta kani na bitata bitenye Unwoti lɛlɔ. Na bitaya na liƒu lɛdi lɛda-mii na bekyuli bani nkya kalɔ kammɔ kemmo lɛlɔ ɔsu. Ɔsika basɔ beeebo bɔgyumana bɔdi, nsu Unwoti uli ku abu na bɔdubo-ma bubweli. Anwuɔsu bitayia!”

english_verse: The crowd threatened to stone Moses and Aaron to death. But just then, the Lord appeared in a cloud at the sacred tent. Moses Prays for the People
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bábla kasusu ka badubo Yosua ku Kaleb atabi bubo ni, mmɔ na Unwoti bukeye bɔ́bwɛ bɔ́lɛ Unwoti Adi Kevo anumi na Israelƒuɔ bánu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I have done great things for these people, and they still reject me by refusing to believe in my power.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti úye Mose ɔnini, “Na akɔla ala lidu lidu lɛni na lɛ́bla na bekyuli bamɛni anumi kama ni, uwi ɛlɛ na badubuni-mi bétédu, na baláƒɔ-mi baladi, na bataata teenye taanu-mi anumi lɛni?

english_verse: So they will no longer be my people. I will destroy them, but I will make you the ancestor of a nation even stronger than theirs.”
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ndubo ɔ́lɛ buɛ ɔdi buti bɔkya bekyuli bammɔ akɔ na lɛyila-ma udu. Nsu awɔ Mose anwu ni, ndubo bɔya na kadi bekyuli pii bani na bemomo betulo bamɛni balɛ basi-ɔ kemmo na bayu ɔkplu lɛnɔ betulo-ma.”

english_verse: Show us your great power, Lord. You promised
translation_verse: “Ɔmɛni ɔsu muuvele-ɔ, O Unwoti, die ƒula ɔyikun unengudi keyi aani kalɛ na ásu ése anii,

english_verse: that you love to show mercy and kindness. And you said that you are very patient, but that you will punish everyone guilty of doing wrong—not only them but their children and grandchildren as well.
translation_verse: ‘Ami Unwoti ndi Katɔti ɔni mɔɔnu kɔnyana, na mɔɔbla lɛƒɔndia uwi ƒui, na neeeti kɔnyi pla pla. Mmomu mɔɔyɔ́ mina bekyuli na muuti bani nénwini kama bákya bana ulikplu ala ku bani mɔɔta teenye-mi lɛlɔ ku ekpidi ƒui taakyiɛ. Nsu mɔɔní bekyuli bani mɔɔƒiɔ́-mi ƒui kɔtu. Naaayiƒala kudii ka lɛni bana bebi ku bawɔ kɔtu utédu kaba katɛdi ku kenedi lɛlɔ ɔ́si ekpidi ani na bana bawɔne bábla ɔsu.’

english_verse: You are merciful, and you treat people better than they deserve. So please forgive these people, just as you have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛnku ƒula lɛƒɔndia bonwu ɔsu ni, ti bana ekpidi kyiɛ-ma aani kalɛ kani na eeti takyiɛ-ma ɔ́si uwi ɔni na bɔ́lɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ úbedu ɔƒaani.”

english_verse: But as surely as I live and my power has no limit,
translation_verse: Nsu mɔɔsu geen ka ni, ami Unwoti ɔni nli ngba na mina bukeye bɔ́ƒɔ kayawi ƒui mɛni ni,

english_verse: I swear that not one of these Israelites will enter the land I promised to give their ancestors. These people have seen my power in Egypt and in the desert, but they will never see Canaan. They have disobeyed and tested me too many times.
translation_verse: bana kemmo ɔdi biala ulanu kalɔ kani líse kenye ka meti mete bana bati kuuku mmɔ. Na ukyuli biala nétenu-mi litemi na ɔbu-mi uleduo mmɔ.

english_verse: But my servant Caleb isn't like the others. So because he has faith in me, I will allow him to cross into Canaan, and his descendants will settle there.
translation_verse: Nsu ka mina kabla ɔblane Kaleb anwu úbo kɔyu kɔni návumana na úti nwuna kayi ƒui ɔsiaku-mi kama ɔsu ni, ndubuti anwu ku nwuna kaba bekyuli na betéduo kalɔ kammɔ kemmo na badubo kalɔ kammɔ ala bɔdi.

english_verse: Now listen, Moses! The Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valleys of Canaan. And tomorrow, you'll need to turn around and head back into the desert toward the Red Sea. The Israelites Are Punished for Complaining
translation_verse: Na ka Amalekƒuɔ ku Kanaanƒuɔ belie bésie kɔwɛ kemmo ɔsu ni, kɔnaadi binwini bitásia ketele kalɔ kakwiidi ulu ɔni na úti anumi ɔɔtina Ɛpugyie mmɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ku Aaron ɔnini,

english_verse: to give this message to the people of Israel: You sinful people have complained against me too many times! Now I swear by my own life that I will give you exactly what you wanted.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu kɔ lɛsa na asu-ma anini, ‘Ami Unwoti nnii na ami ɔni nli ngba mɛni anumi ni, lɛla lɛni na línu lɛ́siku-mii kenye kemmo mɛni na ndubɔya na lɛlɛku-mii.

english_verse: will enter the land that I solemnly promised to give you as your own—only Caleb and Joshua will go in.
translation_verse: Ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kamɛni kemmo na bɛdubo bukpi, amii bani ƒui nákɛ akwa aavlanyɔ ku kama, amu ntu Yeƒune ubidi Kaleb ku Nun ubidi Yosua kani ndubo mmɔ buduo.

english_verse: You were worried that your own children would be captured. But I, the Lord, will let them enter the land you have rejected.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na bina bebi bani mmomu na bɛ́kya bɛɛsu bɛnii badubo-ma buƒie batɔlɔku mmɔ ni, ama na ndubo bɔkpanku na betélie kalɔ kani na amii bíni mmɔ lɛlɔ na badi-ka ebi bakɛ ebiti.

english_verse: You will die here in the desert!
translation_verse: Nsu amii amu mɛni na bɛdubo bukpi bɔtɛ na kalɔ kakwiidi kamɛni kemmo.

english_verse: So they got up early the next morning and got ready to head toward the hill country of Canaan. They said, “We were wrong to complain about the Lord. Let's go into the land that he promised us.”
translation_verse: Amu ka kadi kégye ɔtanta tutuutu ni, béyile bésie abi eli na bétévele básu banini, “Unwoti, bɔ́bla likpidi, anwuɔsu buuvele ka bɔdu busie kalɔ kani na awɔ Unwoti ásu ése ka adubute-bu mmɔ kemmo.”

english_verse: Ten of the men sent to explore the land had brought back bad news and had made the people complain against the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu bekyuli bani na Mose ɔ́tala ka besie na bátávi kalɔ kammɔ kemmo bánu mmɔ, na bénwini bébedie kenye kekpidi básu bekyuli bammɔ ɔsu na baadɔ bana lɛlɔ kemmo kalɔ kalɔ na Unwoti lɛlɔ ni,

english_verse: but he let Joshua and Caleb live. The Israelites Fail To Enter Canaan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani ƒui nésie batávi bánu kalɔ kammɔ akɔ ni, Nun ubidi Yosua ku Yeƒune ubidi Kaleb kani nákɛ ngba.

english_verse: But Moses replied, “You're disobeying the Lord! Your plan won't work,
translation_verse: Nsu Mose úye-ma ɔnini, “Na bi ɔsu na biládi Unwoti bunyimi lɛlɔ? Lɛla lɛni bɛɛbla mɛni lɛɛɛdubo bɔtɛ bute-mii!

english_verse: The Amalekites and the Canaanites came down from the hill country, defeated the Israelites, and chased them as far as the town of Hormah.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Amalekƒuɔ ku Kanaanƒuɔ báta na bétékpoku-ma na bádi-ma lɛlɔ na bábi básiaku-ma laa bétédu Horma.

english_verse: The people of Israel were very sad after Moses gave them the Lord's message.
translation_verse: Amu ka Mose únwini úsie Israelƒuɔ kudɔ na útásu-ma lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu mɛni ni, béwulo bana lɛlɔ geen.

english_verse: so don't even try it. The Lord refuses to help you, because you turned your backs on him. The Amalekites and the Canaanites are your enemies, and they will attack and defeat you.”
translation_verse: Na si bísie bɛnii bitékpoku Amalekƒuɔ ku Kanaanƒuɔ ni, badubo-mii lɛlɔ bɔdi na badu-mii ku kuwii. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔɔɔdubo-mii kama bɔsiaku ka bíni nwuna litemi na bítadi-ni lɛlɔ ɔsu.”

english_verse: But the Israelites ignored Moses and marched toward the hill country, even though the sacred chest and Moses did not go with them.
translation_verse: Ina ka Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka iye Mose útasiaku-ma ni, báyu kayi ɔkplu na báta bésie abi lɛma ka betékpo.

english_verse: to give the Israelites the following laws about offering sacrifices:
translation_verse: ‘Si bísie na bítéduo kalɔ kani kemmo na lɛ́su ka meti mete-mii na biti-ka bɛbla bina keliekɔ

english_verse: Bulls or rams or goats are the animals that you may burn on the altar as sacrifices to please me. You may also offer sacrifices voluntarily or because you made a promise, or because they are part of your regular religious ceremonies. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices is pleasing to me.
translation_verse: na ɔdi ɔɔyɔ́ ka uti ebuo ɔdi ɔsiku nwuna bebuo lidu akɔ ɔbla bɔkyula akpala ƒɛƒɛɛ ani mɔɔyɔ́ ami Unwoti kaƒɔ, iye kenye kadi na úse na ɔnii ɔɔbla akpala iye kayi ƒaa akpala iye akpala ani ndanku emeyi bɔdi ni,

english_verse: If a bull is offered as a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing,
translation_verse: “ ‘Na si ɔmantɛ akɔ na ɔdi úti ɔɔbla bɔkyula ute Unwoti, iye kenye buse kayu bɔƒɔ akpala iye unwi bɔbla akpala adi ni,

english_verse: you must offer three kilograms of flour mixed with two liters of olive oil.
translation_verse: ɔlɛka ɔwia ɔlaaƒɔ buni akyami atɛ ku kakɛ ɔni na básala ku nnɔ lɛsii bonwu inyɔ ku kakɛ uboku aani edula ebi akpala,

english_verse: Two liters of wine must also be poured on the altar. The smell of this smoke is pleasing to me.
translation_verse: ku ntɛ lɛsii inyɔ na uti ɔbla bɔkyula akpala ammɔ na ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ɔyɔ Unwoti kaƒɔ.

english_verse: If you are a native Israelite, you must obey these rules each time you offer a bull, a ram, or a goat as a sacrifice.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na ukyuli biala na ɔdi Israelni ubi geen na úti nwuna akpala úboku ka ubakyula na nwuna ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ Unwoti kaƒɔ ni, ɔlɛka ɔbla akpala amɛni ɔsiaku ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ.

english_verse: This law will never change. I am the Lord, and I consider all people the same, whether they are Israelites or foreigners living among you.
translation_verse: Ɔda bubo bɔmɛni buunyimi amii ku baƒɔ bani na bakya-mii akɔ ƒui.’ ”

english_verse: When you eat food in the land that I am giving you, remember to set aside some of it as an offering to me.
translation_verse: na bɛɛdi-ka edula ni, na bidie adi bise na biti bɛkpa bite Unwoti.

english_verse: From the first batch of bread dough that you make after each new grain harvest, make a loaf of bread and offer it to me, just as you offer grain.
translation_verse: Na ɔlaaƒɔ udeedi ɔni na bɛdubo bɔkɔ bɔsiku bina mmo edula ebi edeedi ani na bɛdubo buwiile buse kakpa ni, biti-nwu bɛbla bodobodo bɛbla akpala bite-mi.

english_verse: All your descendants must follow this law and offer part of the first batch of bread dough.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela uwi ƒui ku bina bebi ku bawɔ akɔ ni, ɔlɛka biti akpala amɛni biboku Unwoti ɔsiku bina edula ebi edeedi ɔlaaƒɔ udeedi ɔni na bɛdubɔkɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The Lord also told Moses to tell the people what must be done if they ever disobey his laws:
translation_verse: iye ɔda bubo bamba biala na ɔkɛnku-mi lɛlɔ na Mose úte amii kadi bekyuli bammɔ ɔ́si limeyi lɛni lɛlɔ na Unwoti únyimi-mu úti úsela uwi ɔni mebo ƒui kemmo

english_verse: If all of you disobey one of my laws without knowing it, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice, a wine offering, and a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: na kadi kammɔ ƒui bátadi-mu lɛlɔ na tati tati ɔsu ni, ɔlɛka bawia akɔ na beti babla bɔkyula akpala na ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ɔyɔ Unwoti kaƒɔ ku nwuna lɛlɔ edula ebi ku ntɛ akpala, aani kalɛ na bényimi bése, ku ketukpa na beti babla likpidi lili buvele akpala.

english_verse: Then the priest will pray and ask me to forgive you. And since you did not mean to do wrong, and you offered sacrifices,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ɔkpane ɔdubɔbla akpala ute bana likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie na kadi bekyuli bammɔ ƒui lili na badubuti bakyiɛ-ma, ɔsika bátati asa na bábla-ni, na ɔmmɔ ɔsu béboku etela ka bakyula bete Unwoti ku likpidi lili buvele akpala.

english_verse: But if one of you does wrong without knowing it, you must sacrifice a year-old female goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: “ ‘Nsu si ukyuli unwi ɔ́bla likpidi lɛni na útati asa na ɔ́bla-ni ni, ɔlɛka ɔwia ese uledi ɔni nákɛ lɛkwa linwi na uti ubabla likpidi lili buvele akpala.

english_verse: The priest will then ask me to forgive you, and your sin will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔlɛka ɔbla akpala ute Unwoti úte ukyuli ɔni na tati tati ɔsu na ɔ́bla likpidi lɛmmɔ na Unwoti ɔdubuti ɔkyiɛ-nwu.

english_verse: The law will be the same for anyone who does wrong without meaning to, whether an Israelite or a foreigner living among you.
translation_verse: Na ɔda bubo bɔmɛni buse bute ukyuli biala maƒiɔ ɔni na útati útese asa na ɔ́bla likpidi lɛdi, amii ɔmantɛ bebi ku baƒɔ bani nkya-mii akɔ ƒui.

english_verse: But if one of you does wrong on purpose, whether Israelite or foreigner, you have sinned against me by disobeying my laws. You will no longer belong to my people. A Man Put to Death for Gathering Firewood on the Sabbath
translation_verse: Ɔsika útabu Unwoti litemi na ɔ́ta únye nwuna ɔda bubo lɛlɔ, ɔsu ɔlɛka bekulo ukyuli ɔmmɔ udu bedie nwuna bekyuli akɔ kede kede na anwu ɔlati ɔdubuti nwuna likpidi etila.’ ” Kɔtu Bɔni Na Kabla Bɔbla Na Lɛnwunameyi Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Once, while the Israelites were traveling through the desert, a man was caught gathering firewood on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bákya ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo ni, bekyuli badi bánu ka ɔnana ɔdi ɔkya ɔɔyɔ́ ekyweni na lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: He was taken to Moses, Aaron, and the rest of the community.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani nánu-nwu mmɔ béƒie-nwu bésienku Mose ku Aaron ku Israelƒuɔ ƒui anumi,

english_verse: But no one knew what to do with him, so he was not allowed to leave.
translation_verse: na béti-nwu bátákya ɔtɔ, ɔsika balati lɛla lɛni na babla-nwu.

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Tell the people to take that man outside the camp and stone him to death!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Ukyuli ɔni nábla lɛla lɛmmɔ udu ɔ́manku kukpi. Anwuɔsu ɔdi ka kadi bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bakpanku-nwu balɛku bana kakyakɔ na bétébo-nwu atabi bádu.”

english_verse: So he was killed, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. The Tassels on the People's Clothes
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bákpanku-nwu bálɛku na bétebo-nwu atabi aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo-ma ɔda. Unwo Lɛbuli Lɛlɔ Bunyimi

translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

translation_verse: Na adi linwo lɛmmɔ lɛdubɔya na biteenyimo kalɛ na bɛdi mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ na bɛbla lɛlɔ sɛsɛɛ bise bite bina Katɔti.

translation_verse: na báta bénye Mose lɛlɔ. Na Israelƒuɔ banana babune geen bani na badi kelisa benengu nkyuli eti alɔ (
