translation_verse: Bekyuli bamɛni báta na lisu kemmo bésie Mose ku Aaron kudɔ na bátásu-ma banini, “Bɛɛyɔ́ bisie ɔgyu bɛgya! Israel kadi bekyuli ƒui bese kedee bete Unwoti bana ɔdi biala, na Unwoti ulieku bula ƒui. Na bi ɔsu na bɛɛnu lɛlɔ katɔ katɔ teetuloku Unwoti bekyuli lɛni?”

english_verse: When Moses heard this, he knelt down to pray.
translation_verse: Ka Mose únu etemila amɛni ni, ɔ́yu úbi kalɔ na ɔ́kpali Katɔti.

english_verse: Then he said to Korah and his followers: Tomorrow morning the Lord will show us the person he has chosen to be his priest, and that man will faithfully serve him.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́su Kora ku nwuna bekyuli bani nsiaku-nwu kama ɔnini, “Kɔnaadi ɔtanta ni, Unwoti ɔdubɔtina ukyuli ɔni ndi nwuna ɔdi na use kedee, na ɔdubɔya na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔni ude-nwu. Na ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́ƒuna mmɔ ni, Unwoti ɔlati ɔdubɔya na ɔni ude-nwu.

english_verse: Korah, here is what you and your followers must do: Get some fire pans, fill them with coals and incense, and place them near the sacred tent. And the man the Lord chooses will be his priest. Korah, this time you Levites have gone too far!
translation_verse: na kɔnaadi bidie ogya ku oloƒui biwi-ni kemmo na Unwoti anumi. Na ukyuli ɔni na Unwoti ɔ́ƒuna ni, anwu nse kedee. Amii Lewiƒuɔ mmomu nésie ɔgyu bɛgya!”

english_verse: You know that the God of Israel has chosen you Levites from all Israel to serve him by being in charge of the sacred tent and by helping the community to worship in the proper way. What more do you want?
translation_verse: Israelƒuɔ Katɔti nédie-mii sɛsɛɛ ɔ́lɛku Israelƒuɔ akɔ na ɔ́ya na bɛ́ni bíde-nwu ka bitaabla kabla na Unwoti Adi Kevo kemmo, na binye bekyuli bammɔ kenye bitaabla-nwu kabla teete-ma. Ɔmɛni lɛti útabɔ-mii?

english_verse: The Lord has given you a special responsibility, and now, Korah, you think you should also be his priest.
translation_verse: Anwu nédie amii ku Lewiƒuɔ bakladi ɔ́bla nwuna ɔdi. Nsu bɛnu, ɔƒɛni bɛɛwia ka bɛƒɔ ɔkpane kabla lɛnɔ bɛbla bina ɔdi.

english_verse: Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, but they sent back this message: “We won't come!
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́tala ɔnii bátálɔ Datan ku Abiram bani ndi Eliab bebi na bebo. Nsu básɔku kenye bémene Mose banini, “Bɔɔɔdubo mmɔ!

english_verse: It's bad enough that you took us from our rich farmland in Egypt to let us die here in the desert. Now you also want to boss us around!
translation_verse: Ɔni lɛti na ákpanku-bu ásiku Egyipte kalɔ kani kana egyiibi ntu bɔɔyu emini aani uwɔ na kana lɛlɔ bebuo baayu anyi ntu pii éboku ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kamɛni kemmo ka bubekpi bɔyii udu útabɔ? Na ɔƒɛni aawia ka asɔ ataadi-bu lɛlɔ lɛlati na mɛni?

english_verse: Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, “Don't listen to these men! I haven't done anything wrong to them. I haven't taken as much as a donkey.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mose úbakɛ kɔnyi geen na ɔ́su Unwoti ɔnini, “Taƒɔ bekyuli bamɛni akpala adi. Ńtaƒɔ bana ɔdi lɛla lɛdi ina ebuo ala utine, na ńtaƒiɔ ɔdi lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: Then he said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and your followers must go with Aaron to the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔsu Kora ɔnini, “Kɔnaadi ni, awɔ ku ƒula basiakune ku Aaron ƒui bisie Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ anumi.

english_verse: Each of you take along your fire pan with incense in it and offer the incense to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na ɔdi biala uti nwuna oloƒui bɔkyula libui na udie ogya ku oloƒui uwi-ni kemmo na biti-nya biboku Unwoti anumi, na ebui ammɔ ƒui adubɔbla eti alɔ (

english_verse: The next day the men placed incense and coals in their fire pans and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔdi biala úti nwuna oloƒui bɔkyula libui na úwi ogya ku oloƒui, na bana ƒui besie beténye Unwoti Adi Kevo kayakun ku Mose ku Aaron lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Korah had convinced the rest of the Israelites to rebel against their two leaders. When that happened, the Lord appeared in all his glory
translation_verse: Amu ka Kora ɔ́sala nwuna bekyuli bani nsiaku-nwu kama ɔ́wɔlɔ na bébenye baanu Mose ku Aaron anumi na Unwoti Adi Kevo kayakun kenye mmɔ ni, kɔnakunwi ni, Unwoti bukeye bonwu bɔ́bwɛ búbewi bekyuli bammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and said to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ku Aaron ɔnini,

english_verse: “Get away from the rest of the Israelites so I can kill them at once!”
translation_verse: “Bɛmami lɛlɔ bɛsiku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui kudɔ na ɔdia-mi na lɛyila-ma udu ƒui kɔnakunwi.”

english_verse: But the two men bowed down and prayed, “Our God, you gave these people life. Why would you punish everyone here when only one man has sinned?”
translation_verse: Nsu Mose ku Aaron báyula bana lili kalɔ na báva momoomo bákpali Katɔti basu-nwu banini, “O Katɔti, awɔ Katɔti ndi bayawine ƒui ayu ɔti, buti na adubuti kɔnyi akya kasala kammɔ ƒui na ukyuli unwi ɔdi likpidi ɔsu?”

english_verse: The Lord answered Moses,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: “Tell the people to stay away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
translation_verse: “Su Israelƒuɔ bani ƒui nlie nde Kora ku Datan ku Abiram nvo kudɔ na bata balɛ-ma kudɔ mmɔ besie kama.”

english_verse: Moses walked over to Dathan and Abiram, and the other leaders of Israel followed.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose útiku Israelƒuɔ benengu na báta bésie Datan ku Abiram kudɔ.

english_verse: Then Moses warned the people, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men! Don't touch anything that belongs to them or you'll be wiped out.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na útébo Israelƒuɔ ɔda ɔnini, “Bɛta bina kuliekɔ mɛni na bɛkpɛ bɛlɛ bekyuli bekpidi bamɛni nvo kudɔ. Na ɔdi biala uteti nwuna kɔnu utetuku bekyuli bammɔ lɛla lɛdi kalɛ na ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ ɔdi uletuku ɔdi ɔ́si bana likpidi ɔsu.”

english_verse: Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know:
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mose ɔ́su bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ɔnini, “Ɔmɛni na bɛdubuti bɛnu bɛti ka Unwoti nátala-mi ɔnii mbabla ala amɛni. Na ɔɔɔdi ami ɔlati kasusu kadi.

english_verse: If these men die a natural death, it means the Lord hasn't chosen me.
translation_verse: Si bekyuli bamɛni békpi kukpi kɔni kani na bekyuli ƒui beekpi ni, na ɔɔɔdi Unwoti nátala-mi.

english_verse: But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
translation_verse: Nsu si Unwoti údie lɛla lɛwɔdi keyi na ɔ́ya na kalɔ kébimi kenye na kébweli-ma ku ngba ku ngba ama ku bana akɛla ani ƒui na bebo ni, bɛdubɔnu bɔti ka bátanu Unwoti bátabu munu munu.”

english_verse: As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up
translation_verse: Amu ka Mose ɔ́wɔlɔ nwuna butemi pɛ kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na Datan ku Abiram bene benye mmɔ kábwɛ kemmo inyɔ.

english_verse: and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bammɔ béduo kekpine ku ngba ku ngba, ku bana ala ani ƒui na bebo na kalɔ kammɔ kásɔ kébile kenye, na báyii udu na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui akɔ.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bénu kɔvanu momoomo kɔni bekyuli bani kalɔ kebweli mmɔ bedie uwi ɔni baanyi mmɔ ni, ama lɛnɔ béti usi bétuku na baava taasu banini, “Abu lɛnɔ kalɔ kadubo-bu bubweli!”

english_verse: Suddenly the Lord sent a fire that burned up the
translation_verse: Kɔnakunwi ni, ogya ɔ́si katɔ úbakyula nkyuli eti alɔ bani mɔɔkyula oloƒui mmɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: “Tell Aaron's son Eleazar to take the fire pans from the smoldering fire and scatter the coals. The pans are now sacred,
translation_verse: “Su ɔkpane Aaron ubidi Eleasar na ɔla oloƒui bɔkyula ebui ammɔ udie ogya ntɔ bɔmmɔ kemmo na ugyingya ogya ɔmmɔ usienku kama ƒui, ɔsika ebui ammɔ ese kedee,

english_verse: because they were used for offering incense to me. Have them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar. Those men died because of their sin, and now their fire pans will become a warning for the rest of the community.”
translation_verse: na adi ebui ani na bekyuli bani nábla likpidi béti bana ngba báƒɔ bana likpidi lili kayu adi. Bitu ebui ammɔ bɛbla abuala kɔlɛkɛ bɛbɛɛbɛ bibi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ, ɔsika béti-nya béte Unwoti na ese kedee, na unwini likposela ute Israelƒuɔ.”

english_verse: Eleazar collected the pans and had them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar,
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔkpane Eleasar ɔ́la oloƒui ebui ani na bekyuli bani na ogya ɔ́kyula mmɔ béboku na ɔ́ya na bétu-nya bábla kɔlɛkɛ bɛbɛɛbɛ bébi Unwoti Lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ

english_verse: just as the Lord had told Moses. The pans were a warning to the Israelites that only Aaron's descendants would be allowed to offer incense to the Lord. Anyone else who tried to would be punished like Korah and his followers. The Israelites Rebel and Are Punished
translation_verse: aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda. Na ɔmɛni ɔ́bla bɔlɛ úte Israelƒuɔ kaduɛ ka ukyuli ɔni nátasi Aaron kaba kemmo utalɛka usie Unwoti lɛkpabi kudɔ ɔnii utákyula oloƒui ute Unwoti. english_verse: The next day the people of Israel again complained against Moses and Aaron, “The two of you killed some of the Lord's people!”
translation_verse: Ka kalɔ kébweli Kora badi kadi kégye kani na Israelƒuɔ ƒui báta na bákya baakya ku Mose ku Aaron unyeƒi na baasu-ma banii, “Amii nádu Unwoti bekyuli badi.”

english_verse: As the people crowded around them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the sacred tent, and the Lord appeared in his glory in the cloud covering the tent.
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ básala lɛlɔ na baakya ku Mose ku Aaron unyeƒi mmɔ ni, béti anumi bátina Unwoti Adi Kevo na kɔnakunwi liƒlukutu lɛ́si líbewi ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ, na Unwoti bukeye bonwu bɔ́bwɛ bɔ́lɛ mmɔ.

english_verse: So Moses and Aaron walked to the front of the tent,
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ku Aaron bésie béténye Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ anumi.

english_verse: where the Lord said to them,
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: “Stand back! I am going to wipe out these Israelites once and for all.” They immediately bowed down and prayed.
translation_verse: “Bɛkpɛ bɛlɛ Israelƒuɔ bammɔ kudɔ kalɛ na ɔdia-mi na lɛyila-ma udu kɔnakunwi.” Nsu Mose ku Aaron báyu bébi kalɔ.

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Grab your fire pan and fill it with hot coals from the altar. Put incense in it, then quickly take it to where the people are and offer it to the Lord, so they can be forgiven. The Lord is very angry, and people have already started dying!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mose ɔ́su Aaron ɔnini, “Babla na eti ƒula oloƒui libui na edie ogya asiku Unwoti lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ na ewi oloƒui, na ekeli esie Israelƒuɔ bammɔ akɔ na atábla akpala ete Unwoti úte bana likpidi kɔtu bɔni budie. english_verse: Israelites were dead, not counting those who had died with Korah and his followers.
translation_verse: ) békpi na ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ kemmo bébunku bani nékpi ɔ́si Kora atuɔkplu ɔsu.

english_verse: Aaron walked back and stood with Moses at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama na Aaron ɔ́sɔ únwini úsie Mose kudɔ na Unwoti Adi Kevo mmɔ, ɔsika ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ kenye kékulo.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you.
translation_verse: Na eti ligyii lɛmmɔ etése Unwoti Adi Kevo kemmo na Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ anumi kesii kani na mɔɔsiáku-mii.

english_verse: I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔni na lɛ́ƒuna ni, nwuna ugyii ɔdubo bɔta budie evete. Na ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na ndubɔsia na Israelƒuɔ badaku-ɔ unyeƒi bɔkya baya na lɛda kalaka kamɛni udu bunu lɛya.”

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Mose ɔ́kɔ litemi lɛmmɔ lɛsa úte Israelƒuɔ na bana kaba batɔnkune bammɔ ɔdi biala úti nwuna ugyii ɔdadi úboku Mose. Na ligyii lɛmmɔ ƒui lɛdi leevu-inyɔ. Na Aaron ugyii ɔdadi lɛnɔ ubunku.

english_verse: Moses took them and placed them in the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na Mose úti ligyii lɛmmɔ úsienku Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo na úti-ni útése Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ anumi.

english_verse: The next day when Moses went into the tent, flowers and almonds were already growing on Aaron's stick.
translation_verse: Ka kadi kégye ni, Mose úsie Unwoti Kevo kemmo na ka ɔ́nu ni, na Aaron ugyii ɔni nnye nte Lewiƒuɔ mmɔ ɔ́ta na údie evete ku anwula na ɔ́nwu ebi.

english_verse: Moses brought the twelve sticks out of the tent and showed them to the people. Each of the leaders found his own and took it.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mose ɔ́la ligyii lɛmmɔ ƒui ɔ́siku Unwoti anumi na úti-ni úsienku Israelƒuɔ kudɔ. Na ɔtɔnkune biala ɔ́nu nwuna ugyii údie.

english_verse: But the Lord told Moses, “Put Aaron's stick back! Let it stay near the sacred chest as a warning to anyone who might think of rebelling. If these people don't stop their grumbling about me, I will wipe them out.”
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Sɔku Aaron ugyii tése Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ anumi. Na ugyii ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla likposela ute Israelƒuɔ batuɔkplune. Na ɔdubɔya na bada bɔdɔ na bana lɛlɔ kemmo na mina lɛlɔ baya kalɛ na balása bukpi ƒui.”

english_verse: Moses did what he was told.
translation_verse: Na Mose ɔ́bla ɔ́sia kalɛ kani Unwoti úbo-nwu ɔda.

english_verse: The Israelites cried out to Moses, “We're done for
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ básu Mose banini, “Bɔdubo bukpi! Bɔ́yii ɔƒɛni amu! Bula ƒui bɔyii!

english_verse: and doomed if we even go near the sacred tent!”
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala mani mede Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ muedi ɔdubukpi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bula ƒui bɔdubo bukpi?”

english_verse: The Levites are your relatives and are here to help you in your service at the tent.
translation_verse: Kpanku Lewiƒuɔ ku ƒula kaba bekyuli na bebebunku-ɔ si uwi ɔni awɔ ku ƒula bebi bɛkya bɛɛbla bakpane kabla na Unwoti Adi Kevo kemmo mmɔ.

english_verse: You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die.
translation_verse: Na Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ badubɔkya-a kalɔ na ama ndubɔbla kabla biala na Kevo mmɔ, na bana akɔ ɔdi biala na útamanku utani utede ala kedee ani na Kevo kemmo mmɔ ku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ, si ɔɔɔdi lɛni amii ku-ma ƒui bɛdubo bukpi.

english_verse: No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it.
translation_verse: Badubo na bebunku-ɔ na bitaabla kabla biala na Kevo kammɔ kemmo ku kana lɛlɔ bɔnu, na ukyuli bamba ɔdi utani utede-mii na mmɔ.

english_verse: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
translation_verse: “Amii na ɔlɛka bitaanu Adi Kevo kammɔ lɛlɔ ku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ, kalɛ na mina kɔnyi kɔsɔ kuláda kulálɛ Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Ami ɔlati náƒuna Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ lɛ́lɛku Israelƒuɔ akɔ líte-ɔ lɛ́bla na bese sɛsɛɛ bete Unwoti ka babla kabla na Unwoti Adi Kevo kemmo.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Nsu awɔ ku ƒula bebi bananabi kani na ɔlɛka bitaabla bakpane kabla biala na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ku kakpakɔ bule kɔdi kɔmmɔ kama mmɔ. Na líti ɔkpane kabla kamɛni muute-mii aani etela kalɛ. Na ɔmmɔ kama ukyuli biala mani mede kakpakɔ kammɔ kudɔ ɔlɛka badu-nwu.” Bakpane Ku Lewiƒuɔ Kadikɔ

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Bana lɛna lɛdi bina ɔdi aani kalɛ kani na bebuo bani kayi ɔvu ku ebuli lɛna bákɔliku katɔ bátina-mi bébo-ni kudu lɛdi bina ɔdi.

english_verse: The Lord said to Aaron: I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar.
translation_verse: Na akpala kedee ani na balákyula na lɛkpabi lɛlɔ aani edula ebi akpala ku likpidi lili buvele akpala biala adi bina ɔdi. Na akpala biala na béti béboku-mi na ese kedee ƒui adi awɔ ku ƒula bebi bananabi ɔdi.

english_verse: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
translation_verse: Na si bɛɛdi ala ammɔ na bɛdi-nya na kesii kani nse kedee. Na awɔ ku ƒula bebi bananabi kani ɔlɛka bɛdi adila ammɔ. Bɛbu adila ammɔ ka ese kedee.

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: “Ɔmmɔ kama akpala sɛsɛɛ biala Israelƒuɔ badubuti beboku-mi adi awɔ ku ƒula bebi ɔdi. Na líti-nya muute awɔ ku ƒula bebi bananabi ku belekubi ɔƒɛni ku uwi ɔni mebo ƒui. Na ukyuli biala nási ƒula kaduli kemmo na ukyuli ɔmmɔ use sɛɛn ɔkana ɔdi ala ammɔ adi.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: “Na edula edeedi abuni ani na Israelƒuɔ badubɔkɛ aani nnɔ ku ntɛ bɔwɔdi ku edula ebi ani na badubuti beboku Unwoti ni, lɛ́sɔku-nya muute-mii.

english_verse: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
translation_verse: Na kalɔ kammɔ ƒui edula edeedi ani béti béboku Unwoti adubɔbla bina ɔdi. Na ukyuli biala nlie-ɔ kaduli na use sɛɛn ɔkana ɔdi adila ammɔ adi.

english_verse: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
translation_verse: “Na lɛla biala nkya Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ na bédie-ni sɛsɛɛ bése béte Unwoti ɔdi bina ɔdi.

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: Na kaƒɔ biala ubi udeedi ku ebuo udeedi biala na báwɔ, na Israelƒuɔ béti-nwu béboku Unwoti ɔdi bina ɔdi. Nsu ɔnanabi udeedi ku ebuo ala utine biala anwu ni, ɔlɛka basɔku-nwu beye basiku-mi kudɔ.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Na kayu kani na ɔlɛka baƒɔ na ɔnanabi ubi udeedi biala na báwɔ-nwu na ɔ́kɛ kɔbuli ɔdi sika ɔƒualadi ebi alɔ na kakpakɔ ala bɔkɔku kenye.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: “Nsu ɔmantɛ akɔ, ku koƒonu ku ese udeedi biala na báwɔ ɔdi Unwoti ɔdi na utalɛka beti ebuo ɔmmɔ ɔdi beye. Ama bese kedee na ɔlɛka badu-ma na beti bana ubugya bakuna bewi lɛkpabi lɛlɔ na bakya bana lɛmwi lɛmmɔ ogya bakyula na ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: Ala ani ƒui na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ béte-mi ɔ́siku Israelƒuɔ etela ani na béboku-mi kemmo ni, líti muute awɔ Aaron ku ƒula bebi bananabi ku belekubi. Na bunyimi bɔmɛni na Unwoti únyimi úse úte awɔ ku ƒula bebi ku bawɔ úsela uwi ƒui na ulavumana.”

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Aaron ɔnini, “Aaadubo kadikɔ kadi bɔkɛ na Israel, na belele lɛla lɛdi lɛnɔ belete-ɔ, ɔsika ami Unwoti kani ndi ƒula kadikɔ ku lɛla lɛni nédu-ɔ na Israelƒuɔ akɔ.

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: “Na ala ani ƒui na Israelƒuɔ bákɛ básiku bana kabla kani baabla kemmo lɛkpa leevudi ni, líti muute Lewiƒuɔ ka beti babla bana kadikɔ na Unwoti Adi Kevo kemmo kabla kani na baabla kenye.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: Lewiƒuɔ kani na ɔlɛka bataabla kabla na Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo. Na si lɛla lɛdi lɛ́lɛ mmɔ ama kani ndubɔnuku-ni. Ɔda bubo bɔmɛni buse úsela uwi ƒui útédu bina bawɔ bawɔ akɔ lɛnɔ. Na ama beeebo kadikɔ kadi na Israelƒuɔ akɔ.

english_verse: they will be given the crops and newborn animals that the Israelites offer to me. What the Levites Must Give
translation_verse: Mmomu Israelƒuɔ ala lɛkpa leevudi lɛni beeti teeboku Unwoti aani akpala ndubɔbla bana kadikɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu na lɛ́su nnii, ‘Beeebo kadikɔ kadi na Israelƒuɔ akɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: “Temi te Lewiƒuɔ na asu-ma anini, ‘Ala lɛkpa leevudi lɛni lɛ́su Israelƒuɔ ka beti beboku-mii aani bina kadikɔ mmɔ si béti béboku ni, amii lɛnɔ bidie lɛkpa leevudi na biti bɛbla akpala bite Unwoti.

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Na badubuti etela ammɔ aani edula ebi ani nási bina mmo edula ebi kewiilekɔ iye egyiibi ntu bɔni nási bina ntɛ kebulokɔ.

english_verse: so the best of what you receive will be mine.
translation_verse: Na ɔdi ka bɛsia anu na ala ammɔ kabunikɔ ƒui kani nse kedee na biti bite Unwoti.’

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: “Na asu Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ anini, ‘Si bíti ala ammɔ kabunikɔ kammɔ ƒui bíboku Unwoti ni, badubɔnu-nya aani edula ebi ani na bíwiile bíwi kakpa iye egyiibi ntu bɔni nási bina ntɛ kebulokɔ.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na amii ku bina kaduli bekyuli bɛkana na bɛdi ɔkladi na kesi kesii ƒaa, ɔsika ɔmmɔ ndi bina lɛyuƒɔla na kabla kani na bɛɛbla na Unwoti Adi Kevo kemmo kenye.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Na si bídie ala ammɔ kabunikɔ ƒui bíte Unwoti ni, biiibo kɔtɔ budu bɔdi na ɔmɛni kemmo, na ɔɔɔdubo bɔya na Israelƒuɔ akpala ammɔ ese lɛlɔ, na amii lɛnɔ bilekpi.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: “Ala ani nkɛnku ɔda bubo bɔni na Unwoti úte-mii ndi ɔmɛni, bɛsu Israelƒuɔ na beboku ɔmantɛ akɔ ugyiedi uledi ɔkɔdi ɔni na bɔsɔ bɔdi buuubo-nwu lɛlɔ na bátabala-nwu kɔgba kɔdi na ɔbla kabla kadi kudii.

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: Na beti-nwu beboku ɔkpane Eleasar, na beti akɔ ammɔ balɛku bana keliekɔ mmɔ bésienku kama na badu-nwu mmɔ na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ anumi.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na si bádu-nwu báwɔlɔ ni, na Eleasar uti ubugya ɔmmɔ na uti nwuna lɛnimi ɔkya ubugya ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na uti nwuna anumi ɔtina kesii kani na Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kenye na ɔkuna ubugya ɔmmɔ umene Kevo kammɔ anumi maatɛ.

english_verse: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama na unye ɔnu na bakyula ebuo umodi ɔmmɔ ku nwuna ɔku ku ubugya ku nwuna kaƒɔ ala ƒui.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama Eleasar ɔwia kegyiikɛ kadi ku hisope ku kabuli kegyiedi kadi na ubo-nya ɔkya ogya ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Na si ɔ́bla ala ammɔ ƒui ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔlɛka utáƒɔ nwuna adala na ɔkpi ntu. Na ammɔ kama ɔkana na unwini utéduo bana kakyakɔ mmɔ. Nsu nwuna lɛlɔ lɛɛɛdubo buse sɛɛn wetédu useyi uwi.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔni nákyula akɔ ammɔ lɛnɔ ɔlɛka ɔƒɔ nwuna adala na ɔkpi ntu, nsu anwu lɛnɔ ɔɔɔdubo buse sɛɛn utédu useyi uwi.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: “Na ukyuli ɔni nse sɛɛn ndubɔbuma akɔ ntɔ bɔmmɔ utéwi kesii kani nse sɛɛn na bana keliekɔ kammɔ kama. Na ntɔ bɔmmɔ bɔdubuwi mmɔ bute Israelƒuɔ kadi kammɔ na beteewi ntu kemmo taabla lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Na ɔnana ɔni mabuma ntɔ bɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔlɛka ɔƒɔ nwuna adala, na ɔɔɔdubo buse sɛɛn wetédu useyi uwi. Ɔda ubo bɔmɛni buse bute Israelƒuɔ ku baƒɔ bani nkya-ma akɔ úte uwi ƒui.

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: “Ukyuli biala meti kɔnu metuku ukpine ɔdi ɔ́sɔ na ulése sɛɛn emeyi maatɛ.

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛtɛdi ku limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka uti ntu bɔmmɔ ɔbla lɛlɔ sɛɛn, na nwuna lɛlɔ lɛdubɔbla sɛɛn. Nsu si úteti ntu bɔmmɔ útabla lɛlɔ sɛɛn na limeyi lɛtɛdi ku maatɛdi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, ɔɔɔdubo buse sɛɛn.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala meti kɔnu metuku ukpine na uni na utabla sɛɛn bɔbla ɔdi ɔmmɔ ni, ɔ́ya na Unwoti kakpakɔ keesé lɛlɔ, na ɔlɛka bada ukyuli ɔmmɔ bedie Israelƒuɔ akɔ. Ɔsika batakuna ntu bɔni mɔbla sɛɛn bétewi-nwu lɛlɔ ɔsu uusé lɛlɔ. Na nwuna sɛɛn tabla ɔmmɔ ɔkya-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: “Na si ubebo ute ka ukyuli ɔdi ukpi na nwuna kɔdi ɔtɔ kemmo ni, bekyuli bani nkya mmɔ asa na ukpi iye ukyuli biala meduo ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo ɔdubuse lɛlɔ emeyi maatɛ.

english_verse: Any open jar in the tent is unclean.
translation_verse: Na akyami ku ebui ani neeebo libila na alɛ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo lɛlɔ lɛdubuse lɛlɔ.

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala metuku ukyuli ɔni bébo-nwu bádu iye anwu alati kukpi na úkpi iye útuku ukpine likubi iye kaƒiɔtɔ ni, ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔdubuse lɛlɔ emeyi maatɛ.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔni nse sɛɛn na ulese lɛlɔ ɔlɛka ɔwia hisope lɛla lɛni lɛdia ntu bɔkuna buwi lɛla lɛdi lɛlɔ. Na uti ɔkya ntu libui lɛmmɔ kemmo na ɔkuna uwi Adi Kevo ɔtɔ ɔni na ukyuli úkpi-nwu kemmo mmɔ ku bekyuli bani nákya mmɔ ƒui. Kunyɔdi ukyuli ɔni nse sɛɛn ɔlɛka ɔkuna ntu bɔmmɔ uwi ukyuli ɔni nétuku ukpine likubi iye utuku ukpine ɔni na bádu iye anwu ɔlati nékpi iye kaƒiɔtɔ.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛtɛdi ku maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, ukyuli ɔni nse sɛɛn ɔkuna ntu bɔmmɔ uwi ukyuli ɔni neeese sɛɛn mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ ukyuli mmɔ ɔlɛka ɔƒɔ nwuna adala na ɔkpi ntu. Na ɔmmɔ kama ukyuli ɔni nákuna ntu bɔmmɔ úwi lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔbla-nwu sɛɛn. Na si ɔƒɔ na ukyuli mmɔ ɔbla sɛɛn.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: “Nsu si ukyuli ɔdi ɔkya-mii akɔ na úni na útabla lɛlɔ sɛɛn ɔlɛka bada-nwu bedie bina akɔ. Ɔsika uti eƒi utuku Unwoti kakpakɔ ka béteti ntu bɔni mɔɔbla ukyuli ɔni eƒi akya-nwu lɛlɔ betewi-nwu lɛlɔ ɔsu. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na uuse lɛlɔ.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Na ɔda bubo bɔmɛni buse busela uwi ƒui. Na ukyuli ɔni maakuna ntu bɔni mɔɔyá ukyuli ɔɔbla sɛɛn mmɔ mewi ukyuli ɔdi ɔlɛka anwu lɛnɔ ɔƒɔ nwuna adala. Na ukyuli biala meetuku ntu bɔdi ɔdubuse lɛlɔ wetédu useyi uwi.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Ukyuli biala na ukyuli ɔni lɛlɔ muusé lɛlɔ weti kɔnu wetuku-nwu ɔdubuse lɛlɔ. Na ukyuli biala lɛnɔ metuku-nwu ɔdubuse lɛlɔ wetédu useyi uwi.”

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Kɔbuli kudeedi kemmo na Israelƒuɔ ƒui bétéduo Sin Ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo na báda bana keliekɔ na Kades. Mmɔ na Miriam úkpi na báva-nwu.

english_verse: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ ni, ntu biala bútakya mmɔ na bakɛ bani, anwuɔsu Israel kadi bekyuli bammɔ básala lɛlɔ báta bénye Mose ku Aaron lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na bádɔnku Mose banini, “Si bukpi na abu lɛnɔ búkpi-ku bekyuli bani nékpi na Unwoti anumi mmɔ nka ɔdia-bu utulo!

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: Bi ɔsu na éti bula ƒui ku bula bebuo ébewi ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kamɛni kemmo na bukpi bɔkya mɛni?

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Na bi ɔsu na ákpanku-bu ásiku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ábakya ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kamɛni kemmo, kesii kani na edula ebi adi iye kɔnwingyie iye egyiibi lidu adi eeebo, na ntu biala muedi buuubo na bɔni?”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mose ku Aaron bátɔlɔ bekyuli bani násala mmɔ kudɔ na bátáyu bátɛ kalɔ na béti bana anumi bébi kalɔ na Unwoti Adi Kevo anumi. Mmɔ na Unwoti bukeye bɔ́bwɛ búbewi-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: “Ti ugyii ɔdadi ɔmmɔ na awɔ ku Aaron bɛsala bekyuli bammɔ ƒui. Na etemi ete lɛtakpɛ lɛmmɔ na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui anumi. Na ntu bɔdubo bɔlɛ lɛtakpɛ lɛmmɔ kemmo na bekyuli bammɔ ku bana bebuo bani.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Mose úti ugyii ɔdadi ɔmmɔ ɔ́siku Unwoti anumi aani kalɛ kani na úbo-nwu ɔda.

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: Na anwu ku Aaron básala bekyuli bammɔ na lɛtakpɛ lɛmmɔ kudɔ. Na Mose ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Amii batuɔkplune, binu! Bɛwia ntu bɛni bɛsiku lɛtakpɛ lɛmɛni kemmo?”

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mose ɔ́talaku ugyii ɔmmɔ katɔ na ɔ́ƒiɛmi lɛtakpɛ lɛmmɔ kunyɔ na ntu bɔ́bwɛ bɔ́lɛ-ni kemmo. Na bekyuli bammɔ ku bana bebuo báni kaduɛ.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ku Aaron ɔnini, “Ka bitaƒɔ-mi bítadi geen na bite-mi ɔbu ka nse kedee na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ anumi ɔsu ni, bɛsɔ bɛɛɛdubo bekyuli bammɔ bɔkpanku busienku kalɔ kani lɛ́su ka ndubo-ma bute kemmo.”

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Ala amɛni álɛ na Meriba. Ɔsika mmɔ na Israelƒuɔ bákyaku Unwoti unyeƒi na údie ɔtina-ma ka Unwoti ɔni use kedee na ɔdi na bana akɔ. Edomƒuɔ Ɔga Úni Ka Israelƒuɔ Bavi Nwuna Kalɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo Mose ɔ́tala bekyuli badi ɔ́kya Edomƒuɔ ɔga na bátásu-nwu banini, “Ƒ'ɔnwani Israel ɔnini, ‘Agyi lɛbibo lɛni néebo-bu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: Bula bati kuuku bétélie Egyipte kalɔ akwa pii. Na Egyipteƒuɔ bamɛni bábla abu ku bula bati kuuku kalala geen.

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: Nsu ka búwulo bɔ́kpali Unwoti ni, únu bula buwulo. Na ɔ́tala nwuna ɔtu ɔdi ɔkya-bu, na úbada-bu údie Egyipteƒuɔ enu kemmo. “ ‘Na ɔƒɛni búusie lɛgba laa búbedu Kedes ɔma ɔni nkya ƒula ɔmii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Na buuvele-ɔ ka te-bu kuƒi na bɔsia bɔvia ƒula kalɔ ku lɛma kemmo. Na bulávi bina mmo iye adingyii mmo bɔdi kemmo. Na buláni bina abiɔ ntu bɔdi lɛnɔ. Bɔsia kani na bɔdubo ƒula lilu linengudi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ bɔsia bɔvi na bulenwini bulanu kɔmii iye kɔdianu útédu ka bɔ́vi ƒula kalɔ kemmo bɔ́wɔlɔ.’ ”

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Nsu Edomƒuɔ ɔga údie batalane bammɔ kenye ɔnini, “Kuƒi kuuubo ka bɛvi mmɔ. Na si bɛ́yu atuɔkplu bɔdubɔta na buti bula kuwii na bubekpoku-mii.”

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ básɔ bédie kenye banini, “Ulu unengudi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ kani bɔdubo bɔsia. Na si bula ɔdi iye bula ebuo ɔdi ɔ́ni bina ntu bɔdi bɔdubɔƒɔ kayu. Mmomu kalɛ kani na bɔsia mmɔ bɔvi ku lɛgba kani na bɔɔwia.”

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Edomƒuɔ básɔ bédie-ma kenye banini, “Kuƒi kuuubo ka bɛsia-bu kalɔ kemmo.” Amu na Edomƒuɔ bamɛni báta na béti bana bekpone bani mbo ɔyikun kaduɛ ka betékpoku-ma.

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Na ka Edomƒuɔ bétete kuƒi ka basia bana kalɔ kemmo bavi ɔsu ni, Israelƒuɔ bédeyi na bátásia ulu bamba. Aaron Úkpi

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ báta Kades na bébedu Hor Kɔbi kaƒɔna.

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: “Aaron ɔdubusie utánwuna ku nwuna bati. Na ɔɔɔdubo buduo kalɔ kani líti muute Israelƒuɔ mmɔ kemmo, ɔsika awɔ Mose ku Aaron bɛ́ta binye mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ na Meriba Ketudɔ.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Kpanku Aaron ku ubidi Eleasar sienku Hor Kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili.

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: Die Aaron lɛwu gyɔlɔɔ lɛmmɔ na eti-ni akya ubidi Eleasar, ɔsika Aaron ɔdubo busie nwuna bati kudɔ mmɔ.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Mose lɛnɔ ɔ́bla kalɛ kani na Unwoti úbo-nwu ɔda. Na ɔ́kpanku-ma úsienku Hor Kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui anumi.

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mose údie Aaron lɛwu gyɔlɔɔ lɛmmɔ na úti-ni ɔ́kya ubidi Eleasar. Na Aaron úkpi na kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili. Na Mose ku Eleasar báyu kɔbi kɔmmɔ lili bébo kalɔ.

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ báti ka Aaron úkpi ni, Israelƒuɔ béwulo-nwu emeyi avlaatɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bésie bási Hor Kɔbi lɛlɔ na Ɛpugyie ulu lɛlɔ bétédu Edom na bésela ni, Israelƒuɔ bamɛni basɔ balakɛ kayi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bétemi béwi Mose ku Unwoti na básu banini, “Bi ɔsu na bɛ́da-bu bídie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ na bubekpi bɔkya ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kamɛni kemmo? Kesii kani na bodobodo ku ntu buuubo? Na adila ani bɔɔdi mɛni éedu-bu ɔkwɛ!”

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu Unwoti údie balakpi bani mbo ugyulo ukpidi ɔkya-ma na bádu Israelƒuɔ badu kaduɛ.

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bekyuli bammɔ bákpɛ bede Mose na básu-nwu banini, “Bɔ́bla likpidi na awɔ ku Unwoti anumi, ɔsika bútemi buwi-mii. Anwuɔsu buuvele na akpali Unwoti na ɔda balakpi bamɛni udie-bu akɔ.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Mose ɔ́kpali Unwoti na úvele ute bekyuli bammɔ.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Vɔ kɔlakpi udu ɔdi na akɔliku-nwu aƒala ugyii ɔdi eli. Na ukyuli biala na kɔlakpi kɔ́du-nwu na unwini ɔnu kɔlakpi kɔni nƒa ugyii lɛlɔ mmɔ na nwuna ɔlɛ ɔba-nwu.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose úti lɛbualagyie na ɔ́vɔ kɔlakpi na úti-nwu ɔ́ƒala ugyii lɛlɔ. Mmɔ na si kɔlakpi kɔ́du ukyuli ɔdi na ɔ́talaku nwuna lili ɔ́nu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ pɛ na nwuna ɔlɛ ɔ́ɔba-nwu. Israelƒuɔ Básɔ Báta Báyu Ulu

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ bésie na betédu Obot.

english_verse: and then in the Zered Gorge.
translation_verse: Na ka básɔ báta mmɔ ni, basɔ bétédu Sared Kɔwɛ kemmo.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Na ka básɔ bási mmɔ ni, bakɛ lɛgya lɛgya na betédu Aron ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kani nkɛ utédu Amoriƒuɔ ɔmii lɛlɔ. Na Arnon ndi Moabƒuɔ ɔmii ɔni nkya Moabƒuɔ ku Amoriƒuɔ ntɛ.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu na bénweni bákya Kekpo Ɔku kemmo banini, “Waheb ɔma ɔni nkya Suƒa ku Arnon Kɔwɛ

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: ku kɔwɛ kɔni náyu kútédu Ar, na ɔkɛ étédu Moab.”

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Ka bási mmɔ ni, bésie bétédu kesii kani baalɔ banini, Beer. Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Sala bekyuli bammɔ ƒui lisu na ndubo-ma ntu bute na bani.”

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ na Israelƒuɔ bátu kɔgya kɔmɛni. “Abiɔ, bitaayu ntu pii, na bɔdubo kɔgya buti bɔkya-mii kenye.

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: Libiɔ lɛni na bagadine béku, na bekyuli bammɔ batɔnkune bátu kɔgya. Béti bagadine ɔyikun ugyii lɛbuala ku batɔnkune ligyii lɛdadi béku.” Na báta bási ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo bésie Matana.

english_verse: then at Nahaliel, and then at Bamoth.
translation_verse: Na bási Matana bésie Nahaliel na bási Nahaliel bésie Bamot.

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Na bási Bamot bésie kɔwɛ kɔni nkya Moab kesii kani Pisga uwi katɔ kakɛ na akana enye anu ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ. Israelƒuɔ Békpo Bádi Sihon Ku Og Lɛlɔ

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: Na Hesbon ndi Amoriƒuɔ Ɔga Sihon ɔma unengudi. Anwu nékpo ku Moabƒuɔ ɔga ɔkukudi na úti nwuna kɔlɔ ƒui útédu Arnon.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ bátala batu bákya Amoriƒuɔ Ɔga Sihon ka,

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: ute kuƒi na basia nwuna kalɔ lɛlɔ bavi. Na beledeyi belésie kemo iye adingyii kemo kadi. Na baláni nwuna abiɔ ntu bɔdi lɛnɔ. Na Ɔga Ulu Unengudi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ kani badubo busie bɔvi útédu ka bɔ́via nwuna ɔmii.

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Nsu Sihon útete kuƒi na bavi nwuna kalɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́sala nwuna bekpone ƒui na bésie ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo ka betékpo-ku Israelƒuɔ. Na ka bédu Yahas ni, békpoku Israelƒuɔ.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bádu-ma kaduɛ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu béti bana kalɔ ɔ́si Arnon útédu Yabok. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdi Amonƒuɔ kakɛ. Ɔsika Amonƒuɔ bágyumana bana ɔmii kaduɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ békpo báƒɔ Amoriƒuɔ lɛma linengudi ƒui na béti-ni ku Hesbon ku lɛma lɛni nde-ni ƒui.

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na baatu asugba kɔgya banini, “Bibo na bɔsɔ bɔda Hesbon ɔma. Na bɛya bɔsɔku Ɔga Sihon ɔma unengudi use aani kalɛ use kuuku.

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Dii ni, Hesbon ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni Sihon bekpone báta aani kalɛ lɛgyavonku lɛsala. Na útáyila Moabƒuɔ ɔma Ar na bése bétebile ala na abi ani nkya Arnon katɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Amii Moabƒuɔ bɔbuɛ ɔdi bina ɔdi. Amii kadi bekyuli bani mɔɔkpá Kemos baƒiɔ bɛyii ku udu. Bɛya na bina bananabi bekeli betenwini kadi bamba bekyuli. Na bina belekubi ni, Amoriƒuɔ Ɔga Sihon ɔdubo-ma buƒie bɔtɔlɔku.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: Nsu búgyingya-ma ƒui na Hesbon ɔ́yii udu útédu Dibon. Na bɔ́yila-ma butédu Noƒa laa útédu Medeba.”

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israelƒuɔ báda keliekɔ na Amoriƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Mose ɔ́tala bekyuli badi ka batánu Yaser ɔma. Na Israelƒuɔ békpo na báƒɔ kɔlɔ kɔni nkya amadɔ mmɔ. Na bábɔku Amoriƒuɔ bani nlie mmɔ bene.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama bénwini na bátásia ulu ɔni úti úsela Basan. Amu na Og ɔni ndi Basanƒuɔ ɔga úti nwuna bekpone ka betékpoku Israelƒuɔ na Edrei.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Tayia bekyuli bammɔ, ɔsika líti ɔga ɔmmɔ ku nwuna bekpone ku kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛ́kya-a enu kemmo na kalɛ na ábla Sihon ɔni ndi Amoriƒuɔ ɔga ɔni nádi lɛga na Hesbon lɛni kani na ɔlɛka abla Ɔga Og.”

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bádu ɔga ɔmmɔ ku nwuna bebi bananabi ku bekpone bammɔ ƒui ɔni na ukyuli unwi muedi utebu. Na béti bana kalɔ kammɔ.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Anu na Israelƒuɔ báta bátáda keliekɔ na Moab kalɔ ƒiaa lɛlɔ na Yordan Ketudɔ kesii kani nde Yeriko ɔma.

english_verse: When King Balak of Moab and his people heard how many Israelites there were and what they had done to the Amorites, he and the Moabites were terrified and panicked.
translation_verse: liƒu lɛ́da Moabƒuɔ geen, ɔsika bemomo geen. Na sɔsɔ ni, liƒu lɛ́du Moab ɔ́si Israelƒuɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Amu na Moabƒuɔ básu Midianƒuɔ batɔnkune banii, “Bekyuli lisu lɛmɛni badubo lɛla biala lɛkya bula amadɔ mɛni udu bɔyila aani kalɛ ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔɔkun livo lɛni lɛdia.” Ɔmɛni ɔsu Sipor ubidi Balak ɔni ndi Moabƒuɔ ɔga na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: ɔ́tala bekyuli badi ka besie Beor ubidi Bileam ɔni nli Petor ɔni nde ketu kani nkya nwuna ɔma mmɔ kudɔ ɔnii batásu-nwu banini, “Bekyuli badi báta bási Egyipte na bébeyi mina kalɔ lɛlɔ na belie bede-mi.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bo na ebewida bekyuli bamɛni. Ɔsika bekyuli bammɔ bebo ɔyikun geen betulo-mi. Na si ewida-ma ni, ndubɔkana bukpo bɔdi-ma lɛlɔ na lɛbɔku-ma lidie kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔsika ngyi ka bekyuli bani na ásu ka kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku-ma ni, ɔdubɔsiaku-ma lɛni kani. Na bani lɛnɔ na éwida ni, ewida adubɔsiaku-ma lɛni kani.”

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Amu na Moabƒuɔ ku Midianƒuɔ batɔnkune báyu ulu na béti egulabi ani baaƒɔ asa na beebó like bada. Na ka beteduo Bileam kudɔ ni, básu-nwu lɛla lɛni Balak ɔ́su-ma.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Amu na Bileam ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛtɛ-mi kudɔ usien ɔmɛni na lɛla lɛni Unwoti ubo ka ɔsu-mii ni, ndubɔsu-mii.” Ɔmɛni ɔsu Moabƒuɔ batɔnkune bamɛni bátɛ mmɔ usien ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Katɔti úbo Bileam kudɔ na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bekyuli bamani nkya-a kudɔ mɛni?”

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Amu na Bileam údie Katɔti kenye ɔnini, “Sipor ubidi Balak ɔni ndi Moabƒuɔ ɔga néti kenye kamɛni úmene-mi ɔnini,

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: ‘Bekyuli lisu lɛni nási Egyipte bébo bákya mɛni béti kalɔ ƒui. Anwuɔsu bo na ebewida bekyuli bammɔ. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na lɛkana-ma bukpoku na lɛbɔku-ma lidie kalɔ kammɔ kemmo.’ ”

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Nsu Katɔti ɔ́su Bileam ɔnini, “Awɔ ku bekyuli bammɔ bitesie kesii kadi. Lɛnɔ ni, tewida Israelƒuɔ bammɔ. Ɔsika badi bekyuli bani na béte kusɛ kusɛ.”

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Ka kadi kégye ni, Bileam ɔ́ta na ɔ́lɔ Moabƒuɔ batɔnkune bammɔ na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Binwini biteesie bina ɔma. Ɔsika Unwoti útete-mi kuƒi ka lɛsiaku-mii.”

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Moabƒuɔ bammɔ bénwini bésie Balak kudɔ na básu-nwu banini, “Bileam úni ka ɔsiaku-bu.”

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Balak ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tala bekyuli bamba bani na basɔ bemomo na bebo ɔbu betulo bekyuli bedeedi.

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: Na bésie Bileam kudɔ na bátásu-nwu banini, “Lɛni na Sipor ubidi Balak ɔɔsu-bu ka bɔ́su-ɔ. Ɔnii taya na lɛla lɛdi litele-ɔ ulu na mina kudɔ bubo.

english_verse: Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God.
translation_verse: Nsu Bileam údie bekyuli bammɔ kenye ɔnini, “Ina Balak úti sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi úyile nwuna kaduli kani kemmo na ulie ɔɔdi lɛga ute-mi muedi naaakana na lini mina Unwoti Katɔti ɔda ɔni na úbo-mi na ulu biala lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ami lɛnɔ bɛtɛ mɛni aani kalɛ bedeedi bammɔ bátɛ kalɛ. Na lɛwia lɛsiku Unwoti kudɔ lɛla lɛni na wasu-mi na litemi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Ka kadi kégye ni, Bileam úti nwuna ebuo ala utine na ɔ́kɔ úlie-nwu kama. Na anwu ku Moab bekyuli bani na ɔ́tala mmɔ bátɔlɔ.

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Nsu ka úsela ni, Unwoti úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya Bileam. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Unwoti ɔtu ɔdi útáda-nwu únyene ulu lɛlɔ na uléte ebuo ɔmmɔ kuƒi ka ɔvi. Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo Bileam útiku nwuna kabla bablane inyɔ ɔda na béli ebuo ɔmmɔ kama.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Ka ebuo ɔmmɔ ɔ́nu Unwoti ɔtu ɔmɛni ka únye ulu ntɛ na ɔ́kpa lɛtula ɔda ni, ebuo ɔmmɔ údeyi ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na úti anumi ɔ́tina kemo kadi kemmo. Na Bileam uubó ebuo ɔmɛni ka ɔsɔ unwini ubasia ulu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔtu ɔmɛni ɔ́sɔ únye ulu blii suɛ ɔdi lɛlɔ na adingyii mmo inyɔ bɔdi ntɛ. Na bátu awodu bákya-mu lɛƒɛnyi inyɔ bɔmmɔ.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Na ka ebuo ɔmmɔ ɔ́nu Unwoti ɔtu ɔmmɔ ni, úti lɛlɔ útámana lɛwoduku lɛmmɔ na lɛɛmana Bileam ɔgba momoomo. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Bileam ɔ́sɔ úbi ebuo ɔmmɔ kugyiimi ubu.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔtu ɔmmɔ úsie anumi na úténye kesii kani nse klo klo na kuƒi kɔdi kuuubo na akana lɛlɔ bunwini buse kɔdianu iye kɔmii kakɛ.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti úbimi ebuo ɔmɛni kenye na úse kalɔ uutemi taasu Bileam ɔnini, “Bi na lɛ́bla-a ɔsu na eebó-mi kɔtɛ sɔɔn?”

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Amu na Bileam údie ebuo ɔmmɔ kenye ɔnini, “Ɔsika ábu-mi kɔdɔlɔ! Na si kewii na nka nda ni, nka ndubo-ɔ bɔdu ɔƒɛni kani.”

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Amu na ebuo ɔmɛni úye Bileam ɔnii, “Ɔɔɔdi ami ndi ebuo ɔni lɛlɔ na élie ƒula ngba emeyi ƒui? Na lɛ́ɛbla-a lɛmɛni udu dii?” Na Bileam údie kenye ɔnini, “Átabla lɛni kudii.”

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Amu na Bileam údie ɔtu ɔmmɔ kenye ɔnini, “Lɛ́bla likpidi. Ńtati ka awɔ nnye ulu lɛlɔ étile-mi. Nsu muuvele-ɔ ka si ɔɔɔdia ka lɛsɔ nteesie ulu ɔmmɔ ni, na asu-mi na linwini nteesie kaduli.”

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti Ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Awɔ ku bekyuli bammɔ biteesie. Nsu lɛla lɛni kani na lɛ́su-ɔ ni, ani kani na ɔlɛka asu.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Bileam ku bekyuli bammɔ bágyu na bátɔlɔ.

translation_verse: Amu na Bileam údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛ́ɛda ḿbalɛ, nsu lɛɛɛdubo-ɔ bɔsu lɛla lɛni ami ɔlati mɔɔyɔ́, mmomu lɛla lɛni na Katɔti weti wakya-mi kenye kani na ndubo-ɔ bɔsu.”

translation_verse: Amu na Bileam údie Balak kenye ɔnini, “Lɛla lɛni na Unwoti úti ɔ́kya-mi kenye kemmo ni, ani kani na ɔlɛka lɛsu?” Bileam Kenye Kanyɔdi Kani Ɔsɔ Údie

english_verse: Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni gyu lɛgba na atɔlɔ eteesie ƒula ɔma! Líse kenye ka nka mete-ɔ lɛyuƒɔla nsu Unwoti únye útile-ɔ ka akɛ lɛyuƒɔla lɛmmɔ!”

english_verse: that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
translation_verse: ‘Ina Balak úti sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi úyile nwuna kaduli kani kemmo na ulie ɔɔdi lɛga ute-mi muedi, naaakana na lini mina Unwoti Katɔti ɔda ɔni na úbo-mi na ulu biala lɛlɔ, na lɛbla lɛla lɛni ami ɔlati mɔɔyɔ́. english_verse: So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.” Balaam's Fourth Message
translation_verse: Amu na Bileam ɔ́su Balak ɔnini, “Ɔƒɛni lisela mina bekyuli kudɔ. Nsu asa na matɔlɔ ni, muubó-ɔ ɔda ɔmɛni na lɛsu-ɔ lɛla lɛni Israelƒuɔ badubo ƒula bekyuli bɔbla limeyi lɛdi.”

english_verse: Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Bileam úse kalɔ uudie Unwoti kenye kamɛni ɔnini, “Kenye kani na Boer ubidi Bileam udie. Etemila ani na ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnu kaduɛ ubo na udie.

english_verse: My knowledge comes from God Most High, the Lord All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: Etemila ani na ukyuli ɔni muunú lɛla lɛni na Katɔti ɔɔsu ubo na udie, ukyuli ɔni úbo lɛlati ɔsiku Katɔti kudɔ, ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnu budie bɔtina taasiku Ɔyikune Ƒui kudɔ, ukyuli ɔni náyu ɔ́tɛ na nwuna anumi ebi kalɔ nsu ɔɔnu nwaa.

english_verse: “What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.
translation_verse: “Mɔɔnu-nwu nsu ɔɔɔdi ɔƒɛni mɔɔnu taati nsu uuude. Kayabi kadi kadubo bɔbwɛ bɔlɛ Yakob kaba kemmo. Ɔgagyii ɔdi ɔdubɔlɛ Israelƒuɔ akɔ, na ubo Moabƒuɔ batɔnkune ƒui uwi kalɔ, na ɔƒɛ Set bekyuli ƒui uwi kalɔ.

english_verse: Israel will conquer Edom and capture the land of that enemy nation.
translation_verse: Na ɔdubɔdi nwuna bekisine bani nkya Edom lɛlɔ. Na ɔdubɔdi Seirƒuɔ bani muukpóku-nwu lɛlɔ. Nsu Israelƒuɔ ama ni, bana ɔyikun katɔ kani ɔdubɔkɔ.

english_verse: The king of Israel will rule and destroy the survivors of every town there.
translation_verse: Lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔdubɔlɛ bɔsiku Yakob kaba kemmo, na ɔyila bekyuli bani nébu ɔma unengudi udu.” Bileam Kenye Kekplodi Kani Údie

english_verse: “And I saw this vision about the Amalekites: Their nation is now great, but it will someday disappear forever.
translation_verse: Amu Na Bileam ɔ́nu Amelekƒuɔ na údie kenye kamɛni ɔnini, “Amalekƒuɔ ndi bekyuli bedeedi na kadi akɔ. Nsu badubo bɔyii udu na kawɔlɔkɔ.”

english_verse: “And this is what I saw about the Kenites: They think they're safe, living among the rocks,
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́nu Keniƒuɔ na údie kenye kamɛni ɔnini, “Bɛgyumana bina keliekɔ kaduɛ na bɛtu bina ayu bɛkya atakpɛ kemmo.

english_verse: but they will be wiped out when Assyria conquers them.
translation_verse: Nsu badubo-mii udu bɔyila si uwi ɔni Asiriaƒuɔ bébeƒie-mii ɔni na bɛɛɛgyi biiise.”

english_verse: “No one can survive if God plans destruction.
translation_verse: Amu na údie kenye kamɛni ɔnini, “Aa! Ɔma ndubɔkana bunye bɔnu uwi ɔni Katɔti ɔɔbla ɔmɛni?

english_verse: Ships will come from Cyprus, bringing people who will invade the lands of Assyria and Eber. But finally, Cyprus itself will be ruined.”
translation_verse: Lɛkɔlɔ libendi lɛdubɔsia Kittim Ɛpu kɔtu na badi Asiriaƒuɔ ku Eberƒuɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu ama lɛnɔ badubɔyila-ma udu.”

english_verse: After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_verse: Ka Bileam ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔ́ta na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie nwuna ɔma, na Balak lɛnɔ ɔ́wia nwuna ulu ɔ́sia.

english_verse: While the Israelites were camped at Acacia, some of the men had sex with Moabite women.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bákya Sitim ni, na ama ku Moab belekubi bése kalɔ baatɛ.

english_verse: These women then invited the men to ceremonies where sacrifices were offered to their gods. The men ate the meat from the sacrifices and worshiped the Moabite gods.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu beleku bamɛni baakpanku banana bammɔ teesienku bana lɛƒiɔkpa emeyi bɔdi kalɔ. Na Israelƒuɔ baadi adila ani béti bákpa béte baƒiɔ na baalɛ-ma akɔnkɔ kalɔ.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel because they had worshiped the god Baal Peor.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Israelƒuɔ béti lɛlɔ bébunku Moabƒuɔ na baakpá baƒiɔ bani baalɔ banii Baal-Peor. Ɔmmɔ ɔ́ya na Unwoti úti kɔnyi kati kati ɔ́kya-ma.

english_verse: So he said to Moses, “Take the Israelite leaders who are responsible for this and have them killed in front of my sacred tent where everyone can see. Maybe then I will stop being angry with the Israelites.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Kpanku Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune bammɔ ƒui lɛku na adu-ma ɔƒiiwi ketee na bekyuli bammɔ anumi na ukyuli biala ɔnu kalɛ na Unwoti kɔnyi kati kati kɔni na úti mmɔ kenye kayɔ na Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Moses told Israel's officials, “Each of you must put to death any of your men who worshiped Baal.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ litemi batɛne ɔnini, “Bina akɔ ukyuli biala ɔdu nwuna lɛlɔ bekyuli bani ndi banana bani néti lɛlɔ bákya Baal-Peor lɛƒiɔkpa kemmo.”

english_verse: Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family.
translation_verse: Amu na Israelni ɔnana ɔdi ɔ́kpanku Midiani ulekubi ɔdi úboku nwuna kaduli na Mose ku Israelƒuɔ ƒui anumi uwi ɔni na básala lisu na Unwoti Adi Kevo anumi beewulo.

english_verse: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw the couple and left the crowd. He found a spear
translation_verse: Na ka Pinehas ɔni ɔti ndi Eleasar ɔni ɔti ndi Aaron ɔ́nu lɛla lɛni na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́bla ni, ɔ́ta mmɔ na útéti lɛtula

english_verse: and followed the man into his tent, where he ran the spear through the man and into the woman's stomach. The Lord immediately stopped punishing Israel with a deadly disease,

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”
translation_verse: Na nwuna bekyuli ndubo bakpane kabla bɔbla usela uwi ƒui. Ɔsika úkpo kɔgyulo úte-mi na ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́ya na líti likpidi lɛni bekyuli bammɔ babla lɛkyiɛ-ma.”

english_verse: The Israelite man that was killed was Zimri son of Salu, who was one of the leaders of the Simeon tribe.
translation_verse: Na Israelni ɔni bádu ku Midiani uleku ɔmmɔ lɛnyi ndi Simri ɔni ndi Salu ubidi na ɔdi Simeon kaba ɔtɔnkune.

translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: “The Midianites are now enemies of Israel, so attack and defeat them! They tricked the people of Israel into worshiping their god at Peor, and they are responsible for the death of Cozbi, the daughter of one of their own leaders.”
translation_verse: ɔsika bábla-mii likyulikpi ala aani bekisine na bátɔlɔ-mii na bítákpa baƒiɔ na Peor ku Midiani ɔtɔnkune ubidi ulekubi ɔni baalɔ Kosbi na bádu-mmɔ kalɛ na ɔ́blaku-mii unwi ɔsu.”

translation_verse: “Bɛka Israelƒuɔ bammɔ bani nákɛ akwa aavlanyɔ ku kama na bédu kekpo busie. Na bɛka-ma na kɔduli kenye.”

translation_verse: Anwuɔsu uwi ɔni na bakya Moab kalɔ ƒiaa lɛlɔ na Yordan Ketu kɔtu ni, Mose ku ɔkpane Eleasar bétemi béte bekyuli bammɔ banini,

translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bumomo ƒui bɔdi mpim eti leevu-anyɔ ku unwi ku eti leevu-ene ku avlaatɛ (

english_verse: The tribe of Levi included the clans of the Gershonites, Kohathites, Merarites,

english_verse: as well as the clans of Libni, Hebron, Mahli, Mushi, and Korah. Kohath the Levite was the father of Amram,
translation_verse: Na bamɛni ndi Lewiƒuɔ kaba bekyuli. Libniƒuɔ Hebronƒuɔ Mahliƒuɔ Musiƒuɔ Koraƒuɔ Na Kehat náwɔ Amram.

english_verse: the husband of Levi's daughter Jochebed, who was born in Egypt. Amram and Jochebed's three children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
translation_verse: Na Amram ulekudi lɛnyi ndi Yokebed na ɔ́si Lewi kaba kemmo, na anwu náwɔ Lewiƒuɔ na Egyipte. Na anwu náwɔ Aaron ku Mose ku nwuna ɔnwani ulekubi Miriam.

english_verse: except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. The Lord had said that everyone else would die there in the desert.

english_verse: One day his daughters went to the sacred tent, where they met with Moses, Eleazar, and some other leaders of Israel, as well as a large crowd of Israelites. The young women said:

english_verse: You know that our father died in the desert. But it was for something he did wrong, not for joining with Korah in rebelling against the Lord. Our father left no sons
translation_verse: “Bula ɔti úkpi na ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo ɔni na útawɔ ubi ɔnanabi ɔdi. Na lɛnɔ uuubunku Kora kama basiakune bani náta bénye Unwoti lɛlɔ. Na anwu ɔlati likpidi kukpi na úkpi.

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord what should be done,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose úti bana litemi lɛmɛni útáva Unwoti anumi.

english_verse: and the Lord answered:
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

translation_verse: “Lɛla lɛni na Seloƒehad bebi belekubi baasu mɛni lɛdi sɔsɔ. Anwuɔsu ɔlɛka ete-ma bana bati kadikɔ kadi na kabla bana ɔdi. Anwuɔsu sɔku bana ɔti kadikɔ te-ma.”

english_verse: If he has no daughter, his brothers will inherit the land.

english_verse: But if he has no brothers, his father's brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Na si ukpine ɔmmɔ uuubo banwani bananabi badi ya na nwuna ɔti banwani bananabi badi nwuna ala.

english_verse: And if his father has no brothers, the land must be given to his nearest relative in the clan. This is my law, and the Israelites must obey it. Joshua Is Appointed Israel's Leader (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Na si uuubo ɔti banwani badi ya na nwuna ukyuli ɔni na ude-nwu na nwuna ɔtɔ kemmo ɔdi nwuna ala. Na ɔda bubo bɔmɛni bɔdi Israelƒuɔ ɔda ɔni ɔlɛka badi-nwu lɛlɔ geen. Na lɛni na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda.” Yosua Úti Mose Keliekɔ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “One day you will go up into the Abarim Mountains, and from there you will see the land I am giving the Israelites.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Kɔ sie Abarim Kɔbi kɔmɛni lili na atánu kalɔ kani líti muute Israelƒuɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: After you have seen it, you will die, just like your brother Aaron,

english_verse: because both of you disobeyed me at Meribah near the town of Kadesh in the Zin Desert. When the Israelites insulted me there, you didn't believe in my holy power.”
translation_verse: ɔsika awɔ ku Aaron ƒui bɛ́ta bínye mina ɔda ɔni líbo-mii lɛlɔ na Sin ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ ƒui báta bénye-mi lɛlɔ na bítabu-mi na bana anumi ka nse kedee.” Ala amɛni álɛ na Meriba Ketudɔ na Kades na Sin Ketele kemmo.

english_verse: “You are the Lord God, and you know what is in everyone's heart. So I ask you to appoint a leader for Israel.

english_verse: Your people need someone to lead them into battle, or else they will be like sheep wandering around without a shepherd.”
translation_verse: ɔni ndubo butaakpanku-ma teesienku taasɔku teeboku kalɛ na belénwini aani baƒonu bani neeebo ɔdane.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Joshua son of Nun can do the job. Place your hands on him to show that he is the one to take your place.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Ti Nun ubidi Yosua, ukyuli ɔni na mina kɔyu kɔ́ƒɔ-nwu lɛlɔ kemmo, na eti ƒula kɔnu asia-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then go with him and tell him to stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the Israelites. Appoint Joshua as their new leader
translation_verse: Na aya na unye ɔkpane Eleasar ku Israelƒuɔ ƒui anumi asa na ese-nwu ƒula kenye unyene.

english_verse: and tell them they must now obey him, just as they obey you.
translation_verse: Na ete-nwu ƒula ɔyikun ɔmmɔ ɔdi kalɛ na Israelƒuɔ ƒui babu-nwu.

english_verse: But Joshua must depend on Eleazar to find out from me what I want him to do as he leads Israel into battle.”

english_verse: Moses followed the Lord's instructions and took Joshua to Eleazar and the people,

english_verse: then he placed his hands on Joshua and appointed him Israel's leader.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: Offer sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, so that I will smell the smoke and be pleased.
translation_verse: “Bo ɔda te Israelƒuɔ anini, ‘Bitaabla akpala teete-mi na uwi ɔni líse-mii lɛlɔ limeyi ndi limeyi. Na akpala ammɔ uyɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ.’

english_verse: Each day offer two rams a year old as sacrifices to please me. The animals must have nothing wrong with them;
translation_verse: “Na akpala amɛni na ɔlɛka biteeti taabla limeyi ndi limeyi akpala teete ami Unwoti. Bɛwia baƒonu bagyani inyɔ bani náakɛ lɛkwa linwi limeyi ndi limeyi na bɔsɔ bɔdi buuubo-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Along with each of them, one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice.
translation_verse: Na akpala biala kemmo ni, bɛwia edula ebi ɔlaaƒɔ akyami anyɔ na bɛwia nnɔ bɔni bɔdia geen lɛɛƒɛɛ inyɔ bɛsala-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: Finally, along with each of these two sacrifices, a liter of wine must be poured on the altar as a drink offering.
translation_verse: Na ɔtanta koƒonu kɔni bɛdubo buti bɔbla akpala ammɔ ni, bɛwia ntɛ bɔni bébulo lɛɛƒɛɛ inyɔ na biwilimi biwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: On the first day of each month, bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na limeyi lideedi na kɔbuli biala kalɔ kesekɔ ni, na bawia bakɔ bakɔdi inyɔ ku koƒonu kɔgyani kunwi ku baƒonu bebi maatɛ bani nákɛ lɛkwa na bɔsɔ bɔdi buuubo-ma lɛlɔ na beti babla bɔkyula akpala bete Unwoti.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Na akɔ ɔkɔdi biala badubo bɔbla akpala ni, na bawia edula ebi ɔlaaƒɔ akyami aku na bɛsala-nwu ku nnɔ. Na koƒonu akpala bawia kakpa akyami ene na bawia ɔlaaƒɔ ɔni muukeye na beti nnɔ basala-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: Celebrate Passover in honor of me on the fourteenth day of the first month of each year.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na limeyi leevu-linedi biala na kɔbuli kudeedi lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka badi Unwoti Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi.

english_verse: The following day will begin the Festival of Thin Bread, which will last for a week. During this time you must honor me by eating bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Na limeyi leevu-lɛlɔndi na kɔbuli kɔmmɔ kemmo kani na beti emeyi maatɛ badi emeyi bete Unwoti. Na emeyi ammɔ bɔdi kemmo ni, ɔdi utadi bodobodo ɔni na bɔnyii bɔkya-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: On the first day of this festival, you must rest from your work and come together for worship.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ni, bɛsa bɔsa kedee na mina lɛnyi lɛlɔ na ɔdi utabla limeyi ndi limeyi kabla kadi.

english_verse: Bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. And then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Na beti bakɔ inyɔ ku koƒonu kɔgyani kunwi ku baƒonubi maatɛ bani nákɛ lɛkwa na bɔsɔ bɔdi buuubo-ma lɛlɔ na beti babla bɔkyula akpala bete Unwoti.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Na akɔ biala badubuti babla akpala ni, na bawia edula ebi akyami aku na beti nnɔmii basala-nwu kemmo na beti babla akpala. Na koƒonu akpala na beti kakpa akyami ene

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: na baƒonubi maatɛ bammɔ ni, bawia kakpa akyami anyɔ bite koƒonu biala.

english_verse: All of these are to be offered each day of the festival in additional to the regular sacrifices, and the smoke from them will please me.
translation_verse: Na lɛni badubo adila ani bebeti bataabla bɔkyula akpala limeyi biala na emeyi maatɛ ammɔ ƒui kemmo. Na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔyɔ Unwoti kaƒɔ. Na ɔlɛka banwa adila ammɔ bebunku bɔkyula akpala ku ntɛ akpala ani baayɔ́ bɔbla lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then on the last day of the festival, you must once again rest from work and come together for worship. The Sacrifices during the Harvest Festival (Leviticus
translation_verse: Na limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, bɛsa bɔsa kedee na mina lɛnyi lɛlɔ na ɔdi utabla limeyi ndi limeyi kabla kadi. Edula Bɔƒɛ Limeyi Bɔdi

english_verse: On the first day of the Harvest Festival, you must rest from your work, come together for worship, and bring a sacrifice of new grain.
