translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́su ɔnii balɔ adua benengu ku bana bebunkune bammɔ ƒui beboku na ɔtɛmi ute-ma. Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Lɛla lɛni mɔɔsu-mii ni, katɔ ku kalɔ ndubudie bina bɔƒiɔ ɔtina-mii.

english_verse: I am going to die soon, and I know that in the future you will stop caring about what is right and what is wrong, and so you will disobey the Lord and stop living the way I told you to live. The Lord will be angry, and terrible things will happen to you. The Song of Moses
translation_verse: Ngyi ka mina kekpima ni, bekyuli bamɛni badubo bekyuli bekpidi bunwini na badubo ala ani na lɛ́tina-ma mɛni buni. Na uwi ɔdi ɔdubo ɔni na badubo ɔgbankpi bɔsiaku, na uwi ɔdi ɔdubo ɔni na badubo Unwoti kɔnyi bɔkya na bataabla ala ani na úbo-ma ɔda ɔnii batabla.” Mose Ɔ́tu Ɔnu Ɔdi

english_verse: Earth and Sky, listen to what I say!
translation_verse: Katɔ ku kalɔ, binu mina etemila na bise atu kaduɛ, na binu lɛla lɛni ndubo bɔsu.

english_verse: Israel, I will teach you. My words will be like gentle rain on tender young plants, or like dew on the grass.
translation_verse: Mina ala bɔtina adubɔyu aani kalɛ na ɔnantu ɔɔna na ubewi kalɔ aani amii. Mina etemila adubɔyu aani kalɛ na ɔnantu uuwi blii blii teewi edula ani na átalɛ tɔ lili lɛlɔ. Na adubɔyu ewi livo lɛni na ɔƒɛni na lɛɛkwɛ́ lɛlɔ blii blii.

english_verse: Join with me in praising the wonderful name of the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Ndubumwi Unwoti lɛnyi, na nwuna bekyuli badubɔsu nwuna ala ebendi ani na ɔɔbla.

english_verse: The Lord is a mighty rock, and he never does wrong. God can always be trusted to bring justice.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ndi bina lɛtakpɛ lɛni na bíkpo kama, na nwuna ablala ƒui ese siin, na bɔƒiɔ bɔdi buuubo-nwu kemmo. Bina Unwoti ablala ƒui adi sɔsɔ, na ɔɔbla ala ani nse siin na akɛ ulu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But you lie and cheat and are unfaithful to him. You have disgraced yourselves and are no longer worthy to be his children.
translation_verse: Nsu bana ablala aaadi sɔsɔ, na bátamanku ka babla nwuna bekyuli. Ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli béyi ku likpidi ku katɔlɔ.

english_verse: Israel, the Lord is your Father, the one who created you, but you repaid him by being foolish.
translation_verse: Ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na bɛdubɔsia bise bina Unwoti kɔdɛ na ɔdi mmɔ? Amii bekyuli badɔlɔdi biiibo kasusu kadi. Unwoti ndi bina Ɔti ku bina Udiene. Na anwu nábla-mii na ɔ́vɔ-mii.

english_verse: Think about past generations. Ask your parents or any of your elders. They will tell you
translation_verse: Binyimo ala ani nébo abavi ku kuuku ala, na biye bina bati na basu-mii ala ani nálɛ dii. Na biye bina benengu bani náabi, na basu-mii ala ani nálɛ dii.

english_verse: but the Lord himself takes care of Israel.
translation_verse: Ɔsika Unwoti ɔlati néti Israelƒuɔ bani ndi Yakob bebi ɔ́bla nwuna badi.

english_verse: Israel, the Lord discovered you in a barren desert filled with howling winds. God became your fortress, protecting you as though you were his own eyes.
translation_verse: Na bese-nwu aani bekyuli bakɛdi na kalɔ kakwiidi kani kemmo na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni mɔɔkula ala uukpó uwi ƒui ku kudu. Na Katɔti nébenwini bana kabɛkɔ. Na ɔkya ɔɔgyumana-ma aani nwuna lɛnumi kebi.

english_verse: The Lord was like an eagle teaching its young to fly, always ready to swoop down and catch them on its back.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́bla-ma aani kɔdigbo aasɛ ɔni mɔɔtina ubidi buveyi. Na si ɔ́yu kalɔ na úƒie-nwu ɔ́sia nwuna avwi kama. Na Unwoti ɔ́gyumana Israel kalɛ na ulebuli.

english_verse: Israel, the Lord led you, and without the aid of a foreign god,
translation_verse: Na Unwoti lɛti pɛ ɔ́tɔnku nwuna bekyuli ɔni na útawia kebunku kadi útasiku kadi kadi baƒiɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: he helped you capture the land. Your fields were rich with grain. Olive trees grew in your stony soil, and honey was found among the rocks.
translation_verse: Na úbunku-ma na békpo baƒɔ kɔlɔ. Na bana edula ani báva na bana mmo ádia na bádi. Na bana nnɔ egyii adia na atakpɛ lɛlɔ. Na uwɔ úlie na atakpɛ akɔ.

english_verse: Your flocks and herds produced milk and yogurt, and you got choice meat from your sheep and goats that grazed in Bashan. Your wheat was the finest, and you drank the best wine.
translation_verse: Ɔ́ya na bana ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku bese bákɛ anyi ntu pii. Na bebo baƒonu ku bese ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ bani ndia ntulo. Na bákɛ edula abuni, na bákɛ ntɛ bɔni mɔɔda ɔkwɛ geen.

english_verse: Israel, you grew fat and rebelled against God, your Creator you rejected the Mighty Rock, your only place of safety.
translation_verse: Unwoti bekyuli bákɛ lɛlɔ, nsu balábu-nwu. Bélie lɛmwi, na bádi bémo. Nsu bénwini kama bákya bana Katɔti ɔni ndi bana Udiene. Na béni bana Ɔƒɔne Ɔyikune ƒui.

english_verse: You made God jealous and angry by worshiping disgusting idols and foreign gods.
translation_verse: Bana baƒiɔ bani kama básiaku ni, ɔ́ya na úkpo kogyulo. Na likpidi lɛni bábla ɔ́ya na úti kɔnyi.

english_verse: You offered sacrifices to demons, those useless gods that never helped you, new gods that your ancestors never worshiped.
translation_verse: Bádu bebuo bákpa béte baƒiɔ bani naaadi ku lɛla, baƒiɔ bani bana bati kuuku baaagyi kudii, baƒiɔ bani na Israel úni ka balakpa kudii.

english_verse: You turned away from God, your Creator; you forgot the Mighty Rock, the source of your life.
translation_verse: Na báyiƒala bana Katɔti ɔni ndi bana Ɔƒɔne Ɔyikune ƒui ɔni náya na belie ngba.

english_verse: You were the Lord's children, but you made him angry. Then he rejected you
translation_verse: Ka Unwoti ɔ́nu ɔmɛni ni, úti kɔnyi. Na úni nwuna bebi belekubi ku bananabi.

english_verse: and said, “You are unfaithful and can't be trusted. So I won't answer your prayers; I'll just watch and see what happens to you.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su ɔnii ɔsɔ ulebunku-ma lɛnɔ. Na ɔdubunye bɔnu lɛla lɛni malɛku-ma. “Bekyuli bamɛni báyii ulu na bana ablala eeese siin.

english_verse: You worshiped worthless idols, and made me jealous and angry! Now I will send a cruel and worthless nation to make you jealous and angry.
translation_verse: Baƒiɔ bani na bábla ɔ́ya na líti kɔnyi lɛ́kya-ma. Na muukpó kogyulo ku bana baƒiɔ bani naaadi ku lɛla mmɔ sɔsɔ. Anwuɔsu ndubuti kadi bekyuli bani naaadi lɛla lɛdi lɛkya-ma kɔnyi. Na ndubɔya na bana bekisine babla bekyuli geen.

english_verse: “My people, I will breathe out fire that sends you down to the world of the dead. It will scorch your farmlands and burn deep down under the mountains.
translation_verse: “Mina kɔnyi kɔdubo bɔta bɔda aani ogya kalɛ na lɛkyula lɛla biala na kayawi. Na ɔvi utákyula lɛla biala na lɛkya kalɔ kalɔ. Na ɔkyula abi ƒui.

english_verse: I'll send disaster after disaster to strike you like arrows.
translation_verse: Ndubɔya na ɔgbankpi ɔni kenye naaadubo bɔyɔ kudii ubo-ma lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na baata kataminta.

english_verse: You'll be struck by starvation and deadly diseases, by the fangs of wild animals and poisonous snakes.
translation_verse: Na kɔka ku lɛlɔ bɔbi ɔdubo-ma bɔdu. Na lɛlɛ lidu lidu lɛdubo-ma bɔdu. Na ndubɔya na beƒiebuo bebekpoku-ma na balakpi bani mbo ugyulo ukpidi ɔdu-ma.

english_verse: Young and old alike will be killed in the streets and terrified at home.
translation_verse: Na kekpo kalɛ na bekyuli bekpi beyile lɛblɔnu, na liƒula libeyi kɔduli kemmo. Na bakloƒu ku begblebi badubo bukpi. Na banamu ku benengu lɛnɔ balanu-ma kɔnyana.

english_verse: “I wanted to scatter you, so no one would remember that you had ever lived.
translation_verse: “Lɛ́yɔ ka lɛyila-ma udu kede kede kalɛ na ukyuli biala ulenyimo-ma.

english_verse: But I dreaded the sound of your enemies saying, ‘We defeated Israel with no help from the Lord.’ ”
translation_verse: Nsu naaawia ka bana bekisine bataakun lɛmɛnɛ taasu banii, ‘Bɔ́di-ma lɛlɔ ɔni na kebunku kadi kátasi Unwoti kudɔ.’ ”

english_verse: People of Israel, that's what the Lord has said to you. But you don't have good sense, and you never listen to advice.
translation_verse: Israelƒuɔ ƒui badi bekyuli bani neeebo kasusu. Na bátada anu kula kula.

english_verse: If you did, you could see where you are headed.
translation_verse: Ɔsika bátawia-nwu kemmo na banu lɛla lɛni ɔsu na bádi-ma lɛlɔ. Na belenu kalɔ lɛla lɛni ɔsu na ɔ́lɛ lɛni.

english_verse: How could one enemy soldier chase a thousand of Israel's troops? Or how could two of theirs pursue ten thousand of ours? It can only happen if the Lord stops protecting Israel and lets the enemy win.
translation_verse: Bi mɔɔlɛ́ ɔsu na ukpone ukisine unwi pɛ ɔ́bi ɔ́siaku Israelƒuɔ bekpone apim? Na bekisine bekpone inyɔ bábi básiaku Israelƒuɔ bekpone mpim leevu?

english_verse: Even our enemies know that only our God is a Mighty Rock.
translation_verse: Bula bekisine alati bagyi ka bana baƒiɔ bese kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ, na beeebo ɔyikun aani Israel Katɔti.

english_verse: Our enemies are grapevines rooted in the fields of Sodom and Gomorrah. The grapes they produce are full of bitter poison;
translation_verse: Na bana adingyii ese aani Sodom ku Gomora adingyii. Na adingyii ebi ammɔ ebo ɔdu kati kati, na ugyulo ukpidi ɔkya-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: their wine is more deadly than cobra venom.
translation_verse: Bana ntɛ buse aani ugyulo ukpidi ɔni mɔɔlɛ́ balakpi kunye.

english_verse: But the Lord has written a list of their sins and locked it in his vault.
translation_verse: Unwoti uunyimo lɛla lɛni na bula bekisine bábla. Na unye ɔɔnu anumi uwi ɔbuni ɔni na weti wani-ma kɔtu.

english_verse: Soon our enemies will get what they deserve— suddenly they will slip, and total disaster will quickly follow.
translation_verse: Na uwi uletu badubɔnu lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka banu. Na uwi ɔdubo ɔni na bana ƒui badubo bubuli. Na bana kɔtu bɔni uwi úude.

english_verse: When only a few of the Lord's people remain, when their strength is gone, and some of them are slaves, the Lord will feel sorry for them and give them justice.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔdubo nwuna bekyuli bukpo bɔƒɔ uwi ɔni na ɔ́nu ka bana ɔlɔkplu ɔ́yuɛ. Na ɔdubo bani muumwi-nwu kɔnyana bɔnu si ɔ́nu kalɛ na bábla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: But first the Lord will say, “You ran for safety to other gods— couldn't they help you?
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔdubuye nwuna bekyuli ɔnini, “Wɛ na baƒiɔ bani na bɛɛsu ka bebo ɔyikun ɔsu na bɛ́ƒɔ-ma bɛdi mmɔ bakya?

english_verse: You offered them wine and your best sacrifices. Can't those gods help you now or give you protection?
translation_verse: Na biti bebuo bani nélie lɛmwi bɛkpa bite-ma. Na bite-ma ntɛ na bani. Bɛsu-ma na bebo bebebunku-mii ɔƒaani. Bɛya na bekeli babaƒɔ-mii.

english_verse: Don't you understand? I am the only God; there are no others. I am the one who takes life and gives it again. I punished you with suffering. But now I will heal you, and nothing can stop me!
translation_verse: “Bɛnu! Ami lɛti ndi Katɔti, na ɔdi ɔsɔ uuubo. Ami mbo ngba ku kukpi lɛlɔ ɔyikun. Na muudie lɛlɛ teeboku na mɔɔbwi-ni lɛnɔ. Na lɛla biala liiibo na linye litile lɛla lɛni mɔɔbla kenye.

english_verse: “I make this solemn promise: Just as I live forever,
translation_verse: “Ami ndi Ngba Ƒui Katɔti na lɛ́talaku mina kɔnu katɔ na muusé kenye nnii

english_verse: I will take revenge on my hateful enemies. I will sharpen my sword and let it flash like lightning.
translation_verse: ndubo mina kewii kani mɔɔda ku ogya bɔdɔ, na liti lɛƒɔ mina bekisine kayu na lɛni bani muukisi-mi kɔtu uti utédu ka lɛbla lɛla biala na ulu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: My arrows will get drunk on enemy blood; my sword will taste the flesh and the blood of the enemy. It will kill prisoners, and cut off the heads of their leaders.”
translation_verse: Na ubugya ɔdubɔƒɔ mina kɔtaminta lɛlɔ ƒui. Na mina kewii kɔdubɔdu ukyuli ɔni mɔɔta teenye-mi lɛlɔ. Na ukyuli biala mebekpoku-mii ni, neeeti naaakyiɛ-nwu. Ina bani nápila ku bani béƒie muedi ni, badubo bukpi.”

english_verse: Tell the heavens to celebrate and all gods to bow down to the Lord, because he will take revenge on those hateful enemies who killed his people. He will forgive the sins of Israel and purify their land.
translation_verse: Kadi ƒui bekyuli, ɔlɛka bimwi Unwoti. Ɔsika ɔɔní bekyuli bani ƒui mɔɔdú nwuna bekyuli kɔtu. Na ɔɔƒɔ nwuna bekisine kayu teete nwuna bekyuli. Na uuti nwuna bekyuli ekpidi taakyiɛ-ma.

english_verse: he said, “Always remember this song I have taught you today. And let it be a warning that you must teach your children to obey everything written in The Book of God's Law.
translation_verse: ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bɛnu ka bɛ́di ɔda bubo bɔni líti muute-mii ɔmwi mɛni lɛlɔ ƒui. Na bitaasia kama teeti-nya taatina bina bebi kalɛ na badi Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Law isn't empty words. It can give you a long life in the land that you are going to take.” Moses Will See the Land
translation_verse: Na ala bɔtina bɔmɛni bɔɔɔdi etemila keeke. Mmomu bɔdanku bina ngba. Anwuɔsu bɛdi ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔni na bɛdubo Yordan Ketu bɔvia busie butéle kalɔ kani na béti beete-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Later that day the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛmmɔ kani Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini,

english_verse: Go up into the Abarim Mountain range here in Moab across the Jordan River valley from Jericho. And when you reach the top of Mount Nebo, you will be able to see the land of Canaan, which I am giving to Israel.
translation_verse: “Teesie Abarim abi ani nkya Moab na Yeriko ɔƒɛnyi kakɛ. Na akɔ Nebo Kɔbi na atánu Kanaan kalɔ kani na líti muute Israelƒuɔ.

english_verse: Then you will die and be buried on the mountaintop, just as your brother Aaron died and was buried on Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Na adubukpi kɔbi kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ aani kalɛ kani na ƒula ɔnwani Aaron úkpi ɔ́tɛ Hor Kɔbi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Both of you were unfaithful to me at Meribah Spring near Kadesh in the Zin Desert. I am God, but there in front of the Israelites, you did not treat me with the honor and respect I deserve.
translation_verse: Ɔsika awɔ ku Aaron ƒui bítadi mina etemila lɛlɔ na Israelƒuɔ anumi ɔsu. Uwi ɔni binye Meriba Ketudɔ kesii kani nde ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Kades na Sin kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo ni, bíni litemi lɛni lɛ́su-mii na Israelƒuɔ anumi.

english_verse: So I will give the land to the people of Israel, but you will only get to see it from a distance.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu adubuti ƒula anumi anu kalɔ kani líti muute Israelƒuɔ, nsu ƒula ɔgba ɔɔɔdubo mmɔ bɔnya.”

english_verse: Moses was a prophet, and before he died, he blessed the tribes of Israel by saying:
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ndi kusɛ kusɛ ɔni na Katɔti Kenye Udiene Mose úte Israelƒuɔ asa na úkpi. Ɔ́su ɔnini,

english_verse: The Lord came from Mount Sinai. From Edom, he gave light to his people, and his glory was shining from Mount Paran. Thousands of his warriors were with him, and fire was at his right hand.
translation_verse: “Unwoti ɔ́si Sinai kɔbi lɛlɔ. Na nwuna bukeye bɔ́lɛ aani kalɛ na ɔƒɛ ɔ́tu ɔ́si Seir na úkeye ɔ́si Paran Kɔbi uwi nwuna bekyuli. Na ka ɔdubo ni, katɔ batu mpim leevu básiaku-nwu. Na nwuna kɔdianu kɔɔda ani ogya.

english_verse: The Lord loves the tribes of Israel, and he protects his people. They listen to his words and worship at his feet. *
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔɔyɔ́ nwuna bekyuli na ɔɔgyumana bani ndi nwuna badi. Anwuɔsu bɔɔlɛ-nwu akɔnkɔ kalɔ na bɔɔdi nwuna ɔda bubo lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I called a meeting of the tribes of Israel and gave you God's Law.
translation_verse: Na bɔɔdi ɔda bubo bɔni Mose úte-bu mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔda bubo bɔmɛni bɔdi abu Israelƒuɔ lɛkɛ linengudi.

english_verse: Then you and your leaders made the Lord your king.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti úbenwini ɔga úte nwuna bekyuli uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ kaba ƒui ku bana benengu básala lisu.”

english_verse: Tribe of Reuben, you will live, even though your tribe will always be small.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose úte Ruben kaba kusɛ kusɛ ɔnini, “Ina ka Ruben bekyuli beeemomo ni, belekpi kudii.”

english_verse: The Lord will listen to you, tribe of Judah, as you beg to come safely home. You fought your enemies alone; now the Lord will help you.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su Yuda kɔdua bekyuli ɔnini, “Unwoti ɔdubunu-mii bɔkpali si bíwulo bɛ́kpali-nwu ka bɛɛwia kebunku. Na uti-mii ɔsala ku kaba bakladi lɛnɔ. Na Unwoti ukpo bina kekpo ute-mii. Na Unwoti ubunku-mii na bɛdi bina bekisine lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: At Massah and Meribah Spring, the Lord tested you, tribe of Levi. You were faithful, and so the priesthood belongs to the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su Lewi kaba ɔnini, “Na Masa ku Meriba Ketudɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́kɔku-mii ɔ́nu. Nsu ɔ́nu ka bɛɛbla bina ala ulu lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu akpala kabla kammɔ kadi bina ɔdi.

english_verse: Protecting Israel's agreement with the Lord was more important to you than the life of your father or mother, or brothers or sisters, or your own children.
translation_verse: Ɔsika bídie bina Unwoti kama bɔsiaku bɔyɔ bɛtina geen. Na bɔyɔ bɔmmɔ bubo ɔkplu butulo bɔni bibo bite bina bawɔne ku banwani ku bebi muedi.

english_verse: You teach God's laws to Israel, and at the place of worship you offer sacrifices and burn incense.
translation_verse: Na amii bɛtina Israelƒuɔ Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ. Na kesii kani na Unwoti ɔ́su-mii ka bitaakpa-nwu na bitaabla nwuna akpala ku oloƒui bɔkyula ɔdi mmɔ.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will bless everything you do, and make you strong enough to crush your enemies.
translation_verse: Unwoti ute-mii kusɛ kusɛ na lɛla biala bɛɛbla kemmo. Na ɔya na bɛyu ɔkplu na bɛkana-ma lɛlɔ bɔdi.”

english_verse: The Lord Most High loves you, tribe of Benjamin. He will live among your hills and protect you.
translation_verse: Na Benyamin kaba ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Unwoti Katɔti udie nwuna bɔyɔ ɔtina-mii. Na ulie bina abi lɛlɔ na ɔgyumana-mii.”

english_verse: Descendants of Joseph, the Lord will bless you with precious water from deep wells and with dew from the sky.
translation_verse: Na Yoseƒ kaba ama ni, ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Unwoti kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku-mii. Na ute-mii ntu bɔbuni ɔsiku katɔ ku kalɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Month by month, your fruit will ripen in the sunshine.
translation_verse: Na kɔbuli biala kemmo ni, bina adingyii ataanwu teete-mii ɔkɛnku ɔƒɛ ku kɔbuli bukeye bɔni na adingyii ammɔ aakɛ́ ɔsu.

english_verse: You will have a rich harvest from the slopes of the ancient hills.
translation_verse: Na bina adingyii ani nkya bina kuuku abinkpo lɛlɔ ese anumi ataanwu ebi buni ani bɛɛyɔ́ teete-mii.

english_verse: The Lord who appeared in the burning bush wants to give you the best the land can produce, and it will be a princely crown on Joseph's head.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔni butemi na bínu na kalɔ kakwiidi kani mɔɔkywí kemmo ɔya na kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku-mii, na bina kɔlɔ kulie lɛmwi kaduɛ. Ɔya na kusɛ kusɛ ɔni muute-mii mɛni ubo-nwu kemmo ute Yoseƒ Kaba. Ɔsika Yoseƒ ɔmɛni ndi nwuna banwani ƒui ɔtɔnkune.

english_verse: The sea will make you wealthy, and from the sandy beach you will get treasure. So invite the other tribes to celebrate with you and offer sacrifices to God.
translation_verse: Ɔsika bɛ́kɛ bina lɛkɛ bɛ́siku ama bani nlie ɛpu amadɔ kudɔ. Bɛlɔ-ma ka bebo babakpa Katɔti na abi lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Tribe of Gad, the Lord will bless you with more land. So shout his praises! Your tribe is like a lion ripping up its victim.
translation_verse: Na Gad kɔdua lɛlɔ ni, ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bimwi Katɔti ɔni náya na Gad kalɔ kébomo kébu. Na Gad use aani gyata ɔni nnye kagyumana mɔɔwia ebuo ɔni weƒie na ɔmami-nwu kɔnu iye lili.

english_verse: Your leaders met together and chose the best land for your tribe, but you obeyed the Lord and helped the other tribes.
translation_verse: Na ama nákɛ kalɔ kammɔ kesii kani kakɛ ndia ntulo. Na lɛla lɛni námanku ɔtɔnkune ni, béti béte-nwu. Ɔsika ama nádi Unwoti ɔda bubo etemila lɛlɔ uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune ƒui basala lisu.”

english_verse: Tribe of Dan, you are like a lion cub, startled by a snake.
translation_verse: Na Dan kɔdua lɛlɔ ni, ɔ́su ɔnini, “Dan use aani gyata ɔkɔdi ɔni nábɛ ubi Basan kalɔ lɛlɔ na mmɔ na ɔɔba agyu taasi teetéƒie bebuo.”

english_verse: The Lord is pleased with you, people of Naphtali. He will bless you and give you the land to the west and the south.
translation_verse: Na Naƒtali kɔdua lɛlɔ ni, ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bina lɛlɔ lɛɛda Unwoti kubiti. Anwuɔsu ɔdubo-mii kusɛ kusɛ bute. Na kalɔ kani nási ɔ́si kɔmii kakɛ úti útédu lɛba kemmo ni, kadubɔbla bina ɔdi.”

english_verse: The Lord's greatest blessing is for you, tribe of Asher. You will be the favorite of all the other tribes. You will be rich with olive oil
translation_verse: Na Aser kɔdua lɛlɔ ni, ɔ́su ɔnini, “Unwoti kusɛ kusɛ kenengudikɔ kabla bina ɔdi. Na kaba kammɔ ƒui akɔ ni, amii na baayɔ́ teetulo. Na bɛkɛ nnɔ egyii ebi pii.

english_verse: and have strong town gates with bronze and iron bolts. Your people will be powerful for as long as they live.
translation_verse: Na beti abuala ani mbo ɔkplu geen bagyumana bina lɛma kɔyakun. Na ɔyikun ɔkya bina bekyuli akɔ.

english_verse: Israel, no other god is like ours— the clouds are his chariot as he rides across the skies to come and help us.
translation_verse: “Israelƒuɔ! Ɔti ɔdi uuutulo bula Katɔti. Na anwu muuti liƒlukutu taabla aani nwuna ɔpɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ na ɔda ɔɔví na uubo teebebunku-mii.

english_verse: The eternal God is our hiding place; he carries us in his arms. When God tells you to destroy your enemies, he will make them run.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti kani muukpó bina kekpo ƒui teete-mii. Na nwuna enubɔ mɔɔyá na bulayia. Na anwu mɔɔgyú taatɔ teetékpo taadi bina bekisine lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́su-mii ɔnini, ‘Biteesie! Na bitayia-ma!’

english_verse: Israel, you will live in safety; your enemies will be gone. The dew will fall from the sky, and you will have plenty of grain and wine.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yakob bawɔ, bilie na atu bɔyɔ kemmo. Na bilie kpli na kalɔ kani Unwoti úti uute-mii mmɔ kaduɛ. Kalɔ kani nélie lɛmwi na edula ku adingyii ani beeti taabla ntɛ adubɔdia-ka lɛlɔ. Na Unwoti ɔɔyá na amii aasí katɔ teebewi-ka ntu.

english_verse: The Lord has rescued you and given you more blessings than any other nation. He protects you like a shield and is your majestic sword. Your enemies will bow in fear, and you will trample on their backs.
translation_verse: Israelƒuɔ, bɛya na lɛlɔ lɛyɔ-mii. Ɔsika bekyuli badi beeebo aani bina kalɛ. Bɛdi bekyuli bani na Unwoti náƒɔ-mii ngba. Na Unwoti ɔlati ndi bina ekpola. Na biti-nya bikpo bɛdi lɛlɔ. Na bina bekisine badububo bebevele-mii ka bɛnu-ma kɔnyana. Nsu bitenu kalɔ, na bibo-ma bɛdu ƒui.”

english_verse: Sometime later, Moses left the lowlands of Moab. He went up Mount Pisgah to the peak of Mount Nebo, which is across the Jordan River from Jericho. The Lord showed him all the land as far north as Gilead and the town of Dan.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔ́kɔ úsie Moab kalɔ kani nwi ƒiaa ɔ́si Nebo Kɔbi na útédu Pisga Kɔbi lili na Yeriko ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́tina-nwu kalɔ kammɔ ƒui ɔ́si Gilead úti útédu Dan

english_verse: He let Moses see the territories that would soon belong to the tribes of Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh, and Judah, as far west as the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: ku Naƒtali ƒui ku Eƒraim ku Manase ku Yuda kalɔ ƒui úti útédu ɛpu kama kama ƒui.

english_verse: The Lord also showed him the land in the south, from the valley near the town of Jericho, known as The City of Palm Trees, down to the town of Zoar.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tina-nwu kalɔ kani na kewi káyu ɔ́si kɔwɛ kɔni nde Yeriko na baalɔ mmɔ banii Ebo Ɔma úti útédu ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Soar.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, this is the land I was talking about when I solemnly promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that I would give land to their descendants. I have let you see it, but you will not cross the Jordan and go in.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose ɔnini, “Kalɔ kamɛni na líse kenye ka meti mete Abraham ku Isak ku Yakob ku bana bawɔ. Ɔƒɛni lɛ́ya-na éti ƒula anumi ánu kalɔ kammɔ. Nsu aaadubo mmɔ busie.”

english_verse: And so, Moses the Lord's servant died there in Moab, just as the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Mose ɔni ndi Unwoti kabla ɔblane úkpi na Moab kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ. Na úbo úte aani kalɛ kani na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu.

english_verse: The Lord buried him in a valley near the town of Beth-Peor, but even today no one knows exactly where.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́va-nwu na kɔwɛ kɔni nkya Moab na ɔma ɔni nde Bet-Peor. Na úti úbedu ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ ni, ukyuli biala ɔɔɔgyi kesii kani báva-nwu.

english_verse: The people of Israel stayed in the lowlands of Moab, where they mourned and grieved
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ béti emeyi avlaatɛ bábla-nwu kekwa na Moab kalɔ ƒiaa kammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Before Moses died, he had placed his hands on Joshua, and the Lord had given Joshua wisdom. The Israelites paid attention to what Joshua said and obeyed the commands that the Lord had given Moses. Moses Was a Great Prophet
translation_verse: Na asa na Mose wekpi ni, úti nwuna enu ɔ́sia Yosua lili na ɔ́kpali katɔ, na Unwoti úte Yosua lɛnunda kɔyu. Anwuɔsu Israelƒuɔ béti ɔbu béte Yosua na beenú-nwu litemi na baadi ɔda bubo bɔni na Unwoti úti úte-ma lɛlɔ ɔkɛnku Mose lɛlɔ.

english_verse: There has never again been a prophet in Israel like Moses. The Lord spoke face to face with him
translation_verse: Na Katɔti kenye udiene ɔdi útakya Israel kudii aani Mose kalɛ. Na Unwoti útaatɛmi-ku Mose anumi ku anumi.

english_verse: and sent him to perform powerful miracles in the presence of the king of Egypt and his entire nation.
translation_verse: Na kenye udiene ɔdi lɛnɔ útabla akɔla lidu lidu budie taatina kudii aani akɔla lidu lidu lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́tala Mose na útábla ɔ́tina Egyipteƒuɔ Ɔga ku nwuna kabla bablane ku Egyipte kalɔ bekyuli ƒui.

english_verse: No one else has ever had the power to do such great things as Moses did for everyone to see.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔdi lɛnɔ útakɛ ɔyikun ɔni na Mose ɔ́kɛ na ɔ́bla liƒu ala ku ɔtɔtɔ ala ani nálɛ na Israelƒuɔ anumi kudii.

english_verse: Moses, the Lord's servant, was dead. So the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, who had been the assistant of Moses. The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ka Mose ɔni ndi Unwoti kabla ɔblane úkpi kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́su Yosua ɔni ndi Nun ubidi ɔnini,

english_verse: My servant Moses is dead. Now you must lead Israel across the Jordan River into the land I'm giving to all of you.
translation_verse: “Mina kabla ɔblane Mose úkpi. Anwuɔsu awɔ ku Israelƒuɔ ƒui bɛklibi lɛlɔ na bɛvia Yordan Ketu na biteesie kalɔ kani na ndubuti lite-mii kemmo.

english_verse: Wherever you go, I'll give you that land, as I promised Moses.
translation_verse: Na kesii biala bísie bɛ́vi na kalɔ kammɔ kemmo ni, ndubuti-ka lite-mii aani kalɛ lɛ́su Mose.

english_verse: It will reach from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains in the north, and to the northeast as far as the great Euphrates River. It will include the land of the Hittites, and the land from here at the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea on the west.
translation_verse: Na kalɔ kammɔ ɔmii ɔ́si kalɔ kani nákwii na kewi mɛni útédu Lebanon ɔ́vi úsie útédu Euƒrate Ketu bonwu kammɔ kemmo na ɔƒɛ katukɔ. Na ɔ́kɛ Hetiƒuɔ kalɔ ƒui kemmo úti útédu Mediterenia Ɛpu ɔni nwi ɔƒɛ kanukɔ.

english_verse: Joshua, I will always be with you and help you as I helped Moses, and no one will ever be able to defeat you.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔsu-ɔ ka ukyuli ndi ukyuli ɔdi ulakana bɔta bukpoku-ɔ ƒula ngba emeyi ƒui kemmo. Na kalɛ kani na lílieku Mose ni, lɛni kani na ndubulieku-ɔ. Na lɛɛɛdubo-ɔ bɔnyonu iye lidie-ɔ atu kudii.

english_verse: Long ago I promised the ancestors of Israel that I would give this land to their descendants. So be strong and brave! Be careful to do everything my servant Moses taught you. Never stop reading The Book of the Law he gave you. Day and night you must think about what it says. If you obey it completely, you and Israel will be able to take this land.
translation_verse: Na tada ɔda bubo ɔku ɔmɛni kemmo etemila kalɔ budie teete bekyuli taya. Nu kaduɛ na eteeduo-nya kemmo usien ku ɔƒɛ. Kalɛ na eteenyimo na ataabla taasiaku etemila ani ƒui bénweni bákya ɔku ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na si aabla lɛni ni, ɔdubɔtɛku-ɔ na lɛla biala na aabla ni, lɛdubuse-ɔ kaduɛ.

english_verse: I've commanded you to be strong and brave. Don't ever be afraid or discouraged! I am the Lord your God, and I will be there to help you wherever you go. The Eastern Tribes Promise To Help
translation_verse: Nyimo ka lɛ́su-ɔ ka nye kpakplaa na ese kayi. Na taya na liƒu lɛdi lɛda-a iye enu aƒɛ-ɔ. Ɔsika ami ɔni ndi ƒula Unwoti Katɔti nlieku-ɔ uwi biala kemmo.” Yosua Úbo Nwuna Bekyuli Ɔda

english_verse: Joshua ordered the tribal leaders
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yosua úbo Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune bammɔ ɔda ɔnini,

english_verse: to go through the camp and tell everyone: In a few days we will cross the Jordan River to take the land that the Lord our God is giving us. So prepare as much food as you'll need for the march into the land.
translation_verse: “Bɛvi bekyuli bammɔ lɛlɔ na bana kɔkyakɔ na bɛsu-ma bɛnini, ‘Bɛklibi lɛlɔ na bɛwia adila adi bise bite lɛlɔ. Ɔsika emeyi atɛ kama bɔdubɔvia Yordan Ketu na busie kalɔ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su ka wete-mii kemmo.’ ”

english_verse: Joshua told the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh:
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́su Ruben ku Gad kaba bekyuli ku Manase kaba kakɛ kadi bekyuli ɔnini,

english_verse: conquer the land that the Lord is giving them. The Lord will give peace to them as he has given peace to you, and then you can come back and settle here in the land that Moses promised you.
translation_verse: úti útédu ka Unwoti úte-ma keliekɔ aani kalɛ na ɔ́bla úte-mii. Na si Unwoti ɔ́ya na Israelƒuɔ bakladi bammɔ bákɛ keliekɔ ni, uwi ɔmmɔ na bekpone bammɔ badubɔsɔ benwini besie bana keliekɔ kani na Unwoti kabla ɔblane Mose úte-ma na Yordan ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ.”

english_verse: The men answered: We'll cross the Jordan River and help our relatives. We'll fight anywhere you send us.
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bammɔ bédie kenye na básu Yosua banini, “Lɛla biala na ásu-bu ni, bɔdubɔdi-ni lɛlɔ. Na kesi kesii na átala-bu ni, bɔdubusie.

english_verse: If the Lord our God will help you as he helped Moses, and if you are strong and brave, we will obey you as we obeyed Moses. We'll even put to death anyone who rebels against you or refuses to obey you.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala ɔni mata menye-ɔ lɛlɔ na uladi ƒula litemi iye ɔda ɔni na ébo-nwu lɛlɔ ni, bɔdubɔdu-nwu. Mmomu awɔ ni, nye kpakplaa na ese kayi.”

english_verse: Joshua chose two men as spies and sent them from their camp at Acacia with these instructions: “Go across the river and find out as much as you can about the whole region, especially about the town of Jericho.” The two spies left the Israelite camp at Acacia and went to Jericho, where they decided to spend the night at the house of a prostitute named Rahab.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Nun ubidi Yosua ɔ́tala batu inyɔ badi ɔ́siku Sitim kesii kani bákya. Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛbɛ bitánu Kanaan kalɔ kammɔ. Ɔni ntulo ƒui ndi ka biduo bana ɔma unengudi ɔni baalɔ banii Yeriko na bɛnu mmɔ kalɛ na use.” Amu ka bétéduo Yeriko ni, bésie bétéduo uleku ɔyalɛ ɔni baalɔ banii Rahab kaduli na bátɛ mmɔ.

english_verse: But someone found out about them and told the king of Jericho, “Some Israelite men came here tonight, and they are spies.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yeriko ɔga ɔmmɔ únu ka Israelƒuɔ badi bébo ɔma ɔmɛni usien bébelie mɛni na bávi bánu bula kalɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Rahab went back up to her roof. The spies were still awake, so she told them:
translation_verse: Na asa na Israelƒuɔ inyɔ bamɛni badubo bɔtɛ usien ɔmmɔ ni, Rahab ɔ́kɔ úsie-ma kudɔ na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini,

english_verse: I know that the Lord has given Israel this land. Everyone shakes with fear because of you.
translation_verse: “Ngyi ka Unwoti úuti kalɔ kamɛni úte-mii. Ɔsika ukyuli biala ɔni nkya kalɔ kamɛni kemmo ɔtɔtɔ ɔɔgyú-nwu geen ɔ́si amii ɔsu.

english_verse: We heard how the Lord dried up the Red Sea so you could leave Egypt. And we heard how you destroyed Sihon and Og, those two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Na búnu kalɛ na Unwoti ɔ́ya na Ɛpugyie ɔ́kwii uwi ɔni na bísie bɛ́via Egyipte kalɔ bɛdubo. Na bɔ́sɔ búnu lɛnɔ kalɛ na bɛ́du Amoriƒuɔ baga inyɔ bani nlie Yordan ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ na baalɔ-ma banii Sihon ku Og.

english_verse: We know that the Lord your God rules heaven and earth, and we've lost our courage and our will to fight.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bɔ́nya búnu ala amɛni ƒui ni, ɔtɔtɔ úse kalɔ ɔɔgyú-bu. Na enu ése kalɔ aaƒɛ-bu ɔ́si amii ɔsu. Ɔsika Unwoti Katɔti ɔmɛni ndi katɔ ku kalɔ ɔti.

english_verse: Please promise me in the Lord's name that you will be as kind to my family as I have been to you. Do something to show
translation_verse: “Na mɔɔwia ka bise-mi kenye na Katɔti lɛnyi kemmo ka bɛdubɔbla ami ku mina kaduli bekyuli lɛƒɔndia aani kalɛ na lɛ́bla líte-mii. Anwuɔsu bɛbla likpose lɛla lɛdi bɛtina-mi kalɛ na makana maƒɔ-mii madi.

english_verse: that you won't let your people kill my father and mother and my brothers and sisters and their families.
translation_verse: Na bise kenye ka bɛɛɛdubo bula ɔdi bɔdu! Mina ɔti iye mina uni iye mina banwani bananabi ku belekubi ku bana kɔduli bekyuli ni, biládu bula ɔdi!”

english_verse: “Rahab,” the spies answered, “if you keep quiet about what we're doing, we promise to be kind to you when the Lord gives us this land. We pray that the Lord will kill us if we don't keep our promise!”
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ batu inyɔ bamɛni básu Rahab banini, “Si bútadi lɛla lɛni bɔdubo-ɔ bɔsu mɛni lɛlɔ ni, Katɔti ɔdu-bu. Na si átasu ukyuli ɔdi lɛla lɛni ɔsu búbo mɛni ni, buusé-ɔ kenye ka bɔdubɔbla-mii lɛƒɔndia si Unwoti úti kalɔ kamɛni ɔ́kya-bu enu kemmo.”

english_verse: Rahab's house was built into the town wall, and one of the windows in her house faced outside the wall. She gave the spies a rope, showed them the window, and said, “Use this rope to let yourselves down to the ground outside the wall.
translation_verse: Na Rahab ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ɔdanku ɔma ɔmmɔ lɛwoduku bonwu lɛmmɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔ́lɛmi nwuna ƒansili na ɔ́ya na béti kabuli bébo bada. Na Israel batu inyɔ bammɔ básia kabuli kammɔ lɛlɔ báyu bátɔlɔ.

english_verse: Then hide in the hills. The men who are looking for you won't be able to find you there. They'll give up and come back after a few days, and you can be on your way.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na badubo bɔtɔlɔ ni, Rahab ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bikeli bɛsia abi lɛlɔ ulu ɔmmɔ. Na si bídu abi lɛlɔ mmɔ ni, na bɛbɛ bilie mmɔ emeyi atɛ úti útédu ka bekyuli bani mɔɔsia-mii kama mmɔ básɔ bénwini. Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ulu ɔdubɔbla nwaa na bɛtɔlɔ. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, bekyuli bammɔ badubɔnu-mii.”

english_verse: “I'll do exactly what you said,” Rahab promised. Then she sent them on their way and tied the red rope to the window.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Rahab únu kalɔ na ɔ́ya na bátɔlɔ. Uwi ɔni bátɔlɔ ni, Rahab úbo kɔdi kugyiedi kɔmmɔ ɔda ƒansili ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The spies hid in the hills for three days while the king's soldiers looked for them along the roads. As soon as the soldiers gave up and returned to Jericho,
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ batu bammɔ bátɔlɔ bésie abi lɛlɔ mmɔ na bátábɛ. Na ɔga batu bammɔ bátɛ-ma anu laa na ulu lɛlɔ emeyi atɛ. Nsu bátanu-ma. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu básɔ bénwini bésie Yeriko.

english_verse: the two spies went down into the Jordan valley and crossed the river. They reported to Joshua and told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Israelƒuɔ batu bammɔ báyu abi eli mmɔ bébo kalɔ. Na bátávia Yordan Ketu na bénwini bésie Yosua kudɔ. Na básu-nwu lɛla biala nálɛ.

english_verse: “We're sure the Lord has given us the whole country,” they said. “The people there shake with fear every time they think of us.”
translation_verse: Na básu-nwu banini, “Bɔɔƒɔ́ taadi ka Unwoti úti kalɔ kammɔ ƒui úte-bu. Ɔsika bekyuli bani ƒui nkya kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ɔtɔtɔ úse kalɔ ɔɔgyú-ma ɔ́si abu ɔsu.”

english_verse: Early the next morning, Joshua and the Israelites packed up and left Acacia. They went to the Jordan River and camped there that night.
translation_verse: Amu na kadi kégye ɔtanta tutuutu ni, Yosua ku Israelƒuɔ ƒui báta Sitim na bátɔlɔ bétélie Yordan Ketudɔ kesii kani na badubulie asa na bavia ketu kammɔ.

english_verse: Two days later their leaders went through the camp,
translation_verse: Nwuna emeyi atɛ kama ni, bana batɔnkune bávi bekyuli bammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ na bana kakyakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: shouting, “When you see some of the priests carrying the sacred chest, you'll know it is time to cross to the other side. You've never been there before, and you won't know the way, unless you follow the chest. But don't get too close! Stay about a kilometer back.”
translation_verse: Ka bítebo mɛni kudii ɔsu ni, bakpane bani nti Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ ndubɔtina-mii ulu. Nsu ɔdi utakpɛ utede Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ. Na bɛya na kuƒi kɔkya amii ku Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ ntɛ aani liluku kakɛ na bitani bitede-nwu.”

english_verse: Joshua told the people, “Make yourselves acceptable to worship the Lord, because he is going to do some amazing things for us.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Yosua ɔ́su bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ɔnini, “Ɔdi biala ɔbla lɛlɔ sɛɛn. Ɔsika kɔnaadi Unwoti ɔdubo akɔla bɔbla na bina akɔ.”

english_verse: Then Joshua turned to the priests and said, “Take the chest and cross the Jordan River ahead of us.” So the priests picked up the chest by its carrying poles and went on ahead.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama Yosua ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Katɔti Bakpane bammɔ ka bagyu Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ beti na bagyu batɔ bekyuli bammɔ animi. Anwuɔsu ama lɛnɔ bábla kalɛ na Yosua ɔ́su-ma mmɔ.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua, “Beginning today I will show the people that you are their leader, and they will know that I am helping you as I helped Moses.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su Yosua ɔnini, “Lɛla lɛni ndubo bɔbla ɔmwi kadi mɛni ɔdubɔya na Israelƒuɔ bese kalɔ bataabu-ɔ aani ukyuli ubendi na adi. Na badubo bɔnu bɔti ka nlieku-ɔ aani kalɛ kani na lílie-ku Mose.

english_verse: Now, tell the priests who are carrying the chest to go a little way into the river and stand there.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu su Bakpane bani nti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ anini, ‘Si bídu Yordan Ketudɔ ni, na biduo ketu kammɔ kemmo na bisie anumi blii asa na bidi binye utubli ɔmmɔ kudɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Joshua spoke to the people: Come here and listen to what the Lord our God said he will do!
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́su bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ɔnini, “Bɛni bide-mi na bise atu na binu lɛla lɛni na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubo-mii bɔsu.

english_verse: The Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites control the land on the other side of the river. But the living God will be with you and will force them out of the land when you attack. And now, God is going to prove that he's powerful enough to force them out.
translation_verse: Ɔni na bísela mɛni ni, Bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubo Kanaanƒuɔ ku Hetiƒuɔ ku Hewiƒuɔ ku Perisiƒuɔ ku Girgasiƒuɔ ku Amoriƒuɔ ku Yebusiƒuɔ bɔbɔku bɔlɛku kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na mmɔ bɛdubo bɔnu bɔti ka Katɔti ɔni nlie ngba mmɔ ɔkya-mii akɔ sɔsɔ.

english_verse: Just watch the sacred chest that belongs to the Lord, the ruler of the whole earth. As soon as the priests carrying the chest step into the Jordan, the water will stop flowing and pile up as if someone had built a dam across the river. The Lord has also said that each of the twelve tribes should choose one man to represent it.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni kani na bakpane bani nti Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka badubɔnya ntu bɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Yordan Ketu kammɔ kadubɔda bɔgba bɔya kɔnakunwi. Na ntu bɔni mɔɔgbá taasi katɔ kakɛ bɔdubo ni, bɔdubudi bunye liku linwi.”

english_verse: The Israelites packed up and left camp. The priests carrying the chest walked in front,
translation_verse: Amu ka Israelƒuɔ bammɔ báta banii baavia Yordan Ketu ni, bakpane bani nti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ nágyu batɔ-ma.

english_verse: until they came to the Jordan River. The water in the river had risen over its banks, as it often does in springtime. But as soon as the feet of the priests touched the water,
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ketu kammɔ kéyi geen na ɔdi edula ɔƒɛ uwi. Nsu uwi ɔni kani na bakpane bani nti Adaka ɔmmɔ bédu ketu kammɔ na bákya-ka lɛgba ni,

english_verse: the river stopped flowing, and the water started piling up at the town of Adam near Zarethan. No water flowed toward the Dead Sea, and the priests stood in the middle of the dry riverbed near Jericho while everyone else crossed over.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti bakpane bani nti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ benye ketu kakwiidi kammɔ ntɛntɛ úti útédu ka bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bávia báwɔlɔ.

english_verse: After Israel had crossed the Jordan, the Lord said to Joshua:
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui bávia Yordan Ketu báwɔlɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́su Yosua ɔnini,

english_verse: Tell one man from each of the twelve tribes to pick up a large rock from where the priests are standing. Then tell the men to set up those rocks as a monument at the place where you camp tonight.
translation_verse: na aya na ɔdi biala utágyu lɛtakpɛ na kesii kani na bakpane bammɔ benye na Yordan Ketu ntɛ mmɔ. Na asu-ma na beti-nya betesie kesii kani badubo bulie usien ɔmɛni.”

english_verse: Joshua chose twelve men; then he called them together
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́lɔ nkyuli leevu-inyɔ bammɔ ɔsala lisu.

english_verse: and said: Go to the middle of the riverbed where the sacred chest is, and pick up a large rock. Carry it on your shoulder to our camp. There are twelve of you, so there will be one rock for each tribe.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Biteesie Yordan kemmo na kesii kani bakpane bani nti Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka mmɔ benye. Na ɔdi biala utágyu lɛtakpɛ linwi ɔsia lɛmangba lɛlɔ. Na lɛtakpɛ biala linye lite Israel kaba kenwi.

english_verse: Someday your children will ask, “Why are these rocks here?” Then you can tell them how the water stopped flowing when the chest was being carried across the river. These rocks will always remind our people of what happened here today.
translation_verse: Na bɛsu-ma ka uwi ɔni na Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔɔvia Yordan Ketu ni, ketu kammɔ káda na ntu bɔmmɔ bɔ́kwii na Israelƒuɔ bávia. Na atakpɛ amɛni adubɔya na Israelƒuɔ beteenyimo lɛla lɛni nálɛ mɛni uwi biala.”

english_verse: The men followed the instructions that the Lord had given Joshua. They picked up twelve rocks, one for each tribe, and carried them to the camp, where they put them down.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bekyuli bammɔ bábla kalɛ na Yosua ɔ́su-ma. Na aani kalɛ kani na Unwoti ɔ́su Yosua ni, bágyu atakpɛ leevu-anyɔ básiku Yordan Ketu ntɛ mmɔ. Na lɛtakpɛ biala linye lite Israel kaba kenwi. Na béti atakpɛ ammɔ bétéwi kesii kani na bélie.

english_verse: It was the tenth day of the first month of the year when Israel crossed the Jordan River. They set up camp at Gilgal, which was east of the land controlled by Jericho.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bávia Yordan Ketu kammɔ báwɔlɔ na kɔbuli kudeedi limeyi leevudi lɛlɔ. Na bételie ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Gilgal na Yeriko ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: The men who had carried the twelve rocks from the Jordan brought them to Joshua, and they made them into a monument.
translation_verse: Gilgal mmɔ na Yosua úti atakpɛ leevu-anyɔ ani básiku Yordan Ketu mmɔ bátálɛ.

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Years from now your children will ask you why these rocks are here.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ ɔnini, “Limeyi lɛdi si bina bawɔ báta na béye-mii banii bi na atakpɛ amɛni enye ete ni,

english_verse: Tell them, “The Lord our God dried up the Jordan River so we could walk across. He did the same thing here for us that he did for our people at the Red Sea,
translation_verse: Na bɛsu-ma ka bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na Yordan Ketu kákwii úti útédu ka Israelƒuɔ ƒui bávia-ka aani kalɛ kani na ɔ́ya na, Ɛpugyie ɔ́kwii asa na Israelƒuɔ bávia.

english_verse: because he wants everyone on earth to know how powerful he is. And he wants us to worship only him.”
translation_verse: Ɔ́bla ɔmɛni úti ɔ́tina kayawi bekyuli ƒui na banu bati ka ubo ɔyikun geen. Na ɔmɛni ɔdubɔya na bayia Unwoti bana Katɔti uwi biala.”

english_verse: The Amorite kings west of the Jordan River and the Canaanite kings along the Mediterranean Sea lost their courage and their will to fight, when they heard how the Lord had dried up the Jordan River to let Israel go across. Israel Gets Ready To Celebrate Passover
translation_verse: Amu ka Amoriƒuɔ baga bani nlie bésie Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ kanukɔ ku Kanaanƒuɔ baga bani nlie ɛpu amadɔ ƒui bénu kalɛ na Unwoti ɔ́ya na Yordan ɔ́kwii na Israelƒuɔ bésie bávi-nwu kemmo ni, liƒu lɛda-ma geen na enu áƒɛ-ma na Israelƒuɔ bamɛni ɔsu. Yosua Úkulo Israelƒuɔ Ago Na Gilgal

english_verse: While Israel was camped at Gilgal, the Lord said, “Joshua, make some flint knives and circumcise the rest of the Israelite men and boys.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo kani na Unwoti ɔ́su Yosua ɔnini, “Wia atabi na adɔ-nya kunye na eti ekulo Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ago.”

english_verse: This had to be done, because none of Israel's baby boys had been circumcised during the
translation_verse: Na bana bebi bani náta bákɔ ƒui ni, bétekulo ago. Anwuɔsu kaba kawɔdi kamɛni na Yosua úkulo ago.

english_verse: Everyone who had been circumcised needed time to heal, and they stayed in camp.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni békulo-ma ago báwɔlɔ ni, bekyuli bammɔ belie mmɔ úti útédu ka bana lɛlɛ lɛmmɔ lɛ́sa.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua, “It was a disgrace for my people to be slaves in Egypt, but now I have taken away that disgrace.” So the Israelites named the place Gilgal, and it still has that name.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Yosua ɔnini, “Kɔƒa kɔni mɔɔdu-mii ka bɛdi kabla bablane bite Egyipteƒuɔ ni, lídie-ku bina lɛlɔ ɔmwi.” Anwuɔsu básia kesii kammɔ lɛnyi banii Gilgal. Na lɛni kani baalɔ mmɔ úti úbedu ɔmwi.

english_verse: Israel continued to camp at Gilgal in the desert near Jericho, and on the fourteenth day of the same month, they celebrated Passover.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bamu bakya Gilgal na kalɔ kani nwi ƒiaa na Yeriko kudɔ ni, bádi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia limeyi useyi ɔmmɔ na kɔbuli kɔmmɔ limeyi leevu-inedi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The next day, God stopped sending the Israelites manna to eat each morning, and they started eating food grown in the land of Canaan. They ate roasted grain and thin bread made of the barley they had gathered from nearby fields. Israel Captures Jericho
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si uwi ɔmmɔ kama ni, adila ani naasí katɔ na baalɔ-nya banii manna áda bɔna aya. Na Israelƒuɔ básɔ bátadi ɔdi kudii. Na edula ani kani nkya Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ kani na baadi. Yosua Ɔ́nu Katɔti Ukpone Unengudi

english_verse: One day, Joshua was near Jericho when he saw a man standing some distance in front of him. The man was holding a sword, so Joshua walked up to him and asked, “Are you on our side or on our enemies' side?”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Yosua ɔni uude Yeriko ni, ka ɔ́talaku anumi ni, kɔnakunwi kani na ɔ́nu ɔnana ɔdi ka unye-nwu anumi na ɔ́da kewii kagyɔlɔɔ kadi. Amu na Yosua ɔni ude-nwu na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Adi bula bekpone akɔ unwi, munuu ukisine na adi-bu?”

english_verse: “Neither,” he answered. “I am here because I am the commander of the Lord's army.” Joshua fell to his knees and bowed down to the ground. “I am your servant,” he said. “Tell me what to do.”
translation_verse: Na ukpone ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛɛɛdi bana akɔ ɔdi. Mmomu Katɔti bekpone ɔtɔnkune ƒui na ndi. Na ɔƒɛni na líbo.” Amu ka Yosua únu lɛni ni, ɔ́yu ubi kalɔ kɔnakunwi na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Buvele, Ati, bi na aayɔ́ ka ami, ƒula kabla ɔblane, lɛbla lite-ɔ?”

english_verse: “Take off your sandals,” the commander answered. “This is a holy place.” So Joshua took off his sandals.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti Ukpone Ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ ɔ́su Yosua ɔnini, “Da ƒula lɛgbanvuo die. Ɔsika kesii kani na enye mɛni kese kedee.” Na Yosua ɔ́da nwuna lɛgbanvuo údie aani kalɛ na Unwoti ukpone ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-nwu.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Jericho had been locking the gates in their town wall because they were afraid of the Israelites. No one could go out or come in.
translation_verse: Na Yerikoƒuɔ ni, bákalɛ bana kɔyakun kpakplaa ɔ́si Israelƒuɔ bɔyia ɔsu. Na kɔyakun kenye benyene beléte kuƒi ka ukyuli ɔdi uduo ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo iye ɔlɛ keyi.

english_verse: Take along the sacred chest and tell seven priests to walk in front of it, carrying trumpets. But on the seventh day, march slowly around the town seven times while the priests blow their trumpets.
translation_verse: Na bakpane maatɛ ɔdi biala uti kakpɛɛ ɔda. Na ama ndubo bɔgyu bɔtɔ asa na Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ ɔsiaku-ma kama. Na limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, awɔ ku bekpone bammɔ bɛka bɛmana ɔma ɔmmɔ maatɛ. Na bakpane bammɔ bataavwi bana kakpɛɛ.

english_verse: Then the priests will blast on their trumpets, and everyone else will shout. The wall will fall down, and your soldiers can go straight in from every side.
translation_verse: Na si béti kɔkpɛɛ kɔmmɔ na bédie kɔku momoomo kɔdi ni, na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bebo kudu. Na ɔma ɔmmɔ awodu ƒui adubo bɔƒɛ buwi kalɔ. Na bekpone bammɔ ƒui beduo ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo.”

english_verse: Joshua called the priests together and said, “Take the chest and tell seven priests to carry trumpets and march ahead of it.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́lɔ bakpane bammɔ na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Biti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ biti, na bina maatɛ lɛnɔ biti kɔkpɛɛ na bɛgyu bɛtɔ Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ.”

english_verse: They obeyed Joshua's orders and carried the chest once around the town before returning to camp for the night.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bekpone bammɔ ku bekyuli bani nti Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ bésie bámana Yeriko ɔma ɔmmɔ limeyi lideedi. Na basɔ bénwini bébo bana kakyakɔ na bakya mmɔ usien ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: On the seventh day, the army got up at daybreak. They marched slowly around Jericho the same as they had done for the past six days, except on this day they went around seven times.
translation_verse: Na limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, bekyuli bammɔ ƒui báta lɛdigye na besie bátáka bamana ɔma ɔmmɔ aani kalɛ bataabla. Na limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ amu ni, baka bamana ɔma ɔmmɔ maatɛ.

english_verse: Then the priests blew the trumpets, and Joshua yelled: Get ready to shout! The Lord will let you capture this town.
translation_verse: Si báka bámana ɔma ɔmmɔ na udu maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, kɔkpɛɛ bavwine bammɔ bedie bana kɔku kɔmmɔ. Mmɔ na Yosua úbo nwuna bekyuli bammɔ ɔda ɔnii babla kudu, na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Unwoti úti ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni ɔ́kya-mii enu kemmo.

english_verse: But you must destroy it and everything in it, to show that it now belongs to the Lord. The woman Rahab helped the spies we sent, so protect her and the others who are inside her house. But kill everyone else in the town.
translation_verse: Bɛyila ala ani ƒui nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo udu na enwini akpala ete Unwoti. Nsu ɔyalɛ Rahab ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli amu ni, bitabla-ma lɛla lɛdi. Ɔsika anwu nábala bula batu bani na bátala na Yeriko.”

english_verse: The silver and gold and everything made of bronze and iron belong to the Lord and must be put in his treasury. Be careful to follow these instructions, because if you see something you want and take it, the Lord will destroy Israel. And it will be all your fault.
translation_verse: Na sika ugyiedi iye ɔƒualadi ku ala ani ƒui béti abuala udu ɔdi bábla énwini Unwoti adi. Na si ɔdi ɔ́nu adi ni, uti ubakya Unwoti kavumi kemmo.”

english_verse: The priests blew their trumpets again, and the soldiers shouted as loud as they could. The walls of Jericho fell flat. Then the soldiers rushed up the hill, went straight into the town, and captured it.
translation_verse: Amu na bakpane bammɔ bávwi kɔku gyɔlɔɔ kɔdi ku bana atunkpɛ. Na ka bekyuli bammɔ bénu kɔku kɔmmɔ ni, bése kalɔ beedie kudu momoomo. Mmɔ na awodu ammɔ áƒɛ éwi kalɔ kɔnakunwi. Na bekpone bammɔ bétéduo ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na békpo bádi-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: After Jericho was destroyed, Joshua warned the people, “Someday a man will rebuild Jericho, but the Lord will put a curse on him, and the man's oldest son will die when he starts to build the town wall. And by the time he finishes the wall and puts gates in it, all his children will be dead.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ka báyila Yeriko ɔma ɔmmɔ udu báwɔlɔ ni, mmɔ na Yosua úbo bekyuli bammɔ ɔda kpakplaa na Unwoti anumi, na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ukyuli ɔni nsɔ mayɔ ka wasɔ watu Yeriko ɔma ɔdubɔnuku-ni. Na awɔ ɔni malɛ kowodu ni, ƒ'ubidi unengudi lili na aalɛ́-ku. Na awɔ ɔni matu awodu kɔyakun ni, ƒula kawɔkpulo lili lɛlɔ na aatu-ka.”

english_verse: The Lord helped Joshua in everything he did, and Joshua was famous everywhere in Canaan.
translation_verse: Na ala ani nálɛ mɛni kemmo ƒui ni, Unwoti ulieku Yosua na ɔ́ya na nwuna lɛnyi lɛ́ƒɔ kuye, nwuna lɛnyi lígyingya líyile kalɔ kammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: The Lord had said that everything in Jericho belonged to him. But Achan from the Judah tribe took some of the things from Jericho for himself. And so the Lord was angry with the Israelites, because one of them had disobeyed him.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔda ɔni na úbo Israelƒuɔ ka beteti lɛla biala batakya lɛlɔ si bésie betékpoku Yerikoƒuɔ ni, bátadi-ni lɛlɔ. Ɔsika ɔnana ɔni baalɔ Akan úti ala ammɔ adi ɔ́kya lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu Unwoti úti kɔnyi kati kati ɔkya Israelƒuɔ. Na Akan ɔmɛni ɔ́si Yuda kaba kemmo na Serah ɔtɔ kemmo. Na Serah náwɔ Sabdi, na Sabdi náwɔ Karmi, na Karmi náwɔ Akan ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Joshua and the leaders of Israel tore their clothes and put dirt on their heads to show their sorrow. They lay facedown on the ground in front of the sacred chest until sunset.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛla lɛni nálɛ mɛni ɔsu ni, ɔ́bla Yosua ku Israelƒuɔ benengu kalɛ kadi. Na báni bana lɛwu bábuɛ na báyu bébi kalɔ na Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka anumi. Na bébi kalɔ mmɔ úti útédu useyi uwi. Na béti ɔtumu bewi lili úti ɔɔtina kalɛ baadu kɔnyana.

english_verse: Then Joshua said: Our Lord, did you bring us across the Jordan River just so the Amorites could destroy us? This wouldn't have happened if we had agreed to stay on the other side of the Jordan.
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́kpali Katɔti na ɔ́su ɔnini, “O Unwoti Katɔti Ɔni Ntulo Ƒui, báyila-bu udu! Na bi ɔsu na átaya na bɔsɔ bɔkya Yordan Ketu ɔvi ɔni nye mmomu?

english_verse: I don't even know what to say to you, since Israel's army has turned and run from the enemy.
translation_verse: Unwoti nsɔ naaati lɛla lɛni lɛsu muedi ɔni na bula bekpone békeli na bátakana bunye bɔsiaku bula bekisine mɛni.

english_verse: Everyone will think you weren't strong enough to protect your people. Now the Canaanites and everyone else who lives in the land will surround us and wipe us out.
translation_verse: Kanaanƒuɔ ku bekyuli ƒui badubo bunu ala ani mɔɔlɛ́ mɛni. Na badubo bɔsala na bebo-bu ƒui badu kede kede. Na si ɔmɛni udu ɔlɛ ni, dɛ na adubɔblaku ƒula lɛnyi lɛni lɛƒɔ kuye mɛni?”

english_verse: The Lord answered: Stop lying there on the ground! Get up!
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Yosua ɔnini, “Ta pla! Bi ɔsu na ebi kalɔ lɛni?

english_verse: I said everything in Jericho belonged to me and had to be destroyed. But the Israelites have kept some of the things for themselves. They stole from me and hid what they took. Then they lied about it.
translation_verse: Mɔɔsu-ɔ ka Israelƒuɔ bábla likpidi. Na báta bénye ɔda ɔni na líbo-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na béti ala ani na lɛ́su-mi ka bayila mmɔ adi. Na mɔɔsu-ɔ ka buyu na béyu na bányi ɔkɔ lɛnɔ básia-nwu lɛlɔ na béti ala ammɔ bakya bana ala akɔ.

english_verse: What they stole was supposed to be destroyed, and now Israel itself must be destroyed. I cannot help you anymore until you do exactly what I have said. That's why Israel turns and runs from its enemies instead of standing up to them.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu na Israelƒuɔ bátakana bunye bɔsiaku bana bekisine na bukeli mmomu na bekeli-ma. Ɔsika ala ani udu na ɔlɛka bɛyila ni, bíti-nya bɛkya lɛlɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu na ɔ́lɛku-mii lɛni. Na nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo bukpo bute-mii lɛnɔ wetédu uwi ɔni na bɛyila lɛla biala lɛni na lɛ́su-mii.”

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel, “Tomorrow you will meet with the Lord your God, so make yourselves acceptable to worship him. The Lord says that you have taken things that should have been destroyed. You won't be able to stand up to your enemies until you get rid of those things.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Unwoti ɔ́su Yosua ɔnini, “Ta na asu bekyuli bammɔ ka babla lɛlɔ sɛɛn bese kaduɛ na bɔsa kɔnaadi. Ɔsika ami Unwoti Israel Katɔti mɔɔsu-ma nnii, ‘Ala ani na líbo-mii ɔda nnii biti-nya bɛkpa bite-mi ni, bíti adi bɛkya lɛlɔ. Na mɔɔsu-mii ka bilakana bina bekisine anumi bunye bɔsiaku úti útédu ka bídie ala ammɔ bíboku.

english_verse: “Tomorrow morning everyone must gather near the place of worship. You will come forward tribe by tribe, and the Lord will show which tribe is guilty. Next, the clans in that tribe must come forward, and the Lord will show which clan is guilty. The families in that clan must come, and the Lord will point out the guilty family. Finally, the men in that family must come,
translation_verse: “ ‘Anwuɔsu ya na bekyuli bammɔ bebo-mi anumi kɔnaadi ɔtanta na bebenye bana kaba kenye. Na kaba kani na Unwoti ɔ́lɛ lɛnumi ni, na balɛ bebo ɔtɔ kenye. Na ɔtɔ ɔni na Unwoti ɔ́lɛ lɛnumi ni, balɛ bebo na kaduli kenye. Na kaduli kammɔ banana badubɔlɛ bebo unwi unwi.

english_verse: and the Lord will show who stole what should have been destroyed. That man must be put to death, his body burned, and his possessions thrown into the fire. He has done a terrible thing by breaking the sacred agreement that the Lord made with Israel.”
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔni ndubɔlɛ lɛnumi ni, nwuna kudɔ na ala ammɔ akya. Na beti ogya bakyula-nwu ku nwuna akɛla ƒui. Ɔsika úti kɔƒa kubendi uboku Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ. Na útadi bunyimi bɔni na Katɔti únyimi-ku Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Joshua got up early the next morning and brought each tribe to the place of worship, where the Lord showed that the Judah tribe was guilty.
translation_verse: Amu ka kadi kégye ɔtanta Yosua ɔ́ya na Israelƒuɔ ƒui bebenye-nwu anumi na kaba kaba kenye. Na Katɔti ɔ́lɛ Yuda kaba lɛnumi.

english_verse: Then Joshua brought the clans of Judah to the Lord, and the Lord showed that the Zerah clan was guilty. One by one he brought the leader of each family in the Zerah clan to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Zabdi's family was guilty.
translation_verse: Na Yosua ɔ́ya na Yuda kaba kammɔ kalɛ kebo na lɛtɔ kenye. Na Katɔti ɔ́lɛ Serah ɔtɔ lɛnumi. Na Yosua ɔ́ya na Serah ɔtɔ bekyuli bálɛ bebo bebenye kaduli kaduli kenye. Na Unwoti ɔ́lɛ Sabdi kaduli bekyuli lɛnumi.

english_verse: Finally, Joshua brought each man in Zabdi's family to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Achan was the guilty one.
translation_verse: Na Yosua ɔ́ya na Sabdi kaduli banana bálɛ bebo unwi unwi. Na Akan ɔni ndi Karmi ubidi na ɔdi Sabdi uwɔ ni, Katɔti ɔ́lɛ-nwu lɛnumi.

english_verse: “Achan,” Joshua said, “the Lord God of Israel has decided that you are guilty. So tell me what you did, and don't try to hide anything.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Yosua úye Akan ɔnini, “Mina ubi, die lɛlɔ kalɔ na Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti anumi na asu lɛla lɛni na ábla. Na teti lɛla lɛdi tabɛla.”

english_verse: “It's true,” Achan answered. “I sinned and disobeyed the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Amu na Akan údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛ́bla likpidi lɛ́ƒiɔ Unwoti Israel Katɔti sɔsɔ. Ya na lɛsu lɛla lɛni lɛ́bla.

english_verse: They brought them back and put them in front of the sacred chest, so Joshua and the rest of the Israelites could see them.
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bammɔ bétéku ala ammɔ balɛku kevo kammɔ kemmo beboku. Na béti-nya béboku Yosua na Israelƒuɔ lɛnɔ bánu ala ammɔ. Na Yosua úti ala ammɔ útéwi Unwoti anumi.

english_verse: Then everyone took Achan and the things he had stolen to Trouble Valley. They also took along his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys, and sheep, his tent, and everything else that belonged to him.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Yosua ku Israelƒuɔ béƒie Akan ku bebi bananabi ku belekubi ku nwuna ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu ku bebuo beblidi ala betine bani na ubo ku sika ɔƒualadi ku awu gyɔlɔɔ ku sika ugyiedi ugyii ku nwuna kevo ku ala ani nse-nwu, na béti anwu ku ala ammɔ ƒui bésienku kɔwɛ kɔni baalɔ banii Akɔ nwuna kalɔ ndi Lɛbibo Kɔwɛ.

english_verse: Joshua said, “Achan, you caused us a lot of trouble. Now the Lord is paying you back with the same kind of trouble.” The people of Israel then stoned to death Achan and his family. They made a fire and burned the bodies, together with what Achan had stolen, and all his possessions.
translation_verse: Na Yosua ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na áya na lɛbibo lɛmɛni líbo-bu lɛlɔ. Unwoti ɔdubɔya na awɔ lɛnɔ ebo abi ɔmwi!” Amu na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ bébo Akan atabi badu. Na bébo nwuna bebi ku bebuo bammɔ lɛnɔ atabi badu. Na bákya bana ƒui ku ala ammɔ ogya.

english_verse: They covered the remains with a big pile of rocks, which is still there. Then the Lord stopped being angry with Israel. That's how the place came to be called Trouble Valley.
translation_verse: Na bála atabi lisu pim lɛdi bálɛ Akan lɛlɔ. Na atabi lisu lɛmmɔ lɛlɛ mmɔ úti úbedu ɔmwi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na baalɔ kesii kammɔ banii Lɛbibo Kɔwɛ. Na ɔmɛni ɔ́ya na Unwoti kɔnyi kati kati kɔmmɔ kɔyɔ.

english_verse: you come out of hiding. The Lord our God will help you capture the town.
translation_verse: Na si ɔlɛ lɛni ni, na bɛta bina kabɛkɔ mmɔ na bitádi ɔma ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔsika Unwoti Katɔti ɔdubo ɔma ɔmmɔ buti bɔkya bina enu kemmo.

english_verse: Then set it on fire, as the Lord has told us to do. Those are your orders,
translation_verse: Na si úti ɔma ɔmmɔ ɔkya bina enu kemmo ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, na bɛtu ogya bɛkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na bɛbla bɛsia Unwoti ɔda ɔni na úbo-mii lɛlɔ. Na bɛdi mina litemi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Early the next morning he got his troops ready to move out, and he and the other leaders of Israel led them to Ai.
translation_verse: Kadi kegye ɔtanta tutuutu ni, Yosua ɔ́ta na ɔ́lɔ nwuna bekpone bakladi ƒui ɔ́sala. Na anwu ku Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune bátɔnku-ma na bakɔ bésie Ai.

english_verse: They set up camp in full view of the town, across the valley to the north.
translation_verse: Na anwu ku bekpone bani ƒui nkya-nwu kudɔ bésie Ai ɔma kabɛnye na katɔ kakɛ na kɔwɛ kɔni nkya ama ku Aiƒuɔ ntɛ.

english_verse: Now all his troops were in place. Part of the army was in the camp to the north of Ai, and the others were hiding to the west, ready to make a surprise attack. That night, Joshua went into the valley.
translation_verse: Na Yosua bekpone ketulodikɔ bátábɛ bakya ɔma ɔmmɔ ɔƒɛ katɔ kakɛ. Na bakladi lɛnɔ bátábɛ bakya ɔma ɔmmɔ ɔ́ƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ. Nsu Yosua anwu ni, ɔ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ ɔkya kɔwɛ kɔmmɔ kemmo usien ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Finally, the Lord told Joshua, “Point your sword at the town of Ai, because now I am going to help you defeat it!” As soon as Joshua pointed his sword at the town,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Yosua ɔnini, “Ti ƒula lɛtula tina Ai, ɔsika líti ɔma ɔmmɔ lɛ́kya-a enu kemmo.” Anwuɔsu Yosua ɔ́bla aani kalɛ kani na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu.

english_verse: the soldiers who had been hiding jumped up and ran into the town. They captured it and set it on fire.
translation_verse: Na ka úti lɛtula lɛmmɔ ɔ́tina ɔma ɔmmɔ lɛni ni, nwuna bekyuli bani nábɛ ƒui báta kɔnakunwi na békeli bétéduo ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na bátu ogya bakya-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the other Israelite soldiers had come from the town and attacked the men of Ai from the rear. The Israelites captured the king of Ai and brought him to Joshua. They also chased the rest of the men of Ai into the desert and killed them. The Israelite army went back to Ai and killed everyone there.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bádu Aiƒuɔ bani nábi básiaku-ma na kekpokɔ mmɔ ku kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo mmɔ na bátu-ma kuwii ƒui báwɔlɔ ni, bénwini bésie Ai ɔma kemmo na bátádu bekyuli bani ƒui nkya mmɔ.

english_verse: Joshua made sure every building in Ai was burned to the ground. He told his men to kill the king of Ai and hang his body on a tree. Then at sunset he told the Israelites to take down the body, throw it in the gateway of the town, and cover it with a big pile of rocks. translation_verse: Na Yosua ɔ́kya Aiƒuɔ ɔga kabuli ɔda kugyii lɛlɔ na ɔ́da-nwu ɔ́ƒala mmɔ úti útédu useyi. Na ɔƒɛ úsela kanukɔ ni, ɔ́ya na bédie-nwu kabuli kammɔ na bétébo-nwu báva ɔma ɔmmɔ kabɛnye. english_verse: The people of Gibeon had also heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai.
translation_verse: Na ka Gilbeonƒuɔ bénu kalɛ na Yosua ɔ́bla Yerikoƒuɔ ku Aiƒuɔ ni,

english_verse: So they decided that some of their men should pretend to be messengers to Israel from a faraway country. The men put worn-out bags on their donkeys and found some old wineskins that had cracked and had been sewn back together.
translation_verse: bábla lɛkwɛ lɛdi, na bedie bekyuli badi ka bésie bététi adila bakya aƒo akukudi adi kemmo ku bebuo lɛku ntɛ aƒo akukudi na bényimi-nya basia bebuo beblidi ala betine lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Their sandals were old and patched, and their clothes were worn out. They even took along some dry and crumbly bread.
translation_verse: Na bágyu lɛwu ku lɛgbanvuo lɛni ndaku bɔbwɛ bákya. Na béti bodobodo ɔni nétu uwi na útili bada.

english_verse: Then they went to the Israelite camp at Gilgal, where they said to Joshua and the men of Israel, “We have come from a country that is far from here. Please make a peace treaty with us.”
translation_verse: Amu na bésie Yosua kudɔ na Gilgal na básu-nwu ku Israelƒuɔ banini, “Kesii kani na bɔ́si ni, kágyu geen. Anwuɔsu bɔɔyɔ́ ka abu ku-mii bɔbla unwi.”

english_verse: The Israelites replied, “But maybe you really live near us. We can't make a peace treaty with you if you live nearby.” The Gibeonites said, “If you make a peace treaty with us, we will be your servants.” “Who are you?” Joshua asked. “Where do you come from?” They answered:
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bammɔ básu Yosua banini, “Lɛla biala na bɛsu-bu ni, bɔdubɔbla.” Amu na Yosua úye-ma ɔnini, “Amii ndi ɔma? Na wɛ kakɛ na bɛ́si bíbo mɛni?”

english_verse: We are your servants, and we live far from here. We came because the Lord your God is so famous. We heard what the Lord did in Egypt
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bamɛni bédie kenye banini, “Ati, buvele bɔda-a, kesii kani na bɔ́si kágyu. Na búnu lɛla biala na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́bla na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ

english_verse: and what he did to those two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan: King Og of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, and King Sihon of Heshbon.
translation_verse: ku lɛla lɛni na úti ɔ́bla Amoriƒuɔ baga inyɔ bani nélie Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na baga bammɔ ndi Ɔga Sihon ɔni nási Hesbon ku Ɔga Og ɔni nási Basan na ɔɔdi lɛga na Astarot.

english_verse: Our leaders and everyone who lives in our country told us to meet with you and tell you that all of us are your servants. They said to ask you to make a peace treaty with our people. They told us to be sure and take along enough food for our journey.
translation_verse: Na bula batɔnkune ku bula bekyuli bani ƒui nlie bula kalɔ lɛlɔ nása kenye na básu-bu banii bɔwia adila adi bɔda bula ulu busie na bɔta na bɔyu ulu na bubasiaku-mii. Na básu-bu ka buboku lɛlɔ kalɔ bute-mii na buvele-mii na bunyimiku-mii na bɔ́bla unwi.

english_verse: See this dry, crumbly bread of ours? It was hot out of the oven when we packed the food on the day we left our homes.
translation_verse: Bɛnu adila ani udu bɔda. Uwi ɔni na bɔ́ta ɔma na bɔdubo ni, nka bodobodo ɔni béƒi ɔwɔdi na búti bɔda. Nsu binwini bɛnu kalɛ na ɔ́kwii na útili ɔ́bla!

english_verse: These cracked wineskins were new when we filled them, and our clothes and sandals are worn out because we have traveled so far.
translation_verse: Lɛnɔ uwi ɔni búwi ntɛ buyile bula aƒo amɛni ni, ese ɔwɔdi. Nsu bɛnu ka ana ƒui ábwɛ. Na ɔ́si ulu ɔgyu ɔni bɔ́si ɔsu. Na bula lɛwu ku agbanvuo lɛnɔ ƒui ábwɛ.”

english_verse: The Israelites tried some of the food, but they did not ask the Lord if he wanted them to make a treaty.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Israelƒuɔ bénu bekyuli bammɔ kalɔ na báƒɔ bana adila ani bada mmɔ adi bádi. Nsu béteye Unwoti kasusu asa na bénu kalɔ.

english_verse: So Joshua made a peace treaty with the messengers and promised that Israel would not kill their people. Israel's leaders swore that Israel would keep this promise.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Yosua únu kalɔ na bényimi na bábla unwi. Na Israel batɔnkune bákpali Katɔti lɛnyi bálɛ ugyii béte-ma ka balabla-ma lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: A couple of days later, the Israelites found out that these people actually lived in the nearby towns of Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-Jearim. So the Israelites left the place where they had camped and arrived at the four towns two days later.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Israelƒuɔ báta báyu ulu. Na limeyi lɛtɛdi lɛlɔ bétéduo bana lɛma lɛni kemmo belie. Na lɛma lɛmmɔ ndi Gibeon ku Keriƒa ku Beerot ku Kiriat-Yearim.

english_verse: But they did not attack the towns, because the Israelite leaders had sworn in the name of the Lord that they would let these people live. The Israelites complained about their leaders' decision not to attack,
translation_verse: Nsu Israelƒuɔ bátadu-ma, ɔsika Israelƒuɔ benengu bése-ma kenye na bana Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti lɛnyi kemmo ɔsu. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israelƒuɔ béti kɔnyi bakya bana benengu bammɔ.

english_verse: Joshua told some of his soldiers, “I want to meet with the Gibeonite leaders. Bring them here.” When the Gibeonites came, Joshua said, “You live close to us. Why did you lie by claiming you lived far away?
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́ya na bálɔ Gibeonƒuɔ bebenyene nwuna anumi. Na úye-ma ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na bilie bide-bu mɛni na bɛɛtɔlɔ-bu ka bina kasikɔ kágyu?

english_verse: So now you are under a curse, and from now on your people will have to send workers to cut wood and carry water for the place of worship.”
translation_verse: Ɔ́si lɛla lɛni bɛ́bla mɛni ɔsu ni, Katɔti úwida-mii. Na bina kabla kani na bɛdubo butaabla ndi ka bɛdubo ekyweni butaayɔ na biteesie ketu teesienku Katɔti kakpakɔ.”

english_verse: The Gibeonites answered, “The Lord your God told his servant Moses that you were to kill everyone who lives here and take their land for yourselves. We were afraid you would kill us, and so we tricked you into making a peace treaty. But we agreed to be your servants,
translation_verse: Amu na Gibeonƒuɔ bammɔ bédie kenye banini, “Ati! Lɛla lɛni ɔsu bɔ́nyi ɔkɔ ɔmmɔ udu ndi ka búnu na ɔdi sɔsɔ ka bina Unwoti Katɔti úbo nwuna kabla ɔblane Mose ɔda ka ɔdubo kalɔ kani ƒui nkya mɛni buti bute-mii. Na ɔdubɔya na bɛdu bekyuli bani ƒui nkya-ka kemmo uwi ɔni na bikpo bisela anumi mɛni. Ɔƒɛni lɛnɔ bɔbla lɛni, ɔsika bɔɔyia-mii geen na bɔgyi ka bula ngba bɔkya ɔgbankpi kemmo.

english_verse: and you are strong enough to do anything to us that you want. We just ask you to do what seems right.”
translation_verse: Na ɔƒɛni bɔkya bina enu kemmo. Lɛla biala bɛɛyɔ́ ni, bɛbla-bu.”

english_verse: Joshua did not let the Israelites kill the Gibeonites,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Yosua únye utile Gibeonƒuɔ na ɔ́ya na Israelƒuɔ batadu-ma.

english_verse: King Adonizedek of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured and destroyed the town of Ai, and then killed its king as he had done at Jericho. He also learned that the Gibeonites had signed a peace treaty with Israel.
translation_verse: Yerusalem ɔga ɔni baalɔ banii Adoni-Sedek únu ka Yosua úkpo ɔ́di Ai lɛlɔ na ɔ́yila ɔma ɔmmɔ udu kede kede na ɔ́du Aiƒuɔ ɔga aani kalɛ kani na ɔ́bla Yerikoƒuɔ ɔga. Na únu lɛnɔ ka Gibeonƒuɔ bésie bétévele Israelƒuɔ na bényimiku-ma na bábla unwi. Na belie bede-ma.

english_verse: This frightened Adonizedek and his people. They knew that Gibeon was a large town, as big as the towns that had kings, and even bigger than the town of Ai had been. And all of the men of Gibeon were warriors.
translation_verse: Na lɛla lɛmɛni lɛ́da Yerusalemƒuɔ ɔga liƒu geen. Ɔsika Gibeon ɔma ɔdi ɔma unengudi na bana ɔga ɔƒɔ kuye geen na ɔma ɔmmɔ úbomo útulo Ai, na bana banana ƒui lɛnɔ bagyi bukpo geen.

english_verse: So Adonizedek sent messages to the kings of four other towns: King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon. The messages said,
translation_verse: Ɔ́si ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Yerusalemƒuɔ Ɔga Adoni-Sedek ɔmɛni ɔ́tala bekyuli ka beteesie batasu Hebron ɔga ɔni baalɔ banii Hoham ku Yarmut ɔga ɔni baalɔ Piram ku Lakis ɔga ɔni baalɔ Yaƒia ku Eglon ɔga ɔni baalɔ Debir banii

english_verse: “The Gibeonites have signed a peace treaty with Joshua and the Israelites. Come and help me attack Gibeon!”
translation_verse: beti bana bekpone ƒui na bebo na bebebunku-nwu na bekpoku Gibeonƒuɔ. Ɔsika Gibeonƒuɔ bábla ku Yosua ku Israelƒuɔ ƒui unwi.

english_verse: the Gibeonites sent a message to the Israelite camp at Gilgal: “Joshua, please come and rescue us! The Amorite kings from the hill country have joined together and are attacking us. We are your servants, so don't let us down. Please hurry!”
translation_verse: Amu na Gibeonƒuɔ bátala bekyuli bésienku Yosua kudɔ na Gilgal kesii kani na Israelƒuɔ básala belie, ka bátásu-nwu banii, “Ati, buvele bɔda-a, ta ku ƒula bekpone kɔnakunwi na bibekpo bɛƒɔ-bu! Ɔsika Amoriƒuɔ baga bani nlie abi amadɔ ƒui básala lisu na béti bana bekpone na bébo bébekpoku-bu.”

english_verse: Joshua and his army, including his best warriors, left Gilgal.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yosua úti nwuna bekpone ƒui ku bani muukpó kaduɛ ƒui na báta bási Gilgal na bésie.

english_verse: “Joshua,” the Lord said, “don't be afraid of the Amorites. They will run away when you attack, and I will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su Yosua ɔnini, “Tayia Amoriƒuɔ baga ku bana bekpone bammɔ Líiti-ma lɛ́kya-a enu kemmo kukuuku. Na mɔɔsu-ɔ ka ni, ina ukyuli unwi ulakana-a anumi bɔkpɛ bude.”

english_verse: Joshua marched all night from Gilgal to Gibeon and made a surprise attack on the Amorite camp.
translation_verse: Na usien umodi Yosua ku nwuna bekpone bésie bási Gilgal bétéduo Gibeon. Na kɔnakunwi bátáda balɛ Amoriƒuɔ lɛlɔ na bése kalɔ beekpóku-ma.

english_verse: The Lord made the enemy panic, and the Israelites started killing them right and left. They chased the Amorite troops up the road to Beth-Horon and kept on killing them, until they reached the towns of Azekah and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́ya na Amoriƒuɔ beƒu uwi ɔni kani na bánu Israelƒuɔ bekpone. Na Israelƒuɔ bádu Amoriƒuɔ kaduɛ na Gibeon mmɔ na bábɔku-ma betédu ulu ɔni uti ɔɔkɔ́ use Bet-Horon. Na básiaku-ma baadu-ma laa betédu Aseka ku Makeda.

english_verse: And while these troops were going down through Beth-Horon Pass, the Lord made huge hailstones fall on them all the way to Azekah. More of the enemy soldiers died from the hail than from the Israelite weapons.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni Amoriƒuɔ badaku bukeli taatɔlɔ Israelƒuɔ bekpone kudɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na etubankɛ bonwu bonwu ánu ábayu-ma lɛlɔ úti útédu Aseka, na békpi ƒui kede kede. Na bani na etubankɛ áyu-ma lɛlɔ na békpi ni, bémomo bétulo bani na Israelƒuɔ bekpone bádu.

english_verse: The Lord was helping the Israelites defeat the Amorites that day. So about noon, Joshua prayed to the Lord loud enough for the Israelites to hear: “Our Lord, make the sun stop in the sky over Gibeon, and the moon stand still over Aijalon Valley.” So the sun and the moon stopped and stood still until Israel defeated its enemies. This poem can be found in The Book of Jashar. The sun stood still and didn't go down for about a whole day.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔƒɛ údi unye, na kɔbuli lɛnɔ kúdi kunye úti útédu ka Israelƒuɔ bádi bana bekisine lɛlɔ. Na lɛla lɛni nálɛ mɛni bénweni-nya bákya ɔku ɔni na Yasor únweni kemmo. Na mmɔ na bénweni banii ɔƒɛ údi unye kayaa limeyi limodi na útéduo lɛyu.

english_verse: Never before and never since has the Lord done anything like that for someone who prayed. The Lord was really fighting for Israel.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛmmɔ udu lɛdi lítalɛ kudii lɛni. Na Unwoti únu na ɔ́bla ɔsia ukyuli ɔyawine litemi lɛni ɔ́su-nwu lɛlɔ. Na Unwoti únye Israelƒuɔ kama na úkpo úte-ma.

english_verse: After the battle, Joshua and the Israelites went back to their camp at Gilgal. Joshua Kills the Five Enemy Kings
translation_verse: Amu ka Yosua ku nwuna bekpone békpo báwɔlɔ ni, básɔ bénwini bésie Gilgal. Yosua Ɔ́du Amoriƒuɔ Baga Ɛlɔ

english_verse: While the enemy soldiers were running from the Israelites, the five enemy kings ran away and hid in a cave near Makkedah.
translation_verse: Amu na Amoriƒuɔ baga ɛlɔ bani nkya mmɔ békeli bátábɛ bakya atabi ubu ɔdi kemmo na Makeda.

english_verse: Joshua's soldiers told him, “The five kings have been found in a cave near Makkedah.”
translation_verse: Na bekyuli badi bánu baga bamɛni na bébo bábasu Yosua.

english_verse: Joshua answered, “Roll some big stones over the mouth of the cave and leave a few soldiers to guard it.
translation_verse: Na Yosua ɔ́su bekyuli bammɔ ɔnini, “Bisie na bitéminime atakpɛ ebendi adi na biti-nya bitile ubu ɔmmɔ kenye. Na bɛya na bagyumanane badi basɔ benye ubu ɔmmɔ kenye mmɔ.

english_verse: But you and everyone else must keep going after the enemy troops, because they will be safe if they reach their walled towns. Don't let them get away! The Lord our God is helping us get rid of them.”
translation_verse: Nsu amii bitasɔ bitenye mmɔ. Mmomu bɛvi bitada-ma bɛsiku kama kakɛ kalɛ balakɛ kuƒi beduo bana lɛma. Ɔsika Unwoti bina Katɔti úti bina bekisine bammɔ ɔkya-mii enu kemmo.”

english_verse: So Joshua and the Israelites almost wiped out the enemy soldiers. Only a few safely reached their walled towns.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yosua ku nwuna bekpone bádu bekisine bammɔ ƒui. Nsu badi bakana bukeli bétéduo bana lɛma lɛni bátu awodu bámana-nya kemmo na bátadu-ma.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp at Makkedah, where Joshua was waiting for them. No one around there dared say anything bad about the Israelites.
translation_verse: Na Yosua bekpone bani ɔ́tala mmɔ ƒui básɔ bénwini bebo Makeda kesii kani na Israelƒuɔ bákya. Na bekyuli bani nlie amadɔ ƒui ɔdi biala ɔyia ka ɔlɔ Israel lɛnyikpi.

english_verse: Joshua told his soldiers, “Now, move the rocks from the entrance to the cave and bring those five kings to me.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́su nwuna bekpone bammɔ badi ɔnini, “Bidi atakpɛ ammɔ bidie ubu ɔmmɔ kenye. Na bɛni baga ɛlɔ bammɔ biboku-mi anumi.”

english_verse: The soldiers opened the entrance to the cave and brought out the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bédi atakpɛ ammɔ bédie na báni Amoriƒuɔ baga ɛlɔ bani ndi Yerusalem ɔga ku Hebron ɔga ku Yarmut ɔga ku Lakis ɔga ku Eglon ɔga bálɛku ubu ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: After Joshua had called the army together, he forced the five kings to lie down on the ground. Then he called his officers forward and told them, “You fought these kings along with me, so put your feet on their necks.” The officers did this,
translation_verse: Na béti-ma bábava Yosua anumi. Na Yosua ɔ́ya na Israelƒuɔ ƒui bálɛ bébo, na úbo bekpone batɔnkune bani na ama ku Yosua bése kekpokɔ ɔda ka balɛ na beti bana lɛgba banya baga bammɔ amɔ lɛlɔ. Na ama lɛnɔ bábla lɛni.

english_verse: and Joshua continued, “Don't ever be afraid or discouraged. Be brave and strong. This is what the Lord will do to all your enemies.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́su bekpone bammɔ banini, “Bitayia, na enu lɛnɔ ataƒɛ-mii. Mmomu bɛkya ɔkplu na bise kayi. Na lɛni na Unwoti ɔdubuti ɔbla bina bekisine bani ƒui amii ku-ma bɛdubo bukpo.”

english_verse: Joshua killed the five kings and told his men to hang each body on a tree. Then at sunset
translation_verse: Na Yosua ɔ́du baga ɛlɔ bammɔ na úti-ma ɔ́ƒala egyii alɔ lɛlɔ. Na báƒa mmɔ útédu useyi uwi.
