english_verse: he told some of his troops, “Take the bodies down and throw them into the cave where the kings were found. Cover the entrance to the cave with big rocks.” Joshua's troops obeyed his orders, and those rocks are still there. Joshua Continues the Fighting
translation_verse: Amu ka ɔƒɛ úsela kanukɔ ni, Yosua ɔ́ya na báƒami-ma na bétéƒwimi-ma bakya ubu ɔni kemmo na nka bábɛ bakya mmɔ. Na béti atakpɛ bonwu bonwu bétile ubu ɔmmɔ kenye. Na atakpɛ ammɔ amu ese mmɔ ubedu ɔmwi. Yosua Ku Nwuna Bekpone Békpo Bádi Amoriƒuɔ Lɛma Pii Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Later that day, Joshua captured Makkedah and killed its king and everyone else in the town, just as he had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yosua ku Israelƒuɔ besie na bétékpoku Makedaƒuɔ na ɔ́di-ma lɛlɔ limeyi lɛmmɔ kani. Na ɔ́du ukyuli biala na ɔkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo ɔni na ukyuli biala útebu. Na lɛla lɛni na ɔ́bla Yeriko ɔga ni, lɛni kani na ɔ́bla Makeda ɔga.

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Makkedah and attacked the town of Libnah.
translation_verse: Na ka bási Makeda ni, bésie bétékpoku Libnaƒuɔ.

english_verse: The Lord let them capture the town and its king, and they killed the king and everyone else, just as they had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́ya na Israelƒuɔ bádi Libnaƒuɔ lɛlɔ. Na bádu bekyuli bani ƒui nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo ɔni na bátanu ukyuli ɔdi kɔnyana. Na lɛla lɛni na béti bábla Yeriko ɔga ni, lɛla lɛmmɔ kani na béti bábla Libna ɔga lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Joshua then led his army to Lachish, and they set up camp around the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yosua ku nwuna bekpone bátɔlɔ Libna mmɔ bésie Lakis bátáka-ma bakya na békpoku-ma. Na limeyi linyɔdi lɛlɔ ni, Katɔti ɔ́ya na békpo bádi Lakisƒuɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: King Horam of Gezer arrived to help Lachish, but Joshua and his troops attacked and destroyed him and his army.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na bakya beekpóku Lakisƒuɔ bamɛni ni, Ɔga Horam ɔni nási Geser ku nwuna bekpone bébo bébebunku-ma. Nsu Yosua ku nwuna bekpone békpo bádi-ma lɛlɔ. Na bádu-ma ƒui kede kede ɔni na ina ukyuli unwi útebu.

english_verse: From Lachish, Joshua took his troops to Eglon, where they set up camp surrounding the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Yosua ku nwuna bekpone básɔ báta Lakis bésie Eglon na báka-ma bákya na békpoku-ma.

english_verse: captured it that same day, then killed everyone, as they had done at Lachish.
translation_verse: Na bádi-ma lɛlɔ limeyi lɛmmɔ kani. Na bádu bekyuli bammɔ ƒui kede kede aani kalɛ kani na béti bábla Lakisƒuɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Eglon and attacked Hebron.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama ni, Yosua ku nwuna bekpone báta Eglon na bésie Hebron na bétékpoku-ma.

english_verse: They captured the town and the nearby villages, then killed everyone, including the king. They destroyed Hebron in the same way they had destroyed Eglon.
translation_verse: Na bádi Hebronƒuɔ lɛlɔ na bádu bekyuli bani ƒui nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo ku bana ɔga. Na bávi bésie akpaklɔ ani nde Hebron na bádu bekyuli bani nkya mmɔ ƒui kede kede aani kalɛ na bábla Eglonƒuɔ. Na báyila ɔma ɔmmɔ udu ku bekyuli bani nli-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: Joshua and the Israelite army turned and attacked Debir.
translation_verse: Na Yosua ku nwuna bekpone bénwini bésie Debir na bétékpoku-ma.

english_verse: They captured the town, and its nearby villages. Then they destroyed Debir and killed its king, together with everyone else, just as they had done with Hebron and Libnah.
translation_verse: Na bádi Debirƒuɔ lɛlɔ na béƒie Debirƒuɔ ɔga ku bekyuli bani ƒui nkya Debir mmɔ ku akpaklɔ ani nde mmɔ bekyuli na bádu-ma kede kede. Na kalɛ kani na úti ɔ́bla Debir ku nwuna ɔga ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ni, lɛni kani na ɔ́bla Hebron ku Libna baga lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Joshua captured towns everywhere in the land: In the central hill country and the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert and the region that slopes down toward the Dead Sea. Whenever he captured a town, he would kill the king and everyone else, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yosua ɔ́di kalɔ kammɔ bekyuli ku baga bammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Úti ɔ́si lɛma lɛni nwi abi lɛlɔ na ɔƒɛ katukɔ ku lɛma lɛni nwi kɔbi kaƒɔna na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ lɛma lɛni nwi kalɔ ƒiaa lɛlɔ na kada kakɛ ni, ɔ́yila lɛla biala mbo bɔnwuna udu aani kalɛ na Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti úbo-ma ɔda.

english_verse: Joshua wiped out towns from Kadesh-Barnea to Gaza, everywhere in the region of Goshen, and as far north as Gibeon.
translation_verse: Na Yosua ɔ́di bekyuli bammɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́si Kades-Barnea útédu Gasa, na ɔ́si Gosen kalɛkɛ útédu Gibeon.

english_verse: King Jabin of Hazor heard about Joshua's victories, so he sent messages to many nearby kings and asked them to join him in fighting Israel. He sent these messages to King Jobab of Madon, the kings of Shimron and Achshaph,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Hasorƒuɔ Ɔga Yabin únu kalɛ na Yosua ku nwuna bekpone béekpo taadi bekyuli lɛlɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́tala bekyuli ɔkya Madonƒuɔ Ɔga Yobab ku Aksa Ɔga ku Simron ɔga.

english_verse: the kings in the northern hill country and in the Jordan River valley south of Lake Galilee, and the kings in the foothills and in Naphath-Dor to the west.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́tala batu ɔkya baga bani ƒui nlie abi lɛlɔ na kalɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ ku lɛma lɛni nkya Yordan Ketu ɔkwalɛ na Galilea Ɛpu lɛba kada kakɛ ku lɛma lɛni nwi abi kaƒɔna ku lɛma lɛni nkya ɛpu kudɔ na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ na Dor.

english_verse: He sent messages to the Canaanite kings in the east and the west, to the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, and Jebusite kings in the hill country, and to the Hivite kings in the region of Mizpah, near the foot of Mount Hermon.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́tala batu bamba na Kanaanƒuɔ bani nlie Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ katukɔ ku kanukɔ ku Amoriƒuɔ ku Hetiƒuɔ ku Perisiƒuɔ ku Yebusiƒuɔ bani nlie abi eli ku Hewiƒuɔ bani nlie Harmon Kɔbi kaƒɔna na kada kakɛ na Mispa kalɔ lɛlɔ ka bebo na bebebunku-ma na bekpoku Israelƒuɔ.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua: Don't let them frighten you! I'll help you defeat them, and by this time tomorrow they will be dead. When you attack, the first thing you have to do is to cripple their horses. Then after the battle is over, burn their chariots.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Yosua ɔnini, “Tayia bekyuli bammɔ, ɔsika ndubɔya na bɛdu-ma ƒui asa na wedu kɔnaadi uwi ɔmɛni kemmo. Na lɛla lɛni na bɛdubo bɔbla ndi ka bikulo bana bapɔnkɔ bammɔ lɛgba nti. Na bɛkyula bana bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ lɛmmɔ ƒui.”

english_verse: Joshua and his army made a surprise attack against the enemy camp at Merom Pond
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ku nwuna bekpone bétéyu bekyuli bammɔ batu kɔnakunwi na Merom Ketudɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Up to this time, the king of Hazor had controlled the kingdoms that had joined together to attack Israel, so Joshua led his army back and captured Hazor. They killed its king
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua únwini úsie útékpo na ɔ́di Hasorƒuɔ lɛlɔ na ɔ́du bana ɔga. Na asa na Yosua ɔ́di Hasorƒuɔ lɛlɔ ni, Hasor ndi ɔga unengudi na amadɔ mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: and everyone else, then they set the town on fire.
translation_verse: Na bádu ukyuli biala ku lɛla biala mɔɔnwuna. Na bákyula ɔma ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Joshua captured all the towns where the enemy kings had ruled. These towns were built on small hills, and Joshua did not set fire to any of these towns, except Hazor. The Israelites kept the animals and everything of value from these towns, but they killed everyone who lived in them, including their kings. That's what the Lord had told his servant Moses to do, that's what Moses had told Joshua to do, and that's exactly what Joshua did.
translation_verse: Na kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔni ndi nwuna kabla ɔblane ɔda ni, lɛni kani na Mose lɛnɔ úbo Yosua ɔda. Na Yosua lɛnɔ ɔ́bla ɔ́siaku kalɛ kani na Mose úbo-nwu ɔda ɔmmɔ ɔni na útada útavia ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔdi. Ɔ́bla lɛla biala pɛpɛɛpɛ aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda. Yosua Ɔ́di Kɔlɔ Kɔni Blɔti Ɔ́tina-nwu Ƒui Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Joshua and his army took control of the northern and southern hill country, the foothills to the west, the Southern Desert, the whole region of Goshen, and the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Na Yosua ku nwuna bekpone békpo báƒɔ kɔlɔ kɔni ƒui nwi ɔ́si katɔ kakɛ utédu kada kakɛ ku kɔlɔ kɔni nwi abi eli ku abi kaƒɔna ku kɔlɔ kɔni nwi Gosen amadɔ ku kɔlɔ kɔkwiidi kɔni nwi kada kakɛ uti usie kɔwɛ kɔni nwi Yordan Ketu.

english_verse: They took control of the land from Mount Halak near the country of Edom in the south to Baal-Gad in Lebanon Valley at the foot of Mount Hermon in the north. Joshua and his army were at war with the kings in this region for a long time, but finally they captured and put to death the last king.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́ƒɔ ɔ́siku Halak abi lɛlɔ ɔ́kɔ úsie Seir úti útédu Baal-Gad ku Lebanon Kɔwɛ na Hermon abi kaƒɔna lɛlɔ ƒui. Na Yosua ku kɔlɔ kɔmɛni baga békpo bétu uwi na úƒie-ma na ɔ́du-ma ƒui kede kede.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he wanted the towns in this region destroyed and their people killed without mercy. That's why the Lord made the people in the towns stubborn and determined to fight Israel. The only town that signed a peace treaty with Israel was the Hivite town of Gibeon. The Israelite army captured the rest of the towns in battle.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́ya na lɛma lɛmmɔ kɔyi kɔ́yu ɔkplu kalɛ na Israelƒuɔ bakɛ kuƒi na bekpoku-ma na bayila-ma udu kede kede ɔni na kɔnyana bɔnu bɔdi buuubo. Na ɔmɛni ndi ɔda ɔni na Unwoti úbo Mose ka ɔbla.

english_verse: During this same time, Joshua and his army killed the Anakim from the northern and southern hill country. They also destroyed the towns where the Anakim had lived, including Hebron, Debir, and Anab.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yosua ɔ́sɔ úsie Hebron ku Debir ku Anak na útékpoku Anakƒuɔ bani nli lɛma lɛmmɔ. Na ɔ́di-ma lɛlɔ na ɔ́yila bekyuli bammɔ ku bana lɛma udu ɔ́siku Yuda ku Israel abi eli.

english_verse: There were not any Anakim left in the regions where the Israelites lived, although there were still some in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
translation_verse: Na Anakƒuɔ bammɔ badi básɔ bétebu na Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ amu ntu ɛlɛɛ badi kani nébu belie Gasa ku Gad ku Asdod lɛma kemmo.

english_verse: That's how Joshua captured the land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua divided it up among the tribes. Finally, there was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Yosua úkpo ɔ́di kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ aani kalɛ kani na Unwoti úbo Mose ɔda. Na Yosua úle kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ úte Israelƒuɔ na bana kaba kenye. Na kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ kúnwini bana kɔdikɔ. Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Israelƒuɔ bánwuna na básɔ bétekpoku bekyuli badi.

english_verse: Before Moses died, he and the people of Israel had defeated two kings east of the Jordan River. These kings had ruled the region from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, including the eastern side of the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Israelƒuɔ békpo bádi baga inyɔ badi lɛlɔ. Na béti bana kɔlɔ kɔni nwi Yordan Ketu úti úsie ɔƒɛ katukɔ na ɔ́si Arnon Kɔwɛ útédu Hermon.

english_verse: Sihon also controlled the eastern side of the Jordan River valley from Lake Galilee south to Beth-Jeshimoth and the Dead Sea. In addition to these regions, he ruled the town called Slopes of Mount Pisgah and the land south of there at the foot of the hill.
translation_verse: Na ɔdanku Yordan Kɔwɛ uti ɔsi Galilea Ɛpu lɛba kada kakɛ utédu Bet-Yesimot na Mma Ɛpu ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ na ɔkɛ Pisga Kɔbi kaƒɔna.

english_verse: Next, Moses and the Israelites defeated King Og of Bashan, who lived in the town of Ashtaroth part of each year and in Edrei the rest of the year. Og was one of the last of the Rephaim.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bamɛni bádi ɔga unyɔdi ɔni baalɔ banii Ɔga Og ɔni nási Basan lɛlɔ. Na ɔdi bekyuli bagyangladi bekplodi kemmo unwi ɔni nébu. Na ɔ́di lɛga na Astarot ku Edrei.

english_verse: His kingdom stretched north to Mount Hermon, east to the town of Salecah, and included the land of Bashan as far west as the borders of the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. He also ruled the northern half of Gilead.
translation_verse: Na Og ɔ́di lɛga na Hermon Kɔbi ku Salka ku Basan kɔlɔ lɛlɔ ƒui úti útédu Gesurƒuɔ ku Maakatƒuɔ ɔmii lɛlɔ ku Gilead kɔlɔ kakɛ kadi úti útédu Ɔga Sihon ɔni nási Hesbon ɔmii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Moses, the Lord's servant, had led the people of Israel in defeating Sihon and Og. Then Moses gave their land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na baga inyɔ bamɛni na Mose ku Israelƒuɔ békpo na bádi-ma lɛlɔ. Na Mose ɔni ndi Unwoti kabla ɔblane úti kalɔ kammɔ úte Rubenƒuɔ ku Gadƒuɔ na úti kalɔ kammɔ kakladi lɛnɔ úte Manase kaba bekyuli kakɛ kenwi. Yosua Ku Israelƒuɔ Békpo Na Bádi Kalɔ Kadi Baga Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Many years later, the Lord told Joshua: Now you are very old, but there is still a lot of land that Israel has not yet taken.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni Yosua ɔ́ɔbi geen na nwuna akwa lɛnɔ éesie anumi geen. Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Yosua ɔnini, “Áabi lɛlɔ na ƒula akwa lɛnɔ éesie anumi, nsu kɔlɔ kɔdi kɔmu kɔkya ɔni na ɔlɛka ekpo na eti-ku.

english_verse: Moses had already given land east of the Jordan River to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na kalɔ kani nkya késie Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ ni, Mose ɔni ndi Unwoti kabla ɔblane úle kalɔ kammɔ úte Ruben kaba ku Gad kaba ku Manase kaba bekyuli kakɛ kani nébu.

english_verse: This region stretched north from the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, and included the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley. It covered the flatlands of Medeba north of Dibon,
translation_verse: Na bana lɛmii lisie lítédu Aroer ɔni ntɛ útédu Arnon Kɔwɛ kemmo ku ɔma ubendi ɔni nkya kɔwɛ kɔmmɔ ntɛ ku kɔbi lili kalɔ kani nwi ƒiaa ɔ́si Medeba laa útédu Dibon

english_verse: and took in the towns that had belonged to Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon. Some of these towns were as far east as the Ammonite border.
translation_verse: ku lɛma lɛni ndi Amoriƒuɔ ɔga ɔni baalɔ Sihon ɔni nádi lɛga na Hesbon úti útédu Amonƒuɔ ɔmii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord God of Israel had told them, “Instead of land, you will receive the sacrifices offered at my altar.” The Land Moses Gave to the Reuben Tribe
translation_verse: Nsu Lewi kaba aka ni, Mose útete-ma kalɔ kammɔ kadi. Ɔsika akpala ani na bekyuli beeti taakyula teete Israelƒuɔ Unwoti ni, ana kemmo na baakɛ bana kadikɔ aani kalɛ na Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su úse. Mose Úti Kalɔ Kakɛ Kadi Ɔ́kya Ruben Kaba Bekyuli Enu Kemmo

english_verse: Moses gave land to each of the clans in the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Mose úte Ruben kaba bekyuli kalɔ kakɛ kadi ka béti ka babla bana kadikɔ.

english_verse: Their land started in the south at the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, took in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley, and went as far north as the flatlands around Medeba.
translation_verse: Na kalɔ kammɔ kási Aroer ɔni ntɛ úsie Arnon Kɔwɛ kemmo ku ɔma ɔni nkya kɔwɛ kɔmmɔ ntɛ ku abi eli ku kalɔ kani nwi ƒiaa na kásia Medeba.

english_verse: The Amorite King Sihon had lived in Heshbon and had ruled the towns in the flatlands. Now Heshbon belonged to Reuben, and so did the following towns in the flatlands: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill in the valley, Beth-Peor, Slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth. Moses defeated Sihon and killed him and the Midianite chiefs who ruled parts of his kingdom for him. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
translation_verse: Na lɛma lɛmɛni nwi kɔbi eli kalɔ kani nwi ƒiaa mmɔ lɛlɔ ku Amoriƒuɔ Ɔga Sihon ɔni nádi lɛga na Hesbon. Anwu na Mose úkpo na ɔ́di-nwu lɛlɔ ku Midian baga ku Ewi ku Rekem ku Sur ku Hur ku Reba beleku baga bani nási Sihon na béli kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites also killed Balaam the son of Beor, who had been a fortuneteller.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani na Israelƒuɔ bádu ndi Bileam ɔni na uubó like na ɔdi Beor ubidi.

english_verse: This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border. The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
translation_verse: Na Rubenƒuɔ bammɔ ɔmii ndi Yordan Ketu. Na ɔmɛni ndi kadikɔ nte Rubenƒuɔ. Na béle lɛma lɛmmɔ bete bana kaduli bekyuli. Mose Úti Kalɔ Kadi Úte Gad Kaba Bekyuli

english_verse: Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose úti kalɔ kadi úte Gadƒuɔ ka béti-ka babla bana kadikɔ.

english_verse: The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si Hesbon útédu Ramat-Mispa ku Betonim na ɔ́si Mahanaim úti útédu Debir ɔmii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon.
translation_verse: Ɔkɛ Yordan Ketu kɔwɛ kɔmmɔ kemmo ku Bet-Haram ku Bat-Nimra ku Sukot ku Saƒon ɔni ndi Hesbon Ɔga Sihon kalɔ kakladi. Na Yordan Ketu ndi ɔmii úti útédu ɛpu kada kakɛ na Galilea Ɛpu úti ɔ́via úsie Yordan ɔƒɛ katukɔ.

english_verse: These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe. The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
translation_verse: Na lɛma ku akpaklɔ amɛni ndi Gadƒuɔ kadikɔ na béle lɛma ku akpaklɔ ammɔ béte bana kaduli bekyuli. Mose Úti Kalɔ Kakɛ Kadi Úte Manase Kaba Kakɛ Kenwi

english_verse: Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Mose úti kalɔ kakɛ kadi úte Manase kaba bekyuli kakɛ kenwi ka béti mmɔ bábla bana kadikɔ.

english_verse: Their land started at Mahanaim and took in the region that King Og of Bashan had ruled, including Ashtaroth and Edrei, the two towns where he had lived. The villages where the Jair clan settled were part of Manasseh's land, and so was the northern half of the region of Gilead. The clans of this half of Manasseh had
translation_verse: Na Gilead kakɛ ku Astarot ku Edrei ɔni ndi Ɔga Og lɛma lɛni nkya Basan aka na béti béte Makir kaduli bekyuli kakɛ kenwi. Na Makir ɔmɛni ɔ́si Manase kaba kemmo.

english_verse: That was how Moses divided up the Moab Plains to the east of Jericho on the other side of the Jordan River, so these two and a half tribes would have land of their own.
translation_verse: Lɛni na Mose úti kadikɔ kɔlɔ kɔni nkya Yordan Ketu kɔwɛ na Yeriko ɔƒɛ katukɔ úte Israelƒuɔ uwi ɔni na ɔ́kya Moab kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
translation_verse: Nsu Mose útéte Lewiƒuɔ kalɔ kadi. Na bɔsu na ɔ́su-ma ka bana kadikɔ ndi akpala ani na beeti taakpa teete Israelƒuɔ Unwoti Katɔti.

english_verse: One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua: You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, bekyuli bani nási Yuda kaba kemmo bébo Yosua kudɔ na Gilgal. Na bekyuli bammɔ kemmo unwi ndi Kaleb ɔni ndi Yeƒune ubidi ɔdi Kenesini. Na úbasu Yosua ɔnini, “Agyi lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su Mose, nwuna kabla ɔblane, uwi ɔni na bɔ́kya Kades-Barnea na ami ku-ɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God.
translation_verse: Nsu bekyuli bani na ami ku-ma búsie ni, báya na bɔyia ku liƒu liduo bula bekyuli kemmo. Nsu ami lɛ́di Mina Unwoti Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ geen.

english_verse: The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
translation_verse: Ɔsi lɛla lɛni lɛ́bla-mɛni ɔsu ni, Mose úse ami ku mina bebi kenye ka ni, kalɔ kani kemmo na lísie lɛ́vi ƒui kadubo bunwini ami ku mina bebi kadi.

english_verse: So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ti kalɔ ku lɛma lɛni nwi abi lɛlɔ te-mi aani kalɛ na Unwoti úse kenye úte-mi limeyi lɛni na ami ku mina bekyuli búnwini búbeduo mmɔ. Ɔsika limeyi lɛmmɔ ni, énye mmɔ na énu kalɛ na básu kalɛ na bekyuli kangyaa bani nli mmɔ bese ku kalɛ bátu bana awodu bonwu báka bamana lɛma lɛmmɔ. Nsu lɛ́ƒɔ lɛ́di ka Unwoti ɔdubunyeku-mi na lɛbɔku-ma na bekeli balɛ aani kalɛ na use kenye úse.”

english_verse: Joshua prayed that God would help Caleb, then he gave Hebron to Caleb and his descendants.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Yosua úte Kaleb ɔni ndi Yeƒune ubidi kusɛ kusɛ na úti ɔma ɔni baalɔ Hebron úte-nwu ka úti mmɔ ɔbla nwuna kadikɔ.

english_verse: And Hebron still belongs to Caleb's descendants, because he was faithful to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yeƒune ubidi Kaleb ɔni nási Kenesin kaba kemmo ni, anwu mɔɔdi Hebron ɔ́si uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo. Ɔsika Kaleb ɔ́di Unwoti ɔnii ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ ku kayi ƒui ɔsu.

english_verse: Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim. There was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Kuuku ni, Hebron bátaalɔ Kiriat-Arba. Na Arba ɔmɛni ndi ukyuli ɔni mbo ɔyikun ntulo na bekyuli kangyaa bani baalɔ Anakƒuɔ bammɔ akɔ. Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Israelƒuɔ bánwuna na básɔ bétekpoku bekyuli badi.

english_verse: Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Na kada kakɛ ɔmii ɔ́wɔ Mma Ɛpu kawɔlɔkɔ.

english_verse: As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka,
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛ Katamlukpa Ulu úti úsela ɔƒɛ kanukɔ ɔkɛ útádanku Sin kalɔ kakwiidi. Na ɔ́kɔ útédu Kades-Barnea na ɔkɛ Herson na ɔ́danku Adar na udeyi útédu Karka.

english_verse: and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́vi ɔkɛ Asmon na útáda ɔlɛ Egyipte Kɔwɛ kemmo na úti útédu ɛpu kenye.

english_verse: Judah's eastern border ran the full length of the Dead Sea. The northern border started at the northern end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ ni, ɔmii ɔmmɔ ɔkɛ utédu Mma Ɛpu. Na katɔ kakɛ ɔmii use kalɔ ɔ́si Yordan Ketu ku Mma Ɛpu kasakɔ.

english_verse: From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Na ɔmii ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɛ útédu Bet-Hogla na katɔ kakɛ útásia Bet-Araba. Na ɔkɛ mmɔ útédu Ruben ubidi Bohan lɛtakpɛ.

english_verse: From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel,
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si Akor Kɔwɛ lɛlɔ útédu Debir na ɔ́bu ɔkɛ útédu Gilgal Adumim ulu ubendi na Akor Kɔwɛ kada kakɛ. Na ɔ́vi ɔ́kɛ En-Semes Ketu kenye na úti útédu En-Rogel.

english_verse: and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites. Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛ Hinom Kɔwɛ kemmo na Yebusiƒuɔ ɔma ɔni ndi Yerusalem. Na ɔkɛ kɔbi kɔni nkya Hinom Kɔwɛ kɔni nkya ɔƒɛ kanukɔ na Reƒaiƒuɔ Kɔwɛ na katɔ kakɛ úti útédu eli kakɛ.

english_verse: At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛ kɔbi kɔmmɔ eli úti útédu Neƒtoa Ketu kenye. Na ɔ́si mmɔ lɛnɔ úsie Eƒron Kɔbi lɛma lɛlɔ. Na uti ɔɔyu Baala ɔni ndi Kiriat-Yearim.

english_verse: From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛ katɔ kakɛ na Baala úsie ɔƒɛ kanukɔ na Seir Kɔbi lɛlɔ. Na únwini ɔkɛ Har-Yearim Kɔbi iye Kesalon Kɔbi na ɔkɛ Bet-Semes, na údeyi ɔkɛ Timna.

english_verse: It continued along to the hillside north of Ekron, curved around to Shikkeron, and then went to Mount Baalah. After going to Jabneel, the border finally ended at the Mediterranean Sea,
translation_verse: Na údeyi ɔkɛ Ekron na katɔ kakɛ na ɔ́kanti úsie Sikron. Na ɔ́vi ɔkɛ Baala Kɔbi lɛlɔ, na ɔkɛ Yabneel útédu Mediterenia Ɛpu.

english_verse: Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Na Kaleb úse útékpoku Debirƒuɔ. Na kuuku ni, Debir na bátaalɔ banii Kiriat-Seƒer.

english_verse: Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
translation_verse: Kalɛ kani na Unwoti úbo Yosua ɔda ni, lɛni na Yosua úte Kaleb ɔni ndi Yeƒune ubidi kalɔ na kakɛ kani na Yuda kaba bebi belie-ka kemmo. Na Hebron na baalɔ banii Kiriat Arba. Na Arba ndi Anak ɔti kuuku.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
translation_verse: Na Kaleb ɔ́bɔku Anak bawɔ ɛtɛ ku bana kaba bekyuli ɔ́lɛku ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na bawɔ bammɔ ndi Sesai ku Ahiman ku Talmai.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Amu na Kaleb ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ukyuli biala ɔni ndubɔkana na ukpoku Kiriat-Seƒer na ɔ́di-ma lɛlɔ ni, ndubuti mina ubidi ulekubi ɔni baalɔ banii Aksa lite-nwu na uti.”

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Na ka béti lɛlɔ báwɔlɔ ni, Otniel ɔ́su Aksa ka ɔsu ɔti Kaleb ka ute-nwu kalɔ kadi. Amu na Aksa úsie ɔti kudɔ. Na ka Aksa ɔɔyu nwuna ɔpɔnkɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, Ɔti Kaleb úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi na aayɔ́ ka lɛbla lite-ɔ?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond. Towns in Judah's Land
translation_verse: Amu na ubidi ɔmɛni ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Mɔɔyɔ́ ka ete-mi kalɔ kani na abiɔ akya-nya kemmo. Ɔsika kalɔ kani na éti éte-mi ni, kadi kalɔ kakwiidi.” Ɔmɛni ɔsu Kaleb úti abiɔ ani mɔɔyu na akya katɔ ku kada kakɛ úte-nwu. Yosua Úti Lɛma Lɛdi Úte Yuda Kaba

english_verse: The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
translation_verse: Na lɛma lɛni na Yosua úle úte Yuda kaba ka beti-ka bábla bana kadikɔ ndi amɛni.

english_verse: The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following
translation_verse: ku Lebaot ku Silhim ku Ain ku Rimon. Lɛma lɛmmɔ ƒui lɛdi aavlanyɔ-yaalenwi ku nina akpaklɔ.

english_verse: The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: ku Saaraim ku Aditam ku Gedera ɔni basɔ baalɔ Gederotiam. Lɛma lɛmmɔ lɛdi lɛma leevu-ine ku nina akpaklɔ.

english_verse: The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: ku Gederot ku Bet-Dagon ku Naama ku Makeda. Lɛma lɛmmɔ lɛdi lɛma libendi leevu-ɛku ku nina akpaklɔ.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
translation_verse: Na Yebusiƒuɔ bani nli Yerusalem ama ni, Yudaƒuɔ bátakana na babɔku-ma. Anwuɔsu Yebusiƒuɔ ku Yudaƒuɔ baamu beli Yerusalem bébedu ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni.

english_verse: The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon
translation_verse: Na ɔmii ɔni na bɔdubo bɔtina ndi Eƒraimƒuɔ kaba bekyuli ɔdi. Na bana ɔmii ɔni ntɛ ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ ndi Atarot-Adar ɔ́kɔ úti útédu Bet-Horon eli.

english_verse: Ephraim also had some towns and villages that were inside Manasseh's tribal land.
translation_verse: Na lɛma ku akpaklɔ ani ndi Manase kaba bekyuli ɔdi ni, béti-ka béte Eƒraim kaba ka beti-ka babla bana kadikɔ.

english_verse: Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Nsu Kanaanƒuɔ bani nli Geser na béƒu basala ku Eƒraimƒuɔ ni, bátabɔku-ma. Mmomu buti na béti Kanaanƒuɔ bamɛni bábla bekyuli bani mɔɔbla kabla teete-ma. Na bamu bakya baabla kabla teete-ma úti úbedu ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The land of the Manasseh tribe went from its northern border with the Asher tribe south to Michmethath, which is to the east of Shechem. The southern border started there, but curved even farther south to include the people who lived around Tappuah Spring.
translation_verse: Na Manase ɔmii ɔ́si Aser úsie Makmetat ɔni ntɛ Sekem ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na ɔ́tɛ úsie kada kakɛ na ɔkɛ En-Tapuaƒuɔ kalɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
translation_verse: Na Tapua kalɔ kammɔ kadi Manase ɔdi. Na Tapua ɔma ɔni nkya Manase ɔmii lɛlɔ ɔdi Eƒraim ɔdi.

english_verse: Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands: Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
translation_verse: Na lɛma lɛni na Manase ɔ́kɛ na Isakar ku Asar ntɛ ndi Bet-San ku Yibleam ku bani nli Dor ɔni lɛnɔ baalɔ Naƒot ku nwuna lɛma ku En-Darƒo ku Taanakƒuɔ ku Megidoƒuɔ ku nina akpaklɔ ani náka amana-ma.

english_verse: But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them.
translation_verse: Na Manase bebi batákana na bábɔku Kanaanƒuɔ bálɛku ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo. Ɔsika bálɛ ugyii kpakplaa ka balatɔlɔ.

english_verse: When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave. Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ baakɛ́ ɔyikun teebu ni, benye Kanaanƒuɔ bammɔ lɛlɔ na béti-ma babla kabla bablane bete-ma. Anwuɔsu bátábɔku Kanaanƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui. Yoseƒ Bawɔ Béye Kadikɔ Bébu

english_verse: One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yoseƒ kaba bekyuli bébo Yosua kudɔ na béye-nwu banini, “Bi ɔsu na kadikɔ kenwi pɛ kani na éte-bu? Nsu bumomo na Unwoti lɛnɔ úte-bu kusɛ kusɛ.”

english_verse: Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Si bimomo na Eƒraim abi lɛlɔ kese blii suɛ kete-mi ni, amu biteesie lɛku kemmo ngye na bitáda ɔma mmɔ na Perisiƒuɔ ku bablani bammɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: “Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yoseƒ kaba bekyuli bammɔ básu Yosua banini, “Abi kalɔ kammɔ kese bliisuɛ kete-bu. Na Kanaanƒuɔ bani nlie kɔbi kaƒɔna na kalɔ kani nwi ƒiaa ku bani nlie Bet-San amadɔ lɛma ku bani nlie Yesreel Kɔwɛ kemmo ƒui bebo bapɔnkɔ abuala kɛɛkɛ.”

english_verse: “Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful,
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yosua ɔ́su Yoseƒ kaba bekyuli bani nási Eƒraim ku Manase kaba kemmo ɔnini, “Bɛdi bekyuli bani mmomo na bibo ɔyikun. Anwuɔsu utalɛka bɛkɛ kadikɔ kenwi kani.

english_verse: so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
translation_verse: Mmomu abi kalɔ kɔmmɔ kabla bina ɔdi. Ina ka akun na adi ni, bɛtuma-nya na biti mmɔ bɛbla bina kadikɔ bitédu kesii kani na bɛkana bɔda. Na bɛbɔku Kanaanƒuɔ bani nlie mmɔ ina ka bebo bapɔnkɔ ku abuala kɛɛkɛ na bebo ɔyiku lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: There were still seven tribes without any land,
translation_verse: Nsu kaba maatɛ kébu ɔni na bétele tɔ kalɔ kadi bétete-ma na bakɛ bana kadikɔ.

english_verse: Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
translation_verse: Amu ka banana bani na Yosua ɔ́tala ka besie na batálɛ lɛmii mmɔ badubo bɔtɔlɔ ni, úbo-ma ɔda kpakplaa ɔnini, “Bɛvi kalɔ kammɔ ƒui kemmo na bɛlɛ lɛmii na binweni kalɛ na bɛ́bla kabla kammɔ bɛ́vinku na biti biboku-mi. Na ndubɔtu egulabi lɛnu na Silo mɛni na liye Unwoti kasusu leti-mii.”

english_verse: The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu banana bammɔ bávi kalɔ kammɔ ƒui kemmo na bénweni bákya kakunkɛ kemmo kalɛ na béle kalɔ kammɔ akpa maatɛ ku lɛma lɛni nkya-ka kemmo. Na bénwini bébo Yosua kudɔ na Silo.

english_verse: Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided. Benjamin's Land
translation_verse: Na Yosua ɔ́tu egulabi ɔ́nu na úye Unwoti kasusu ute-ma. Na mmɔ na Yosua úle kalɔ kammɔ úte Israelƒuɔ kalɛ na ɔ́manku úte-ma. Yosua Ɔ́tina Benyamin Kaba Bana Ɔmii

english_verse: Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north.
translation_verse: Amu ka ɔ́tu egulabi ɔ́nu ni, Benyamin kaba bekyuli ɔdi nálɛ na úti kalɔ kani nkya Yuda ku Yoseƒ kaba ntɛ úte-ma.

english_verse: Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert.
translation_verse: Na bana ɔmii ɔni nkya katɔ kakɛ úse kalɔ ɔ́si Yordan Ketu. Na ɔkɛ Yeriko katɔ kakɛ na ɔ́kɛ ɔ́vi kɔbi lɛlɔ útédu ɔƒɛ kanukɔ. Na nwuna kenye kétédu Bet-Awen kalɔ kakwiidi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town. These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛ na útédeyi ɔkɛ ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ, na ɔkɛ kɔbi kɔni ntɛ Bet-Horon na kada kakɛ. Na ɔdubudu Kiriat-Baal ɔni basɔ baalɔ banii Kiriat-Yearim na ɔdi Yudaƒuɔ ɔma.

english_verse: Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring.
translation_verse: Na kada ɔmii ɔ́si Kiriat-Yearim úsie ɔƒɛ kanukɔ, na ɔkɛ úsie Neƒtoa Ketu kenye.

english_verse: From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
translation_verse: Na údeyi ɔkɛ kɔbi kɔni ntɛ Hinom úsie utédu Reƒaiƒuɔ Kɔwɛ kemmo na katɔ kakɛ. Na údeyi ɔkɛ Hinom utédu kɔwɛ úsie Yebusiƒuɔ kada ntɛ, na ɔ́kanti ɔkɛ En-Rogel.

english_verse: At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Na údeyi ɔkɛ katɔ kakɛ, na ɔkɛ En-Semes, na ɔkɛ úsie Gelilot, na ɔ́kɔ úsie Adumim Kɔwɛ na ɔ́bu úsie Ruben ubidi Bohan lɛtakpɛ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛ úsie katɔ na Bet-Araba Kɔbi na ɔkɛ utédu Yordan Ketu kɔwɛ kemmo.

english_verse: Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Na udeyi ɔkɛ Bet-Hogla katɔ kakɛ ɔkɛ utédu kesii kani na Yordan Ketu ku Mma Ɛpu kasakɔ Na ɔmɛni ndi kada ɔmii.

english_verse: The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border. These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
translation_verse: Na Yordan ndi ɔmii ɔni ntɛ úsie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na ɔmɛni ndi kalɔ kani na béti béte Benyamin kaba bekyuli.

english_verse: Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders.
translation_verse: Ka Yosua ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tu egulabi kunyɔdi ɔ́nu ni, Simeon kaba ɔdi nálɛ. Na bana kalɔ kakya Yuda kaba ɔdi akɔ.

english_verse: In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following
translation_verse: ku Bet-Lebaot ku Saruben na ɔdi lɛma leevu-ɛtɛ ku nina akpaklɔ.

english_verse: and continued north to Gath-Hepher, Ethkazin, and Rimmonah, where it curved toward Neah
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛ ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ úsie Gat-Heƒer ku Et-Kasin. Na ɔkɛ Rimon na údeyi ɔkɛ Nea.

english_verse: In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages: Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
translation_verse: Ain ku Rimon ku Etar ku Asan. Anwu lɛnɔ ɔdi lɛma ine ku nina akpaklɔ

english_verse: Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
translation_verse: ku akpaklɔ ani nkya lɛma lɛmɛni amadɔ úti útédu Baalat-Beer ɔni lɛnɔ baalɔ banii Ramat ku kalɔ kakwiidi na kada kakɛ. Kalɔ kamɛni béle béte Simeon kaba bekyuli.

english_verse: Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon. Zebulun's Land
translation_verse: Na ka kalɔ kani na béti béte Yuda kaba bekyuli kébomo kágya ɔsu ni, bámini kadi béte Simeon kaba. Yosua Úle Kalɔ Kadi Úte Sebulon Kaba

english_verse: and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́bu ɔ́kɛ katɔ kakɛ úti útédu Hanaton na nwuna kenye kátáwɔlɔ Yiƒta-El Kɔwɛ kemmo.

english_verse: Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Na ɔdanku Katat ku Nahalal ku Simron ku Yidala ku Betlehem. Na lɛma lɛmmɔ lɛdi leevu-inyɔ ku nina akpaklɔ.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh. Asher's Land
translation_verse: Na lɛma lɛmɛni ku nina akpaklɔ ndi kalɔ kani béti béte Sebulon kaba. Yosua Úle Kalɔ Kadi Úte Isakar Kaba

english_verse: Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following
translation_verse: Na lɛma lɛmɛni ku ana akpaklɔ na beti béte Isakar kaba. Yosua Úle Kalɔ Kadi Úte Aser Kaba

english_verse: then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel,
translation_verse: Na údeyi ɔ́kɛ ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ na úti úsie Bet-Dagon, na útédu Sebulon Kɔwɛ na Yiƒta-El na ɔkɛ katɔ kakɛ úsie Bet-Emek ku Neiel, na úti úsie Kubul

english_verse: Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon.
translation_verse: ku Ebron ku Rehob ku Hamon ku Kana úti útédu Sidon-bonwu kemmo.

english_verse: Then it turned west to become the northern border and went to Ramah and the fortress-city of Tyre. Near Tyre it turned toward Hosah and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. Asher had a total of
translation_verse: Kɔlɔ ku lɛma lɛmɛni ku ana akpaklɔ na béti béte Aser kaba. Yosua Úle Kalɔ Kadi Úte Naƒtali Kaba

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages, including Mahalab, Achzib, Acco, Aphek, and Rehob. Naphtali's Land
translation_verse: Na ɔmii ɔmmɔ útáwɔlɔ Tabor Kɔbi ku Sahasima ku Bet-Semes útédu Yordan Ketu. Na lɛma lɛmmɔ ƒui lɛdi leevu-ɛku ku ana akpaklɔ.

english_verse: The Naphtali clans received this region as their tribal land, and it included
translation_verse: Lɛma lɛmɛni ku nina akpaklɔ na béti béte Naƒtali kaba. Yosua Úle Kalɔ Kadi Úte Dan Kaba

english_verse: The Israelites were still gathered in Shiloh in front of the sacred tent, when Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the family leaders of Israel finished giving out the land to the tribes. The Lord had told the people to give Joshua whatever town he wanted. So Joshua chose Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and the people gave it to him. Joshua went to Timnath-Serah, rebuilt it, and lived there.
translation_verse: Egulabi na bátu béle kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ ƒui. Na Katɔti Ɔkpane Eleasar ku Yosua ɔni ndi Nun ubidi ku Israel batɔnkune bani nnye nte Israel kaba bekyuli néle kalɔ kammɔ na Silo na egulabi bɔtu kenye na beti béye Unwoti kasusu. Mmɔ na bátu Unwoti Adi Kevo ɔtɔ bálɛ kesii kani na bátu béte kaba kammɔ ƒui. Na ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ básia asa na bákana kalɔ kammɔ bule báwɔlɔ.

english_verse: These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
translation_verse: Lɛma lɛmɛni na bédie bése bete katamikukɔ béte Israelƒuɔ ku baƒɔ bani nkya-ma kudɔ. Ka si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́du ɔkpana ɔni na ɔɔɔgyi uuuse ni, ɔkana na ukeli utátamiku benengu bammɔ kalɛ na ukyuli ɔni na bádu mmɔ bekyuli baladu ukyuli ɔdune ɔmmɔ balasia uti utédu ka bátɛku-nwu litemi.

english_verse: One day the Lord told Joshua:
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Unwoti ɔ́su Yosua ɔnini,

english_verse: When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns.
translation_verse: “Kɔ lɛsa te Israelƒuɔ anii bedie lɛma lɛdi bese kalɛ na ukyuli ɔkana ukeli utatamiku na mmɔ aani kalɛ na lɛ́su Mose lɛ́vi.

english_verse: If a person accidentally kills someone and the victim's relatives say it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of the Safe Towns and be safe from the victim's relatives. The one needing protection will stand at the entrance to the town gate and explain to the town leaders what happened. Then the leaders will bring that person in and provide a place to live in their town.
translation_verse: “Na si uwi ɔni na ukyuli ɔdune ɔmmɔ úkeli úsie lɛma lɛmmɔ lɛdi biala kemmo ni, na uténye ɔma ɔmmɔ kabɛnye na udie lɛlɔ kalɔ ɔtina ɔma ɔmmɔ benengu. Na si údie kenye ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, na beti ukyuli ɔmmɔ beduoku ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na bete-nwu keliekɔ. Na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔsɔ ɔkya-ma kudɔ.

english_verse: One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies.
translation_verse: Na si bekyuli bani ukyuli na ɔ́du békeli basiaku ukyuli ɔdune ɔmmɔ ni, benengu bammɔ betedie ukyuli ɔmmɔ betete-ma. Ɔsika ukyuli ɔdune ɔmmɔ ɔɔɔgyi uuuse asa na ɔ́du ɔkpanadi ɔmmɔ. Na kadɔ kadi lɛnɔ keeebo-ma ntɛ asa na ɔ́du-nwu.

english_verse: The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder. Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔdune ɔmmɔ ɔlɛka ɔsɔ ɔkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo utédu ka batɛku-nwu litemi. Na si bátadu-nwu kɔtɔ ni, ɔsɔ ɔkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na Katɔti ɔkpane unengudi ɔni nkya uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo úkpi. Na ɔmmɔ kama ukyuli ɔdune ɔmmɔ ubo kuƒi ka ɔsɔ unwini usie nwuna ɔma na kesii kani na úkeli ɔ́si.”

english_verse: The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns: Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, lɛma lɛni bédie na Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ kanukɔ ndi Kedes na Naƒtali abi lɛlɔ na Galilea ku Sekem na Eƒram Kɔbi lɛlɔ ku Kiriat-Arba ɔni básɔ baalɔ bani Hebron na ɔkya Yuda abi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
translation_verse: Bédie lɛma bamba lɛnɔ bése na Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ katukɔ na Yeriko. Na ani ndi Beser ɔni nkya kalɔ kakwiidi kani nwi ƒiaa na ɔ́si Ruben kaba kemmo ku Ramot ɔni nkya Gilead na ɔ́si Gad kaba kemmo ku Golan ɔni nkya Basan na ɔ́si Manase kaba kemmo.

english_verse: Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu kalɛ na Unwoti úbo-ma ɔda mmɔ ɔsu ni, Israelƒuɔ béti lɛma ku kalɔ kani na livo lɛni na bebuo baakun lɛkya béte Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ.

english_verse: The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive. The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given
translation_verse: Na ka bátu egulabi bánu ni, Kohat kaduli bekyuli bani ndi Aaron bawɔ na badi Lewiƒuɔ lɛlɔ na ɔ́sia. Na béte-ma lɛma leevu-ɛtɛ básiku Yuda ku Simeon ku Benyamin kaba kemmo.

english_verse: The clans that were descendants of Merari received
translation_verse: Na Marari bawɔ bákɛ lɛma leevu-inyɔ lɛni nási Ruben ku Gad ku Sebulon kaba kemmo.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did. Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu kalɛ na Israelƒuɔ bátu egulabi bánu ni, lɛni kani na béle lɛma lɛmmɔ ku kalɔ kani na livo lɛni bebuo baakun lɛkya béte Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo-ma ɔda ɔkɛnku Mose lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
translation_verse: Na lɛma ku bebuo kɔdikɔ kɔlɔ kɔni na béte Aaron bawɔ ni, libo lɛma leevu-ɛtɛ.

english_verse: The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received
translation_verse: Na lɛma lɛni nási Gerson adua ammɔ kemmo libo leevu-ɛtɛ ku nina bebuo kɔdikɔ kɔlɔ.

english_verse: The people of the Levi tribe had a total of
translation_verse: Na ɔma ɔdi biala ubo bebuo kadikɔ kalɔ. Katɔti Ɔ́di Nwuna Litemi Lɛlɔ

english_verse: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Unwoti úti kɔlɔ kɔni ƒui na úse kenye ka weti wete Israelƒuɔ bati kuuku úte Israelƒuɔ na bételie-ka kemmo.

english_verse: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́ya na bákɛ atu bɔyɔ na kalɔ kammɔ ƒui kemmo aani kalɛ na ɔ́su bana bati kuuku úse. Na bana bekisine ƒui bátakana na bénye basiaku-ma. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔlati nékpo úte Israelƒuɔ.

english_verse: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_verse: Na linyese biala na Unwoti úse Israelƒuɔ ni, ɔ́di-ni lɛlɔ ƒui pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Yosua ɔ́lɔ Ruben ku Gad kaba ku Manase kaba kakɛ bekyuli ƒui ɔ́sala.

english_verse: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
translation_verse: Na litemi lɛmmɔ ndi ka bitenwini kama bitakya bina banwa Israelƒuɔ uwi ɔmɛni ƒui kemmo. Ɔƒɛni lɛnɔ bɛ́nu kaduɛ na bɛ́di bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔda ɔni úbo-mi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Na aani kalɛ na ɔ́su úse ni, bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na kaba kammɔ ƒui bákɛ atu bɔyɔ. Anwuɔsu bɛsɔ binwini na biteesie bitélie bina kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na bitélie kalɔ kani na Unwoti kabla ɔblane Mose úti úte-mii aani bina kadikɔ na Yordan ɔƒɛ katukɔ mmɔ.”

english_verse: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
translation_verse: Nsu Yosua ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Binyimo ɔda ɔni na Unwoti kabla ɔblane Mose úbo-mii. Na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ ndi ka bɛyɔ bina Unwoti Katɔti na bɛsia nwuna litemi anu kaduɛ, na bɛdi nwuna ɔda bubo lɛlɔ, na biti lɛlɔ bɛsia-nwu lɛlɔ, na biti bina kayi ku kɔyu ƒui bitaabla-nwu kabla.”

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
translation_verse: Na ka Israelƒuɔ bakladi bénu ka bekyuli badi bakya baasu banini, “Rubenƒuɔ ku Gadƒuɔ ku Manase kaba kakɛ bekyuli bátu lɛkpabi bonwu lɛdi bálɛ Kanaan ɔmii lɛlɔ na Yordan kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ na ɔvi ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ kalɔ” ni,

english_verse: But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Israelƒuɔ bátala Pinehas Katɔti Ɔkpane Eleasar ubidi ka uteesie Ruben ku Gad kaba ku Manase kaba kakɛ bekyuli bammɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
translation_verse: Na bédie ɔtɔ benengu leevu bani ntɔnku Israel kaba ka basiaku-nwu.

english_verse: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
translation_verse: Amu na bátásu Ruben ku Gad kaba ku Manase kaba kakɛ bekyuli banini,

english_verse: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
translation_verse: “Israelƒuɔ ƒui benye Unwoti lɛnyi kemmo beeye-mii lɛla lɛni ɔsu na bɛ́bla lɛla likpidi lɛmɛni udu biti bɛta binye Israelƒuɔ Katɔti lɛlɔ? Ɔsika ɔbladu ɔmmɔ ɔ́ta únye Unwoti lɛlɔ ɔkɛnku lɛkpabi lɛni na bɛ́tu bite lɛlɔ ɔsu! Dɛ na ɔ́bla asa na bínwini kama bɛ́kya-nwu?

english_verse: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
translation_verse: Binyimo lɛla lɛni nálɛku-bu na Peor ɔkɛnku likpidi lɛni bɔ́bla ɔsu. Unwoti ɔ́ya na ɔlɛ ukpidi ɔdi úbeduo-bu akɔ. Na úti úbedu ɔmwi kadi bɔɔmu bɔkya buubo abi ɔ́si ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ ɔsu. Na buuye-mii si ukpidi ɔmmɔ útemo-mii tɔ?

english_verse: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
translation_verse: Na buuye-mii bɔnii bɛɛyɔ́ ka bɛsɔ binwini kama bɛkya Unwoti kunyɔdi? “Na si bɛ́ta bínye Unwoti lɛlɔ ɔmwi kadi ni, ɔdubuti kɔnyi ɔkya Israelƒuɔ ƒui kɔnaadi.

english_verse: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu si kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na bilie kaaadia ka bɛkpa Unwoti ni, bɛta na bibo Unwoti kalɔ lɛlɔ na kesii kani na nwuna kakpakɔ kalɛ. Na bibelie-bu kudɔ. Na bitata bitenye Unwoti lɛlɔ na wabla aani si bula ƒui náta bunye-nwu lɛlɔ. Ɔkɛnku lɛkpabi lɛni na bɛ́tu bite lɛlɔ mɛni biti biibunku bula Unwoti Katɔti lɛkpabi.

english_verse: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
translation_verse: Na binyimo Serah ubidi Akan atu ɔkplu ani na ɔ́bla kalɛ na ɔ́bɛ úti ala ani na Unwoti ɔ́su-bu ka bɔyila-nya udu. Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́ya na Unwoti kɔnyi kúbo bula ƒui lɛlɔ ɔni na ɔɔɔdi Akan lɛti nékpi ina ka anwu lɛti nábla likpidi lɛmmɔ.”

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh answered:
translation_verse: Amu na Rubenƒuɔ ku Gadƒuɔ ku Manase kaba kakɛ bekyuli bamɛni básu Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune bamɛni banini,

english_verse: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
translation_verse: “Unwoti Katɔti ndi Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui. Na anwu ndi Unwoti, na ɔgyi lɛla lɛni ɔsu na bɔ́bla lɛla lɛmɛni. Na abu lɛnɔ bɔɔyɔ́ ka amii lɛnɔ bɛti lɛla lɛni ɔsu na bɔ́tu lɛkpabi lɛmɛni. Na si bɔtu na bɔ́tu-nwu ka buuti bɔta bunye Unwoti lɛlɔ iye ka bɔɔlɛ́-nwu kama ni, bibo kuƒi ka bɛdu-bu.

english_verse: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: “Ɔmɛni ɔsu na bɔ́tu lɛkpabi lɛmɛni. Na bútatu-ni ka buti butaabla bɔkyula akpala iye akpala adi.

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔkpane Pinehas ɔni ndi Eleasar ubidi ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔƒɛni na bɔ́nu bɔ́ti ka Unwoti ɔkya-bu akɔ. Na bítata bítenye Unwoti lɛlɔ, na ɔmɛni ɔsu bɛ́ƒɔ-bu bɛlɛku Unwoti kɔtu bɔni kemmo.”

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
translation_verse: Amu na Pinehas ku batɔnkune bakladi béye ulu básiku Ruben kaba ku Gad kaba bekyuli kudɔ na Gilead, na bénwini bésie Kanaan. Na bátásu Israelƒuɔ kalɛ na ala ƒui ávi.

english_verse: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
translation_verse: Na ka Israelƒuɔ bénu etemila ammɔ ni, kaƒɔ káyɔ-ma na bémwi Katɔti. Anwuɔsu básɔ bétesie bétetékpoku-ma na bɔyila-ma udu.

english_verse: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Rubenƒuɔ ku Gadƒuɔ básu banini, “Lɛkpabi lɛmɛni lɛdi likposela lite bula ƒui uti ɔtina ka Unwoti ndi Katɔti.” Anwuɔsu básia lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛnyi banii Likposela.

english_verse: The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age.
translation_verse: Ɔ́ɔƒɔ uwi geen ka Unwoti ɔ́ya na Israelƒuɔ bákɛ bɔnwuna básiku bana bekisine enu kemmo. Ɔƒɛni lɛnɔ Yosua ɔ́ɔbi lɛlɔ na nwuna akwa lɛnɔ éesie anumi geen.

english_verse: One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them: I am now very old.
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́lɔ Israelƒuɔ ƒui ku bana benengu ku batɔnkune ku litemi batɛne ƒui ɔ́sala na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔƒɛni lɛ́ɛbi na mina akwa lɛnɔ éesie anumi.

english_verse: You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land.
translation_verse: Na amii alati bɛ́nu lɛla lɛni na bina Unwoti Katɔti úti ɔ́bla kadi bamba bekyuli ɔ́si amii ɔsu. Na bina Unwoti Katɔti nékpo bina kekpo ƒui úte-mii.

english_verse: There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Na kɔlɔ kɔni nébu na bútekpo tɔ na bɔƒɔ-ku ni, bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔlati ɔdubo-ma bɔbɔku bɔlɛku kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na bise bitéti-ku aani kalɛ kani na bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su-mii úse.

english_verse: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu bɛkya ɔkplu na bɛnu kaduɛ na ɔdi biala ɔdi Mose ɔda bubo etemila ɔku ɔni úti úte-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ ƒui. Na bitada bitavia ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bitese kɔmii iye kɔdianu.

english_verse: Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods.
translation_verse: Biteti lɛlɔ bitasala ku kadi bamba bekyuli bani nkya mmɔ akɔ, na bitakpali bana baƒiɔ bani na baakpa anyi, na bitese kenye kadi na bana baƒiɔ bammɔ badi kudɔ na bitakpa-ma iye bitalɛ-ma akɔnkɔ kalɔ.

english_verse: Be as faithful to the Lord as you have always been.
translation_verse: Mmomu binye bina Unwoti Katɔti kama kpakplaa aani kalɛ bɛɛbla úti úbedu ɔƒɛni.

english_verse: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
translation_verse: “Ɔsika ɔ́si amii ɔsu ni, Unwoti ɔ́bɔku kadi bamba bekyuli bani mbo ɔlɔkplu. Na úti úbedu ɔmwi kadi ni, ukyuli ɔdi útakana na unye ɔsiaku-mii.

english_verse: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Bina kemmo ukyuli biala ɔkana na ɔya na bekisine apim unwi bekeli, ɔsika bina Unwoti Katɔti muukpó bina kekpo teete-mii aani kalɛ na ɔ́su úse.

english_verse: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu bɛnu kaduɛ geen na biti bɔyɔ bite bina Unwoti Katɔti.

english_verse: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
translation_verse: bise likpo ka bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔsɔ ɔɔɔdubo bukpoku kadi bamba bekyuli bani nébu mmɔ bute-mii lɛnɔ. Mmomu bina ɔbladu ɔmmɔ ɔdubunwini kakpagyuɛ ute-mii, na ɔlɛ ɔni bɛdubunu ɔdubɔbla aani kalɛ na beewi ukyuli kugyiimi iye aani kalɛ na alakpi eeduo ukyuli anumi uti utédu ka bina Unwoti ɔ́yila bina ƒui udu na kalɔ kabuni kani na úti úte-mii mɛni lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
translation_verse: “Na ɔƒɛni mina kukpi uwi úude. Na amii alati bɛgyi bɛsiku bina kɔyi ku kɔyu kemmo ka bina Unwoti Katɔti úte-mii ala abunidi ani ƒui na úse kenye ka wete-mii. Na kenye biala na úse-mii ni, ɔ́di-ka lɛlɔ na útada unwi pɛ útese.

english_verse: Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́lɔ Israel kaba bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ɔ́sala na Sekem. Na ɔ́lɔ kaba kammɔ benengu ku batɔnkune ku litemi batɛne ƒui bani nkya Israel na bébo na bébenye Katɔti anumi.

english_verse: Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su bekyuli bammɔ ka Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti ɔɔsu-ma ɔnini, “Uwi ɔdi nábavi ni, bina bati kuuku na nka bélie Euƒrate Ketu ɔvi na baƒiɔ na báakpa. Na bina bati kuuku bammɔ kemmo ɔdi ndi Tera ɔni náwɔ Abraham ku Nahor.

english_verse: But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants.
translation_verse: Amu na líti Abraham ɔni ndi bina bati kuuku unwi lɛ́lɛku mmɔ na lɛ́ya na úsie ɔ́vi Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui. Na líte-nwu bawɔ pii. Na lɛ́ya na Abraham ɔ́wɔ Isak.

english_verse: Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Isak lɛnɔ ɔ́wɔ Yakob ku Esua. Na líti kɔbi kalɔ kani nkya Seir líte Esau ka uti-ka ɔbla nwuna kadikɔ. Na Yakob ku nwuna bebi bésie bétélie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched. You lived in the desert for a long time,
translation_verse: Amu na bíwulo bɛ́kpali Unwoti ka ubo na ubebunku-mii. Amu na líti lɛdisa bonwu lɛ́kya amii ku Egyipteƒuɔ ntɛ. Na lɛ́ya na ɛpu ɔmmɔ ɔ́nyina-ma. Na ɔmɛni ƒui ɔ́lɛ na bina anumi kalɛ na lɛ́bla Egyipteƒuɔ bammɔ. Na bílie kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo uwi gyɔlɔɔ.

english_verse: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
translation_verse: “Amu na líti-mii líboku Amoriƒuɔ bani nlie Yordan Ketu ɔƒɛ katukɔ. Na báta bébekpoku-mii na líti-ma lɛ́kya bina enu kemmo na lɛ́yila-ma udu na bina anumi. Na bíti bana kalɔ bɛbla bina kadikɔ.

english_verse: King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you.
translation_verse: Amu na Moab Ɔga Sipor ɔni ndi Balak ubidi ɔ́ta na útékpoku Israelƒuɔ. Na ɔ́tala na bététiku Bileam ɔni ndi Beor ubidi ka ubewida-mii.

english_verse: But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
translation_verse: Nsu ntakpete lɛla lɛni na Bileam ɔ́su mmɔ. Mmomu kusɛ kusɛ na úte-mii. Anwuɔsu lɛ́da-mii lídie Balak enu kemmo.

english_verse: You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all.
translation_verse: “Ɔmmɔ kama ka bɛ́via Yordan Ketu bísie Yeriko ni, Yerikoƒuɔ báta na bébekpoku-mii. Lɛni kani na Amoriƒuɔ ku Perisiƒuɔ ku Kanaanƒuɔ ku Hetiƒuɔ ku Girgasiƒuɔ ku Hewiƒuɔ ku Yebusiƒuɔ lɛnɔ bébekpoku-mii. Nsu líti bana ƒui lɛ́kya-mii enu kemmo.

english_verse: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Na lɛ́kya-ma liƒu na bayia. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Amoriƒuɔ baga inyɔ bammɔ békeli ɔni na ɔɔɔdi bina ekpola nábla kabla kadi.

english_verse: You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
translation_verse: Líti Lɛma lɛni na ɔɔɔdi amii nada-ni lite-mii na bilie-ni kemmo. Na liti kɔlɔ ku mmo bɔni na ɔɔɔdi amii natuma-ni asa na bɛɛdi nwuna egyiibi na bɛɛkɛ́ nnɔ taasiku mmo bɔni na ɔɔɔdi amii nátuma-mu kemmo.”

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua úse anumi na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛyia Unwoti na bitaabla-nwu kabla ulu lɛlɔ. Na bɛda baƒiɔ bani na bina bati kuuku bákpa na ketu ɔvi ku Egyipte mmɔ bidie bina akɔ. Na bitaabla Unwoti kabla kani.

english_verse: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
translation_verse: Nsu si Unwoti kama bɔsiaku buláda-mii kubiti ni, amii bidie ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni anwu ɔni geen na bɛɛyɔ́ ka bɛsiaku. Si baƒiɔ bani na bina bati kuuku bákpa na Euƒrate Ketu ɔvi ngye iye Amoriƒuɔ kalɔ kani bilie mɛni baƒiɔ na bɛɛyɔ́ ni, bidie. Nsu ami ku mina kaduli bekyuli abu ni, Unwoti lɛti na bɔdubɔsiaku.”

english_verse: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui bédie kenye banini, “Kudii, bulálɛ Unwoti kama, na bulasiaku baƒiɔ badi kama.

english_verse: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
translation_verse: Ɔsika bula Unwoti Katɔti náda abu ku bula bati údie abi ani na bɔkya buubó na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ kemmo. Na abu ɔlati bɔ́nu akɔla budie lidu lidu lɛni na ɔ́bla, na ɔda-bu kɔkɔɔkɔ na bula ulu busie na kadi bamba akɔ.

english_verse: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti nábɔku Amoriƒuɔ bani ƒui nkya kɔlɔ kɔni lɛlɔ na bulie mɛni ƒui nédie. Anwuɔsu abu lɛnɔ bɔdubɔsiaku Unwoti. Ɔsika anwu lɛti ndi bula Katɔti.”

english_verse: Joshua said: The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it.
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ ɔnini, “Ngyi ka bilakana Unwoti bɔɔsiaku, ɔsika ɔdi Katɔti ɔni nse kedee na uukpó kogyulo na si bɛ́ta binye-nwu lɛlɔ ni, uleti bina ekpidi ulakyiɛ-mii.

english_verse: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
translation_verse: Na si bíni Unwoti na bitásiaku kadi bamba baƒiɔ ni, ɔdubɔya na ɔgbankpi ubo-mii lɛlɔ na ɔyila-mii udu ina ka ɔ́yɔ-mii litemi dii.”

english_verse: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ básu Yosua banini, “Kudii! Unwoti lɛti na bɔdubɔsiaku.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?” “Yes, it's true,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Yosua ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Amii alati bɛdi kenye bediene bite lɛlɔ ka amii náƒuna ka bɛdubɔsiaku Unwoti.” Amu na Israelƒuɔ básu banini, “Ɛɛn, bɔdi kenye bediene bute ɔmɛni.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Si ɔdi lɛni ni, na bibo baƒiɔ bani nkya-mii akɔ mmɔ bivaakun na biti bina kɔyi bɛsia Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ básu Yosua banini, “Unwoti ɔni ndi bula Katɔti lɛti bɔdubɔsiaku. Na bɔdubɔnu-nwu litemi.”

english_verse: Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu limeyi lɛmmɔ Yosua únyimiku Israelƒuɔ bammɔ na Sekem, na úte-ma ɔda bubo etemila ka badi-nya lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem
translation_verse: Na Yosua únweni etemila ammɔ ɔ́kya Katɔti ɔda bubo ɔku kemmo. Ɔmmɔ kama úti lɛtabi bonwu lɛdi úse mmɔ na kugyii kubendi kɔni nde Unwoti kakpakɔ kedee mmɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ɔnini, “Bɛnu lɛtabi lɛmɛni lɛdi bula ƒui kenye budie. Ɔsika únu etemila ani ƒui na Unwoti útemi úte-bu. Anwuɔsu ani ndubudie-mii kenye si bɛlɛ Katɔti kama.”

english_verse: Joshua sent everyone back to their homes. Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
translation_verse: Amu na Yosua ɔ́ya na ɔdi biala ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie nwuna kalɔ lɛlɔ. Yosua Ku Eleasar Békpi

english_verse: Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Ala amɛni kama ni, Unwoti kabla ɔblane Yosua ɔni ndi Nun ubidi úkpi. Na ɔ́kɛ akwa eti anyɔ ku leevu.

english_verse: The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Na báva-nwu na anwu ɔlati kalɔ na Timnat-Sera. Na Eƒraim abi lɛlɔ na kɔlɔ kɔni nkya kusie Gaas Kɔbi lɛlɔ na katɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Yosua úlie ngba ni, Israelƒuɔ básiaku Unwoti kama. Na nwuna kekpima lɛnɔ ni, ka bana batɔnkune bani nánu akɔla budie taatina lidu lidu lɛni Unwoti ɔ́bla úte Israelƒuɔ bamu belie ngba ɔsu ni, Israelƒuɔ básiaku Unwoti kani.

english_verse: When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for
translation_verse: Na Yoseƒ likubi lɛni béti básiku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, béti likubi lɛmmɔ bátava na Sekem kalɔ lɛlɔ. Kalɔ kammɔ na Yakob úye egulabi ɔƒualadi eti anyɔ ɔ́siku Hamor bebi unwi ɔni ndi Sekem Ɔti. Na kalɔ kammɔ na béti béte Yoseƒ kaba bekyuli.

english_verse: When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti Ɔkpane Eleasar ɔni ndi Aaron ubidi lɛnɔ úkpi na báva-nwu na Gibea na ɔma ɔni na béti béte ubidi Pinehas na Eƒraim abi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the Lord, “Which of our tribes should attack the Canaanites first?”
translation_verse: Na Yosua kekpima ni, Israelƒuɔ béye Unwoti banini, “Bula akɔ ɔmani nka Kanaanƒuɔ butékpoku?”

english_verse: “Judah!” the Lord answered. “I'll help them take the land.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Yuda kɔdua baka busie butékpoku-ma. Ɔsika líti kalɔ kammɔ lɛ́kya-ma enu kemmo.”

english_verse: The people of Judah went to their relatives, the Simeon tribe, and said, “Canaanites live in the land God gave us. Help us fight them, and we will help you.” Troops from Simeon came to help Judah.
translation_verse: Amu na Yuda kɔdua bekyuli bammɔ básu Simeon kɔdua bekyuli banini, “Bibo na bibebunku-bu na butékpoku Kanaanƒuɔ, na bɔƒɔ kalɔ kani béti béte-bu. Abu lɛnɔ bɔdubo na bubenku-mii, na bukpo bɔƒɔ kalɔ kani na béti béte-mii.” Anwuɔsu Simeon kɔdua bekyuli básiaku-ma.

english_verse: After that, they attacked the Canaanites who lived at Hebron, defeating the three clans called Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. At that time, Hebron was called Kiriath-Arba.
translation_verse: Na bésie anumi bétékpoku Kanaanƒuɔ bani nlie Hebron, kesii kani na bátaalɔ banii Kiriat-Arba, na básɔ bésie bétékpoku Sesai ku Ahiman ku Talmai kadi bekyuli, na bádi-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The king tried to escape, but soldiers from Judah caught him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes,
translation_verse: Adoni-Besek úkeli, nsu bábi básiaku-nwu na békulo-nwu lɛgba ku enu animigya ƒui.

english_verse: They attacked Jerusalem, captured it, killed everyone who lived there, and then burned it to the ground.
translation_verse: Amu na Yuda kɔdua bekyuli báta na bétékpoku Yerusalemƒuɔ, na béƒie-nwu báƒɔ. Na bádu-ma ƒui ku kuwii, na bátu ogya bakya ɔma ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Judah's army fought the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Southern Desert, and the foothills to the west.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama básɔ bésie bétékpoku Kanaanƒuɔ bani nlie abi lɛlɔ ku bani nlie abi kalɔ ku bani nlie ketele kalɔ kakwiidi lɛlɔ na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ.

english_verse: From Hebron, Judah's army went to attack Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Ka bási mmɔ ni, bésie bétékpoku Debir, kesii kani na bátaalɔ banii Kiriat-Seƒer.

english_verse: Caleb told his troops, “The man who captures Kiriath-Sepher can marry my daughter Achsah.”
translation_verse: Na bekpone bammɔ kemmo unwi ɔni baalɔ banii Kaleb ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ukyuli ɔni ndubɔkana na ukpo ɔdi Kiriat-Seƒerƒuɔ lɛlɔ ni, ndubuti Aksa, mina ubi ulekubi, lite-nwu na uti.”

english_verse: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, so Caleb let him marry Achsah. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Amu na Kaleb ɔmmɔ kani ɔnwani ɔnamudi ɔni baalɔ Kena ubidi Otiel úsie útékpoku Debir ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni bekyuli na ɔ́di-ma lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu Kaleb úti ubidi Aksa ɔmmɔ úte-nwu na úti.

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, uwi ɔni na ulekubi ɔmɛni úubo uli Otiel kudɔ ni, Otiel ɔ́su ulekudi ɔnii ɔsu ɔti Kaleb na ute-nwu nwuna kemo kadi. Amu na ulekubi ɔmɛni úti ɔpɔnkɔ na úsie ɔti kudɔ. Na ɔni kani na ɔ́yu ɔpɔnkɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ úbenye kalɔ ni, mmɔ kani na ɔti úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi na aawia ka lɛbla lite-ɔ?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so please give me some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds named Higher Pond and Lower Pond.
translation_verse: Amu na ulekubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Mɔɔyɔ́ ka abla-mi lɛƒɔndia sɛsɛɛ lɛdi na ete-mi abiɔ adi. Ɔsika kalɔ kani na éte-mi mmɔ kadi kalɔ kakwiidi.” Anwuɔsu Kaleb úte-nwu abiɔ anyɔ adi na kalɔ kammɔ katɔ ku kada kakɛ.

english_verse: The people who belonged to the Kenite clan were the descendants of the father-in-law of Moses. They left Jericho with the people of Judah and settled near Arad in the Southern Desert of Judah not far from the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Amu na Mose ɔgyanti kaba bekyuli bani ndi Keniƒuɔ ku Yudaƒuɔ banana náta bási kesii kani baalɔ banii ebo ɔma unengudi na Yeriko, na bésie bétélieku bekyuli bani nli Yuda kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo akɔ na kesii kani nde Arad ɔma.

english_verse: Judah's army helped Simeon's army attack the Canaanites who lived at Zephath. They completely destroyed the town and renamed it Hormah.
translation_verse: Yuda ku Simeon kɔdua bekyuli básala lɛlɔ na bétékpoku Kanaanƒuɔ bani nlie Seƒat. Na bádu bekyuli bammɔ na báyila ɔma ɔmmɔ udu. Na básia ɔma ɔmmɔ lɛnyi banii Horma.

english_verse: The Lord helped the army of Judah capture Gaza, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the land near those towns. They also took the hill country. But the people who lived in the valleys had iron chariots, so Judah was not able to make them leave or to take their land.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti únye ku Yuda kɔdua bekyuli na békpo béti kɔlɔ kɔni nkya abi lɛlɔ mmɔ. Nsu bátakana na babɔku bekyuli bani nlie ɔkwalɛ ɔmmɔ kemmo, ɔsika bebo bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ɔni ndi abuala sɔɔn.

english_verse: The tribe of Judah gave the town of Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had told them to do. Caleb defeated the three Anakim clans and took over the town. The Benjamin Tribe Does Not Capture Jerusalem
translation_verse: Béti Hebron kalɔ béte Kaleb aani kalɛ na Mose úbo-ma ɔda úse, ɔsika Kaleb ɔmmɔ nékpoku Anak bebi ɛtɛ kaba bekyuli bani nélie mmɔ na ɔ́bɔku-ma ɔ́lɛku mmɔ.

english_verse: The Jebusites were living in Jerusalem, and the Benjamin tribe did not defeat them or capture the town. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Benjamin. The Ephraim and Manasseh Tribes Capture Bethel
translation_verse: Nsu Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli ama bátakana Yebusiƒuɔ bɔbɔku bɔlɛku Yerusalem mmɔ, anwuɔsu ama ku Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli bamu belie mmɔ úbedu ɔmwi kadi.

english_verse: The Ephraim and Manasseh tribes were getting ready to attack Bethel, which at that time was called Luz. And the Lord helped them when they sent spies to find out as much as they could about Bethel.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bátala batu badi ka besie batásia Betel ɔni na bátaalɔ banii Lus mɛni anu kaduɛ ni,

english_verse: While the spies were watching the town, a man came out, and they told him, “If you show us how our army can get into the town, we will make sure that you aren't harmed.”
translation_verse: batu bammɔ bánu ɔnana ɔdi ka ɔ́si ɔɔlɛ́ ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na básu-nwu banini, “Tina-bu kesii kani na bɔsia buduo ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo, na bɔdubɔda-a kaduɛ na ukpidi ɔdi ulálɛku-ɔ.”

english_verse: The man showed them, and the two Israelite tribes attacked Bethel, killing everyone except the man and his family. The two tribes made the man and his family leave,
