translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔ́tina-ma ulu, na Eƒraim ku Manase kɔdua bekyuli bádu ukyuli biala nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo. Nsu bátadu ɔnana ɔmmɔ ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli.

english_verse: so they went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town. He named the town Luz, and that is still its name. Israel Does Not Get Rid of All the Canaanites
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́ta na útélie Hetiƒuɔ kudɔ na ɔ́da ɔma unengudi ɔdi, na ɔ́sia-nwu lɛnyi ɔnii Lus. Na Lus ɔma ɔmɛni ɔmu ɔkya úbedu ɔmwi kadi.

english_verse: The Ephraim tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived there with Israelites all around them.
translation_verse: Na lɛni kani na Eƒraim kɔdua bekyuli lɛnɔ bátabɔku Kanaanƒuɔ bani nlie Geser bétedie. Anwuɔsu ama ku Kanaanƒuɔ bammɔ bamu belie ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The Zebulun tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Kitron and Nahalol, and the Canaanites stayed there with Israelites around them. But the people of Zebulun did force the Canaanites into slave labor.
translation_verse: Na Sebulon kɔdua bekyuli bátabɔku bekyuli bani nlie Kitron ku Nahalo lɛma kemmo bétedie, nsu bénye-ma lɛlɔ na baabla kabla teete-ma ina ka ama ku-ma bamu beli.

english_verse: The Naphtali tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, but they did force the Canaanites into slave labor. The Naphtali tribe lived with Canaanites around them.
translation_verse: Naƒtali kɔdua bekyuli bátabɔku bekyuli bani nlie Bet-Semes ku Bet-Anat lɛma kemmo bétedie. Mmomu ama ku-ma bélie básala, nsu bénye-ma lɛlɔ na baabla kabla teete-ma.

english_verse: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.
translation_verse: Amoriƒuɔ bábɔku Dan kɔdua bekyuli bákɔliku abi lɛlɔ na bétete-ma kuƒi na bayu bebelie ɔkwalɛ kemmo.

english_verse: The Amorites on Mount Heres and in Aijalon and Shaalbim were also determined to stay. Later on, as Ephraim and Manasseh grew more powerful, they forced those Amorites into slave labor. The Amorite-Edomite Border
translation_verse: Amoriƒuɔ báƒɔ lɛlɔ bákya Ayalon ku Saalbim ku Heres abi lɛlɔ. Nsu ka Eƒraim ku Manase kɔdua bekyuli bábakɛ ɔyikun ni, bénye-ma lɛlɔ na Amoriƒuɔ bamɛni baabla-ma kabla.

english_verse: The old Amorite-Edomite border used to go from Sela through Scorpion Pass into the hill country.
translation_verse: Amoriƒuɔ ɔmii ɔ́si Akrabim úti ɔ́kɔ úsie Sela ku nwuna kama kakɛ.

english_verse: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Unwoti ɔtu ɔdi ɔ́si Gilgal úsie Bokim, na ɔ́kɔ lɛsa úte Israelƒuɔ ɔnini, “Lídie-mii lɛ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ, na líti-mii lísienku kalɔ kani líse kenye ka meti mete bina bati kuuku lɛlɔ. Na lɛ́su ka lɛɛɛdubo bɔlɛ bunyimi bɔni na línyimiku-mii mmɔ kama.

english_verse: and you promised not to make any peace treaties with the other nations that live in the land. Besides that, you agreed to tear down the altars where they sacrifice to their idols. Why haven't you kept your promise?
translation_verse: Na lɛ́su-mii ka ɔdi biala utenyimi lɛla lɛdi ku bekyuli bani nlie kalɔ kammɔ kemmo. Na bibo bana akpabi ƒui bɛƒɛ biwi kalɔ. Nsu bítadi mina litemi lɛlɔ. Na muuye-mii nnii bi ɔsu bɛ́bla lɛni?

english_verse: And so, I'll stop helping you defeat your enemies. Instead, they will be there to trap you into worshiping their idols.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu mɔɔsu-mii nnii lɛɛɛdubo bekyuli bamɛni bɔbɔku bute-mii ɔni na bíti bísela anumi mɛni. Na bekyuli bammɔ badubo bunwini liyu bete-mii na bataatu-mii lɛƒɛnyi. Na bana baƒiɔ badubo bunwini kɔkpagyuɛ kuteedie-mii.”

english_verse: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na baalɔ mmɔ banii Bokim na nwuna kalɔ ndi Buwulo. Mmɔ na bábla akpala béte Unwoti. Israelƒuɔ Bábla Atuɔkplu Na Bádi-ma Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Na báva-nwu na nwuna kalɔ kemmo na Timnat-Heres kesii kani ndi nwuna kadikɔ kani nédu-nwu na Eƒraim Kɔbi lɛlɔ kesii kani néti késie Gaas Kɔbi ɔƒɛnyi na katɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔdi kama ni, kaba kammɔ bekyuli ƒui békpi na bása bɔtɔlɔ busie bana bati kudɔ. Na kaba kabambadi nási bákɔ ɔni na ama baaagyi Unwoti, na bátanu ala ani lɛnɔ na ɔ́bla úte Israel úbavi.

english_verse: From time to time, the Lord would choose special leaders known as judges. These judges would lead the Israelites into battle and defeat the enemies that made raids on them.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́ya na litemi batɛne bákɔ bálɛ-ma akɔ, na báƒɔ-ma bálɛku bana bekisine enu kemmo.

english_verse: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmɛni kama ƒui belenu litemi batɛne bamɛni litemi. Na béti lɛlɔ bénwini bayalɛ, na bakɛ basiaku baƒiɔ lidu kama baakpá-ma. Kaba kamɛni bekyuli ama bávumana ƒui kede kede, na beeese aani bana bati, na baaasiaku bana ɔbladu kama, na bétenu litemi na bataadi Unwoti ɔda bubo lɛlɔ.

english_verse: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
translation_verse: Uwi biala na Unwoti ɔ́ya na litemi ɔtɛne ɔdi ɔ́kɔ ɔ́lɛ Israelƒuɔ akɔ ni, uunye litemi ɔtɛne ɔmmɔ kama nwuna ngba kemmo ƒui, na uukpó taaƒɔ-ma taalɛku bana bekisine enu kemmo. Na Unwoti ɔɔnu-ma kɔnyana si beedumo na ɔgbankpi ɔni kemmo na bana bekisine béti-ma bákya ɔsu.

english_verse: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
translation_verse: Nsu si litemi ɔtɛne ɔmmɔ ɔ́nya úkpi ni, na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui beenwíni teesie bana ɔbladu ukpidi ɔni ntulo bana bati ɔdi ɔni bátaabla kemmo. Na baasiaku baƒiɔ kama na baakpá-ma na baabla-ma kabla. Na beení ka bedie bana ɔbladu buɛ ku atuɔkplu atu.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu úti kɔnyi geen ɔ́kya Israelƒuɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ka kaba kamɛni báta bénye-mi lɛlɔ na baládi mina lɛla lɛni na línyimi líte bana bati kuuku lɛlɔ na belenu-mi litemi ɔsu ni,

english_verse: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
translation_verse: nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo kadi bamba bekyuli bani nébu asa-na Yosua úkpi bɔbɔku bute-ma lɛnɔ.

english_verse: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: Na ndubuti kadi bekyuli bammɔ lɛkɔku Israelƒuɔ lɛnu si badubo bɔvumana kayi na basia ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na bana bati kuuku básia.”

english_verse: That's why the Lord had not let Joshua get rid of those enemy nations all at once.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Unwoti ɔ́ya na kadi bamba bekyuli bammɔ básɔ bakya kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ, na útabɔku-ma kɔnakunwi na ɔnyonu-ma ɔkya Israelƒuɔ enu kemmo aani kalɛ na ɔ́su Yosua úse ka wabla.

english_verse: the Philistines and their five rulers, as well as the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that lived in the Lebanon Mountains from Mount Baal-Hermon to Hamath Pass.
translation_verse: Na bani nébu kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ kemmo ndi Ƒilistiƒuɔ baga ɛlɔ ku Kanaanƒuɔ ku Sidonƒuɔ ku Hewiƒuɔ bani nlie Lebanon abi lɛlɔ úti ɔ́si Baal-Hermon Kɔbi lɛlɔ útédu Lebo Hamat.

english_verse: Moses had told the Israelites what the Lord had commanded them to do, and now the Lord was using these nations to find out if Israel would obey.
translation_verse: Ama na báda bése Israelƒuɔ na beti-ma bakɔku banu si badubɔdi Unwoti ɔda bubo bɔni úte bana bati kuuku ɔkɛnku Mose lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But they refused. And some of them even married Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who lived all around them. That's how they started worshiping foreign gods. Othniel
translation_verse: Na kadi bekyuli bamɛni ku Israelƒuɔ beeti lɛlɔ, na Israelƒuɔ baakpá bana baƒiɔ. Otniel Nékpo Ɔ́ƒɔ Israelƒuɔ

english_verse: The Israelites sinned against the Lord by forgetting him and worshiping idols of Baal and Astarte.
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ bábla likpidi na Unwoti anumi. Na ɔkɛnku ɔmɛni ɔsu báyiƒala bana Unwoti Katɔti, na bénwini bátákpa Baal ku Asera baƒiɔ.

english_verse: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
translation_verse: Ɔ́si kalɛ na Unwoti úti kɔnyi kati kati ɔ́kya Israelƒuɔ ɔsu ni, Unwoti ɔ́nyonu-ma ɔ́kya Ɔga Kusan Risataim enu kemmo. Na Israelƒuɔ bénwini kabla bablane béte nwuna bekyuli na Naharaim Aram kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ akwa maane.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Nsu ka Israelƒuɔ béwulo bákpali Unwoti ni, Unwoti úte-ma udiene ɔdi, na anwu ndi Otniel, Kaleb ɔnwani ɔnamudi ubidi Kenas. Na anwu nékpo ɔ́ƒɔ-ma.

english_verse: Once more the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let them be defeated by King Eglon of Moab,
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ básɔ bábla likpidi na Unwoti anumi. Na ɔ́si likpidi lɛni bábla mɛni ɔsu ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na Moab ɔga ɔni baalɔ banii Eglon ɔ́kɛ ɔyikun na Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: who had joined forces with the Ammonites and the Amalekites to attack Israel. Eglon and his army captured Jericho.
translation_verse: Na Eglon ɔmɛni ɔ́ya na Amoriƒuɔ ku Amalekƒuɔ bébebunku na bétékpoku Israelƒuɔ. Na bádi Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ na béti bana ɔma unengudi Yeriko ɔni baalɔ banii Ebo Ɔma.

english_verse: Ehud and some other Israelites took the taxes to Eglon, who was a very fat man. As soon as they gave the taxes to Eglon, Ehud said it was time to go home.
translation_verse: Ka Ehud úti etela ammɔ úte ɔga ɔmɛni ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔ́su banana bani nti etela ammɔ ka benwini na beteesie ɔma.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and the Lord chose Ehud from the Benjamin tribe to rescue them. They put Ehud in charge of taking the taxes to King Eglon, but before Ehud went, he made a double-edged dagger. Ehud was left-handed, so he strapped the dagger to his right thigh, where it was hidden under his robes.
translation_verse: Na Ehud ɔmɛni ɔ́bla kewii kani bádɔ-ka lɛƒɛnyi inyɔ úte lɛlɔ, na kewii kammɔ bune bɔbla aani lɛgba bɔka unwi ku kakɛ. Na úbo kewii kammɔ ɔ́da nwuna kɔdianu kavobi kakɛ, na ɔ́kya awu ɔ́sia-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Ehud went with the other Israelites as far as the statues at Gilgal. Then he turned back and went upstairs to the room where Eglon had his throne. Ehud said, “Your Majesty, I need to talk with you in private.” Eglon replied, “Don't say anything yet!” His officials left the room, and Eglon stood up as Ehud came closer. “Yes,” Ehud said, “I have a message for you from God!”
translation_verse: Amu na Ehud ɔ́ni úde-nwu na nwuna lɛsa ɔtɔ eli, na kesii kani na anwu lɛti uulie taaƒɔ ɔƒɛƒɛɛ. Mmɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Mbo litemi lɛdi lɛ́siku Katɔti kudɔ ka lɛsu-ɔ.” Amu ka ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́nya ɔ́ta nwuna liboku lɛlɔ kani na

english_verse: Ehud pulled out the dagger with his left hand and shoved it so far into Eglon's stomach
translation_verse: Ehud úti nwuna kɔmii na ɔ́ni nwuna kewii kani nƒa nwuna kavobi mmɔ ɔ́kpa na ɔ́tu ɔga ɔmmɔ kaƒɔ.

english_verse: and left. When the king's officials came back and saw that the doors were locked, they said, “The king is probably inside relieving himself.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na ɔ́tɔlɔ kama ƒui ni, ɔga ɔmmɔ kabla bablane bébo, na bánu ka bábala ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ bényene. Na básu banini, “Ɔƒɛni kalɛ kuvodɔ na ɔga úsie na katɔma ƒui.”

english_verse: They stood there waiting until they felt foolish, but Eglon still didn't open the doors. Finally, they unlocked the doors and found King Eglon lying dead on the floor.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bénye bágya-nwu uwi ɔdi ka nka ɔdubɔlɛmi na ɔlɛ, nsu bétenu lɛla lɛdi. Mmɔ na beti ɔlɛmidi na bálɛmi ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ. Na bánu ka ɔga ɔmmɔ úkpi ɔtɛ kalɔ.

english_verse: But by that time, Ehud had already escaped past the statues. Ehud went to the town of Seirah
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni kemmo na kabla bablane bammɔ benye bagya ɔga mmɔ ni, Ehud úukeli ɔ́tɔlɔ na ɔkɛ baƒiɔ bammɔ kudɔ úsie Seira ɔma.

english_verse: in the hill country of Ephraim and started blowing a trumpet as a signal to call the Israelites together. When they came, he shouted, “Follow me! The Lord will help us defeat the Moabites.” The Israelites followed Ehud down to the Jordan valley, and they captured the places where people cross the river on the way to Moab. They would not let anyone go across,
translation_verse: Amu na údie lɛdi na úbo-ma ɔda ɔnini, “Bɛsiaku-mi kama, ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́ya na bɛ́di Moabƒuɔ bani ndi bina bekisine lɛlɔ.” Anwuɔsu Israelƒuɔ bammɔ lɛnɔ básiaku-nwu kama na báyu abi na béténye báda Yordan Ketu kesii kani baavia teesie Moab, na bétete kuƒi ka Moabni ɔdi biala ɔvia mmɔ.

english_verse: and before the fighting was over, they killed about
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛmmɔ Israelƒuɔ bádu Moabƒuɔ bekpone bani ngyi bukpo geen mpim leevu (

english_verse: Moabite warriors—not one escaped alive.
translation_verse: ), na ɔdi útakana bukeli.

english_verse: Moab was so badly defeated that it was a long time before they were strong enough to attack Israel again. And Israel was at peace for
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛmmɔ Israelƒuɔ bádi Moabƒuɔ lɛlɔ, na Israelƒuɔ bákɛ atubɔyɔ akwa liti ku avlaatɛ. Samgar Únwini Litemi Ɔtɛne

english_verse: Shamgar the son of Anath was the next to rescue Israel. In one battle, he used a sharp wooden pole to kill
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Israelƒuɔ básɔ bákɛ litemi ɔtɛne bamba. Na anwu ndi Samgar na ɔti ndi Anat, na anwu lɛnɔ úkpo ɔ́ƒɔ Israelƒuɔ. Na úti ugyii ɔdadi ɔ́du Ƒilistiƒuɔ nkyuli eti leevu-anyɔ (

english_verse: After the death of Ehud, the Israelites again started disobeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Ehud kekpima ni, Israelƒuɔ básɔ bábla likpidi na Unwoti anumi.

english_verse: So the Lord let the Canaanite King Jabin of Hazor conquer Israel. Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, lived in Harosheth-Ha-Goiim.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Unwoti ɔ́nyonu-ma ɔ́kya Kanaanƒuɔ Ɔga Yabin ɔni mɔɔdi lɛga na Hasor enu kemmo. Na Yabin bekpone ɔtɔnkune baalɔ banii Sisera na úlie Haroset-Hagoyim.

english_verse: iron chariots ready. Then he led his army away from Harosheth-Ha-Goiim to the Kishon River.
translation_verse: ) lɛni ndi abuala sɔɔn. Na ɔ́kɛ ɔyikun na ɔ́bla Israelƒuɔ likyulikpi ala akwa aavlanyɔ sɔɔn. Ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Israelƒuɔ béwulo bákpali Unwoti ka ubebunku-ma.

english_verse: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” Sisera told her. “If someone comes by and asks if anyone is inside, tell them ‘No.’ ”
translation_verse: Amu na Sisera ɔ́su Yael ɔnini, “Sɔ nye kayaku kenye mmɔ, na si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́si ɔɔví na úye-ɔ ɔnii ukyuli ɔdi úduo-ɔ kudɔ mɛni ni, na asu-nwu ka oowo.”

english_verse: Deborah the wife of Lappidoth was a prophet and a leader of Israel during those days.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Debora ɔni ndi Unwoti Kenye Udiene na ɔdi Lapidot ulekudi ni, anwu mɔɔtɛ Israelƒuɔ etemila.

english_verse: She would sit under Deborah's Palm Tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites would come and ask her to settle their legal cases.
translation_verse: Na Debora úse litemi katɛkɔ kadi úse kubo kɔdi kalɔ kesii kani na baalɔ Debora Kubo. Na mmɔ kakya Rama ku Betel lɛma ntɛ na Eƒraim abi kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na Israelƒuɔ beesié-nwu kadɔ na ɔɔtɛ bana etemila.

english_verse: One day, Barak the son of Abinoam was in Kedesh in Naphtali, and Deborah sent word for him to come and talk with her. When he arrived, she said: I have a message for you from the Lord God of Israel! You are to get together an army of
translation_verse: Amu na limeyi lɛdi ni, Debora ɔ́tala na bátálɔ Barak ɔni ndi Abinoam ubidi na uli Kades-Naƒtali béte-nwu. Ka úbo ni, ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti ɔɔsu-ɔ ɔnini, ‘Ti bekpone mpim leevu (

english_verse: The Lord will trick Sisera into coming out to fight you at the Kishon River. Sisera will be leading King Jabin's army as usual, and they will have their chariots, but the Lord has promised to help you defeat them.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ndubɔya na Sisera ɔni ndi Yabin bekpone ɔtɔnkune ubekpoku-mii na Kison Ketu kenye. Ɔdubuti nwuna bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ku nwuna bekpone uboku, na ndubɔya na adi-ma lɛlɔ.’ ”

english_verse: “I'm not going unless you go!” Barak told her.
translation_verse: Amu na Barak ɔ́su Debora ɔnini, “Ndubusie si adubɔsiaku-mi. Nsu si elésie ni, ami lɛnɔ lɛɛɛdubo busie.”

english_verse: “All right, I'll go!” she replied. “But I'm warning you that the Lord is going to let a woman defeat Sisera, and no one will honor you for winning the battle.” Deborah and Barak left for Kedesh,
translation_verse: Amu na Debora ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔdia, ami ku-ɔ bɔdubusie. Nsu mɔɔyá-a na ati ka kalɛ na enye aabla mɛni ɔsu ni, aaadubo lɛnyi lɛmmɔ bɔƒɔ. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubo Sisera bɔnyonu bɔkya uleku enu kemmo.” Anwuɔsu Debora ku Barak bátɔlɔ bésie Kades.

english_verse: At this time, Heber of the Kenite clan was living near the village of Oak in Zaanannim, not far from Kedesh. The Kenites were descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, but Heber had moved and had set up his tents away from the rest of the clan.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Heber ɔni nási Keni útáda nwuna keliekɔ na Kedes na kugyii kubendi kɔdi kudɔ na Saananim. Na ɔ́mami lɛlɔ ɔ́lɛku Keniƒuɔ bakladi kudɔ. Na bekyuli bammɔ badi Mose ulekudi ɔnwani ɔnanabi kaba bekyuli.

english_verse: When Sisera learned that Barak had led an army to Mount Tabor,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni básu Sisera ka Barak ɔni ndi Abinoam ubidi ɔ́kɔ úsie Tabor Kɔbi eli ni,

english_verse: Deborah shouted, “Barak, it's time to attack Sisera! Because today the Lord is going to help you defeat him. In fact, the Lord has already gone on ahead to fight for you.” Barak led his
translation_verse: Amu na Debora ɔ́su Barak ɔnini, “Yu teesie! Ɔsika ɔmwi kadi Unwoti úti Sisera ɔ́kya-a enu kemmo.” Anwuɔsu Barak úti nwuna bekpone mpim leevu ɔ́siku Tabor Kɔbi mmɔ.

english_verse: And during the battle, the Lord confused Sisera, his chariot drivers, and his whole army. Everyone was so afraid of Barak and his army, that even Sisera jumped down from his chariot and tried to escape.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Barak ku nwuna bekpone bese kalɔ beekpóku-ma ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na Sisera bekpone ku nwuna bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ bekpone béƒu. Na ɔmɛni ɔ́ya na Sisera ɔ́yu nwuna ɔpɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ lɛlɔ na úti lɛgba na úkeli.

english_verse: Barak's forces went after Sisera's chariots and army as far as Harosheth-Ha-Goiim. Sisera's entire army was wiped out.
translation_verse: Na Barak ɔ́bi ɔ́siaku Sisera bekpone ku bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ kama útédu Haroset-Hagoyim. Na bádu Sisera bekpone ƒui ɔni ina unwi muedi útebu.

english_verse: Only Sisera escaped. He ran to Heber's camp, because Heber and his family had a peace treaty with the king of Hazor. Sisera went to the tent that belonged to Jael, Heber's wife.
translation_verse: Amu na Sisera úti lɛgba na úkeli útéduo Heber ɔni nási Keni ulekudi Yael adi kevo kemmo. Ɔsika atubɔyɔ bɔkya Hasorƒuɔ Ɔga Yabin ku Heber kaduli bekyuli ntɛ.

english_verse: She came out to greet him and said, “Come in, sir! Please come on in. Don't be afraid.” After they had gone inside, Sisera lay down, and Jael covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Amu na Yael ɔ́lɛ keyi na útásiaku Sisera na ɔ́su-nwu ɔ́nini, “Mina ati, bo, na ebeduo ɔtɔ kemmo. Taya na liƒu lɛda-a.” Anwuɔsu Sisera lɛnɔ úbeduo ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo, na Yael úti ala úbi-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: “Could I have a little water?” he asked. “I'm thirsty.” Jael opened a leather bottle and poured him some milk, then she covered him back up.
translation_verse: Amu na Sisera ɔ́su Yael ɔnini, “Buvele nda-a, te-mi ntu bɔdi na lɛni.” Amu na Yael úti ntu koƒo kɔni na anyintu buwi-nwu kemmo úte-nwu na ɔ́ni. Na ɔ́sɔku ala úbi-nwu.

english_verse: Sisera was exhausted and soon fell fast asleep. Jael took a hammer and drove a tent-peg through his head into the ground, and he died.
translation_verse: Nsu Sisera lɛlɔ líitu-nwu, ɔmɛni ɔsu úduo lɛlɛɛ kemmo úsie ɔgyu. Amu na Yael ɔni ndi Heber ulekudi útéti kevo liwele ku lɛtabi na úsie kesii kani na Sisera ɔtɛ ɔlɛɛ mmɔ na úbo liwele lɛmmɔ ɔ́lɛ-nwu lɛtukpo ɔ́kana-nwu ɔ́mana kalɔ, na Sisera úkpi.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Barak had been following Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “The man you're looking for is inside,” she said. “Come in and I'll show him to you.” They went inside, and there was Sisera—dead and stretched out with a tent-peg through his skull.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Barak ɔkɛ ɔɔví taawia Sisera ni, Yael ɔ́lɛ útásiaku-nwu na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Bo, na lɛtina-a ukyuli ɔni na ákɛ aaví taawia mmɔ.” Ɔmɛni ɔsu Yael ku Barak básiaku lɛlɔ bétéduo ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo na bátánu ka kevo liwele lɛlɛ Sisera lɛtukpo lɛ́da kalɔ, na úkpi ɔtɛ.

english_verse: That same day God defeated the Canaanite King Jabin while the Israelites looked on, and his army was no longer powerful enough to attack the Israelites.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛmmɔ Katɔti ɔ́ya na Israelƒuɔ bádi Yabin ɔni ndi Kanaanƒuɔ ɔga lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Jabin grew weaker while the Israelites kept growing stronger, until at last the Israelites destroyed him.
translation_verse: Na bánya Kanaanƒuɔ ɔga ɔmɛni bámana kpakplaa útédu ka báyila-nwu udu.

english_verse: After the battle was over that day, Deborah and Barak sang this song:
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛmmɔ ni, Debora ku Abinoam ubidi ɔni baalɔ banii Barak bátu kɔgya kɔmɛni.

english_verse: We praise you, Lord! Our soldiers volunteered, ready to follow you.
translation_verse: “Israel bagadine bammɔ bágyu bátɔ, na bekyuli bammɔ lɛnɔ bénu kalɔ béti lɛlɔ bákpa na básiaku-ma. Anwuɔsu bɛya na bumwi Unwoti!

english_verse: Listen, kings and rulers, while I sing for the Lord, the God of Israel.
translation_verse: “Amii baga, binu! Amii lɛlɔ badine bise atu. Ndubo ɔnu budie lɛtu kɔgya limwi Unwoti, Israel Katɔti.

english_verse: Our Lord, God of Israel, when you came from Seir, where the Edomites live,
translation_verse: “O Unwoti, uwi ɔni na álɛ Seir kalɔ lɛlɔ na ésie ávi Edom kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, kalɔ kákunku na kayaa kénwini na ulɔyɔ únwini ɔnantu ɔ́na.

english_verse: rain poured from the sky, the earth trembled, and mountains shook.
translation_verse: “Abi ákunku na Unwoti anumi, anwu ɔni ndi Sinai Unwoti, Israel Katɔti.

english_verse: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, and now again in Jael's time, roads were too dangerous for caravans. Travelers had to take the back roads,
translation_verse: “Na Anat ubidi Samgar uwi ku Yael uwi ni, bekyuli béni lilu linengudi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ bɔsia na belusiene baasia lilu lɛni nse gonti gonti lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and villagers couldn't work in their fields. Then Deborah took command, protecting Israel as a mother protects her children.
translation_verse: Ngba bulie na akpaklɔ lɛma na Israel kenye kébo kalɔ. Úbo kalɔ úti útédu uwi ɔni na ami Debora líbo. Na líbo aani ubi uni úte Israel ƒui.

english_verse: The Israelites worshiped other gods, and the gates of their towns were then attacked. But they had no shields or spears to fight with.
translation_verse: Si uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ báƒuna baƒiɔ bawɔdi ni, kekpo kaadá taalɛ ɔma kabanye. Na lɛtula iye lɛgyumanala lɛdi lilalɛ na bula Israelƒuɔ mpim aavlene bani nkya akɔ

english_verse: I praise you, Lord, and I am grateful for those leaders and soldiers who volunteered.
translation_verse: Nsu mina kayi kasia Israelƒuɔ bagabi lɛlɔ ku nkyuli ɛlɛɛ bani néti lɛlɔ béte ƒaa lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu bɛya na bumwi Unwoti.

english_verse: Listen, everyone! Whether you ride a donkey with a padded saddle or have to walk.
translation_verse: “Amii bani nlie bapɔnkɔ baƒualadi lɛlɔ na kuntu kuliekɔ kɔni na bíbo bɛda-ma mmɔ lɛlɔ na bɛkɛ lilu lɛlɔ biisié taavi ni, bɛbu ɔmɛni bɛnu.

english_verse: Even those who carry water to the animals will tell you, “The Lord has won victories, and so has Israel.” Then the Lord's people marched down to the town gates
translation_verse: Na kɔgya bediene básala na abiɔ atu na beedie kɔgya taasu kalɛ na Unwoti ɔ́di lɛlɔ úte Israelƒuɔ ku bekpone bammɔ kabla. “Mmɔ na Unwoti bekyuli báyu bésie bana ɔma unengudi ɔban kayakun kenye.

english_verse: and said, “Deborah, let's go! Let's sing as we march. Barak, capture our enemies.”
translation_verse: Na básu banii, ‘Debora, tɔnku-bu! Debora tɔnku-bu! Na atɔnku-bu ku kɔgya. Awɔ Barak, Abinoam ubidi, ta na eti ƒula bekyuli beƒiedi kɔnakunwi!’

english_verse: The Lord's people who were left joined with their leaders and fought at my side.
translation_verse: “Ɔmɛni kama ni, banana bani nébu bébo bábanu bana benengu. Na Unwoti bekyuli bakladi básala lɛlɔ ku bana bayikune bébo.

english_verse: Troops came from Ephraim, where Amalekites once lived. Others came from Benjamin; officers and leaders came from Machir and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Badi bási Eƒraim na kalɔ kani Amalekƒuɔ béli dii. Na Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli lɛnɔ bábasiaku-ma. Na Makir bekpone batɔnkune bébo. Na bani mɔɔda kekpo lɛdi bediene ugyii lɛnɔ bási Sebulon bébo.

english_verse: The rulers of Issachar came along with Deborah, and Issachar followed Barak into the valley. But the tribe of Reuben was no help at all!
translation_verse: Na Isakar bagabi básiaku Debora. Na badi lɛnɔ basiaku Barak ku usi bétédu kɔwɛ kemmo. Na Ruben kɔdua ama béle lɛlɔ kemmo inyɔ, anwuɔsu bátati lɛla lɛni babla.

english_verse: Reuben, why did you stay among your sheep pens? Was it to listen to shepherds whistling for their sheep? No one could figure out why Reuben wouldn't come.
translation_verse: Na beeye banii bi ɔsu na básɔ bakya baƒonu bammɔ kudɔ, na beteenu kalɛ baƒonu badane bammɔ bakpali bana bebuo. Sɔsɔ na ɔdi ka Ruben kɔdua béle lɛlɔ kemmo inyɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu na bábla kasusu ka belésie.

english_verse: The people of Gilead stayed across the Jordan. Why did the tribe of Dan remain on their ships and the tribe of Asher stay along the coast near the harbors?
translation_verse: Na Gad kɔdua bélie Yordan ɔƒɛ kanukɔ. Na Dan kɔdua ama básɔ bakya ɔkɔlɔ bonwu ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na Aser kɔdua bélie ɛpu kɔtu, na básɔ bakya ɛpu amadɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: But soldiers of Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to attack the enemy.
translation_verse: Nsu Sebulon ku Naƒtali béti bana ngba bákya ɔgbankpi kemmo na kekpo kammɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: Canaanite kings fought us at Taanach by the stream near Megiddo— but they couldn't rob us of our silver.
translation_verse: “Na Taanak kalɔ lɛlɔ baga bébo na bébekpo na Megido Ketu kɔtu. Na Kanaan baga lɛnɔ békpo, nsu bátakana na beti sika ɔƒualadi ɔdi batɔlɔku.

english_verse: From their pathways in the sky the stars fought Sisera,
translation_verse: Ayabi ébekpo na kayaa kemmo uwi ɔni na ákya eesié taavi. Na ási katɔ katɔ ébekpoku Sisera.

english_verse: and his soldiers were swept away by the ancient Kishon River. I will march on and be brave.
translation_verse: Na Kison Ketu kani náƒɔ lɛnyi kukuuku mmɔ kéti-ma kátɔlɔku. Sie anumi, na enye kpakplaa.

english_verse: Sisera's horses galloped off, their hoofs thundering in retreat.
translation_verse: Amu na bapɔnkɔ bébo na babagyu na baabla kudu.

english_verse: The Lord's angel said, “Put a curse on Meroz Town! Its people refused to help the Lord fight his powerful enemies.”
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔtu ɔdi úbo na ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Biwida Meros, na bɛsɔ biwida bekyuli bani nli mmɔ. Ɔsika bétebo bétebebunku Unwoti na bekpo. Nka bɔlɛ na balɛ bebo bebebunku-nwu na bekpo otogyi ɔmmɔ.’

english_verse: But honor Jael, the wife of Heber from the Kenite clan. Give more honor to her than to any other woman who lives in tents. Yes, give more honor to her than to any other woman.
translation_verse: “Na bite Yael kusɛ kusɛ, anwu ndi Heber ɔni nási Keni ulekudi. Na ɔdi uleku ɔni kuli kɔ́dia kútulo na beleku bani nli kevo ɔtɔ kemmo akɔ.

english_verse: Sisera asked for water, but Jael gave him milk— cream in a fancy cup.
translation_verse: Sisera ɔ́su ka utukwɛ ɔɔda-nwu na úte-nwu anyintu na ɔ́ni. Na lɛkyami lɛni mɔɔdia bɔnu kaduɛ kemmo na úti anyi ntu ku ala ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔkya na uti úboku-nwu.

english_verse: She reached for a tent-peg and held a hammer in her right hand. And with a blow to the head, she crushed his skull.
translation_verse: Na úti kevo liwele ɔkya kɔnu kudeedi na úti lɛtabi lɛnɔ ɔkya kɔnu kunyɔdi na úti ɔ́ƒiɛmi Sisera kelima na kuli kɔ́bwɛ-nwu. Na úbo liwele lɛmmɔ ɔ́lɛ-nwu lɛtukpo.

english_verse: Sisera sank to his knees and fell dead at her feet.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́yu úbo uleku ɔmmɔ lɛgba kalɔ, na úbuli ɔtɛ mmɔ kani, na úkpi.

english_verse: Sisera's mother looked out through her window. “Why is he taking so long?” she asked. “Why haven't we heard his chariots coming?”
translation_verse: “Amu na Sisera uni ɔ́kya lili ɔnu nwuna ƒansili, na úye lɛlɔ ɔnini, ‘Bi ɔsu na Sisera bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ bakpɛ kama lɛni? Na bi ɔsu na nwuna bapɔnkɔ lɛnɔ belebo?’

english_verse: She and her wisest women gave the same answer:
translation_verse: Na nwuna begblebi ɔnundane ɔdi údie-nwu kenye ɔnini,

english_verse: “Sisera and his troops are finding treasures to bring back— a woman, or maybe two, for each man, and beautiful dresses for those women to wear.”
translation_verse: ‘Ala kama basiaku na bekpo baƒɔ-nya, na uleku unwi iye beleku inyɔ benye basiaku ukpone unwi. Kɔdi na banii kɔɔdia bɔnu lɛni bete Sisera ka uti ɔda-a limɔ aani ɔga uleku ɔsu.’

english_verse: Our Lord, we pray that all your enemies will die like Sisera. But let everyone who loves you shine brightly like the sun at dawn. Midian Steals Everything from Israel There was peace in Israel for about
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu, O Unwoti, ƒula bekisine ƒui bayii udu! Nsu bani mɔɔyɔ-ɔ litemi ama ni, bekeye aani ɔƒɛ ɔtu ɔdubo.” Amu na kalɔ kammɔ kakɛ bɔnwuna akwa aavlene sɔɔn.

english_verse: Then once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord, so he let the nation of Midian control Israel for seven years.
translation_verse: Na uwi bamba ɔdi lɛlɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ básɔ bábla likpidi na Unwoti anumi. Ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔ́ya na Israelƒuɔ bénwini kabla bablane béte Midianƒuɔ akwa maatɛ sɔɔn.

english_verse: The Midianites were so cruel that many Israelites ran to the mountains and hid in caves.
translation_verse: Ka Midianƒuɔ bamɛni bebo ɔyikun bétulo Israelƒuɔ ɔsu ni, Israelƒuɔ bátáwia kɔkyakɔ na abi akɔ ku atakpɛ libu ku kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa kemmo.

english_verse: Every time the Israelites planted crops, the Midianites invaded Israel together with the Amalekites and other eastern nations.
translation_verse: Na uwi biala na Israelƒuɔ bákya edula ni, na Midianƒuɔ ku Amalekƒuɔ ku bekyuli bamba bani nási ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ beebo teebeyu-ma taatu na bekpoku-ma.

english_verse: They rode in on their camels, set up their tents, and then let their livestock eat the crops as far as the town of Gaza. The Midianites stole food, sheep, cattle, and donkeys. Like a swarm of locusts, they could not be counted, and they ruined the land wherever they went.
translation_verse: Beeti bana bebuo lisu bonwu ku bana nvo teeboku, na bebewi mmɔ aani baalɔlɔ, na bebile ala ƒui ɔni na lɛla lɛdi lɛsɔ lilebu. Na ukyuli ɔdi ulakana-ma bɔka na bana bumomo ɔsu.

english_verse: The Midianites took almost everything that belonged to the Israelites, and the Israelites begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Ka Israelƒuɔ béwulo bákpali Unwoti ka ubedie-ma na Midianƒuɔ bukpoku bɔmɛni ɔsu ni,

english_verse: I am your God, and I told you not to worship Amorite gods, even though you are living in the land of the Amorites. But you refused to listen. The Lord Chooses Gideon
translation_verse: Lɛ́su-mii ka ami ndi bina Unwoti Katɔti, na ɔdi utakpa Amoriƒuɔ baƒiɔ na kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na bilie mɛni ɔƒɛni. Nsu bítenu mina litemi.”

english_verse: One day an angel from the Lord went to the town of Ophrah and sat down under the big tree that belonged to Joash, a member of the Abiezer clan. Joash's son Gideon was nearby, threshing grain in a shallow pit, where he could not be seen by the Midianites.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔtu ɔdi úbo na úbelie kugyii bonwu kɔdi kalɔ na Oƒra ɔma kemmo. Na kugyii kɔmmɔ kɔdi Yoas ɔni nási Abi-Eser kɔdi. Mmɔ na ubidi Gideon ɔkya uuwiile edula ebi teewi ntɛ kebulokɔ kalɛ na Midianƒuɔ balanu-nya beledie kemmo.

english_verse: The angel appeared and spoke to Gideon, “The Lord is helping you, and you are a strong warrior.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔtu ɔmmɔ údie lɛlɔ ɔ́tina Gideon na mmɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Unwoti ulieku-ɔ, awɔ ukpone ɔyikune.”

english_verse: Gideon answered, “Please don't take this wrong, but if the Lord is helping us, then why have all of these awful things happened? We've heard how the Lord performed miracles and rescued our ancestors from Egypt. But those things happened long ago. Now the Lord has abandoned us to the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Amu na Gideon údie kenye ɔnini, “Ati, si Unwoti ulieku-bu ni, bi ɔsu na ala amɛni aalɛ́ku-bu lɛni? Wɛ na nwuna akɔla ala budie taatina akya? Ɔɔɔdi bɔsu na bati básu-bu banini, ‘Unwoti nédie-bu ɔ́lɛku Egyipteƒuɔ enu kemmo.’ Nsu ɔƒɛni amu údie-bu atu na ɔ́nyonu-bu ɔ́kya Midianƒuɔ enu kemmo.”

english_verse: Then the Lord himself said, “Gideon, you will be strong, because I am giving you the power to rescue Israel from the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ami mɔɔtala-a nnii teesie ku ɔyikun ɔni ƒui na ebo na etédie Israelƒuɔ alɛku Midianƒuɔ enu kemmo.”

english_verse: Gideon replied, “But how can I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest one in Manasseh, and everyone else in my family is more important than I am.”
translation_verse: Amu na Gideon údie kenye ɔnini, “Unwoti, dɛ na ndubo bɔbla asa na makana Israelƒuɔ bukpo bɔƒɔ? Na Manase kɔdua bekyuli akɔ ni, abu nse kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ntulo ƒui, na ami lɛnɔ ndi ukplodi na mina ɔtɔ badi akɔ.”

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord answered, “you can rescue Israel because I am going to help you! Defeating the Midianites will be as easy as beating up one man.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Gideon ɔnini, “Nnyeku-ɔ, na adubukpoku Midianƒuɔ ƒui na abla-ma kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “It's hard to believe that I'm actually talking to the Lord. Please do something so I'll know that you really are the Lord.
translation_verse: Amu na Gideon údie kenye ɔnini, “Unwoti, si sɔsɔ na mina lɛlɔ lɛ́ƒɔ-ɔ anu bɔdi ni, ya na lɛnu ƒula akɔla budie taatina adi na lɛti ka awɔ geen mɔɔtɛmiku-mi.

english_verse: And wait here until I bring you an offering.” “All right, I'll wait,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Na buvele kemmo ni, tatɔlɔ mɛni úti útédu ka liti mina etela líboku ḿbese-ɔ anumi.” Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Línu, na ndubulie mɛni lɛgya-a wetédu ka énwini ébo.”

english_verse: Gideon went home and killed a young goat, then started boiling the meat. Next, he opened a big sack of flour and made it into thin bread. When the meat was done, he put it in a basket and poured the broth into a clay cooking pot. He took the meat, the broth, and the bread and placed them under the big tree.
translation_verse: Amu na Gideon únwini úsie kaduli na útádu ese ɔkɔdi ɔdi na ɔ́bla kutu ƒɛƒɛɛ na úti ɔlaaƒɔ ɔni kemmo na bɔnyii buubo, na úƒi bodobodo na úti ala ammɔ ƒui ɔ́kya kagyigyɛ kemmo ku lɛna ku kutu lɛnwabui lɛmmɔ ƒui úboku kugyii kubendi kɔmmɔ kalɔ úbete-nwu.

english_verse: God's angel said, “Gideon, put the meat and the bread on this rock, and pour the broth over them.” Gideon did as he was told.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́su Gideon ɔnini, “Ti lɛna ku bodobodo ɔmmɔ na eti asia lɛtakpɛ lɛmɛni lɛlɔ, na ewilimi kutu kɔmmɔ ewi-nwu lɛlɔ.” Na Gideon lɛnɔ ɔ́bla ɔ́sia kalɛ ɔ́su-nwu mmɔ.

english_verse: The angel was holding a walking stick, and he touched the meat and the bread with the end of the stick. Flames jumped from the rock and burned up the meat and the bread. When Gideon looked, the angel was gone.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti ɔtu ɔmmɔ úti ugyii ɔni ɔ́da mmɔ kenye útuku lɛna ku bodobodo ɔmmɔ. Na ogya ɔ́buɛ ɔlɛ lɛtakpɛ lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ na ɔ́kyula lɛna ku bodobodo ɔmmɔ. Mmɔ kani na Unwoti ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́yii ɔ́kya.

english_verse: Gideon realized that he had seen one of the Lord's angels. “Oh!” he moaned. “Now I'm going to die.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Gideon ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka Unwoti ɔtu na ɔdi ni, ɔ́va kɔnakunwi na ɔ́su ɔnini, “O Unwoti, Ɔyikune Ƒui! Lɛ́nu Unwoti ɔtu anumi ku anumi!”

english_verse: “Calm down!” the Lord told Gideon. “There's nothing to be afraid of. You're not going to die.”
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Keyi buɛɛ kasiaku-ɔ! Na ada bɔyia aya. Ɔsika elekpi.”

english_verse: Gideon built an altar for worshiping the Lord and called it “The Lord Calms Our Fears.” It still stands there in Ophrah, a town in the territory of the Abiezer clan. Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar
translation_verse: Amu na Gideon ɔ́tu lɛkpabi úte Unwoti na ɔ́sia-nwu lɛnyi ɔnii, “Unwoti Ɔdi Keyi Buɛɛ Unwoti.” Na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛmu lɛ́lɛ Oƒra Abi-Eser kalɔ kemmo.

english_verse: That night the Lord spoke to Gideon again: Get your father's second-best bull, the one that's seven years old. Use it to pull down the altar where your father worships Baal and cut down the sacred pole next to the altar.
translation_verse: Amu na usien ɔmmɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́su Gideon ɔnini, “Ti ƒula ɔti ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔni nsiaku ebuo unengudi kama unyɔdi ɔni náakɛ akwa maatɛ. Na atáƒɛ ƒ'ɔti Baal baƒiɔ bani na ɔ́tu ɔ́lɛ mmɔ. Na amɛnɛ Asera kugyii kɔni kunye-nwu kudɔ mmɔ ewi kalɔ.

english_verse: Then build an altar for worshiping me on the highest part of the hill where your town is built. Use layers of stones for my altar, not just a pile of rocks. Cut up the wood from the pole, make a fire, kill the bull, and burn it as a sacrifice to me.
translation_verse: Na atu lɛkpabi buni lɛni nákuku ete ƒula Unwoti Katɔti na katɔ mmɔ. Na eti ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔmmɔ abla bɔkyula akpala ete-mi. Na eti kugyii kɔni na amɛnɛ mmɔ ekyweni abla akpala ammɔ.”

english_verse: Gideon chose ten of his servants to help him, and they did everything God had said. But since Gideon was afraid of his family and the other people in Ophrah, he did it all at night.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Gideon úti nwuna kabla bablane leevu ɔ́da aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo-nwu ɔda. Nsu ka ɔyia nwuna bawɔne ku ɔma ɔmmɔ bananabi ɔsu ni, usien mmomu na ɔ́bla ala ammɔ, na ɔɔɔdi ɔƒiiwi.

english_verse: When the people of the town got up the next morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been knocked over, and the sacred pole next to it had been cut down. Then they noticed the new altar covered with the remains of the sacrificed bull.
translation_verse: Ka kadi kégye na ɔma ɔmmɔ bananabi báta ni, bánu ka Baal lɛkpabi lɛ́ƒɛ lɛtɛ kalɔ, na Asera kugyii kɔni nnye-nwu kudɔ lɛnɔ bámɛnɛ-ku báva kalɔ. Na bátu lɛkpabi lɛwɔdi na bádu ɔmantɛ akɔ unyɔdi ɔmmɔ bábla akpala na lɛkpa lɛwɔdi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: “Who could have done such a thing?” they asked. And they kept on asking, until finally someone told them, “Gideon the son of Joash did it.”
translation_verse: Amu na bakya beeye lɛlɔ banii, “Ɔma geen nábla ala amɛni?” Amu ka beduo ala kemmo kaduɛ ni, bábanu bati ka Yoas ubidi Gideon nábla ala ammɔ.

english_verse: The men of the town went to Joash and said, “Your son Gideon knocked over Baal's altar and cut down the sacred pole next to it. Hand him over, so we can kill him!”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔma ɔmmɔ bananabi bátásu Yoas banii, “Ti ƒ'ubidi Gideon boku. Ɔ́manku ka badu-nwu, ɔsika ɔ́ƒɛ Baal lɛkpabi uwi kalɔ na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́mɛnɛ kugyii kɔni nnye lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ ɔ́va kalɔ.”

english_verse: The crowd pushed closer and closer, but Joash replied, “Are you trying to take revenge for Baal? Are you trying to rescue Baal? If you are, you will be the ones who are put to death, and it will happen before another day dawns. If Baal really is a god, let him take his own revenge on someone who tears down his altar.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yoas údie kenye na otogyi ɔmmɔ anumi ɔnini, “Amii ndubɔtɛ litemi lɛmmɔ bite Baal? Munuu amii mɔɔwia ka bɛƒɔ-nwu ngba? Na mɔɔsu-mii nnii ukyuli biala mata mekpo mete-nwu ni, ɔlɛka badu-nwu ɔtanta ɔmɛni kani. Na nsɔ mɔɔsu lɛnɔ ka si Baal ɔgyi ka ɔyikune na ɔdi ni, na anwu ɔlati ukpo ute lɛlɔ si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́ƒɛ nwuna lɛkpabi.”

english_verse: That same day, Joash changed Gideon's name to Jerubbaal, explaining, “He tore down Baal's altar, so let Baal take revenge himself.” Gideon Defeats the Midianites
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔ́si limeyi lɛmmɔ básia Gideon lɛnyi banii Yerubaal, ɔni kalɔ ndi “Bɛya na Baal alati ukpoku Gideon.” Ɔsika ɔ́ƒɛ Baal lɛkpabi.

english_verse: All the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations got together and crossed the Jordan River. Then they invaded the land of Israel and set up camp in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama ni, Midianƒuɔ ku Amalekƒuɔ ku bani ƒui nli ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ bátu akpagya na bávia Yordan Ketu, na bésie batásala lisu na Yesreel Kɔwɛ kemmo.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of Gideon, and Gideon blew a trumpet as a signal for the men in the Abiezer clan to follow him.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti Kɔyu kɔ́ƒɔ Gideon lɛlɔ kemmo na úti kakpɛɛ na ɔ́vwi momoomo ɔ́kpali Abi-Eserƒuɔ ka batu akpagya bábasiaku-nwu.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, telling the men of these tribes to come and join his army. Then they set out toward the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́tala bekyuli ɔ́kya Manase ku Aser ku Sebulon ku Naƒtali kɔdua bekyuli ƒui ka batu akpagya na besie betékpo. Na ama lɛnɔ báta sɔsɔ na básiaku-ma.

english_verse: Gideon prayed to God, “I know that you promised to help me rescue Israel, but I need proof. Tonight I'll spread a sheep skin on the stone floor of that threshing-place over there. If you really will help me rescue Israel, then tomorrow morning let there be dew on the skin, but let the stone floor be dry.”
translation_verse: na ndubuti kpekpe liwi kakpa kamɛni lɛlɔ, na si amii áyu éwi na ɔ́ƒɔyi kpekpe ɔmmɔ, nsu kalɔ kataƒɔyi ni, na ndubɔƒɔ lɛdi ka adubɔsia-mi lɛlɔ, na áƒɔ Israelƒuɔ ngba aani kalɛ na ásu ése.”

english_verse: And that's just what happened. Early the next morning, Gideon got up and checked the sheep skin. He squeezed out enough water to fill a bowl.
translation_verse: Na úbo ute lɛni pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ka Gideon ɔ́ta ɔtanta tutuutu ni, úti kpekpe ɔmmɔ na ɔ́ka-nwu. Na ntu bɔni nálɛ kpekpe ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ buyii lɛkpibui.

english_verse: But Gideon prayed to God again. “Don't be angry with me,” Gideon said. “Let me try this just one more time, so I'll really be sure you'll help me. Only this time, let the skin be dry and the stone floor be wet.”
translation_verse: Amu na Gideon ɔ́su Unwoti ɔnini, “Buvele nda-a, teti kɔnyi takya-mi. Ya na lɛsɔ lɛsu-ɔ na abla lɛla lɛdi na kpekpe ɔmɛni lɛlɔ ete-mi. Ɔƒɛni ya na kpekpe ɔmmɔ utaƒɔyi, na aya na amii ammɔ ɔƒɔyi kalɔ kammɔ mmomu.”

english_verse: That night, God made the stone floor wet with dew, but he kept the sheep skin dry.
translation_verse: Na usien ɔmmɔ ni, Katɔti ɔ́bla lɛni kani. Koƒo kɔmmɔ kútaƒɔyi, nsu amii áƒɔ kalɔ kammɔ na káƒɔyi.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Gideon and his army got up and moved their camp to Fear Spring. The Midianite camp was to the north, in the valley at the foot of Moreh Hill.
translation_verse: Kadi kégye ɔtanta tutuutu Yerubaal ɔni ndi Gideon ku nwuna bekpone bátábɛ bakya Harod libiɔ kɔmadɔ. Nsu kesii kani na Midianƒuɔ bátábɛ bakya ni, kakya Gideon bekyuli kada kakɛ na kɔwɛ kɔni nde More kɔbi kudɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army is too big. I can't let you win with this many soldiers. The Israelites would think that they had won the battle all by themselves and that I didn't have anything to do with it.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́su Gideon ɔnini, “Bekyuli bani nésela betékpo Midianƒuɔ bammɔ bemomo bagya. Na kalɛ na Israelƒuɔ balakun lɛmɛne balatina-mi ka bana ɔyikun lɛlɔ na békpo bádi lɛlɔ ɔsu ni,

english_verse: So call your troops together and tell them that anyone who is really afraid can leave Mount Gilead and go home.” Twenty-two thousand men returned home, leaving Gideon with only
translation_verse: su bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ka, ‘Ukyuli biala na liƒu lɛɛda-nwu ni, unwini na ɔtɔlɔ Gilead kɔbi lɛlɔ mɛni.’ ” Anwuɔsu nkyuli mpim aavlanyɔ-inyɔ bénwini na kasɔ kebu nkyuli mpim leevu.

english_verse: but if you're still afraid, you and your servant Purah should sneak down to their camp.
translation_verse: Nsu si ayia ka etékpoku-ma ni, esie etétiku ƒula kabla ɔblane Pura na bisie bana kakyakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord said, “you still have too many soldiers. Take them down to the spring and I'll test them. I'll tell you which ones can go along with you and which ones must go back home.”
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Gideon ɔnini, “Bekyuli bammɔ bamu bemomo bagya. Anwuɔsu ti-ma sienku ketu kani nwi mmɔ kemmo na ami ɔlati ndubɔƒuna-ma bute-ɔ na mmɔ. Na si lɛ́su-ɔ ka ukyuli ɔmɛni ɔsiaku-ɔ ni, ɔdubɔsiaku-ɔ. Na si lɛ́su-ɔ ka ukyuli ɔmɛni utasiaku-ɔ ni, ulasiaku-ɔ.”

english_verse: When Gideon led his army down to the spring, the Lord told him, “Watch how each man gets a drink of water. Then divide them into two groups—those who lap the water like a dog and those who kneel down to drink.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Gideon úti bekyuli bammɔ úsienku ketu kammɔ kemmo. Na Unwoti ɔ́su Gideon ɔnini, “Die bekyuli bani ƒui néti bana linyemi baaƒɔ́ ntu bɔmmɔ na akɔkɔ kemmo teewi kenye aani kalɛ akpewe ɔɔní ntu se sɛsɛɛ asiku bani ƒui nálɛ akɔnkɔ béti bana inye bébi ntu bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ asa báni ntu kudɔ.”

english_verse: men stay here. The rest of you may go home, but leave your food and trumpets with us.” Gideon's army camp was on top of a hill overlooking the Midianite camp in the valley.
translation_verse: ) bammɔ básɔ bákya na ama nda kɔkpɛɛ ku adila ani na bada. Amu na Midianƒuɔ kakyakɔ kakya kɔwɛ kɔni nwi-bana kada kakɛ mmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: That night, the Lord said to Gideon. “Get up! Attack the Midianite camp. I am going to let you defeat them,
translation_verse: Usien ɔmmɔ ni, Unwoti údie lɛdi na ɔ́su Gideon ɔnini, “Ta na etékpoku Midianƒuɔ bammɔ na kesii kani na bakya mmɔ. Ɔsika ndubuti-ma lɛ́kya-a enu kemmo.

english_verse: When you hear what the Midianites are saying, you'll be brave enough to attack.” Gideon and Purah worked their way to the edge of the enemy camp, where soldiers were on guard duty.
translation_verse: Na bise atu na binu ala ani baasu. Mmɔ na bɛdubuse kayi na bɛta bikpoku-ma.” Anwuɔsu Gideon ku nwuna kabla ɔblane Pura báyu besie kesii kani na bana bekisine básala bakya mmɔ.

english_verse: The camp was huge. The Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations covered the valley like a swarm of locusts. And it would be easier to count the grains of sand on a beach than to count their camels.
translation_verse: Midianƒuɔ ku Amalekƒuɔ ku kadi bamba bekyuli bani nási ɔƒɛ katukɔ ƒui bábla kakyakɔ na kɔwɛ kɔmmɔ kemmo na lisu bonwu kemmo aani baalɔlɔ. Na bana bebuo ala betine ku keƒu bemomo geen aani ɛpu kɔnwinimi, na balakana-ma bɔka.

english_verse: Gideon overheard one enemy guard telling another, “I had a dream about a flat loaf of barley bread that came tumbling into our camp. It hit the headquarters tent, and the tent flipped over and fell to the ground.”
translation_verse: Na ka Gideon útéduo mmɔ ni, únu ka ukyuli ɔdi ɔkya ɔɔsu nwuna ɔkpana ɔdi kɔna kɔni na úgye. Na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bodobodo ɔdi uminime úduo bula kakyakɔ, na kalɛ na úbatuaku kevo kammɔ ku ɔyikun ɔsu ni, kevo kammɔ káƒɛ kewi kalɔ.”

english_verse: The other soldier answered, “Your dream must have been about Gideon, the Israelite commander. It means God will let him and his army defeat the Midianite army and everyone else in our camp.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔkpana ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdi lɛla bamba lɛdi na ánu utulo Yoas ubidi Gideon, Israelni ɔmmɔ kewii. Katɔti úti Midianƒuɔ ku abu bani ƒui násala bɔ́bla unwi mɛni ɔ́kya-nwu enu kemmo.”

english_verse: As soon as Gideon heard about the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to praise God. Then he went back to the Israelite camp and shouted, “Let's go! The Lord is going to let us defeat the Midianite army.”
translation_verse: Amu ka Gideon únu kɔna kɔmmɔ ku kalɛ bédie-nwu kalɔ ni, ɔ́lɛ akɔnkɔ na ɔ́kpali Unwoti. Mmɔ kani na únwini úsie Israelƒuɔ kakyakɔ na ɔ́kpali bekpone bammɔ ɔnini, “Bɛta na bɔgyu! Unwoti úti Midianƒuɔ bammɔ ku bana kevo ɔ́kya-bu enu kemmo.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “When we get to the enemy camp, spread out and surround it. Then wait for me to blow a signal on my trumpet. As soon as you hear it, blow your trumpets and shout, ‘Fight for the Lord! Fight for Gideon!’ ”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na ami ku bekyuli bani nsiaku-mi bɔ́nya bɔ́vwi bula kɔkpɛɛ ni, na amii bani náka bɛ́mana ƒui lɛnɔ bɛvwi bina kɔdi na bidie lɛdi ku kudu momoomo bɛnini, ‘Yiidu ute bula Unwoti ku bula ɔtɔnkune Gideon.’ ”

english_verse: Gideon and his group reached the edge of the enemy camp a few hours after dark, just after the new guards had come on duty. Gideon and his soldiers blew their trumpets and smashed the clay jars that were hiding the torches.
translation_verse: Gideon ku nwuna nkyuli eti anyɔ báni béde kesii kani na Midianƒuɔ bammɔ básala lɛlɔ mmɔ na uwi ɔni kani na ukyuli ɔni mɔɔgyumana Midianƒuɔ bammɔ bavumana lɛlɔ na usien ntɛ ɔmmɔ. Mmɔ kani na bávwi bana kɔkpɛɛ na bébo bana ebui bábwɛ.

english_verse: The rest of Gideon's soldiers blew the trumpets they were holding in their right hands. Then they smashed the jars and held the burning torches in their left hands. Everyone shouted, “Fight with your swords for the Lord and for Gideon!”
translation_verse: Na akpa anyɔ akladi lɛnɔ bábla lɛni kani. Na bana ƒui béti bana likpo ɔni bada mmɔ bákya kɔmiinu kɔnu na bada bana kɔkpɛɛ na kɔdianu na bédie lɛdi momoomo básu banini, “Kewii kenwi kenye kéte Unwoti, na kanyɔdi lɛnɔ kenye kéte Gideon.”

english_verse: The enemy soldiers started yelling and tried to run away. Gideon's troops stayed in their positions surrounding the camp
translation_verse: Ukyuli biala ɔ́ta unye nwuna kenyekɔ na kesii kani bákya mmɔ. Na bekisine bammɔ békeli bésela ku kɔvanu.

english_verse: and blew their trumpets again. As they did, the Lord made the enemy soldiers pull out their swords and start fighting each other. The enemy army tried to escape from the camp. They ran to Acacia Tree Town, toward Zeredah, and as far as the edge of the land that belonged to the town of Abel-Meholah near Tabbath.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Gideon bekyuli bakya baavwi bana kɔkpɛɛ ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na bekisine bammɔ béti bana atula na bakya beekpóku lɛlɔ. Na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui békeli bakɛ Serera bétédu Bet-Sita na bákɛ bétédu Abel-Mehela ɔni nde Tabat.

english_verse: Gideon sent word for more Israelite soldiers to come from the tribes of Naphtali, Asher, and both halves of Manasseh to help fight the Midianites.
translation_verse: Na Gideon ɔ́tala bekyuli ɔ́kya Naƒtali ku Aser ku Manase kalɔ lɛlɔ, na bekyuli bási bébo bábasiaku Midianƒuɔ.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to tell all the men who lived in the hill country of Ephraim, “Come and help us fight the Midianites! Put guards at every spring, stream, and well, as far as Beth-Barah before the Midianites can get to them. And guard the Jordan River.” Troops from Ephraim did exactly what Gideon had asked,
translation_verse: Amu na Gideon ɔ́tala bekyuli ɔ́kya Eƒraim lɛma lɛni nwi abi eli ka batásu-ma banii bebo na bebekpoku Midianƒuɔ bekpo baƒɔ Yordan Ketu uti utédu Bet-Bara. Anwuɔsu Eƒraim bálɛ na bétékpo báƒɔ Yordan Ketu utédu Bet-Bara.

english_verse: and they even helped chase the Midianites on the east side of the Jordan River. These troops captured Raven and Wolf, the two Midianite leaders. They killed Raven at a large rock that has come to be known as Raven Rock, and they killed Wolf near a wine-pit that has come to be called Wolf Wine-Pit. The men of Ephraim brought the heads of the two Midianite leaders to Gideon.
translation_verse: Na béƒie Midianƒuɔ batɔnkune inyɔ bani ndi Oreb ku Seeb. Na bádu Oreb na Oreb Atakpɛ lɛlɔ. Na bádu Seeb na Seeb Ntɛ Kablakɔ. Na bábi basiaku Midianƒuɔ na béti Oreb ku Seeb eli bésienku Gideon na Yordan Ketu kɔtu.

english_verse: But the men were really upset with Gideon and complained, “When you went to war with Midian, you didn't ask us to help! Why did you treat us like that?”
translation_verse: Amu na Eƒraim Kɔdua bekyuli béye Gideon banini, “Bi ɔsu na ábla-bu lɛni, na átalɔ-bu úwi ɔni na ésela etékpoku Midianƒuɔ na bubebunku-ɔ?” Na bédie-nwu bɔƒiɔ kaduɛ.

english_verse: Gideon answered: Don't be upset! Even though you came later, you were able to do much more than I did. It's just like the grape harvest: The grapes your tribe doesn't even bother to pick are better than the best grapes my family can grow.
translation_verse: Amu na Gideon ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Lɛla lɛni na lɛ́kana bɔ́bla ni, beleti-ni balákɔku lɛla lɛni amii bɛ́bla. Amii Eƒraim kɔdua bekyuli bɛ́bla litulo lɛla lɛni na ami Gideon ku mina ɔtɔ Abieser bekyuli bɔ́bla.

english_verse: Besides, God chose you to capture Raven and Wolf. I didn't do a thing compared to you. By the time Gideon had finished talking, the men of Ephraim had calmed down and were no longer angry with him. Gideon Finishes Destroying the Midianite Army
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔyikun lɛlɔ ɔsu na bɛ́kana Ɔga Oreb ku Ɔga Seeb bɔ́du. Na bi ndi lɛla lɛni na lɛ́bla mɛni muedi? Balakana beti-ni bakɔku bina lɛdi lɛni na bɛ́bla.” Na ka Gideon ɔ́su-ma lɛni ni, bana kɔnyi kɔ́yɔ-ma.

english_verse: The town of Succoth was nearby, so he went there and asked, “Please give my troops some food. They are worn out, but we have to keep chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the two Midianite kings.”
translation_verse: Na ka bébedu Sukot ni, ɔ́su Sukot bekyuli ɔnini, “Bite mina bekpone bamɛni bodobodo ɔdi na badi, ɔsika lɛlɔ lítu-ma, nsu lɛ́mu nsiaku Seeba ku Salmuna bani ndi Midian baga kama mɔɔbɔku-ma.”

english_verse: The town leaders of Succoth answered, “Why should we feed your army? We don't know if you really will defeat Zebah and Zalmunna.”
translation_verse: Nsu Sukot batɔnkune bammɔ básu Gideon banini, “Ɔni na éteƒie tɔ Seeba ku Salmuna bekyuli mɛni ni, bi ɔsu na ɔlɛka bute ƒula bekpone adila adi na badi?”

english_verse: “Just wait!” Gideon said. “After the Lord helps me defeat them, I'm coming back here. I'll make a whip out of thorns and rip the flesh from your bones.”
translation_verse: Amu na Gideon ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔdia! Si uwi ɔni na Unwoti úti Seeba ku Salmuna ɔ́kya-mi enu kemmo ni, ndubuti ketele liyu ligyii libo-mii kaduɛ!”

english_verse: After leaving Succoth, Gideon went to Penuel and asked the leaders there for some food. But he got the same answer as he did at Succoth.
translation_verse: Na ka Gideon ɔ́si mmɔ ni, úsie Penuel na úye ama lɛnɔ lɛla lɛni kani na úye Sukot kadi bekyuli. Na kenye kani na Sukotƒuɔ bédie ni, aka kani na Penuelƒuɔ lɛnɔ bédie.

english_verse: “I'll come back safe and sound,” Gideon said, “but when I do, I'm going to tear down your tower!”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Si lísie ńtádi lɛlɔ na línwini líbo ni, ndubo bina katu taasia ɔtɔ gyɛnglɛɛ ɔni bɛ́tu mɛni bubo bɔƒɛ.”

english_verse: Gideon went to the town officials and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. Remember how you made fun of me? You said, ‘We don't know if you really will defeat those two Midianite kings. So why should we feed your worn-out army?’ ”
translation_verse: Amu na Gideon úsie Sukot na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Biinyimo uwi ɔni na bíni bɛnii bilete-mi kebunku? Bɛ́su-mi bɛnii bilete mina bekpone bani na lɛlɔ lítu adila adi na badi ka ńtakana tɔ Seeba ku Salmuna lɛlɔ bɔdi ɔsu. Aanu baga bammɔ mɛni.”

english_verse: Gideon reached the enemy camp by going east along Nomad Road past Nobah and Jogbehah. He made a surprise attack,
translation_verse: Na Gideon ɔ́sia belusiene ulu ɔni nkɛ ɔ́vi Noba ku Yogbeha ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ útáda ɔ́lɛ bekpone bani naaagyi beeese mmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and the enemy panicked. Zebah and Zalmunna tried to escape, but Gideon chased and captured them.
translation_verse: Midian baga inyɔ Seeba ku Salmuna békeli, nsu Gideon ɔ́bi ɔsiaku-ma na útéƒie-ma na úgyingya bekpone bammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: After the battle, Gideon set out for home. As he was going through Heres Pass,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Yoas ubidi Gideon úkpo ɔ́wɔlɔ na únwini úsela ni, útásia Heres abi ntɛ ulu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: he caught a young man who lived in Succoth. Gideon asked him who the town officials of Succoth were, and the young man wrote down
translation_verse: Mmɔ na úƒie okloƒu ɔdi nási Sukot na úye-nwu ala. Na okloƒu ɔmmɔ únweni Sukot batɔnkune liti ku aavlanyɔ-maatɛ anyi úte Gideon.

english_verse: Gideon made a whip from thorn plants and used it to beat the town officials.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Gideon úti liyu kugyiimi kɔni na ɔ́ƒɛ ɔ́siku ketele kemmo na úbo Sukot batɔnkune bammɔ kaduɛ.

english_verse: Afterwards he went to Penuel, where he tore down the tower and killed all the town officials.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́ƒɛ katu taasia ɔtɔ gyɛnglɛɛ ɔni nlɛ Panuel mmɔ uwi kalɔ, na úbo ɔma batɔnkune bammɔ ɔdu.

english_verse: Then Gideon said, “Zebah and Zalmunna, tell me about the men you killed at Tabor.” “They were a lot like you,” the two kings answered. “They were dignified, almost like royalty.”
translation_verse: Amu na Gideon úye Seeba ku Salmuna ɔnini, “Bekyuli bamɛni udu na bɛ́du na Tabor?” Amu na bédie kenye banii, “Bekyuli bammɔ bálɛ-mii. Na ɔdi biala ɔɔdi ɔga ubi lɛnyi.”

english_verse: “They were my very own brothers!” Gideon said. “I swear by the living Lord that if you had let them live, I would let you live.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Gideon ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bekyuli bammɔ badi mina banwani geen na ami ku-ma bɔdi benibi. Na muusé kenye ka si bɔdu na bítadu-ma ni, nka ami lɛnɔ lɛɛɛdubo-mii bɔdu.”

english_verse: kilograms. In addition, there was the gold from the camels' ornaments and from the beautiful jewelry worn by the Midianite kings. Gideon also took their purple robes.
translation_verse: Na Gideon ɔ́su ubidi udeedi ɔni baalɔ banii Yeter ɔnini, “Du-ma!” Nsu Yeter útani nwuna kewii útalɛku livuo kemmo, ɔsika ɔnamu na ɔdi. Ɔƒɛni lɛnɔ ni, ɔɔyia.

english_verse: “What's the matter, Gideon?” Zebah and Zalmunna asked. “Do it yourself, if you're not too much of a coward!” Gideon jumped up and killed them both. Then he took the gold ornaments from the necks of their camels. The Israelites Ask Gideon To Be Their King
translation_verse: Amu na Seeba ku Sulmuna básu Gideon banini, “Awɔ ɔlati bo na abadu-bu. Ɔsika ɔnanabi mɔɔbla ɔnanabi kabla.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Gideon ɔ́du-ma na ɔ́da adala ani nkya bana baƒlumu bammɔ údie.

english_verse: After the battle with the Midianites, the Israelites said, “Gideon, you rescued us! Now we want you to be our king. Then after your death, your son and then your grandson will rule.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Israelƒuɔ básu Gideon banini, “Bɔɔyɔ́ ka abla bula ɔtɔnkune, awɔ ku ƒula bebi ku bawɔ. Ɔsika awɔ nédie-bu álɛku Midianƒuɔ enu kemmo.”

english_verse: “No,” Gideon replied, “I won't be your king, and my son won't be king either. Only the Lord is your ruler.
translation_verse: Amu na Gideon ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ami iye mina bebi ɔdi ulabla bina ɔtɔnkune. Mmomu Unwoti ndubɔbla bina ɔtɔnkune.”

english_verse: But I will ask you to do one thing: Give me all the earrings you took from the enemy.” The enemy soldiers had been Ishmaelites, and they wore gold earrings.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔ-ma ɔnini, “Mɔɔyɔ́ ka livele-mii lɛla lɛdi. Bina akɔ ɔdi biala ute-mi kɔtu lɛsikpɛɛ na ala ani bíƒie bɛ́ƒɔ bɛ́siku bina bekisine kudɔ mmɔ kemmo.” Na ɔdi Ismaelƒuɔ ɔdi ka bakya atu asikpɛɛ ani beti sika ugyiedi babla.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers replied, “Of course we will give you the earrings.” Then they spread out a robe on the ground and tossed the earrings on it.
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bamɛni bédie kenye banii, “Bula ƒui bɔdubute kɔtu asikpɛɛ ammɔ ku kaƒɔ ƒaa.” Anwuɔsu bégyingya kɔdi bewi kalɔ, na ɔdi biala úƒwimi nwuna lɛdi lɛni na ɔ́kɛ ɔ́siku kekpokɔ mmɔ útáva kɔdi kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: He even had a wife who lived at Shechem. They had a son, and Gideon named him Abimelech.
translation_verse: Na nwuna ɔsɔnɔ ɔni na úbo na úli Sekem lɛnɔ ɔ́wɔ ubi úte-nwu na ɔ́sia-nwu lɛnyi ɔnii Abimelek.

english_verse: Gideon lived to be an old man. And when he died, he was buried in the family tomb in his hometown of Ophrah, which belonged to the Abiezer clan.
translation_verse: Yoas ubidi Gideon ɔ́bi asa na úkpi, na báva-nwu na ɔti Yoas kaƒiɔtɔ kemmo na Oƒra ɔma, na mmɔ kadi Abi-Eserƒuɔ kalɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Soon after Gideon's death, the Israelites turned their backs on God again. They set up idols of Baal and worshiped Baal Berith as their god.
translation_verse: Na uwi klukui ɔdi kemmo na Gideon kekpima ni, Israelƒuɔ básɔ bése kalɔ baakpá Baal baƒiɔ. Na béti Baal-Berit bábla bana Katɔti.

english_verse: The Israelites forgot that the Lord was their God, and that he had rescued them from the enemies who lived around them.
translation_verse: Na bétenyimo bana Unwoti Katɔti ɔni nédie-ma ɔ́lɛku bana bekisine ƒui enu kemmo.

english_verse: Besides all that, the Israelites were unkind to Gideon's family, even though Gideon had done so much for Israel.
translation_verse: Na bétenyimo na babla lɛƒɔndia lɛdi beti bete Yerubaal ɔni ndi Gideon bebi na ala abuni ani na ɔ́bla úte-ma ɔsu.

english_verse: and told them to say to the leaders of Shechem, “Do you think it would be good to have all
translation_verse: “Biye Sekem ɔma bekyuli ƒui binu bɛnii ɔmani ndia-ma utulo, baayɔ́ ka Yerubaal bebi bananabi liti ku aavlanyɔ bammɔ bataadi-ma lɛlɔ, munuu ukyuli unwi. Nsu binyimo ka amii ni, bina ubugya nawɔ-mi, na ami ku-mii ɔlɔna ɔdi unwi.”

english_verse: Abimelech's uncles talked it over with the leaders of Shechem who agreed, “Yes, it would be better for one of our relatives to be king.”
translation_verse: Amu ka Abimelek banwani bátásɔku etemila amɛni básu Sekemƒuɔ ni, bana ƒui kasusu kátina-ma ka basiaku Abimelek, ɔsika básu banini, “Bula ɔnwani na ɔdi.”

english_verse: Abimelech and his soldiers went to his father's home in Ophrah and brought out Gideon's other sons to a large rock, where they murdered all
translation_verse: Na úsie ɔti kesii na Oƒra. Mmɔ ka ɔ́nya uƒiɛmi lɛtabi kunwi pɛ amu ɔ́du nwuna banwani liti ku aavlanyɔ bani ndi Gideon bebi. Nsu Yerubaal kawɔkpulo ɔni baalɔ banii Yotam úkeli ɔbɛ.

english_verse: The leaders of Shechem, including the priests and the military officers, met at the tree next to the sacred rock in Shechem to crown Abimelech king.
translation_verse: Na Sekem bekyuli ku Bet-Milo bekyuli ƒui bátása kugyii kubendi kalɔ na bése Abimelek ɔga mmɔ.

english_verse: Jotham heard what they were doing. So he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and shouted down to the people who were there at the meeting: Leaders of Shechem, listen to me, and maybe God will listen to you.
translation_verse: Ka Yotam únu litemi lɛmɛni ni, ɔ́kɔ úsie Gerisim Kɔbi lili, na mmɔ na ɔ́kɔ lɛsa momoomo ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ami Sekemƒuɔ binu mina litemi kalɛ na Unwoti lɛnɔ wenu bina litemi.

english_verse: Once the trees searched for someone to be king; they asked the olive tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Dii ni, egyii ásala lɛlɔ lisu ka bese ɔga bete lɛlɔ. Amu na básu nnɔ kugyii banini, ‘Bla bula ɔga.’

english_verse: But the olive tree replied, “My oil brings honor to people and gods. I won't stop making oil, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: “Nsu nnɔ kugyii kɔ́su-ma ɔnini, ‘Nda nnɔ bɔni na nda mɔɔkya Katɔti ku bekyuli kunuunu lɛya na ntátaaka-mu teewi egyii lɛlɔ?’

english_verse: Then they asked the fig tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: “Amu na básɔ básu kɔdingyii banini, ‘Bo na ababla bula ɔga.’

english_verse: But the fig tree replied, “I won't stop growing my delicious fruit, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: “Nsu kɔdingyii kúdie kenye ɔnini, ‘Liti mina egyiibi ani ndia na ebo emini mɛni ntátaaka-mu teewi egyii lɛlɔ?’

english_verse: Next they asked the grape vine, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: “Amu na egyii ásu ntɛ kubo ɔnini, ‘Bo na ababla bula ɔga.’

english_verse: But the grape vine replied, “My wine brings cheer to people and gods. I won't stop making wine, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: “Nsu ntɛ kubo kúdie kenye ɔnini, ‘Nda mina ntɛ bɔni bubo emini mɛni bute benwoti ku bekyuli lɛya na liti-nwu nteete egyii?’

english_verse: Finally, they went to the thornbush and asked, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: “Ukplodi ni, egyii ásu liyu egyii ɔnini, ‘Bo na ababla bula ɔga.’

english_verse: The thornbush replied, “If you really want me to be your king, then come into my shade and I will protect you. But if you're deceiving me, I'll start a fire that will spread out and destroy the cedars of Lebanon.” After Jotham had finished telling this story, he said:
translation_verse: “Amu liyu egyii ásu egyii anini, ‘Si sɔsɔ na bɛɛyɔ́ ka lɛbla ɔga lite-mii ni, na bibo na bibabɛ na mina ɔyuli kalɔ. Nsu si bilayɔ-nwu lɛni amu ni, na ogya ɔsi liyu egyii amɛni kemmo na ubakyula bina egyii enengudi ani nnye Lebanon!’ ”

english_verse: My father Gideon risked his life for you when he fought to rescue you from the Midianites. Did you reward Gideon by being kind to his family? No, you did not! You attacked his family and killed all
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmwi bɛ́ta bínye mina ɔti bebi lɛlɔ na bíti lɛtabi linwi pɛ na bɛ́du mina ɔti bebi liti ku aavlanyɔ. Na bíti Abimelek ɔni ndi uleku uyedi ubidi bise Sekem ɔga ka ɔdi bina ɔnwani ɔsu.

english_verse: So, you leaders of Shechem, if you treated Gideon and his family the way you should have, then I hope you and Abimelech will make each other very happy.
translation_verse: Na si lɛla lɛni bɛ́bla ɔmwi mɛni ɔdia na ɔdi ulu lɛlɔ na Yerubaal bebi akɔ ni, na bitaakɛ lɛlɔyɔ na Abimelek lɛlɔ na Abimelek lɛnɔ utaakɛ lɛlɔyɔ na bina lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But if it was wrong to treat Gideon and his family the way you did, then I pray that Abimelech will destroy you with fire, and I pray that you will do the same to him.
translation_verse: Nsu si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, bɛya na ogya ɔsi Abimelek kudɔ na ubakyula Sekem ku Bet-Miloƒuɔ bananabi. Na ami Sekemƒuɔ ku Bet-Milo lɛnɔ bɛya na ogya ɔsi-mii kudɔ na ubakyula Abimelek!”

english_verse: Jotham ran off and went to live in the town of Beer, where he could be safe from his brother Abimelech. Abimelech Destroys Shechem
translation_verse: Amu na Yotam úkeli na útabɛ uli Beer. Ɔsika ɔɔyia ɔnwani Abimelek ɔsu.

english_verse: Abimelech had been a military commander of Israel for three years,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ka Abimelek ɔ́di lɛga na Israel kalɔ akwa atɛ ni,

english_verse: when God decided to punish him and the leaders of Shechem for killing Gideon's
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔ́bla ɔmɛni ɔ́si kalɛ na Abimelek ku Sekem bananabi bákya Abimelek ogya na útádu Gideon bebi liti ku aavlanyɔ, na úti ɔmmɔ ɔƒɔ bana likpidi kayu.

english_verse: Then they sent some men to hide on the hilltops and watch for Abimelech and his troops, while they sent others to rob everyone that went by on the road. But Abimelech found out what they were doing.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bátásu Abimelek ka Sekem banana badi bátábɛ bakya abi eli kalɛ na si Abimelek bekyuli basia ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na beƒie bana ala ani bada baƒɔ.

english_verse: One day, Gaal son of Ebed went to live in Shechem. His brothers moved there too, and soon the leaders of Shechem started trusting him.
translation_verse: Na Ebed ubidi Gaal ku nwuna banwani báva besie Sekem. Na Sekemƒuɔ béti lɛlɔ basia-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The time came for the grape harvest, and the people of Shechem went into their vineyards and picked the grapes. They gathered the grapes and made wine. Then they went into the temple of their god and threw a big party. There was a lot of eating and drinking, and before long they were cursing Abimelech.
translation_verse: Na bana ƒui bésie bana adingyii mmo na bétéde egyiibi na béti bábla ntɛ na báni bádi limeyi. Na bésie bana lɛkpabi lɛni bátu balɛ kudɔ. Na uwi ɔni na bakya baadi na banii teekpi ni, beewida Abimelek.

english_verse: Gaal said: Hamor was the founder of Shechem, and one of his descendants should be our ruler. But Abimelech's father was Gideon, so Abimelech isn't really one of us. He shouldn't be our king, and we shouldn't have to obey him or Zebul, who rules Shechem for him.
translation_verse: Amu na Ebed ubidi Gaal ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔma ndi Abimelek, na ɔma lɛnɔ ndi Sekem ɔni ba bɔkya-nwu kalɔ? Ɔɔdi anwu ndi Gideon ubidi, na Sebul muubunku kabla si uuubo yoo? Ɔlɛka bɛsala ku Hamor kaba bekyuli mmomu. Ɔsika ama ndi Sekem ɔti. Bi ɔsu na bɛmu bɛkya Abimelek kalɔ?”

english_verse: If I were the ruler of Shechem, I'd get rid of that Abimelech. I'd tell him, “Get yourself an even bigger army, and we will still defeat you.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Si bekyuli bamɛni bakya-mi kalɔ ni, nka lɛ́ɛda-nwu lídie na lɛsu Abimelek nnii, ‘Lɔ ƒula bekpone ƒui sala!’ ”

english_verse: Zebul was angry when he found out what Gaal had said.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Sebul ɔni mɔɔnu ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ únu lɛla lɛni na Ebed ubidi Gaal ɔ́su ni, úti kɔnyi geen.

english_verse: This is what I think you should do. Lead your army here during the night and hide in the fields.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu awɔ ku ƒula bekpone bɛta usien na bitábɛ bakya mmo kemmo na bitaatu-ma.

english_verse: Get up the next morning at sunrise and rush out of your hiding places to attack the town. Gaal and his followers will come out to fight you, but you will easily defeat them.
translation_verse: Na si kadi kégye na ɔƒɛ úsela katukɔ ni, bikeli bitéduo ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na si Gaal ku nwuna bekyuli bata banii bebekpoku-mii ni, bɛbla lɛla biala bɛɛyɔ́.”

english_verse: So one night, Abimelech led his soldiers to Shechem. He divided them into four groups, and they all hid near the town.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Abimelek ku nwuna bekpone báta usien na béle lɛlɔ akpa ene na batábɛ kesii kani námanku na Sekem kudɔ.

english_verse: The next morning, Gaal went out and stood in the opening of the town gate. Abimelech and his soldiers left their hiding places,
translation_verse: Na Ebed ubidi Gaal ɔ́ta na uténye kayakun kenengudi kani nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kabanye. Mmɔ kani na Abimelek ku nwuna bekpone bávi bálɛ bana kabɛkɔ.

english_verse: and Gaal saw them. Zebul was standing there with Gaal, and Gaal remarked, “Zebul, that looks like a crowd of people coming down from the mountaintops.” “No,” Zebul answered, “it's just the shadows of the mountains. It only looks like people moving.”
translation_verse: Na ka Gaal ɔ́nu-ma ni, ɔ́su Sebul ɔnini, “Nu! Bekyuli békeli usi bási abi eli badubo.” Amu na Sebul údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdi bekyuli badi, mmomu abi ɔyuli na ɔdi.”

english_verse: “But Zebul, look over there,” Gaal said. “There's a crowd coming down from the sacred mountain, and another group is coming along the road from the tree where people talk with the spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Nsu Gaal ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Nu nii! Bekyuli bási abi eli, na lɛkpa linwi lɛ́si kugyii kubendi kɔni kalɔ na like bebone beelie.”

english_verse: Then Zebul replied, “What good is all of your bragging now? You were the one who said Abimelech shouldn't be the ruler of Shechem. Out there is the army that you made fun of. So go out and fight them!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Sebul ɔ́su Gaal ɔnini, “Wɛ na ƒula lɛmɛnɛ lɛni akya aakun lɛkya? Ɔɔɔdi awɔ néye anini, ‘Bi ɔsu na ɔlɛka bɔkya Abimelek ɔmɛni kalɔ?’ Na ɔɔɔdi awɔ nkya muutemi enyekpi teewi bekyuli bamɛni? Ta na eteesie etékpoku-ma!”

english_verse: Gaal and the leaders of Shechem went out and fought Abimelech.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Gaal ɔ́tɔnku Sekem bekyuli na bétékpoku Abimelek.

english_verse: Soon the people of Shechem turned and ran back into the town. However, Abimelech and his troops were close behind and killed many of them along the way.
translation_verse: Na Abimelek ɔ́bi ɔ́siaku Gaal útédu ɔma kabanye, na bana pii báƒɔ ɔlɛ uwi ɔni na békeli bésela mmɔ.

english_verse: Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul forced Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
translation_verse: Na Abimelek ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kya Aruma, na Sebul ɔ́bɔku Gaal ku nwuna banwani ɔ́lɛku Sekem.

english_verse: The next morning, the people of Shechem were getting ready to work in their fields as usual, but someone told Abimelech about it.
translation_verse: Ka kadi kégye ni, Sekemƒuɔ bésie bana mmo, na badi bésie bátásu Abimelek lɛla lɛni nálɛ.

english_verse: Abimelech divided his army into three groups and set up an ambush in the fields near Shechem. When the people came out of the town, he and his army rushed out from their hiding places and attacked.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu anwu lɛnɔ úti nwuna bekpone na úle-ma akpa atɛ na bátábɛ bákya bana mmo mmɔ. Uwi ɔni na ɔ́nu ka bekyuli bammɔ bálɛ ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo badubo ni, ɔ́ta na útékpoku-ma.

english_verse: Abimelech and the troops with him ran to the town gate and took control of it, while two other groups attacked and killed the people who were in the fields.
translation_verse: Na Abimelek ku nwuna bekpone bani na úle akpa atɛ mmɔ békeli na béténye ɔma ɔmmɔ kabanye. Na akpa anyɔ bábi básiaku bani nkya mmo na ɔ́du-ma.

english_verse: He and his troops fought in Shechem all day, until they had killed everyone in town. Then he and his men tore down the houses and buildings and scattered salt everywhere.
translation_verse: Na Abimelek úti limeyi limodi na ɔkya uukpóku bani nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ útédu ka ɔ́di-ma lɛlɔ na ɔ́du-ma ƒui kede kede. Na ɔ́yila ɔma ɔmmɔ udu, na ɔ́gya mma úyile ɔma ɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo.

english_verse: Earlier that day, the leaders of the temple of El Berith at Shechem had heard about the attack. So they went into the temple fortress,
translation_verse: Na ka Sekem batɔnkune bénu litemi lɛmɛni ni, békeli bésie baƒiɔ Berit katu taasia kagyumanakɔ kpakplaa.

english_verse: but Abimelech found out where they were.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Abimelek únu ka bekyuli bakya mmɔ ni,

english_verse: He led his troops to Mount Zalmon, where he took an ax and chopped off a tree branch. He lifted the branch onto his shoulder and shouted, “Hurry! Cut off a branch just as I did.”
translation_verse: anwu ku bekyuli bani ƒui nkya-nwu kudɔ békeli bésie Salmon Kɔbi eli. Na Abimelek úti oloma na ɔ́da kugyii kɔgba kɔdi na uti-ku ɔsia amangba lɛlɔ. Na úbo nwuna basiakune ɔda ka ɔdi biala ɔbabla na ɔbla kalɛ na bla mmɔ!

english_verse: When they all had branches, they followed Abimelech back to Shechem. They piled the branches against the fortress and set them on fire, burning down the fortress and killing about
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bana ƒui báda egyii kɔgba na béti basia bana amangba na básiaku Abimelek kama. Na béti kɔgba kɔmmɔ ƒui bewi baƒiɔ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na bátu ogya bákya-nwu kemmo. Anwuɔsu bekyuli bani ƒui nkya Sekem baƒiɔ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo békpi. Na banana ku beleku bani nékpi mmɔ badubɔbla aani apim unwi.

english_verse: After destroying Shechem, Abimelech went to Thebez. He surrounded the town and captured it.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Abimelek ɔ́vi úsie Tebes na utáda-ma ɔ́kya na ɔ́di-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But there was a tall fortress in the middle of the town, and the town leaders and everyone else went inside. Then they barred the gates and went up to the flat roof.
translation_verse: Nsu na ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, katu taasia ɔtɔ gyɛnglɛɛ ɔ́di ɔ́lɛ. Na ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli ƒui banana ku beleku békeli betéduo ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo, na bákalɛ lɛlɔ bákya mmɔ. Na bákɔ bésie ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ katɔ.

english_verse: Abimelech and his army rushed to the fortress and tried to force their way inside. Abimelech himself was about to set the heavy wooden doors on fire,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Abimelek ɔ́ni uudé ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kayaku ka utégyingya-ma na ɔtu ogya ɔkya-nwu kemmo ni,

english_verse: when a woman on the roof dropped a large rock on his head and cracked his skull.
translation_verse: uleku ɔdi úti lɛtakpɛ bonwu lɛdi na ɔ́nyonu-ni, na úbaƒiɛmi Abimelek kuli na kɔ́bwɛ.

english_verse: The soldier who carried his weapons was nearby, and Abimelech told him, “Take out your sword and kill me. I don't want people to say that I was killed by a woman!” So the soldier ran his sword through Abimelech.
translation_verse: Amu na Abimelek ɔ́babla na ɔ́kpali nwuna ubunkune ɔni mɔɔda-nwu ala ɔnii ubo. Na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Die ƒula kewii na adu-mi kalɛ na bekyuli bammɔ balasu banii, ‘Uleku nádu-nwu.’ ” Anwuɔsu nwuna ubunkune ɔmmɔ údie nwuna kewii na ɔ́wɔ-nwu ɔ́du.

english_verse: And when the Israelite soldiers saw that their leader was dead, they went back home.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bánu ka Abimelek úkpi ni, bana ƒui bénwini bésie bana kɔduli.

english_verse: That's how God punished Abimelech for killing his brothers and bringing shame on his father's family.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Katɔti ɔ́ƒɔ Abimelek kayu ɔkɛnku likyulikpi lɛni na ɔ́bla na ɔti lɛlɔ ɔsu. Ɔsika ɔ́du nwuna banwani banana liti ku aavlanyɔ.

english_verse: God also punished the people of Shechem for helping Abimelech. Everything happened just as Jotham's curse said it would.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti lɛnɔ ɔ́ƒɔ Sekemƒuɔ kayu ɔkɛnku likyulikpi lɛni bábla ɔsu. Na Gideon ubidi Yotam ewida ani na úwida-ma ébo-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Tola was the next person to rescue Israel. He belonged to the Issachar tribe, but he lived in Shamir, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His father was Puah, and his grandfather was Dodo.
translation_verse: Na Abimelek kukpi kama ni, ukyuli ɔni nási Isakar kɔdua kemmo náta na úkpo ɔ́ƒɔ Israelƒuɔ. Anwu ndi Tola ɔni ɔti ndi Pua ɔni ɔti ndi Dodo. Tola úlie Samir na Eƒraim abi kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Tola was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Na ɔ́tɔnku Israelƒuɔ akwa aavlanyɔ-atɛ na úkpi na báva-nwu na Samir. Yair Lɛlɔ Kɔtɛ

english_verse: The next leader of Israel was Jair, who lived in Gilead. He was a leader for
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama Yair ɔni nási Gilead nábatɔnku-ma. Na ɔ́tɔnku Israelƒuɔ akwa aavlanyɔ-anyɔ.

english_verse: When he died, he was buried in the town of Kamon. Israel Is Unfaithful to God
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Yair úkpi ni, báva-nwu na Kamon. Yeƒta Lɛlɔ Kɔtɛ

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and decided to let Philistia and Ammon conquer them.
translation_verse: Unwoti úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya-ma. Na ɔ́nyonu-ma úte Ƒilistiƒuɔ ku Amonƒuɔ na bakya-ma enu kemmo.

english_verse: So the same year that Jair died, Israel's army was crushed by these two nations. For
translation_verse: Na akwa leevu-maane sɔɔn bekyuli bamɛni bakya baanya Israelƒuɔ bani nlie bésie Yordan ɔƒɛ katukɔ na Gilead, na Amoriƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ taakya, na baabla-ma kalala.
