english_verse: The leaders of Gilead asked each other, “Who can lead an attack on the Ammonites?” Then they agreed, “If we find someone who can lead the attack, we'll make him the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Amu na Gilead batɔnkune básu lɛlɔ banini, “Ukyuli ɔni maka Amonƒuɔ bɔta bukpoku ni, anwu ndubɔbla bula ɔtɔnkune ute bekyuli bani ƒui nlie Gilead.”

english_verse: Then the Ammonites began crossing the Jordan and attacking the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Life was miserable for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Na Amonƒuɔ lɛnɔ bávia Yordan na bétékpoku Yuda ku Benyamin ku Eƒraim adua bekyuli na Israelƒuɔ béduo ɔgbankpi ubendi kemmo.

english_verse: They begged the Lord for help and confessed, “We were unfaithful to you, our Lord. We stopped worshiping you and started worshiping idols of Baal.”
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ béwulo bákpali Unwoti banini, “O Katɔti, bɔ́bla likpidi na ƒula anumi, na búni-ɔ búse, na búsie bɔsiaku Baal baƒiɔ ku bana lidu bamba.”

english_verse: But I'm not going to rescue you any more! You've left me and gone off to worship other gods. If you're in such big trouble, go and cry to them for help!
translation_verse: Biteesie na bitákpali baƒiɔ bani na amii bɛnii ama bɛɛyɔ́ mmɔ. Bɛya na ama baƒɔ-mii si bɛkya bukpoku bɔdi kemmo.”

english_verse: “We have been unfaithful to you,” the Israelites admitted. “If we must be punished, do it yourself, but please rescue us from the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Nsu Israelƒuɔ ama kɔtɔ kani na bakya beekpi Unwoti taasu banini, “Bɔ́bla likpidi na ƒula anumi. Anwuɔsu bla-bu lɛla biala na námanku-bu. Nsu buvele bɔda-a, ƒɔ-bu lɛku bekyuli bamɛni enu kemmo.”

english_verse: Then the Israelites got rid of the idols of the foreign gods, and they began worshiping only the Lord. Finally, there came a time when the Lord could no longer stand to see them suffer. The Ammonites Invade Gilead
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bébo baƒiɔ bani na báƒɔ bése lɛlɔ mmɔ bévaakun, na bése kalɔ baabla Unwoti kabla. Ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔ́sɔ útakana bunye bɔnu Israelƒuɔ abi ani na beebó mmɔ.

english_verse: The rulers of Ammon called their soldiers together and led them to Gilead, where they set up camp. The Israelites gathered at Mizpah and set up camp there.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Amonƒuɔ bekpone básala na besie bákya Gilead ni, na Israelƒuɔ lɛnɔ básala lɛlɔ na besie bakya Mispa.

english_verse: “Didn't you hate me?” Jephthah replied. “Weren't you the ones who forced me to leave my family? You're only coming to me now because you're in trouble.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yeƒta ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdi amii nábɔku-mii bɛ́lɛku mina ɔti kaduli iye ka biikisi-mi ɔsu? Na ɔƒɛni bɛ́ta bíbo-mi kudɔ mɛni ka bɛkya ɔgbankpi kemmo ɔsu, ɔɔɔdi lɛni?”

english_verse: “But we do want you to come back,” the leaders said. “And if you lead us in battle against the Ammonites, we will make you the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Amu básu Yeƒta banini, “Oowo, bulatuna! Ɔmɛni ɔsu búbo-ɔ kudɔ ka abatɔnku-bu na butékpoku Amonƒuɔ. Na ɔƒɛni lɛnɔ adubɔbla ɔtɔnkune ete Gileadƒuɔ ƒui!”

english_verse: “All right,” Jephthah said. “If I go back with you and the Lord lets me defeat the Ammonites, will you really make me your ruler?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yeƒta úye-ma ɔnini, “Ya buti-nwu bɔnii biti-mi na bútekpoku Amonƒuɔ na Unwoti úti-ma ɔkya mina enu kemmo, sɔsɔ na ɔdi ka bɛdubuti-mi bɛbla bina ɔtɔnkune?”

english_verse: “You have our word,” the leaders answered. “And the Lord is a witness to what we have said.”
translation_verse: Amu na Gilead batɔnkune bammɔ básu banini, “Unwoti ɔdubudie-bu kenye ka lɛla biala násu-bu ni, bɔdubɔdi-ni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: So Jephthah went back to Mizpah with the leaders of Gilead. The people of Gilead gathered at the place of worship and made Jephthah their ruler. Jephthah also made promises to them.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yeƒta ku Gilead batɔnkune bammɔ bátɔlɔ, na bábla-nwu bana ɔtɔnkune. Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su ala amɛni ƒui na Unwoti anumi na Mispa.

english_verse: After the ceremony, Jephthah sent messengers to say to the king of Ammon, “Are you trying to start a war? You have invaded my country, and I want to know why!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yeƒta ɔ́tala bekyuli ɔ́kya Amonƒuɔ ɔga ka batásu-nwu banii, “Bi na bɔ́bla-a ɔsu na ébekpoku bula kalɔ bekyuli?”

english_verse: The king of Ammon replied, “Tell Jephthah that the land really belongs to me, all the way from the Arnon River in the south, to the Jabbok River in the north, and west to the Jordan River. When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they stole it. Tell Jephthah to return it to me, and there won't be any war.”
translation_verse: Amu na Amonƒuɔ ɔga údie kenye na ɔ́su Yeƒta batalane bammɔ ɔnini, “Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bálɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, békpeli mina kalɔ kani ntɛ ɔ́si Arnon na ɔ́kɛ Yabok útédu Yordan báƒɔ. Anwuɔsu sɔku mina kalɔ te-mi buɛɛ.”

english_verse: Jephthah sent the messengers back to the king of Ammon,
translation_verse: Na Yeƒta ɔ́ya na batalane bammɔ básɔ bénwini na bátásu Amonƒuɔ ɔga banini, “Lɛni na Yeƒta ɔɔsu!

english_verse: When the Israelites came from Egypt, they traveled across the desert to the Red Sea and then to Kadesh.
translation_verse: Mmomu uwi ɔni bálɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, ketele ulu na bakɛ batáda bálɛ Ɛpugyie na bétédu Kades.

english_verse: They sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, “Please, let us go through your country.” But the king of Edom refused. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he wouldn't let them cross his country either. And so the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Israelƒuɔ bátala bekyuli bákya Edomƒuɔ ɔga banini, ‘Tebu kuƒi na busie bɔvia ƒula kalɔ lɛlɔ.’ Nsu Edomƒuɔ ɔga ɔmɛni úni. Lɛni kani na bátala bekyuli bákya Moabƒuɔ ɔga, na anwu lɛnɔ útatuna. Anwuɔsu Israelƒuɔ básɔ bákya Kades.

english_verse: A little later, the Israelites set out into the desert, going east of Edom and Moab, and camping on the eastern side of the Arnon River gorge. The Arnon is the eastern border of Moab, and since the Israelites didn't cross it, they didn't even set foot in Moab.
translation_verse: “Ɔmmɔ kama básia ketele ulu ɔni ntɛ úsie Edom ku Moab kalɔ, na bakɛ baaka taamana úti útédu ka bédu Moab ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ, na bétélie mmɔ na Arnon Ketudɔ. Na béteduo Moab kalɔ kemmo, ɔsika Arnon ndi bana ɔmii.

english_verse: The Israelites sent messengers to the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. “Please,” they said, “let our people go through your country to get to our own land.”
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ bátala bekyuli bákya Amoriƒuɔ Ɔga Sihon ɔni mɔɔdi lɛga na Hesbon ka batásu-nwu banini, ‘Te-bu kuƒi na bɔsia ƒula ɔma bɔvi busie bula kalɔ lɛlɔ.’

english_verse: towns between Aroer and Minnith, and others as far as Abel-Keramim. After that, the Ammonites could not invade Israel any more. Jephthah's Daughter
translation_verse: Nsu Sihon útete kuƒi na Israelƒuɔ basia bana kalɔ kemmo. Mmomu bɔya na ɔ́ya na nwuna bekpone bátábɛ bakya Yahas na békpoku Israelƒuɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord God helped Israel defeat Sihon and his army. Israel took over all of the Amorite land where Sihon's people had lived,
translation_verse: “Amu na Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti úti Sihon ku nwuna bekpone ƒui ɔ́kya Israelƒuɔ enu kemmo na békpo bádi-ma lɛlɔ. Na Israelƒuɔ béti Amoriƒuɔ kalɔ ƒui

english_verse: The messengers also told the king of Ammon that Jephthah had said: The Lord God of Israel helped his nation get rid of the Amorites and take their land. Now do you think you're going to take over that same territory?
translation_verse: “Ɔƒɛni uwi ɔni na Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti ɔ́bɔku Amoriƒuɔ úte nwuna bekyuli bani ndi Israelƒuɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, bi kuƒi na bibo na biti kalɔ kammɔ?

english_verse: If Chemosh your god takes over a country and gives it to you, don't you have a right to it? And if the Lord takes over a country and gives it to us, the land is ours!
translation_verse: Na biletéti kalɔ kani bina baƒiɔ bani baalɔ banii Kemos úte-mii. Na lɛni kani na bɔdubuti lɛla biala na bula Unwoti Katɔti úte-bu.

english_verse: Are you better than Balak the son of Zippor? He was the king of Moab, but he didn't quarrel with Israel or start a war with us.
translation_verse: Munuu aakali ka áƒɔ kuye etulo Moab Ɔga Balak, Sipor ubidi? Bɔkya na anwu ku Israel bákya unyeƒi iye ɔ́ta úkpoku-ma dii?

english_verse: I haven't done anything to you, but it's certainly wrong of you to start a war. I pray that the Lord will show whether Israel or Ammon is in the right.
translation_verse: Na ɔɔɔdi ami náƒiɔ-mii, mmomu amii náƒiɔ-mi. Ɔsika bɛɛbla kasusu ka bibekpoku-mi. Anwuɔsu bɛya na Unwoti ɔni ndi litemi ɔtɛne geen ɔtɛ litemi lɛni nkya Israelƒuɔ ku Amonƒuɔ ntɛ.”

english_verse: But the king of Ammon paid no attention to Jephthah's message.
translation_verse: Nsu Amonƒuɔ ɔga ɔmɛni útakpete kenye kani batalane bani na Yeƒta ɔ́tala mmɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Jephthah, and Jephthah went through Gilead and Manasseh, raising an army. Finally, he arrived at Mizpah in Gilead, where
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti Kɔyu kɔ́ƒɔ Yeƒta kemmo na ɔ́ta na úsie Gilead ku Manase, na ɔ́vi úsie Gilead-Mispe. Na ka ɔ́si Gilead-Mispe ni, útáda ɔ́lɛ Amonƒuɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: he promised the Lord, “If you will let me defeat the Ammonites
translation_verse: Amu na Yeƒta úse kenye úte Unwoti ɔnini, “Si ákana na éti Amonƒuɔ ákya-mi enu kemmo si bútékpoku-ma ni,

english_verse: and come home safely, I will sacrifice to you whoever comes out to meet me first.”
translation_verse: ndubuti lɛla biala na ndubɔsiaku na mina kayakun kenye lɛbla bɔkyula akpala lite-ɔ uwi ɔni na líbo lɛ́siku Amonƒuɔ kekpokɔ.”

english_verse: From Mizpah, Jephthah attacked the Ammonites, and the Lord helped him defeat them.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yeƒta ɔ́ta na útékpoku Amonƒuɔ, na Unwoti úti-ma ɔ́kya-nwu enu kemmo.

english_verse: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, the first one to meet him was his daughter. She was playing a tambourine and dancing to celebrate his victory, and she was his only child.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Yeƒta ɔ́si úsela nwuna ɔma Mispa ni, ka ɔɔnu ni, aanu ukyuli ɔdi nátási ɔdubo na ɔda kabontobi ɔɔkunku na ɔɔtɔ́. Ubidi ulekubi unwi pɛ ɔni na ɔdi. Ɔsika ɔsɔ uuubo ubi ulekubi iye ɔnanabi ɔdi.

english_verse: “Oh no!” Jephthah cried. Then he tore his clothes in sorrow and said to his daughter, “I made a sacred promise to the Lord, and I must keep it. Your coming out to meet me has broken my heart.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni kani na ɔ́nu-nwu ni, mmɔ kani na ɔ́ni nwuna awu ɔ́bwɛ na úwulo momoomo, na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “O mina ubi, áya na mina lɛlɔ lɛɛdu kɔnyana geen. Ɔsika líse kenye líte Unwoti na naaakana masu nnii naaadi-ka lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: “Father,” she said, “you made a sacred promise to the Lord, and he let you defeat the Ammonites. Now, you must do what you promised, even if it means I must die.
translation_verse: Amu na ubidi ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Ati, awɔ nése kenye éte Unwoti. Anwuɔsu babla-mi kalɛ kani na ásu Unwoti. Ɔsika ɔƒɛni na Unwoti úti ƒula bekisine bani ndi Amonƒuɔ ɔ́kya-a enu kemmo.

english_verse: But first, please let me spend two months, wandering in the hill country with my friends. We will cry together, because I can never get married and have children.”
translation_verse: Nsu buvele nda-a, te-mi kuƒi na lɛkɔ lisie abi ku mina bakpana na betéwuloku-mi abuli anyɔ sɔɔn. Ɔsika nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo kɔgya bulie kudii.”

english_verse: “Yes, you may have two months,” Jephthah said. She and some other girls left, and for two months they wandered in the hill country, crying because she could never get married and have children.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Teesie.” Na anwu ku nwuna bakpana belekubi bésie abi lɛlɔ na béteewuloku-nwu abuli anyɔ. Ɔsika ɔsɔ ɔɔɔdubo kɔgya bulie kudii.

english_verse: Then she went back to her father. He did what he had promised, and she never got married. That's why
translation_verse: Na ka abuli anyɔ ammɔ édu ni, únwini úsie ɔti kudɔ. Na ɔti ɔ́bla-nwu kalɛ kani na úse kenye. Na ubi ɔmmɔ ɔdi adagyaa. Ɔƒɛni ɔ́si uwi ɔmmɔ kama Israelƒuɔ beleku béti lɛla lɛni nálɛ mɛni bábla ɔdi,

english_verse: every year, Israelite girls walk around for four days, weeping for Jephthah's daughter.
translation_verse: ɔni na si lɛkwa biala lídu ni, Israelƒuɔ begblebi baalɛ́ emeyi ene na beesié teetényimo Yeƒta Gileadni ɔmmɔ ubidi ulekubi.

english_verse: The men of the Ephraim tribe got together an army and went across the Jordan River to Zaphon to meet with Jephthah. They said, “Why did you go to war with the Ammonites without asking us to help? Just for that, we're going to burn down your house with you inside!”
translation_verse: Eƒraimƒuɔ banana bálɔ bana bekpone básala na bávia Saƒon na bátásu Yeƒta banini, “Bi ɔsu na ésie na étékpoku Amonƒuɔ na átalɔ-bu na bubebunku-ɔ? Ɔmɛni ɔsu bɔdubo ƒula kaduli bɔkyula bɔsia-a lili.”

english_verse: “But I did ask for your help,” Jephthah answered. “That was back when the people of Gilead and I were having trouble with the Ammonites, and you wouldn't do a thing to help us.
translation_verse: Amu na Yeƒta údie kenye ɔnini, “Kadɔ kebendi kadi kébeduo Amonƒuɔ ku ami ku mina bekyuli ntɛ. Na ina ka liye-ɔ kebunku ni, átakpete-mi na aƒɔ-mi alɛku bana enu kemmo.

english_verse: So when we realized you weren't coming, we risked our lives and attacked the Ammonites. And the Lord let us defeat them. There's no reason for you to come here today to attack me.”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka aaadubo-mi bubunku ni, líti mina ngba lɛ́kpa na lɛ́vi lísie ńtékpoku Amonƒuɔ. Na Unwoti úti-ma ɔ́kya-mi enu kemmo. Na bi ɔsu na bíbo mɛni bibekpoku-mi?”

english_verse: But the men from Ephraim said, “You people of Gilead are nothing more than refugees from Ephraim. You even live on land that belongs to the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh.” So Jephthah called together the army of Gilead, then they attacked and defeated the army from Ephraim.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yeƒta ɔ́lɔ nwuna bekpone bani nkya Gilead ɔ́sala na bétékpoku Eƒraimƒuɔ. Na Gileadƒuɔ bádu-ma kaduɛ, ɔsika básu banii, “Amii Gileadƒuɔ, bɛ́mami lɛlɔ bɛ́lɛku Eƒraimƒuɔ ku Manaseƒuɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The army of Gilead also posted guards at all the places where the soldiers from Ephraim could cross the Jordan River to return to their own land. Whenever one of the men from Ephraim would try to cross the river, the guards would say, “Are you from Ephraim?” “No,” the man would answer, “I'm not from Ephraim.”
translation_verse: Na kalɛ na Eƒraimƒuɔ békeli ɔsu ni, Gileadƒuɔ békpo báƒɔ kesii kani na baasia taavia Yordan Ketu. Na si Eƒraim ɔdi ɔɔwia ka ubavi na uvele kuƒi ni, na Gileadƒuɔ banana beeye-nwu banini, “Eƒraimni na adi?” Na ɔdubɔsu ɔnini, “Oowo.”

english_verse: The guards would then tell them to say “Shibboleth,” because they knew that people of Ephraim could say “Sibboleth,” but not “Shibboleth.” If the man said “Sibboleth,” the guards would grab him and kill him right there. Altogether,
translation_verse: Mmɔ na baasu-nwu ka ɔlɔ “Shibolet.” Nsu ɔdubɔsu ɔnii, “Sibolet.” Ɔsika ulakana lɛnyi lɛmmɔ bɔlɔ kaduɛ. Mmɔ kani na beeƒie-nwu na badu-nwu na kesii kani baavia Yordan mmɔ. Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, bádu Eƒraimƒuɔ bekyuli mpim aavlene-inyɔ.

english_verse: Jephthah was a leader of Israel for six years, before he died and was buried in his hometown Mizpah in Gilead. Ibzan
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Yeƒta ɔ́tɔnku Israelƒuɔ akwa aku, asa na úkpi na báva-nwu na nwuna ɔma ɔni ndi Gilead. Ibsan Ku Elon Ku Abdon Lɛlɔ Litemi

english_verse: Ibzan, the next leader of Israel, came from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Yeƒta kukpi kama ni, Ibsan ɔni nási Betlehem úbatɔnku Israelƒuɔ.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Bethlehem. Elon
translation_verse: Amu na Ibsan úkpi na báva-nwu na Betlehem.

english_verse: Elon from the Zebulun tribe was the next leader of Israel. He was a leader for ten years,
translation_verse: Ibsan kama ni, Sebulonni Elon ɔ́tɔnku Israelƒuɔ akwa leevu.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Aijalon that belonged to the Zebulun tribe. Abdon
translation_verse: Na ka úkpi ni, báva-nwu na Ayalon na Sebulon kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Abdon the son of Hillel was the next leader of Israel. He had
translation_verse: Na Abdon ɔni ndi Hilel ubi ɔmɛni úkpi na báva-nwu na Piraton na Eƒraim kalɔ kani nkya Amalekƒuɔ abi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let the Philistines take control of Israel for
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ básɔ bábla likpidi na Unwoti anumi. Ɔmɛni ɔsu Unwoti ɔ́nyonu-ma ɔkya Ƒilistiƒuɔ enu kemmo akwa aavlene sɔɔn.

english_verse: Manoah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zorah. His wife was not able to have children,
translation_verse: Na okloƒu ɔdi ɔ́kya na ɔ́si Sora na ɔ́si Dan kɔdua kemmo na baalɔ-nwu banii Manoa, na ulekudi ɔdi udinkɔ.

english_verse: She went to Manoah and said, “A prophet who looked like an angel of God came and talked to me. I was so frightened, that I didn't even ask where he was from. He didn't tell me his name,
translation_verse: Amu uleku ɔmɛni únwini úsie ɔgyani kudɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Katɔti ukyuli ɔdi úbo-mi kudɔ. Na ukyuli ɔmɛni ɔ́lɛ Katɔti ɔtu ɔdi. Na ka ɔɔda liƒu ɔsu ni, ńtakana na liye-nwu nwuna lɛnyi ku kesii kani ɔ́si.

english_verse: but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
translation_verse: Nsu bɔsu kani na ɔ́su-mi ɔnii ndubo kaƒɔ bɔda na lɛwɔ ɔnanabi. Ɔƒɛni ntani ntɛ kpakplaa iye ntɛ biala. Na ntadi adila ani muusé lɛlɔ lɛnɔ. Ɔsika ubi ɔmmɔ ɔdubunwini Unwoti ukyuli ɔƒunadi ɔ́si nwuna bɔwɔ uwi úti útédu nwuna kukpi uwi.”

english_verse: Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Manoa ɔkpali Katɔ úvele Unwoti ɔnini, “O Unwoti, ya na ƒula ɔtu ɔni na átala mmɔ ɔsɔ ubo na ubatina-bu ulu ɔni lɛlɔ bɔdubɔsia na bɔnyuɛ ubi ɔmmɔ si báwɔ-nwu.”

english_verse: God answered Manoah's prayer, and the angel went back to Manoah's wife while she was resting in the fields. Manoah wasn't there at the time,
translation_verse: Na sɔsɔ ni, Katɔti únu Manoa bɔkpali na Katɔti ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ úbo ulekudi kudɔ uwi ɔni na ɔkya kemo. Nsu uwi ɔmmɔ na ɔgyani Manoa uuubo mmɔ.

english_verse: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na uleku ɔmɛni ɔ́babla na úkeli útásu ɔgyani ka, “Katɔti ɔtu ɔni nédie lɛlɔ ɔ́tina-mi dii mmɔ ɔ́sɔ úbo.”

english_verse: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
translation_verse: Na Manoa ɔ́ta na ɔ́siaku ulekudi kama. Na uwi ɔni báni béde ɔtu ɔmmɔ ni, Manoa úye-nwu ɔnini, “Awɔ ndi ɔtu ɔni nátɛmi-ku mina ulekudi?” Na ɔtu ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnii, “Ɛɛn, ami mmɔ.”

english_verse: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
translation_verse: Amu na Manoa úye ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Si úbo úte lɛni ni, bi na ubi ɔmmɔ ɔdubo bɔbla? Na bi ngba udu ɔdubo bulie?”

english_verse: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
translation_verse: Na ɔtu ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Ƒ'ulekudi ɔdi ka ɔbla ɔsia lɛla biala na lɛ́su-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: “She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
translation_verse: Na anya ndi ka útalɛka ɔdi lɛla biala na bébulo iye ɔni ntɛ kpakplaa iye ntɛ bɔdi biala iye ɔdi adila ani muusé lɛlɔ biala. Na ɔlɛka ɔdi ɔda ɔni ƒui líbo-nwu lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: “Please,” Manoah said, “stay here with us for just a little while, and we'll fix a young goat for you to eat.”
translation_verse: Amu na Manoa ɔ́su Unwoti ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Tatɔlɔ útédu ka bɔ́du ese ɔkɔdi na búti bɔ́nwa adila adi bute-ɔ.”

english_verse: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔtu ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Ina ka bɛ́ƒɔ-mi bɛ́kya mɛni ni, lɛɛɛdubo bina adila adi bɔdi. Nsu si bɔkyula akpala bɛdubɔbla amu ni, na biti akpala ammɔ bite Unwoti.” Na Manoa útati ɔnii Unwoti Ɔtu na ɔdi.

english_verse: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Manoa úye ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Su-bu ƒula lɛnyi kalɛ na si ƒula litemi líbo líte lɛni ni, bɔdubɔkɔliku-ɔ lɛnyi katɔ.”

english_verse: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
translation_verse: Na ɔtu ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na aawia mina lɛnyi ati? Ɔmmɔ uuubo kalɔ bunu.”

english_verse: So Manoah took a young goat over to a large rock he had chosen for an altar, and he built a fire on the rock. Then he killed the goat, and offered it with some grain as a sacrifice to the Lord. But then an amazing thing happened.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Manoa úti ese ɔkɔdi ku ɔlaaƒɔ, na úti ɔ́bla akpala na lɛtakpɛ lɛdi lɛlɔ úte Unwoti. Na Unwoti ɔ́bla akɔla budie taatina bɔdi na Manoa ku ulekudi anumi.

english_verse: The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na baakyula akpala ammɔ na aada taakɔ katɔ ni, Unwoti ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́sia ogya ɔmmɔ kemmo úsie katɔ. Ka Manoa ku ulekudi bánu lɛla lɛni nálɛ mmɔ ni, báyu bátɛ na béti bana anumi bébi kalɔ.

english_verse: Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels.
translation_verse: Na ka Unwoti ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ útedie lɛlɔ útatina Manoa ku ulekudi ni, mmɔ na bánu báti ka Unwoti ɔtu na ɔdi.

english_verse: Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
translation_verse: Amu na Manoa ɔ́su ulekudi ɔnii, “Bɔdubo bukpi, ɔsika búti bula anumi bɔ́nu Katɔti.”

english_verse: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
translation_verse: Nsu ulekudi udie kenye ɔnini, “Si banii Unwoti bɔbla na ɔbla kasusu ka wadu-bu ni, nka útaƒɔ bula akpala ani bɔ́bla búte-nwu. Iye nka útasu-bu ala ani na ɔ́su-bu mɛni na udie lɛla lɛdi ɔtina-bu.”

english_verse: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
translation_verse: Amu na uleku ɔmɛni úbawɔ ubi ɔnanabi na ɔ́sia-nwu lɛnyi ɔnii Simson. Na ɔnanabi ɔmɛni ɔ́lɛ lili na Unwoti úte-nwu kusɛ kusɛ.

english_verse: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti Kɔyu kúse kalɔ kɔɔƒɔ́-nwu lɛlɔ kemmo uwi ɔni na ɔkya Dan kalɛkɛ, na Sora ku Estaol ntɛ.

english_verse: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
translation_verse: Amu na Simson ɔ́vi úsie Timna. Na mmɔ ɔ́nu Ƒilistini ugblebi ɔdi.

english_verse: When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na únwini úsie ɔti ku uni kudɔ ni, ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Lɛ́nu Ƒilistini ugblebi ɔdi na Timna. Anwuɔsu bitévele-nwu bite-mi na liti-nwu.”

english_verse: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Na ɔti ku uni béye-nwu banini, “Uleku ɔdi uuubo na ɔɔdia bɔnu na ɔmanku-ɔ na bula ɔtɔ kemmo? Iye ɔdi uuubo na bula kadi akɔ? Bi ɔsu na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bani neeekulo ago mɛni kudɔ na adubusie etéti uleku?” Nsu Simson únye ɔti lɛlɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Tévele-nwu te-mi. Ɔsika anwu námanku-mi.”

english_verse: At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ƒui na nwuna bawɔne baagyi ka ala amɛni ƒui ási Unwoti kudɔ. Na Unwoti ɔɔwia kuƒi kɔni na ɔsia na ukpoku Ƒilistiƒuɔ. Ɔsika uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, na Ƒilistiƒuɔ mɔɔdi Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson.
translation_verse: Na Simson ku ɔti ku uni báta na bésie Timna. Uwi ɔni badaku adingyii kemo kadi nde Timna budu ni, kɔnakunwi gyata ɔkɔdi ɔ́da ɔ́lɛ na ɔ́ƒulu úsie Simson kudɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti Kɔyu kúbeduo Simson lɛlɔ kemmo ku ɔyikun, na úƒie gyata ɔmmɔ ɔ́duli aani kalɛ na baaduli ese ubi. Nsu útasu ɔti iye uni lɛla lɛni na ɔ́bla.

english_verse: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na úsie uleku ɔmmɔ kudɔ na báda kɔtɛ, ɔsika nwuna lɛlɔ lɛɛda-nwu kubiti.

english_verse: Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔdi kama Simson únwini úsie ɔnii utéti ulekudi ɔmmɔ. Na ka údu kesii kani na ɔ́du gyata ɔmmɔ ni, únwini ɔ́nu gyata ekubi ka ewi mmɔ na banwɛnwɛ bakya-nwu kemmo na uwɔ úyi-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
translation_verse: Na údie ɔdi na ɔda ɔɔdi na nwuna ulu busie kemmo. Na uwi ɔni na útásiaku nwuna bawɔne ni, úte-ma na ama lɛnɔ bádi ɔdi. Nsu útasu-ma ka gyata ekubi ani nákwi ewi kemmo na údie uwɔ ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
translation_verse: Na Simson ɔti úsie ulekubi ɔmɛni kaduli, na Simson ɔ́ya na bádi limeyi béte ulekudi aani kalɛ na bana ɔdi ɔɔtina ka babla bete uleku utidi.

english_verse: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
translation_verse: Ka Ƒilistiƒuɔ bánu Simson ni, bédie nkyuli avlaatɛ ka betélie-nwu kudɔ.

english_verse: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
translation_verse: Na si bítakana agyolo ammɔ kalɔ budie ni, na amii lɛnɔ bɛdubute-mi adi abuni avlaatɛ ku lɛwu lɛbuni avlaatɛ.” Amu bekyuli bammɔ básu Simson banini, “Tu agyolo ammɔ boku!”

english_verse: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
translation_verse: Mmɔ Simson úse agyolo amɛni kalɔ ku bɔtu ɔnini, “Ɔdivone kemmo na lɛdila lɛ́si, na ɔlɔkplune kemmo na emini álɛ.” Nsu emeyi atɛ sɔɔn bekyuli bamɛni batakana agyolo amɛni kalɔ budie.

english_verse: Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
translation_verse: Na limeyi linedi lɛlɔ bekyuli bammɔ bésie Simson ulekudi kudɔ na básu-nwu banini, “Tɔlɔ ƒ'ɔgyani na udie agyolo ammɔ kalɔ ɔtina-a na asu-bu. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni bɔdubo awɔ ku ƒula ɔti kaduli bɔkyula bɔsala.” Na béye ulekubi ɔmmɔ banii, “Munuu buti na éti ɔnanabi ɔmɛni éboku anii ubeyu-bu?”

english_verse: Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.” “But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Simson ulekudi úsie Simson kudɔ na ɔ́da keku, na úƒwimi lɛlɔ útava ɔgyani lɛlɔ, na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Mɔɔnu geen ka ɔɔɔdi ƒula kayi kemmo na éti aayɔ́-mi. Ɔsika átu agyolo adi éte mina bekyuli, nsu ami amu átasu-mi na edie-nya kalɔ atina-mi.” Amu na Simson ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Agyolo amɛni ni, ńtedie-nya kalɔ ńtatina mina ɔti ku uni muedi. Anwuɔsu bi ɔsu na ɔlɛka lidie-nya kalɔ lɛtina?”

english_verse: For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ulekudi ɔmɛni úwulo emeyi maatɛ ani ƒui bakya baadi limeyi mmɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ Simson údie agyolo amɛni kalɔ ɔ́tina ulekudi, ka únye-nwu lɛlɔ ɔsu. Na ulekudi ɔmɛni úkeli úsie útásu nwuna bekyuli agyolo amɛni kalɔ.

english_verse: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
translation_verse: Asa na ɔƒɛ ɔdubuduo nwuna lɛyu kemmo limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli básu Simson banini, “Bi ndubɔyu ɔkplu butulo gyata?” Mmɔ na Simson údie kenye ɔnini, “Si ɔɔɔdi mina ɔmantɛ akɔ na bɛda biinwíni kalɔ ni, nka úti úbedu ɔƒaani ni, bilakana agyolo ammɔ kalɔ budie!”

english_verse: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
translation_verse: Na béti Simson ulekudi béte ɔkpana ɔni bédie béte Simson na nwuna ulekudi ketikɔ.

english_verse: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Simson ɔnini, “Lɛ́ɛƒɔ lɛ́di geen ka eekisi uleku ɔmmɔ, anwuɔsu líti-nwu líte ƒula ɔkpana. Nsu ɔnamudi ɔkya, na ɔɔdia bɔnu teetulo-nwu ƒui. Anwuɔsu akana eti anwu mmomu.”

english_verse: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
translation_verse: Amu na Simson ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔƒɛni ukyuli biala ɔsɔ uládu-mi kɔtɔ na lɛla lɛni ndubo Ƒilistiƒuɔ bamɛni bɔbla lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
translation_verse: Na úti beƒukutu bammɔ anumi ɔ́tina Ƒilistiƒuɔ edula mmo na ɔ́nyonu-ma. Na békeli bétéduo-mu kemmo. Na ogya úduo mmo bɔmmɔ ƒui na bɔ́kywi. Na ogya ɔmmɔ ɔ́vi útákyula bana adingyii ku bana nnɔ egyii mmo lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒilistiƒuɔ béye banii, “Ɔma nábla udu ɔmɛni?” Na básu-ma ka Simson ɔni ndi Timnani ɔmmɔ ubidi ɔgyani nábla udu ɔmmɔ. Ɔsika békpeli ulekudi báƒɔ béte nwuna ɔkpana ɔsu. Anwuɔsu Ƒilistiƒuɔ bésie na bátákyula uleku ɔmmɔ ku ɔti lɛnɔ.

english_verse: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
translation_verse: Na Simson ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔ́si lɛla lɛni na bɛ́bla mɛni ɔsu ni, lɛɛɛdubo-mii bɔda bukpoku bɔya úti útédu ka bɛ́ƒɔ-mi kayu ƒui.”

english_verse: Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword. Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock.
translation_verse: Na úkpoku-ma kaduɛ na ɔ́du-ma pii. Amu na úsie útélie atakpɛ ubu ɔdi kemmo na Etan. Simson Úkpo Ɔ́di Ƒilistiƒuɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒilistiƒuɔ báta bétékpoku Yudaƒuɔ na kesii kani nde Lehi. Na Yuda bekyuli béye-ma banini, “Bi ɔsu na bɛ́ta bíbekpoku-bu?”

english_verse: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na nkyuli mpim ɛtɛ bási Yuda na bésie Etan na bátánu Simson na atakpɛ ubu ɔni kemmo ɔ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ ɔkya mmɔ. Na básu-nwu banini, “Aaagyi ka Ƒilistiƒuɔ kalɔ na bɔkya na ama mɔɔdi-bu lɛlɔ yoo? Na bi ɔsu na ábla-bu lɛni?” Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Lɛla lɛni bábla-mi ni, ani kani na ami lɛnɔ lɛ́bla-ma.”

english_verse: “We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah. “I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na básu-nwu banini, “Búbo ka bubenyimi-ɔ na buti-ɔ butákya Ƒilistiƒuɔ enu kemmo.” Amu na Simson ɔ́su-ma ɔnii, “Bise kenye ka amii alati biládu-mi.”

english_verse: “We promise,” the men said. “We will only tie you up and turn you over to the Philistines. We won't kill you.” Then they tied up his hands and arms with two brand-new ropes and led him away from Etam Rock. When the Philistines saw that Samson was being brought to their camp at Jawbone, they started shouting and ran toward him. But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and Samson broke the ropes, as though they were pieces of burnt cloth.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na badaku Lehi budu ni, Ƒilistiƒuɔ bálɛ bébo ku kɔvanu. Mmɔ na Unwoti Kɔyu kɔ́ƒɔ Simson lɛlɔ kemmo ku ɔyikun. Na kɔbuli kɔni béti bényimi-nwu enu mmɔ kɔ́bla aani kɔbuli kɔni ogya ɔ́kyula-ku. Na kɔ́lɛ-nwu enu kemmo kúwi kalɔ.

english_verse: Samson glanced around and spotted the jawbone of a donkey. The jawbone had not yet dried out, so it was still hard and heavy. Samson grabbed it and started hitting Philistines—he killed
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́nu ebuo ala utine ɔnungla likubi lɛdi ni, úti-ni na ɔ́du bekyuli apim unwi.

english_verse: After the fighting was over, he made up this poem about what he had done to the Philistines: I used a donkey's jawbone to kill a thousand men; I beat them with this jawbone over and over again.
translation_verse: Amu na Simson ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ka líti ebuo ala utine likubi linwi ni, lɛ́kɛ ekubi ammɔ pii. Na ka líti ebuo ala utine ɔnungla likubi linwi ni, lɛ́du nkyuli apim unwi.”

english_verse: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́tɛmi ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, úbo ebuo ala utine likubi lɛmmɔ úvaakun. Na kesii kani na ala ammɔ álɛ mmɔ baalɔ banii Ramat-Lehi.

english_verse: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
translation_verse: Na ka utukwɛ úbo ɔɔda Simson ɔsu ni, úwulo ɔ́kpali Unwoti ɔnini, “Awɔ náya na ƒula kabla ɔblane úkpo ɔ́di lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu bunye na adubunye anu na utukwɛ ɔdu-mi na anyonu-mi akya bekyuli bani neeekulo ago mɛni enu kemmo?”

english_verse: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́ya na kalɔ kébimi na Lehi mmɔ, na ntu bɔ́bwɛ bɔlɛ mmɔ. Na Simson ɔ́ni ntu bɔmmɔ na úse kalɔ ɔɔkɛ́ lɛlɔkplu. Ɔmɛni ɔsu básia libiɔ lɛmmɔ lɛnyi banii En-Hakore. Na libiɔ lɛmmɔ lɛmu lɛkya Lehi mmɔ úbedu ɔmwi kadi.

english_verse: years, but the Philistines were still the rulers of Israel.
translation_verse: Simson ɔ́tɔnku Israelƒuɔ akwa aavlanyɔ na Ƒilistiƒuɔ uwi ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bátásu Gasaƒuɔ banini, “Simson úbo ɔkya Gasa mɛni.” Ɔmɛni ɔsu bekyuli bamɛni bábɛ na báka bámana kesii kani na Simson ɔ́kya mmɔ. Na badi benye ɔma ɔmmɔ kayaku bagya-nwu. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu básu lɛlɔ banini, “Usien lɛdibantɛ kemmo bɔdubɔdu-nwu.”

english_verse: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔdi kama Simson úbanu ugblebi ɔni nlie Sorek Kɔwɛ kemmo na baalɔ-nwu banii Delila. Ka ɔ́nu ugblebi ɔmɛni ni, na ɔɔyɔ́-nwu.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you
translation_verse: Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ benengu bákpɛ béde ugblebi ɔmɛni na básu-nwu banini, “Sia ulu biala lɛlɔ na atɔlɔ Simson na ɔsu-ɔ kesii kani na ɔ́kɛ nwuna ɔyikun bonwu ɔmɛni ɔ́siku. Na abu bɔdubɔwia ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na bɔdubɔsia na bunyimi-nwu na buboku-nwu kalɔ. Na bula ƒui ɔdi biala ɔdubute-ɔ sika ɔƒualadi ebi apim unwi ku eti anyɔ.”

english_verse: The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Delila ɔ́su Simson ɔnini, “Su-mi kesii kani na aakɛ́ ƒula ɔyikun bonwu ɔmmɔ taasiku ku kalɛ si bényimi-ɔ ni, na alakana bukpo bɔlɛ.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Amu na Simson údie kenye ɔnini, “Si ukyuli ɔdi úti kɔbuli kɔwɔdi maatɛ kɔni nátakwii tɔ únyimi-mi ni, ndubɔbla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ aani ukyuli keeke biala.”

english_verse: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Delila ɔ́su Simson ɔnini, “Ábu-mi kɔdɔlɔ na átɔlɔ-mi. Bo mɛni na asu-mi kalɛ ɔlɛka benyimi-ɔ.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su Delila ɔnini, “Si ukyuli ɔdi úti kɔbuli kɔwɔdi kɔni na béteti bátabla lɛla lɛdi kudii na bényimi-mi kpakplaa ni, ndubɔbla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ aani ukyuli keeke biala.”

english_verse: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Delila úti kɔbuli kɔwɔdi na únyimi-nwu. Na bekyuli badi bábɛ bakya ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo mmɔ. Na uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpali-nwu ɔ́su ɔnini, “Simson, Ƒilistiƒuɔ bási badubo.” Nsu úkulo kɔbuli kɔmmɔ ɔ́lɛku nwuna enu kemmo aani kalɛ na beekúlo unwo kabuli.

english_verse: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Amu na Delila ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Simson ɔnini, “Uwi ɔmɛni ƒui ni, akya aabu-mi kɔdɔlɔ na aanyi ɔkɔ taatina-mi. Anwuɔsu su-mi kalɛ na ɔlɛka benyimi-ɔ.” Mmɔ na Simson ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Si ébo mina lili linwini lɛni bámii báda lɛlɔ maatɛ mɛni áda kɔdi kɔni nkya bedine ɔkɔlɔ kemmo ni, ndubɔbla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ aani ukyuli keeke biala.” Anwuɔsu uwi ɔni na Simson ɔtɛ ɔɔlɛɛ ni, Delila úbo nwuna linwini lɛni na bámii maatɛ mmɔ ɔ́da kɔdi kɔni nkya ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: While Samson was asleep, Delilah wove his braids into the threads on a loom and nailed the loom to a wall. Then she shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson woke up and pulled the loom free from its posts in the ground and from the nails in the wall. Then he pulled his hair free from the woven cloth.
translation_verse: Na úti ugyii ɔni mɔɔbala ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ ɔ́kya kabalakɔ. Amu na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kpali-nwu ɔnini, “Ƒilistiƒuɔ bási badubo!” Mmɔ na Simson ɔ́gyinya kɔnakunwi, na úkulo kɔbuli kɔni bébo báda ligyii lɛlɔ mmɔ údie.

english_verse: “Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.”
translation_verse: Amu na Delila úye Simson ɔnini, “Dɛ na akana asu anii aayɔ́-mi uwi ɔni na alasu-mi ƒula litemi geen mɛni? Ɔsika kɔtɛ sɔɔn mɛni na adaku-mi kɔdɔlɔ bɔbu. Na átakana na asu-mi kesii kani na ƒula ɔyikun bonwu ɔmɛni ɔɔsí teebo.”

english_verse: Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
translation_verse: Na Delila ɔkya uukpóku Simson limeyi ndi limeyi na litemi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ úti útédu ka lɛlɔ lítu-nwu na ɔ́su ɔnii si nka úkpi muedi ni, ɔdia-nwu utulo.

english_verse: Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔ́su Delila lɛla biala ɔnini, “Ɔ́si mina lɛwɔmeyi ni, béteti lɛla lɛdi bétekpeyi-mi linwini kudii. Ɔsika ndi Katɔti ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́ƒuna úte lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.” The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her.
translation_verse: Na ka Delila ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka Simson ɔ́su-nwu lɛla biala ni, ɔ́tala bekyuli ɔ́kya Ƒilistiƒuɔ benengu ka bátásu-ma banii, “Bɛsɔ binwini bibo kɔkladi, ɔsika ɔƒɛni na Simson ɔ́su-mi lɛla biala.” Anwuɔsu Ƒilistiƒuɔ benengu bamɛni báta na béti sika ɔƒualadi báda.

english_verse: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
translation_verse: Amu na Delila úti Simson lili ɔ́sia nwuna ebuli lɛlɔ na ɔ́ya na ɔ́lɛɛ. Mmɔ na ɔ́lɔ ɔnana ɔdi na úbekpeyi nwuna kɔgyasu maatɛ kɔmmɔ. Na úse kalɔ ɔɔwiɛ, na nwuna ɔlɔkplu lɛnɔ ɔɔbla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bébo báda-nwu na bákpa-nwu anumi, na béti abuala egyiedi bábla kabuli na bényimi-nwu, na béti-nwu bésienku Gasa. Na bátákya-nwu ɔtɔ na mmɔ. Na báya na anwu mɔɔkɔ́ kukɔ na ɔtɔ katɛnkɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
translation_verse: Nsu uwi útetu asa na Simson linwini líse kalɔ lɛɛkwɛ́. Simson Úkpi

english_verse: The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said: Samson was our enemy, but our god Dagon helped us capture him!
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒilistiƒuɔ batɔnkune bábasa lisu ka babla akpala bete bana baƒiɔ bani baalɔ banii Dagon, na badi limeyi. Ɔsika baasu banii, “Bula baƒiɔ bamɛni néti Simson ɔni ndi bula ukisine ɔ́kya-bu enu kemmo.”

english_verse: A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
translation_verse: Simson ɔ́su ukyuli ɔni néti-nwu utényene lɛkpa lɛmmɔ kudɔ mmɔ ɔnini, “Ti-mi tényene lɛkpa lɛni nda ɔtɔ ɔmɛni kpakplaa kudɔ, na lɛkada likpo-nwu lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Simson ɔ́kpali Katɔti úvele-nwu ɔnini, “O Ɔyikune ƒui Unwoti, nyimo-mi. Na buvele nda-a, kya-mi ɔlɔkplu kɔkladi kɔmɛni. O Katɔti, ya na lɛbla Ƒilistiƒuɔ kalala kani bábla-mi ɔkɛnku mina anumi ani bákpa ɔsu.”

english_verse: Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand.
translation_verse: Amu na Simson ɔ́kpɛ úde akpa anyɔ ani nda ɔtɔ umodi ɔmmɔ. Na ka úti kayi úkpo-nya lɛlɔ ni, úti nwuna kɔmii úƒie lɛkpa linwi ɔ́da. Na úƒie linyɔdi lɛnɔ ɔ́da ku nwuna kɔdianu.

english_verse: Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Simson ɔ́su lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Ami ku Ƒilistiƒuɔ bɔdubo bukpi bɔsala.” Anwuɔsu úti nwuna ɔyikun ƒui na ɔ́kunku akpa ammɔ, na ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ƒui ɔ́ƒɛ ɔ́yu batɔnkune bammɔ ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu Simson ɔ́du bekyuli na nwuna kukpi uwi útulo uwi ɔni na úlie ngba.

english_verse: His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Amu na nwuna banwani bananabi ku ɔti bene ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli bésie na bététi nwuna ukpine. Na bénwini bátáva-nwu na Sora ku Estaol ntɛ, na ɔti Manoa kaƒiɔtɔ kudɔ. Na Simson ɔ́tɔnku Israelƒuɔ akwa aavlanyɔ.

english_verse: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.” But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took
translation_verse: Amu ka Mika úti sika ɔƒualadi ɔmɛni úsienku uni ni, uni úti sika ɔƒualadi ebi eti ene, na úti úte ɔkywɛne ɔdi ka uti ɔvɔ kɔlɛmii ute-nwu. Na ɔkywɛne ɔmmɔ ɔ́bla ala ammɔ úte-nwu, na Mika úti-nya útése nwuna kaduli.

english_verse: He had a shrine for worshiping God there at his home, and he had made some idols and a sacred priestly vest. Micah chose one of his own sons to be the priest for his shrine.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mika ɔmɛni úse baƒiɔ úte lɛlɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu úti ubidi ɔnana unwi na ɔ́ka ɔkpane awu úte-nwu, na úti-nwu úse baƒiɔ bammɔ kenye aani ɔkpane kalɛ.

english_verse: This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo ni, na Israelƒuɔ beeebo ɔga ɔdi. Anwuɔsu ukyuli biala ɔɔbla lɛla lɛni mɔɔyɔ́-nwu kaƒɔ.

english_verse: One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
translation_verse: Okloƒu ɔmɛni ɔ́tɔlɔ bekyuli bammɔ kudɔ ka utáwia kesii bamba kadi ulie. Ka ɔkɛ ɔɔví ni, útáda ɔ́lɛ Mika kaduli na Eƒraim abi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: “Where are you from?” Micah asked. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
translation_verse: Na Mika úye-nwu ɔnini, “Wɛ na ási ébo mɛni?” Amu na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Lewini na ndi, na lɛ́si Betlehem. Na nkɛ mɔɔví taawia kesii kadi na lilie.”

english_verse: Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.” The young man went for a walk,
translation_verse: Amu na Mika ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Bo na ebelie-mi kudɔ na ndubuti-ɔ bɔbla mina ɔti ku ɔkpane. Na ndubuteete-ɔ adila ku adala. Na lɛkwa biala lɛnɔ ndubutaaƒɔ-ɔ sika ɔƒualadi ebi leevu.”

english_verse: then he agreed to stay with Micah and be his priest. He lived in Micah's house, and Micah treated him like one of his own sons.
translation_verse: Mika úse okloƒu ɔmɛni likpo na úbenwini nwuna ɔkpane, na ɔ́ƒɔ-nwu ɔ́kya nwuna kaduli.

english_verse: Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mika ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔmwi ni, ngyi ka Unwoti ɔdubo-mi lɛƒɔndia lɛdi bɔbla. Ɔsika Lewini ɔmɛni únweni mina ɔkpane.”

english_verse: These things happened before kings ruled Israel. The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo Israelƒuɔ beeebo ɔga ɔdi tɔ. Na emeyi amɛni kemmo kani na Dan kɔdua bekyuli lɛnɔ báta na bakɛ baaví taawia kesii kani bada bana keliekɔ. Ɔsika kɔnu kútetuku-ma tɔ bana kadikɔ na Israelƒuɔ adua kemmo.

english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Dan kɔdua bekyuli bamɛni bédie bekpone ɛlɔ básiku bana kaduli kemmo na bási Sore ku Estaol lɛma kemmo. Na bébo-ma ɔda ka besie na betéyu bana kalɔ kammɔ banu. Bekyuli bamɛni benye béte kaba kammɔ ɔtɔ bekyuli ƒui. Ka bétéduo ɔma ɔni nwi Eƒraim abi eli ni, bátálɛlɛ Mika kaduli.

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bakya mmɔ ni, bábanu Lewini okloƒu ɔdi báti. Ɔmɛni ɔsu bákpɛ béde-nwu na béye-nwu banini, “Bi na aabla mɛni? Na ɔma lɛnɔ néti-ɔ úboku mɛni?”

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: Na údie kenye ɔnini, “Ami ku Mika nátɛmi na línu kalɔ ka mabla ɔkpane mete-nwu na utaaƒɔ-mi kayu.”

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Na batu bammɔ bévele ɔkpane ɔmmɔ banini, “Ye siku Katɔti kudɔ si bula ulu busie ɔdubɔdia ute-bu?”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛla biala liiibo na lɛdubukpoku-mii. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔkya ɔɔgyumana-mii na bina ulu busie bɔmɛni kemmo.”

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu nkyuli ɛlɔ bamɛni bátɔlɔ na béduo ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Lais. Na bánu kalɛ na bekyuli bammɔ belie ƒaa aani Sidonƒuɔ, na bese buɛɛ na beli ku atubɔyɔ. Na ɔdi ulákyaku ɔkpanadi unyeƒi. Na bébo lɛla biala baawia. Na ama ku Sidonƒuɔ bágyunku lɛlɔ, na ama ku bekyuli biala beeebo kɔna kɔdi.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Ka nkyuli ɛlɔ bamɛni bénwini bésie Sore ku Estaol ni, bana banwani béye-ma banini, “Dɛ na bɛ́nu ala ammɔ bɛ́vinku?”

english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Na si bísie bítéduo mmɔ ni, bɛdubɔnu ka bekyuli bammɔ baaadaku lɛla lɛdi. Na ɔma ubendi lɛnɔ na ɔdi. Na bebo lɛla biala na ukyuli ɔɔwia. Na bɔɔsu-mii bɔnii Katɔti úuti bekyuli bammɔ ɔ́kya-mii enu kemmo kukuuku.”

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Amu na Dan kɔdua bekyuli nkyuli eti leevu-anyɔ bátu akpagya na báta bási Sore ku Estaol ka betékpoku-ma.

english_verse: One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp.
translation_verse: Ka bésela ni, bétédi benye Kiriat-Yearim na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na Kiriat-Yearim kada kakɛ baalɔ banii Dan Kalɛlɛkɔ úti úbedu ɔmwi kadi.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Na ka bási mmɔ ni, bávi bátásia Eƒraim abi eli na bétédu Mika kaduli.

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Amu ka nkyuli ɛlɔ bani nétéyu Lais ɔma bánu mmɔ ni, básu bana banwani banini, “Bɛgyi ka kaduli kadi kakya mɛni kani na bánwi baƒiɔ badi na béti sika ɔƒualadi bákwa-nwu, na baƒiɔ bamba lɛnɔ ku ɔkpane awu gyɔlɔɔ lɛnɔ bese mmɔ? Bi ndi bina kasusu na lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka bɔbla lɛlɔ?”

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
translation_verse: Na banana bammɔ bédie kenye banini, “Ba lɛsɛ na tasu ku lɛla. Mmomu siaku-bu kama na ababla bula ɔkpane ku bula ɔti. Na buuye-ɔ bɔnii ɔɔɔdia ka ataabla kaba ku ɔtɔ bekyuli kabla utulo ka ataabla ukyuli unwi kaduli bekyuli kabla?”

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Mmɔ na kubiti kɔ́da ɔkpane ɔmmɔ, na úti ɔkpane awu ku kaduli baƒiɔ ku ligyii lɛnwidi lɛmmɔ ɔ́da na ɔ́siaku-ma ɔ́tɔlɔ.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Na bénwini bátɔlɔ na báya na bana bebi ku bebuo ku bana akɛla ágyu atɔ-ma.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Ka bésie ulugyuɔ bási Mika kaduli ni, Mika ɔ́kpali nwuna liku bekyuli ɔ́sala ka bebebunku-nwu na betékpo. Na bésie bátáda bálɛ Dan kɔdua bekyuli lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Na bése kalɔ baakwanyiku Danƒuɔ. Na Danƒuɔ bamɛni bénwini na béye Mika banini, “Bi mɔɔlɛ́ku-ɔ ɔsu na éti bekpone bamɛni ka bebekpoku-bu?”

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: Na Mika údie kenye ɔnini, “Bíti mina baƒiɔ bani lɛ́vɔ ku mina ɔkpane bɛ́tɔlɔku. Na ɔƒɛni ni, bi nsɔ mbo lite lɛlɔ? Na biiye-mi bɛnii, ‘Bi mɔɔlɛ́ku-mi?’ ”

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Na Danƒuɔ bamɛni básu Mika banini, “Takyaku-bu unyeƒi ɔdi. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, bekyuli badi badubo kɔnyi bɔkɛ na bekpoku-ɔ. Na ƒula kaduli bekyuli badubɔyila bana ngba.”

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Danƒuɔ báwia ulu na bátɔlɔ. Na ka Mika ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka Danƒuɔ bamɛni bebo ɔyikun bétulo-nwu ɔsu ni, únwini kama na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie kaduli.

english_verse: But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
translation_verse: Na básia ɔma ɔmmɔ lɛnyi banii Dan ɔni ndi bana bati kuuku ɔti. Na Dan ɔmɛni ɔti ndi Yakob. Na nka ɔma ɔmmɔ na bátaalɔ banii Lais.

english_verse: Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Israelƒuɔ beeebo ɔga ɔdi. Na Lewini ɔdi nlie ɔgyu kalɔ kadi na Eƒraim abi lɛlɔ. Na úti ulekubi ɔdi ɔni na ɔ́si Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ na Betlehem ɔ́bla nwuna ɔsɔnɔ.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: Nsu uleku ɔmɛni úbeti kɔnyi ɔ́kya ɔgyani ɔmɛni. Anwuɔsu ɔ́tɔlɔ-nwu kudɔ na úsie ɔkya ɔti kudɔ na Betlehem. Na ɔ́kya mmɔ abuli atɛ.

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: Amu na Lewini ɔmmɔ ɔ́sia-nwu kama ka utásia-nwu kɔnu na ɔsɔ unwini ubo-nwu kudɔ. Na ɔdanku nwuna kabla ɔblane ku bebuo ala betine inyɔ. Na ka údu mmɔ ni, uleku ɔmmɔ úti-nwu utéduoku ɔti kaduli. Ka ɔti ɔ́nu-nwu ni, ɔ́ƒɔ-nwu ku ebiti.

english_verse: and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
translation_verse: Na ulekubi ɔmɛni ɔti ɔ́su-nwu kpakplaa ka ɔkya-nwu kudɔ blii. Ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔ́kya-nwu kudɔ emeyi atɛ. Na baadi na baaní na ɔɔtɛ kaduli mmɔ.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Na limeyi linedi ɔtanta tutuutu ni, báta na banii bésela. Nsu uleku ɔmɛni ɔti ɔ́su Lewini ɔnini, “Ya na bɔwia lɛla lɛdi na adi na akɛ kubiti. Na ɔmmɔ kama akana na atɔlɔ.”

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bana inyɔ bélie kalɔ na bádi na báni básala. Mmɔ na uleku ɔmɛni ɔti ɔ́su Lewini ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Buvele nda-a, ka atɛ usien ɔmɛni na akɛ kubiti.”

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Nsu Lewini ɔmɛni ɔ́ta ka úsela, nsu ulekubi ɔmɛni ɔti únye-nwu lɛlɔ ka utatɔlɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔ́su ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kya usien ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛlɔndi ɔtanta tutuutu ɔ́ta ka úsela na ulekubi ɔmɛni ɔti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Buvele nda-a, wia lɛla lɛdi na adi asa. Na si kadi káta blii akana na atɔlɔ.” Anwuɔsu nkyuli inyɔ bamɛni bádi básala.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Lewini ɔmmɔ ku nwuna ɔsɔnɔ ku nwuna kabla bablane bábla kasusu ka bagyu ni, Lewini ɔsɔnɔ ɔti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Nu, useyi úudu ɔ́wɔlɔ na uwi uletu asa na kadi kasa. Anwuɔsu tɛ na akɛ kubiti kɔkladi. Na kɔnaadi ata ɔtanta tutuutu na atɔlɔ.”

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔnana ɔmɛni úni ɔnii ɔsɔ ulatɛ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu anwu ku ulekudi ku kabla bablane ku nwuna bebuo ala betine inyɔ báta na béti anumi bátina Yebus ɔni baalɔ banii Yerusalem.

english_verse: It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na badaku Yebus bɔni bude ni, kadi kása. Na kabla bablane ɔmmɔ ɔ́su nwuna unwoti ɔnini, “Bibo na busie butátɛ Yebusiƒuɔ bamɛni kudɔ usien ɔmɛni.”

english_verse: “No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah,
translation_verse: Mmɔ na nwuna unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Oowo! Bulésie bulatátɛ bekyuli bamɛni kudɔ, ɔsika baaadi Israelƒuɔ. Mmomu bɔdubusie Gibeaƒuɔ kudɔ.”

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bésie na bétéduo Gibea na Benyamin ɔmii lɛlɔ. Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, na ɔƒɛ úuduo lɛyu.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Usien ɔmmɔ ni, unengu ɔdi ɔ́si nwuna kemo. Ɔdi Eƒraimni ɔni nási abi lɛlɔ ɔma, nsu ɔƒɛni úbo úlie Gibea kesii kani na Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli belie.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na unengu ɔmɛni ɔ́nu belusiene bamɛni ka belie ɔblɔnu lɛlɔ ni, ɔ́kpɛ úde-nwu na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Wɛ na bɛ́si na wɛ lɛnɔ bísela?”

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Amu na Lewini ɔmɛni údie kenye ɔnini, “Bɔ́si Betlehem na Yudaƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ, na bɔ́vi búsela Eƒraim abi ɔma ɔni nágyu, kesii kani ukyuli na ndi. Mmɔ na mɔɔbla kabla na Unwoti kakpakɔ. Na nlie mɛni, ɔsika ńtakɛ ukyuli ɔdi kaduli na liduo lɛtɛ.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: Nsu bubo adila ku kakpa na bute bula bebuo ala betine bamɛni, na bɔda bodobodo ku ntɛ bɔni na ami ku ulekubi ɔmɛni ku mina kabla ɔblane bɔdi na bɔni. Na nka bɔsɔ buláwia lɛla lɛdi.”

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Na unengu ɔmɛni ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Bibeduo-mi kaduli na ndubɔnu-mii lɛlɔ, ɔsika útamanku ka bɛsɔ bɛtɛ ɔblɔnu lɛlɔ mɛni bigye kadi.”

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu útiku-ma úsienku kaduli na úte nwuna bebuo adila na bádi. Ɔmmɔ kama ka báwia ntu bɔdi báƒɔ lɛgba ni, bádi na báni básala.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni bakya baaní taakɛ ebiti ni, bekyuli bekpidi bani nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo bábaka bámana unengu ɔmmɔ kaduli. Na bakya beebó kaduli kammɔ kayakun, na baakpali unengu ɔni mbo kaduli kammɔ ka udie ɔnana ɔni néduo-ma kaduli mmɔ ɔlɛku na ama ku-nwu batɛ.

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Kaduli ɔlati ɔmmɔ ɔ́lɛ keyi na útásu-ma ɔnini, “Oowo! Mina bakpana, bitaya na bɔbla likyulikpi lɛmɛni udu. Ɔsika ukyuli ɔmɛni ɔdi ɔƒɔ ɔni néduo-mi. Ɔmɛni ɔsu bitaya bɔkya lɛlɔ kɔƒa.”

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛɛnu mina adagyaa ulekubi ku nwuna ɔsɔnɔ. Ndubo-ma budie búboku na bibo kuƒi ka bɛbla-ma lɛla biala na bɛɛyɔ́. Nsu ɔƒɔ ɔmɛni amu ni, bitakya lɛlɔ kɔƒa kɔmɛni udu.”

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Nsu banana bamɛni banii belénu kalɔ kudii. Ɔmɛni ɔsu Lewini ɔmmɔ úsie na útetiku nwuna ɔsɔnɔ ɔlɛku keyi. Na úti-nwu úte-ma, na bánya-nwu bámana na ama ku-nwu bátɛ ulikplu usien umodi ɔmmɔ ƒui. Na uwi ɔni kadi késela bugye ni, bédie-nwu ulu.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Lɛdigye lɛmmɔ uleku ɔmɛni únwini úsie bana keduokɔ kammɔ, na útébuli ɔ́tɛ-nwu kayaku. Na ɔ́tɛ mmɔ útédu ka kadi kégye.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Lewini ɔta na ɔ́lɛmi ɔtɔ ka uteesie nwuna ulu ni, ɔ́nu ka nwuna ɔsɔnɔ úbuli ɔtɛ kayakun na nwuna kɔnu kɔda kayakun ugyii.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́lɔ-nwu ɔnini, “Ta na beteesie.” Nsu útedie kenye. Anwuɔsu ɔ́gyu uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́sia nwuna ebuo ala utine kama na úti-nwu ɔ́tɔlɔku úsienku ɔma.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: Na ka úduo kaduli ni, úti kewii na úle ɔsɔnɔ ɔmmɔ eku eku leevu-inyɔ. Na úti lɛna lɛmmɔ umene Israel kaba leevu-inyɔ.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala manu lɛna lɛmɛni ɔ́su ɔnini, “Litemi lɛmɛni udu lítalɛ kudii ɔ́si uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bálɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔlɛka bɔbla lɛla lɛdi bɔsiku litemi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ! Anwuɔsu bɛya na buti-ni kasusu! Na bɔnu kalɛ bɔbla-ni!”

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Amu na Lewini, ɔni ndi uleku ɔni bádu mmɔ ɔgyani, údie kenye ɔnini, “Ami ku mina ɔsɔnɔ bútéduo Gibea ɔni nkya Benyamin kɔdua kalɔ lɛlɔ ka butátɛ mmɔ.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Na líti mina ɔsɔnɔ ukpine ɔmɛni na líle-nwu eku eku leevu-inyɔ na líti límene Israel kaba leevu-inyɔ bammɔ. Ɔsika bábla likyulikpi ku kɔƒa ala na Israel.

english_verse: The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home.
translation_verse: Na bana ƒui báta na bédie kenye kenwi aani ukyuli unwi pɛ muutemi, na básu banini, “Ukyuli biala útesela kaduli, ina ukyuli unwi utenwini utesie nwuna kaduli!

english_verse: Everyone agreed that Gibeah had to be punished.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Israelƒuɔ banana ƒui básala lisu aani ukyuli unwi kalɛ ka betékpoku ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli.

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bidie bekyuli bani nábla likpidi lɛmmɔ biboku na bɔdu-ma, na likyulikpi lɛmɛni udu lɛlɛ Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ.” Nsu Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli bamɛni bátakpete litemi lɛni básu-ma mmɔ.

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: Na Benyamin lɛma linengudi ƒui bekyuli bábasala lɛlɔ ka betékpoku Israelƒuɔ.

english_verse: The other Israelite tribes organized their army and found they had
translation_verse: Na Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli kama ni, Israelƒuɔ kaba bekyuli ƒui básala bekpone mpim eti maane ɔni na bana ƒui badi bekpone kpakplaa.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Lɛdigye ni, Israelƒuɔ bátásala lɛlɔ na Gibea kudɔ.

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: Na báta banii betékpoku Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli. Anwuɔsu báya na bana bekpone bátu akpagya na béti anumi bátina Gibea ɔma ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over,
translation_verse: Na Benyamin bekyuli bálɛ bási Gibea na bétékpoku Israelƒuɔ. Na limeyi lɛmmɔ bádu Israelƒuɔ bekpone mpim aavlanyɔ-inyɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Israelƒuɔ bátábɛ bakya alakpi adi akɔ na Gibea amadɔ.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: Na bábla kasusu ka bekeli na balɛ-ma enu kemmo. Anwuɔsu béti anumi bátina ɔma bamba ulu. Nsu bátakana bukeli bɔlɛ-ma enu kemmo. Na Israelƒuɔ bekpone geen ku bekpone bani nási baalɛ́ ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo báda Benyaminƒuɔ bákya na báyila-ma udu.

english_verse: who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah,
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ béyu-ma bátu na bétebile uwi ɔdi, mmomu bábi básiaku-ma bétédu Gibea ɔƒɛ katukɔ, na bakɛ baadú-ma ka béti bésela.

english_verse: Some other warriors of Benjamin turned and ran down the road toward Rimmon Rock in the desert. The Israelites killed
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani nékeli básia ulu ɔni ntɛ úsie Rimon atakpɛ kemmo ni, bádu nkyuli mpim ɛlɔ. Na Israelƒuɔ bábi básiaku bakladi bétédu Gidom, na bádu mpim inyɔ.

english_verse: Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors.
translation_verse: Na Benyaminƒuɔ bekpone bani ƒui bádu limeyi lɛmmɔ badi bekpone mpim aavlanyɔ-ɛlɔ. Na badi bekpone bani mbo kayi geen.

english_verse: The Israelites turned back and went to every town in Benjamin's territory, killing all the people and animals, and setting the towns on fire.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bénwini bétékpoku Benyaminƒuɔ bakladi na bádu bana banana ku beleku ku bana bebi ku bana bebuo ƒui kede kede. Na bátu ogya bákya lɛma lɛni nkya amadɔ mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ banana básala belie Mispa ni, bése kenye ka ɔdi biala uleti nwuna ubi ulekubi ulete Benyamin kɔdua ukyuli ɔdi na weti.

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani nésie Betel ni, bétélie Katɔti anumi na beewulo momoomo ɔ́si ɔtanta útédu useyi uwi taasu banini,

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: “O Unwoti, Israel Katɔti, bi ɔsu na ala amɛni udu álɛku Israelƒuɔ lɛni? Bi ɔsu na bula kɔdua kunwi kɔyii ɔmwi kadi?”

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Lɛdigye tutuutu ni, bekyuli bammɔ bátu lɛkpabi na bábla bɔkyula ku unwi bɔbla akpala.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Amu ba béye lɛlɔ banini, “Ɔma bene nébu na bula kaba bekyuli akɔ na beeebo Unwoti anumi na mɛni?” Ɔsika bése kenye banii kɔdua kɔni néni ka ubo Unwoti anumi na Mispa ni, ɔlɛka bayila kɔdua kammɔ ƒui udu.

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Na mmɔ lɛnɔ na Israelƒuɔ béwulo Benyamin kɔdua lili. Ɔsika básu banii, “Ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni kɔdua kunwi kɔ́yii na Israel adua kemmo.”

english_verse: Only a few men of Benjamin weren't killed in the war. We need to get wives for them, so the tribe won't completely disappear. But how can we do that, after promising in the Lord's name that we wouldn't let them marry any of our daughters?”
translation_verse: Na béye lɛlɔ banini, “Dɛ na bɔdubɔbla na bɔkɛ beleku bute banana bani nébu, ɔsika búse kenye na Unwoti anumi ka bɔɔɔdubo bula belekubi buti bute-ma na beti kudii?”

english_verse: The warriors attacked Jabesh in Gilead, and returned to their camp at Shiloh in Canaan with
translation_verse: Na ka bésie ni, bákɛ badagyaa belekubi eti maane ɔni na ama ku ɔnana ɔdi bátatɛ kudii. Na béti beleku bamɛni bésienku Israelƒuɔ kasalakɔ na Silo na Kanaan kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ ƒui bátala bekyuli bákya Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli bani nkya Rimon atakpɛ kemmo, na bátásu-ma ka keyi kayɔ-ma.

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli bammɔ bénwini bésie ɔma uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo, na béti beleku bani na bátadu na bási Yabes-Gilead béte-ma. Nsu beleku bammɔ bétedu bana bumomo.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bekyuli béwulo kɔnyana béte Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli bammɔ. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́ya na Israel ɔ́yila kaba kadi na nwuna adua kemmo.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu benengu bani násala lisu mmɔ básu banini, “Ka beleku badi basɔ beeebo Benyamin kɔdua kemmo mɛni ni, dɛ na bɔdubɔbla na bɔkɛ beleku bute banana bani nátakɛ tɔ beleku na beti-ma?”

english_verse: If they don't have children, one of the Israelite tribes will die out.
translation_verse: Amu na básu banini, “Ɔlɛka bɔkɛ kadikɔ kadi bute Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli bani nébu kalɛ na kɔdua kɔdi kalayii na Israel adua kemmo.”

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Na básu lɛlɔ banini, “Bulakana na buti bula belekubi bute-ma na beti-ma. Na kenye kani búse mmɔ ndi ka, ‘Bɔbuɛ bɔdi bute ukyuli ɔni meti nwuna ubi ulekubi wete Benyamin kɔdua kɔdi ka uti-nwu.’

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Nsu bɛnu! Uwi údu na bɔdi Unwoti lɛkwa ndi lɛkwa limeyi na Silo ɔni nkya Betel katɔ kakɛ. Na Silo ɔkya ɔƒɛ kanukɔ ulu ɔni néti úsela ɔ́si Betel úsie Sekem na útédu Lebon kada kakɛ.”

english_verse: The leaders told the men of Benjamin who still did not have wives: Go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards near the festival.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu bébo Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli ɔda banini, “Bisie na bitábɛ adingyii mmo kemmo,

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: na binye kagyumana. Na si uwi ɔni na bɛnu ka beleku bani nási Silo bebo baatɔ́ ni, na bikeli bɛlɛ adingyii mmo bɔmmɔ kemmo, na ɔdi biala utéƒie uleku unwi ɔbla ulekudi, na bɛtɔlɔ bisie Benyamin kalɔ kemmo.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Na si beleku bammɔ bati ku banwani bananabi bebo-bu kudɔ bábakya-mii kakya na lɛla lɛni bɛ́bla mɛni ɔsu ni, bɔdubo-ma bɔsu bɔnini, ‘Bɛya na kaƒɔ kayɔ-mii na bite-ma kebunku. Ɔsika kekpo uwi kemmo ni, bútakɛ beleku unwi unwi butéte-ma. Nsu ɔɔɔdi amii néti beleku bammɔ bíte-ma. Anwuɔsu bina litemi libo ubo.’ ”

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu lɛni na Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli bammɔ bábla uwi ɔni na beleku bammɔ bakya baatɔ́ mmɔ. Ɔnana biala úkeli na útéƒie uleku unwi na úti-nwu ɔ́bla ulekudi. Mmɔ na bénwini bésie bana kalɔ lɛlɔ, na bátásɔku bana lɛma báda na bélie-ni kemmo.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo Israelƒuɔ bátɔlɔ kesii kani bakya mmɔ, na ɔdi biala únwini útéduo nwuna kɔdua lɛtɔ kemmo na bana kesii kani na bana kadikɔ kakya.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo kani na Israelƒuɔ beeebo ɔga ɔdi. Ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔdi biala ɔɔbla lɛla lɛni na ɔɔyɔ́.

english_verse: Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there,
translation_verse: Na ɔnana ɔmɛni baalɔ banii Elimelek. Na ulekudi baalɔ banii Naomi. Na nwuna bebi bananabi inyɔ bammɔ baalɔ banii Mahlon ku Kilion. Bekyuli bamɛni bási Eƒrat kaba kemmo na Betlehem na Yudaƒuɔ kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ. Na bátɔlɔ bésie Moab kalɔ lɛlɔ, na bétélie mmɔ.

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Na bananabi inyɔ bamɛni béti Moabƒuɔ beleku. Unwi úti uleku ɔni baalɔ banii Orpa, na unyɔdi lɛnɔ úti uleku ɔni baalɔ banii Rut.

english_verse: When Naomi heard that the Lord had given his people a good harvest, she and her two daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab and go to Judah. As they were on their way there,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔ́ta na ɔ́klibi lɛlɔ ku nwuna bebi bele bammɔ ka batɔlɔ Moab kalɔ lɛlɔ. Amu na báta banii beteesie Yudaƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ.
