english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni bésela ni, Naomi ɔ́su nwuna bebi bele bamɛni ɔnini, “Binwini biteesie bina ɔma na bitélie bina beni kudɔ. Na muuvele Unwoti nnii ɔbla lɛƒɔndia ute-mii aani kalɛ na bɛ́bla lɛƒɔndia bíte-mi ku bina bagya bani nékpi mmɔ.

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Nsu Naomi ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Mina bebi belekubi, ɔdi ka binwini. Bi ɔsu na bɛɛyɔ́ ka bɛsiaku-mi kama? Nsɔ naaakana bebi bananabi babambadi bɔwɔ bute-mi na bilieku-ma.

english_verse: You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu binwini biteesie bina ɔma. Ɔƒɛni lɛnɔ ni, lɛ́ɛbi ɔni na nsɔ naaakana kɔgya bulie. Ina banii lɛkɛ kɔgya kɔdi ɔmwi limeyi na banii lɛwɔ bebi bananabi usien ɔmɛni kani ni, bɛɛɛdubo bɔkana bunye bɔgya bebi bammɔ na balɛ lili asa na bilieku-ma.

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
translation_verse: Na ɔmɛni ɔsu bɛɛɛdubo kɔgya kɔdi bulie. Mina bebi, bɛgyi ka ɔmɛni ɔɔɔdubo bɔtɛ lɛni. Uuduo ami ɔlati teetulo amii muedi. Unwoti náya na úbo úte-mi lɛni.”

english_verse: They cried again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu básɔ bése kalɔ beewulo. Na Orpa ɔ́kya nwuna ugyieni kɔgbu na únwini ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie kaduli. Nsu Rut ɔmu úƒie Naomi ɔda kpakplaa.

english_verse: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
translation_verse: Na Naomi ɔ́su Rut ɔnini, “Nu! Ƒ'ɔgyani ɔnwani ulekudi únwini ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie nwuna bekyuli ku bana baƒiɔ kudɔ. Anwuɔsu awɔ lɛnɔ nwini na atásiaku-nwu kama na eteesie bina ɔma.”

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Amu ka Naomi ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka lɛla biala liiibo na ɔsu Rut na unwini ɔsu ni, ɔ́da-nwu bɔtɛmiku ɔ́ya.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: Amu na beleku inyɔ bamɛni básiaku lɛlɔ bétédu Betlehem. Na ka béduo Betlehem ni, owogyo ubendi ɔdi úwi ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na ama ɔsu. Na beleku bani nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo beeye banini, “Naomi geen mɛni?”

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Amu na Naomi ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bitalɔ-mi Naomi. Mmomu bɛlɔ-mi Mara, ɔsika Katɔti útaya na keyi kayɔku-mi.

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na lɛ́tɔlɔ mɛni ni, mbo ala geen. Nsu Unwoti ɔ́ya na linwini libo ku enukplu. Na bi ɔsu na bɛɛlɔ-mi Naomi? Unwoti ɔ́ya na líbo abi, na ɔ́ya na ɔgbankpi ɔ́siaku-mi.”

english_verse: One day, Ruth said to Naomi, “Let me see if I can find someone who will let me pick up the grain left in the fields by the harvest workers.” Naomi answered, “Go ahead, my daughter.” So immediately Ruth went out to pick up grain in a field. She didn't know it was owned by Boaz, a relative of Naomi's husband Elimelech, as well as a rich and important man.
translation_verse: Amu na Naomi ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔdia! Mina ubi, teesie.” Anwuɔsu Rut ɔ́ta na úsie kemo kadi na ɔkpɛ kemo kammɔ kabla bablane kama na ɔɔla edula ani na báda béwi. Asa wanu wati ni, ɔdi Boas ɔni nási Elimelek ɔtɔ kemmo. Nwuna kemo kani na Rut ɔkya ɔɔla edula amɛni.

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: Na uwi útetu asa na Boas ɔlati ɔ́si Betlehem na ɔ́da ɔ́lɛ kemo mmɔ. Na ɔ́kya kabla bablane bammɔ kenye ɔnini, “Blɔti ulieku-mii.” Na kabla bablane bammɔ lɛnɔ bédie kenye banini, “Blɔti ute-ɔ kusɛ kusɛ.”

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Amu na Boas úye kabla bablane bammɔ unengu ɔnini, “Wɛ na ugblebi ɔmɛni ɔ́si?”

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Amu na kabla bablane unengu ɔmɛni údie kenye ɔnini, “Ulekubi ɔmɛni ndi Moabni ɔni nási Moab kalɔ lɛlɔ na ɔ́siaku Naomi úbo mmɔ.”

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: Na kabla bablane unengu ɔmɛni ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Boas ɔnini, “Ulekubi ɔmɛni úvele-mi ɔnii nte kuƒi na ɔsiaku kabla bablane bamɛni kama na utaala edula ani na báda béwi. Na unye kabla kamɛni lɛlɔ ɔ́si ɔtanta tutuutu úbedu ɔƒɛni. Na ɔƒɛni kani na ɔ́ta úlie kalɔ ɔɔnwuna.”

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Amu na Boas ɔ́su Rut ɔnini, “Mina ubi, nu mina litemi. Tesie ukyuli bamba kemo tatála edula adi ntu mina kemo kani. Ɔmɛni ɔsu sɔ kya mɛni kani, na asiaku beleku bamɛni kama na ataala ƒula edula.

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: Nu ekpo ani bakya baaƒɛ edula na ablaku-ma kabla. Na líbo mina kabla bablane ɔda ka ɔdi biala utabla-a lɛla lɛdi. Na uwi biala na utukwɛ ɔɔda-a ni, sie na atáni ntu bɔni na bédu béyile kutubui kɔni nlɛ mmɔ kemmo.”

english_verse: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
translation_verse: Amu na Rut ɔ́lɛ akɔnkɔ na úti anumi úbi kalɔ na ɔ́su Boas ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na ami kadi bamba ukyuli lɛlɔ lɛɛkywí-ɔ kaƒɔ lɛni?”

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Amu na Boas údie kenye ɔnini, “Ƒula ugyieni ɔ́su-mi lɛla biala na ábla éte-nwu úti ɔ́si uwi ɔni na ƒ'ɔgyani úkpi. Na ngyi kalɛ na áda ƒ'ɔti ku ƒ'ini ku ƒula kadi bekyuli ése na ébo élieku bekyuli bani na aaagyi kudii mɛni.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: Muuvele Blɔti nnii ɔƒɔ-ɔ kayu na lɛla lɛni na ábla mɛni ɔsu. Na nsɔ muuvele Unwoti Israel Katɔti ɔni kudɔ na ébo mɛni ka ɔgyumana-a na ɔƒɔ-ɔ kayu ƒui.”

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Amu na Rut údie kenye ɔnini, “Ati, átɛmiku-mi buɛɛ na ákya-mi ɔkplu lɛnɔ, ina ka ńtamanku ƒula kabla bablane ɔdi biala muedi.”

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ka uwi údu ka badi ni, Boas ɔ́su Rut ɔnini, “Bo na abaƒɔ adila adi na akya kutu kemmo na adi.” Anwuɔsu anwu ku kabla bablane bélie kalɔ, na Boas úti adila ani bánwa bada mmɔ adi úte Rut ka ɔdi. Na ɔ́di na úmo na ɔdi muedi úbu.

english_verse: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
translation_verse: Amu ka Rut ɔ́ta na úsie ɔkya ɔɔla edula ammɔ ni, Boas úbo nwuna kabla bablane bammɔ ɔda ɔnini, “Bɛya na utaala edula ammɔ. Na si ina ɔ́buma ani nlɛ lisu mmɔ adi muedi ni, biteye-nwu lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: Be sure to pull out some stalks of grain from the bundles and leave them on the ground for her. And don't speak harshly to her!”
translation_verse: Na bɛƒɛ edula ammɔ adi bɛlɛ lisu na bɛda bise-nwu na ubabuma. Na ɔdi biala lɛnɔ utadɔnku-nwu.”

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Rut ɔ́la edula na kemo kammɔ ɔ́si ɔtanta úti útédu useyi uwi. Ka úbo edula ebi ammɔ ni, ɔ́kɛ kagyigyɛ bonwu keyile.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: Ka ɔ́gyu edula amɛni úti ni, ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie kaduli na úti-nya útátina nwuna ugyieni. Na ɔ́su-nwu ka edula amɛni na ɔ́kɛ. Na ɔ́sɔ úte ugyieni ɔmɛni adila ani na Boas ɔ́nwa na ɔ́di úbu mmɔ adi na ɔ́di.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Amu ka Naomi ɔ́nu edula amɛni ni, úye Rut ɔnini, “Wɛ kakɛ na átála edula ɔmwi kadi? Na ɔma kemo na ákya ábla kabla? Muuvele Unwoti nnii ute ukyuli ɔmmɔ kusɛ kusɛ na lɛƒɔndia lɛni ɔ́bla-a mɛni ɔsu.” Amu na Rut ɔ́su Naomi ka ukyuli ɔni kemo na ɔkya ɔɔbla kabla mmɔ baalɔ banii Boas.

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Naomi ɔ́su Rut ɔnini, “Muuvele Unwoti ɔni mɔɔdi nwuna linyese lɛlɔ teete bekyuli bani nlie ngba ku bani nékpi ka ute ukyuli ɔmmɔ kusɛ kusɛ.” Amu na úsie anumi na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ukyuli ɔni nétɔ-ɔ ala mmɔ ni, ɔ́si bula ɔtɔ kemmo. Na ɔdi ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo bekyuli bammɔ badi akɔ unwi ɔni na ɔkana na ute-bu kebunku.”

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Amu na Rut úye Naomi ɔnini, “Lɛkana ntaabla ku nwuna kabla bablane kabla uti utédu ka báƒɛ edula ammɔ báwɔlɔ?”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Na Naomi ɔ́su Rut ɔnini, “Ɛɛn, mina ubi, ɔdia ka ataabla kabla na Boas kemo ku beleku bammɔ. Ɔsika si ésie átábla kabla na ukyuli bamba kemo ni, badubo-ɔ kalala kadi bɔbla.”

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Rut ɔ́bla kabla ku Boas beleku úti útédu ka báƒɛ edula ammɔ báwɔlɔ. Nsu Rut ɔ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́kya ugyieni kudɔ.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Limeyi linwi Naomi ɔ́su Rut ɔnini, “Ɔlɛka libunku-ɔ na akɛ kɔgya kɔni na elie na ataakɛ ala ani na aawia.”

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Amu na Naomi úye Rut ɔnini, “Eenyimo ɔnana ɔni baalɔ Boas ɔni kabla awɔ ku beleku bammɔ bɛɛbla mmɔ? Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔdi bula ɔtɔ ukyuli. Na mɔɔwia ka enu litemi lɛni ndubo-ɔ bɔsu mɛni. Usien ɔmɛni ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔdubo nwuna edula bubo.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ta na awia ntu bɔdi na akpi, na awia oloƒui ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔdi awɛɛ, na eti ƒula awu ani mɔɔdia bɔnu teetulo akya. Na eteesie kesii kani na beebó edula ammɔ. Nsu taya na Boas ɔnu ɔti ka akya mmɔ uti utédu ka ɔ́wɔlɔ.

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: Si úsie útátɛ ni, na anu kesii kani na ɔtɛ mmɔ ese likpo. Na si ɔlɛɛ ni, bla buɛɛ na ebimi nwuna kɔdi na ayu atɛ-nwu kudɔ. Na ɔdubɔsu-ɔ lɛla lɛni na adubɔbla.”

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Rut úsie kesii kani beebó edula ammɔ, na útábla lɛla lɛni na ugyieni ɔ́su-nwu mmɔ.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Ka Boas ɔ́di na ɔ́wɔlɔ lɛla biala ni, ɔ́vi úsie útátɛ edula lisu lɛni bébo béwi mmɔ eli.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Usientɛ ka Boas úkeyi lɛlɔ ɔ́gyinya kɔnakunwi ni, ɔ́nu ka ulekubi ɔdi ɔtɛ-nwu kudɔ. Na ɔ́bla-nwu kalɛ kadi.

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: Amu na úye ɔnini, “Awɔ, ɔma ntɛ mɛni?” Amu na Rut údie kenye ɔnini, “Ati, ami Rut mmɔ.” Na Rut ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ka adi mina ɔtɔ ukyuli ɔsu ni, mɔɔnu ka awɔ na ɔlɛka anu-mi lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu muuvele-ɔ nnii ti-mi.”

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Amu na Boas ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Katɔti kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku-ɔ, ɔsika bɔyɔ bɔni na édie átina-mi mɛni butulo bɔni na édie átina ƒula ugyieni ɔ́si lɛla lɛni na ábla mɛni ɔsu. Ɔƒɛni lɛnɔ átawia okloƒu ɔni ndi ɔlakɛne iye ɔwabane ka elieku-nwu.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: Amu na Boas ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Sɔsɔ na ɔdi ka ndi ƒula lɛlɔ ukyuli na ɔdi ka ntaanu-ɔ lɛlɔ, nsu ukyuli ɔdi ɔkya na ɔsɔ ude-ɔ utulo-mi.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu tɛ mɛni usie ɔmɛni na si kadi kégye ni, bɔdubɔwia ukyuli ɔni na ɔlɛka uti ƒula etila mmɔ kama ulu. Na si bɔ́nu-nwu na ɔ́tuna ni, na ɔdia. Nsu si útatuna lɛnɔ ni, lɛkpali Katɔti ɔni nlie ngba muusé kenye ka ndubuti ƒula etila. Anwuɔsu sɔ tɛ mɛni utédu ka kadi kégye.”

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tɛ mmɔ útédu lɛdigye. Nsu úyile bɔta ɔtanta tutuutu, ɔsika Boas ulayɔ ka ukyuli ɔdi ɔti ka Rut úbatɛ mmɔ.

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Amu na Boas ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ta na egyingya ƒula kɔdi ewi kalɔ.” Amu na Rut ɔ́bla lɛni na Boas úwilimi edula ɔbla aani akyami aavlanyɔ-ene úwi-ku kemmo na únyimi-ku. Na ɔ́gyu útile-nwu ɔnii uti uteesienku kaduli.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: Kawɔlɔkɔ ni, ɔ́su Naomi ka Boas úwilimi edula ɔbla aani akyami aavlanyɔ-ene úte-nwu na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnii útalɛka unwini usie kaduli ku enu kplu.

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Amu na Naomi ɔ́su Rut ɔnini, “Kɛ kayi, na anu kalɛ na lɛla biala lɛdubo libavi. Ɔsika Boas ulákɛ bɔnwuna ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni wetédu ka ɔnu litemi lɛmmɔ lili ku lɛgba.”

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: Amu na Boas ɔ́ta úsie ulie ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli kasakɔ kani nkya kabanye. Na ɔ́nu ukyuli ɔni lɛlɔ kɔtɛ na ɔ́tɛmi ku Rut ka ɔlɛka ɔdi Elimelek ala. Amu na Boas ɔ́kpali-nwu ɔnini, “Mina ɔkpana, bo na ebelie-mi kudɔ mɛni.” Amu na ɔnana ɔmɛni lɛnɔ úsie útélie-nwu kudɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Na Boas ɔ́wia ɔma ɔmmɔ benengu leevu na bébo bébelie-nwu kudɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su ɔtɔ bekyuli bamɛni ɔnini, “Ɔƒaani ni, Naomi ɔ́sɔ únwini ɔ́si Moab kalɔ lɛlɔ úbo. Na ɔɔyɔ́ ka uti Elimelek ɔni nékpi na ɔdi bula ɔtɔ ubi mmɔ kalɔ uye.

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: Na mɔɔyɔ́ ka bɛti ɔmɛni.” Amu na ɔ́su ɔnana ɔni na ɔlɛka ɔdi Elimelek ala mmɔ ɔnini, “Si aayɔ́ ka eye kalɔ kammɔ ni, na eye-ka na benengu bani nlie mɛni anumi. Nsu si alayɔ ka eye-ka lɛnɔ ni, na aya na bati. Ɔsika awɔ ndi ɔnanabi udeedi ɔni ntɔ na ebo kuƒi ka eye-ka asa na nsia.” Amu na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-ma ka ɔdubuye kalɔ kammɔ.

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Amu na Boas ɔ́su ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Si éye kalɔ kammɔ ásiku Naomi kudɔ ni, na ɔlɛka eti Rut abla ƒula ulekudi. Na si awɔ ku-nwu bɛ́wɔ bebi badi ni, na ƒula akɛla ammɔ ƒui adubɔbla Rut ɔgyani udeedi adi.”

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Na si lɛni na ala ammɔ ese bɔdi ni, lɛɛɛdubo kalɔ kammɔ buye. Ɔsika ɔmɛni ɔdubo lɛsɛ bɔkya na mina bebi ntɛ, na lɛyila mina kadikɔ kani na ami ɔlati lɛ́bla.” Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, ɔ́su Boas ɔnini, “Awɔ akana na eye kalɔ kammɔ. Ami lɛɛɛdubo-ka buye.”

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: Amu ka ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́su Boas ɔnii ɔkana na uye kalɔ kammɔ ni, ɔnana ɔmɛni údie nwuna lɛgbanvuo na úti-ni úte Boas.

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Amu na Boas ɔ́su benengu bani ƒui nli mmɔ ɔnini, “Amii ndi mina kenye bediene. Ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni, líye ala ani ƒui na Elimelek ku Kilion ku Mahlon bebo lɛ́siku Naomi kudɔ.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni Rut ɔni ndi Moabni na ɔdi Mahlon ukpinele lɛnɔ ɔdubunwini mina uleku kalɛ na Mahlon lɛnyi lilayi ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na amii ndi ala amɛni ƒui kenye bediene ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Amu na benengu bammɔ ku bekyuli bani ƒui nli mmɔ básu banini, “Ɛɛn, bɔdi kenye bediene bute-ɔ. Na buuvele Unwoti bɔnii ulekubi ɔni ndubo ubelie-ɔ kaduli mmɔ ni, ɔbla-nwu aani Rahel ku Lea kalɛ. Rahel ku Lea bamɛni náwɔ bebi pii béte Israel. Na buuvele bɔnii kɛ akɛla pii na Eƒrata ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na Unwoti ɔ́bla-a ukyuli ɔni náƒɔ kuye na Betlehem.

english_verse: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
translation_verse: Na buuvele Unwoti lɛnɔ bɔnii bebi bani na ɔdubo-ɔ bute ɔsiku ulekubi ɔmɛni lɛlɔ ni, ɔya na bina bebi bammɔ babla bebi bani náƒɔ kuye na babla aani bebi bani Peres ɔ́wɔ kalɛ ɔni bawɔne ndi Tama ku Yuda.” Boas Ku Nwuna Kaba Bekyuli Lɛlɔ Kɔtɛ

english_verse: Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed her with a son.
translation_verse: Amu na Boas úti Rut ɔ́bla nwuna ulekudi. Na Unwoti únyeku-nwu na Rut ɔ́da kaƒɔ na ɔwɔ ɔnanabi.

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Liku lɛmmɔ beleku bammɔ básu Naomi banini, “Buumwi Unwoti ɔni náya na ákɛ uwɔ ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni. Anwu ndubo-ɔ lɛlɔ bɔnu, ɔya na ubiwɔ ɔmmɔ ɔƒɔ lɛnyi na Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: Ƒula ubile ɔmɛni ɔɔyɔ́-ɔ litemi geen na ɔdubɔya na lɛlɔ litaayɔ-ɔ, na ɔdubo-ɔ lɛlɔ butaanu uwi ɔni na énwini unengu geen. Na ubiwɔ ɔni na ákɛ mɛni ubo kɔsia utulo si ina bebi pii na ebo.”

english_verse: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
translation_verse: Amu na Naomi ɔ́gyu ubiwɔ ɔmɛni ɔ́talaku katɔ na úti-nwu ɔ́mana kayi na úse kalɔ ɔɔnu-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Amu na liku bekyuli beleku bani nli mmɔ básu banini, “Naomi ɔ́kɛ ubi ɔnanabi.” Na beleku bammɔ básia ubi ɔmmɔ lɛnyi banii Obed. Na Obed ɔmɛni náwɔ Yisai, na Yisai lɛnɔ ɔ́wɔ Dawid. Obed Kaba Kasikɔ Bekyuli

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
translation_verse: Kuuku ni, ɔnana ɔdi ɔ́kya na baalɔ-nwu Elkana. Ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́si ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Ramataim na Eƒraim abi lɛlɔ kalɛkɛ. Na ɔ́si Suƒ ɔtɔ kemmo na Eƒraim kɔdua kemmo. Elkana ɔmɛni ɔti baalɔ Yeroham. Na ɔtieku baalɔ Elihu ɔni ndi Tohu ubidi.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: Elkana úti beleku inyɔ. Unwi baalɔ Hana na unyɔdi baalɔ Penina. Na Penina ubo bebi, nsu Hana ɔdi udinkɔ.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Lɛkwa ndi lɛkwa ni, Elkana ɔɔsí nwuna ɔma mmɔ teesie Silo kesii kani na uusié taatákpa Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui. Na mmɔ na Unwoti Katɔti bakpane inyɔ badi bákya na badi Eli bebi. Ama baalɔ Hoƒni ku Pinehas.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Uwi biala si limeyi lídu ka Elkana ɔkpa Unwoti Katɔti ni, uule lɛna teete ulekudi Penina ku nwuna bebi bananabi ku belekubi ƒui.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: Nsu ulekudi Hana anwu ni, uute-nwu lɛna lɛni na úte bakladi akpa anyɔ, ɔsika ɔɔyɔ́-nwu geen, nsu Katɔti útete-nwu kɔwɔ.

english_verse: Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children,
translation_verse: Hana tawɔ tawɔ ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, ogyulo ɔɔyɔ́-nwu kenye uwi biala kalɛ na uteewulo kɔnyana.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: Udu ɔmɛni nákya-ma ntɛ lɛkwa biala. Na si bésie Unwoti kakpakɔ lɛni ni, ogyulo ɔdubukpoku Hana lɛni laa utédu ka uuwulo na ɔsɔ uladi muedi.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: Si úbo lɛni ni, na Elkana ɔlɔ ulekudi na ɔdɔdɔ-nwu na uye-nwu ɔnini, “Hana, bi ɔsu na eewulo na anii aladi na kayi keekpóku-ɔ lɛni? Ami lɛti pɛ ńtabɔ-ɔ liiitulo si ina bebi leevu na áwɔ?”

english_verse: When the sacrifice had been offered, and they had eaten the meal, Hannah got up and went to pray. Eli was sitting in his chair near the door to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ka bésie Silo mmɔ na báwɔlɔ bɔdi ku bɔni ni, Hana ɔ́ta únye. Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Katɔti Ɔkpane Eli ulie kalɔ na kakpakɔ kayakun kenye, na liboku lɛdi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́kpali ala úse kenye ɔnini, “O Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, ƒula kabla ɔblane na ndi, nsu mina lɛlɔ libo kɔnyana. Taya na kɔnyana kɔdu-mi. Kɛ te-mi ubi ɔnanabi unwi pɛ na lɛwɔ. Na si énu-mi bɔkpali na ábla éte-mi lɛni ni, ndubɔsɔku ubi ɔmmɔ lite-ɔ kusɛ kusɛ nwuna ngba emeyi ƒui. Na ukyuli ɔdi ulékulo-nwu linwini kudii.”

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni kabɛnsɛ ɔsu ni, nwuna lɛdi lilalɛ momoomo, nwuna enyekuli kani muubóku lɛlɔ na lɛla biala lɛɛsí-nwu kayi ku lili kemmo. Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Eli ɔ́kali ka ntɛ bɔdi mɔɔda-nwu.

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔ́su Hana ɔnini, “Uwi ɛlɛ sɔɔn na ntɛ bɔmmɔ bɔdubɔda-a butédu na ada ntɛ ekpila ammɔ bɔbla aya na mɛni?”

english_verse: “Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
translation_verse: Tanu ami ƒula kabla ɔblane aani uleku ukpidi ɔdi, ɔsika ala ani muukpóku-mi mmɔ ɔsu na mɔɔkpali Katɔti kalɛ na mina lɛlɔ lɛɛbla-mi kɔnyana ɔsu.”

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Eli ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Teesie ku keyi buɛɛ. Na Israel Katɔti ɔdubɔbla lɛla lɛni na aawia ute-ɔ.”

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Amu na Hana údie kenye ɔnini, “Ati, mɔɔgyá-a enu na ƒula kenye kani na ásu ɔsu. Ubo-nwu kemmo lɛni.” Na ɔ́gyu ɔ́tɔlɔ útáwia lɛla lɛdi ɔ́kya kenye na kayi káyɔ-nwu.

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Ka kadi kégye ni, Elkana ku nwuna badi ƒui báta na ka bátákpa Katɔti báwɔlɔ ni, bátɔlɔ bésie bana ɔma na Rama. Na Elkana ku ulekudi Hana bátɛ, na Unwoti anu asia-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Hana úbada kaƒɔ na ɔ́wɔ ubi ɔnanabi. Na ɔ́sia-nwu lɛnyi ɔnii Samuel, na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔsika Unwoti na lívele na únu-mi bɔkpali na úte-mi ubi ɔmmɔ.”

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka lɛkwa línwini na uwi ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ údu ni, Elkana ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ƒui béti akpala na bésie batákpa Katɔti.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Nsu Hana anwu útasiaku-ma mmomu ɔ́su ɔgyani ɔnini, “Si ɔnamu ɔmmɔ úkulo lɛnyi ni, ndubuti-nwu lisienku Katɔti na ɔsɔ ɔkya mmɔ nwuna ngba bulie uwi ƒui.”

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Amu na Elkana údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔdia, awɔ ngyi lɛla lɛbuni lɛni na ɔlɛka bɔbla. Anwuɔsu bɛsɔ bɛkya kama na ada-nwu kaduɛ utédu ka úkulo lɛnyi. Mmomu buuvele bɔnii Katɔti ɔdi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ na ɔnamu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Hana ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kya kama na ɔ́nu ɔnamu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ útédu ka úkulo lɛnyi.

english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Hana ɔ́su Eli ɔnini, “Ati, akwa alɛɛ adi návi ni, ami nébenye ƒula kudɔ mɛni lɛ́kpali Unwoti.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: Na lívele-nwu nnii ute-mi ubi na lɛwɔ. Na Unwoti únu-mi bɔkpali sɔsɔ, na ɔ́ya lɛ́wɔ ubi ɔni na nda mɛni.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, líti-nwu muute Unwoti na unwini nwuna ɔdi nwuna ngba bulie uwi ƒui.” Na ɔmɛni kama ni, bákpa Unwoti na mmɔ.

english_verse: Hannah prayed: You make me strong and happy, Lord. You rescued me. Now I can be glad and laugh at my enemies.
translation_verse: Amu na Hana ɔ́kpali Unwoti na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Kayi kaayɔ́-mi geen na Unwoti lɛlɔ. Ɔsika Katɔti ɔ́ya na mina lili lɛ́kɔ lɛ́lɛ katɔ ƒui aani ebuo lise. Na mɔɔkun lɛmɛnɛ na mina bekisine ɔsu. Ɔsika ebiti geen aada-mi ka údie-mi mina bekisine enu kemmo.

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔdi uuuse kedee aani awɔ Unwoti kalɛ. Na ɔdi lɛnɔ uuubunku-ɔ. Na lɛtakpɛ bonwu lɛdi liiibo na lɛdi kama kekpokɔ aani awɔ bula Katɔti.

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Amii bani muukú lɛlɔ ni, bɛda bina lɛlɔ buku ku asula bɛya. Ɔsika Unwoti ndi Katɔti ɔni ngyi lɛla biala. Na ɔɔkɔ́ku ablala ƒui taanu.

english_verse: Our Lord, you break the bows of warriors, but you give strength to everyone who stumbles.
translation_verse: Anwu mɔɔƒɛ bekpone kɔtaminta. Nsu ɔɔkya bani na lɛlɔ lɛ́bla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ɔkplu.

english_verse: People who once had plenty to eat must now hire themselves out for only a piece of bread. But you give the hungry more than enough to eat. A woman did not have a child, and you gave her seven, but a woman who had many was left with none.
translation_verse: Bani na ala ása ese-ma na baadi teemo ni, ama muusé lɛlɔ ɔkpa asa baakɛ́ lɛdila. Nsu bani nátaatɛ kɔka ni, ama mɔɔdi teemo ɔƒɛni. Na udinkɔ nábawɔ bebi maatɛ. Nsu uwele ɔni na ubo bebi pii ɔyila nwuna bebi ƒui.

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: Unwoti mɔɔyá na ukyuli uukpi na anwu kani mɔɔyá na ukyuli uulie ngba. Anwu mɔɔyá bekyuli beeduo kekpine. Na anwu kani mɔɔgyila-ma taasiku kekpine.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: Unwoti muute lɛkɛ. Na anwu kani mɔɔyá kɔwaba kɔɔda ukyuli. Anwu mɔɔkɔliku ukyuli katɔ. Na anwu kani muuboku ukyuli kalɔ.

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: Anwu mɔɔtalaku bawabane katɔ na baalɛ́ ɔtumu akɔ, na bani mɔɔyaki ala mmɔ baata ntɔ kewikɔ, na beelie kuliekɔ kunengudi kɔni bagabi beelie. Unwoti nése kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛtabi ɔka kalɔ. Na nwuna lɛlɔ na ɔ́tu kayawi ƒui ɔ́lɛ na kadi nwuna kadi.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: Ɔdubɔgyumana nwuna bekyuli kedee ƒui na bana kɔvinkɔ. Nsu balalane ni, badubo bɔyi bɔkya lɛdisa kemmo na bayii ku udu. Ukyuli ulélie ngba ɔkɛnku anwu ɔlati ɔyikun lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: Na bani muukpóku Unwoti ni, ɔdubɔkɔ-ma lɛlɔ ɔvi na babwɛ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ. Na kayaa kadubɔbwɛ ogya kebewi-ma lɛlɔ. Unwoti ɔdubɔtɛku bayawine ƒui litemi utédu kalɔ kammɔ ƒui kawɔkɔ. Ɔga ɔni na úse ni, ɔdubɔkya-nwu ɔyikun na ɔya na nwuna lili lɛlɛ aani ebuo lise. Ɔsika anwu na úwi nnɔmii lili úse likpo.”

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Elkana únwini úsie nwuna ɔma na Rama. Na ubidi ɔnanabi ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kya Eli kudɔ na Katɔti kakpakɔ mmɔ útaabla kabla. Eli Bebi Bábla Likyulikpi Ala

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni bana ɔbladu ukpidi ɔmmɔ úbenwini-ma udu. Na si ukyuli ɔdi úboku ebuo ɔnii ubakpa na lɛna lɛmmɔ lɛsia ogya lɛlɔ ni, na baatala bana kabla ɔblane ɔdi na uti ɔvili ɔni mbo atula atɛ ɔda.

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: Kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ uuti ɔvili ɔmmɔ na ubatu lɛna lɛni nsia ogya mmɔ lɛdi udie na libui kemmo. Na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔƒɔ-ni. Na lɛni kani na baabla ku Israelni biala ɔni nébo Silo mmɔ.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Na ɔƒaani ni, lɛmwi lɛmmɔ muedi asa na badubɔkyula-ni ni, kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ uubo na ubasu ukyuli ɔni mɔɔbla akpala ammɔ ɔnini, “Bite ɔkpane nwuna lɛna na ɔgyi, ɔsika ulawia ka buƒulo nwuna lɛna mmomu ɔɔwia-ni ɔwɔdi.”

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Uwi pii si úbo lɛni ni, bɔsu na bekyuli bammɔ baasu banii kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ ɔlati udie lɛni na ɔɔyɔ́. Mmomu ɔya na baka-ni buti bɔkpa bute Unwoti asa. Nsu kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ ɔɔsu-ma ɔnini, “Oowo, na si bitenu-mi kalɔ bɔdi ni, ndubudie lɛni mɔɔyɔ́ ɔkplu kemmo.”

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Eli bebi bamɛni beléte Unwoti akpala ɔbu ɔdi ɔni na bana likpidi lɛmɛni lɛdi bɔƒiɔ bunengudi geen na Unwoti anumi.

english_verse: The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔmmɔ ƒui ni, na ubi Samuel ɔkya Katɔti kakpakɔ mmɔ ɔɔbla nwuna kabla. Na ɔkya bakpane awu ɔƒualadi kedee.

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa ndi lɛkwa ni, uni uudí awu bamba teesienku-nwu si uwi ɔni na anwu ku ɔgyani bésela batábla lɛkwa akpala.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Na Eli uute Elkana ku ulekudi kusɛ kusɛ. Na ɔɔsu-ma ɔnini, “Unwoti ute-mii bebi bamba na bɛwɔ, na ama benye udeedi kenye ka anwu na ƒ'ulekudi úvele Unwoti na úte-nwu, na ɔ́sɔku-nwu úte Unwoti.” Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, baasɔ teenwini teesie bana ɔma.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́bla Hana lɛƒɔndia sɔsɔ na ɔsɔ úbada kaƒɔ na ɔ́wɔ bebi bananabi ɛtɛ ku belekubi inyɔ. Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Katɔti anumi ásia Samuel lɛlɔ na ɔ́lɛ lili geen na kakpakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Eli was now very old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Eli lɛnɔ ɔ́ɔbi geen na uunú lɛnɔ kalɛ na nwuna bebi bamɛni baabla Israel kadi bekyuli ƒui. Na Adi Kevo kani kemmo baasiáku Katɔti kenye, baatɛnku beleku bani mɔɔbla kabla mmɔ.

english_verse: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
translation_verse: Si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́bla nwuna ɔkpana lɛla lɛdi ni, Katɔti ɔɔkana na ɔɔklibi bana ntɛ litemi na unwi bɔbla bubo. Nsu si Unwoti ɔmmɔ ɔlati na áƒiɔ bɔƒiɔ bonwu bɔdi udu ni, ɔma ndubɔkana awɔ ku Unwoti ntɛ buduo na uvele ute-ɔ?” Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui ni, bebi bammɔ bétenu bana ɔti bɔdɔnku ku bɔlɛ. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́ɔlɛ ugyii ka ɔyila-ma udu.

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ƒui ni, Samuel ɔɔlɛ́ lili geen na nwuna lɛlɔ lɛɛda Unwoti ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ebiti. Kenye Udiene Ɔ́su Ka Ɔgbankpi Ɔdubo Eli Kaduli

english_verse: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, Katɔti kenye Udiene ɔdi úbo Eli kudɔ na úbasu-nwu ɔnini, “Se atu na enu lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔnii mbeye-ɔ. Ɔɔsu ɔnini, ‘Ɔɔɔdi ami nédie lɛlɔ lɛtina ƒula bati kuuku kaduli bekyuli uwi ɔni na bákya Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ na Ɔga Ƒarao kalɔ yoo?

english_verse: Out of all the tribes of Israel, I chose your family to be my priests. I wanted them to offer sacrifices and burn incense to me and to find out from me what I want my people to do. I commanded everyone to bring their sacrifices here where I live, and I allowed you and your family to keep those that were not offered to me on the altar. But you honor your sons instead of me! You don't respect the sacrifices and offerings that are brought to me, and you've all grown fat from eating the best parts.
translation_verse: Na etela ku akpala ani na béti béboku-mi aani kalɛ na lɛ́tina ka babla na mina keliekɔ ni, bi ɔsu na bɛɛyá na eesé lɛlɔ? Na bi ɔsu na aabu ƒula bebi teetulo-mi, na bíti mina bekyuli bammɔ etela ku akpala ammɔ kɔdikɔ kɔbuni ƒui bínwini amii kɔdi na bílie lɛmwi?’

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti ɔnini, ‘Lɛ́lɛ ugyii ka ƒula kaduli ku ƒ'ɔti kaduli bekyuli kani ndubunye-mi anumi butaabla-mi kabla uwi ƒui.’ Nsu ɔƒɛni ni, Unwoti ɔɔsu ka ɔmmɔ ɔsɔ ɔɔɔdubo buse lɛni. Mmomu ukyuli ɔni mɔɔbu-mi ni, ami lɛnɔ ndubo-nwu bɔbu. Nsu ukyuli ɔni naaabu-mi ni, ami lɛnɔ lɛɛɛdubo-nwu bɔbu.

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔdi ɔdubo ɔni na ndubɔya na awɔ ku ƒula ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli ngba bɔda liku ɔni na basɔ baaadubo unengu ɔdi bɔkɛ na bina kaduli kemmo. Na bina ɔyikun lɛnɔ ɔdubɔyii udu.

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: Na ɔgbankpi ɔdubo bina ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli bɔsiaku ina ka ndubɔya na kusɛ kusɛ pii ɔsiaku Israelƒuɔ. Nsu amii bina ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli ama ni, basɔ baaadubo unengu ɔdi bɔkɛ.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: Na ina lɛ́ya na bina akɔ ɔdi únwini ɔkpane na mina lɛkpabi lɛlɔ ni, ɔdubɔya na imii sɔɔn bɔƒɔ-mii anumi na ala eteekpoku-mii. Na bina ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli ƒui ni, bana lɛkloƒu uwi kani na badubo buteekpi.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: “Na lɛla lɛni ndubɔlɛku ƒula bebi Hoƒni ku Pinehas ni, anwu na adubuti ati lɛla lɛni na mɔɔsu-ɔ mɛni. Bana inyɔ badubo bukpi limeyi linwi.

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Na ndubudie ɔkpane bamba ɔni mabla mina kayi ku kasusu lɛyɔla. Ndubɔya na nwuna ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli benye kpakplaa na ɔbla-mi kabla uwi biala uti ubunku ɔga ɔni na lɛ́ƒuna.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala ɔni mebu na ƒula ɔtɔ kaba bebi akɔ ni, mina ɔkpane ɔmɛni na ɔdububo ubakya lili kalɔ ute na uvele-nwu sika iye bodobodo asa wakɛ lɛdila. Na ɔdubuvele ka ɔya na ɔkɛ ɔkpane kabla kadi utaabla kalɛ limeyi lɛdila ani lɛsɔ lilabɔ-nwu.”

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: Na ka Samuel ɔ́wɔlɔ nwuna kabla ni, ɔ́yu ɔ́tɛ ɔnii utaalɛɛ na kakpakɔ mmɔ kesii kani na Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ ɔlɛ kudɔ na asogya ɔma ɔɔda.

english_verse: when the Lord called out Samuel's name. “Here I am!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́kpali Samuel na ɔ́tuna ɔnii, “Ati aanu-mi.”

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: Amu na úkeli úsie Eli kudɔ na útásu-nwu ɔnii únu ka ɔ́kpali-nwu ɔsu úubo. Mmɔ na Eli údie kenye ɔnini, “Ńtakpali-ɔ. Teesie na atátɛ.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Samuel únwini útátɛ.

english_verse: Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?” Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
translation_verse: Ka ɔ́bla blii ni, Unwoti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kpali-nwu kunyɔdi na Samuel ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tuna na úkeli úsie Eli kudɔ na útásu-nwu ɔnini, “Ati aanu-mi. Líibo, ɔsika línu ka ákpali-mi.” Eli ɔ́sɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Ubi, ńtakpali-ɔ, teesie na atátɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ni, Unwoti útatɛmiku tɔ Samuel kudii na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo, na Samuel lɛnɔ útati tɔ Unwoti.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kpali Samuel kɔtɛdi. Na anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́ta úkeli úsie Eli kudɔ útásu-nwu ɔnii, “Ati aanu-mi. Líibo, ɔsika ákpali-mi.” Mmɔ ni, Eli ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka Unwoti na ɔdi mɔɔkpali Samuel.

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Eli ɔ́su Samuel ɔnini, “Teesie na atátɛ. Na si énu ka básɔ bákpali-ɔ ni, na asu anii, ‘Unwoti, aanu ami ƒula kabla ɔblane. Su-mi lɛla lɛni na lɛbla.’ ” Anwuɔsu Samuel ɔ́sɔ únwini útátɛ nwuna katɛnkɔ kalɛ na ɔɔyɔ́ bɔbla.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́sɔ úbo úbakpali Samuel aani kudeedi kalɛ ɔnii, “Samuel, Samuel.” Amu na Samuel ɔ́tuna ɔnini, “Unwoti, aanu ami ƒula kabla ɔblane. Su-mi lɛla lɛni na lɛbla.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́su Samuel ɔnini, “Nu! Ndubo lɛla lɛdi bɔbla na Israel ɔni na ɔtɔtɔ ɔdubɔgyu ukyuli biala ɔni menu lɛla lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: Ɔsika lɛ́su-nwu ka ndubo anwu ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ƒui kɔtɔ bɔdu na likpidi lɛni na ɔgyi nwaa, nsu údie atu ɔsu. Nwuna bebi ala bɔbla émo bekyuli bammɔ ƒui, nsu útakana na ɔ́bala-ma ɔsiku ɔbladu buɛ ɔmmɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu líse kenye na lɛ́su ka Eli ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli likpidi lɛni na bábla ni, akpala iye kɔtɔ bukpi etela adi alakana likpidi lɛmmɔ budie.”

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Nwuna kama ni, Samuel úsie útátɛ ɔ́lɛɛ laa na kadi kegye asa na ɔ́ta ɔ́lɛmi kakpakɔ mmɔ. Na lɛla lɛni na Unwoti údie ɔ́tina-nwu ni, ɔɔyia ka udie-ni ɔsu Eli.

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Nsu Eli ɔ́kpali ɔnini, “Mina Ubi. Samuel.” Na anwu lɛnɔ úkeli úsie na útásu-nwu ɔnini, “Ati, aanu-mi mɛni.”

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Eli úye Samuel ɔnini, “Bi na Unwoti ɔ́su-ɔ? Teti lɛla lɛdi tabɛla-mi. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni na ébu lɛla lɛdi ése na átasu-mi ani ni, Unwoti ɔni-ɔ kɔtu geen.”

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Samuel ɔ́sɔku lɛla biala ɔ́su Eli na útabɛla-nwu lɛla lɛdi. Amu na Eli údie kenye ɔnini, “Anwu ndi bula Unwoti, anwuɔsu buuubo lɛla lɛdi na bɔsu, mmomu ɔbla nwuna lɛyɔla lɛni na ɔ́nu ka lɛdia na lɛ́manku.”

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Kalɛ kani na Samuel ɔɔbi lɛlɔ teebu ni, lɛni na Unwoti ɔsiaku-nwu. Na ala ani ƒui na ɔɔsu ni, eebo-nwu kemmo lɛni, na ɔdi ulásia kɔmadɔ.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ bekyuli ƒui ɔ́si ɔma ɔni baalɔ Dan útédu Beer-Seba ni, bánu ɔmmɔ báti na beedie kenye ka Samuel ɔdi Unwoti Kenye Udiene.

english_verse: The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_verse: Unwoti úsie anumi na uudie lɛlɔ taatina na Silo mmɔ ɔkɛnku ala ani na ɔɔsu Samuel lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Israelƒuɔ báta banii betékpoku Ƒilistiƒuɔ. Na bátábla kakyakɔ na kesii kani baalɔ Eben-Eser. Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bábla kakyakɔ na Aƒek.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bésie na bététi Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ. Na nwuna lɛlɔ ni, Unwoti batu bebweyi inyɔ badi udu bénye bani baalɔ Kerub na bebo avwi. Na Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ kudɔ ni, Eli bebi inyɔ, Hoƒni ku Pinehas, benye.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
translation_verse: Ka bekpone bakladi bénwini bébo bana kakyakɔ ni, bana benengu bammɔ béye banini, “Bi ɔsu na Unwoti ɔ́ya na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bádi-bu lɛlɔ ɔmwi? Bɛya na butágyu Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka bɔsiku Silo buboku, na buti bɔdanku kekpokɔ mmɔ. Na ɔdubɔƒɔ ute-bu na bula bekisine ɔsu.”

english_verse: brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Ka Bunyimi Adaka ɔmɛni úbeduo Israelƒuɔ kakyakɔ mmɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ bébo kudu momoomo geen ɔni náya na kalɔ kákunku.

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Na ɔni na kɔkun kɔmmɔ kúwi Ƒilistiƒuɔ ni, béye banii, “Bi kɔvanu na Hebriƒuɔ bamɛni baabla lɛni na bana kakyakɔ?” Amu ka bébenu ka Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ na béti béboku mmɔ ni,

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: liƒu bonwu líduo Ƒilistiƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui. Mmɔ na básu banini, “Báƒiɔ badi bébo bébeduo Israelƒuɔ kudɔ na bana kakyakɔ mmɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu búduo ɔgbankpi kemmo, ɔsika lɛla lɛmɛni udu lítalɛ kudii.

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: Ɔlɛka bɔnu lɛlɔ kemmo kaduɛ. Ɔma ndubo-bu budie na baƒiɔ bamɛni enu kemmo? Bɔgyi ka baƒiɔ bekpone na badi. Na ama nékpoku Egyipteƒuɔ na kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo ku lɛlɛ lidu lidu.

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Ƒilistiƒuɔ, binye kpakplaa na bɛdi lɛnanabi. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni bɛdubo bunwini Israelƒuɔ kabla bablane aani kalɛ kani na ama bákya-bu kalɔ dii!”

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: Na béƒie Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ báƒɔ, na Eli bebi inyɔ bammɔ lɛnɔ békpi. Eli Úkpi

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛni kani lɛlɔ na Eli bebi békpi mmɔ ni, ɔnana ɔdi ɔ́si Benyamin kɔdua kemmo úkeli ɔ́si kekpokɔ mmɔ úsie Silo. Nwuna adala áduli ƒui na ɔtumu uwi-nwu kuli.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́da úbalɛ ni, Eli uli nwuna liboku lɛlɔ na ulu kɔtu ɔɔnu ulu, ɔsika Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ kani na nwuna anu asia. Ɔƒɛni ka ɔnana ɔmmɔ úduo ɔma kemmo na ɔ́su bekyuli lɛla lɛni nálɛ ni, ɔma ɔmmɔ ƒui lɛsɛ ku kɔvanu kani nda.

english_verse: “Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: Mɛni na ɔnana ɔni ndanku kenye kamɛni úboku údie kenye ɔnini, “Israelƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ ni, bukeli na búkeli Ƒilistiƒuɔ bammɔ ɔni na bádu bula bekyuli pii. Ɔƒɛni ƒula bebi inyɔ bammɔ lɛnɔ békpi na béƒie Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ báƒɔ.”

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Amu ka Eli únu ka ɔ́lɔ Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ lɛnyi ni, ɔ́kada úsie kama kama na útáyu kalɔ akpatete na ɔban ɔmmɔ kayakun kenye. Na ɔ́ƒɛ limɔ na úkpi, ɔsika ɔ́ɔbla unengu geen. Akwa aavlene na ɔ́tɔnku Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ bekyuli.

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ubidi Pinehas ulekudi ni, ɔda kaƒɔ uwi ɔmmɔ na káabi ƒui lɛnɔ ka ɔwɔ. Na únye mmɔ na únu ka Ƒilistiƒuɔ béƒie Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ baƒɔ na ɔgyani lɛnɔ úkpi. Na ɔ́nu lɛnɔ ka ɔgyanti lɛnɔ ɔ́lɛ útébo kalɔ na anwu lɛnɔ úkpi. Mmɔ ni, kawɔƒɔ kése kalɔ kaadu-nwu.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: Na ka únu kɔwɔ kɔmmɔ ɔlɛ ɔ́vili úti ubunku lɛla lɛni muukpóku-nwu ɔsu ni, anwu lɛnɔ úkpi kawɔkɔ mmɔ ina ka bekyuli bani mɔɔƒɔ́-nwu kɔwɔ bése-nwu kayi ka ɔnanabi ɔdi na ɔ́wɔ.

english_verse: Instead she kept thinking about losing her husband and her father-in-law. So she said, “My son will be named Ichabod, because the glory of Israel left our country when the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na ɔɔyula ni, mmɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bɛsia-nwu lɛnyi bɛnii Ikabod, ɔsika Katɔti ɔ́ya na Israelƒuɔ bukeye bɔ́yii udu na Bunyimi Adaka ɔni na béƒie báƒɔ mmɔ ɔsu.”

english_verse: The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod.
translation_verse: Ka Ƒilistiƒuɔ béƒie Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ báƒɔ ni, béti-nwu básiku Eben-Eser bésienku Asdod.

english_verse: They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
translation_verse: Na ka béti-nwu béboku mmɔ ni, béti-nwu bétése bana baƒiɔ ɔtɔ na badi baƒiɔ benengudi bani na baakpá na baalɔ-ma Dagon. Béti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ bényene Dagon baƒiɔ bani na bávɔ bényene mmɔ kɔmadɔ.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: Amu ka kadi kégye ni, Asdod ɔma bekyuli báta bébo ɔƒiɔtɔ mmɔ. Na bánu ka Dagon baƒiɔ lɛtabi lɛni na bávɔ mmɔ lɛ́lɛ líbo. Na nina anumi ebi kalɔ na Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ anumi. Amu na bátala lɛtabi lɛmmɔ bényene.

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
translation_verse: Nsu ka kadi bamba kégye ni, banu ka lɛtabi lɛmmɔ lɛ́sɔ lɛ́lɛ líbo, na nina anumi ebi kalɔ na Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ anumi aani kudeedi kalɛ kani. Nsu ɔƒaani ni, bánu ka nwuna lili ku enu áƒɛ álɛ-nwu lɛlɔ. Na lili ku enuku ammɔ ewi kalɔ na atabi akɔ na kayakun.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu úti úbedu ku ɔmwi si baƒiɔ bakpane bammɔ ku bana basiakune beeduo ɔƒiɔtɔ mmɔ ni, balánya kayakun. Mmomu baadá taavia kesii kani na Dagon baƒiɔ bammɔ lili ku enuku áƒɛ ébewi na kayakun mmɔ. Na balánya mmɔ kudii.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́ya na ɔgbankpi pii ɔ́siaku Asdod ɔma bekyuli ku ekutɛ mmɔ badi ƒui. Na ɔ́ya na alɛbi álɛ éwi-ma lɛlɔ ƒui na ɔ́yila badi udu. Ɔmɛni ɔsu bana ƒui báta bábla susuusu.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Kawɔlɔkɔ ni, ama alati básu banini, “Israel Katɔti nábla ɔmɛni. Anwu náya na ɔmɛni ɔɔlɛ́ku-bu ku bula baƒiɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔ́lɛka bɔda Bunyimi Adaka ɔmɛni budie bula ɔƒiɔtɔ mɛni kɔnakunwi.”

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Amu na Asdod ɔma bekyuli bálɔ Ƒilistiƒuɔ agyina besiene ƒui básala na Asdod mmɔ na béye-ma banini, “Bi na ɔlɛka bɔblaku Israelƒuɔ Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmɛni?” Amu na batɔnkune bammɔ bédie kenye banini, “Biti-nwu bimene ɔma ɔni baalɔ Gat.” Amu na béti-nwu bétése mmɔ.

english_verse: the Lord made sores break out on everyone in town. The people of Gath were frightened,
translation_verse: Nsu útaƒɔ uwi asa alɛbi álɛ éwi bana ɔdi biala lɛnɔ lɛlɔ na mmɔ. Na ɔmɛni úbakya Gat ɔma bekyuli liƒu geen.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ama lɛnɔ béti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ bémene ɔma ɔni baalɔ Ekron. Nsu ka bétédu mmɔ ni, bátavia ɔma ɔmmɔ ɔban kenye asa Ekron ɔma bekyuli bése kalɔ beení-ma ku kɔvanu momoomo banini, “Béti Israel Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka badububoku bula ɔma. Na ɔdubo abu ku bula bebi bɔdu.” Ƒilistiƒuɔ Básɔku Bunyimi Adaka Bátɔlɔku

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Ka bétenuku-ma kalɔ ɔsu ni, Ekron ɔma bekyuli lɛnɔ bálɔ Ƒilistiƒuɔ agyina besiene kelisa na básu-ma banini, “Bɛsɔku Bunyimi Adaka ɔmɛni bimene bekyuli bani ɔdi na ɔdi kalɛ na bulása bukpi.” Liƒu líduo ɔdi biala ɔƒɛni amu, ɔsika ɔgbankpi geen ndaku bɔlɛ kesii kani ƒui na bada Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ baavínku. Na Israel Katɔti ɔdaku nwuna ɔyikun budie taatina geen.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Na bani na bétekpi tɔ muedi beenú ɔlɛ geen na alɛbi ani nsia-ma lɛlɔ ɔsu. Na benye baakpali bana baƒiɔ kpakplaa ka baƒɔ bete-ma.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔ́kya Ƒilistiƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, ɔbla abuli maatɛ.

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bálɔ bana bakpane ku like bebone na béye-ma banini, “Bi na bɔdubo bɔbla ku Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmɛni? Bɛsu-bu kalɛ na bɔdubo bɔbla asa na wasɔ wetédu kesii kani na ɔ́si.”

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bédie kenye banini, “Si bɛ́sɔku Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ bíselaku Israel ni, biteti anwu lɛti bitada, mmomu biti etela adi bibunku bitékpi kɔtɔ. Na bina ɔlɛ ɔdubɔba-mii. Na bɛdubɔti lɛnɔ lɛla lɛni ɔsu na Unwoti ɔ́ya na ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni udu ɔ́siaku-mii lɛni.”

english_verse: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
translation_verse: Na bi ɔsu na bɛɛbla atuɔkplu aani kalɛ na Egyipteƒuɔ ku Ƒarao bábla? Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu na ɔ́ni-ma kɔtu kpakplaa útálɛ ka bágya Israelƒuɔ bálɛku bana ɔma na béti bana ulu?

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: “Ɔƒɛni ni, bɛwia kɛɛkɛ ɔwɔdi ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ inyɔ bani muute bana bebi anyi. Na bɛnu ka bétebo kɔbuli bátada-ma na bani kɛɛkɛ ɔdi kudii iye bátabala-ma anwami bonwu ku kɔgba na batuma kudii. Na bɛmami bebi bammɔ bana lɛlɔ bitákya kesii bamba asa na bibo kɛɛkɛ ɔmmɔ lɛbuli bɛda-ma.

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, bɛgyu Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ bɛkya kɛɛkɛ ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na biti sika ugyiedi kɔlɛmii kɔmmɔ bɛkya obo bamba kemmo bise adaka ɔmmɔ kɔmadɔ. Na bidie bebuo bani ndubɔni kɛɛkɛ ku ala ammɔ ƒui ulu.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: Na bitaasia-nwu anumi taanu, si ɔ́sia ɔma ulu lɛlɔ siin úsela Bet-Semes ni, na bɛgyi ka ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni ɔ́si Unwoti kudɔ asa na úbo-bu lɛlɔ. Na si útasia lɛni bɔdi ni, na bɛgyi ka ɔgbankpi keeke kani nátuaku-bu.”

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bábla ala amɛni ƒui. Na béti kɛɛkɛ ɔmmɔ lɛbuli bébo báda ɔmantɛ bakɔ bammɔ lɛlɔ na bámami bana bebi bammɔ bátákya kesii bamba.

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: Amu na béti Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ básia kɛɛkɛ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ku obo ɔni kemmo na sika ugyiedi besi ku alɛbi udu ɔni bávɔ mmɔ akya.

english_verse: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔmantɛ bakɔ bammɔ báyu ulu, na bakɛ siin bésela Bet-Semes. Na bakɛ beebó kudu na ulu lɛlɔ uwi ƒui. Na bétedeyi kɔmii iye kɔdianu. Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ batɔnkune bammɔ basiaku-ma kama laa útédu Bet-Semes ɔmii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Bet-Semes bekyuli bakya baaƒɛ bana edula ebi ani na bákya na ɔkwalɛ kemmo. Ka bátalaku anumi ni, bánu ka Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmɛni ɔsia kɛɛkɛ lɛlɔ ɔɔyu. Na lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ-ma geen.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Ƒilsitiƒuɔ agyina besiene ɛlɔ bani nsiaku kɛɛkɛ ɔmmɔ kama bébo mmɔ bábanu ɔmɛni ƒui asa na bénwini bésie Ekron limeyi lɛmmɔ kani lɛlɔ.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Sika ugyiedi alɛbi udu ɔni na Ƒilistiƒuɔ béti bésienku bétékpi Unwoti kɔtɔ ni, unwi ɔdi Asdod ɔdi, Gasa ɔdi unwi, Askelon ɔdi unwi, Gat ɔdi unwi, na Ekron ɔdi lɛnɔ unwi.

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: Na sika ugyiedi ɔni bávɔ na besi udu kenye lɛnɔ ubo ɛlɔ na Ƒilistiƒuɔ lɛma ɛlɔ bɔni kenye na agyina besiene bammɔ benye bumomo kenye. Na lɛma lɛmmɔ ndi lɛni na bátu awodu bámana ku lɛma lɛwɛwɛlɛdi lɛni mma-ni lɛlɔ. Na lɛtakpɛ lɛni lɛlɔ na bágyu Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ bálɛ ni, ɔmu ɔdi likposela na Yosua ɔni nási Bet-Semes kalɔ kemmo ku ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Bet-Semesƒuɔ béye banini, “Ɔma mbo ɔyikun na ɔkali ɔnii uunye ɔsiaku Unwoti Katɔti Kedee ɔmɛni. Na ɔma na bɔdubuti Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmɛni bumene ɔƒaani?”

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Amu na bátala batu bákya Kiriat-Yearimƒuɔ banii, “Ƒilistiƒuɔ básɔku Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ béboku. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bibo na bibeti-nwu bitése bina kudɔ.”

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Kiriat-Yearim bekyuli bébo na bébeti Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ bésienku Aminadab kesii. Na nwuna kaduli kakya abi lɛlɔ na bana ɔma kemmo. Na ubidi Eleasa na báƒuna ka utaanu Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, Samuel ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ ƒui ɔnini, “Si bɛɛyɔ́ ka binwini udu na biti lɛlɔ bite Unwoti bɔdi ni, amu ɔlɛka bidie bɛtina nwaa na bina ɔbladu kemmo. Na bɛyila baƒiɔ bani na bɛ́vɔ bíte lɛlɔ udu. Na bɛyila Astarot baƒiɔ bani lɛnɔ bɛ́vɔ mmɔ udu. Binwini kama bɛkya baƒiɔ bammɔ ƒui na biti bina kayi bite Unwoti ƒui kede kede. Na bitaakya lili kalɔ teete anwu lɛti pɛ na ɔda-mii udie Ƒilsitiƒuɔ enu kemmo.”

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Sɔsɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ báda Baal baƒiɔ ku Astarot baƒiɔ bammɔ bɔkpa báya. Na bése kalɔ baakpá Unwoti lɛti.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Amu na Samuel ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ɔnini, “Bɛya na Israelni biala ubo. Na bɛsala lɛlɔ na Mispa na ndubɔkpali Unwoti na livele-nwu lite-mii.”

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Amu uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ básala lɛlɔ na Mispa ni, Samuel únye aani Israelƒuɔ ɔtɔnkune kalɛ na Mispa, na bédu ntu na libiɔ kemmo na beebó-mu teewi kalɔ teete Unwoti aani lɛlɔ buti teete-nwu akpala. Na bélie kɔka limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ, na bédie bana alaekpidi kalɔ básu Unwoti banini, “O Unwoti, bɔ́bla likpidi bɔ́ƒiɔ-ɔ.”

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Ka Ƒilistiƒuɔ bénu ka Israelƒuɔ ƒui bása na Mispa ni, Ƒilsitiƒuɔ agyina besiene báta banii bebekpoku-ma na mmɔ. Amu ɔni na Israelƒuɔ lɛnɔ bénu lɛni ni, liƒu lɛ́da-ma na báyia geen na Ƒilistiƒuɔ ɔkplu ɔsu.

english_verse: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na básu Samuel banini, “Tada bula Unwoti Katɔti bɔkpali taya na bula lili. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ ɔdubunu ƒula bɔkpali na udie-bu na Ƒilsitiƒuɔ enu kemmo.”

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Ɔni na Samuel uwi lɛkpa lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ geen ni, Ƒilistiƒuɔ lɛnɔ bátu akpagya badubo banii bebéyu-ma batu na mmɔ na bekpoku-ma. Nsu mmɔ kani ni, Unwoti ɔ́bɔku Ƒilistiƒuɔ ku lɛdi momoomo lɛni náku aani kalɛ katɔ keedu ku kudu bonwu. Na ɔmmɔ ɔ́ya na Ƒilistiƒuɔ báyia bávili bébu ɔni na use aani lɛla lɛdi nágyu-ma ku lɛgba ɔ́bɔku-ma údie Israelƒuɔ anumi mmɔ.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ lɛnɔ bábi básiaku-ma ɔ́si Mispa mmɔ. Na bádu Ƒilistiƒuɔ bammɔ ukpone biala na ulu lɛlɔ laa útédu kesii kani baalɔ bani Bet-Kar.

english_verse: The Philistines were so badly beaten that it was quite a while before they attacked Israel again. After the battle, Samuel set up a monument between Mizpah and the rocky cliffs. He named it “Help Monument” to remind Israel how much the Lord had helped them. For as long as Samuel lived, the Lord helped Israel fight the Philistines.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Israelƒuɔ bádi Ƒilistiƒuɔ lɛlɔ na básɔ bátakana na benye basiaku Israelƒuɔ kudii na bana kalɛkɛ mmɔ kesii kadi. Na Samuel ngba bulie uwi ƒui ni, Ƒilistiƒuɔ bátakɛ bɔnwuna bɔdi na Unwoti lɛkɔkɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni Israelƒuɔ lɛma lɛni na Ƒilistiƒuɔ báƒɔ ɔ́si Ekron útédu Gat ni, Israelƒuɔ básɔ báƒɔ-ni. Na kalɛkɛ kani na Ƒilistiƒuɔ báƒɔ na amadɔ mmɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ báƒɔ mmɔ lɛnɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu atu bɔyɔ bɔ́kya Amonƒuɔ ku Israelƒuɔ ntɛ ƒui.

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Samuel ɔ́tɔnku Israelƒuɔ aani bana litemi ɔtɛne nwuna ngba kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa ndi lɛkwa ni, uusié taavi-ma lɛlɔ ɔ́si Betel úsie Gilgal útédu Mispa taatátɛ etemila.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: Nsu uwi biala kemmo ni, ɔɔsɔ teenwini teesie Rama kesii kani ndi-nwu keliekɔ geen. Na mmɔ lɛnɔ ɔɔnu ka Israelƒuɔ bammɔ bábla lɛla biala kaduɛ. Na ɔ́tu lɛkpabi lɛdi úte Unwoti na mmɔ.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: Na ubidi udeedi baalɔ Yoel. Na unyɔdi baalɔ Abiya. Na bana inyɔ ƒui bátaabla Unwoti kabla na Beer-Seba.

english_verse: But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
translation_verse: Nsu bebi bamɛni balabla ala siin na Unwoti ulu lɛlɔ. Mmomu bénwini kama bákya-nwu na baabla bekyuli ulikplu ala na baaƒɔ́-ma ala taadi na bɔbɛ kemmo. Na balábla lɛla lɛdi ulu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Israelƒuɔ benengu bammɔ básala lɛlɔ na bébo Samuel kudɔ na Rama.

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: Na bábasu-nwu banini, “Bɔɔnu ka áabi lɛlɔ geen. Na ngba buni bɔni na élie ni, amu kani na atina ƒula bebi. Nsu bɔɔnu ka bebi bammɔ beeelie ngba bɔmmɔ udu. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bɔɔwia ka ese ɔga ete-bu na ɔtɔnku-bu aani kalɛ kani na use na kadi bamba bekyuli akɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Nsu ka básu banini, “Te-bu ɔga ɔni matɔnku-bu” ni, lɛla lɛmɛni lítayɔ Samuel kaƒɔ. Anwuɔsu ɔ́kpali Unwoti na úti litemi lɛmmɔ ɔ́kya-nwu lɛkɔkɔ.

english_verse: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti údie kenye ɔnini, “Awɔ, nu lɛla lɛni na baasu-ɔ. Ɔsika ɔɔɔdi awɔ na béni. Mmomu ami na béni ka balayɔ ka lɛdi-ma ɔga.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: Kalɛ na béni banii baladi mina etemila lɛlɔ na baakpá baƒiɔ ɔ́si ɔni na lɛ́kpanku-ma lɛ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ úti úbalɛku ɔmwi limeyi lɛlɔ ni, udu ɔmmɔ kani na beedie taatina-a ɔƒɛni.

english_verse: Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
translation_verse: Ɔƒaani ni, awɔ nu lɛla lɛni na baasu-ɔ. Mmomu tɛmiku-ma kpakplaa na aya na bati bese kalɛ na ukyuli ɔni ndubo-ma lɛlɔ bɔdi ɔdubo buse.”

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Samuel ɔ́sɔku lɛla biala lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ benengu bani mɔɔwia ka bese ɔga bete-ma mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔga ɔni na bɛɛwia ka lise lite-mii ni, binu kalɛ na ɔdubo buse. Ɔdubo bina bebi lɛlɔ bunye na benwini nwuna bekpone. Na bataabla kabla na nwuna kekpo bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ kemmo. Na babambadi badubunwini bekpone bani muulie bapɔnkɔ. Na badi lɛnɔ bakɛ lɛgba na nwuna bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ anumi.

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
translation_verse: Na bina bebi belekubi ni, ɔdubɔƒɔ-ma, na ɔya na bataabla ala awɛɛdi ƒɛƒɛɛ teete-nwu. Na badi lɛnɔ bataanwi nwuna adila na beteeƒi bodobodo lɛnɔ.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: “Bina kalɔ edula abunidi ƒui ɔdubɔƒɔ-nya unwini anwu ɔdi. Na bina adingyii mmo lidu ƒui lɛnɔ ɔdubuƒie-mu ɔƒɔ ute nwuna kabla bablane.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: Na bina edula ani na bɛdubo bɔƒɛ ni, ɔdubɔƒɔ ana lɛkpa leevudi ɔsiku ɔdi biala kudɔ bute nwuna bekpone benengu ku lɛgadi benengu.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: “Bina bananabi ku beleku kabla bablane ƒui ni, ɔdubɔya na benwini bataabla-nwu kabla. Na bina ɔmantɛ bakɔ bani mɔɔtuma teete-mi ku bebuo ala betine ƒui bataabla nwuna kabla.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: Bina baƒonu ni, ɔdubɔƒɔ bana lɛkpa leevudi. Na amii alati binwini nwuna kabla bablane.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni limeyi lɛdubo lɛni na bɛdubo buwulo bɔkpali-mi bɛnii nƒɔ-mii nlɛku ɔga ɔni na amii alati bɛ́ƒuna bíte lɛlɔ mmɔ enu kemmo. Nsu lɛɛɛdubo-mii bɔkpete limeyi lɛmmɔ.”

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na abu lɛnɔ buse aani bekyuli bakladi kalɛ. Na bɔkɛ ɔga na ɔtɔnku-bu si búsela kekpokɔ biala.”

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Ka Samuel únu ala ani na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ básu ni, ɔ́sɔku-nya ƒui ɔ́su Unwoti. Amu na Unwoti lɛnɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Awɔ, nu-ma litemi na ese ɔga ete-ma.”

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Samuel lɛnɔ ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ banana bammɔ ƒui ɔnini, “Ɔdi biala unwini uteesie nwuna ɔma.”

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ɔnana ɔlakɛne ɔdi ɔ́kya na baalɔ-nwu Kis. Na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́si Aƒia kaba kemmo na Benyamin kɔdua kemmo. Na Aƒia ubidi ndi Bekorat ɔni ubi ndi Seror ɔni ubi ndi Abiel ɔni ubi ndi Kis.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: Na Kis ɔmɛni ɔ́wɔ ɔnanabi ɔdi na baalɔ-nwu Saul. Okloƒu ɔmɛni ɔ́lɛ lɛblani utulo ɔdi biala na Israel mmɔ na ɔɔdia bɔnu geen na ɔ́kuku utulo ukyuli biala.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, Saul ɔmɛni ɔti Kis bebuo ala betine báyii. Amu na Kis ɔ́kpali ubidi Saul, na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Kpanku kabla bablane bammɔ akɔ unwi da, na bisie na bitáwia bebuo bammɔ.”

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu básia Eƒraim abi kalɔ lɛlɔ ulu na bakɛ Salisa kalɛkɛ kemmo, nsu bátanu-ma. Na ka bási mmɔ ni, bátásia Saalim kalɛkɛ kemmo, nsu bátanu-ma na mmɔ lɛnɔ. Anwuɔsu bátásia Benyamin kalɔ kemmo, nsu bátanu-ma.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ka bakɛ bétédu Suƒ kalɛkɛ kemmo na bátanu-ma ni, Saul ɔ́su kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Ya na bɔ́sɔ bunwini, ɔsika búutu uwi na ɔƒɛni kalɛ mina ɔti wakali ka abu lɛnɔ bɔ́yii na wasɔ weteeti-bu lɛlɔ kasusu bun na ɔda bebuo bammɔ ɔdi ɔya.”

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Nsu kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ ɔ́su Saul ɔnini, “Nu, Katɔti Kenye Udiene ɔdi ɔkya ɔma ɔmɛni kemmo ɔni na bekyuli baabu geen. Na lɛla biala na ɔ́su ni, liibo-nwu kemmo lɛni. Anwuɔsu ya na busie na butánu-nwu. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ ɔdubɔsu-bu kesii kani na bɔdubɔvi bɔsia.”

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
