translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Saul úye nwuna kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Bi na bɔdubo ɔnana ɔmɛni bute si búsie mmɔ? Adila ani bɔda ƒui áasa na bula kavumi kemmo. Na buuubo lɛla bamba lɛdi lɛnɔ. Bi ndi lɛla lɛni na bɔdubo Katɔti Kenye Udiene ɔmɛni bute. Bi nse-bu?”

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Amu na kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Nu, mbo sika ɔƒualadi ebi adi. Ndubuti ɔmmɔ lite Katɔti Kenye Udiene ɔmmɔ, na ɔtina-bu kesii kani na bunwini bɔsia.”

english_verse: “Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets. Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, ka kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ ɔ́su Saul kenye kammɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, Saul ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔdia, si use lɛni ni, amu bo na buteesie.” Anwuɔsu báyu ulu na béti bésela ɔma ɔni kemmo na Katɔti Kenye Udiene ɔmmɔ ɔkya.

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bákɔ abi ammɔ bésela ɔma ɔmmɔ ni, básiaku belekubi badi ka badubo bebedu ntu na abiɔ kemmo. Amu na béye-ma banini, “Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnu ala taasu mmɔ ɔkya?”

english_verse: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
translation_verse: Na ama lɛnɔ bédie kenye banini, “Ɛɛn, ɔkya aanu-nwu ntɔ-mii anumi mmɔ. Bɛbabla, ɔƒaani na úbo úbavi úsela bula ɔma. Ɔsika baabla akpala adi na bula ɔma lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
translation_verse: Na si bíduo ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo kani ni, bɛdubo-nwu bɔnu asa na weti wataakɔ utádi na kesii kani na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ linye. Na bekyuli bammɔ baaadubo bɔdi tɔ wetédu uwi ɔni na úbo, ɔsika anwu na ɔdi ka úti enu ɔ́sia adila ammɔ lɛlɔ úwi-nya kusɛ kusɛ, asa bekyuli bani na bálɔ béboku mmɔ bese kalɔ ku bɔdi. Bɛkɔ bisie mmɔ, na bɛdubɔkana na bɛnu-nwu uwi ɔmɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Amu ka bákɔ bétéduo ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na kabanye mmɔ ni, bánu Samuel ka ɔdubo ubavi utaakɔ kesii kani na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ linye.

english_verse: The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel,
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛni ntɔ asa na Saul úbo úbasiaku Samuel mɛni ni, Unwoti údie ala ammɔ ƒui ɔ́tina Samuel.

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Kɔnaadi aani uwi ɔni kemmo na mɔɔtɛmiku-ɔ mɛni ni, ndubɔya na ɔnana ɔdi ubo-ɔ kudɔ. Na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́si Benyamin kalɔ kemmo. Wi-nwu lili nnɔmii na ese-nwu likpo na unwini ɔtɔnkune ute mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ. Anwu ndubo-ma bɔtɔnku na lɛƒɔ-ma na Ƒilistiƒuɔ enu kemmo. Ɔsika lɛla lɛni na bévele-mi ni, línu-ma bɔkpali.”

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ka Samuel ɔ́nu Saul kani na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔnana ɔni lɛlɔ litemi na lɛ́su-ɔ ni, anwu mɛni. Na anwu ndubo mina kadi bekyuli bɔtɔnku.”

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Amu na Saul úsie útásiaku Samuel na ɔban kenye na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Ati buvele wɛ na Katɔti kenye udiene ɔni nkya mɛni uli?”

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Amu na Samuel údie kenye ɔnini, “Ami na ɔdi mɛni. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu tɔ na akɔ eteesie kɔbi lili kesii kani na baabla akpala mmɔ. Na ɔmwi ni, ami ku-ɔ bɔdubo bɔdi. Na si kadi kégye ɔtanta kɔnaadi ni, ndubɔsu-ɔ lɛla lɛni na adanku ɔ́si ƒula kayi kemmo asa na asɔ enwini eteesie ɔma.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: Na bebuo ala betine bani náyii emeyi atɛ ani návi mmɔ lɛlɔ ni, sɔ tekpoku lɛlɔ na bana lɛlɔ, ɔsika báanu-ma. Na ɔƒɛni ni, ɔma lɛlɔ na aabu anii Israelƒuɔ benye baawia kpakplaa si ɔɔɔdi awɔ ku ƒ'ɔti kaduli bekyuli?”

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Saul údie kenye na ɔ́su Samuel ɔnini, “Kɔdua kubliidi ƒui ndi Benyamin kɔdua na Israelƒuɔ akɔ, na mmɔ lɛ́si. Na mina ɔtɔ bekyuli ndi bani neeebo kenyekɔ geen kadi na Benyamin kɔdua kɔmmɔ kemmo. Bi ɔsu na aasu-mi lɛmɛni udu?”

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Na adila ɔnwane ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ úti ebuo libuli lɛni na lɛmwi lɛkya-ni lɛlɔ mmɔ úboku úbasia Samuel anumi. Mmɔ na Samuel ɔ́su Saul ɔnini, “Aanu lɛna lɛni na lídie líse-ɔ sɛsɛɛ, ti-ni kun. Ɔsika uwi ɔni na lɛ́lɔ mina benengu ka bebo na babadiku-mi ni, uwi ɔmmɔ kani na lídie lɛna lɛmɛni líse-ɔ ka abakun-ni si uwi ɔni na bula ƒui bɔɔdi.” Mmɔ ni, Saul ku Samuel básala bádi.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Ka bádi na báni báwɔlɔ ni, báyu bási kɔbi lɛlɔ mmɔ bésie ɔma kemmo. Amu na Samuel ɔ́ya na bákɔ bésie ɔtɔ katɔ na lɛsa kesii kani bábla na beelie, na anwu ku-nwu bátɛmi na mmɔ.

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: Kadi kégye ni, Samuel ɔ́su Saul ɔnii ɔklibi lɛlɔ na use-nwu ulu. Ka Saul ɔ́klibi lɛlɔ ni, anwu ku Samuel básia bálɛ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Bésie bétédu ɔma kabanye. Na mmɔ ni, Samuel ɔ́su Saul ɔnini, “Su ƒula kabla ɔblane na ɔgyu utaatɔ-bu anumi blii.” Saul lɛnɔ ɔ́ya na nwuna kabla ɔblane ɔ́ti na ɔ́gyu ɔ́tɔ sɔsɔ. Amu na Samuel ɔ́su Saul ɔnini, “Kywɛ-mi blii na lɛsu-ɔ lɛla lɛni na Katɔti ɔ́su-mi ɔ́siku-ɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured it on Saul's head. Then he kissed Saul and told him: The Lord has chosen you to be the leader and ruler of his people.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Samuel úti ɔsii ɔdi na nnɔmii buwi-nwu kemmo na úwilimi nnɔmii bɔmmɔ úwi Saul lili na ɔ́kya-nwu kɔgbu na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Geen geen ni, Katɔti ɔ́ƒuna-a ka enwini nwuna kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ ɔga.

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu si átɔlɔ-mi kudɔ mɛni ɔmwi na étédu Selsa na Benyamin kalɛkɛ ɔmii lɛlɔ ni, adubɔsiaku banana inyɔ na kesii kani na báva Rahel. Na badubɔsu-ɔ banini, ‘Bebuo ala betine bani náyii mmɔ ni, bánu-ma. Na bana lɛlɔ litemi lɛsɔ lilekpoku ƒ'ɔti, mmomu awɔ ku ƒula kabla ɔblane lɛlɔ kasusu muukpóku-nwu. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na ɔkya uuye-mii lili uwi biala ka lɛla lɛni na wabla wasiku-mii lɛlɔ?’

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: “Na ƒula ulu busie kemmo ni, adubɔsɔ asiaku nkyuli ɛtɛ bamba badi na kugyii kunengudi kɔni nnye Tabor kalɔ kemmo. Na bási bésela Betel batákpa bete Katɔti. Adubɔnu ka ukyuli udeedi ɔda bese bakɔdi ɛtɛ badi. Na ukyuli unyɔdi ɔda bodobodo ɛtɛ. Na ɔtɛdi ɔda bebuo ɔku koƒo kɔni kemmo na ntɛ buwi.

english_verse: After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
translation_verse: Badubo-ɔ bugyele, na bawia ka bete-ɔ bodobodo ɔni bada mmɔ inyɔ. Awɔ, ƒɔ bodobodo ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
translation_verse: “Ɔmmɔ kama ni, teesie Katɔti kɔbi lili. Mmɔ ni, Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone keliekɔ kede. Na si áni eedé ɔma ɔmmɔ ni, adubɔnu Katɔti kenye bediene kasala kadi. Ka bénwini bási kesii kani na bátábla akpala béte Katɔti mmɔ badubo. Na bana anumi ni, lɛbentaa ku ebi bagyane ku kɔkpɛɛ bavwine badi batɔ. Na badubo Katɔti kudu buteebo ku adi lidu.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti Kɔyu kɔdubɔƒɔ-ɔ lɛlɔ kemmo ku nwuna ɔyikun na ese kalɔ eteebo kudu aani bana kalɛ, na adubo bunwini ukyuli udu ɔwɔdi.

english_verse: After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
translation_verse: Si ala amɛni álɛ ni, kabla biala na anii aabla ni, na enye-ka lɛlɔ kpakplaa ɔsika Katɔti ulieku-ɔ.

english_verse: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
translation_verse: “Mɔɔyɔ́ ka agyu atɔ-mi na Gilgal. Na ami ndubɔsia-a kama libo mbanu-ɔ na mmɔ. Na bɔdubɔbla akpala bɔkyula bute Katɔti ku unwi bɔbla akpala lɛnɔ. Nsu ɔlɛka enye agya-mi emeyi maatɛ wetédu ka líbo ḿbatina-a lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka abla.”

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Ka Saul ɔ́gyu ɔɔtɔlɔ Samuel kudɔ kani na Katɔti únwini-nwu kayi ɔ́bla ɔwɔdi, na lɛla biala na Samuel ɔ́su-nwu líbo líte lɛni kani na limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Na sɔsɔ ka bédu Gibea ni, Katɔti kenye bediene badi bábasiaku Saul. Na Katɔti kɔyu kɔ́ƒɔ-nwu lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui. Na anwu lɛnɔ úduo-ma akɔ na uubó kudu bana kalɛ.

english_verse: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Bekyuli pii badi bakya mmɔ bani ngyi Saul kukuuku. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ka bánu-nwu ka uubó kudu ku kenye bediene bakladi ni, béye lɛlɔ banini, “Eei, bi nálɛku Kis ubidi? Saul lɛnɔ ɔkya kenye bediene akɔ?”

english_verse: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Nsu ukyuli ɔdi na uli mmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Na ɔma ndi bana ɔti?” Ɔmɛni ɔsu Saul litemi lɛmɛni línwini lɛsugba na baasu banini, “Saul lɛnɔ ɔkya kenye bediene akɔ?”

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Ka Saul ɔ́da kudu bubo ɔ́ya ni, ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie kakpakɔ na kɔbi lili mmɔ.

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: Amu na Saul ɔti ɔwani úye-nwu ɔnini, “Na bi na Samuel ɔ́su-mii?”

english_verse: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
translation_verse: Saul údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔ́su-bu ɔnii bɔsɔ butekpoku lɛlɔ, ɔsika báanu bebuo ala betine bammɔ.” Na ɔmmɔ kani na Saul ɔ́su nwuna ɔti ɔwani. Nsu útasu-nwu ka Samuel ɔ́su ka anwu Saul ndubo ɔga bunwini.

english_verse: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
translation_verse: Na emeyi adi kama ni, Samuel ɔ́lɔ Israelƒuɔ ƒui ka bebo na basa Mispa na ɔsu-ma lɛla lɛni na Katɔti ubo ute-ma.

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: Ɔ́su-ma ka Unwoti Israel Katɔti ɔnini, “Lídie Israelƒuɔ ƒui lɛ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ku bana ɔyikun kalɔ ku lɛgakɔdikɔ bamba bani baga mɔɔnya-mii taakya enu kemmo.

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: Na muuye-mii nnii, ɔɔɔdi ami ndi bina Katɔti. Na muudie-mii na ala ani muukpóku-mii ku bina lɛbibo kemmo? Nsu bíni-mi na bɛɛwia ka ukyuli ɔdi-mii lɛga. Amii alati náƒuna lɛla lɛni na bɛɛyɔ́. Na ami lɛnɔ ndubuse ɔga lite-mii. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bɛsala lɛlɔ ƒui bibenye-mi anumi na bina atɔƒi kenye.”

english_verse: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Amu ka Samuel ɔ́sala Israel adua ammɔ ƒui úboku na bébenye-nwu anumi ni, Benyamin kɔdua na ɔ́ƒuna.

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Katɔti ɔ́lɛ Benyamin kɔdua kemmo bekyuli lɛnumi ka ama na ɔ́ƒuna. Na kɔdua kɔmmɔ kemmo lɛnɔ ni, ɔ́ya na Matri ɔtɔ kemmo banana bálɛ bébo, na ɔ́ƒuna Saul ɔni ndi Kis ubidi ka anwu madi lɛga lɛmmɔ. Nsu ka bátɛ anumi bámana ni, bátanu Saul na kesii biala.

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bábabla bátálɔ-nwu béboku. Na ka úbenye-ma akɔ ni, ɔ́kuku úbo ɔ́vi ukyuli biala na unye mmɔ.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Amu na Samuel ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui ɔnini, “Bɛɛnu bina ɔga ɔni na Katɔti ɔ́ƒuna úte-mii. Na bina akɔ ƒui ni, ɔdi uuuse aani nwuna kalɛ.” Mmɔ na bana ƒui báva momoomo banini, “Ɔga ulie ngba gyɔlɔɔ!”

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Samuel lɛnɔ úsie anumi na údie ɔga ɔmmɔ kabla ku nwuna ɔyikun ɔni na ubo ɔ́tina-ma. Na únweni ala ammɔ ƒui ɔ́sia kakunkɛ lɛlɔ na bakono bése sɛsɛɛ na Katɔti anumi. Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Samuel údie-ma ulu na bátɔlɔ bésie bana kɔduli.

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Na Saul lɛnɔ ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie nwuna kaduli na Gibea. Na banana bani mbo kayi na Katɔti ɔlati ɔ́lɛ-ma animi ni, ama ntɔnku-nwu.

english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Nsu bekyuli badi bákya unyeƒi na Saul lɛlɔ básu banini, “Dɛ na ukyuli ɔmɛni udu wakana na waƒɔ-bu?” Anwuɔsu nwuna lɛlɔ lítada-ma kubiti, na béteboku-nwu etela adi. Nsu Saul útakpete-ma.

english_verse: About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
translation_verse: Nahas ɔni ndi Amonƒuɔ ɔga ni, ɔ́tɔnku nwuna bekpone na bésie bátáka ɔma unengudi ɔnii baalɔ Yabes bákya na Gilead kalɔ lɛlɔ. Amu na Yabes banana bammɔ básu-nwu banini, “Si ése-bu kenye ka aládu-bu ni, bɔdubɔkya-a kalɔ na butaabla-a kabla.”

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: Nsu Nahas Amonni ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔmmɔ uuubo ɔkplu, nsu asa menu ɔmmɔ kalɔ ni, lɛla linwi lɛdi kani na ami lɛnɔ mɔɔyɔ́ ka lɛbla-mii. Ndubudie ɔnana biala kɔdianu lɛnumi liti lɛkya Israelƒuɔ ƒui kɔƒa.”

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Ka Yabes benengu bénu ɔmɛni ni, básu-nwu banini, “Te-bu emeyi maatɛ na bɔtala bekyuli bɔkya Israel kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ bekyuli. Na si bútakɛ bekyuli bani nedie-bu ni, na bɔdubɔkya lili kalɔ bute-ɔ.”

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Amu na batalane bammɔ báyu ulu na bátɔlɔ na bétédu Gibea kesii kani na Saul uli. Ka básu bekyuli bammɔ kenye kammɔ ni, bana ƒui béwulo momoomo.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ tutuutu ni, Saul ɔ́kpanku nwuna ɔmantɛ bakɔ benengudi ɔ́siku nwuna kemo úsela kaduli. Na ka únu kɔvanu kɔmmɔ ni, úye bekyuli bani nnye mmɔ ɔnini, “Bi mɔɔlɛ́ku bekyuli bammɔ? Na bi ɔsu na beewulo?” Amu na ama lɛnɔ básu-nwu kenye kani na bekyuli bani nási Yabes badanku béboku.

english_verse: Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious.
translation_verse: Ka Saul únu kenye kamɛni ni, Katɔti kɔyu kɔ́ƒɔ-nwu lɛlɔ kemmo kɔnakunwi na ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi geen.

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani na úƒie ɔmantɛ bakɔ inyɔ ɔ́du na úle lɛna lɛmmɔ wɛlɛwɛlɛ. Amu na úti lɛna lɛmmɔ úte nwuna batalane badi na ɔ́su-ma ɔnii beti lɛna lɛmmɔ na bavi Israelƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui na batásu-ma banini, “Bɛnu! Ebuo ɔni na ami Saul lɛ́du líle mɛni, si ukyuli ɔni na útata na ɔsiaku-mi ku Samuel na busie butékpo ku Amonƒuɔ ni, ndubɔya na beƒie ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔmantɛ bakɔ na badu-ma aani kalɛ na líƒie ɔmɛni lɛ́du na líle-nwu wɛlɛwɛlɛ na bɛɛnu mɛni.” Na ka bénu Saul kenye kammɔ ni, Katɔti ɔ́ya na bana ƒui báyia geen, ɔsika bánu ka Katɔti úti ɔyikun ɔdi úte-nwu. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bana ƒui bénu kalɔ ka basiaku-nwu na betékpo.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: Mmɔ na básu batalane bani nébo mmɔ banini, “Bisie na bitásu Yabes Gilead banana bɛnini, ‘Asa na uteedu ɔƒiiwi kɔnaadi ni, bɔdubo bubekpo na bɔƒɔ-mii.’ ” Na ka batalane bammɔ lɛnɔ bénwini bátásu Yabes banana kenye kani na badanku ni, ebiti áda bana ƒui geen.

english_verse: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yabesƒuɔ básu Amonƒuɔ banini, “Kɔnaadi ni, bɔdubɔkya-mii lili kalɔ na bɛbla-bu lɛla lɛni na bɛɛyɔ́.”

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni údu uwi ɔni na kadi keteegye ni, Saul úle nwuna bekyuli kemmo akpa atɛ. Na ɔtanta tutuutu ni, bétéyu Amonƒuɔ bátu na bádu-ma laa útédu ɔƒiiwi. Na Amonƒuɔ bakladi bani nébu ni, bégyingya bákya aku kemmo ƒui bávi ɔni na básɔ bátasala lisu na kesii kadi.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Ka kekpo kammɔ kayɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ básu Samuel banini, “Dɛ na bɔdubɔbla bekyuli bani na balayɔ ka Saul ɔdi lɛga mmɔ? Bɛkpanku-ma biboku na bɔdu-ma!”

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Nsu Saul ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Kudi kudii, ukyuli unwi pɛ muedi batadu ɔdi. Ɔsika ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ na Unwoti údie-bu ɔ́lɛku bula bekisine enu kemmo.”

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Amu na Samuel ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ɔnini, “Bɛya na busie Gilgal na bɔsɔ busie butálɛ ugyii ka Saul ndi Israelƒuɔ ɔga.”

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bésie Gilgal, na mmɔ ni, bana ƒui bénu kalɔ ka Saul ndi Israelƒuɔ ɔga na Unwoti anumi mmɔ. Na bábla akpala béte Unwoti na bákun lɛna lɛmmɔ básala. Ɔmmɔ kama Saul ku Israelƒuɔ bammɔ bádi limeyi na bákɛ ebiti kaduɛ.

english_verse: Samuel told the Israelites: I have given you a king, just as you asked.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Samuel ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ ɔnini, “Lɛ́bla lɛla lɛni na bívele-mi líte-mii. Na lɛ́ƒuna ɔga ɔni na bɛɛwia ka utaadi-mii lɛlɔ líte-mii.

english_verse: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
translation_verse: Ɔƒaani ni, bibo ɔga ɔni mɔɔtɔnku-mii. Na ami ni, mina akwa éesie anumi na mina lili lɛ́ƒuala. Na mina bebi bakya-mii akɔ mɛni. Ami nátɔnku-mii ɔ́si mina lɛnamu uwi ƒui úti úbedu ɔƒaani.

english_verse: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
translation_verse: Na bɛɛnu kalɛ na nnye-mii anumi ɔmwi. Na ɔni na bunye Unwoti ku bina ɔga ɔƒunadi anumi mɛni ni, ɔdi ɔdubɔkana na udie ɔtina likpidi lɛni na lɛ́bla-nwu? Bina akɔ ɔmani ɔmantɛ akɔ iye ebuo ala utine na líƒie lɛ́ƒɔ? Munuu ɔdi ɔkya-mii akɔ ɔni na lɛ́nya-nwu lɛ́kya na ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ? Iye ni, líti etila adi lɛ́sia ɔdi lɛlɔ? Iye lɛ́bɛ lɛ́ƒɔ lɛla lɛdi lɛ́siku ɔdi kudɔ lɛ́di, na lɛ́du ɔbambadi kalala kɔtɔ na líte anwu ubo? Na si ɔdi ɔ́kana na údie kenye ka ala amɛni ɔdi use lɛni ni, bɛsu bɛlɛku na lɛƒɔ kayu kammɔ na lɛla lɛmmɔ lili.”

english_verse: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Samuel ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Unwoti ɔlati náƒuna Mose ku Aaron ka batɔnku bula bati kuuku. Na ama nákpanku-ma bálɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
translation_verse: Na ɔƒaani ni, bibimi bina atu na binu kaduɛ ka bɛ́ƒiɔ Unwoti ɔni na nka anwu mɔɔtɔnku-mii na bíti bina anu ƒui bɛ́sia-nwu lɛlɔ. Na bitaakali taanu ala abuni ani na ɔ́bla úte amii ku bina bati kuuku.

english_verse: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
translation_verse: “Uwi ɔni na Yakob ku nwuna kaba bekyuli bátɔlɔ bésie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ kama ƒui ni, bákpali Unwoti bévele-nwu ku keku ka ubunku-ma. Amu na Unwoti ɔ́ya Mose ku Aaron bákpanku-ma bálɛku Egyipteƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ béboku kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na bilie mɛni kemmo.

english_verse: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
translation_verse: “Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui ni, bula bati kuuku bammɔ báyiƒala Unwoti bana Katɔti. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na anwu lɛnɔ úte kuƒi na bana bekisine békpoku-ma. Na bekisine bammɔ akɔ ɔdi ndi Sisera, Hasor bekpone ɔtɔnkune. Ukisine ɔbambadi ɔni nádi-ma lɛlɔ lɛnɔ ndi Ƒilistiƒuɔ. Na Moabƒuɔ ku bana ɔga lɛnɔ bábadi-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Na uwi biala na bádi-ma lɛlɔ lɛni ni, beenwíni kayi na bewulo bevele Unwoti banini, ‘Bɔ́bla alaekpidi bɔ́ƒiɔ-ɔ, O Unwoti, na búnwini kama bɔ́kya-a na bɔɔkpá ala bamba, aani Baal baƒiɔ ku Astarot baƒiɔ. Nsu ɔƒaani ni, die-bu lɛku bula bekisine enu kemmo na bɔdubɔbla-a kabla.’

english_verse: The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́tala Yerubaal ɔni basɔ baalɔ Gideon, Barak ku Yeƒta. Na kawɔlɔkɔ kamɛni ni, ɔ́tala ami Samuel. Na úkpo ɔ́ƒɔ-mii ɔ́lɛku bina bekisine bani nkya bina amadɔ ƒui enu kemmo na bɛ́kɛ bɔnwuna.

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: “Nsu ina ka bina Unwoti Katɔti nádi bina ɔga ni, bíni-nwu uwi ɔni na Amonƒuɔ Ɔga Nahas ɔ́tɔnku nwuna bekpone ka bebekpoku-mii. Na bɛ́su bɛnini, ‘Bɔɔwia ɔga na utaadi-bu lɛlɔ.’

english_verse: You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king.
translation_verse: Bɛɛnu ɔga ɔni na bɛ́ƒuna na bívele ka bese bete-mii. Unwoti úse ɔga ɔmmɔ úte-mii, na utaadi-mii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
translation_verse: Na ɔƒaani si bɛɛbu Unwoti bina Katɔti, na amii ku bina ɔga ƒui bɛɛdi nwuna etemila lɛlɔ na bítenwini kama bítakya-nwu ni, lɛla biala lɛdubɔtɛ lite-mii.

english_verse: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
translation_verse: Nsu si bɛ́ta bínye Unwoti ɔda bubo lɛlɔ na bíni ka bɛsiaku-nwu kama ni, ɔdubo-mii kɔtu bɔni aani kalɛ na ɔ́ni bina bati kukuuku kɔtu.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: “Bise atu na binu ala abuni ebendi ani na Unwoti ɔdubo bɔbla na bina anumi.

english_verse: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
translation_verse: Ɔɔɔdi uwi ɔmɛni na baaƒɛ kamu yoo? Na bɛgyi lɛnɔ ka si edula ɔƒɛwi ɔmɛni údu ni, ɔnantu ɔsɔ ulána. Nsu ina ka use lɛni ni, ndubo Katɔti bɔkpali na ɔya na ɔnantu ɔna. Na kayaa kataabwɛ ogya. Na ɔmɛni ɔdubɔya na bɛti kalɛ na likpidi lɛni na bɛ́bla líbomo ɔni na bíye bɛnii bete-mii ɔga na utaadi-mii lɛlɔ ɔsu.”

english_verse: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bévele Samuel banini, “Vele Unwoti ƒula Katɔti te abu ƒula kabla bablane kalɛ na bulekpi. Bɔɔyia ka bɔdubo bukpi, ɔsika na alaekpidi ani ƒui na bɔ́bla kama ni, bɔ́sɔ bɔ́su-nwu ka use ɔga ute-bu.”

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Nsu Samuel úse-ma kayi ɔnini, “Bɛsɔ bitayia. Sɔsɔ na ɔdi ka bɛ́bla ala buɛ amɛni. Nsu bɛda udu ɔmmɔ bɛya na bɛsɔ bitenwini kama bitakya Unwoti. Mmomu biti bina kayi ƒui bɛbla-nwu kabla.

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Biteni Unwoti na bitaakpa baƒiɔ. Ala ammɔ kama bɔsiaku buuubo kɔsia kɔdi. Na alakana-mii bubunku lɛnɔ, iye aƒɔ-mii na bina bekisine enu kemmo.

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Nwuna lɛnyi bonwu lɛni náƒɔ kuye ɔsu ni, Unwoti ɔɔɔdubo nwuna bekyuli buni, ɔsika ɔɔyɔ́-nwu kaƒɔ ka ɔbla-mii nwuna kadi bekyuli.

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: “Na ami geen ni, uwi ɔdi uuubo na basu banii ndubɔda Unwoti bɔkpali bɔya na bina lili, na unwini-mi likpidi. Na ndubɔtina-mii lɛla lɛni ndi lɛbuni na lɛdia ka bitaabla.

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Nsu bɛsia anu na bitaayia Unwoti, na bɛsiaku-nwu kama siin, na bitaadi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ ku bina kayi ƒui. Na biteenyimo ala ebendi ani na ɔ́ɔbla úte-mi.

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Na mmomu si bɛmu binye bɛɛbla alaekpidi ni, bekisine badubo amii ku bina ɔga ƒui lɛlɔ bɔdi na bayila-mii udu.”

english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na Israel lɛma kemmo ƒui ni, bekyuli bammɔ bénu ka Saul ɔ́di Ƒilistiƒuɔ kakɛ kadi lɛlɔ. Na bagyi lɛnɔ ka Ƒilistiƒuɔ beekisi Israelƒuɔ geen. Anwuɔsu bálɔ bekyuli bammɔ ka besie batásiaku Saul na Gilgal.

english_verse: The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits.
translation_verse: Ka Israelƒuɔ bánu ka bana kenyekɔ kaaadia na baabɔku bana bekpone bammɔ geen ɔsu ni, ketulodikɔ bábɛ. Na badi bábɛ na atakpɛ libu kemmo ku abiɔ akukudi ku libu lɛnɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: Israelƒuɔ bammɔ badi muedi bávia Yordan Ketu bonwu kammɔ bésie Gad ku Gilead kalɛkɛ. Na Saul ku bekpone báƒɔ lɛlɔ bakya Gilgal ɔni na liƒu lɛɛda-ma na lɛlɔ lɛɛtɔ́-ma geen.

english_verse: and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come.
translation_verse: Na Samuel anwu ni, ɔ́su Saul ka emeyi maatɛ kama asa na ɔdububo. Nsu emeyi maatɛ ammɔ áavi na Samuel útebeduo tɔ Gilgal. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Saul bekpone bése kalɔ baatɔlɔ-nwu kudɔ unwi unwi.

english_verse: Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.” Saul killed one of the animals,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Saul ɔ́su ɔnini, “Biti bɔkyula akpala ebuo ku unwi bɔbla akpala ebuo ɔmmɔ biboku.” Amu na Saul ɔ́du bebuo bammɔ na anwu ɔlati ɔ́bla akpala ammɔ.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni kani na ɔ́wɔlɔ akpala ammɔ bɔbla kani na Samuel lɛnɔ úbeduo. Mmɔ na Saul úte-nwu eduo.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani ni, Samuel úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ndi lɛla lɛni na ábla mɛni?” Amu na Saul údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛ́nu ka banana bammɔ beegyingya. Na lɛnɔ ni, étebeduo uwi ɔni na ése lɛlɔ, na Ƒilistiƒuɔ badaku lɛlɔ bɔsala na Mikmas.

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu lɛ́bla kasusu ka Ƒilistiƒuɔ bammɔ badubɔta banii bebekpoku-mi na Gilgal uwi ɔni na ngyi ka ńtakpali tɔ Unwoti ka ubebunku-mi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na lɛ́bla akpala ammɔ.”

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Amu na Samuel ɔ́su Saul ɔnini, “Adɔlɔla geen na adi na ábla mɛni. Bi ɔsu na átadi Unwoti etemila lɛlɔ. Si banii bɔdi na ádi nwuna etemila lɛlɔ ni, nka Unwoti ɔdubɔya na awɔ ku ƒula kaba kemmo bebi bɛdi lɛga na Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ uwi ƒui.

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: Nsu ɔƒaani ni, ƒula lɛgadi lɛsɔ lilenye uwi ƒui. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́ɔƒuna ukyuli bamba ɔni na nwuna kayi kaayɔ́ ka ɔtɔnku nwuna kadi bekyuli. Ɔsika awɔ átadi nwuna ɔda bubo lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Then Samuel left Gilgal. Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Samuel ɔ́yu ulu na ɔ́tɔlɔ Gilgal mmɔ. Na Saul ku bekpone bani nébu basiaku-nwu bátɔlɔ Gilgal mmɔ bésie bátásiaku nwuna bekpone bakladi na Gibea na Benyamin kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ. Na Saul ɔ́ka nwuna bekpone bani nébu basiaku-nwu. Na bana bumomo bɔbla aani nkyuli eti leevu-anyɔ kani.

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Saul ku ubidi Yonatan ku bana bekpone báda keliekɔ na Geba na Benyamin kalɛkɛ mmɔ. Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone ama bakya Mikmas.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni uwi uwi ni, Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone aani akpa atɛ baalɛ́ teesie teetékpoku bekyuli na bana lɛma na beƒie-ma ala baƒɔ. Lɛkpa lideedi lɛɛsia teesie Oƒra ɔma unengudi na kalɛkɛ kani baalɔ Sual lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
translation_verse: Na linyɔdi liti lisie Bet-Horon. Na lɛkpa lɛtɛdi lɛsia ɔmii lɛlɔ kalɔ kesii kani na si enye ni, na aanu Seboim Kɔwɛ teemene kesii kani mɔɔtina kalɔ kakwiidi kakɛ.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ala bakywɛne badi beeebo Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ kesii kadi, ɔsika Ƒilistiƒuɔ bétete-ma kuƒi. Na básu banii, “Si búte-ma kuƒi ni, Hebriƒuɔ bamɛni badubo kuwii ku atula bɔkywɛ bute lɛlɔ!”

english_verse: So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, uwi ɔni na Ƒilistiƒuɔ ku Israelƒuɔ békpo ni, Saul ku ubidi Yonatan kani nda kuwii ku atula. Yonatan Úsie Útékpoku Ƒilistiƒuɔ

english_verse: The Philistines moved their camp to the pass at Michmash,
translation_verse: Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone badi bésie bátágyumana abi atɛ ulu ɔni ntɛ úsie Mikmas.

english_verse: Jonathan decided to get to the Philistine camp by going through the pass that led between Shiny Cliff and Michmash to the north and Thornbush Cliff and Geba to the south.
translation_verse: Lɛtakpɛ linwi lɛdanku lísie katɔ kakɛ na Mikmas. Na lɛtakpɛ lɛni na ɔvi unyɔdi lɛdanku lísie kada kakɛ na Geba.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yonatan ɔ́su nwuna ekpola utine ɔnini, “Bo na bɔsia abi ntɛ ulu ɔmmɔ busie Ƒilistiƒuɔ bani nétekulo ago mmɔ keliekɔ. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ Unwoti ɔdubukpo ute-bu, ɔsika lɛla lɛdi lilétile Unwoti bɔƒɔ kuƒi si ina bumomo iye buse blii suɛ.”

english_verse: “This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yonatan ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔdia, bo, bɔdubo bɔkɔ bɔvia buteesie bekyuli bammɔ kudɔ kakɛ na bɔya na banu-bu.

english_verse: If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp.
translation_verse: Na si bákyaku-bu unyeƒi na bábala-bu banii bɔsɔ bunye utédu ka ama bébo-bu kudɔ ni, bɔdubudi bunye kesii kani na bunye mmɔ na bɔsɔ bulákɔ bulésie-ma kudɔ.

english_verse: But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
translation_verse: Nsu si bébo-bu kɔnu ka buteebo-ma kudɔ mmɔ ni, bɔdubɔkɔ busie mmɔ. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla likposela ute-bu ɔ́si Unwoti kudɔ ka ɔdubo-bu bubunku na bɔdi-ma lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier stood at the bottom of the hill where the Philistines could see them. The Philistines said, “Look! Those worthless Israelites have crawled out of the holes where they've been hiding.” Then they yelled down to Jonathan and the soldier, “Come up here, and we will teach you a thing or two!” Jonathan turned to the soldier and said, “Follow me! The Lord is going to let us win.”
translation_verse: Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone bani nkya bana keliekɔ mmɔ bákpali bémene Yonatan ku nwuna ekpola utine banini, “Amii bɛkɔ bibo-bu kudɔ mɛni na bɔdubɔtina-mii lɛla lɛni bɛɛwia.” Anwuɔsu Yonatan ɔ́su nwuna ekpola utine ɔnini, “Siaku-mi taakɔ kɔbi kɔmmɔ. Unwoti unye abu Israelƒuɔ kama na bɔdi Ƒilistiƒuɔ bamɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Yonatan ɔ́kpɛ enu ku akɔnkɔ ɔ́kɔ útálɛ atakpɛ ammɔ eli, na nwuna ukpone ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔsiaku-nwu kama. Yonatan uubó Ƒilistiƒuɔ bammɔ taaƒiɛmi kalɔ. Na nwuna ekpola utine ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔsiaku-nwu kama ɔɔdú-ma.

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: Si nka bɔya na ɔ́ya na bula bekyuli bádi adila ani béƒie báƒɔ bula bekisine kudɔ mmɔ adi ni, nka ɔdia geen na badubɔdu Ƒilistiƒuɔ bammɔ betulo kalɛ na bádu-ma mmɔ muedi.”

english_verse: Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
translation_verse: Amu na Saul ku nwuna badi básala lɛlɔ na bésie bétékpo ku Ƒilistiƒuɔ bammɔ. Ka bédu kekpokɔ mmɔ ni, bánu ka Ƒilistiƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui béƒu útédu ka benye beekpóku ama alati lɛlɔ muedi.

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone lisu limodi lɛmmɔ ku bani nkya bana nvo kemmo ku bani nnye muukpó ƒui béƒu. Na Katɔti ɔ́ya na kalɔ kammɔ kákunku na liƒu lɛ́da-ma líbu. Na Katɔti ɔlati náya na liƒu bonwu lɛmɛni líbo-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Saul ku nwuna bekpone bakya Gibea na Benyamin kalɛkɛ. Na bekpone bani nnye mɔɔgyumana mmɔ bánu bémene ka liƒu líƒie Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ na bakɛ beekeli taavi.

english_verse: Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
translation_verse: Amu na Saul ɔ́su nwuna badi bani nkya-nwu kudɔ mmɔ ɔnini, “Bɛsala bekpone bammɔ ƒui na bɛnu bani nálɛ-mii akɔ.” Na ka bábla lɛni ni, bánu báti ka Yonatan ku nwuna ekpola utine ɔmmɔ neeebo-ma akɔ.

english_verse: At that time, Ahijah was serving as priest for the army of Israel, and Saul told him, “Come over here! Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Amu na Saul ɔ́su ɔkpane Ahiya ɔnini, “Ti Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ boku.” Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, na adaka ɔmmɔ ɔ́kya Israelƒuɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
translation_verse: Ɔni na Saul unye ɔɔtɛmiku Ahiya ni, owogyo ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kɔ katɔ úbu. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Saul ɔ́su Ahiya ɔnini, “Awɔ, da ya!”

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Na asa kekpo kammɔ kadubɔlɛ ni, na Hebriƒuɔ badi bátábla unwi ku Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone na bakya-ma kudɔ na mmɔ. Nsu ɔƒaani na kekpo kammɔ kemmo ni, bénwini bábabla unwi ku bana kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu básalaku Saul ku Yonatan.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Ka Israelƒuɔ bani na nka bátábɛla lɛlɔ bákya abi adi akɔ na Eƒraim kalɛkɛ bénu ka bana kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ baabɔku Ƒilistiƒuɔ ni, ama lɛnɔ bébo bébebunku na kekpo kammɔ kemmo na bábɔku-ma kpakplaa.

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Lɛlɔ lítu Israelƒuɔ geen na bábla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ na kɔka ɔsu. Ɔsika asa na badubusie kekpokɔ kammɔ ni, Saul ɔ́kpali Katɔti ɔ́kya-ma úse kenye na úbo-ma ɔda ɔnini, “Ukyuli biala uuubo kuƒi na ɔkya lɛdila lɛdi kenye wetédu ka lídie bula bekisine bamɛni kasi. Na ukyuli biala ɔni náta únye ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na ɔ́bla lɛla bamba ni, Katɔti ɔdubuwida-nwu.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bekpone bammɔ ɔdi biala útakya lɛla lɛdi kenye.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Nsu ka baayia lɛla lɛni maalɛ ɔ́si kenye kani na Saul úse ɔsu ni, ɔdi útetuku uwɔ ɔni mɔɔyu taagba mmɔ kenye muedi útanu.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Nsu Yonatan anwu ni, uuubo mmɔ uwi ɔni na ɔti Saul ɔkpali Katɔti ɔ́kya bekpone bammɔ úse kenye. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu anwu útenu ɔmmɔ lɛla lɛdi. Na ka ɔ́nu uwɔ ɔmmɔ ni, únene nwuna ugyii ɔdadi ɔ́kya kɔtakɛ kɔmmɔ kemmo na ɔ́di uwɔ ɔmmɔ ɔdi, na ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kya-nwu ɔyikun úbu.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Ka ukpone ɔdi ɔ́nu-nwu ni, ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdi ulu ka bula ɔdi ɔkya lɛdila lɛdi kenye ɔmwi. Ɔsika ƒ'ɔti ɔ́kpali Katɔti ɔ́kya bula ƒui ka butadi lɛla lɛdi. Na ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Katɔti ɔdubuwida bina akɔ ɔni makya lɛla lɛdi kenye.’ Na ɔmɛni ɔsu na buse kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.”

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Amu ka Yonatan únu kenye kammɔ ni, ɔ́su ɔnini, “Mina ɔti ɔ́kya bula bekyuli ɔgbankpi kemmo. Awɔ ɔlati ánu áti ka ɔyikun bamba úduo-mi lɛlɔ kemmo ka lɛ́di uwɔ ɔmmɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛmmɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ békpoku Ƒilistiƒuɔ ɔ́si Mikmas útédu Ayalon na bádi-ma lɛlɔ. Nsu ina ka bádi-ma lɛlɔ ni, bekpone bammɔ bábla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bénwini bélie bebuo bani na béƒie básiku bana bekisine kudɔ mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na bádu-ma ogya ogya. Mmɔ kani na baaduli lɛna lɛwɔdi lɛmmɔ ku ubugya taakun.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔdi útásu Saul ɔnini, “Nu, bekyuli bamɛni baabla lɛla lɛni náta línye Unwoti lɛlɔ, ɔsika baakun lɛna lɛni kemmo na ubugya ɔmu ɔkya.” Amu na Saul ɔ́va ku lɛdi momoomo ɔnini, “Bíbile bula bɔƒɔtaadi bɔmmɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu biminime lɛtabi linengudi lɛdi biboku-mi kudɔ mɛni kɔnakunwi.”

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su batɔnkune bammɔ unwi ɔnini, “Sie na atásu bekyuli bammɔ na beti bana ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu beboku na badu-ma bewi lɛtabi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ na ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ. Na ɔmmɔ kama bakana na beti lɛna lɛmmɔ bakun. Na utalɛ ka bataaƒiɔ Unwoti na bataakun lɛna lɛni kemmo na ubugya ɔkya.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu béti bana ɔmantɛ bakɔ béboku na bábadu-ma na kesii kammɔ.

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Na usien ɔmmɔ ni, Saul ɔ́tu lɛkpabi na bábla akpala béte Unwoti na mmɔ. Na ɔmmɔ ndi kudeedi ka Saul ɔ́bla lɛni.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Amu na Saul ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bɛya na bɔbɔku Ƒilistiƒuɔ usien ɔmɛni. Na bɔdu-ma ƒui na buƒie bana ala ƒui bɔƒɔ.” Mmɔ na ama lɛnɔ bédie kenye banini, “Ƒula kasusu kammɔ kadia geen na bɔdubɔbla lɛni.” Nsu ɔkpane ɔni nkya mmɔ bɔ́su ɔnini, “Kudeedi ni, ɔlɛka bɔka Katɔti kasusu buye bunu asa.”

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Saul úye Katɔti ɔnini, “Nkpoku Ƒilistiƒuɔ bamɛni na lɛbɔku-ma? Na adubɔya na bɔdi-ma lɛlɔ?” Nsu Katɔti útakpete Saul limeyi lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Saul ɔ́su ɔnini, “Agyi anii ukyuli ɔdi náƒiɔ Katɔti ɔmwi. Anwuɔsu, mina benengu ƒui, bɛlɛ bibo na bɔwia ukyuli ɔmmɔ bɔti ku likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla.

english_verse: I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.” No one said a word.
translation_verse: Mɔɔkpali Unwoti ɔni nli ngba na uukpó taaƒɔ Israelƒuɔ na bula bekisine enu kemmo nnii ina mina ubi Yonatan ɔdi nábla lɛla lɛmɛni ni, ɔdi ka ukpi.” Nsu nwuna benengu bammɔ ƒui ɔdi útasu lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Saul úbo ɔda úte Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui ɔnini, “Biténye ɔvi ɔngye. Na ami ku mina ubi Yonatan bunye ɔvi ɔmɛni.” Amu na bédie kenye banini, “Bɔdubɔbla lɛla biala na ásu-bu.”

english_verse: Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?” The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army.
translation_verse: Amu na Saul ɔ́kpali Unwoti ɔnini, “Bula Unwoti, Israel Katɔti, bi ɔsu na bɔ́kpali-ɔ na étedie lɛla lɛni na búye-ɔ kenye étete-bu? Die ukyuli ɔni náƒiɔ tina-bu si ami ku mina ubi Yonatan na ɔdi iye bekpone bammɔ akɔ ɔdi na ɔdi.” Mmɔ na kenye budie bɔmmɔ búbo ka ɔga ku Yonatan akɔ ɔdi na ɔdi, na útasi bekyuli bammɔ.

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Saul ɔ́su Ahiya ɔnini, “Amu die tina ami ku Yonatan ntɛ bula akɔ ɔni geen na ɔdi.” Na úbalɛ Yonatan lɛlɔ ka anwu nábla likpidi.

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Amu na Saul úye Yonatan momoomo ɔnini, “Su-mi lɛla lɛni na ábla!” Mmɔ na Yonatan údie kenye ɔnini, “Mina ugyii ɔdadi na líti lɛ́tu uwɔ lɛ́yalɛ. Anwuɔsu bukpi na ɔlɛka likpi?”

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Saul údie kenye ɔnini, “Katɔti ɔbla-mi lɛla biala na ɔɔyɔ́ si ńtaya na badu awɔ, Yonatan.”

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bekpone bammɔ básu banini, “Bulénu kalɔ bɔnii ukpi, ɔsika Yonatan na Katɔti úbunku asa na bɔ́di kekpo kamɛni lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu ɔkɛnku Unwoti ɔni nli ngba lɛlɔ ni, bɔɔɔdubo bɔtuna na ina nwuna lili linwini linwi pɛ muedi lɛtimi-nwu lili.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bekpone bammɔ békpo báƒɔ Yonatan na bátadu-nwu.

english_verse: Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home. Saul Fights His Enemies
translation_verse: Amu na Saul ɔ́da Ƒilistiƒuɔ kama bɔsia ɔ́ya na bátɔlɔ bésie bana kalɔ.

english_verse: When Saul became king, the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, the Philistines, and the Amalekites had all been robbing the Israelites. Saul fought back against these enemies and stopped them from robbing Israel. He was a brave commander and always won his battles. Saul's Family
translation_verse: Úkpo lɛnanabi kemmo na ɔ́di Amalekƒuɔ lɛlɔ na údie Israel na bekisine bani ƒui nnye muukpóku-nwu na beeƒie-ma ala taaƒɔ ƒui enu kemmo. Saul Ku Nwuna Kaduli Bekyuli

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Na Ɔga Saul ngba bulie uwi ƒui ni, kekpo kpakplaa kákya ama ku Ƒilistiƒuɔ ntɛ geen. Anwuɔsu uwi biala na Saul ɔ́nu ukyuli ɔni na ubo kayi ni, na ɔɔwia ka ɔni-nwu ɔkya lɛlɔ na utaabla-nwu kabla.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told Saul: The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord:
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Samuel ɔ́su Saul ɔnini, “Ami na Unwoti ɔ́tala na ḿbese-ɔ likpo na énwini ɔga éte mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ. Na ɔƒaani ni, nu kenye kani nási Unwoti kudɔ.

english_verse: “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
translation_verse: Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔnini, ‘Ndubo Amalekƒuɔ kɔtu bɔni na lɛla lɛni na bábla Israelƒuɔ ɔni na béténye báda-ma ulu uwi ɔni na bási baalɛ́ Egyipte kalɔ kemmo ɔsu.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu sie na etékpoku-ma na ayila-ma lɛla biala na bebo udu. Tanu ɔdi biala kɔnyana. Banana ku beleku ku banamu ku bebiwɔ ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu ku bebuo ala betine bani mbo keƒu ku baƒlumu ƒui, na tebu ɔdi tese.’ ”

english_verse: Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Saul ɔ́lɔ nwuna bekpone ɔ́siku kesii biala na bátásala na ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Telaim kemmo. Na bebo bekpone mpim eti ene. Na bana mpim leevu bási Yuda kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Lord told Samuel,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti kenye kébedu Samuel kudɔ ɔnini,

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Amu na Saul útiku bekpone bammɔ na bésie Amalek ɔma unengudi bátábɛ na ketu kakwiidi kadi kemmo.

english_verse: Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.” The Kenites left,
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su Keni kadi bekyuli bani nkya mmɔ ɔnini, “Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ ƒui bási baalɛ́ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, amii bítekpoku-bu, mmomu bɛ́nu-bu kɔnyana. Anwuɔsu bɛkpɛ bɛlɛ-ma lɛlɔ kalɛ na naaadu-mii neeebunku Amalekƒuɔ.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Keniƒuɔ bammɔ báta Amalekƒuɔ kudɔ mmɔ bésie kesii bamba.

english_verse: and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Saul úkpoku Amalekƒuɔ ɔ́si ɔma ani baalɔ Hawila útédu Sur na Egyipte ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: Every Amalekite was killed except King Agag.
translation_verse: Saul úƒie Amalekƒuɔ Ɔga Agag, nsu útadu-nwu. Mmomu nwuna kadi bekyuli ƒui ama ɔ́du-ma.

english_verse: Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak. The Lord Rejects Saul
translation_verse: Saul ku nwuna bekpone béni na bátadu Ɔga Agag ku baƒonu ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku bana bebi bani na bánu ka bélie lɛmwi kaduɛ mmɔ ƒui ku ala bamba ani lɛnɔ na bánu ka adia-ma. Na akladi ani ƒui naaadia-ma ni, báyila-nya udu.

english_verse: “Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night.
translation_verse: “Úduo-mi geen ka lɛ́ya na Saul ɔ́di lɛga, ɔsika únwini kama ɔ́kya-mi na útadi mina kenye kani na lɛ́su-nwu lɛlɔ.” Lɛla lɛmɛni líkpoku Samuel geen, anwuɔsu útalɛɛ, mmomu ɔkya ɔɔkpali Katɔti teevele usien umodi ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Kadi kégye ɔtanta tutuutu ni, Samuel ɔ́ta na úsie utánu Saul. Nsu ka úsie ni, básu-nwu banini, “Saul úsie kesii kani baalɔ banii Karmel. Mmɔ na útátu enyimo lɛtabi lɛdi únyene úte lɛlɔ kalɛ na bekyuli bataakali taanu kalɛ na úkpo ɔ́di lɛlɔ na bataabu-nwu. Ɔmmɔ kama na únwini úsie Gilgal.”

english_verse: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
translation_verse: Ka Samuel útásiaku-nwu ni, Saul náka-nwu kenye bɔkya ɔnini, “Katɔti kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku-ɔ, ɔsika lísie ńtábla lɛla lɛni na ásu-mi.”

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Nsu Samuel ɔ́ƒɔ kɔnakunwi na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Na baƒonu ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ bamani kɔvanu na muunú na mɛni?”

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Amu na Saul údie kenye ɔnini, “Bekpone bammɔ néti-ma básiku Amalek kalɔ lɛlɔ béboku na badi baƒonu ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ babuni ƒui na bana akɔ ka beti babakpa bete Katɔti, na bakladi ƒui ama báyila-ma udu.”

english_verse: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Samuel ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ba lɛsɛ! Na enu lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi kamaadi usien.” Amu na Saul lɛnɔ ɔ́ƒɔ ɔnini, “Taasu kenye kammɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Samuel úsie anumi ɔnini, “Uwi ɔni na awɔ ɔlati muedi átanu tɔ lɛlɔ átati ka adi lɛla lɛdi ni, Unwoti úse-ɔ likpo na énwini ɔga na Israel kadi bekyuli adua pii ammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔmmɔ nátala-a ɔnini, ‘Sie na etékpoku Amalekƒuɔ belikplune bammɔ utédu ka áyila-ma udu ƒui kede kede.’

english_verse: Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
translation_verse: Bi ɔsu na étenu Unwoti kenye na adi-ka lɛlɔ? Na bi ɔsu na bana ala kani négyie-ɔ anumi ka eƒie aƒɔ na ábla likpidi lɛmɛni udu na Unwoti anumi?”

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Nsu Saul ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Lísie ńtábla lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi na lɛ́du Amalekƒuɔ ƒui na líƒie bana Ɔga Agag líboku.

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Bekpone bammɔ néƒie baƒonu ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ bani ndia ntulo ƒui, na bana akɔ béboku ka beti bakpa bete Katɔti na Gilgal.”

english_verse: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
translation_verse: Nsu Samuel údie kenye ɔnini, “Akpala na Unwoti ɔɔwia ɔnii bakyula bete-nwu, munuu nwuna litemi lɛlɔ na ɔɔwia ka bekyuli badi? Si eenú-nwu litemi na aadi-ni lɛlɔ ni, ɔdia utulo ka eti akpala iye baƒonu lɛmwi akpa ete-nwu.

english_verse: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
translation_verse: Ɔsika si elenu Unwoti litemi na adi-ni lɛlɔ mmomu aatalaku lɛlɔ katɔ na ƒula likyulikpi ɔsu ni, átavumanaku bekyuli bani mɔɔkpá baƒiɔ na beeye-ma ala teenu. Na ka éni Unwoti litemi ɔsu ni, anwu lɛnɔ úni-ɔ ka asɔ adi ɔga na nwuna bekyuli lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Saul ɔ́su Samuel ɔnini, “Lɛ́bla likpidi lɛ́ƒiɔ Unwoti na lɛ́ta línye nwuna litemi lɛlɔ. Na ńtenu ƒula bɔlɛ, ɔsika lɛ́yia bekyuli bammɔ mmomu, na línu-ma litemi.

english_verse: Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu líkpi kɔtɔ. Ti kyiɛ-mi na asɔ enwini abasiaku-mi na busie ntákya lili kalɔ lite Unwoti.”

english_verse: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
translation_verse: Nsu Samuel úni na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo bunwini bubasiaku-ɔ, ɔsika éni ka adi Unwoti litemi lɛlɔ, anwuɔsu Unwoti lɛnɔ úni ka awɔ asɔ adi nwuna ɔga na Israel lɛlɔ!”

english_verse: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
translation_verse: Mmɔ ka Samuel únwini ɔɔtɔlɔ ni, Saul ɔ́da-nwu awu kɔtu na mmɔ kábwɛ.

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you.
translation_verse: Amu na Samuel ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Unwoti ɔ́bwɛ Israelƒuɔ lɛga kadikɔ ɔ́lɛku-ɔ lɛkɔkɔ. Na úti-ka úte ƒula badi bammɔ akɔ ɔdi. Na ɔdi ukyuli ɔni na ɔdia utulo-ɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ni, Unwoti ɔɔɔdi ukyuli ɔyawine ɔni na muunwíni nwuna kasusu. Mmomu Israel Katɔti ɔni muukeye na ɔdi, na ɔɔsu litemi geen lɛmmɔ na ulányi ɔkɔ. Anwuɔsu ɔsɔ ulavumana kenye kammɔ.”

english_verse: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Saul ɔnini, “Lɛ́bla likpidi sɔsɔ, nsu te-mi ɔbu na mina bekpone ku Israel kadi bekyuli bammɔ ƒui anumi, na abasiaku-mi na lɛsɔ ntákya lili kalɔ lite Unwoti, ƒula Katɔti.”

english_verse: Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Samuel ɔ́sɔ únwini ɔ́siaku Saul na ɔ́kya lili kalɔ úte Unwoti.

english_verse: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Samuel ɔ́kpali momoomo ɔnini, “Bɛkpanku Amalekƒuɔ Ɔga Agag biboku-mi mɛni.” Na Agag lɛnɔ úsie úbo-nwu kudɔ ku kayi ƒaa, na ɔ́bla kasusu ɔnii uwi ɔni na basɔ badu-nwu ɔ́vi.

english_verse: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
translation_verse: Nsu Samuel ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Kalɛ na ƒula kewii káya na beleku badi bakya na basɔ balanu bana kaƒɔ bebi ni, lɛni na ƒ'ini lɛnɔ ɔdubo bɔkya beleku bamba akɔ na ɔsɔ ulanu nwuna kɔƒɔ ubi.” Mmɔ kani na Samuel ɔ́du Agag na Unwoti anumi na Gilgal.

english_verse: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Samuel ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Rama. Nsu Saul anwu ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie nwuna ɔma na Gilgal.

english_verse: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ útédu limeyi lɛni na Samuel úkpi ni, ɔ́sɔ útésie útatánu Saul kudii, ina ka Saul lɛlɔ litemi líkpoku-nwu na úwulo-nwu kɔnyana. Na úduo Katɔti lɛnɔ ka úse Saul lɛga úte Israelƒuɔ.

english_verse: One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Unwoti úye Samuel ɔnini, “Uwi ɛlɛ na adubo bulie buteewulo kɔnyana na Saul lɛlɔ butálɛ? Líni nnii ɔsɔ utadi lɛga na Israel. Ta na eyile ƒula lise ku nnɔmii na ayu ulu eteesie Betlehem ɔma kemmo na ɔnana ɔni baalɔ banii Yisai kesii. Nwuna bebi akɔ na lɛ́ɛƒuna ukyuli ɔni madi mina ɔga líse.”

english_verse: Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.” “Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me,
translation_verse: Nsu Samuel údie kenye ɔnini, “Dɛ na ndubo ulu bɔyu buteesie mmɔ? Saul ɔdubo bunu na ubo ubadu-mi.” Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ti koƒonu kɔkɔdi da na asu bekyuli bammɔ anii akpala na ébo ababla ete-mi.

english_verse: then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Na alɔ Yisai na ubo kakpakɔ kammɔ, na ndubɔtina lɛla lɛni na adubo bɔbla na ese ukyuli ɔni mɔɔwia likpo ete-mi.”

english_verse: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
translation_verse: Samuel ɔ́bla lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu. Na ka údu Betlehem ni, ɔma benengu bammɔ báyia geen na béye-nwu banini, “Buɛɛ na ɔdi bɔdi?”

english_verse: “Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɛɛn, use buɛɛ ƒui! Na akpala adi na líbo mbabla lite Unwoti. Anwuɔsu bɛklibi lɛlɔ na bibo bibasiaku-mi na butábla akpala ammɔ bɔsala.” Na ɔ́ya na Yisai ku nwuna bebi lɛnɔ báklibi lɛlɔ na bébo mmɔ.

english_verse: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bébeduo mmɔ ni, Samuel ɔ́nu Eliab, Yisai ubidi unengudi. Mmɔ na ɔ́su lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Ngyi ka okloƒu ɔmɛni na Unwoti ɔɔwia use lɛga.”

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti ɔ́su Samuel ɔnini, “Tanu kalɛ na ɔ́kuku na ɔɔdia bɔnu kani, ɔsika ńtaƒuna-nwu. Na ɔɔɔdi ala ani na ukyuli ɔɔnu na ukyuli lɛlɔ na ami Unwoti mɔɔnu taaƒuna-nwu. Ɔlɔna ala kani na amii bɛɛnu. Nsu ami mɔɔnu nwuna kayi kemmo.”

english_verse: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Yisai ɔ́ya na Aminadab úsie Samuel kudɔ, nsu Samuel ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdi anwu na Unwoti ɔ́ƒuna.”

english_verse: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
translation_verse: Nwuna kama Yisai ɔ́ya na ubidi Sama lɛnɔ úsie, nsu Samuel ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdi anwu na Unwoti ɔ́ƒuna.”

english_verse: One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men.
translation_verse: Yisai ɔ́ya na nwuna bebi maatɛ ƒui básia Samuel kudɔ bávi, nsu Samuel ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdi bebi bamɛni akɔ ɔdi na Unwoti ɔ́ƒuna.”

english_verse: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Samuel úye Yisai ɔnini, “Bebi bananabi bamɛni kani na ebo?” Mmɔ na Yisai údie kenye ɔnini, “Kawɔkpulo ɔni na ɔdi ɔnamu blii ɔdi kani nébu, na anwu nésie ɔɔnu baƒonu lɛlɔ.” Amu na Samuel ɔnini, “Tala na batálɔ-nwu beboku, na bula ɔdi ulelie tɔ kalɔ wetédu uwi ɔni na úbeduo.”

english_verse: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yisai ɔ́tala na bátálɔ-nwu béboku, na ɔdi ɔnamu ɔni na ubo ɔlɔkplu na úgyie na ɔɔdia bɔnu lɛnɔ. Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su Samuel ɔnini, “Ta na ewi-nwu nnɔmii lili, ɔsika anwu na lɛ́ƒuna.”

english_verse: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
translation_verse: Amu na Samuel úwilimi nnɔmii bɔmmɔ úwi Dawid lili na nwuna banwani anumi. Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo kani na Katɔti Kɔyu kúbo na kɔ́ƒɔ Dawid lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui ku ɔyikun. Na Samuel lɛnɔ únwini úsie Rama.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
translation_verse: Katɔti Kɔyu kɔ́tɔlɔ Saul kudɔ, na kɔyu kukpidi kɔdi mmomu na Katɔti ɔ́ya na kúbo kuukpóku-nwu.

english_verse: “It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him.
translation_verse: Na nwuna benengu básu-nwu banini, “Nu! Kɔyu kukpidi kɔdi na Unwoti ɔ́ya na kuukpóku-ɔ.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ni, bula Ɔga Ɔbune, ya na butáwia ukyuli ɔni na ɔgyi ɔbentaa bɔgya kaduɛ na ubataagya-nwu teete-ɔ kalɛ na si kɔyu kukpidi kɔmmɔ kɔ́si Unwoti kudɔ kúbo kuukpóku-ɔ ni, na lɛlɔ litaabla-a buɛɛ.”

english_verse: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
translation_verse: Amu na Saul údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔdia, bɛwia ukyuli ɔdi biboku ɔni na ɔgyi ɔbentaa bɔgya kaduɛ.”

english_verse: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na benengu bammɔ akɔ unwi ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔnana ɔdi ɔ́si Betlehem na baalɔ-nwu Yisai. Ubo ubi ɔnanabi ɔni ngyi ɔbentaa bɔgya geen, na ɔdi ukpone ɔni mbo kayi, na ɔgyi bɔtɛmi na ɔɔdia bɔnu, na Unwoti lɛnɔ ɔsiaku-nwu geen.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
translation_verse: Amu na Saul ɔ́tala ukyuli ɔ́kya Yisai ku kenye ɔnini, “Su ƒ'ubidi Dawid na ɔnyonu baƒonu bammɔ lɛlɔ bɔnu na ɔtɔlɔ ubo-mi kudɔ mɛni.”

english_verse: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
translation_verse: Amu na Yisai úti ebuo ɔku ɔdi na úyile-nwu ku ntɛ, na úti bodobodo úbunku-nwu lɛlɔ na únyimi ɔ́sia ebuo ala utine lɛlɔ, na úti ese ɔkɔdi úbunku na úti úte Dawid ɔnii uti usienku Ɔga Saul.

english_verse: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
translation_verse: Dawid útéduo Saul kudɔ na úse kalɔ ɔɔbla-nwu kabla. Na nwuna lɛlɔ lɛ́da Saul kubiti geen, anwuɔsu ɔ́ya na úse kalɔ uuti nwuna ekpola.

english_verse: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
translation_verse: Uwi útetu asa na Ɔga Saul ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tala ukyuli ɔ́kya Yisai ɔnini, “Mɔɔyɔ́ ƒ'ubidi Dawid geen, anwuɔsu muuvele-ɔ ya na ɔsɔ ɔkya-mi kudɔ mɛni utaabla-mi kabla.”

english_verse: Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni uwi biala na kɔyu kukpidi kɔmmɔ kúbo kuukpóku Saul ni, Dawid ɔɔgyá nwuna ɔbentaa, na Saul lɛlɔ kemmo kaayɔ́ buɛɛ na kɔyu kɔmmɔ kɔtɔlɔ.

english_verse: The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Ƒilistiƒuɔ básala bana bekpone na Soko na Yuda kalɔ kemmo ka betékpo. Anwuɔsu bátáda keliekɔ na Soko ku Aseka ntɛ na kesii kani baalɔ banii Eƒes-Damin.

english_verse: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔkwalɛ ɔmmɔ ɔkya bana akpa anyɔ ntɛ, na Ƒilistiƒuɔ beli kɔbi kunwi lili na Israelƒuɔ lɛnɔ beli kɔbi kunyɔdi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Philistine army had a hero named Goliath who was from the town of Gath and was about three meters tall.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔnana ɔdi na baalɔ banii Goliat na ɔdi ukpone lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔdi ɔ́lɛ ɔ́si Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone akɔ úbo, na ɔ́si ɔma ɔni na baalɔ banii Gat kemmo. Ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kuku utulo lɛgba bɔka yaalenwi.

english_verse: He wore a bronze helmet and had bronze armor to protect his chest and legs. The chest armor alone weighed about
translation_verse: Na adi lɛnɔ ada-nwu lɛgba na aagyumana-nwu, asa na lɛbuala lɛtula bonwu lɛdi lɛda-nwu kama kukulo.

english_verse: When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head. Abner took David to Saul,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Dawid únwini úsie bana keliekɔ na Goliat bɔdu kama ni, Abner ɔ́kpanku-nwu úboku Saul kudɔ. Na úbenye Saul anumi na ɔmu ɔda Ƒilistini ɔmmɔ lili.

english_verse: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
translation_verse: Nwuna ugyii lɛtula gyɔlɔɔ lɛni na ɔda use aani bedine ɔkɔlɔ. Na lɛbuala lɛni ntu-nwu kenye unu ɔbla aani antabi akyami maatɛ unu. Anwuɔsu ukpone ɔbambadi ɔni muuti nwuna agyumanala ɔɔtɔ-nwu anumi uwi biala.

english_verse: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒilistini ɔmɛni ɔ́va ku lɛdi momoomo ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na bíbo bínye mmɔ bɛnii abu Ƒilistiƒuɔ na bibekpoku? Ƒilistini ukpone lɛlɔ ɔdine unengudi ƒui na ndi, na amii lɛnɔ bɛdi Saul bekpone. Bidie bina ukpone unengudi ƒui na ubo ubasiaku-mi na mɛni.

english_verse: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
translation_verse: Na si ɔ́kana na úkpoku-mi na ɔ́du-mi ni, bɔdubunwini bɔkya-mii kalɔ na butaabla-mii kabla. Na si ami nádi-nwu lɛlɔ na lɛ́du-nwu ni, bɛdubɔkya-bu kalɔ na bitaabla-bu kabla.”

english_verse: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
translation_verse: Ka Ɔga Saul ku Israelƒuɔ bakladi bénu Ƒilistini ɔmmɔ kenye kamɛni ni, liƒu lɛ́da-ma na báyia geen.

english_verse: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
translation_verse: Na Saul lɛga bɔdi uwi kemmo ni, unengu ɔdi ɔ́kya na baalɔ-nwu Yisai. Ɔdi Eƒrat kɔdua ukyuli na ulie Betlehem na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ, na ɔ́ɔbi geen. Ubo bebi bananabi maane. Na bebi bammɔ akɔ unwi ndi Dawid.

english_verse: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
translation_verse: Anwu muusié Saul kudɔ teesie taasɔ taatánu ɔti bebuo lɛlɔ na Betlehem.

english_verse: Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for
translation_verse: Na emeyi aavlene kemmo ƒui ni, Ƒilistini ɔmɛni uusié teebo teebenye mmɔ lɛdigye ku useyi uwi taakun lɛmɛnɛ taakya Israelƒuɔ bammɔ.

english_verse: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
translation_verse: Na úti nwuna ugyii ɔdadi ɔni na ɔɔkpanku bebuo na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie ketu kadi útála atabi suɛlɛ suɛlɛ alɔ ɔ́kya nwuna koƒo kemmo. Amu na údie nwuna kavwinvwi ɔ́da kɔnu, na úti ulu ulu kɔnakunwi úsela Goliat kudɔ.

english_verse: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, Yisai ɔ́su Dawid ɔnini, “Ti antabi agyidi amɛni ku bodobodo leevu ɔmɛni sienku ƒula banwani na bekpone keliekɔ kesii kani na bakya.

english_verse: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
translation_verse: Na eti bebuo anyi ntu akuladi eku leevu amɛni esienku bekpone ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ. Na anu kalɛ na ƒula banwani bakya, na abasu-mi na lɛti si bakya kaduɛ.

english_verse: They're with Saul's army, fighting the Philistines in Elah Valley.”
translation_verse: Ama ku Israelƒuɔ banana bakladi ƒui nkya Ela Kɔwɛ kɔmmɔ kemmo beekpóku Ƒilistiƒuɔ.”

english_verse: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
translation_verse: Kadi kegye ɔtanta tutuutu ni, Dawid ɔ́da baƒonu bammɔ ɔ́kya lɛlɔ ɔnune bamba enu kemmo, na únyimi ala ɔ́sia nwuna bebuo ala utine lɛlɔ na ɔ́yu ulu ɔ́tɔlɔ kalɛ na ɔti ɔ́su-nwu. Nwuna mmɔ buduo kani na uunú ka beebó kekpo kudu ka bata besie kekpokɔ.

english_verse: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
translation_verse: Na sɔsɔ Israelƒuɔ ku Ƒilistiƒuɔ bammɔ béesie beenye anumi ku anumi ka beteekpo.

english_verse: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani na Dawid ɔ́da nwuna ala úse ɔgyumanane ɔni nnye mɔɔnu ala lɛlɔ kudɔ, na úkeli úsie útákya ɔnwani bene kenye.

english_verse: While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.
translation_verse: Ka benye baatɛmi kani na Goliat Ƒilistini ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́da úbalɛ ku nwuna lɛmɛnɛ bɔkun ku kɔvanu etemila, na Dawid únu.

english_verse: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
translation_verse: Ka Israelƒuɔ bánu ka Goliat ɔ́sɔ ɔ́da úbalɛ kani na békeli bébo kama ku liƒu.

english_verse: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni náavi kemmo ƒui ni, Israelƒuɔ bamɛni bátaasu lɛlɔ banini, “Bɛnu kalɛ na ukyuli ɔmɛni uusié teebo teebedumi-bu bɔdi. Nsu Ɔga Saul ɔ́ɔsu ka ɔdubuti nwuna ubidi ulekubi bute ukyuli ɔni makana Ƒilistini ɔmɛni bɔdu na uti. Na ɔni nsɔ nsia lɛnɔ ndi ka ukyuli ɔmmɔ ku nwuna ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli ƒui basɔ baaadubo kalɔ kammɔ kemmo kuyii kɔdi butaaƒɔ teete ɔga. Na ɔmmɔ kama ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔdubute ukyuli ɔmmɔ ala pii.”

english_verse: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
