translation_verse: Ka Dawid úbo úbasiaku lɛla lɛmɛni ni, úye ukpone ɔni nnye nwuna kɔmadɔ ɔnini, “Bi na badubo bɔbla bute ukyuli ɔni makana Ƒilistini ɔmɛni bɔdu na ɔda bula kadi Israelƒuɔ kɔƒa bɔkya ɔya? Ɔma na Ƒilistini ɔni na útekulo lego mɛni ɔɔkali ka ɔdi na ubataakun lɛmɛnɛ taakya Katɔti ɔni nli ngba uwi ƒui bekpone lɛni?”

english_verse: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
translation_verse: Amu na bekpone bammɔ básɔku ala ani na Ɔga Saul ɔ́su ka wete ukyuli ɔni madu Goliat mmɔ báka béte Dawid.

english_verse: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
translation_verse: Ka Dawid ɔnwani unengudi Eliab únu ka Dawid ku bekpone bammɔ benye baatɛmi ni, ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi ɔ́kya-nwu geen na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi na ébo aawia mɛni? Ɔma na áda baƒonu ɛlɛɛ bammɔ ése na ɔɔnu lɛlɔ? Ngyi-ɔ kalɛ na aakun ala lɛmɛnɛ ku kayi kekpidi kani nkya-a. Ɔɔɔdi kekpo kamɛni ɔsu na ébo mɛni abanu lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́?”

english_verse: “Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ Dawid údie ɔnwani kenye ɔnini, “Bi na lɛ́ɛbla ɔƒɛni? Naaakana lɛla lɛdi lɛnɔ buye bunu?”

english_verse: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid únwini na úye ukpone bamba lɛla lɛmmɔ kani na anwu lɛnɔ kenye kani na básu-nwu kudeedi mmɔ kani na anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́su.

english_verse: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
translation_verse: Bekpone bamba bénu lɛla lɛni Dawid ɔ́su na bésie batásu Ɔga Saul. Anwuɔsu Saul ɔ́tala na bátálɔ Dawid béboku.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔga Ɔbune, utalɛka Ƒilistini ɔmɛni ɔnu-bu aani bekyuli bani na bubo liƒu. Ami ndubusie na ntékpoku-nwu!”

english_verse: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Saul ɔ́su Dawid ɔnini, “Naaanu kalɛ na adubuti adi ukyuli ɔmɛni lɛlɔ. Ɔsika ɔnamu kani na adi na anwu ɔdi ukpone ɔ́si nwuna lɛkloƒu uwi ƒui úbedu ɔƒaani.”

english_verse: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
translation_verse: Nsu Dawid ɔ́su Saul ɔnini, “Mina ɔti baƒonu lɛlɔ kani na mɔɔnu uwi biala. Na si gyata iye kegidi kéƒie ɔdi ni,

english_verse: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
translation_verse: mɔɔsiaku-nwu kama teetédu ka lɛ́ƒɔ-nwu nwuna kudɔ. Na si ɔdi únwini ɔnii uukpóku-mi ni, mɔɔda-nwu lɛkoolobi na lɛdu-nwu.

english_verse: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
translation_verse: Ami ƒula kabla ɔblane lɛ́ɛdu gyata ku kegidi. Na ndubɔkana na lɛdu Ƒilistini ɔni nétekulo lego mɛni lɛnɔ aani bana kalɛ, ɔsika ɔ́nu Katɔti ɔni nli ngba bekpone ka baaadi lɛla lɛdi na nwuna anumi!

english_verse: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔni nédie-mi ɔ́siku gyata ku kegidi aƒiɔ akɔ ndubudie-mi bɔsiku Ƒilistini ɔmɛni enu kemmo.” Amu na Saul ɔnini, “Ɔdia, amu teesie na etékpoku-nwu. Bula ƒui bubo lɛnunsia ka Katɔti ɔdubo-ɔ bubunku na akana-nwu lɛlɔ bɔdi.”

english_verse: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
translation_verse: Saul ɔlati ubo kekpo awu ku adala bamba na úti-nya úte Dawid ku lɛbuala kabua na úbi lili.

english_verse: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
translation_verse: Amu na úti kewii lɛnɔ ɔ́bala nwuna kavobi na úsie ɔ́vi. Nsu Dawid ɔnini, “Ala amɛni átama-mi bɔkya na naaakana na lisie lɛvi muedi.” Anwuɔsu Dawid údie ekpola ammɔ úwi.

english_verse: Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Goliat ɔ́ni uudé Dawid, na nwuna ukpone ɔni nti-nwu ekpola ɔtɔ-nwu anumi.

english_verse: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
translation_verse: Nsu ka Goliat ɔ́nu Dawid ni, ɔ́nu ka okloƒu kani na ɔdi. Na ina ka ubo ɔlɔkplu na ɔɔdia bɔnu ni, nwuna lɛlɔ líƒi-nwu livo.

english_verse: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
translation_verse: Amu na Goliat úye Dawid ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na ada ugyii ɔmmɔ? Munuu ákali ka akpewe ɔdi na adubo ebebo adu yoo?” Mmɔ na ɔ́kpali nwuna baƒiɔ na ɔ́kanti ɔ́kya Dawid na úwida-nwu ɔnini,

english_verse: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
translation_verse: “Awɔ, bo mɛni na lɛtina-a lɛla lɛdi. Ndubo-ɔ bɔmɛnɛ eku eku lite baasɛ ku beƒiebuo na bakun!”

english_verse: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Awɔ ni, ƒula kewii ku lɛtula ku lɛbuala kalɛkɛ kani na ada aagyumana lɛlɔ kani na ada ebekpo-mi. Nsu ami ni, nkɛ ku Unwoti Ɔyikune ƒui lɛnyi kemmo mbekpoku-ɔ. Na anwu ndi Israel bekpone Katɔti ɔni na awɔ eedumi.

english_verse: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmwi ni, Unwoti ɔdubɔya na lɛdi-ɔ lɛlɔ. Na ndubukulo-ɔ lili lɛnɔ. Na ɔɔɔdi ɔmmɔ lɛti pɛ. Mmomu bina Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone ni, badubo-ma bɔdu geen ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ na bana ɔlɔna unwini lɛdila ute baasɛ ku bebuo bamba na bakun. Na kayawi bekyuli ƒui banu bati ka abu Israelƒuɔ ni, bubo Katɔti ɔni muukpó teete-bu.

english_verse: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
translation_verse: Lɛla lɛdi litatɔlɔ-ɔ, ɔsika Unwoti mɔɔyá na ukyuli ɔɔdi lɛlɔ, na ɔɔɔdi kewii iye lɛtula ɔyikun kemmo. Ɔsika kekpo kammɔ kadi Unwoti kadi. Na anwu ɔmmɔ ndubɔya na bɔdi-ɔ lɛlɔ lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: When Goliath started forward, David ran toward him.
translation_verse: Na ka Goliat ɔɔní uudé-nwu ni, Dawid lɛnɔ úkeli úsela na basa na bekpo.

english_verse: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́kya kɔnu nwuna koƒo kemmo na údie lɛtabi ɔ́kya nwuna kavwinvwi kemmo na úƒwimi ɔ́siaku Goliat. Lɛtabi lɛmmɔ lítáda-nwu lɛtɛntɛ na lɛ́ƒuala líduo-nwu lili kemmo na Goliat úbuli útébi kalɔ.

english_verse: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Dawid úti kavwinvwi lɛtabi linwi ɔ́du Goliat ɔni ndi Ƒilistini ɔni na ɔɔɔda kewii muedi.

english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid úkeli úsie Goliat kudɔ na kesii kani na úbuli ɔtɛ mmɔ. Na ɔ́ni Goliat ɔlati kewii kani nkya-nwu livuo kemmo na nwuna ɔƒɛnyi ɔ́kpa, na ɔ́tu-nwu ɔ́du na úkulo-nwu lili. Ka Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone bakladi bánu ka ukpone unengu ɔni lɛlɔ na ama baakun lɛmɛnɛ úkpi ni, bana ƒui békeli bátɔlɔ.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Na Israel ku Yuda bekpone bávwi kekpo lise ku kudu momoomo na bábɔku Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ laa bétédu bana lɛma linengudi lɛni ndi Gat ku Ekron kɔbanye. Na bádu bana bekpone bammɔ béwi ulu lɛlɔ geen úsela ɔma ɔni baalɔ Saraim.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Ka Israelƒuɔ báda-ma bɔbɔku báya ni, bénwini bébo kesii kani na Ƒilistiƒuɔ báda bana keliekɔ mmɔ na bébeti bana ala ani na báda bése mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: Dawid úti Goliat lili úsienku Yerusalem. Na úti Goliat ekpola ani na úti mmɔ úwi nwuna ɔtɔ.

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Dawid úsela utékpoku Goliat ni, Saul ɔ́nu-nwu. Na úye nwuna bekpone ɔtɔnkune Abner ɔnini, “Ɔma ubidi ndi okloƒu ɔmmɔ?” Mmɔ na Abner údie kenye ɔnini, “Bula Ɔga Ɔbune, geen geen ni, lɛɛɛgyi kebii kammɔ ɔti.”

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Saul úye Dawid ɔti lili. Na Dawid údie kenye ɔnini, “Ƒula kabla ɔblane Yisai ubidi na ndi. Na ɔ́si Betlehem.”

english_verse: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ kani ni, Saul ɔ́sɔ útete Dawid kuƒi na ɔtɔlɔ usie ɔti kaduli lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan ku Dawid bényimi kpakplaa ka bana kɔkpana kɔsɔ kulékulo kudii, ɔsika baayɔ́ lɛlɔ geen.

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Na kalɛ na Yonatan ɔɔyɔ́ Dawid ɔsu ni, Yonatan údie nwuna awu gyɔlɔɔ ɔni na ɔɔkya úte Dawid na úti nwuna kekpo adala ku kewii ku kataminta ku kabuli kani na ɔɔsia kavobi mmɔ lɛnɔ úte-nwu.

english_verse: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
translation_verse: Na lɛla biala na Saul úbo Dawid ɔda ka ɔbla ni, ɔɔbla-ni kaduɛ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Saul úti Dawid ɔ́bla bekpone batɔnkune akɔ unwi ɔni na ubo kenyekɔ geen na bekpone bammɔ akɔ. Na lɛla lɛmɛni lɛ́da bekyuli bammɔ ƒui kubiti ku Saul bekpone batɔnkune bammɔ muedi.

english_verse: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni limeyi lɛni na Dawid ɔ́du Goliat mmɔ ni, anwu ku bekpone bakladi bénwini bésela ɔma. Ka básia Israelƒuɔ lɛma lɛmmɔ kemmo bésela ni, beleku bammɔ bálɛ bábasiaku Ɔga Saul na baatu yiiduu teete-nwu ku kɔgya na baatɔ́. Bédie lɛlɔyɔ lɛnu ku lɛbentaa ku agyala abambadi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
translation_verse: Na beleku bani nkya mɔɔtɔ́ mmɔ beedie lɛnu banini, “Saul ɔ́du bekisine mpim mpim. Na Dawid anwu ɔ́du bana mpim leevu leevu.”

english_verse: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛmmɔ kadi kégye ni, kɔyu kukpidi kɔdi kúbelie Saul lɛlɔ kpakplaa. Kɔyu kɔmmɔ kɔ́ya na Saul ɔkya uudie ala adi bene kenye na nwuna kaduli na eeebo lili ku lɛgba. Na ɔda nwuna lɛtula. Na uwi ɔmmɔ kani lɛlɔ ni, Dawid unye ɔɔgyá nwuna ɔbentaa aani kalɛ kani na ɔɔyɔ́ bɔbla.

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: Kɔnakunwi ni, Saul ubo nwuna lɛtula ɔnii ɔɔlɛ Dawid ku kasusu ka ɔkana-nwu ɔmana kowodu lɛlɔ mmɔ. Na kunyɔ sɔɔn na ɔ́bla ɔbladu ɔmɛni, nsu Dawid ababla ɔsu ni, úliiku lɛlɔ ɔni na lɛtula lɛmmɔ lítakɛ-nwu.

english_verse: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
translation_verse: Saul úbo ɔɔyia Dawid geen, ɔsika ɔ́nu ɔ́ti nwaa ka Unwoti ɔsiaku Dawid geen. Nsu anwu Saul ni, Unwoti údie-nwu atu.

english_verse: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
translation_verse: Na lɛla biala na Dawid wabla ni, lɛɛtɛ teete-nwu, ɔsika Unwoti ɔsiaku-nwu geen.

english_verse: This made Saul even more afraid of David.
translation_verse: Ka Saul ɔ́nu kalɛ na ala aatɛku-nwu ɔsu ni, úbo ɔɔyia-nwu.

english_verse: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
translation_verse: Nsu Israelƒuɔ ƒui ku Yuda baayɔ́ Dawid na kalɛ na ɔ́tɔnku-ma úsienku kekpokɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Amu na limeyi lɛdi ni, Saul ɔ́lɔ Dawid na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Aanu mina ubi ulekubi unengudi Merab mɛni. Ndubuti-nwu lite-ɔ na eti aani ƒ'ulekudi si adubɔbla-mi kabla aani ukpone ɔni mɔɔbla kayi, na ekpo kekpo na Unwoti lɛnyi kemmo.” Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui ni, kɔkwɛ kani na Saul ɔɔkya, ɔsika ɔɔwia ka Ƒilistiƒuɔ badu Dawid si bésie kekpokɔ, na ulekpi na Saul ɔlati enu kemmo.

english_verse: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
translation_verse: Nsu Dawid údie kenye ɔnini, “Ami ndi ɔma, na ɔma bene ndi mina ɔti iye mina kɔdua bekyuli na Israel ka liti ɔga ubi na linwini ɔga ubi ɔgyani?”

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ka uwi údu ka nka beti Saul ubidi Merab bete Dawid na uti ni, béti-nwu béte ɔnana ɔni baalɔ Adriel na ɔ́si Mehola ɔma kemmo.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni Saul ubidi ulekubi bamba ɔni baalɔ Mikal úbo ɔɔyɔ́ Dawid geen. Na ka Saul únu lɛni ni, ɔ́da-nwu ebiti geen.

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́bla kasusu ɔnini, “Ndubuti mina ubi ɔmɛni lite-nwu kalɛ na makana-nwu kakpagyuɛ bɔkywɛɛ na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bakɛ-nwu badu.” Anwuɔsu Saul ɔ́su Dawid ɔnini, “Kuƒi kunyɔdi kɔ́lɛmi-ɔ na ndubuti mina ubi ulekubi lite-ɔ na enwini-mi ubi ɔgya.”

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: Amu na béti kenye kamɛni bésienku-nwu sɔsɔ. Nsu ka Dawid únu kenye kamɛni ni, ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔwabane na ndi na ńtaƒɔ lɛnyi. Na ɔƒɛni ni, uuuse kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ka linwini ɔga ubi ɔgya.”

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ama lɛnɔ bátásɔku Dawid kenye kammɔ básu Saul.

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Saul ɔ́tala-ma ɔnii batásu Dawid banini, “Uleku buti elila ani kani na mɔɔwia taasiku-ɔ kudɔ ni, anwu ndi ka adu Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone eti anyɔ na ekulo-ma ago kenye ɔlɔna ɔmmɔ abatina-mi ka ádu-ma sɔsɔ. Na ɔmmɔ na ami lɛnɔ ndubuti lidie mina bekisine bammɔ kasi na lɛla lɛni na bábla ɔsu.” Na Saul kasusu ndi ka ɔsia ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na ɔya na Dawid uduo Ƒilistiƒuɔ enu kemmo na badu-nwu.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Amu ka bekpone batɔnkune bammɔ bátásu Dawid kenye kammɔ ni, ɔ́da-nwu ebiti, ɔsika anwu lɛnɔ ɔɔyɔ́ ka ɔga unwini-nwu ɔƒanti. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu asa na elila bɔbla limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛdubudu ni,

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Saul ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka Unwoti ɔsiaku Dawid sɔsɔ na ubidi Mikal lɛnɔ ɔɔyɔ́-nwu geen ni,

english_verse: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
translation_verse: Dawid lɛlɔ lɛ́sɔ lɛ́da Saul liƒu líbu. Na ɔ́si uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, Saul úkisi Dawid nwuna ngba emeyi kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Na uwi ndi uwi ni, Ƒilistiƒuɔ batɔnkune beetiku bana bekpone teetékpoku Israelƒuɔ. Nsu uwi biala na báta lɛni ni, Dawid ku nwuna bekpone baadi-ma lɛlɔ. Na Saul ukpone ɔtɔnkune ɔdi ɔsɔ ulákana-ma lɛlɔ bɔdi aani Dawid kalɛ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Dawid úbaƒɔ lɛnyi geen.

english_verse: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, Saul ɔ́su ubidi Yonatan ku bekpone batɔnkune bakladi ɔnii badu Dawid. Nsu Yonatan ɔɔyɔ́ Dawid geen.

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: Kama ni, ami ku mina ɔti bɔdububo mmɔ, na bulagyunku kesii kani na adubɔbɛ. Na kudeedi ni, ami ku-nwu bɔdubɔda ƒula kɔtɛ bɔnu. Na lɛla biala na bɔ́su ni, ndubɔya na ati nwuna kasusu.”

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: Bɔnu na átanu átati kalɛ na úti lɛlɔ ɔ́kpa na ƒula lili uwi ɔni na útékpoku Goliat? Na bɔnu na átanu ka Unwoti ɔ́ya na abu Israelƒuɔ bɔ́di Ƒilistiƒuɔ lɛlɔ ɔkɛnku lɛla lɛni na ɔ́bla ɔsu? Awɔ ɔlati ánu ɔmɛni na ebiti áda-a sɔsɔ. Na bi ɔsu na ɔlɛka abla likpidi lɛmɛni udu na aya na badu Dawid? Útabla likpidi lɛdi!”

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Saul únu ubidi Yonatan buvele ku bɔlɛ na úse kenye ɔnini, “Nkɛnku Unwoti ɔni nli ngba uwi ƒui lɛlɔ muusé kenye ka lɛɛɛdubo bɔya na badu Dawid.”

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Kama ni, Yonatan ɔ́lɔ Dawid na ɔ́sɔku bana kɔtɛ kɔmmɔ ƒui ɔ́su-nwu. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́kpanku Dawid úboku kaduli na Saul kudɔ, na úbo ɔɔbla-nwu kabla aani kalɛ kani na útaabla.

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔdi kama ni, kekpo kásɔ kábalɛ Israelƒuɔ ku Ƒilistiƒuɔ ntɛ. Na Dawid ɔ́tɔnku bekpone úsienku kekpokɔ. Na úkpoku-ma geen útálɛ ka ɔ́bɔku-ma na békeli bátɔlɔ.

english_verse: One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
translation_verse: Kɔnakunwi ni, Saul ɔ́tu nwuna lɛtula lɛni na ɔda úmene ɔnii utálɛ Dawid na ɔkana-nwu ɔmana kowodu lɛlɔ. Nsu Dawid ɔ́babla na úliiku lɛlɔ kɔnakunwi na lɛtula lɛmmɔ lɛ́vi lítálɛ kowodu lɛlɔ. Na usien ɔmmɔ ni, Dawid úkeli ɔ́tɔlɔ Saul kudɔ.

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Saul ɔ́tala bekyuli badi na úbo-ma ɔda ɔnii bataatu Dawid na nwuna kaduli kalɛ na uteedu kadi bugye ni, na badu-nwu. Nsu Dawid ulekudi Mikal ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Keli tɔlɔ mɛni usien ɔmɛni kani! Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, badubo-ɔ bɔdu asa na kadi kegye.”

english_verse: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Mikal úti kabuli na ɔ́yula ɔgyani ɔ́siku ƒansili úbenyene kalɔ, na úkeli ɔ́tɔlɔ bekyuli bani mɔɔwia-nwu badu mmɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Dawid ɔ́tɔlɔ kama ni, ulekudi Mikal úti baƒiɔ bani na béti ugyii bánwi na úti-nwu ɔ́va katɛnkɔ mmɔ na úbi-nwu ala aani ukyuli kalɛ. Na úti bese linwini úwi-nwu lili.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Kama ka Saul ɔ́tala bekyuli badi ɔnii betéƒie Dawid ni, Mikal údie kenye ka ɔgyani uuƒi.

english_verse: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bammɔ bénwini na bátásu Saul lɛla lɛni na Mikal ɔ́su-ma. Nsu Saul ɔ́sɔku bekyuli bammɔ úmene na ɔ́su-ma lɛnɔ ɔnini, “Bɛkpanku-nwu biboku-mi ina kalɛ na ɔtɛ uuƒi mmɔ, na ami ɔlati lɛdu-nwu.”

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Nsu ka bésie na béduo ɔtɔ kemmo ni, bánu ka baƒiɔ kani ntɛ na bese linwini liwi-nwu lili.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Ka Saul únu ɔmɛni ni, útéye Mikal ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na átɔlɔ-mi lɛni na áya na mina ukisine úkeli ɔ́tɔlɔ-mi kudɔ?” Mmɔ na Mikal ɔ́su Saul ɔnini, “Bɔsu na mina ɔgyani ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Ya na nteesie si alayɔ anii ndu-ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na Dawid úkeli mmɔ ni, ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Samuel kudɔ na ɔma ɔni baalɔ Rama. Na útásu-nwu ala ani ƒui na Saul ɔ́bla anwu Dawid. Ka ɔ́su Samuel ala amɛni ƒui ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, bana inyɔ bávi bálɛ ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na bétélie kesii kani baalɔ banii Naiot.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Saul úbenu ka Dawid ɔkya lɛkpaklɔ lɛdi na Naiot na Rama kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Saul ɔ́tala bekyuli badi ɔnii bétéƒie Dawid beboku. Nsu ka batu bammɔ bétédu mmɔ ni, bánu ka Samuel ɔtɔnku kenye bediene lisu lɛdi na benye beebo Katɔti kudu buteebo ku adi lidu. Na mmɔ ni, Katɔti Kɔyu kɔ́ƒɔ Saul batu bammɔ lɛlɔ kemmo na ama lɛnɔ bése kalɔ beebo Katɔti kudu aani bana kalɔ.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Na ka Saul únu lɛla lɛmɛni ni, ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tala bekyuli bamba ɔnii betéƒie Dawid. Na ama lɛnɔ ni, lɛni kani na Katɔti Kɔyu kɔ́tɔnku-ma na bése kalɔ beebo Katɔti kudu. Ɔmmɔ ƒui Saul ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tala bekyuli kɔtɛdi, na ama lɛnɔ ni, ɔmmɔ kani nálɛku-ma.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Kawɔlɔkɔ ni, anwu ɔlati ɔ́ta úsela Rama mmɔ. Na ka úbedu libiɔ linengudi lɛni baalɔ banii Seku mmɔ kɔtu ni, úye bekyuli badi na mmɔ kesii kani na Samuel ku Dawid bakya. Na básu-nwu banii ɔdubɔnu-ma na Naiot.

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́yu ulu úti úsela mmɔ. Nsu kɔnakunwi ni, Katɔti Kɔyu kɔ́ƒɔ Saul lɛlɔ kemmo na úse kalɔ uubó Katɔti kudu ku adi lidu na ulu lɛlɔ úbedu Naiot.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, ɔ́da nwuna adala údie úwi na uudie Katɔti uubó kudu kɔmmɔ na Samuel anumi muedi. Na limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ƒui ni, bɔtɛ kani na Saul ɔtɛ kalɔ mmɔ ku kasɔngya. Na ɔ́si litemi lɛmɛni ɔsu ni, lɛsugba lɛdi lɛkya na baayɔ́ buye banini, “Saul lɛnɔ únwini Katɔti Kenye Udiene yoo?”

english_verse: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid úkeli ɔ́si Naiot na Rama kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ úsie Yonatan kudɔ. Na útéye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi lɛ́bla iye bɔƒiɔ bɔmadi udu na lɛ́ƒiɔ iye likpidi lɛmani na lɛ́bla ɔsu na ƒ'ɔti ɔsiaku-mi ɔɔwia-mi ɔdu?”

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yonatan údie kenye ɔnini, “Oowo, ɔmmɔ ulebo-nwu kemmo lɛni kudii! Ɔsika si geen geen na mina ɔti ɔɔbla kasusu ka ɔdu-ɔ ni, nka ɔdubɔsu-mi. Ɔsika mina ɔti ulabla lɛla lɛdi na uledie-mi kɔtɛ. Ami ńtaƒɔ lɛla lɛmmɔ.”

english_verse: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
translation_verse: Nsu Dawid ɔ́su ɔnini, “Litemi lɛmmɔ lɛkya-nwu kemmo sɔsɔ. Ƒ'ɔti ɔgyi nwaa ka ami ku-ɔ bɔdi bakpana kpakplaa. Anwuɔsu ulasu-ɔ ka ɔɔwia-mi ɔdu, ɔsika ɔmmɔ ɔdubo-ɔ bukpoku geen. Mɔɔsu-ɔ na Katɔti ɔni nli ngba lɛnyi kemmo ka mina ngba bɔkya ɔgbankpi kemmo, ɔsika ƒ'ɔti ɔɔwia ka ɔdu-mi.”

english_verse: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yonatan ɔ́su Dawid ɔnini, “Lɛla biala na aawia ka lɛbla lite-ɔ ni, ndubo-ni bɔbla.”

english_verse: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Dawid ɔ́su Yonatan ɔnini, “Nu! Kɔnaadi ni, anwu na beesé kalɔ ku kɔbuli kɔwɔdi limeyi bɔdi. Na ɔdi ka ami ku ɔga bɔdi bɔsala. Nsu ya na lisie na ntábɛla lɛlɔ lɛkya lɛku kemmo kesii kadi utédu limeyi lɛtɛdi useyi uwi.

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: Na si ƒ'ɔti úye-mi lili ɔnii wɛ na lɛ́vi ni, na asu-nwu ka lívele-ɔ kuƒi nnii muukeli lisie mina ɔma na Betlehem na ami ku mina ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli ƒui bɔbla lɛkwa ndi lɛkwa kawɔlɔkɔ ɔdi akpala bɔsala.

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: Na si ɔ́su ɔnii mina takya útebile lɛla lɛdi ni, agyi anii ƒ'ɔti uuubo kasusu kekpidi kadi na mina lɛlɔ. Nsu si mina takya ɔ́ya na úti kɔnyi ni, na adubɔnu ati ka ɔɔwia-mi ɔdu sɔsɔ.

english_verse: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ka unwi bɔbla bunyimi nkya ami ku-ɔ ntɛ na Unwoti anumi ɔsu ni, muuvele-ɔ na atina-mi ƒula lɛƒɔndia. Na si bɔnu na awɔ lɛnɔ ánu áti ka lɛ́bla lɛla likpidi lɛdi ni, teti tesienku ƒ'ɔti, mmomu awɔ ɔlati du-mi kɔnakunwi.”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yonatan údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛɛɛdubo-ɔ bɔdu kudii! Na si bunu na línu iye lɛ́ti lɛnɔ ka mina ɔti ɔɔwia ka ɔdu-ɔ ni, áƒɔ ádi ka ndubuti lɛbɛla-a?”

english_verse: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
translation_verse: Amu na Yonatan ɔ́su Dawid ɔnini, “Bo na busie lɛku kemmo kesii kadi.” Na bágyu bésie mmɔ sɔsɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Yonatan ɔ́su Dawid ɔnini, “Mɔɔsu-ɔ kpakplaa na Unwoti, Israel Katɔti anumi nnii asa na limeyi lɛtɛdi liteedu ni, ndubuye mina ɔti na lɛnu-nwu kasusu lɛti na ƒula lɛlɔ. Na nsɔ mɔɔsu-ɔ kpakplaa nnii ndubɔya na ati mina ɔti kasusu si ɔɔwia-a lɛbuni.

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: Nsu si mina ɔti ɔda kasusu kekpidi ka ɔbla-a lɛla lɛdi na ami Yonatan ńtete-ɔ bɔti na ekeli aƒɔ ƒula lili ngba ni, na Unwoti ɔni-mi kɔtu kpakplaa biala námanku-mi. Muuvele Unwoti nnii ulieku-ɔ kalɛ kani na úlieku mina ɔti úbavi.

english_verse: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
translation_verse: Nsu si úbebo úte ka nsɔ liiibo ngba lɛnɔ ni, tada mina kaduli bekyuli lɛƒɔndia bɔbla taya. Na muuvele nnii sia ɔmɛni anu na abla ete-mi na uwi ɔni na Unwoti ɔdubɔyila Dawid bekisine ƒui udu na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Jonathan and David made an agreement that even David's descendants would have to keep. Then Jonathan said, “I pray that the Lord will take revenge on your descendants if they break our promise.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yonatan ku Dawid bényimi ku lɛlɔ na Yonatan ɔ́su ɔnini, “Muuvele Unwoti nnii ɔtɛku Dawid bekisine ƒui litemi na bana ɔbladu kenye.”

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan ɔ́ya na Dawid ɔ́lɛ bunyimi linyese lɛmmɔ ugyii ɔkɛnku bana bɔyɔ kenye, ɔsika ɔɔyɔ́ Dawid aani nwuna lɛlɔ kalɛ.

english_verse: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yonatan ɔ́su Dawid ɔnini, “Kɔnaadi na bɔɔdi bula kɔbuli kɔwɔdi bɔlɛ limeyi. Na bekyuli bani ndubo mmɔ badubo bɔnu bɔti ka awɔ eeebo-bu akɔ.

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu limeyi lɛtɛdi useyi uwi ni, sie tábɛ Esel Lɛtabi kama, kesii kani na ábɛ mina ɔti kudeedi mmɔ ataakywɛɛ-mi.

english_verse: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
translation_verse: Na ndububo kataminta atula atɛ buboku lɛtabi lɛmmɔ kamadɔ aani si lɛla lɛdi na lɛ́nu.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: Na ndubɔtala ɔnamu ɔni nsiaku-mi mmɔ nnii ubo ubawia atula ammɔ uboku-mi. Na si lɛ́su ɔnamu ɔmmɔ nnii, ‘Nu! Atula ammɔ atɛ ƒula kɔmadɔ mmɔ, tiboku-mi’ ni, na mɔɔsu-ɔ na Unwoti ɔni nli ngba anumi ka lɛla biala lise buɛɛ. Na akana na asɔ enwini ebo, ɔsika eleduo ɔgbankpi ɔdi kemmo.

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: Nsu si lɛ́su ɔnamu ɔmmɔ nnii, ‘Atula ammɔ aaatɛ mmɔ, mmomu atɛ ƒula kama ngye’ ni, na adubɔti ka akya ɔgbankpi kemmo, na Unwoti ɔɔwia ka ekeli.

english_verse: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
translation_verse: Na tayiƒala bula bunyimi bɔni na búnyimi búte lɛlɔ ami ku-ɔ. Nyimo ka Unwoti anumi na ami ku-ɔ ƒui bunye asa na búnyimi ɔmɛni. Na anwu ndubo-bu kenye budie uwi ƒui.”

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Dawid útábɛ na lɛku kemmo mmɔ. Na ka kɔbuli kɔwɔdi limeyi bɔdi búse kalɔ ni, Ɔga Saul lɛnɔ úbo úbelie kadikɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: Na keliekɔ kani na uulie kuuku mmɔ ni, aka kani na útélie na kowodu kudɔ. Na Yonatan ulie-nwu anumi na Abner ulie-nwu kɔdianu kakɛ. Nsu ka Dawid útebo ɔsu ni, nwuna keliekɔ kese ukpludi.

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: Saul ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka Dawid útebo kadikɔ mmɔ, nsu útasu lɛla lɛdi. Na ɔ́bla kasusu ɔnini, “Ɔƒɛni kalɛ Dawid útabla lɛlɔ sɛɛn kalɛ na ɔkana-bu akɔ bɔkya. Na sɔsɔ uuuse sɛɛn.”

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: Nsu kadi kegye kɔbuli kɔmmɔ limeyi linyɔdi ni, Dawid ɔ́sɔ úni na útebo kadikɔ. Mmɔ na Saul úye Yonatan ɔnini, “Bi nálɛku Yisai ubidi Dawid ɔsu na kamaadi ku ɔmwi ƒui útebo kadikɔ?”

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: Na údie kalɔ úte-mi na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Muuvele-ɔ ka bula ɔtɔ kemmo bɔɔbla akpala adi na bɔdi limeyi lɛdi na Betlehem. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu mina ɔnwani ɔlɔ-mi ɔnii mbakya-ma akɔ. Na ɔmɛni ɔsu na muuvele-ɔ kuƒi ka enu kalɔ na lisie mmɔ.’ Ami lɛnɔ línu kalɔ líte-nwu na ɔmmɔ ɔsu na uuubo-bu akɔ mɛni na ɔdi ku ɔga.”

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
translation_verse: Litemi lɛmɛni líƒi Saul livo geen na ɔ́su ubidi Yonatan ɔnini, “Ɔsɔnɔbi geen na adi na ƒ'ini ɔ́wɔ! Lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka enye Dawid kama kalɛ na bɛta binye-mi lɛlɔ. Na kɔƒa kɔni neeebo kalɔ budie lɛla na ábla mɛni. Na édie awɔ ku ƒ'ini udu keyi.

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Munuu ulábla-a nwaa ka si Dawid uli ngba ni, alakana ɔga bunwini na Israelƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ? Babla na atáwia-nwu eboku mɛni pla! Ɔlɛka ukpi!”

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Nsu Yonatan údie kenye buɛɛ na úye ɔti ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na ɔdi ka Dawid ukpi, na bi likpidi na ɔ́bla?”

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Nsu Saul ɔ́tu nwuna lɛtula ɔnii ɔɔdú-nwu. Mmɔ na ɔ́bla Yonatan nwaa ka sɔsɔ na ɔti Saul ɔɔwia Dawid ɔdu.

english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Yonatan lɛnɔ ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi na ɔ́ta ɔtɔlɔ ɔti kudɔ na kadikɔ mmɔ. Na úni adila na kɔbuli kɔwɔdi limeyi linyɔdi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔsika kɔnyi ku kɔnyana kúƒie-nwu na kɔƒa ala ani na Saul ɔ́su úwi Dawid ɔsu.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: Na kadi kégye ni, Yonatan ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie lɛku kemmo kesii kani na Dawid ɔkya, na ɔ́kpanku ɔnamu ɔkɔdi ɔdi ɔda.

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su ɔnamu ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Si líbo kataminta kamɛni ni, na ekeli atáwia atula ammɔ kesii kani na áyu, na eti eboku.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔnamu ɔmmɔ úse kalɔ uukeli. Na Yonatan úbo atula ammɔ útáva-nwu anumi.

english_verse: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
translation_verse: Ka ɔnamu ɔmmɔ údu kesii kani na lɛtula lɛmmɔ lɛ́yu ni, Yonatan ɔ́kpali-nwu úmene na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Sie anumi! Lɛtula lɛmmɔ lísie anumi ƒui.” Mmɔ na Yonatan ɔ́sɔ ɔ́va ɔ́su ɔnamu ɔmmɔ ɔnini,

english_verse: Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!” The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan,
translation_verse: “Babla, na tasɔ tenye mmɔ!” Ɔnamu ɔmmɔ ɔ́nu lɛtula lɛmmɔ na úti-ni úboku Yonatan.

english_verse: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔnamu ɔmmɔ anwu ɔɔɔgyi katɛmise kani nkya Dawid ku Yonatan ntɛ.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́sala atula ammɔ na úti úbunku kataminta kammɔ úte ɔnamu ɔmmɔ ɔnii uti uteesienku ɔma.

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Ka ɔnamu ɔmmɔ ɔ́tɔlɔ ni, Dawid ɔ́lɛ ɔ́si nwuna kabɛkɔ mmɔ úbasiaku Yonatan. Úbo kalɔ buɛɛ na ɔ́kya-nwu lili kalɔ kɔtɛ. Ɔmmɔ kama bátu báda lɛlɔ na bákya lɛlɔ kɔgbu na bana ƒui béwulo. Nsu Dawid úwulo útulo.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yonatan ɔ́su Dawid ɔnini, “Ɔlɛka atɔlɔ. Na Unwoti ɔsiaku-ɔ. Anwu nnye na únu bula bunyimi, anwuɔsu ala ani na bɔ́su ƒui ebo-nwu kemmo lɛni ute bula kaba kemmo bebi.” Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Dawid ɔ́yu ulu ɔ́tɔlɔ. Na Yonatan lɛnɔ únwini úsie ɔma.

english_verse: David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
translation_verse: Ka Dawid ɔ́tɔlɔ ni, úsie ɔkpane ɔni baalɔ banii Ahimelek kudɔ na Nob. Uwi ɔni na Ahimelek ɔ́nu ka Dawid ɔdubo na úsie útásiaku-nwu ni, lɛlɔ kani mɔɔtɔ́-nwu, ɔsika ɔ́yia geen. Na úye Dawid ɔnini, “Dɛ na ɔ́bla na ébo mɛni na awɔ lɛti nkɛ?”

english_verse: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid údie kenye ɔnini, “Ami lɛti nkɛ, ɔsika bula ɔga nátala-mi ɔnii mbabla lɛla kpakplaa lɛdi nte-nwu. Na ɔ́su-mi ɔnii ntaya na ɔdi ɔti lɛla lɛni na ɔ́tala-mi ɔnii mbabla. Na mina bekyuli ama ni, lɛ́su-ma nnii ami ku-ma bɔdubɔsa na kesii bamba.

english_verse: Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
translation_verse: Bi adila na ebo ɔƒɛni? Ɔƒaalɛ ndubɔkɛ bodobodo ɛlɔ iye lɛla bamba lɛdi lɛƒɔ na ƒula kudɔ.”

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: Nsu Ɔkpane Ahimelek údie kenye ɔnini, “Ao, ɔnwa, ásiaku-mi ku enukplu. Liiibo bodobodo ɔni na ukyuli biala ɔkana na ɔdi. Bodobodo ɔni nse ni, béti-nwu bákpa béte Unwoti. Na lɛkana na lite-mii ɔdi si bina akɔ ɔdi ku uleku bátasa emeyi klukui amɛni kemmo.”

english_verse: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid údie kenye ɔnini, “Sɔsɔ, abu ku bula beleku bɔ́sɔ bútatɛ tɔ dii. Ɔsika uwi biala na búsela butábla kabla kadi ni, bɔɔsia anumi teekisi lɛlɔ geen na bula ɔdi kenye na bulaƒiɔ. Anwuɔsu ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na bɔkɛ ka ɔga nátala-bu ɔsu ni, bɔ́klibi lɛlɔ kaduɛ.”

english_verse: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Ahimelek úti bodobodo ɔni na béti bákpa béte Unwoti mmɔ úte Dawid na béƒi ɔbambadi bése ɔmmɔ kenye.

english_verse: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Saul bebuo lɛlɔ banune kabla ɔblane unengu ɔdi na baalɔ-nwu Doeg na ɔdi Edomni lɛnɔ ɔkya mmɔ.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid úye Ahimelek ɔnini, “Ebo kewii kadi na ete-mi? Ɔsika ńteti likpola lɛdi ina mina kewii muedi lɛɛɛda, ɔsika usi usi nkɛ na lɛ́yu ulu, ka ɔlɛka lɛbabla ku kabla kani na bula ɔga ɔnii mbo mbabla mmɔ ɔsu.”

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: Amu na ɔkpane údie kenye ɔnini, “Goliat, Ƒilistini ɔni na ádu na Ela Ɔkwalɛ kemmo ni, nwuna kewii kese-mi kudɔ mɛni. Na línyimi-ka lɛ́kya kɔdi kemmo mɛni. Na líti-ka líse kakpakɔ ala kedee ammɔ kama. Na si aawia-ka ni, lɛkana na liti-ka lite-ɔ. Na bɔsɔ buuubo kewii iye likpola lɛbambadi lɛdi na mɛni buuutulo ɔmmɔ.” Mmɔ na Dawid lɛnɔ údie kenye kɔnakunwi ɔnini, “Kewii kadi kasɔ kaaadia kétedu kammɔ. Ti-ka te-mi.”

english_verse: David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish.
translation_verse: Amu na limeyi lɛmmɔ kani lɛlɔ ni, Dawid ɔ́tɔlɔ mmɔ na úkeli Saul úsie Ƒilistiƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na útéduo Gat Ɔga Akis kudɔ.

english_verse: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
translation_verse: Nsu Ɔga Akis kabla bablane béye-nwu banini, “Ɔɔɔdi Dawid ɔmɛni ndi Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔni lɛlɔ ɔnu na bánwi na beeti taatɔ, na baasu banini, “ ‘Saul ɔ́du bekisine apim apim, na Dawid anwu ɔ́du mpim leevu leevu’?”

english_verse: David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish.
translation_verse: Amu ka Dawid únu ka baasu-nwu lɛlɔ litemi ni, úkpoku-nwu na ɔ́ya na Gat Ɔga Akis lɛlɔ lɛ́da-nwu liƒu.

english_verse: So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔ́bla lɛlɔ aani ukyuli ɔni na lili kemmo kébie-nwu na bana anumi mmɔ, na ɔɔyu lisuo taakya nwuna ukwi. Na ɔkɛ uunweni ala taasia awodu lɛlɔ ku kɔyakun kenye.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́su nwuna kabla bablane ɔnini, “Bilánu ɔnana ɔmɛni taati ka lili kemmo kébie-nwu? Bi ɔsu na bíti-nwu bíboku-mi?

english_verse: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_verse: Bebuokpine bani nkya-mi kudɔ mɛni bátabɔ tɔ? Bi ɔsu na bɛɛsɔ bɛƒɔ ukyuli ɔmɛni udu biboku-mi na ubataabla ala amɛni udu na mina anumi? Bɔƒɔ na ɔlɛka lɛsɔ lɛƒɔ ɔmɛni lɛkya mina kaduli?”

english_verse: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, Dawid ɔ́kɛ kuƒi na úkeli ɔ́tɔlɔ Gat ɔma bonwu ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na útábɛ na lɛtabi ubu ɔdi kemmo na kesii kani baalɔ Adulam. Amu ka nwuna kaduli bekyuli ku nwuna banwani bénu kesii kani na ɔkya ni, bésie bátáwia-nwu banu na mmɔ.

english_verse: A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of
translation_verse: Bekyuli bamba lɛnɔ bébebunku-ma. Na bana badi ndi bekyuli bani na baanya taakya ku bayune ku bani nánu ka bana keliela kalátɛ-ma ƒui bébo bábasiaku Dawid ku anwu badi. Na Dawid únwini bana ɔtɔnkune ɔni na bana ƒui bumomo bɔbla aani nkyuli eti maane.

english_verse: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
translation_verse: Na uwi klukui ɔdi kama ni, Dawid ɔ́tɔlɔ kesii kani na ɔkya mmɔ úsie ɔma ɔni baalɔ Mispa na Moabƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ. Mmɔ na úvele ɔga ɔmmɔ kuƒi ɔnini, “Adubɔtuna na ami ku mina ɔti ku uni ƒui bubelie ƒula kalɔ lɛlɔ, wetédu ka lɛ́nu lɛla lɛni na Katɔti ɔɔwia ka lɛbla lɛti?”

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: Ɔga ɔmmɔ únu kalɔ úte Dawid, anwuɔsu Dawid ɔ́ya na ɔti ku uni bébo bakya Moab ɔga ɔmmɔ kudɔ na Mispa mmɔ. Na anwu ɔlati útábɛla lɛlɔ ɔ́kya kabɛkɔ kagyumanakɔ kpakplaa kadi.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Nsu Katɔti Kenye Udiene Gad ɔ́su Dawid ɔnini, “Tasɔ telie kabɛkɔ kpakplaa kamɛni kemmo, mmomu tɔlɔ teesie Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ.” Anwuɔsu Dawid ɔ́tɔlɔ mmɔ na útélie lɛku lɛdi kemmo na kesii kani nde ɔma ɔni baalɔ Heret.

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, na Saul ulie kugyii kolo kolo kɔdi ɔyuli kalɔ na kɔbi kɔdi lɛlɔ. Na mmɔ ude Gibea ɔma kemmo. Na nwuna bekpone batɔnkune benye bámana-nwu. Na ɔda nwuna lɛtula na kɔnu. Ɔƒɛni ukyuli ɔdi úyu ɔ́su Saul ka ɔgyi kesii kani na Dawid ku bani ƒui nsiaku-nwu kama bábɛ bakya.

english_verse: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
translation_verse: Amu na Saul ɔ́kpali ɔnii beteenu, “Amii Benyamin kaba kemmo bebi, bɛɛkali ka Yisai ubidi ɔnanabi ɔmmɔ ɔdubute-mii kɔlɔ ku adingyii mmo? Bɛɛkali ka ɔdubo-mii bɔbla na binwini bekpone mpim mpim batɔnkune ku eti anyɔ anyɔ batɔnkune?

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: Lili na bɛɛsa mina lɛlɔ ka bɛtu-mi lɛga? Ami ɔlati ubidi únyimiku Yisai ubidi Dawid kenye na mina lɛlɔ, na bina ɔdi útasu-mi! Bina akɔ ina ukyuli unwi muedi uláwia-mi bɔdia. Na ɔdi útasu-mi ka mina ubi ɔɔkya mina kabla ɔblane ogya ka unye utaatu-mi kalɛ na ɔɔbla ɔmwi mɛni!”

english_verse: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
translation_verse: Nsu Doeg ɔni ndi Edomni na unye Saul benengu bammɔ kudɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Lɛ́nu Yisai ubidi ɔmmɔ ka úbo Ahitub ubidi Ahimelek kudɔ na Nob.

english_verse: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
translation_verse: Na anwu nébunku-nwu na úvele Katɔti úte Dawid kalɛ na ɔti lɛla lɛni na ɔbla. Úte-nwu adila adi. Na úti Goliat Ƒilistini kewii kani na útaada mmɔ úte-nwu.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Ka Saul únu kenye kamɛni ni, kɔnakunwi ɔ́tala ɔnii batálɔ Ɔkpane Ahimelek ku nwuna lɛlɔ bekyuli bani ndi bakpane mmɔ beboku. Ama lɛnɔ bénu-nwu bɔlɔ na báta bébo ɔga kudɔ mmɔ kɔnakunwi.

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: Ka bébedu mmɔ kani na Saul ɔ́kpali Ahimelek ɔnii uteenu. Ahimelek lɛnɔ údie kenye ɔnii, “Ati, taatɛmi.”

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Saul úse kalɔ ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na awɔ ku Yisai ubidi Dawid bɛ́sa lili na mina lɛlɔ, na éte-nwu adila ku kewii, na évele Unwoti éte-nwu kalɛ na ɔta unye-mi lɛlɔ, na unye ɔgya kalɛ na ɔdu-mi aani kalɛ na ɔdaku bɔbla ɔmwi?”

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: Geen ni, lívele Katɔti líte-nwu na lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka ɔbla lɛlɔ. Ɔsika ɔmɛni ɔɔɔdi kudeedi ɔni na lívele Katɔti líte Dawid. Na útabla-a kɔnyi lɛnɔ dii! Anwuɔsu na buvele kemmo ni, tada ami-ku mina kaduli bekyuli kenye lɛni. Ami, ƒula kabla ɔblane, lɛɛɛgyi lɛla lɛdi ńtasiku litemi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Nsu Ɔga Saul údie kenye ɔnini, “Ahimelek, ɔlɛka lɛdu-ɔ ku ƒula lɛlɔ bekyuli ƒui.”

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: Amu na Saul únwini na ɔ́su nwuna bagyumanane bani nnye-nwu kɔmadɔ ɔnini, “Binwini na bɛdu Katɔti bakpane bamɛni, ɔsika ama lɛnɔ bebunku Dawid na bagyi ka bukeli na ɔda asa na béni na bátasu-mi.” Nsu bekpone benengu bammɔ ɔdi útayɔ ka ɔdu Unwoti bakpane bammɔ kalɛ na ɔga úbo-ma ɔda.

english_verse: Saul turned to Doeg, who was from Edom, and said, “Kill the priests!” On that same day, Doeg killed
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Saul únwini na ɔ́su Doeg ɔnini, “Awɔ, nwini na adu bakpane bamɛni!” Anwuɔsu Doeg, Edomni ɔmmɔ, únwini na ɔ́du bana nkyuli liti ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ bani nkya bana bɔkpa kabla lɛwu buni benye mmɔ.

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: Na ɔ́du Nob bekyuli ƒui, banana ku beleku ku banamu ku bebiwɔ ku ɔmantɛ bebuo ku bebuo ala betine ku baƒonu ƒui na ɔma ɔni kemmo na bakpane bammɔ bélie mmɔ.

english_verse: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
translation_verse: Nsu Ahitub uwɔ ɔni baalɔ Abiatar na ɔdi Katɔti Ɔkpane Ahimelek ubidi anwu úkeli na útasiaku Dawid na bábla unwi.

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: Ɔ́su Dawid ka Saul ɔ́ya na bádu Katɔti bakpane bammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama Dawid lɛnɔ ɔ́su Abiatar ɔnini, “Limeyi lɛmmɔ ni, Doeg ɔni ndi Edomni ɔmmɔ unye mmɔ. Ngyi ka anwu kani ndubɔsu Ɔga Saul ala amɛni ƒui. Na ɔkɛnku ami ɔsu na ƒ'ɔti ku nwuna lɛlɔ bekyuli ƒui baakɛ́ kukpi.

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: Nsu awɔ, taayia. Sɔ kya-mi kudɔ mɛni. Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔwia ka ɔdu-ɔ ni, anwu kani nsiaku ami lɛnɔ na ɔɔwia-mi ɔdu. Nsu lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛdubo-ɔ bɔbla.”

english_verse: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
translation_verse: Bekyuli badi bábasu Dawid limeyi lɛdi banini, “Ƒilistiƒuɔ bébo bakya beekpóku Keila ɔma bekyuli na beeyú-ma edula ani na bébo bése kakpa.”

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?” “Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid úye Unwoti kasusu únu ɔnini, “Nsie ntékpoku Ƒilistiƒuɔ bamɛni?” Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Sie na etékpoku-ma na aƒɔ Keila ɔma bekyuli!”

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: Nsu Dawid bekyuli básu-nwu banini, “Na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mɛni muedi bɔɔyia. Amu na si búsie Keila mmomu bɔnii butékpoku Ƒilistiƒuɔ ni, dɛ na ɔdubo buse?”

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Dawid ɔ́sɔ útéye Unwoti kunyɔdi si usie utékpoku-ma, na Unwoti údie kenye ɔnini, “Awɔ, teesie Keila, ɔsika ndubuti Ƒilistiƒuɔ lɛkya-a enu kemmo na adi-ma lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Dawid ku nwuna bekpone báyu ulu bésie Keila na bétékpoku Ƒilistiƒuɔ na béƒie-ma bebuo ku ala pii báƒɔ, na údie Keila ɔma bekyuli.

english_verse: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Dawid únu ka Saul ɔɔwia ulu ɔni na ubo ubeƒie-nwu ni, ɔ́su Ɔkpane Abiatar ɔnini, “Ti ƒula bɔkpa awu ɔmmɔ boku.”

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Dawid úvele ɔnini, “Unwoti, Israel Katɔti, ami ƒula kabla ɔblane línu nwaa ka Saul ɔɔwia ulu ɔni na ubo Keila mɛni na ubayila ɔma ɔmmɔ udu na ami ɔsu.

english_verse: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Na muuvele-ɔ liye linu si kadi kamɛni bekyuli badubudie-mi bete Saul si úbo úte lɛni sɔsɔ?” Amu na Katɔti údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔdubo.”

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Dawid ɔ́sɔ úye Katɔti ɔnini, “Keila kadi bekyuli badubuti ami ku mina bekyuli bakya Saul enu kemmo?” Amu na Katɔti ɔnini, “Ɛɛn.”

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: Dawid ɔ́kya kɔbɛkɔ na Siƒ kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo na abi lɛlɔ. Na uwi ɔmmɔ ƒui ni, na Saul ɔ́kɛ útaawia-nwu, nsu Katɔti úteti Dawid útakya Saul enu kemmo.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Dawid ɔ́kya Siƒ abi kalɔ kakwiidi lɛlɔ na kesii kani na baalɔ banii Hores ni, únu ka banii Saul úbo ekutɛ mmɔ ka nka ubadu-nwu.

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: Na Saul ubidi Yonatan úsie Hores mmɔ na útakya Dawid ɔkplu kalɛ na use-nwu kayi na Katɔti lɛlɔ.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: Ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Tayia, mina ɔti Saul kɔnu kulétuku-ɔ. Geen ni, awɔ ndubo ebenwini Israelƒuɔ ɔga na ami ndubɔbla ƒula ubunkune. Na mina ɔti muedi ɔgyi ɔmɛni lɛni.”

english_verse: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bana inyɔ bényimi na Unwoti anumi ka lɛla lɛdi lilebile-ma ntɛ. Na Yonatan únwini ɔ́tɔlɔ, nsu Dawid anwu ɔ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ ɔkya Hores mmɔ.

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, bekyuli badi bási Siƒ ɔma kemmo na bátásu Saul na Gibea banini, “Dawid ubo kabɛkɔ kadi na bula kudɔ, na Yesimon kada kakɛ na mmɔ kede Hores na Hakila abi lɛlɔ si éti ésela na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
translation_verse: Amu na Saul údie kenye ɔnini, “Katɔti úte-mii kusɛ kusɛ na kalɛ na biiti-mi lɛlɔ kasusu ɔsu.

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: Na bɛsɔ bisie na bitásia anumi kaduɛ na bɛnu kesii kani bene na Dawid uusié ku ukyuli ɔni nánu-nwu na mmɔ. Ɔsika básu-mi ka Dawid ubo lɛkwɛ na ɔ́da anu geen.

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: Bɛnu kesii kani ƒui na ɔɔyɔ́ busie taatábɛ taakya na bibasu-mi lɛla lɛni geen na lɛdi. Na ami ku-mii bɔdubusie na butáwia-nwu na ntɛ mmɔ, na ntékpo-nwu lɛlɛku na Yuda adua ammɔ ƒui kemmo si mmɔ na ɔkya geen geen.”

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bekyuli bammɔ básɔ bágyu batɔ Saul na Siƒ ɔma. Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, na Dawid ku nwuna bekyuli bámu bakya Maon kalɔ kakwiidi lɛlɔ na Yesimon kada kakɛ.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Saul ku nwuna bekyuli bése kalɔ ku Dawid ku nwuna bekyuli bɔwia. Amu ka Dawid únu ka Saul ɔkya ɔɔwia-nwu ni, ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie lɛtakpɛ na Maon kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo. Na ka Saul únu lɛni ni, ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Maon kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo mmɔ úsie ɔkya ɔɔwia Dawid.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Na Saul ku nwuna bekyuli bakɛ kɔbi ɔvi ɔmɛni baatú Dawid ku nwuna bekyuli. Na Dawid lɛnɔ ɔkɛ ɔvi ɔni ngye uukeli Saul. Amu na uwi ɔni lɛlɔ geen na Saul ku nwuna bekyuli báni beedé Dawid ku nwuna bekyuli na beƒie-ma na mmɔ ni,

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: mmɔ kani na ɔtu ɔdi ɔdanku kenye úboku Saul ɔnini, “Ɔbune, Nwini bo pla! Ɔsika Ƒilistiƒuɔ béduo-bu kalɔ kemmo na badaku-bu ala buti taatɔlɔku, na beebile kalɔ kammɔ ala.”

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani na Saul ɔ́da Dawid kama bɔsiaku ɔ́ya na únwini utásiaku Ƒilistiƒuɔ bammɔ. Anwuɔsu na baalɔ kesii kani na lɛla lɛmmɔ líbo lɛni banii Sela Hamahlekot, na nwuna kalɔ ndi bukeli lɛtakpɛ.

english_verse: David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ɔ́tɔlɔ mmɔ úsie útákya kesii kani baalɔ banii En-Gedi.

english_verse: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Saul úsie útábɔku Ƒilistiƒuɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, únu ka banii Dawid ku nwuna bekyuli bésie bakya En-Gedi kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo.

english_verse: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
translation_verse: Saul úbo úbedu kesii kani na baƒonu ayu adi enye na ulu kɔtu na lɛtakpɛ ubu ɔdi ɔkya mmɔ. Amu na úduo mmɔ ɔnii utése kuvodɔ. Na ubu ɔmmɔ kani kemmo na Dawid ku nwuna bekyuli bakya na kama kama ƒui.

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid bekyuli bammɔ básu-nwu buɛɛ banini, “Limeyi lɛmɛni geen ndi limeyi lɛni lɛlɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su lɛla lɛdi úse, ɔni na ɔ́su-ɔ ɔnini, ‘Ndubuti ƒula ukisine lɛkya-a enu kemmo na esusu-nwu kalɛ na aayɔ́.’ ” Amu na Dawid ɔ́kpɛ buɛɛ na útékulo Saul awu gyɔlɔɔ ɔni na ɔkya kɔtu, na Saul útati.

english_verse: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
translation_verse: Kama ƒui ni, Dawid kayi kékpoku-nwu na kalɛ na úkulo-nwu awu kɔtu ɔsu.

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: Lɛni na Dawid ɔ́dɔnku nwuna bekpone, na bátabla Saul lɛla lɛdi. Ka Saul ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔ́ta ɔ́lɛ lɛtakpɛ ubu ɔmmɔ kemmo ka ɔtɔlɔ.

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid lɛnɔ ɔ́lɛ lɛtabi ubu ɔmmɔ kemmo na ɔ́kpali úmene ɔnini, “Ati, mina Ɔga Ɔbune!” Kɔnakunwi Saul únwini ɔ́nu kama na ɔ́nu ka Dawid úboku lili kalɔ úte-nwu.

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́su Saul ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na si bekyuli baatɔ́lɔ-ɔ banii mɔɔwia-a lɛdu ni, na aaƒɔ́-ma taadi?

english_verse: You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ ni, awɔ ɔlati ánu ku ƒula anumi nwaa ka nka Unwoti úti-ɔ ɔ́kya-mi enu kemmo na lɛtabi ubu ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na mina bekpone badi bénye-mi lɛlɔ banii ndu-ɔ, nsu líni na lɛ́su-ma nnii lɛɛɛdubo mina kɔnu bɔtala bɔbla awɔ mina ati lɛla lɛdi, ɔsika Unwoti ukyuli ɔni na úse likpo na adi.

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: Ati, aanu ƒula awu gyɔlɔɔ ɔni na akya kɔtu na líkulo nda mɛni. Ami ɔlati nékulo awu ɔmmɔ kɔtu, nsu ńtadu-ɔ. Ɔƒaani ni, mɔɔwia ka awɔ ɔlati anu ati nwaa ka ńtabla lɛla lɛdi ńtaƒiɔ-ɔ, na ńtata ńtenye-ɔ lɛlɔ lɛnɔ, nsu awɔ asiaku-mi aatú-mi uwi biala ka adu-mi.

english_verse: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
translation_verse: Muuvele Unwoti ka ɔtɛ litemi lɛmɛni na ami ku-ɔ ntɛ, na anwu ndubo-ɔ kayu bɔƒɔ na ala ani na aabla-mi kenye. Ɔɔɔdi ami ndubo mina kɔnu budie butuku-ɔ.

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Lɛni na benengu bébo lɛgba banini, ‘Alaekpidi bablane alati ndanku bana likpidi bakɛ,’ anwuɔsu mina kɔnu kɔɔɔdubo-ɔ butuku.

english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: “Bi ɔsu na Israelƒuɔ ƒui ɔga ɔ́ta na ɔkɛ ɔɔtú ami ɔni naaadi lɛla lɛdi? Nse aani akpewe ukpine iye alɔlɔ. Bi na adubɔkɛ si ádu-mi?

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
translation_verse: Unwoti kani ndi bula litemi ɔtɛne, na anwu ndubo litemi lɛmmɔ bukulo na ami ku-ɔ ntɛ. Anwu mɔɔnu mina lɛbibo na ɔdubute-mi ubo na udie-mi na ƒula enu kemmo.”

english_verse: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su Dawid ɔnini, “Adi ukyuli ɔni na ƒula ablala ese siin etulo ami adi. Awɔ ábla lɛla biala kaduɛ éte-mi na ami mmomu nábla-a likpidi.

english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: Ɔmwi ni, ásu-mi lɛbuni lɛni na ábla-mi. Unwoti úti-mi ɔ́kya-a enu kemmo, nsu átadu-mi.

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: Ɔsika ńtenu dii ka ukyuli ɔkɛ nwuna ukisine na ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na ɔnyonu-nwu na ɔtɔlɔ kudii. Unwoti ute-ɔ kusɛ kusɛ na lɛla lɛni na ábla éte-mi ɔmwi mɛni ɔsu.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: Ngyi nwaa ka awɔ ndubo abadi lɛga. Na ɔkɛnku ƒula lɛlɔ na Israel lɛga kadikɔ kammɔ kadubunye kpakplaa.

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: Na ɔƒaani ni, mɔɔwia ka ese-mi kenye kadi na Unwoti lɛnyi kemmo ka alayila mina bebi ku bawɔ udu kalɛ na mina lɛnyi lilayii na Israel bekyuli akɔ.”

english_verse: So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Dawid úse kenye kammɔ úte Saul. Ɔmmɔ kama Saul únwini úsie ɔma, nsu Dawid ku nwuna bekyuli bátɔlɔ bésie bana kabɛkɔ kpakplaa kammɔ.

english_verse: One day, Nabal was in Carmel where his servants were cutting the wool from his sheep. David was in the desert when he heard about it.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ka Dawid ɔ́kya kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ kemmo ni, únu ka Nabal úsie Karmel na kesii kani na nwuna kabla bablane beekúlo nwuna baƒonu linwini.

english_verse: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
translation_verse: Na bɛsu-nwu bɛnini, ‘Muuvele Unwoti nnii ute-ɔ ngba gyɔlɔɔ! Na ute awɔ ku ƒula kaduli bekyuli ƒui ɔlɔkplu. Na ɔya na ƒula ala ani ƒui na ebo akya kpakplaa!

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɔƒɛni ni, línu ka eekúlo ƒula bebuo linwini uwi ɔmɛni kemmo. Nsu nyimo ka uwi ɔni na ƒula bebuo lɛlɔ banune bébo Karmel ni, bútabla-ma kalala, na bana lɛla lɛdi lɛnɔ lítayii na uwi ɔni na béti bákya-bu kudɔ na mmɔ.

english_verse: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
translation_verse: Na eye ƒula kabla bablane na badubɔsu-ɔ. Anwuɔsu na buvele kemmo ni, nu mina bakloƒu bamɛni kɔnyana ka lɛlɔyɔ uwi na ɔdi mɛni ɔsu. Na ete ƒula kabla bablane bamɛni lɛla lɛni na ƒula kɔnu kútuku na baƒɔ beboku ami ƒula ubi Dawid lɛnɔ.’ ”

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: Ka Dawid batu bamɛni bétédu mmɔ ni, básu Nabal kenye kammɔ na básɔ benye baanu-nwu.

english_verse: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
translation_verse: Amu na Nabal udie lɛla lɛni na bábasu-nwu kenye ɔnini, “Ɔma ndi Dawid ku Yisai ubidi ɔmmɔ? Kabla bablane pii bukeli na benye beekeli bana batɔlati emeyi amɛni kemmo.

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: Na bi ɔsu na muuti mina bodobodo ku ntu ku lɛna lɛni na lɛ́du muute mina kabla bablane bani muukúlo baƒonu linwini teete-mi lite bekyuli bani na lɛɛɛgyi-ma kasikɔ ku kesii kani na bésela?”

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid batu bammɔ bénwini na bátɔlɔ. Na ka bétéduo ni, básɔku ala ani nálɛ ƒui básu Dawid.

english_verse: “Everybody get your swords!” David ordered. They all strapped on their swords. Two hundred men stayed behind to guard the camp, but the other
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani na Dawid ɔ́bala nwuna kewii na ɔ́su nwuna bekpone aani eti maane ɔnini, “Bɛbala bina kuwii na bɔyu ulu.” Na bekpone bani nébu na bana ala kudɔ babla aani nkyuli eti ene.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu, ti litemi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ kasusu na anu kalɛ na bɔdubo bɔbla, ɔsika ɔgbankpi ɔ́ɔsi ɔdubo bula ɔtɔlati ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ƒui lɛlɔ. Na bula ɔtɔlati ubo lili ɔkplu ɔni na uláwia ka unu ukyuli ɔdi litemi.”

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su nwuna kabla ɔblane ɔnini, “Awɔ, taatɔ na ndubo mbasiaku-ɔ ɔƒaani.” Nsu útaya na ɔgyani Nabal ɔti lɛla lɛmɛni kemmo lɛla biala.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: Ka ulie nwuna ebuo lɛlɔ ɔdubo na úbedu abi adi ɔkɔkɔ ni, ɔ́nu ka Dawid ku nwuna bekyuli lɛnɔ báyu bási anumi kakɛ badubo-nwu kudɔ asa na útásiaku-ma.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ɔ́su lɛla lɛdi ɔɔwɔlɔ asa na bása ɔnini, “Keeke na lɛ́kya ńtaanu ukyuli ɔmɛni ala lɛlɔ na kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo mmɔ nnii lɛla lɛdi litayii-nwu. Aanu ka likpidi na úti ɔ́ƒɔ-mi lɛbuni lɛni na lɛ́bla-nwu kayu.

english_verse: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔni ami Dawid kɔtu kɔni naaadia si ńtayila ukyuli ɔmɛni ku nwuna kaduli ala ƒui udu asa na kadi kégye ɔni na ina ukyuli unwi pɛ ɔsɔ ulébu.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Abigail ɔ́nu Dawid kani na ɔ́yu nwuna ebuo ala utine lɛlɔ na úboku lɛlɔ kalɔ buɛɛ na ɔ́kya Dawid lili kalɔ.

english_verse: Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him! I didn't see the men you sent,
translation_verse: Muuvele-ɔ nnii die ulikplune Nabal ɔmɛni atu na takpete-nwu. Nwuna ɔbladu útavumana ku nwuna lɛnyi lɛni kalɔ ndi kɔdɔlɔ. Anwuɔsu lisusu ala kani na ɔɔbla uwi ndi uwi. Nsu ni, ami ƒula kabla ɔblane ńtanu ƒula batu bammɔ bubo.

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: Buvele kemmo, ti ƒula kabla ɔblane bɔƒiɔ ƒui kyiɛ-nwu. Unwoti ɔdubɔgyumana-a ku ƒula kaduli bekyuli ƒui uwi ndi uwi, ɔsika nwuna kekpo na enye eekpó. Na muuvele lɛnɔ nnii na ƒula ngba bulie uwi ƒui ni, Unwoti udie-ɔ na alabla lɛla likpidi lɛdi.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: Unwoti ƒula Katɔti ɔdubɔƒɔ-ɔ na ƒula bekisine enu kemmo ina ka basiaku-ɔ banii baadú-ɔ. Na Unwoti ɔmmɔ ɔlati ɔdubɔyila-ma ngba kɔnakunwi, utulo kalɛ na adubɔkya lɛtabi na kavwinvwi kemmo eƒwimi.

english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: Na si Unwoti ɔ́bla kenye kani na úse awɔ mina Ati úte-ɔ na ɔ́bla-a Israel lɛlɔ ɔdine ni,

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: na kayi kabla-a ƒaa kalɛ na ƒula kayi kaládu awɔ, mina Ati, kɔtɔ kɔdi ka áƒiɔ na ádu ukyuli ɔdi édie-nwu kasi. Ɔƒɛni si uwi ɔni na Unwoti ɔ́ya na ala amɛni ƒui ébo-nwu kemmo ni, tayiƒala ami ƒula kabla ɔblane.”

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid ɔ́su Abigail ɔnini, “Bemwi Unwoti Israel Katɔti ɔni nátala-a ɔ́kya-mi ɔnii bo basiaku-mi ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ.

english_verse: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
translation_verse: Na muuvele nnii Unwoti ɔmmɔ ute-ɔ kusɛ kusɛ na kalɛ na ánu litemi geen lɛmɛni na átɛ-ni ásiaku ulu lɛlɔ ɔsu. Édie-mi na ńtewi ubugya kalɔ iye liti mina enu na lidie kasi kadi lite lɛlɔ.

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Si ɔɔɔdi ɔni na ébo ábanu-mi pla lɛni ɔsu ni, mɔɔsu-ɔ na Unwoti Israel Katɔti ɔni nátaya na lɛbla-a lɛla lɛdi anumi ka nka ina ukyuli unwi ɔdi muedi ulébu na Nabal kaduli asa na kadi kadubugye.”

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Dawid ɔ́ƒɔ ala ani na Abigail ɔda úboku-nwu na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Línu ƒula etemila. Nwini teesie ku keyi buɛɛ na ndubɔbla kalɛ na ásu-mi.”

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Abigail ɔ́sɔ únwini útéduo kaduli ni, Nabal ku anwu badi belie baadi taani aani ɔga mɔɔdi limeyi. Na ɔ́ɔni-mu sɔsɔ na aatí ka bɔsia-nwu anumi. Anwuɔsu Abigail útasu-nwu lɛla lɛdi useyi uwi ɔmmɔ útédu ka kadi kégye.

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Amu ka kadi kégye ni, Abigail ɔ́sɔku ala ani ƒui nálɛ ɔ́su Nabal. Na ka únu-nya lɛnɔ ni, kayi kékulo-nwu na ɔ́gyini unye aani lɛtabi.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Na emeyi leevu kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́ƒɔ Nabal ngba na úkpi.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: Amu na úbo kalɔ buɛɛ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Línu kalɔ ka ndi-nwu kabla ɔblane na lɛ́tuna ka maƒɔ-nwu lɛgba na mabla-nwu kabla.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Abigail ɔ́babla na ɔ́kɔ úlie nwuna ebuo ala utine lɛlɔ na nwuna kabla bablane ɛlɔ lɛnɔ básiaku-nwu, na ama ku batu bammɔ bátɔlɔ na útélieku Dawid.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: Asa na Abigail ɔdubusie utélieku-nwu ni, na Dawid úuti uleku ɔni baalɔ Ahinoam ɔ́siku Yesreel ɔma, anwuɔsu bana inyɔ nákya-nwu kesii aani nwuna beleku.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: Nsu na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Saul ɔ́ɔsɔku ubidi Mikal ɔni na nka Dawid úti mmɔ úte ɔnana ɔni baalɔ banii Las ubidi okloƒu ɔni baalɔ Paltiel na bási Galim ɔma.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Na uwi bamba ɔdi lɛnɔ ni, Siƒuɔ badi bésie Saul kudɔ na Gibea bátásu-nwu banini, “Dawid ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla kabɛkɔ kadi na Hakila Kɔbi lɛlɔ kesii kani nde Yesimon.”

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Saul ɔ́da keliekɔ na Hakila Kɔbi lɛlɔ kesii kani néti anumi kátina Yesimon. Nsu Dawid anwu ɔ́bɛ ɔkya kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ kemmo. Na ka únu ka Saul úbo ɔkya ɔɔwia-nwu ni,

english_verse: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
translation_verse: ɔ́tala batu badi ɔnii batásia anu banu kaduɛ si Saul úbo ɔkya mmɔ sɔsɔ.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
