english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: “Sie mina kabla ɔblane Dawid kudɔ na atásu-nwu ka lɛla lɛni na ami Unwoti muuye-nwu anini, ‘Awɔ ndubɔtu ɔtɔ ete-mi na lilie-nwu kemmo?

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Ńtelie ɔtɔ ɔni na bayawine béti bana enu bátu kudii, mmomu Adi Kevo kani na baagyú taada taavinku kemmo na lílie ɔ́si uwi ɔni na lídie mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ lɛ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ úti úbedu ɔmwi.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Na uwi biala na mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ báta bási kesii kadi bésela kesii bamba ni, ami lɛnɔ nsiaku-ma. Na batɔnkune bani na lɛ́ƒuna mmɔ ni, ɔmani na lɛ́su nnii beti egyii ani náƒɔ kuye mmɔ adi batu keliekɔ kadi bete-mi na lilie dii?’

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: “Na ɔƒɛni ni, su mina kabla ɔblane Dawid anii ami Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui nnii, ‘Asa na ndubɔƒuna-a na enwini mina kadi Israel ɔtɔnkune ni, na nka baƒonu kani na aakpanku teesienku kadikɔ.

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Na kesii biala na akɛ ni, lɛ́siaku-ɔ. Na líbunku-ɔ na ádi ƒula bekisine ƒui lɛlɔ. Na ɔƒaani lɛnɔ ni, ndubɔbla-a na aƒɔ lɛnyi aani baga bamba bani náƒɔ lɛnyi bétulo ƒui na kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ni, ndubɔƒuna keliekɔ sɛsɛɛ kadi lise lite mina kadi bekyuli ka belie. Na ndubɔya na belie kesii kammɔ ɔni na bekyuli badi basɔ belékpoku-ma lɛnɔ aani kalɛ na kadi bamba badi bábla bábavi.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Na si uwi ɔni na ebekpi na átɔlɔ ébo ƒula bati kudɔ ni, ƒula kaba kemmo ubi na ndubɔya na bese lɛga na ƒula kenye na ɔdubɔlɛ ɔsi awɔ ɔlati kemmo. Na ndubɔya na nwuna lɛga kadikɔ kenye kpakplaa.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Na ubi ɔmmɔ ndubɔtu ɔtɔ ute mina lɛnyi. Na ndubɔya nwuna lɛgakadikɔ liboku lɛdubuse liteesie uwi ƒui.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Ndubɔdi-nwu kɔti. Na anwu lɛnɔ ɔdi mina ubi. Na si ɔ́bla lɛla lɛdi ɔ́ƒiɔ-mi ni, ndubɔni-nwu kɔtu aani kalɛ na ubi ɔti ɔɔní ubidi kɔtu,

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: “O Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, Israelƒuɔ Katɔti, édie átina-mi na ásu-mi ka awɔ ndubo mina lɛgadi ɔtɔ bɔtu bute-mi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na ami ƒula kabla ɔblane líse kayi mɔɔkpali-ɔ na lɛda ala amɛni lɛva-a anumi.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Ka Dawid únu ala amɛni ni, anwu kani na ɔ́ta úsie Adi Kevo kani kemmo na beesié taatákpali Unwoti na útélie kalɔ. Mmɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “O Unwoti ɔni ntulo ƒui, ami ku mina kaduli bekyuli bútamanku lɛƒɔndia libendi lɛni udu na ábla éte-bu.

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: “O Unwoti, bi na ami Dawid nsɔ mbo lɛnɔ na masu-ɔ, ɔsika agyi ami ƒula kabla ɔblane.

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: Ɔkɛnku ƒula litemi ku lɛƒɔyɔ lɛlɔ na ábla ala enengudi amɛni na édie-nya átina ami ƒula kabla ɔblane.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: “O Unwoti Ɔbune, ébomo geen na ɔdi uuuse aani ƒula kalɛ. Na aani kalɛ na búnu ku bula atu ni, Katɔti ɔdi uuubo ntu awɔ kani.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli badi lɛnɔ beeese aani ƒula kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ kalɛ na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ. Ama kani na awɔ Katɔti étédie álɛku Egyipteƒuɔ lɛlɔ bɔdi kalɔ éte lɛlɔ na bénwini ƒula kadi bekyuli. Na ƒula lɛnyi lɛ́ƒɔ kuye na ábla ala enengudi éte-bu ku akɔla ala budie taatina ani mɔɔda bekyuli liƒu. Na ábɔku kadi bamba bekyuli ku bana baƒiɔ álɛku bana kuliekɔ na bana kalɔ kénwini abu Israelƒuɔ bati kadi.

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Éti abu Israelƒuɔ énwini ƒula kadi bekyuli geen uwi ƒui. Na awɔ Unwoti énwini bula Katɔti.

english_verse: And now, Lord God, please do what you have promised me and my descendants.
translation_verse: “Unwoti Katɔti, ɔƒaani ni, bla ƒula linyese lɛlɔ te ami ƒula kabla ɔblane ku mina kaduli bekyuli aani kalɛ na ásu.

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: Na ƒula lɛnyi lɛdubusie ɔgyu uti úsela uwi ƒui. Na kadi ƒui bekyuli badubɔsu banini, ‘Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui mɔɔdi Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ. Na Dawid kaba kemmo bebi ndi bagadine bani na ɔ́ƒuna.’

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: O Unwoti Ɔbune, awɔ ndi bula Katɔti ɔni lɛlɔ kani na ukyuli ɔdubɔkɛ kama kekpokɔ. Na ásu-mi kpakplaa ka adubɔbla ala abuni enengudi amɛni ete-mi anii ƒula kabla ɔblane kalɛ.

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu muuvele-ɔ nnii te mina kaduli bekyuli kusɛ kusɛ. Na ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ kani na adubuti ada-ma na ataanu-ma lɛlɔ uwi ƒui. Ɔsika lɛni na awɔ Unwoti Ɔbune ásu kpakplaa ése. Na si ábla ɔmɛni sɔsɔ ni, na adubute mina kaduli bekyuli kusɛ kusɛ ɔmmɔ geen úsela uwi ƒui!”

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: Na Benaia, ɔni ndi Yehoiada ubidi, mɔɔnu Keretiƒuɔ ku Peletiƒuɔ lɛlɔ. Na Dawid bebi badi ɔga kasusu betene.

english_verse: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
translation_verse: Dawid ɔ́di Moabƒuɔ lɛnɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́ya na Moabƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ básɔ bátɛ kalɔ na lɛgaala kemmo. Ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́ya na béti kabuli kadi udu bákɔku bana linene na béle-ma kemmo akpa atɛ. Na akpa anyɔ edeedi ni, ɔ́ya na bádu-ma. Na lɛkpa lɛtɛdi kani na bátadu. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Moabƒuɔ bénwini bakya Dawid kalɔ na baaƒɔ lɛlɔ bɔdi kadikɔ kayu teete Dawid.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Na kekpo bamba kemmo ni, Dawid ku nwuna bekpone békpoku Sobaƒuɔ. Na bana ɔga ndi Rehob ubidi ɔni ndi Hadadeser. Na kekpo kammɔ kálɛ uwi ɔni na Hadadeser ku nwuna bekpone bátu akpagya na bási bésela betékpoku kadi kani bekyuli nli Euƒrate Ketu amadɔ.

english_verse: When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed
translation_verse: Amu ka Siriaƒuɔ bani na bási Damasko lɛnɔ bébo banii bebebunku Sobaƒuɔ Ɔga Hadadeser ni, Dawid ɔ́du bana mpim aavlanyɔ-inyɔ.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Dawid úle nwuna bekpone ɔ́kya Damasko na ɔ́kɛ ɔyikun na Siriaƒuɔ lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu Siriaƒuɔ lɛnɔ baaƒɔ lɛlɔ bɔdi kadikɔ kayu teete Dawid. Na kesi kesii na Dawid úsie ni, Unwoti uubunku-nwu na ɔɔdi nwuna bekisine lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na kekpo kammɔ kama ni, Dawid úƒie Hadadeser benengu sika ugyiedi lɛlɔ agyumanala ɔ́ƒɔ na úti-nya úsienku Yerusalem.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: Na abuala egyiedi ani baakywɛɛ ala na Beta ku Berotai lɛma lɛni lɛlɔ na Ɔga Hadadeser útaadi mmɔ ni, úti ketulodikɔ ɔ́tɔlɔku.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: ɔ́tala ubidi Yoram ɔ́kya Dawid na Yerusalem, ɔnii utégyele-nwu na ute-nwu mmo. Na uwi ɔdi návi kemmo ni, Ɔga Toi ɔmɛni ku Hadadeserƒuɔ békpo. Na asa na Yoram ɔdubusie Dawid kudɔ na Yerusalem mmɔ ni, ɔdanku sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ku abuala egyiedi úsienku Dawid.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
translation_verse: Dawid úti etela ammɔ ɔ́kya Unwoti lɛkɔkɔ aani kalɛ na ɔ́bla uwi ɔni na ɔ́ƒɔ sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi na lɛma lɛni na úkpo ɔ́di lɛlɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: Na bakpane benengudi ndi Ahitub ubidi ɔni baalɔ Sadok ku Abiatar ubidi ɔni baalɔ Ahimelek. Na Dawid ɔku unwenine baalɔ Seraia.

english_verse: David ruled all Israel with fairness and justice.
translation_verse: Ɔ́di Israelƒuɔ ƒui lɛlɔ kaduɛ ɔni na ɔ́bla ala siin úte nwuna bekyuli.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Na Seruia ubidi Yoab ndi bana bekpone bammɔ ɔtɔnkune. Na Ahilud ubidi ɔni baalɔ Yehosaƒat mɔɔnu ekposela ala lɛlɔ.

english_verse: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, Dawid úye Israelƒuɔ bammɔ únu ɔnini, “Saul kaba kemmo ubi ɔdi ɔsɔ ɔkya ngba? Na si ɔdi ɔkya ni, mɔɔyɔ́ ka lɛbla-nwu lɛƒɔndia lɛdi ɔkɛnku Yonatan ɔsu.”

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid úye-nwu ɔnini, “Saul kaba kemmo ubi ɔdi ɔsɔ útebu ɔɔɔkya ngba na lɛbla-nwu Katɔti lɛƒɔndia?” Mmɔ na Siba údie kenye ka ukyuli ɔdi ɔkya. Na anwu ndi Meƒiboset ɔni na ɔdi Yonatan ubidi. Nsu ubidi ɔmɛni ɔ́ƒɛ uwi kalɔ.

english_verse: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Dawid úye-nwu ɔnini, “Wɛ na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔkya?” Siba údie kenye ka, “Ɔkya ɔnana ɔdi baalɔ Makir ɔni ɔti ndi Amiel kaduli na ɔma ɔni baalɔ Lo-Debar.”

english_verse: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Ka Yonatan ubidi Meƒiboset úbeduo ni, úbo kalɔ buɛɛ na ɔ́kya Ɔga Dawid lili kalɔ ku ɔbu. Amu na Ɔga Dawid úye-nwu ɔnini, “Awɔ ndi Meƒiboset?” Údie kenye ɔnini, “Ati ami ƒula kabla ɔblane na ɔdi.”

english_verse: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Dawid ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Tayia, ɔsika lɛ́bla kasusu ka lɛbla-a lɛƒɔndia. Na ndubɔnu-ɔ lɛlɔ na ƒ'ɔti Yonatan ɔsu. Na ndubɔsɔku kɔlɔ kɔni ƒui ndi ƒula nana ɔnana Saul kɔdi ƒui lite-ɔ. Na ɔɔɔdi ɔmmɔ lɛti, mmomu adubo butaadiku-mi uwi biala na mina kadikɔ.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
translation_verse: Meƒiboset ɔ́kya lili kalɔ buɛɛ ka únu kenye kamɛni na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ati, ami liiibo lɛla lɛdi kablakɔ. Na nse aani akpewe ɔni na úkpi. Bi ɔsu na eete-mi ɔbu ɔmɛni udu na ákɔliku-mi étésie kenyekɔ kenengudi kamɛni udu.”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Dawid ɔ́ya na bálɔ Siba béte-nwu na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ala ani ƒui na adi Saul ku nwuna kaba kemmo bekyuli adi ni, lɛ́sɔku-nya líte ƒula ati Saul uwɔ.

english_verse: Ziba replied, “Your Majesty, I will do exactly what you tell me to do.” So Ziba's family and servants worked for Mephibosheth. Mephibosheth was lame, but he lived in Jerusalem and ate at David's table, just like one of David's own sons. And he had a young son of his own, named Mica.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Meƒiboset ɔni na ɔdi ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́ƒɛ uwi kalɔ na ulákana busie anwu ɔlati ni, ɔ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́kya Yerusalem na Dawid kesii, ɔsika mmɔ na ɔɔdi nwuna adila biala.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na baga bani nkya Ɔga Hadadeser kalɔ bánu kalɛ na Israelƒuɔ békpo bádi-ma lɛlɔ ni, báblaku Israelƒuɔ unwi na béti lɛlɔ bákya-ma kalɔ. Anwuɔsu liƒu lɛ́da Siriaƒuɔ na básu ka basɔ belete Amonƒuɔ kebunku kadi.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
translation_verse: Ka Dawid únu-nwu kukpi ni, ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ndubɔbla lɛla lɛbuni lɛdi lite Hanun. Ɔsika lɛni kani na ɔti Nahas ɔ́bla-mi lɛƒɔndia.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Dawid ɔ́tala nwuna bekyuli badi ka batásia Hanun kɔnu na ɔti kukpi ɔsu. Ka Dawid bekyuli bétéduo Amon kalɔ lɛlɔ ni,

english_verse: But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.”
translation_verse: básu-ma Dawid kenye kani na badanku. Nsu ka báwɔlɔ ni, Ɔga Hanun benengu bammɔ básu bana ɔga banini, “Aabu anii Ɔga Dawid ɔɔbu-ɔ na ɔɔyɔ́-ɔ ka ɔ́tala bekyuli bamɛni ɔnii babasia-a kɔnu ka ƒ'ɔti úkpi ɔsu? Alati ka bɔtala na Dawid ɔ́tala-ma aani batu na babasia bula ɔma ɔmmɔ anu kaduɛ na bebekpoku-bu na badi-bu lɛlɔ?”

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Hanun ɔ́ya na béƒie-ma na békpeyi ɔdi biala ukwi kakɛ kenwi. Lɛni kani na ɔ́ya na nwuna bekpone békulo lɛwu gyɔlɔɔ lɛni bakya mmɔ kalɔ bédie ɔ́si kavobi. Ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́ya na bédie-ma ulu na bátɔlɔ bésie bana ɔma.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Ka ala ani nálɛ mmɔ litemi líbedu Dawid kudɔ ni, ɔ́tala batu badi na bátásiaku bekyuli bani na bábla kalala bákya-ma kɔƒa geen mmɔ na ulu lɛlɔ ɔnii batásu-ma ka ɔga ɔnini, “Bɛsɔ bɛkya Yeriko útédu ka bina likwi lɛ́sɔ lɛ́kwɛ linwini. Na ɔmmɔ kama na binwini bibo.”

english_verse: The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Amonƒuɔ bánu báti ka Dawid ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi geen na lɛla lɛni na bábla nwuna batu ɔsu ni, bésie na bétévo Siriaƒuɔ bekpone mpim aavlanyɔ básiku Bet-Rehob ku Soba lɛma kemmo na básɔ bévo apim unwi básiku Maaka ɔga kudɔ na bévo mpim leevu-inyɔ básiku Tob lɛnɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu binye momoomo na bise kayi na bukpo bula bekisine na bula kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ ɔsu. Na bukpo na bɔƒɔ bula lɛma lɛni na Unwoti úte-bu ka bulie-ni kemmo buse. Unwoti ɔbla lɛla lɛni na anwu ɔlati ɔ́nu ka lɛdia.”

english_verse: David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
translation_verse: Ka Dawid únu ɔmɛni ni, ɔ́ya na nwuna bekpone ɔtɔnkune Yoab ɔ́tɔnku bekpone bammɔ ƒui ɔnii betékpoku-ma.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
translation_verse: Amonƒuɔ bekpone bésie bási bana ɔma unengudi kemmo bálɛ bébo na bekpone udu kenye bébenye ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔban kayakun na báklibi lɛlɔ béte kekpo kammɔ. Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Siriaƒuɔ bekpone bani na bási Soba ku Rehob ku Tob ku Maaka lɛnɔ bálɛ bénye ɔma ɔmmɔ kɔƒɛlɛ egyu egyu.

english_verse: Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Yoab ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka bekisine bammɔ baayɔ́ ka beyu-ma batu na bekpoku-ma ɔ́si anumi ku kama. Anwuɔsu ɔ́ƒuna bekpone babuni ɔnii ama batuaku Siriaƒuɔ bekpone.

english_verse: He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Na bakladi ni, Yoab ɔ́ya na ɔnwani Abisai ɔ́tɔnku-ma ɔnii ama bekpoku Amonƒuɔ.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Na Yoab ɔ́su Abisai ɔnini, “Si ánu ka Siriaƒuɔ baayɔ́ ka bayu ɔkplu betulo ami ku mina bekpone ni, na bibo bibekpo bɛƒɔ-bu. Na si Amonƒuɔ lɛnɔ mɔɔdi-mii lɛlɔ lɛnɔ ni, ami ku mina bekpone bɔdubo na bubekpo bɔƒɔ-mii.

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yoab ku nwuna bekpone bésie anumi na bénye ka bekpoku Siriaƒuɔ, nsu usi na bekisine bammɔ bakɛ békeli bátɔlɔ.

english_verse: When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na ka Amonƒuɔ bánu ka Siriaƒuɔ békeli bátɔlɔ ni, ama lɛnɔ békeli bétéduo bana ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo. Anwuɔsu Yoab ku nwuna bekpone ƒui bénwini bésie Yerusalem.

english_verse: The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ka Siriaƒuɔ bánu ka Israelƒuɔ bádi-ma lɛlɔ ni, básɔ bálɔ lɛlɔ básala.

english_verse: Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Hadadeser ɔ́tala na básɔ bátálɔ Siriaƒuɔ bekpone bamba bani nási ketu ɔvi. Na Hadadeser bekpone ɔtɔnkune ɔni baalɔ Sobak ɔ́kpanku bekpone bammɔ úsienku ɔma ɔni baalɔ Helam kemmo.

english_verse: David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them.
translation_verse: Litemi lɛmɛni lɛnɔ líbeduo Dawid kɔtu. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́sala Israelƒuɔ bekpone ƒui. Na bávia Yordan Ketu bésie Helam ɔma ɔmmɔ. Siriaƒuɔ lɛnɔ bátu akpagya na bekpo Dawid ku nwuna bekpone.

english_verse: It was now spring, the time when kings go to war. David sent out the whole Israelite army under the command of Joab and his officers. They destroyed the Ammonite army and surrounded the capital city of Rabbah, but David stayed in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛkwa kalɔ kesekɔ, uwi ɔni na baga baata teekpoku lɛlɔ ni, Dawid úti Yoab ku ɔga bekpone batɔnkune ku Israel bekpone bammɔ ƒui úmene ka betékpoku Amonƒuɔ. Bésie na bátádi Amonƒuɔ lɛlɔ na báka ɔma ɔni baalɔ Raba bákya. Nsu Dawid ɔlati anwu útesie kekpokɔ, mmomu ɔ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́kya kama na Yerusalem.

english_verse: he may get angry and ask, “Why did you go so near the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot arrows from the wall?
translation_verse: ɔƒɛni kalɛ ɔga ɔdubɔkɛ kɔnyi geen na uye-ɔ ɔnii, ‘Bi ɔsu na bɛ́ni bíde ɔma ɔmmɔ suɛlɛ suɛlɛ lɛni bɛnii bitékpo? Bɛɛɛgyi bɛnii badubo atula buteebo taalɛ-mii ɔ́si awodu bonwu ani náka ámana ɔma ɔmmɔ eli?

english_verse: But later, when she found out that she was going to have a baby, she sent someone to David with this message: “I'm pregnant!”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔdi kama ni, uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́nu ka kɔbuli kɔ́vi-nwu. Anwuɔsu ɔ́tala ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́kya Dawid ɔnii utásu-nwu ka kɔbuli kɔ́vi-nwu.

english_verse: David sent a message to Joab: “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.” Joab sent Uriah
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Dawid ɔ́tala ukyuli ɔ́kya nwuna bekpone unengu Yoab ɔnii ɔya na Uria Hitini ɔmmɔ ubo ubanu-nwu kɔnakunwi. Anwuɔsu Yoab lɛnɔ úti-nwu úmene-nwu.

english_verse: to David's palace, and David asked him, “Is Joab well? How is the army doing? And how about the war?”
translation_verse: Ka Uria úbeduo Dawid kudɔ ni, úye-nwu kalɛ na Yoab ɔkya ku kalɛ na bekpone bakladi ku kekpo kammɔ ƒui kese.

english_verse: Then David told Uriah, “Go home and clean up.” Uriah left the king's palace, and David had dinner sent to Uriah's house.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Dawid ɔ́su Uria ɔnini, “Teesie ƒula kesii na atáƒɔ lɛlɔ ku anumi na anwuna.” Anwuɔsu Uria ɔ́vi ɔ́lɛ Dawid kaduli mmɔ. Na Dawid úti etela úmene ɔnii beti besienku-nwu kaduli.

english_verse: But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside the entrance to the royal palace, where the king's guards slept.
translation_verse: Nsu Uria útesie kaduli, mmomu ɔ́tɛ Dawid kaduli kayakun kenye ku Dawid kabla bablane bakladi.

english_verse: Someone told David that Uriah had not gone home. So the next morning David asked him, “Why didn't you go home? Haven't you been away for a long time?”
translation_verse: Ka básu Dawid ka Uria útesie nwuna kaduli ni, úye Uria ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na étesie na atákya lɛlɔ ebiti adi ka átɔlɔ na uwi útu lɛni?”

english_verse: Uriah answered, “The sacred chest and the armies of Israel and Judah are camping out somewhere in the fields with our commander Joab and his officers and troops. Do you really think I would go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? I swear by your life that I would not!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Uria údie kenye ɔnini, “Dɛ na ndubɔkana lɛmmɔ udu bɔbla. Israelƒuɔ ƒui ku Yudaƒuɔ benye kekpo. Na nvo kemmo na baatɛ. Na Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔkya-ma kudɔ mmɔ. Mina unengu Yoab ku nwuna bebunkune lɛnɔ kɔyɔ lɛlɔ na baatɛ na baaakya lɛma kemmo muedi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ami lɛnɔ naaakana kaduli busie na ntádi na lɛni na ami ku mina uleku lɛnɔ bɔtɛ. Uwi ɔni na eli ngba mɛni ni, lɛɛɛdubo ɔmmɔ udu bɔkana bɔbla!”

english_verse: Then David said, “Stay here in Jerusalem today, and I will send you back tomorrow.” Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day. Then the next day,
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid ɔ́su Uria ɔnini, “Sɔ kya Yerusalem mɛni ɔmwi na kɔnaadi na lɛsɔku-ɔ limene kekpokɔ.” Anwuɔsu Uria ɔ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́kya Yerusalem limeyi lɛmmɔ ku nwuna kadi kegye.

english_verse: David invited him for dinner. Uriah ate with David, who gave him so much to drink that he got drunk. But Uriah still did not go home. He went out and slept on his mat near the palace guards.
translation_verse: Dawid ɔ́lɔ-nwu ka ubadiku-nwu. Na ɔ́ya na ɔ́di na ɔ́ni ntɛ lɛnɔ na úkpi-mu. Nsu useyi ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ni, Uria úni na útesie kaduli útatátɛ. Mmomu ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tɛ kesii kani na ɔ́tɛ kudeedi mmɔ ku Dawid kabla bablane bammɔ.

english_verse: Early the next morning, David wrote a letter and told Uriah to deliver it to Joab.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ka kadi kégye ɔtanta ni, Dawid unweni ɔku ɔdi ute Yoab na úti ɔ́siaku Uria ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The letter said: “Put Uriah on the front line where the fighting is the worst. Then pull the troops back from him, so that he will be wounded and die.”
translation_verse: Na ɔku ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, únweni ɔnini, “Ti Uria mene kesii kani na kekpo kammɔ kebo ɔkplu geen. Na aya na bekpone bakladi bebo kama na bada anwu lɛti bakya anumi kakɛ, na bekisine bammɔ betulo-nwu na badu-nwu.”

english_verse: Joab had been carefully watching the city of Rabbah, and he put Uriah in a place where he knew there were some of the enemy's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Amu ka Yoab ku nwuna bekpone benengu bánu ka báka bana bekisine ɔma ɔdi bákya ni, Yoab ɔ́ya na Uria ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie kesii kani na kekpo kammɔ kaabi kenye geen.

english_verse: When the men of the city came out, they fought and killed some of David's soldiers—Uriah the Hittite was one of them.
translation_verse: Bekisine bekpone bammɔ báta ku lisu bábasiaku Yoab ku nwuna badi na bádu Dawid bekpone badi. Na bani na bádu mmɔ akɔ unwi ndi Uria Hitini ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Joab sent a messenger to tell David everything that was happening in the war.
translation_verse: Amu na Yoab ɔ́tala ɔtu ɔ́kya Dawid na útásu-nwu ala ani ƒui nálɛ na kekpokɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: He gave the messenger these orders: When you finish telling the king everything that has happened,
translation_verse: Na Yoab úbo ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔda ɔnini, “Si ásu Dawid kekpo kammɔ ala ani nálɛ áwɔlɔ ni,

english_verse: Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?” Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Munuu bítenyimo ukyuli ɔni nádu Yerubeset ubidi Abimelek na kekpo kani návi kemmo? Binyimo ka uleku na ɔdi. Na kukɔ na ɔ́yula ɔ́si kowodu lili na kúbayu-nwu lili na úkpi na Tebes mmɔ. Na ɔlɛka nka bɛtɛya lɛnunda bɛsiku ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na biláni biléde kowodu kɔmmɔ lɛni.’ ” Yoab ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Si Dawid ɔ́su-ɔ lɛni na ƒula kenye budie na kekpo kammɔ lɛlɔ kama ni, na eti kenye kamɛni lɛnɔ ebunku ka Hitini ukpone ɔni ndi Uria lɛnɔ úkpi na mmɔ.”

english_verse: The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him.
translation_verse: Yoab ɔtu ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ úsie Yerusalem útásu Dawid kenye kammɔ ƒui lɛni kani.

english_verse: He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate.
translation_verse: Na ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́su Dawid ɔnini, “Bekisine bammɔ báyu ɔkplu bétulo-bu na bálɛ bási ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na békpoku-bu na kalɔ kani na kewi ƒiaa mmɔ. Nsu búnye momoomo na bɔ́bɔku-ma bɔ́sɔku búsienku ɔma ɔmmɔ ɔban kayakun kenye.

english_verse: Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, bana bekpone bammɔ badi bébo bana atula bálɛ bula badi ɔ́si awodu ammɔ lili na ƒula bekpone badi békpi. Na ɔɔɔdi ɔmmɔ lɛti mmomu ƒula Hitini ukpone ɔni ndi Uria lɛnɔ úkpi.”

english_verse: David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid ɔ́su ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Sie na atásu Yoab anini, ‘Sɔ tekpoku lɛlɔ lɛni, ɔsika na kekpokɔ ni, ukyuli ɔdi kani muukpi.’ Na asu-nwu ka enu ataƒɛ-nwu, mmomu unye kpakplaa na bikpo na bɛdi bekisine bammɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
translation_verse: Na ka Bat-Seba únu ka ɔgyani úkpi ni, úwulo-nwu aani ukpinele kalɛ.

english_verse: Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son. The Lord's Message for David The Lord was angry because of what David had done,
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́bla ukpinele ala ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, Dawid ɔ́ya na bátákpanku-nwu béboku nwuna kaduli. Na úti-nwu únwini ulekudi na ɔ́wɔ ubi ɔnanabi úte-nwu. Nsu Dawid ɔbladu ɔmɛni ƒui útayɔ Unwoti kaƒɔ.

english_verse: The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle,
translation_verse: Na ɔlakɛne ɔmɛni ubo baƒonu ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ, na bemomo geen.

english_verse: One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
translation_verse: “Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo kani ni, ulusiene ɔdi úbeduo ɔlakɛne ɔmmɔ. Nsu ɔlakɛne ɔmmɔ úni na úteƒie koƒonu kɔdi iye ɔmantɛ akɔ na nwuna bebuo akɔ na uti ɔbla nwuna ulusiene ɔmmɔ lɛƒɔ. Mmomu úsie útéƒie ɔwabane ɔmmɔ koƒonu kuledi kunwi kɔni na ubo, na úti ɔ́nwa úte nwuna ɔƒɔ ɔmmɔ.”

english_verse: David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die!
translation_verse: Litemi lɛmɛni lɛ́ya na Dawid ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi geen na ɔlakɛne ɔmmɔ ɔbladu ɔmmɔ ɔsu. Mmɔ na ɔ́su Natan ɔnini, “Ɔkɛnku Unwoti ɔni nli ngba uwi ƒui lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka ukyuli ɔni nábla lɛla lɛmmɔ ukpi!

english_verse: And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
translation_verse: Na ɔlɛka ɔƒɔ koƒonu kɔni na úƒie mmɔ kayu akpa ene. Ɔsika ɔ́bla ulikplu na útanu kɔnyana.”

english_verse: Then Nathan told David: You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul
translation_verse: Amu na Natan ɔ́su Dawid ɔnini, “Awɔ ndi ukyuli ɔni nábla lɛla lɛmmɔ! Ɔƒɛni teenu. Unwoti Israel Katɔti ɔnini, ‘Líwi-ɔ nnɔmii lili na líse-ɔ lɛga ka ataadi Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ. Na lídie-ɔ na Saul enu kemmo.

english_verse: and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more.
translation_verse: Líti ƒula ɔtɔlati kaduli líte-ɔ. Na nwuna beleku lɛnɔ bakya-a enu kemmo. Israel ku Yuda kaba kemmo bebi ƒui awɔ mɔɔdi-ma lɛlɔ. Na si ala amɛni ƒui átabɔ-ɔ ni, lɛkana na liti abambadi libunku-nya lite-ɔ.

english_verse: Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
translation_verse: Bi ɔsu na átadi Unwoti litemi lɛlɔ na ábla likpidi na nwuna anumi? Awɔ nádu Uria Hitini ku kewii na áƒɔ ulekudi énwini awɔ ɔdi. Ɔkɛnku awɔ ɔsu na Amonƒuɔ bádu-nwu ku kewii.

english_verse: “Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace.
translation_verse: Na ɔƒɛni ni, ka éni na átadi mina litemi lɛlɔ mmomu éƒie Uria ulekudi áƒɔ éti ɔsu ni, kekpo kaaadubo bɔsa ƒula kaduli kudii.’

english_verse: Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on.
translation_verse: “Na asɔ enu lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su. Ɔnini, ‘Awɔ ɔlati ƒula kaduli ubi na ndubɔya na ɔgbankpi ubo-ɔ lɛlɔ. Na ndubɔya na enye ataanu nwaa asa na liti ƒula beleku lite ƒula kaduli ukyuli ɔni mma-a lɛlɔ geen. Na anwu ku-ma badubo bɔtɛ ɔƒiiwi.

english_verse: What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
translation_verse: Lɛla lɛni na awɔ ábla ni, ábla-ni na bɔbɛ kemmo. Nsu ami ndubɔya na babla-a lɛla lɛmmɔ ɔƒiiwi nwaa na Israel kadi ƒui anumi.’ ”

english_verse: David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.” “Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.”
translation_verse: Nsu ka lɛla lɛni na ábla ɔsu áya na Unwoti bekisine baasu ala teewi-nwu lɛlɔ na basɔ balánu-nwu taabu ɔsu ni, ubi ɔni na báwɔ béte-ɔ mmɔ ɔdubo bukpi.”

english_verse: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Natan ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie kaduli na Katɔti ɔ́ya na ɔlɛ kpakplaa úbo ubi ɔni na Uria ulekudi ɔ́wɔ úte Dawid mmɔ.

english_verse: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
translation_verse: Dawid úvele Katɔti na ubi ɔmmɔ lili. Únyimi kenye na ɔ́kalɛ lɛlɔ ɔ́kya ɔtɔ, na kalɔkplu kani na ɔɔtɛ usien biala.

english_verse: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
translation_verse: Na benengu bani nkya-nwu kaduli bénye-nwu lɛlɔ ka nka ɔta na ubadi lɛla lɛdi, nsu úni ɔnii ulata na wakya lɛla lɛdi lɛnɔ kenye.

english_verse: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
translation_verse: Na limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, ubi ɔmmɔ úbekpi. Nsu Dawid kabla bablane baayia ka basu-nwu ka ubi ɔmmɔ úkpi. Ɔsika bákali na básu banini, “Uwi ɔni na ubi ɔmmɔ ɔtɛ na útekpi tɔ ni, bɔ́su Dawid lɛla biala, nsu útakpete-bu. Dɛ na bɔdubo-nwu bɔsu ɔƒɛni bɔnii ubidi úkpi na utéti lɛla lɛdi ɔbla lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ka badaku ɔmɛni ni, Dawid únu-ma kabɛnsɛ na ɔ́ti ka ubi ɔmmɔ úkpi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu úye-ma ɔnini, “Bukpi na ubi ɔmmɔ úkpi?” Amu na bédie kenye banini, “Ɛɛn ubi ɔmmɔ úkpi.”

english_verse: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
translation_verse: Dawid kabla bablane béye-nwu banini, “Bi ɔsu na aabla lɛla lɛmɛni udu? Uwi ɔni na ƒ'ubidi ɔkya ni, ényimi kenye na éwulo kɔnyana geen. Na ɔƒɛni ka ubi ɔmmɔ úkpi ni, áta na eli aadi!”

english_verse: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Dawid údie kenye ɔnini, “Uwi ɔni na ubi ɔmmɔ uli ngba ni, línyimi kenye na líwulo kɔnyana. Na mina kasusu ndi ka ukyuli ɔdi ɔɔɔgyi lɛla, ɔƒɛni kalɛ Unwoti ɔdubɔnu-mi kɔnyana na ɔya na ubi ɔmmɔ ɔnwanya na ɔsɔ ulekpi.

english_verse: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
translation_verse: Nsu ka útebo-nwu kemmo lɛni na bukpi na úkpi ni, bi ɔsu na ɔlɛka lɛsɔ nteenyimi kenye lɛnɔ? Bɔkana na ndubɔkana na lɛsɔku-nwu liboku ngba? Ami kani ndubo bukpi na lisie-nwu kudɔ na anwu ɔsɔ ulénwini ulebo-mi kudɔ.”

english_verse: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Dawid ɔ́sia ulekudi Bat-Seba kɔnu. Na anwu ku-nwu básɔ bátɛ na báwɔ ubi bamba na básia-nwu lɛnyi banii Salomo. Na ubi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ lɛ́da Unwoti ebiti.

english_verse: and sent Nathan the prophet to tell David, “The Lord will call him Jedidiah.” The End of the War with Ammon (
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛ ɔmmɔ ɔsu Unwoti ɔ́tala nwuna Kenye Udiene Natan ɔnii utásia-nwu lɛnyi ɔnii Yedidia na nwuna kalɔ ndi Unwoti ɔɔyɔ́-nwu.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Yoab úkpoku Amonƒuɔ na bana ɔma unengudi ɔni baalɔ Raba kemmo na úƒie bana ɔga lɛgbanya lɛni na ɔ́tu ɔ́mana ɔ́ƒɔ.

english_verse: and sent a messenger to tell David: I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply.
translation_verse: Na ɔtala batu ɔ́kya Dawid ɔnii batásu-nwu banini, “Líkpoku Raba ɔma bekyuli na líƒie bana ketu kani na beedú ntu lɛ́ƒɔ-ma kudɔ.

english_verse: Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu sala bekpone bakladi na beyu ɔma ɔmmɔ batu na bikpoku-ma na bɛƒɔ ɔma ɔmmɔ. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, ndubukpo lɛƒɔ ɔma ɔmmɔ na liti mina lɛnyi lɛsia mmɔ.”

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Dawid ɔ́sala bekpone bammɔ ƒui na báyu ulu bésie Raba bétékpoku-ma na béƒie ɔma ɔmmɔ báƒɔ.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: Únye bani ƒui na kekpo kéƒie mmɔ lɛlɔ, na útákya-ma kɔdadi ku anwami ku atumala bamba enu, na beekúlo atimbɔ. Na lɛni kani na ɔ́bla na Amonƒuɔ lɛma bamba kemmo ƒui lɛnɔ. Ɔmmɔ kama Dawid ku nwuna bekpone bammɔ bénwini bésie Yerusalem.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔdi kama ni, Dawid ubidi Amnon úbo ɔɔyɔ́ ɔnwani ulekubi ɔni baalɔ Tamar geen, na ɔdi Dawid ubidi Absalom ɔnwani ulekubi ɔni mɔɔdia bɔnu geen.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Amnon ɔɔyɔ́ ɔnwani Tamar geen ɔni na únwini-nwu ɔlɛ muedi na kuƒi kɔni na ɔɔwia-nwu lɛlɔ ɔsu. Ɔsika adagyaa na ɔdi na ɔɔbla Amnon aani ka kuƒi kɔdi kɔɔɔdubo bɔlɛmi bute-nwu na anwu ku-nwu batɛ.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ Amnon ubo ɔkpana ɔdi na baalɔ-nwu Yonadab ɔni ndi ɔnana ɔni baalɔ Simea ubidi. Simea ɔmɛni ɔdi Dawid ɔnwani. Yonadab ɔdi ukyuli ɔni na ubo lɛkwɛ geen.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Yonadab ɔmɛni úye Amnon ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na awɔ ɔga ubi ƒula anumi aatina aani lɛla lɛdi muukpóku-ɔ ɔtanta ndi ɔtanta si áta na uládia-a na asu-mi?” Mmɔ na Amnon údie kenye ɔnini, “Mɔɔyɔ́ Tamar mina ɔnwani Absalom ɔnwani ulekubi geen.”

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Amu na nwuna ɔkpana Yonadab ɔ́kya-nwu kasusu ɔnini, “Teesie na atátɛ kpoo aani si buƒi na ada. Na si ƒ'ɔti úbo ubegyele-ɔ ni, na asu-nwu anini, ‘Mɔɔwia ka mina ɔnwani ulekubi Tamar ubawia lɛla lɛdi ute-mi na lɛdi. Anwuɔsu ya na ubo ubanwa adila ammɔ na mina anumi na ntaanu-nwu na anwu kani ɔkya-mi adila ammɔ ku nwuna kɔnu.’ ”

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Amnon úsie útátɛ na ɔ́nyi ɔkɔ ɔnii buƒi na ɔda. Na ka ɔti úbo ɔnii ubanu-nwu ni, Amnon ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Mɔɔwia ka mina ɔnwani ulekubi Tamar ubo na ubabla bodobodo sɛsɛɛ ɔdi ute-mi na mina anumi na anwu kani ɔkya-mi na lɛdi lɛsiku nwuna kɔnu kemmo.”

english_verse: David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.”
translation_verse: Ka Dawid ɔ́tɔlɔ ni, ɔ́ya na bátálɔ Tamar na ɔga kesii mmɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Teesie ƒ'ɔnwani Amnon kesii na atánwa lɛla lɛdi ete-nwu.”

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Tamar lɛnɔ ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie ɔnwani Amnon ɔni ntɛ mmɔ kesii na útéti bodobodo ɔlaaƒɔ ɔdi na ɔ́nwu na úbo-nwu ƒui na nwuna anumi na úƒi-nwu.

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama úti bodobodo ɔmmɔ ɔ́kya lɛkyami kemmo útése-nwu, nsu ɔnii uladi. Mmɔ na Amnon ɔsu-nwu ɔnini, “Gya ukyuli biala lɛku mɛni!” Anwuɔsu bana ƒui bávi bálɛ.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Amu na Amnon ɔ́su Tamar ɔnii, “Ti adila ammɔ boku-mi na mina ɔtɔ ɔtɛdi kemmo mɛni na awɔ ɔlati akya-mi na lɛdi.” Na Tamar lɛnɔ úti bodobodo ɔni na úƒi mmɔ na úduo-nwu kudɔ na ɔtɔ ɔtɛdi mmɔ.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔni na úti bodobodo ɔmmɔ úte-nwu ka ɔdi ni, anwu kani na úƒie-nwu ɔkplu kemmo na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Mina ɔnwani, bo na ami ku-ɔ bɔtɛ!”

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, ɔnwani ulekubi ɔmɛni ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔnwa, tabla! Tenye-mi lɛlɔ anii bɔɔbla lɛla lɛmɛni udu. Útalɛka bɔbla lɛla lɛmɛni udu na Israel! Tabla likyulikpi lɛla lɛmɛni udu.

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Na si ina dɛ na use-ɔ ni, alabu-mi lɛlɔ alanu anii dɛ na mabla ku kɔƒa litemi lɛmɛni udu. Na awɔ ɔlati nɔɔ? Adubuti lɛlɔ abla aani ukyuli ɔlalane ɔni neeebo kasusu na Israel kadi bekyuli akɔ? Buvele si ina bi na ɔdi ni, ya na bula ɔti ɔni ndi ɔga ɔti. Lɛ́ƒɔ lɛ́di ka uléni na ɔdubɔbla lɛla biala na eti-mi,”

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui ni, ɔnwani Amnon úni kasusu kani na uute-nwu na ɔ́tɛnku-nwu ɔkplu kemmo.

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Tamar lɛlɔ líse kalɔ liiƒí ɔnwani Amnon livo na úti-nwu bukisi mmɔ mmɔ útulo kalɛ na nka útaayɔ-nwu. Na ɔ́bɔku-nwu ɔnini, “Ta na avi alɛ-mi ɔtɔ kemmo!”

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔnwani ulekubi ɔmɛni lɛnɔ úni na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Si ábɔku-mi álɛku mmomu na éti lɛla biala ébile étulo lɛni na ábla.” Nsu ɔmmɔ ƒui ɔnwani útenu útete-nwu.

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: Na Amnon ɔ́lɔ nwuna kabla ɔblane na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ni uleku ɔmɛni lɛku-mi ɔtɔ kemmo na akalɛ ada-nwu.”

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu nwuna kabla ɔblane lɛnɔ ɔ́ni Tamar ɔ́lɛku na ɔ́kalɛ ɔ́da-nwu. Na ɔkya awu buni gyɔlɔɔ ɔdi na bákya-nwu bɔdia kaduɛ. Ɔsika lɛwu lɛmmɔ udu na baga bebi bani ndi belekubi badagyaa baakya.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Tamar úti ntɔ úwi lili na ɔ́ni awu buni ɔni na ɔkya mmɔ ɔ́bwɛ. Na úti enu úwi lili na ɔkɛ uuwulo momoomo ɔ́tɔlɔ.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔwani Absalom únu-nwu kɔku na úbeye-nwu ɔnini, “Ƒ'ɔnwani úbile-ɔ loo? Ba lɛsɛ tebo kudu na bekyuli bati, ɔsika ƒ'ɔnwani na ɔdi. Da lɛla biala die kayi na ayiƒala.” Na Tamar ɔ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́kya ɔnwani Absalom kesii ku kɔnyana.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Nsu Absalom útakpete ɔnwani Amnon na ɔsu-nwu ɔnii ɔ́bla lɛbuni iye ɔ́bla likpidi. Mmomu úti-nwu bukisi kpakplaa ɔ́si kalɛ na úbile ɔnwani ulekubi ɔsu. Absalom Ɔ́du Amnon

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Na akwa anyɔ kama ni, Absalom bebuo lɛlɔ banune bésie betékulo baƒonu linwini na kesii kani baalɔ banii Baal Hasor na ude Eƒraim ɔma ɔmii kudɔ. Na Absalom ɔ́lɔ nwuna banwani bananabi bani ndi Ɔga Dawid bebi banana ƒui ka bebo mmɔ.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Absalom úsie ɔga kudɔ na útásu-nwu ɔnini, “Lɛ́lɔ bebunkune ku mina baƒonu linwini bekulone na béebo bábasa. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu muuvele-ɔ ka awɔ ku ɔga kaduli bekyuli ƒui bibo bibasalaku-bu na mmɔ.”

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga údie kenye ɔnini, “Oowo! Ubi, bula ƒui bulakana bubo lɛni. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni bubenwini etila bɔsia-a lɛlɔ.” Ina ka Absalom únye-nwu lɛlɔ laa muedi ni, útenuku-nwu kalɔ. Mmomu úte-nwu nwuna kusɛ kusɛ ka ɔsiaku-nwu.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Ka ɔ́su-nwu lɛni ni, Absalom úvele ɔti ɔnini, “Si bina ƒui bilebo ni, ya na mina ɔnwani Amnon anwu ubo.” Mmɔ ni, ɔga úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na aawia ka ƒ'ɔnwani Amnon ubo mmɔ?”

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Nsu Absalom únye-nwu lɛlɔ laa na únu kalɔ ka Amnon ku baga bebi bakladi basiaku-nwu.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Absalom úsie útébo nwuna kabla bablane ɔda na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Binu kaduɛ! Si uwi ɔni na bɛ́nu ka Amnon ɔ́ni ntɛ úkpi na bɔdaku-nwu bɔda ni, ndubo-mii bɔsu nnii, ‘Bibo Amnon bɛva kalɔ.’ Na mmɔ ni, bɛdu-nwu. Na bitayia. Ami nébo-mii ɔda lɛni. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bise kayi na bɛdi lɛnanabi.”

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Absalom kabla bablane bádu Amnon kalɛ na Absalom ubo-ma ɔda. Ɔmmɔ kama ɔga bebi bakladi báta na bákɔ bélie bana bebuo ala betine lɛlɔ na békeli bátɔlɔ.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Amu uwi ɔni na bakɛ ulu ni, kenye kéesie kétédu Dawid kukuuku ka banini, “Absalom ɔ́du ɔga bebi bammɔ ƒui na unwi pɛ muedi útebu.”

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔga ɔ́ta únye na ɔ́ni nwuna awu ɔ́bwɛ na ɔ́yu úwi kalɔ. Lɛni kani na nwuna kabla bablane lɛnɔ báni bana lɛwu babwɛ na benye-nwu kudɔ ku kɔnyana.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Nsu Dawid ɔnwani Simea ubidi Yonadab úbo na úbasu ɔnini, “Mina Ati, takali anii badu-ɔ bebi bammɔ ƒui. Mmomu Amnon kani nékpi. Na kasusu kamɛni nákya Absalom lili kemmo ɔ́si uwi ɔni na Amnon úbile Tamar na ɔ́kya útaatu-nwu uwi biala.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: Ati, mina ɔga, taya na kayi kekpoku-ɔ na kenye kani na énu ka ƒula bebi ƒui békpi. Mmomu Amnon kani nékpi.”

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na badaku ɔmɛni ni, Absalom úukeli. Ɔƒɛni ɔgyumanane ɔni nnye ɔga kaduli mɔɔgyumana ni, ɔ́nu úmene na ɔ́nu bekyuli lisu bonwu lɛdi ka bási kɔbi kɔmadɔ baayu na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ. Mmɔ na úsie útásu ɔga ɔnini, “Lɛ́nu bekyuli límene Horonaim ɔma kakɛ na abi lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yonadab ɔ́su ɔga ɔnini, “Aanu ɔga bebi bammɔ náada bábalɛ. Lɛla lɛni tutuutu na ami ƒula kabla ɔblane lɛ́su.”

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: Ka ɔ́wɔlɔ bɔtɛmi kani na baga bebi bammɔ béduo kaduli ku keku momoomo. Lɛni kani na ɔga ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ƒui beewulo geen na kalɛ na lɛla lɛmmɔ liikpóku-ma ɔsu.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ka Amnon kukpi kɔmmɔ kayi kábla Dawid buɛɛ kama ƒui ni, nwuna kayi kásɔ kénwini kásia Absalom lɛlɔ ɔni na ɔɔwia geen ka ɔnu-nwu.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Seruia ubidi Yoab ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka Ɔga Dawid kayi kasia Absalom lɛlɔ na ɔɔwia-nwu ɔnu.

english_verse: and he sent someone to bring in the wise woman who lived in Tekoa. Joab told her, “Put on funeral clothes and don't use any makeup. Go to the king and pretend you have spent a long time mourning the death of a loved one.” Then he told her what to say.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama na esie Ɔga Dawid kudɔ na atásɔku ala ani ƒui na masu makya-a kenye asu-nwu.” Na Yoab ɔ́su-nwu lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka utásu Ɔga Dawid ɔ́kya-nwu kenye.

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ndi lɛla lɛni muukpóku-ɔ lɛni?” Mmɔ na uleku ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Geen geen ni, mina ɔgyani úkpi, anwuɔsu ukpinele na ndi.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: Na ami ƒula kabla ɔblane mbo bebi inyɔ. Na kadɔ kébeduo bana inyɔ ntɛ na alakpi akɔ na únwini ka békpo. Ɔƒɛni ka ukyuli ɔdi uuubo mmɔ na ɔda kadɔ kammɔ iye ugyingya-ma ntɛ ɔsu ni, unwi úbo ɔkladi ɔ́du.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu kɔdua kɔmmɔ bekyuli ƒui báta bénye-mi lɛlɔ banii nnyonu mina ubi unwi pɛ ɔmmɔ nte na badu anwu lɛnɔ. Ɔsika kalɛ na úbile ɔnwani ngba ni, lɛni kani na ɔlɛka badu anwu lɛnɔ. Na anwu kani nébu na ɔdi bula ala ɔdine. Na si lɛ́nyonu-nwu líte-ma ni, ami ɔdi ɔ́sa. Lɛgyabi linwi pɛ lɛni nébu-mi asi kemmo na badubo bunine mmɔ. Na mina ɔgyani lɛnyi lɛyii na uledie kaba kadi ulése na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su uleku ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Teesie ƒula kaduli na ndubɔkɛ lɛla lɛdi lɛsu bekyuli bammɔ lite-ɔ.”

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Tekoani uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́su Ɔga Dawid ɔnini, “O Ati, mina ɔga, ya na likpidi lɛmmɔ lɛsia ami ku mina ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli lɛlɔ. Na ɔɔɔdanku ɔga iye nwuna lɛgadi lɛmmɔ.”

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ukyuli biala meye-ɔ lɛla lɛdi wasiku litemi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, na akpanku-nwu eboku-mi na ɔsɔ uleboku litemi lɛmmɔ ƒula kudɔ kudii.”

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bula ɔga, vele Unwoti na ukyuli ɔni mɔɔwia udie kasi na ubugya ɔni na béwi kalɔ lili ɔsu na ulésie anumi ulebile ala ulebu si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, badubɔdu mina ubi lɛnɔ.” Mmɔ kani na ɔga údie kenye ɔnini, “Na uwi ɔni na Unwoti uli ngba mɛni ni, ƒ'ubidi lili linwini ina linwi muedi belékulo-ni baláva kalɔ.”

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na uleku ɔmɛni úsie anumi ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na éti lɛla lɛmɛni udu kasusu ásiku Katɔti bekyuli lɛlɔ? Ɔsika kenye kani na aasu mɛni ɔƒɛni ni, ɔɔtina ka awɔ bula ɔga áƒiɔ ka átaya na bekyuli bani na ágya álɛku ɔma basɔ benwini bebo ɔsu.

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Na geen ni, bɔdubo bukpi, ɔsika buse aani ntu bɔni néwiakun na basɔ balakana-mu bɔkpala. Nsu Katɔti anwu uláda ukyuli ngba teedie lɛni, mmomu ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́gya na nwuna anumi ni, uléti-nwu teebo teevaakun ƒui.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: “Na lɛla lɛni ɔsu na líbo ḿbasu-ɔ kenye kamɛni ni, mina Unwoti ɔga, ani ndi ka bekyuli báya na mɔɔyia geen, anwuɔsu na ami ƒula kabla ɔblane lɛ́bla kasusu ka libo mbasu-ɔ kenye kamɛni na ɔƒɛni kalɛ adubɔbla lɛla lɛni na muuvele-ɔ mɛni ete-mi.

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: Na lɛ́ƒɔ lɛ́di ka adubudie-mi alɛku ukyuli ɔni mɔɔwia ka ɔdu ami ku mina ubi na bɔyii udu na Israel kaba ƒui akɔ.

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: “Lɛ́su lɛlɔ na mina kakali kemmo nnini, ‘Kuli kɔdia na linu lɛla lɛni mɔɔyu kayi buɛɛ lɛsiku ɔga kudɔ, ɔsika kalɛ na Katɔti batu bese ni, lɛni kani na mina ɔga use ute-mi. Na ɔdubɔnu likpidi ku lɛbuni kavumana ɔti na ɔƒuna lɛbuni. Na muuvele nnii Unwoti ɔni ndi ƒula Katɔti ulieku-ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Ɔga Dawid údie kenye na ɔ́su uleku ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Buvele, lɛla biala na meye-ɔ ni, teti ɔdi tabɛla-mi.” Amu na uleku ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔ́su Ɔga Dawid ɔnini, “Buvele, mina unwoti ɔga, awɔ su lɛla lɛni nkya-a.”

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Dawid úye-nwu ɔnini, “Ala ani ƒui na áka mɛni ni, Yoab kɔnu kɔkya-nya kemmo?” Mmɔ na uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́ƒɔ enu ɔnini, “Mina ati ku ɔga, uwi ɔni na eli ngba mɛni ni, ukyuli ɔdi ulakana na wedeyi ku ƒula litemi lɛni na éye-mi mɛni busienku kɔmii iye kɔdianu. Sɔsɔ na ɔdi ka ƒula kabla ɔblane Yoab násu etemila amɛni ƒui ɔ́kya ami, ƒula kabla ɔblane, kenye ka mbasu.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: Na Yoab ɔ́bla lɛni ka ɔɔyɔ́ ka kalɛ na ala ese ɔƒaani ni, avumana ɔsu. Nsu awɔ áda anu geen aani Katɔti batu kalɛ, na aanu ala ƒui taati na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ!”

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su Yoab ɔnini, “Nu! Ɔƒaani ni, ndubɔbla bɔsia lɛla lɛni na ásu-mi lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu teesie na atákpanku okloƒu Absalom eboku.”

english_verse: Joab bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, I thank you for giving your permission. It shows that you approve of me.”
translation_verse: Yoab ɔ́yu úbi kalɔ ka únu lɛni na úte ɔga kusɛ kusɛ ku ɔbu na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔmwi ni, ami ƒula kabla ɔblane lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka mina ala áyɔ-ɔ kaƒɔ, mina Unwoti Ɔga, ka énu kalɔ ka abla lɛla lɛni na lívele-ɔ ɔ́su.”

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yoab ɔ́ta na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Gesur na útákpanku Absalom úboku Yerusalem.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Nsu Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su Yoab ɔnini, “Ya na uteesie nwuna kaduli na utebo-mi kudɔ mɛni na lɛnu-nwu anumi.” Anwuɔsu Absalom ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie nwuna kaduli na anwu ku Ɔga Dawid anumi átasa.

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: Na uwi uwi na uukúlo nwuna lili linwini si uwi ɔni na lɛɛyu-nwu unu taavili. Na si bákɔku-ni ni, nina unu ɔdubɔbla aani antabi akyami anyɔ unu.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Bebi bananabi ɛtɛ na Absalom ɔ́wɔ ku ulekubi unwi ɔni baalɔ banii Tamar na ɔɔdia bɔnu geen.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Akwa anyɔ na Absalom ɔ́kya Yerusalem na útanu Ɔga Dawid kudii.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Absalom ɔ́tala ɔnii batálɔ Yoab bete-nwu na ubakpanku-nwu na besie ɔga kudɔ, nsu útebo. Anwuɔsu Absalom ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tala ukyuli kunyɔdi, nsu Yoab úni na útebo ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su nwuna kabla bablane ɔnini, “Bɛɛnu Yoab kemo ka kewi kede ami kadi lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́kya edula ani nse aani kakpa. Bisie na bitátu ogya bɛkya-ka.” Na Absalom kabla bablane lɛnɔ bákya-ka ogya.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yoab ɔ́ta kɔnakunwi na úbeye Absalom ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na ƒula kabla bablane bákya-mi kemo ogya?”

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Amu na Absalom údie kenye ɔnini, “Nu, lɛ́tala nnii babalɔ-ɔ na etéye ɔga lɛla lɛni ɔsu na lɛ́si Gesur líbo mɛni. Na si mmɔ na lɛ́sɔ nkya muedi na nka ɔɔɔdia uuutulo? Anwuɔsu ya na lɛnu ɔga anumi kɔnakunwi, na si lɛ́bla likpidi lɛdi ni, na ɔdu-mi.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yoab úbaya na ɔga ɔ́ti na ɔ́ya na bálɔ Absalom béboku. Na ka úbeduo ni, ɔ́yu úbi kalɔ na ɔga anumi mmɔ. Na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́kya Absalom kɔgbu.

english_verse: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔdi kama ni, Absalom ɔ́wia bapɔnkɔ ku bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ɔdi ku bekpone bani muusié lɛgba liti ka bagyu batɔ-nwu anumi.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: Absalom ɔɔyɔ́ bɔta ɔtanta tutuutu teeténye ulu lɛlɔ na ɔma ɔban kayakun kenye. Na si ukyuli ɔdi ɔda litemi lɛdi úselaku ɔga na basu-ni bete-nwu ni, na Absalom ɔkpali ukyuli ɔmmɔ na uye-nwu kesii kani na ɔ́si. Na ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔsu-nwu ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo ubi na ɔdi.

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Absalom uusé ukyuli ɔmmɔ kayi ka nwuna litemi libo ubo, nsu ɔga uuubo ukyuli ɔni mebunku-nwu litemi lɛmmɔ kasusu buti.

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ukyuli biala mani mede-nwu ɔnii uuboku lɛlɔ kalɔ na uti anumi ubi kalɔ ni, Absalom ɔɔkya ukyuli ɔmmɔ kɔgbu.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Lɛni sɔɔn na Absalom útaabla Israelƒuɔ bani ƒui néti litemi lɛdi béboku Ɔga Dawid kudɔ ka ɔtɛ-ni ute-ma. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu úyu Israelƒuɔ bammɔ kayi na nwuna ala áda-ma ebiti. Israelƒuɔ bammɔ anumi énwini ásia-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Na akwa ene kawɔlɔkɔ ni, Absalom ɔ́su Ɔga Dawid ɔnii, “Buvele ya na lisie Hebron na ntáƒɔ kayu na lidie lili na kenye kani na líse líte Unwoti na mmɔ.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Ɔsika ami ƒula kabla ɔblane líse Unwoti kenye uwi ɔni na lɛ́kya Gesur na Aram kalɛkɛ ka si ɔ́ya na línwini líbo Yerusalem ni, ndubɔkyula akpala lite-nwu.”

english_verse: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔtalane ɔdi úbasu Ɔga Dawid ɔnini, “Israelƒuɔ ƒui béti bana kayi básia Absalom lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Dawid ɔ́su nwuna kabla bablane bani ƒui nkya Yerusalem ɔnini, “Bɛta na bukeli si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, ɔƒɛni kalɛ bulálɛ Absalom ku nwuna bekyuli enu kemmo. Bɛya na bɔbabala amu ɔdubɔvi utáda-bu na ɔya na ɔgbankpi ubo-bu lɛlɔ na ɔdu ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli ƒui.”

english_verse: David left behind ten of his wives to take care of the palace, but the rest of his family and his officials and soldiers went with him. They stopped at the last house at the edge of the city.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔga ku bekyuli bani ƒui nébu basiaku-nwu bátɔlɔ. Uwi ɔni na bésela ni, bétédi bénye kaduli kekplodi na ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
translation_verse: Na ɔ́ya na nwuna bekyuli ƒui bávi bátɔ-nwu anumi ku Keretiƒuɔ ku Peletiƒuɔ ku Gatƒuɔ bani ƒui nási Gat kalɔ lɛlɔ aani bekyuli eti leevu-inyɔ ama ku ɔga nkɛ.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su Gatni ɔni baalɔ Itai ɔnini, “Útalɛka awɔ lɛnɔ asiaku-bu. Sɔ nwini teesie Ɔga Absalom kudɔ, ɔsika ɔƒɔ na adi na ékeli ébo akya mɛni.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Kaama kani na ási ébeduo na utalɛka ɔmwi ɔmɛni na litiku-ɔ na butátaaka taamana kalɔ bamba ƒui lɛlɔ ɔni na lɛɛɛgyi kesii kani na bɔdubɔwɔ. Nwini ku ƒula bekyuli na biteesie na Unwoti ɔnu-ɔ kɔnyana na ute-ɔ kusɛ kusɛ.”

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Nsu Itai údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔkɛnku Unwoti ɔni nli ngba uwi ƒui ku awɔ mina ati ku ɔga ɔni lɛnɔ nli ngba ɔƒɛni ni, kesii biala na mina ati ku ɔga ɔdubɔkya ni, mmɔ kani na ami lɛnɔ ndubɔkya. Kukpi kɔdi o-o ngba o-o ni, mmɔ kani na ami ƒula kabla ɔblane ndubunye.”

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Dawid ɔ́su Itai ɔnini, “Amu vi na buteesie” Na Itai ɔni ndi Gatni mɛni lɛnɔ ɔ́vinku nwuna bekyuli banana ku banamu bani ƒui nsiaku-nwu.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli béwulo keku momoomo uwi ɔni na Ɔga Dawid ku nwuna badi bávi baalɛ́-nwu kemmo. Bávia Kidron Kɔwɛ ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui na béti anumi bátina ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ Sadok ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui bébunku-ma na béti Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ. Na béti Katɔti adaka ɔmmɔ bátálɛ kalɔ na Ɔkpane Abiatar ɔ́bla akpala útédu ka bekyuli lisu lɛmmɔ ƒui bávi báwɔlɔ.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su Sadok ɔnini, “Bɛsɔku Katɔti Adaka ɔmmɔ bisienku Yerusalem ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na si mina ala áyɔ Katɔti kaƒɔ na ɔ́nu-mi ku lɛƒɔndia ni, ɔdubɔsɔku-mi uboku na mbanu Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ ku kesii kani na beesé-nwu lɛnɔ.

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: Nsu si ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Ƒula ala asɔ alada-mi kubiti’ ni, na nnye kágyumana ka ɔbla-mi kalɛ biala na ɔɔyɔ́.”

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: Ɔga Dawid ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Sadok ɔnini, “Katɔti ɔɔyá na aanu ala taati, anwuɔsu nwini teesie Yerusalem ɔma kemmo buɛɛ na akpanku ƒula bebi bananabi inyɔ Ahimas ku Abiatar ubidi ɔnanabi Yonatan ada.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Nu! Ndubunye ketu kammɔ kaviakɔ kesii kani néti késela ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo wetédu ka lɛ́ƒɔ kenye kadi lɛ́siku-ɔ kudɔ.”

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Sadok ku Abiatar bénwiniku Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ bétése Yerusalem, na básɔ bákya mmɔ.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Ɔga Dawid úti ɔ́kɔ úsela Nnɔ Egyii Kɔbi lɛlɔ na uuwulo na ulu lɛlɔ. Na úti ala úbi lili na ɔkɛ lɛgbakplu. Lɛni kani na bani nsiaku-nwu ƒui bebi ala lili na bakɛ beewulo na ulu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Na ɔƒɛni ni, bábasu Dawid banini, “Ahitoƒel lɛnɔ ɔkya Absalom badi bani nása lili likpidi ƒula lɛlɔ akɔ.” Mmɔ na Dawid ɔ́kpali katɔ ɔnini, “O Unwoti, nwini Ahitoƒel kasusu kani na ɔɔkya-ma bla adɔlɔla.”

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Dawid údu kɔbi lili kesii kani na bekyuli bátaakpa Katɔti ni, ɔ́nu Arkini ɔni baalɔ Husai ka uli mmɔ ɔnii ɔɔnu Ɔga Dawid. Na awu ɔni na ɔkya ɔ́bwɛ na ɔtumu uwi-nwu lili.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Si ásiaku-mi ni, adubunwini-mi etila.

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu nwini teesie Absalom kudɔ na Yerusalem na atásu-nwu anini, ‘O mina ɔga, ndubunwini ƒula kabla ɔblane. Nka kudeedi ni, ńtaabla kabla teete ƒ'ɔti. Nsu ɔƒɛni ni, awɔ na ndubɔbla kabla lite.’ Ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na adubɔsia na eƒu Ahitoƒel kasusu kani na wakya Absalom na kalálɛ ɔbuni.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Na lɛla biala na adubunu na ɔga kesii ni, awɔ su Sadok ku Abiatar, ɔsika bakya mmɔ.

english_verse: Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
translation_verse: Sadok ubidi Ahimas ku Abiatar ubidi Yonatan bebi bananabi inyɔ bammɔ lɛnɔ bakya mmɔ. Tala-ma kya-mi si énu lɛla lɛdi.”

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Dawid ɔkpana Husai ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Yerusalem, na anwu ku Absalom mmɔ buduo bɔ́bla unwi.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ɔga Dawid úye Siba ɔnini, “Bi na adanku ala amɛni ababla?” Na Siba lɛnɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Bebuo ala betine bammɔ ni, awɔ ɔga ku ƒula kaduli bekyuli mbo-ma ka bilie-ma lɛlɔ. Na adila ku adingyii ebi ammɔ adi bekyuli bani nsiaku-ɔ ɔdi. Na ntɛ bɔmmɔ bɔdi bani na lɛlɔ líitu na ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ kemmo ka bani-mu na basɔ bakɛ ɔlɔkplu.”

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid úye-nwu ɔnini, “Na wɛ na ƒula ɔtɔlati uwɔ anwu ɔkya?” Siba údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔkya Yerusalem, ɔsika na nwuna kakali kenye ni, ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Ɔmwi Israelƒuɔ badubɔsɔku mina nana ɔnana Saul Lɛga kadikɔ bete-mi.’ ”

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su Siba ɔnini, “Ala ani ƒui na Meƒiboset ubo ni, énwini awɔ adi.” Amu na Siba ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ntɛ kalɔ na awɔ ɔsu, mina ati ku ɔga, nu-mi ku lɛƒɔndia.” Simei Úwida Dawid

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ka Dawid ɔdaku Bahurim ɔma buduo ni, ɔnana ɔdi baalɔ Simei na ɔti ndi Gera na ɔ́si Saul kɔdua kemmo úbasiaku-nwu. Simei ɔmɛni úse kalɔ uuwida Ɔga Dawid uwi ɔni kani na ɔ́si ɔdubo.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Na ɔɔla atabi teebo teemene Dawid ku nwuna benengu bammɔ ƒui ina ka bekpone ku bagyumanane bammɔ benye-nwu kɔmii ku kɔdianu.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Ka Simei uuwida ni, ɔ́su Dawid ɔnini, “Gyu mɛni! Gyu mɛni! Awɔ ɔni na ubugya ɔ́ƒɔ-ɔ enu na adi ɔkantankpine.

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: Unwoti údie-ɔ kasi na ubugya ɔni ƒui na éwi kalɔ na Saul kaduli bekyuli akɔ. Na nwuna kenyekɔ na aadi lɛga. Na lɛgadi lɛmmɔ na Unwoti úkpeli ɔ́ƒɔ uute Absalom. Ɔƒaani énwini ukyuli ɔni na áyii udu, ɔsika adi ukyuli ɔni na éwi ubugya kalɔ ágya.”

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Amu na Abisai ɔni ndi Seruia ubidi ɔ́su Ɔga Dawid ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na akpewe ukpine ɔmɛni uteewida mina ati ku ɔga lɛni? Bite-mi kuƒi na ntámɛnɛ-nwu lili lɛti-mi.”

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Nsu Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su ɔnini, “Seruia bebi, bi nkɛ-mii na lɛmɛni lɛlɔ? Ɔƒɛni kalɛ Unwoti násu-nwu ɔnini, ‘Teesie na etéwida Dawid.’ Ɔma ndubɔkana na weye ɔnini, ‘Bi ɔsu na aasu lɛni?’ ”

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Dawid ɔ́su Abisai ɔnini, “Mina kaƒɔ ubi ɔni nási-mi lɛlɔ kemmo mɔɔwia-mi ɔdu amu útedu ka ukyuli bamba ɔni nási Benyamin kɔdua kemmo. Nyonu-nwu na uteewida-mi, ɔsika Unwoti násu-nwu ɔnii ɔbla lɛni.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni kalɛ Unwoti ɔdubɔnu-mina lɛbibo na uti lɛbuni ɔƒɔ-mi kayu na ewida ammɔ kenye.”

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Dawid ku nwuna bekyuli béti bana ulu na bésela na Simei lɛnɔ ɔ́si ɔɔyu kɔbi kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na uubó atabi ku ɔtumu taasiaku-ma na uuwida.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Na Ɔga Dawid ku anwu badi bétédu kesii kani na bésela. Na lɛlɔ lɛnɔ lítu-ma na baanwuna na mmɔ.

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, Absalom ku Israelƒuɔ banana bammɔ ƒui béebo bébeduo Yerusalem na Ahitoƒel lɛnɔ ɔkya-ma kudɔ.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Na Dawid ɔkpana Husai ɔni ndi Arkini mmɔ úsie Absalom kudɔ na útásu-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔga, ƒula ngba gyɔlɔɔ! Ɔga ƒula ngba gyɔlɔɔ!”

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Amu na Absalom úye Husai ɔnini, “Bɔyɔ bɔni na ebo ete ƒula ɔkpana ƒui na bɔdi mɛni? Bi ɔsu na átatásiaku ƒula ɔkpana?”

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Husai údie kenye ɔnini, “Tasu lɛni, ukyuli ɔni na Unwoti ɔlati ɔ́ƒuna na bekyuli bamɛni ku Israelƒuɔ akɔ na básia kɔnu ni, anwu ɔdi na ndi na ndubuti lɛlɔ lite-nwu.

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: Na ɔni na utulo ni, ɔma na ɔdi ka lɛbla kabla lite, ɔɔɔdi awɔ ubi ɔmmɔ? Kalɛ na lɛ́bla kabla líte ƒ'ɔti ni, lɛni kani na ndubɔbla kabla lite-ɔ.”

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Amu na Absalom ɔ́su Ahitoƒel ɔnini, “Bi ndi-ɔ kasusu, su-bu lɛla lɛni na aayɔ́ ka bɔbla?”

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ahitoƒel údie kenye ɔnini, “Sie na awɔ ku ƒ'ɔti basɔnɔ bani na ɔ́da úse kama ka bataanu kaduli lɛlɔ bɛtɛ. Si ábla lɛni ni, Israelƒuɔ badubɔnu bati ka éwi ƒ'ɔti anumi kalɔ ɔni na bɛsɔ bilakana unwi bɔbla lɛnɔ na Israel kadi bekyuli badubunwini basiaku-ɔ kama geen.”

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bálɛ adi kevo kadi na lɛsa katɔ béte Absalom na ɔ́tɛnku beleku bammɔ unwi unwi útáwɔlɔ na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui anumi.

english_verse: Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, kasusu biala na Ahitoƒel weboku ni, use aani ukyuli ɔni néye Katɔti kasusu únu. Na lɛni na Dawid ku Absalom ƒui baabu Ahitoƒel bɔlɛ ƒui taasiaku.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
