translation_verse: Na bɔdubɔkana na bukpoku-nwu kesii biala na bɔ́siaku-nwu na bulie-nwu lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na amii aayu teewi kalɔ. Na anwu iye nwuna basiakune ɔdi ulébu ulakya ngba.

english_verse: while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David,
translation_verse: Na lísela ntékpoku-nwu uwi ɔni na lɛlɔ lítu-nwu na ɔ́bla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ. Na ndubukpoku-nwu na liƒu bonwu liƒie anwu ku nwuna bekyuli ƒui na bani nsiaku-nwu ƒui bekeli. Ɔga Dawid kani na ndubɔdu.

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: Na lɛsɔku bekyuli bakladi ƒui liboku-ɔ. Ɔsika ukyuli unwi pɛ ɔni kani na aawia adu ni, anwu ndubɔya na bekyuli bakladi ƒui benwini bebo-ɔ kudɔ Na bekyuli bammɔ ama baláƒɔ ɔlɛ.”

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Kasusu kamɛni kádia Absalom ku Israelƒuɔ benengu bammɔ bunu.

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Nsu Absalom ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bɛlɔ Husai ɔni ndi Arkini lɛnɔ biboku na bunu lɛla lɛni na anwu lɛnɔ ubo na wasu.”

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Ka Husai úbo ni, Absalom ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Kasusu kani na Ahitoƒel ɔ́kya-bu na kadi mɛni. Aayɔ́ ka bɔbla lɛla lɛni na ɔ́su munuu bi ndi awɔ ƒula kasusu si alayɔ lɛni?”

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Husai údie kenye na ɔ́su Absalom ɔnini, “Ahitoƒel kasusu kani na ɔ́kya-mii kaaadia tɔ uwi ɔmɛni.

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Ɔsika agyi ka ƒ'ɔti ku nwuna bekyuli badi bekpone geen na bebo ogya aani eƒiebuo ɔni na béƒie-nwu bebi. Na ɔni ntulo ndi ka ƒ'ɔti ɔgyi kekpo kɔkwɛ geen, Na ulakya bekpone bammɔ akɔ usien ɔmɛni.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni muedi ni, ɔ́bɛ ɔkya lɛtabi ubu ɔdi kemmo iye ɔkya kesii bamba kadi. Ɔƒɛni si ɔ́ka kekpo bɔta na ƒula bekpone lɛlɔ ni, ukyuli biala menu kɔku kɔmmɔ ni, ɔdubɔsu ɔnini, ‘Bádu bekyuli na Absalom bekpone akɔ.’

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, ina ukpone ɔni mbo kayi aani gyata muedi ni, lɛlɔ lɛdubo-nwu bɔtɔ ku liƒu, ɔsika Israelni biala ɔgyi ka ƒ'ɔti ni, ukpone geen na ɔdi na nwuna basiakune lɛnɔ bebo kayi geen.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu ami mina kasusu ndi ka aya na Israelƒuɔ ƒui ɔ́si Dan útédu Beer-Seba na kalɛ na bemomo aani ɛpu kɔnwinimi kenye ni, basala na awɔ atɔnku-ma esienku kekpo kammɔ.

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: Na si ɔma unengudi ɔdi na wekeli wetéduo ni, Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui badubuti abuli beboku na bɔni ɔma ɔmmɔ butéwi ɔkwalɛ kemmo na nwuna kakɛ kadi muedi kasɔ kelébu.”

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Amu na Absalom ku Israelƒuɔ bammɔ básu banini, “Husai Arkini ɔmmɔ kasusu kani na ɔ́kya kadia ketulo Ahitoƒel kadi.” Ɔsika Unwoti ɔlati úse ka uƒu Ahitoƒel kasusu ɔkya na ɔgbankpi ubo Absalom lɛlɔ.

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Husai ɔ́su Sadok ku Abiatar bani ndi bakpane ɔnini, “Ahitoƒel úte Absalom ku Israelƒuɔ benengu kasusu ka babla lɛni ku lɛni, nsu ami lɛ́su-ma ka babla-nwu kekuma.

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni bɛsia Ɔga Dawid kenye kɔnakunwi bɛnini, ‘Taƒɔ lɛlɔ tatɛ ketu kaviakɔ na ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo mmɔ. Mmomu via-ka ɔ́bla bi ɔ́bla dɛ si ɔɔɔdi lɛni badubo-mii lɛlɔ bulie na mmɔ na badu-mii bedie.’ ”

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni Yonatan ku Ahimas bakya kesii kani baalɔ banii En Rogel. Na ulekubi kabla ɔblane ɔdi na ɔlɛka usie utásu-ma na ama beti kenye kammɔ besienku Dawid. Ɔsika utalɛka banu-ma ka beeduo Yerusalem ɔma kemmo.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Nsu okloƒu ɔdi ɔ́nu-ma na ɔsu Absalom. Anwuɔsu nkyuli inyɔ bammɔ békeli mmɔ kɔnakunwi bésie ɔnana ɔdi baalɔ Bahurim kesii. Ɔnana ɔmɛni ubo libiɔ lɛdi na nwuna kesii na nkyuli inyɔ bammɔ báyu béduo-ni kemmo.

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: Na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ulekudi úti kebila kadi úbi ubu ɔmmɔ kenye na úgyingya antabi úwi-nwu lɛlɔ ɔni na ɔdi ɔɔɔgyi ɔnii bekyuli badi bakya mmɔ.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amu ka Absalom bekyuli bébo mmɔ ni, bébeye uleku ɔmmɔ banini, “Wɛ na Ahimas ku Yonatan bávi?” Mmɔ na uleku ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛ́nu ka bávia ketu kammɔ na béti bésela.” Na Absalom bekyuli bammɔ báwia-ma, nsu bátanu-ma. Anwuɔsu bénwini bésie Yerusalem.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Ka bénwini ni, bakloƒu bammɔ bálɛ libiɔ lɛmmɔ kemmo bátásu Dawid kenye kammɔ. Básu-nwu banini, “Ti ala na avia ketu kammɔ kɔnakunwi, ɔsika Ahitoƒel úte Absalom kasusu kekpidi ɔ́siku-ɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Ɔga Dawid ku nwuna bekyuli bani ƒui nsiaku-nwu bávia Yordan Ketu ɔni na asa na kadi kegye ni, bana ƒui báasa bɔvia.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ka Ahitoƒel ɔ́nu ka béteti nwuna kasusu kani na ɔ́kya-ma ni, ɔ́bala nwuna ebuo ala utine na ɔ́kɔ úlie-nwu lɛlɔ na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie nwuna ɔma. Na ka ɔ́klibi ala úsie nwuna ɔtɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, úsie útákya lɛlɔ ɔbuli na úkpi na báva-nwu bana ɔti kaƒiɔtɔ.

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kama ni, Dawid ɔ́ɔtɔlɔ útédu Mahanaim na Absalom lɛnɔ ku Israelƒuɔ banana bani ƒui nsiaku-nwu bávia Yordan Ketu.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Na Absalom ɔ́ƒuna Amasa ka ɔtɔnku bekpone bammɔ na Yoab kenye. Na Amasa ɔmɛni ɔdi ɔnana ɔni baalɔ Yitra ubidi ɔnanabi. Yitra ɔmɛni ɔdi Israelni ɔni néti Abigail. Ɔnana ɔni baalɔ banii Nahas náwɔ Abigail na Nahas ɔnwani ulekubi ɔni baalɔ Seruia náwɔ Yoab.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Na Gilead kalɔ kemmo na Absalom ku anwu badi bátáda keliekɔ.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, na Dawid úubo úbedu Mahanaim. Na Nahas ɔni ndi Amonni na ɔ́si Raba ɔma ubo ubi ɔdi na baalɔ-nwu Sobi. Sobi ɔmɛni ku Makir ɔni ɔti ndi Amiel na ɔ́si Lo-Debar ku Barsilai ɔni ndi Gileadni na ɔ́si Rogelim

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: Bada uwɔ ku bebuo anyii ntu ani béƒulo bábla adila lidu lidu ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ anyi ntu ani bébo na ɔmii béboku Dawid ku nwuna badi banii badi, ɔsika bánu ka lɛlɔ líitu-ma, na bánu lɛnɔ ka utukwɛ ku kɔka kɔɔda-ma na ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ kemmo mmɔ.

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: Dawid údie bekpone bammɔ ulu na esu atɛ kemmo. Na Yoab ntɔnku linwi na ɔnwani Abisai ɔni ndi Seruia ubidi ntɔnku linyɔdi. Na Itai ɔni ndi Gatni ɔtɔnku lɛkpa lɛtɛdi. Na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, ami ɔlati lɛnɔ ndubo-mii bɔsiaku.

english_verse: But the soldiers said, “No, don't go into battle with us! It won't matter to our enemies if they make us all run away, or even if they kill half of us. But you are worth
translation_verse: Nsu bekyuli bammɔ básu-nwu banini, “Útalɛ ka awɔ alɛ ebo mmɔ, ɔsika si ɔƒɛni kalɛ úbo ka baabɔku-bu iye bula kakɛ bekyuli békpi muedi ni, balakpete. Mmomu awɔ áƒɔ kuye etulo nkyuli mpim leevu muedi. Anwuɔsu awɔ taakya-bu ogya akpagya taasiku ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo kani na ɔ́bɔ.”

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: Ka Yoab bekpone akɔ unwi ɔ́nu ɔmɛni ni, ɔ́su Yoab ɔnini, “Ɔƒɛni kani na lɛ́nu ka Absalom ɔƒa kayaa na kugyii bonwu kɔdi kɔgba akɔ.”

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Kekpo kammɔ kégyingya késie kesii amadɔ mmɔ bene ƒui na bana pii bátáyii bákya na békpi, nsu ɔɔɔdi kewii kenye na békpi.

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Absalom ɔ́tuaku Dawid bekpone badi uwi ɔni na ulie nwuna ebuo ala utine lɛlɔ. Ɔƒɛni ka ebuo ɔmmɔ úkeli ɔ́sia kugyii bonwu kɔdi kagba kadi nébomo ku evete yuu kalɔ ni, nwuna lili lɛ́bala kɔgba kɔmmɔ na ebuo ɔmmɔ ɔ́vi ɔ́lɛ-nwu kalɔ na úkeli úsela na Absalom ɔlati ɔ́yɔlɔ ɔƒa kayaa.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yoab úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi na aasu mɛni! Ánu-nwu sɔsɔ na ébulo-nwu bɔdu na ɔsi ubayu kalɔ? Nka ndubute-ɔ sika ɔƒualadi ɔni unu mabla antabi lɛkyami linwi unu. Na ndubuti bekpone katɔ bɔkɔliku ɔbu lɛduni lɛbala-a kayi.”

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni si bɔti na ńtati kalɛ na banii lɛ́bla-nwu lɛla lɛdi, nka mina ngba búduo ɔgbankpi kemmo, ɔsika lɛla lɛdi lilábɛ Ɔga Dawid. Na awɔ adubunye sɛsɛɛ.”

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Yoab útete bunu mmomu ɔnini, “Lɛɛɛdubo bunye buteebile uwi ƒula lɛlɔ.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu úti atula gyɔlɔɔ atɛ ɔ́da na útáƒuala Absalom kayi uwi ɔni na ɔƒa kayaa na útekpi tɔ na kugyii bonwu kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off.
translation_verse: Yoab ekpola badane leevu bábaka bámana Absalom na bébo-nwu bádu.

english_verse: Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yoab ɔ́vwi lise na bekpone bakladi báda Israelƒuɔ bɔbɔku báya, ɔsika Yoab ɔ́sia-ma kɔnu ka bada baya.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: Na beti Absalom bétébo bákya ubu bonwu ɔdi kemmo na lɛku kemmo mmɔ na bála atabi lisu bonwu básia-nwu lɛlɔ. Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Israelƒuɔ békeli bésie bana lɛma.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Na Absalom ngba uwi ƒui ni, ɔ́vɔ atabi lɛkpa lɛdi únyene ɔga kɔwɛ kemmo aani lɛlɔ likposela, ɔsika ɔ́su lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Liiibo ubi ɔnanabi ɔni mabla lɛla lɛni maya na mina lɛnyi lilayii.” Na úti mmɔ ɔ́sia nwuna lɛnyi lɛni bekyuli baalɔ úti úbedu ɔmwi kadi banii Absalom Likposela. Dawid Uwulo Ubidi

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Sadok ubidi Ahimas ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bɛya na likeli ntásu ɔga lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́, ka Unwoti údie-nwu ɔ́lɛku nwuna bekisine enu kemmo.”

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yoab ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdi awɔ ndubuti kenye kamɛni busienku Ɔga Dawid ɔmwi. Mmomu adubuti kenye bamba esienku-nwu limeyi bamba na ɔɔɔdi ɔni na Ɔga Dawid ubidi nékpi mɛni.”

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Nwuna kama Yoab ɔ́su Kusni ɔdi ɔnini, “Teesie na atásu Ɔga Dawid lɛla lɛni na ánu.” Na Kusni ɔmmɔ úboku lili kalɔ úte Yoab na úkeli ɔ́tɔlɔ.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Sadok ubidi Ahimas ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Yoab ɔnini, “Buvele nda-a, ya na likeli lɛsia Kusni ɔmmɔ kama.” Nsu Yoab údie kenye na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Ubi, bi ɔsu na aayɔ́ ka esie atásu kenye kamɛni udu ka ɔɔɔdi kenye buni na adanku iye linugya etela adi na badubo-ɔ bute?”

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ahimas údie kenye ɔnini, “Ina bi na ɔdi mebo ni, mɔɔyɔ́ ka likeli lɛsia Kusni ɔmmɔ kama.” Anwuɔsu Yoab údie-nwu ulu ɔnini, “Keli sie.” Mmɔ na Ahimas úti ɔ́sia Yordan Ketu ɔkwalɛ kemmo na úsie útébo ɔ́vi Kusni ɔni náagyu ɔtɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ka Ɔga Dawid ulie ɔma ɔban kayakun kenengudi ku kebliidi ntɛ ni, ɔgyumanane ɔni mɔɔnu mmɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́kɔ úsie ɔban ɔmmɔ kayakun lɛsa eli, Mmɔ ni, ɔ́nu ka ɔnana ɔdi úkeli ɔ́si ɔdubo anwu lɛti.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Amu na ɔgyumanane ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpali Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su-nwu lɛla lɛni na ɔɔnu. Mmɔ na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Si anwu lɛti nkɛ bɔdi ni, na agyi anii kenye kabuni na ɔdanku.” Na ɔnana ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔ́ni uudé-ma teebu.

english_verse: when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!” David said, “He must have some news too.”
translation_verse: Nwuna kama ni, ɔgyumanane ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́nu ka ukyuli bamba lɛnɔ úkeli ɔsia ɔdubo. Na ɔ́kpali kayakun kenye unyene ɔnini, “Nu! Ukyuli bamba lɛnɔ úkeli ɔsia ɔdubo anwu lɛti.” Na ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su ɔnini, “Kenye buni na anwu lɛnɔ ɔdanku ɔduboku.”

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Ɔgyumanane ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Use-mi aani ukyuli udeedi ɔni ntɔ mmɔ ni, Sadok ubidi Ahimas na ɔdi.” Mmɔ na Ɔga Dawid ɔnini, “Ukyuli ɔbuni na Ahimas ɔdi ɔsu kenye kabuni na úti ɔduboku.”

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Ahimas ɔ́ɔni úde-ma geen ɔsu ɔ́kpali na ɔ́su Ɔga Dawid úmene ɔnini, “Blɔti! Lɛla biala lise buɛɛ.” Na úboku lili kalɔ úte Ɔga Dawid. Ɔ́yu úbi kalɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bemwi Unwoti ƒula Katɔti! Ɔ́ya na bɔ́di ƒula bekisine lɛlɔ. Ama bani náta bénye ka bekpo awɔ mina ɔga ku unwoti.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ɔga Dawid úye ɔnini, “Na dɛ na use ku mina okloƒu Absalom, lɛla lɛdi lítabla-nwu nɔɔ?” Ahimas údie kenye ɔnini, “Uwi ɔni na Yoab údie-mi ulu na meti matɔlɔ mmɔ ni, lɛ́nu bekyuli lisu bonwu lɛdi na ntɛ mmɔ bɔdi na ɔ́bla aani lɛlɔ bɔnwanɛ ku lɛsɛ bonwu bɔdi bɔkya mmɔ, nsu ńtati lɛla lɛni nébo.”

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Nye kɔƒɛlɛ.” Na ɔ́sɔ únye mmɔ.

english_verse: The Ethiopian came and said, “Your Majesty, today I have good news! The Lord has rescued you from all your enemies!”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Kusni ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ úbalɛ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Mina ati ku ɔga, nu kenye buni kani na ndanku! Unwoti údie-ɔ na ƒula bekisine bani náta banii beekpó-ɔ enu kemmo ɔmwi.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Dawid úye anwu lɛnɔ ɔnini, “Na Absalom mina okloƒu ɔmmɔ nɔɔ? Lɛla lɛdi lítabla-nwu?” Mmɔ na Kusni ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Muuvele ka bekisine bani ƒui mata banii beekpó mina ati ku ɔga ni, bayila-ma udu aani kalɛ na ɔ́lɛku okloƒu ɔmmɔ.”

english_verse: David started trembling. Then he went up to the room above the city gate to cry. As he went, he kept saying, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I could have died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Lɛla lɛmmɔ líkpoku Ɔga Dawid na lɛlɔ lɛ́tɔ-nwu. Na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie ɔtɔ ɔni nkya ɔma ɔban kayakun kudɔ mmɔ kemmo na úwulo geen. Uwi ɔni na ɔ́gyu úsela mmɔ ni, ɔ́su ɔnini, “O mina ubi ɔnanabi Absalom! Mina ubi, mina ubi ɔnanabi Absalom! Bi ɔsu na ɔɔɔdi ami nékpi na ƒula kenye. O Absalom, mina ubi o-o! Mina ubi!”

english_verse: Someone told Joab, “The king is crying because Absalom is dead.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, básu Yoab banini, “Ɔga Dawid ɔkya uuwulo ubidi.”

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: Na bekpone bammɔ lɛlɔ bɔdi búnwini kɔnyana, ɔsika bénu ka básu banini, “Ɔga Dawid ɔkya uuwulo ubidi.”

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bɔbɛ na bekpone bammɔ bábɛ béduo ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo aani kalɛ na bekyuli bani na bábɔku na kekpokɔ baabɛ́ teeduo ɔma na kɔƒa ɔsu.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Ɔga Dawid úti enu úbi anumi na úwulo momoomo ɔ́kpali ɔnini, “O mina ubi Absalom, O Absalom, mina ubi mina ubi!”

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yoab úduo úsie-nwu kudɔ na ɔtɔ kemmo mmɔ na ɔ́su ɔga ɔnini, “Ɔmwi ni, áya na ƒula bekyuli anumi éwi kalɔ. Ama nédie-ɔ ɔgbankpi kemmo ɔƒɛni kani ɔni na uwi útetu tɔ, na bédie ƒula bebi bananabi ku belekubi ku ƒula beleku ku basɔnɔ ƒui ngba.

english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: Aayɔ́ ƒula bekisine na eekisi bani mɔɔyɔ́-ɔ. Édie átina-bu nwaa ɔmwi ka ƒula bekpone batɔnkune ku bekpone bammɔ ƒui ngba buuubo-ɔ kɔsia kɔdi. Na si bɔkya na Absalom ɔkya ngba ɔmwi na abu bakladi ƒui búkpi ni, ɔdi-a utulo.

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: Mɔɔwia ka alɛ esie ƒula bekpone kudɔ na atásia-ma kɔnu na akya-ma ogya ɔƒɛni kani. Na lɛ́kpali Unwoti muusé kenye ka si átalɛ átatábla lɛni ni, ukyuli ina unwi pɛ asɔ alanu na ƒula kudɔ mɛni asa na ɔƒɛ wasa. Na ɔdi lɛla lɛni ndubɔyu-ɔ ɔkplu butulo ala ani néekpoku-ɔ ɔ́si lɛkloƒu uwi úti úbedu ɔƒɛni.”

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Ɔga Dawid ɔ́ta na útélie kalɔ na ɔma ɔban ɔmmɔ kayakun kenye. Na ka básu bekyuli bammɔ banii Ɔga Dawid ulie ɔban kenye mmɔ ni, bana ƒui bálɛ bébo-nwu kudɔ. Dawid Únwini Úsie Yerusalem Uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ békeli bésie bana lɛma.

english_verse: everyone in Israel started arguing. They were saying to each other, “King David rescued us from the Philistines and from our other enemies. But then we chose Absalom to be our new leader, and David had to leave the country to get away. Absalom died in battle, so why hasn't something been done to bring David back?”
translation_verse: Na Absalom ɔni na bése lɛga ka utaadi-bu lɛlɔ lɛnɔ útékpi na kekpokɔ. Na si use lɛni ni, bi ɔsu na bilásu lɛla lɛdi na Dawid bɔsɔku buboku lɛlɔ?”

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Ɔga Dawid ɔ́sia Sadok ku Abiatar bakpane bammɔ kenye ɔnini, “Biye Yuda kaba bekyuli bɛnini, ‘Bi ɔsu na amii na ɔlɛka bɛbla bekyuli bekplodi bani ndubɔsɔku ɔga biboku nwuna kaduli. Ka líinu ala ani ƒui na Israelƒuɔ badaku bɔka?

english_verse: He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
translation_verse: Amii ndi mina banwani bani na bude butulo. Bi ɔsu na amii mmomu mɔɔkpɛ kama ka bɛya lɛsɔ linwini libo mina lɛgakadikɔ?’

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: Na biye Amasa bɛnini, ‘Ɔɔɔdi ubugya ku ɔlɔna unwi bebi na bɔdi yoo? Lɛ́kpali Katɔti muusé kenye ka si ńteti-ɔ ńtenwini mina bekpone ɔtɔnkune na Yoab kenye ɔ́si ɔmɛni kama na ɔni-mi kɔtu biala na ɔɔyɔ́.’ ”

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ɔga Dawid ala ásɔ áda Yuda kaba bekyuli bammɔ ebiti ɔni na básɔ básala lɛlɔ aani ukyuli unwi na benye Dawid kama. Na básia Ɔga Dawid kenye banini, “Awɔ ku ƒula bekyuli ƒui bɛsɔ binwini bibo.”

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Gera ubidi Simei ɔni ndi Benyamin kaba kemmo ubi na ɔ́si Bahurim ɔ́babla ɔsiaku Yudaƒuɔ bammɔ ka batásiaku Ɔga Dawid.

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: Ɔsika ami ƒula kabla ɔblane ngyi ka lɛ́bla likpidi. Nsu ɔmwi ni, líbo mɛni aani Yoseƒ kɔdua kemmo ubi udeedi ka mbasiaku awɔ mina ati ku ɔga.”

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Na bávia ketu kammɔ na kesii kani nátagyu mmɔ ka betétiku ɔga ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli na béti-ma béboku kalɛ na bataabla Ɔga Dawid lɛyɔla teete-nwu. Ka Gera ubidi Simei ɔ́via Yordan Ketu ni, ɔ́yu úbi Ɔga Dawid anumi.

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Mina ati, muuvele-ɔ nnii, tanu mina alaekpidi. Na takali tanu likpidi lɛni na ami ƒula kabla ɔblane lɛ́bla na limeyi lɛni lɛlɔ na aatɔlɔ Yerusalem. Mmomu muuvele-ɔ ka ada-ni edie ƒula kasusu kemmo.

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ɔga Dawid údie kenye ɔnini, “Ami ku amii Seruia bebi ni, buuuse likeke na ulu biala lɛlɔ. Na ɔmwi ni, bínwini mina bekisine! Bi ɔsu na ɔlɛka badu ukyuli ɔdi na Israel kalɔ kemmo ɔmwi? Ɔmwi ni, ngyi nwaa ka ami ndi Israelƒuɔ ƒui ɔga.”

english_verse: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔga ɔ́su Simei ɔnini, “Aaadubo bukpi.” Na ɔdi kenye na ɔga úse-nwu.

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: Meƒiboset údie kenye ɔnini, “Ka ukyuli ɔni náƒɛ uwi kalɔ na ndi ɔsu ni, mina ati ku ɔga, lɛ́bala mina ebuo ala utine ka nka lilie-nwu lɛlɔ na lɛsiaku-ɔ. Nsu mina kabla ɔblane Siba úbo-ɔ kudɔ úbakya-mi kakya.

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: Na ubanyi ɔkɔ ɔ́sia ami, ƒula kabla ɔblane, úte awɔ mina ati ku ɔga. Mina ati ku ɔga, ese aani Katɔti ɔtu, anwuɔsu bla lɛla biala mɔɔyɔ́-ɔ kaƒɔ.

english_verse: David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Dawid ɔnini, “Ɔdia taka ala gyɔlɔɔ. Ami nébo ɔda ka awɔ ku Siba bile kalɔ kammɔ.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Meƒiboset ɔ́su Ɔga Dawid ɔnini, “Ya-nwu na ɔ́kpa uti ala ana ƒui ka awɔ mina ati ku ɔga áasi ébeduo Yerusalem buɛɛ ɔsu.”

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Amu na Gileadni ɔni baalɔ Barsilai lɛnɔ ɔ́si Rogelim ɔma úbo úbavia Yordan Ketu ku Ɔga Dawid na úse-nwu ulu ɔ́si mmɔ.

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: Ɔga Dawid ɔsu Barsilai ɔnini, “Ya bɔvia Yordan Ketu kammɔ na ebo ebelie-mi kudɔ na Yerusalem na ami ndubɔnu-ɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Nsu Barsilai údie kenye ɔnini, “Akwa alɛ na nsɔ ndubo ngba bulie na mɔɔsiaku mina ɔga nteesie Yerusalem?

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: Ami ƒula kabla ɔblane ndubɔvia Yordan Ketu ku mina ati ku ɔga na bɔkɛ busie anumi blii kani na ɔmmɔ lɛti ɔ́bɔ-mi ɔ́vili.

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: Ya na ami ƒula kabla ɔblane linwini lisie mina ɔma na ntékpi kalɛ na naaagyunku mina ɔti ku uni kesii kani na báva-ma. Nsu ni, aanu ƒula kabla ɔblane Kimham. Ya na awɔ mina ati ku ɔga ku anwu bɛvia Yordan Ketu. Na ablaku-nwu kalɛ na aayɔ́.”

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ɔga Dawid údie kenye ɔnini, “Kimham ɔdubɔviaku-mi Yordan Ketu na ndubɔda-nwu kalɛ biala na aayɔ́. Na lɛla biala na aayɔ́ ni, ndubɔbla lite-ɔ.”

english_verse: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bávia Yordan Ketu, na ɔmmɔ kama Ɔga Dawid lɛnɔ ɔ́via. Na ka bávia ni, ɔga ɔ́kya Barsilai kɔgbu na úte-nwu kusɛ kusɛ, na Barsilai ɔ́sɔ únwini úsie ɔma.

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́via úsie útédu Gilgal ni, Kimham lɛnɔ ɔsiaku-nwu. Na Yudaƒuɔ bekpone ƒui ku Israelƒuɔ bekpone bumomo ƒui kakɛ kenwi ama nétiku Ɔga Dawid bésienku mmɔ.

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: Uwi útetu asa na Israelƒuɔ ƒui beebo Ɔga Dawid kudɔ teebeye-nwu banini, “Bi ɔsu na bula banwa Yudaƒuɔ béyu-ɔ bátɔlɔku na ama kani néti-ɔ ku ƒula kaduli bekyuli bávialaku Yordan Ketu?”

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yudaƒuɔ ƒui bédie kenye banini, “Ɔɔɔdi keeke na bɔ́bla lɛni, ɔsika abu bude geen. Na dɛ na amii bɛ́kali ɔsu na ɔmɛni uukpóku-mii? Ɔɔɔdi kayu kadi na ɔga ɔ́ƒɔ úte-bu iye adila adi na úte-bu iye búti-nwu lɛla lɛdi búnwini abu lɛdi.”

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ bédie Yudaƒuɔ bammɔ kenye banini, “Bubo kadikɔ akpa leevu na lɛgadi lɛmmɔ kemmo. Na si banii buti-nwu ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, bubo kuƒi na Dawid lɛlɔ butulo-mii, ɔsika abu náka kasusu buboku ka bɔsɔku bula ɔga buboku. Anwuɔsu ulu ɔmani lɛlɔ ɔsu na bɛɛnu-bu anumi?” Nsu Yudaƒuɔ bétete Israelƒuɔ lɛla lɛdi bɔsu.

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, lɛsɛ ɔkyane ɔdi baalɔ Seeba na ɔdi Bikri ubidi na Benyamin kɔdua kemmo ɔ́kya mmɔ. Na ɔ́vwi kakpɛɛ momoomo ɔnini, “O Israelƒuɔ, buuubo kadikɔ kadi na Dawid lɛgadi kemmo. Na bɔɔɔkɛnku Yisai ɔni ndi ɔti lɛla lɛdi kemmo lɛnɔ. Anwuɔsu bina ƒui ɔdi biala unwini na biteesie bina adi nvo kemmo.”

english_verse: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israelƒuɔ banana ƒui bátɔlɔ Dawid kudɔ na báda-nwu bése na básiaku Bikri ubidi Seeba ɔmmɔ kama bátɔlɔ. Nsu Yudaƒuɔ ama báƒɔ lɛlɔ bákya kama na basiaku Ɔga Dawid ɔ́si Yordan Ketu útédu Yerusalem.

english_verse: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Dawid únwini úsie nwuna kaduli na Yerusalem ni, ɔ́ya na béti nwuna basɔnɔ leevu bani na ɔ́da ɔ́kya kama ka bataanu kaduli lɛlɔ mmɔ batákya liku lɛdi na ɔ́ya na beete-ma na baadi na baaní, nsu ɔ́sɔ útesie ɔdi kudɔ kudii na batɛ ɔnana ku uleku kalɛ. Mmomu bákya mmɔ aani bekpinele útédu ka ɔdi biala úkpi.

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔga ɔ́tala Amasa ɔnini, “Sie na atásala Yudaƒuɔ ƒui na bebo emeyi atɛ kama ɔ́si ɔmwi na awɔ ɔlati akya-ma akɔ.”

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Nsu ka Amasa úsie útásala Yudaƒuɔ bamɛni ni, ɔ́di emeyi útulo kalɛ na ɔga ɔ́su-nwu.

english_verse: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su Abisai ɔnini, “Ɔƒɛni ni, lɛ́nu ka Bikri ubidi Seeba ni, nwuna ablala adubo abanyi anyi etulo Absalom adi. Anwuɔsu tiku bekyuli badi na ƒula bekpone benengu badi akɔ na bɛsia-nwu kama kɔnakunwi kalɛ na ulatákɛ kabɛkɔ kadi na lɛma linengudi lɛni bátu bámana mmɔ ɔdi kemmo na walɛ-bu enu kemmo.”

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Yoab bekyuli ku Keretiƒuɔ ku Peletiƒuɔ ku bekpone benengudi bani náƒɔ lɛnyi geen mmɔ báta básiaku Abisai na báyu ulu lɛnanabi kemmo bási Yerusalem bátásia Bikri ubidi Seeba kama.

english_verse: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bétédu kesii kani baalɔ banii Lɛtakpɛ Bonwu na Gibeon ni, Amasa úbasiaku-ma na mmɔ. Na Yoab ɔkya nwuna kekpo lɛwu na kewii kakya livuo kemmo na kada-nwu kavobi. Ka Yoab údie ɔgba úsienku anumi kani na kewii kammɔ kálɛ livuo kemmo kébo kalɔ.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yoab úgyele Amasa na úye ɔnii, “Ɔnwa akya kaduɛ?” Ka uuye-nwu ɔmɛni ni, Yoab údie kɔdianu na úƒie Amasa ukwi ɔ́da aani si kɔgbu na ɔnii ɔɔkya-nwu.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Amasa ɔ́sɔ útasia anumi ɔnii Yoab úti kewii kani nálɛ kébo mmɔ ɔda. Anwuɔsu tati tese kemmo ni, Yoab ɔ́tu Amasa kaƒɔ ɔ́ƒuala na livo lɛ́lɛ líwi kalɔ. Na kunwi kɔni na ɔ́tu-nwu mmɔ kani na Amasa úkpi. Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yoab ku ɔnwani Abisai bábi básia Bikri ubidi Seeba ɔmmɔ kama.

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Yoab kama basiakune akɔ unwi úténye Amasa kudɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ukyuli biala ɔni mɔɔyɔ́ ka Yoab ɔtɔnku-bu na unye ute Dawid ni, ɔsiaku Yoab kama!”

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Na Amasa ɔtɛ nwuna ubugya kemo mmɔ ɔɔkpɛ́ kukpi akɔnɔnɔ na ulu ɔmmɔ ntɛntɛ. Yoab kama ɔsiakune ɔmmɔ ɔ́nu ka bekpone bammɔ ƒui bédi bénye. Ɔƒɛni ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́nu ka si ukpone biala úbedu Amasa kudɔ mmɔ na udi unye. Anwuɔsu ɔ́ni-nwu úsienku kɔmadɔ na alakpi akɔ na úti awu gyɔlɔɔ ɔdi úbi-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: Ka báda Amasa bédie ulu mmɔ ni, bekpone bammɔ básiaku Yoab ku Abisai na bábi básia Bikri ubidi Seeba ɔmmɔ kama.

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Seeba ɔ́tɔlɔ ni, úsie útásia Israelƒuɔ kaba kammɔ bekyuli akɔ útédu ɔma ɔni baalɔ Abel Bet-Maaka na ɔkɛ ɔ́vi Bikriƒuɔ kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ ƒui na básala basiaku-nwu.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Yoab ku nwuna bekpone bani ƒui nsiaku-nwu kama bébo na bábaka Seeba bákya na Abel Bet-Maaka. Na básia libili na ulu lɛlɔ útédu ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ na ɔdanku awodu akpa bonwu bonwu ani na bátu béti benyimi awodu ani na bátu bámana ɔma ɔmmɔ. Ɔmmɔ kama bése kalɔ baawɔ́ awodu geen ammɔ ala kalɛ na aƒɛ ewi kalɔ.

english_verse: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ka badaku ɔmmɔ ni, uleku ɔnundane ɔdi ɔ́kpali úmene ɔ́si ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bɛsɔ binye na binu! Yoab o-o, ni de-mi mɛni na bɔtɛmi!”

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Amu na anwu lɛnɔ úsie úsela uleku ɔmmɔ kudɔ. Uleku ɔmmɔ úye-nwu ɔnini, “Awɔ ndi Yoab?” Na Yoab lɛnɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Ami geen mɛni.” Mmɔ na uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Nu lɛla lɛni na ami, ƒula kabla ɔblane, mɔɔsu-ɔ.” Na Yoab lɛnɔ úte-nwu kuƒi ɔnii utaasu.

english_verse: She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na úsie anumi na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Kuuku ni, baasu banini, ‘Si lɛla lɛdi liikpóku-ɔ ni, na esie Abel na adubɔnu-ni lili ku lɛgba,’ na nwuna kawɔlɔkɔ ndi mmɔ sɔsɔ.

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: Abu ndanku keyi buɛɛ na bɔɔdi litemi lɛlɔ siin na Israel kalɔ kemodi lɛlɔ. Nsu awɔ aawia ka ebile ɔma unengudi ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ ƒui uni. Bi ɔsu na aayɔ́ ka ebile lɛla lɛni ndi Unwoti kese?”

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Amu na Yoab úveli enu ɔnini, “Oowo, énu! Lɛɛɛdanku lɛmmɔ udu nnii mbebile iye lɛyila ɔma ɔmmɔ udu.

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Mmomu ɔnana ɔdi baalɔ Seeba na ɔdi Bikri ubidi na ɔ́si Eƒraim abi lɛlɔ ɔma ni, anwu náta únye bula Ɔga Dawid lɛlɔ ɔnii uunye ɔsiaku-nwu. Die ukyuli ɔmɛni kani te-bu na bɔgyu bɔtɔlɔ na bɔsɔ bulétuku ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni lɛla lɛdi.” Mmɔ na uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́su Yoab ɔnini, “Ndubo nwuna lili bubo bɔva-a ɔƒɛni kani ɔ́si kowodu lili mɛni.”

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
translation_verse: Amu na uleku ɔmmɔ úsie na útéti nwuna lɛnunda kasusu kammɔ ɔ́va bekyuli pii anumi. Na békulo Seeba lili sɔsɔ na úbebo-ni ɔ́va Yoab ɔ́siku kowodu lili. Anwuɔsu Yoab ɔ́vwi kakpɛɛ úte nwuna badi na bávi bálɛ ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo, na ɔdi biala ɔtɔlɔ úsie nwuna ɔma. Na Yoab lɛnɔ ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Ɔga Dawid kudɔ na Yerusalem.

english_verse: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Yoab mɔɔdi Israelƒuɔ ƒui bekpone lɛlɔ. Na Benaia ɔni ndi Yoiada ubidi ɔɔdi Keretiƒuɔ ku Peletiƒuɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
translation_verse: Na Adoniram ɔɔdi bani mɔɔnu enu kabla lɛlɔ. Na Ahilud ubidi ɔni baalɔ Yehosaƒat mɔɔnu ekposela ala lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
translation_verse: Na Seva ndi ɔku unwenine. Na Sadok ku Abiatar badi bakpane.

english_verse: Ira from Jair was David's priest.
translation_verse: Na Ira ɔni nási Yair kɔdua kemmo ndi ɔkpane ute Ɔga Dawid.

english_verse: The Gibeonites were not Israelites; they were descendants of the Amorites. The people of Israel had promised not to kill them, but Saul had tried to kill them because he wanted Israel and Judah to control all the land. David had the Gibeonites come, and he talked with them.
translation_verse: Ɔga Dawid ɔ́ya na bálɔ Gibeonƒuɔ bani nébu bakya na ɔ́tɛmiku-ma. Ɔƒɛni Gibeonƒuɔ bamɛni ni, baaadi Israelƒuɔ kaba bekyuli, mmomu Amoriƒuɔ bani na kekpo kéteƒie na badi. Na Israelƒuɔ bákpali ala bése kenye ka balabla-ma lɛla lɛdi. Nsu Saul úti lɛnungyie kemmo ka ukpo ute Israelƒuɔ ku Yudaƒuɔ ɔsu na ɔ́yɔ ka ɔyila-ma udu ƒui.

english_verse: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid úye Gibeonƒuɔ bamɛni ɔnini, “Bi na bɛɛyɔ́ ka lɛbla lite-mii? Na dɛ na ndubɔyala-mii kaƒɔ na ɔmɛni kemmo kalɛ na Unwoti kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku nwuna bekyuli?”

english_verse: They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel.
translation_verse: Bédie kenye banini, “Ukyuli ɔni náyɔ ka ɔyila-bu udu ka abu bɔsɔ butakɛ keliekɔ kadi na Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ kesii biala ɔsu na ɔsiaku-bu uukpóku-bu ulu biala lɛlɔ ni,

english_verse: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.
translation_verse: buuvele ka ete-bu nwuna bananabi maatɛ na bɔdu-ma na buti-ma bɔƒala Katɔti anumi na Gibea Saul ɔma unengudi kemmo.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Ɔga Dawid lɛnɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ndubute-mii bekyuli bammɔ.”

english_verse: David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
translation_verse: Na Meƒiboset ɔni ndi Saul uwɔ na ɔdi Yonatan ubidi ni, Ɔga Dawid ɔ́ƒɔ-nwu ngba. Ɔsika Ɔga Dawid lɛnɔ ɔ́kpali ala úse kenye kadi na Unwoti anumi na anwu ku Saul ubidi Yonatan ntɛ.

english_verse: turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest. Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
translation_verse: Na Ɔga Dawid úti nkyuli maatɛ bamɛni úte Gibeonƒuɔ na bádu na béti-ma báƒala Unwoti anumi na kɔbi kɔdi lili. Na bádu bana ƒui básala na emeyi edeedi ani na bése kalɔ ku edula bɔƒɛ mmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain. The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
translation_verse: Ka úbo lɛni ni, Aia ubidi ulekubi Rispa úti adikpi ɔ́va lɛtakpɛ lɛlɔ mmɔ na ɔɔtɛ mmɔ ɔ́si edula ɔƒɛwi ɔmmɔ útédu ka ɔnantu úse kalɔ ɔɔna na ɔ́na úwi bekyuli bani na bádu béwi mmɔ lɛlɔ. Rispa ɔmɛni útaya na baasɛ iye beƒiebuo badi betuku bekyuli bammɔ ɔlɔna na ɔƒiiwi iye usien.

english_verse: Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. The people of Jabesh in Gilead had secretly taken the bodies away, but David found out what Saul's wife Rizpah had done, and he went to the leaders of Jabesh to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: ɔ́ya na bátáƒɔ Saul ku ubidi Yonatan ekubi na Yabes Gilead kadi bekyuli kudɔ. Na ekubi ammɔ ni, buyu na bekyuli bammɔ bétéyu-nya báƒami na kesii kani na bádu-ma báƒala Bet-San kuyeya uwi ɔni na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bádu Saul na Gilboa.

english_verse: David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, béti Saul ku ubidi Yonatan bátáva kesii kani na báva Saul ɔti ɔni baalɔ Kis kaƒiɔtɔ kemmo na Sela na Benyamin kalɔ kemmo. Na bábla lɛla biala aani kalɛ na Ɔga Dawid úbo-ma ɔda. Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Katɔti únu-ma bɔkpali na ɔ́nu kalɔ kammɔ ƒui kɔnyana. Israelƒuɔ Békpoku Ƒilistiƒuɔ

english_verse: There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
translation_verse: Kekpo bamba kani násɔ kálɛ na kesii kani baalɔ Gat ni, ɔnana bonwu ɔdi ɔ́si Raƒa kaba kemmo ɔni na ubo enu animi aku aku. Na lɛgba lɛnɔ lɛni kani, anwuɔsu ana ƒui ebo aavlanyɔ-ine.

english_verse: One time David got very tired when he and his soldiers were fighting the Philistines.
translation_verse: Na uwi bamba ni, Israelƒuɔ ku Ƒilistiƒuɔ básɔ báta kekpo. Na Ɔga Dawid ɔsiaku nwuna bekpone na bésie bétékpoku Ƒilistiƒuɔ. Lɛlɔ líbetu-nwu na ɔ́nɔ geen.

english_verse: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ukpone ɔni baalɔ Yisbi-Benob na ɔdi Raƒa kaba kemmo ubi ni, ɔda lɛtula lɛdi na nwuna lili lɛmmɔ lɛti pɛ unu wabla aani antabi akyami anyɔ unu. Na ɔda kewii kawɔdi na ɔ́su ka wadu Ɔga Dawid.

english_verse: But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine. David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
translation_verse: Nsu Seruia ubidi Abisai úkeli na úbaƒɔ Dawid na ɔ́tu ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́va kalɔ na ɔ́du-nwu. Mmɔ na Israelƒuɔ bákpali ala bése kenye ka basɔ beleti Dawid balada bana kekpokɔ kadi kalɛ na bana asogya weni.

english_verse: There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, kekpo kásɔ kálɛ na Israelƒuɔ ku Ƒilistiƒuɔ ntɛ na kesii kani baalɔ banii Gob. Na mmɔ ukpone ɔni baalɔ Sibekai na ɔdi Husani ɔ́du ukpone Saƒ ɔni nási Raƒa kaba kemmo.

english_verse: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Na kekpo bamba kani na Israelƒuɔ ku Ƒilistiƒuɔ básɔ békpo na Gob ni, ɔnana ɔni baalɔ Elhanan nádu Goliat ɔni ndi Gatni na ɔda lɛtula lɛni lili akpɛlɛ nébomo aani bedine abuala. Na Elhanan ɔti ndi Yaare-Oregim na ɔ́si Betlehem.

english_verse: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
translation_verse: Ka ɔ́kya uudumi Israelƒuɔ na ɔɔpii-ma ni, Dawid ɔnwani Simei ubidi Yonatan úbebo-nwu ɔ́va kalɔ na ɔ́du-nwu.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
translation_verse: Nkyuli ine bani ƒui na bádu mmɔ badi bekyuli bani na báta katɔ na badi Raƒa kaba kemmo bebi na bási Gat na Dawid ku nwuna bekpone enu kemmo na bákɛ kukpi.

english_verse: You rescued me from enemies who were hateful and too powerful for me.
translation_verse: Údie-mi ɔ́lɛku mina bekisine kpakplaa bani muukisi-mi enu kemmo na ɔ́ƒɔ-mi na bani nábi básiaku-mi na bebo ɔkplu betulo-mi kudɔ.

english_verse: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
translation_verse: Dawid údie ɔnu ɔdi úte Unwoti uwi ɔni na údie-nwu ɔ́lɛku nwuna bekisine ƒui ku Saul enu kemmo.

english_verse: I will praise you, Lord, and I will honor you among the nations.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, O mina Unwoti, ndubumwi-ɔ lɛnyi na kadi bekyuli ƒui akɔ. Na ndubudie agya lɛkɔliku-ɔ lɛnyi katɔ.

english_verse: Our Lord and our God, you are my mighty rock, my fortress, my protector.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Unwoti unye ute-mi aani lɛtakpɛ ku katamikukɔ kani lɛlɔ na líkpo kama.

english_verse: You are the rock where I am safe. You are my shield, my powerful weapon, and my place of shelter. You rescue me and keep me safe from violence.
translation_verse: Ɔɔgyumana-mi aani ukyuli ɔni muunye teetile-mi na ɔɔƒɔ́-mi, na ɔɔyá na mɔɔkɛ́ ɔyikun. Anwu nédie-mi na balalane enu kemmo.

english_verse: I praise you, our Lord! I prayed to you, and you rescued me from my enemies.
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti, awɔ námanku bumwi. Lɛ́kpali-ɔ na édie-mi álɛku mina bekisine enu kemmo.

english_verse: Death, like ocean waves, surrounded me, and I was almost swallowed by its flooding waters.
translation_verse: “Kukpi kabuli kényimi-mi. Na útiku-mi úselaku aani kalɛ ketu kani néyi keeminime.

english_verse: Ropes from the world of the dead had coiled around me, and death had set a trap in my path.
translation_verse: Kukpi abuli ényimi-mi. Na kunye-mi anumi kɔɔkya-mi liƒu uwi ndi uwi.

english_verse: I was in terrible trouble when I called out to you, but from your temple you heard me and answered my prayer.
translation_verse: Na mina lɛbibo lɛmɛni kemmo ni, lɛ́kpali mina Unwoti Katɔti na líwulo lɛ́kya-nwu nnii ubunku-mi. Na únu-mi lɛdi ɔ́siku nwuna kakpakɔ na úbunku-mi.

english_verse: Earth shook and shivered! The columns supporting the sky rocked back and forth. You were angry
translation_verse: “Kalɔ kemodi kaagyú taawɔ na kaatɔ́ kpakpaakpa. Na abi ƒui ákunku, ɔsika Unwoti úti kɔnyi.

english_verse: and breathed out smoke. Scorching heat and fiery flames spewed from your mouth.
translation_verse: Uyɔ ɔ́lɛ-nwu enwu kemmo na ogya lɛnɔ ɔ́lɛ-nwu kenye kemmo ɔ́kyula ala. Na ogya agyabi ani náƒɔ ogya geen sɔsɔ aasí taabayu.

english_verse: You opened the heavens like curtains, and you came down with storm clouds under your feet.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́lɛmi katɔ na ɔ́yu úbo kalɔ na liƒlukutu lɛ́ƒɔ-nwu lɛgba kalɔ ƒui na ɔ́bla suu.

english_verse: You rode on the backs of flying creatures. You appeared with the wind as wings.
translation_verse: Na ulie ɔtu udu ɔdi mbo avwi na baalɔ-nwu Kerub lɛlɔ na úveyi ɔ́yu úbo.

english_verse: Darkness was your tent! Thunderclouds filled the sky, hiding you from sight.
translation_verse: Na lɛdisa libi-nwu lɛlɔ aani awu. Na liƒlukutu lɛni némini na lise suu lɛ́ka lɛ́mana-nwu na lɛ́bɛla-nwu.

english_verse: Fiery coals lit up the sky in front of you.
translation_verse: Nwuna bɔda bɔlɛ ku bukeye bɔni nédie lɛlɔ kayaa kaabwɛ ogya taalɛ mmɔ.

english_verse: You roared at the sea, and its deepest channels could be seen. You snorted, and the earth shook to its foundations.
translation_verse: Ɔ́bɔku ɛpu na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni mɔɔlɛ́-nwu enwu ɔ́ya na ɛpu ɔmmɔ kalɔ kátina nwaa na kalɔ kemmo atabi ɔka údie lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You reached down from heaven, and you lifted me from deep in the ocean.
translation_verse: “Ɔkɛnku nwuna ɔyikun lɛlɔ na úbedie-mi ɔ́lɛku ligyu ntu bɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: On the day disaster struck, they came and attacked, but you defended me.
translation_verse: Mina bekisine bénye báda-mi ka nkya ɔgbankpi kemmo ɔsu. Nsu Unwoti údie-mi, ɔsika nwuna lɛlɔ na líkpo kama.

english_verse: When I was fenced in, you freed and rescued me because you love me.
translation_verse: Údie-mi bana akɔ únyene kanwaadikɔ na lɛ́kɛ bɔnwuna, ɔsika mina lɛlɔ lɛɛda-nwu ebiti.

english_verse: You are good to me, Lord, because I do right, and you reward me because I am innocent.
translation_verse: “Unwoti ɔ́bla-mi lɛƒɔndia, ɔsika nsiaku-nwu kama siin na úse-mi kɔdɛ, ɔsika likpidi lɛdi lɛɛɛda-mi.

english_verse: I do what you want and never turn to do evil.
translation_verse: Mɔɔdi Unwoti ɔda bubo lɛlɔ. Na ńtedeyi ńtalɛ nwuna ulu lɛlɔ na lɛ́ƒiɔ-nwu.

english_verse: I keep your laws in mind and never turn away from your teachings.
translation_verse: Ngyi nwuna ɔda bubo ƒui na ńtedie ɔdi atu.

english_verse: I obey you completely and guard against sin.
translation_verse: Ɔgyi kalɛ na nda lɛlɔ siin na ńtabla likpidi lɛdi.

english_verse: You have been good to me because I do right; you have rewarded me for being innocent by your standards.
translation_verse: Unwoti úse-mi kɔdɛ, ɔsika mɔɔbla ala siin na ɔgyi ka likpidi liiibo-mi kayi.

english_verse: With all who are sincere you are sincere, but you treat the unfaithful as their deeds deserve.
translation_verse: Na bani mɔɔsia bana ablala anu ni, awɔ lɛnɔ aasia ala anu teete-ma. Na bani na balásia bana ablala anu ni, aaní-ma kɔtu na bana ablala kenye.

english_verse: You rescue the humble, but you look for ways to put down the proud.
translation_verse: Aaƒɔ́ bekyuli bani muuboku lɛlɔ kalɔ, nsu bani mɔɔtalaku lɛlɔ katɔ na balábu ni, eeboku-ma kalɔ.

english_verse: Our Lord and God, you are my lamp. You turn darkness to light.
translation_verse: O Blɔti, awɔ nda-mi ukpo na uléni. Na kesii kani nse-mi suu ƒui kékeye.

english_verse: Your way is perfect, Lord, and your word is correct. You are a shield for those who run to you for help.
translation_verse: “Katɔti lilu ƒui lise kede kede. Na ɔkɔ biala uuubo-nwu kemmo. Ɔdi lɛgyumanala ute bekyuli bani nátamiku-nwu.

english_verse: You alone are God! Only you are a mighty rock.
translation_verse: Na ɔma lɛnɔ ndi Katɔti ɔmmɔ si ɔɔɔdi Blɔti? Ɔsika anwu kani ndi lɛtakpɛ lɛni lɛlɔ na bula kama kekpo.

english_verse: You are my strong fortress, and you set me free.
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti mɔɔtu-mi akpagya ɔkɛnku nwuna ɔyikun lɛlɔ. Na ɔɔmɛnɛ kuƒi siin teete-bu.

english_verse: You make my feet run as fast as those of a deer, and you help me stand on the mountains.
translation_verse: Ɔ́ya na mina lɛgba lɛ́yu ɔkplu aani akwa. Na ɔɔtɔnku-mi taavinku ulu siin lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You teach my hands to fight and my arms to use a bow of bronze.
translation_verse: Na anwu mɔɔtina-mi kekpo kɔkwɛ ƒui kalɛ lɛkana lɛda kataminta kani mbo ɔkplu geen.

english_verse: You alone are my shield, and by coming to help me, you have made me famous.
translation_verse: O Unwoti, awɔ mɔɔgyumana-mi na aaƒɔ́-mi ngba. Na áya na lɛ́ƒɔ lɛnyi ɔkɛnku ƒula ɔyikun bonwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You clear the way for me, and now I won't stumble.
translation_verse: Ábwɛ mina kasiakɔ éte-mi na kábɛbɛ na ńtagbanta ńteduo mina bekisine enu.

english_verse: I kept chasing my enemies until I caught them and destroyed them.
translation_verse: “Lɛ́bi lɛ́siaku-ma kama úti útédu ka lɛ́siaku-ma. Na ńtenwini kama útédu uwi ɔni na lɛ́yila-ma udu.

english_verse: I destroyed them! I stuck my sword through my enemies, and they were crushed under my feet.
translation_verse: Líbo-ma líwi kalɔ ɔni na basɔ balákana bɔta na kesii kani na batɛ na mina lɛgba akɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: You helped me win victories and forced my attackers to fall victim to me.
translation_verse: Átu-mi akpagya ku ƒula ɔyikun na lísie kekpokɔ. Na áya na lɛ́di mina bekisine ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You made my enemies run, and I killed them.
translation_verse: Na áya na lɛ́bɔku mina bekisine na békeli bátɔlɔ. Na bekyuli bani muukisi-mi ƒui áya na lɛ́yila-ma udu.

english_verse: They cried out for help, but no one saved them; they called out to you, but there was no answer.
translation_verse: Báva bákpali ka ukyuli ɔdi ubaƒɔ-ma, nsu ɔdi uuubo na ɔƒɔ-ma. Na bákpali Unwoti muedi, nsu útakpete-ma.

english_verse: I ground them to dust, and I squashed them like mud in the streets.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na lɛ́kɔ-ma lɛ́bla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ aani ɔtumu ɔni na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ uuti taatɔlɔku. Na lɛ́tu-ma lídie aani aba ntéwi ulu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You rescued me from my stubborn people and made me the leader of foreign nations, who are now my slaves.
translation_verse: “Áƒɔ-mi álɛku batuɔkplune enu kemmo. Na áya na línwini kadi bekyuli ƒui ɔtɔnkune. Na kadi bekyuli bani na lɛɛɛgyi kudii mɛni muedi ni, awɔ Unwoti áya na bakya-mi kalɔ.

english_verse: They have lost all courage and from their fortresses they come trembling.
translation_verse: Na bálɛ bási bana kɔbɛkɔ bébo ku liƒu, ɔsika básɔ beeebo lɛnunsia lɛdi.

english_verse: You are the living Lord! I will praise you! You are a mighty rock. I will honor you for keeping me safe.
translation_verse: “Bɛya bumwi Unwoti ɔni nli uwi ndi uwi. Anwu ndi mina lɛtakpɛ lɛni lɛlɔ na nkpo. Ndubo-nwu lɛnyi katɔ bɔkɔliku, ɔsika anwu mɔɔƒɔ́-mi.

english_verse: You took revenge for me, and you put nations in my power.
translation_verse: Anwu muudie mina bekisine kasi teete-mi. Na anwu mɔɔyá na kadi bamba bekyuli baakya eli kalɔ teete-mi.

english_verse: You protected me from violent enemies, and you made me much greater than all of them.
translation_verse: Unwoti údie-mi ɔ́lɛku mina bekisine enu kemmo. Na úti-ma ɔ́kya-mi lɛgba kalɔ. Na ɔ́gyumana-mi ɔ́siku bakantankpine kudɔ.

english_verse: You give glorious victories to your chosen king. Your faithful love for David and for his descendants will never end.
translation_verse: Awɔ náya na Dawid ƒula ɔga ɔƒunadi ɔɔdi nwuna bekisine lɛlɔ geen. Na éti ƒula bɔyɔ bɔni naaavumana kudii éte anwu ɔni na ése likpo mmɔ ku nwuna bawɔ úsela uwi ƒui.”

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord has told me what to say.
translation_verse: “Unwoti Kɔyu kɔ́tɛmi kɔ́siaku-mi lɛlɔ na kuna etemila asia-mi unyemi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Our Mighty Rock, the God of Jacob, told me, “A ruler who obeys God and does right
translation_verse: Israel Katɔti ɔni ndi lɛtakpɛ lɛni lɛlɔ na békpo kama násu-mi ɔnini, ‘Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔdi bekyuli lɛlɔ na ulu siin lɛlɔ, na ɔɔyia Katɔti na ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na ɔ́sia ɔɔdi bekyuli lɛlɔ ni,

english_verse: I have ruled this way, and God will never break his promise to me. God's promise is complete and unchanging; he will always help me and give me what I hope for.
translation_verse: “Na geen ni, lɛni na nda lɛlɔ na mina kaduli líte Katɔti. Ɔsika úti bunyimi bɔni ndanku uwi ƒui úte-mi, ɔni na nwuna kenye kelékulo iye wavumana lɛnɔ. Na ɔdubɔƒɔ ute-mi uwi ƒui, na ɔbla ala ani na muuvele-nwu ute-mi.

english_verse: But evil people are pulled up like thornbushes. They are not dug up by hand,
translation_verse: Nsu bekyuli bekpidi ni, badubo-ma bɔgyu budie bana kenyekɔ aani liyu livo, ɔsika baaadi lɛla lɛni na bada bakya lɛkɔkɔ.

english_verse: but with a sharp spear and are burned on the spot. The Three Warriors (
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ukyuli ɔni magyu liyu medie lɛnɔ ɔlɛka ɔnu ka ɔda atula ku abuala ani na ɔdubuti ɔda-nya udie ute na bakyula kɔnakunwi.”

english_verse: except Eleazar. He killed Philistines until his hand was cramped, and he couldn't let go of his sword. When Eleazar finished, all the Israelite troops had to do was come back and take the enemies' weapons and armor. The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
translation_verse: Anwu nénye na úteebeyi Ƒilistiƒuɔ bammɔ taadu útédu ka nwuna kɔnu kɔ́sinsi na nwuna animi ágoglo áda kewii kammɔ lɛlɔ. Na Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na bádi-ma lɛlɔ geen na limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na Israelƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ bénwini bábasiaku Eleasa kama na beedie Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone bani na ɔ́du mmɔ lɛlɔ ala.

english_verse: and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was the commander of the Thirty Warriors, but he still did not become one of the Three Warriors.
translation_verse: Na kalɛ na baabu-nwu na bekpone ɛtɛ bammɔ akɔ ɔsu na úbenwini bana ɔtɔnkune. Nsu uuubunku bekpone benengu ɛtɛ kpakplaa bammɔ akɔ.

english_verse: These are the names of David's warriors: Ishbosheth the son of Hachmon was the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle, he killed
translation_verse: Na Dawid basiakune kpakplaa bani ndi-nwu bayikune geen ndi Yoseb-Basebet ɔni ndi Tahkemonni na ɔdi bekpone batɔnkune bammɔ unengu. Na anwu nádu nkyuli eti leevu-ɛku na kekpo kenwi kemmo.

english_verse: The next one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite. One time when the Philistines were at war with Israel, he and David dared the Philistines to fight them. Every one of the Israelite soldiers turned and ran,
translation_verse: Na ɔbambadi ɔni nsia-nwu kama ɔdi Ahohini ɔni baalɔ Dodo ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Eleasar. Na ɔdi Dawid bekpone batɔnkune ɛtɛ bammɔ akɔ unwi ɔni nényeku-nwu na bénye básiaku Ƒilistiƒuɔ bani násala lɛlɔ na békpoku-ma uwi ɔni na Israel kadi bekyuli bátɔlɔ kama.

english_verse: but Shammah stood in the middle of the field and killed the Philistines. The crops were saved, and the Lord gave Israel a great victory.
translation_verse: Nsu Sama anwu útenwini kama mmomu únye kalɔ kammɔ kemmo na úkpoku-ma na úbeyi Ƒilistiƒuɔ ɔ́du geen na ɔ́ƒɔ-ka. Na Unwoti ɔ́ya na ɔ́di-ma lɛlɔ geen.

english_verse: One year at harvest time, the Three Warriors went to meet David at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
translation_verse: Ka edula ɔƒɛwi údu ni, bekpone benengudi avlaatɛ bammɔ akɔ ɛtɛ badi bébo Dawid kudɔ na Adulam lɛtakpɛ ubu kesii kani na ɔ́kya. Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone kasala bammɔ lɛnɔ bábla keliekɔ na Reƒaiƒuɔ Kɔwɛ kemmo na beli mmɔ.

english_verse: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in his fortress,
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na Dawid ɔkya kabɛkɔ kagyumanadi geen. Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone bakya Betlehem.

english_verse: and he was very thirsty. He said, “I wish I had a drink from the well by the gate at Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ni, utukwɛ úbo ɔɔda Dawid geen na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ao, si bɔkɛ na ndubɔkɛ ntu lɛsiku libiɔ lɛni nkya Betlehem ɔma ɔban kayakun kenye na lɛni ni, nka ɔdia geen!”

english_verse: The Three Warriors sneaked into the Philistine camp and got some water from the well near Bethlehem's gate. But after they brought the water back to David, he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as a sacrifice
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bekpone ɛtɛ kpakplaa bammɔ bábɛ béduo Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ kesii kani na benye baagyumana mmɔ na bétédu ntu libiɔ lɛni na Betlehem ɔban kayakun kenye mmɔ béboku-nwu. Nsu Dawid útani-mu. Mmomu úti-mu úbo úwi kalɔ úvele Katɔti.

english_verse: and said to the Lord, “I can't drink this water! It's like the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.” The Three Warriors did these brave deeds. The Thirty Warriors (
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su ɔnini, “O Katɔti, naaakana ntu bɔmɛni bɔni. Na si lɛ́ni-mu ni, na use aani bekyuli bani béti bana ngba bése na lɛla lɛmɛni lɛlɔ ubugya ɔdi na mɔɔni.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu, Dawid úni ka ɔ́ni ntu bɔmmɔ. Na kayi buse ala amɛni na bekpone ɛtɛ bamɛni bábla na báƒɔ lɛnyi.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔnana ɔni baalɔ Yohaiada na ɔ́si Kabseel ɔma ni, ubo ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Benaia. Ubi ɔmɛni ɔ́di ukpone geen na ɔ́du Moabƒuɔ bekpone kpakplaa inyɔ bani mbo ogya geen. Lɛni kani na ɔ́du gyata na ubu ɔdi kemmo na limeyi lɛdi na etubankɛ áƒɔ kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Another time, he killed an Egyptian, as big as a giant. The Egyptian was armed with a spear, but Benaiah only had a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
translation_verse: Ɔ́du Egyipteni ukpone unengudi ɔdi. Na ina ka Egyipteni ɔmmɔ ɔda kewii gyɔlɔɔ kadi ni, ligyiiku lɛdi kani na Benaia ɔda útásiaku-nwu na úƒie nwuna kewii kammɔ ɔ́ƒɔ na úti ɔ́tu-nwu ɔ́du.

english_verse: Benaiah did these things. He never became one of the Three Warriors, but he was just as famous as they were and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. David made him the leader of his bodyguard.
translation_verse: Na nwuna lɛnyi lɛ́kɔ lítulo bekpone avlaatɛ bammɔ. Nsu béteti-nwu lɛnyi bétebunku bekpone ɛtɛ bammɔ. Na Dawid ɔ́ya na anwu mɔɔnu nwuna bagyumanane lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and said, “Your Majesty! Why have you come to see me?” David answered, “I've come to buy your threshing place. I have to build the Lord an altar here, so this disease will stop killing the people.”
translation_verse: Na uye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi nébo na mina Unwoti ɔga ákɔ ami ƒula kabla ɔblane lɛlɔ lɛni?” Amu na Dawid údie kenye ɔnini, “Líbo nnii mbeye ƒula kakpa kamɛni na lɛtu lɛkpabi lite Unwoti Katɔti na buvele-nwu na ɔlɛ ku kukpi kɔmɛni kuse kama na bekyuli bammɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: They went to Gilead and to Kadesh in Syria. Then they went to Dan, Ijon, and on toward Sidon.
translation_verse: Na bésie Gilead ku Tahtim-Hodsi kalɛkɛ na bétédu Dan-Yaan ku Sidon amadɔ.

english_verse: So David told Joab and the army officers, “Go to every tribe in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north all the way south to Beersheba, and count everyone who can serve in the army. I want to know how many there are.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su Yoab ɔni ntɔnku bekpone bammɔ ɔnini, “Távi Israel adua ammɔ ƒui akɔ ɔsi Dan útédu Beer-Seba na enweni bana ƒui anyi na lɛti bana bumomo.”

english_verse: But when David refused to change his mind, Joab and the army officers went out and started counting the people.
translation_verse: Na ka ɔga útenu kalɔ ka ɔvumana nwuna kasusu ɔsu ni, Yoab ku nwuna bekpone benengu bammɔ bésie na bátáka Israel kadi bekpone bammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: They crossed the Jordan River and began with Aroer and the town in the middle of the river valley. From there they went toward Gad and on as far as Jazer.
translation_verse: Ka bávia Yordan Ketu ni, báda keliekɔ na Aroer na bási mmɔ bésela ɔma ɔni nkya kɔwɛ ntɛntɛ útédu Gad kalɛkɛ úsela Yaser kakɛ.

english_verse: After they had gone through the whole land, they went back to Jerusalem. It had taken them
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na básia kalɔ kammɔ kemmo ƒui bávi báwɔlɔ ni, bénwini bésie Yerusalem na abuli yaalenwi ku emeyi aavlanyɔ kawɔlɔkɔ.

english_verse: Araunah looked and saw David and his soldiers coming up toward him. He went over to David, bowed down low,
translation_verse: Ka Arauna ɔ́nu úmene ka Ɔga Dawid ku nwuna kabla bablane bási badubo ni, ɔ́babla ɔ́lɛ úbasaku-nwu na úboku lili kalɔ buɛɛ úti anumi úbi kalɔ úte Ɔga Dawid.

english_verse: David saw the angel killing everyone and told the Lord, “These people are like sheep with me as their shepherd. I have sinned terribly, but they have done nothing wrong. Please, punish me and my family instead of them!” David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place (
translation_verse: Ka Dawid ɔ́nu Katɔti ɔtu ɔni mɔɔdú bekyuli bammɔ ni, ɔ́su Unwoti Katɔti ɔnini, “Ami ndi ukyuli ɔni nábla likpidi lɛmmɔ na bamɛni ama ni, baƒonu na badi. Bi na ama bábla? Ya na ƒula kukpi kɔtu bɔni bɔmmɔ bubo ami ku mina kaduli bekyuli lɛlɔ mmomu.”

english_verse: After everyone had been counted, David realized he had done wrong. He told the Lord, “What I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Lord, please forgive me.”
translation_verse: Ka Dawid ɔ́wɔlɔ bekyuli bammɔ bɔka ƒui ni, ɔ́nu ka ɔ́ƒiɔ na ɔ́su Katɔti ɔnini, “Lɛla lɛni na lɛ́bla lɛdi adɔlɔla ku likpidi bonwu. Unwoti, buvele, ti kyiɛ-mi.”

english_verse: Before David even got up the next morning, the Lord had told David's prophet Gad
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni asa na Dawid wata kadi kegye ni, Unwoti úuti litemi ɔ́kya Kenye Udiene Gad ɔni mɔɔnu ala taasu Dawid kenye.

english_verse: to take a message to David. Gad went to David and told him: You must choose one of three ways for the Lord to punish you: Will there be seven years when the land won't grow enough food for your people? Or will your enemies chase you and make you run from them for three months? Or will there be three days of horrible disease in your land? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God, who sent me.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Gad úbo na úbasu Dawid lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Aayɔ́ ka kɔka kubo kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ akwa atɛ? Munuu bina bekisine na aayɔ́ ka babɔku-mii abuli atɛ sɔɔn na basiaku-mii? Munuu ɔlɛ ukpidi kpakplaa na aayɔ́ ka ubo bina kadi bekyuli lɛlɔ emeyi atɛ? Ti-nwu kasusu na asu-mi lɛni na áƒuna na ntásu Unwoti Katɔti ɔni nátala-mi.”

english_verse: David was really frightened and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid ɔ́su ɔnini, “Liƒu bonwu lɛla lɛdi mɛni, na kayi kaakpulu-mi. Nu, si Unwoti ɔlati ɔ́ni-bu kɔtu ni, ɔdia utulo, ɔsika ɔɔnu kɔnyana na ɔdia utulo ka liduo bekyuli lɛkɔkɔ.”

english_verse: Araunah said, “Take whatever you want and offer your sacrifice. Here are some oxen for the sacrifice. You can use the threshing-boards and the wooden yokes for the fire.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Arauna ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Lɛla biala na aawia ni, ti-ni ƒaa na eti akpa. Aanu ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku kudenkɛ kɔni lɛlɔ muubó edula ebi ku ligyii lɛni mɔɔbala ɔmantɛ bakɔ bammɔ ti bla ekyweni ƒaa.

english_verse: Take them—they're yours! I hope the Lord your God will be pleased with you.”
translation_verse: Ami Arauna líti lɛla biala muute awɔ mina ɔga na muuvele Unwoti Katɔti nnii ƒula lɛlɔ lɛda-nwu kubiti.”

english_verse: But David answered, “No! I have to pay you what they're worth. I can't offer the Lord my God a sacrifice that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing place and the oxen for
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui ni, Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su Arauna ɔnini, “Oowo! Ulebo-nwu kemmo lɛni, ɔdi ka lɛƒɔ kayu kadi na kakpa kammɔ lili. Ɔsika naaakana akpala adi bɔbla bute mina Unwoti Katɔti na ńtebile lɛla lɛdi ami ɔlati.” Anwuɔsu Dawid ɔ́ƒɔ mmɔ úye ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ bammɔ sika ɔƒualadi ebi antabi akyami anyɔ unu.

english_verse: Then he built an altar for the Lord. He offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. The Lord answered the prayers of the people, and no one else died from the terrible disease.
translation_verse: Ɔga Dawid ɔ́tu lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ úte Unwoti na mmɔ na ɔ́bla akpala bɔkyula ɔdi ku unwi bɔbla akpala úte Katɔti. Na ɔmmɔ kama Unwoti Katɔti lɛnɔ akpala ammɔ áƒɔ-nwu anu ɔsu únu-ma buvele na ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ kenye kékulo.

english_verse: King David was now an old man, and he always felt cold, even under a lot of blankets.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́bi na nwuna akwa éesie anumi geen ni, si bébi-nwu ala dɛ muedi ni, lɛlɔ lilábla-nwu gugungu.

english_verse: His officials said, “Your Majesty, we will look for a young woman to take care of you. She can lie down beside you and keep you warm.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu nwuna kabla bablane básu-nwu banini, “Ati, ya na bɔwia ugblebi ɔdi bute-ɔ na ubelie-ɔ kudɔ na utaanu-ɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔdubɔtɛ-ɔ kudɔ na ɔma-a lɛlɔ na lɛlɔ lɛdubutaaƒɔ-ɔ ogya.”

english_verse: They looked everywhere in Israel until they found a very beautiful young woman named Abishag, who lived in the town of Shunem. They brought her to David, and she took care of him. But David did not have sex with her. Adonijah Tries To Become King
translation_verse: Na ugblebi ɔni mɔɔdia bɔnu mɛni ɔɔtɛ ɔga ɔmmɔ kudɔ na ɔɔnu-nwu lɛlɔ, nsu anwu ku ɔga ɔmmɔ bétesie lɛlɔ kudɔ aani ɔnana ku uleku kalɛ kudii. Adonia Ɔ́wia Ka Ukpo Ɔƒɔ Lɛga Liboku Lɛmmɔ

english_verse: Adonijah was the son of David and Haggith. He was Absalom's younger brother and was very handsome. One day, Adonijah started bragging, “I'm going to make myself king!” So he got some chariots and horses, and he hired
translation_verse: Na okloƒu ɔbuni ɔni mɔɔdia bɔnu geen mɛni nsia Absalom kama, nsu ɔti Dawid úteye-nwu kudii ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na aabla udu ɔni na aabla mɛni?”

english_verse: Adonijah himself was afraid of what Solomon might do to him, so he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
translation_verse: Nsu ka Adonia ɔɔyia Salomo ɔsu ni, úsie na útébo ɔ́da bebuo ese ani nlɛ lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Adonijah met with Joab the son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest and asked them if they would help him become king. Both of them agreed to help.
translation_verse: Amu na Adonia ku Seruia ubidi Yoab ku ɔkpane Abiatar bása lili na bénye Adonia kama.

english_verse: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's bodyguards all refused.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔkpane Sadok ku Yoiada ubidi Benia ku Kenye Udiene Natan ku Simei ku Rei ku Dawid ɔgyumanane geen ama bátablaku Adonia unwi.

english_verse: Adonijah invited his brothers and David's officials from Judah to go with him to Crawling Rock near Rogel Spring, where he sacrificed some sheep, cattle, and fat calves.
translation_verse: Amu na Adonia ɔ́du baƒonu ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku bana bebi bani nélie lɛmwi na Sohelet lɛkpabi lɛni nde En-Rogel kudɔ. Na ɔ́lɔ ɔga bebi bammɔ ƒui bani ndi nwuna banwani ku Yudaƒuɔ banana bani ndi bagadine benengu,

english_verse: But he did not invite Nathan, Benaiah, David's bodyguards, or his own brother Solomon.
translation_verse: nsu útalɔ Katɔti Kenye Udiene Natan ku Benaia ku ɔnwani Salomo iye ɔga ɔgyumanane geen ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: When Nathan heard what had happened, he asked Bathsheba, Solomon's mother: Have you heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has made himself king? But David doesn't know a thing about it.
translation_verse: Amu na Natan úye Salomo uni Bat-Seba ɔnini, “Étenu tɔ ka Hagit ubidi Adonia úbenwini ɔga ɔni na ɔti Dawid ɔɔɔgyi-nwu kemmo lɛla lɛdi?

english_verse: You and your son Solomon will be killed, unless you do what I tell you.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ya na lɛlɛ-ɔ kalɛ na aƒɔ awɔ ku ƒ'ubidi Salomo ngba.

english_verse: While you are still talking to David, I'll come in and tell him that everything you said is true.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na amu akya aatɛmiku ɔga ɔmmɔ ni, ndubɔda bɔlɛ mmɔ na lɛlɛ lɛla lɛni na ásu mmɔ ugyii.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was in his bedroom where Abishag was taking care of him because he was so old. Bathsheba went in
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu úsie útánu ɔga ɔni náabi lɛlɔ mmɔ na nwuna ɔtɔ kemmo, na kesii kani na Abisag ɔni ndi Sunamni ɔmmɔ ɔɔnu-nwu lɛlɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: and bowed down. “What can I do for you?” David asked.
translation_verse: Amu na Bat-Seba ɔ́lɛ akɔnkɔ na úboku lɛlɔ kalɔ. Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi na aayɔ́ ka lɛbla lite-ɔ?”

english_verse: Bathsheba answered: Your Majesty, you promised me in the name of the Lord your God that my son Solomon would be the next king.
translation_verse: Amu na Bat-Seba ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Mina ati, awɔ ɔlati nése kenye éte ami ƒula kabla ɔblane na Unwoti Katɔti anumi anini, ‘Ƒ'ubidi Salomo ndubɔdi lɛga si nsɔ liiibo. Na anwu ndubulie mina liboku lɛlɔ.’

english_verse: But Adonijah has already been made king, and you didn't know anything about it.
translation_verse: Nsu Adonia nébenwini ɔga, na awɔ mina ati ku ɔga aaagyi-nwu kemmo lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: He sacrificed a lot of cattle, calves, and sheep. And he invited Abiathar the priest, Joab your army commander, and all your sons to be there, except Solomon, your loyal servant.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́du ɔmantɛ bakɔ pii ku baƒonu bani nélie lɛmwi na ɔ́lɔ ɔga bebi bananabi ƒui ku ɔkpane Abiatar ku ukpone ɔtɔnkune Yoab, nsu útalɔ ƒula kabla ɔblane Salomo.

english_verse: Your Majesty, everyone in Israel is waiting for you to announce who will be the next king.
translation_verse: Mina ati ɔga, Israelƒuɔ ƒui anumi asia-a lɛlɔ ka benu basiku-ɔ kudɔ ukyuli ɔni ndubulie-ɔ liboku lɛlɔ aani ɔga kalɛ si asɔ eeebo.

english_verse: If you don't, they will say that Solomon and I have rebelled. They will treat us like criminals and kill us as soon as you die.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔsu-ɔ ka si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, si awɔ bula ɔga énwini kama na átátɛ ƒula bati bene kudɔ ni, ami ku mina ubidi Salomo badubo-bu kalala bɔbla aani bekyuli bekpidi kalɛ.”

english_verse: Someone told David that he was there, and Nathan came in. He bowed with his face to the ground
translation_verse: Amu na básu ɔga ɔmmɔ banini, “Kenye Udiene Natan unye mɛni ɔɔwia.” Anwuɔsu úsie ɔga ɔmmɔ anumi na úboku lɛlɔ kalɔ buɛɛ na ɔ́kya-nwu lili kalɔ.

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, did you say that Adonijah would be king?
translation_verse: Amu na Natan ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Mina ati ku ɔga, awɔ néte bɔti ka si eeebo ni, Adonia ndubulie-ɔ lɛgaboku lɛlɔ utaadi lɛga?

english_verse: Earlier today, he sacrificed a lot of cattle, calves, and sheep. He invited the army commanders, Abiathar, and all your sons to be there. They are already eating and drinking and shouting, “Long live King Adonijah!”
translation_verse: Mɔɔsu-ɔ ka ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni usien ni, úsie útádu ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku bana bebi bani nélie lɛmwi kaduɛ ku baƒonu na ɔ́lɔ ɔga bebi bananabi ƒui ku bekpone ɔtɔnkune ku ɔkpane Abiatar na anwu ku-ma básala belie baadi na baaní ɔƒaani, na baasu banini, ‘Ɔga Adonia ulie ngba gyɔlɔɔ!’

english_verse: But he didn't invite me or Zadok the priest or Benaiah or Solomon.
translation_verse: Nsu ami ƒula kabla ɔblane ku ɔkpane Sadok ku Yoiada ubidi Benaia ku ƒula kabla ɔblane Salomo abu útalɔ-bu.

english_verse: Did you say they could do this without telling the rest of us who would be the next king? Solomon Becomes King
