translation_verse: Mina ati ku ɔga, muuye-ɔ nnii lɛni na álɛ ugyii ése ka abla na atáya na ƒula kabla bablane bati ukyuli ɔni na ɔlɛka ulie ƒula liboku lɛlɔ utaadi lɛga si asɔ eeebo?” Dawid Úse Salomo Lɛga

english_verse: David said, “Tell Bathsheba to come here.” She came and stood in front of him.
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bɛlɔ Bat-Seba bite-mi.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu uleku ɔmmɔ úbenye ɔga anumi ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Then he said, “The living Lord God of Israel has kept me safe. And so today, I will keep the promise I made to you in his name: Solomon will be the next king!”
translation_verse: kenye kani na lɛ́kpali Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti lɛ́su-ɔ líse ni, ndubɔnu ka lɛ́di-ka lɛlɔ ɔmwi kadi. Na kenye kammɔ ndi ka ƒ'ubidi Salomo ndubɔdi lɛga si nsɔ liiibo na ulie mina liboku lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and said, “Your Majesty, I pray that you will live a long time!”
translation_verse: Amu na Bat-Seba ɔ́lɛ akɔnkɔ na úti anumi úbi kalɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Muuvele nnii, mina ati Ɔga Dawid ulie ngba gyɔlɔɔ!”

english_verse: Then David said, “Tell Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah to come here.” When they arrived,
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Dawid ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bɛlɔ ɔkpane Sadok ku Kenye Udiene Natan ku Yoiada ubidi Benaia bite-mi.” Amu ka bekyuli bammɔ bébenye ɔga ɔmmɔ anumi ni,

english_verse: he told them: Take along some of my officials and let Solomon ride my own mule to Gihon Spring.
translation_verse: ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛkpanku mina kabla bablane bɛda na bɛgyu mina ubidi Salomo bɛsia ami ɔlati mina ɔpɔnkɔ lɛlɔ na bɛkpanku-nwu bisienku Gihon.

english_verse: When you get there, Zadok and Nathan will pour olive oil over Solomon's head to show that he is the new king of Israel. Then order someone to blow a trumpet and tell everyone to shout, “Long live King Solomon!”
translation_verse: Na mmɔ ni, bɛya ɔkpane Sadok ku Kenye Udiene Natan bewi-nwu lili nnɔmii na bese-nwu likpo ka anwu ndi Israelƒuɔ ɔga. Na bavwi kɔkpɛɛ na bebo kudu momoomo basu banii, ‘Ɔga Salomo ulie ngba gyɔlɔɔ!’

english_verse: Bring him back here, and he will take my place as king. He is the one I have chosen to rule Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, na bitiku-nwu biboku, ɔsika anwu na ɔlɛka ubelie-mina liboku lɛlɔ utaadi lɛga na mina kenye. Na lɛ́bla-nwu Israel ku Yuda lɛlɔ ɔdine.”

english_verse: Benaiah answered, “We will do it, Your Majesty. I pray that the Lord your God will let it happen.
translation_verse: Amu na Yoiada ubidi Benaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Muuvele nnii Unwoti Katɔti ɔya na lɛla lɛni na mina ati ku Ɔga ɔ́su mɛni libo-nwu kemmo lɛni!

english_verse: The Lord has always watched over you, and I pray that he will now watch over Solomon. May the Lord help Solomon to be an even greater king than you.”
translation_verse: Na kalɛ na Unwoti úlieku awɔ mina ati ku ɔga ni, ulieku Salomo lɛnɔ lɛni kani. Na ɔya na nwuna lɛgadi libomo litulo mina Ɔga Dawid lɛdi muedi!”

english_verse: Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah left and took along the two groups of David's special bodyguards. Solomon rode on David's mule as they led him to Gihon Spring.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔkpane Sadok ku Kenye Udiene Natan ku Yoiada ubidi Benaia ku Keretiƒuɔ ku Peletiƒuɔ bésie na bátágyu Salomo básia Ɔga Dawid ɔpɔnkɔ lɛlɔ na bákpanku-nwu bésienku Gihon.

english_verse: Zadok the priest brought some olive oil from the sacred tent and poured it on Solomon's head to show that he was now king. A trumpet was blown and everyone shouted, “Long live King Solomon!”
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane Sadok úduo úsie Unwoti Adi Kevo kedee kammɔ kemmo na útéti ebuo lise lɛdi kemmo na nnɔmii buwi ɔ́lɛku. Na úwilimi nnɔmii bɔmmɔ úwi Salomo lili úse-nwu likpo. Na ɔmmɔ kama bávwi kakpɛɛ kadi momoomo na bekyuli ƒui báva momoomo banini, “Ɔga Salomo ulie ngba gyɔlɔɔ!”

english_verse: Then they played flutes and celebrated as they followed Solomon back to Jerusalem. They made so much noise that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui basiaku-nwu kama na beebó kudu ku ebiti na baavwi atoloyii na kalɔ kammɔ kaakunku ɔkɛnku kudu kɔmmɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: Adonijah and his guests had almost finished eating when they heard the noise. Joab also heard the trumpet and asked, “What's all that noise about in the city?”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Adonia ku bekyuli bani na ɔ́lɔ mmɔ badaku bɔdi ku bɔni taawɔlɔ ni, bénu kakpɛɛ kammɔ kudu. Amu na Yoab úye ɔnini, “Bi kudu mɔɔlɛ́ na ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni kemmo lɛni?”

english_verse: Just then, Jonathan son of Abiathar came running up. “Come in,” Adonijah said. “An important man like you must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Na asa na utaawɔlɔ lɛla lɛmɛni buye ni, ɔkpane Abiatar ubidi Yonatan ɔ́da ɔ́lɛ mmɔ. Amu na Adonia ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Bo beduo ɔtɔ, ɔsika bɔgyi ka adi ukyuli ɔni na áƒɔ kuye geen. Na bɔgyi lɛnɔ ka ada kɔtɛ kɔbuni aduboku.”

english_verse: Jonathan answered: No, I don't! David has just announced that Solomon will be king.
translation_verse: Amu na Yonatan údie kenye ɔnini, “Oowo, lɛɛɛda kɔtɛ kɔbuni munu munu! Anwu ndi ka bula Ɔga Dawid úse Salomo lɛga.

english_verse: Solomon rode David's own mule to Gihon Spring, and Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and David's special bodyguards went with him. When they got there, Zadok and Nathan made Solomon king. Then everyone celebrated all the way back to Jerusalem. That's the noise you hear in the city.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane Sadok ku Kenye Udiene Natan béwi-nwu nnɔmii lili aani ɔga kalɛ na Gihon. Na ka bási mmɔ ni, bakɛ beebó ebiti kudu kɔni mɔɔku taasia kama na ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo na anwu ndi kudu kɔni na eenú.”

english_verse: And listen to this! David's officials told him, “We pray that your God will help Solomon to be an even greater king!” David was in his bed at the time, but he bowed
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔga bakutine bammɔ bébo bébete Ɔga Dawid mmo na básu-nwu banini, “Buuvele ƒula Katɔti bɔnii ɔya na Salomo ɔƒɔ lɛnyi na lɛkɔ katɔ litulo ƒula lɛdi ƒui. Na nwuna lɛgadi libomo litulo ƒula lɛdi. Amu na Dawid úboku lɛlɔ kalɔ na kesii kani na ɔtɛ mmɔ na ɔ́kya lili kalɔ úte Katɔti

english_verse: and prayed, “I praise you, Lord God of Israel. You have made my son Solomon king and have let me live to see it.”
translation_verse: na ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Bemwi Unwoti Israel Katɔti, ɔsika ɔ́ya na mina anumi ánu ukyuli ɔni ndubulie mina liboku lɛlɔ na mina kama ɔmwi kadi.’ ”

english_verse: Adonijah's guests shook with fear when they heard this news, and they left as fast as they could.
translation_verse: Amu ka Adonia bekyuli bani nlie mɔɔdiku-nwu mmɔ bénu kɔtɛ kɔmmɔ ni, liƒu lɛ́da-ma. Na báta na bégyingya.

english_verse: Someone told Solomon, “Adonijah is afraid of you and is holding onto the corners of the altar. He wants you to promise that you won't kill him.”
translation_verse: Amu na básu Salomo banini, “Adonia ɔɔyia Ɔga Salomo. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu úkeli na útébo ɔda bebuo ese ani nlɛ lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ na ɔɔsu ɔnini, ‘Bɛya na Ɔga Salomo use kenye ute-mi ɔmwi ka uleti nwuna kewii uládu ami nwuna kabla ɔblane.’ ”

english_verse: Solomon answered, “If Adonijah doesn't cause any trouble, I won't hurt him. But if he does, I'll have him killed.”
translation_verse: Amu na Salomo údie-nwu kenye ɔnini, “Si údie lɛlɔ ɔ́tina ka ɔdi ukyuli ɔbuni iye ɔda kasusu kabuni ni, ina nwuna lili linwini linwi muedi lilétuku kalɔ. Nsu si kasusu kekpidi na ɔda bɔdi ni, na ɔdubukpi.”

english_verse: Then he sent someone to the altar to get Adonijah. After Adonijah came and bowed down, Solomon said, “Adonijah, go home.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Salomo ɔ́tala banana badi na bétetiku-nwu basiku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ mmɔ béboku. Na Adonia úbalɛ akɔnkɔ na Ɔga Salomo anumi. Ɔmmɔ kama Salomo ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ta na eteesie kaduli.”

english_verse: Not long before David died, he told Solomon:
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Dawid ɔ́nu ka nwuna kukpi kúude ni, úti bɔlɛ bɔmɛni úte ubidi Salomo.

english_verse: My son, I will soon die, as everyone must. But I want you to be strong and brave.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Mina uwi údu ka lisie ati bene kudɔ na kalɔ ɔgyu lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu mɔɔlɛ-ɔ nnii kya ɔkplu na atina lɛlɔ ka ɔnana na adi.

english_verse: Do what the Lord your God commands and follow his teachings. Obey everything written in the Law of Moses. Then you will be a success, no matter what you do or where you go.
translation_verse: Na adi ƒula Unwoti Katɔti etemila lɛlɔ ku ala ani ƒui na únyimi na nwuna ɔda bubo kemmo na bénweni bákya Mose ɔda bubo ɔku kemmo. Na ataasia-nya anu na asia nwuna ulu lɛlɔ kalɛ na lɛla biala na aabla lɛtɛku-ɔ. Na keyi kayɔdi kasiaku-ɔ na kesi kesii na akɛ.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always faithfully obey the Lord. If you do, he will keep the solemn promise he made to me that someone from our family will always be king of Israel.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ndubɔya na Unwoti wadi nwuna kenye kani na úse-mi lɛlɔ ɔni na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Si ƒula bawɔ básia bana keliela anu na baadi mina etemila lɛlɔ na basiaku-mi kama siin ku bana kɔyu ku kayi ƒui ni, bana akɔ na ubi ɔnanabi ɔdubɔsi na ulie Israelƒuɔ lɛgaboku lɛlɔ uwi biala kemmo.’ ”

english_verse: Solomon, don't forget what Joab did to me by killing Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of Israel's army. He killed them as if they were his enemies in a war, but he did it when there was no war. He is guilty, and now it's up to you to punish him
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Salomo ɔnii, “Awɔ ɔlati ágyi lɛla lɛni na Seruia ubidi Yoab ɔ́bla ami ku Israelƒuɔ bekpone inyɔ bani ndi Ner ubidi Abner ku Yeter ubidi Amasa. Ɔ́du-ma aani kekpo kenye benye, nsu ɔɔɔdi kekpo nálɛ. Na ubugya ɔmmɔ ɔma-nwu lɛlɔ na úsusu nwuna kavobi kabuli ku nwuna agbanvuo lɛlɔ.

english_verse: in the way you think best. Whatever you do, don't let him die peacefully in his old age.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ti ƒula lɛnunda na abla-nwu asia kalɛ na ɔ́manku. Nsu taya na ɔkɛ bɔnwuna bɔdi na utéduo kaƒiɔtɔ kemmo ku lili ƒuala.

english_verse: Be sure to do something about Shimei son of Gera from Bahurim in the territory of Benjamin. He cursed and insulted me the day I went to Mahanaim. But later, when he came to meet me at the Jordan River, I promised that I wouldn't kill him.
translation_verse: “Na enyimo Gera ubidi Simei ɔni nási Bahurim na Benyamin kɔdua kemmo. Anwu nákpali ewida etemila úwi-mi lɛlɔ kaduɛ limeyi lɛni na lísie Mahanaim. Na uwi ɔni na úbasiaku-mi na Yordan Ketudɔ ni, lɛ́kpali Unwoti lɛnyi líse kenye na lɛ́su-nwu nnini, ‘Lɛɛɛdubo-ɔ bɔdu ku kewii.’

english_verse: Now you must punish him. He's an old man, but you're wise enough to know that you must have him killed. David Dies
translation_verse: Nsu ɔƒɛni ni, sɔ tanu-nwu aani ukyuli ɔni na lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-nwu. Ngyi ka adi ukyuli ɔni na áda anu na adubɔnu lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka abla-nwu. Na aya na nwuna kuli ƒuala kɔmmɔ kɔsia ubugya lɛlɔ kuduo kaƒiɔtɔ kemmo.”

english_verse: he saddled his donkey and went after them. He found them and brought them back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Simei ɔ́ta na úti nwuna ɔpɔnkɔ na úsie Akis kudɔ na Gat ɔnii útáwia nwuna kabla bablane. Na útánu-ma na ɔ́kpanku-ma úboku.

english_verse: Joab's family will always suffer because of what he did, but the Lord will always bless David's family and his kingdom with peace.
translation_verse: Na bekpone bammɔ ubugya ni, muuvele ka ɔsia Yoab ku nwuna kaba bekyuli ƒui lili. Nsu Dawid ku nwuna kaba bekyuli ama ni, muuvele nnii Unwoti ɔya na nwuna kaduli ku nwuna lɛgadi lɛkɛ atu bɔyɔ uwi ƒui.”

english_verse: His son Solomon became king and took control of David's kingdom. Adonijah Is Killed
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Salomo úlie ɔti Dawid liboku lɛlɔ na nwuna lɛgadi línye kaduɛ. Salomo Lɛgadi Línye Kpakplaa

english_verse: One day, Adonijah went to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and she asked, “Is this a friendly visit?” “Yes.
translation_verse: Amu na Hagit ubidi Adonia úsie Salomo uni Bat-Seba kudɔ. Na Bat-Seba úye-nwu ɔnini, “Buɛɛ ulu na akɛ?” Amu na Adonia údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɛɛn, buɛɛ ulu na nkɛ o-o!”

english_verse: I just want to talk with you.” “All right,” she told him, “go ahead.”
translation_verse: Amu na Adonia ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Mbo lɛla lɛdi na lɛsu-ɔ.” Amu uleku ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Akana ataasu.”

english_verse: “You know that I was king for a little while,” Adonijah replied. “And everyone in Israel accepted me as their ruler. But the Lord wanted my brother to be king, so now things have changed.
translation_verse: Amu na Adonia úse kalɔ ɔnini, “Awɔ ɔlati ágyi ka nka Israel lɛgadi lɛdi mina lɛdi. Na Israelƒuɔ ƒui baanu anumi ka ami mabla bana ɔga. Nsu ala ébo énwini. Na béti lɛgadi lɛmmɔ béte mina ɔnwani. Ɔsika Unwoti kudɔ na ɔ́si.

english_verse: Would you do me a favor?” “What do you want?” Bathsheba asked.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni mɔɔyɔ́ ka ete-mi kebunku kamɛni, na muuvele-ɔ nnii teni.” Amu na Bat-Seba ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Akana ataasu.”

english_verse: “Please ask Solomon to let me marry Abishag. He won't say no to you.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Adonia úsie anumi na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Buvele nda-a, su Ɔga Salomo na uti Sunamni ulekubi ɔni baalɔ Abisag mmɔ ute-mi na liti.”

english_verse: “All right,” she said. “I'll ask him.”
translation_verse: Amu na Bat-Seba údie kenye ɔnini, “Awo, línu, na ndubɔtɛmi-ku ɔga lite-ɔ.”

english_verse: When Bathsheba went to see Solomon, he stood up to meet her, then bowed low. He sat back down and had another throne brought in, so his mother could sit at his right side.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Bat-Seba úsie Ɔga Salomo kudɔ ka útáda litemi lɛmmɔ ɔ́va-nwu anumi ni, ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́ta ka ɔ́nu-nwu na útasiaku-nwu na ɔ́kya-nwu lili kalɔ. Na ɔ́sɔ únwini útélie nwuna liboku lɛlɔ. Mmɔ na ɔ́ya na béti lɛgaboku bamba béboku uni na ɔ́ya na úlie-nwu kɔdianu kakɛ.

english_verse: Bathsheba sat down and then asked, “Would you do me a small favor?” Solomon replied, “Mother, just tell me what you want, and I will do it.”
translation_verse: Amu na uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔga ɔnini, “Buvele nda-a, ndanku lɛla blii lɛdi na mbevele-ɔ. Na teni-mi.” Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Mina uni, taasu na lɛɛɛdubo-ɔ buni.”

english_verse: “Allow your brother Adonijah to marry Abishag,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu úse kalɔ ɔnini, “Ti Sunamni ulekubi ɔni baalɔ Abisag mmɔ te ƒ'ɔnwani Adonia na uti.”

english_verse: Solomon said: What? Let my older brother marry Abishag? You may as well ask me to let him rule the kingdom! And why don't you ask such favors for Abiathar and Joab?
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Salomo údie uni kenye ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na aawia ka Abisag Sunamni ɔmmɔ utélieku Adonia? Ɔɔɔdi ɔmmɔ lɛti, ƒɔ lɛgadi lɛmmɔ lɛnɔ bunku-nwu gyɔnkɔ. Ɔsika na ulu biala lɛlɔ ni, mina ɔnwani unengudi na ɔdi. Na ngyi lɛnɔ ka ɔkpane Abiatar ku Seruia ubidi Yoab bebunku-nwu.”

english_verse: I swear in the name of the Lord that Adonijah will die because he asked for this! If he doesn't, I pray that God will severely punish me.
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Salomo ɔ́kpali Unwoti úse kenye ɔnini, “Si ńtaya na Adonia ukpi na uti nwuna ngba ɔƒɔ kayu na lɛla lɛni na úye mɛni ɔsu ni, na Katɔti ɔni-mi kɔtu biala na ɔɔyɔ́.

english_verse: The Lord made me king in my father's place and promised that the kings of Israel would come from my family. Yes, I swear by the living Lord that Adonijah will die today.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔni néti-mi úse mina ɔti Dawid liboku lɛlɔ, na úse kenye ka lɛgadi lɛmmɔ lɛdubuse lite ami ku mina kaba kemmo bebi úsela uwi ƒui lɛnyi kemmo ni, muusé kenye na Unwoti ɔmmɔ lɛnyi kemmo ka ndubɔya na badu Adonia ɔmwi ɔmɛni kani.”

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “go kill Adonijah.” So Adonijah died. Abiathar Is Sent Back Home
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Ɔga Salomo úbo Yoiada ubidi Benaia ɔda na útádu Adonia.

english_verse: Solomon sent for Abiathar the priest and said: Abiathar, go back home to Anathoth! You ought to be killed too, but I won't do it now. When my father David was king, you were in charge of the sacred chest, and you went through a lot of hard times with my father.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔkpane Abiatar ɔnini, “Nka ámanku ka lɛdu-ɔ. Nsu naaadu-ɔ ɔƒaani. Ɔsika awɔ néti Unwoti adaka átɔnku mina ɔti Dawid anumi, na awɔ ku-nwu bíbo abi bɛ́sala. Anwuɔsu nwini na asɔ eteesie ƒula kalɔ lɛlɔ na Anatot.”

english_verse: But I won't let you be a priest of the Lord anymore. And so the promise that the Lord had made at Shiloh about the family of Eli came true. Joab Is Killed
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Salomo ɔ́da Abiatar údie ɔkpane kabla kemmo, na kenye kani na Unwoti ɔ́su ɔ́siku Eli ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli lɛlɔ na Silo úbo úte lɛni.

english_verse: Joab had not helped Absalom try to become king, but he had helped Adonijah. So when Joab learned that Adonijah had been killed, he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
translation_verse: Ka Yoab únu lɛla lɛni na Ɔga Salomo ɔ́bla mmɔ ni, úkeli, ɔsika anwu ku Adonia nábla kasusu. Nsu anwu ku Absalom bátabla kasusu kadi. Amu na Yoab úkeli útéduo Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo na útéƒie bebuo ese ani nlɛ lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́da.

english_verse: When Solomon heard about this, he sent someone to ask Joab, “Why did you run to the altar?” Joab sent back his answer, “I was afraid of you, and I ran to the Lord for protection.” Then Solomon shouted, “Benaiah, go kill Joab!”
translation_verse: Amu ka básu Ɔga Salomo ka Yoab úkeli útéduo Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo na unye lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ ni, Salomo ɔ́su Benaia ɔnini, “Teesie na atáƒiɛmi-nwu ava kalɔ!”

english_verse: Benaiah went to the sacred tent and yelled, “Joab, the king orders you to come out!” “No!” Joab answered. “Kill me right here.” Benaiah went back and told Solomon what Joab had said.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Benaia útéduo Unwoti Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo mmɔ na ɔ́su Yoab ɔnini, “Ɔga ɔnini, ‘Lɛ bo!’ ” Amu na Yoab údie kenye ɔnini, “Oowo! Neeebo! Mɔɔyɔ́ ka likpi mɛni kani.” Mmɔ na Benaia útásu ɔga ɔnini, “Lɛni na Yoab údie kenye úte-mi.”

english_verse: Solomon replied: Do what Joab said. Kill him and bury him! Then my family and I won't be responsible for what he did to Abner the commander of Israel's army and to Amasa the commander of Judah's army. He killed those innocent men without my father knowing about it. Both of them were better men than Joab. Now the Lord will make him pay for those murders.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔdubɔya na ɔ́ƒɔ ubugya ɔni na úwi kalɔ mmɔ kayu. Ɔsika útasu mina ɔti Dawid útese asa na úteti nwuna kewii ɔ́du Ner ubidi Abner ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ ukpone ɔtɔnkune ku Yeter ubidi Amasa ɔni lɛnɔ ndi Yudaƒuɔ ukpone ɔtɔnkune. Na bekpone bamɛni báƒɔ kuye betulo Yoab ɔni nádu-ma mmɔ ɔlati.

english_verse: Benaiah went back and killed Joab. His body was taken away and buried near his home in the desert.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yoiada ubidi Benaia úsie na útaƒiɛmi Yoab ɔ́du na mmɔ. Na béti-nwu bátáva anwu ɔlati kalɔ na ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo.

english_verse: Solomon put Benaiah in Joab's place as army commander, and he put Zadok in Abiathar's place as priest. Shimei Is Killed
translation_verse: Na ɔga úti kenyekɔ kani na Yoab únye na bekpone akɔ úte Yoiada ubidi Benaia. Na ɔ́ya Sadok úti ɔkpane Abiatar keliekɔ.

english_verse: Solomon sent for Shimei and said, “Build a house here in Jerusalem and live in it. But whatever you do, don't leave the city!
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔga ɔ́ya na bálɔ Simei béte-nwu na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Awɔ ɔlati tu kaduli na Yerusalem na asɔ elie-ka kemmo. Nsu talɛ mmɔ tesie kesi kesii.

english_verse: If you ever cross Kidron Valley and leave Jerusalem, you will be killed. And it will be your own fault.”
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛni na adubɔlɛ na atávia Kidron Kɔwɛ ni, adubukpi. Na ƒula ubugya ɔdubɔsia awɔ ɔlati lili.”

english_verse: About three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to King Achish in Gath. When Shimei found out where they were,
translation_verse: Na akwa atɛ kama ni, Simei kabla bablane inyɔ békeli bésie Gat Ɔga Maaka ubidi Akis kudɔ. Amu na básu Simei banini, “Ƒula kabla bablane bakya Gat.”

english_verse: Someone told Solomon that Shimei had gone to Gath and was back.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni básu Ɔga Salomo ka Simei ɔ́lɛ Yerusalem na úsie Gat na ɔ́sɔ únwini úbo ni,

english_verse: Solomon sent for him and said: Shimei, you promised in the name of the Lord that you would never leave Jerusalem. I warned you that you would die if you did. You agreed that this was fair, didn't you?
translation_verse: Ɔga Salomo ɔ́tala na bálɔ Simei béboku. Na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Ńtaya na ákpali Unwoti na ése kenye kadi? Na libo-ɔ ɔda kpakplaa lɛnɔ ka limeyi lɛni na adubɔlɛ Yerusalem esie kesii bamba kadi ni, adubukpi na édie kenye anini, ‘Lɛla lɛni na ásu-mi mɛni lɛdia na ndubɔdi-ni lɛlɔ?’

english_verse: You have disobeyed me and have broken the promise you made to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na bi ɔsu na átadi kenye kani na ákpali Unwoti ése ku mina ɔda ɔni líbo-ɔ lɛlɔ?”

english_verse: I know you remember all the cruel things you did to my father David. Now the Lord is going to punish you for what you did.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Simei ɔnini, “Awɔ ɔlati agyi na ƒula kayi kemmo ala ekpidi ani na ábla mina ɔti Dawid. Ɔƒɛni Unwoti ɔdubɔya na aƒɔ ekpidi ammɔ kayu.

english_verse: But the Lord will bless me and make my father's kingdom strong forever.
translation_verse: Nsu Ɔga Salomo anwu ni, ɔdubute-nwu kusɛ kusɛ. Na Dawid lɛgadi lɛdubunye kpakplaa na Unwoti anumi uwi ƒui.”

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “kill Shimei.” So Shimei died. Solomon was now in complete control of his kingdom.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔga úbo Yoiada ubidi Benaia ɔda na ɔ́ƒiɛmi-nwu ɔ́du. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu lɛgadi lɛmmɔ línye kpakplaa na Salomo enu kemmo.

english_verse: At that time, there was no temple for worshiping the Lord, and everyone offered sacrifices at the local shrines.
translation_verse: Na bana kadi bekyuli ni, bamu baakpá na abi eli, ɔsika bátatu Unwoti kakpakɔ tɔ.

english_verse: I'll also give you what you didn't ask for. You'll be rich and respected as long as you live, and you'll be greater than any other king.
translation_verse: Lɛnɔ ni, ndubute-ɔ akɛla ku ɔbu ɔni na éteye muedi kalɛ na ƒula ngba emeyi ƒui beleti ɔga biala balákɔku-ɔ.

english_verse: One night while Solomon was in Gibeon, the Lord God appeared to him in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
translation_verse: Na Gibeon mmɔ ni, Unwoti údie lɛlɔ ɔ́tina Salomo na kɔna kemmo usien ɔdi. Na Katɔti ɔ́su Salomo ɔnini, “Vele-mi lɛla biala na aayɔ́ na ndubuti-ni lite-ɔ.”

english_verse: Solomon answered: My father David, your servant, was honest and did what you commanded. You were always loyal to him, and you gave him a son who is now king.
translation_verse: Amu na Salomo údie kenye ɔnini, “Édie kɔnyana bɔnu geen átina ƒula kabla ɔblane ɔni ndi mina ɔti Dawid. Ɔsika ɔ́bla ala ulu lɛlɔ na úse siin na nwuna kayi kemmo na ƒula anumi. Na ésie anumi na eedie kɔnyana bɔnu bɔmɛni taatina-nwu, na éte-nwu anwu ɔlati kaƒɔ ubi anii úlie nwuna liboku lɛlɔ ɔmwi kadi.

english_verse: Lord God, I'm your servant, and you've made me king in my father's place. But I'm very young and know so little about being a leader.
translation_verse: “O mina Unwoti Katɔti, ɔƒɛni ni, áya na ami ƒula kabla ɔblane línwini ɔga na mina ɔti Dawid kenyekɔ. Nsu ɔnamu kani ndi, na lɛɛɛgyi kalɛ na lɛbla kabla kamɛni udu lɛvinku.

english_verse: And now I must rule your chosen people, even though there are too many of them to count.
translation_verse: Na nnye-ɔ anumi mɛni aani ƒula kabla ɔblane na ƒula kadi bekyuli baƒunadi pii bamɛni akɔ bani na ukyuli biala ulakana-ma bɔka.

english_verse: Please make me wise and teach me the difference between right and wrong. Then I will know how to rule your people. If you don't, there is no way I could rule this great nation of yours.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu te ami ƒula kabla ɔblane kayi kani na liti lɛda ƒula bekyuli bamɛni na lɛnu lɛbuni ku likpidi lɛti. Ɔsika si átabla ɔmɛni ni, ɔma ndubɔkana ƒula bekyuli pii bamɛni udu bɔda?”

english_verse: God said: Solomon, I'm pleased that you asked for this. You could have asked to live a long time or to be rich. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom to make right decisions.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Katɔti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ka ɔmɛni na éye-mi na éteye ngba gyɔlɔɔ iye akɛla étete lɛlɔ iye aya ƒula bekisine ƒui bekpi, mmomu bɔwia na áwia ka ati bekyuli bammɔ bɔda siin ɔsu ni,

english_verse: If you obey me and follow my commands, as your father David did, I'll let you live a long time.
translation_verse: Na si ásia mina ulu lɛlɔ na ádi mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na ƒ'ɔti Dawid ɔ́bla ni, ndubute-ɔ ngba gyɔlɔɔ.”

english_verse: Solomon woke up and realized that God had spoken to him in the dream. He went back to Jerusalem and stood in front of the sacred chest, where he offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. Then Solomon gave a feast for his officials. Solomon Makes a Difficult Decision
translation_verse: Amu na Salomo ɔ́gyinya na ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka kɔna na úgye. Mmɔ ni, ɔ́sɔ únwini úsie Yerusalem na úténye Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ kudɔ. Na ɔ́bla bɔkyula ku unwi bɔbla akpala úte Unwoti. Ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́ya na bánwa adila kaduɛ na anwu ku kabla bablane bani mɔɔbla-nwu kabla na kaduli mmɔ bádi limeyi. Salomo Ɔ́tɛ Litemi Lɛnunda Kemmo

english_verse: One day two women came to King Solomon,
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, bayalɛ inyɔ badi bébo ɔga kudɔ na bébenye-nwu anumi.

english_verse: and one of them said: Your Majesty, this woman and I live in the same house. Not long ago my baby was born at home,
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bana kemmo unwi ɔ́su ɔnini, “Mina ati, uleku ɔni nnye-mi kudɔ mɛni ni, ami ku-nwu nli kaduli kenwi, na lɛ́wɔ na anwu ɔlati anumi.

english_verse: and three days later her baby was born. Nobody else was there with us.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛtɛdi kama ka lɛ́wɔ ubi ɔmmɔ ni, uleku ɔmɛni lɛnɔ ɔ́wɔ. Bula inyɔ kani nkya na ukyuli biala uuulie kaduli kammɔ asa na bɔ́wɔ.

english_verse: One night while we were all asleep, she rolled over on her baby, and he died.
translation_verse: “Na usien ni, uleku ɔmɛni ubidi úbekpi. Ɔsika ɔ́tɛ-nwu lɛlɔ ɔ́du.

english_verse: Then while I was still asleep, she got up and took my son out of my bed. She put him in her bed, then she put her dead baby next to me.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́ta usien lɛdibantɛ na úbagyu mina ubi ɔni ntɛ-mi kudɔ uwi ɔni na ami ƒula kabla ɔblane ntɛ mɔɔlɛɛ, na úti ɔ́va nwuna lɛnyii kudɔ. Na úti ɔni nékpi mmɔ lɛnɔ úbava mina lɛnyii kudɔ.

english_verse: In the morning when I got up to feed my son, I saw that he was dead. But when I looked at him in the light, I knew he wasn't my son.
translation_verse: Amu ka kadi kégye ni, lɛ́ta nnii muute mina ubi lɛnyii. Na ka mɔɔnu ni, na ubiwɔ ɔmmɔ úkpi. Ka lɛ́sia-nwu anu kaduɛ uwi ɔni na kadi kábla nwaa ni, lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka ɔɔɔdi ubi ɔni lɛ́wɔ mmɔ na ɔdi.”

english_verse: “No!” the other woman shouted. “He was your son. My baby is alive!” “The dead baby is yours,” the first woman yelled. “Mine is alive!” They argued back and forth in front of Solomon,
translation_verse: Amu na uleku ɔkladi ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Oowo! Ɔni nékpi mmɔ ndi ƒula ɔdi. Na ɔni nli ngba ndi mina ɔdi.” Nsu uleku udeedi ɔmmɔ unye kpakplaa na ɔɔsu ɔnini, “Oowo! Ɔni nékpi mmɔ ndi ƒula ɔdi na ɔni nli ngba ndi mina ɔdi.” Na lɛni bákya unyeƒi laa na ɔga anumi.

english_verse: Someone bring me a sword.” A sword was brought, and Solomon ordered,
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔga ɔ́su ɔnini, “Biti kewii bite-mi.” Anwuɔsu béti kewii béboku ɔga ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: “Cut the baby in half! That way each of you can have part of him.”
translation_verse: Amu na úbo ɔda ɔnini, “Bile ubiwɔ ɔni nli ngba mmɔ kemmo inyɔ na biti kakɛ bite unwi, na biti kakɛ kanyɔdi bite ɔkladi.”

english_verse: “Please don't kill my son,” the baby's mother screamed. “Your Majesty, I love him very much, but give him to her. Just don't kill him.” The other woman shouted, “Go ahead and cut him in half. Then neither of us will have the baby.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na uleku ɔni ngyi ka ubidi nli ngba mmɔ ni, kaƒɔ kákywi-nwu kéte ubidi na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Mina ati, buvele nda-a, ti ubi ɔmmɔ te-nwu, na batadu-nwu!” Nsu uleku unyɔdi ɔmmɔ anwu ɔnini, “Kudii! Bile-nwu kemmo inyɔ na ami ku-ɔ ƒui ɔdi ɔsɔ ulákɛ ubi ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: Solomon said, “Don't kill the baby.” Then he pointed to the first woman, “She is his real mother. Give the baby to her.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔga ɔ́da litemi lɛmmɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Biti ubiwɔ ɔni nli ngba mmɔ bite uleku udeedi ɔmmɔ na bitadu-nwu. Ɔsika ubi ɔmmɔ uni mmɔ.”

english_verse: Everyone in Israel was amazed when they heard how Solomon had made his decision. They realized that God had given him wisdom to judge fairly.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ ƒui bénu kalɛ na ɔga ɔ́tɛ litemi lɛmmɔ ɔ́vinku ni, báyia ɔga ɔmmɔ. Ɔsika bánu báti ka Katɔti lɛnunda na úti ɔ́tɛ litemi lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: Solomon chose twelve regional officers, who took turns bringing food for him and his household. Each officer provided food from his region for one month of the year.
translation_verse: Na Salomo ubo kɔlɛkɛ leevu-inyɔ aban bagadine na Israel kalɔ ƒui. Na ama mɔɔwia adila teeboku ɔga ku ɔga kaduli bekyuli. Na ɔlɛka ɔdi biala ɔwia kɔbuli kunwi adila na lɛkwa kemmo.

english_verse: These were the twelve officers: The son of Hur was in charge of the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Na bagadine bammɔ anyi ndi bamɛni. Ben-Hur ɔni mɔɔnu Eƒraim kalɛkɛ abi lɛma kalɛkɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The son of Deker was in charge of the towns of Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-Shemesh, and Elon-Beth-Hanan.
translation_verse: Na Ben-Deker mɔɔnu Makas ku Saalbim ku Bet-Semes ku Elon-Bet-Hanan lɛma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The son of Abinadab was in charge of Naphath-Dor and was married to Solomon's daughter Taphath.
translation_verse: Na Ben-Abinadab ɔni néti Salomo ubidi ulekubi Taƒat mɔɔnu Naƒat-Dor kalɛkɛ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The son of Geber was in charge of the town of Ramoth in Gilead and the villages in Gilead belonging to the family of Jair, a descendant of Manasseh. He was also in charge of the region of Argob in Bashan, which had
translation_verse: Na Ben-Geber mɔɔnu Ramot-Gilead kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ ku Manase ubidi Yair akpaklɔ lɛma lɛni nkya Gilead mmɔ ku Argob kalɔ kani nkya Basan kalɛkɛ. Na lɛma lɛmmɔ ƒui lɛdi liti ku leevu. Na bátu awodu bámana-nya. Na béti abuala egyiedi bábla-ni kɔyakun.

english_verse: Ahinadab son of Iddo was in charge of the territory of Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Na Ido ubidi Abinadab mɔɔnu Mahanaim lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Ahimaaz was in charge of the territory of Naphtali and was married to Solomon's daughter Basemath.
translation_verse: Na Ahimaas mɔɔnu Naƒtali lɛlɔ. Na anwu néti Salomo ubidi ulekubi Basmat.

english_verse: Baana son of Hushai was in charge of the territory of Asher and the town of Bealoth.
translation_verse: Na Husai ubidi Baana mɔɔnu Aser ku Alot lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was in charge of the territory of Issachar.
translation_verse: Na Parua ubidi Yehosaƒat mɔɔnu Isakar lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Shimei son of Ela was in charge of the territory of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Na Ela ubidi Simei mɔɔnu Benyamin lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Geber son of Uri was in charge of Gilead, where King Sihon of the Amorites and King Og of Bashan had lived. And one officer was in charge of the territory of Judah. The Size of Solomon's Kingdom
translation_verse: Na Uri ubidi Geber mɔɔnu Gilead kalɔ lɛlɔ ku Sihon ɔni ndi Amoriƒuɔ ɔga ku Og ɔni ndi Basanƒuɔ ɔga kɔlɔ lɛlɔ. Na anwu kani ndi aban ɔgadine na mmɔ ƒui. Beete Salomo Adila Limeyi Biala

english_verse: Solomon ruled every kingdom between the Euphrates River and the land of the Philistines down to Egypt. These kingdoms paid him taxes as long as he lived.
translation_verse: Na Salomo ɔ́di kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Ɔ́si Euƒrate Ketu ɔkɛ Ƒilisti útédu Egyipteƒuɔ ɔmii. Na kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ bekyuli beeyi kuyi teete Ɔga Salomo. Na bákya-nwu kalɔ nwuna ngba bulie uwi ƒui.

english_verse: Solomon ruled the whole region west of the Euphrates River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, and he was at peace with all of the countries around him.
translation_verse: Na úbo-ma ɔda ɔmɛni, ɔsika anwu mɔɔdi lɛgakɔdikɔ kɔni ƒui nkya ketu kammɔ ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ ɔ́si Tiƒsa úbedu Gasa lɛlɔ. Na bekyuli bákɛ atu bɔyɔ.

english_verse: Everyone living in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, was safe as long as Solomon lived. Each family sat undisturbed beneath its own grape vines and fig trees.
translation_verse: Na Salomo ngba bulie uwi ƒui ni, Yuda ku Israel ɔ́si Dan útédu Beer-Seba ni, bana ƒui bélie ku keyi buɛɛ na ɔdi biala ɔ́di nwuna adingyii mmo ebi ku atu bɔyɔ.

english_verse: Each of the twelve regional officers brought food to Solomon and his household for one month of the year. They provided everything he needed,
translation_verse: Na kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ banune ɔdi biala úti ɔ́sia lɛlɔ na uute ala ani ƒui na ɔga ku bekyuli bani muubo-nwu kudɔ taabadi baawia na kɔbuli kɔni na béle béte ɔdi biala kemmo na ɔdi útayaki lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: Solomon was brilliant. God had blessed him with insight and understanding.
translation_verse: Katɔti úte Salomo lɛnunda ku ala kemmo bɔnu taati ku lɛlati lɛni neeebo bɔkɔku aani kalɛ na ɛpu kɔnwinimi kuse kalɛ.

english_verse: He was wiser than anyone else in the world, including the wisest people of the east and of Egypt. He was even wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Mahol's three sons, Heman, Calcol, and Darda. Solomon became famous in every country around Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Na nwuna lɛnunda litulo ukyuli biala ku Etan ɔni ndi Esrahini lɛdi. Na ɔ́da anu utulo Heman ku Kalkol ku Darda bani ndi Mahol bebi. Na nwuna lɛnyi lígyingya lítédu kadi bamba lɛma lɛni nkya amadɔ mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: He could talk about all kinds of plants, from large trees to small bushes, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́tɛmi ɔ́siku egyii lidu lidu ngba lɛlɔ ɔ́si sida egyii ani nkya Lebanon ku alakpi ani baalɔ hisope na aakwɛ́ na awodu lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tina ala ɔ́siku bebuo ku baasɛ ku kɔkpaku ku bebuo bani mɔɔkpɛ́ kaƒɔ lɛlɔ lɛnɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Kings all over the world heard about Solomon's wisdom and sent people to listen to him teach.
translation_verse: Na kayawi baga ƒui baatala bekyuli na beesié teeténu Ɔga Salomo lɛnunda etemila ani na ɔɔtɛmi.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre had always been friends with Solomon's father David. When Hiram learned that Solomon was king, he sent some of his officials to meet with Solomon.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Hiram ɔni ndi Tiroƒuɔ ɔga únu ka béti Salomo bése ɔti Dawid keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ ni, ɔ́tala bekyuli ɔ́kya-nwu. Ɔsika anwu ku Dawid ntɛ búse kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ geen.

english_verse: The Lord God promised my father that when his son became king, he would build a temple for worshiping the Lord. So I've decided to do that.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu mɔɔyɔ́ ka lɛtu kakpakɔ lite mina Unwoti Katɔti. Lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su mina ɔti Dawid ɔnini, ‘Ƒula ubidi ɔni ndubulie-ɔ keliekɔ na ƒula liboku lɛlɔ ni, anwu ndubo mina kakpakɔ bɔtu.’

english_verse: I'd like you to send your workers to cut down cedar trees in Lebanon for me. I will pay them whatever you say and will even have my workers help them. We both know that your workers are more experienced than anyone else at cutting lumber.
translation_verse: “Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, bo ɔda na bekulo sida egyii kpakplaa ani na Lebanon mmɔ bete-mi. Na ƒula bekyuli ku mina badi babla kabla basala. Na kayu biala na ɔlɛka lɛƒɔ ƒula kabla bablane na kabla kamɛni lɛlɔ ni, ndubɔƒɔ-ka. Na awɔ ɔlati agyi ka buuubo bekyuli bani na bagyi egyii bɔda lɛlɔ kabla aani Sidonƒuɔ.”

english_verse: Hiram was so happy when he heard Solomon's request that he said, “I am grateful that the Lord gave David such a wise son to be king of that great nation!”
translation_verse: Amu ka Hiram únu Salomo kenye kamɛni ni, kubiti kɔ́da-nwu geen na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Bekyuli ƒui bemwi Unwoti ɔmwi kadi, ɔsika úte Dawid ubi ɔnundane ɔni na ɔdi kadi bekyuli bonwu bamɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Then he sent back his answer: I received your message and will give you all the cedar and pine logs you need.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Hiram lɛnɔ úti kenye kamɛni úmene Salomo ɔnini, “Lɛ́ƒɔ ƒula kenye kani na ásia-mi mmɔ. Na sida egyii ku egyii bamba etenku ani na aawia mmɔ ni, ndubute-ɔ ana ƒui.

english_verse: My workers will carry them down from Lebanon to the Mediterranean Sea. They will tie the logs together and float them along the coast to wherever you want them. Then they will untie the logs, and your workers can take them from there. To pay for the logs, you can provide the grain I need for my household.
translation_verse: Na ndubɔya na mina bekyuli bani etenku ammɔ basiku Lebanon bebedu ɛpu kɔtu na batɛ-nya bakya ɔkɔlɔ kemmo na beti basia ntu anumi na ɛpu lɛlɔ bebedu kesii kani na aawia-nya. Na si bédu mmɔ ni, mina bekyuli badubɔƒɛnimi etenku ammɔ, na ƒula bekyuli babla ɔkladi. Na lɛla lɛni mɔɔwia ka abla ndi ka eteete mina bekyuli adila.”

english_verse: assistants to keep track of the work and to supervise the workers.
translation_verse: ), na ama nkya abi eli beekú atabi ammɔ taanwi.

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise and made Solomon wise. Hiram and Solomon signed a treaty and never went to war against each other. Solomon's Workers
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́di nwuna linyese lɛlɔ ɔkɛnku lɛnunda lɛni na úte Salomo ɔsu. Na atu bɔyɔ bɔ́kya Hiram ku Salomo ntɛ kaduɛ na bana inyɔ bényimi unwi bɔbla kenye béte lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and he put Adoniram in charge of these workers. Solomon divided them into three groups of
translation_verse: Na úti Adoniram ɔnii utaanu-ma lɛlɔ. Na úle bekyuli bammɔ akpa atɛ, na lɛkpa biala baakya Lebanon kɔbuli kunwi. Na beenwíni teesie bana lɛma taatánwuna abuli anyɔ.

english_verse: He ordered the workers to cut and shape large blocks of good stone for the foundation of the temple.
translation_verse: Na Ɔga Salomo ɔda bubo kenye ni, bekyuli bammɔ béku atabi bálɛku kalɔ kemmo na bánwi atabi bonwu bonwu ammɔ na aadia bɔnu kalɛ na beti bakya kakpakɔ kammɔ awodu ɔka kalɔ.

english_verse: Solomon's and Hiram's men worked with men from the city of Gebal, and together they got the stones and logs ready for the temple.
translation_verse: Na Ɔga Salomo ku Hiram kabla bablane ku banana bani nási Gebal bánwi atabi ammɔ kalɛ na ɔdia kakpakɔ kammɔ bɔtu.

english_verse: Solomon's workers started building the temple during Ziv, the second month of the year. It had been
translation_verse: Ka Israelƒuɔ bálɛ Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ lɛkwa eti yaalenwi ku avlaatɛdi (

english_verse: The windows were narrow on the outside but wide on the inside.
translation_verse: Na údie ɔƒɛƒɛɛ eƒi ɔ́kya kakpakɔ kammɔ awodu atɔdi kemmo.

english_verse: Solomon put them next to each other in the most holy place. Their wings were spread out and reached across the room.
translation_verse: Na béti bebweyi bammɔ bálɛ katɔma kedee kammɔ kemmo. Na bana avwi ammɔ eli ásaku lɛlɔ na ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ntɛ, na ɔdi biala kɔvwi kɔkladi lili liitúku awodu ammɔ ɔvi ɔni ku ɔni.

english_verse: The roof of the temple was made out of beams and cedar boards. The workers finished building the outside of the temple.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Ɔga Salomo ɔ́tu kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ, na úti sida kugyii kpakplaa kɔmmɔ ɔ́bla lɛta ku kugyiikɛ úbi ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Along the sides and back of the temple, there were three levels of storage rooms. The rooms on the bottom level were just over two meters wide, the rooms on the middle level were over two and a half meters wide, and those on the top level were just over three meters wide. There were ledges on the outside of the temple that supported the beams of the storage rooms, so that nothing was built into the temple walls.
translation_verse: Na katutaasia ɔtɔ ɔlɔndi bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba bɔka maatɛ ku kakɛ. Na ɔni nkya ntɛ bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba bɔka yaalenwi. Na ɔtɔdi ƒui bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba bɔka leevu ku kakɛ. Na ubili bamba na básia ku lɛta bonwu bonwu bámana kakpakɔ kammɔ béte lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ kalɛ na balaƒuala kakpakɔ awodu ammɔ alati.

english_verse: Solomon did not want the noise of hammers and axes to be heard at the place where the temple was being built. So he gave orders for the workers to shape the blocks of stone at the quarry.
translation_verse: Na atabi ani na béti bátu kakpakɔ kammɔ ni, bánwi-nya básiku atabi kabwɛkɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, ukyuli biala ɔdi útenu lɛbuala lɛdi aani oloma iye libola lɛbuala bamba lɛdi lɛlɔ kabla kɔku na katukɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Storage rooms just over two meters high were all around the temple, and they were attached to the temple by cedar beams.
translation_verse: Na katutaasia lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ lɛdanku kakpakɔ kammɔ lɛ́mana, na sida lɛta kpakplaa ubili ɔni na básia mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔdi biala bɔkuku bɔdi lɛgba bɔka maatɛ ku kakɛ.

english_verse: The Lord told Solomon:
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Salomo ɔnini,

english_verse: The floor of the temple was made out of pine, and the walls were lined with cedar from floor to ceiling.
translation_verse: Na kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo awodu lɛlɔ ni, béti sida egyii bébo bámana ɔ́si kalɔ útédu lɛsa. Na béti egyii kpakplaa kugyiikɛ bámana ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kalɔ.

english_verse: The most holy place was in the back of the temple, and it was nine meters square. Cedar boards standing from floor to ceiling separated it from the rest of the temple.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́ya na béle kakpakɔ kammɔ kama kakɛ bábla katɔma, na bébo sida ligyii bɛbɛɛbɛ báda mmɔ ɔ́si kalɔ útédu lɛsa. Na kama kakɛ mmɔ kebo lɛgba bɔka avlaatɛ. Na mmɔ ndi Katɔti Katɔma Kedee.

english_verse: The inside walls were lined with cedar to hide the stones, and the cedar was decorated with carvings of gourds and flowers.
translation_verse: Na sida kugyiikɛ na béti bámana atabi ɔtɔ kemmo awodu ammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui bávi. Na bánwi kugyii ebi adi udu ku egyii anwula ani néebimi evete básia kugyiikɛ kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The sacred chest was kept in the most holy place.
translation_verse: Na báklibi katɔma kedee kammɔ kemmo, na kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo kesii kani na badubɔlɛ Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Solomon had two statues of winged creatures made from olive wood to put in the most holy place. Each creature was four and a half meters tall
translation_verse: Na béti nnɔ kugyiikɛ bánwi kubweyi inyɔ badi udu na bebo avwi bényene, na baalɔ-ma Kerub. Na ɔdi biala bɔkuku bɔdi lɛgba bɔka leevu-ɛlɔ. Na béti-ma bálɛ katɔma kedee kammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The creatures were also covered with gold.
translation_verse: Na béti sika ugyiedi bámana bebweyi inyɔ bammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The walls of the two rooms were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures.
translation_verse: Na ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ katɔma ku anumi ƒui ni, bánwi Kerub bebweyi bamɛni ku ebo ku egyii anwula ani néebimi lidu, bámana awodu ammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Even the floor was covered with gold.
translation_verse: Na katɔma ku ɔtɔ anumi ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kalɔ muedi ni, sika ugyiedi béti bámana.

english_verse: The two doors to the most holy place were made out of olive wood and were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures. The doors and the carvings were covered with gold. The door frame came to a point at the top.
translation_verse: Na kɔlɛmikɔ kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, bánwi Kerub bebweyi ku ebo ku anwula ani néebimi bámana. Na bebweyi ku ebo ku anwula ani néebimi ani bánwi bámana kɔlɛmikɔ kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, béti sika ugyiedi bámana ana ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The doors were covered with gold and were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures.
translation_verse: Na bánwi bebweyi ku ebo ku anwula ani néebimi bámana-ni lɛlɔ. Na béti sika ugyiedi bámana-ni lɛlɔ ƒui na kɔlɛmikɔ kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The inner courtyard of the temple had walls made out of three layers of cut stones with one layer of cedar beams.
translation_verse: Na kakpakɔ kaduli kemmo kowodu kɔni na bátu ni, básia atabi anwidi bámana kɔtɛ na bánwi sida ligyii bábla lɛta básia atabi ammɔ eli.

english_verse: Work began on the temple during Ziv, the second month of the year, four years after Solomon became king of Israel.
translation_verse: Na bése kalɔ ku kakpakɔ kammɔ bɔtu na kɔbuli kunyɔdi kɔni baalɔ Siw kemmo, na lɛkwa linedi lɛni Ɔga Salomo ɔɔdi lɛga.

english_verse: Seven years later the workers finished building it during Bul, the eighth month of the year. It was built exactly as it had been planned.
translation_verse: Na kɔbuli maanedi kɔni baalɔ Bul na lɛkwa leevu-linwidi kemmo ɔni na Ɔga Salomo ɔɔdi lɛga ni, ɔ́tu kakpakɔ kammɔ ƒui ɔ́wɔlɔ aani kalɛ na ɔ́bla kasusu úse. Na akwa maatɛ na Ɔga Salomo úti ɔ́tu Unwoti kakpakɔ kammɔ.

english_verse: ) This is a list of the bronze items that Hiram made for the Lord's temple:
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Salomo ɔ́tu nwuna ɔga kaduli, na akwa leevu-atɛ na úti ɔ́tu-ka.

english_verse: a large bowl; twelve bulls that held up the bowl;
translation_verse: Ɔ́bla ntu kewikɔ bonwu ku bakɔ leevu-inyɔ bani lɛlɔ na ntu kewikɔ kammɔ kenye.

english_verse: -centimeter strip, and there were four braces attached to the corners of each stand. The panels and the supports were attached to the stands,

translation_verse: Nsu ɔ́si ƒ'ɔti Dawid ɔsu ni, lɛɛɛdubo lɛgadi lɛmmɔ bɔƒɔ na ƒula ngba uwi. Mmomu, ndubɔƒɔ-ni lɛlɛku ƒula ubidi enu kemmo.

english_verse: When I do, I will still let him rule one tribe, because I have not forgotten that David was my servant and Jerusalem is my chosen city. Hadad Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
translation_verse: Na lɛɛɛdubo lɛgadi lɛmmɔ ƒui bɔƒɔ bɔlɛku-nwu enu kemmo. Mmomu, ndubɔya na kɔdua kunwi kubu kute-nwu ɔ́si mina kabla ɔblane Dawid ku Yerusalem ɔni na lɛ́ƒuna ɔsu.” Salomo Ɔ́kɛ Bekisine

english_verse: Hadad was from the royal family of Edom, and here is how the Lord made him Solomon's enemy:
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na Hadad ɔni nási Edom lɛgadi kemmo ɔ́ta na útékpoku Salomo.

english_verse: Hadad and his wife had a son named Genubath, and the queen let the boy grow up in the palace with her own children.
translation_verse: Na Tahpenes ɔnwani ulekubi ɔmɛni ɔ́wɔ ɔnanabi. Na ɔ́sia-nwu lɛnyi ɔnii Genubat. Na Tahpenes ɔ́tumini ɔnamu ɔmɛni na ɔga kaduli, na Genubat ku Ƒarao beli básala.

english_verse: When Hadad heard that David and Joab were dead, he said to the king, “Your Majesty, please let me go back to my own country.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Hadad únu na Egyipte ka Dawid úkpi, na Yoab ɔni ndi nwuna ukpone ɔtɔnkune lɛnɔ úkpi ni, Hadad ɔ́su Ɔga Ƒarao ɔnini, “Ya na nteesie mina ɔma.”

english_verse: “Why?” asked the king. “Do you want something I haven't given you?” “No, I just want to go home.” Rezon Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi na aawia-mi kudɔ mɛni na alakɛ, ɔsu na anii aatɔlɔ eteesie bina ɔma?” Amu na Hadad údie kenye ɔnini, “Ńtawia lɛla lɛdi ńtanɔ, nsu awɔ ya na nteesie!”

english_verse: Here is how God made Rezon son of Eliada an enemy of Solomon: Rezon had run away from his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔ́sɔ údie ukisine bamba ɔ́kya Salomo ɔni ndi Eliada ubidi Reson. Bukeli na okloƒu ɔmɛni úkeli ɔ́tɔlɔ nwuna unwoti ɔni baalɔ-nwu Hadad-Eser Sobaƒuɔ ɔga kudɔ.

english_verse: He formed his own small army and became its leader after David had defeated Hadadezer's troops. Then Rezon and his army went to Damascus, where he became the ruler of Syria and an enemy of Israel. Both Hadad and Rezon were enemies of Israel while Solomon was king, and they caused him a lot of trouble. The Lord Makes a Promise to Jeroboam
translation_verse: Na Reson ɔdi Israelƒuɔ ukisine uwi ɔni na Salomo uli ngba ƒui. Ɔsika Hadad lɛnɔ ɔ́kya lɛsɛ lɛdi. Anwuɔsu Reson ɔ́di lɛga na Siria na ɔdi ukisine ute Israelƒuɔ. Yerobeam Ɔ́ta Únye Salomo Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Jeroboam was from the town of Zeredah in Ephraim. His father Nebat had died, but his mother Zeruah was still alive. Jeroboam was one of Solomon's officials, but even he rebelled against Solomon.
translation_verse: Nabat ubidi Yerobeam ɔni ndi Ɔga Salomo kabla bablane unwi lɛnɔ ɔ́ta únye-nwu lɛlɔ. Na Yerobeam ɔmɛni ɔdi Eƒratni, na ɔ́si Sereda, na uni ɔdi ukpinele ɔni baalɔ Serua.

english_verse: Here is how it happened: While Solomon's workers were filling in the land on the east side of Jerusalem and repairing the city walls,
translation_verse: Kɔtɛ kɔmɛni ndanku kalɛ na ɔ́bla asa na Yerobeam ɔ́ta únye Ɔga Salomo lɛlɔ. Ɔga Salomo ɔ́sia ubili ɔ́bala ɔti Dawid ɔma unengudi awodu ammɔ ɔ́mana na úyile eƒi ani ƒui nkya-ku kemmo.

english_verse: Solomon noticed that Jeroboam was a hard worker. So he put Jeroboam in charge of the work force from Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Yerobeam ɔdi okloƒu ɔni na úbo ɔlɔkplu. Na uwi ɔni na Salomo lɛnɔ ɔ́ti kalɛ na ɔɔkya ɔyikun taabla kabla kogyoklo mmɔ ni, úti-nwu ɔ́bla Yoseƒ ɔtɔ bekyuli bani mɔɔbla kabla teete-nwu ɔtɔnkune.

english_verse: But Solomon will still rule one tribe, since he is the son of David my servant, and Jerusalem is my chosen city.
translation_verse: Nsu mina kabla ɔblane Dawid ku Yerusalem ɔma unengudi ɔni lɛ́ƒuna na Israel adua kemmo líte lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, ndubute Salomo kɔdua kunwi.

english_verse: “Solomon and the Israelites are not like their ancestor David. They will not listen to me, obey me, or do what is right. They have turned from me to worship Astarte the goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Ndubo ɔmɛni bɔbla, ɔsika béni-mi na bésie bátákpa Sidonƒuɔ baƒiɔ bani ndi Astarot ku Moabƒuɔ baƒiɔ Kemos ku Amonƒuɔ baƒiɔ bani ndi Milkom. Na bátasia mina ulu lɛlɔ iye babla ala ani nse siin na mina anumi iye badi mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na Salomo ɔti Dawid ɔ́bla kalɛ.

english_verse: “Solomon is David's son, and David was my chosen leader, who did what I commanded. So I will let Solomon be king until he dies.
translation_verse: “ ‘Nsu lɛɛɛdubo lɛgadi lɛmmɔ ƒui bɔƒɔ bɔsiku Salomo enu kemmo. Na lɛ́ɛya na ɔ́di lɛga na nwuna ngba emeyi ƒui kemmo ɔ́si mina kabla ɔblane Dawid ɔni na lɛ́ƒuna ɔsu ku kalɛ na ɔ́di mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: Then I will give you ten tribes to rule,
translation_verse: Na ndubɔƒɔ lɛgadi lɛmmɔ lɛ́siku ubidi enu kemmo na lite-ɔ adua leevu.

english_verse: but Solomon's son will still rule one tribe. This way, my servant David will always have a descendant ruling in Jerusalem, the city where I have chosen to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Na liti kɔdua kunwi lite ubidi kalɛ na asogya ɔkya mina kabla ɔblane Dawid lɛkɔkɔ na unye-mi anumi na Yerusalem uwi biala, ɔsika mmɔ na lɛ́ƒuna ka mina lɛnyi lɛsia.

english_verse: “You will be king of Israel and will rule every nation you want.
translation_verse: Nsu awɔ amu ni, ndubuti-ɔ na adi lɛga na Israel kalɛ biala na ƒula kayi kaayɔ́.

english_verse: I'll help you if you obey me. And if you do what I say, as my servant David did, I will always let someone from your family rule in Israel, just as someone from David's family will always rule in Judah. The nation of Israel will be yours.
translation_verse: Na si ádi ɔda biala mebo-ɔ lɛlɔ, na ásia mina ulu lɛlɔ ábla ala siin na mina anumi, na ádi mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na mina kabla ɔblane Dawid ɔ́bla ni, ndubulieku-ɔ na lɛya na ƒula lɛgakadikɔ kenye kpakplaa na ketu uwi aani kalɛ na lɛ́bla líte Dawid, na liti Israel lite-ɔ na adi-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the book about him and his wisdom.
translation_verse: Na ala ani ƒui na Ɔga Salomo ɔ́bla na nwuna lɛgadi uwi ku nwuna lɛnunda etemila ani na ɔ́su ni, bénweni-nya bákya Salomo lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: After he had ruled
translation_verse: Na ɔ́di lɛga na Yerusalem akwa aavlene,

english_verse: he died and was buried there in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_verse: na úkpi na báva-nwu na Dawid ɔma unengudi, na ubidi Yerobeam úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ.

english_verse: His younger advisors said: Here's what we think you should say to them: “Compared to me, my father was weak.
translation_verse: Amu na nwuna ligyekpa bakloƒu bammɔ bédie kenye banini, “Bekyuli bani násu-ɔ banini, ‘Ƒ'ɔti útile-bu etila ani na étulo-bu, awɔ bla-nya na abla-bu ƒaa ƒaa’ mmɔ ni, su-ma anini, ‘Mina kɔnu lɛnimi libliidi ƒui líbomo litulo mina ɔti kavobi.

english_verse: But the people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israelƒuɔ bátala na bátálɔ Yerobeam béboku, na anwu ku Israelƒuɔ kasala kammɔ bekyuli ƒui báta bésie Yerobeam kudɔ na básu-nwu banini,

english_verse: “Give me three days to think about it,” Rehoboam replied, “then come back for my answer.” So the people left.
translation_verse: Amu na Rehabeam údie-ma kenye ɔnini, “Binwini bibo emeyi atɛ kama na ndubɔsu-mii kalɛ na use.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bekyuli bammɔ básɔ bénwini bátɔlɔ.

english_verse: Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Ɔga Rehabeam ɔ́ni úde benengu bani na nka bátaalɛ ɔti Ɔga Salomo na ɔ́su-ma etemila ammɔ. Na úye benengu bammɔ ɔnini, “Bi kenye na bɛɛyɔ́ ka ntédie lɛsu bekyuli bammɔ?”

english_verse: They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should do what they ask today. Tell them you will make their work easier.”
translation_verse: Amu na benengu bammɔ bédie kenye banini, “Si aayɔ́ ka abla-ma kabla kaduɛ bɔdi ni, na enu bana etemila ani baasu-ɔ mmɔ. Na abla ete-ma. Na ama lɛnɔ badubɔbla-a kabla kaduɛ.”

english_verse: But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials.
translation_verse: Nsu Rehabeam úni benengu bammɔ bɔlɛ bɔmmɔ. Na únwini úsie bekyuli bani ndi nwuna ligyekpa na baabla-nwu kabla kudɔ mmomu útéye-ma bana kasusu.

english_verse: He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na úye bakloƒu bammɔ ɔnini, “Bi na bɛɛyɔ́ ka lɛbla? Na bi na ɔlɛka lɛsu bekyuli bani nábasu-mi banini, ‘Ƒ'ɔti útile-bu etila ani na étulo-bu, awɔ bla-nya na abla-bu ƒaa ƒaa’ mmɔ?”

english_verse: Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older advisors.
translation_verse: Na Ɔga Rehabeam útemiku-ma ku kɔnyi na úni kasusu kani na benengu bammɔ bákya-nwu,

english_verse: He spoke bluntly and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
translation_verse: na úti bakloƒu bammɔ mmomu kasusu kani na bákya-nwu na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Mina ɔti úti etila ani na ebo unu ɔ́sia-mii lɛlɔ. Nsu mɔɔsu-mii ka mina adi adubɔyu unu etulo nwuna adi. Na kugyiimi na úti úbo-mii, na nsu ami ndubuti batamlukpa lɛka bɔta-mii.”

english_verse: When the Israelites heard that Jeroboam was back, they called everyone together. Then they sent for Jeroboam and made him king of Israel. Only the people from the tribe of Judah remained loyal to David's family. Shemaiah Warns Rehoboam (
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bénu ka Yerobeam únwini ɔ́si Egyipte úbo ni, bekyuli bammɔ bálɔ-nwu na anwu ku-ma bátɛmi, na bábla-nwu Israelƒuɔ ɔga. Na Yuda kɔdua bekyuli lɛti ndi bani nsiaku Dawid bekyuli kama.

english_verse: After Rehoboam returned to Jerusalem, he decided to attack Israel and take control of the whole country. So he called together
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Rehabeam útéduo Yerusalem ni, údie bekpone bani ngyi bukpo kaduɛ eti atɛ ku avlaatɛ (

english_verse: Meanwhile, God told Shemaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Nsu Katɔti ɔ́su Kenye Udiene Semaia

english_verse: to give Rehoboam and everyone from Judah and Benjamin this warning:
translation_verse: ka utásu Rehabeam ku Yuda ku Benyamin adua bekyuli ƒui ɔnini,

english_verse: “Don't go to war against the people from Israel—they are your relatives. Go home! I am the Lord, and I made these things happen.” Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord and went home. Jeroboam Makes Religious Changes
translation_verse: “Bitesie bitetékpoku bina banwani Israelƒuɔ. Mmomu ɔdi biala unwini uteesie nwuna kaduli, ɔsika ami náya na úbo úte lɛni.” Anwuɔsu bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bénu Unwoti ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ na bénwini bésie kaduli. Bávɔ Sika Bakɔ Bebi Bése Betel Ku Dan

english_verse: Jeroboam rebuilt Shechem in Ephraim and made it a stronger town, then he moved there. He also fortified the town of Penuel.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Ɔga Yerobeam ɔ́tu ɔ́mana Sekem na Eƒraim abi lɛlɔ kalɔ kemmo na uli mmɔ. Ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́ta úsie útáda Panuel ɔma.

english_verse: One day, Jeroboam started thinking, “Everyone in Israel still goes to the temple in Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the Lord. What if they become loyal to David's family again? They will kill me and accept Rehoboam as their king.”
translation_verse: Na si bekyuli bamɛni bésie Unwoti kakpakɔ na Yerusalem banii batábla akpala ni, badubunwini kasusu na benwini basiaku Ɔga Rehabeam na bakya-nwu kalɔ na badu ami.”

english_verse: Jeroboam asked for advice and then made two gold statues of calves. He showed them to the people and said, “Listen everyone! You won't have to go to Jerusalem to worship anymore. Here are your gods who rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́wia bekyuli kasusu únu ni, ɔga ɔmmɔ úti sika ugyiedi ɔ́bla bakɔ bebi inyɔ. Na ɔ́su bekyuli bammɔ ɔnini, “Yerusalem busie teesie taatábla akpala ɔdubuduoku-mii lɛlɔ bɔvili. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, O Israel, bɛɛnu bina benwoti bani nákpanku-mii bálɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Then he put one of the gold calves in the town of Bethel and the other in the town of Dan.
translation_verse: Na úti baƒiɔ bammɔ unwi útálɛ Betel na úti ɔkladi lɛnɔ útálɛ Dan ɔma kemmo.

english_verse: The people sinned because they started going to these places to worship.
translation_verse: Na ala amɛni ebenwini-ma likpidi. Na bekyuli muedi baata teesie Dan ku Betel taatákpa baƒiɔ bammɔ na mmɔ.

english_verse: Jeroboam built small places of worship at the shrines and appointed men who were not from the tribe of Levi to serve as priests.
translation_verse: Yerobeam ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tu aƒiodu bamba na abi eli na anwu ɔlati údie bakpane ɔ́siku kesii biala na ɔɔyɔ́ ina ka baaadi Lewiƒuɔ.

english_verse: He also decided to start a new festival for the Israelites on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, just like the one in Judah. On that day, Jeroboam went to Bethel and offered sacrifices on the altar to the gold calf he had put there. Then he assigned the priests their duties.
translation_verse: Na kɔbuli maanedi limeyi leevu-lɛlɔndi lɛdi limeyi lɛni na anwu Yerobeam údie úse na uusié Betel taatákyula akpala na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na údie-ni aani limeyi bɔdi úte Israelƒuɔ.

english_verse: One day, Jeroboam was standing at the altar in Bethel, ready to make an offering. Suddenly one of God's prophets arrived from Judah and shouted: The Lord sent me with a message about this altar. A child named Josiah will be born into David's family. He will sacrifice on this altar the priests who make offerings here, and human bones will be burned on it.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́kya kenye udiene ɔmmɔ litemi kenye na ɔ́va ɔ́kpali ɔnini, “O lɛkpabi, lɛkpabi! Unwoti ɔnii, ‘Badubo ubi ɔnanabi bɔwɔ na Dawid kaduli na balɔ-nwu banii Yosia. Na ƒula lɛlɔ na ɔdubo bɔdu abi eli baƒiɔkpane ƒui bani nnye ka babla akpala na ƒula lɛlɔ ɔƒaani, na ƒula lɛlɔ na badubɔkyula bana ekubi.’ ”

english_verse: You will know that the Lord has said these things when the altar splits in half, and the ashes on it fall to the ground.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛmmɔ kani ni, Katɔti kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́bla likposela lɛdi na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔmɛni ndi Unwoti likposela ka lɛkpabi lɛmɛni lɛdubo bɔbwɛ na lile lɛlɔ kemmo inyɔ. Na ntɔ bɔni na buwi-nwu kemmo ni, buwilimi buwi kalɔ.”

english_verse: The altar split in half, and the ashes fell to the ground, just as the prophet had warned.
translation_verse: Na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛnɔ lile lɛlɔ kemmo inyɔ. Na ntɔ bɔni buwi-nwu kemmo búwilimi búwi kalɔ.

english_verse: “Please pray to the Lord your God and ask him to heal my hand,” Jeroboam begged. The prophet prayed, and Jeroboam's hand was healed.
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Yerobeam ɔ́su kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Vele ƒula Unwoti Katɔti na akpali-nwu na ɔsɔku mina kɔnu ɔklibi aani kalɛ kuse kudeedi.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu, kenye udiene ɔmmɔ úvele Unwoti na ɔ́ya na ɔga ɔmmɔ kɔnu kɔ́bla aani kalɛ kuse kudeedi.

english_verse: “Come home with me and eat something,” Jeroboam said. “I want to give you a gift for what you have done.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́su Katɔti kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Siaku-mi na busie na ntáwia lɛla lɛdi lite-ɔ na adi, na lɛwia etela adi lɛnɔ lite-ɔ.”

english_verse: “No, I wouldn't go with you, even if you offered me half of your kingdom. I won't eat or drink here either.
translation_verse: Nsu kenye udiene ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Si ina ƒula akɛla kemmo na anii eele kemmo akpa anyɔ na eti kakɛ ete-mi muedi ni, lɛɛɛdubo-ɔ bɔsiaku, iye lɛni ntu iye lɛdi na mɛni.

english_verse: The Lord said I can't eat or drink anything and that I can't go home the same way I came.”
translation_verse: Ɔsika Unwoti úbo-mi ɔda ɔnini, ‘Tadi adila adi, na tani ntu bɔdi, na tenwini tasia ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na akɛ ébo mɛni tatɔlɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Then he started home down a different road. An Old Prophet from Bethel
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́sia ulu bamba ɔ́tɔlɔ. Na ɔ́sɔ útasia ulu ɔni na ɔ́sia úbo Betel.

english_verse: At that time an old prophet lived in Bethel, and one of his sons told him what the prophet from Judah had said and done.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni kenye udiene ɔdi na ɔ́ɔbi lɛlɔ geen ɔdi úli Betel. Na nwuna bebi bébo-nwu kudɔ na básu-nwu ala ani ƒui na kenye udiene bamba ɔni nébo mmɔ úbabla limeyi lɛmmɔ. Na básu bana ɔti lɛla lɛni lɛnɔ na kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔga ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: “Show me which way he went,” the old prophet said, and his sons pointed out the road.
translation_verse: Amu na bana ɔti úye-ma ɔnini, “Wɛ ulu na kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔkɛ ɔ́tɔlɔ?” Amu na nwuna bebi bammɔ bátina-nwu ulu ɔni na kenye udiene ɔni nási Yuda mmɔ ɔkɛ.

english_verse: “Put a saddle on my donkey,” he told them. After they did, he got on the donkey
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́su nwuna bebi ɔnini, “Bɛƒɛnimi mina ɔpɔnkɔ bite-mi.” Amu ka báƒɛmini-nwu béte-nwu báwɔlɔ ni, ɔ́kɔ úlie-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and rode off to look for the prophet from Judah. The old prophet found him sitting under an oak tree and asked, “Are you the prophet from Judah?” “Yes, I am.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sia kenye udiene ɔni nátɔlɔ mmɔ kama. Na útánu-nwu ka úlie kugyii kubendi kɔdi kalɔ. Amu na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Awɔ ndi kenye udiene ɔni nási Yuda?” Amu na údie kenye ɔnini, “Ami mmɔ.”

english_verse: “Come home with me,” the old prophet said, “and have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Amu na kenye udiene ɔmɛni ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Siaku-mi na ntétɔ-ɔ lɛla lɛdi na adi.”

english_verse: “I can't go back with you,” the prophet replied, “and I can't eat or drink anything with you.
translation_verse: Amu na kenye udiene ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Naaakana bɔsɔ bunwini na buteesie, na naaakana lɛla lɛdi lɛnɔ bɔdi iye lɛni na mɛni.

english_verse: The Lord warned me not to eat or drink or to go home the same way I came.”
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔkɛnku nwuna litemi lɛlɔ ɔnini, ‘Útalɛ ka adi iye ani lɛla lɛdi na mmɔ iye asɔ enwini asia ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na ásia ésie mmɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The old prophet said, “I'm a prophet too. One of the Lord's angels told me to take you to my house and give you something to eat and drink.” The prophet from Judah did not know that the old prophet was lying,
translation_verse: Amu na kenye udiene ɔni náabi lɛlɔ mmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Ami lɛnɔ kenye udiene na ndi aani ƒula kalɛ. Na Katɔti ɔtu ɔdi ɔ́su-mi ka Unwoti ɔnii, ‘Nwiniku-nwu boku ƒula kaduli na ubadi na ɔni lɛla lɛdi.’ ” Nsu ɔkɔ na unengu ɔmmɔ ɔɔnyi.

english_verse: so he went home with him and ate and drank.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Katɔti kenye udiene ɔmmɔ únwini na ɔ́siaku-nwu na útádi na ɔ́ni na nwuna kaduli.

english_verse: During the meal the Lord gave the old prophet
translation_verse: Amu uwi ɔni bakya baadi ni, Unwoti litemi líbo kenye udiene ɔni náabi lɛlɔ mmɔ kudɔ,

english_verse: a message for the prophet from Judah: Listen to the Lord's message. You have disobeyed the Lord your God.
translation_verse: na ɔ́va ɔ́su kenye udiene ɔni nási Yuda mmɔ ka lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu ɔnini, “Átabu Unwoti litemi na átadi ɔda ɔni na Unwoti ƒula Katɔti úbo-ɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: He told you not to eat or drink anything here, but you came home and ate with me. And so, when you die, your body won't be buried in your family tomb.
translation_verse: Ásɔ énwini ébo kama, na ábadi adila na áni ntu na kesii kani na ɔ́su-ɔ ka tadi iye tani lɛla lɛdi. Ɔkɛnku ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, baaadubo ƒula ɔlɔna bɔva na ƒula bati kaƒiɔtɔ kemmo.”

english_verse: After the meal the old prophet got a donkey ready,
translation_verse: Amu ka bádi báwɔlɔ ni, kenye udiene ɔni náabi lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔ́bala nwuna ebuo ala utine úte-nwu.

english_verse: and the prophet from Judah left. Along the way, a lion attacked and killed him, and the donkey and the lion stood there beside his dead body.
translation_verse: Na ka úsela ni, útásiaku gyata na ulu lɛlɔ. Na gyata ɔmmɔ ɔ́du-nwu. Na ukpine ɔmmɔ ɔtɛ ulu ntɛ mmɔ. Na ebuo ala utine ɔmmɔ ku gyata ɔmmɔ ƒui benye ukpine ɔmmɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: Some people walked by and saw the body with the lion standing there. They ran into Bethel, telling everyone what they had seen.
translation_verse: Amu ka bekyuli badi bási baaví ni, bánu ukpine ɔmmɔ ka ɔtɛ kuludɔ na gyata ɔmmɔ unye-nwu kudɔ. Na bekyuli bammɔ bésie Betel bátásu lɛla lɛni bánu.

english_verse: When the old prophet heard the news, he said, “That must be the prophet from Judah. The Lord warned him, but he disobeyed. So the Lord sent a lion to kill him.”
translation_verse: Amu ka kenye udiene ɔni nénwiniku-nwu úboku nwuna kaduli mmɔ únu litemi lɛmmɔ ni, mmɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdi ukyuli biala na ɔdi, mmomu kenye udiene ɔni nétenu Katɔti litemi mmɔ na ɔdi. Unwoti néti-nwu úte gyata ɔmmɔ na ɔ́du aani kalɛ na Unwoti litemi lɛ́su-nwu líse kalɛ.”

english_verse: The old prophet told his sons to saddle his donkey, and when it was ready,
translation_verse: Amu na kenye udiene ɔni náabi lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔ́su nwuna bebi ɔnini, “Bɛbala mina ebuo ala utine bite-mi.” Na banamu bammɔ lɛnɔ bábla lɛni.

english_verse: he left. He found the body lying on the road, with the donkey and lion standing there. The lion had not eaten the body or attacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔ́vi ɔ́lɛ útánu ka kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ukpine ɔtɛ kuludɔ. Na gyata ɔmmɔ ku nwuna ebuo ala utine ƒui bénye-nwu kudɔ. Na gyata ɔmmɔ útakun lɛna lɛmmɔ lɛdi iye ɔbla ebuo ala utine ɔmmɔ lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: The old prophet picked up the body, put it on his own donkey, and took it back to Bethel, so he could bury it and mourn for the prophet from Judah.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́gyu ukpine ɔmmɔ ɔ́mana nwuna ebuo ala utine kama na úti-nwu úsienku nwuna ɔma ka utéwulo-nwu na ɔva-nwu.

english_verse: He buried the body in his own family tomb and cried for the prophet.
translation_verse: Na úti ukpine ɔmmɔ útáva anwu ɔlati kaƒiɔtɔ kemmo. Na béwulo-nwu na ɔ́su ɔnini, “O mina ɔnwani!”

english_verse: He said to his sons, “When I die, bury my body next to this prophet.
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́va-nwu ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔ́su nwuna bebi ɔnini, “Si líkpi ni, na bɛva-mi kesii kani na lɛ́va kenye udiene ɔmɛni. Na ami ku-nwu ekubi atɛ liku linwi.

english_verse: I'm sure that everything he said about the altar in Bethel and the shrines in Samaria will happen.”
translation_verse: Ɔsika etemila ani ƒui Unwoti úbo-nwu ɔda na ɔ́su na adanku lɛkpabi lɛni nkya Betel ku aƒiodu ani ƒui na akya lɛma lɛni nkya Samaria adubo-nwu kemmo lɛni kani.”

english_verse: But Jeroboam kept on doing evil things. He appointed men to be priests at the local shrines, even if they were not Levites. In fact, anyone who wanted to be a priest could be one.
translation_verse: Nsu na ɔmɛni ƒui kama ni, Ɔga Yerobeam útavumana nwuna likyulikpi ɔbladu ɔmmɔ. Na busie na úsie anumi na uudie bekyuli keeke taasiku kɔduli kemmo na beenwíni bakpane teete nwuna akpabi ani na ɔ́tu ɔ́lɛ abi eli. Na ukyuli biala mɔɔyɔ́ ka ɔbla ɔkpane ni, na uti-nwu ɔbla ɔkpane.

english_verse: About the same time, Abijah son of Jeroboam got sick.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Ɔga Yerobeam ubidi ɔni baalɔ Abia úbo ɔkya uuƒi.

english_verse: Jeroboam told his wife: Disguise yourself so no one will know you're my wife, then go to Shiloh, where the prophet Ahijah lives. Take him ten loaves of bread, some small cakes, and honey, and ask him what will happen to our son. He can tell you, because he's the one who told me I would become king.
translation_verse: Na si ésela ni, ti bodobodo leevu ku agyidi ƒɛƒɛɛ ku uwɔ ɔsii bonwu unwi ada. Na eye-nwu lɛla lɛni ndubɔlɛku bula ubidi ɔni muuƒi mmɔ. Ɔdubɔsu-ɔ lɛla biala.”

english_verse: She got ready and left for Ahijah's house in Shiloh. Ahijah was now old and blind,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ulekudi ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Ahia kudɔ na Silo. Na Ahia ɔ́ɔbi ɔsu ɔsɔ ulánu lɛnɔ.

english_verse: But when Ahijah heard her walking up to the door, he said: Come in! I know you're Jeroboam's wife—why are you pretending to be someone else? I have some bad news for you.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu uwi ɔni na Ahia únu uleku ɔmmɔ bɔnya na nwuna kayakun kenye ni, ɔ́su ɔnini, “Yerobeam ulekudi, duo ɔtɔ. Bi ɔsu na ábla lɛlɔ aani ukyuli bamba na adi? Unwoti ɔ́kya-mi litemi likpidi kenye ka lɛsu-ɔ.

english_verse: Give your husband this message from the Lord God of Israel: “Jeroboam, you know that I, the Lord, chose you over anyone else to be the leader of my people Israel.
translation_verse: Nwini tásu Yerobeam ka lɛni na Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti ɔɔsu, ‘Lídie-ɔ lɛ́lɛku bekyuli bammɔ akɔ na líti-ɔ lɛ́bla mina bekyuli Israelƒuɔ ɔtɔnkune.

english_verse: I even took David's kingdom away from his family and gave it to you. But you are not like my servant David. He always obeyed me and did what was right.
translation_verse: Na líle Ɔga Dawid lɛga kemmo na líti líte-ɔ. Nsu átabla aani mina kabla ɔblane Dawid ɔni nádi mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ. Na úti nwuna kayi ƒui ɔ́siaku-mi kama. Na ɔ́bla ala ani kani nse siin na mina anumi.

english_verse: “You have made me very angry by rejecting me and making idols out of gold. Jeroboam, you have done more evil things than any king before you.
translation_verse: Na awɔ ni, ábla likpidi étulo baga bani ƒui nélie asa na ébo. Na éti lɛbuala ávɔ baƒiɔ éte lɛlɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu ákya-mi kɔnyi geen, ɔsika énwini kama ákya-mi.

english_verse: “Because of this, I will destroy your family by killing every man and boy in it, whether slave or free. I will wipe out your family, just as fire burns up trash.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɔkɛnku ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, ndubuti ɔgbankpi liboku Yerobeam kaduli. Na bananabi kawɔ kplo biala na bakya Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ, Israelni na ɔdi o-o kadi bamba bekyuli bani mɔɔbla-ma kabla o-o ni, ndubo-ma bɔdu budie Yerobeam lɛlɔ na kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui. Na ɔmɛni ɔdubuse kalɔ ɔsiku Israel. Na lɛkyula Yerobeam kaduli kemodi kammɔ ƒui aani kebu alakpi, utédu ka lɛla biala lɛ́kywi lɛ́sa.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel will mourn at his funeral. But he will be the last one from Jeroboam's family to receive a proper burial, because he's the only one the Lord God of Israel is pleased with.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ ƒui badubo-nwu buwulo na bava-nwu, ɔsika anwu kani ndi Yerobeam ubidi unwi pɛ ɔni na Unwoti ɔni ndi Israel Katɔti ɔ́nu ka ɔdanku lɛla lɛbuni lɛdi.

english_verse: The Lord will soon choose a new king of Israel, who will destroy Jeroboam's family. And I mean very soon.
translation_verse: “Na Unwoti ɔlati ɔdubudie ukyuli ɔni madi lɛga na Israel. Na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔdubukulo Yerobeam kaduli bekyuli udie ɔmwi ɔmɛni kani. Nu! Kɔnakunwi kɔmɛni muedi, na ɔɔɔdubo uwi bubile.

english_verse: The people of Israel have made the Lord angry by setting up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. So the Lord will punish them until they shake like grass in a stream. He will take them out of the land he gave to their ancestors, then scatter them as far away as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔdubɔni Israel kɔtu na ɔkunku-nwu aani kalɛ na ntu buubó ketu kemmo alakpi teesie teebo. Na ɔdubɔgyu Israel udie kalɔ kabuni kani na úti úte bana bati kuuku, na úgyingya-ma útákya ketu ɔvi. Ɔsika bákya Unwoti kɔnyi ɔkɛnku Asera lɛƒiɔgyii lɛni na bálɛ mmɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: years from Jerusalem, the city where the Lord had chosen to be worshiped. His mother Naamah was from Ammon.
translation_verse: Ka kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́tɛmi ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, mmɔ na Yerobeam ulekudi ɔ́ta na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Tirsa. Uwi ɔni kani na nwuna ɔgba útuku kaduli kayakun ni, mmɔ kani na ɔnamu ɔmmɔ úkpi.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel came and mourned at his funeral, just as the Lord's servant Ahijah had said. Jeroboam Dies
translation_verse: Na báva-nwu. Na Israelƒuɔ béwulo-nwu aani kalɛ kani na Unwoti ɔ́su ɔ́siaku nwuna Kenye Udiene Ahia lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including the battles he won, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani na álɛku Yerobeam na nwuna lɛga bɔdi uwi ku kekpo kani na úkpo ku kalɛ na ɔ́di nwuna lɛga ɔ́vinku ni, bénweni-nya bákya Israelƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: The people of Judah disobeyed the Lord and made him even angrier than their ancestors had.
translation_verse: Yudaƒuɔ bábla likpidi na Unwoti anumi. Na bana ekpidi ágyila Unwoti kɔnyi kɔni muukpó kɔgyulo útulo bana bati kuuku adi ani bábla muedi.

english_verse: They also built their own local shrines and stone images of foreign gods, and they set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Bátu akpabi ekpo ekpo na bálɛ atabi ani banii ese kedee ku lɛƒiɔgyii béte Asera baƒiɔ na abi ƒui eli ku egyii enengudi ani nábla ɔyuli kaduɛ kalɔ.

english_verse: Even worse, they allowed prostitutes at the shrines, and followed the disgusting customs of the foreign nations that the Lord had forced out of Canaan.
translation_verse: Na bebo banana na bakya aƒiodu ammɔ na benye bete lɛyalɛ ala bɔbla kani na kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Na Israelƒuɔ ƒui béti lɛlɔ béte ala ani muusé lɛlɔ bɔbla aani kalɛ na bekyuli bani na Unwoti ɔ́bɔku ɔ́lɛku kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ na Israelƒuɔ anumi baabla.

english_verse: After Rehoboam had been king for four years, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa lɛlɔndi kemmo na Rehabeam lɛga bɔdi kemmo ni. Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ɔni baalɔ Sisa útékpoku Yerusalemƒuɔ.

english_verse: He took everything of value from the temple and the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
translation_verse: Na úti sika kɔlɛmii kɔni nkya kakpakɔ ku ɔga kaduli mmɔ na ɔ́sɔ úti sika lɛgyumanala lɛni na Ɔga Salomo ɔ́bla úse mmɔ ɔ́tɔlɔku.

english_verse: Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe.
translation_verse: Na Ɔga Rehabeam úti abuala egyiedi ɔ́bla agyumanala bamba na úti-nya ɔ́kya bagyumanane bani nnye kaduli kayakun enu kemmo.

english_verse: Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he was finished.
translation_verse: Na uwi biala na ɔga wesie kakpakɔ mmɔ ni, bekyuli bammɔ baagyú abuala egyiedi agyumanala ammɔ taada. Na si ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, baasɔku-nya teetése ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo agyumanala ammɔ eesé.

english_verse: Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani na Ɔga Rehabeam ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-nya bákya Yudaƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: He and Jeroboam were constantly at war.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmɛni ƒui kemmo ni, Rehabeam ku Yerobeam béteekpoku lɛlɔ pla pla.

english_verse: Rehoboam's mother Naamah was from Ammon, but when Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Abijam then became king.
translation_verse: Na Rehabeam úkpi na báva-nwu na baga kavakɔ na Dawid ɔma unengudi kemmo mmɔ. Na uni baalɔ Naama. Na Amonni na ɔdi. Na Abia úlie ɔti keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ.

english_verse: His own grandmother Maacah had made an idol of Asherah, and Asa took it and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
translation_verse: Na nwuna nana uleku ɔni ɔdi uleku ɔga ni, ɔ́tu-nwu lɛga, ɔsika ɔ́bla Asera baƒiɔ badi ɔ́lɛ. Na Ɔga Asa ɔ́da kugyii kɔmmɔ na ɔ́kyula-ku na Kidron Kɔwɛ kemmo.

english_verse: Abijam became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel,
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa leevu-maanedi lɛlɔ ɔni na Nebat ubidi Yerobeam ɔɔdi lɛga ni, Abia úbenwini ɔga na Yuda.

english_verse: Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to strengthen the town of Ramah. Then he used these same stones and wood to fortify the town of Geba in the territory of Benjamin and the town of Mizpah.
translation_verse: Amu na Asa úbo ɔda úte Yudaƒuɔ ƒui ɔni na bátada ɔdi bétedie ɔnii beti atabi ku ligyii lɛni na Basa ɔ́ya na béti bébewi Rama mmɔ ka batu bamana-nwu na ɔbla kagyumanakɔ kpakplaa mmɔ batɔlɔku mmɔ. Na ɔ́ya na béti atula ammɔ kani bátu bámana Geba na Benyamin kalɛkɛ, ku Mispa lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Abijam did not truly obey the Lord his God as his ancestor David had done. Instead, he was sinful just like his father Rehoboam.
translation_verse: Na ekpidi ani ƒui na ɔti ɔ́bla asa na báwɔ-nwu ni, Abia lɛnɔ úbabla-nya. Na útakana na uti nwuna kayi ƒui ute Unwoti Katɔti aani kalɛ na nwuna Nana Dawid ɔ́bla.

english_verse: David had always obeyed the Lord's commands by doing right, except in the case of Uriah. And since Abijam was David's great-grandson, the Lord kept Jerusalem safe and let Abijam have a son who would be the next king.
translation_verse: Ɔsika na Dawid ngba bulie kemmo ƒui ni, ɔ́bla ala ani na ese siin na Unwoti anumi, na útedie atu na Unwoti ɔda bubo biala lɛlɔ. Ntu anwu ku Uria ɔni ɔdi Hetini likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla mmɔ kani.

english_verse: The war that had broken out between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continued during the time that Abijam was king. Everything else Abijam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani nálɛku Abia ku ala ani na ɔ́bla na nwuna lɛga bɔdi uwi ni, bénweni-nya bákya Yudaƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo. Na kekpo kákya Abia ku Yerobeam ntɛ.

english_verse: Abijam died and was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Asa became king. King Asa of Judah (
translation_verse: Na Abia úkpi na báva-nwu na Dawid ɔma unengudi. Na ubidi Asa úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ. Asa Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Yuda

english_verse: He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔku sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ɔni na anwu ku nwuna bati bédie bése sɛsɛɛ béte Unwoti mmɔ úsienku kakpakɔ.

english_verse: Asa was always at war with King Baasha of Israel.
translation_verse: Kekpo sɔɔn nákya Ɔga Asa ku Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Basa ntɛ uwi ɔni na bélie bátaadi lɛga.

english_verse: Asa obeyed the Lord, as David had done.
translation_verse: Asa ɔ́bla lɛla lɛni nse siin na Unwoti anumi aani kalɛ na ɔti Dawid ɔ́bla.

english_verse: Asa became king of Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's rule in Israel,
