translation_verse: Na lɛkwa aavlanyɔdi kemmo na Yerobeam lɛga bɔdi uwi na Israel ni, Asa úbenwini Yudaƒuɔ ɔga.

english_verse: He forced the prostitutes at the shrines to leave the country, and he got rid of the idols his ancestors had made.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́bɔku banana bayalɛ bani na bakya aƒiodu mmɔ ƒui údie kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Na baƒiɔ bani ƒui na nwuna bati bátu bálɛ ni, úgyingya-ma ƒui.

english_verse: As long as Asa lived, he was completely faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines.
translation_verse: Ina ka útegyingya baƒiɔ bammɔ na ekpo adi bene ni, Asa kayi kásia Unwoti lɛlɔ nwuna ngba emeyi ƒui.

english_verse: One time, Baasha invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, so he could put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Basa útátu awodu ɔ́mana Rama kalɛ na busie teetenku lɛlɔ bɔdi bɔsɔ bulakya ama ku Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Asa ku nwuna bekyuli ntɛ.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. He gave it to some of his officials and sent them to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: Ka Asa únu ɔmɛni ni, úti sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ɔnaƒui ɔni nébu ɔ́siku nwuna lɛgakadikɔ ku Unwoti kakpakɔ na úti úmene Aram Ɔga Benhadad ɔni ɔti ndi Tabrimon ɔni ɔti ndi Hesion na Damasko ɔ́siaku nwuna bakutine benengu lɛlɔ ɔnii batásu-nwu kenye kamɛni banini,

english_verse: “Our fathers signed a peace treaty. Why don't we do the same thing? This silver and gold is a present for you. So, would you please break your treaty with Baasha and force him to leave my country?”
translation_verse: “Mɔɔyɔ́ ka abu ku-ɔ bɔbla unwi aani kalɛ na ƒ'ɔti ku mina ɔti bábla unwi dii. Nu, líti sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ɔmɛni muumene-ɔ, na ekulo unwi bɔbla bɔni nkya awɔ ku Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Basa ntɛ, na ɔda nwuna bekpone udie mina ɔmii lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, and Abel-Bethmaacah, and the territories of Chinneroth and Naphtali.
translation_verse: Benhadad ɔ́bla lɛla lɛni na Asa ɔ́su-nwu na úti Siriaƒuɔ bekpone úmene Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ na bétékpo Iyon ku Dan ku Abel-Bet-Maaka ku Kinerot ƒui ku Naƒtali kɔlɔ ƒui.

english_verse: When Baasha heard about it, he left Ramah and went back to Tirzah.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Ɔga Basa únu lɛla lɛni nálɛ ni, ɔ́da Rama bɔtu ɔ́ya na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Tirsa.

english_verse: Everything else Asa did while he was king, including his victories and the towns he rebuilt, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. When he got older, he had a foot disease.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani na Ɔga Asa ɔ́bla ku nwuna kayi kani na ɔ́kya ku lɛma lɛni na ɔ́tu awodu ɔ́mana ni, bénweni-nya bákya Yuda baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo. Nsu na Ɔga Asa lɛlɔ bɔbi uwi ni, ɔ́kɛ lɛgba ɔlɛ ɔdi.

english_verse: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Asa's second year as king of Judah, and he ruled two years.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa linyɔdi kemmo ɔni na Ɔga Asa ɔ́di lɛga na Yuda ni, Ɔga Yerobeam ubidi Nadab únwini ɔga na Israel. Na ɔ́di lɛga akwa anyɔ.

english_verse: Nadab disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of his father, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Na aani kalɛ na ɔti ɔ́bla kalɛ ni, anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́bla likpidi. Na ɔ́tɔnku Israelƒuɔ lɛnɔ na bábla likpidi na Unwoti anumi.

english_verse: The Lord's prophet Ahijah had earlier said, “Not one man or boy in Jeroboam's family will be left alive.” And, as soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family,
translation_verse: Na ka bése-nwu lɛga kani na úse kalɔ ɔɔdú Yerobeam kaduli bekyuli. Na ɔmɛni úbo úte lɛni ɔkɛnku kenye kani na Unwoti ɔ́sia nwuna Kenye Udiene Ahia ɔni na ɔ́si Silo ɔ́su úse. Na Yerobeam kaduli bekyuli békpi ɔni na unwi muedi útebu.

english_verse: because Jeroboam had made the Lord God of Israel angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Na ɔmɛni úbo úte lɛni, ɔsika Yerobeam ɔ́kya Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti kɔnyi ɔ́kɛnku likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla ku lɛla lɛni na ɔ́ya na Israelƒuɔ lɛnɔ bábla ɔsu.

english_verse: Everything else Nadab did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani na Nadab ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-nya bákya Israelƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war. King Baasha of Israel
translation_verse: Na Ɔga Asa ɔni na ɔ́si Yuda ku Ɔga Basa ɔni ɔ́si Israel lɛga bɔdi uwi ni, kekpo lɛti lɛti nákya-ma ntɛ. Basa Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Israel

english_verse: Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa lɛtɛdi na Ɔga Asa ɔni na ɔ́si Yuda lɛga bɔdi kemmo ni, Ahia ubidi Basa únwini Israelƒuɔ ɔga. Na ɔ́di lɛga lɛmmɔ na Tirsa. Na ɔ́di-ni akwa aavlanyɔ-ine.

english_verse: Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́bla likpidi na Unwoti anumi aani kalɛ na Yerobeam ɔ́bla. Na ɔ́tɔnku Israelƒuɔ lɛnɔ na bábla likpidi.

english_verse: The Lord sent Jehu son of Hanani to say to Baasha:
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Unwoti útemi úte Hanani ubidi Kenye Udiene Yehu ka útásu Ɔga Basa ɔnini,

english_verse: Nobody knew who you were until I, the Lord, chose you to be the leader of my people Israel. And now you're acting exactly like Jeroboam by causing the Israelites to sin. What you've done has made me so angry
translation_verse: “Nka ukyuli keeke kani na adi. Na ami lɛ́bla-a ɔtɔnkune líte mina bekyuli Israelƒuɔ. Na ɔƒɛni ábla likpidi aani Yerobeam kalɛ. Na ákpanku mina bekyuli átákya likpidi kemmo. Na áya na bana likpidi lɛmmɔ lɛgyila mina kɔnyi.

english_verse: that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu, nu! Ndubo awɔ ku ƒula kaduli bekyuli ƒui bɔdu aani kalɛ lɛ́bla Yerobeam.

english_verse: Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Na ƒula kaduli ukyuli biala mekpi na ɔma unengudi kemmo ni, bakpewɛ ndubo-nwu lɛna bɔkun. Na ɔdi biala na wekpi na alakpi akɔ ni, baasɛ ndubo-nwu lɛna bɔduli.”

english_verse: Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family! Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king. King Elah of Israel
translation_verse: Na kenye kani na Unwoti úti úte Hanani ubidi Kenye Udiene Yehu na Basa ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli lɛlɔ ni, ɔ́si likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla na ɔ́gyila Unwoti kɔnyi na nwuna ablala ɔsu aani kalɛ kani na Yerobeam ɔ́bla, ku kalɛ na ɔ́du Yerobeam kaduli bekyuli ƒui ɔsu. Ela Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Israel

english_verse: Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel after Asa had been king of Judah for
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa aavlanyɔ-lɛkundi kemmo ka Ɔga Asa ɔɔdi lɛga na Yuda ni, Basa ubidi Ela úbenwini Israelƒuɔ ɔga. Na úlie Tirsa ɔ́di lɛga lɛmmɔ akwa anyɔ.

english_verse: Omri did more evil things than any king before him.
translation_verse: Nsu Omri ɔ́bla likpidi na Unwoti anumi. Na nwuna likpidi lítulo bani nádi lɛga bábavi ƒui.

english_verse: Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots, and he made plans to kill Elah. One day, Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his prime minister,
translation_verse: Na Simri ɔni na ɔdi ɔga ɔmmɔ bakutine benengu akɔ unwi na anwu mɔɔnu nwuna bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ kakɛ kenwi ƒui lɛlɔ ni, ɔ́lɛ-nwu kama na údie kasusu kekpidi nwuna lɛlɔ. Limeyi lɛdi ni, Ɔga Ela ɔ́kya Tirsa na nwuna baga kesii lɛlɔ ɔnune Arsa kesii ɔɔní ntɛ na ɔdaku-mu bukpi.

english_verse: when Zimri went there and killed Elah. So Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Simri útéduo kaduli kammɔ kemmo na ɔ́du Ɔga Ela. Na úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ, na Ɔga Asa lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa aavlanyɔ-maatɛdi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni kani na bése Simri liboku lɛlɔ na úse kalɔ ɔɔdi bekyuli bammɔ lɛlɔ ni, mmɔ kani na ɔ́du Basa kaduli bekyuli ƒui. Na útebu ɔnana ɔdi útakya kama na ɔdi nwuna lɛlɔ ukyuli iye nwuna bakpana muedi.

english_verse: Baasha and Elah sinned and caused the Israelites to sin, and they made the Lord angry by worshiping idols.
translation_verse: ɔ́si likpidi lɛni na Basa ku ubidi Ela bábla. Bákpanku Israelƒuɔ bátákya likpidi kemmo, na bágyila Unwoti Israel Katɔti kɔnyi ɔkɛnku bana baƒiɔ lidu bani na bánwi na bávɔ bése lɛlɔ na liiibo kɔsia ɔsu.

english_verse: Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Zimri of Israel
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani lɛnɔ na Ela ɔ́bla na nwuna lɛga bɔdi uwi ni, bénweni-nya bákya Israelƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo. Simri Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Israel

english_verse: Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah. Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day.
translation_verse: Na ka Israelƒuɔ bénu ka Simri ɔ́bla kasusu kekpidi na ɔga lɛlɔ na ɔ́du-nwu ni, limeyi lɛmmɔ kani na bekpone bammɔ ƒui bébo kudu na bana kakyakɔ mmɔ ka bana bekpone ɔtɔnkune ɔni baalɔ banii Omri únwini Israelƒuɔ ɔga.

english_verse: At once, Omri and his army marched to Tirzah and attacked.
translation_verse: Amu na Omri ku nwuna bekpone bátɔlɔ Gibeton. Na bátábɛ bámana Tirsa ɔma.

english_verse: When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Simri ɔ́nu ka báka ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ bákya ni, úkeli úsie ɔga kaduli na útéduo ɔtɔ kagyumanakɔ kpakplaa kammɔ kemmo na ɔ́tu ogya ɔ́mana lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́du lɛlɔ ɔ́kya ogya ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Omri of Israel
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani na Simri ɔ́bla ku kalɛ na ɔ́ta únye ɔga lɛlɔ na ɔ́bla ala ɔ́vinku ni, bénweni-nya bákya Israelƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo. Omri Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Israel

english_verse: After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Israelƒuɔ béle lɛlɔ kemmo inyɔ. Na kakɛ benye bete ka beti Ginat ubidi Tibni bese lɛga. Na badi lɛnɔ benye bete Omri.

english_verse: in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah. Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na lɛkwa avlaatɛ-linwidi ka Asa ɔɔdi Yudaƒuɔ lɛga ni, Omri úbenwini Israelƒuɔ ɔga. Na ɔ́di lɛga lɛmmɔ akwa leevu-anyɔ. Na akwa aku edeedi ni, Tirsa ɔma na úlie.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
translation_verse: Na anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́sia Nebat ubidi Yerobeam ulu lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́kya Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti kɔnyi ɔkɛnku likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla ku ala ani na ɔ́tɔnku Israelƒuɔ na bábla na bágyila Unwoti Israel Katɔti kɔnyi ɔkɛnku bana baƒiɔ bani neeebo kɔsia kɔdi ablala ɔsu.

english_verse: Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani na Ɔga Omri ɔ́bla ku ala ani nálɛ-nya kemmo ni, bénweni-nya bákya Israelƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king. King Ahab of Israel
translation_verse: Omri úbekpi na báva-nwu na Samaria, na ubidi Ahab úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ. Ahab Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Israel

english_verse: Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa avlaatɛ-maanedi kemmo ka Asa ɔɔdi lɛga na Yuda ni, Omri ubidi Ahab úbenwini Israelƒuɔ ɔga. Na ɔ́di lɛga lɛmmɔ na Samaria akwa aavlanyɔ-inyɔ.

english_verse: Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́bla likpidi na Unwoti anumi útulo baga bani ƒui nélie.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Ɔ́sia Yerobeam ekpidi ani na ɔ́bla kama na ammɔ lɛti átabɔ-nwu. Mmomu úsie útéti Sidomƒuɔ Ɔga Etbaal ubidi ulekubi ɔni baalɔ banii Isebel ɔ́bla ulekudi, na úse kalɔ ɔɔkpá Baal baƒiɔ na ɔɔbla-ma kabla.

english_verse: Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria
translation_verse: Na ɔ́tu lɛkpabi úte baƒiɔ bammɔ ku kakpakɔ na Samaria mmɔ.

english_verse: and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́lɛ ɔƒiɔgyii úte Asera baƒiɔ. Na ɔ́bla ala ani na ányi anyi geen etulo baga bani ƒui nádi lɛga na Israel úti ɔ́gyila Unwoti Israel Katɔti kɔnyi.

english_verse: While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_verse: Ahab lɛga bɔdi uwi ni, Hiel ɔni nási Betel ɔ́sɔku Yeriko ɔ́tu. Na nwuna bɔtu kemmo uwi ɔni na ɔɔkya ɔma ɔmmɔ ɔka kalɔ ni, Hiel úti ubidi unengudi Abiram ɔ́kpa. Na úti ubidi Segub lɛnɔ ɔ́kpa uwi ɔni na ɔɔkya awodu ammɔ kɔyakun. Na ala amɛni ƒui ébo éte lɛni ɔkɛnku Unwoti kenye kani na ɔ́su ɔ́siaku Nun ubidi Yosua lɛlɔ úse ɔsu.

english_verse: Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
translation_verse: Amu na kenye udiene ɔni baalɔ Elia na ɔ́si Tisbi na Gilead kalɛkɛ kemmo úsie útásu Ɔga Ahab ɔnini, “Mɔɔsu-ɔ na Unwoti Israel Katɔti ɔni kabla na mɔɔbla na uli ngba lɛnyi kemmo ka ni, na akwa alɛɛ adi kemmo ni, amii iye ɔnantu ɔsɔ ulana ulewi kalɔ si ɔɔɔdi ami násɔ lɛ́su nnii ɔna.”

english_verse: Later, the Lord said to Elijah,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Elia ɔnini,

english_verse: “Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: “Tɔlɔ kesii kani na enye mɛni na eteesie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ na atábɛ na Kerit Kɔwɛ kemmo na Yordan kudɔ.

english_verse: You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
translation_verse: Ketu kani nkya mmɔ kadubuteete-ɔ ntu na ataani. Na líbo ɔda líte baasɛ batondi badi ka beteeti adila teeboku-ɔ.”

english_verse: Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek.
translation_verse: Na baasɛ bammɔ beeboku-nwu adila ku lɛna lɛdigye ku useyi uwi na ɔɔní ketu kani na kakya mmɔ ntu. Ukpinele Ɔdi Ɔ́kya Sareƒat

english_verse: But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain. Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
translation_verse: Ketu kammɔ kábakwii na uwi klukui ɔdi kama, ɔsika ɔnantu ulána.

english_verse: The Lord told Elijah,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Elia ɔnini,

english_verse: “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
translation_verse: “Teesie ɔma ɔni baalɔ Sareƒat na ude Sidon na etélie mmɔ. Ɔsika líbo ɔda líte ukpinele ɔdi nli mmɔ ka uteete-ɔ adila.”

english_verse: When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Elia ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Sareƒat mmɔ. Na uwi ɔni na útédu ɔma ɔmmɔ kabanye ni, ɔ́nu ukpinele ɔdi ka ɔkya ɔɔyɔ́ ekyweni. Amu na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Buvele nda-a, te-mi ntu bɔdi na lɛni.”

english_verse: As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na ukpinele ɔmmɔ úsela utédu ntu bɔmmɔ ni, mmɔ na Elia ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kpali-nwu ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Buvele nda-a, ti bodobodo ɔdi boku-mi o-o!”

english_verse: The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na uleku ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Na Unwoti Katɔti anumi ni, bodobodo ɔdi biala uuubo-mi. Lɛla lɛni mbo ndi ɔlaaƒɔ lɛkɔkɔ linwi lɛni nwi ɔɔƒɛɛ kemmo ku nnɔ blii bɔni nwi libui kemmo kani na mbo. Na líbo mbayɔ ekyweni adi kalɛ na lisie ɔma ntéti ɔmmɔ lɛnwa lite ami ku mina ubi. Na si bɔ́di bɔ́wɔlɔ ni, bɔsɔ bulie kɔka kɔmmɔ kemmo butaanu kukpi anumi.”

english_verse: Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me.
translation_verse: Amu na Elia údie kenye ɔnini, “Uleku, taya na ɔmɛni ukpoku-ɔ. Awɔ teesie tánwa kalɛ na ásu, nsu ka ɔdi bɔsala na anwa kanagyie blii kadi eboku-mi asa na anwa awɔ ku ƒ'ubidi ɔdi.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
translation_verse: Ɔsika bɔsu na Unwoti ɔni ndi Israel Katɔti ɔɔsu ɔnii, ‘Ɔlaaƒɔ ɔni nwi ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ kemmo iye nnɔ bɔni nwi libui kemmo mmɔ ni, bulása kudii utédu ka anwu Unwoti ɔ́ya na ɔnantu ɔ́sɔ ɔ́na.’ ”

english_verse: The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ukpinele ɔmmɔ útábla adila ammɔ aani kalɛ na Elia ɔ́su-nwu. Na ɔ́si ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, Elia ku ukpinele ɔmmɔ ku ubidi ƒui baakɛ́ lɛla lɛdi taadi limeyi ndi limeyi.

english_verse: The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil. Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
translation_verse: Na aani kalɛ na Unwoti úse uleku ɔmmɔ kenye ɔ́siaku Elia lɛlɔ ni, ɔlaaƒɔ ɔni nwi ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ kemmo iye nnɔ bɔni nwi libui lɛmmɔ kemmo bútasa kudii.

english_verse: Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔdi kama ni, ukpinele ɔmmɔ ubidi ɔnanabi úbo uuƒi. Na ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ katɔ kani na ɔɔkɔ́ na ɔnamu ɔmmɔ úbekpi.

english_verse: The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
translation_verse: Amu na ukpinele ɔmmɔ ɔ́su Elia ɔnini, “Katɔti ukyuli, bi ɔsu na ábla-mi lɛni? Bubo na ébo mɛni ka abaya na linyimo mina likpidi na adu mina ubidi?”

english_verse: “Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed
translation_verse: Amu na Elia ɔ́su uleku ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Ti ɔnamu ɔmmɔ te-mi!” Amu na ɔ́ƒɔ ɔnamu ɔmmɔ ɔ́lɛku uleku ɔmmɔ lɛkɔkɔ na úti-nwu úsienku ɔtɔ katɔ kesii kani na úduo. Na úti-nwu ɔ́va nwuna atɛla lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́kpali Katɔti ɔ́su ɔnini, “O mina Unwoti Katɔti, bi ɔsu na áya na ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni udu ɔ́lɛku ukpinele ɔni kudɔ na líbo nkya uwi ɔmɛni ƒui lɛni? Na áya na ubidi úkpi?”

english_verse: Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Elia únene lɛlɔ kɔtɛ úboku ɔnamu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na ɔ́kpali Katɔti ɔnini, “O mina Katɔti, sɔku ɔnamu ɔmɛni ngba kya-nwu kemmo.”

english_verse: The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti únu Elia bɔkpali. Na ɔnamu ɔmmɔ úse kalɔ ɔɔnwuna na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kɛ ngba.

english_verse: Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
translation_verse: Amu na Elia ɔ́gyu ɔnamu ɔmmɔ na ɔ́yu úsie kalɔ. Na úsie útásu ɔnamu ɔmmɔ uni ɔnini, “Nu! Ƒ'ubidi uli ngba.”

english_verse: “You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
translation_verse: Amu na uleku ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔƒɛni na lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka Katɔti ukyuli na adi. Na Unwoti uutemi taasiaku-ɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: At that time Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace, but he faithfully worshiped the Lord. In fact, when Jezebel was trying to kill the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Isebel ɔ́kya útaadu Unwoti kenye bediene ni, Obadia úti kenye bediene bammɔ eti anyɔ útábɛla atabi libu bonwu inyɔ bɔdi kemmo. Na úle-ma ɔ́kya mmɔ liti liti na uute-ma adila ku ntu na mmɔ.

english_verse: and said, “We have to find something for our horses and mules to eat. If we don't, we will have to kill them. Let's look around every creek and spring in the country for some grass.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Ɔga Ahab ɔ́su Obadia ɔnini, “Ya na busie na butávi bɔwia livo lɛdi na abiɔ kɔtu ku awɛ ammɔ kemmo bɔnu. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ bɔdubɔkɛ kesii kani na livo lɛdi lɛ́kwɛ linye na bɔkɛ bute bula bapɔnkɔ ku bula bebuo ala betine na belie ngba kalɛ na buládu bula bebuo bammɔ badi.”

english_verse: You go one way, and I'll go the other.” Then they left in separate directions.
translation_verse: Na bénu kalɔ na bánu kesii kani na ɔdi ka ɔdi biala ɔsia.

english_verse: As Obadiah was walking along, he met Elijah. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down, and asked, “Elijah, is it really you?”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Obadia úsela ni, kɔnakunwi kani na ɔ́siaku Elia. Na ka ɔ́nu Elia ɔ́ti ɔsu ni, úbo kalɔ úte-nwu na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Ati awɔ geen mɛni?”

english_verse: Obadiah replied: King Ahab would kill me if I told him that. And I haven't even done anything wrong.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Obadia údie kenye ɔnini, “Bi likpidi na lɛ́bla na eeti ami, ƒula kabla ɔblane, ete Ahab na ɔdu?

english_verse: I swear to you in the name of the living Lord your God that the king has looked everywhere for you. He sent people to look in every country, and when they couldn't find you, he made the leader of each country swear that you were not in that country.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔsu-ɔ ka ni, uwi ɔni na ƒula Unwoti Katɔti uli ngba mɛni ni, ɔma biala uuubo iye ɔga biala uuubo ɔni na mina ati útatala ukyuli ɔdi útakya ka buye ƒula lɛlɔ. Na ɔma biala iye ɔga biala ɔni masu ka eeebo mmɔ ni, ɔɔyá na beesé kenye ka báwia-a na bátanu-ɔ.

english_verse: Do you really want me to tell him you're here?
translation_verse: Na ɔƒɛni aasu-mi aani ntásu mina ati nnii, ‘Elia ɔkya mɛni.’

english_verse: What if the Lord's Spirit takes you away as soon as I leave? When Ahab comes to get you, he won't find you. Then he will surely kill me. I have worshiped the Lord since I was a boy.
translation_verse: Nsu lɛɛɛgyi kesii kani na Unwoti Kɔyu kɔdubuti-ɔ kusienku si lɛ́tɔlɔ-ɔ kudɔ mɛni. Na si lísie ńtásu Ahab na úbo na útanu-ɔ ni, ɔdubo-mi bɔdu. Nsu ami ƒula kabla ɔblane líse kalɔ mɔɔkpá Unwoti mina lɛkloƒu uwi.

english_verse: Elijah said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord All-Powerful, and I swear in his name that I will meet with Ahab today.”
translation_verse: Amu na Elia ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔni na Unwoti ɔni ntulo ƒui uli ngba mɛni na nwuna kabla na mɔɔbla ni, ndubudie lɛlɔ lɛtina Ɔga Ahab ɔmwi kadi.” Elia Úsie Karmel Kɔbi Lili

english_verse: Obadiah left and told Ahab where to find Elijah. Ahab went to meet Elijah,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Obadia útásiaku Ɔga Ahab na ɔ́su-nwu ka ɔ́nu Elia. Na Ahab lɛnɔ útásiaku Elia.

english_verse: and when he saw him, Ahab shouted, “There you are, the biggest troublemaker in Israel!”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Ahab ɔ́nu Elia ni, ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Awɔ Elia mmɔ? Awɔ nákya Israel ƒui lɛsɛ mmɔ?”

english_verse: Elijah answered: You're the troublemaker—not me! You and your family have disobeyed the Lord's commands by worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Amu na Elia údie kenye ɔnini, “Ńtakya lɛsɛ lɛdi na Israel. Nsu awɔ ku ƒ'ɔti kaduli na ɔ́si. Ɔsika bíni Unwoti ɔda bubo na bísie bɛ́siaku Baal kama.

english_verse: Ahab got everyone together, then they went to meet Elijah on Mount Carmel.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Ahab ɔ́kɔ lɛsa na Israel ƒui na ɔ́ya na bekyuli bammɔ ku Baal kenye bediene bátása lisu na Karmel Kɔbi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Elijah stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you try to have things both ways? If the Lord is God, worship him! But if Baal is God, worship him!” The people did not say a word.
translation_verse: Amu na Elia úsie ɔ́vi bekyuli bammɔ akɔ na uuyé-ma ɔnini, “Uwi ɛlɛ geen na bɛdubulie bitaabla kasusu kunyɔ kunyɔ bitálɛ? Si Unwoti ndi Katɔti ni, bɛsiaku-nwu kama. Na si Baal lɛnɔ ndi bina Katɔti ni, na bɛsiaku-nwu kama.” Nsu bekyuli bammɔ bétedie kenye kadi.

english_verse: Then Elijah continued: I am the Lord's only prophet, but Baal has
translation_verse: Amu na Elia ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ami kani ndi Unwoti kenye udiene ɔni nébu. Nsu Baal ubo kenye bediene eti yaalenwi (

english_verse: Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
translation_verse: Bɛwia ɔmantɛ bakɔ inyɔ bite-bu. Na baƒuna unwi bete lɛlɔ na bekulo lɛna lɛmmɔ eku eku basia ekyweni lɛlɔ. Nsu batatu ogya batakya. Na ami lɛnɔ ndubɔdu akɔ unwi na likulo-nwu lɛsia ekyweni lɛlɔ, nsu lɛɛɛdubo ogya bɔtu bɔkya-nwu.

english_verse: The prophets of Baal will pray to their god, and I will pray to the Lord. The one who answers by starting the fire is God. “That's a good idea,” everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama na bɛkpali bina Katɔti, na ami lɛnɔ lɛkpali Unwoti. Na ati ɔni nátuna ku ogya bɔda ni, anwu ndi Katɔti geen.” Amu na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui básu banini, “Lɛla lɛni na ásu mɛni lɛdia geen.”

english_verse: Elijah said to Baal's prophets, “There are more of you, so you go first. Pick out a bull and get it ready, but don't light the fire. Then pray to your god.”
translation_verse: Amu na Elia ɔ́su Baal kenye bediene bammɔ ɔnini, “Bɛƒuna ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku ekyweni esu ammɔ akɔ unwi ɔni na bɛɛyɔ́, ɔsika bimomo. Na bɛkpali bina ati bɛnii ogya uduo-nwu kemmo. Nsu ukyuli biala utatu ogya utakya.”

english_verse: They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bédie akɔ ɔni béti béte-ma na básala ekyweni, na béti lɛna lɛni békulo mmɔ básia-nwu lɛlɔ. Ɔmmɔ kama ka báwɔlɔ ni, bákpali Baal básiku ɔtanta laa bétédu ɔƒiiwi. Na kenye bediene bammɔ baasu banii, “Baal, nu-bu bɔkpali nii!” Na baava takpali-nwu. Nsu lɛla biala lítalɛ. Na bétenu kenye budie bɔdi lɛnɔ. Na baƒiɔ bakpane bammɔ baatɔ́ taamana bana lɛkpabi lɛni bátu bálɛ mmɔ.

english_verse: At noon, Elijah began making fun of them. “Pray louder!” he said. “Baal must be a god. Maybe he's daydreaming or using the toilet or traveling somewhere. Or maybe he's asleep, and you have to wake him up.”
translation_verse: Amu ka udu ɔƒiiwi lɛbo ni, Elia úse kalɔ uubo-ma kenye ɔnini, “Bitaakpali-nwu momoomo, ngyi ka ɔkya uuti kasusu kadi. Ɔsika unwoti na ɔdi. Iye kɔnu kɔda-nwu kpakplaa. Iye úsie ulu ɔdi iye ngyi ka ɔtɛ ɔlɛɛ na ɔlɛka bagyila-nwu.”

english_verse: The prophets kept shouting louder and louder, and they cut themselves with swords and knives until they were bleeding. This was the way they worshiped,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu báva bákpali-nwu momoomo na báda atula ku lɛkɛɛ beekúlo lɛlɔ útédu ka ubugya muedi ɔɔlɛ́, ɔsika lɛni na baayɔ́.

english_verse: and they kept it up until time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no answer of any kind.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛ ɔmmɔ úulii, nsu bátada bɔkpali bɔmmɔ bátaya útédu ka useyi akpala uwi údu. Nsu lɛla biala lítalɛ. Na lɛla biala lɛnɔ lítakpete-ma.

english_verse: Then he used twelve stones to build an altar in honor of the Lord. Each stone stood for one of the tribes of Israel, which was the name the Lord had given to their ancestor Jacob. Elijah dug a ditch around the altar, large enough to hold about
translation_verse: Na úti atabi ammɔ ɔ́tu lɛkpabi na Unwoti lɛnyi kemmo na úku ubu ɔ́mana lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kalɛ na ntu alɔkumbui anyɔ eduo ubu ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: He placed the wood on the altar, then they cut the bull into pieces and laid the meat on the wood. He told the people, “Fill four large jars with water and pour it over the meat and the wood.” After they did this,
translation_verse: Na úti ekyweni ammɔ ɔ́tɛ ɔ́sia lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́du ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔmmɔ na úkulo-nwu eku eku ɔ́sia ekyweni ammɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́su bekyuli bammɔ ɔnini, “Biti alɔkumbui ene na bidu ntu biyile-nya kemmo. Na biti biwi lɛna ku ekyweni ammɔ lɛlɔ.” Na ama lɛnɔ bábla lɛni.

english_verse: he told them to do it two more times. They did exactly as he said
translation_verse: Amu na Elia ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛ́sɔ bisie kunyɔdi bibewi!” Na ama lɛnɔ básɔ bábla lɛni. Amu na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛsɔ bisie kɔtɛdi.” Na ama lɛnɔ bábla lɛni.

english_verse: until finally, the water ran down the altar and filled the ditch.
translation_verse: Na ntu bɔmmɔ bɔ́gba bɔ́vi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ƒui. Na ntu bɔmmɔ búyi ubu ɔni na úku ɔmana mmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah prayed: Our Lord, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Now, prove that you are the God of this nation, and that I, your servant, have done this at your command.
translation_verse: Ka useyi akpala bɔbla uwi údu ni, Kenye Udiene Elia ɔ́lɛ úsie úténye anumi. Amu na ɔ́kpali Katɔti ɔnini, “O Unwoti ɔni ndi Abraham ku Isak ku Israel Katɔti! Ya na bekyuli bamɛni banu bati ɔmwi ka ni, awɔ ndi Israel Katɔti. Na ami lɛnɔ ndi ƒula kabla ɔblane. Na ala ani lɛ́bla mɛni ni, ƒula ɔda bubo kenye na lɛ́bla-nya.

english_verse: Please answer me, so these people will know that you are the Lord God, and that you will turn their hearts back to you.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ni, O Unwoti! Die-mi kenye! Unwoti, die-mi kenye! Kalɛ na bekyuli bamɛni banu bati ka ni, awɔ O Unwoti ndi Katɔti. Na eti atina ka ni, ásɔku-ma kayi eeboku ƒula kudɔ ɔkɛnku ɔmɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord immediately sent fire, and it burned up the sacrifice, the wood, and the stones. It scorched the ground everywhere around the altar and dried up every drop of water in the ditch.
translation_verse: Amu na kɔnakunwi ni, Unwoti ogya ɔ́si katɔ na úbakyula akpala ammɔ ku ekyweni ammɔ ku atabi ammɔ ku lɛti lɛni nwi mmɔ. Na ogya ɔmmɔ ɔ́ta útéduo ntu bɔni béku ubu na buwi-nwu kemmo mmɔ na ɔ́da na ɔkyula-mu ƒui kede kede.

english_verse: When the crowd saw what had happened, they all bowed down and shouted, “The Lord is God! The Lord is God!”
translation_verse: Amu ka bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bánu ɔmɛni ni, báyu bátɛ kalɔ na baava momoomo na baasu banini, “Unwoti ndi Katɔti! Unwoti ndi Katɔti!”

english_verse: Just then, Elijah said, “Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let any of them get away.” So the people captured the prophets and took them to Kishon River, where Elijah killed every one of them. It Starts To Rain
translation_verse: Amu na Elia úbo bekyuli bammɔ ɔda ɔnini, “Biƒie Baal kenye bediene bammɔ ƒui, na bitaya na ɔdi biala ukeli.” Amu na béƒie-ma na Elia ɔ́ya béti-ma bésienku Kison Kɔwɛ kemmo na bádu bana ƒui na mmɔ.

english_verse: Elijah told Ahab, “Get something to eat and drink. I hear a heavy rain coming.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Elia ɔ́su Ahab ɔnini, “Teesie kaduli na atáwia lɛla lɛdi adi na ani. Ɔsika muunú kɔku ka ɔnantu bonwu ɔdi ɔdubo bɔna.”

english_verse: Ahab left, but Elijah climbed back to the top of Mount Carmel. Then he stooped down with his face almost to the ground
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Ahab ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie kaduli na útáwia lɛla lɛdi ɔ́di na ɔ́ni. Nsu Elia ɔ́kɔ úsie Karmel Kɔbi lili. Na mmɔ ni, Elia úbo kalɔ na úti nwuna kuli ɔ́kya nwuna lɛgba akɔ.

english_verse: and said to his servant, “Look toward the sea.” The servant left. And when he came back, he said, “I looked, but I didn't see anything.” Elijah told him to look seven more times.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su nwuna kabla ɔblane ɔnini, “Teesie na ataanu ɛpu kakɛ.” Amu na kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ úsie útánu na úbasu-nwu ɔnini, “Ka lísie ni, ńtánu lɛla lɛdi.” Na maatɛ sɔɔn na Elia ɔ́su nwuna kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Sɔ nwini sie mmɔ.”

english_verse: After the seventh time the servant replied, “I see a small cloud coming this way. But it's no bigger than a fist.” Elijah told him, “Tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and start home now. Otherwise, the rain will stop him.”
translation_verse: Na maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, úbasu Elia ɔnini, “Lɛ́nu liƒlukutu bli suɛ lɛdi ka lɛ́si lɛɛlɛ́ ɛpu kemmo aani ukyuli kɔnu kalɛ.” Amu na Elia úbo nwuna kabla ɔblane ɔda ɔnini, “Keli na atásu Ɔga Ahab na uti nwuna ɔpɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ na ukeli uteesie kaduli kalɛ na ɔnantu uláda-nwu ulakya ulu lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: A few minutes later, it got very cloudy and windy, and rain started pouring down. So Elijah wrapped his coat around himself, and the Lord gave him strength to run all the way to Jezreel. Ahab followed in his chariot.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔyikun úbo Elia lɛlɔ na údie nwuna awu na úti ɔ́sabla kavobi. Na úkeli usi útávi Ahab na útéduo Yesreel.

english_verse: Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done and that he had killed the prophets.
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Ahab ɔ́su ulekudi Isebel lɛla biala na Elia ɔ́bla ku kalɛ na ɔ́du Baal kenye bediene bammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: She sent a message to Elijah: “You killed my prophets. Now I'm going to kill you! I pray that the gods will punish me even more severely if I don't do it by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ahab ulekudi Isebel úti kenye úmene Elia ɔnini, “Asa na uteedu kɔnaadi ɔƒaalɛ bene si ńtaya na awɔ lɛnɔ ekpi aani bana kalɛ ni, na baƒiɔ bammɔ bani-mi kɔtu biala na baayɔ́.”

english_verse: Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ka Elia únu kenye kammɔ ni, liƒu lɛ́da-nwu na úkeli ku nwuna kabla ɔblane kalɛ na balákɛ-nwu baládu. Na ka bédu Beer-Seba na Yuda kalɔ kemmo ni, ɔ́da-nwu ɔ́kya mmɔ,

english_verse: then walked another whole day into the desert. Finally, he came to a large bush and sat down in its shade. He begged the Lord, “I've had enough. Just let me die! I'm no better off than my ancestors.”
translation_verse: na anwu lɛti ɔ́sɔ úsie limeyi linwi ulu na ɔkɛ ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo. Na ka úbedu kugyii kɔdi kalɔ ni, ɔ́yu úlie kalɔ mmɔ na ɔ́kpali Katɔti úvele ka ɔya na ukpi. Na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Lɛ́ɛnɔku-ni. Ƒɔ-mi ngba, ɔsika lɛɛɛdia liiitulo mina bati kuuku.”

english_verse: Then he lay down in the shade and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel woke him up and said, “Get up and eat.”
translation_verse: Ka ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tɛ kugyii kɔmmɔ kalɔ na ɔ́lɛɛ. Kɔnakunwi ni, Katɔti ɔtu ɔdi útuku-nwu na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ta na adi.”

english_verse: Elijah looked around, and by his head was a jar of water and some baked bread. He sat up, ate and drank, then lay down and went back to sleep.
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́ta ni, ɔ́tɛ anu. Na ka ɔ́nu nwuna eli kakɛ ni, bodobodo ɔni béƒi-nwu na uuƒí ku ntu ɔsii ɔdi ɔlɛ mmɔ. Mmɔ na ɔ́di na ɔ́ni na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́yu ɔ́tɛ.

english_verse: So Elijah sat up and ate and drank. The food and water made him strong enough to walk
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔ́ta na ɔ́di na ɔ́ni. Na ka adila ammɔ ákya-nwu ɔkplu ni, úsie lɛgba usien ku ɔƒɛ emeyi aavlene útédu ka údu Katɔti kɔbi kɔni baalɔ banii Horeb.

english_verse: and he spent the night there in a cave. The Lord Appears to Elijah While Elijah was on Mount Sinai, the Lord asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na útéduo lɛtakpɛ ubu ɔdi kemmo na ɔ́tɛ mmɔ usien umodi ɔmmɔ. Unwoti Údie Lɛlɔ Ɔ́tina Elia Amu na Unwoti úye-nwu ɔnini, “Elia, bi na aabla mɛni?”

english_verse: He answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Amu na Elia údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛ́sia anu kpakplaa na lɛ́kpa Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui uwi biala. Na Israelƒuɔ béni ƒula bunyimi na bábwɛ ƒula akpabi. Na bádu ƒula kenye bediene ƒui ku lɛkɛɛ, na ami lɛti nébu. Na ɔƒaani benye baawia kuƒi ka badu ami lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: “Go out and stand on the mountain,” the Lord replied. “I want you to be there when I pass by.” All at once, a strong wind shook the mountain and shattered the rocks. But the Lord was not in the wind. Next, there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛ ténye kɔbi kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na Unwoti anumi. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubo ubasia mmɔ ɔvi.” Amu na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ubendi ɔdi úkpo, na úle kɔbi kɔmmɔ kemmo inyɔ, na úgyingya atakpɛ ammɔ na Unwoti anumi. Nsu Unwoti uuubo ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ kama ni, kalɔ kákunku, nsu Unwoti uuubo kalɔ bɔkunku bɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. Finally, there was a gentle breeze,
translation_verse: Na kalɔ bɔkunku bɔmmɔ kama ni, lɛgyavonku lɛ́bwɛ lɛ́lɛ, nsu Unwoti uuubo ogya ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na ogya ɔmmɔ kama ni, únu butemi bɔdi ku kabɛnsɛ.

english_verse: and when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance to the cave. A voice asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Na ka Elia únu lɛdi lɛmmɔ ni, ɔni nwuna awu ɔtɔdi úbi anumi na ɔ́lɛ úténye ubu ɔmmɔ kenye. Mmɔ na lɛdi lɛmmɔ líye Elia ɔnini, “Bi na aabla mɛni?”

english_verse: Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Amu na Elia údie kenye ɔnini, “Uwi biala ni, mɔɔkpá awɔ Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, na Israelƒuɔ béni ƒula bunyimi na bábwɛ ƒula akpabi na bádu ƒula kenye bediene ƒui ku lɛkɛɛ, na ami kani nébu. Na ɔƒaani benye baawia kuƒi ka badu ami lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Elijah, you can go back to the desert near Damascus. And when you get there, appoint Hazael to be king of Syria.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su Elia ɔnini, “Nwini na atásia ulu ɔni na akɛ ébo. Na eteesie Damasko ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo. Na si édu mmɔ ni, na ewi Hasael lili nnɔmii na ese-nwu Siriaƒuɔ ɔga.

english_verse: Then appoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king of Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat to take your place as my prophet.
translation_verse: Na ewi Nimsi ubidi Yehu lɛnɔ nnɔmii lili na ese-nwu Israelƒuɔ ɔga. Na ewi Saƒat ubidi Elisa ɔni na ɔ́si Abel-Mehola nnɔmii lili na uti-ɔ kenyekɔ aani kenye udiene kalɛ.

english_verse: Hazael will start killing the people who worship Baal. Jehu will kill those who escape from Hazael, and Elisha will kill those who escape from Jehu.
translation_verse: Na Yehu ɔdubɔdu ukyuli biala na úkeli na útekpi na Hasael ɔkɛɛ kenye. Na Elisa ɔdubɔdu ukyuli biala na úkeli na útekpi na Yehu ɔkɛɛ kenye.

english_verse: Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Elia ɔ́tɔlɔ mmɔ na útánu Saƒat ubidi Elisa na kemo kadi ka bébo anwami báda ɔmantɛ bakɔ inyɔ akpa leevu-anyɔ. Na Elisa ɔda lɛkpa leevu-linyɔdi na baatu kalɔ teenwini. Amu na Elia úsie-nwu kudɔ mmɔ, ka úti nwuna lɛduni lɛni na ɔda úbo úwi-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said. “You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
translation_verse: Amu na Elisa lɛnɔ ɔ́da nwuna ɔmantɛ bakɔ bammɔ ɔ́nyonu na ɔbi ɔ́siaku Elia na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ya na lisie na ntákada mina bawɔne asa bɔtɔlɔ.” Amu na Elia údie kenye ɔnini, “Teesie, nsu bla kasusu na lɛla lɛni na lɛ́bla-a lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_verse: Amu na Elisa únwini úsie nwuna ɔmantɛ bakɔ kudɔ na ɔ́du-ma, na úti ala ani na úbo ɔ́da-ma mmɔ ɔ́bla ekyweni na úti úƒulo lɛna lɛmmɔ. Na úti lɛna lɛmmɔ úte nwuna bekyuli na bákun. Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Elisa únwini útásiaku Elia kama aani nwuna ubunkune kalɛ.

english_verse: They dressed in sackcloth and put ropes on their heads, then they went to Ahab and said, “Your servant Benhadad asks you to let him live.” “Is he still alive?” Ahab asked. “Benhadad is like a brother to me.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu béti kekwa adi báda bana kavobi na bébo lɛbuli báda lɛkwɛ. Na bésie Ɔga Ahab kudɔ bátásu-nwu banini, “Ƒula kabla ɔblane Ben-Hadad uuvele-ɔ ka anu-nwu kɔnyana o-o!” Amu na Ɔga Ahab údie kenye ɔnini, “Ben-Hadad ɔmu uli ngba? Mina ɔnwani na ɔdi.”

english_verse: Benhadad sent a messenger to tell King Ahab of Israel,
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́tala bekyuli ɔ́kya Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Ahab ka bátásu-nwu banini, “Lɛni na Ɔga Ben-Hadad ɔɔsu.

english_verse: Later, Benhadad sent another messenger to say to Ahab, “I already told you to give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your children.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama batalane bammɔ básɔ bébo bábasu-nwu banini, “Lɛni na Ben-Hadad ɔɔsu. ‘Kudeedi lɛ́tala ka ndubɔƒɔ ƒula sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ku ƒula beleku ku bebi,

english_verse: But tomorrow at this time, I will send my officials into your city to search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take everything else that you own.”
translation_verse: nsu uteedu kɔnaadi ɔƒaalɛ bene ni, ndubo mina kabla bablane bɔtala na babawia ƒula kaduli kemmo ƒui ku ƒula kabla bablane kɔduli kemmo ƒui. Na lɛla biala na libo kɔsia na bekyuli bammɔ banu ni, badubuti-ni batɔlɔku.’ ”

english_verse: “Don't listen to him!” they answered. “You don't have to do what he says.”
translation_verse: Amu na benengu bammɔ ku bekyuli bani nkya mmɔ bédie kenye banini, “Sɔ tenu-nwu litemi lɛnɔ, iye tete-nwu ala ani na ɔɔwia mmɔ.”

english_verse: So Ahab sent someone to tell Benhadad, “Your Majesty, I'll give you my silver and gold, and even my wives and children. But I won't let you have anything else.” When Benhadad got his answer,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu úti kenye kamɛni úmene Ben-Hadad batalane ɔnii, “Bɛsu ati ɔga bɛnii nwuna kabla ɔblane ɔdubɔbla lɛla lɛni úye-nwu kudeedi mmɔ ute-nwu. Nsu lɛla lɛni na úye kunyɔdi mɛni ani ni, naaakana bɔbla bute-nwu.” Na batalane bammɔ bénwini ku kenye kammɔ bésienku Ben-Hadad.

english_verse: he replied, “I'll completely destroy Samaria! There won't even be enough of it left for my soldiers to carry back in their hands. If I don't do it, I pray that the gods will punish me terribly.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Ben-Hadad úti kenye kabambadi úmene Ahab ɔnini, “Bula baƒiɔ badu-mi si ńtabla lɛla lɛni mɔɔsu mɛni. Samaria ɔma ni, lɛla lɛdi lɛsɔ lilébu uletulo ɔtumu, na uyi lɛkɔkɔ muedi!”

english_verse: Ahab then answered, “Benhadad, don't brag before the fighting even begins. Wait and see if you live through it.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ɔga Ahab lɛnɔ úti kenye úmene ɔnini, “Bɛsu Ɔga Ben-Hadad bɛnii ukyuli ɔni mɔɔkya kekpo awu ni, ulákun lɛmɛne teetulo ukyuli ɔni muudie kekpo awu.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad and the other kings had been drinking in their tents. But when Ahab's reply came, he ordered his soldiers to prepare to attack Samaria, and they all got ready.
translation_verse: Amu ka Ben-Hadad únu kenye kammɔ uwi ɔni na anwu ku nwuna baga bákya adi kevo kemmo baaní ntɛ ni, mmɔ na ɔ́su nwuna bekpone ɔnini, “Batu akpagya na betékpoku Israelƒuɔ.” Anwuɔsu ama lɛnɔ báklibi lɛlɔ ka betékpoku ɔma unengudi bekyuli. Ahab Úkpo Ɔ́di Ben-Hadad Lɛlɔ

english_verse: At that very moment, a prophet ran up to Ahab and said, “You can see that Benhadad's army is very strong. But the Lord has promised to help you defeat them today. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmɛni kani kemmo ni, kenye udiene ɔdi úbo Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Ahab kudɔ úbakɔ lɛsa ɔ́su ɔnini, “Lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu ɔnii, ‘Bɛɛnu bekpone lisu bonwu bamɛni? Ndubo-ma buti bɔkya bina enu kemmo ɔmwi kadi, na mmɔ na bɛdubo bɔnu bɔti ka Unwoti na ndi.’ ”

english_verse: At noon, King Ahab and his Israelite army marched out of Samaria, with the young soldiers in front. King Benhadad of Syria and the
translation_verse: Na bekpone bakɔdi bammɔ nágyu bátɔ kudeedi. Na Ben-Hadad údie batu badi ɔnii batánu lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́, na ama bénwini bábasu-nwu banini, “Bekyuli badi bási Samaria badubo.”

english_verse: “Take them alive!” Benhadad ordered. “I don't care if they have come out to fight or to surrender.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-ma ka, “Si keyi buɛ kemmo na bakɛ ni, biƒie-ma nsu bitadu-ma. Na si kekpo lɛnɔ ɔsu bakɛ muedi ni, bitadu-ma.”

english_verse: The young soldiers led Israel's troops into battle,
translation_verse: Na bekpone bakɔdi bammɔ ni, ama néseku kekpo kammɔ kalɔ asa na Israelƒuɔ bekpone lɛnɔ bétébunku.

english_verse: and each of them attacked and killed an enemy soldier. The rest of the Syrian army turned and ran, and the Israelites went after them. Benhadad and some others escaped on horses,
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bekpone bádu ukpone biala na békpoku. Na Siriaƒuɔ bammɔ békeli, na Israelƒuɔ bammɔ bábi básiaku-ma. Nsu Siriaƒuɔ Ɔga Ben-Hadad ku nwuna bekyuli badi béti bapɔnkɔ na békeli.

english_verse: but Ahab and his soldiers followed them and captured their horses and chariots. Ahab and Israel's army crushed the Syrians.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́bi ɔ́siaku-ma na útavi bapɔnkɔ ku bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ lɛmmɔ. Na ɔ́du Siriaƒuɔ kaduɛ.

english_verse: Later, the prophet went back and warned Ahab, “Benhadad will attack you again next spring. Build up your troops and make sure you have some good plans.” Syria Attacks Israel Again
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ úbo Israelƒuɔ ɔga kudɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Nye ƒula kenyekɔ kpakplaa na anu lɛla lɛni malɛ. Ɔsika ketudi uwi kani ndubo mɛni ni, Siriaƒuɔ badubo bebekpoku-mii lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad's officials went to him and explained: Israel's gods are mountain gods. We fought Israel's army in the hills, and that's why they defeated us. But if we fight them on flat land, there's no way we can lose.
translation_verse: Amu na Siriaƒuɔ ɔga benengu básu-nwu banini, “Israelƒuɔ Katɔti ni, abi eli katɔti na ɔdi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na bákana-bu lɛlɔ bɔ́di. Nsu si búsie butékpoku-ma na kalɔ ƒiaa lɛlɔ ni, ina dɛ bɔdubɔdi-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then get more soldiers, horses, and chariots, so your army will be as strong as it was before. We'll fight Israel's army on flat land and wipe them out. Benhadad agreed and did what they suggested.
translation_verse: Na asɔ edie bekpone bani udu nésie kekpo kudeedi ku bapɔnkɔ bani na ebo mmɔ, na awia bana udu kani kalɛ na bɔkana bukpoku Israelƒuɔ kalɔ ƒiaa lɛlɔ. Na si ákana na ábla lɛni ni, bɔdubɔyu ɔkplu butulo-ma.” Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ únu kalɔ na ɔ́bla lɛni pɛpɛɛpɛ úte-ma.

english_verse: In the spring, Benhadad got his army together, and they marched to the town of Aphek to attack Israel.
translation_verse: Na ka ketudi kammɔ kédu ni, Ben-Hadad ɔ́lɔ Siriaƒuɔ bekpone na anwu ku-ma bésie ɔma unengudi ɔni baalɔ Aƒek ka betékpo ku Israelƒuɔ.

english_verse: The prophet went to Ahab and said, “The Syrians think the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys. So he has promised to help you defeat their powerful army. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Amu na kenye udiene ɔdi úsie Ɔga Ahab kudɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu. Siriaƒuɔ básu ka ami abi lɛlɔ Katɔti na ndi na lɛɛɛdi kalɔ ƒiaa katɔti ɔsu ni, ndubɔya na bɛdi Siriaƒuɔ lɛlɔ. Na mmɔ na awɔ ku ƒula bekyuli bɛdubɔnu bɔti ka Unwoti na ndi.”

english_verse: For seven days the two armies stayed in their camps, facing each other. Then on the seventh day the fighting broke out, and before sunset the Israelites had killed
translation_verse: Na emeyi maatɛ Israelƒuɔ ku Siriaƒuɔ ƒui básala lɛlɔ na bénye báanu lɛlɔ anumi. Na limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, bésie kalɔ beekpó na Israelƒuɔ bádu Siriaƒuɔ mpim eti anyɔ.

english_verse: The rest of the Syrian army ran back to Aphek, but the town wall fell and crushed
translation_verse: Na bani nébu békeli bésie Aƒek ɔma, na mmɔ lɛnɔ ɔma ɔmmɔ awodu áƒɛ áyu Siriaƒuɔ bekpone mpim aavlanyɔ-maatɛ na békpi. Nsu Ben-Hadad úkeli útéduo ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na útábɛ ɔtɔ ɔdi katɔma.

english_verse: His officials said, “Your Majesty, we've heard that Israel's kings keep their agreements. We will wrap sackcloth around our waists, put ropes around our heads, and ask Ahab to let you live.”
translation_verse: Na nwuna benengu bésie bátasu-nwu banini, “Búnu ka Israelƒuɔ baga bebo kɔnyana bɔnu. Anwuɔsu te-bu kuƒi na busie Israelƒuɔ ɔga kudɔ na buti bula kekwa adi bɔda bula kavobi na buti lɛbuli bɔda ɔkwɛ. Ɔƒaalɛ, badubɔnu-bu kɔnyana na baládu-bu.”

english_verse: Benhadad's officials were trying to figure out what Ahab was thinking, and when he said “brother,” they quickly replied, “You're right! You and Benhadad are like brothers.” “Go get him,” Ahab said. When Benhadad came out, Ahab had him climb up into his chariot.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bakloƒu bammɔ beti kenye kani na ɔga ɔmmɔ údie mmɔ kɔnakunwi na bédie kenye banini, “Ɛɛn! Ƒula ɔnwani Ben-Hadad ɔmu uli ngba.” Amu na Ɔga Ahab ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bitéti-nwu biboku.” Uwi ɔni na Ben-Hadad úbo ni, Ahab ɔ́ya na anwu ku-nwu bákɔ bélie nwuna ɔpɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Benhadad said, “I'll give back the towns my father took from your father. And you can have shops in Damascus, just as my father had in Samaria.” Ahab replied, “If you do these things, I'll let you go free.” Then they signed a peace treaty, and Ahab let Benhadad go. A Prophet Condemns Ahab
translation_verse: Amu na Ben-Hadad ɔ́su Ahab ɔnini, “Lɛma lɛni ƒui mina ɔti ɔ́ƒɔ ɔ́siku ƒula ɔti kudɔ ni, ndubɔsɔku-ni lite-ɔ. Na akana atu kuye kubendi kɔdi na Damasko ete lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na mina ɔti ɔ́tu ɔdi na Samaria.” Amu na Ahab údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛla lɛni na ásu mɛni ɔsu ni, ndubɔnyonu-ɔ na atɔlɔ kusɛ kusɛ.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bana inyɔ bábla unwi bɔbla kakunkɛ na bákya kɔnu nwuna kalɔ, na Ahab ɔ́ya na Ben-Hadad ɔ́tɔlɔ. Kenye Udiene Ɔdi Ɔ́dɔnku Ahab Lɛla Lɛni Na Ɔ́bla Ɔsu

english_verse: About this time the Lord commanded a prophet to say to a friend, “Hit me!” But the friend refused,
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔda bubo kenye ni, kenye udiene ɔdi ubidi ɔnanabi ɔ́su nwuna kenye udiene kpana ɔnini, “Ti ƒula ekpola ani na ada mmɔ ƒiɛmi-mi.” Nsu nwuna ɔkpana ɔmmɔ úni.

english_verse: and the prophet told him, “You disobeyed the Lord, and as soon as you walk away, a lion will kill you.” The friend left, and suddenly a lion killed him.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ka átadi Unwoti ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, si átɔlɔ-mi kudɔ pɛ gyata ɔdubo-ɔ bɔdu.” Na sɔsɔ ka ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔnya ɔ́tɔlɔ-nwu kudɔ pɛ kani gyata ɔdi ɔ́nu-nwu na ɔ́du-nwu.

english_verse: The prophet found someone else and said, “Hit me!” So this man beat him up.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́nu ukyuli bamba na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Buvele nda-a, ti lɛla lɛdi ƒiɛmi-mi.” Na ɔnana ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔ́ƒiɛmi-nwu na ɔ́pila-nwu.

english_verse: The prophet left and put a bandage over his face to disguise himself. Then he went and stood beside the road, waiting for Ahab to pass by.
translation_verse: Na kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́wia kɔdi únyimi anumi kalɛ balanu-nwu baláti. Na úténye ulu lɛlɔ ɔɔnu uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ ɔga wavi.

english_verse: When Ahab went by, the prophet shouted, “Your Majesty, right in the heat of battle, someone brought a prisoner to me and told me to guard him. He said if the prisoner got away, I would either be killed or forced to pay
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́si ɔɔví ni, kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́pkali-nwu ɔnini, “Ati, ƒula kabla ɔblane ɔkya kekpo kani kebo ɔkplu kemmo uukpó asa na ukpone ɔdi úti nwuna ukisine ɔni na úbeƒie úboku-mi na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Taagyumana ɔnana ɔmɛni. Na si úkeli ni, adubuti ƒula ngba aƒɔ kayu. Iye ndubɔƒɔ sika ɔƒualadi mpim eti aku.’

english_verse: But I got busy doing other things, and the prisoner escaped.” Ahab answered, “You will be punished just as you have said.”
translation_verse: Nsu ka anumi égyie-mi na mɔɔbla ala bamba ɔsu ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ úkeli.” Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Awɔ ɔlati ádu ƒula lɛlɔ kɔtɔ, na ɔlɛka aƒɔ kayu kani bébo-ɔ mmɔ.”

english_verse: The man quickly tore the bandage off his face, and Ahab saw that he was one of the prophets.
translation_verse: Ka kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔnya ɔ́su lɛni ɔ́wɔlɔ kani ɔ́ƒɛnimi kɔdi kɔmmɔ údie nwuna anumi. Mmɔ kani na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́nu-nwu ɔ́ti ka ɔdi kenye bediene bammɔ kemmo unwi.

english_verse: The prophet said, “The Lord told you to kill Benhadad, but you let him go. Now you will die in his place, and your people will die in place of his people.”
translation_verse: Na kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu ɔnii, ‘Ukyuli ɔni na líbo-ɔ ɔda ka badu-nwu ni, áya na úkeli. Anwuɔsu adubuti ƒula ngba aƒɔ kayu. Na ƒula bekpone lɛnɔ badubɔyii ku udu, ɔsika áya na Ben-Hadad bekpone békeli.’ ”

english_verse: Ahab went back to Samaria, angry and depressed.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔga ɔmmɔ únwini úsie nwuna ɔma Samaria ku kɔnyi, na etemila ammɔ akya eekpóku-nwu.

english_verse: One day, Ahab said, “Naboth, your vineyard is near my palace. Give it to me so I can turn it into a vegetable garden. I'll give you a better vineyard or pay whatever you want for yours.”
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, Ahab ɔ́su Nabot ɔnini, “Kalɛ na ƒula kevoma kemo kamɛni kede mina kaduli ɔsu ni, ti-ka te-mi na liti-ka lɛbla kevoma evete kemo. Na ndubute-ɔ kalɔ bamba iye si aayɔ́ ni, ndubɔƒɔ-ɔ kayu kani námanku.”

english_verse: Naboth answered, “This vineyard has always been in my family. I won't let you have it.”
translation_verse: Amu na Nabot údie kenye ɔnini, “Mina bati kuuku kalɔ kadi. Na ɔmwi kebenwini mina kadikɔ. Na Unwoti úbo-mi ɔda ka nteti-ka netete-ɔ.”

english_verse: So Ahab went home, angry and depressed because of what Naboth had told him. He lay on his bed, just staring at the wall and refusing to eat a thing.
translation_verse: Amu na Ahab únwini úsie kaduli ɔni na úƒu na úti kɔnyi ɔ́si lɛla lɛni na Nabot ɔ́su-nwu mmɔ ɔsu. Ɔsika ɔ́su-nwu ka. “Lɛɛɛdubo-ɔ mina bati kuuku kalɔ buti bute.” Na úsie ɔ́tɛ bana atɛla lɛlɔ na únwini anumi ɔ́tina kowodu na úni ka ɔdi muedi.

english_verse: Jezebel his wife came in and asked, “What's wrong? Why won't you eat?”
translation_verse: Amu na ulekudi Isebel úbo na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi muukpóku-ɔ lɛni na éni anii aladi muedi?”

english_verse: “I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard or to let me give him a better one,” Ahab replied. “And he told me I couldn't have it.”
translation_verse: Amu na údie ulekudi kenye ɔnini, “Lɛ́su Nabot ɔni ndi Yesreelni ka uti nwuna kevoma kemo kalɔ kammɔ ute-mi na lite-nwu kalɔ kabambadi. Nsu ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Lɛɛɛdubo-ka buti bute-ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: “Aren't you the king of Israel?” Jezebel asked. “Get out of bed and eat something! Don't worry, I'll get Naboth's vineyard for you.”
translation_verse: Amu na Isebel ɔ́su ɔgyani ɔnini, “Lɛni na ɔlɛka awɔ Israelƒuɔ ɔga abla ala avinku? Ta na adi na akɛ ebiti. Na ndubɔƒɔ Yesreelni Nabot kalɔ kammɔ lite-ɔ.”

english_verse: After receiving her letters, they did exactly what she had asked.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu benengu ku bakutine bani nási Yerseel mmɔ bábla kalɛ na Isebel úbo-ma ɔda mmɔ.

english_verse: They told the people that it was a day to go without eating, and when they all came together, they seated Naboth at the front.
translation_verse: Na bése kenye bunyimi limeyi lɛmmɔ, na básala bekyuli bammɔ lisu, na béte Nabot keliekɔ kani náƒɔ kuye.

english_verse: The two liars came in and sat across from Naboth. Then they accused him of cursing God and the king, so the people dragged Naboth outside and stoned him to death.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama báwia nkyuli inyɔ bani mbo likyulikpi na bénye bekyuli akɔ mmɔ na báda Nabot kenye banini, “Nabot ɔkya uuwida Katɔti ku Israelƒuɔ ɔga.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bákpanku-nwu bálɛku ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na bébo-nwu atabi bádu.

english_verse: The leaders of Jezreel sent a message back to Jezebel that said, “Naboth is dead.”
translation_verse: Na béti kenye bémene Isebel banii, “Bébo Nabot bádu.”

english_verse: As soon as Jezebel got their message, she told Ahab, “Now you can have the vineyard Naboth refused to sell. He's dead.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni kani na kenye kammɔ kédu Isebel kudɔ kani na útásu Ahab ɔnini, “Nabot úkpi, anwuɔsu ta na etéti kevoma kalɔ kemo kammɔ.”

translation_verse: Amu na Ahab ɔ́ta kɔnakunwi ka utéti kalɔ kammɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Elijah the prophet,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Unwoti ɔ́su Kenye Udiene Elia ɔni na ɔ́si Tisbi ɔnini,

english_verse: “King Ahab of Israel is in Naboth's vineyard right now, taking it over.
translation_verse: “Ta na atásiaku Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Ahab ɔni mɔɔdi Samaria lɛlɔ. Ɔkya Nabot kevoma kemo kalɔ lɛlɔ ka utéti-ka ɔbla nwuna kadi.

english_verse: Go tell him that I say, ‘Ahab, you murdered Naboth and took his property. And so, in the very spot where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they will lick up your blood.’ ” When Elijah found him,
translation_verse: Na asu-nwu anini, ‘Lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu. Ɔɔɔdi bɔdu na ádu ukyuli na ékpeli nwuna kadikɔ aaƒɔ́?’ Ɔmmɔ kama na asu-nwu anii, ‘Lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu. Kesii kani na bakpɛwe báyalɛ Nabot ubugya ni, mmɔ kani badubo awɔ lɛnɔ ƒula ɔdi geen bɔyalɛ!’ ”

english_verse: Ahab said, “So, my enemy, you found me at last.” Elijah answered: Yes, I did! Ahab, you have managed to do everything the Lord hates.
translation_verse: Amu na Ahab ɔ́su Elia ɔnini, “Bi? Bɔnu na awɔ mina ukisine ánu-mi?” Amu na Elia údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛ́nu-ɔ, ɔsika éti lɛlɔ éye éte likpidi na Unwoti anumi.

english_verse: Now you will be punished. You and every man and boy in your family will die, whether slave or free.
translation_verse: Na anwu mɔɔsu-ɔ ɔnii, ‘Ndubo ɔgbankpi buti buboku-ɔ lɛlɔ. Na lɛyila Ahab lɛnyi ku ƒula kaba bekyuli ƒui udu útédu ɔnanabi ukplodi lɛlɔ, ina kabla ɔblane na ɔdi iye uli ute lɛlɔ na badi awɔ badi na Israel kalɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Your whole family will be wiped out, just like the families of King Jeroboam and King Baasha. You've made the Lord very angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Na lɛni na ndubɔbla ƒula kaduli aani kalɛ lɛ́bla Nebat ubidi Yerobeam ku Ahia ubidi Basa kadi. Ɔsika ákya-mi kɔnyi na áya na Israelƒuɔ lɛnɔ bábla likpidi.’

english_verse: And as for Jezebel, dogs will eat her body there in Jezreel.
translation_verse: “Na Isebel anwu ni, lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu ɔnii, ‘Bakpɛwe ndubo-nwu lɛna bɔduli na Yesreel awodu lɛlɔ.’

english_verse: Dogs will also eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: “Na bakpɛwe badubɔkun Ahab lɛna na ɔma unengudi, na kayaa baasɛ badubɔduli bani nékpi na alakpi akɔ lɛna.”

english_verse: Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
translation_verse: Na asu-ma ka lɛni na ɔga ɔɔsu ɔnini, ‘Biti okloƒu ɔmɛni bɛkya ɔtɔ. Na bitete-nwu lɛla biala na ɔdi, si ɔɔɔdi bodobodo ku ntu kani wetédu ka línwini ḿbeduo buɛɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Ahab asked his officials, “Why haven't we tried to get Ramoth in Gilead back from the Syrians? It belongs to us.”
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́su nwuna kabla bablane ɔnini, “Bɔgyi na bɛɛɛgyi ka abu mbo Ramot-Gilead ɔsu búdie lɛlɔ atu na bulie na bulála lɛla lɛdi na bɔƒɔ mmɔ bɔsiku Siriaƒuɔ ɔga kudɔ?”

english_verse: Then he asked Jehoshaphat, “Would you go to Ramoth with me and attack the Syrians?” “Just tell me what to do,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu úye Yehosaƒat ɔnini, “Adubo ebebunku-mi na butékpoku Ramot-Gilead?” Amu na Yehosaƒat údie Israelƒuɔ ɔga kenye ɔnini, “Nse aani ƒula kalɛ na mina bekyuli badi ƒula bekyuli na mina bapɔnkɔ badi ƒula bapɔnkɔ.”

english_verse: prophets and asked, “Should I attack the Syrians at Ramoth?” “Yes!” the prophets answered. “The Lord will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: ) ɔ́sala na úye-ma ɔnini, “Nteesie Ramot-Gilead na ntékpoku-ma munuu ntesie?” Amu na kenye bediene bammɔ básu-nwu banini, “Teesie! Ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubo-ma buti bɔkya awɔ ɔga enu kemmo.”

english_verse: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
translation_verse: Nsu Yehosaƒat úye Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔnini, “Unwoti kenye udiene biala ɔ́sɔ uuubo mɛni na buye-nwu litemi lɛmɛni bunu?”

english_verse: Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́lɔ nwuna kabla ɔblane unwi na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Tiku Imla ubidi Mikaia boku mɛni ɔƒaani.”

english_verse: All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria. They were listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ ɔga ku Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Yehosaƒat bakya bana baga ala na beli bana baga eboku lɛlɔ. Na beli Samaria ulu lɛlɔ na kesii kani baakɔ́ ɔlaaƒɔ. Na kenye bediene bammɔ ƒui beli-ma kudɔ baasu ala na bana anumi.

english_verse: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
translation_verse: Na Kenaana ubidi Sedekia úti lɛbuala na ɔ́bla bebuo ese anyɔ adi na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu ɔnini, ‘Ese amɛni na adubuti akya Siriaƒuɔ ɔlɛ lɛlɔ útédu ka áyila-ma udu ƒui.’ ”

english_verse: All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth, and they promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
translation_verse: Na lɛni kani na kenye bediene bakladi ƒui lɛnɔ baasu banini, “Biteesie bitékpoku Ramot-Gilead na bɛdubɔdi-ma lɛlɔ, ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubuti-ma ɔkya ɔga enu kemmo.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
translation_verse: Na ɔtalane ɔni bátála ka útéti Mikaia uboku mmɔ ɔɔsu Mikaia ɔnini, “Nu, awɔ lɛti pɛ ndi kenye udiene ɔni nébu. Na kenye bediene bakladi baasu lɛla lɛni ndia teete ɔga. Anwuɔsu, ya ƒula etemila ku bani ngye adi abla unwi. Na asu lɛla lɛni ndubɔyɔ ɔga kaƒɔ.”

english_verse: “I'll say whatever the living Lord tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
translation_verse: Nsu Mikaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Na Unwoti ɔni nli ngba lɛnyi kemmo ni, lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi kani ndubo bɔsu.”

english_verse: Then Micaiah went to Ahab, and Ahab asked, “Micaiah, should I attack the Syrians at Ramoth?” “Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Mikaia úbeduo ni, ɔga úye-nwu ɔnini, “Nsie ntékpoku Ramot-Gilead munuu ntesie?” Amu na Mikaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Teesie na etékpoku-ma, na adubɔdi lɛlɔ. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubuti-ma ɔkya-a enu kemmo.”

english_verse: “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth!” Ahab shouted. “What does the Lord really say?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔga ɔmmɔ úye Mikaia ɔnini, “Kɔlɛ na ɔlɛka lɛya-a na ese kenye ka alasu lɛla lɛdi eletulo lɛla lɛni ndi sɔsɔ geen litemi na Unwoti lɛnyi kemmo?”

english_verse: He answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers walking around in the hills like sheep without a shepherd to guide them. The Lord said, ‘This army has no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mikaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛ́nu ka Israelƒuɔ ƒui bégyingya bewi abi eli aani baƒonu bani na beeebo lɛlɔ ɔnune. Na Unwoti ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Bekyuli bamɛni beeebo ɔtɔnkune, anwuɔsu ya na ɔdi biala unwini uteesie nwuna kaduli ku atu bɔyɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Micaiah replied: Listen to this! I also saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him.
translation_verse: Amu na Mikaia úsie anumi ku nwuna kenye budie ɔnini, “Ɔmmɔ ɔsu binu Unwoti litemi. Lɛ́nu ka Unwoti úli nwuna liboku lɛlɔ na katɔ batu ƒui bénye-nwu kɔmii ku kɔdianu.

english_verse: This is exactly what has happened, Ahab. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu ni, Ahab, lɛla lɛni na mɔɔsu mɛni geen nálɛku-ɔ lɛni kani pɛpɛɛpɛ. Unwoti ɔ́ya na ƒula kenye bediene bányi ɔkɔ bátɔlɔ-ɔ, na ɔgyi lɛnɔ ka blii kani nébu na badubo-ɔ udu bɔyila ƒui kede kede.”

english_verse: Zedekiah walked up to Micaiah and slapped him on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Kenaana ubidi Sedekia úsie na útáƒiɛmi Mikaia lɛtukpo. Na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Uwi ɔmani na Unwoti Kɔyu kɔ́lɛ-mi lɛlɔ kemmo na úbo ubatɛmiku-ɔ?”

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ahab ɔ́va ku lɛdi momoomo ɔ́su ɔnini, “Biƒie Mikaia! Biti-nwu bisienku ɔga ubi Yosa ku Samaria aban ɔgadine Amon kudɔ.

english_verse: However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab where two pieces of his armor joined. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
translation_verse: Amu na Siriani ukpone ɔdi úbo nwuna kataminta na kávi Ɔga Ahab lɛgyumanala kasakɔ na kálɛ-nwu. Mmɔ kani na Ɔga Ahab ɔ́va ɔ́kpali nwuna kɛɛkɛ ɔkane ɔnini, “Bákya-mi ɔlɛ lɛlɔ, ɔmmɔ ɔsu nwini lɛlɔ na alɛku-mi kekpokɔ mɛni.”

english_verse: Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ ɔga ku Ɔga Yehosaƒat bésie Ramot-Gilead ka bétékpoku bekyuli bammɔ.

english_verse: Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Then Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Ahab ɔ́su Ɔga Yehosaƒat ɔnini, “Ami ndubɔda mina agala ani nkya lidie na lɛbla lɛlɔ aani ukyuli keeke ɔdi. Nsu awɔ ti ƒula agala kya.” Anwuɔsu Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́bla lɛlɔ aani ukyuli keeke ɔdi na úsie kekpokɔ.

english_verse: So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But when Jehoshaphat shouted out to them,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ka bapɔnkɔ bakane bammɔ bánu Ɔga Yehosaƒat ni, bábu banii anwu ndi Israelƒuɔ ɔga. Na bésie bétékpoku-nwu. Nsu ka údie lɛdi ni,

english_verse: As the sun was going down, someone in Israel's army shouted to the others, “Retreat! Go back home!”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na ɔƒɛ úsela kanukɔ ni, kɔvanu kubendi kɔdi kɔ́lɛ bekpone bammɔ akɔ na baasu banini, “Ukyuli biala uteesie nwuna ɔma. Na ukyuli biala uteesie nwuna kalɔ lɛlɔ!”

english_verse: Ahab's body was taken to Samaria and buried there.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Ɔga Ahab úkpi na béti-nwu bésienku Samaria na bátáva-nwu na mmɔ.

english_verse: Some workers washed his chariot near a spring in Samaria, and prostitutes washed themselves in his blood. Dogs licked Ahab's blood off the ground, just as the Lord had warned.
translation_verse: Na béti nwuna kɛɛkɛ ɔmmɔ bésienku ligyu lɛdi na Samaria na bátáƒɔ. Mmɔ ndi kesii kani na bayalɛ baakpí, na bakpewɛ báyalɛ nwuna ubugya na mmɔ aani kalɛ na Unwoti litemi lɛ́su ka ɔdubo-nwu bɔlɛku.

english_verse: Everything else Ahab did while he was king, including the towns he strengthened and the palace he built and furnished with ivory, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba akladi ani na Ɔga Ahab ɔ́bla ku kalɛ na úti ɔtunkpɛ ɔ́klibi nwuna kaduli ku lɛma linengudi lɛni ƒui na ɔ́da ni, bénweni-nya bákya Israelƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: Ahab died, and his son Ahaziah became king. King Jehoshaphat of Judah (
translation_verse: Na Ahab úkpi na ubidi Ahasia úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ. Yehosaƒat Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Yuda

english_verse: Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in Ahab's fourth year as king of Israel.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa linedi kemmo na Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Ahab lɛga bɔdi kama ni, Asa ubidi Yehosaƒat úbenwini Israelƒuɔ ɔga.

english_verse: The country of Edom had no king at the time, so a lower official ruled the land.
translation_verse: Na Edomƒuɔ beeebo ɔga geen ɔdi na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo, mmomu ɔga kenye unyene nátaadi-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat had seagoing ships built to sail to Ophir for gold. But they were wrecked at Ezion-Geber and never sailed.
translation_verse: Na Yehosaƒat ɔ́nwi lɛkɔlɔ bonwu bonwu kalɛ na nka liteesie taatádi kuye teeye sika ugyiedi teeboku, nsu lɛkɔlɔ lɛmmɔ lítakana ulu busie tɔ kudii asa na ɔgbankpi úbalɛku-ni na lɛ́yii udu na Esion-Geber kesii kani na linye mmɔ.

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab offered to let his sailors go with Jehoshaphat's sailors, but Jehoshaphat refused.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king. King Ahaziah of Israel
translation_verse: Amu na Yehosaƒat úkpi na báva-nwu na Dawid ɔma unengudi. Na ubidi Yehoram úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ. Ahasia Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Israel

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa leevu-maatɛdi na Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Yehosaƒat lɛga bɔdi kemmo ni, ubidi Ahasia úbenwini Israelƒuɔ ɔga. Na úlie Samaria ɔ́di lɛga lɛmmɔ na mmɔ akwa anyɔ.

english_verse: Ahaziah disobeyed the Lord, just as his father, his mother, and Jeroboam had done. They all led Israel to sin.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́bla likpidi na Unwoti anumi. Na ɔ́siaku ɔti Ahab ku uni Isebel ku Yerobeam likyulikpi lɛmmɔ kama. Na bákpanku Israelƒuɔ bátákya likpidi kemmo.

english_verse: Ahaziah worshiped Baal and made the Lord God of Israel very angry, just as his father had done.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́kpa Baal na ɔɔkya-nwu lili kalɔ aani kalɛ na ɔti ɔ́bla na ɔ́kya Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti kɔnyi.

english_verse: Soon after King Ahab of Israel died, the country of Moab rebelled against his son King Ahaziah. One day, Ahaziah fell through the wooden slats around the porch on the flat roof of his palace in Samaria, and he was badly injured. So he sent some messengers to the town of Ekron with orders to ask the god Baalzebub if he would get well.
translation_verse: Na Ɔga Ahasia úbuli ɔ́siku nwuna ɔtɔ katɔ úbayu kalɔ na Samaria, na nwuna lɛlɔ lɛ́ƒɔ ɔlɛ kaduɛ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu, ɔ́tala batu badi na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bisie na bitéye Baal-Sebub ɔni ndi Ekronƒuɔ baƒiɔ si ndubo bɔta na ɔlɛ ɔni na muuƒi mɛni kemmo?”

english_verse: About the same time, an angel from the Lord sent Elijah the prophet from Tishbe to say to the king's messengers, “Ahaziah has rejected Israel's own God by sending you to ask Baalzebub about his injury.
translation_verse: Nsu Katɔti ɔtu ɔdi ɔ́su Elia ɔni ndi Tisbini ɔnini, “Ta na atásiaku batalane bani na Samariaƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́tala mmɔ. Na eye-ma anini, ‘Ka Katɔti uuubo Israel ɔsu na bísela Ekronƒuɔ baƒiɔ Baal-Sebub kudɔ?’

english_verse: Tell him that because he has done this, he's on his deathbed!” And Elijah did what he was told.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ni, lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu, ‘Alata atɛla ani lɛlɔ na atɛ mmɔ. Na si ina ábla bi muedi adubukpi.’ ” Amu na Elia úsie na ɔ́su-ma kenye kammɔ.

english_verse: When the messengers returned to Ahaziah, he asked, “Why are you back so soon?”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na batalane bammɔ bénwini bébo ɔga ɔmmɔ kudɔ ni, úye-ma ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na bɛ́sɔ bínwini bíbo?”

english_verse: “A man met us along the road with a message for you from the Lord,” they answered. “The Lord wants to know why you sent us to ask Baalzebub about your injury and why you don't believe there's a God in Israel. The man also told us that the Lord says you're going to die.”
translation_verse: Amu na bédie kenye banini, “Ɔnana ɔdi úbasiaku-bu ulu. Na ɔ́su-bu ɔnii bunwini na bubasu-ɔ bɔnini, ‘Lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu! Ka Katɔti ɔdi uuubo Israel ɔsu na átala bekyuli ka batánu Ekronƒuɔ baƒiɔ Baal-Sebub? Ɔ́si ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, alata ƒula atɛla ani lɛlɔ na atɛ mmɔ. Na bukpi kani na adubukpi.’ ”

english_verse: “What did the man look like?” Ahaziah asked.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ úye-ma ɔnini, “Dɛ na ɔnana ɔni nábasiaku-mii mmɔ use?”

english_verse: “He was hairy and had a leather belt around his waist,” they answered. “It must be Elijah!” replied Ahaziah.
translation_verse: Amu na ama lɛnɔ bédie kenye banini, “Ɔdi ɔnana ɔni na nwuna lɛlɔ libo linwini na úti ebuo ɔku ɔda nwuna kavobi.” Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Tisbini, Elia mmɔ.”

english_verse: Fire has already wiped out the other officers and their soldiers. Please don't let it happen to me.”
translation_verse: Nu! Ogya ɔ́si katɔ na úbakyula batɔnkune inyɔ bedeedi ku bana bekyuli ƒui. Nsu ami muuvele-ɔ ka ti ɔbu te mina ngba!”

english_verse: The angel from the Lord said to Elijah, “Go with him and don't be afraid.” So Elijah got up and went with the officer.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔtu ɔdi úbasu Elia ɔnini, “Yu na awɔ ku-nwu bɛtɔlɔ, na tayia-nwu.” Mmɔ na Elia ku ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ báyu bésie kalɔ na bátɔlɔ bésie ɔga ɔmmɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: When Elijah arrived, he told Ahaziah, “The Lord wants to know why you sent messengers to Ekron to ask Baalzebub about your injury. Don't you believe there's a God in Israel? Ahaziah, because you did that, the Lord says you will die.”
translation_verse: Amu na Elia ɔ́su ɔga ɔnini, “Lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu, ‘Ɔni na eeebo Katɔti ɔdi na Israel na eye-nwu lɛla lɛdi enu ɔsu na átala bekyuli na Ekronƒuɔ baƒiɔ Baal-Sebub kudɔ? Na lɛla lɛni na ábla mɛni ɔsu ni, alata ƒula atɛla ani lɛlɔ na atɛ mɛni, na bukpi kani na adubukpi!’ ”

english_verse: Ahaziah died, just as the Lord had said. But since Ahaziah had no sons, Joram his brother then became king. This happened in the second year that Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔga ɔmmɔ úkpi aani kalɛ na Unwoti ɔ́su Elia ka ɔsu-nwu. Na ka Ahasia uuubo ubi ɔnanabi ɔsu ni, Yehoram úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ, na lɛkwa linyɔdi lɛni na Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Yehosaƒat ubidi Yehoram ɔɔdi lɛga.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ala ani nálɛku Ɔga Ahasia ku ala bamba ani na ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-nya bákya Israelƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: Not long before the Lord took Elijah up into heaven in a strong wind, Elijah and Elisha were leaving Gilgal.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Unwoti ɔɔyɔ́ ka uti Elia usienku katɔ na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni mɔɔkya ligede kemmo ni, Elia ku Elisa báta bási Gilgal.

english_verse: Elijah said to Elisha, “The Lord wants me to go to Bethel, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Bethel.
translation_verse: Amu na Elia ɔ́su Elisa ɔnini, “Sɔ nye mɛni, ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́tala-mi ɔnii nteesie Betel.” Amu na Elisa údie-nwu kenye ɔnini, “Na awɔ ku Unwoti ɔni nli ngba mɛni anumi ni, lɛɛɛdubo-ɔ bɔnyonu!” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bana inyɔ ƒui básiaku lɛlɔ bésie Betel.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Katɔti kenye bediene lɛkpa lɛni nkya Betel bébo Elisa kudɔ na béye-nwu banini, “Agyi ka Unwoti ɔdubo ƒula ati buti bɔtɔlɔku ɔmwi kadi?” Amu na Elisa údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɛɛn, ngyi! Nsu bɛya-nwu kɔtɛ kɔmmɔ kɔwɔ mmɔ.”

english_verse: Elijah then said, “Elisha, now the Lord wants me to go to Jericho, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life, that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Jericho.
translation_verse: Amu na Elia ɔ́su Elisa ɔnini, “Sɔ nye mɛni, ɔsika Unwoti ɔtala-mi Yeriko.” Amu na Elisa údie kenye ɔnini, “Na awɔ ku Unwoti ɔni nli ngba mɛni anumi ni, lɛɛɛdubo-ɔ bɔnyonu.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu básiaku lɛlɔ bátɔlɔ bésie Yeriko.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti kenye bediene lɛkpa lɛni nkya Yeriko bésie Elisa kudɔ na béteye-nwu banini, “Agyi ka Unwoti ɔdubo ƒula ati buti bɔtɔlɔku ɔmwi kadi?” Amu na Elisa údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɛɛn, ngyi! Nsu kɔtɛ kɔmmɔ kɔwɔ mmɔ.”

english_verse: Elijah then said to Elisha, “Now the Lord wants me to go to the Jordan River, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will never leave you!” So the two of them walked on together.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Elia ɔ́su Elisa ɔnini, “Sɔ nye mɛni, ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́tala-mi na Yordan Ketu.” Amu na Elisa údie kenye ɔnini, “Na awɔ ku Unwoti ɔni nli ngba mɛni anumi ni, lɛɛɛdubo bɔsɔ bunye.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bana inyɔ ƒui bátɔlɔ.

english_verse: Fifty prophets followed Elijah and Elisha from Jericho, then stood at a distance and watched as the two men walked toward the river.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na kenye bediene lisu lɛmmɔ bésie na béténye kɔƒɛlɛ, na benye baanu kesii kani na Elia ku Elisa bédi bénye na Yordan Ketu kɔtu.

english_verse: When they got there, Elijah took off his coat, then he rolled it up and struck the water with it. At once a path opened up through the river, and the two of them walked across on dry ground.
translation_verse: Amu na Elia údie nwuna lɛduni lɛni na ɔda na ɔ́ƒɛ-ni ɔ́sala na úti ɔ́ƒiɛmi Yordan Ketu. Na ketu kammɔ kéle lɛlɔ kemmo inyɔ na bákɛ ketu kammɔ kemmo bávia kalɔ kakwiidi lɛlɔ bésie ɔvi unyɔdi.

english_verse: After they had reached the other side, Elijah said, “Elisha, the Lord will soon take me away. What can I do for you before that happens?” Elisha answered, “Please give me twice as much of your power as you give the other prophets, so I can be the one who takes your place as their leader.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bávia báwɔlɔ ni, Elia ɔ́su Elisa ɔnini, “Su-mi lɛla lɛni na aayɔ́ ka lite-ɔ asa na beti-mi batɔlɔku na ƒula kudɔ.” Amu na Elisa údie kenye ɔnini, “Ya na kɔnu kutuku-mi Katɔti Kɔyu ɔyikun ɔni náƒɔ-ɔ lɛlɔ kemmo akpa anyɔ.”

english_verse: “It won't be easy,” Elijah answered. “It can happen only if you see me as I am being taken away.”
translation_verse: Amu na Elia ɔ́su Elisa ɔnini, “Éye lɛla lɛni libo ɔkplu geen. Nsu si enye aanu uwi ɔni na béti-mi baatɔlɔku ƒula kudɔ béselaku katɔ ni, kɔnu kɔdubutuku-ɔ lɛla lɛni na éye. Nsu ɔmmɔ kama anwu ni, alákɛ lɛla lɛmmɔ.”
