english_verse: Jehu left for Samaria, and along the way, he met some relatives of King Ahaziah of Judah at a place where shepherds meet. He asked, “Who are you?” “We are relatives of Ahaziah,” they answered. “We're going to visit his family.”
translation_verse: mmɔ na ɔ́siaku Yudaƒuɔ ɔga ɔkukudi Ahasia lɛlɔ bekyuli badi. Amu na Yehu úye-ma ɔnini, “Ɔma bene na bɛdi?” Amu na bekyuli bammɔ bédie kenye banini, “Bɔdi Ɔga Ahasia lɛlɔ bekyuli. Na búsela Yesreel butánu Ɔga Uleku Isebel bebi ku bekyuli bakladi bani nkya ɔga kaduli mmɔ na bɔnu kalɛ na bakya.”

english_verse: “Take them alive!” Jehu said to his officers. So they grabbed them and led them to the well near the shepherds' meeting place, where they killed all
translation_verse: Amu na Yehu ɔ́su nwuna bekyuli ɔnini, “Biƒie-ma enu ku enu.” Anwuɔsu béƒie-ma na bákpanku-ma bésienku Bet-Eked libiɔ kɔtu na bátádu bana nkyuli aavlene-inyɔ na mmɔ ɔni na útaya na ɔdi ubu.

english_verse: As Jehu went on, he saw Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. Jehu greeted him, then said, “Jehonadab, I'm on your side. Are you on mine?” “Yes, I am.” “Then give me your hand,” Jehu answered. He helped Jehonadab into his chariot
translation_verse: Ka ɔ́tɔlɔ mmɔ úsela ni, útásiaku Rekab ubidi ɔni baalɔ-nwu banii Yehonadab. Na Yehu ɔ́kya-nwu kenye ɔnini, “Aabu ka ami ku-ɔ bɔdi benwi aani kalɛ ami mɔɔkali?” Amu na Yehonadab údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɛɛn, bɔdi benwi geen.” Amu na Yehu ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Si use lɛni bɔdi na ete-mi kɔnu.” Amu na béte lɛlɔ enu. Na Yehu úbunku-nwu na ɔ́kɔ úduo nwuna ɔpɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ kemmo.

english_verse: and said, “Come with me and see how faithful I am to the Lord.” They rode together in Jehu's chariot
translation_verse: Na Yehu ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Siaku-mi na awɔ ɔlati anu ku ƒula anumi kalɛ na mbo kogyoklo nte Unwoti kabla.” Amu na bana inyɔ ƒui bélie ɔpɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ɔmmɔ bésie Samaria.

english_verse: to Samaria. Jehu killed everyone there who belonged to Ahab's family, as well as all his officials. Everyone in his family was now dead, just as the Lord had promised Elijah. Jehu Kills All the Worshipers of Baal
translation_verse: Ka bétéduo ni, Yehu ɔ́du Ahab lɛlɔ bekyuli ƒui na útanu ina unwi kɔnyana. Ɔsika lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su Elia ka ɔdubɔlɛ. Bádu Baal Baƒiɔ Bakpane Ƒui

english_verse: Jehu called together the people in Samaria and said: King Ahab sometimes worshiped Baal, but I will be completely faithful to Baal.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔ́lɔ Samaria bekyuli ƒui ɔ́sala na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Kabla blii kadi kani na Ɔga Ahab ɔ́bla úte Baal baƒiɔ. Na ami ndubɔbla kabla kenengudi lite-nwu.

english_verse: I'm going to offer a huge sacrifice to him. So invite his prophets and priests, and be sure everyone who worships him is there. Anyone who doesn't come will be killed. But this was a trick—Jehu was really planning to kill the worshipers of Baal.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ni, bɛlɔ Baal kenye bediene ƒui ku nwuna bakpane ku benengu ƒui bɛsala na ɔdi utada lɛlɔ utedie-nwu kemmo, ɔsika ndubo akpala bonwu adi bɔbla bute Baal. Na ɔkpane biala ɔni mada lɛlɔ medie-nwu kemmo ndubɔya badu-nwu.” Ɔmɛni ɔdi kakwɛ kani na Yehu ɔ́bla kalɛ na ɔkɛ Baal bakpane ƒui ɔdu.

english_verse: He said, “Announce a day of worship for Baal!” After the day had been announced,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yehu úbo ɔda ɔnini, “Bise limeyi na bula ƒui bubo bubadi limeyi na bɔkya lili kalɔ bute Baal.” Anwuɔsu bése limeyi sɔsɔ.

english_verse: Jehu sent an invitation to everyone in Israel. All the worshipers of Baal came, and the temple was filled from one end to the other.
translation_verse: Na Yehu úti kenye úmene Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui ka bani ƒui mɔɔkpá Baal bebo, na ina unwi utebu. Na bétéduo Baal kakpakɔ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo na bakpane bammɔ béyii ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo ku atu ku atu.

english_verse: Jehu told the official in charge of the sacred robes to make sure that everyone had a robe to wear.
translation_verse: Amu Yehu úbo ɔkpane ɔni mɔɔnú bakpane lɛwu kesekɔ lɛlɔ ɔda ɔnii udie bakpane lɛwu na uti ute bakpane bammɔ.

english_verse: Jehu and Jehonadab went into the temple, and Jehu said to the crowd, “Look around and make sure that only the worshipers of Baal are here. No one who worships the Lord is allowed in.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Yehu ɔlati ku Rekab ubidi Yehonadab bétéduo kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo. Mmɔ na Yehu ɔ́su bekyuli bani nkya ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo ɔnini, “Bɛsia anu na bɛnu kaduɛ ka Baal bakpane lɛti nkya ɔtɔ ɔmɛni kemmo. Na Unwoti ɔkpane biala uuubunku-ma akɔ.”

english_verse: As soon as Jehu finished offering the sacrifice, he told the guards and soldiers, “Come in and kill them! Don't let anyone escape.” They slaughtered everyone in the crowd and threw the bodies outside. Then they went back into the temple
translation_verse: Ka Yehu ɔ́bla nwuna akpala ɔ́wɔlɔ kani na ɔ́su bekyuli bani nkya baagyumana ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Biduo na bitádu-ma ƒui na bitaya na ɔdi ukeli.” Amu na bekyuli bammɔ bétéduo ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo na bákpa bana atula na bádu-ma ƒui kede kede, na bákpɛ-ma bálɛku ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo bébewi keyi. Na básɔ bétéduo kakpakɔ kammɔ katɔma,

english_verse: and carried out the image of Baal. They burned it
translation_verse: na bátágyu Baal baƒiɔ lɛtabi kedee lɛmmɔ bálɛku bábakyula.

english_verse: and broke it into pieces, then they completely destroyed Baal's temple. And since that time, it's been nothing but a public toilet.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bábwɛ Baal lɛtabi kedee lɛmmɔ na báƒɛ Baal kakpakɔ kammɔ ƒui béwi kalɔ, na béti mmɔ bénwini kuvodɔ kesiekɔ.

english_verse: But he did not stop the worship of the gold statues of calves at Dan and Bethel that Jeroboam had made for the people to worship.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔ́siaku Nebat ubidi Ɔga Yerobeam likpidi kama na ɔ́kpanku Israelƒuɔ na bésie bakya baakpá ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔni bávɔ bálɛ na Betel na Dan kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Later the Lord said, “Jehu, you have done right by destroying Ahab's entire family, just as I had planned. So I will make sure that the next four kings of Israel will come from your own family.”
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́su Yehu ɔnini, “Ka ábla ásiaku lɛla lɛni na lɛ́su-ɔ nnii, ‘Bla Ahab kaba bekyuli lɛlɔ’ ɔsu na líse-ɔ kenye ka ɔ́si ƒula kaba kedeedi útédu kenedi lɛlɔ ni, badubɔdi lɛga na Israel.”

english_verse: But Jehu did not completely obey the commands of the Lord God of Israel. Instead, he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam had caused the Israelites to do. Jehu Dies
translation_verse: Nsu Yehu úteti nwuna kayi ƒui útasia Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ ɔti ɔda bubo lɛlɔ. Mmomu ɔ́siaku Yerobeam ɔbladu kama na ɔ́kpanku Israelƒuɔ útákya likpidi kemmo.

english_verse: In those days the Lord began to reduce the size of Israel's territory. King Hazael of Syria defeated the Israelites and took control
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Unwoti úse kalɔ ɔɔyá na Israel kalɔ kaaƒana. Na Siriaƒuɔ Ɔga Hasael úkpo ɔ́di lɛlɔ na Israel kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo,

english_verse: of the regions of Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan River and north of the town of Aroer near the Arnon River. This was the land where the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh had once lived.
translation_verse: ɔ́si Yordan ɔƒɛ katukɔ na Gilead kalɔ kemmo ɔkɛ Gad ku Ruben ku Manase kɔlɛkɛ kunengudi kemmo, ɔ́si Aroer ɔma na ɔkɛ Arnon Ketudɔ na ɔ́sia ɔ́vi Gilead útédu Basan.

english_verse: Everything else Jehu did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani na Yehu ɔ́bla ku nwuna kayi kani na úse ni, bénweni-nya bákya Israelƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: Jehu died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoahaz became king.
translation_verse: Na Yehu úkpi na báva-nwu na Samaria. Na ubidi Yehoahas úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ.

english_verse: Jehu had ruled Israel
translation_verse: Na Yehu ɔ́di lɛga na Israel akwa aavlanyɔ-maane.

english_verse: Jehoiada brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David and gave them to the commanders.
translation_verse: Na Yehoiada úti Dawid atula ku agyumanala ani nse kakpakɔ mmɔ úte benengu ku bagyumanane bammɔ.

english_verse: Jehoiada brought Joash outside, where he placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, while the crowd clapped and shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Yehoiada ɔ́kpanku Yoas ɔ́lɛku keyi. Na úti ɔga kabua úbi-nwu na úti bunyimi kakunkɛ ɔ́kya-nwu enu kemmo. Na béwi Yoas nnɔmii lili na bébo-nwu kudu ka anwu ndi ɔga. Na bekyuli bammɔ bágya anukpɛ na báva momoomo básu banini, “Ɔga uli ngba gyɔlɔɔ!”

english_verse: Joash hid in the temple with Jehosheba for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah. Jehoiada Makes Joash King of Judah (
translation_verse: Na Yehoseba úti ɔnamu ɔmmɔ ɔ́bɛla ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo akwa aku na ɔɔnu-nwu lɛlɔ mmɔ uwi ɔni na Atalia ɔdi uleku ɔga.

english_verse: Joash was only seven years old when this happened.
translation_verse: Na Yoas ɔ́ɔkɛ akwa maatɛ asa na bése-nwu lɛga.

english_verse: Joash son of Ahaziah had hidden in the Lord's temple six years. Then in the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest sent for the commanders of the king's special bodyguards and the commanders of the palace guards. They met him at the temple, and he asked them to make a promise in the name of the Lord. Then he brought out Joash
translation_verse: Nsu lɛkwa maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, Yehoiada ɔni ndi ɔkpane ɔ́ya na bálɔ bagyumanane esu esu bani mɔɔnu ɔga kaduli lɛlɔ benengu ƒui béboku Unwoti kakpakɔ mmɔ. Na anwu ku-ma bényimi lɛla lɛdi na bése kenye ka baláda balavia lɛla lɛni na badubo bɔbla. Ɔmmɔ kama úti Ɔga ubidi ɔmmɔ ɔ́tina-ma.

english_verse: and said to them: Here's what I want you to do. Three of your guard units will be on duty on the Sabbath. I want one unit to guard the palace.
translation_verse: Na úbo-ma ɔda ɔmɛni ɔnii, “Si bíbo kabla kablakɔ na lɛnwunameyi biala ni, bile lɛlɔ akpa atɛ na lɛkpa linwi bataagyumana ɔga kaduli.

english_verse: Another unit will guard Sur Gate, and the third unit will guard the palace gate and relieve the palace guards.
translation_verse: Na lɛkpa linwi lɛnɔ basɔ benye na bataagyumana kayakun kani baalɔ Sur. Na lɛkpa lɛkladi bataagyumana kayakun kani nkya bagyumanane kama kesii kani na baavumana lɛlɔ taagyumana kakpakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: The other two guard units are supposed to be off duty on the Sabbath. But I want both of them to stay here at the temple and protect King Joash.
translation_verse: Na akpa anyɔ bani na belesie kabla na lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ ni, basɔ benye bataagyumana kakpakɔ kammɔ teete ɔga.

english_verse: Make sure they follow him wherever he goes, and tell them to keep their swords ready to kill anyone who tries to get near him.
translation_verse: Na bidie atula bɛda na bitaagyumana Ɔga Yoas. Na bilie-nwu kudɔ na si úsela kesii kadi na bɛsiaku-nwu. Na ukyuli biala makpɛ mede-mii ni, na bɛdu-nwu.”

english_verse: The commanders followed Jehoiada's orders. Each one called together his guards—those coming on duty and those going off duty.
translation_verse: Amu na esu esu ammɔ benengu bénu kalɔ ka badi etemila ani na Yehoiada ɔ́su-ma mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na béti bana bagyumanane bani muusié kabla lɛnwunameyi ku bani neeesie kabla lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ béboku Ɔkpane Yehoiada kudɔ.

english_verse: Then they gave the weapons to their guards, who took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect Joash on every side.
translation_verse: Na bagyumana bammɔ bákpa bana atula báda na báka bámana ɔga ɔmmɔ na kesii kani nde lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ. Na bakladi benye kakpakɔ kammɔ baagyumana ɔ́si katɔ kakɛ útédu kada kakɛ.

english_verse: There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns, which was the usual place for the king. The singers and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the people were celebrating and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́nu ɔga ɔwɔdi ɔmmɔ ka unye kakpakɔ kayakun ɔtɔ lɛkpa lɛdi kudɔ aani kalɛ na baabla lɛga buse ɔdi ɔmmɔ. Na benengu ku kɔkpɛɛ bavwine báka bámana-nwu. Na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui beedie lɛlɔyɔ kudu na baavwi bana kɔkpɛɛ. Mmɔ na ɔ́bla Atalia ɔkuɛnu na ɔ́ni nwuna lɛwu ɔ́bwɛ na ɔ́va momoomo ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bɛ́ta bínye ɔda bubo lɛlɔ! Bɛ́ta bínye ɔda bubo lɛlɔ!”

english_verse: At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Kill her! But don't do it anywhere near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops and kill anyone who is with her!”
translation_verse: Na ka Yehoiada útayɔ ka badu Atalia na kakpakɔ amadɔ mmɔ ɔsu ni, ɔ́su bekpone benengu ɔnini, “Bɛni-nwu bɛlɛku kesii kani na ɔkya mmɔ biboku lɛlɔ na bɛdu ukyuli biala masiaku-nwu.” Ɔsika ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnii, “Útalɛka badu-nwu na Unwoti kakpakɔ mmɔ.”

english_verse: So the commanders dragged her to the gate where horses are led into the palace, and they killed her there.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu uwi ɔni na uudú kayakun kani na bapɔnkɔ baasia teeduo kaduli mmɔ kani na béƒie-nwu na bádu-nwu.

english_verse: Jehoiada the priest asked King Joash and the people to promise that they would be faithful to each other and to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane Yehoiada údie bunyimi bɔdi keyi na Unwoti ku ɔga ɔmmɔ ku bekyuli bammɔ ntɛ ka badubunwini Unwoti kadi bekyuli. Na ɔ́sɔ údie bunyimi bamba keyi na ɔga ku bekyuli bammɔ ntɛ.

english_verse: Then the crowd went to the temple built to honor Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal right in front of the altars. After Jehoiada had placed guards around the Lord's temple,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, bekyuli bammɔ bésie Baal kakpakɔ bátáƒɛ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ. Na bábwɛ akpabi ani bátu bálɛ mmɔ ku ala ani bátu bálɛ mmɔ ƒui. Na bádu Matan ɔni mɔɔkpá Baal na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ anumi. Amu na Ɔkpane Yehoiada úti bagyumanane badi útényene Unwoti kakpakɔ kammɔ na baagyumana mmɔ.

english_verse: he called together all the commanders, the king's special bodyguards, the palace guards, and the people. They led Joash from the temple, through the Guards' Gate, and into the palace. He took his place on the throne and became king of Judah.
translation_verse: Na Yehoiada útiku bagyumanane esu esu ammɔ batɔnkune ku ɔga bagyumanane ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui na bákpanku Ɔga Yoas básiku kakpakɔ mmɔ bésienku ɔga kaduli. Na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔkɛ bagyumanane kayakun na útélie nwuna lɛgaboku lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
translation_verse: Na ebiti áƒɔ bekyuli bammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ kemmo, nsu ɔma ɔmmɔ use diin, ɔsika bádu Atalia na ɔga kaduli mmɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: Jehoiada the priest taught Joash what was right, and so for the rest of his life Joash obeyed the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Yoas ɔ́bla lɛla lɛni na lɛ́yɔ Unwoti kaƒɔ akwa ani ƒui na ɔkpane Yehoiada útaalɛ-nwu mmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The fines that had to be paid along with the sacrifices to make things right and the sacrifices for sin did not go to the temple. This money belonged only to the priests.
translation_verse: Na egulabi ani na baakɛ́ taasiku bɔƒiɔ ku ekpidi lili buvele atela ani na bekyuli beeboku ni, beléboku-nya Unwoti kakpakɔ mmɔ beeti-nya teete bakpane, ɔsika ama ɔdi na ɔdi.

english_verse: But even Joash did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Nsu Yoas útegyingya aƒiodu ani na bátu bálɛ abi eli mmɔ. Anwuɔsu bekyuli bammɔ bésie anumi na baabla bana akpala na baakyula oloƒui na mmɔ.

english_verse: One day, Joash said to the priests, “Collect all the money that has been given to the Lord's temple, whether from taxes or gifts,
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, Yoas ɔ́lɔ bakpane bammɔ ƒui ɔ́sala na úbo-ma ɔda ɔnini, “Egulabi ani na beeyi na Unwoti kakpakɔ ku ani na bekyuli beeboku aani etela kedee ku kenye buse etela ku kaƒɔ ƒaa etela ni, bɛsala egulabi ammɔ ƒui lisu.

english_verse: and use it to repair the temple whenever you see the need.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane biala ɔƒɔ egulabi ammɔ ɔsiku egulabi kusekɔ kɔmmɔ kudɔ na beti baklibi Unwoti kakpakɔ kammɔ kesii biala na bɛ́nu ka kébie.”

english_verse: But the priests never started repairing the temple. So in the twenty-third year of his rule,
translation_verse: Nsu úti útédu akwa aavlanyɔ-lɛtɛdi lɛlɔ na Yoas lɛga bɔdi kemmo ni, bakpane bammɔ bátaklibi lɛla biala tɔ na kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Joash called for Jehoiada and the other priests and said, “Why aren't you using the money to repair the temple? Don't take any more money for yourselves. It is only to be used to pay for the repairs.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Ɔga Yoas ɔ́lɔ ɔkpane Yehoiada ku bakpane badi úbunku lɛlɔ na úye-ma ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na biláklibi kakpakɔ ala ani na ébie mmɔ? Ɔ́si ɔmmɔ ɔsu, bɛsɔ bɛɛɛdubo kakpakɔ egulabi bɔda. Ɔlɛka bɛnyonu-nya bite na bataaklibi ala ani na ébie na kakpakɔ mmɔ.”

english_verse: The priests agreed that they would not collect any more money or be in charge of the temple repairs.
translation_verse: Amu na bakpane bammɔ bénu kalɔ ka basɔ balada egulabi ammɔ, na ɔɔɔdi ama alati lɛnɔ ndubɔklibi kakpakɔ kammɔ.

english_verse: Jehoiada found a wooden box; he cut a hole in the top of it and set it on the right side of the altar where people went into the temple. Whenever someone gave money to the temple, the priests guarding the entrance would put it into this box.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yehoiada ɔ́bla egulabi kakyakɔ kadi na ɔ́ƒuala-ka katɔ údie liƒi lɛdi. Na úti adaka ɔmmɔ útálɛ kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo kɔdianu kakɛ si eeduo ɔtɔ kemmo na ude lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ. Na ɔkpane ɔni mɔɔgyumana kakpakɔ kammɔ kayakun uuti egulabi ani na bekyuli bammɔ beeyi taakya-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: When the box was full of money, the king's secretary and the chief priest would count the money and put it in bags.

english_verse: Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel in the fifteenth year of Amaziah's rule in Judah. Jeroboam ruled
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa leevu-lɛlɔndi kemmo ɔni na Amasia, Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Yoas ubidi, ɔɔdi lɛga ni, bése Yehoas ubidi Yerobeam lɛga na Israel, na ɔ́di lɛga lɛmmɔ na Samaria akwa aavlene-unwi.

english_verse: The Lord helped Jeroboam do this because he had seen how terribly the Israelites were suffering, whether slave or free, and no one was left to help them.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́nu lɛbibo libendi lɛni kemmo na Israelƒuɔ ƒui ku bana kabla bablane bákya, nsu ukyuli ɔdi uuubo na ute-ma kebunku.

english_verse: And since the Lord had promised that he would not let Israel be completely destroyed, he helped Jeroboam rescue them.
translation_verse: Na ka Unwoti útasu ka wayila Israelƒuɔ ƒui udu kede kedee ɔsu ni, údie-ma ɔ́lɛku lɛbibo lɛmmɔ kemmo ɔ́siaku Ɔga Yerobeam ɔni ndi Yehoas ubidi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he recaptured the towns of Damascus and Hamath, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Yerobeam ɔ́bla ala bamba ani nálɛ kɔsia na nwuna kekpo ku kayi kani na úse na kekpo kemmo. Úkpo ɔ́ƒɔ Damasko ku Hamat lɛma ɔ́sɔku úboku Israel kalɔ kemmo. Na bénweni-nya bákya Israelƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: Everything else Pekahiah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Pekah of Israel
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani na Ɔga Pekahia ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-nya bákya Israelƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo. Peka Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Israel

english_verse: Pekahiah became king of Israel in the fiftieth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Na akwa liti kemmo, ka Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Asaria ɔɔdi lɛga ni, bése Menahem ubidi Pekahia lɛga na lɛkwa liti lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ na Israel. Na ɔ́di lɛga lɛmmɔ na Samaria akwa anyɔ.

english_verse: Azariah obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́siaku ɔti Amasia ɔbladu kama na ɔ́bla ala ani náƒɔ Unwoti anu.

english_verse: But Azariah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Nsu bátabwɛ aƒiodu ani na abi eli mmɔ, anwuɔsu bekyuli bammɔ bésie anumi na baabla bana akpala na baakyula bana oloƒui na mmɔ.

english_verse: The Lord punished Azariah with leprosy for the rest of his life. He wasn't allowed to live in the royal palace, so his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́ya ɔlɛgyie úwi ɔga ɔmmɔ, na ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ ɔ́da-nwu útédu nwuna likpimeyi, anwuɔsu kaduli bamba na ɔ́kya na ɔsɔ ulábla lɛla lɛdi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ubidi Yotam nélie ɔga kaduli kammɔ útaadi kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Everything else Azariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani na Asaria ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-nya bákya Yudaƒuɔ baga ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: Azariah died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Jotham then became king. King Zechariah of Israel
translation_verse: Asaria úbekpi na báva-nwu bédenku nwuna bati na Ɔga Dawid ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo, na ubidi Yotam úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ. Sakaria Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Israel

english_verse: Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, but he ruled only six months from Samaria.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa avlaatɛ-maanedi kemmo uwi ɔni na Asaria ɔɔdi lɛga na Yuda ni, bése Yerobeam ubidi Sakaria lɛga na Israel na ɔ́di lɛga lɛmmɔ na Samaria abuli aku.

english_verse: Shallum son of Jabesh plotted against Zechariah and killed him in public. Shallum then became king.
translation_verse: Na Yabes ubidi Salum úti kasusu kekpidi na únyimi na Sakaria lɛlɔ, na úténye ɔ́siaku-nwu na bekyuli anumi. Na ɔ́du-nwu na úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ.

english_verse: So the Lord had kept his promise to Jehu that the next four kings of Israel would come from his family. Everything else Zechariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Shallum of Israel
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu kenye kani na Unwoti ɔ́su úse ɔkɛnku Yehu lɛlɔ kébo-nwu kemmo lɛni ɔni na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ƒula kaba kemmo bebi badubɔdi lɛga na Israel útédu kaba kenedi lɛlɔ.” Salum Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Israel

english_verse: Shallum became king of Israel in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah's rule in Judah. But only one month after Shallum became king,
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa avlaatɛ-yaalenwidi ɔni na Usia ɔɔdi lɛga na Yuda ni, bése Yabes ubidi Salum lɛga na Israel na ɔ́di lɛga lɛmmɔ kɔbuli kunwi.

english_verse: Menahem became king of Israel in Azariah's thirty-ninth year as king of Judah, and he ruled Israel ten years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa avlaatɛ-yaalenwidi kemmo ka Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Asaria ɔɔdi lɛga ni, bése Gadi ubidi Menahem lɛga na Israel. Na ɔ́di lɛga lɛmmɔ na Samaria akwa leevu.

english_verse: He constantly disobeyed the Lord by following the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́siaku Nebat ubidi Ɔga Yerobeam ɔbladu kama. Na ɔ́bla likpidi na Unwoti anumi na ɔ́kpanku Israelƒuɔ útákya likpidi kemmo útédu nwuna likpimeyi.

english_verse: During Menahem's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria invaded Israel. He agreed to help Menahem keep control of his kingdom, if Menahem would pay him over
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Asiriaƒuɔ Ɔga Pul útéti Israel kalɔ. Na Menahem ɔ́wia sika ɔƒualadi antabi aƒo eti maatɛ ku aavlanyɔ (

english_verse: Jotham followed the example of his father by obeying the Lord and doing right.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́siaku ɔti Usia ɔbladu kama. Na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́bla lɛla lɛni náƒɔ Unwoti anu.

english_verse: Everything else Menahem did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani na Menahem ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-nya bákya Israelƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah became king. King Pekahiah of Israel
translation_verse: Na Menahem úkpi na báva-nwu na ubidi Pekahia úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ. Pekahia Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Israel

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and caused the Israelites to sin, just as Jeroboam son of Nebat had done.
translation_verse: Na Pekahia ɔ́bla likpidi na Unwoti anumi, ɔsika útenwini kama útakya Nebat ubidi Yerobeam ɔbladu ukpidi ɔmmɔ kama.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and followed the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́siaku Nebat ubidi Ɔga Yerobeam ɔbladu ukpidi kama ɔsu ɔ́bla likpidi na Unwoti anumi. Ɔni na ɔ́kpanku Israelƒuɔ útákya likpidi kemmo.

english_verse: During Pekah's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria marched into Israel. He captured the territories of Gilead and Galilee, including the towns of Ijon, Abel-Bethmaacah, Janoah, Kedesh, and Hazor, as well as the entire territory of Naphtali. Then he took Israelites from those regions to Assyria as prisoners.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Peka ɔdi ɔga na Israel ni, Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔni baalɔ Tiglat-Pileser úkpo ɔ́ƒɔ Iyon ku Abel-Bet-Maaka ku Yanoa ku Kedes ku Hasor ku Gilead ku Galilea ku Naƒtali lɛma ƒui. Na úƒie bekyuli bammɔ úsienku Asiria na útákya-ma ɔtɔ.

english_verse: In the twentieth year of Jotham's rule in Judah, Hoshea son of Elah plotted against Pekah and murdered him. Hoshea then became king of Israel.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa aavlanyɔdi lɛlɔ na Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Usia ubidi Yotam lɛga bɔdi uwi ni, Ela ubidi Hosea ɔ́bla kasusu kekpidi na Ɔga Peka lɛlɔ na ɔ́du-nwu na úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ.

english_verse: Everything else Pekah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Jotham of Judah (
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani na Peka ɔ́bla na nwuna lɛga bɔdi kemmo ni, bénweni-nya bákya Israelƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo. Yotam Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Yuda

english_verse: Jotham son of Azariah became king of Judah in the second year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa linyɔdi kemmo ka Amalia ubidi Peka ɔɔdi lɛga na Israel ni, bése Usia ubidi Yotam lɛga na Yuda.

english_verse: It was Jotham who rebuilt the Upper Gate that led into the court around the Lord's temple. But the local shrines were not destroyed, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Nsu aƒiodu ani na abi eli anya ni, útegyingya-nya. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bekyuli bammɔ bésie anumi baakyula oloƒui na akpabi ammɔ lɛlɔ. Na Ɔga Yotam násɔku Unwoti kakpakɔ kayakun kani na katɔ kakɛ mmɔ ɔ́tu.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani na Ɔga Yotam ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-nya bákya Yudaƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: During his rule, the Lord let King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel start attacking Judah.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo na Unwoti úse kalɔ uudie bekisine taakya Yudaƒuɔ ka bétékpoku-ma. Na ama ndi Siriaƒuɔ Ɔga Resin ku Remalia ubidi Peka.

english_verse: Jotham died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: Na Yotam úkpi na báva-nwu na Dawid ɔma unengudi baga kavakɔ. Na ubidi Ahas úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ.

english_verse: Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah in the seventeenth year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa leevu-maatɛdi lɛni na Remalia ubidi Peka ɔɔdi lɛga na Israel ni, bése Yotam ubidi Ahas lɛga na Yuda.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Hezekiah became king.
translation_verse: Na Ahas úkpi na báva-nwu na Dawid ɔma unengudi baga kavakɔ, na ubidi ɔni baalɔ Hesekia úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ.

english_verse: Uriah did everything Ahaz told him.
translation_verse: Na Uria ɔ́bla aani kalɛ kani ɔga úbo-nwu ɔda.

english_verse: and was even more sinful than the kings of Israel. He sacrificed his own son, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́siaku Israelƒuɔ baga bedeedi ɔbladu ukpidi kama na úti ubidi muedi ɔ́kyula ɔ́kpa úte baƒiɔ, na ɔkɛ ɔsiaku kadi bekyuli bekpidi bani na Unwoti ɔ́bɔku ɔ́lɛku-ma anumi mmɔ ɔbladu kama.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛ abi ƒui eli ku egyii enengudi ɔyuli kalɔ ɔɔbla akpala na ɔɔkyula oloƒui.

english_verse: While Ahaz was ruling Judah, the king of Edom recaptured the town of Elath from Judah and forced out the people of Judah. Edomites then moved into Elath, and they still live there. About the same time, King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel marched to Jerusalem and attacked, but they could not capture it.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Edomƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́sɔ úkpo ɔ́ƒɔ Elat ɔma. Na ɔ́bɔku Yudaƒuɔ bani ƒui nli mmɔ. Na Edomƒuɔ bénwini béduo kalɔ kammɔ kemmo na bamu beli mmɔ úbedu ɔmwi kadi.

english_verse: Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria that said, “Your Majesty, King Rezin and King Pekah are attacking me, your loyal servant. Please come and rescue me.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Ahas ɔ́tala batu ɔ́kya Asiriaƒuɔ Ɔga Tiglat-Pileser ku kenye kamɛni ɔnini, “Ƒula ubi kabla ɔblane na ndi. Bo, na ebekpo aƒɔ-mi alɛku Siriaƒuɔ ɔga ku Israelƒuɔ ɔga enu kemmo.”

english_verse: Along with the message, Ahaz sent silver and gold from the Lord's temple and from the palace treasury as a gift for the Assyrian king.
translation_verse: Na Ahas úti sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ɔni nse kakpakɔ ku ɔga kavumii úbunku ka beti betéte Siriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: As soon as Tiglath Pileser received the message, he and his troops marched to Syria. He captured the capital city of Damascus, then he took the people living there to the town of Kir as prisoners and killed King Rezin.
translation_verse: Na ka Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga únu litemi lɛmɛni ni, útiku nwuna bekpone na bétékpoku Damaskoƒuɔ. Na bádu Ɔga Resin. Na béti bekyuli bakladi bammɔ bésienku Kir, batɔntɛne kalɛ.

english_verse: Later, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser. And while Ahaz was there, he saw an altar and sent a model of it back to Uriah the priest, along with the plans for building one.
translation_verse: Ka Ɔga Ahas úsie Damasko útásiaku Asiriaƒuɔ Ɔga Tiglat-Pileser na Damasko ni, ɔ́nu lɛkpabi lɛdi na mmɔ. Na ɔ́ta kalɛ na béti bátu-ni úmene ɔkpane Uria na ɔ́su-nwu ka ɔtu lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ udu pɛpɛɛpɛ ute-nwu.

english_verse: Uriah followed the plans and built an altar exactly like the one in Damascus, finishing it just before Ahaz came back.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Uria lɛnɔ ɔ́tu lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kalɛ kani na báta-ni mmɔ.

english_verse: When Ahaz returned, he went to see the altar and to offer sacrifices on it. He walked up to the altar
translation_verse: Na ka Ahas ɔ́si Damasko úbeduo ni, ɔ́nu ka báatu lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ báwɔlɔ.

english_verse: and poured wine over it. Then he offered sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessings.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́bla bɔkyula akpala ku edula akpala na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na úti ntɛ ɔ́bla akpala, na unwi bɔbla akpala ani na ɔ́bla ni, úti ubugya ɔmmɔ ɔ́kuna úwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: After that, he had the bronze altar moved aside, so his new altar would be right in front of the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Na abualagyie lɛkpabi lɛni nnye Unwoti anumi mmɔ ni, Ahas ɔ́gyu lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ útálɛ katɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: He told Uriah the priest: From now on, the morning and evening sacrifices as well as all gifts of grain and wine are to be offered on this altar. The sacrifices for the people and for the king must also be offered here. Sprinkle the blood from all the sacrifices on it, but leave the bronze altar for me to use for prayer and finding out what God wants me to do.
translation_verse: Na úbo Uria ɔda ɔnini, “Awɔ ti mina lɛkpabi libendi lɛni na lɛ́tu mmɔ na ataabla ɔtanta bɔkyula akpala ku useyi uwi edula akpala. Na ɔga ku bekyuli bammɔ bɔkyula ku edula akpala ku ntɛ akpala anya ni, bɛƒɔ bebuo bani ƒui béti bákpa mmɔ ubugya bɛkuna biwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu abualagyie lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ani ni, da-ni se-mi na nteebo like nwuna lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Ahaz also had the side panels and the small bowls taken off the movable stands in the Lord's temple. He had the large bronze bowl, called the Sea, removed from the bronze bulls on which it rested and had it placed on a stand made of stone.
translation_verse: Na Ɔga Ahas ɔ́lɛmi adaka ɔni nlɛ kakpakɔ mmɔ. Na údie akyami ani nkya-nwu kemmo. Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́timi ntu kewikɔ bonwu kani nsia abualagyie ɔmantɛ bakɔ bani na bávɔ bálɛ mmɔ básia atabi adi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: He took down the special tent that was used for worship on the Sabbath and closed up the private entrance that the kings of Judah used for going into the temple. He did all these things to please Tiglath Pileser.
translation_verse: Na ɔga keliekɔ kani na bátu na Unwoti kakpakɔ kemmo ni, Ahas ɔ́gyingya-ka na úbimi likpɔtɔ lɛni mbi mmɔ. Na ɔ́kalɛ kayakun kani na ɔga lɛti ɔɔsia teeduo kakpakɔ mmɔ kalɛ na kaƒɔ kayɔ Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani na Ɔga Ahas ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-nya bákya Yudaƒuɔ baga lɛlɔ kɔtɛ ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in the twelfth year of Ahaz's rule in Judah, and he ruled nine years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa leevu-linyɔdi kemmo ɔni na Ɔga Ahas ɔɔdi lɛga na Yuda ni, bése Ela ubidi Hosea lɛnɔ lɛga na Israel. Na ɔ́di lɛga lɛmmɔ na Samaria akwa yaalenwi.

english_verse: Hoshea disobeyed the Lord and sinned, but not as much as the earlier Israelite kings had done.
translation_verse: Ɔ́bla likpidi na Unwoti anumi. Nsu nwuna likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla ni, lítedu Israelƒuɔ baga bani nélie bávi lɛdi.

english_verse: During Hoshea's rule, King Shalmaneser of Assyria invaded Israel; he took control of the country and made Hoshea pay taxes.
translation_verse: Na Asiriaƒuɔ Ɔga Salmaneser útékpoku Ɔga Hosea. Na Hosea ɔ́kya-nwu kalɔ aani kadi bekyuli bani lɛlɔ na ɔɔdi kalɛ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu, uuyi kuyi teesienku Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga lɛkwa biala.

english_verse: But later, Hoshea refused to pay the taxes and asked King So of Egypt to help him rebel. When Shalmaneser found out, he arrested Hoshea and put him in prison. Samaria Is Destroyed and the Israelites Are Taken to Assyria
translation_verse: Nsu lɛkwa lɛdi ni, Ɔga Hosea ɔmɛni ɔ́tala bekyuli ɔ́kya Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ɔni baalɔ banii So ka ubebunku-nwu na betékpoku Asiriaƒuɔ na ɔda nwuna lɛkwa ndi lɛkwa kuyii kɔmmɔ bɔyii ɔya. Na ka Ɔga Salmaneser únu litemi lɛmɛni ni, ɔ́ya béteƒie Ɔga Hosea bákya ɔtɔ.

english_verse: Shalmaneser invaded Israel and attacked the city of Samaria for three years,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́nwanɛ lɛlɔ úduo Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ, na ɔ́ka Samaria ɔma ɔ́kya akwa atɛ.

english_verse: before capturing it in the ninth year of Hoshea's rule. The Assyrian king took the Israelites away to Assyria as prisoners. He forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
translation_verse: Na Ɔga Hosea lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa yaalenwidi kemmo ni, Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga úƒie Israelƒuɔ bammɔ úsienku Asiria. Na ɔ́ya na bélie Hala kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ na ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Gosan na Habor Ketudɔ ku Mediaƒuɔ lɛma kemmo. Kekpo Kéƒie Israelƒuɔ Na Likpidi Ɔsu

english_verse: All of this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had rescued them from Egypt, where they had been slaves. They worshiped foreign gods,
translation_verse: Ala amɛni ƒui álɛku Israelƒuɔ na likpidi lɛni na bábla báƒiɔ bana Unwoti Katɔti ɔni nékpo ɔ́ƒɔ-ma ɔ́lɛku Egyipteƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ ku bana Ɔga Ƒarao enu kemmo ɔsu. Bákya bátaakpa baƒiɔ lidu bamba,

english_verse: followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel, and were just as sinful as the Israelite kings.
translation_verse: na básiaku bekyuli bani na Unwoti ɔ́bɔku ɔ́lɛku kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ kemmo na bana anumi, na básiaku bana ɔbladu kama ku ɔdi ɔwɔdi ala bɔbla bɔni na Israel baga bammɔ béti bákya bekyuli bammɔ akɔ na baabla ɔsu.

english_verse: Even worse, the Israelites tried to hide their sins from the Lord their God. They built their own local shrines everywhere in Israel—from small towns to large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bákya bátaabla ala kalɔ kalɔ na bɔbɛ kemmo ani na Unwoti útete kuƒi. Na ɔ́si ɔma kagyumanakɔ kpakplaa katɔ mmɔ úbedu ɔma unengudi ɔni na bátu bámana ku lɛma lɛkladi ƒui kemmo ni, bátu akpabi bálɛ abi eli kesi kesii.

english_verse: They also built stone images of foreign gods and set up sacred poles for the worship of Asherah on every hill and under every shady tree.
translation_verse: Na abi ƒui lɛlɔ ku egyii biala na ebo ɔyuli kalɔ ni, bálɛ atabi kedee ku lɛƒiɔgyii béte Asera baƒiɔ.

english_verse: They offered sacrifices at the shrines, just as the foreign nations had done before the Lord forced them out of Israel. They did sinful things that made the Lord very angry.
translation_verse: Na bakɛ abi ƒui eli baakyula oloƒui aani kalɛ na kadi bamba bekyuli bani na Unwoti ɔ́bɔku ɔ́lɛku kalɔ kammɔ kemmo bátaabla. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bákya Unwoti kɔnyi ɔkɛnku bana ulikplu ala bɔbla ɔsu.

english_verse: Even though the Lord had commanded the Israelites not to worship idols, they did it anyway.
translation_verse: Na bakya baakpá baƒiɔ ina ka Unwoti ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bitabla ala amɛni udu.”

english_verse: So the Lord made sure that every prophet warned Israel and Judah with these words: “I, the Lord, command you to stop doing sinful things and start obeying my laws and teachings! I gave them to your ancestors, and I told my servants the prophets to repeat them to you.”
translation_verse: Unwoti úbo-ma ɔda geen ɔkɛnku nwuna bekyuli ku kenye bediene bani na ɔ́tala ɔ́kya Israelƒuɔ ku Yudaƒuɔ lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Binwini bina ɔbladu ukpidi ɔmmɔ kama. Na bitaadi mina ɔda bubo ku mina bunyimi lɛlɔ ɔkɛnku ɔda bubo bɔni ƒui na líte bina bati ka bataadi-mu lɛlɔ ku kalɛ na mina kabla bablane ku kenye bediene básu-mii lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: But the Israelites would not listen; they were as stubborn as their ancestors who had refused to worship the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmɛni kama ƒui ni, béni mina ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ na bábla atuɔkplu aani bana bati bani néteti bana kayi ƒui bátasia Unwoti bana Katɔti lɛlɔ, bati bani na bátaƒɔ bana Unwoti bátadi mmɔ.

english_verse: They ignored the Lord's warnings and commands, and they rejected the solemn agreement he had made with their ancestors. They worshiped worthless idols and became worthless themselves. The Lord had told the Israelites not to do the things that the foreign nations around them were doing, but Israel became just like them.
translation_verse: Béni nwuna ɔda bubo, na bátadi bunyimi bɔni na únyimiku bana bati kuuku lɛlɔ ku kalɛ na ɔ́lɛ-ma kpakplaa mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na basia baakpá baƒiɔ bani neeebo kɔsia. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ama lɛnɔ bátalɛ kɔsia kɔdi. Na básiaku kadi bamba bekyuli bani náka bámana-ma baatɛya bana ablala ina ka Unwoti ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bitabla ala ani na baabla.” Nsu ala ani lɛlɔ geen na Unwoti úbo-ma ɔda ka batabla ni, anya basia baabla.

english_verse: The people of Israel disobeyed all the commands of the Lord their God. They made two gold statues of calves and set up a sacred pole for Asherah; they also worshiped the stars and the god Baal.
translation_verse: Na báda bávia bana Unwoti Katɔti ɔda ɔni ƒui na úbo-ma lɛlɔ. Na bávɔ ɔmantɛ bakɔ bebi inyɔ udu bálɛ na baakpá-ma ku Asera ɔƒiɔgyii. Na baakya lili kalɔ teete ayabi ku Baal baƒiɔ.

english_verse: They used magic and witchcraft and even sacrificed their own children. The Israelites were determined to do whatever the Lord hated.
translation_verse: Na beeti bana bebi bananabi ku belekubi taabla akpala teete baƒiɔ bammɔ. Na beesié like bebone ku bana lidu bamba kudɔ. Na béti bana uwi ƒui baabla likpidi na Unwoti anumi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu kɔnyi kɔ́kɔ Unwoti.

english_verse: The Lord became so furious with the people of Israel that he allowed them to be carried away as prisoners. Only the people living in Judah were left,
translation_verse: Na Unwoti úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya Israelƒuɔ na úkulo-ma údie nwuna anumi. Na úti Yudaƒuɔ lɛti ɔ́bla nwuna badi.

english_verse: but they also disobeyed the Lord's commands and acted like the Israelites.
translation_verse: Nsu na ɔmɛni kama ƒui ni, Yudaƒuɔ bátadi bana Katɔti ɔda bubo lɛlɔ. Na básiaku Israelƒuɔ ɔbladu kama.

english_verse: So the Lord turned his back on everyone in Israel and let them be punished and defeated until no one was left.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu Unwoti úni Israelƒuɔ ƒui na ɔ́ni-ma kɔtu. Na Unwoti úti-ma útákya bekisine bani na bebo ɔkplu enu kemmo útédu ka bana ƒui báyii-nwu anumi.

english_verse: Earlier, when the Lord took the northern tribes away from David's family, the people living in northern Israel chose Jeroboam son of Nebat as their king. Jeroboam caused the Israelites to sin and to stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Unwoti úle Israel ku Yuda kemmo inyɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ béti Nebat ubidi Yerobeam bábla bana ɔga. Na Yerobeam ɔ́ya Israelƒuɔ béni Katɔti. Na ɔ́kpanku-ma útákya likpidi bonwu kemmo.

english_verse: until the Lord got rid of them, just as he had warned his servants the prophets. That's why the people of Israel were taken away as prisoners to Assyria, and that's where they remained. Foreigners Are Resettled in Israel
translation_verse: útédu ka Unwoti úkulo-ma údie nwuna anumi na kawɔlɔkɔ aani kalɛ na úbo-ma ɔda ɔ́siaku nwuna kabla bablane ku kenye bediene lɛlɔ ka si bábla lɛla lɛdi ni, lɛni na ɔdubo-ma bɔbla. Anwuɔsu, bábakpanku Israelƒuɔ bátákya Asiria kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na bakya mmɔ úbedu ɔmwi kadi. Asiriaƒuɔ Bátáda Keliekɔ Na Israel

english_verse: The king of Assyria took people who were living in the cities of Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and forced them to move to Israel. They took over the towns where the Israelites had lived, including the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Amu na Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga úti bekyuli badi ɔ́siku Babel ku Kuta ku Awa ku Hamat ku Seƒarwaim na ɔ́ya na bétélie Samaria na keliekɔ kani na ɔ́kpanku Israelƒuɔ ɔ́lɛku. Na bekyuli bammɔ béti lɛma lɛmmɔ bábla bana lɛdi.

english_verse: At first these people did not worship the Lord, so he sent lions to attack them, and the lions killed some of them.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na bekyuli bammɔ báka mmɔ butélie ni, na bekyuli bammɔ balákya lili kalɔ teete Unwoti. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Unwoti ɔ́ya na bagyata bábadu badi.

english_verse: A messenger told the king of Assyria, “The people you moved to Israel don't know how to worship the god of that country. So he sent lions that have attacked and killed some of them.”
translation_verse: Na béte Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga bɔti banini, “Bekyuli bawɔdi bani na éti ábakya Samaria lɛma lɛmmɔ ni, baaagyi kalɔ kammɔ baƒiɔ lɛla lɛni na baayɔ́ ka babla bete-ma. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu baƒiɔ bammɔ báya na bagyata bébo bakya baadú badi.”

english_verse: The king replied, “Get one of the Israelite priests we brought here and send him back to Israel. He can live there and teach them about the god of that country.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔga ɔmmɔ úbo ɔda ɔmɛni ɔnini, “Bɛya na Israelƒuɔ bani búƒie mmɔ kemmo unwi na ɔdi ɔkpane unwini utélie Samaria mmɔ na ɔtina bekyuli bammɔ kalɔ kammɔ Katɔti ɔda bubo.”

english_verse: One of the Israelite priests was chosen to go back to Israel. He lived in Bethel and taught the people how to worship the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israelni ɔkpane ɔni bábɔku bálɛku Samaria únwini na útélie Betel na ulie mmɔ ɔɔtina bekyuli bammɔ kalɛ na baakpá Unwoti.

english_verse: But in towns all over Israel, the different groups of people made statues of their own gods, then they placed these idols in local Israelite shrines.
translation_verse: Nsu bekyuli bani nátáda Samaria ɔma belie mmɔ ni, badi biala ku bana baƒiɔ bani na bábla béte lɛlɔ. Na béti-ma bétése Samariaƒuɔ aƒiodu ani na bátu bákya abi eli mmɔ.

english_verse: The people from Babylonia made the god Succoth-Benoth; those from Cuthah made the god Nergal; those from Hamath made Ashima;
translation_verse: Na Babelƒuɔ bávɔ Sukot-Benot baƒiɔ, na Kutƒuɔ bávɔ Nergal baƒiɔ, na Hamatƒuɔ bávɔ Asima baƒiɔ,

english_verse: those from Avva made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the people from Sepharvaim sacrificed their children to their own gods Adrammelech and Anammelech.
translation_verse: na Awiƒuɔ bávɔ Nibhas ku Tartak baƒiɔ, na Seƒarwiƒuɔ beeti bana bebi taabla bɔkyula akpala teete Adramelek ku Anamelek baƒiɔ bani nási Seƒarwaim.

english_verse: They worshiped their own gods, just as they had before they were taken away to Israel. They also worshiped the Lord, but they chose their own people to be priests at the shrines.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bekyuli bammɔ baakpá Unwoti na basɔ baakpá bana baƒiɔ lɛnɔ kalɛ na bana ɔma ɔni bási ɔdi ɔɔtina.

english_verse: Everyone followed their old customs. None of them worshiped only the Lord, and they refused to obey the laws and commands that the Lord had given to the descendants of Jacob, the man he named Israel.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bammɔ bamu basiaku bana kuuku ɔdi kama úbedu ɔmwi kadi. Na balakpa Unwoti na baládi nwuna ɔda bubo lɛlɔ, ɔda bubo bɔni na úti úte bana ati kuuku ɔni ndi Yakob ɔni na ɔ́sia lɛnyi ɔnii Israel ku nwuna kaba kemmo bekyuli lɛlɔ.

english_verse: At the time when the Lord had made his solemn agreement with the people of Israel, he told them: Do not worship any other gods! Do not bow down to them or offer them a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Unwoti únyimiku Israelƒuɔ bunyimi bɔni nkya-ma ntɛ ni, úbo-ma ɔda ɔnii, “Bitakpa baƒiɔ bamba badi na bitakya lili kalɔ bitete-ma na bitabla-ma kabla kadi na bitabla akpala adi bitete-ma.

english_verse: Worship only me! I am the one who rescued you from Egypt with my mighty power. Bow down to me and offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti ɔni nákpanku-mii ɔ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ, na údie kɔnu ɔ́bla ɔyikun ala ni, bitaadi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ, na bitaakya lili kalɔ teete anwu lɛti, na bitaabla akpala teete-nwu.

english_verse: Never worship any other god, always obey my laws and teachings,
translation_verse: Bɛsia anu kaduɛ na bɛda bunyimi ku ɔda bubo bɔni na únweni úte-mii lɛlɔ. Na bitakpa baƒiɔ badi.

english_verse: except me. I am the Lord your God, and I will rescue you from all your enemies.
translation_verse: Mmomu bɛkpa Unwoti bina Katɔti, ɔsika anwu ndi ukyuli ɔni kani ndubo-mii budie bɔsiku bina bekisine enu kemmo.”

english_verse: But the people living in Israel ignored that command and kept on following their old customs.
translation_verse: Nsu bekyuli bammɔ béni ka benu litemi na bésie anumi na bakya baabla bana kuuku ala ammɔ kani.

english_verse: They did worship the Lord, but they also worshiped their own idols. Their descendants did the same thing.
translation_verse: Na ina ka bekyuli baakpá Unwoti ni, bamu bakya baabla kabla teete bana baƒiɔ. Na úti úbedu ɔmwi kadi kamɛni lɛlɔ ni, bana bebi ku bawɔ lɛnɔ bámu bakya baabla ala ani na bana bati bábla.

english_verse: Don't be fooled by Hezekiah. He can't save you.
translation_verse: ‘Bitaya na Hesekia ɔtɔlɔ-mii. Ɔɔɔdubo bɔkana na ɔƒɔ-mii ɔlɛku mina enu kemmo.

english_verse: Stop listening to Hezekiah! Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns
translation_verse: “Bitenu Hesekia litemi. Bɔsu na Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔda-mii ɔnii, ‘Bibo na buwi kenye ntu mmomu, na biti bina lɛlɔ bite-mi. Na ndubɔya na bina ƒui bɛkɛ kuƒi na bɛdi bina adingyii mmo ebi na bɛni ntu na bina abiɔ kemmo

english_verse: Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
translation_verse: Munuu aakali ka bɔta kani na lɛ́ta mbekpoku-mii keeke ɔni na ɔɔɔdi Unwoti násu-mi lɛla lɛdi? Mɔɔsu-mii nwaa ka ni, Unwoti ɔlati násu-mi ka mbekpoku kalɔ kamɛni ƒui na lɛyila-mii udu.’ ”

english_verse: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́siaku ɔti Dawid ɔbladu kama. Na ɔ́bla ala ani na Unwoti ɔɔyɔ́.

english_verse: He destroyed the local shrines, then tore down the images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. He also smashed the bronze snake Moses had made. The people had named it Nehushtan and had been offering sacrifices to it.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́bwɛ aƒiodu ani na abi eli mmɔ ƒui, na ɔ́ƒɛ atabi kedee lɛƒiɔgyii lɛni na bálɛ béte Asera baƒiɔ mmɔ. Na lɛbualagyie lɛni na Mose úti ɔ́vɔ kɔlakpi mmɔ ni, úbo-ni ɔ́bwɛ, ɔsika Israelƒuɔ baakyula oloƒui teete-ni. Na baalɔ-ni Nehustan.

english_verse: Hezekiah trusted the Lord God of Israel. No other king of Judah was like Hezekiah, either before or after him.
translation_verse: Hesekia ɔ́ƒɔ Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti ɔ́di. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu, Israelƒuɔ básɔ bátakɛ ɔga ɔni nse lɛni kudii na nwuna lɛga bɔdi kama.

english_verse: He was completely faithful to the Lord and obeyed the laws the Lord had given to Moses for the people.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́bla ala siin na Unwoti anumi na útalɛ-nwu kama kudii. Na ɔ́nu kaduɛ na ɔ́di ɔda bubo bɔni na Unwoti úti ɔ́siaku Mose lɛlɔ ƒui.

english_verse: The Lord helped Hezekiah, so he was successful in everything he did. He even rebelled against the king of Assyria, refusing to be his servant.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na Unwoti úlieku-nwu. Na lɛla biala na ɔ́bla ni, lɛ́tɛ líte-nwu. Na limeyi lɛdi ni, ɔ́ta unye Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga lɛlɔ na úni ka ɔkya-nwu kalɔ.

english_verse: Hezekiah defeated the Philistine towns as far away as Gaza—from the smallest towns to the large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Na úkpo ɔ́di Ƒilistiƒuɔ lɛlɔ. Na úkpeli bana ala ani bébo ku ani nse-ma ƒui ɔ́ƒɔ. Ɔ́si ɔma kagyumanakɔ útédu ɔma unengudi ɔni na bátu awodu bámana. Na Gasa ku lɛma lɛni nkya-nwu amadɔ ƒui libunku.

english_verse: During the fourth year of Hezekiah's rule, which was the seventh year of Hoshea's rule in Israel, King Shalmaneser of Assyria led his troops to Samaria, the capital city of Israel. They attacked
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa linedi lɛlɔ ɔni na Hesekia ɔɔdi lɛga na ɔdi lɛkwa maatɛdi ka Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Hosea lɛnɔ ɔɔdi lɛga ni, Asiria Ɔga Salmaneser útékpo úduo Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ na ɔ́ka Samaria ɔma ɔ́kya.

english_verse: and captured it three years later, in the sixth year of Hezekiah's rule and the ninth year of Hoshea's rule.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa lɛtɛdi lɛni na ɔ́ka Samaria ɔ́kya mmɔ ni, bádi Samariaƒuɔ lɛlɔ na Hesekia lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa lɛkundi kemmo. Na ɔdi lɛkwa yaalenwidi ka Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Hosea ɔɔdi lɛga.

english_verse: The king of Assyria took the Israelites away as prisoners; he forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
translation_verse: Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga úƒie Israelƒuɔ úsienku Asiria kalɔ lɛlɔ, na ɔ́ya na bétélie Hale na Gosan kalɔ kemmo na Habor Ketudɔ ku Media lɛma kemmo.

english_verse: All of that happened because the people of Israel had not obeyed the Lord their God. They rejected the solemn agreement he had made with them, and they ignored everything that the Lord's servant Moses had told them. King Sennacherib of Assyria Invades Judah (
translation_verse: Békpo bádi Samariaƒuɔ lɛlɔ, ɔsika Israelƒuɔ bátadi bana Unwoti Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ. Na ɔda ɔni na úbo-ma ɔ́siaku Mose ɔni ndi Unwoti kabla ɔblane lɛlɔ ni, bátadi ɔdi biala lɛlɔ. Na béni muedi ka benu ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ na badi-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards, raise your own grain, and have plenty of olive oil and honey. Believe me, you won't starve there. Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him.
translation_verse: úti utédu ka bula ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́wia-mii kɔkyakɔ kɔni nse aani amii alati kɔdi. Mmɔ ni, bɛdubɔkɛ edula ku ntɛ bɔbuni na bɛkɛ adila ku adingyii abuni ku nnɔ egyii ku uwɔ. Bɛƒuna ngba na ɔɔɔdi kukpi!’ “Bitenu Hesekia litemi, ɔsika bɔkpanku na ɔda-mii utáyila si ɔɔsu ɔnii, ‘Unwoti ɔdubo-mii budie.’

english_verse: One of the Assyrian commanders told them: I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Asiriaƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ unengu ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛsu Ɔga Hesekia bɛnini, “ ‘Lɛni na Ɔga ɔyikune Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔɔsu. Bi ndi ƒula kama kekpokɔ ɔsu na eesé kayi lɛni?

english_verse: Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
translation_verse: Na si bɔsu na ada-mi lɛnɔ anii, “Bula Unwoti Katɔti lɛlɔ na búkpo kama” ni, ɔɔɔdi Unwoti ɔmɛni na Hesekia ɔ́ya báƒɛ nwuna akpabi, na ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ ku Yudaƒuɔ ka bataakpa Unwoti ɔmmɔ na lɛkpabi lɛni nlɛ Yerusalem lɛlɔ kani?

english_verse: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah's rule in Judah, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded the country and captured every walled city, except Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa leevu-linedi kemmo ɔni na Hesekia ɔɔdi lɛga ni, Asiriaƒuɔ Ɔga Sanaherib útékpoku Yuda lɛma linengudi lɛni na bátu awodu bámana ƒui na úƒie-ni ɔ́ƒɔ.

english_verse: Hezekiah sent this message to Sennacherib, who was in the town of Lachish: “I know I am guilty of rebellion. But I will pay you whatever you want, if you stop your attack.” Sennacherib told Hezekiah to pay ten tons of silver and one ton of gold.
translation_verse: Amu na Hesekia ɔ́sia kenye úmene Asiria ɔga na Lakis ɔnini, “Lɛ́bla lɛla lɛni naaadia. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu da ƒula bukpoku bɔni na aayɔ́ ka ebekpoku-bu mmɔ ya. Na lɛla biala na aawia asiku-mi kudɔ ni, ndubute-ɔ.” Anwuɔsu Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔmmɔ únye Ɔga Hesekia lɛlɔ ka uti sika ɔƒualadi antabi aƒo eti anyɔ unu ku sika ugyiedi antabi aƒo leevu unu uboku-nwu.

english_verse: So Hezekiah collected all the silver from the Lord's temple and the royal treasury.
translation_verse: Na Hesekia úti sika ɔƒualadi ɔni ƒui nkya kakpakɔ kavumii ku ɔga kavumii kemmo,

english_verse: He even stripped the gold that he had used to cover the doors and doorposts in the temple. He gave it all to Sennacherib.
translation_verse: na ɔ́sɔ útámami sika ugyiedi ɔni mma Unwoti kakpakɔ kɔyakun lɛlɔ ku kɔni na anwu ɔlati úti ɔ́mana kɔyakun kɔlɛmikɔ mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na úti ala ammɔ ƒui úte Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga. Sanaherib Ɔ́kya Yerusalemƒuɔ Liƒu

english_verse: The king of Assyria ordered his three highest military officers to leave Lachish and take a large army to Jerusalem. When they arrived, the officers stood on the road near the cloth makers' shops along the canal from the upper pool.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga úti bekpone batɔnkune lidu ɛtɛ ɔ́siku nwuna bekpone akɔ na bátɔnku bekpone pii badi básiku Lakis na bésie Ɔga Hesekia kudɔ na Yerusalem. Na ka bétéduo Yerusalem ni, béduo ɔkwalɛ ulu ɔni na ntu bɔɔsí teetéwi ligyu lɛni nnye katɔ kakɛ kemmo.

english_verse: They called out to Hezekiah, and three of his highest officials came out to meet them. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na benengu bamɛni bátala ka batálɔ Hesekia. Amu na Hesekia ɔ́tala Hilkia ubidi Eliakim ɔni mɔɔnu ɔga kaduli lɛlɔ ku Sebna ɔni ndi litemi bɔtɛ ɔku unwenine ku Asaƒ ubidi ɔni mɔɔnu kɔkunkɛ kemmo ka besie na batásiaku bekpone bammɔ.

english_verse: Does he think he can plan and win a war with nothing but words? Who is going to help him, now that he has turned against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Aasu ka ebo kekpo kɔkwɛ na ebo kekpo ɔyikun, nsu lɛmɛne kani na aakun. Na ɔma geen na aanu ɔsu na áta énye-mi lɛlɔ?

english_verse: Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
translation_verse: Nu! Mɔɔsu-ɔ ka Egyipteƒuɔ lɛlɔ na ékpo kama. Nsu mɔɔyá-a na ati ka ugyii kakɛ kani ndubo bɔƒɛ bɔtu-ɔ kɔnu si éti ƒula unu ƒui ásia-nwu lɛlɔ na ɔdi! Ɔyikun ɔmmɔ udu na Ƒarao Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ubo ute bani ƒui néti bana anu básia-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The king of Assyria wants to make a bet with you people. He will give you
translation_verse: “ ‘Bo na awɔ ku mina unengu Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga binyimi lɛla lɛdi. Na ndubute-ɔ bapɔnkɔ mpim inyɔ si adubɔkɛ bekyuli bani melie-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: How could you even defeat our lowest ranking officer, when you have to depend on Egypt for chariots and cavalry?
translation_verse: Na mɔɔsu-ɔ ka alakana Asiriani ukpone ɔnamudi ƒui muedi lɛlɔ bɔdi ina ka éti anu ásia Egyipteƒuɔ bapɔnkɔ beliene ku bana bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Sir, we don't want the people listening from the city wall to understand what you are saying. So please speak to us in Aramaic instead of Hebrew.”
translation_verse: Amu na Hilkia ubidi Eliakim ku Sebna ku Yoa básu bekpone unengu ɔmmɔ banini, “Awɔ ku ƒula bekpone bammɔ bɛtɛmiku-bu na Siriaƒuɔ lɛdi kemmo na abu bɔdubunu kalɔ. Na bitatɛmi na Yudaƒuɔ lɛdi kemmo bitete-bu. Ɔsika bekyuli bani ƒui na bákɔ benye awodu amɛni lɛlɔ beenú.”

english_verse: The Assyrian army commander answered, “My king sent me to speak to everyone, not just to you leaders. These people will soon have to eat their own body waste and drink their own urine! And so will the three of you.”
translation_verse: Amu na bekpone benengu bammɔ bédie kenye banini, “Bɛɛkali ka amii ku bina ɔga kani na bula ɔga ɔ́tala ɔ́kya ka bubasu-mii etemila amɛni? Oowo! Bekyuli bani na bákɔ benye awodu lɛlɔ lɛnɔ ɔlɛka benu ɔdi. Ɔsika ama lɛnɔ badubɔdi bana kuvodɔ na bani bana kɔnɔ aani bina kalɛ!”

english_verse: Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted in Hebrew: Listen to what the great king of Assyria says!
translation_verse: Amu na unengu ɔmmɔ ɔ́ta únye na údie lɛdi momoomo na Yudaƒuɔ lɛdi kemmo na ɔ́su ɔ́nini, “Binu, Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔyikune ɔnini,

english_verse: Don't trust him when he tells you that the Lord will protect you from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: Na bitaya na Hesekia ɔdɔdɔ-mii na uƒu-mii kasusu na biti bina anu bɛsia bɛnii, “Unwoti ɔdubudie-bu na ulu biala lɛlɔ, na ɔɔɔdubo ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni bɔnyonu bɔkya Asiriaƒɔ ɔga enu kemmo.” ’

english_verse: Were any other gods able to defend their land against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Bíinu dii ka kalɔ kadi baƒiɔ báaƒɔ bana bekyuli básiku Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga enu kemmo?

english_verse: What happened to the gods of Hamath and Arpad? What about the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Were the gods of Samaria able to protect their land against the Assyrian forces?
translation_verse: Na wɛ na Hamat ku Arpad baƒiɔ bakya? Na wɛ lɛnɔ na Seƒarwaim ku Hera ku Iwa baƒiɔ bakya? Na ɔdi úukpo ɔ́ƒɔ Samaria ɔ́lɛku-mi enu dii?

english_verse: None of these gods kept their people safe from the king of Assyria. Do you think the Lord your God can do any better?
translation_verse: Na kalɔ kamani geen baƒiɔ néekpo báƒɔ bana kalɔ bekyuli básiku-mi enu kemmo? Na dɛ na Unwoti anwu ɔdubɔkana na ɔƒɔ Yerusalem na mina enu kemmo?”

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah had been warned by King Hezekiah not to answer the Assyrian commander. So they tore their clothes in sorrow and reported to Hezekiah everything the commander had said.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Hilkia ubidi Eliakim ɔni ndi ɔga kesii lɛlɔ ɔnune ku ɔku unwenine Sebna ku Asaƒ ubidi Yoa ekposela ala unwenine báni bana lɛwu bábwɛ na bénwini bésie Ɔga Hesekia kudɔ na bátásɔku ala ani na básu-ma ƒui básu-nwu.

english_verse: One day he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, when his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with their swords. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon became king.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, ka Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔkya ɔɔkpá nwuna baƒiɔ Nisrok na nwuna kakpakɔ ni, ɔga ɔmmɔ bebi inyɔ bani ndi Adramelek ku Sareser béti bana kuwii na bétébeyi-nwu bádu, na békeli bésie Ararat kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na ubidi bamba ɔni baalɔ bani Esarhadon úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ.

english_verse: As soon as Hezekiah heard the news, he tore off his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he went into the temple of the Lord.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Hesekia ɔnya únu bekyuli bammɔ kenye kani na ɔ́ni nwuna adala ɔ́duli na lɛƒɛda kemmo, na úti adikpi ɔ́da lɛlɔ na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Unwoti kakpakɔ.

english_verse: The kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah have all disappeared. Hezekiah Prays (Isaiah
translation_verse: Na wɛ na Hamat ku Arpad ku Seƒarwaim ku Hena ku Iwa baga bakya ɔmwi?” Hesekia Ɔ́kpali Katɔti

english_verse: He told Prime Minister Eliakim, Assistant Prime Minister Shebna, and the senior priests to dress in sackcloth and tell the prophet Isaiah:
translation_verse: Na ɔ́tala Eliakim ɔni mɔɔnu ɔga kaduli lɛlɔ ku Sebna ɔni ndi ɔku unwenine ku bakpane benengudi ɔ́kya Amos ubidi Kenye Udiene Yesaia na bana ƒui benyimi adikpi.

english_verse: These are difficult and disgraceful times. Our nation is like a woman too weak to give birth, when it's time for her baby to be born.
translation_verse: Na bátásu-nwu banini, “Lɛni na Hesekia ɔɔsu, ɔmwi limeyi lɛdi kɔnyana limeyi geen lɛni na bédumi-bu na bákya-bu kɔƒa. Na buse aani uleku ɔni na kawɔƒɔ kaadu-nwu, nsu ulákana bɔwɔ ka ɔyikun ɔ́sa-nwu ɔsu.

english_verse: Please pray for those of us who are left alive. The king of Assyria sent his army commander to insult the living God. Perhaps the Lord heard what he said and will do something, if you will pray.
translation_verse: Na ɔƒɛni kalɛ Unwoti ƒula Katɔti únu ala ani na Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́tala nwuna bekpone benengu na bábasu-bu na bédumi Katɔti ɔni na uli ngba. Na muuvele nnii ƒula Unwoti Katɔti unu edumi ammɔ na ɔni bani nédumi-nwu mmɔ kɔtu. Anwuɔsu kpali Katɔti na evele ete bula bekyuli ku abu bani nli ngba.”

english_verse: When these leaders went to Isaiah,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Yesaia únu Ɔga Hesekia kenye kammɔ ni,

translation_verse: ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛsu bina ati bɛnini, ‘Unwoti ɔnii taya na lɛla lɛni na básu-ɔ mmɔ lɛkya-a liƒu. Na tayia lɛla lɛni na Asiria ɔga kalɔ bakyane bammɔ básu béti bédumi-mi.

english_verse: I will upset him with rumors about what's happening in his own country. He will go back, and there I will make him die a violent death.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔdubɔya na Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔmmɔ unu etemila adi ɔsiku nwuna ɔma na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na unwini usie mmɔ. Na si útéduo ni, Unwoti ɔdubɔya na badu-nwu na mmɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the commander of the Assyrian forces heard that his king had left the town of Lachish and was now attacking Libnah. So he went there.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Asiriaƒuɔ benengu bammɔ bénu ka bana ɔga ɔ́tɔlɔ Lakis na úsie ɔ́kya Libna amadɔ uukpó ni, úsie mmɔ na útánu-nwu.

english_verse: About this same time the king of Assyria learned that King Tirhakah of Ethiopia was on his way to attack him. Then the king of Assyria sent some messengers with this note for Hezekiah:
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, kenye kédu Asiriaƒuɔ Ɔga Sanaherib ka Egyipteƒuɔ bekpone báklibi lɛlɔ na bana Ɔga Tirhaka ɔ́tɔnku-ma ka bébekpoku-ma. Anwuɔsu ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tala batu ɔ́kya Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Hesekia ɔnini,

english_verse: Don't trust your God or be fooled by his promise to defend Jerusalem against me.
translation_verse: “Bɛsu Hesekia bɛnini, ‘Kayi katatɔlɔ-ɔ. Taƒɔ Katɔti tadi si ɔ́su-ɔ ɔnii Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ulakana Yerusalem bɔƒɔ.’

english_verse: You have heard how we Assyrian kings have completely wiped out other nations. What makes you feel so safe?
translation_verse: Ngyi nwaa ka énu kalɛ na Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́bla kɔlɔ kɔni na amadɔ ƒui ku kalɛ na ɔ́yila-ku udu kede kede. Na aabu ka awɔ adubɔkana na alɛ-mi enu kemmo?

english_verse: The Assyrian kings before me destroyed the towns of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and everyone from Eden who lived in Telassar. What good did their gods do them?
translation_verse: Na mina bati kuuku báyila Gosan ku Haran ku Reseƒ na báyila bana lɛma udu. Na bádu bekyuli bani nli Eden na Telasar. Nsu bana baƒiɔ badi biala bátakana-ma bukpo bɔ́ƒɔ.

english_verse: After Hezekiah had read the note from the king of Assyria, he took it to the temple and spread it out for the Lord to see.
translation_verse: Ɔga Hesekia ɔ́ƒɔ kakunkɛ kamɛni ɔ́siku batalane bammɔ kudɔ na ɔ́ka. Ɔmmɔ kama ni, úti ɔku ɔmmɔ ɔ́da na útégyingya-nwu úwi Unwoti anumi na nwuna kakpakɔ.

english_verse: Isaiah went to Hezekiah and told him that the Lord God of Israel had said: Hezekiah, I heard your prayer about King Sennacherib of Assyria.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Kenye Udiene Yesaia ɔ́sia Ɔga Hesekia kenye ɔnini, “Lɛni na Unwoti Israel Katɔti ɔɔsu ɔnii línu ƒula bɔkpali ɔ́siku Asiria Ɔga Sanaherib lɛlɔ.

english_verse: He prayed: Lord God of Israel, your throne is above the winged creatures. You created the heavens and the earth, and you alone rule the kingdoms of this world.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́kpali Unwoti ɔ́su ɔnini, “O Unwoti, ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti, awɔ nli ƒula lɛgaboku lɛlɔ na katɔ katɔ na kesii kani na Kerub ngba bebweyi bammɔ begyingya bana avwi bámana. Na awɔ lɛti ndi Katɔti ɔni mɔɔdi kayawi kamɛni lɛgakɔdikɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Na awɔ nédie katɔ ku kalɔ.

english_verse: It is true, our Lord, that Assyrian kings have turned nations into deserts.
translation_verse: “Unwoti, sɔsɔ na ɔdi ka Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́yila lɛma pii udu, na kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ kuwi ukpludi.

english_verse: They destroyed the idols of wood and stone that the people of those nations had made and worshiped.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́kyula bana baƒiɔ bani na geen ni, baaadi lɛla lɛdi beetulo egyiiku ku atabi ani na bekyuli béti bana enu bánwi kani.

english_verse: But you are our Lord and our God! We ask you to keep us safe from the Assyrian king. Then everyone in every kingdom on earth will know that you are the only God. The Lord's Answer to Hezekiah (Isaiah
translation_verse: Unwoti bula Katɔti ƒɔ-bu lɛku Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔmɛni enu kemmo kalɛ na kayawi lɛgakɔdikɔ bekyuli ƒui banu bati ka awɔ Unwoti kani ndi Katɔti.” Yesaia Ɔ́su Yudaƒuɔ Bɔƒɔ Litemi Úse

english_verse: Now this is what I say to that king: The people of Jerusalem hate and make fun of you; they laugh behind your back.
translation_verse: Na lɛla lɛni na Katɔti ɔ́su ɔ́siku-nwu lɛlɔ ndi ɔnii, “ ‘Sion ubi ugblebi adagyaa úni-ɔ na ɔɔmá-a. Yerusalem ubi ulekubi, uuƒwimi nwuna lili ɔni na ékeli ésela.

translation_verse: Na usien ɔmmɔ ni, Unwoti ɔtu ɔdi úsie Asiriaƒuɔ bekpone kakyakɔ, na ɔ́du bekpone mpim eti atɛ ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ (

english_verse: Sennacherib, you cursed, shouted, and sneered at me, the holy God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ɔma na akya eedumi taama? Na ɔma na aakwanyi taakya ku lɛdi momoomo? Na ɔma na aanu ɔnusɛ ku bɔpii? Israel Katɔti Kedee ɔmmɔ na ɔdi!

english_verse: You let your officials insult me, the Lord. And this is how you bragged about yourself: “I led my chariots to the highest heights of Lebanon's mountains. I went deep into its forest, cutting down the best cedar and cypress trees.
translation_verse: Átala bekyuli ákya Unwoti, na bákpila-nwu edumi. Na ásu anini, “Nkɛnku mina bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ lɛlɔ na lɛ́ɛkɔ abi ani na ákuku ƒui eli lɛ́vi na Lebanon kesii kani bene na kákuku ketulo ƒui. english_verse: I dried up every stream in the land of Egypt, and I drank water from wells I had dug.”
translation_verse: Na líku abiɔ lɛ́kya kesii kani na kadi baƒɔ kɔlɔ kemmo, na lɛ́ni ntu na mmɔ. Mina lɛgba kalɔ geen na líti lɛ́nya Egyipte ntukpa bɔni nákwii mmɔ.”

english_verse: Sennacherib, now listen to me, the Lord. I planned all this long ago. And you don't even realize that I alone am the one who decided that you would do these things. I let you make ruins of fortified cities.
translation_verse: “ ‘Bunu na étenu ɔmɛni kudii? Ami nábla ala amɛni líse kukuuku. Na lɛ́tina kalɛ na adubo buse na uwi ɔni návi ƒui kemmo. Na ɔƒɛni lɛ́ya na ébo-nwu kemmo. Na ákana na énwini lɛma linengudi lɛni na bátu bámana ábla aani atabi ani na bála básala lisu.

english_verse: Their people became weak, terribly confused. They were like wild flowers or tender young grass growing on a flat roof, scorched before it matures.
translation_verse: Badi bekyuli bani na békpeli-ma ɔyikun báƒɔ, na ɔ́bla-ma kalɛ kadi ku kɔƒa. Bese aani livo lɛni nnye alakpi akɔ, na bese aani livo lɛni mɔɔta ɔwɔdi. Na bálɛ livo lɛni mɔɔkwɛ́ na ɔtɔ katɔ, na ɔƒɛ ɔɔkyula-ni asa na lɛ́bi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I know all about you, even how fiercely angry you are with me.
translation_verse: “ ‘Nsu ngyi kesii kani na elie, ku uwi ɔni na eebo taatɔlɔ, ku kalɛ na aata ku kɔnyi taasiaku-mi.

english_verse: I have seen your pride and the tremendous hatred you have for me. Now I will put a hook in your nose, a bit in your mouth, then I will send you back to where you came from.
translation_verse: Na ka áta ásiaku-mi ku kɔnyi, ku ƒula ukyuli tabu bɔni na línu ku mina atu ɔsu ni, ndubɔkya-a ɔdaliwa enwu na liti kenye kabuli lɛbala-a kenye, na lɛya na enwini asia ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na ásia ébo.’

english_verse: Hezekiah, I will tell you what's going to happen. This year you will eat crops that grow on their own, and the next year you will eat whatever springs up where those crops grew. But the third year you will plant grain and vineyards, and you will eat what you harvest.
translation_verse: “O Hesekia, ɔmɛni ndubɔbla ƒula likposela. “Na lɛkwa lɛmɛni kemmo ni, edula ani na anya alati nákwɛ na adubo bɔdi. Na lɛkwa bamba ni, edula akukudi ani násɔ áta ebi na adubo bɔdi. Nsu lɛkwa lɛtɛdi ni, awɔ ɔlati kya edula na aƒɛ-nya na ese adingyii mmo na ede ebi ammɔ adi.

english_verse: Those who survive in Judah will be like a vine that puts down deep roots and bears fruit.
translation_verse: Na Yudaƒuɔ ɛlɛɛ bani nébu badubɔsɔ bedie ligyiitu aani kugyii kalɛ besie kalɔ kemmo ɔgyu na banwu ebi na kayaa.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will see to it that some who live in Jerusalem will survive.
translation_verse: Ɔsika ukyuli ɔdi ɔdubɔlɛ ɔsi Yerusalem. Na bani ndubɔkɛ ngba lɛnɔ basi Sion Kɔbi. Ɔsika kalɛ na anumi égyie ɔsu ɔdubɔya na ɔmɛni ubo-nwu kemmo lɛni.

english_verse: I promise that the king of Assyria won't get into Jerusalem, or shoot an arrow into the city, or even surround it and prepare to attack.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu taasiku Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga lɛlɔ ɔnii, “ ‘Ɔɔɔdubo ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo buduo iye ubo nwuna kataminta kunwi muedi na mɛni. Na ulebo mmɔ ku lɛgyumanala, iye ubatu kesii kani na ɔdubunye ukpoku ɔma ɔmmɔ ɔmana.

english_verse: As surely as I am the Lord, he will return by the way he came and will never enter Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na ɔkɛ úbo na ɔdubɔsɔ ɔsia ɔtɔlɔ. Ɔɔɔdubo ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo buduo. Lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su.

english_verse: I will protect it for myself and for my servant David. The Death of King Sennacherib (Isaiah
translation_verse: Na ndubɔgyumana na likpo lɛƒɔ ɔma ɔmmɔ, na mina lɛnyi ku mina kabla ɔblane Dawid ɔsu.’ ”

english_verse: After this King Sennacherib went back to Assyria and lived in the city of Nineveh.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Asiriaƒuɔ Ɔga Sanaherib ɔ́ya na báta mmɔ na bénwini bésie Niniwe na bétélie mmɔ.

english_verse: Hezekiah died, and his son Manasseh became king.
translation_verse: Hesekia úkpi na ubidi Manase úti-nwu keliekɔ aani ɔga kalɛ.

english_verse: “Don't forget that I have been faithful to you, Lord. I have obeyed you with all my heart, and I do whatever you say is right.” After this, he cried bitterly.
translation_verse: “Unwoti nyimo ka lɛ́bla ala siin na ulu lɛlɔ na ƒula anumi. Na líti mina kayi lɛnɔ lɛ́sia awɔ lɛti lɛlɔ. Na lɛ́kya ɔkplu ka lɛ́bla lɛla lɛni na aayɔ́.” Ɔmmɔ kama úsie kalɔ uuwulo momoomo.

english_verse: the Lord sent him back to Hezekiah with this message: Hezekiah, you are the ruler of my people, and I am the Lord God, who was worshiped by your ancestor David. I heard you pray, and I saw you cry. I will heal you, so that three days from now you will be able to worship in my temple.
translation_verse: “Sɔ nwini sie Hesekia, mina kadi bekyuli ɔtɔnkune kudɔ na asu-nwu anii, ‘Lɛni na Unwoti, ƒula ɔti Dawid Katɔti, ɔɔsu. Línu ƒula bɔkpali ku keku kani na éwulo ku imii, na ndubo-ɔ bɔbwi. Ɔ́si ɔmwi útédu limeyi lɛtɛdi lɛlɔ ni, adubo bɔta busie Unwoti kakpakɔ.

english_verse: Then Isaiah said to the king's servants, “Bring some mashed figs and place them on the king's open sore. He will then get well.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yesaia ɔ́su bekyuli bani mɔɔnu ɔga ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Bɛwia kɔnwingyie ebi.” Na ama lɛnɔ báwia-nya na bákɔ-nya básia-nwu eƒula ammɔ lɛlɔ na ása-nwu.

english_verse: Isaiah replied, “The Lord will prove to you that he will keep his promise. Will the shadow made by the setting sun on the stairway go forward ten steps or back ten steps?”
translation_verse: Amu na Yesaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Unwoti likposela lɛni na ɔdubɔtina-a ka ɔdubɔbla lɛla lɛni na ɔ́su ndi ɔmɛni. Bɔyu na ɔtɔ ɔmɛni ɔyuli ɔdubɔyu nwuna kanyakɔ libili lɛlɔ ubo kalɔ lɛgba leevu, munuu ɔdubuti ɔkɔ katɔ lɛgba leevu?”

english_verse: “It's normal for the sun to go forward,” Hezekiah answered. “But how can it go back?”
translation_verse: Na Hesekia údie kenye ɔnini, “Use kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ka ɔyuli ɔmɛni ubo kalɔ lɛgba leevu. Anwuɔsu ya na uti ɔkɔ lɛgba leevu mmomu.”
