translation_verse: Na bagyumanane bamɛni bataakɛ kebunku taasiku bana lɛlɔ bekyuli bani nli akpaklɔ ammɔ kudɔ. Na ɔgyumanane biala ɔ́ɔbla kabla emeyi maatɛ asa na baavumana-nwu.

english_verse: The four full-time guards were Levites, and they supervised the other guards and were responsible for the rooms in the temple and the supplies kept there.
translation_verse: Na bagyumanane benengu bammɔ badi ine. Na ama mɔɔbla kabla kammɔ taawɔlɔ. Na ama mɔɔnu kakpakɔ lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ kemmo iye si ukyuli ɔdi ɔɔwia lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: They guarded the temple day and night and opened its doors every morning. The Duties of the Levites
translation_verse: Na béli béde Unwoti kakpakɔ kammɔ. Ɔsika ɔdi bana kabla ka, bataagyumana ka na bataalɛmi kɔyakun kammɔ teewi ɔtanta biala.

english_verse: Some of the Levites were responsible for the equipment used in worship at the temple, and they had to count everything before and after it was used.
translation_verse: Na badi lɛnɔ mɔɔnú akyami ani báda báabla kakpakɔ kammɔ kabla lɛlɔ. Na asa na badubuti akyami ammɔ babla lɛla lɛdi ni, báaka-nya taanu nwuna bumomo. Na si bábla báwɔlɔ lɛnɔ ni, báaka-nya taanu asa na baaƒɔ́ teese.

english_verse: But only the priests could mix the spices.
translation_verse: Na bakpane bammɔ badi mɔɔsála akyala.

english_verse: Mattithiah, Shallum's oldest son, was a member of the Levite clan of Korah, and he was in charge of baking the bread used for offerings.
translation_verse: Na Lewini ɔni baalɔ banii, Matitia na ɔdi Salum ubidi udeedi na ɔ́si kora kaba kemmo muuƒi bodobodo.

english_verse: The Levites from the Kohath clan were in charge of baking the sacred loaves of bread for each Sabbath.
translation_verse: Na Kehatƒuɔ bammɔ banwani badi mɔɔbla bodobodo ɔni na beeti taasia Unwoti kakpakɔ lɛnwuna limeyi lɛlɔ lɛnwuna limeyi biala.

english_verse: The Levite family leaders who were the musicians also lived at the temple. They had no other responsibilities, because they were on duty day and night.
translation_verse: Na Lewiƒuɔ batɔnkune bani mɔɔtu lɛnu ama beli kakpakɔ lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ kemmo. Na balaya na ama baabla kabla kadi. Ɔsika bana kabla kani baabla mmɔ usien ku ɔƒɛ na baabla-ka

english_verse: All of these men were family leaders in the Levi tribe and were listed that way in their family records. They lived in Jerusalem. King Saul's Family (
translation_verse: Na bamɛni ƒui ndi Lewiƒuɔ benengu ku batɔnkune aani kalɛ na bénweni-ma Anyi bákya bɔwɔ ɔku kemmo na belie Yerusalem. Ɔga Saul Kaba Bekyuli Anyi Ndi Bamɛni

english_verse: the father of Shimeam. Some of them went to live in Jerusalem near their relatives.
translation_verse: Na Miklot ɔti ndi Simea. Na belie béde bana banwani na Yerusalem.

english_verse: Jeiel had settled the town of Gibeon, where he and his wife Maacah lived.
translation_verse: Yeiel ɔni ɔti ndi Gibeon na uli Gibeon. Na ulekudi ndi Maaka.

english_verse: They had ten sons, who were born in the following order: Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
translation_verse: Na ubi udeedi ndi Abdon na Sur ku Kis ku Baal ku Ner ku Nadab

english_verse: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth
translation_verse: ku Gedor ku Ahio ku Sakaria ku Miklot basia.

english_verse: Ner was the father of Kish and the grandfather of King Saul. Saul had four sons: Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
translation_verse: Na Ner ɔ́wɔ Kis na Kis ɔ́wɔ Saul. Na Saul ɔ́wɔ Yonatan ku Malki-Saul ku Abinadab ku Esbaal.

english_verse: Jonathan was the father of Meribbaal, the grandfather of Micah, and the great-grandfather of Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
translation_verse: Na Mika bebi ndi Piton ku Melek ku Tahrea ku Ahas.

english_verse: The descendants of Ahaz included Jarah, Alemeth, Azmaveth, Zimri, Moza, Binea, Rephaiah, Eleasah, and Azel and his six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan.
translation_verse: Na Asel ubo bananabi ɛku. Na bana anyi ndi Asrikam ku Bokeru ku Ismael ku Searia ku Obadia ku Hanan. Na bamɛni ndi Asel bebi.

english_verse: The Philistines fought against Israel in a battle at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒilistiƒuɔ békpoku Israelƒuɔ na baabɔku-ma geen na bana anumi na bádu bana akɔ pii lɛnɔ na Gilboa Kɔbi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Saul died because he was unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord. He even asked advice from a woman who talked to spirits of the dead,
translation_verse: Na Saul úkpi, ɔsika útasiaku Unwoti siin. Na úni Unwoti ɔda bubo na úsie like bebone kudɔ ka úteye ala únu muedi.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons and killed three of them: Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Nsu Ƒilistiƒuɔ bábi básiaku-ma na béƒie Saul bebi ɛtɛ na bádu-ma. Na bebi ɛtɛ bamɛni ndi Yonatan ku Abinadab ku Malki-Saul.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Na kekpo kammɔ kébo kaayú ɔkplu na kesii kani na Saul ɔkya. Na Saul bekisine kemmo unwi ɔ́ta kataminta úbalɛ-nwu na nwuna ɔ́ƒɔ ɔlɛ geen.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want those godless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Then Saul stuck himself in the stomach with his own sword and fell on the blade.
translation_verse: Amu na Saul ɔ́su nwuna ekpola ala utine ɔnini, “Ni ƒula kewii kpa livuo kemmo na atu-mi adu, kalɛ na kadi bamba bekyuli bani na bétekulo-ma ago mɛni balábadu-mi na bataakun lɛmɛnɛ teedumi-mi.” Nsu Saul ekpola utine ɔmmɔ ɔ́yia ka ɔbla lɛni. Anwuɔsu Saul údie anwu ɔlati nwuna kewii na úbuli útébi-ka lɛlɔ.

english_verse: When the soldier realized that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Amu ka nwuna ekpola ala utine ɔ́nu ka Saul úkpi ni, anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́kpa nwuna kewii na úbuli útébi-ka lɛlɔ, na úkpi.

english_verse: Saul, three of his sons, and all his male relatives were dead.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Saul ku nwuna bebi ɛtɛ békpi basala. Na nwuna kaba kadi kátadi lɛga kudii.

english_verse: The Israelites who lived in Jezreel Valley learned that their army had run away and that Saul and his sons were dead. They ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites left behind.
translation_verse: Na ka Israelƒuɔ bani beli kɔwɛ kemmo mmɔ bénu ka bekpone bammɔ ƒui békeli ni, békeli na báda bana lɛma béwi. Amu na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bébo na bébelie bana lɛma lɛmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The next day the Philistines came back to the battlefield to carry away the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers. When they found the bodies of Saul and his sons on Mount Gilboa,
translation_verse: Kadi kegye ni, ka Ƒilistiƒuɔ bésie bani bétedie bekpine bammɔ adala ni, mmɔ na bánu Saul ku nwuna bebi ka békpi bátɛ Gilboa Kɔbi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: they took Saul's weapons, pulled off his armor, and cut off his head. Then they sent messengers everywhere in Philistia to spread the news among their people and to thank the idols of their gods.
translation_verse: Békulo-nwu lili na bédie nwuna ekpola ani na ɔkya na bátala batu na bávi Ƒilistiƒuɔ lɛma ƒui básu kenye kamɛni na bana baƒiɔ kakpakɔ ku bekyuli ƒui akɔ.

english_verse: They put Saul's armor in the temple of their gods and hung his head in the temple of their god Dagon.
translation_verse: Amu na béti Saul kekpo adala bétese bana baƒiɔ ɔtɔ unwi kemmo. Na béti nwuna lili bátaƒala bana baƒiɔ bani baalɔ-ma banii Dagon ɔtɔ kemmo.

english_verse: When the people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
translation_verse: Na ka bekyuli bani beli Yabes ɔni nnkya Gilead bénu kalɛ na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bábla Saul ni,

english_verse: some brave men went to get his body and the bodies of his three sons. The men brought the bodies back to Jabesh, where they buried them under an oak tree. Then for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: bana bekpone bani mbo kayi geen bésie na béteti Saul ukpine ku nwuna bebi béboku Yabes. Na báva-ma na kugyii kubendi kɔdi kalɔ. Na bekyuli bammɔ bényimi kenye emeyi maatɛ.

english_verse: instead of asking the Lord. So the Lord had Saul killed and gave his kingdom to David, the son of Jesse.
translation_verse: Ɔni na Unwoti kudɔ na nka ɔlɛka úsie mmomu. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu, Unwoti ɔ́du-nwu. Na únwini lɛgadi lɛmmɔ úte Yisai ubidi Dawid.

english_verse: The Jebusites said, “You won't be able to get in here!” But David captured the fortress of Mount Zion, which is now called the City of David.
translation_verse: Nsu ina ka básu lɛni ni, Dawid ku nwuna bekpone bádi-ma lɛlɔ na béƒie ɔma ɔni na bátu awodu bámana na baalɔ-nwu Sion mmɔ báƒɔ. Na básia mmɔ lɛnyi banii Dawid Ɔma.

english_verse: Israel's leaders met with David at Hebron and said, “We are your relatives,
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ ƒui bésie Dawid kudɔ na Hebron na bábasu-nwu banini, “Abu lɛnɔ bɔdi ƒula lɛlɔ bekyuli.

english_verse: So we have come to crown you king of Israel.” David made an agreement with the leaders and asked the Lord to be their witness. Then the leaders poured olive oil on David's head to show that he was now king of Israel. This happened just as the Lord's prophet Samuel had said. David Captures Jerusalem (
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israel benengu ƒui bébo Hebron na Dawid kudɔ mmɔ. Na bényimi bunyimi bɔdi ku lɛlɔ na Unwoti anumi. Na bébo Dawid kudu na béwi-nwu lili nnɔmii béti bése-nwu likpo ka anwu ndi Israelƒuɔ ɔga aani kalɛ na Unwoti úse kenye ɔ́siaku Samuel lɛlɔ.

english_verse: David had told his troops, “The first soldier to kill a Jebusite will become my army commander.” And since Joab son of Zeruiah attacked first, he became commander.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ukyuli udeedi ɔni ndubɔka Yebusini bɔdu ni, anwu ndubɔbla bekpone ɔtɔnkune.” Na Yoab ɔni uni ndi Seruia ɔtɔnku kekpo na únwini Israel ɔtɔnkune.

english_verse: The Lord had promised that David would become king, and so everyone in Israel gave David their support. Certain warriors also helped keep his kingdom strong.
translation_verse: Na bani nébunku Dawid na nwuna lɛgadi lɛ́kɛ ɔyikun lígyingya lɛ́kya kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na Unwoti úse Dawid kenye.

english_verse: Jerusalem was called Jebus at the time, and David led Israel's army to attack the town.
translation_verse: Amu na anwu ku nwuna bekpone bésie banii bétékpoku-ma. Nsu Yebusiƒuɔ básu Dawid banini, “Bilakana mɛni buduo.”

english_verse: Later, David moved to the fortress—that's why it's called the City of David.
translation_verse: Dawid úsie útélie ɔma kagyumanakɔ kpakplaa kammɔ kemmo. Na baalɔ mmɔ banii Dawid Ɔma.

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side. The Three Warriors (
translation_verse: Na ka Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔsiaku Dawid ɔsu ni, nwuna ɔyikun ɔ́sɔ úsie anumi kaduɛ. Dawid Bekpone Bani Náƒɔ Lɛnyi

english_verse: Another time he killed an Egyptian who was over two meters tall and was armed with a spear. Benaiah only had a club, so he grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
translation_verse: Ɔ́du Egyipteni ukpone unengudi ɔdi na nwuna bɔkuku bɔdi lɛgba bɔka maatɛ ku kakɛ. Na ina ka Egyipteni ɔmmɔ ɔda kewii gyɔlɔɔ ni, ligyiiku lɛdi kani na Benaia ɔda útásiaku-nwu na úƒie nwuna kewii kammɔ ɔ́ƒɔ na úti ɔ́tu-nwu ɔ́du. Na ɔ́da lɛtula gyɔlɔɔ aani ɔta kalɛ. Na Benaia ɔ́wia ligyiiku na útekpoku-nwu. Na úkpeli Egyipteni ɔmmɔ lɛtula lɛmmɔ ɔ́ƒɔ na úti ɔ́du-nwu.

english_verse: and he said, “I'm very thirsty. I wish I had a drink of water from the well by the gate to Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ni, utukwɛ úbo ɔɔda Dawid geen na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ao, si bɔkɛ na ndubɔkɛ ntu lɛsiku libiɔ lɛni nkya Betlehem ɔma ɔban kayakun kenye na lɛni ni, nka ɔdia geen!”

english_verse: The first of these warriors was Jashobeam the son of Hachmoni, the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle he killed
translation_verse: Na Dawid bekpone bammɔ anyi ndi bamɛni, Hakmoni ubidi Yasobeam anwu ndi bekpone bammɔ ɔtɔnkune. Na anwu nádu nkyuli eti aku na kekpo kenwi kemmo.

english_verse: except Eleazar, who stayed with David. They took their positions in a nearby barley field and defeated the Philistines! The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu anwu ku nwuna bekyuli bénye kakpa kemo kammɔ ntɛ na békpoku Ƒilistiƒuɔ na Unwoti ɔ́ya na bádi lɛlɔ geen.

english_verse: One time the Three Warriors went to meet David among the rocks at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, bekpone benengudi avlaatɛ bammɔ akɔ ɛtɛ badi bébo Dawid kudɔ na Adulam lɛtakpɛ ubu kesii kani na ɔ́kya. Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone kasala bammɔ lɛnɔ bábla keliekɔ na Reƒaiƒuɔ Kɔwɛ kemmo na beli mmɔ.

english_verse: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in a fortress,
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na Dawid ɔkya kabɛkɔ kagyumanadi geen. Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone bakya Betlehem.

english_verse: and said, “Drinking this water would be like drinking the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.” The Three Warriors did these brave deeds. The Thirty Warriors (
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Naaakana ntu bɔmɛni bɔni. Na si lɛ́ni-mu ni, na use aani bekyuli bani béti bana ngba bése na lɛla lɛmɛni lɛlɔ ubugya ɔdi na mɔɔni.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu, Dawid úni ka ɔ́ni ntu bɔmmɔ. Na kayi buse ala amɛni na bekpone ɛtɛ bamɛni bábla na báƒɔ lɛnyi.

english_verse: Joab's brother Abishai was the leader of the Thirty Warriors, and in one battle he killed
translation_verse: Abisai ɔni ndi Yoab ɔnwani ni, anwu ndi bekpone ɛtɛ bammɔ ɔtɔnkune. Na anwu néti nwuna kewii na ɔ́du nkyuli eti aku. Na mmɔ na ɔ́ƒɔ lɛnyi geen aani ɛtɛ bani ngye.

english_verse: and was more famous than the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was their commander, but he never became one of the Three Warriors.
translation_verse: Na nwuna lɛnyi lɛ́kɔ litulo ɛtɛ bammɔ. Na úbenwini bana ɔtɔnkune ina ka ɔɔɔdi bana akɔ unwi.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. One time he killed two of Moab's best fighters, and one snowy day he went into a pit and killed a lion.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔnana ɔni baalɔ Yohaiada na ɔ́si Kabseel ɔma ni, ubo ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Benaia. Ubi ɔmɛni ɔ́di ukpone geen na ɔ́du Moabƒuɔ bekpone kpakplaa inyɔ bani mbo ogya geen. Lɛni kani na ɔ́du gyata na ubu ɔdi kemmo na limeyi lɛdi na etubankɛ áƒɔ kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Benaiah did things like that; he was just as brave as the Three Warriors,
translation_verse: Na Yohaiada ubidi Benaia kayi buse ablala amɛni udu ɔsu ni, anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́ƒɔ lɛnyi aani bekpone ɛtɛ bammɔ.

english_verse: even though he never became one of them. And he was certainly as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. So David made him the leader of his own bodyguard.
translation_verse: Na nwuna lɛnyi lɛ́kɔ lítulo bekpone avlaatɛ bammɔ. Nsu béteti-nwu lɛnyi bétebunku bekpone ɛtɛ bammɔ. Na Dawid ɔ́ya na anwu mɔɔnu nwuna bagyumanane lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Several of these warriors were from King Saul's own tribe of Benjamin. They were experts at using a bow and arrows, and they could shoot an arrow or sling a stone with either hand.
translation_verse: Bebo kɔtaminta, na baakana-ku bubo geen. Na bagyi atabi lɛnɔ buƒwimi kaduɛ kɔmii ku kɔdianu. Na badi Saul lɛlɔ bekyuli bani nási Benyamin kaba kemmo akɔ.

english_verse: Men from the tribe of Gad also joined David at his fortress in the desert and served as his warriors. They were also brave soldiers—fierce as lions and quick as gazelles. They were always prepared to fight with shields and spears.
translation_verse: Gadƒuɔ badi bámami lɛlɔ bétébunku Dawid na nwuna kagyumanakɔ kpakplaa kani na úsie ɔkya na ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo. Na badi bekpone bani mbo kayi na benye kagyumana bete kekpo, na bagyi atula ku kayi lɛgyumanala bɔda kaduɛ. Bekyuli bamɛni anumi álɛ bagyata anumi, na bebo ababla aani lɛku kemmo abi lɛlɔ bakwa.

english_verse: All these men were army officers; some were high-ranking officers over a thousand troops, and others were officers over a hundred troops.
translation_verse: Na Gadƒuɔ bekpone bamɛni badi bekpone batɔnkune. Na bani ndi bayikune geen baatɔnku bekpone apim na bani nsia baatɔnku eti anyɔ.

english_verse: Earlier, they had crossed the Jordan River when it flooded, and they chased out the people who lived in the valleys on each side of the river. Warriors from the Benjamin and Judah tribes
translation_verse: Na ama ndi bekyuli bani na bávia bésie Yordan Ketu bésie ɔvi ɔni ngye uwi ɔni na ketu kammɔ kéyi ku atu na kɔbuli kedeedi kemmo bátábɔku bekyuli bani ƒui nli kɔwɛ kemmo ɔ́si ɔƒɛ katukɔ útédu kanukɔ. Benyamin Ku Yuda Kaba Bekyuli Badi Básiaku Dawid Kama

english_verse: One time a group of men from the tribes of Benjamin and Judah went to the fortress where David was staying.
translation_verse: Benyamin ku Yuda kaba bekyuli badi lɛnɔ bébo Dawid kudɔ na nwuna kagyumanakɔ na kesii kani na ɔkya.

english_verse: David met them outside and said, “If you are coming as friends to fight on my side, then stay and join us. But if you try to turn me over to my enemies, the God our ancestors worshiped will punish you, because I have done nothing wrong.”
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid úsie útásiaku-ma na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Si atubɔyɔ kemmo na bɛkɛ bibo ka bibebunku-mi ni, nnye kagyumana ka lɛƒɔ-mii libunku lɛlɔ. Nsu si bubo na bíbo bɛnii bibedie-mi bite mina bekisine ɔni na mina enu ese sɛɛn na ńtabla likpidi lɛdi bɔdi ni, na muuvele bula bati Katɔti nnii, ɔtɛku-mii litemi lɛmmɔ.”

english_verse: Some of the warriors who joined David were from the tribe of Manasseh. They had earlier gone with David when he agreed to fight on the side of the Philistines against King Saul. But as soon as the Philistine rulers realized that David might turn against them and rejoin Saul, they sent David away to the town of Ziklag.
translation_verse: Bekpone badi bási Manase kaba kemmo na bébo bébenye Dawid kama uwi ɔni na ɔ́siaku Ƒilistiƒuɔ ka bétékpoku Ɔga Saul. Nsu geen ni, bétebunku Ƒilistiƒuɔ kekpo kammɔ. Ɔsika Ƒilistiƒuɔ batɔnkune básu banini, “Bɔdubɔyii udu si Dawid ɔ́sɔ ɔ́blaku Ɔga Saul unwi.”

english_verse: and brave soldiers, and so David made them officers in his army. They fought on his side when enemy troops attacked.
translation_verse: Na bébunku Dawid na békpoku bekpone bamba bani mɔɔta kekpo teebile ala ɔsika bebo kayi na beekpó geen, na úti-ma ɔ́bla batɔnkune.

english_verse: Other Israelites from as far away as the territories of Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought cattle and sheep to slaughter for food. They also brought donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen that were loaded down with flour, dried figs and raisins, wine, and olive oil. Everyone in Israel was very happy.
translation_verse: Lɛnɔ ni, bana liku bekyuli bani na bási ɔgyu ƒui aani Sebulon ku Isakar ku Naƒtali kaba bekyuli béti adila pii básia bana bebuo ala betine lidu lɛlɔ béboku-ma. Na ɔlaaƒɔ ku ala agyidi lidu lidu ku ntɛ ku nnɔmii ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu bábu. Na sɔsɔ ni, ebiti ákya Israel.

english_verse: All of these soldiers voluntarily came to Hebron because they wanted David to become king of Israel. In fact, everyone in Israel wanted the same thing.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bamɛni ƒui ndi bekpone bani néti lɛlɔ béte ƒaa ka besie na betékpo. Na bana ƒui bébo Hebron ka bébese Dawid lɛga na ɔdi Israel ƒui lɛlɔ. Na lɛni kani na Israelƒuɔ bakladi ƒui bada kasusu kenwi ka bése Dawid lɛga.

english_verse: The soldiers stayed in Hebron three days, eating and drinking what their relatives had prepared for them.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bammɔ bádi emeyi atɛ na Dawid kudɔ mmɔ. Na baadi na baaní ɔsika bana kɔduli bekyuli béte-ma adila ku anila na bada bésienku mmɔ.

english_verse: Then he led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They went there to get the sacred chest and bring it to Jerusalem, because it belonged to the Lord God, whose throne is above the winged creatures on the lid of the chest.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bésie Yudaƒuɔ ɔma ɔni ndi Baala na basɔ baalɔ-nwu Kiriat-Yearim ka bátaƒɔ Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka ɔni na Unwoti lɛnyi lɛ́sia-nwu lɛlɔ na unye bebweyi badi udu ku avwi lɛlɔ na baalɔ-ma Kerub.

english_verse: David was afraid what the Lord might do to him, and he asked himself, “Should I really be the one to take care of the sacred chest?”
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛmmɔ ni, Dawid ɔ́yia Katɔti geen na úye ɔnini, lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Dɛ na ndubɔbla na liti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmɛni lisienku mina kaduli?”

english_verse: The people agreed this was the right thing to do.
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bénu kalɔ ka bádubusie ɔsika ɔdia-ma lɛni.

english_verse: David gathered everyone from the Shihor River in Egypt to Lebo-Hamath in the north.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Dawid ɔ́lɔ Israelƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui ɔ́siku Sihor Ketu kudɔ na Egyipte útédu Hamat ka bésie betéti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ basiku Kiriat-Yearim.

english_verse: The sacred chest was still at Abinadab's house, and when David and the crowd arrived there, they brought the chest outside and placed it on a new ox cart. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio guided the cart,
translation_verse: Bététi Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ básiku Abinadab kaduli. Na béti adaka ɔmmɔ básia kɛɛkɛ ɔwɔdi ɔdi lɛlɔ. Na Usa ku Ahio bákya báagyumana kɛɛkɛ ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: while David and the crowd danced and sang praises to the Lord with all their might. They played music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
translation_verse: Na ulu lɛlɔ ni, Dawid ku Israelƒuɔ bammɔ bakɛ beemwi Katɔti ku agya. Na beedie lɛnu na baatɔ́. Bada lɛbentaa ku ebi ku enukpɛ agyala ku abambadi baagyá ku kɔkpɛɛ.

english_verse: But when they came to Chidon's threshing place, the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out and took hold of the chest to stop it from falling.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni bédu Kidon kakpa kesii kani beewiile edula ebi ni, Usa údie kɔnu ɔnii uunyene adaka ɔmmɔ ɔsika ebuo ɔni nti adaka ɔmmɔ ɔ́gbanta.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi ɔ́kya Usa na ɔ́ƒiɛmi-nwu ɔ́va kalɔ ka útuku adaka ɔmmɔ ɔsu. Anwuɔsu úkpi na Unwoti anumi mmɔ.

english_verse: David then got angry with God for killing Uzzah. So he named that place “Attack on Uzzah,” and it's been called that ever since.
translation_verse: Dawid ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi na Unwoti kɔnyi kɔni na úti ɔ́kya Usa mmɔ ɔsu ɔ́si kɔnyi kɔni na Unwoti úti ɔ́kya Usa ɔsu. Anwuɔsu úti úbedu ɔmwi ni, kesii kammɔ baalɔ bani Peres-Usa

english_verse: So instead of taking it to Jerusalem, David decided to take it to the home of Obed-Edom, who lived in the town of Gath.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Dawid úteti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ útesienku Yerusalem. Mmomu ɔ́da-nwu úse ɔnana ɔdi baalɔ banii Obed-Edom kaduli na ɔdi Gatni.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord blessed Obed-Edom, his family, and everything he owned.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ úse Obed-Edom kaduli kammɔ abuli atɛ. Na Unwoti úte Obed-Edom kaduli kusɛ kusɛ na lɛla biala baabla kemmo.

english_verse: David and his army marched to Baal-Perazim, where they attacked and defeated the Philistines. He said, “I defeated my enemies because God broke through them like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Dawid ku nwuna bekpone báta bésie Baal-Perasim. Na mmɔ na bátádi Ƒilistiƒuɔ lɛlɔ. Na Dawid ɔ́su ɔnini, “Kalɛ na ntu bɔɔbwɛ taalɛ kesii kadi ni, lɛni na Katɔti ɔ́bwɛ ɔ́lɛ mina bekisine lɛlɔ na úti-ma ɔ́kya-mi enu kemmo.” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu kesii kammɔ baalɔ bani Baal-Perasim.

english_verse: David obeyed God and he defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Gibeon to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Dawid ɔ́bla kalɛ kani na Unwoti úbo-nwu ɔda. Na békpo bádi Ƒilistiƒuɔ bekpone lɛlɔ. Ɔsi Gibeon utédu Geser.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. They brought along carpenters and stone workers, and enough cedar logs to build David a palace.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Ɔga Hiram ɔni mɔɔdi lɛga na Tiro ɔ́tala bekyuli badi úmene Dawid. Na béti egyii kpakplaa etenku ku banwine ku bani ngyi kalɛ na baatú atabi lɛtɔ kalɛ na bátátu keliekɔ kabuni geen béte-nwu.

english_verse: After David moved to Jerusalem, he married more women and had more sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Dawid ɔɔdi lɛga na Yerusalem ni, úti beleku pii na ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́kɛ bebi bananabi ku belekubi pii.

english_verse: From then on, David became even more famous, and the Lord made all the nations afraid of him.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Dawid ɔ́ƒɔ lɛnyi na kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Na Unwoti ɔ́ya kadi ƒui baayia-nwu.

english_verse: When the Philistines heard that David had become king of Israel, they came to capture him. But David heard about their plan and marched out to meet them in battle.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Ƒilistiƒuɔ bénu ka bése Dawid lɛga ka utaadi Israelƒuɔ ƒui lɛlɔ ni, bana bekpone ƒui bátu akpagya ka batawia-nwu na bekpoku-nwu. Nsu Dawid únu litemi lɛmmɔ na anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́ta ka utekpoku-ma.

english_verse: The Philistines had already camped in Rephaim Valley and were raiding the nearby villages.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ni, Ƒilistiƒuɔ bébo bakya Reƒaim Kɔwɛ kemmo na bakya beebile ala na mmɔ.

english_verse: David asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help me win?” The Lord told David, “Yes, attack them! I will give you victory.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Dawid úye ɔ́siku Katɔti kudɔ ɔnini, “Nteesie ntékpoku Ƒilistiƒuɔ? Adubɔnyonu-ma akya-mi enu kemmo?” Amu na Unwoti údie kenye ɔnini, “Teesie na ndubuti-ma lɛkya-a enu kemmo.”

english_verse: Then David ordered his troops to burn the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ báda bana baƒiɔ báva mmɔ. Na Dawid ɔ́ya na bákyula-ma.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi lɛnɔ ni, Ƒilistiƒuɔ básɔ báta bésie kɔwɛ kɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: David asked God what he should do, and God answered, “Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind them where the balsam trees are.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Dawid ɔ́sɔ úye Katɔti únu lɛla lɛni na ɔbla. Na Katɔti údie-nwu kenye ɔnini, “Bítesie siin. Mmomu bɛka bɛmana-ma na bikpoku-ma na kugyii kubendi kɔmmɔ anumi mmɔ.

english_verse: Wait there until you hear the treetops making the sound of marching troops. That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army. So you must then attack quickly!”
translation_verse: Na si bɛnya binu kɔku ka ɔbla aani bekyuli esie mɔɔví kugyii kubendi kɔmmɔ katɔ kakɛ na bikeli bitekpoku-ma. Ɔsika ɔmɛni ndubɔtina ka Katɔti ɔ́gyu ɔ́tɔ bina anumi útekpoku Ƒilistiƒuɔ bammɔ.”

english_verse: David had several buildings built in Jerusalem, and he had a tent set up where the sacred chest would be kept.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Dawid ɔ́tu lɛtɔ úte lɛlɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ na kesii baalɔ Dawid ɔma unengudi ni, ɔ́klibi kesii kadi lɛnɔ úte Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka. Na ɔ́tu Adi Kevo úte-nwu.

english_verse: Next, David invited everyone to come to Jerusalem and watch the sacred chest being carried to the place he had set up for it.
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid ɔ́lɔ Israelƒuɔ ƒui ɔ́sala na Yerusalem na ɔ́su-ma ka betéti Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ beboku. Na uti use kesii kani ɔ́klibi úse úte-nwu.

english_verse: He also sent for Aaron's descendants and for the Levites. The Levites that came were:
translation_verse: Na ɔ́lɔ Aaron kaba bekyuli ƒui ɔ́sala ku Lewiƒuɔ bamɛni.

english_verse: David called together these six Levites and the two priests, Zadok and Abiathar.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Dawid ɔ́lɔ bakpane Sadok ku Abiatar ku Lewiƒuɔ bamɛni, Uriel ku Asaia ku Yoel ku Semaia ku Eliel ku Aminadab

english_verse: The first time we tried to bring the chest to Jerusalem, we didn't ask the Lord what he wanted us to do. He was angry with us, because you Levites weren't there to carry the chest.”
translation_verse: Amii ɔsu na Unwoti ɔ́kɛku-bu kɔnyi kukpidi kɔmmɔ ɔsika ɔɔɔdi amii nágyu Adaka ɔmmɔ kudeedi na búteye Unwoti lɛnɔ bútenu ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na bɔsia bɔgyu Adaka ɔmmɔ kalɛ na ɔɔyɔ́.”

english_verse: The priests and the Levites made themselves clean. They were now ready to carry the sacred chest
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ békisi lɛkɔ bábla lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi kalɛ na bakana beti Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: on poles that rested on their shoulders, just as the Lord had told Moses to do.
translation_verse: Na béti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ básia ligyii lɛlɔ na bágyu básia amangba aani kalɛ na Mose ɔ́tina-ma ka babla.

english_verse: David then told the leaders to choose some Levites to sing and play music on small harps, other stringed instruments, and cymbals.
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid ɔ́su batɔnkune bammɔ ɔnii baƒuna Lewiƒuɔ badi na beteedie lɛnu na bataagya agyala na lɛbentaa ku kɔbuli agyala bamba lɛlɔ ku enukpɛ agyala.

english_verse: Four Levites were then appointed to guard the sacred chest. They were Berechiah, Elkanah, Obed-Edom, and Jehiah. Finally, David chose priests to walk in front of the sacred chest and blow trumpets. They were Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer. The Sacred Chest Is Brought to Jerusalem (
translation_verse: Na bakpane bani ndi Sebania ku Yosaƒat ku Netanel ku Amasai ku Sekaria ku Benaia ku Elieser ni, ama ndubunye bunye adaka ammɔ anumi bataavwi kɔkpɛɛ. Na Obed-Edom ku Yehia lɛnɔ badubo bubunku bani mɔɔgyumana Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ kayaku lɛlɔ.

english_verse: David, the leaders of Israel, and the army commanders were very happy as they went to Obed-Edom's house to get the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Dawid ku Israel benengu bammɔ ku bekpone batɔnkune bammɔ bakɛ ku lɛlɔyɔ ka bésela Obed-Edom kaduli betétiku Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: God gave the Levites the strength they needed to carry the chest, and so they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti úte Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ɔlɔkplu ku ɔyikun ɔni na badubuti beti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ, anwuɔsu bádu ɔmantɛ bakɔ maatɛ ku baƒonu bagyani maatɛ béti bákpa.

english_verse: David, the Levites, Chenaniah the music director, and all the musicians were wearing linen robes, and David was also wearing a linen cloth.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ku Lewiƒuɔ bani nti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ ku Kenania, kɔgya lɛlɔ ɔnune ɔmmɔ, ku lɛnu bediene bammɔ ƒui bakya lɛwu gyɔlɔɔ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: While the sacred chest was being carried into Jerusalem, everyone was celebrating by shouting and playing music on horns, trumpets, cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na beti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ na beeduo Yerusalem ni, ukyuli biala ɔɔva ku lɛdi momoomo na baagyá agyala ku bebuo ese ku kɔkpɛɛ ku enukpɛ agyala ku lɛbentaa ku kɔbuli agyala bamba lidu lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing in honor of the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Amu na Saul ubidi ulekubi ɔni ndi Dawid beleku akɔ unwi údie lili ɔ́siku nwuna ƒansili na ɔ́nu ka beti adaka ɔmmɔ badububoku Dawid ɔma unengudi kemmo. Na ka ɔ́nu kalɛ na Dawid ɔɔtɔ́ ku lɛlɔyɔ ni, Dawid ala ékpi-nwu ɔkwɛ kɔnakunwi.

english_verse: After David had finished, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord
translation_verse: Na ka Dawid ɔ́wɔlɔ ala amɛni bɔbla ni, úvele ka Unwoti kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku bekyuli bammɔ.

english_verse: and gave every person in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins.
translation_verse: Na úte bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ɔdi biala bodobodo umodi unwi ku lɛna lɛdi ku egyiibi lidu kangyiɛ.

english_verse: David appointed some of the Levites to serve at the sacred chest; they were to play music and sing praises to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Amu na Dawid ɔ́ƒuna Lewiƒuɔ badi ka benye bataabla kabla kadi na Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ kudɔ na beteevele Katɔti ala na beteemwi-nwu na bataagya-nwu enu lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Asaph was their leader, and Zechariah was his assistant. Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and another man named Jeiel were appointed to play small harps and stringed instruments. Asaph himself played the cymbals,
translation_verse: Na Asaƒ ndi bana ɔtɔnkune na Sekaria ɔdi nwuna ubunkune. Yeiel ku Semiramot ku Yehiel ku Matitia ku Eliab ku Benaia ku Obed-Edom ku ukyuli bamba ɔni lɛnɔ na baalɔ Yeiel ama na báƒuna ka bataagya lɛbentaa ku lidu ku enukpɛ agyala.

english_verse: and the two priests Benaiah and Jahaziel were to blow trumpets every day in front of the sacred chest. David's Song of Praise (Psalms
translation_verse: Na bakpane inyɔ bani ndi Benaia ku Yahasiel ndubo kɔkpɛɛ butaavwi limeyi ndi limeyi na Katɔti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ anumi. Dawid Ɔ́ya Na Bédie Bumwi Lɛnu

english_verse: We must never forget his agreement and his promises, not in thousands of years. *
translation_verse: Nwuna anu asia lɛla lɛni na únyimi lɛlɔ uwi ƒui. Na nwuna linyese lise lite kaba mpim mpim bekyuli.

english_verse: You belong to the family of Israel, his servant; you are his chosen ones, the descendants of Jacob.
translation_verse: Nwuna kabla ɔblane Israel kaba bebi na bɛdi. Na bɛdi-nwu bekyuli baƒunadi bani ndi Yakob bebi.

english_verse: That same day, David instructed Asaph and his relatives for the first time to sing these praises to the Lord:
translation_verse: Amu na limeyi lɛmmɔ kani lɛlɔ ni, Dawid ɔ́su Asaƒ ku nwuna lɛlɔ bekyuli kudeedi ɔnii batu kɔgya kɔni ndubo mɛni beti bemwi Unwoti.

english_verse: Praise the Lord and pray in his name! Tell everyone what he has done.
translation_verse: Bɛgya Unwoti enu. Na bitaakpali-nwu lɛnyi. Bɛsu kadi bekyuli ƒui ala ani na ɔ́bla.

english_verse: Sing praises to the Lord! Tell about his miracles.
translation_verse: Bidie bumwi lɛnu bite-nwu, na bibo nwuna akɔla ala budie taatina kudu.

english_verse: Celebrate and worship his holy name with all your heart.
translation_verse: Amii bani ƒui mɔɔwia Unwoti ni, lɛlɔ lɛyɔ-mii na bimwi-nwu lɛnyi kedee na bɛkɔliku-nwu katɔ.

english_verse: Trust the Lord and his mighty power. Worship him always.
translation_verse: Biti bina anu bɛsia Unwoti ku nwuna ɔyikun lɛlɔ na bitaanu-nwu anumi uwi biala.

english_verse: Remember his miracles and all his wonders and his fair decisions.
translation_verse: Binyimo nwuna akɔla ala budie taatina ani na ɔ́bla ku kalɛ na ɔ́tɛ litemi na ulu siin lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Lord is our God, bringing justice everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Unwoti ndi bula Katɔti. Na anwu mɔɔtɛku kayawi ƒui litemi.

english_verse: when he said, “I'll give you the land of Canaan.”
translation_verse: Ɔ́su ɔnini, “Amii na ndubuti Kanaan kalɔ ƒui lite na kana ƒui kenwini bina kadikɔ.”

english_verse: At the time there were only a few of us, and we were homeless.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, beeemomo. Na lɛnɔ ni, baƒɔ na badi na kalɔ kammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: We wandered from nation to nation, from one country to another.
translation_verse: Na busie kani bakɛ beesié taavi kadi bamba bekyuli akɔ ɔ́si lɛga kadikɔ úsie lɛga kadikɔ.

english_verse: God did not let anyone mistreat our people. Instead he protected us by punishing rulers
translation_verse: Na ɔ́gyumana-ma ɔni na ukyuli ina unwi útanya-ma útakya. Mmomu ɔ́tɛmiku baga bammɔ kpakplaa na ama ɔsu.

english_verse: and telling them, “Don't touch my chosen leaders or harm my prophets!”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔdi biala utetuku mina kadi bekyuli bani na lɛ́ƒuna. Na ɔdi utabla mina kenye bediene badi likpidi lɛdi.”

english_verse: Everyone on this earth, sing praises to the Lord. Day after day announce, “The Lord has saved us!”
translation_verse: Amii kadi ƒui bekyuli, bɛtu ɔnu bite Unwoti. Bidie ɔnu na bɛsu bekyuli limeyi ndi limeyi kalɛ na ɔ́ƒɔ-bu ngba.

english_verse: Tell every nation on earth, “The Lord is wonderful and does marvelous things!
translation_verse: Bɛkɔ lɛsa bite bekyuli kalɛ na uukeye na kadi ƒui akɔ. Na bɛsu akɔla ala budie taatina ani na ɔ́bla na bekyuli ƒui akɔ.

english_verse: The Lord is great and deserves our greatest praise! He is the only God worthy of our worship.
translation_verse: Ɔsika bula Unwoti úbomo na nwuna lɛnyi lɛ́kɔ katɔ anwuɔsu na ɔlɛka bumwi-nwu na bɔyia-nwu butulo baƒiɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Give honor and praise to the Lord, whose power and beauty fill his holy temple.”
translation_verse: Unwoti úbomo geen na nwuna bukeye bɔ́ka bɔ́mana-nwu. Na nwuna ɔyikun ku lɛlɔyɔ bɔ́ƒɔ nwuna kakpakɔ kedee kammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Tell everyone of every nation, “Praise the glorious power of the Lord.
translation_verse: Amii kadi ƒui bekyuli, bidie Unwoti kenyekɔ kani muukeye bɛtina ku kalɛ na ubo ɔyikun.

english_verse: He is wonderful! Praise him and bring an offering into his temple. Worship the Lord, majestic and holy.
translation_verse: Bimwi Unwoti lɛnyi lɛni muukeye na biti etela biboku-nwu. Amii kalɔ lɛlɔ bekyuli ƒui biboku eli kalɔ na bimwi Unwoti ɔni nébomo na use kedee.

english_verse: Everyone on earth, now tremble!” The world stands firm, never to be shaken.
translation_verse: Na lɛlɔ litaatɔ-mii ku liƒu na nwuna anumi. Kalɔ kemodi kammɔ kenye kana lɛgba lɛlɔ kpi na kalákunku kudii.

english_verse: Tell the heavens and the earth to be glad and celebrate! And announce to the nations, “The Lord is King!”
translation_verse: Na ebiti ataada awɔ kalɔ ku kana ala ƒui. Na bɛsu na kadi ƒui bekyuli akɔ bɛnini, “Unwoti Katɔti mɔɔdi lɛga.”

english_verse: Command the ocean to roar with all of its creatures and the fields to rejoice with all of their crops.
translation_verse: Na ɛpu ɔmmɔ uteedie lɛdi momoomo ku ala ani ƒui nkya-nwu kemmo. Na mmo bɔmmɔ ƒui ku ala ani nkya aku kemmo ƒui bidie lɛnu ku lɛlɔyɔ bite yiiduu.

english_verse: Then every tree in the forest will sing joyful songs to the Lord. He is coming to judge all people on earth.
translation_verse: Na egyii ammɔ adubudie lɛnu ebo kudu na Unwoti ɔni ndubo anumi. Ɔsika ɔdubo ubatɛku kayawi bekyuli litemi na ulu siin lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Praise the Lord because he is good to us, and his love never fails.
translation_verse: Bɛgya Unwoti enu, ɔsika ɔdia na ɔɔyɔ́-bu uwi ndi uwi.

english_verse: Say to him, “Save us, Lord God! Bring us back from among the nations. Let us celebrate and shout in praise of your holy name.
translation_verse: Bɛva momoomo bɛnini, “Unwoti bula Ɔƒɔne, ƒɔ-bu ngba!” Na asiku-bu kɔlɔ bamba lɛlɔ asɔku abásala. Ya na lɛlɔ lɛyɔ-bu na bɔgya-a enu na bumwi ƒula lɛnyi kedee ku kudu.

english_verse: Lord God of Israel, you deserve to be praised forever and ever.” After David finished, the people shouted, “Amen! Praise the Lord!” David Appoints Worship Leaders at Jerusalem and Gibeon
translation_verse: Bimwi Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti lɛnyi ɔsi ɔƒɛni úsela uwi ƒui. Mmɔ na ukyuli biala ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔsia lɛni,” ku “Bimwi Unwoti.”

english_verse: David chose Asaph and the Levites in his clan to be in charge of the daily worship at the place where the sacred chest was kept.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Dawid ɔ́ƒuna Asaƒ ku Lewiƒuɔ ɔ́siku nwuna kɔdua kemmo ka bataabla akpala limeyi ndi limeyi na kesii kani na Bunyimi Adaka kedee ɔmmɔ use.

english_verse: David also chose Zadok the priest and his relatives who were priests to serve at the Lord's sacred tent at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Dawid ɔ́ƒuna ɔkpane Sadok lɛnɔ ku nwuna lɛlɔ bekyuli bani ndi bakpane ka bataabla kabla na Katɔti Adi Kevo kammɔ kemmo na Gibeon.

english_verse: They were to offer sacrifices on the altar every morning and evening, just as the Lord had commanded in the Law he gave Israel.
translation_verse: Na bataabla akpala ɔtanta biala ku useyi uwi biala aani kalɛ na ɔkya ɔda bubo bɔni na Unwoti úte Israelƒuɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Heman and Jeduthun were their assistants, as well as the other men who had been chosen to praise the Lord for his never-ending love.
translation_verse: Heman ku Yedutum ndi bana bebunkune úbunku bekyuli bamba bani lɛnɔ na báƒuna ka beteemwi Unwoti na kalɛ na ɔɔyɔ́-bu uwi ndi uwi ɔsu.

english_verse: Heman and Jeduthun were also responsible for blowing the trumpets, and for playing the cymbals and other instruments during worship at the tent. The Levites in Jeduthun's clan were the guards at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Na Heman ɔmɛni ku Yedutum ndubo kɔkpɛɛ lɛnɔ butaavwi na bataagya enukpɛ agyala ku agyala bamba lɛnɔ si uwi ɔni na baakpá na kevo kammɔ kemmo mmɔ. Na Yedutum kɔdua bekyuli ndi bagyumanane na Gibeon.

english_verse: After that, everyone went home, and David went home to his family.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔmmɔ kama ni, bekyuli bammɔ bátɔlɔ bésie bana kɔduli na Dawid lɛnɔ únwini úsie nwuna kaduli bekyuli kudɔ.

english_verse: Soon after David moved into his new palace, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest is kept in a tent.”
translation_verse: Ka Dawid úsie uli nwuna ɔga kaduli kawɔdi kammɔ kemmo uwi klukwii ɔdi kama ni, ɔ́su Kenye Udiene Natan ɔnini, “Ami nli ɔga lɛgbanya lɛni na béti egyii ani na áƒɔ kuye geen bátu. Nsu Unwoti Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ anwu ɔlɛ kevo kemmo.”

english_verse: and yet you have promised to do even more for my descendants. You are treating me as if I am a very important person.
translation_verse: asa na ásɔ eesé-bu kenye kamɛni ka asɔ abla ala ani na etulo ammɔ ete ami ku mina kaba kemmo bebi. Adanku-mi aani ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́ƒɔ kuye geen kɔdi.

english_verse: That night, the Lord told Nathan
translation_verse: Nsu usien ɔmmɔ kani ni, Unwoti ɔ́su Natan ɔnini,

english_verse: to go to David and tell him: David, you are my servant, so listen carefully: You are not the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: “Sie mina kabla ɔblane Dawid kudɔ na atásu-nwu ka lɛla lɛni na ami Unwoti mɔɔsu-nwu nnini, ‘Ɔɔɔdi awɔ Dawid ndubɔtu ɔtɔ ete-mi na lilie-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Ńtelie ɔtɔ ɔni na bayawine béti bana enu bátu kudii, mmomu Adi Kevo kani na baalɛ taagyu ɔ́si likpo linwi úsie kesii bamba kemmo na lílie ɔ́si uwi ɔni na lídie mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ lɛ́lɛku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ úti úbedu ɔmwi.

english_verse: I chose special leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Na uwi biala na mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ báta bási kesii kadi bésela kesii bamba ni, ami lɛnɔ nsiaku-ma. Na lɛlɔ badine bani na lɛ́ƒuna mmɔ ni, ɔmani na lɛ́su nnii beti egyii ani náƒɔ kuye mmɔ adi batu keliekɔ kadi bete-mi na lilie dii?’

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Na kesii biala na akɛ ni, lɛ́siaku-ɔ. Na líbunku-ɔ na ádi ƒula bekisine ƒui lɛlɔ. Na ɔƒaani lɛnɔ ni, ndubɔbla-a na aƒɔ lɛnyi aani baga bamba bani náƒɔ lɛnyi bétulo ƒui na kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace. They will no longer have to tremble with fear—evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ni, ndubɔƒuna keliekɔ sɛsɛɛ kadi lise lite mina kadi bekyuli ka belie. Na ndubɔya na belie kesii kammɔ ɔni na bekyuli badi basɔ belékpoku-ma lɛnɔ aani kalɛ na kadi bamba badi bábla bábavi.

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people, and I will keep your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that like you, your descendants will be kings.
translation_verse: Ɔsika kuuku ni, lɛni na kadi bamba bekyuli bamɛni békpoku mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ ɔ́si uwi ɔni na líse kalɔ mɔɔƒuna batɔnkune teete-ma ka batɔnku-ma. Nsu ndubɔdi-ma lɛlɔ. “ ‘Na ɔƒaani ni, muusé-ɔ kenye ka ƒula kaba kemmo bebi ndubo lɛga butaadi ƒula kalɛ.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried beside your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Na si uwi ɔni na ékpi na átɔlɔ ébo ƒula bati kudɔ ni, ƒula kaba kemmo ubi na ndubɔya na bese lɛga na ƒula kenye, na ɔdubɔbla awɔ ɔlati bebi akɔ unwi. Na ndubɔya na nwuna lɛga kadikɔ kenye kpakplaa.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Na ubi ɔmmɔ ndubɔtu ɔtɔ ute mina lɛnyi na ndubɔya nwuna lɛgaboku lise liteesie uwi ƒui.

english_verse: I will be like a father to him, and he will be like a son to me. I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Ndubɔdi-nwu kɔti. Na anwu lɛnɔ ɔdi mina ubi. Na bɔyɔ bɔni nkya ami ku-nwu ntɛ bulékulo kudii aani ami ku Saul ɔni náka-nwu bulie ɔdi kalɛ.

english_verse: I will make sure that your son and his descendants will rule my people and my kingdom forever.
