translation_verse: “Ɔƒɛni kalɛ bakana na baƒiɔ-ɔ na ani-ma kɔtu na étile kayaa na ɔnantu ɔsɔ ulana. Nsu si báda bana ekpidi bɔbla báya na bénwini bánu kakpakɔ kamɛni na bévele-ɔ lɛla lɛdi na ƒula lɛnyi kemmo ni,

english_verse: listen from your home in heaven and forgive them. The people of Israel are your servants, so teach them to live right. And send rain on the land you promised them forever.
translation_verse: na enu-ma bɔkpali asiku ƒula keliekɔ na katɔ mmɔ na eti akyiɛ-ma. Israel kadi bekyuli ƒui badi ƒula kabla bablane, anwuɔsu tina-ma kalɛ na belie ngba siin na ulu lɛlɔ. Na aya na ɔnantu ɔna uwi kalɔ kani na ese kenye ete bana bati kuuku lɛlɔ ka beti uwi ƒui mmɔ.

english_verse: Sometimes the crops may dry up or rot or be eaten by locusts or grasshoppers, and your people will be starving. Sometimes enemies may surround their towns, or your people will become sick with deadly diseases.
translation_verse: “Ɔkana na ubo ute uwi ɔdi ka baalɔlɔ bebile ala iye edula ammɔ ebu na kalɔ kemmo, Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu kɔka kubataada ƒula bekyuli, iye bekisine babaka kalɔ kammɔ ƒui bakya, iye ɔlɛ buɛ ubo kalɔ kammɔ bekyuli lɛlɔ na bese kalɔ beteekpi.

english_verse: Please listen when anyone in Israel truly feels sorry and sincerely prays with arms lifted toward your temple.
translation_verse: Muuvele nnii nu ukyuli biala ɔni ndubɔkpali-ɔ uvele buti taakyiɛ na údie enu ɔ́tina ƒula kakpakɔ kamɛni ka nwuna ekpidi éduo-nwu geen.

english_verse: You know what is in everyone's heart. So from your home in heaven answer their prayers, according to what they do and what is in their hearts.
translation_verse: Agyi lɛla lɛni na lɛkya ukyuli biala kayi kemmo, anwuɔsu nu ɔdi biala buvele na abla ete-nwu ɔkɛnku nwuna ɔbladu ku lɛla lɛni nkya ukyuli ɔmmɔ kayi kemmo kenye asiku ƒula keliekɔ na katɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Then your people will worship you and obey you for as long as they live in the land you gave their ancestors.
translation_verse: Na ƒula bekyuli badubo-ɔ bɔbu na benu-ɔ litemi uwi ɔni ƒui na béti belie kalɔ kani na éti éte bana bati kuuku mmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Foreigners will hear about you and your mighty power, and some of them will come to live among your people Israel. If any of them pray toward this temple,
translation_verse: “Baƒɔ badubo ƒula kɔku bunu na bati ƒula ɔyikun bonwu ɔni na ebo na bebelie abu ƒula kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ akɔ. Si bana ɔdi ɔɔnu kakpakɔ kamɛni na úvele-ɔ lɛla lɛdi ni,

english_verse: listen from your home in heaven and answer their prayers. Then everyone on earth will worship you, just as your own people Israel do, and they will know that I have built this temple in your honor.
translation_verse: na enu ete-nwu asiku ƒula keliekɔ na katɔ mmɔ na badubɔnu bati ka ami nátu kakpakɔ kamɛni líte ƒula lɛnyi bumwi ku bɔbu.

english_verse: Sometimes you will order your people to attack their enemies. Then your people will turn toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, and they will pray to you.
translation_verse: “Uwi ɔdi ni, adubɔsu ƒula kadi bekyuli kpakplaa ka bekpoku bana bekisine. Na ama lɛnɔ badubo bunwini na banu ƒula kakpakɔ kani na lɛ́tu líte-ɔ na ƒula ɔma unengudi ɔni na áƒuna mɛni kemmo na bakpali-ɔ.

english_verse: Answer their prayers from heaven and give them victory.
translation_verse: Nu-ma bɔkpali siku katɔ kesii kani na eli mmɔ na aya na badi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Everyone sins. But when your people sin against you, suppose you get angry enough to let their enemies drag them away to foreign countries.
translation_verse: “Ukyuli biala ɔɔbla likpidi. Nsu si banii ƒula kadi bekyuli báƒiɔ-ɔ akana na eti kɔnyi kpakplaa geen na akana na aya na bana bekisine beƒie-ma batɔlɔku.

english_verse: Later, they may feel sorry for what they did and ask your forgiveness. Answer them when they pray toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, here in this land you gave their ancestors. From your home in heaven, listen to their sincere prayers and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
translation_verse: Nsu si kama ƒui na bánu bana bɔƒiɔ báti na bénwini bánu kakpakɔ kamɛni na bévele-ɔ ni, na eti akyiɛ-ma asiku katɔ kesii kani na eli. Aka na lɛ́tu líte-ɔ na ƒula ɔma unegudi kemmo mɛni na kalɔ kani na éti éte bula bati kuuku mɛni kemmo.

english_verse: Lord God, hear us when we pray in this temple.
translation_verse: “Unwoti Katɔti, nu-bu bɔkpali si buuvele-ɔ lɛla lɛdi taasiku kakpakɔ kamɛni kemmo.

english_verse: Come to your new home, where we have already placed the sacred chest, which is the symbol of your strength. I pray that when the priests announce your power to save people, those who are faithful to you will celebrate what you've done for them.
translation_verse: “O Unwoti Katɔti, ta ku ƒula Bunyimi Adaka na atina ƒula ɔyikun. Na esie etélie ƒula keliekɔ. Unwoti Katɔti, ya na ƒula bakpane bataabla ala ani nse siin uwi biala. Na aya na ƒula bekyuli kedee lɛlɔ lɛyɔ na lɛla lɛni na ábla éte-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Always remember the love you had for your servant David, so that you will not reject your chosen kings.
translation_verse: Na muuvele nnii taakali kalɛ na áyɔ ƒula kabla ɔblane Dawidi uwi biala, na teni ƒula ukyuli Ɔƒunadi ɔmmɔ.”

english_verse: and the priests could not go in.
translation_verse: na bakpane bammɔ muedi bátakana na beduo ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: When the crowd of people saw the fire and the Lord's glory, they knelt down and worshiped the Lord. They prayed: “The Lord is good, and his love never ends.”
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na bekyuli lisu bani nnye mmɔ bánu ogya ku Katɔti bukeye bɔmmɔ ni, bana ƒui bálɛ akɔnkɔ na bákya lili kalɔ béte Katɔti na bákpali-nwu basu banini, “Ɔsika ɔdia na ɔɔyɔ́-bu uwi ndi uwi.”

english_verse: Then they will answer, “It was because the people of Israel rejected the Lord their God, who rescued their ancestors from Egypt, and they started worshiping other gods.”
translation_verse: Na ama badubudie kenye banini, ‘Ɔni na Israelƒuɔ béni Unwoti bana Katɔti ɔni nédie bana bati kuuku ɔ́lɛku Egyipteƒuɔ enu kemmo na bése kalɔ baakpá kadi bamba baƒiɔ ɔsu.’ ”

english_verse: Everybody stood up during the ceremony. The priests were in their assigned places, blowing their trumpets. And the Levites faced them, playing the musical instruments that David had made for them to use when they praised the Lord for his never-ending love.
translation_verse: Na ɔdi ɔmmɔ bɔbla kemmo ni, ukyuli biala ɔ́ta únye. Na bakpane benye bana kenyekɔ kani na béte-ma na baavwi bana kɔkpɛɛ. Na Lewiƒuɔ lɛnɔ bana anumi aatina bakpane bammɔ kudɔ na baagyá bana lɛbentaa ku agyala ani na Dawidi ɔ́bla úte-ma ka bataagya si uwi ɔni na beemwi Katɔti na kalɛ na ɔɔyɔ́-bu uwi ndi uwi na uuubo kawɔkɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: If my own people will humbly pray and turn back to me and stop sinning, then I will answer them from heaven. I will forgive them and make their land fertile once again.
translation_verse: Si ami ɔlati mina kadi bekyuli badubo lɛlɔ kalɔ buboku na bakpali-mi bevele na benwini bebo-mi kudɔ na bada ekpidi bɔbla baya ni, ndubunu bana buvele na liti bana ekpidi lɛkyiɛ-ma na lɛya na kalɔ kammɔ kasɔ kataadia edula.

english_verse: Then on the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent everyone home. They left very happy because of all the good things the Lord had done for David and Solomon, and for his people Israel. The Lord Appears to Solomon Again (
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama kɔbuli maatɛdi limeyi aavlanyɔ-lɛtɛdi lɛlɔ ni, Salomo údie ɔdi biala ulu na ɔ́sɔ únwini úsie nwuna ɔma. Na lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ-ma geen uwi na bakɛ ulu bésela na ala abuni ani na Unwoti ɔ́bla úte Dawid ku Salomo ku nwuna kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ ƒui ɔsu.

english_verse: The Lord's temple and Solomon's palace were now finished. In fact, everything Solomon had planned to do was completed.
translation_verse: Báwɔlɔ Unwoti kakpakɔ ku Salomo ɔga kesii kammɔ bɔtu ɔƒɛni amu. Na geen ni, lɛla biala na Salomo ɔ́lɛ ugyii ka ɔbla ni, lɛ́sa bɔbla na.

english_verse: Some time later, the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream and said: I heard your prayer, and I have chosen this temple as the place where sacrifices will be offered to me.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔdi kama ni, Unwoti údie lɛlɔ ɔ́tina Salomo na kɔna kemmo na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Línu ƒula bɔkpali na lɛ́ƒuna kakpakɔ kamɛni aani kesii kani na bekyuli badubo akpala butaakyula teete-mi.

english_verse: Suppose I hold back the rain or send locusts to eat the crops or make my people suffer with deadly diseases.
translation_verse: “Ɔkana na ubo ute ka lítile kayaa na ɔnantu ɔ́sɔ ulana iye baalɔlɔ bébile edula ammɔ iye ɔlɛ buɛ ɔdi úbo bekyuli bammɔ.

english_verse: I will hear the prayers made in this temple,
translation_verse: Na ala ani ƒui na bɛdubo-mi bɔkpali buvele na kakpakɔ kamɛni kemmo ni, ndubunu na lɛbla lɛsia lɛni

english_verse: because it belongs to me, and this is where I will be worshiped forever. I will never stop watching over it.
translation_verse: ɔsika kakpakɔ kammɔ kadi mina kadi na mɛni na bekyuli badubo-mi butaakpa ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela uwi ƒui. Na lɛɛɛdubo-ka lɛlɔ bɔda bɔnu bɔya kudii.

english_verse: Your father David obeyed me, and now, Solomon, you must do the same. Obey my laws and teachings,
translation_verse: “Salomo, ƒ'ɔti Dawid únu-mi litemi na ɔ́di-ni lɛlɔ. Awɔ lɛnɔ ɔlɛka abla lɛni kani. Bla siaku mina ɔda bubo ku ala ani na mɔɔtina lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and I will keep my solemn promise to him that someone from your family will always be king of Israel.
translation_verse: Na kenye kpakplaa kani na líse-nwu ka nwuna ɔtɔ kemmo na ukyuli ɔdubɔsi ɔdi lɛga na Israel kalɔ uwi biala ni, ndubɔdi-ka lɛlɔ lite-nwu.

english_verse: But if you or any of the people of Israel disobey my laws or start worshiping foreign gods,
translation_verse: “Nsu si awɔ iye Israel kadi bekyuli bammɔ akɔ ɔdi úse kalɔ ɔɔkpá baƒiɔ bani na kadi bamba bekyuli baakpá mmɔ ni,

english_verse: I will pull you out of this land I gave you. I will desert this temple where I said I would be worshiped, so that people everywhere will think it is only a joke and will make fun of it.
translation_verse: ndubo-mii bɔbɔku budie kalɔ kani na líte-mii mɛni kemmo na aani kalɛ na baagyú lɛla lɛdi teedie nina kenyekɔ na lidie kakpakɔ kani na lɛ́su ka bekyuli badubo-mi butaakpa mmɔ atu na lɛda-ka liwi na bekyuli ƒui na kesi kesii beti kenye kammɔ babla aani lɛƒiankula na baataakya-ka lɛlɔ lɛma.

english_verse: This temple is now magnificent. But when these things happen, everyone who walks by it will be shocked and will ask, “Why did the Lord do such a terrible thing to his people and to this temple?”
translation_verse: Kakpakɔ kamɛni kadi kesii kani na káƒɔ kuye geen na bekyuli baabu-ka ɔƒɛni. Nsu si ala ani ɔda na líbo-mii mɛni álɛ ni, ukyuli biala na ɔ́sia mɛni ɔɔví ni, ɔdubo-nwu bɔbla kalɛ kadi na uye ɔnini, ‘Bi ɔsu na Unwoti ɔ́bla lɛla lɛni na libo ɔkplu lɛni?’

english_verse: Solomon did not force the Israelites to do his work. Instead, they were his soldiers, officers, army commanders, and cavalry troops. But he did make slaves of the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who were living in Israel. These were the descendants of those foreigners the Israelites did not destroy, and they remained Israel's slaves.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui ni, Salomo útenye Israel kadi bekyuli lɛlɔ ka babla kabla kamɛni mmomu ɔ́bla-ma nwuna bekpone ku lɛku batine ku bekpone batɔnkune ku bekpone bapɔnkɔ beliene. Nsu úti Hitiƒuɔ ku Amoriƒuɔ ku Perisiƒuɔ ku Hiwiƒuɔ ku Yebusiƒuɔ bani nli Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ únwini nwuna kabla bablane. Na bekyuli bamɛni ndi baƒɔ bani na Israelƒuɔ bátadu bebi ku bawɔ bani nébu bakya kalɔ kammɔ kemmo na bénwini bana kabla bablane.

english_verse: After that, Solomon had his workers rebuild the towns that Hiram had given him. Then Solomon sent Israelites to live in those towns.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Salomo ɔ́ya na nwuna kabla bablane bátásɔku lɛma lɛni na Ɔga Hiram úte-nwu bátu. Na ɔ́ya na Israelƒuɔ bésie bétélie-ni kemmo.

english_verse: Solomon attacked and captured the town of Hamath-Zobah.
translation_verse: Amu na Salomo úsie útékpo ɔma ɔni baalɔ Hamat-Soba na úƒie-nwu ɔ́ƒɔ.

english_verse: He ordered his workers to build the town of Tadmor in the desert and some towns in Hamath where he could keep his supplies.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, anwu ku nwuna kabla bablane bátu Tadmor ɔma ɔni na kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo ku lɛma lɛni na lɛkya Hamat kalɛkɛ kesii kani na ɔɔklibi nwuna ala adi bene buse.

english_verse: He strengthened Upper Beth-Horon and Lower Beth-Horon by adding walls and gates that could be locked.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔku ɔma ɔni baalɔ Bet-Horon ɔni nkya katɔ kakɛ ku kada kakɛ ɔdi ƒui ɔ́tu ku awodu kpakplaa na ɔ́kya ɔban kɔlɛmikɔ kɔni na baabala.

english_verse: He did the same thing to the town of Baalath and to the cities where he kept supplies, chariots, and horses. Solomon ordered his workers to build whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and anywhere else in his kingdom.
translation_verse: Na lɛni kani na ɔ́bla ɔma ɔni ndi Baalat ku lɛma linengudi lɛni kemmo na ɔɔklibi ala buse ku nwuna bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ku bapɔnkɔ bammɔ alati. Salomo ɔ́ya na nwuna kabla bablane bátu lɛla biala na ɔɔwia bákya Yerusalem ku Lebanon ku kesii bamba biala lɛnɔ na ɔɔyɔ́ na nwuna lɛgakadikɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Solomon's wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt, moved from the part of Jerusalem called David's City to her new palace that Solomon had built. The sacred chest had been kept in David's City, which made his palace sacred, and so Solomon's wife could no longer live there.
translation_verse: Amu na Salomo ulekudi ɔni ndi Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ubidi ulekubi ɔ́tɔlɔ Yerusalem kakɛ kani na baalɔ banii Dawidi ɔma unengudi úbo ɔga kesii kawɔdi kani na Salomo ɔ́tu mmɔ. Na nka Dawid ɔma unengudi kemmo mmɔ na Bunyimi Adaka ɔmmɔ use ɔsu mmɔ kadi kesii kani na kese kedee na Salomo ulekudi ulakana na wasɔ welie mmɔ lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Solomon offered sacrifices to the Lord on the altar he had built in front of the temple porch.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Salomo ɔ́kyula akpala úte Unwoti na lɛkpabi lɛni na ɔ́tu lɛlɔ na linye kaduli kemmo mmɔ na kakpakɔ kammɔ anumi.

english_verse: He followed the requirements that Moses had given for sacrifices offered on the Sabbath, on the first day of each month, the Festival of Thin Bread, the Harvest Festival, and the Festival of Shelters.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́bla akpala amɛni ɔ́siaku kalɛ na Mose únweni úse ka babla ute akpala bɔkyula na lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ ku kɔbuli biala limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ku Bodobodo Ɔni Néteƒu Limeyi ku Edula Bɔƒɛ Limeyi bɔdi lɛlɔ ku Kevo Kemmo Bulie Emeyi bɔdi kemmo.

english_verse: Solomon then assigned the priests and the Levites their duties at the temple, and he followed the instructions that his father, the man of God, had given him. Some of the Levites were to lead music and help the priests in their duties, and others were to guard the temple gates
translation_verse: Amu na Salomo úti kabla ɔ́kya bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ na kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo. Na ɔ́bla ɔmɛni ƒui ɔ́siaku lɛla lɛni na ɔti Dawid ɔ́su-nwu lɛlɔ. Na Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ badi ɔlɛka batɔnku bekyuli na lɛnu budie kemmo na bebunku bakpane na bana kabla bɔbla kemmo na bakladi bataagyumana kakpakɔ kammɔ lɛban kɔyakun ƒui

english_verse: Everything Solomon had planned to do was now finished—from the laying of the temple's foundation to its completion.
translation_verse: Na ɔƒaani ni, lɛla biala na Salomo ɔ́lɛ ugyii ka ɔbla lɛ́sa bɔbla ɔƒaamu ɔ́si ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ɔka kalɔ bɔkya útédu nwuna bɔwɔlɔ.

english_verse: Solomon went to Ezion-Geber and Eloth, two Edomite towns on the Red Sea.
translation_verse: Salomo úsie Edomƒuɔ lɛma inyɔ bɔdi kemmo kesii kani baalɔ banii Esion-Geber ku Elot na Ɛpugyie kalɛkɛ.

english_verse: Hiram sent him ships and some of his experienced sailors. They went with Solomon's own sailors to the country of Ophir and brought back more than
translation_verse: Ɔga Hiram úmene-nwu lɛkɔlɔ libendi ku lɛkɔlɔ lɛmmɔ bakane bani ngyi kabla kammɔ lɛlɔ geen. Na ama ku Salomo lɛkɔlɔ bakane ƒui bási bésie kesii kani baalɔ banii Oƒir na bététi sika ugyiedi antabi aƒo eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ (

english_verse: He answered every question, no matter how difficult it was.
translation_verse: Na Salomo lɛnɔ údie ɔdi biala kenye ina dɛ na lɛla lɛmmɔ libo ɔkplu.

english_verse: She said: Solomon, in my own country I had heard about your wisdom and all you've done.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Salomo, ɔ́si mina kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui na línu kalɛ na ebo lɛnunda geen ku ala ani udu na ábla.

english_verse: But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are greater than I was told.
translation_verse: Nsu ńtaƒɔ ńtadi úti úbedu uwi ɔni na ami ɔlati lɛ́nu ɔmɛni ku mina anumi! Na lɛ́nu ala bamba pii ani na etulo ani na línu asa na líbo mɛni. Na geen ni, etulo kalɛ na básu-mi muedi.

english_verse: Your people and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
translation_verse: Kuli kɔdia ƒula bakutine ku kabla bablane ka bakya mɛni na beteenu ƒula lɛnunda etemila ani na aasu.

english_verse: I praise the Lord your God. He is pleased with you and has made you king of Israel. God loves the people of this country and will never desert them, so he has given them a king who will rule fairly and honestly.
translation_verse: “Muumwi Unwoti ƒula Katɔti. Ƒula lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ-nwu kaƒɔ na ɔ́bla-a Israelƒuɔ ɔga. Na Katɔti ɔɔyɔ́ kadi kamɛni bekyuli na uledie-ma atu lɛnɔ kudii, anwuɔsu na úte-ma ɔga ɔni ndubɔdi-ma lɛlɔ na ɔtɛ lɛla biala na ulu siin lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The Queen of Sheba gave Solomon more than four tons of gold, a large amount of jewels, and the best spices anyone had ever seen.
translation_verse: Seeba uleku ɔga ɔmɛni úte Salomo sika ugyiedi bumomo bɔni unu ndubɔbla antabi aƒo liti ku asɛɛ ebi ku kutu akyala abuni ƒui ani na ukyuli ɔ́ɔkana na úti anumi ɔ́nu dii.

english_verse: not counting what the merchants and traders brought him. The kings of Arabia and the leaders of Israel also gave him gold and silver.
translation_verse: na balaka lɛla lɛni mɔɔsí beyedine ku bani mɔɔsíku ala limomo ɔlɔgyu teebeye kudɔ. Lɛni kani na Arabiaƒuɔ ɔga ku Israel aban bagadine lɛnɔ beeboku-nwu sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi.

english_verse: Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the records of Nathan the prophet, Ahijah the prophet from Shiloh, and Iddo the prophet who wrote about Jeroboam son of Nebat.
translation_verse: Na lɛla bamba biala na Salomo ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-mi bákya Kenye Udiene Natan ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo ku Ahiya ɔni na ɔ́si Silo ku Ido ɔni nénweni ala ɔ́siku Yeroboam ɔni nási Nebat.

english_verse: His throne was made of ivory and covered with pure gold.
translation_verse: Na nwuna lɛgaboku ni, atu ɔtunkpɛ na béti bábla-ni na bákwaa-ni ku sika ugyiedi.

english_verse: It had a gold footstool attached to it and armrests on each side. There was a statue of a lion on each side of the throne,
translation_verse: Na libo lɛgba kanyakɔ kani ndanku liboku lɛmmɔ kesii kani na baasia enu na sika ugyiedi na béti bábla-ka. Na bábla gyata kavɔ udu bálɛ lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ ɔƒɛnyi ɔni ku ɔni.

english_verse: and there were two lion statues on each of the six steps leading up to the throne. No other throne in the world was like Solomon's.
translation_verse: Na bagyata kavɔ udu bamba balɛ lɛgba kanyakɔ libili ɛku lɛni néti lɛ́kɔ lísie lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ kudɔ ɔƒɛnyi ɔni ku ɔni. Na bebo leevu-inyɔ. Na lɛgaboku lɛdi lɛsɔ liiibo kayawi kamɛni na lise aani Salomo lɛdi lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: Solomon's cups and dishes in Forest Hall were made of pure gold, because silver was almost worthless in those days.
translation_verse: Salomo lɛɛƒɛɛ ku akyami ani nsi Lɛku Ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo, ɔsika na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, sika ɔƒualadi ɔɔɔdi lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Salomo ubo lɛkɔlɔ libendi pii lɛni muusié ketu lɛlɔ teete-nwu. Na akwa atɛ biala kemmo ni, ɔɔtala na beeti-ni ku Ɔga Hiram lɛkɔlɔ na beesié ntu anumi na beesié teetéti sika ugyiedi ku sika ɔƒualadi ku atunkpɛ ku bagyii ku baasɛ bonwu badi muubimi lɛlɔ si beesié teeboku-nwu.

english_verse: Solomon was the richest and wisest king in the world.
translation_verse: Na sɔsɔ ni, Salomo nádi ɔlakɛne ubendi ɔnundane unengudi ƒui utulo na kayawi.

english_verse: Year after year, other kings came to hear the wisdom God had given him. And they brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa ndi lɛkwa ni, baga bamba beebo teebenu lɛnunda etemila ani na Katɔti ute Salomo na nwuna kudɔ. Na beeboku-nwu etela aani sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ku adala ku ekpola ku kutu akyala ku bapɔnkɔ ku bebuo ala betine.

english_verse: He ruled all the nations from the Euphrates River in the north to the land of Philistia in the south, as far as the border of Egypt.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́di kayawi kemodi kammɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́si Euƒrate Ketu na kalɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ útédu Ƒilistia na kada kakɔ na Egyipteƒuɔ ɔmii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: While Solomon was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as the sycamore trees in the western foothills.
translation_verse: Na Salomo lɛgadi uwi ni, ɔ́ya na sika ɔƒualadi ɔ́bu na Yerusalem aani atabi. Na ɔ́ya na bálɛ sida egyii na émomo geen aani kɔnwingyie egyii ani nábu akya Yuda abi kaƒɔna mmɔ.

english_verse: Solomon's horses were brought in from other countries, including Musri. Solomon Dies (
translation_verse: Na Salomo bapɔnkɔ bammɔ ni, nwuna beyedine néye-ma básiku Egyipte ku kɔlɔ bamba lɛlɔ. Salomo Úkpi

english_verse: he died and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_verse: úbekpi na báva-nwu na Dawid ɔma unengudi kemmo. Na ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ banii Rehoboam únwini ɔga.

english_verse: Rehoboam went to Shechem where everyone was waiting to crown him king.
translation_verse: Rehoboam úsie Sekem kesii kani na Israelƒuɔ ƒui benye bagya-nwu ka bese-nwu lɛga na bebi-nwu gagabwa kammɔ.

english_verse: Three days later, Jeroboam and the others came back.
translation_verse: Rehoboam ku anwu badi bammɔ bénwini bébo emeyi atɛ kama.

english_verse: Jeroboam son of Nebat heard what was happening, and he returned from Egypt, where he had gone to hide from Solomon.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Nabat ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Yeroboam únu lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́, anwuɔsu únwini ɔ́si Egyipte úbo ɔ́si kesii kani na nka úsie útábɛ Salomo.

english_verse: The people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said,
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ adua ani na akya kalɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ bátala na bátálɔ Yeroboam béboku. Amu na bana ƒui báta bésie Rehoboam kudɔ na bátásu-nwu banini,

english_verse: “Your father Solomon forced us to work very hard. But if you make our work easier, we will serve you and do whatever you ask.”
translation_verse: “Ƒ'ɔti Salomo únye-bu lɛlɔ na bútaabla kabla kpakplaa. Nsu si awɔ áya na bula kabla kammɔ kákɔsi ɔkplu bɔyu lɛni ni, bɔdubo lili kalɔ bɔkya bute-ɔ na babla lɛla biala na adubɔsu-bu anii bɔbla bute-ɔ.”

english_verse: Rehoboam replied, “Come back in three days for my answer.” So the people left.
translation_verse: Amu na Rehoboam úde kenye ɔnini, “Binwini bibo na emeyi atɛ kama na ndubudie lɛla lɛni na bíye-mi kenye lite-mii.”

english_verse: Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Rehoboam ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie bakutine benengudi ku batɔnkune badi kudɔ bani nádi benengu béte ɔti uwi ɔni na ɔ́kya na útéye-ma ɔnini, “Bi na ɔlɛka lɛsu bekyuli bamɛni?”

english_verse: They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should be kind and promise to make their work easier.”
translation_verse: Amu na bédie kenye banini, “Si aayɔ́ anii bekyuli bamɛni bábla-a kabla na beteenu-ɔ litemi bɔdi ni, amu taabla lɛƒɔndia na ese-ma kenye ka adubɔya na bana kabla kasɔ kalayu ɔkplu mmomu kadubɔbla buɛɛ.”

english_verse: But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials.
translation_verse: Nsu Rehoboam úni na úteti bana kasusu kani na bákya-nwu. Mmomu ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie bakloƒu bakɔdi kudɔ bani ndi-nwu ligye na ɔƒaani badi nwuna bakutine kudɔ.

english_verse: He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
translation_verse: Ama na útéye ɔnini, “Bi na bɛɛkali ka lɛsu bekyuli bani mɔɔsu-mi mɛni banii mbla na bana kabla kabla-ma kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ?”

english_verse: He made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
translation_verse: Ɔ́ya na bɛ́bla kabla kpakplaa, nsu ami ndubɔya na bɛbla bitulo lɛni. Na si ɔdi ɔ́ƒiɔ ni, kugyiimi na uuti taaní ukyuli ɔmmɔ kɔtu, nsu ndubuti ebola ani na bábla ku abuala ani mbo ɔbi yayaaya bɔni bani maƒiɔ kɔtu!’ ”

english_verse: Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older advisors. He spoke bluntly
translation_verse: Na Rehoboam úni benengu bammɔ bɔlɛ na úteti-mu munu munu mmomu útemi ku ogya geen

english_verse: and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested. He said: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
translation_verse: na ɔ́su-ma kasusu kani na ɔ́ƒɔ ɔ́siku nwuna kasusu bakyane bakɔdi kudɔ ɔnini, “Mina ɔti ɔ́ya na bɛ́bla kabla kpakplaa, nsu ami ndubɔya na bɛbla kani na kebo ɔkplu ketulo kammɔ muedi. Na ɔ́ni bekyuli bani náƒiɔ kɔtu ku kugyiimi, nsu ebola ani na béti abuala ani na ebo yayaaya na ndubuti lɛni bani maƒiɔ kɔtu.”

english_verse: When the people realized that Rehoboam would not listen to them, they shouted: “We don't have to be loyal to David's family. We can do what we want. Come on, people of Israel, let's go home! Rehoboam can rule his own people.” Adoniram was in charge of the work force, and Rehoboam sent him to talk to the people. But they stoned him to death. Then Rehoboam ran to his chariot and hurried back to Jerusalem. Everyone from Israel's northern tribes went home, leaving Rehoboam to rule only the people from Judah. And since that day, the people of Israel have been opposed to David's descendants in Judah. All of this happened just as Ahijah the Lord's prophet from Shiloh had told Jeroboam.
translation_verse: Amu ka bekyuli bammɔ bánu báti ka Rehoboam ɔɔɔdubo-ma litemi bunu ɔsu ni, báva momoomo básu banini, “Bɔdubɔta bunye Dawid ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli litemi lɛlɔ na utalɛka bunu-ma litemi na bɔdi-ni lɛlɔ. Bɔkana na butaabla lɛla lɛni na abu alati bɔɔyɔ́. Bula kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ, bibo na bɛya na buteesie bula ɔma! Na Rehoboam utaadi nwuna bekyuli lɛlɔ.” Amu na Rehoboam ɔ́tala Adoniram ɔni nnye kabla bɔbla kenye ɔnii utátɛmiku bekyuli bammɔ, nsu bekyuli bammɔ bébo-nwu atabi bádu. Mmɔ na Rehoboam úkeli úsie nwuna ɔpɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ kudɔ na útéti-nwu na úkeli ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Yerusalem. Na ɔmmɔ kama Israelƒuɔ adua ani na ási kalɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ ƒui bátɔlɔ bésie bana kalɔ lɛlɔ na bányonu Rehoboam na utaadi bani ndi Yudaƒuɔ kani lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́si limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ adua atɔdi ammɔ áta enye Dawid ku nwuna ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli bani na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: After Rehoboam returned to Jerusalem, he decided to attack Israel and regain control of the whole country. So he called together
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Rehoboam únwini úsie Yerusalem kama ni, ɔ́bla kasusu ka útékpo Israel na ɔsɔ utaadi kalɛkɛ kemodi kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu ɔ́lɔ bekpone mpim eti atɛ ku avlaatɛ ɔ́siku Yuda ku Benyamin adua kemmo úbasala.

english_verse: as well as with shields and spears. He used these fortified cities to keep control of Judah and Benjamin. The Priests and the Levites Support Rehoboam
translation_verse: Lɛni kani na úte-ma atula ku kekpo agyumanala. Na ekpo amɛni na nwuna ɔyikun ɔni na úti ɔda Yuda ku Benyamin adua ammɔ ɔ́sala ɔkya. Bakpane Ku Lewiƒuɔ Benye Rehoboam Kama

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Lord had told Shemaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Nsu na uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́ɔtɛmiku Kenye Udiene Semaia

english_verse: to tell Rehoboam and everyone from Judah and Benjamin,
translation_verse: ɔnii ɔsu Rehoboam ku ukyuli biala na Yuda ku Benyamin adua kemmo ɔnini,

english_verse: “The Lord warns you not to go to war against the people from the northern tribes—they are your relatives. Go home! The Lord is the one who made these things happen.” Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord's message and did not attack Jeroboam and his troops. Rehoboam Fortifies Cities in Judah
translation_verse: “Unwoti uubó-mii ɔda ɔnii bina ɔdi utata kekpo ku adua ani na akya katɔ kakɛ mmɔ ɔdi. Ɔsika bina lɛlɔ bekyuli kani na badi. Binwini biteesie ɔma! Ɔsika Unwoti ɔlati náya na ala amɛni ébo éte lɛni.” Rehoboam ku nwuna bekpone bénu Unwoti litemi na bétekpoku Yeroboam ku nwuna bekpone. Rehoboam Ɔ́tu Bɔgyumana Awodu Kpakplaa Ɔ́mana Yuda Lɛma Linengudi Ƒui

english_verse: Rehoboam ruled from Jerusalem, and he had several cities in Judah turned into fortresses so he could use them to defend his country. These cities included
translation_verse: Yerusalem na Rehoboam úlie útaadi lɛga na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ na ubo lɛma linengudi pii lɛni na úti únwini kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa kesii kani na nwuna bekpone. Na lɛma lɛmmɔ lɛdi ndi

english_verse: Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,
translation_verse: Betlehem ku Etam ku Tekoa,

english_verse: Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,
translation_verse: Gat ku Maresa ku Siƒ ku

english_verse: Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,
translation_verse: Adoraim ku Lakis ku Aseka ku

english_verse: Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron. After he had fortified these cities in the territories of Judah and Benjamin,
translation_verse: Sora ku Aiyalon ku Hebron. Na uwi ɔni na ɔ́tu ɔmana lɛma lɛmɛni ɔ́wɔlɔ na Yuda ku Benyamin kalɛkɛ ni,

english_verse: he assigned an army commander to each of them and stocked them with supplies of food, olive oil, and wine,
translation_verse: ɔ́wia bekpone ɔtɔnkune úte lɛma lɛmmɔ ɔdi biala bekpone na úti adila ku ntɛ ku nnɔ útése-ma kudɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: The priests and Levites from the northern tribes of Israel gave their support to King Rehoboam.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmɛni kemmo ƒui ni, bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bani na bakya adua atɔdi ammɔ kemmo ƒui ni, ama benye Ɔga Rehoboam kama.

english_verse: And since Jeroboam and the kings of Israel that followed him would not allow any Levites to serve as priests, most Levites left their towns and pasturelands in Israel and moved to Jerusalem and other towns in Judah.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ka Yeroboam ku baga bamba bani násia-nwu kama bétenu kalɔ ka Lewini ɔdi ɔbla ɔkpane kabla na Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, Lewiƒuɔ pii bátɔlɔ na báda bana lɛma ku bebuo kɔdikɔ kɔlɔ kammɔ ƒui béwi na bátɔlɔ bésie Yerusalem ku Yuda lɛma bamba lɛnɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Jeroboam chose his own priests to serve at the local shrines in Israel and at the places of worship where he had set up statues of goat-demons and of calves.
translation_verse: Yeroboam ɔlati ɔ́ƒuna nwuna bakpane bani mɔɔkpá na kadi bamba baƒiɔ bani na bése béte lɛlɔ na abi eli mmɔ lɛlɔ na Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ na ekpo ani na ɔ́tu bese ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ bebi ayu ekpidi baƒiɔ ɔ́lɛ mmɔ.

english_verse: But some of the people from Israel wanted to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done. So they followed the priests and Levites to Jerusalem, where they could offer sacrifices to the Lord.
translation_verse: Nsu Israelƒuɔ badi baayɔ́ ka bataakpa Unwoti Katɔti ɔni na bana bati kuuku bákpa mmɔ, anwuɔsu bekyuli bamɛni básiaku Lewiƒuɔ ku bakpane bammɔ bátɔlɔ bésie Yerusalem kesii kani na badubɔkana na babla akpala bete Unwoti.

english_verse: For the next three years, they lived in Judah and were loyal to Rehoboam and his kingdom, just as they had been loyal to David and Solomon. Rehoboam's Family
translation_verse: Na akwa atɛ kemmo ƒui ni, na bákya Ɔga Rehoboam kalɔ na baadi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ na nwuna lɛgakadikɔ kemmo aani kalɛ na béteenu Dawid ku Salomo litemi na bátaadi-ni lɛlɔ. Rehoboam Údie Kaba

english_verse: Rehoboam and Mahalath had three sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
translation_verse: Rehoboam ku Mahalat báwɔ bebi bananabi ɛtɛ na bana anyi ndi Yeus ku Semaria ku Saham.

english_verse: Then Rehoboam married Maacah the daughter of Absalom. Their sons were Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
translation_verse: Rehoboam úti uleku bamba ɔni baalɔ banii Maaka ɔni ndi Absalom ubidi ulekubi. Na bebi bananabi bani na báwɔ ndi Abiya ku Atai ku Sisa ku Selomit.

english_verse: so he chose their oldest son Abijah to be the next king.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu anwu ku-nwu ubidi ɔnanabi udeedi ɔni baalɔ Abiya na ɔ́ɔƒuna úse ka ɔdi lɛga si uwi ɔni na anwu ɔsɔ uuubo.

english_verse: Rehoboam was wise enough to put one of his sons in charge of each fortified city in his kingdom. He gave them all the supplies they needed and found wives for every one of them.
translation_verse: Na Rehoboam ɔ́da anu geen ɔsu ni, nwuna bebi bananabi akɔ unwi unwi na úti únyene lɛma lɛni na bátu bése kalɔ kammɔ bɔgyumana kenye na nwuna lɛgakadikɔ. Na ɔ́wia ala ani ƒui na baawia úte ɔdi biala na ɔ́wia beleku lɛnɔ úte bana akɔ ɔdi biala na uti.

english_verse: but he still did wrong and refused to obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔ́bla likyulikpi, ka úni ɔnii ulasiaku Unwoti ulu lɛlɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: So in the fifth year of Rehoboam's rule, the Lord punished them for their unfaithfulness and allowed King Shishak of Egypt to invade Judah.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na Rehoboam lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa lɛlɔndi kemmo ni, Unwoti ɔ́ni-ma kɔtu na ɔ́ya na Egyipteƒuɔ Ɔga Sisak úbekpo Yuda kalɔ kammɔ ƒui na kalɛ na basɔ baaasiaku-nwu siin mmomu bálɛ-nwu kama ɔsu.

english_verse: He captured every one of the fortified cities in Judah and then marched to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na bébeƒie bekyuli bani ƒui na bakya Yuda lɛma kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa kɔmmɔ kemmo ƒui asa na bábwɛ bétéduo Yerusalem.

english_verse: Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah had gone to Jerusalem to escape Shishak's invasion. And while they were there, Shemaiah the prophet told them, “The Lord says that because you have disobeyed him, he has now abandoned you. The Lord will not help you against Shishak!”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Rehoboam ku Yudaƒuɔ benengu bammɔ békeli bésie Yerusalem batábɛ Sisak kekpo kammɔ. Mmɔ na Kenye Udiene Semaia ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Unwoti ɔnii ka bɛ́bla atuɔkplu na bítenu-nwu litemi ɔsu ni, anwu lɛnɔ úni-mii na údie-mii atu. Na Unwoti ɔɔɔdubo-mii bubunku na Sisak kekpo kani na ɔ́ta-mii lɛlɔ mɛni kemmo!”

english_verse: Rehoboam and the leaders were sorry for what they had done and admitted, “The Lord is right. We have deserted him.”
translation_verse: Lɛla lɛni na Rehoboam ku batɔnkune bamɛni bábla líduo-ma na básu banini, “Unwoti ɔdi ɔ́tɛ. Abu nálɛ-nwu kama sɔsɔ.”

english_verse: When the Lord heard this, he told Shemaiah: The people of Judah are truly sorry for their sins, and so I won't let Shishak completely destroy them. But because I am still angry,
translation_verse: Amu ka Unwoti únu lɛni ni, ɔ́su Semaia ɔnini, “Lɛla lɛni na Yuda kadi bekyuli bábla ni, ekpidi ammɔ éduo-ma sɔsɔ. Anwuɔsu lɛɛɛdubo bɔya na Sisak ku nwuna bekpone badi-ma lɛlɔ na bayila-ma udu ƒui kede kede. Nsu kɔnyi kɔmmɔ kútayɔ-mi tɔ ɔsu ni,

english_verse: he will conquer and rule them. Then my people will know what it's like to serve a foreign king instead of serving me.
translation_verse: ɔdubo-ma lɛlɔ bɔdi na kekpo kamɛni kemmo na bakya-nwu kalɔ na utaadi-ma lɛlɔ. “Na mina bekyuli bada anu na ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na kavumana kani nkya ka bataabla baƒɔ ɔga ɔdi kabla ku ɔni na bataabla-mi kabla ntɛ.”

english_verse: Shishak attacked Jerusalem and took all the valuable things from the temple and from the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
translation_verse: Sisak úsie útékpo Yerusalem sɔsɔ na úƒie bana ala ani náƒɔ-ma kuye na kakpakɔ ku ɔga kesii ubunku Salomo sika ugyiedi abuala kekpo agyumanala ƒui ɔ́ƒɔ ɔ́tɔlɔku.

english_verse: Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe.
translation_verse: Amu na Rehoboam ɔ́ya na bábla abuala egyiedi agyumanala bése sika ugyiedi adi ammɔ kenye na úbo bagyumanane bani nnye lɛma linengudi lɛmmɔ ɔban kenye ka bada-mi edu kaduɛ.

english_verse: Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he had finished worshiping.
translation_verse: Na uwi ndi na Rehoboam úsie Unwoti kakpakɔ mmɔ ni, bagyumanane bammɔ beeti abuala egyiedi agyumanala ammɔ teesienku kakpakɔ mmɔ na basɔku-nwu beboku kesii kani na beli baagyumana mmɔ uwi biala na Rehoboam ɔ́wɔlɔ nwuna lɛkpa.

english_verse: Rehoboam turned back to the Lord, and so the Lord did not let Judah be completely destroyed, and Judah was prosperous again. Rehoboam's Rule in Judah (
translation_verse: Rehoboam ɔ́sɔ únwini anumi úboku Unwoti lɛlɔ, anwuɔsu Unwoti útaya na bayila Yuda udu ƒui kede kede, anwuɔsu ala ásɔ ádianku-nwu.

english_verse: Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king, including a history of his family, is written in the records of the two prophets, Shemaiah and Iddo. During Rehoboam's rule, he and King Jeroboam of Israel were constantly at war.
translation_verse: Na ala ani ƒui na Rehoboam ɔ́bla ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli kɔtɛ ƒui ni, bénweni ala ammɔ bákya kenye bediene inyɔ badi lɛku kemmo bani ndi Semaia ku Ido. Na Ɔga Rehoboam lɛga bɔdi kemmo ni, anwu ku Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Yeroboam béteekpo bukpo bukpo.

english_verse: When Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Abijah became king.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Rehoboam úbekpi ni, báva-nwu na nwuna bati kuuku kudɔ na Yerusalem na ubidi ɔnanabi Abiya úbenwini ɔga.

english_verse: Abijah became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel,
translation_verse: Ka Yeroboam ɔɔdi lɛga na Israel kalɛ lɛlɔ lɛkwa leevu-maanedi kemmo ni, Abiya lɛnɔ úbenwini ɔga na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and the troops let out a battle cry. Then with Abijah leading them into battle, God defeated Jeroboam and Israel's army.
translation_verse: na bekpone bammɔ lɛnɔ bédie kekpo lɛdi, na Abiya ɔ́tɔnku-ma na Katɔti úbunku-ma, na bádi Yeroboam ku nwuna bekpone lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Now you and your powerful army think you can stand up to the kingdom that the Lord has given to David's descendants. The only gods you have are those gold statues of calves that Jeroboam made for you.
translation_verse: “Na mɔɔnu ka awɔ ku ƒula bekpone bayikune bani na aanu ka ebo mɛni bɛɛkali ka bɛdubɔkana na binye bɛsiaku lɛgakadikɔ kani na Unwoti úti úte Dawid ku nwuna ɔtɔ kemmo bawɔ. Lɛla lɛni kani na ebo ndi Yeroboam sika ugyiedi baƒiɔ bani na bávɔ béte-ɔ na ɔmantɛ bakɔ bebi udu kenye.

english_verse: and he ruled from Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel from Gibeah. Some time later, Abijah and King Jeroboam of Israel went to war against each other.
translation_verse: Na úlie Yerusalem akwa atɛ útaadi lɛga. Na uni baalɔ banii Mikaia ɔni ndi Uriel ɔni nási Gibea ubidi ulekubi. Amu na uwi ɔdi kama ni, Abiya ku Yeroboam báta lɛlɔ kekpo.

english_verse: Abijah went to the top of Mount Zemaraim in the hills of Ephraim and shouted: Listen, Jeroboam and all you Israelites!
translation_verse: Abiya ɔ́kɔ úsie Semaraim Kɔbi lili na Eƒraim abi kalɔ lɛlɔ na ɔ́va ɔ́su ɔnini, “Yeroboam ku amii Israel kadi bekyuli, bise atu na binu!

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has made a solemn promise that every king of Israel will be from David's family.
translation_verse: Unwoti Israel Katɔti úse kenye kpakplaa úse ka Israel ɔga biala ndubulie liboku lɛlɔ ni, Dawid ɔtɔ kemmo na ɔdubɔsi.

english_verse: But Jeroboam, you were King Solomon's official, and you rebelled.
translation_verse: Nsu awɔ Yeroboam ni, Ɔga Salomo ɔkutine kani na adi asa na áta énye-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then right after Rehoboam became king, you and your bunch of worthless followers challenged Rehoboam, who was too young to know how to stop you.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ka Salomo ubidi Rehoboam únwini ɔga ni, awɔ ku ƒula bakantankpine bɛ́ta bínye na bíkpoku okloƒu ɔmɛni ɔni na útabi tɔ lɛlɔ na ɔti kalɛ na unye ɔsiaku-mii na utile-mii kuƒi kɔmɛni ɔsu.

english_verse: You don't even have descendants of Aaron on your side, because you forced out the Lord's priests and Levites. In their place, you appoint ordinary people to be priests, just as the foreign nations do. In fact, anyone who brings a bull and seven rams to the altar can become a priest of your so-called gods.
translation_verse: Na Aron bawɔ muedi beeenye-ɔ kama, ɔsika énye-ma lɛlɔ na ábɔku Unwoti bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ ƒui álɛku kalɛ kammɔ kemmo. Na átáƒuna bekyuli keeke ka bataabla bakpane kabla bakpane kabla kammɔ aani kalɛ na kadi bamba bekyuli baabla. Na geen ni, ukyuli biala ɔni nákɛ ɔmantɛ akɔ ku baƒonu bagyani maatɛ béboku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ ɔkana na unwini ƒula ala ani na aanu aani baƒiɔ bayikune badi ɔkpane.

english_verse: But we have not turned our backs on the Lord God! Aaron's own descendants serve as our priests, and the Levites are their assistants.
translation_verse: “Nsu abu ni, bútenwini kama bútakya bula Unwoti Katɔti! Aron bawɔ bammɔ kani mmu nnye baabla ɔkpane kabla kammɔ na abu bula akɔ na Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ndi bana bebunkune.

english_verse: Two times every day they offer sacrifices and burn incense to the Lord. They set out the sacred loaves of bread on a table that has been purified, and they light the lamps in the gold lampstand every day at sunset. We follow the commands of the Lord our God—you have rejected him!
translation_verse: Na limeyi biala ni, kunyɔ na baakyula akpala ku oloƒui teete Unwoti. Na ala kasiakɔ kani na bábla-ka na kese kedee lɛlɔ na beeti bodobodo ɔni nse kedee mmɔ taasia na batu asogya ɔni nsia sika ugyiedi ligyii lɛlɔ mmɔ bese limeyi biala useyi uwi si ɔƒɛ ɔ́nu. Na bɔsiaku Unwoti bula Katɔti ɔda bubo, nsu amii bíni-nwu!

english_verse: That's why God is on our side and will lead us into battle when the priests sound the signal on the trumpets. It's no use, Israelites. You might as well give up. There's no way you can defeat the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na Katɔti unye-bu kama na ɔdubo-bu bɔtɔnku na kekpo kamɛni kemmo na bɔdubɔta bukpo-mii uwi ɔni na bula bakpane bávwi bana ese ammɔ na béte-bu kati. Israelƒuɔ, kɔsia kɔdi kuuubo-nwu kemmo kuuute-mii, ɔsika bɛdubo lili bute, ɔsika ulu biala uuubo na bɛdubɔkana Unwoti Katɔti ɔni na bina bati kuuku bátaakpa lɛlɔ bɔdi.”

english_verse: But while Abijah was talking, Jeroboam had sent some of his troops to attack Judah's army from behind, while the rest attacked from the front.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na Abiya unye ɔɔtɛmi mɛni ni, Yeroboam ɔ́ɔtala batu badi ka bátásia Abiya kama kakɛ na beyu-nwu batu bekpoku-nwu na bana bakladi bekpo-nwu basiku anumi mɛni.

english_verse: Judah's army won because they had trusted the Lord God of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Na Yudaƒuɔ bekpone bádi lɛlɔ, ɔsika béti bana anu ƒui básia bana bati kuuku Unwoti Katɔti lɛlɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: Abijah kept up his attack on Jeroboam's army and captured the Israelite towns of Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, as well as the villages around them.
translation_verse: Amu na Abiya ɔ́bi ɔsiaku-ma Yeroboam bekpone laa na útéƒie Israelƒuɔ lɛma lɛdi ɔ́ƒɔ lɛni ndi Betel ku Yesana ku Eƒron ku lɛma lɛni náka lɛ́mana ekutɛ mmɔ.

english_verse: Jeroboam never regained his power during the rest of Abijah's rule. The Lord punished Jeroboam, and he died, but Abijah became more powerful.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni kemmo na Abiya úti ɔ́di lɛga ƒui ni, Yeroboam ɔ́sɔ útakana na ɔkɛ ɔyikun ɔdi kudii. Ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́ni Yeroboam kɔtu na úbekpi, nsu Abiya anwu ni, nwuna ɔyikun ɔ́kɔ katɔ úbu.

english_verse: Everything Abijah said and did while he was king is written in the records of Iddo the prophet.
translation_verse: Na ala ani ƒui na Ɔga Abiya ɔ́su na ɔ́bla lɛnɔ ni, bénweni-nya bákya Kenye Udiene Ido ɔku kemmo bése.

english_verse: Asa obeyed the Lord his God and did right.
translation_verse: Asa ɔ́di Unwoti nwuna Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ na útaabla ala ulu lɛlɔ siin.

english_verse: He destroyed the local shrines and the altars to foreign gods. He smashed the stone images of gods and cut down the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah.
translation_verse: Úbo baƒiɔ ƒui ɔ́bwɛ ku bana abi ƒui. Na úkulo baƒiɔ ligyii lɛni na bálɛ béte Asera baƒiɔ bɔkpa mmɔ bene ƒui. Na ala ani na bávɔ ku atabi ani bánwi bábla báƒiɔ mmɔ ƒui ɔ́bwɛ-nya úwi kalɔ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: Then he told everyone in Judah to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done, and to obey his laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́su ukyuli biala na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔnii utaakpa Unwoti Katɔti kalɛ kani na bana bati kuuku bábla. Na ɔdi biala utaadi Unwoti ɔmmɔ ɔda bubo ku nwuna ala ani na ɔ́tina mmɔ lɛlɔ kaduɛ.

english_verse: He destroyed every local shrine and incense altar in Judah.
translation_verse: Baƒiɔ lɛtɔ lɛni ƒui na bátu ku oloƒui kakyulakɔ abi ƒui ɔ́bwɛ lɛla lɛdi biala na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: The Lord blessed Judah with peace while Asa was king, and so during that time, Asa fortified many of the towns.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti úte Yuda kusɛ kusɛ na atu bɔyɔ búbo uwi ɔni ƒui na Asa ɔɔdi lɛga mmɔ. Na ɔ́ya na bátu bámana lɛma pii na línwini kagyumanakɔ kpakplaa.

english_verse: He said to the people, “Let's build walls and defense towers for these towns, and put in gates that can be locked with bars. This land still belongs to us, because we have obeyed the Lord our God. He has given us peace from all our enemies.” The people did everything Asa had suggested.
translation_verse: Ɔ́lɔ bekyuli bammɔ ɔ́sala na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛya na bɔtu awodu bɔmana lɛma lɛmmɔ na bɔtu kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa lɛnɔ na bɔbla lɛban lɛni na buti abuala kpakplaa butaabala-ni kenye. Ɔsika kalɔ kamɛni kamu kadi abu kadi, ɔsika bɔɔdi bula Unwoti Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ. Ɔ́ya na atu áyɔ-bu ásiku bula bekisine kudɔ.” Na bekyuli bammɔ lɛnɔ bénu lɛla lɛni na Ɔga Asa ɔ́su-ma na bábla básia lɛɛni.

english_verse: Asa met him there, and the two armies prepared for battle in Zephathah Valley.
translation_verse: Asa úsie útásiaku-nwu na mmɔ na bana akpa anyɔ ƒui báklibi lɛlɔ béte kekpo na kɔwɛ kɔni na baalɔ banii Saƒata kemmo.

english_verse: Asa prayed: Lord God, only you can help a powerless army defeat a stronger one. So we depend on you to help us. We will fight against this powerful army to honor your name, and we know that you won't be defeated. You are the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Amu na Asa ɔ́kpali úvele ɔnini, “Unwoti Katɔti awɔ kani ndubɔkana na ebunku bekpone bani neeebo ɔyikun na badi bani na bebo ɔyikun lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu ƒula lɛlɔ na bula anu asia ka ebunku-bu. Na bɔdubo bekpone bani mbo ɔyikun geen mɛni bukpoku buti bute ƒula lɛnyi ɔbu. Na bɔgyi ka ulakana na wadi-ɔ lɛlɔ, ɔsika awɔ ndi Unwoti bula Katɔti.”

english_verse: The Lord helped Asa and his army defeat the Ethiopians. The enemy soldiers ran away,
translation_verse: Unwoti úbunku Asa ku nwuna bekpone na bádi Kus bekpone bamɛni lɛlɔ. Na bana bekisine bekpone bamɛni békeli bátɔlɔ.

english_verse: but Asa and his troops chased them as far as Gerar. It was a total defeat—the Ethiopians could not even fight back! The soldiers from Judah took everything that had belonged to the Ethiopians.
translation_verse: Nsu Asa ku nwuna bekpone bábɔku-ma laa útédu kesii kani baalɔ banii Gerar. Na bususu geen na bésusu-ma ɔni na Kusƒuɔ básɔ bátakana na benwini benye basiaku-ma! Amu na Yudaƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ béti lɛla biala na lɛdi Kusƒuɔ bamɛni lɛdi bénwini bana ɔdi.

english_verse: The people who lived in the villages around Gerar learned what had happened and were afraid of the Lord. So Judah's army easily defeated them and carried off everything of value that they wanted from these towns.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani nkya Gerar ekutɛ mmɔ bénu lɛla lɛni nálɛ na béti bɔyia geen béte Unwoti. Anwuɔsu úse ɔ́bla Yudaƒuɔ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ geen ka badi bana bekisine bammɔ lɛlɔ na béti bana ala ani ƒui náƒɔ-na kuye bálɛku bana lɛma kemmo bátɔlɔku.

english_verse: They also attacked the camps where the shepherds lived and took a lot of sheep, goats, and camels. Then they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na akpaklɔ ani na bana bebuo lɛlɔ banune bábla na baanu bebuo lɛlɔ ni, bétékpoku-ma na béti bana bese ku baƒonu pii bátɔlɔku. Na bénwini bésie Yerusalem.

english_verse: At once, Azariah went to Asa and said: Listen to me, King Asa and you people of Judah and Benjamin. The Lord will be with you and help you, as long as you obey and worship him. But if you disobey him, he will desert you.
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani na Asaria ɔ́ta kɔnakunwi úsie Asa kudɔ na útásu-nwu ɔnini, “Awɔ Ɔga Asa ku Yuda ku Benyamin kadi bekyuli, binu! Uwi biala na bɛɛsia Unwoti ɔda bubo anu na bɛɛdi-mu lɛlɔ na bɛɛkpá-nwu ni, ɔdubulieku-mii na ubunku-mii na uledie-mii atu na uni-mii kudii.

english_verse: For a long time, the people of Israel did not worship the true God or listen to priests who could teach them about God. They refused to obey God's Law.
translation_verse: “Ɔsika uwi gyɔlɔɔ ɔdi mɛni ni, Israelƒuɔ béni na basɔ balakpa Katɔti geen ɔmmɔ na iye benu bakpane bani na nka badubɔkana na batina-ma ala basiku Katɔti ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na béni na baladi Unwoti ɔda bubo lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But whenever trouble came, Israel turned back to the Lord their God and worshiped him.
translation_verse: Nsu uwi biala na ɔgbankpi ɔdi anwu úbo ni, beenwíni teebo Unwoti Katɔti kudɔ ka bakpa-nwu.

english_verse: There was so much confusion in those days that it wasn't safe to go anywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Ala ƒui éƒu ákya Israel na emeyi ammɔ kemmo ɔni na ɔdi ɔgbankpi ute ukyuli biala ka usie mmɔ kesii kadi.

english_verse: Nations were destroying each other, and cities were wiping out other cities, because God was causing trouble and unrest everywhere.
translation_verse: Kɔlɔ kuukpóku lɛlɔ na lɛma na bekyuli baabwɛ lɛlɔ lɛma linengudi taayila-nu udu. Ɔsika Katɔti ɔ́ya na lɛbibo bɔnwuna takɛ bɔ́ƒɔ kesi kesii.

english_verse: As soon as Asa heard what Azariah the prophet said, he gave orders for all the idols in Judah and Benjamin to be destroyed, including those in the towns he had captured in the territory of Ephraim. He also repaired the Lord's altar that was in front of the temple porch.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni kani na Ɔga Asa únu kenye udiene Asaria kenye kamɛni ni, mmɔ kani na úbo ɔda ɔnii bebo baƒiɔ biala babwɛ na Yuda ku Benyamin kalɔ kemmo mmɔ na bayila-ma udu. Na babwɛ bani ƒui na bakya lɛma lɛni na úkpo úƒie ɔ́ƒɔ na Eƒraim kalɛkɛ kemmo mmɔ lɛnɔ ƒui. Na ɔ́sɔku lɛkpabi lɛni nnye kakpakɔ lɛgbanya anumi mmɔ lɛnɔ ɔ́klibi.

english_verse: Asa called together the people from Judah and Benjamin, as well as the people from the territories of Ephraim, West Manasseh, and Simeon who were living in Judah. Many of these people were now loyal to Asa, because they had seen that the Lord was with him.
translation_verse: Asa ɔ́ya na bálɔ Yuda ku Benyamin kalɔ bekyuli ƒui bábasala ku bekyuli bani na bakya Eƒraim kalɛkɛ kemmo mmɔ ƒui. Na bálɔ Manase ku Simeon kɔdua bekyuli bani nkya ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ na Yuda kalɔ kemmo. Ɔsika bekyuli bamɛni ketulodikɔ benye Ɔga Asa kama na baadi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ, ɔsika bánu báti ka Unwoti ɔsiaku-nwu geen.

english_verse: In the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's rule, they all met in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amu na Asa lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa leevu-lɛlɔndi kemmo ni, bana ƒui bása na Yerusalem.

english_verse: They made a solemn promise to faithfully worship the Lord God their ancestors had worshiped,
translation_verse: Na bése kenye kpakplaa ka badubɔsiaku Unwoti Katɔti kama siin na basɔ balálɛ-nwu kama mmomu badubo butaakpa anwu ɔni nabana bati kuuku bákpa-nwu lɛti pɛ.

english_verse: and to put to death anyone who refused to obey him.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala na úni ɔnii ulénu Unwoti Katɔti litemi na wadi-ni lɛlɔ ni, badubɔdu-nwu.

english_verse: The crowd solemnly agreed to keep their promise to the Lord, then they celebrated by shouting and blowing trumpets and horns.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala úse kenye kpakplaa ka badubɔdi linyese lɛmɛni lɛlɔ bete Unwoti. Na bádi limeyi lɛmmɔ ku ebiti kɔvanu kɔkpɛɛ.

english_verse: Everyone was happy because they had made this solemn promise, and in return, the Lord blessed them with peace from all their enemies.
translation_verse: Lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ ukyuli biala na kenye kpakplaa kani na bése mɛni ɔsu na ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu Unwoti lɛnɔ úte-ma kusɛ kusɛ ɔnii keyi kayɔku-ma na bakɛ bɔnwuna ɔsiku bana bekisine kudɔ.

english_verse: Asa's grandmother Maacah had made a disgusting idol of the goddess Asherah, so he cut it down, crushed it, and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
translation_verse: Asa unieku ɔni baalɔ Maaka ɔ́tu baƒiɔ bonwu badi úte uleku Asera kɔwɔ baƒiɔ, anwuɔsu Asa ɔ́bwɛ-ma úwi kalɔ na ɔ́la bana lɛla biala útákyula na Kidron Kɔwɛ kemmo. Na ɔ́ya na bátu Maaka ɔmɛni beleku lɛga lɛni na ɔɔdi.

english_verse: As long as Asa lived, he was faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines in Israel.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni ƒui na Asa úlie ni, útaadi Unwoti litemi lɛlɔ kaduɛ ina ka ɔɔɔdi baƒiɔ bani ƒui na nkya Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ na ɔ́bwɛ.

english_verse: He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to God.
translation_verse: Na sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ala ani ƒui na bédie bése Unwoti ni, úti-nya útése kakpakɔ ɔtɔ kemmo.

english_verse: There was peace in Judah until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's rule.
translation_verse: Keyi buɛɛ kákya Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ na akwa avlaatɛ ani kemmo na Asa ɔ́di lɛga mmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. Then he sent it to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: Ka Asa únu ɔmɛni ni, úti sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ɔ́siku nwuna lɛgakadikɔ ku Unwoti kakpakɔ na úti úmene Aram Ɔga Benhadad na Damasko ɔnii batásu-nwu kenye kamɛni banini,

english_verse: “I think we should sign a peace treaty, just as our fathers did. This silver and gold is a present for you. Would you please break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel and force him to leave my country?”
translation_verse: “Mɔɔyɔ ka abu ku-ɔ bɔbla unwi aani kalɛ na ƒ'ɔti ku mina ɔti bábla unwi dii. Nu, líti sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ɔmɛni muumene-ɔ, na ekulo unwi bɔbla bɔni nkya awɔ ku Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Basa ntɛ, na ɔda nwuna bekpone udie mina ɔmii lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and all the towns in Naphtali where supplies were kept.
translation_verse: Benhadad ɔ́bla lɛla lɛni na Asa ɔ́su-nwu na úti Siriaƒuɔ bekpone úmene Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ na bétékpo Iyon ku Dan ku Abel-Maim ku Neƒtali lɛma lɛni kemmo na baaklibi ala buse ƒui na béƒie-ni báƒɔ.

english_verse: When Baasha heard about it, he stopped his work on the town of Ramah.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Ɔga Basa únu lɛla lɛni nálɛ ni, ɔ́da Rama bɔtu ɔ́ya na údie kabla kammɔ atu.

english_verse: Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to fortify Ramah. Then he fortified the towns of Geba and Mizpah with these same stones and wood. Hanani the Prophet Condemns Asa
translation_verse: Amu na Asa údie lɛdi úte ukyuli biala na ɔkya Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔnii beti atabi ku ligyii lɛni na Baasa ɔ́ya na béti bébewi Rama mmɔ ka batu bamana-nwu na ɔbla kagyumanakɔ kpakplaa mmɔ batɔlɔku mmɔ. Na ɔ́ya na béti atula ammɔ kani bátu bámana Geba ku Mispa. Kenye Udiene Hanani Ɔ́du Ɔga Asa Kɔtɔ

english_verse: Soon after that happened, Hanani the prophet went to Asa and said: You depended on the king of Syria instead of depending on the Lord your God. And so, you will never defeat the Syrian army.
translation_verse: Na ala ammɔ bɔlɛ bɔwɔlɔ kama uwi klukwii ɔdi kama ni, Kenye Udiene Hanani úsie Asa kudɔ na útásu-nwu ɔnini, “Siriaƒuɔ ɔga lɛlɔ na éti ƒula anu ásia na ɔni na eti ƒula anu asia Unwoti ƒula Katɔti lɛlɔ? Ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, aaadubo bɔkana na adi Siriaƒuɔ bekpone lɛlɔ kudii.

english_verse: Remember how powerful the Ethiopian and Libyan army was, with all their chariots and cavalry troops! You trusted the Lord to help you then, and you defeated them.
translation_verse: Nyimo Kus ku Libia bekpone kalɛ na bebo ɔkplu geen ku bana bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ku bekpone bapɔnkɔ beliene bammɔ! Nsu ka éti ƒula anu ásia Unwoti lɛlɔ ka ubunku-ɔ na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ɔsu ni, ákana-ma lɛlɔ bɔdi.

english_verse: The Lord is constantly watching everyone, and he gives strength to those who faithfully obey him. But you have done a foolish thing, and your kingdom will never be at peace again.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔɔsia ukyuli biala anu uwi biala na uuti nwuna ɔyikun teete bani na béti bana anu básia-nwu lɛlɔ na basiaku-nwu kama siin uwi biala. Nsu kɔdɔlɔ lɛla na awɔ ábla mɛni. Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu keyi buɛɛ kasɔ kaaadubo ƒula lɛgakadikɔ kammɔ bɔkya uwi ɔdi lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: When Asa heard this, he was so angry that he put Hanani in prison. Asa was also cruel to some of his people. Asa Dies (
translation_verse: Ka Asa únu lɛla lɛmɛni ni, úti kɔnyi geen na ɔ́ya na bákya Hanani aban ɔtɔ. Na lɛni kani na ɔ́bla anwu ɔlati nwuna bekyuli kalala. Asa Úkpi

english_verse: Everything Asa did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Lɛla biala na Ɔga Asa ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-ni bákya Yudaƒuɔ ku Israelƒuɔ baga ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: In the thirty-ninth year of his rule, he got a very bad foot disease, but he relied on doctors and refused to ask the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Na nwuna lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa avlaatɛ-yaalenwidi kemmo ni, Asa úbakɛ ɔgba ɔdi na ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ ɔ́yu-nwu ɔkplu geen. Nsu nwuna anu ƒui ásia alakpi bablane lɛlɔ kani na ɔɔɔdi Unwoti ka ubunku-nwu.

english_verse: He died two years later.
translation_verse: Na akwa anyɔ kama ni, úbekpi.

english_verse: Earlier, Asa had his own tomb cut out of a rock hill in Jerusalem. So he was buried there, and the tomb was filled with spices and sweet-smelling oils. Then the people built a bonfire in his honor.
translation_verse: Amu na asa na uwi ɔmɛni ubo lɛni ni, Ɔga Asa ɔ́ya na béku nwuna kaƒiɔtɔ bése na ɔdi atabi ubu ɔni na bédie na Yerusalem atakpɛ kɔbi kɔdi lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu mmɔ na báva-nwu. Na béti kesudi ku ugyulo nnɔmii ƒɛƒɛɛ bɔdi béwi kɔƒiɔtɔ kammɔ kemmo ƒui tɛɛ. Na bákyula likpose ekyweni livongu bonwu lɛdi béte-nwu na mmɔ béti bákɔliku-nwu lɛnyi katɔ.

english_verse: He assigned troops to the fortified cities in Judah, as well as to other towns in Judah and to those towns in Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
translation_verse: Na úti bekpone úmene Yudaƒuɔ lɛma linengudi lɛni ndi bana kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa mmɔ kemmo ku lɛma bamba kemmo lɛnɔ úbunku lɛma lɛni nkya Eƒraim kalɛkɛ kani na ɔti Asa úkpo ɔƒɔ kemmo lɛnɔ.

english_verse: When Jehoshaphat's father had first become king of Judah, he was faithful to the Lord and refused to worship the god Baal as the kings of Israel did. Jehoshaphat followed his father's example and obeyed and worshiped the Lord. And so the Lord blessed Jehoshaphat
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Yehosaƒat ɔti úse kalɔ ku lɛga bɔdi na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, útaadi Unwoti litemi lɛlɔ kaduɛ na úni na útakpa Baal baƒiɔ aani kalɛ na baga bani nágyu bátɔ-nwu bábla kalɛ. Na Yehosaƒat lɛnɔ úse kalɔ ɔsiku ɔti ɔbladu kama. Na útaabu Unwoti geen na ɔɔkpá-nwu lɛnɔ. Anwuɔsu úte-nwu kusɛ kusɛ

english_verse: and helped him keep firm control of his kingdom. The people of Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, but even after he became very rich and respected,
translation_verse: na úbunku-nwu na ɔ́ya na ɔɔkana na ɔɔdi nwuna lɛgakadikɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ kaduɛ ku ɔyikun. Na Yuda kadi bekyuli bammɔ beeboku-nwu etela ɔni náya na úbenwini ɔlakɛne geen na beete-nwu ɔbu.

english_verse: he remained completely faithful to the Lord. He destroyed all the local shrines in Judah, including the places where the goddess Asherah was worshiped.
translation_verse: Ɔ́siaku Unwoti kama siin na ulu biala lɛlɔ na ɔ́sɔ útalɛ-nwu kama. Na kadi bamba baƒiɔ bani ƒui na bávɔ béte lɛlɔ na mmɔ ni, ɔ́ya na bábwɛ bana ƒui na Yuda mmɔ ku kesii kani na baakpá Asera baƒiɔ lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Their assistants were the following nine Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah. Two priests, Elishama and Jehoram, also went along.
translation_verse: Na bebo Lewiƒuɔ bebunkune yaalenwi badi bani ndi Semaia ku Netania ku Sebadia ku Asahel ku Semiramot ku Yehonatan ku Adonia ku Tobia ku Tob-Adonia. Na Katɔti bakpane inyɔ badi lɛnɔ basiaku-ma bani na baalɔ banii Elisama ku Yehoram.

english_verse: They carried with them a copy of the Lord's Law wherever they went and taught the people from it.
translation_verse: Na ɔni na bakɛ ulu ƒui ni, na bada Unwoti ɔda bubo ɔku ɔmmɔ na kesi kesii na bésela na nwuna kemmo na baatina bekyuli bammɔ ala taasiku.

english_verse: The nations around Judah were afraid of the Lord's power, so none of them attacked Jehoshaphat.
translation_verse: Amu na kadi bekyuli bani ƒui náka bámana Yuda kalɔ mmɔ baayia Unwoti ɔyikun ɔni na ubo geen, anwuɔsu badi bátakana na bata bekpoku Yehosaƒat.

english_verse: Philistines brought him silver and other gifts to keep peace. Some of the Arab people brought him
translation_verse: Na Ƒilistiƒuɔ béboku-nwu sika ɔƒualadi ku etela bamba kalɛ na keyi buɛɛ kakya ama ku Yehosaƒat. Na Arabiaƒuɔ lɛnɔ béboku-nwu baƒonu mpim maatɛ ku eti leevu-ine. Na bese lɛnɔ lɛni kani.

english_verse: As Jehoshaphat became more powerful, he built fortresses and cities
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu kalɛ na Yehosaƒat ɔɔkɛ́ ɔyikun teebu ni, lɛni kani na ɔɔtú kɔgyumanakɔ lɛma kpakplaa ku lɛma linengudi lɛnɔ

english_verse: where he stored supplies. He also kept in Jerusalem some experienced soldiers
translation_verse: kesii kani na uusé ala. Na ɔ́ya na bekpone babuni geen bakya Yerusalem.

english_verse: from the Judah and Benjamin tribes. These soldiers were grouped according to their clans. Adnah was the commander of the troops from Judah, and he had
translation_verse: Na bási Yuda ku Benyamin adua kemmo. Na básala bekpone bammɔ na bana adua adua kenye. Amu na bábla Adna, na ɔdi bekpone bani nási Yuda ɔtɔnkune na bekpone mpim eti aku bakya-nwu kalɔ na ɔɔnu-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Amasiah son of Zichri, who had volunteered to serve the Lord, was third in command, with
translation_verse: Na Sikri ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Amasia, na anwu ɔlati úti lɛlɔ úte ka utaabla Unwoti kabla, ɔdi ubunkune ɔtɛdi. Na bekpone mpim eti ene nkya-nwu kalɔ na ɔɔnu-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: These were the troops who protected the king in Jerusalem, not counting those he had assigned to the fortified cities throughout the country.
translation_verse: Bekpone bamɛni ndi bekpone bani mɔɔgyumana ɔga ɔmmɔ na Yerusalem. Nsu bani na úte kabla na bakya kɔgyumanakɔ lɛma linengudi lɛmmɔ kemmo na kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ baaakɛ.

english_verse: Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Ahab ku Yehosaƒat bɔtɔnku bana bekpone na báyu ulu bésie Ramot na Gilead kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: One day, Jehoshaphat went to visit Ahab in his capital city of Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle and prepared a big feast to honor Jehoshaphat and the officials with him. Ahab talked about attacking the city of Ramoth in Gilead,
translation_verse: Amu na limeyi linwi na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yehosaƒat ɔ́vi ɔgbami úsie Ahab kudɔ na Samaria ɔma unengudi kesii kani na uli mmɔ. Na Ahab lɛnɔ ɔ́du baƒonu ku bebuo bamba na ɔ́di limeyi úte Yehosaƒat ku nwuna benengu bani na basiaku-nwu ƒui. Mmɔ na Ahab ɔ́tɛmi Yehosaƒat kɔtɛ ɔ́siku kalɛ na ɔɔyɔ́ ka ukpo Ramot ɔma na Gilead kalɔ kemmo.

english_verse: and finally asked, “Jehoshaphat, would you go with me to attack Ramoth?” “Yes,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army is at your command.
translation_verse: Ahab úye Yehosaƒat ɔnini, “Adubo ebebunku-mi na butékpoku Ramot-Gilead?” Amu na Yehosaƒat údie Israelƒuɔ ɔga kenye ɔnini, “Nse aani ƒula kalɛ na mina bekyuli badi ƒula bekyuli na bɔdubunyeku-ɔ na kekpo kammɔ kemmo.”

english_verse: But first let's ask the Lord what to do.”
translation_verse: Nsu Yehosaƒat ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔnini, “Mmomu, ka Unwoti kasusu bɔwia asa.”

english_verse: prophets and asked, “Should I attack the city of Ramoth?” “Yes!” the prophets answered. “God will help you capture the city.”
translation_verse: ) ɔ́sala na úye-ma ɔnini, “Nteesie Ramot-Gilead na ntékpoku-ma munuu ntesie?” Amu na kenye bediene bammɔ básu-nwu banini, “Teesie! Ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubo-ma buti bɔkya awɔ ɔga enu kemmo.”

english_verse: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
translation_verse: Nsu Yehosaƒat úye Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔnini, “Unwoti kenye udiene biala ɔ́sɔ uuubo mɛni na buye-nwu litemi lɛmɛni bunu?”

english_verse: Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́lɔ nwuna kabla ɔblane unwi na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Tiku Imla ubidi Mikaia boku mɛni ɔƒaani.”

english_verse: All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria, listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ ɔga ku Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Yehosaƒat bakya bana baga ala na beli bana baga eboku lɛlɔ. Na beli Samaria ulu lɛlɔ na kesii kani baakɔ́ ɔlaaƒɔ. Na kenye bediene bammɔ ƒui béli-ma kudɔ baasú ala na bana anumi.

english_verse: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
translation_verse: Na Kenaana ubidi Sedekia úti lɛbuala na ɔ́bla bebuo ese anyɔ adi na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu ɔnini, ‘Ése amɛni na adubuti akya Siriaƒuɔ ɔlɛ lɛlɔ útédu ka áyila-ma udu ƒui.’ ”

english_verse: All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth and promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
translation_verse: Na lɛni kani na kenye bediene bakladi ƒui lɛnɔ baasu banini, “Biteesie bitékpoku Ramot-Gilead na bɛdubɔdi-ma lɛlɔ, ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubuti-ma ɔkya ɔga enu kemmo.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
translation_verse: Na ɔtalane ɔni bátála ka útéti Mikaia uboku mmɔ ɔɔsu Mikaia ɔnini, “Nu, awɔ lɛti pɛ ndi kenye udiene ɔni nébu. Na kenye bediene bakladi baasu lɛla lɛni ndia teete ɔga. Anwuɔsu, ya ƒula etemila ku bani ngye adi abla unwi. Na asu lɛla lɛni ndubɔyɔ ɔga kaƒɔ.”

english_verse: “I'll say whatever the living Lord my God tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
translation_verse: Nsu Mikaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Na Unwoti ɔni nli ngba lɛnyi kemmo ni, lɛla lɛni na mina Katɔti ɔ́su-mi kani ndubo bɔsu.”

english_verse: Then Micaiah went up to Ahab, who asked, “Micaiah, should we attack Ramoth?” “Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you capture the city.”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Mikaia úbeduo ni, ɔga úye-nwu ɔnini, “Nsie ntékpoku Ramot-Gilead munuu ntesie?” Amu na Mikaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Teesie na etékpoku-ma, na adubɔdi lɛlɔ ɔsika badubo-ma buti bɔkya-a enu enu kemmo.”

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth! What does the Lord really say?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔga ɔmmɔ úye Mikaia ɔnini, “Kɔlɛ na ɔlɛka lɛya-a na ese kenye ka alasu lɛla lɛdi eletulo lɛla lɛni ndi sɔsɔ geen litemi na Unwoti lɛnyi kemmo?”

english_verse: Micaiah answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers wandering around, lost in the hills like sheep without a shepherd. The Lord said, ‘These troops have no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mikaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Lɛ́nu ka Israelƒuɔ ƒui bégyingya bewi abi eli aani baƒonu bani na beeebo lɛlɔ ɔnune. Na Unwoti ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Bekyuli bamɛni beeebo ɔtɔnkune, anwuɔsu ɔdi biala unwini uteesie nwuna kaduli ku atu bɔyɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Ahab turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “I told you he would bring me bad news!”
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́su Yehosaƒat ɔnini, “Ńtasu-ɔ ka ukyuli ɔmɛni ulásu lɛla lɛbuni na mina lɛlɔ ntu likpidi kani?”

english_verse: Micaiah replied: I then saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him.
translation_verse: Amu na Mikaia úsie anumi ku nwuna kenye budie ɔnini, “Ɔmmɔ ɔsu binu Unwoti litemi. Lɛ́nu ka Unwoti úli nwuna liboku lɛlɔ na katɔ batu ƒui bénye-nwu kɔmii ku kɔdianu.

english_verse: The Lord asked, “Who can trick Ahab and make him go to Ramoth where he will be killed?” They talked about it for a while,
translation_verse: Na Unwoti úye-ma ɔnini, ‘Ɔma ndubɔkana na ɔtɔlɔ Ahab na usie Ramot kesii kani na badubo-nwu bɔdu mmɔ?’ “Na bani nása bénye mmɔ bátɛmi básiku ɔmɛni lɛlɔ uwi klukwii ɔdi.

english_verse: then finally a spirit came forward and said to the Lord, “I can trick Ahab.” “How?” the Lord asked.
translation_verse: Kawɔlɔkɔ ni, kɔyu kunwi kɔ́lɛ kúbenye Unwoti anumi na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, ‘Ndubɔkana na ntátɔlɔ-nwu.’ “Mmɔ na Unwoti úye-ku ɔnini, ‘Dɛ na adubo bɔbla?’

english_verse: “I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.” “Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it. You will be successful.”
translation_verse: “Mmɔ na kɔyu kɔmmɔ kɔnini, ‘Ndubusie na liti ɔkɔ etemila lɛkya kenye bediene bammɔ ƒui kenye.’ “Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, ‘Adubɔkana-nwu bɔtɔlɔ sɔsɔ, anwuɔsu teesie na atábla lɛni.’

english_verse: Zedekiah walked over and slapped Micaiah on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Kenaana ubidi Sedekia úsie na útáƒiɛmi Mikaia lɛtukpo. Na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Ka Unwoti kɔyu kɔlɛ-mi kemmo ni, wɛ kakɛ na kɔ́vi kɔ́sia asa na kubetemiku-ɔ?”

english_verse: Micaiah answered, “You'll find out on the day you have to hide in the back room of some house.”
translation_verse: Amu na Mikaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Limeyi lɛdi lɛdubo na adubo bɔnu ka ɔlɛka abɛla lɛlɔ na ɔtɔ ɔdi kama kesii kadi.”

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ahab ɔ́va ku lɛdi momoomo ɔ́su ɔnini, “Biƒie Mikaia! Biti-nwu bisienku ɔga ubi Yosa ku Samaria aban ɔgadine Amon kudɔ.

english_verse: Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
translation_verse: Na asu-ma ka lɛni na ɔga ɔɔsu, ‘Biti okloƒu ɔmɛni bɛkya ɔtɔ. Na bitete-nwu lɛla biala na ɔdi, si ɔɔɔdi bodobodo ku ntu kani wetédu ka línwini ḿbeduo buɛɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Micaiah said, “If you do come back, I was wrong about what the Lord wanted me to say.” Then he told the crowd, “Don't forget what I said!” Ahab Dies at Ramoth (
translation_verse: Amu na Mikaia údie kenye ɔnini, “Si énwini ébeduo buɛɛ ni, na agyi anii Unwoti útatɛmi útasiaku-mi lɛlɔ.” Amu na ɔ́su bekyuli bammɔ ɔnini, “Bise mina litemi lɛni lɛ́su mmɔ likpo!” Ahab Úkpi Na Ramot

english_verse: Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
translation_verse: Na asa na badubusie kekpokɔ kammɔ ni, Ahab ɔ́su Yehosaƒat ɔnini, “Yehosaƒat, ndubo lɛlɔ udu bɔvumana, nsu awɔ kya ƒula agala.” Anwuɔsu Ahaba ɔ́vumana lɛlɔ udu na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie kekpokɔ.

english_verse: The king of Syria had ordered his chariot commanders to attack only Ahab.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kani lɛlɔ ni, Siriaƒuɔ ɔga úubo nwuna bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ batɔnkune ka Ahab lɛti kani na ɔdi ka bekpoku kaduɛ.

english_verse: So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But Jehoshaphat prayed, and the Lord made the Syrian soldiers stop.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ka bekpone bammɔ bánu Yehosaƒat na nwuna agala kemmo ni, bábu ka Ɔga Ahab ɔmmɔ na ɔdi mmɔ. Anwuɔsu bése kalɔ nka beteekpoku-nwu geen. Nsu Yehosaƒat ɔ́kpali Unwoti úvele-nwu kpakplaa na Unwoti lɛnɔ ɔ́ya na Siriaƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ báda báya.

english_verse: However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab between two pieces of his armor. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
translation_verse: Na tabla tabla uwi ɔni na kekpo kammɔ kéti késela anumi ni, ukpone ɔdi úbo nwuna kataminta lɛtula lɛdi na lɛ́vi Ahab kekpo agyumanala anyɔ ani nda-nwu lɛlɔ mmɔ kuƒi blii kɔdi ntɛ na lɛ́tu-nwu, nsu ɔɔɔdi bɔsusu na ɔ́susu mmɔ asa na úbo lɛtula lɛmmɔ. Mmɔ kani na Ahab ɔ́va ɔ́kpali nwuna ɔpɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ɔkane ɔnini, “Babla na abada-mi edie likpo lɛmɛni, ɔsika ukpone ɔdi lɛtula lɛ́kɛ-mi!”

english_verse: The fighting lasted all day, with Ahab propped up in his chariot so he could see the Syrian troops. He stayed there until evening, and by sundown he was dead.
translation_verse: Kekpo kammɔ késie anumi limeyi limodi na bákada Ahab békpo nwuna kɛɛkɛ kemmo kalɛ na ɔkana na utaanu Siriaƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ teemene. Na úlie mmɔ laa útédu useyi uwi na uwi ɔni na ɔƒɛ utaanu kani na úkpi.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amu na Yehosaƒat anwu ɔ́sɔ únwini úbeduo Yerusalem buɛɛ na nwuna ɔga kesii.

english_verse: But the prophet Jehu son of Hanani met him and said: By helping that wicked Ahab, you have made friends with someone who hates the Lord. Now the Lord God is angry with you!
translation_verse: Nsu Hanani ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni ndi Kenye Udiene Yuhu úbasiaku-nwu na ulu lɛlɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Na kebunku kani na éte Ahab ɔlalane ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, éti lɛlɔ énwini ukyuli ɔni muukisi Unwoti ɔkpana. Anwuɔsu Unwoti úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya-a!

english_verse: But not everything about you is bad. You destroyed the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah—that shows you have tried to obey the Lord. Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges To Settle Cases
translation_verse: Nsu ɔɔɔdi ala ƒui nébie na ƒula lɛlɔ. Awɔ náƒɛ Asera baƒiɔ lɛƒiɔgyii lɛni na bálɛ na baakpá-ma na lise-ma kedee ƒui na ɔmmɔ lɛti ɔɔtina ka aayɔ́ ka ataadi Unwoti litemi lɛlɔ.” Yehosaƒat Ɔ́ƒuna Litemi Batɛne Bani Ndubo Etemila Butaatɛ

english_verse: Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, but he often traveled through his kingdom, from Beersheba in the south to the edge of the hill country of Ephraim in the north. He talked with the people and convinced them to turn back to the Lord God and worship him, just as their ancestors had done.
translation_verse: Yerusalem na Yehosaƒat ɔ́kya, nsu ɔɔyɔ́ busie taatávi nwuna lɛgakadikɔ kammɔ kemmo ɔ́si Beerseba na kalɔ kammɔ kada kakɛ útédu Eƒraim abi lɛlɔ kalɔ kammɔ kawɔkɔ na katɔ kakɛ. Na ɔɔtɛmiku bekyuli bammɔ teedie ala kalɔ teete-ma kalɛ na basɔ benwini bebo Unwoti kudɔ na batakpa-nwu kalɛ kani na ɔni na bana bati kuuku bákpa kalɛ.

english_verse: He assigned judges to each of the fortified cities in Judah
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́ƒuna litemi batɛne úte kagyumakɔ lɛma linengudi lɛmmɔ ƒui na Yuda kalɔ kemmo

english_verse: and told them: Be careful when you make your decisions in court, because you are judging by the Lord's standards and not by human standards, and he will know what you decide.
translation_verse: na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛnu lɛlɔ kemmo kaduɛ si uwi ɔni na bɛɛlɛ bina etemila adi ugyii na bina litemi katɛkɔ. Ɔsika Unwoti kadi bekyuli na badi mɛni. Na lɛla biala na bɛ́lɛ ugyii ni, lɛdi lɛɛɛdubo-nwu bɔbɛ.

english_verse: So do your work in honor of him and know that he won't allow you to be unfair to anyone or to take bribes.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bɛnu ka bɛ́bla bina kabla ƒui na bíti ɔbu bíte-nwu. Na bɛti lɛnɔ ka ɔɔɔdubo-mii kuƒi bute na bɛnu ukyuli ɔdi anumi bɛbla lɛla lɛdi iye bɛbɛ bɛƒɔ lɛla lɛdi bɛsiku ɔdi kudɔ bɛdi.”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat also chose some Levites, some priests, and some of the family leaders, and he appointed them to serve as judges in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Yehosaƒat ɔ́ƒuna Lewiƒuɔ badi lɛnɔ ku bakpane ku lɛtɔ benengu badi ka benwini litemi batɛne bamɛni na Yerusalem.

english_verse: He told them: Faithfully serve the Lord!
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛbla Unwoti kabla siin na bitalɛ-nwu kama!

english_verse: The people of Judah will bring you legal cases that involve every type of crime, including murder. You must settle these cases and warn the people to stop sinning against the Lord, so that he won't get angry and punish Judah. Remember, if you follow these instructions, you won't be held responsible for anything that happens.
translation_verse: Yudaƒuɔ kadi bekyuli badubo etemila lidu lidu buti buboku-mii kudɔ banii bɛtɛ bite-ma ku bekyuli bɔdu etemila muedi. Ɔdi ka bɛtɛ etemila amɛni udu ƒui na bibo bekyuli bammɔ ɔda ka bada ekpidi bɔbla bɔƒiɔ Unwoti baya kalɛ na uleti kɔnyi ulakya Yudaƒuɔ ƒui na ɔni-ma kɔtu. Na binyimo ka si bɛ́siaku ala ani kalɔ na muudie teete-mii mɛni lɛlɔ ni, Unwoti ɔɔɔdubo-mii bɔƒiɔ bɔdi budie na uubo ka bani-mii kɔtu kɔdi.

english_verse: Amariah the high priest will have the final say in any religious case. And Zebadiah, the leader of the Judah tribe, will have the final say in all other cases. The rest of the Levites will serve as your assistants. Be brave, and I pray that the Lord will help you do right.
translation_verse: “Na lɛla biala na lɛdanku bɔƒɔtaadi ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ ni, ɔkpane unengudi ɔni ndi Amaria ni, anwu kani ndubo bɔkana na ɔlɛ ugyii. Na Ismael ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni ndi Sebadia na ɔdi Yudaƒuɔ ɔtɔnkune ni, anwu ndubɔkana na ɔlɛ etemila bamba anya ugyii. Na Lewiƒuɔ bakladi badubo-ɔ kebunku buteete. Nye kpakplaa na ndubo Unwoti buteevele teete-ɔ kalɛ na ubunku-ɔ na akana na ataabla lɛbuni lɛmmɔ uwi biala.”

english_verse: Messengers told Jehoshaphat, “A large army from Edom east of the Dead Sea has invaded our country. They have already reached En-Gedi.”
translation_verse: Na batu bábasu Yehosaƒat banini, “Bekisine bekpone lisu bonwu lɛdi lɛ́si Edom abi lɛlɔ kalɔ kemmo na Ɛpugyie ɔmmɔ ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ bébo na bébekpo bula kalɔ na béedu kesii kani na baalɔ En Gedi.”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat was afraid, so he asked the Lord what to do. He then told the people of Judah to go without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Amu na Yehosaƒat ɔ́kpali Unwoti na úvele-nwu ɔnii ɔtina-nwu lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka ɔbla, ɔsika ɔ́yia geen.

english_verse: They immediately left for Jerusalem to ask for the Lord's help.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu kɔnakunwi ni, báyu ulu bésie Yerusalem kesii kani na bétevele-nwu ka ubunku-ma.

english_verse: After everyone from Judah and Jerusalem had come together at the Lord's temple, Jehoshaphat stood in front of the new courtyard
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na bekyuli bani na bási Yuda ku Yerusalem mmɔ bábasa na Unwoti kakpakɔ mmɔ báwɔlɔ ni, Yehosaƒat ɔ́ta únye kakpakɔ kaduli kawɔdi kammɔ anumi na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui anumi

english_verse: and prayed: You, Lord, are the God our ancestors worshiped, and from heaven you rule every nation in the world. You are so powerful that no one can defeat you.
translation_verse: na ɔ́kpali Unwoti úvele ɔnini, “Awɔ Unwoti ndi Katɔti ɔni na bula bati kuuku bákpa. Na eli katɔ kakaaka mmɔ na aadi kayawi kamɛni kadi biala bekyuli lɛlɔ. Na ebo ɔyikun geen ɔni na ukyuli ɔdi biala ulakana-a lɛlɔ bɔdi.
