english_verse: Our God, you forced out the nations who lived in this land before your people Israel came here, and you gave it to the descendants of your friend Abraham forever.
translation_verse: Bula Katɔti, awɔ nábɔku kadi bekyuli bani ƒui na nka beli mɛni kukuuku álɛku mɛni asa na ƒula kadi bekyuli bani ndi abu Israelƒuɔ búbelie mɛni. Na awɔ néti kalɔ kamɛni éte ƒula ɔkpana ɔni ndi Abraham bebi ku bawɔ ka kenwini bana kadikɔ uwi ƒui.

english_verse: Our ancestors lived in this land and built a temple to honor you.
translation_verse: Mɛni na bula bati kukuuku béli na bátu kakpakɔ béte-ɔ kalɛ na bataakpa-a teete-ɔ ɔbu.

english_verse: They believed that whenever this land is struck by war or disease or famine, your people can pray to you at the temple, and you will hear their prayer and save them.
translation_verse: Na báƒɔ bádi ka uwi biala na kekpo iye ɔlɛ iye kɔka kúbo kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ ni, ƒula kadi bekyuli bamɛni bakana na beduo ƒula kakpakɔ kamɛni kemmo na bakpali-ɔ na adubudie-ma.

english_verse: You can see that the armies of Ammon, Moab, and Edom are attacking us! Those are the nations you would not let our ancestors invade on their way from Egypt, so these nations were not destroyed.
translation_verse: “Aanu ka Amonƒuɔ ku Moabƒuɔ ku Edomƒuɔ bekpone benye beekpó-bu! Badi kɔlɔ kɔni bekyuli na nka awɔ Unwoti átatuna ka bula kadi bekyuli bekpo-ma uwi ɔni na bɔkɛ ulu bɔ́si Egyipte bɔdubo, anwuɔsu na bátayii udu.

english_verse: Now they are coming to take back the land you gave us.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔƒaani ni, aanu-ma nási badubo bebeƒie kalɔ kani na éte-bu baƒɔ-bu kudɔ benwini ama kadi.

english_verse: Aren't you going to punish them? We won't stand a chance when this army attacks. We don't know what to do—we are begging for your help.
translation_verse: Aaadubo-ma kɔtu bɔni? Buuubo kenyekɔ kadi na bekpone bamɛni udu anumi si banii beekpó-bu sɔsɔ. Bɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛni na bɔbla, anwuɔsu kebunku kani na buuvele.”

english_verse: While every man, woman, and child of Judah was standing there at the temple,
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na Yudaƒuɔ banana ku beleku ku banamu bammɔ ƒui benye kakpakɔ anumi mmɔ ni,

english_verse: the Lord's Spirit suddenly spoke to Jahaziel, a Levite from the Asaph clan.
translation_verse: Unwoti Kɔyu kútemiku Yahasiel ɔni ndi Lewini na ɔ́si Asaƒ kɔdua kemmo kɔnakunwi.

english_verse: Then Jahaziel said: Your Majesty and everyone from Judah and Jerusalem, the Lord says that you don't need to be afraid or let this powerful army discourage you. God will fight on your side!
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yahasiel ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔga Ɔbune ku ukyuli biala na ɔ́si Yuda ku Yerusalem, Unwoti ɔnii utalɛka bina ɔdi ɔyia iye bekpone bayikune bamɛni ɔbladu ɔdi ɔda-mii ɔƒɛ na enu aƒɛ-mii. Katɔti ɔdubo kekpo kammɔ bukpo bute-mii!

english_verse: So here's what you must do. Tomorrow the enemy armies will march through the desert around the town of Jeruel. March down and meet them at the town of Ziz as they come up the valley.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu binu lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka bɛbla. Kɔnaadi ni, bekisine bekpone bammɔ badubo lɛlɔ bɔsiaku na babwɛ bavi kalɔ kakwiidi kani náka kámana Yeruel ɔma mmɔ. Amii lɛnɔ bisie na bitásiaku-ma na Sis ɔma kemmo si uwi ɔni na béti bákɔ baalɛ́ kɔwɛ kɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: You won't even have to fight. Just take your positions and watch the Lord rescue you from your enemy. Don't be afraid. Just do as you're told. And as you march out tomorrow, the Lord will be there with you.
translation_verse: Amii bitasu bɛnii biikpó-ma munu munu. Mmomu bɛwia kunyekɔ na binye bitaanu kalɛ na Unwoti ɔdubo-mii budie bɔlɛku-ma enu kemmo. Bitayia. Amii bɛbla bɛsiaku lɛla lɛni na bínu lɛlɔ. Na uwi ɔni na bɛdubo busie buteesie mmɔ kɔnaadi ƒui ni, Unwoti anwu ɔdubo bɔgyu bɔtɔ uténye mmɔ kukuuku.”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat bowed low to the ground and everyone worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Amu na Yehosaƒat úboku lɛlɔ kalɔ buɛɛ na ɔ́kya lili kalɔ úte Unwoti na bakladi ƒui lɛnɔ bábla lɛni kani.

english_verse: Then some Levites from the Kohath and Korah clans stood up and shouted praises to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Lewiƒuɔ badi na bási Kohat ku Kora adua kemmo báta bénye na bédie bumwi lɛnu béte Unwoti Israel Katɔti.

english_verse: Early the next morning, as everyone got ready to leave for the desert near Tekoa, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, “Listen my friends, if we trust the Lord God and believe what these prophets have told us, the Lord will help us, and we will be successful.”
translation_verse: Amu na kadi kegye ɔtanta tutuutu uwi ɔni na ukyuli biala ɔdaku lɛlɔ bɔklibi ka bayu ulu beteesie kakɔ kakwiidi kani nde Tekoa mmɔ ni, Yehosaƒat ɔ́ta únye na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Banwa, binu! Si bula ƒui búti bula kɔyi bɔ́sia Unwoti lɛlɔ na bɔ́ƒɔ lɛla lɛni na kenye bediene básu-bu mmɔ bɔ́di ni, Unwoti ɔdubo-bu bubunku na bɔdi lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Then he explained his plan and appointed men to march in front of the army and praise the Lord for his holy power by singing: “Praise the Lord! His love never ends.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na údie ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na badubo bɔsia busie mmɔ ɔ́tina-ma. Na ɔ́ƒuna bekyuli badi batɔ bakladi ƒui anumi na baatu lɛnu teemwi Unwoti taasu kalɛ na nwuna ɔyikun ɔni na ubo use kedee taasu banini, “Bɛgya Unwoti enu, ɔsika ɔdia na ɔɔyɔ́-bu uwi ndi uwi.”

english_verse: so that the Ammonite and Moabite troops attacked and completely destroyed those from Edom. Then they turned against each other and fought until the entire camp was wiped out!
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Amonƒuɔ ku Moabƒuɔ básala lɛlɔ na békpo Edomƒuɔ na bádu-ma ƒui. Na ɔmmɔ kama bana akpa anyɔ lɛnɔ bénwini bálɛku lɛlɔ na békpoku lɛlɔ na bádu lɛlɔ béwi bana kakyakɔ bewi kalɔ kede kede na asɔ alanu ukyuli ɔdi na bana nvo bɔmmɔ kemmo!

english_verse: When Judah's army reached the tower that overlooked the desert, they saw that every soldier in the enemy's army was lying dead on the ground.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na Yudaƒuɔ bédu ɔma kagyumanakɔ kani na si enye na aanu kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ teemene ni, bánu ka bekisine bekpone bammɔ ƒui ɔdi biala ukpi ɔtɛ kalɔ na bana nvo bɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Then on the fourth day, everyone came together in Beracah Valley and sang praises to the Lord. That's why that place was called Praise Valley.
translation_verse: Amu na limeyi linedi lɛlɔ ni, ukyuli biala ɔ́lɛ úbo na bábasa na kɔwɛ kɔni na baalɔ banii Baraka Kɔwɛ kemmo. Na mmɔ na bédie lɛnu bémwi Unwoti. Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu na baalɔ mmɔ banii Bumwi Kɔwɛ.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat led the crowd back to Jerusalem. And as they marched, they played harps and blew trumpets. They were very happy because the Lord had given them victory over their enemies, so when they reached the city, they went straight to the temple.
translation_verse: Yehosaƒat ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tɔnku bekyuli bammɔ na bénwini bésie Yerusalem. Na bakɛ baagyá lɛbentaa na baavwi kɔkpɛɛ. Na lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ-ma geen, ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́ya na bádi bana bekisine lɛlɔ. Na ka bébeduo ɔma kemmo ni, bávi bésie kakpakɔ kɔnakunwi.

english_verse: When the other nations heard how the Lord had fought against Judah's enemies, they were too afraid
translation_verse: Amu ka kadi bamba bekyuli bani na beli bede mmɔ bénu kalɛ na Unwoti úkpo Yuda bekisine úte-ma ni, liƒu bonwu líƒie-ma na báyia geen

english_verse: to invade Judah. The Lord let Jehoshaphat's kingdom be at peace. Jehoshaphat Dies (
translation_verse: kalɛ na ɔdi ɔsɔ ɔta ɔnii utékpo Yuda. Na Unwoti ɔ́ya na Yehosaƒat lɛgakadikɔ kákɛ keyi buɛɛ ku atu bɔyɔ. Yehosaƒat Úkpi

english_verse: While Jehoshaphat was king, he signed a peace treaty with Ahaziah the wicked king of Israel.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Yehosaƒat ɔ́di lɛga ni, anwu ku Israel ɔga ɔlalane ɔni baalɔ Ahasia bényimi unwi bɔbla lɛla lɛdi bése.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat obeyed the Lord, just as his father Asa had done,
translation_verse: Yehosaƒat ɔ́di Unwoti litemi lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na ɔti ɔni baalɔ Asa lɛnɔ ɔ́bla.

english_verse: but he did not destroy the local shrines. So the people still worshiped foreign gods, instead of faithfully serving the God their ancestors had worshiped.
translation_verse: Nsu anwu Yehosaƒat útabwɛ baƒiɔ bani na bekyuli bávɔ bése abi lɛlɔ bátaakpa mmɔ. Anwuɔsu bekyuli básiaku lɛƒiɔkpa ala bɔbla kama na ɔni na basiaku Unwoti kama siin aani kalɛ na bana bati kuuku bábla kalɛ.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoshaphat did while he was king is written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani that are included in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na lɛla biala na Yehosaƒat ɔ́bla uwi ɔni na ɔ́di lɛga ni, bénweni-mi bákya Yehu ɔni ndi Hanani ubidi ɔnanabi ala alɛdi Israel baga ablala ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: They agreed to build several seagoing ships at Ezion-Geber.
translation_verse: Na bénu kalɔ lɛnɔ ka banwi lɛkɔlɔ libendi lɛni ndubo ntu anumi buteesie ntu anumi.

english_verse: But the prophet Eliezer warned Jehoshaphat, “The Lord will destroy these ships because you have supported Ahaziah.” The ships were wrecked and never sailed.
translation_verse: Nsu Kenye Udiene Elieser ɔ́lɛ Yehosaƒat kpakplaa ɔnini, “Unwoti ɔdubo lɛkɔkɔ lɛmɛni udu bɔyila, ɔsika ébunku Ahasia.” Na sɔsɔ ni, lɛkɔlɔ lɛmɛni lɛ́bwɛ na lítasia ntu anumi lítabla kabla kadi.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king. King Jehoram of Judah (
translation_verse: Yehosaƒat úbekpi na báva-nwu na kesii kani na nwuna bati kuuku bátɛ na Yerusalem na ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Yehoram ubenwini ɔga. Yehoram Úbenwini Yuda Ɔga

english_verse: King Jehoshaphat had seven sons: Jehoram, Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah.
translation_verse: Bebi maatɛ na Ɔga Yehosaƒat ɔ́wɔ. Na ama ndi Yehoram ku Asaria ku Yehiel ku Sekaria ku Asariahu ku Mikael ku Seƒatia.

english_verse: years from Jerusalem. He died, and no one even felt sad. He was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na Yehoram ɔɔdi lɛga mmɔ ni, Edom abi lɛlɔ kalɔ bekyuli báta bénye-nwu lɛlɔ na báƒuna bana ɔga.

english_verse: The Lord later caused the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians to become angry with Jehoram.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na Ƒilistiƒuɔ ku Arabiaƒuɔ bani na beli bede Kus mmɔ béti kɔnyi bákya Yehoram.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat gave each of them silver and gold, as well as other valuable gifts. He also put them in charge of the fortified cities in Judah, but he had chosen his oldest son Jehoram to succeed him as king.
translation_verse: Yehosaƒat úte bana ɔdi biala sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ku ala bamba ani náƒɔ kuye geen. Na ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́ya na bénwini lɛlɔ badine na kɔgyumanakɔ lɛma linengudi lɛmmɔ kemmo na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu ubidi udeedi anwu ni, ɔ́ƒuna-nwu ka unwini ɔga na nwuna kenye.

english_verse: After Jehoram had taken control of Judah, he had his brothers killed, as well as some of the nation's leaders.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Yehoram ɔ́nu ka nwuna ɔyikun ɔ́di Yuda ƒui lɛlɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔ́ya na bádu nwuna banwani bakladi ƒui ku Yuda kadi batɔnkune badi.

english_verse: Jehoram married Ahab's daughter and followed the sinful example of Ahab's family and the other kings of Israel. He disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong,
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Yehoram úti Ahab ubidi ulekubi na ɔ́siaku Ahab ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ɔbladu ukpidi ku Israel baga bamba udunkpi ala bɔbla kama. Na úni Unwoti litemi bunu na ɔɔƒiɔ́-nwu mmomu.

english_verse: but because the Lord had made a solemn promise to King David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah, he refused to wipe out David's descendants.
translation_verse: Nsu ka Unwoti úse kenye ka Dawid bebi ku bawɔ akɔ na ukyuli ɔdubɔsi uwi biala na ɔdi lɛga na Yuda ɔsu ni, útayila Dawidi ɔtɔ kemmo bebi ku bɔwɔ udu.

english_verse: Jehoram, his officers, and his cavalry marched to Edom, where the Edomite army surrounded them. He escaped during the night,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yehoram ku nwuna bakutine ku bapɔnkɔ beliene báta bésie Edom. Na mmɔ ni, Edom bekpone bábaka-ma bákya na anwu úkeli ku usien.

english_verse: but Judah was never able to regain control of Edom. Even the town of Libnah rebelled at that time. Those things happened because Jehoram had turned away from the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔ́bla bi ɔ́bla dɛ ni, Yuda ɔ́sɔ útakana Edomƒuɔ lɛlɔ bɔdi. Na Libna ɔma bekyuli muedi báta bénye Yehoram lɛlɔ uwi ɔmmɔ. Na ala amɛni ƒui álɛ lɛni, ɔsika Yehoram únwini kama ɔ́kya Unwoti ɔni ndi nwuna bati kuuku Katɔti.

english_verse: Jehoram even built local shrines in the hills of Judah and let the people sin against the Lord by worshiping foreign gods.
translation_verse: Yehoram ɔ́tu baƒiɔ ɔ́lɛ abi eli na bekyuli béteesie taatákpa na ɔ́ya na bekyuli báƒiɔ Unwoti.

english_verse: One day, Jehoram received a letter from Elijah the prophet that said: I have a message for you from the Lord God your ancestor David worshiped. He knows that you have not followed the example of Jehoshaphat your father or Asa your grandfather.
translation_verse: Amu na limeyi linwi lɛdi ni, Kenye Udiene Elia únweni ɔku ɔdi úte Yehoram na ɔdanku kenye kadi ɔnini, “Lɛ́ƒɔ linyesia lɛdi lɛ́siku Unwoti Katɔti ɔni na bula ɔti kuuku Dawid ɔ́kpa líboku-ɔ. Na kenye kammɔ ndi ka Unwoti ɔnii ɔgyi ka átasiaku ƒ'ɔti Yehosaƒat ɔbladu kama iye Nana Asa ɔbladu kama.

english_verse: Instead you have acted like those sinful kings of Israel and have encouraged the people of Judah to stop worshiping the Lord, just as Ahab and his descendants did. You even murdered your own brothers, who were better men than you.
translation_verse: Mmomu elie ngba aani Israel baga bekpidi bammɔ kalɛ na ákya Yuda kadi bekyuli ka bada Unwoti bɔkpa baya kalɛ kani na Ahab ku nwuna ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli bábla kalɛ. Na awɔ ɔlati ƒula banwani bani na nka badia betulo-ɔ ƒui muedi ádu-ma.

english_verse: Because you have done these terrible things, the Lord will severely punish the people in your kingdom, including your own family, and he will destroy everything you own.
translation_verse: “Na alaekpidi bonwu ani na ábla mɛni ɔsu ni, Unwoti ɔdubo ƒula lɛgakadikɔ bekyuli ku ƒula ɔtɔ kemmo bekyuli kɔtu bɔni geen na ubile ala ani ƒui na ebo na ayii udu kede kede.

english_verse: You will be struck with a painful stomach disease and suffer until you die.
translation_verse: Na kaƒɔ ɔlɛ kpakplaa ɔdi ɔdubo-ɔ bubo na ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ na adubo buƒi ebo abi laa na eti ekpi.”

english_verse: They invaded Judah and stole the royal property from the palace, and they led Jehoram's wives and sons away as prisoners. The only one left behind was Ahaziah, his youngest son.
translation_verse: Kadi kamɛni bekyuli bébo bébekpo Yuda na béyu-ma agala ƒui bátɔlɔku básiku ɔga kesii mmɔ. Na béƒie Yehoram ulekudi ku bebi ƒui bátɔlɔku aani batɔntɛne kalɛ. Na ubi unwi ɔni kani nébu ndi ɔnamudi ƒui ɔni baalɔ Ahasia.

english_verse: After this happened, the Lord struck Jehoram with an incurable stomach disease.
translation_verse: Amu ka ala amɛni álɛ lɛni áwɔlɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na kaƒɔ ɔ́lɛ ɔdi úbo Yehoram ɔni na ukyuli biala ulakana bɔbwi.

english_verse: About two years later, Jehoram died in terrible pain. No bonfire was built to honor him, even though the people had done this for his ancestors.
translation_verse: Na ɔbla akwa anyɔ kama ni, Yehoram úbekpi na únu ɔlɛ geen. Na bátakyula likpose livongu lɛdi bétete-nwu ka úkpi ina ka lɛni na bekyuli bammɔ bábla béte nwuna bati kuuku.

english_verse: and while Jehu was doing that, he saw some of Judah's leaders and Ahaziah's nephews who had come with Ahaziah. Jehu killed them on the spot,
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Yehu ɔdaku ɔmɛni bɔbla ni, ɔ́nu ka Yudaƒuɔ batɔnkune badi ku Ahasia ɔnwani bebi bananabi badi bani na ama ku Ahasia nébo ɔma mmɔ bébo mmɔ. Na mmɔ mmɔ kani na Yehu ɔ́du-ma

english_verse: then gave orders to find Ahaziah. Jehu's officers found him hiding in Samaria. They brought Ahaziah to Jehu, who immediately put him to death. They buried Ahaziah only because they respected Jehoshaphat his grandfather, who had done his best to obey the Lord. There was no one from Ahaziah's family left to become king of Judah. Queen Athaliah of Judah (
translation_verse: na ɔ́kya batu ɔnii batáwia Ahasia ɔmmɔ ɔlati beboku. Na Yehu batu bamɛni bátánu-nwu ka ɔ́bɛ ɔkya Samaria. Mmɔ na bákpanku Ahasia béboku Yehu na ɔ́du anwu lɛnɔ kɔnakunwi. Na ka baabu Yehosaƒat ɔsu ni, báva Ahasia ukyuli bɔva, ɔsika nwuna nana ndi Yehosaƒat ɔmɛni na anwu ɔ́sia ulu biala lɛlɔ ka ɔdi Unwoti litemi lɛlɔ. Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ uuubo na Ahasia kaduli na bese-nwu Yudaƒuɔ lɛga. Yudaƒuɔ Beleku Ɔga Úti Kasusu Kekpidi

english_verse: In fact, after his father's death, Ahaziah sinned against the Lord by appointing some of Ahab's relatives to be his advisors. Their advice led to his downfall.
translation_verse: Geen na ɔti kukpi kama ni, Ahasia ɔ́bla likpidi ɔ́ƒiɔ Unwoti na uwi ɔni na útáƒuna Ahab lɛlɔ bekyuli ka benwini-nwu kasusu bakyane. Na ɔkɛnku kasusu kani na baakya-nwu ɔsu na úbo kalɔ.

english_verse: He listened to them and went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle,
translation_verse: Bana litemi na únu ɔsu na úsie útásiaku Israel Ɔga Yoram na bétékpo Ɔga Hasael ku Siriaƒuɔ bekpone na Ramot ɔma kemmo na Gilead kalɔ lɛlɔ. Kekpo kammɔ kemmo na Ɔga Yoram ɔ́ƒɔ ɔlɛ kaduɛ

english_verse: and he went to the town of Jezreel to recover. And Ahaziah later went there to visit him.
translation_verse: na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Yesreel ɔma utábwi lɛlɔ. Na Ahasia úsie mmɔ kama kama útánu-nwu.

english_verse: It was during that visit that God had Ahaziah put to death. When Ahaziah arrived at Jezreel, he and Joram went to meet with Jehu grandson of Nimshi. The Lord had already told Jehu to kill every male in Ahab's family,
translation_verse: Na Ahasia mmɔ busie butánu Yoram kemmo na Katɔti ɔ́ya na úkpi. Amu na uwi na Ahasia útéduo Yesreel mmɔ ni, anwu ku Yoram bésie bátása ku Yehu ɔni ndi Nimsi uwɔ. Na uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́ɔsu Yehu ɔnii ɔdu ɔnanabi biala na Ahab ɔtɔ kemmo.

english_verse: but Jehosheba rescued Joash son of Ahaziah just as the others were about to be murdered. Jehosheba, who was Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's half sister, was married to Jehoiada the priest. So she was able to hide her nephew Joash and his personal servant in a bedroom in the Lord's temple where he was safe from Athaliah.
translation_verse: nsu Yehoseba ɔni ndi Yehoram ubidi ulekubi na ɔdi Ahasia ɔtibi údie Yoas na ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni kemmo uwi ɔni kani lɛlɔ na nka báasala nwuna banwani bakladi na badubo-ma bɔdu. Yehoseba ɔmɛni ulieku ɔkpane ɔni baalɔ Yehoiada. Anwuɔsu ɔ́kana na útiku Ahasia ubidi ɔnanabi ɔnamu blii ɔni ndi Yoas ɔmɛni ku nwuna kabla ɔblane lɛlɔ ɔnune útábɛla ɔtɔ ɔtɛdi ɔdi kemmo na kakpakɔ mmɔ na úkeli Atalia kasusu kekpidi kani na ɔdanku mɛni.

english_verse: As soon as Athaliah heard that her son King Ahaziah was dead, she decided to kill any relative who could possibly become king. She would have done just that,
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni kani na Atalia únu ka bádu ubidi ɔnanabi Ahasia ni, ɔ́bla kasusu ka ɔdu Ahasia lɛlɔ bekyuli bani ndi bagadine mmɔ ɔdi biala. Na ɔ́ɔkɛ kuƒi kɔmmɔ lɛnɔ,

english_verse: Joash hid in the temple with them for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah.
translation_verse: Yoas ɔ́bɛ ɔ́kya kakpakɔ mɛni akwa aku uwi ɔni na Atalia ɔɔdi Yuda lɛlɔ aani uleku ɔga.

english_verse: These five men went to the towns in Judah and called together the Levites and the clan leaders. They all came to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Nkyuli ɛlɔ bamɛni bésie Yuda lɛma kemmo na bátálɔ Lewiƒuɔ ku adua benengu bammɔ na bébo Yerusalem.

english_verse: Jehoiada and his sons brought Joash outside, where they placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of the instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, and the crowd cheered and shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yehoiada úsie útákpanku Yoas ɔ́lɛku úboku kesii kani na béti kagabwa bébi-nwu lili na úti kakunkɛ kani mɔɔtina ɔga kalɛ na ɔdi nwuna kadi bekyuli lɛlɔ bákya-nwu kɔnu. Na béwi-nwu lɛga buse nnomii lili béti bátina ka bése-nwu lɛga sɔsɔ. Mmɔ na kasalakɔ bekyuli bammɔ béte yiiduu ku kɔvanu básu banini, “Ɔga ulie ngba gyɔlɔɔ!”

english_verse: Here is what we will do. Three groups of priests and Levites will be on guard duty on the Sabbath—one group will guard the gates of the temple,
translation_verse: Na ndubo-mii bɔtina lɛla lɛni na ɔdi bɔbla. Bakpane kasala esu atɛ ku Lewiƒuɔ badi badubunye kagyumana na Lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ. Na lisu linwi lɛdubo kakpakɔ ɔban kenye butaagyumana.

english_verse: Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔ́tɔ ku ebiti, ɔsika bádu beleku Ɔga Atalia na keyii buɛɛ kásɔ kébo Yerusalem ɔƒaamu.

english_verse: After Ahaziah's son Joash had hidden in the temple for six years, Jehoiada the priest knew that something had to be done. So he made sure he had the support of several army officers. They were Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na Ahasia ubidi ɔnanabi Yoas ɔ́bɛla lɛlɔ na kakpakɔ kemmo mmɔ akwa aku kama ni, Yehoiada ɔni ndi ɔkpane mmɔ ɔ́nu ɔti ka ɔlɛka babla lɛla lɛdi. Anwuɔsu ɔ́sia ulu biala lɛlɔ na ɔ́nu ka bekpone benengu bammɔ ketulodikɔ benye-nwu kama. Na bana badi ndi Yehoram ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Asaria ku Yehonan ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Ismael ku Obed ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Asaria ku Adaia ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Maaseia ku Sikri ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Elisaƒat.

english_verse: and gathered at the temple, where they agreed to help Joash. Jehoiada said to them: Joash will be our next king, because long ago the Lord promised that one of David's descendants would always be king.
translation_verse: Na bábasala na kakpakɔ kesii kani na bénu kalɔ ka bebunku Yoas. Mmɔ na Yehoiada ɔ́su ɔnini, “Yoas ndubo bula Yudaƒuɔ ɔga bunwini. Ɔsika ɔ́si kukuuku ni, Unwoti ɔ́su úse ka Dawid ɔtɔ kemmo ubi na ɔga ɔdubɔsi ɔdi Yudaƒuɔ ɔga na uwi bilala kemmo.

english_verse: one will guard the palace, and the other will guard Foundation Gate. The rest of you will stand guard in the temple courtyards.
translation_verse: Na lisu linwi litaagyumana ɔga kesii. Na lisu lɛkladi litaagyumana kakpakɔ ɔka ɔmmɔ ɔban ɔmmɔ kayakun. Na amii bekyuli bakladi ƒui binye kagyumana na kakpakɔ kɔduli kɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Only the priests and Levites who are on duty will be able to enter the temple, because they will be the only ones who have gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable. The others must stay outside in the courtyards, just as the Lord has commanded.
translation_verse: Na bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bani mbo kabla limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ kani ndubɔkana na beduo kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo. Ɔsika ama kani nábla lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ɔni na baaka bɔbla asa na akana kakpakɔ kemmo buduo. Na ɔlɛka bakladi basɔ benye kakpakɔ kɔduli kɔmmɔ kemmo kalɛ kani na Unwoti ɔda bubo bɔɔtina kalɛ.

english_verse: You Levites must protect King Joash. Don't let him out of your sight! And keep your swords ready to kill anyone who comes into the temple.
translation_verse: Na amii Lewiƒuɔ ni, ɔlɛka bɛgyumana Ɔga Yoas. Na bina anumi atatimi-nwu lɛlɔ! Na binye kagyumana ku bina kuwii na bɛdu ukyuli bamba biala mebo kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo.”

english_verse: The Levites and the people of Judah followed Jehoiada's orders. The guards going off duty were not allowed to go home, and so each commander had all his guards available—those going off duty as well as those coming on duty.
translation_verse: Amu na Lewiƒuɔ ku bakpane bammɔ ƒui básiaku Yehoiada ulu ɔni na ɔ́tina ka babla ala basiaku mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na bagyumane bani na bana kabla káwɔlɔ muedi beeebo kuƒi ka batɔlɔ besie kɔduli. Anwuɔsu ɔtɔnkune biala ku nwuna kabla bablane bani náwɔlɔ kabla ku bɔwɔdi bani ndubo kabla kalɔ buse ƒui benye mmɔ bese.

english_verse: Jehoiada went into the temple and brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David, and he gave them to the commanders.
translation_verse: Na Yehoiada úduo kakpakɔ na útédie kuwi ku kekpo agyumanala ani na ndi Dawid adi mmɔ ɔ́lɛku keyi na úle-nya úte batɔnkune bammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: They gave the weapons to the guards, and Jehoiada then made sure that the guards took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect the king on every side.
translation_verse: Ama lɛnɔ béle-nya béte bagyumane bammɔ na Yehoiada ɔ́nu ka ɔdi biala unye kagyumana na kesii kani na ɔ́tina ka benye bamana kakpakɔ kammɔ ku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ ƒui kalɛ na bagyumana ɔga ɔmmɔ na lɛƒɛnyi ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: As soon as Queen Athaliah heard the crowd cheering for Joash, she went to the temple.
translation_verse: Amu ka beleku Ɔga Atalia únu ka bekyuli bammɔ béte yiiduu ku kɔvanu lɛni ni, ɔ́ta kɔnakunwi úsie kakpakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns near the entrance, which was the usual place for the king. The commanders and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the musicians were playing instruments and leading the people as they celebrated and blew trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
translation_verse: Na mmɔ na útánu ka Yoas unye lɛkpa lɛdi na lide kayakun kammɔ kudɔ kesii kani na kadi baga kenyekɔ mmɔ. Na bagyumanane batɔnkune ku kɔkpɛɛ bavwine benye-nwu kudɔ. Na bagyane ku lɛnu bediene batɔnku bekyuli bammɔ na baakɛ́ lɛlɔyɔ teedie lɛnu ku ebiti. Mmɔ na Atalia ɔ́ni nwuna lɛwu ɔ́bwɛ na kɔnyi kemmo na ɔ́va ɔ́su ɔnini, “Amii mina bekisine bɛ́lɛ-mi kama na bɛ́kya-mi kakya!”

english_verse: At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Don't kill her near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops, and be sure to kill all of her followers!”
translation_verse: Amu na Yehoiada údie lɛdi kɔnakunwi ɔ́su bagyumanane batɔnkune bɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Bitadu-nwu na Unwoti kakpakɔ kudɔ mmɔ. Bɛgyunku-nwu bɛlɛku bekpone bammɔ anumi na bɛnu ka bɛ́du nwuna kama basiakune lɛnɔ ƒui!”

english_verse: She tried to escape, but the commanders caught and killed her near the gate where horses are led into the palace.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́wia ulu ka nka ukeli, nsu batɔnkune bammɔ béƒie-nwu na bádu-nwu na ɔban kenye kesii kani na beeti bapɔnkɔ taasiaku teeduoku ɔga kesii mmɔ.

english_verse: Jehoiada asked King Joash and the people to join with him in being faithful to the Lord. They agreed,
translation_verse: Amu na Yehoiada úvele Ɔga Yoas ku bekyuli bakladi bammɔ ƒui ka bablaku-nwu unwi na basiaku Unwoti kama siin na basɔ balálɛ-nwu kama. Na bana ƒui bénu kalɔ

english_verse: then rushed to the temple of the god Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and the idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.
translation_verse: na bakɛ-nwu lisu kɔnakunwi békeli bésie bétébo Baal kakpakɔ ɔƒiɔtɔ bábwɛ béwi kalɔ. Na bábwɛ nwuna akpabi ammɔ ƒui ku ala ani na bávɔ bényene na bádu Baal ɔmmɔ ɔkpane ɔni baalɔ Matan na akpabi ammɔ anumi.

english_verse: Jehoiada assigned the priests and Levites their duties at the temple, just as David had done. They were in charge of offering sacrifices to the Lord according to the Law of Moses, and they were responsible for leading the celebrations with singing.
translation_verse: Amu na Yehoiada úle kabla úte bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ na kakpakɔ kemmo mmɔ kalɛ kani na Dawid ɔ́bla. Na mɔɔnu akpala bɔbla teete Unwoti ti kabla lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na Mose ɔda bubo bɔɔtina. Na ama kani na ɔlɛka batɔnku bɔkpa bɔmmɔ ablala ƒui ku lɛnɔ budie.

english_verse: Jehoiada ordered the guards at the temple gates to keep out anyone who was unclean.
translation_verse: Na úbo bagyumanane bani nnye ɔban kɔyakun kɔmmɔ ƒui kenye ka babɔku ukyuli biala na neeese sɛɛn ka uduo kakpakɔ kammɔ batɔlɔku.

english_verse: Finally, Jehoiada called together the army commanders, the most important citizens of Judah, and the government officials. The crowd of people followed them as they led Joash from the temple, through the Upper Gate, and into the palace, where he took his place as king of Judah.
translation_verse: Kawɔlɔkɔ ni, Yehoiada ɔ́lɔ bagyumanane batɔnkune bammɔ ku Yuda kadi benengu belidi belidi ku bakutine bammɔ ɔ́sala ku aban bagadine benengu bammɔ. Na bekyuli lisu lɛkladi lɛmmɔ basiaku-ma kama uwi ɔni na bákpanku Ɔga Yoas básiaku kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo na bátávi ɔban kayakun katɔdi kemmo bétéduoku ɔga kesii. Na mmɔ na útélie kalɔ na nwuna kesii aani Yudaƒuɔ ɔga.

english_verse: Joash and Jehoiada turned the money over to the men who were supervising the repairs to the temple. They used the money to hire stonecutters, carpenters, and experts in working with iron and bronze.
translation_verse: Na Yoas ku Yehoiada béti egulabi ammɔ béte bekyuli bani mɔɔnu kakpakɔ kammɔ bɔklibi ala lɛlɔ na béti báwia atabi banwine ku ligyii banwine ku abuala kpakplaa ku abuala egyiedi lɛlɔ kabla bablane babuni geen.

english_verse: and he was buried in the royal tombs in Jerusalem, because he had done so much good for the people of Israel, for God, and for the temple. Joash Turns Away from the Lord
translation_verse: Na báva-nwu na kɔƒiɔtɔ kɔni kemmo na baavá bagadine na Yerusalem, ɔsika ɔ́bla ɔdi úte Israelƒuɔ ku Katɔti ku kakpakɔ kammɔ ƒui. Yoas Únwini Kama Ɔ́kya Unwoti

english_verse: And now we need it to repair the temple because the sons of that evil woman Athaliah came in and wrecked it. They even used some of the sacred objects to worship the god Baal.”
translation_verse: Na ɔƒaani ni, bɔɔwia egulabi ammɔ kpakplaa na buti bɔklibi kakpakɔ kammɔ, ɔsika Atalia uleku ukpidi ɔmmɔ bebi bananabi bébeduo mɛni na bebile ala geen na mmɔ. Na béti ala ani na ese kedee muedi bátɔlɔku bésie baakpá Baal baƒiɔ.”

english_verse: Jehoiada even chose two women for Joash to marry so he could have a family.
translation_verse: Na Yehoiada ɔ́wia beleku inyɔ muedi úte-nwu ɔnii uti-ma kalɛ na udie kaba.

english_verse: Some time later, Joash decided it was time to repair the temple.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔdi kama ni, Yoas ɔ́bla kasusu ka uwi údu ka básɔku kakpakɔ kammɔ baklibi.

english_verse: He called together the priests and Levites and said, “Go everywhere in Judah and collect the annual tax from the people. I want this done at once—we need that money to repair the temple.” But the Levites were in no hurry to follow the king's orders.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔ́lɔ bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ɔ́sala na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Biteesie Yuda kalɔ kesi kesii na bitáƒɔ lɛkwa kuyii bɛsiku bekyuli bammɔ kudɔ biboku. Na mɔɔwia ka bɛbla ɔmmɔ ɔƒɛni kani ɔni na uwi bubile buuubo, ɔsika ɔlɛka bɔsɔku kakpakɔ kammɔ bɔklibi.” Nsu ɔmmɔ ƒui kama ni, Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bátababla na babla lɛla lɛni na ɔga ɔ́su-ma

english_verse: So he sent for Jehoiada the high priest and asked, “Why didn't you send the Levites to collect the taxes? The Lord's servant Moses and the people agreed long ago that this tax would be collected and used to pay for the upkeep of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́ya na bátálɔ Yehoiada béboku na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na átatala Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ na besie batáƒɔ lɛkwa kuyii kɔmmɔ beboku? Unwoti kabla ɔblane Mose ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bénu kalɔ ɔ́si kukuuku ƒui ka beteete kuyi kɔmɛni na beti-ku bataanu Katɔti kevo kammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Joash gave orders for a wooden box to be made and had it placed outside, near the gate of the temple.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Yoas údie lɛdi úte nwuna kabla bablane ɔnii banwi ugyii adaka ɔdi bese keyi bedenku kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔban kayakun.

english_verse: He then sent letters everywhere in Judah and Jerusalem, asking everyone to bring their taxes to the temple, just as Moses had required their ancestors to do.
translation_verse: Na únweni ɔku úmene Yuda kalɔ kesi kesii ɔnii ukyuli biala ubo ubaƒɔ nwuna kuyi na kakpakɔ mmɔ kalɛ kani na Mose úbo bana bati kuuku ɔda ɔnii bataabala.

english_verse: The people and their leaders agreed, and they brought their money to Jerusalem and placed it in the box.
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bammɔ ku bana batɔnkune ƒui bénu kalɔ na béti bana kuyi béboku Yerusalem bábakya adaka ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Each day, after the Levites took the box into the temple, the king's secretary and the high priest's assistant would dump out the money and count it. Then the empty box would be taken back outside. This happened day after day, and soon a large amount of money was collected.
translation_verse: Na limeyi ndi limeyi ni, Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ beeti adaka ɔmmɔ teeduoku kakpakɔ ɔtɔ kemmo na bewilimi egulabi ammɔ bewi ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔku unwenine ku ɔkpane ɔmmɔ ubunkune anumi na baka-nwu na basɔku adaka ɔmmɔ betése keyi na kesii kani na beesé-nwu mmɔ. Lɛni na bátaabla limeyi ndi limeyi na uwi útetu asa na bákɛ egulabi pii.

english_verse: These workers went right to work repairing the temple, and when they were finished, it looked as good as new.
translation_verse: Amu na bése kakpakɔ kammɔ bɔklibi kalɔ na uwi ɔni na báwɔlɔ ni, kakpakɔ kammɔ kábla aani si kawɔdi na básɔku bátu.

english_verse: They did not use all the tax money for the repairs, so the rest of it was handed over to Joash and Jehoiada, who then used it to make dishes and other gold and silver objects for the temple. Sacrifices to please the Lord were offered regularly in the temple for as long as Jehoiada lived.
translation_verse: Na ɔɔɔdi egulabi ammɔ ƒui na béti bábla kabla kammɔ, anwuɔsu egulabi ani nébu ni, béti-nya béte Yoas ku Yehoiada na ama lɛnɔ béti béte na bábla kakpakɔ sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi akyami lidu lidu bese kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo. Na uwi ɔni ƒui na ɔkpane Yehoiada úlie ngba ƒui ni, bátaabla ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni mɔɔyɔ́ Katɔti kaƒɔ akpala bɔkyula ɔdi teete Unwoti limeyi ndi limeyi.

english_verse: He died at the ripe old age of
translation_verse: Na úlie ngba útu uwi geen na ɔ́ƒɔ akwa eti anyɔ ku avlaatɛ asa na úkpi.

english_verse: After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the leaders of Judah went to Joash and talked him into doing what they wanted.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na Yehoiada úkpi ni, Yudaƒuɔ batɔnkune bammɔ bésie bátátɔlɔ Yoas mini mini na ɔ́tunaku-ma ka ɔbla lɛla lɛni na baawia.

english_verse: The people of Judah soon stopped worshiping in the temple of the Lord God and started worshiping idols and the symbols of the goddess Asherah. These sinful things made the Lord God angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bétebile uwi ɔdi munu munu asa na báda Unwoti Katɔti bɔkpa báya na nwuna kakpakɔ na bése kalɔ baakpa ala ani na bávɔ béte Asera baƒiɔ beledi bammɔ. Na ɔkɛnku ɔmɛni ɔsu Unwoti Katɔti úti kɔnyi kpakplaa ɔ́kya Yudaƒuɔ ku Yerusalemƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: but he still sent prophets who warned them to turn back to him. The people refused to listen.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmmɔ ƒui kama ni, Unwoti ɔmu uumene-ma nwuna kenye bediene kalɛ na batálɛ-ma na benwini bebo-nwu kudɔ, nsu béni na bátaƒɔ-ma litemi.

english_verse: God's Spirit spoke to Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and Zechariah told everyone that God was saying: “Why are you disobeying me and my laws? This will only bring punishment! You have deserted me, so now I will desert you.”
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti Kɔyu kútemiku Yehoiada ubidi ɔnanabi Sakaria na ɔ́sɔku ɔ́su ukyuli biala ka kɔyu kɔmmɔ kɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na bíni na bɛɛbla atuɔkplu na mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ? Lɛtuni kani bɛɛni teewi bina lɛlɔ! Bídie-mi atu, anwuɔsu ami lɛnɔ ndubo-mii atu budie.”

english_verse: King Joash forgot that Zechariah's father had always been a loyal friend. So when the people of Judah plotted to kill Zechariah, Joash joined them and gave orders for them to stone him to death in the courtyard of the temple. As Zechariah was dying, he said, “I pray that the Lord will see this and punish all of you.” Joash Is Killed
translation_verse: Ɔga Yoas ɔ́ɔyiƒala ka Sakaria ɔmɛni ɔti Yehoiada ni, anwu ku-nwu bádi bɔkpana babuni geen. Anwuɔsu uwi ɔni na bekyuli bammɔ bátása lili likpidi Sakaria lɛlɔ ka badu-nwu ni, anwu lɛnɔ únu ku-ma kalɔ na udie lɛdi ka bebo-nwu atabi badu na kakpakɔ kaduli kemmo mmɔ. Amu na uwi ɔni na Sakaria ɔdaku bɔyula ni, ɔ́su ɔnini, “Muuvele Unwoti nnii ɔnu lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́ mɛni na ɔni bina ƒui kɔtu.” Bádu Yoas

english_verse: In the spring of the following year, the Syrian army invaded Judah and Jerusalem, killing all of the nation's leaders. They collected everything of value that belonged to the people and took it back to their king in Damascus.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛkwa lɛni nsia ketudi uwi ni, Siriaƒuɔ báta bébekpo Yuda ku Yerusalem na bádu bana batɔnkune bammɔ ƒui. Na béti bana ala ani náƒɔ-ma kuye mmɔ ƒui bátɔlɔku bésienku bana ɔga na Damasko.

english_verse: The Syrian army was very small, but the Lord let them defeat Judah's large army, because he was punishing Joash and the people of Judah for turning away from him.
translation_verse: Siriaƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ beeemomo munu munu, nsu Unwoti ɔ́ya na bádi Yudaƒuɔ bekpone pii bammɔ lɛlɔ, ɔsika Yoas ku Yudaƒuɔ bammɔ geen na Unwoti ɔɔwia ɔni kɔtu na kalɛ na bénwini kama bákya-nwu ɔsu.

english_verse: Joash was severely wounded during the battle, and as soon as the Syrians left Judah, two of his officials, Zabad and Jehozabad, decided to revenge the death of Zechariah. They plotted and killed Joash while he was in bed, recovering from his wounds. Joash was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs.
translation_verse: Amu na kekpo kammɔ kemmo ni, Yoas ɔ́ƒɔ ɔlɛ geen na uwi ɔni kani na Siriaƒuɔ bammɔ bátɔlɔ ni, nwuna bakutine inyɔ badi bani ndi Sabad ku Yehosabad bábla kasusu ka bedie Sakaria kukpi kasi. Anwuɔsu ka Yoas ɔdaku bɔnwanya na ɔtɛ limeyi linwi ni, bésie na bátádu-nwu. Na báva-nwu na Yerusalem, nsu ɔɔɔdi kɔni kemmo na baavá bana bagadine bammɔ.

english_verse: The History of the Kings also tells more about the sons of Joash, what the prophets said about him, and how he repaired the temple. Amaziah son of Joash became king after his father's death.
translation_verse: Na baga bammɔ ablala ku bana uwi ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo ni, bénweni ala básiku nwuna bebi lɛlɔ ku ala ani na kenye bediene básu-nwu ku kalɛ na ɔ́klibi kakpakɔ kammɔ etemila bákya bébu. Na Yoas ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Amasia úbenwini ɔga na ɔti kukpi kama.

english_verse: One of God's prophets said, “Your Majesty, don't let these Israelite soldiers march into battle with you. The Lord has refused to help anyone from the northern kingdom of Israel,
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti kenye bediene bammɔ akɔ unwi ɔ́su ɔnini, “Mina Ɔga Ɔbune, taya na Israelƒuɔ bekpone bamɛni besie basiaku-ɔ besie kekpokɔ, ɔsika bana lɛgakɔdikɔ kɔni na kɔkya katɔ kakɛ mmɔ ƒui ni, Katɔti úni ka ute bana akɔ ukyuli ɔdi kebunku.

english_verse: Amaziah replied, “What am I supposed to do about all the silver I paid those troops?” “The Lord will give you back even more than you paid,” the prophet answered.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Amasia údie kenye na úye kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Na dɛ na ndubo bɔbla asa na masɔ makɛ mina sika ɔƒualadi ɔni ƒui na líti lɛƒɔ kayu na Israelƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ lili?” Amu na Katɔti kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Unwoti ɔdubɔkana na ɔsɔku sika ɔmmɔ ute-ɔ utulo ɔni na éti áƒɔ kayu kammɔ muedi.”

english_verse: But before the prophet finished speaking, Amaziah interrupted and said, “You're not one of my advisors! Don't say another word, or I'll have you killed.” The prophet stopped. But then he added, “First you sinned and now you've ignored my warning. It's clear that God has decided to punish you!” Israel Defeats Judah (
translation_verse: Nsu kenye udiene ɔmmɔ útawɔlɔ tɔ lɛla lɛni na uuye asa na Ɔga Amasia ɔ́tu-nwu kenye ɔnini, “Aaadi mina kasusu bakyane akɔ ɔdi! Anwuɔsu si aaagyi na ásɔ ébimi kenye ásu lɛla lɛdi ɔƒɛni ni, ndubɔya na badu-ɔ.” Mmɔ kani na kenye udiene ɔmmɔ ɔ́da butemi ɔ́ya. Nsu ɔ́su ɔ́sia ɔnini, “Katɔti úse ka ɔyila-a udu geen! Ɔsika kudeedi ni, ábla likpidi na ásɔ éni mina bɔlɛ.” Israel Ɔ́di Yuda Lɛlɔ

english_verse: King Amaziah of Judah talked with his officials, then sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
translation_verse: Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Amasia ku nwuna bakutine benengu bábla kelisa na ɔ́kya Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Yehoas ɔni ndi Yehu ubidi ɔnanabi ɔtu ɔnini, “Klibi lɛlɔ na ebo na ami ku-ɔ bɔsa anumi ku anumi na kekpokɔ!”

english_verse: Jehoash sent back a reply that said: Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon arranged the marriage between his son and the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yehoas lɛnɔ ɔ́sɔku ɔtu ɔ́kya-nwu úmene ɔnini, “Dii ni, liyu alakpi adi na Lebanon ákya kugyii bonwu kpakplaa kɔdi na Lebanon mmɔ kani ɔtu ɔnii, ‘Mɔɔwia ka eti ƒ'ubidi ulekubi ete-mi na lite mina ɔnanabi na uti.’ Nsu alakpi akɔ ebuo bonwu ɔdi úbo na úbanya liyu alakpi ammɔ úsusu ɔ́mana kalɔ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. But stay at home and do your celebrating. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Amasia, aanu lɛlɔ ka ebo ɔyikun geen ka ékpo ádi Edomƒuɔ lɛlɔ ɔsu. Sɔ lie ƒula ɔma na ataakɛ ƒula kubiti. Bi ɔsu na aawia lɛlɔ lɛsɛ na adubo bɔya na awɔ ku ƒula Yuda lɛgakadikɔ ƒui bɛyii ku udu?”

english_verse: so Jehoash led his army to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Yehoas ɔ́tɔnku nwuna bekpone na anwu ku Amasia bekpone bása na Bet-Semes na Yuda kalɔ kemmo.

english_verse: During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home,
translation_verse: Na bésusu Yudaƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ kaduɛ na bábɔku-ma na békeli bénwini bésie ɔma ƒui kede kede

english_verse: and Jehoash captured Amaziah. Jehoash took Amaziah with him when he went to attack Jerusalem. Jehoash broke down the city wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, a section nearly
translation_verse: na Yehoas úƒie Amasia. Amu na uwi ɔni Yehoas úsie utábwɛ Yerusalem ni, ɔ́kpanku Amasia ɔni na úƒie na kekpokɔ ɔda. Na Yehoas ɔ́bwɛ awodu bonwu ani na bátu bámana ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔ́si kesii kani baalɔ Eƒraim ɔban kenye útédu kesii bamba kani baalɔ banii Okodo ɔban kenye. Na mmɔ bune ɔdubɔdi lɛgba eti leevu-anyɔ.

english_verse: He carried away the gold, the silver, and all the valuable furnishings from God's temple where the descendants of Obed-Edom stood guard. He robbed the king's treasury, took hostages, then returned to Samaria. Amaziah Is Killed (
translation_verse: Na kesii kani geen na Obed-Edom kaba kemmo bebi beenye taagyumana mmɔ geen na ɔ́ya na béti sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ku ala bamba ani na áƒɔ kuye geen mmɔ na ese Katɔti kakpakɔ mmɔ bátalɔku ƒui kede kede. Na egulabi ani na ese Ɔga egulabi kesekɔ mmɔ ku ala bamba na úƒie bekyuli bamba lɛnɔ na ɔ́tɔlɔku-ma ƒui úsienku Samaria kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Everything else Amaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani ƒui na Amasia ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla na nwuna lɛga bɔdi uwi ni, bénweni ana ƒui bákya Yudaƒuɔ baga ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: As soon as Amaziah started disobeying the Lord, some people in Jerusalem plotted against Amaziah. He was able to escape to the town of Lachish, but another group of people caught him and killed him there.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni kani na Amasia úse kalɔ ɔɔta teenye Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ ni, bekyuli badi na Yerusalem mmɔ bása lili na Amasia lɛlɔ. Nsu Amasia úbati na ɔ́wia kuƒi na úkeli úsie ɔma ɔni baalɔ Lakis kemmo, nsu kasala bamba báwia-nwu kama ulu na bátánu-nwu béƒie na bádu-nwu na mmɔ.

english_verse: His body was taken to Jerusalem on horseback and buried beside his ancestors.
translation_verse: Bágyu-nwu ukpine básia ɔpɔnkɔ lɛlɔ bésienku Yerusalem bátáva kesii kani na nwuna nana ati bene batɛ.

english_verse: Uzziah supplied his army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and stones used for slinging.
translation_verse: Usia úte bekpone bamɛni kayi agyumanala ku atula ku kekpo kɔbwa ku agyumanala bamba kɔtaminta ku kavwinvwi atabi.

english_verse: Uzziah had leprosy the rest of his life. He was no longer allowed in the temple or in his own palace. That's why his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
translation_verse: Na ɔlɛ buɛ ɔmɛni úbaƒɔ Usia lɛlɔ ƒui nwuna ngba emeyi akladi ƒui kemmo. Anwuɔsu básɔ bétete-nwu kuƒi ka uduo kakpakɔ mmɔ iye ɔga kesii mmɔ muedi mmomu úlie kesii bamba. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na ubidi Yonatan na béti bése-nwu kenye aani ɔga kalɛ.

english_verse: Everything else Uzziah did while he was king is in the records written by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani ƒui na Usia ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla na nwuna lɛga bɔdi uwi ni, bénweni-nya bákya Kenye Udiene Yesaia ɔni ndi Amos ubidi ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: Some of his skilled workers invented machines that could shoot arrows and sling large stones. Uzziah set these up in Jerusalem at his defense towers and at the corners of the city wall. God helped Uzziah become more and more powerful, and he was famous all over the world. Uzziah Becomes Too Proud
translation_verse: Na nwuna bakywɛɛne babuni bani na ubo ku kabla lidu bamba bablane bani na bebo kasusu geen béti abuala bábla ekpola ani alati mɔɔkana na eebó atula ku atabi taasiaku bekisine. Na Usia úti abuala amɛni ɔ́lɛ Yerusalem na kesii kani bene na ɔ́tu ɔma kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa kɔmmɔ únyene mmɔ. Katɔti ɔ́ya na Usia ɔyikun ku lɛnyi lɛ́ku lísie ɔgyu geen na kɔlɔ ƒui bekyuli akɔ.

english_verse: God helped him defeat the Philistines, the Arabs living in Gur-Baal, and the Meunites.
translation_verse: Katɔti úbunku-nwu na ɔ́di Ƒilistiƒuɔ ku Arabiaƒuɔ bani na bakya Gur-Baal ku Meunite mmɔ bene ƒui.

english_verse: After the death of King Amaziah, the people of Judah crowned his son Uzziah king, even though he was only
translation_verse: Akwa leevu-aku na Usia ɔ́ƒɔ asa na bése-nwu lɛga. Na úlie liboku lɛlɔ akwa liti ku inyɔ. Uni na baalɔ banii Yekolia na ɔ́si Yerusalem.

english_verse: Uzziah became proud of his power, and this led to his downfall. One day, Uzziah disobeyed the Lord his God by going into the temple and burning incense as an offering to him.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔyikun ɔni na úbakɛ mɛni ku kalɛ na nwuna lɛnyi lísie ɔgyu ɔsu ni, Usia úse kalɔ ɔɔkɔliku lɛlɔ katɔ na ɔmmɔ náya-nwu na úbo kalɔ. Limeyi linwi ni, Usia útenu Unwoti nwuna Katɔti litemi na ɔ́ta útéduo kakpakɔ na úsie útéti oloƒui ɔdi ɔɔkyula aani akpala ute-nwu.

english_verse: He obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done.
translation_verse: Únu Katɔti litemi na ɔ́di-ni lɛlɔ na ɔɔbla ala ulu lɛlɔ aani kalɛ ɔti ɔ́bla.

english_verse: Zechariah was Uzziah's advisor and taught him to obey God. And so, as long as Zechariah was alive, Uzziah was faithful to God, and God made him successful.
translation_verse: Sakaria ndi ukyuli ɔni nátina Usia ala na ɔ́tina-nwu kalɛ na unu Katɔti litemi na ɔdi-ni lɛlɔ lɛnɔ. Anwuɔsu uwi ɔni kemmo na Sakaria úlie ngba ƒui ni, Usia útaadi Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ kaduɛ na Katɔti lɛnɔ ɔ́ya na ala átɛku-nwu.

english_verse: While Uzziah was king, he started a war against the Philistines. He smashed the walls of the cities of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, then rebuilt towns around Ashdod and in other parts of Philistia.
translation_verse: Na Usia lɛga bɔdi uwi ni, útékpo Ƒilistiƒuɔ na ɔ́bwɛ bana lɛma lɛni ndi Gat ku Yabne ku Asdod lɛma awodu ani na bátu bámana-ni. Na ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́sɔku lɛma bamba ɔ́tu na Asdod amadɔ mmɔ ku ekpo bamba ka Ƒilistiƒuɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Even the Ammonites paid taxes to Uzziah. He became very powerful, and people who lived as far away as Egypt heard about him.
translation_verse: Na Amonƒuɔ muedi bátaaƒɔ lɛlɔ ɔdine kuyi teete Usia aani nwuna kalɔ bakyane kalɛ. Nwuna lɛnyi ku ɔyikun ɔni na ubo úsie ɔgyu geen ɔni na Egyipteƒuɔ bani na bakya ɔgyu kakaaka muedi bénu-nwu kɔku.

english_verse: In Jerusalem, Uzziah built fortified towers at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the place where the city wall turned inward.
translation_verse: Usia ɔ́tu ɔma kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa únyene Yerusalem na Okodo ɔban kenye ku Kɔwɛ ɔban kenye ku kesii kani na bátu kowodu kɔmmɔ béduoku aani kekpokpo.

english_verse: He also built defense towers out in the desert. He owned such a large herd of livestock in the western foothills and in the flatlands, that he had cisterns dug there to catch the rainwater. He loved farming, so he had crops and vineyards planted in the hill country wherever there was fertile soil, and he hired farmers to take care of them.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́tu kɔgyumanakɔ bamba únyene kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ kemmo. Na ubo bebuo na bemomo-nwu geen na bakya abi ammɔ kaƒɔna ku kalɔ ƒiaa kani nwi mmɔ kemmo lɛnɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔ́ya na bátu abiɔ lɛnɔ na emomo kalɛ na utaaƒɔ ntu teete-ma uwi biala kemmo. Na ka ɔɔyɔ́ kemo busie ɔsu ni, ubo edula ku adingyii lidu mmo geen na abi lɛlɔ kesii kani na kalɔ kammɔ kadia geen ƒui na ɔ́ƒɔ bekyuli ɔ́kya mmɔ na baanu mmo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ na ɔɔƒɔ-ma kayu.

english_verse: Uzziah's army was always ready for battle. Jeiel and Maaseiah were the officers who kept track of the number of soldiers, and these two men were under the command of Hananiah, one of Uzziah's officials.
translation_verse: Usia bekpone benye kagyumana bete kekpo uwi biala. Na Yeiel ku Maaseia ndi bakutine benengu bani mɔɔnu bekpone bammɔ bumomo bɔka lɛlɔ ala uwi biala. Na nkyuli inyɔ bamɛni lɛnɔ bakya Usia benengu akɔ unwi ɔni na baalɔ banii Hanania kalɔ.

english_verse: and said, “Your Majesty, this isn't right! You are not allowed to burn incense to the Lord. That must be done only by priests who are descendants of Aaron. You will have to leave! You have sinned against the Lord, and so he will no longer bless you.”
translation_verse: Béye-nwu etemila geen na básu-nwu banini, “Ɔɔɔdi ulu ka ɔbla lɛla lɛni udu na aabla mɛni, ɔsika Aaron bebi bani na bése likpo aani bakpane kani na ɔlɛka babla bɔkyula ɔdi ɔmɛni udu. Anwuɔsu ɔlɛka avi alɛ mɛni! Ábla likpidi áƒiɔ Unwoti ɔni na nwuna kusɛ kusɛ ɔsɔ ɔɔɔdubo-ɔ bɔsiaku.”

english_verse: Uzziah, who was standing next to the incense altar at the time, was holding the incense burner, ready to offer incense to the Lord. He became very angry when he heard Azariah's warning, and leprosy suddenly appeared on his forehead!
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, Usia ɔda oloƒui libui lɛmmɔ unye ka use kalɔ ku oloƒui ɔmmɔ bɔkyula asa na Ɔkpane Asaria ɔɔdɔnku-nwu na ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi geen. Na uwi ɔni na kɔnyi kɔmmɔ kɔɔkɔ́-nwu lɛni ni, ɔlɛ buɛ ɔdi ɔ́lɛ-nwu atɛntɛ.

english_verse: Azariah and the other priests saw it and immediately told him to leave the temple. Uzziah realized that the Lord had punished him, so he hurried to get outside.
translation_verse: Na Asaria ku bakpane bakladi bánu ɔmɛni báti kɔnakunwi na básu banii ɔvi ɔlɛ kakpakɔ mmɔ. Usia ɔlati ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka Unwoti náni-nwu kɔtu, anwuɔsu ɔ́babla ka ɔvi ɔlɛ mmɔ.

english_verse: Since Uzziah had leprosy, he could not be buried in the royal tombs. Instead, he was buried in a nearby cemetery that the kings owned. His son Jotham then became king.
translation_verse: Na ɔlɛ buɛ ɔni na Usia úƒi ɔsu ni, bátakana na bava-nwu na baga katɛnkɔ mmomu bátáva-nwu na bekyuli kavakɔ kalɔ bamba kani na baga bammɔ kani béye bése. Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, bése ubidi Yonatan lɛga.

english_verse: Jotham obeyed the Lord and did right. He followed the example of his father Uzziah, except he never burned incense in the temple as his father had done. But the people of Judah kept sinning against the Lord.
translation_verse: Yonatan úlie ngba bɔbuni aani ɔti kalɛ, nsu anwu útetéduo kakpakɔ mmɔ kudii ɔnii ɔɔkyula oloƒui kalɛ na ɔti ɔ́bla dii mmɔ. Mmomu bekyuli bammɔ ala bana likyulikpi ala ani na baabla taata teenye Katɔti lɛlɔ kani nátakɔsi.

english_verse: Jotham remained faithful to the Lord his God and became a very powerful king.
translation_verse: Yonatan ɔ́siaku Unwoti Katɔti kama siin na úbenwini ɔga ɔyikune geen.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king, including the wars he fought, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani ƒui na Yonatan ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla ku kekpo kani ƒui na úkpo na nwuna lɛga bɔdi uwi ni, bénweni-nya bákya Israel ku Yudaƒuɔ baga alɛ alɛdi ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: He was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: Báva-nwu na Yerusalem na ubidi Ahas nébenwini ɔga.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees. Syria and Israel Attack Judah (
translation_verse: Ahas ɔ́kɛ ekpo ekpo ƒui ɔɔkyula oloƒui na aƒiodu ani nkya abi eli ku egyii enengudi ani mbo ɔyuli kalɔ.

english_verse: and he offered sacrifices in Hinnom Valley. Worst of all, Ahaz sacrificed his own sons, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
translation_verse: Ɔ́bla akpala úte ala bamba na kesii kani baalɔ banii Ben-Hinom Kɔwɛ kemmo. Na ɔni na utulo ƒui ndi ɔni na ɔsiaku kadi bamba ɔbladu kama na úti ubidi ɔnanabi ɔ́kyula ɔ́kpa. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdi lɛla lɛni muusé Katɔti lɛlɔ geen. Anwuɔsu na ɔ́bɔku-ma ɔ́lɛku Israel kɔlɔ kemmo.

english_verse: If you make slaves of the people of Judah and Jerusalem, you will be as guilty as they are of sinning against the Lord.
translation_verse: Na si bíti Yudaƒuɔ ku Yerusalemƒuɔ bínwini bina kabla bablane ni, amii lɛnɔ bɛ́bla likpidi aani kalɛ na ama bábla báƒiɔ Unwoti.

english_verse: Send these prisoners back home—they are your own relatives. If you don't, the Lord will punish you in his anger.
translation_verse: Bɛsɔku bekyuli beƒiedi bammɔ bimene bana ɔma, ɔsika bina lɛlɔ bekyuli kani na badi. Na si bítabla ɔmɛni ni, Unwoti ɔdubo-mii kɔtu bɔni ku kɔnyi geen.”

english_verse: About the same time, four of Israel's leaders arrived. They were Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai. They agreed with Oded that the Israelite troops were wrong,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni kani na benye baasu ɔmɛni ni, Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune ine badi báda bábalɛ. Na ama ndi Yohanan ubidi Asaria ku Mesilemot ubidi Berekia ku Salum ubidi Yehiskia ku Hadlai ubidi Amasa. Na ama lɛnɔ bénu kalɔ ka lɛla lɛni a Israelƒuɔ bekpone bammɔ bábla ni, lɛɛɛdia sɔsɔ.

english_verse: and they said: If you bring these prisoners into Samaria, that will be one more thing we've done to sin against the Lord. And he is already angry enough with us.
translation_verse: Na básu lɛnɔ banini, “Si bíti bekyuli bamɛni bíboku Samaria ni, ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔdubɔsɔ unwini likpidi bamba lɛni na bɔ́bla bɔ́ƒiɔ Unwoti. Ɔsika bɔ́ɔbla ala pii bɔ́ƒiɔ Unwoti na nwuna kɔnyi kɔsia-bu lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: So in front of the leaders and the crowd, the troops handed over their prisoners and the property they had taken from Judah.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na bɔtɔnkune bammɔ ku bekyuli bakladi anumi ni, bekpone bammɔ bányonu beƒiene bammɔ ku ala ani ƒui na béti bátɔlɔku Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: The four leaders took some of the stolen clothes and gave them to the prisoners who needed something to wear. They later gave them all a new change of clothes and shoes, then fixed them something to eat and drink, and cleaned their wounds with olive oil. They gave donkeys to those who were too weak to walk, and led all of them back to Jericho, the city known for its palm trees. The leaders then returned to Samaria. Ahaz Asks the King of Assyria for Help (
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu batɔnkune bammɔ béti adi awɔdi ku lɛgbanvuo ku adila béte bekyuli bani mɔɔyaki adi na bényimi-ma lɛlɛ ku nnɔmii. Na bani na bábla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ni, bágyu-ma básia bebuo ala betine lɛlɔ na bákpanku bana ƒui básɔku bésienku bana banwani kudɔ na Yeriko kesii kani na ebo akya geen. Ɔmmɔ kama na batɔnkune bammɔ bénwini bébo Samaria.

english_verse: Ahaz gave him gifts from the Lord's temple and the king's palace, as well as from the homes of Israel's other leaders. The Assyrian king still refused to help Ahaz. The Final Sin of Ahaz and His Death
translation_verse: Na Ahas úti etela ɔ́siku Unwoti kakpakɔ ku ɔga kesii mmɔ ku Israelƒuɔ benengu bamba kɔduli úmene-nwu, nsu Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔmɛni úni ka ubunku Ahas. Likpidi Likplodi Lɛni Na Ahas Ɔ́bla Ku Nwuna Kukpi

english_verse: Even after all these terrible things happened to Ahaz, he sinned against the Lord even worse than before.
translation_verse: Ala enengudi ani nálɛku Ahas mɛni ƒui kama ni, ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla alaekpidi enengudi ani nébie etulo kudeedi ƒui ɔ́ƒiɔ Unwoti.

english_verse: He said to himself, “The Syrian gods must have helped their kings defeat me. Maybe if I offer sacrifices to those gods, they will help me.” That was the sin that finally led to the downfall of Ahaz, as well as to the destruction of Judah.
translation_verse: Ɔ́su lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Use-mi aani Siriaƒuɔ baƒiɔ bamɛni nébunku-ma ɔsu na bákana-mi lɛlɔ bɔdi. Anwuɔsu ɔƒɛni kalɛ si lɛ́bla akpala líte-ma ni, badubɔkana na bebunku-mi.” Ɔmmɔ ndi likpidi likplodi lɛni na Ahas ɔ́bla na lítiku-nwu lítákya kukpi kemmo ku Yuda bekyuli udu bɔyii.

english_verse: Ahaz collected all the furnishings of the temple and smashed them to pieces. Then he locked the doors to the temple and set up altars to foreign gods on every street corner in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ala ani ƒui na bánwi bése kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo ni, Ahas útiku-nya ɔ́lɛku na útáƒɛ-nya ekuku ekuku na ɔ́kalɛ kakpakɔ kammɔ únyene. Ɔmmɔ kama na úsie útátu akpabi ɔ́lɛ lilu ƒui lɛlɔ na Yerusalem úte kadi bamba baƒiɔ.

english_verse: In every city and town in Judah he built local shrines to worship foreign gods. All of this made the Lord God of his ancestors very angry.
translation_verse: Na lɛma linengudi ku lɛma lɛkladi ƒui kemmo na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, Ahas ɔ́tu baƒiɔ ɔ́mana kalɛ na bekyuli bataakpa. Na ala amɛni bene ƒui náya na Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi geen.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Na ala bamba ani ƒui na Ahas ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-nya bákya Yudaƒuɔ ku Israelƒuɔ baga ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. His son Hezekiah then became king.
translation_verse: Ahas úbekpi na báva na Yerusalem, nsu ɔɔɔdi baga kɔƒiɔtɔ kemmo. Na ɔmmɔ kama bése ubidi Hesekia lɛga na nwuna kenyekɔ.

english_verse: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord by doing right, just as his ancestor David had done. The Temple Is Purified
translation_verse: Hesekia únu Unwoti litemi na ɔ́siaku-nwu kama siin aani nwuna nana ati Dawid kalɛ. Básɔku Kakpakɔ Kammɔ Bábla Kedee

english_verse: they went back to Hezekiah and said: Your Majesty, we have finished our work. The entire temple is now pure again, and so is the altar and its utensils, as well as the table for the sacred loaves of bread and its utensils.
translation_verse: bénwini bésie Ɔga Hesekia kudɔ na bátásu-nwu banini, “Ɔga Ɔbune, bɔ́wɔlɔ bula kabla na kakpakɔ kammɔ ƒui kese sɛɛn. Na Katɔti lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ku ebui ku akyami ammɔ ƒui ku bodobodo kedee ɔmmɔ kasiakɔ ka akyami ani kemmo na beeƒí-nwu mmɔ bene ƒui ese sɛɛn.

english_verse: Next, Hezekiah assigned the Levites to their places in the temple. He gave them cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments, according to the instructions that the Lord had given King David and the two prophets, Gad and Nathan.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Hesekia ɔ́ya na Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bésie béténye bana kunyekɔ na bana kabla kenye na kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo. Na úti enukpɛ agyala ku lɛbentaa ku agyala bamba ani na béti kɔbuli bábla úte-ma aani kalɛ na Unwoti úbo Ɔga Dawid ku kenye bediene bani ndi Gad ku Natan ɔda kalɛ.

english_verse: After that, Hezekiah and the crowd of worshipers bowed down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Hesekia ku kasalakɔ bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bálɛ akɔnkɔ kalɔ na bákya lili kalɔ béte Unwoti.

english_verse: Then he called the priests and Levites to the east courtyard of the temple
translation_verse: Na ɔ́ya na bálɔ bakpane bammɔ ku lewiƒuɔ bammɔ usienku kakpakɔ kaduli kani na kewi késie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: and said: It's time to purify the temple of the Lord God of our ancestors. You Levites must first go through the ceremony to make yourselves clean, then go into the temple and bring out everything that is unclean and unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Uwi údu ka bɔsɔku bula bati kuuku Unwoti Katɔti kakpakɔ bɔbla kedee. Na amii Lewiƒuɔ na ɔdi ka bɛka lɛlɔ bɔbla kedee ɔdi ɔmmɔ bɔbla kalɛ na biduo kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo na bitéti ala ani ƒui muusé lɛlɔ na Katɔti ulawia-nya ulanu mmɔ bɛlɛku.

english_verse: Some of our ancestors were unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord our God. Not only did they turn their backs on the Lord, but they also completely ignored his temple.
translation_verse: Bula bati kuuku badi ɔbladu útadia bɔnu munu munu, ɔsika bátasiaku-nwu kama siin. Na ɔɔɔdi ɔmmɔ lɛti mmomu béni Katɔti kakpakɔ muedi ƒui kede kede.

english_verse: They locked the doors, then let the lamps go out and stopped burning incense and offering sacrifices to him.
translation_verse: Bákalɛ kakpakɔ kammɔ bényene na lɛsogya lɛmmɔ ƒui líni. Na basɔ balákyula oloƒui ɔdi iye babla akpala adi bete Katɔti lɛnɔ.

english_verse: The Lord became terribly angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and everyone was shocked and horrified at what he did to punish them. Not only were
translation_verse: “Kɔnyi kpakplaa geen na Katɔti úti ɔ́kya Yuda kadi bekyuli ku Yerusalemƒuɔ. Na ala ani ƒui na ɔ́bla úti ɔ́ni-ma kɔtu adi liƒu ala geen ete bekyuli bani nánu ala amɛni kalɛkɔ. Na ɔɔɔdi

english_verse: our ancestors killed in battle, but our own children and wives were taken captive.
translation_verse: bukpi kani na bula bati kuuku békpi na kekpokɔ, mmomu béƒie abu alati bula bebi ku beleku lɛnɔ bátɔlɔku.

english_verse: So I have decided to renew our agreement with the Lord God of Israel. Maybe then he will stop being so angry with us.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu lɛ́lɛ ugyii geen ka bɔsɔku abu ku Israel Unwoti Katɔti ntɛ bunyimi bɔbla ɔwɔdi. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ si bɔ́bla ɔmɛni ni, nwuna kɔnyi na bula lɛlɔ kɔdubɔyɔ-nwu.

english_verse: Let's not waste any time, my friends. You are the ones who were chosen to be the Lord's priests and to offer him sacrifices.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ni, banwa, bitaya na bubile uwi. Amii na Unwoti ɔ́ƒuna ka bɛbla nwuna bakpane na biti akpala bite-nwu.”

english_verse: When Hezekiah finished talking, the following Levite leaders went to work: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah from the Kohath clan; Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel from the Merari clan; Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah from the Gershon clan; Shimri and Jeuel from the Elizaphan clan; Zechariah and Mattaniah from the Asaph clan; Jehuel and Shimei from the Heman clan; Shemaiah and Uzziel from the Jeduthun clan.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na Hesekia ɔ́wɔlɔ-ma bɔtɛmiku ni, Lewiƒuɔ batɔnkune bani nsia bésie mmɔ bése kabla kalɔ kɔnakunwi. Na bana anyi ndubo mɛni. Amasai ubidi Mahat ku Asaria ubidi Yoel bani nási Kohat kɔdua kemmo. Na Abdi ubidi Kis ku Yehalel ubidi Asaria ama lɛnɔ bási Merari kɔdua kemmo. Na Sima ubidi Yoa ku Yoa ubidi Eden ama lɛnɔ bási Gerson kɔdua kemmo. Na Simri ku Yeuel bási Elsaƒan kɔdua. Na Sekaria ku Matania ama bási Asaƒ kɔdua. Na Yehuel ku Simei bási Heman kɔdua. Na Semaia ku Usiel bási Yedutun kɔdua.

english_verse: These leaders gathered together the rest of the Levites, and they all went through the ceremony to make themselves clean. Then they began to purify the temple according to the Law of the Lord, just as Hezekiah had commanded.
translation_verse: Batɔnkune bamɛni bátásala Lewiƒuɔ bakladi na bana ƒui bábla lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ kalɛ na bese sɛɛn. Na ɔmmɔ kama bése kalɔ baabla kakpakɔ kammɔ lɛnɔ kedee ɔkɛnku Unwoti ɔda bubo kenye aani kalɛ na Ɔga Hesekia úbo ɔda kalɛ.

english_verse: The priests went into the temple and carried out everything that was unclean. They put these things in the courtyard, and from there, the Levites carried them outside the city to Kidron Valley.
translation_verse: Bakpane bammɔ béduo kakpakɔ kemmo na bátáda ala ani ƒui na muusé lɛlɔ mmɔ bédie bébewi kakpakɔ kaduli kemmo. Na ɔmmɔ kama Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bála-nya bálɛku ɔmmɔ kemmo bétéwi kesii kani baalɔ banii Kidron Kɔwɛ kemmo.

english_verse: The priests and Levites began their work on the first day of the first month. It took them one week to purify the courtyards of the temple and another week to purify the temple. So on the sixteenth day of that same month
translation_verse: Bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bése kabla kamɛni kalɔ na kɔbuli kudeedi limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ. Na uyolu unwi na béti bábla kakpakɔ kaduli kamɛni sɛɛn. Na uyolu unyɔdi lɛnɔ na béti bábla kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔlati lɛnɔ sɛɛn. Anwuɔsu limeyi leevu-lɛkundi lɛlɔ ni,

english_verse: And we have brought back all the things that King Ahaz took from the temple during the time he was unfaithful to God. We purified them and put them back in front of the altar. Worship in the Temple
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ala ani ƒui na Ɔga Ahas uti ɔ́lɛku kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo uwi ɔni na útadi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ mmɔ ni, bɔ́sɔku-nya búboku na bɔ́bla-nya sɛɛn na búti-nya búse ana kesekɔ na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ anumi.” Bekyuli Bammɔ Bésie Kakpakɔ Bátábla Akpala

english_verse: At once, Hezekiah called together the officials of Jerusalem, and they went to the temple.
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani na Hesekia ɔ́lɔ Yerusalemƒuɔ bakutine bammɔ ɔ́sala na bɔ́tɔlɔ bésie kakpakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: They brought with them seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven goats as sacrifices to take away the sins of Hezekiah's family and of the people of Judah, as well as to purify the temple. Hezekiah told the priests, who were descendants of Aaron, to sacrifice these animals on the altar.
translation_verse: Na badanku ɔmantɛ bɔkɔ maatɛ ku baƒonu bagyani maatɛ ku baƒonu bɔkɔdi maatɛ ku betukpa leevu bani na badubuti babla ekpidi lili buvele akpala na Hesekia ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli lili ku Yuda kadi bekyuli ƒui lili ku kakpakɔ kammɔ ƒui bɔbla kedee ɔsu. Anwuɔsu Hesekia ɔ́su bakpane bani ndi Aaron kaba kemmo bebi ɔnii beti bebuo bammɔ bakpa na Katɔti lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The priests killed the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, then splattered the blood on the altar.
translation_verse: Amu na bakpane bammɔ lɛnɔ bádu ɔmantɛ bakɔ bammɔ ku baƒonu bagyani bammɔ na bákuna béwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: They took the goats to Hezekiah and the worshipers, and they laid their hands on the animals.
translation_verse: Na béti bese bammɔ ama bésienku Hesekia ku bekyuli bani nébo kakpakɔ mmɔ na béti bana enu básia-ma eli.

english_verse: The priests then killed the goats and splattered the blood on the altar as a sacrifice to take away the sins of everyone in Israel, because Hezekiah had commanded that these sacrifices be made for all the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama bakpane bammɔ bádu bese bammɔ na béti bana ubugya bákuna béwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ aani ekpidi lili buvele akpala na Israelƒuɔ ƒui lili.

english_verse: The Levites were ready to play the instruments that had belonged to David; the priests were ready to blow the trumpets.
translation_verse: Na Lewiƒuɔ báklibi lɛlɔ na benye kagyumana ka bagya agyala ani adi Ɔga Salomo adi mmɔ. Na bakpane bammɔ lɛnɔ báklibi na benye kagyumana ka bavwi kɔkpɛɛ kɔmmɔ.

english_verse: As soon as Hezekiah gave the signal for the sacrifices to be burned on the altar, the musicians began singing praises to the Lord and playing their instruments,
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni kani na Hesekia údie kɔnu ɔ́tina bekyuli bammɔ ka bese kalɔ ku akpala ammɔ bɔkyula na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, bagyane bammɔ lɛnɔ bése kalɔ beedie bumwi lɛnu na baagyá bana agyala

english_verse: and everyone worshiped the Lord. This continued until the last animal was sacrificed.
translation_verse: na ukyuli biala ɔɔkya lili kalɔ teete Unwoti na bábu-nwu. Na ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ kani na bewi útédu ka bákyula lɛla biala báwɔlɔ.

english_verse: Then Hezekiah and his officials ordered the Levites to sing the songs of praise that David and Asaph the prophet had written. And so they bowed down and joyfully sang praises to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Hesekia ku nwuna bakutine benengu bammɔ bébo Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ɔda banii beteedie bumwi lɛnu lɛni na Ɔga Dawid ku Kenye Udiene Asaƒ bénweni bése mmɔ. Anwuɔsu béboku eli kalɔ na bédie bumwi lɛnɔ béte Unwoti ku lɛlɔyɔ.

english_verse: Hezekiah said to the crowd, “Now that you are once again acceptable to the Lord, bring sacrifices and offerings to give him thanks.” The people did this, and some of them voluntarily brought animals to be offered as sacrifices.
translation_verse: Amu na Hesekia ɔ́su kasalakɔ bekyuli bammɔ ɔnini, “Ka bɔ́sɔku lɛlɔ bɔ́bla ɔwɔdi búte bula Unwoti ɔsu ni, biti bina etela ku akpala biboku na biti bibagya-nwu enu.” Bekyuli bammɔ bábla lɛni na bádi muedi béti bebuo béboku ku kaƒɔ ƒaa banii badu-ma bakpa.

english_verse: There were not enough priests to skin all these animals, because many of the priests had not taken the time to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. However, since all the Levites had made themselves clean, they helped the priests until the last animal was skinned.
translation_verse: Nsu bakpane bammɔ beeemomo kalɛ na bakana bebuo bammɔ ƒui lɛku budie, ɔsika ɔɔɔdi bakpane bammɔ ƒui nákana lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ bɔbla kalɛ na babla kabla kammɔ. Nsu ka Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ama bana ƒui bábla lɛlɔ sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, bébunku bakpane bammɔ útédu ka bédie ebuo ukplodi ɔku báwɔlɔ.

english_verse: Besides all the sacrifices that were burned on the altar, the fat from the other animal sacrifices was burned, and the offerings of wine were poured over the altar. So the temple was once again used for worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Na bebuo bani na bádu bákyula bábla akpala ammɔ kama ni, beti bana ƒui lɛmwi bábakyula kede aani unwi bɔbla akpala na béti ntɛ akpala ammɔ ƒui lɛnɔ béwi lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu kakpakɔ kammɔ kásɔ kénwini kébese aani kuuku kalɛ, na baakpá Unwoti na mmɔ.

english_verse: Hezekiah and the people of Judah celebrated, because God had helped them make this happen so quickly.
translation_verse: Na Hesekia ku Yuda kadi bekyuli bammɔ bádi limeyi na lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ-ma, ɔsika Unwoti úbunku-ma na bákana na bábla ɔmɛni kɔnakunwi.

english_verse: Everyone from Beersheba in the south to Dan in the north was invited. This was the largest crowd of people that had ever celebrated Passover, according to the official records.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu básia Israel kalɔ bekyuli bammɔ ƒui kenye ɔ́si Beerseba útédu Dan na bálɔ-ma ka bebo Yerusalem mmɔ na badi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi bete Unwoti Israel Katɔti. Na benengu bammɔ alati baatina ka ɔ́si kuuku ƒui ni, bátasiaku bekyuli lisu lɛmɛni udu ka bebo limeyi lɛmɛni kadikɔ lɛni kudii.

english_verse: Hezekiah's messengers went everywhere in Israel and Judah with the following letter: People of Israel, now that you have survived the invasion of the Assyrian kings, it's time for you to turn back to the Lord God our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob worshiped. If you do this, he will stop being angry.
translation_verse: Amu na Hesekia batu bani na ɔ́tala mmɔ báyu ulu linyesia ɔku ɔmɛni bésienku Israel kesii biala. Na ɔku ɔmmɔ kenye kaasu kanini, “Israel kadi bekyuli, ka kuli kɔ́dia-bu na bɔ́lɛ Asiria baga enu kemmo na kekpo kéteƒie-bu ƒui ni, bɛya na ɔƒɛni anwu bunwini bubo Unwoti Katɔti ɔni na bula bati kuuku Abraham ku Isak ku Yakob bákpa kudɔ. Na si bɛ́bla ɔmɛni ni, ɔdubɔda kɔnyi buti bɔkya-bu ɔya.

english_verse: Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. Decide now to obey the Lord our God! Come to Jerusalem and worship him in the temple that will belong to him forever. Then he will stop being angry,
translation_verse: Na bitabla atuɔkplu aani bina bati kuuku bammɔ. Bɛlɛ ugyii geen ɔƒɛni ka bɛdubɔdi Unwoti bula Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ! Bibo Yerusalem na bibadi limeyi na bɛkpa-nwu na nwuna kakpakɔ kani ndubɔdi nwuna kadi uwi ƒui na ɔdubɔda kɔnyi buti bɔkya-bu ɔya.

english_verse: and the enemies that have captured your families will show pity and send them back home. The Lord God is kind and merciful, and if you turn back to him, he will no longer turn his back on you.
translation_verse: “Na bekisine bani néƒie bina lɛlɔ bekyuli badi bátɔlɔku ni, badubɔya na basɔ benwini bebo ɔma. Unwoti Katɔti ubo lɛƒɔndia na ɔɔnu kɔnyana. Na si bínwini bíbo-nwu kudɔ ni, ɔsɔ ɔɔɔdubo nwuna kama bunwini bɔkya-mii kudii.”

english_verse: Only a few people from the tribes of Asher, West Manasseh, and Zebulun were humble and went to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nkyuli ɛlɛɛ badi kani nási Aser ku Manase kakɛ kani nésie ɔƒɛ kanukɔ ku Sebulon adua kemmo béboku lɛlɔ kalɔ na bébo Yerusalem.

english_verse: God also made everyone in Judah eager to do what Hezekiah and his officials had commanded. Passover Is Celebrated
translation_verse: Na Katɔti ɔlati ɔ́ya na lɛlɔ kemmo kaatɔ́ ɔdi biala na Yuda ƒui ka babla lɛla lɛni na Hesekia ku nwuna benengu básu mmɔ.

english_verse: In the second month, a large crowd of people gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread.
translation_verse: Na kɔbuli kunyɔdi kemmo ni, bekyuli lisu bonwu lɛdi líbo líbasala na Yerusalem ka badi Bodobodo Ɔni Néteƒu Limeyi.

english_verse: They took all the foreign altars and incense altars in Jerusalem and threw them into Kidron Valley.
translation_verse: Na akpabi ani na bátu bálɛ Yerusalem béte kadi bamba baƒiɔ biala ku oloƒui kɔkyulakɔ ƒui ni, bágyu ala ammɔ bene ƒui bétébo béwi Kidron Kɔwɛ kemmo.

english_verse: Then, on the fourteenth day of that same month, the Levites began killing the lambs for Passover, because many of the worshipers were unclean and were not allowed to kill their own lambs. Meanwhile, some of the priests and Levites felt ashamed because they had not gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean. They immediately went through that ceremony and went to the temple, where they offered sacrifices to please the Lord. Then the priests and Levites took their positions, according to the Law of Moses, the servant of God. As the Levites killed the lambs, they handed some of the blood to the priests, who splattered it on the altar.
translation_verse: Amu na kɔbuli kunyɔdi kɔmmɔ kuna limeyi leevu-linedi lɛlɔ ni, Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bése kalɔ ku baƒonu bakɔdi bɔdu úte Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi Bɔdi, ɔsika bekyuli bani nébo babakpa mmɔ pii beeese sɛɛn na ɔdi kenye na bétete-ma kuƒi ka badu bebuo bammɔ ama alati. Na lɛnɔ ni, bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ badi lɛnɔ bátabla lɛlɔ sɛɛn bétese na ɔdi ɔmmɔ kenye na kɔƒa geen kuukpó-ma. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu usi na bakɛ na bábla ɔmmɔ kɔnakunwi na béduo kakpakɔ na bátákyula akpala ani mɔɔyɔ́ Unwoti kaƒɔ béte-nwu. Ɔmmɔ kama bakpane bammɔ ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bésie béténye bana kunyekɔ aani kalɛ na Katɔti kabla ɔblane Mose ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔ́tina.

english_verse: Most of the people that came from Ephraim, West Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun had not made themselves clean, but they ignored God's Law and ate the Passover lambs anyway. Hezekiah found out what they had done and prayed, “Lord God, these people are unclean according to the laws of holiness. But they are worshiping you, just as their ancestors did. So, please be kind and forgive them.”
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani na bási Eƒraim ku Manase ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ ku Isakar ku Sebulon bébo mmɔ akɔ pii bátakana lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ kemmo bɔvi, nsu bédie Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ atu na ama lɛnɔ bádi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia adila ammɔ. Hesekia ɔ́nu ɔmmɔ ɔ́ti, anwuɔsu ɔ́kpali Katɔti na úvele-nwu ɔnini, “Unwoti Katɔti bekyuli bamɛni beeese sɛɛn na lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ kenye, nsu ama lɛnɔ benye baakya lili kalɔ teete-ɔ aani kalɛ na bana bati kuuku bábla, anwuɔsu muuvele-ɔ nu-ma kɔnyana na eti akyiɛ-ma.”

english_verse: The Lord answered Hezekiah's prayer and did not punish them.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti lɛnɔ únu kalɛ na Hesekia ɔ́kpali-nwu úvele mmɔ na úti bana bɔƒiɔ bɔmmɔ ɔ́kyiɛ-ma sɔsɔ na útani-ma kɔtu.

english_verse: The worshipers in Jerusalem were very happy and celebrated the Festival for seven days. The Levites and priests sang praises to the Lord every day and played their instruments.
translation_verse: Lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ Israelƒuɔ bani nkya Yerusalem mmɔ geen na bádi Bodobodo Ɔni Néteƒu Limeyi emeyi maatɛ sɔɔn. Na Lewiƒuɔ ku bakpane bammɔ bédie lɛnu bémwi Unwoti limeyi ndi limeyi na baagyá bana agyala ammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Hezekiah thanked the Levites for doing such a good job, leading the celebration. The worshipers celebrated for seven days by offering sacrifices, by eating the sacred meals, and by praising the Lord God of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Hesekia ɔ́gya Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ enu na kabla kabuni kani na bábla ɔsu ku kalɛ na bátɔnku lɛkpa na emeyi ammɔ bɔdi kemmo. Bekyuli bani nébo mmɔ bábakpa lɛnɔ bádi limeyi lɛmmɔ emeyi maatɛ sɔɔn na béteeboku etela ani na béti bákpa na baadi adila kedee na baagyá bana bati kuuku Unwoti Katɔti enu.

english_verse: Everyone was so excited that they agreed to celebrate seven more days.
translation_verse: Limeyi bɔdi bɔmɛni bɔ́da ukyuli biala ebiti geen ɔni na bana ƒui bénu kalɔ besie anumi badi-ni emeyi maatɛ bamba bebu.

english_verse: Everyone was very happy, including those from Judah and Israel, the priests and Levites, and the foreigners living in Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ ukyuli biala geen ku bani na bási Yuda ku Israel ku bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui ku baƒɔ bani na bakya Yuda ku Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui.

english_verse: It was the biggest celebration in Jerusalem since the days of King Solomon, the son of David.
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́si Dawid ubidi Ɔga Salomo uwi ƒui ni, limeyi lɛni ndi limeyi linengudi ƒui lɛmɛni udu, bátadi-ni kudii.

english_verse: The priests and Levites asked God to bless the people, and from his home in heaven, he did.
translation_verse: Bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bévele Katɔti ka ɔya na nwuna kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku bekyuli bammɔ na sɔsɔ ni, únu-ma buvele ɔ́siku nwuna keliekɔ kedee kammɔ na katɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Hezekiah divided the priests and Levites into groups, according to their duties. Then he assigned them the responsibilities of offering sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He also appointed people to serve at the temple and to sing praises at the temple gates.
translation_verse: Hesekia úle bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ɔ́kya kasala esu esu kemmo ɔkɛnku bana kabla kenye. Na úti akpala bɔkyula ku unwi bɔbla akpala kabla ɔ́kya-ma enu kemmo. Na úte babambadi ka beteete kebunku na bataabla bekyuli kabla na kakpakɔ mmɔ. Na badi lɛnɔ beteedie bumwi lɛnu na kakpakɔ lɛban kenye.

english_verse: The official records also included their wives and children, because they had also been faithful in keeping themselves clean and acceptable to serve the Lord.
translation_verse: Na anyi bunweni lɛku lɛmɛni lɛdanku bana beleku ku bebi ƒui lɛnɔ, ɔsika ama lɛnɔ baadi litemi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ na baabla lɛlɔ sɛɛn na báƒɔ Unwoti anu ka babla-nwu kabla.

english_verse: He told the people of Jerusalem to bring the offerings that were to be given to the priests and Levites, so that they would have time to serve the Lord with their work.
translation_verse: Hesekia ɔ́su Yerusalemƒuɔ bammɔ ka beboku etela ani na badubuti bete bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ kalɛ na bakɛ uwi babla Katɔti kabla na bana kabla kani kenye na benye kemmo.

english_verse: After the Festival, the people went to every town in Judah and smashed the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah.
