They destroyed all the local shrines and foreign altars in Judah, as well as those in the territories of Benjamin, Ephraim, and West Manasseh. Then everyone went home. Offerings for the Priests and Levites
translation_verse: Ka bádi limeyi lɛmmɔ báwɔlɔ ni, bekyuli bammɔ bésie Yuda lɛma ƒui kemmo na bátábwɛ atabi baƒiɔ bani ƒui na bátu bálɛ lɛma lɛmmɔ kemmo. Na békulo lɛƒiɔgyii lɛni na bálɛ béte Asera baƒiɔ mmɔ ƒui béwi kalɔ. Na baƒiɔ lidu biala na bátu na abi eli ku bana akpabi ƒui ni, bábwɛ-ma na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui ku Benyamin ku Eƒraim ku Manase ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ ƒui béwi kalɔ na bátɔlɔ bésie bana kɔduli. Ɔlɛka Beboku Bakpane Ku Lewiƒuɔ Etela

english_verse: Hezekiah provided animals from his own herds and flocks to use for the morning and evening sacrifices, as well as for the sacrifices during the Sabbath celebrations, the New Moon Festivals, and the other religious feasts required by the Law of the Lord.
translation_verse: Hesekia úte bebuo ɔ́siku nwuna bebuo akɔ bani na badubuti bataabla akpala na ɔtanta ku useyi uwi ku lɛnwunameyi biala ku emeyi buni bɔdi kemmo ku kɔbuli kɔwɔdi bɔlɛ limeyi bɔdi ku emeyi buni bamba ani na Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔɔtina kalɛ.

english_verse: As soon as the people heard what the king wanted, they brought a tenth of everything they owned, including their best grain, wine, olive oil, honey, and other crops.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni kani na bekyuli bamɛni bénu lɛla lɛni na ɔga ɔɔwia ka babla mmɔ ni, béti bana akɛla lɛkpa leevudi béboku úbunku anta ku kamu udu edula ani na bebo ku nnɔ ku uwɔ ku edula bamba lɛnɔ.

english_verse: The people from the other towns of Judah brought a tenth of their herds and flocks, as well as a tenth of anything they had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Lɛni kani na bekyuli bani na bási Yuda lɛma bamba kemmo lɛnɔ béti bana bebuo bani na bebo lɛkpa leevudi ku ala ani ƒui na béti béte Katɔti na bábla-nya kedee mmɔ lɛkpa leevudi béboku.

english_verse: The people started bringing their offerings to Jerusalem in the third month, and the last ones arrived four months later.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bammɔ bése kalɔ beeti bana etela teeboku Yerusalem na kɔbuli kɔtɛdi kɔni na baalɔ banii Sivan kemmo. Na abuli ene kama asa na béboku etela akladi.

english_verse: When Hezekiah and his officials saw these offerings, they thanked the Lord and the people.
translation_verse: Ka Hesekia ku nwuna benengu bánu ala amɛni ni, bágya Unwoti ku bekyuli bammɔ enu.

english_verse: Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the large amount of offerings.
translation_verse: Amu na Hesekia úye ɔkpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ kalɛ na etela esu ani na beeboku-ma mmɔ ese.

english_verse: The high priest at the time was Azariah, a descendant of Zadok, and he replied, “Ever since the people have been bringing us their offerings, we have had more than enough food and supplies. The Lord has certainly blessed his people. Look at how much is left over!”
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane unengudi ɔni nákya uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo na baalɔ-nwu Asaria ɔni ndi Sadok kaba kemmo ubi ni, údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔ́si uwi ɔni bekyuli bammɔ bése kalɔ ku ala amɛni buboku ni, bɔ́kɛ adila ku ala bamba na etulo kalɛ na bɔɔwia muedi. Na bɔ́nu bɔ́ti ka Unwoti kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku bula bekyuli sɔsɔ. Nu ala ani udu nébu!”

english_verse: So the king gave orders for storerooms to be built in the temple, and when they were completed,
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔ́ya na bátu ala kesekɔ na kakpakɔ kemmo mmɔ. Na ka báwɔlɔ-ka bɔtu ni,

english_verse: all the extra offerings were taken there. Hezekiah and Azariah then appointed Conaniah the Levite to be in charge of these storerooms. His brother Shimei was his assistant, and the following Levites worked with them: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah.
translation_verse: etela bamba ani lɛlɔ kabla na baaadubo bɔbla kɔnakunwi kɔmmɔ ni, baaklibi-nya teese mmɔ. Na Ɔga Hesekia ku ɔkpane unengudi Asaria báƒuna Lewini ɔni baalɔ Konania na ɔɔnu ala ammɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔnwani Simei ndi nwuna ubunkune ku Lewiƒuɔ bamba bani ndi Yehiel ku Asasia ku Natan ku Asahel ku Yerimot ku Yosabad ku Eliel ku Ismakia ku Mahat ku Benaia.

english_verse: Kore son of Imnah was assigned to guard the East Gate, and he was put in charge of receiving the offerings voluntarily given to God and of dividing them among the priests and Levites.
translation_verse: Na Imna ubidi Kore na báƒuna ka utaanu ɔban kenye kani nkya késie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na anwu kani mɔɔƒɔ́ kaƒɔ ƒaa etela ani na bekyuli beeboku Katɔti na uule-nya teete bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ.

english_verse: He had six assistants who were responsible for seeing that all the priests in the other towns of Judah also got their share of these offerings. They were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah. Every priest and every Levite over
translation_verse: Kore ɔmɛni ubo bebunkune ɛku bamba bani mɔɔnu ka ala ani na béle mɛni édu bakpane bakladi bani na bakya Yuda lɛma bamba ƒui kemmo. Na bana anyi ndi Eden ku Miniamin ku Yesua ku Semaia ku Amaria ku Sekania. Ɔƒɛni ɔkpane ku Lewini biala na ɔ́ɔƒɔ utulo akwa avlaatɛ na ɔɔbla kabla limeyi ndi limeyi na kakpakɔ kemmo mmɔ bebo kadikɔ na etela amɛni kemmo ɔkɛnku bana kabla kenye.

english_verse: Hezekiah also appointed other men to take food and supplies to the priests and Levites whose homes were in the pastureland around the towns of Judah. But the priests had to be descendants of Aaron, and the Levites had to be listed in the official records.
translation_verse: Hesekia ɔ́ƒuna bekyuli badi úse kalɛ na beti bakpane kadikɔ kamɛni besienku bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bani na bakya akpaklɔ na bebuo kadikɔ na Yuda lɛma ku amadɔ mmɔ ƒui. Nsu ɔlɛka bakpane bammɔ babla Aaron kaba kemmo bebi na Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ lɛnɔ ɔlɛka bana anyi akya Lewiƒuɔ lɛku lɛni na lɛtɛ lise kemmo.

english_verse: Everything Hezekiah did while he was king of Judah, including what he did for the temple in Jerusalem, was right and good. He was a successful king, because he obeyed the Lord God with all his heart.
translation_verse: Ala ani ƒui na Hesekia ɔ́bla uwi ɔni na ɔɔdi Yuda lɛga ku ala ani ƒui na ɔ́bla úse kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo na Yerusalem ni, adia na ese siin. Nwuna lɛgadi lɛ́lɛ kɔsia, ɔsika ɔ́di Unwoti Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ ku nwuna kayi ƒui.

english_verse: The officials said all these things in Hebrew, so that everyone listening from the city wall would understand and be terrified and surrender.
translation_verse: Na ala amɛni ƒui ni, Yudaƒuɔ lɛdi kemmo na Asiria benengu bammɔ benye baasu-nya kalɛ na si Yerusalemƒuɔ bani na bakya ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo na awodu ammɔ kemmo bénu ni, na bayia na bete lili.

english_verse: You've heard what my ancestors and I have done to other nations. Were the gods of those nations able to defend their land against us?
translation_verse: “Bínu lɛla lɛni na ami ku mina bati kuuku bɔ́bla kadi bamba bekyuli ƒui. Bɔkana na bana baƒiɔ badi bákana kadi kadi bekyuli bɔƒɔ?

english_verse: The Lord rescued Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from Sennacherib and also protected them from other enemies.
translation_verse: Unwoti údie Hesekia ku Yerusalemƒuɔ ƒui na Sanaherib enu ku bekisine bamba enu kemmo.

english_verse: he and his officials worked out a plan to cut off the supply of water outside the city, so that the Assyrians would have no water when they came to attack. The officials got together a large work force that stopped up the springs and streams near Jerusalem.
translation_verse: anwu ku nwuna benengu bábla kasusu ka abiɔ ku ntu bɔni ƒui na bɔkya keyi na awodu ammɔ kama ni, beekúlo-mu kalɛ na si Asiriaƒuɔ bébo mmɔ ni, na balákɛ ntu bɔdi baláni.

english_verse: Hezekiah's workers also repaired the broken sections of the city wall. Then they built defense towers and an outer wall to help protect the one already there. The landfill on the east side of David's City was also strengthened. He gave orders to make a large supply of weapons and shields,
translation_verse: Amu na Hesekia ɔ́ya na batune badi bátásɔku ɔma ɔmmɔ kowodu kesii kani nábwɛ mmɔ báklibi. Na ɔ́ya na bátu kɔgyumanakɔ, na bátu kowodu bamba kɔni nábwɛ mmɔ kama. Na awodu kugyikpo kɔni na bátu bédi Dawid ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ awodu ani nésie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ lɛnɔ ni, básɔ báklibi-nya bɔtu kaduɛ. Ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́ya na bábla ekpola ku kekpo kayi agyumanala pii.

english_verse: and he appointed army commanders over the troops. Then he gathered the troops together in the open area in front of the city gate and said to them:
translation_verse: Na ɔ́ƒuna bekpone batɔnkune bani ndubɔtɔnku bekpone esu esu ammɔ. Amu na ɔ́lɔ bekpone esu esu ammɔ ɔ́sala kanwaadikɔ na ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ anumi na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini,

english_verse: Be brave and confident! There's no reason to be afraid of King Sennacherib and his powerful army. We are much more powerful,
translation_verse: “Bise kayi na bɛƒɔ lɛlɔ bɛdi! Naaanu lɛla lɛni ɔsu na ɔlɛka bɛyia Ɔga Sanaherib ku nwuna bekpone kpakplaa bammɔ. Abu bubo ɔyikun butulo-nwu ƒui.

english_verse: When Sennacherib and his troops were camped at the town of Lachish, he sent a message to Hezekiah and the people in Jerusalem. It said:
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na Ɔga Sanaherib ku nwuna bekpone bébo bábada keliekɔ na bakya Lakis ɔma ni, ɔ́kya Ɔga Hesekia ku Yerusalemƒuɔ ɔtu ɔdi ɔnini,

english_verse: I am King Sennacherib of Assyria, and I have Jerusalem surrounded. Do you think you can survive my attack?
translation_verse: “Ami Siriaƒuɔ Ɔga Sanaherib mɔɔyá-a na ati ka lɛ́ɛka lɛ́mana Yerusalem na muuye-ɔ si aakali ka adubɔkana-mi kekpo kenye bunye na akɛ ngba?

english_verse: Don't be fooled by Hezekiah! No god of any nation has ever been able to stand up to Assyria. Believe me, your God cannot keep you safe!
translation_verse: Bitaya na Hesekia use-mii lisusu lɛmmɔ udu! Baƒiɔ badi bátakana bunye bɔsiaku Asiria kudii na baƒɔ bana kadi bekyuli badi. Anwuɔsu bɛƒɔ-mi bɛdi ka bina Katɔti lɛnɔ ɔɔɔdubo-mii bɔkana bɔƒɔ!”

english_verse: The Assyrian officials said terrible things about the Lord God and his servant Hezekiah.
translation_verse: Asiriaƒuɔ benengu bammɔ bátɛmi enyekpi na bédumi Unwoti Katɔti ku nwuna kabla ɔblane Ɔga Hesekia.

english_verse: Sennacherib's letter even made fun of the Lord. It said, “The gods of other nations could not save their people from Assyria's army, and neither will the God that Hezekiah worships.”
translation_verse: Na ɔku ɔni na Sanaherib únweni kemmo ni, ɔ́kya Unwoti lɛlɔ lɛma na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Kadi bamba baƒiɔ bátakana bana kadi bekyuli bɔƒɔ bɔsiku Asiriaƒuɔ enu kemmo na Hesekia Katɔti ɔni na ɔɔkpá lɛnɔ ɔɔɔdubo lɛla lɛdi bɔkana bɔbla.”

english_verse: People brought offerings to Jerusalem for the Lord and expensive gifts for Hezekiah, and from that day on, every nation on earth respected Hezekiah. Hezekiah Gets Sick and Almost Dies (
translation_verse: Bekyuli béti etela béboku Unwoti na Yerusalem na béboku Hesekia ala ani na áƒɔ kuye geen. Na ka ɔ́si limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, kadi bamba bekyuli baabu Hesekia geen.

english_verse: About this same time, Hezekiah got sick and was almost dead. He prayed, and the Lord gave him a sign that he would recover.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo kani na ɔlɛ ɔdi úbebo Hesekia ɔni na ɔ́yu-nwu ɔkplu na ɔɔyɔ́ ukpi muedi. Mmɔ na ɔ́kpali Unwoti úvele-nwu na anwu lɛnɔ údie lɛla lɛdi ɔ́tina-nwu ka ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔba-nwu.

english_verse: But Hezekiah was so proud that he refused to thank the Lord for everything he had done for him. This made the Lord angry, and he punished Hezekiah and the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nsu Hesekia úbo ɔɔtalaku lɛlɔ katɔ geen ɔni na ɔ́yiƒala Unwoti enu muedi bɔgya. Na ɔmɛni ɔdi lɛla lɛni néƒi Unwoti livo, anwuɔsu ɔ́ni Hesekia ku Yuda ku Yerusalemƒuɔ ƒui kɔtu.

english_verse: Hezekiah and the people later felt sorry and asked the Lord to forgive them. So the Lord did not punish them as long as Hezekiah was king. Hezekiah's Wealth (
translation_verse: Na kama ƒui ni, bekyuli bamɛni bánu ka báƒiɔ na békpi kɔtɔ na bévele Unwoti banii uti ɔkyiɛ-ma. Anwuɔsu Unwoti ɔ́sɔ útani-ma kɔtu uwi ɔni ƒui na Hesekia ɔ́sɔ úlie utaadi lɛga mmɔ. Hesekia Ɔ́kɛ Lɛkɛ Geen

english_verse: Hezekiah was very rich, and everyone respected him. He built special rooms to store the silver, the gold, the precious stones and spices, the shields, and the other valuable possessions.
translation_verse: Hesekia úbenwini ɔlakɛne geen na ukyuli biala ɔɔbu-nwu. Ɔ́tu egulabi kesiekɔ kesii kani na uusé nwuna sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ku atabi bamba ani na áƒɔ kuye ku kutu akyala ku kekpo kayi agyumanala ku ala lidu bamba ani lɛnɔ náƒɔ kuye geen.

english_verse: Storehouses were also built for his supply of grain, wine, and olive oil; barns were built for his cattle, and pens were put up for his sheep.
translation_verse: Ɔ́tu kesii bamba na mmɔ na uusé nwuna edula aani kamu ku antabi udu ku nnɔ. Na ɔ́tu bebuo lidu lidu kɔkyakɔ lɛnɔ, ɔsika Unwoti úte-nwu lɛkɛ geen.

english_verse: God made Hezekiah extremely rich, so he bought even more sheep, goats, and cattle. And he built towns where he could keep all these animals.
translation_verse: Katɔti úse ɔ́ya na kɔnu kemmo kadia Hesekia geen, anwuɔsu ɔ́sɔ úye bese ku baƒonu pii úbu ku ɔmantɛ bɔkɔ lɛnɔ. Na ɔ́da akpakɔlɔ pii ute-ma.

english_verse: It was Hezekiah who built a tunnel that carried the water from Gihon Spring into the city of Jerusalem. In fact, everything he did was successful!
translation_verse: Na údie ubu ɔni kemmo na beeti ntu taasiaku ɔ́si Gihon libiɔ útéduoku Yerusalem ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na sɔsɔ ni, ala ani ƒui na Hesekia ɔ́bla ni, álɛ kɔsia na átɛ geen.

english_verse: Even when the leaders of Babylonia sent messengers to ask Hezekiah about the sign God had given him, God let Hezekiah give his own answer to test him and to see if he would remain faithful. Hezekiah Dies (
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Babilonƒuɔ batɔnkune bátala batu badi banii betéye Hesekia na ɔ́su-ma ala adi ɔsiku akɔla budie taatina ani nálɛ na nwuna kalɔ kemmo mmɔ ni, Katɔti únye ɔ́nu Hesekia na anwu ɔlati udie kenye na anwu ɔlati kasusu kenye na ɔnu si ɔmu ɔsiaku-nwu kama siin. Hesekia Úkpi

english_verse: Everything else Hezekiah did while he was king, including how faithful he was to the Lord, is included in the records kept by Isaiah the prophet. These are written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Lɛla bamba biala na Hesekia ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla uwi ɔni na ɔɔdi lɛga mmɔ ku kalɛ na ɔ́siaku Unwoti kama siin ni, bénweni-ni bákya Kenye Udiene Yesaia ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: When Hezekiah died, he was buried in the section of the royal tombs that was reserved for the most respected kings, and everyone in Judah and Jerusalem honored him. His son Manasseh then became king.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Hesekia úkpi ni, báva-nwu na kesii kani na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ ka bataava baga bani lɛlɔ mbo ɔbu geen. Na ukyuli biala na Yuda ku Yerusalem bábu-nwu. Ɔmmɔ kama na bébese ubidi Manase Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga.

english_verse: But the people of Judah and Jerusalem listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
translation_verse: Nsu Yuda ku Yerusalem bekyuli ƒui béni na bénu Manase litemi mmomu na bábla alaekpidi enengudi ani na etulo ani na kadi bamba bekyuli bani na lɛ́bɔku lɛ́lɛku-ma anumi muedi bábla.”

english_verse: The people obeyed Manasseh, but they worshiped the Lord at their own shrines.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bammɔ bénu lɛla lɛni na Manase ɔ́su-ma, nsu ama alati bana aƒiodu na baakpá Unwoti.

english_verse: Everything else Manasseh did while he was king, including his prayer to the Lord God and the warnings from his prophets, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na lɛla biala na Manase ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla uwi ɔni na ɔdi ɔga ku kalɛ na útaakpali Katɔti teevele ku kalɛ na kenye bediene bálɛ-nwu bávinku ƒui ni, bénweni bákya Israel ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: While Manasseh was held captive there, he asked the Lord God to forgive him and to help him.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na kekpo kéƒie Manase na úusie ɔkya mmɔ ni, úvele Unwoti Katɔti ɔnii uti nwuna ekpidi ɔkyiɛ-nwu na ubunku-nwu.

english_verse: He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. And he continued to worship the stars.
translation_verse: Ɔ́sɔku kadi bamba bekyuli bammɔ aƒiodu ani na ɔti Hesekia ɔ́bwɛ mmɔ ɔ́tu. Na ɔ́tu lɛkpabi úte Baal baƒiɔ na ɔ́sɔku Asera baƒiɔ beledi lɛƒiɔgyii ɔ́lɛ. Na ɔsiaku ayabi kama ɔɔkpá-nya.

english_verse: In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods
translation_verse: Na kakpakɔ geen kemmo muedi kesii kani na nka Unwoti lɛti kani na ɔlɛka bakpa ni, Manase ɔ́tu kadi bamba baƒiɔ akpabi ɔ́lɛ ku

english_verse: and the stars. He placed these altars in both courtyards of the temple
translation_verse: akpabi bamba úse ka bataakpa ayabi lɛnɔ. Na ɔ́ya na bálɛ akpabi amɛni na Unwoti kakpakɔ kɔduli akpa anyɔ ammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: and even set up a stone image of a foreign god. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own sons in Hinnom Valley. He did many other sinful things and made the Lord very angry. Years ago, God had told David and Solomon: Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there in the temple I will be worshiped forever.

translation_verse: Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bédie bebuo bammɔ kɔdikɔ kɔdikɔ kɔni na badubuti babla bɔkyula ƒui ɔdi aani kalɛ na Mose ɔda bubo bɔɔtina bése bekyuli bani néboku bebuo bammɔ. Na lɛni kani na bábla ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ bammɔ lɛnɔ.

english_verse: They sacrificed the Passover animals on the altar and boiled the meat for the other offerings in pots, kettles, and pans. Then they quickly handed the meat to the people so they could eat it.
translation_verse: Bákyula akpala ammɔ na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ, na béƒulo lɛna lɛkladi na ebui lidu lidu kemmo úte etela ɔdi bamba lɛnɔ bɔbla na bábabala béti lɛna lɛmmɔ béte bekyuli bammɔ kalɛ na bakun.

english_verse: All day long, the priests were busy offering sacrifices and burning the animals' fat on the altar. And when everyone had finished, the Levites prepared Passover animals for themselves and for the priests.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu limeyi limodi lɛmmɔ ƒui ni, bakpane bammɔ bátakɛ kɔnu kɔdi, mmomu benye baabla akpala na baakyula bebuo bammɔ lɛmwi na lɛkpabi lɛlɔ. Na uwi ɔni na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ɔdi biala ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, Lewiƒuɔ bánwa Kukpi Lili Bɔvia adila ammɔ béte lɛlɔ ku bakpane bammɔ.

english_verse: During the celebration some of the Levites prepared Passover animals for the musicians and the guards, so that the Levite musicians would not have to leave their places, which had been assigned to them according to the instructions of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king's prophet. Even the guards at the temple gates did not have to leave their posts.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na baadi limeyi lɛmmɔ ni, Lewiƒuɔ badi bánwa adila ammɔ béte lɛnu bediene ku bagyumanane bammɔ kalɛ na Lewiƒuɔ lɛnu bediene bammɔ ɔdi ulágyu nwuna kenyekɔ kani na béte-nwu ka unye aani kalɛ na Dawid ku Asaƒ ku Heman ku Yedutum ɔni ndi kenye udiene ute ɔga ɔmmɔ bátina. Na bagyumanane bani na benye kakpakɔ kɔyakun lɛban kenye muedi ɔdi útalɛ ka ɔdi ɔgyu nwuna kenyekɔ.

english_verse: So on that day, Passover was celebrated to honor the Lord, and sacrifices were offered on the altar to him, just as Josiah had commanded.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, bádi kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi lɛmmɔ béti bákɔliku Unwoti katɔ na bákyula akpala na lɛkpabi lɛlɔ béte-nwu aani kalɛ Yosia úbo ɔda.

english_verse: The worshipers then celebrated the Festival of Thin Bread for the next seven days.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani nébo kakpakɔ mmɔ bésie anumi na bádi Bodobodo Ɔni Néteƒu Limeyi bɔdi emeyi maatɛ.

english_verse: People from Jerusalem and from towns all over Judah and Israel were there. Passover had not been observed like this since the days of Samuel the prophet. In fact, this was the greatest Passover celebration in Israel's history!
translation_verse: Yerusalem ɔma ku lɛma lɛni na Yuda ku Israel kalɔ ƒui bekyuli bébo mmɔ. Na ka ɔ́si Kenye Udiene Samuel uwi ƒui ni, bátadi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi lɛmɛni lɛni kudii. Na geen ni, ɔ́si uwi ɔni na bése kalɔ ku limeyi lɛmɛni bɔdi ni, ɔmɛni ndi limeyi linengudi ƒui lɛni na bádi dii na Israel!

english_verse: All these things happened in the eighteenth year of Josiah's rule in Judah. Josiah Dies in Battle (
translation_verse: Na ala amɛni ƒui álɛ na lɛkwa leevu-maanedi kemmo na Yosia Yuda lɛga bɔdi kemmo. Yosia Úkpi Na Kekpokɔ

english_verse: Some time later, King Neco of Egypt led his army to the city of Carchemish on the Euphrates River. And Josiah led his troops north to meet the Egyptians in battle.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔdi kama ni, Egyipteƒuɔ Ɔga Neko ɔ́tɔnku nwuna bekpone úsienku Karkemis ɔma unengudi kemmo na Euƒrate Ketu kɔtu. Na Yosia lɛnɔ útiku nwuna bekpone útásiaku kalɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ kalɛ na utásiaku Egyipteƒuɔ bammɔ na kekpokɔ.

english_verse: But Josiah ignored Neco's warning, even though it came from God! Instead, he disguised himself and marched into battle against Neco in the valley near Megiddo.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui ni, Yosia útenu Neko litemi ina ka Katɔti náya na ɔ́su-nwu kenye kammɔ! Mmomu úti ala adi na ɔ́bɛla nwuna anumi kalɛ na balanu-nwu baláti na úsie útásiaku-nwu ka bekpo na kesii kani baalɔ banii Medigo Ɔkwalɛ.

english_verse: They carried Josiah out of his chariot, then put him in the other chariot he had there and took him back to Jerusalem, where he soon died. He was buried beside his ancestors, and everyone in Judah and Jerusalem mourned his death.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu báda Yosia bédie kɛɛkɛ ɔmmɔ kemmo bátákya ɔbambadi ɔdi kemmo na béti-nwu bátɔlɔku mmɔ bésienku Yerusalem kesii kani na uwi ɔ́sɔ útetu asa na úkpi. Báva-nwu na kesii kani na nwuna bati kuuku batɛ na ukyuli biala na Yuda ku Yerusalem mmɔ úwulo-nwu geen.

english_verse: Jeremiah the prophet wrote a funeral song in honor of Josiah. And since then, anyone in Judah who mourns the death of Josiah sings that song. It is included in the collection of funeral songs.
translation_verse: Amu na Kenye Udiene Yeremia údie ɔkwanu ɔdi úti ɔ́kɔliku-nwu lɛnyi katɔ. Na ɔ́si uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, ukyuli biala muuwulo Yosia kukpi ni, uudie ɔkwanu ɔmmɔ. Na bénweni ɔnu ɔmmɔ bákya lɛkwanu ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: Everything else Josiah did while he was king, including how he faithfully obeyed the Lord,
translation_verse: Na lɛla bamba biala na Yosia ɔ́sɔ ɔ́bla na nwuna lɛgadi kemmo ku kalɛ na ɔ́siaku Unwoti kama siin ni,

english_verse: is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: bénweni-ni bákya Israel ku Yuda ala alɛdi ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: The message said: I am King Cyrus of Persia. The Lord God of heaven has made me the ruler of every nation on earth. He has also chosen me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. The Lord God will watch over any of his people who want to go back to Judah.
translation_verse: “Lɛni na ami Ɔga Kores mɔɔsu, “ ‘Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikune úti kayawi lɛga kɔdikɔ ƒui ɔ́kya-mi kalɔ, na ɔ́ƒuna-mi ka lɛtu kakpakɔ lite-nwu na Yerusalem na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu nwuna kadi bekyuli akɔ ɔdi biala na ɔkya-mii akɔ ni, nwuna Katɔti ɔsiaku-nwu na unwini usie mmɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar also carried off many of the valuable things in the Lord's temple, and he put them in his palace in Babylon.
translation_verse: Nebukadnesar úti ala abuni bamba ani na áƒɔ kuye geen lɛnɔ na kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo ɔ́tɔlɔku útése nwuna ɔga kesii na Babilon.

english_verse: During Jehoiakim's rule, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia invaded Judah. He arrested Jehoiakim and put him in chains, and he sent him to the capital city of Babylon.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Yehoiakim ɔɔdi lɛga ni, Babilon Ɔga Nebukadnesar úkpo Yuda na úƒie Yehoiakim na úbo-nwu kɔgba na úti-nwu úmene Babilon ɔma unengudi kemmo.

english_verse: The Lord sent King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to attack Jerusalem. Nebuchadnezzar killed the young men who were in the temple, and he showed no mercy to anyone, whether man or woman, young or old. God let him kill everyone in the city.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́tala Babilon Ɔga Nebukadnesar ka utékpo Yerusalem. Na úsie útádu bakloƒu bani nkya kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo na útanu ɔdi kɔnyana. Uleku o-o, ɔnana o-o, unengu o-o, ɔnamu o-o ni, Katɔti ɔ́ya na ɔ́du bana ƒui na ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar carried off everything that was left in the temple; he robbed the treasury and the personal storerooms of the king and his officials. He took everything back to Babylon.
translation_verse: Na úti Katɔti kakpakɔ kemmo ala enengudi ku ebliidi ani nse mmɔ ƒui ɔ́tɔlɔku úsienku Babilon ku ɔga ɔmmɔ ku nwuna benengu akɛla ani nse kakpakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: In the spring of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had Jehoiachin arrested and taken to Babylon, along with more of the valuable items in the temple. Then Nebuchadnezzar appointed Zedekiah king of Judah. King Zedekiah of Judah (
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na ketudi keesé kalɔ ni, Babilon Ɔga Nebukadnesar ɔ́ya na béƒie Yekonia na úti-nwu úsienku Babilon na ɔ́sɔ útiku ala abambadi ani lɛnɔ náƒɔ kuye geen ɔ́siku kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo. Ɔmmɔ kama Nebukadnesar ɔ́ƒuna Sedekia ka unwini Yudaƒuɔ ɔga. Sedekia Ɔ́di Lɛga Na Yuda

english_verse: The survivors were taken to Babylonia as prisoners, where they were slaves of the king and his sons, until Persia became a powerful nation.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani ƒui na bátadu na kuwii kenye ni, ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́ya na béƒie-ma bátɔlɔku, na bénwini anwu ku nwuna bebi kabla bablane úti útédu uwi ɔni na Persia lɛgakadikɔ kébo kaadi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord his God and refused to change his ways, even after a warning from Jeremiah, the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Ɔ́bla likpidi na Unwoti nwuna Katɔti anumi na úni ka uboku lɛlɔ kalɔ ina ka Katɔti Kenye Udiene Yeremia ɔ́dɔnku-nwu geen.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had forced Zedekiah to promise in God's name that he would be loyal. Zedekiah was stubborn and refused to turn back to the Lord God of Israel, so he rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Amu na Sedekia ɔ́ta únye Ɔga Nebukadnesar lɛlɔ ina ka ɔ́kpali Unwoti lɛnyi na úse ɔga ɔmmɔ kenye ka ɔdubɔdi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ siin. Nsu Sedekia ɔ́bla atu ɔkplu na úni ka ɔvumana kayi na unwini ubo Unwoti Israel Katɔti kudɔ. Na ɔ́ta únye Nebukadnesar lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The people of Judah and even the priests who were their leaders became more unfaithful. They followed the disgusting example of the nations around them and made the Lord's holy temple unfit for worship.
translation_verse: Yuda kadi bekyuli ku bana bakpane bani ndi bana batɔnkune ƒui muedi béni ka badi Unwoti litemi lɛlɔ siin. Na bakɛ basiaku kadi bekyuli bani ablala muusé Katɔti lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔbladu kama na báya na Unwoti kakpakɔ kedee kammɔ keesé lɛlɔ na kásɔ kátamanku ka bakpa na mmɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord God felt sorry for his people, and instead of destroying the temple, he sent prophets who warned the people over and over about their sins.
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti Katɔti kadi bekyuli bammɔ lɛlɔ lɛ́kywi-nwu kaƒɔ na ɔni na ɔkyula kakpakɔ kammɔ na kayii udu ni, bɔtala mmomu na ɔ́tala nwuna kenye bediene na bábadɔnku-ma kɔlɛ kɔlɛ na bana ekpidi ɔsu.

english_verse: But the people only laughed and insulted these prophets. They ignored what the Lord God was trying to tell them, until he finally became so angry that nothing could stop him from punishing Judah and Jerusalem. Jerusalem Is Destroyed (
translation_verse: Nsu bɔma kani na bekyuli bamɛni báma kenye bediene bammɔ na bédumi-ma na béni ala ani ƒui na Katɔti ɔɔwia ka ɔsu-ma. Na ɔkɛnku ɔmɛni ɔsu kɔnyi kúbakɔ Unwoti Katɔti kɔ́vili útédu ka ɔni Yuda ku Yerusalem kɔtu. Bákyula Yerusalem

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar's troops burned down the temple and destroyed every important building in the city. Then they broke down the city wall.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama bátu ogya bákya Katɔti kakpakɔ kammɔ na báƒɛ Yerusalem awodu ammɔ béwi kalɔ, na bákyula baga kesii kammɔ ƒui na bébile ala ani náƒɔ kuye mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: In the first year that Cyrus was king of Persia, the Lord had Cyrus send a message to all parts of his kingdom. This happened just as Jeremiah the Lord's prophet had promised.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama na Persia kalɔ Ɔga Kores lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa lideedi kemmo ni, Unwoti úti ɔ́sia-nwu kayi ka ute bɔti bɔdi na nwuna kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ ƒui kalɛ na Yeremia kenye kani na ɔ́su kebo-nwu kemmo na ɔ́ya na bénweni lɛla lɛmɛni bése.

english_verse: Everyone else must provide what is needed. They must give money, supplies, and animals, as well as gifts for rebuilding God's temple.
translation_verse: Na kalɔ biala kemmo na Katɔti kadi bekyuli bamɛni akɔ bani nébu ɔdi ɔkya ni, kalɔ kammɔ bekyuli bete-ma sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ku ala bamba ku bebuo ku kaƒɔ ƒaa etela ute Katɔti kakpakɔ kamɛni bɔtu na Yerusalem.

english_verse: The others helped by giving silver articles, gold, personal possessions, cattle, and other valuable gifts, as well as offerings for the temple.
translation_verse: Na bana liku bekyuli béte-ma sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ku ala ku bebuo ku ala abuni abambadi úbunku kaƒɔ ƒaa etela ani na béte-ma.

english_verse: King Cyrus gave back the things that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the Lord's temple in Jerusalem and had put in the temple of his own gods.
translation_verse: Na Ɔga Kores ɔ́sɔku akyami ku lɛɛƒɛɛ lɛni na Ɔga Nebukadnesar úti ɔ́tɔlɔku Yerusalem kakpakɔ mmɔ, na úti-nya útése nwuna baƒiɔ kakpakɔ ɔtɔ mmɔ úte-ma.

english_verse: Cyrus placed Mithredath, his chief treasurer, in charge of these things. Mithredath counted them and gave a list to Sheshbazzar, the governor of Judah.
translation_verse: Na Persiaƒuɔ Ɔga Kores úti kabla kammɔ ƒui ɔ́kya Sesbasar ɔni ndi bana egulabi lɛlɔ ɔnune enu kemmo, na únweni ala ani ƒui béte-ma ɔ́kya ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: Included among them were:
translation_verse: Sika ugyiedi akyami wɛlɛ wɛlɛ

english_verse: silver bowls; and
translation_verse: ku kanwakɔ akyami bamba

english_verse: gold and silver dishes, bowls, and other articles. Sheshbazzar took them with him when he and the others returned to Jerusalem from Babylonia.
translation_verse: . Na ala amɛni na Sesbasar úti ɔ́da uwi ɔni na anwu ku bekyuli bani kekpo kéƒie-ma bási Babilon bésie Yerusalem.

english_verse: In fact, the governor told them, “You cannot eat the food offered to God until we find out if you really are priests.”
translation_verse: Na kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔnune úbo-ma ɔda ka ɔdi biala utadi adila ani nse kedee ntulo útédu ka bákɛ ɔkpane ɔni mɔɔbla kabla na ɔɔda ala ani baalɔ Urim ku Tumim.

english_verse: There were
translation_verse: Na bebo baƒlumu

english_verse: When the people came to where the Lord's temple had been in Jerusalem, some of the family leaders gave gifts so it could be rebuilt in the same place.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bekyuli bammɔ béduo Katɔti Kaduli na Yerusalem ni, lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ benengu badi béyi akpala ka badubuti ku kaƒɔ ƒaa bebunku Katɔti kaduli kammɔ bɔtu.

english_verse: They gave all they could, and it came to a total of
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bammɔ béyi ala kalɛ na badubɔkana na béti babla kabla kammɔ. Na ala ani na béyi bumomo bɔdi sika ugyiedi ebi

english_verse: Everyone returned to the towns from which their families had come, including the priests, the Levites, the musicians, the temple guards, and the workers.
translation_verse: Na bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ ku lɛnu batune ku kɔyakun bagyumanane ku kakpakɔ kabla bablane bétélie bana lɛma kemmo. Na bekyuli badi bene lɛnɔ bétélieku-ma. Na Israelƒuɔ bakladi ni, ama lɛnɔ bétélie bana lɛma kemmo.

english_verse: During the seventh month of the year, the Israelites who had settled in their towns went to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na kɔbuli maatɛdi kúdu na Israelni biala ɔ́ɔkɛ nwuna keliekɔ na nwuna ɔma ni, bana ƒui bábasala lisu aani kadi kenwi bekyuli na Yerusalem.

english_verse: The priest Joshua son of Jozadak, together with the other priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives rebuilt the altar of Israel's God. Then they were able to offer sacrifices there by following the instructions God had given to Moses, the man of God.
translation_verse: Amu na Yosadak ubidi Yesua ku nwuna bakpane ku Sealtiel ku nwuna bekyuli badi bése kalɔ baatú Israelƒuɔ Katɔti lɛkpabi lɛni lɛlɔ badubo akpala butaakyula aani kalɛ na bénweni bákya Mose ɔni ndi Katɔti ukyuli ɔda bubo ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: And they built the altar where it had stood before, even though they were afraid of the people who were already living around there. Then every morning and evening they burned sacrifices and offerings to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ina ka bákya bátaayia bekyuli bani nkya-ma amadɔ mmɔ ni, básɔku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ bátu na nina ɔka ɔkukudi lɛlɔ, na baabla ɔtanta ku useyi uwi akpala teete Unwoti.

english_verse: The people followed the rules for celebrating the Festival of Shelters and offered the proper sacrifices each day.
translation_verse: Na kalɛ na bénweni bákya ɔda bubo ɔku kemmo ni, bádi Kevo Kemmo Bulie Emeyi, na bábla bɔkyula akpala bumomo bɔni na bénweni bése béte limeyi biala.

english_verse: They offered sacrifices to please the Lord, sacrifices at each New Moon Festival, and sacrifices at the rest of the Lord's festivals. Every offering the people had brought voluntarily was also presented to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, bábla bɔkyula akpala ku kɔbuli kɔwɔdi akpala ku akpala ani na ese ete Unwoti emeyi bɔdi. Na básɔ bábla akpala bamba ani ndi kaƒɔ ƒaa etela ani na bekyuli bammɔ béboku.

english_verse: Although work on the temple itself had not yet begun, the people started offering sacrifices on the Lord's altar on the first day of the seventh month of that year. The Rebuilding of the Temple Begins
translation_verse: Na limeyi lideedi na kɔbuli maatɛdi kɔmmɔ kemmo ni, bése kalɔ baabla bɔkyula akpala teete Unwoti. Ina ka béteseku kalɔ ku Unwoti kakpakɔ bɔtu tɔ. Béseku Unwoti Kakpakɔ Bɔtu Kalɔ

english_verse: King Cyrus of Persia had said the Israelites could have cedar trees brought from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. So they sent grain, wine, and olive oil to the cities of Tyre and Sidon as payment for these trees, and they gave money to the stoneworkers and carpenters.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama béti egulabi adi béte lɛtɔ batune ku banwine badi. Na béti adila ku ntu ku nnɔ ka beti besienku Sidonƒuɔ ku Tiroƒuɔ kalɛ na beti sida kugyiikɛ basia ɛpu lɛlɔ basiku Lebanon beboku Yopa. Na Persiaƒuɔ Ɔga Kores úte kuƒi kɔmɛni.

english_verse: During the second month of the second year after the people had returned from Babylonia, they started rebuilding the Lord's temple. Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jozadak, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else who had returned started working. Every Levite over
translation_verse: Na kɔbuli kunyɔdi na lɛkwa linyɔdi kemmo ni, uwi ɔni na béduo Unwoti kaduli na Yerusalem kama ni, Sealtiel ubidi Serubabel ku Yosadak ubidi Yesua ku bana banwani bakladi ku bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ ku bani kekpo kéƒie-ma na bénwini bébo Yerusalem bése kalɔ ku kabla. Na Lewiƒuɔ bani ƒui nákɛ akwa aavlanyɔ ku kama béti-ma bábla kabla kammɔ lɛlɔ banune.

english_verse: The Levites in charge of the whole project were Joshua and his sons and relatives and Kadmiel and his sons from the family of Hodaviah. The family of Henadad worked along with them.
translation_verse: Na Yesua ku nwuna bebi ku nwuna banwani Kadmiel ku nwuna bebi ku Hodawia kaba bebi ku Henadad bebi ku Lewiƒuɔ béti lɛlɔ básala na bakya baanu bekyuli bani nkya mɔɔtú Katɔti ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: When the builders had finished laying the foundation of the temple, the priests put on their robes and blew trumpets in honor of the Lord, while the Levites from the family of Asaph praised God with cymbals. All of them followed the instructions given years before by King David.
translation_verse: Na si batune bammɔ bákya atabi ani beeti teese Unwoti kakpakɔ ɔtɔ kalɔ bɔtu ni, na bakpane bammɔ bakya bana bakpane lɛwu na beti bana kɔkpɛɛ bada. Na Lewiƒuɔ bani nási Asaƒ kaba kemmo beti bana agyala na bemwi Unwoti aani kalɛ na Ɔga Dawid úbo-ma ɔda ɔ́vi.

english_verse: They praised the Lord and gave thanks as they took turns singing: “The Lord is good! His faithful love for Israel will last forever.” Everyone started shouting and praising the Lord because work on the foundation of the temple had begun.
translation_verse: Na beedie lɛnu teemwi Unwoti na baagyá-nwu enu banini, Unwoti ɔdia geen. Na nwuna bɔyɔ bɔni na ubo ute Israel buse búsela uwi ƒui. Na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bébo kudu momoomo bémwi Unwoti ka bákya Unwoti kakpakɔ kowodu ɔka kalɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: Many of the older priests and Levites and the heads of families wept bitterly because they remembered seeing the first temple years before. But others were so happy that they celebrated with joyful shouts.
translation_verse: Nsu Lewiƒuɔ ku bakpane ku lɛtɔ benengu bani na badaku anumi busie pii na bánu kakpakɔ kedeedi bɔtu béwulo momoomo ka bánu ka bése kalɔ baatú kakpakɔ kammɔ. Na badi lɛnɔ beebó kudu ku lɛlɔyɔ.

english_verse: Their shouting and crying were so noisy that it all sounded alike and could be heard a long way off.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala ɔdi ɔsɔ ulenu buwulo ku lɛlɔyɔ kudu kavumana kadi taati. Ɔsika kudu kɔmmɔ kɔ́kɔ katɔ geen na beenú-ku na ɔgyu kakaaka ƒui.

english_verse: The enemies of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin heard that the people had come back to rebuild the temple of the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bekisine bani nási Yuda ku Benyamin bénu ka bekyuli bani kekpo kéƒie-ma bénwini bébo mmɔ bakya baatú kakpakɔ bete Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti ni,

english_verse: So they went to Zerubbabel and to the family leaders and said, “Let us help! Ever since King Esarhaddon of Assyria brought us here, we have worshiped your God and offered sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: bésie Serubabel ku Israelƒuɔ lɛtɔ benengu kudɔ na básu-ma banini, “Bɛya na bubebunku-mii na bɔtu kakpakɔ kammɔ. Ɔsika Katɔti ɔni bɛɛbu ni, anwu kani na abu lɛnɔ bɔɔbu. Na búuse kalɔ bɔɔbla akpala teete-nwu ɔ́si uwi ɔni na Asiriaƒuɔ Ɔga Esarhadon ɔ́ya na bubo bɔ́kya-nwu kudɔ.”

english_verse: But Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the family leaders answered, “You cannot take part in building a temple for the Lord our God! We will build it ourselves, just as King Cyrus of Persia commanded us.”
translation_verse: Amu na Serubabel ku Yesua ku Israel lɛtɔ benengu bammɔ bédie kenye banini, “Biiibo kuƒi ka bibebunku-bu na ɔtɔ ɔni bɔɔtu bute bula Katɔti kemmo. Abu kani bɔdu bɔkana na bɔtu ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ bute Unwoti ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ Katɔti aani kalɛ na Persiaƒuɔ Ɔga Kores úbo-bu ɔda.”

english_verse: Then the neighboring people began to do everything possible to frighten the Jews and to make them stop building.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama bekyuli bani na belie bede-ma bákya ɔkplu ka baƒɛ Yudaƒuɔ enu. Na baya liƒu liduo-ma kemmo na bada ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ bɔtu baya.

english_verse: During the time that Cyrus was king and even until Darius became king, they kept bribing government officials to slow down the work. Trouble Rebuilding Jerusalem
translation_verse: Na báwia egulabi béte bekyuli badi kalɛ benye betile kabla kammɔ. Na bétile-ma ulu lɛni laa ɔ́si Persiaƒuɔ Ɔga Kores lɛga bɔdi uwi útédu Ɔga Dario uwi.

english_verse: In the first year that Xerxes was king, the neighboring people brought written charges against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Ɔga Ahasweros úse kalɔ ɔɔdi lɛga ni, bekyuli badi bátáda Yudaƒuɔ ku Yerusalemƒuɔ kenye bátina-nwu.

english_verse: Later, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their advisors got together and wrote a letter to Artaxerxes when he was king of Persia. It was written in Aramaic and had to be translated.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si uwi ɔni na Ɔga Artasasta ɔɔdi lɛga na Persia kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, Bislam ku Mitradat ku Tabeel ku nwuna bekyuli badi bénweni ɔku béte Artasasta. Na bénweni ɔku ɔmmɔ na Siria kunweni kemmo na bédie-nwu kalɔ na Siria lɛdi kemmo.

english_verse: This letter said: Your Majesty King Artaxerxes, we are your servants from everywhere in Western Province, and we send you our greetings.
translation_verse: Na ɔku ɔni na béti bémene Ɔga Artasasta kemmo etemila ndi amɛni. “Ɔ́si ƒula kabla bablane banana bani nkya ketu ɔvi kudɔ.

english_verse: You should know that the Jews who left your country have moved back to Jerusalem and are now rebuilding that rebellious city. In fact, they have almost finished rebuilding the walls and repairing the foundations.
translation_verse: “Bɔɔyɔ́ ka ɔga ɔti ka Yudaƒuɔ bani nási ƒula kudɔ na bébo-bu kudɔ, bésie bákya Yerusalem na básɔku likyulikpi ku atuɔkplu ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ baatú. Na básɔku nwuna awodu lɛnɔ baatú. Na benye baaklibi ekpo ekpo ani na ébie lɛnɔ.

english_verse: You should also know that if the walls are completed and the city is rebuilt, the Jews won't pay any kind of taxes, and there will be less money in your treasury.
translation_verse: “Na bɔɔyá na asɔ ati ka, si básɔku ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ bátu ku nwuna awodu ni, bekyuli bammɔ basɔ baaadubo kuyii kɔni na ékulo éte-ma bɔƒɔ. Na ɔma kavumi kadubo bɔbwɛ.

english_verse: We are telling you this, because you have done so much for us, and we want everyone to respect you.
translation_verse: “Ɔsika bula ƒui bubo kuƒi ka bɔnu ka ƒula lɛgadi liisié anumi. Na bulayɔ ka ala amɛni udu ataalɛ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bɔɔyɔ́ ka

english_verse: If you look up the official records of your ancestors, you will find that Jerusalem has constantly rebelled and has led others to rebel against kings and provinces. That's why the city was destroyed in the first place.
translation_verse: ebo ɔda na bawia ƒula bati kuuku kɔkunkɛ kemmo banu. Si ábla lɛni ni, adubɔnu bɔti ka ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni ni, ɔdi atuɔkplu ɔma. Na ɔ́si kukuuku ƒui ni, ɔɔta teenye bagadine lɛlɔ. Na bekyuli bammɔ bɔda bubo ɔkplu. Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu ɔlɛka bayila ɔma ɔmmɔ udu.

english_verse: If Jerusalem is rebuilt and its walls completed, you will no longer have control over Western Province.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu bɔɔnu ka si áya na básɔku ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ku ana awodu bátu ni, bula ɔga ɔbune, asɔ alakana ɔvi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ bɔnu.”

english_verse: King Artaxerxes answered: Greetings to Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and to your advisors in Samaria and other parts of Western Province.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ údie kakunkɛ kani bénweni-nwu kenye na úti úmene ɔnii, “Rehum ɔni ndi bekpone unengu ku ɔku unwenine Simsai ku nwuna bekyuli bakladi bani nli Samaria ku ketu ɔvi ƒui bɔɔkya-mii kenye.

english_verse: After your letter was translated and read to me,
translation_verse: “Ɔku ɔni na bíti bímene-bu mmɔ ni, báka na bédie-nwu kalɔ na mina anumi.

english_verse: I had the old records checked. It is true that for years Jerusalem has rebelled and caused trouble for other kings and nations.
translation_verse: Líbo ɔda na báwia bati kuuku kɔkunkɛ kemmo na bɔ́nu bɔ́ti ka ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni ɔ́si kuuku ƒui ni, bébo atuɔkplu na báata teenye bagadine lɛlɔ.

english_verse: And powerful kings have ruled Western Province from Jerusalem and have collected all kinds of taxes.
translation_verse: Na Yerusalem ɔdi kalɔ kani na baga bani na bebo ɔkplu báadi-ka lɛlɔ dii. Na bátaaƒɔ kuyii teete-ma.

english_verse: I want you to command the people to stop rebuilding the city until I give further notice.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu bibo bekyuli bammɔ ɔda na bada kabla kammɔ baya, kalɛ na basɔ balátu ɔma ɔmmɔ utédu ka básɔ béte kuƒi.

english_verse: Do this at once, so that no harm will come to the kingdom.
translation_verse: Na bɛnu kaduɛ kalɛ na beledie litemi lɛmɛni atu na likpidi lɛdi lilebo-mi lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: As soon as this letter was read, Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and their advisors went to Jerusalem and forced everyone to stop rebuilding the city. Work on the Temple Starts Again
translation_verse: Ka báka Ɔga Artasasta ɔku ɔmmɔ béte Rehum ku ɔku unwenine Simsai ku bakladi pɛ, kani na bésie Yudaƒuɔ bani nkya Yerusalem na bénye-ma lɛlɔ ka bada kabla kammɔ baya.

english_verse: The Jews were forced to stop work on the temple and were not able to do any more building until the year after Darius became king of Persia.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Katɔti kaduli bɔtu na Yerusalem údi únye útédu lɛkwa linyɔdi lɛni lɛlɔ na Ɔga Dario ulie liboku lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord God of Israel told the prophets Haggai and Zechariah to speak in his name to the people of Judah and Jerusalem. And they did.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Kenye Udiene Hagai ku Sakaria ɔni ndi Ido ubidi bése kalɔ baatɛmi teete Yudaƒuɔ bani nli Yerusalem.

english_verse: So Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the priest urged the people to start working on the temple again, and God's prophets encouraged them.
translation_verse: Amu na Sealtiel ubidi Serubabel ku Yosadak ubidi Yesua bénu bana etemila ani baasu mmɔ, na básɔ bése kalɔ báatu Unwoti kakpakɔ na Yerusalem. Na kenye bediene inyɔ bammɔ béte-ma kebunku.

english_verse: Governor Tattenai of Western Province and his assistant Shethar Bozenai got together with some of their officials. Then they went to Jerusalem and said to the people, “Who told you to rebuild this temple?
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo kani ni, kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔdine Tatenai ɔni mɔɔnu ketu ɔvi bekyuli lɛlɔ ku Setar-Bosnai ku nwuna kabla bablane bébo Yerusalem na béye-ma banini, “Ɔma néte-mii kuƒi ka bɛtu kakpakɔ kamɛni ku nwuna awodu?”

english_verse: Give us the names of the workers!”
translation_verse: Na béye-ma lɛnɔ bekyuli bani ƒui nkya muute-ma kebunku na kakpakɔ kammɔ bɔtu anyi.

english_verse: But God was looking after the Jewish leaders. So the governor and his group decided not to make the people stop working on the temple until they could report to Darius and get his advice.
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti anumi asia Yudaƒuɔ benengu bammɔ lɛlɔ, na bátaya na bada bɔtu baya utédu ka béte Ɔga Dario bɔti. Na báƒɔ nwuna kenye budie na kakunkɛ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: which said: King Darius, we wish you the best!
translation_verse: “Ɔga Dario, keyi kayɔku-ɔ na ƒula lɛga lɛni na aadi kemmo.

english_verse: We went to Judah, where the temple of the great God is being built with huge stones and wooden beams set in the walls. Everyone is working hard, and the building is going up quickly.
translation_verse: “Bula ɔbune, bɔɔyɔ́ ka bute-ɔ bɔti ka bútésie bɔ́vi Yuda kalɛkɛ, na bɔ́nu ka básɔku Unwoti Ɔyikune kakpakɔ baatú. Na bákɔliku atabi ebendi ku kugyiikɛ básia awodu lɛlɔ. Na si ánu adubɔti ka baabla kabla kammɔ kaduɛ na keesíe anumi.

english_verse: We asked those in charge to tell us who gave them permission to rebuild the temple.
translation_verse: “Amu na búye batɔnkune bammɔ bɔnii basu-bu ukyuli ɔni néte-ma ɔyikun ka basɔku kakpakɔ kammɔ ku ana awodu batu.

english_verse: We also asked for the names of their leaders, so that we could write them down for you.
translation_verse: Na bɔ́sɔ búye-ma bana anyi kalɛ na bɔkɛ benengu bammɔ anyi na buti anyi ammɔ bumene-ɔ.

english_verse: They claimed to be servants of the God who rules heaven and earth. And they said they were rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago by one of Israel's greatest kings.
translation_verse: “Amu na bédie kenye banini, ‘Bɔdi Katɔti ɔni nédie katɔ ku kalɔ kabla bablane. Na Unwoti kakpakɔ kani na Israelƒuɔ ɔga ɔdi ɔni mbo ɔyikun ɔ́tu dii ni, bɔ́sɔku ka bɔɔtú.

english_verse: We were told that their people had made God angry, and he let them be captured by Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian king who took them away as captives to Babylonia. Nebuchadnezzar tore down their temple,
translation_verse: Nsu ka bula bati kuuku bákya Katɔti ɔni nédie katɔ ku kalɔ kɔnyi ɔsu ni, ɔ́ya na Ɔga Nebukadnesar ɔni ndi Babilonƒuɔ ɔga na ɔdi Kaldeani úbegyingya kakpakɔ kamɛni na ɔ́yila-ka udu. Na úti bula bekyuli útákya Babilonƒuɔ kalɔ.

english_verse: Sheshbazzar then went to Jerusalem and laid the foundation for the temple, and the work is still going on.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Sesbasar ɔmmɔ úbo na úbeseku ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kalɔ ku bɔtu. Na ɔ́si uwi ɔmmɔ úbedu ɔƒɛni ni, ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kabla kammɔ kenye kpakplaa, nsu bútawɔlɔ tɔ bɔtu.’

english_verse: Your Majesty, please order someone to look up the old records in Babylonia and find out if King Cyrus really did give orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem. We will do whatever you think we should.
translation_verse: “Ɔƒɛni ni, Ɔga Ɔbune, ya na bekyuli beduo kɔkunkɛ kɔni nse ɔga kaduli na Babilon na bawia si Ɔga Kores úbo ɔda dii ka basɔku Yerusalem kakpakɔ kammɔ batu. Na ete-bu bɔti na aya bɔti ƒula kasusu lɛnɔ na litemi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: King Darius ordered someone to go through the old records kept in Babylonia.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Ɔga Dario úbo ɔda na báwia kuuku lɛku lɛbɛladi lɛni nse egulabi kesekɔ na Babilon mmɔ kemmo bánu.

english_verse: Finally, a scroll was found in Ecbatana, the capital of Media Province, and it said: This official record will show
translation_verse: Nsu ɔma kagyumanakɔ kpakplaa kani nkya ɔma unengudi ɔni baalɔ banii Ahmeta na Media kalɛkɛ na bátánu kakunkɛ kammɔ. Na bénweni bákya banini,

english_verse: that in the first year Cyrus was king, he gave orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem, so that sacrifices and offerings could be presented there. It is to be built
translation_verse: “Na Ɔga Kores lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa lideedi kemmo ni, úbo ɔda ka basɔku Yerusalem kakpakɔ batu aani kesii kani na bataabla akpala. “Na kakpakɔ kammɔ bɔkuku bɔdi lɛgba bɔka liti ku aavlene na nwuna bɔbɛbɛ lɛnɔ bɔbla lɛni kani.

english_verse: with one row of wooden beams for each three rows of large stones. The royal treasury will pay for everything.
translation_verse: Na nwuna awodu ni, beti ligyii basia atabi atɛ lɛlɔ. Na kayu biala na kadanku kabla kammɔ lɛlɔ ni, na bedie basiku ɔga kavumi kemmo.

english_verse: Then the gold and silver things that Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple and brought to Babylonia are to be returned to their proper places. King Darius Orders the Work To Continue
translation_verse: Lɛnɔ ni, sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ɔni na Ɔga Nebukadnesar úti ɔ́siku Yerusalem kakpakɔ na úti úbese Babilon ni, basɔku besienku Yerusalem na beti bese kesii kani béti-nwu.” Ɔga Dario Úbo Ɔda Ka Kabla Kammɔ Kesie Anumi

english_verse: King Darius sent this message: Governor Tattenai of Western Province and Shethar Bozenai, you and your advisors must stay away from the temple.
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Dario úti kakunkɛ kamɛni úmene. “Amii Tatenai ketu ɔvi kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔnune ku Setar-Bosnai ku bina kabla benengu bani nkya ketu ɔvi, bɛtɔlɔ kakpakɔ kammɔ kudɔ biteesie.

english_verse: Let the Jewish governor and leaders rebuild it where it stood before. And stop slowing them down!
translation_verse: Na bitebile kabla kammɔ anumi busie. Na bɛya na Yudaƒuɔ benengu basɔku Katɔti kakpakɔ batu na kesii kani na báka-ka bɔtu kudeedi.

english_verse: And don't fail to let the priests in Jerusalem have whatever they need each day so they can offer sacrifices to the God of heaven. Give them young bulls, rams, sheep, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and olive oil.
translation_verse: Na lɛla biala na Yerusalem bakpane badubo bɔwia aani ɔmantɛ bakɔ iye edula ebi iye mma iye nnɔ iye ntɛ ka beteeti taabla limeyi ndi limeyi akpala na Katɔti ɔni nkya Katɔ kakpakɔ ni, na beteete-ma na beteni ɔdi bute.

english_verse: I want them to be able to offer pleasing sacrifices to God and to pray for me and my family.
translation_verse: Bɛbla ala amɛni kalɛ na babla akpala ani na maƒɔ Katɔti ɔni nkya katɔ anu, na bataakpali Katɔ teete ɔga ɔmmɔ ku bebi kadia.

english_verse: If any of you don't obey this order, a wooden beam will be taken from your house and sharpened on one end. Then it will be driven through your body, and your house will be torn down and turned into a garbage dump.
translation_verse: “Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, muubó ɔda ka ukyuli biala na wavumana lɛla lɛni na lɛ́lɛ ugyii mɛni ni, nwuna lɛsa na badubo ɔta bɔni budie na baƒala-nwu ugyii ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla ɔsu ni, badubɔgyingya nwuna ɔtɔ umodi ɔmmɔ balɛ lisu aani alakpi.

english_verse: I ask the God who is worshiped in Jerusalem to destroy any king or nation who tries either to change what I have said or to tear down his temple. I, Darius, give these orders, and I expect them to be followed carefully. The Temple Is Dedicated
translation_verse: Na mɔɔkpali Katɔti ɔni náya na nwuna lɛnyi lɛ́kɛ keliekɔ na mmɔ ka ɔtu ɔga biala iye bekyuli bani mata menye lɛla lɛmɛni lɛlɔ iye bakali ka babwɛ kakpakɔ kammɔ na Yerusalem udie ntɛ bɔmmɔ. “Ami Dario nébo ɔda lɛni. Bɛnu ka bɛ́sia anu na bɛ́di-mu lɛlɔ ulu lɛlɔ siin.” Bátu Kakpakɔ Báwɔlɔ Na Béti-ka Bákya Katɔti Lɛkɔkɔ

english_verse: With great success the Jewish leaders continued working on the temple, while Haggai and Zechariah encouraged them by their preaching. And so, the temple was completed at the command of the God of Israel and by the orders of kings Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes of Persia.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yudaƒuɔ benengu bésie anumi ku bana bɔtu kabla kammɔ na bálɛ lili geen ɔkɛnku kenye udiene Hagai ku Sakaria ɔni ndi Ido kaba kemmo ubi etemila kenye budie teete-ma ɔsu. Na báwɔlɔ kakpakɔ kammɔ bɔtu aani kalɛ na Israel Katɔti ɔ́tina ku Ɔga Kores ku Dario ku Artasasta bani ndi Persiaƒuɔ baga ɔda ɔni na bébo-ma ɔsu.

english_verse: On the third day of the month of Adar in the sixth year of the rule of Darius, the temple was finished.
translation_verse: Báwɔlɔ kakpakɔ kammɔ bɔtu na Yudaƒuɔ kɔbuli kɔni baalɔ Ada kuna limeyi lɛtɛdi lɛlɔ na Ɔga Dario lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa lɛkundi kemmo.

english_verse: The people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else who had returned from exile were happy and celebrated as they dedicated God's temple.
translation_verse: Amu na Yudaƒuɔ ku bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui bádi kakpakɔ kammɔ buti taakya Katɔti lɛkɔkɔ limeyi ku lɛlɔyɔ.

english_verse: One hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs were offered as sacrifices at the dedication. Also twelve goats were sacrificed as sin offerings for the twelve tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Na kakpakɔ buti taakya Katɔti lɛkɔkɔ limeyi lɛmɛni bɔdi kemmo ni, béte ɔmantɛ bɔkɔ eti anyɔ ku baƒonu bagyani eti ene ku baƒonu bagyani bakɔdi eti maane ka beti babla likpidi buti taakyiɛ buvele akpala na Israel kadi bekyuli ƒui lili. Na béte betukpa leevu-inyɔ na Israelƒuɔ adua leevu-anyɔ ammɔ kenye.

english_verse: Then the priests and Levites were assigned their duties in God's temple in Jerusalem, according to the instructions Moses had written. The Passover
translation_verse: Na báya na bakpane bammɔ ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bénye bana kunyekɔ na bana esu esu kenye na Yerusalem ka babla kabla bete Katɔti aani kalɛ na bénweni bákya Mose Ɔku kemmo. Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Lɛlɔ Litemi

english_verse: Everyone who had returned from exile celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
translation_verse: Na Yudaƒuɔ kɔbuli kudeedi limeyi leevu-linedi lɛlɔ ni, bekyuli bani na béƒie bátɔlɔku mmɔ bádi Kukpi Lili Bɔvia Limeyi.

english_verse: The priests and Levites had gone through a ceremony to make themselves acceptable to lead in worship. Then some of them killed Passover lambs for those who had returned, including the other priests and themselves.
translation_verse: Na bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ békisi lɛlɔ na bábla lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ɔmmɔ. Na Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bádu Kukpi Lili Bɔvia koƒonu ubi béte bekyuli beƒiedi bammɔ ƒui ku bana banwani ku bakpane ku ama alati lɛnɔ bana lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The sacrifices were eaten by the Israelites who had returned and by the neighboring people who had given up the sinful customs of other nations in order to worship the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bekyuli beƒiedi bani nénwini bébo mmɔ ƒui bádi, úbunku kadi bamba bekyuli bani náda lɛlɔ bámami bana banwani ku bana ablala ƒui lɛlɔ ka basiaku Israel Katɔti kama.

english_verse: For seven days they celebrated the Festival of Thin Bread. Everyone was happy because the Lord God of Israel had made sure that the king of Assyria would be kind to them and help them build the temple.
translation_verse: Na emeyi maatɛ na béti bádi Bodobodo Ɔni Néteƒu Limeyi ku lɛlɔyɔ, ɔsika Katɔti ɔ́ya na lɛlɔyɔ lɛ́ƒɔ-ma lɛlɔ kemmo ɔkɛnku kalɛ na ɔ́ya na Asiriaƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́vumana nwuna ɔbladu na úbunku na bátu Katɔti ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ béte Israel Katɔti ɔsu.

english_verse: Much later, when Artaxerxes was king of Persia, Ezra came to Jerusalem from Babylonia. Ezra was the son of Seraiah and the grandson of Azariah. His other ancestors were Hilkiah, Shallum, Zadok, Ahitub, Amariah, Azariah, Meraioth, Zerahiah, Uzzi, Bukki, Abishua, Phinehas, Eleazar, and Aaron, the high priest. Ezra was an expert in the Law that the Lord God of Israel had given to Moses, and the Lord made sure that the king gave Ezra everything he asked for.
translation_verse: Na Esra ɔmɛni lɛnɔ ɔ́si Babilon úbo. Na ɔdi ala ɔtinane ɔni ngyi Mose ɔda bubo etemila ani Israelƒuɔ Katɔti úti úte-ma kaduɛ. Na lɛla biala na úye ɔga ɔmmɔ ni, uuti-ni teete-nwu, ɔsika nwuna Unwoti Katɔti ɔsiku-nwu geen.

english_verse: Other Jews, including priests, Levites, musicians, the temple guards, and servants, came to Jerusalem with Ezra. This happened during the seventh year that Artaxerxes was king.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ badi bani ndi bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ ku lɛnu batune ku kayakun bagyumanane ku Kakpakɔ kabla bablane badi básiaku-nwu bébo Yerusalem mmɔ na lɛkwa maatɛdi lɛni na Ɔga Artasasta úlie liboku lɛlɔ mmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: God helped Ezra, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month of that seventh year, after leaving Babylonia on the first day of the first month.
translation_verse: Úse nwuna ulu busie kalɔ ɔ́siku Babilon na limeyi lideedi na kɔbuli kudeedi kemmo, na útéduo Yerusalem limeyi lideedi na kɔbuli kɔlɔndi kemmo, ɔsika nwuna Katɔti ndanku-nwu geen ɔkɛ ku nwuna lɛƒɔndia.

english_verse: Ezra was a priest and an expert in the laws and commands that the Lord had given to Israel. One day King Artaxerxes gave Ezra a letter which said:
translation_verse: Na ɔku ɔni na Ɔga Artasasta únweni úte Esra ɔni ndi ala ɔtinane ku ɔkpane ku okloƒu ɔni ngyi Unwoti ɔda bubo ku ala ani ƒui na únyimi úte Israelƒuɔ kemmo kaduɛ na búdie mɛni.

english_verse: Greetings from the great King Artaxerxes to Ezra the priest and expert in the teachings of the God of heaven.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔ́si baga ƒui Ɔga Artasasta kudɔ na líti muute Ɔkpane Esra ɔni ndi Katɔ ƒui Katɔti ɔda bubo ala ɔtinane. Mɔɔkya-a kenye.

english_verse: Any of the people of Israel or their priests or Levites in my kingdom may go with you to Jerusalem if they want to. My seven advisors and I agree that you may go to Jerusalem and Judah to find out if the laws of your God are being obeyed.
translation_verse: Ami ɔga ku mina benengu maatɛ mɔɔtala-a ka teesie Yerusalem ku Yuda na atávi mmɔ bene ƒui na anu kalɛ ƒula Katɔti ɔda bubo ɔku ɔni nkya-a enu kemmo lɛlɔ bɔdi buse na mmɔ.

english_verse: When you go, take the silver and gold that I and my advisors are freely giving to the God of Israel, whose temple is in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Lɛnɔ ni, si ésela na eti sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ɔni na ɔga ku nwuna benengu béte-ɔ, na eti esienku Israelƒuɔ Katɔti ɔni keliekɔ ndi Yerusalem mmɔ.

english_verse: Take the silver and gold that you collect from everywhere in Babylonia. Also take the gifts that your own people and priests have so willingly contributed for the temple of your God in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Lɛnɔ ni, na eti sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ɔni ƒui na adubɔkɛ na Babilon kalɛkɛ ku kaƒɔ ƒaa etela ani ƒui na Israelƒuɔ ku bakpane bani nkya mmɔ badubute-ɔ ka eti etébunku bana Katɔti kakpakɔ kani nkya Yerusalem bɔtu.

english_verse: Use the money carefully to buy the best bulls, rams, lambs, grain, and wine. Then sacrifice them on the altar at God's temple in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na ada egulabi ani búti búte-ɔ mmɔ kaduɛ. Na eti eye ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku bakɔ bakɔdi ku baƒonu bakɔdi ku kakpa ku ntɛ na eti abla akpala na Katɔti kakpakɔ lɛkpabi lɛni nkya Yerusalem mmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: If any silver or gold is left, you and your people may use it for whatever pleases your God.
translation_verse: Na sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ɔni mebu ni, akana na awɔ ku ƒula banwani biti bɛbla lɛla na biala bɛɛyɔ́ na lɛkɛnku ƒula Katɔti lɛƒɔyɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Give your God the other articles that have been contributed for use in his temple.
translation_verse: Na eti akyami ani búti búte-ɔ ka beti bataabla Kakpakɔ kammɔ ala ete Katɔti.

english_verse: If you need to get anything else for the temple, you may have the money you need from the royal treasury.
translation_verse: Na lɛla bamba biala na aawia ka abla na Kakpakɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ni, na edie asiku ɔga egulabi kavumi kammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Ezra, you are a priest and an expert in the laws of the God of heaven, and I order all treasurers in Western Province to do their very best to help you.
translation_verse: Ami Ɔga Artasasta muubó ketu ɔvi egulabi badane bammɔ ƒui ɔda ka lɛla biala na Ɔkpane Esra ɔni ndi Katɔti ɔda bubo ala ɔtinane ɔɔwia ɔsiku-mii kudɔ

english_verse: They must provide whatever the God of heaven demands for his temple, so that he won't be angry with me and with the kings who rule after me.
translation_verse: Na bɛsia anu kaduɛ na bite lɛla biala na Unwoti ɔni nkya Katɔ ɔ́su úse ka beti babla nwuna kakpakɔ lɛlɔ kabla siin lɛni kani, kalɛ na ulákɛ kɔnyi ulakya-mi iye ukyuli ɔni melie-mi kenye.

english_verse: We want you to know that no priests, Levites, musicians, guards, temple servants, or any other temple workers will have to pay any kind of taxes.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔyá na bɛti ka ukyuli biala uuubo kenyekɔ kadi na ɔƒɔ kuyii ɔsiku bakpane iye Lewiƒuɔ iye kabla bablane iye ukyuli biala ɔni mɔɔbla kabla kadi na kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo kudɔ.

english_verse: Ezra, use the wisdom God has given you and choose officials and leaders to govern the people of Western Province. These leaders should know God's laws and have them taught to anyone who doesn't know them.
translation_verse: Na awɔ, Esra, ti lɛnunda lɛni na ƒula Katɔti úte-ɔ na awia litemi batɛne bani ngyi ƒula Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ala na bataatɛ ketu ɔvi badi bammɔ litemi. Na bani na baaagyi ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ni, na atina-ma ala.

english_verse: Everyone who fails to obey God's Law or the king's law will be punished without pity. They will either be executed or put in prison or forced to leave their country, or have all they own taken away. Ezra Praises God
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔni na uládi ƒula Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ iye ɔga ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka badu-nwu iye babɔku-nwu balɛku kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ iye beti kɔnu basia nwuna akɛla ƒui lɛlɔ iye bakya-nwu ɔtɔ kɔnakunwi.

english_verse: Because King Artaxerxes was so kind, Ezra said: Praise the Lord God of our ancestors! He made sure that the king honored the Lord's temple in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amu na Esra úmwi Katɔti ɔnini, “Bemwi Unwoti bula bati kuuku Katɔti ɔni néti lɛla lɛmɛni ɔ́kya ɔga kayi kemmo kalɛ na ɔsia ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na úti ɔbu úte Unwoti kakpakɔ na Yerusalem.

english_verse: God has told the king, his advisors, and his powerful officials to treat me with kindness. The Lord God has helped me, and I have been able to bring many Jewish leaders back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́bla-mi lɛƒɔndia na ɔga ɔmmɔ ku nwuna kasusu bakyane ku nwuna benengu bayikune bammɔ ƒui anumi. Na ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu na líse kayi na lítiku Israel batɔnkune na básiaku-mi na bɔ́kɔ búsie Yerusalem.”

english_verse: Artaxerxes was king of Persia when I led the following chiefs of the family groups from Babylonia to Jerusalem:
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani anyi ndubo mɛni ndi lɛtɔ benengu bani anyi na bénweni bébunku bani ƒui násiaku Esra bási Babilon bénwini bébo Yerusalem na Ɔga Artasasta lɛga bɔdi uwi.

english_verse: polished bronze articles as valuable as gold.
translation_verse: Pinehas kaba ni, Gersom, Itamar kaba ni, Daniel, Dawid kaba ni, Hatus,

english_verse: Gershom of the Phinehas family; Daniel of the Ithamar family; Hattush son of Shecaniah of the David family; Zechariah and
translation_verse: Na Bigwai kaba ni, Utai ku Sabud, na bana banana

english_verse: I said to the priests: You belong to the Lord, the God of your ancestors, and these things also belong to him. The silver and gold were willingly given as gifts to the Lord.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́su-ma nnii, “Amii ku sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ɔmmɔ ƒui ni, bɛdi ala ani bédie bese sɛsɛɛ béte Unwoti. Na sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ɔmmɔ ni, adi kaƒɔ ƒaa etela akpala ete Katɔti ɔni ndi bina bati kuuku Katɔti.

english_verse: I brought everyone together by the river that flows to the town of Ahava where we camped for three days. Not one Levite could be found among the people and priests.
translation_verse: Amu na ami Esra lɛ́ya na bekyuli bani ƒui nsiaku-mi mmɔ bédi bénye ketu kani mɔɔgbá taavi Ahawa ɔma kemmo mmɔ. Na bɔ́kya mmɔ emeyi atɛ sɔɔn. Na mmɔ na lɛ́nu ka bakpane bakya bekyuli bammɔ akɔ. Nsu Lewiƒuɔ beeebo-ma kemmo.

english_verse: So I sent for the leaders Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam. I also sent for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were very wise counselors.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́tala na bátálɔ batɔnkune bani ndi Elieser ku Ariel ku Semaia ku Elnatan ku Yarib ku Elnatan ku Natan ku Sakaria ku Mesulam ku ala batinane inyɔ bani ndi Yoiarib ku Elnatan béboku-mi.

english_verse: Then I sent them to Iddo, the leader at Casiphia, and I told them to ask him and his temple workers to send people to serve in God's temple.
translation_verse: Na lɛ́tala-ma lɛ́kya Ido ɔni ndi Kasiƒia ɔtɔnkune kudɔ. Na lɛ́su-ma lɛla lɛni na badubusie batásu Ido ku nwuna banwani ku kakpakɔ kabla bablane bani nkya Kasiƒia ɔma kemmo mmɔ kalɛ na bawia bekyuli badi bemene-bu na bababla kabla na Katɔti kakpakɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: God was kind to us and caused them to send a skillful man named Sherebiah, who was a Levite from the family of Mahli. Eighteen of his relatives came with him.
translation_verse: Na ka bula Katɔti kɔnu kɔsia-bu lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, bákpanku ɔbune Serebia ɔni na ɔ́si Lewi ubidi Mahli ɔni ɔti ndi Israel kaba kemmo ku nwuna banwani ku nwuna bebi leevu-maane béboku.

english_verse: We were also sent Hashabiah and Jeshaiah from the family of Merari along with
translation_verse: Na Hasabia ku Yesaia bani nási Merari kaba kemmo ku bana badi aavlanyɔ lɛnɔ básiaku-ma bébo.

english_verse: Beside the Ahava River, I asked the people to go without eating and to pray. We humbled ourselves and asked God to bring us and our children safely to Jerusalem with all of our possessions.
translation_verse: Amu uwi ɔni na búdu Ahawa Ketu kudɔ ni, mmɔ na líbo ɔda na ɔ́ya na búnyimi kenye kalɛ na buboku lɛlɔ kalɔ na Katɔti anumi na buvele-nwu ka ɔgyumana abu ku bula bebi ku bula ala ani ƒui na bɔdanku kalɛ na bula ulu busie bɔbla buɛɛ.

english_verse: So we went without food and asked God himself to protect us, and he answered our prayers. The Gifts for the Temple
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu búnyimi kenye na búti etemila ammɔ bɔ́va Katɔti anumi na únu bula bɔkpali.

english_verse: I chose twelve of the leading priests—Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their relatives.
translation_verse: Amu na lídie bakpane benengu leevu-inyɔ na Serebia ku Hasabia bebunku-ma ku bana banwani leevu líbunku-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Be sure to guard them and keep them safe until you reach Jerusalem. Then weigh them inside God's temple in the presence of the chief priests, the Levites, and the heads of the Israelite families.
translation_verse: Bɛgyumana ala ammɔ kaduɛ utédu ka bɛ́kɔku-nya na Unwoti kaduli kani nkya Yerusalem. Na bakpane benengu ku Lewiƒuɔ ku Israelƒuɔ lɛtɔ benengu bammɔ anumi.”

english_verse: The priests and Levites then took charge of the gifts that had been weighed, so they could take them to the temple of our God in Jerusalem. The Return to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ báƒɔ sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ɔni bákɔku bánu mmɔ ku ala akladi ani na ɔdi ka beti besienku Katɔti Kaduli na Yerusalem mmɔ.

english_verse: On the twelfth day of the first month, we left the Ahava River and started for Jerusalem. Our God watched over us, and as we traveled along, he kept our enemies from ambushing us.
translation_verse: Na limeyi leevu-linyɔdi na kɔbuli kudeedi kemmo ni, bɔ́ta bɔ́si Ahawa Ketudɔ na búti anumi bɔ́tina Yerusalem na Katɔti ɔdanku-bu. Na ɔ́gyumana-bu ɔ́lɛku bula bekisine ƒui enu kemmo na ulu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: After arriving in Jerusalem, we rested for three days.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bútéduo Yerusalem na bɔ́nwuna emeyi atɛ na mmɔ.

english_verse: Then on the fourth day we went to God's temple, where the silver, the gold, and the other things were weighed and given to the priest Meremoth son of Uriah. With him were Eleazar son of Phinehas and the two Levites, Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
translation_verse: Na limeyi linedi lɛlɔ ni, búti sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ɔni bɔ́kɔku ku ala akladi ƒui búsienku Katɔti kaduli na bútákɔku-nya búte Uria ubidi Meremot ɔni ndi ɔkpane ku Pinehas ubidi Eleasar ɔni muubunku-nwu. Na Lewiƒuɔ bani ndi Yesua ubidi Yosabad ku Binui ubidi Noadia lɛnɔ bénye mmɔ ɔdi.

english_verse: goats were sacrificed for the sins of the people.
translation_verse: Na Asgad kaba ni, Hakatan ubidi Yahona, na banana

english_verse: Some of those who had returned took the king's orders to the governors and officials in Western Province. Then the officials did what they could for the people and for the temple of God.
translation_verse: Na béti ɔga kɔkunkɛ kɔni ndanku ɔda ɔni na úbo béte aban bagadine ku kɔlɛkɛ kɔni na Euƒrate Ketu ɔvi lɛlɔ badine benengu bammɔ na bénu kalɔ na béte kebunku na Katɔti ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ bɔtu kemmo.

english_verse: Later the Jewish leaders came to me and said: Many Israelites, including priests and Levites, are living just like the people around them. They are even guilty of some of the horrible sins of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na báwɔlɔ ala ammɔ ƒui bɔbla ni, Yudaƒuɔ benengu badi bábasu ami Esra banini, “Israelƒuɔ ku Lewiƒuɔ ku bakpane bani nli mɛni lɛnɔ bebunku bekyuli bani nátamami lɛlɔ bétedie bekyuli bani lɛma nkya bula amadɔ aani Kanaanƒuɔ ku Hitiƒuɔ ku Perisiƒuɔ ku Yebusiƒuɔ ku Amonƒuɔ ku Moabƒuɔ ku Egyipteƒuɔ ku Amoriƒuɔ ala bɔbla ani muusé lɛlɔ mmɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: Some Israelite men have married foreign women and have let their sons do the same thing. Our own officials and leaders were the first to commit this disgusting sin, and now God's holy people are mixed with foreigners.
translation_verse: Na Yudaƒuɔ ku bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ béeti lɛlɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Katɔti bekyuli kedee bénwini bekyuli bani néti lɛlɔ básala ku kadi bamba bekyuli. Na benengu bammɔ ku bakutine bammɔ geen ntɔnku udu buɛ ɔmmɔ bɔbla na bálɛ litemi geen lɛmmɔ kama.”

english_verse: This news made me so angry that I ripped my clothes and tore hair from my head and beard. Then I just sat in shock
translation_verse: Amu ka línu ɔmɛni ni, lɛ́ni mina awu lɛ́bwɛ na lɛ́gyɔ mina lili linwini ku ukwi! Na lɛ́yu lílie kalɔ ku bɔyia geen ku kɔnyana.

english_verse: until the time for the evening sacrifice. Many of our people were greatly concerned and gathered around me, because the God of Israel had warned us to stay away from foreigners. Ezra's Prayer
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani ƒui mbo bɔyia bete Israel Katɔti litemi báni béde-mi, na bekyuli bani kekpo kéƒie na báka bunwini bubo litemi lɛlɔ tadi ku ɔbladu buɛ ɔmɛni ɔsu. Kɔnyana ku bɔyia bɔmɛni kemmo na lɛ́ƒɔ mmɔ bulie útédu useyi akpala bɔbla uwi.

english_verse: At the time of the evening sacrifice, I was still sitting there in sorrow with my clothes all torn. So I got down on my knees, then lifted my arms,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na useyi akpala bɔbla uwi údu ni, lɛ́ta na kesii kani na lɛ́yu líwi mmɔ. Nsu na mmu nkya lɛwu lɛni nábuɛ mmɔ. Na lɛ́lɛ akɔnkɔ na lɛ́talaku mina enu katɔ na lɛ́kpali Unwoti Katɔti.

english_verse: and prayed: I am much too ashamed to face you, Lord God. Our sins and our guilt have swept over us like a flood that reaches up to the heavens.
translation_verse: Na lɛ́su-nwu nnini, “O mina Katɔti, kɔƒa kuukpó-mi ka lɛtalaku mina anumi katɔ muedi na ƒula anumi. Ɔsika bula ekpidi áakuku etulo-bu na ákuku laa na éedu katɔ.

english_verse: Since the time of our ancestors, all of us have sinned. That's why we, our kings, and our priests have often been defeated by other kings. They have killed some of us and made slaves of others; they have taken our possessions and made us ashamed, just as we are today.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si bula bati kuuku uwi úbedu ɔƒɛni ni, abu bani ndi ƒula bekyuli bɔ́bla likpidi bonwu geen. Na ɔ́si bula ekpidi ɔsu ni, bula baga ku bula bakpane béduo baga babambadi enu kemmo. Na bádu badi na béƒie badi ala báƒɔ, na béƒie badi lɛnɔ bátɔlɔku, na búduo kɔƒa kubendi kemmo aani kalɛ bɔmu buse ɔmwi.

english_verse: But for now, Lord God, you have shown great kindness to us. You made us truly happy by letting some of us settle in this sacred place and by helping us in our time of slavery.
translation_verse: “Na ɔƒɛni uwi klukui kama mɛni ni, O Unwoti ɔni ndi bula Katɔti, ánu-bu kɔnyana na áya na bula ɛlɛɛ badi búbu, na bɔ́kɛ kakyakɔ kabuni aani ƒula kɔtɔma kedee. Awɔ náya na bula anumi ásɔ ékeye na bɔ́kɛ bɔnwuna bɔ́siku bekyuli bamba lɛlɔ bɔdi kalɔ.

english_verse: We are slaves, but you have never turned your back on us. You love us, and because of you, the kings of Persia have helped us. It's as though you have given us new life! You let us rebuild your temple and live safely in Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ina ka bɔdi bekyuli bamba kabla bablane ni, awɔ Katɔti átanyonu-bu átakya bekyuli bamba lɛlɔ bɔdi lɛbibo lɛmmɔ kemmo. Mmomu ánu-bu ku lɛƒɔndia na Persiaƒuɔ baga anumi na éte-bu ngba bɔwɔdi kalɛ na bɔsɔku Katɔti kakpakɔ bɔtu na bɔtalaku atɔnku ammɔ. Na awɔ nátu bɔgyumana awodu ɔ́mana-bu na Yuda ku Yerusalem.

english_verse: Our God, what can we say now? Even after all this, we have disobeyed the commands
translation_verse: “Nsu ɔƒɛni ni, O Katɔti, bi na bɔdubɔsu na ala ani ƒui nálɛ mɛni lɛlɔ? Bula ƒui bútabu ƒula ɔda bubo

english_verse: that were given to us by your servants the prophets. They said the land you are giving us is full of sinful and wicked people, who never stop doing disgusting things.
translation_verse: bɔni na éti ásiaku ƒula kabla bablane bani ndi ƒula kenye bediene lɛlɔ anini, ‘Kalɔ kani kemmo na bísela buduo na biti-ka binwini bina kadi mɛni ni, bekyuli bani nákya-ka kemmo bébile-ka ku bana likyulikpi ala bɔbla na ala ani muusé lɛlɔ áƒɔ-ka ƒui tɛɛ ɔ́si ɔvi unwi úsie ɔkladi.

english_verse: And we were warned not to let our daughters and sons marry their sons and daughters. Your prophets also told us never to help those foreigners or even let them live in peace. You wanted us to become strong and to enjoy the good things in the land, then someday to leave it to our children forever.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu biteti bina bebi belekubi bitete-ma na beti iye bɛya na bina bakloƒu beti bana belekubi. Na bitawia ulu ɔdi na amii ku ama bɛbla unwi na ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ. Na bɛdubɔkɛ ɔlɔkplu na bɛdi ala abuni ani nkya kalɔ kammɔ kemmo na bise bina bebi ku bawɔ kama úsela uwi ƒui.’

english_verse: You punished us because of our terrible sins. But you did not punish us nearly as much as we deserve, and you have brought some of us back home.
translation_verse: “Ala ani nálɛku-bu ƒui ni, ɔkɛnku bula likyulikpi ku alaekpidi bonwu ani na bɔ́bla ɔsu na úbo-nwu kemmo lɛni. Nsu awɔ bula Katɔti átani-bu kɔtu kɔni námanku bula ekpidi na áya na bula akɔ badi búbu bulie ngba.

english_verse: Why should we disobey your commands again by letting our sons and daughters marry these foreigners who do such disgusting things? That would make you angry enough to destroy us all!
translation_verse: Na bi ɔsu na ɔlɛka bɔsɔ budie ƒula ɔda bubo atu lɛnɔ na abu ku bekyuli bekpidi bamɛni buteeti lɛlɔ? Si bɔ́bla lɛni ni, adubuti kɔnyi akya-bu geen na ayila-bu udu ƒui ɔni na ina ukyuli unwi pɛ ulelie ngba.

english_verse: Lord God of Israel, you have been more than fair by letting a few of us survive. But once again, our sins have made us ashamed to face you.
translation_verse: O Unwoti, Israel Katɔti, ese siin! Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu na bula ɛlɛɛ bamɛni búbu bɔkya ngba ɔmwi. Aanu-bu nnye ƒula anumi ku bula bɔsɔ ina ka nka bula akɔ ɔdi ulakana-a anumi bɔda bɔlɛ.”

english_verse: While Ezra was down on his knees in front of God's temple, praying with tears in his eyes and confessing the sins of the people of Israel, a large number of men, women, and children gathered around him and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni Esra ɔkya uubó lɛlɔ taava kalɔ na uuwulo taakpali Katɔti na uudie bana alaekpidi kalɔ teevele buti taakyiɛ na Katɔti kaduli ni, bekyuli lisu pii bábaka bámana-nwu na badi beleku ku banana ku banamu na ama lɛnɔ bakya beewulo momoomo.

english_verse: Shecaniah son of Jehiel from the family of Elam said: Ezra, we have disobeyed God by marrying these foreign women. But there is still hope for the people of Israel,
translation_verse: Amu na Yehiel ubidi Sekania ɔni nási Elam kaba kemmo ɔ́kpɛ úde Esra na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Bɔ́lɛ bula Katɔti kama. Ɔsika búsie bɔkya buuti kadi bamba beleku bani nlie nde-bu. Nsu ɔmɛni kama ƒui ni, bɔmu bubo lɛnunsia bute Israelƒuɔ.

english_verse: if we follow your advice and the advice of others who truly respect the laws of God. We must promise God that we will divorce our foreign wives and send them away, together with their children.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, ya na bunyimi lɛla lɛdi na Katɔti anumi na bɔbɔku beleku bamɛni ku bana bebi na batɔlɔ ɔkɛnku lɛla lɛni na awɔ ku bekyuli bani mɔɔbu Katɔti ɔda bubo bɛdubɔsu-bu. Na bɛnu ka bɔ́bla lɛla biala bɔ́siaku ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Ezra, it's up to you to do something! We will support whatever you do. So be brave!
translation_verse: Ta, na abla lɛla lɛdi asiku litemi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ, na bɔdubunye-ɔ kama. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu kya kayi na esie lɛla lɛdi kalɔ.”

english_verse: Ezra stood up and made the chief priests, the Levites, and everyone else in Israel swear that they would follow the advice of Shecaniah.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Esra ɔ́ta na ɔ́ya na bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ benengu ku Israelƒuɔ bakladi bése kenye ka badubɔbla lɛla lɛni na Sekania ɔ́su mmɔ.

english_verse: Then Ezra left God's temple and went to spend the night in the living quarters of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. He felt sorry because of what the people had done, and he did not eat or drink a thing.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ɔ́ta ɔ́lɛ bekyuli bammɔ akɔ na Kakpakɔ anumi mmɔ, na útéduo Eliasib ubidi Yohanan kaduli na ɔtɛ mmɔ uuwulo usien umodi ɔni na útadi iye útani lɛla lɛdi na kalɛ na Israelƒuɔ bekyuli beƒiedi bani nénwini bébo mmɔ bálɛ Katɔti kama ɔsu.

english_verse: The officials and leaders sent a message to all who had returned from Babylonia and were now living in Jerusalem and Judah. This message told them to meet in Jerusalem within three days, or else they would lose everything they owned and would no longer be considered part of the people that had returned from Babylonia.
translation_verse: Na si awɔ ɔni na étebo emeyi atɛ kama ni, badubuti kɔnu basia ƒula akɛla ƒui lɛlɔ, aani kalɛ na benengu ku bakutine bényimi bése. Na badubɔda ukyuli ɔmmɔ bedie Israelƒuɔ bani kekpo kéƒie-ma akɔ.”
