english_verse: Three days later, on the twentieth day of the ninth month, everyone from Judah and Benjamin came to Jerusalem and sat in the temple courtyard. It was a serious meeting, and they sat there, trembling in the rain.
translation_verse: Na emeyi atɛ ammɔ kemmo ni, bekyuli bani ƒui nási Yuda ku Benyamin bábasala na Yerusalem. Na limeyi aavlanyɔdi lɛlɔ na kɔbuli yaalenwidi kemmo ni, na bana ƒui báasa beli Katɔti ɔtɔ anumi kaduli kemmo. Na ɔnantu ɔni nkya mɔɔna ku lɛla lɛni na limeyi lɛmmɔ ablala adanku ɔsu ni, kɔnyana ku kayi bɔkpulu bɔ́ƒɔ ukyuli biala lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: Ezra the priest stood up and said: You have broken God's Law by marrying foreign women, and you have made the whole nation guilty!
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔkpane Esra ɔ́ta únye na ɔ́su bekyuli bammɔ ɔnini, “Bɛ́lɛ Katɔti kama na bíti kadi bamba beleku na bɛ́bla likpidi bɛ́sia Israelƒuɔ ekpidi ani na bábla kama.

english_verse: Now you must confess your sins to the Lord God of your ancestors and obey him. Divorce your foreign wives and don't have anything to do with the rest of the foreigners who live around here.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔƒaani ni, bidie bina ekpidi kalɔ bɛtina bina Unwoti ɔni ndi bina bati kuuku Katɔti na bivele-nwu. Na bɛbla lɛla lɛni mayɔ-nwu kaƒɔ. Na bɛda lɛlɔ bɛmami kadi bamba bekyuli bani na beli bámana-mii mmɔ lɛlɔ na bɛnyonu bana beleku bammɔ.”

english_verse: Everyone in the crowd shouted: You're right! We will do what you say.
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bédie kenye ku kudu básu banini, “Lɛla lɛni na ásu lɛdi ulu! Na ɔdi ka bɔbla bɔsiaku lɛni.

english_verse: But there are so many of us, and we can't just stay out here in this downpour. A lot of us have sinned by marrying foreign women, and the matter can't be settled in only a day or two.
translation_verse: Nsu bekyuli lisu lɛmɛni líbomo lɛ́gya na ɔnantu lɛnɔ ɔɔna momoomo na bulakana-nwu akɔ bɔsɔ bunye lɛni. Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, bulakana litemi lɛmɛni udu bɔdaku bɔwɔlɔ na limeyi linwi iye emeyi anyɔ kemmo. Ɔsika bɔƒiɔ geen na bɔdi-bu na lɛla lɛmɛni kemmo.

english_verse: Why can't our officials stay on in Jerusalem and take care of this for us? Let everyone who has sinned in this way meet here at a certain time with leaders and judges from their own towns. If we take care of this problem, God will surely stop being so terribly angry with us.
translation_verse: Na aya na bula bakutine basɔ bakya Yerusalem na beti kabla kamɛni basia lɛlɔ. Na ukyuli biala na uti kadi bamba uleku ni, bete-nwu uwi na ubo ubasiaku benengu ku litemi batɛne bani nási nwuna ɔma. Na bɔdubɔbla lɛni wetédu ka kaƒɔ káyɔ Katɔti na udie nwuna kɔnyi na litemi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah were the only ones who objected, except for the two Levites, Meshullam and Shabbethai.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala útata útenye kasusu kamɛni lɛlɔ ntu Asahel ubidi Yonatan ku Tikwa ubidi Yahasia, na Mesulam ku Sabetai ɔni ndi Lewini bénye-ma kama.

english_verse: Everyone else who had returned from exile agreed with the plan. So Ezra the priest chose men who were heads of the families, and he listed their names. They started looking into the matter on the first day of the tenth month,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bekyuli bani na kekpo kéƒie-ma na bénwini bébo mmɔ báƒɔ kasusu kani badaku mmɔ. Na ɔkpane Esra údie banana ɔlɛku kaba benengu bammɔ akɔ na únweni bana anyi ɔ́kya ɔku kemmo. Na limeyi lideedi na kɔbuli leevudi kemmo ni, bekyuli bammɔ bése bana kabla kalɔ.

english_verse: and they did not finish until the first day of the first month of the next year. The Men Who Had Foreign Wives
translation_verse: Na ɔni na uteedu kɔbuli kudeedi limeyi lideedi ni, báwɔlɔ ku bekyuli bani néti kadi bamba beleku mmɔ ƒui etemila kemmo buduo. Bálɛ Banana Bani Néti Kadi Bamba Beleku Anumi

english_verse: Hanani and Zebadiah from the family of Immer;
translation_verse: Na Imer kaba kemmo ni, ama ndi Hanani ku Sebadia

english_verse: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah from the family of Harim;
translation_verse: Na Harim kaba kemmo ni, Maaseia ku Elia ku Semaia ku Yehiel ku Usia.

english_verse: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah from the family of Pashhur.
translation_verse: Na Pashur kaba kemmo ni, ama ndi Eliehoenai ku Maaseia ku Ismael ku Netanel ku Yosabad ku Elasa.

english_verse: Those Levites who had foreign wives were: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah , Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
translation_verse: Na Lewiƒuɔ akɔ ni, Yosabad ku Simei ku Kelaia ɔni ndi Kelita ku Petahia ku Yuda ku Elieser.

english_verse: Eliashib, the musician, had a foreign wife. These temple guards had foreign wives: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
translation_verse: Na lɛnu batune akɔ ni, Eliasib. Na kɔyakun bagyumanane ni, Salum ku Telem ku Uri

english_verse: Here is a list of the others from Israel who had foreign wives: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Hashabiah, and Benaiah from the family of Parosh;
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bamba lɛnɔ ndi bamɛni. Na Paros kaba kemmo ni, Ramia ku Yisia ku Malkiya ku Miyamin ku Eleasar ku Malkiya ku Benaia.

english_verse: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah from the family of Elam;
translation_verse: Na Elam kaba kemmo ni, Matania ku Sekaria ku Yehiel ku Abdi ku Yeremot ku Elia.

english_verse: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza from the family of Zattu;
translation_verse: Na Satu kaba kemmo ni, Elieoenai ku Eliasib ku Matania ku Yeremot ku Sabad ku Asisa.

english_verse: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai from the family of Bebai;
translation_verse: Na Bebai kaba kemmo ni, Yehohanan ku Hanania ku Sabai ku Atlai.

english_verse: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth from the family of Bani;
translation_verse: Na Bani kaba kemmo ni, Mesulam ku Maluk ku Adaia ku Yasub ku Seal ku Yeremot.

english_verse: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh from the family of Pahath Moab;
translation_verse: Na Pahat-Moab kaba kemmo ni, Adna ku Kelal ku Benaia ku Maaseia ku Matania ku Besaleel ku Binui ku Manase.

english_verse: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei from the family of Hashum;
translation_verse: Na Hasum kaba kemmo ni, Matenai ku Matata ku Sabad ku Eliƒelet ku Yeremai ku Manase ku Simei.

english_verse: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah from the family of Nebo.
translation_verse: Na Nebo kaba kemmo ni, Yeiel ku Matitia ku Sabad ku Sebina ku Yadai ku Yoel ku Benaia.

english_verse: These men divorced their foreign wives, then sent them and their children away.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bamɛni ƒui néti kadi bamba beleku, na badi báwɔ bebi básiku beleku bammɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: I am Nehemiah son of Hacaliah, and in this book I tell what I have done. During the month of Chislev in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes ruled Persia, I was in his fortress city of Susa,
translation_verse: Hakalia ubidi Nehemia etemila na adi mɛni. Na lɛkwa aavlanyɔdi kɔbuli leevu-kunyɔdi kemmo ni, na lɛ́kya kagyumanakɔ kpakplaa kadi na ɔma unengudi ɔni baalɔ banii Susan kemmo.

english_verse: when my brother Hanani came with some men from Judah. So I asked them about the Jews who had escaped from being captives in Babylonia. I also asked them about the city of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Mina ɔnwani ɔni baalɔ Hanani ku bekyuli bamba badi bási Yuda bébo-mi kudɔ. Mmɔ na líye-ma Yerusalem ku Yudaƒuɔ bakladi bani béteƒie na kekpo kammɔ kemmo lɛlɔ.

english_verse: They told me, “Those captives who have come back are having all kinds of troubles. They are terribly disgraced, Jerusalem's walls are broken down, and its gates have been burned.”
translation_verse: Amu na bédie kenye ka bani nébu na bátakana-ma buƒie mmɔ bakya lɛbibo ku kɔƒa bonwu kɔdi kemmo geen. Ɔsika Yerusalem awodu ani na áka ámana ɔma ɔmmɔ ƒui áƒɛ éwi kalɔ. Na bákyula ana kɔyakun lɛnɔ.

english_verse: When I heard this, I sat down on the ground and cried. Then for several days, I mourned; I went without eating to show my sorrow, and I prayed:
translation_verse: Amu ka línu etemila amɛni ni, lílie kalɔ emeyi adi na líwulo kɔnyana na línyimi kenye na lívele Unwoti ɔni nkya katɔ na lɛ́kpali-nwu.

english_verse: Lord God of heaven, you are great and fearsome. And you faithfully keep your promises to everyone who loves you and obeys your commands.
translation_verse: Na lɛ́su nnini, “O Unwoti Katɔti ɔni nkya katɔ, ébomo na ebo ɔyikun na ámanku ka bɔyia-a. Na adi Ati ɔni na eeti bɔyɔ taadi ƒula bunyimi lɛlɔ teete bekyuli bani na aayɔ́ ka baadi ƒula ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: I am your servant, so please have mercy on me and answer the prayer that I make day and night for these people of Israel who serve you. I, my family, and the rest of your people have sinned
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu buvele nda-a, se atu na ebimi anumi, na enu ami ƒula kabla ɔblane bɔkpali bɔni na mɔɔkpali-ɔ usien ku ɔƒɛ na ƒula kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ lili. Unwoti buvele muudie alaekpidi ani na ami ku mina kaduli bekyuli ku Israelƒuɔ ƒui bɔ́bla kalɔ ka eti-nya kyiɛ-bu.

english_verse: by choosing to disobey you and the laws and teachings you gave to your servant Moses.
translation_verse: Ɔsika bɔ́bla likyulikpi bɔ́kya-a. Na bútadi Mose ɔda bubo bɔni na éte-bu mmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Please remember the promise you made to Moses. You told him that if we were unfaithful, you would scatter us among foreign nations.
translation_verse: “Na enyimo ɔda ɔni na ébo ƒula kabla ɔblane Mose ásu anii, ‘Si bítabla ala bítasiaku ulu lɛlɔ ni, ndubo-mii bɔbɔku butákya kadi bamba bekyuli akɔ.

english_verse: But you also said that no matter how far away we were, we could turn to you and start obeying your laws. Then you would bring us back to the place where you have chosen to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Nsu si bínwini bíbo-mi kudɔ na bɛɛdi mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ni, ina kekpo kéƒie bina bekyuli kátákya ɔgyu kakaaka muedi ni, ndubɔsɔku-ma mbasala. Na basɔ benwini bebo kesii kani na lɛ́ƒuna líse ka bataakpa-mi mɛni.’

english_verse: Our Lord, I am praying for your servants—those you rescued by your great strength and mighty power.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu muuvele-ɔ ka ƒula bekyuli ku kabla bablane na badi na awɔ néti ƒula ɔyikun bonwu ékpo áƒɔ-ma.

english_verse: Please answer my prayer and the prayer of your other servants who gladly honor your name. When I serve the king his wine today, make him pleased with me and let him do what I ask.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu, O Unwoti, se atu na enu ƒula kabla ɔblane ku ƒula kabla bablane bani mɔɔbu ƒula lɛnyi bɔkpali. Na ɔmwi kadi kamɛni ni, na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔnu-mi kɔnyana na etemila ani ndubo bɔda bɔva-nwu anumi lɛlɔ.” Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ami Nehemia nátaaƒɔ ntɛ teete ɔga ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: During the month of Nisan in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king, I served him his wine, as I had done before. But this was the first time I had ever looked depressed.
translation_verse: Na kɔbuli kunedi kama na lɛkwa aavlanyɔdi lɛmmɔ kemmo kani ni, na Ɔga Artasasta ɔ́kya ɔɔdi, ka líti nwuna ntɛ lísienku-nwu ni, ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́nu ka mina anumi ábla kɔnyana geen.

english_verse: So the king said, “Why do you look so sad? You're not sick. Something must be bothering you.” Even though I was frightened,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu úye-mi ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na ábla anumi kɔnyana kɔnyana lɛni ɔni na ɔɔɔdi ɔlɛ ɔdi nda-a? Ɔmɛni ɔɔɔdanku lɛla lɛdi, mmomu kayi kemmo kɔnyana bɔdu muukpóku-ɔ kayi kemmo.” Liƒu pii lɛɛda-mi.

english_verse: I answered, “Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! I feel sad because the city where my ancestors are buried is in ruins, and its gates have been burned down.”
translation_verse: Nsu líse kayi na lɛ́su ɔga ɔmmɔ nnini, “Ƒula lɛgadi lise liteesie uwi ƒui! Bi ɔsu na utalɛka mina anumi adu kɔnyana? Ɔsika bula ɔma unengudi ɔni kemmo na báva mina bati kuuku awodu ani bátu bámana ƒui áƒɛ éwi kalɔ. Na bátu ogya bákya ana kɔyakun ƒui.”

english_verse: The king asked, “What do you want me to do?” I prayed to the God who rules from heaven.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bi na aayɔ́ ka lɛbla lite-ɔ?” Amu na lɛ́kpali Ati ɔni nkya katɔ

english_verse: Then I told the king, “Sir, if it's all right with you, please send me back to Judah, so that I can rebuild the city where my ancestors are buried.”
translation_verse: asa lídie ɔga ɔmmɔ kenye nnini, “Ɔga, si ƒula kabla ɔblane lɛlɔ lɛɛda-a kubiti na awɔ ɔlati lɛnɔ kaƒɔ kaayɔ́-ɔ ni, na atala-mi na lisie Yuda kesii kani na báva mina bati kuuku, na ntásɔku awodu ammɔ lɛtu.”

english_verse: The queen was sitting beside the king when he asked me, “How long will it take, and when will you be back?” The king agreed to let me go, and I told him when I would return.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ ku ɔga uleku ɔni muulie-nwu kudɔ béye-mi banini, “Emeyi alɛ na adubuti esie ƒula ulu? Na uwi ɔmani na adubɔsɔ bunwini bubo?” Na ka lɛ́nu ka kaƒɔ kaayɔ́ ɔga ɔmmɔ ka ɔtala-mi ɔsu ni, líte-nwu uwi.

english_verse: Then I asked, “Your Majesty, would you be willing to give me letters to the governors of the provinces west of the Euphrates River, so that I can travel safely to Judah?
translation_verse: Na lɛ́sɔ lɛ́su ɔga ɔmmɔ nnini, “Si kaƒɔ káyɔ-ɔ ni, na ete-mi kɔkunkɛ kɔni ndubuti bɔda na liti lɛtina bekyuli bani nli Eƒrata ɔmii lɛlɔ kalɛ na beti-mi baviaku buɛɛ wetédu ka liduo Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I will need timber to rebuild the gates of the fortress near the temple and more timber to construct the city wall and to build a place for me to live. And so, I would appreciate a letter to Asaph, who is in charge of the royal forest.” God was good to me, and the king did everything I asked.
translation_verse: Na asɔ ete-mi kakunkɛ kabambadi lisienku Asaƒ ɔni mɔɔnu ɔga ɔmmɔ lɛku lɛlɔ teete-nwu, kalɛ na anwu lɛnɔ wete-mi kugyiikɛ kɔni ndubuti lɛnwi lɛpunu lɛkya kakpakɔ kɔyakun ku awodu kɔyakun ku kaduli kani kemmo ndubulie kayakun.” Na ɔga ɔmɛni úte-mi kɔkunkɛ kɔmɛni ƒui, ɔsika Unwoti ɔsiaku-mi ɔsu.

english_verse: The king sent some army officers and cavalry troops along with me, and as I traveled through the Western Provinces, I gave the letters to the governors.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu lísie bekyuli bani nli Eƒrata ɔmii lɛlɔ, na líti ɔga kɔkunkɛ kɔmmɔ líte-ma. Na ɔma ɔmmɔ ɔga údie bekpone benengu ku bani muulie bapɔnkɔ kama badi na básiaku-mi.

english_verse: But when Sanballat from Horon and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about what had happened, they became very angry, because they didn't want anyone to help the people of Israel. Nehemiah Inspects the Wall of Jerusalem
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Horonni Sanbalat ku Tobia ɔni ɔdi Amonni kabla ɔblane ɔdi bénu etemila amɛni ni, ékpoku-ma geen. Ɔsika bénu ka ukyuli ɔdi úbo ka ɔsɔku Israel ɔklibi. Nehemia Ɔ́vi Ɔ́nu Yerusalem Awodu Ani Náƒɛ

english_verse: Three days after arriving in Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na líduo Yerusalem limeyi lɛtɛdi kama ni,

english_verse: I got up during the night and left my house. I took some men with me, without telling anyone what I thought God wanted me to do for the city. The only animal I took was the donkey I rode on.
translation_verse: líti-ku bekyuli blii badi, na búsie bɔ́vi ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo usien ɔdi. Nsu ńtasu ukyuli ɔdi lɛla lɛni na Unwoti úti ɔ́sia-mi kayi ka mbla na Yerusalem. Na ebuo ɔdi biala muedi uuude-mi amu ntu ɔpɔnkɔ ɔni lɛlɔ kani nli.

english_verse: I went through Valley Gate on the west, then south past Dragon Spring, before coming to Garbage Gate. As I rode along, I took a good look at the crumbled walls of the city and the gates that had been torn down and burned.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́vi lɛ́lɛ Yerusalem na nkɛ kɔwɛ kayakun kani nkya ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ, na ńtásia kada kesii kani na ntu bɔdi bɔɔlɛ́ na nkɛ ńtáda lɛ́lɛ kayakun kani beewiakun alakpi. Uwi ɔni ƒui nkɛ mmɔ ni, na mɔɔtɛ anu taanu awodu ani náƒɛ éwi kalɔ ku kɔyakun lɛpunu lɛni bákyula.

english_verse: On the east side of the city, I headed north to Fountain Gate and King's Pool, but then the trail became too narrow for my donkey.
translation_verse: Na kayakun kani késie ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ ni, nkɛ kayakun kani ntu bɔkya-ka ku ɔga ntu ligyu lɛni na ɔɔkpí ulu lɛlɔ. Na ka ɔpɔnkɔ ɔni lɛlɔ na nli ulakɛ ulu ƒelee ulavi ɔsu ni,

english_verse: So I went down to Kidron Valley and looked at the wall from there. Then before daylight I returned to the city through Valley Gate.
translation_verse: bɔ́yu bɔ́sia kɔwɛ kɔdi kemmo, na nkɛ mɔɔnu awodu ammɔ. Na lɛ́sɔ línwini lɛ́sia ulu ɔni lɛlɔ nkɛ na ńtéduo ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na kɔwɛ kayakun kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ kani.

english_verse: None of the city officials knew what I had in mind. And I had not even told any of the Jews—not the priests, the leaders, the officials, or any other Jews who would be helping in the work.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala ɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛni mɔɔbla ku kesii kani na lísie. Ɔsika ńtasu Yudani ɔdi iye Katɔti bakpane bammɔ badi iye kabla bablane bani mabla awodu bɔtu kabla kamɛni.

english_verse: But when I got back, I said to them, “Jerusalem is truly in a mess! The gates have been torn down and burned, and everything is in ruins. We must rebuild the city wall so that we can again take pride in our city.”
translation_verse: Nsu ɔƒɛni mɔɔsu-ma nnii, “Bɛɛnu lɛbibo lɛni kemmo na bɔkya? Yerusalem únwini atɔnku ɔma, na nwuna kɔyakun lɛpunu ƒui lɛnɔ bákyula-ni. Anwuɔsu bibo na bɔsɔ butásɔku Yerusalem awodu ammɔ bɔtu. Na bɔlɛ kɔƒa kemmo.”

english_verse: Then I told them how kind God had been and what the king had said. Immediately, they replied, “Let's start building now!” So they got everything ready.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́su-ma kalɛ na Katɔti ɔ́nu-mi kɔnyana ku lɛla lɛni na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-mi. Mmɔ na básu lɛlɔ banini, “Bɛya bɔta na bɔtu awodu ammɔ.” Na bákya ɔkplu béte kabla kabuni kammɔ bɔbla.

english_verse: When Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem the Arab heard about our plans, they started insulting us and saying, “Just look at you! Do you plan to rebuild the walls of the city and rebel against the king?”
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔni na Horonni Sanbalat ku Tobia ɔni ɔdi Amonni kabla ɔblane ku Arabini Gesem bénu litemi lɛmɛni ni, báma-bu na bánu-bu anumi klukui. Na béye-bu banii, “Bi bɔdaku bɔbla mɛni? Bɔɔyɔ́ ka bɔta bunye ɔga lɛlɔ?”

english_verse: I answered, “We are servants of the God who rules from heaven, and he will make our work succeed. So we will start rebuilding Jerusalem, but you have no right to any of its property, because you have had no part in its history.”
translation_verse: Amu na lídie kenye na lɛ́su-ma nnini, “Unwoti ɔni nkya katɔ ndubɔya na bɔkana bɔbla. Anwuɔsu abu nwuna kabla bablane bɔdubo awodu ammɔ kalɔ buse butaatu. Nsu bɛɛɛdubo kadikɔ kadi bɔkɛ na mɛni iye Yerusalem, na bɛɛɛdubo bukpo bɔƒɔ lɛla lɛdi lɛnɔ. Na bina lɛnyi lɛnɔ lɛɛɛdubo kakunkɛ kemmo buduo kudii.”

english_verse: These are the people who helped rebuild the wall and gates of Jerusalem: The high priest Eliashib and the other priests rebuilt Sheep Gate and hung its doors. Then they dedicated Sheep Gate and the section of the wall as far as Hundred Tower and Hananel Tower.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane unengudi ɔni baalɔ Eliasib ku nwuna bakpane bésie na bátátu kayakun kani baalɔ Baƒonu Kayakun, na bálɛmi-nwu kenye na béti bákya Unwoti enu kemmo. Na bátu katu taasia gyɔlɔɔ eti anyɔ na béti bákya Unwoti enu kemmo. Na bátu bétédu Hananel katu taasia gyɔlɔɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The people of Jericho rebuilt the next section of the wall, and Zaccur son of Imri rebuilt the section after that.
translation_verse: Na Yeriko banana bátu ɔƒɛnyi unwi. Na Imri ubidi Sakur lɛnɔ ɔ́tu ɔƒɛnyi ɔni ude-ma.

english_verse: The family of Hassenaah built Fish Gate. They put the beams in place and hung the doors, then they added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
translation_verse: Na Senaa ɔtɔ bebi bátu kayakun kani baalɔ banii Kakpaku Kayakun. Na bákya lɛpunu ku lɛla biala pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, completed the next section of the wall. Meshullam, son of Berechiah and grandson of Meshezabel, rebuilt the next section, and Zadok son of Baana rebuilt the section beside that.
translation_verse: Na ɔƒɛnyi ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Hakkos ubidi Uria ubidi Meremot nátu. Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Mesesabel ubidi Berekia ubidi Mesulam nátu. Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Baana ubidi Sadok nátu.

english_verse: The next section was to be repaired by the men of Tekoa, but their town leaders refused to do the hard work they were assigned.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Tekoa bakloƒu nátu. Nsu bana ɔma banana batɔnkune béni kabla kani bana lɛlɔ banune béte-ma ka babla.

english_verse: Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah restored Ancient Gate. They put the beams in place, hung the doors, and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
translation_verse: Na kayakun kani baalɔ Yehana ni, Pasea ubidi Yoiada ku Besodeia ubidi nátu lɛla biala pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Melatiah from Gibeon, Jadon from Meronoth, and the men from Gibeon and Mizpah rebuilt the next section of the wall. This section reached as far as the house of the governor of West Euphrates Province.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Melatia ɔni ɔ́si Gibeon ku Yadon ɔni ɔ́si Merono ku banana bani nási Gibeon ku Mispa nátu. Na bátu bétédu aban lɛtɔ lɛni nlɛ Eƒrata ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: Uzziel son of Harhaiah the goldsmith rebuilt the next section. Hananiah the perfume maker rebuilt the section next after that, and it went as far as Broad Wall.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Harhaia ubidi Usiel ɔni ɔdi sika ugyiedi ɔkywɛne nátu. Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Hanania ɔni mɔɔbla ala ani muunwenyi ƒɛƒɛɛ nátu. Na ɔ́tu laa útédu lɛwoduku bonwu lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Rephaiah son of Hur ruled half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Hur ubidi Reƒaia ɔni mɔɔnu Yerusalem kalɛkɛ kakɛ lɛlɔ nátu.

english_verse: The section after that was close to the home of Jedaiah son of Harumaph, and he rebuilt it. Hattush son of Hashabneiah constructed the next section of the wall.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Harumaƒ ubidi Yedaia nátu lɛwoduku lɛni nde nwuna kaduli. Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Hasabnia ubidi Hutus nátu.

english_verse: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath Moab rebuilt the section after that, and they also built Oven Tower.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Harim ubidi Malkia ku Pahat-Moab ubidi Hasub nátu, na básɔ bátu katu taasia gyɔlɔɔ bodobodo ayu.

english_verse: Shallum son of Hallohesh ruled the other half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. Shallum's daughters also worked with him.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Halohes ubidi Salum ɔni mɔɔnu Yerusalem kakɛ kakladi lɛlɔ nátu. Na nwuna bebi belekubi lɛnɔ bebunku-nwu kabla kammɔ.

english_verse: Hanun and the people who lived in the town of Zanoah rebuilt Valley Gate. They hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. They also rebuilt the wall for
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani élie Hanun ku Sanoa náklibi kɔwɛ kayakun kammɔ. Na básɔku-ka bátu, na bákya ɔpunu ku kɔbwɛlɛmii kɔni beeti taakalɛ. Na básɔ básɔku awodu bɔbla aani lɛgba budie eti leevu, na bátu laa bétédu alakpi kewiakunkɔ kayakun.

english_verse: Malchijah son of Rechab ruled the district of Beth-Haccherem, and he rebuilt Garbage Gate. He hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
translation_verse: Na alakpi kewiakunkɔ kayakun ni, Rekab ubidi Malkia ɔni mɔɔnu Bet-Hakerem kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ násɔku kayakun kammɔ ɔ́tu. Na ɔ́kya-ka kɔbwɛlɛmii kɔni beeti taakalɛ.

english_verse: Shallum son of Colhozeh ruled the district of Mizpah, and he rebuilt Fountain Gate. He put a cover over the gateway, then hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. He also rebuilt the wall at Shelah Pool. This section was next to the king's garden and went as far as the stairs leading down from David's City.
translation_verse: Na kayakun kani kese kesii kani na ntu bɔɔlɛ taasiku ni, Kol-Hose ubidi Sulum ɔni mɔɔnu Mispa kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ násɔku-ka ɔ́tu. Na ɔ́kya ɔpunu ku kɔbwɛlɛmii ku lɛla biala pɛpɛɛpɛ. Na ɔ́sɔku lɛwoduku lɛni ntɛ ese Siloa Ligyu lɛni nde ɔga kevomadɔ kemo útédu Dawid ɔma kayakun ɔ́tu.

english_verse: Nehemiah son of Azbuk ruled half of the district of Beth-Zur, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. It went as far as the royal cemetery, the artificial pool, and the army barracks. Levites Who Worked on the Wall
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Asbuk ubidi Nehemia ɔni mɔɔnu Bet-Sur kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ náklibi lɛwoduku lɛni nkya ɔ́si Dawid bekyuli kɔƒiɔtɔ útédu ligyu lɛni bekyuli béti enu béku ku kɔduli kɔni baalɔ-ku Lɛlɔ Bɔdi Kɔduli. Lewiƒuɔ Bani Nábla Kabla Na Awodu Ammɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: The Levites who worked on the next sections of the wall were Rehum son of Bani; Hashabiah, who ruled half of the district of Keilah and did this work for his district;
translation_verse: Na ɔƒɛni ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Lewini ɔni baalɔ banii Bani ubidi Rehum nátu kakɛ kenwi. Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Hasabia ɔni mɔɔnu Keila kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ nátu. Na ɔ́tu-nwu na kalɛkɛ kammɔ lɛnyi kemmo.

english_verse: Binnui son of Henadad, who ruled the other half of the district of Keilah;
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Henadad ubidi Bawai ɔni mɔɔnu Keila kalɛkɛ kakɛ kadi lɛlɔ nátu.

english_verse: Ezer son of Jeshua, who ruled Mizpah, rebuilt the section of the wall that was in front of the armory and reached to the corner of the wall;
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Yesua ubidi Eser ɔni mɔɔdi Mispa lɛlɔ nátu ɔ́si bekpone ata kesekɔ ɔtɔ anumi útédu kesii kani na lɛwoduku lɛmmɔ lideyi.

english_verse: Baruch son of Zabbai eagerly rebuilt the section of the wall that went all the way to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest;
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Sabai ubidi Baruk nátu laa útédu Ɔkpane unengudi Eliasib kayakun kenye.

english_verse: Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, built up to the far end of Eliashib's house. Priests Who Worked on the Wall
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Hakos ubidi Uria ɔni ɔdi Meremot uwɔ nátu útédu Eliasib kaduli kawɔlɔkɔ. Bakpane Bani Nábla Kabla Na Awodu Ammɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Here is a list of the priests who worked on the wall: Priests from the region around Jerusalem rebuilt the next section of the wall.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, bakpane bamɛni lɛnɔ básɔ bátu awodu pii bébunku. Bakpane bani lɛnɔ nási amadɔ mmɔ ku Yerusalem bátu kakɛ kadi.

english_verse: Benjamin and Hasshub rebuilt the wall in front of their own houses. Azariah, who was the son of Maaseiah and the grandson of Ananiah, rebuilt the section in front of his house.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Benyamin ku Hasub nátu awodu ani nkya-ma kɔduli anumi. Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Anania ubidi Maaseia ɔni ɔdi Asaria uwɔ nátu awodu ani nkya nwuna kaduli anumi.

english_verse: Binnui son of Henadad rebuilt the section of the wall from Azariah's house to the corner of the wall.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Hanadad ubidi Binui nátu ɔ́siku Asaria kaduli kayakun kenye útédu lɛwoduku lɛmmɔ likpo.

english_verse: Palal son of Uzai rebuilt the next section, which began at the corner of the wall and the tower of the upper palace near the court of the guard. Pedaiah son of Parosh rebuilt the next section of the wall.
translation_verse: Na Usai ubidi Palal nábla kabla na ɔga kaduli na kesii kani katutaasia gyɔlɔɔ ɔtɔ ɔlɛ. Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Paros ubidi Pedaia lɛnɔ ɔ́tu.

english_verse: He stopped at a place near the Water Gate on the east and the tower guarding the temple. This was close to a section in the city called Ophel, where the temple workers lived. Other Builders Who Worked on the Wall
translation_verse: Na kakpakɔ kabla bablane bani nli Oƒel Kɔbi lili lɛnɔ báklibi ekpo ekpo bétédu ɔƒɛnyi ɔni nkya ntu kayakun si éti ésela katutaasia ɔtɔ gyɔlɔɔ ɔni nlɛ úsie ɔƒɛ katukɔ. Bekyuli Bamba Bani Básɔ Bébunku Bɔtu

english_verse: The men from Tekoa rebuilt the next section of the wall, and it was their second section. It started at a place across from the large tower that guarded the Temple, and it went all the way to the wall near Ophel.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, bakloƒu bani bási Tekoa lɛnɔ bátu ɔdi. Na bése kalɔ básiku katutaasia ɔtɔ bonwu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ bétédu Oƒel lɛwoduku lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Zadok son of Immer rebuilt the wall in front of his house. Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, who looked after the East Gate, rebuilt the section after that.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Imer ubidi Sadok ɔ́klibi ɔƒɛnyi ɔni nkya ese nwuna kaduli kakɛ. Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Sekania ubidi Semaia ɔni mɔɔgyumana kayakun kani kese ɔƒɛ katukɔ lɛnɔ ɔ́klibi ala adi.

english_verse: Hananiah and Hanun rebuilt the next section, which was the second section for them. Meshullam son of Berechiah rebuilt the next section, which happened to be in front of his house.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Selemia ubidi Hanania ku Hanun ɔni ɔdi Salaƒ ubidi ɔkundi lɛnɔ bábla kadi. Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Berekia ubidi Mesulam náklibi ɔƒɛnyi ɔni nése nwuna kaduli kakɛ.

english_verse: Malchijah, a goldsmith, rebuilt the next section, as far as the house used by the temple workers and merchants. This area was across from Gathering Gate, near the room on top of the wall at the northeast corner.
translation_verse: Na ɔni nsɔ nsia ni, Malkia ɔni ndi sika ugyiedi ɔkywɛne kemmo unwi ɔ́klibi ɔ́si kaduli kani kabla bablane ku kuye badine beli, na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́klibi ɔ́si kayakun kani baawia ala kemmo ɔƒɛnyi útédu ɔtɔ ɔtɔdi ɔni nkya lɛwoduku likpo.

english_verse: The goldsmiths and merchants rebuilt the last section of the wall, which went from the corner room all the way to Sheep Gate.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si ɔtɔ ɔtɔdi lɛwoduku likpo útédu baƒonu kayakun ni, sika ugyiedi bakywɛne ku kuye badine náklibi mmɔ.

english_verse: When Sanballat, the governor of Samaria, heard that we were rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem, he became angry and started insulting our people.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Sanbalat únu ka abu Yudaƒuɔ bɔ́sɔku awodu ammɔ bɔɔtu ni, úti kɔnyi geen na ɔ́ma-bu.

english_verse: In front of his friends and the Samaritan army he said, “What is this feeble bunch of Jews trying to do? Are they going to rebuild the wall and offer sacrifices all in one day? Do they think they can make something out of this pile of scorched stones?”
translation_verse: Na ka unye nwuna bakpana ku Samariaƒuɔ bavinkpana anumi ni, úye lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Bi na Yudaƒuɔ bani lɛlɔ mɔɔdu kɔnyana mɛni baayɔ́ babla? Baayɔ́ ka basɔku Yerusalem awodu batu yoo?” Na ɔ́sɔ úye ɔnini, “Baabu ka si babla akpala adi bakana beti limeyi linwi pɛ babla kabla kammɔ yoo? Na bakali ka badubɔkɛ atabi ani baatu ɔtɔ basiku atabi ani alɛ esu esu na bákyula-nya kemmo?”

english_verse: Tobiah from Ammon was standing beside Sanballat and said, “Look at the wall they are building! Why, even a fox could knock over this pile of stones.”
translation_verse: Amu na Amonni ɔni ndi Tobia na unye Sanbalat kama lɛnɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Awodu ani benye baatu mɛni ni, si kedu kákɔ kenye-nwu lɛlɔ muedi ni, ɔdubo bɔƒɛ. Ɔsika atabi lɛti lɛti na béti bátu-nya.”

english_verse: But I prayed, “Our God, these people hate us and have wished horrible things for us. Please answer our prayers and make their insults fall on them! Let them be the ones to be dragged away as prisoners of war.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Nehemia ɔ́kpali katɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “O bula Katɔti, nu-bu bɔkpali. Ɔsika bɔkya bukpoku kemmo. Ya na edumi ani na beedumi-bu mɛni enwini ese-ma lɛlɔ. Na eti-ma ete bana bekisine. Na babla-ma kalala na kalɔ bamba lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Don't forgive the mean and evil way they have insulted the builders.”
translation_verse: Teti bana ekpidi takyiɛ-ma. Ɔsika béwi bekyuli bani mɔɔtú ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ anumi kalɔ.”

english_verse: The people worked hard, and we built the walls of Jerusalem halfway up again.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bɔkana lɛwoduku lɛmmɔ bɔ́tu bútédu kakɛ. Ɔsika bekyuli bammɔ bédie kayi bábla kabla kaduɛ.

english_verse: But Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people from the city of Ashdod saw the walls going up and the holes being repaired. So they became angry
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔni na Sanbalat ku Tobia ku Arabiƒuɔ ku Amonƒuɔ ku Asdodƒuɔ bénu ka bátu Yerusalem awodu ammɔ bákɔliku katɔ kaduɛ na bakya beeyile eƒi ani nkya awodu ammɔ kemmo ntɛ ni, bákɛ kɔnyi geen.

english_verse: and decided to stir up trouble, and to fight against the people of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bekyuli bamɛni béti kasusu kekpidi básala ka batákya-ku bekyuli bammɔ unyeƒi na bekpoku-ma na Yerusalem.

english_verse: But we kept on praying to our God, and we also stationed guards day and night.
translation_verse: Nsu bɔ́kpali bula ɔti ɔni nkya katɔ na búti bagyumanane búsienku mmɔ na baanu mmɔ usien ku ɔƒɛ kalɛ bɔsɔ bulayia lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Judah were singing a sorrowful song: “So much rubble for us to haul! Worn out and weary, will we ever finish this wall?”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, bekyuli bani nkya Yuda básu banini, “Kabla bablane bammɔ ɔlɔkplu ɔdaku bɔsa. Na leti ku atabi ani nwi kalɔ emomo, na eléte-bu kuƒi ka bɔsɔku awodu ammɔ bɔtu bɔwɔlɔ.”

english_verse: Our enemies were saying, “Before those Jews know what has happened, we will sneak up and kill them and put an end to their work.”
translation_verse: Na bula bekisine lɛnɔ básu banini, “Asa na utaabla-ma nwaa iye bataanu-bu bati ni, na bɔkya-ma akɔ mmɔ butádu-ma, na kabla kammɔ kawɔ mmɔ kani!”

english_verse: On at least ten different occasions, the Jews living near our enemies warned us against attacks from every side,
translation_verse: Amu na Yudaƒuɔ bani nli nde-ma békeli bábasu-bu kɔlɛ kɔlɛ na útulo leevu muedi ka si kesi kesii bɔdubunye ni, badubo-bu bukpoku.

english_verse: and so I sent people to guard the wall at its lowest places and where there were still holes in it. I placed them according to families, and they stood guard with swords and spears and with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: Amu lídie bekyuli badi na béténye kesii kani na lɛwoduku lɛmmɔ lɛ́kuku kalɛ na bekyuli baanu-ma. Na lɛ́ya bésie benye kɔduli kenye. Na báda bana kuwii ku kɔtaminta ku atula.

english_verse: Then I looked things over and told the leaders, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Don't be afraid of your enemies! The Lord is great and fearsome. So think of him and fight for your relatives and children, your wives and homes!”
translation_verse: Amu na ami Nehemia lɛ́ta na ńtánu banamu bakɔdi ku benengu ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui na lɛ́su-ma nnini, “Bitayia-ma. Bɛkali ka Katɔti ɔni nwuna lɛlɔ lɛɛda liƒu mmomu na ɔlɛka bɔyia. Na binye kpakplaa, na bikpo bite bina banwani ku bina beleku ku bina kɔduli.”

english_verse: Our enemies found out that we knew about their plot against us, but God kept them from doing what they had planned. So we went back to work on the wall.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bula bekisine bénu ka bana kasusu kani bada kálɛ keyi ni, Unwoti lɛnɔ ɔ́ya na enu áƒɛ-ma. Na bula ƒui bɔ́sɔ búnwini búse awodu ammɔ kudɔ, na ɔdi biala úse ɔɔbla nwuna kabla.

english_verse: From then on, I let half of the young men work while the other half stood guard. They wore armor and had spears and shields, as well as bows and arrows. The leaders helped the workers
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si limeyi lɛmmɔ úsela ni, mina bekyuli kakɛ benye kabla lɛlɔ. Na kakɛ lɛnɔ báda bana ekpola ku bana kɔtaminta ku atula, na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bénye Yudaƒuɔ

english_verse: who were rebuilding the wall. Everyone who hauled building materials kept one hand free to carry a weapon.
translation_verse: bani nkya mɔɔtu awodu ammɔ kama. Na bekyuli bani mɔɔda ala ani baatu awodu ammɔ bada kɔnu kunwi baatú na bana ekpola lɛnɔ akya-ma kɔnu kɔkladi kemmo.

english_verse: Even the workers who were rebuilding the wall strapped on a sword. The worker who was to blow the signal trumpet stayed with me.
translation_verse: Na ɔtune biala ɔ́kya nwuna ekpola ala na unye nwuna kabla lɛlɔ. Na kɔkpɛɛ bavwine ama basɔ bákya-mi kudɔ.

english_verse: I told the people and their officials and leaders, “Our work is so spread out, that we are a long way from one another.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́su banamu bakɔdi ku benengu ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui nnini, “Kabla kammɔ kese anumi na kégyingya na abu lɛnɔ bugyingya ku lɛlɔ.

english_verse: If you hear the sound of the trumpet, come quickly and gather around me. Our God will help us fight.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu kesi kesii na bɛdubunu kakpɛɛ kammɔ kɔkun ni, na bikeli bibo. Na bula Katɔti ɔdubukpo bula kekpo ute-bu.”

english_verse: Every day from dawn to dark, half of the workers rebuilt the walls, while the rest stood guard with their spears.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu búsienku kabla kammɔ anumi na bekyuli kakɛ báda atula ɔsi lɛdigye útédu ka kɔyabi kɔɔlɛ usien.

english_verse: I asked the men in charge and their workers to stay inside Jerusalem and stand guard at night. So they guarded the city at night and worked during the day.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ami lɛnɔ lɛ́su bekyuli bammɔ nnini, “Ɔdi biala ku nwuna kabla ɔblane úulie Yerusalem use dii, kalɛ na benwini bagyumanane bete-bu asa babla kabla si kadi kegye.”

english_verse: I even slept in my work clothes at night; my relatives, the workers, and the guards slept in theirs as well. And we always kept our weapons close by.
translation_verse: Na ami iye mina banwani iye mina kabla bablane iye mina bagyumanane bani nkya-mi kudɔ, ɔdi biala útedie nwuna awu útewi na ɔdi biala lɛnɔ ɔ́da nwuna ekpola ina úsela ketu muedi.

english_verse: Some of the men and their wives complained about the Jews in power
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔdi kama ni, banana ku beleku bésie kalɔ baakyaku bana banwani Yudaƒuɔ unyeƒi.

english_verse: and said, “We have large families, and it takes a lot of grain merely to keep us alive.”
translation_verse: Na badi baasu banini, “Bubo bebi pii, ɔmmɔ ɔsu bɔɔwia edula ebi na butaanwa teete-ma na bataadi kalɛ na belekpi.”

english_verse: Others said, “During the famine we even had to mortgage our fields, vineyards, and homes to them in order to buy grain.”
translation_verse: Na badi lɛnɔ báasu banini, “Ɔlɛka buti bula kɔduli ku bula mmo ku bula adingyii mmo buti busie ɔkpa na bɔkɛ edula ebi kalɛ na kɔka kuládu-bu.”

english_verse: Then others said, “We had to borrow money from those in power to pay the government tax on our fields and vineyards.
translation_verse: Na badi lɛnɔ benye baasu banini, “Bútáwia kevonkɔ na búti bɔ́ƒɔ ɔga kuyi kɔni na ɔɔƒɔ́ na bula mmo ku adingyii mmo ɔsu.

english_verse: We are Jews just as they are, and our children are as good as theirs. But we still have to sell our children as slaves, and some of our daughters have already been raped. We are completely helpless; our fields and vineyards have even been taken from us.”
translation_verse: Nsu ina ka abu ku Yudaƒuɔ benwi bɔdi na bula bebi lɛnɔ bese aani bana badi ni, búuti bula bebi badi búye búte-ma kalɛ na buti bɔƒɔ kayu kammɔ. Báƒɔ bula begblebi badi, na ɔƒɛni bɔsɔ bulati lɛla lɛni bɔbla. Ɔsika békpeli bula mmo ku adingyii mmo báƒɔ bula enu kemmo.”

english_verse: When I heard their complaints and their charges, I became very angry.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni ami Nehemia línu bana kɔvanu ku bana etemila ani báasu ni, líti kɔnyi geen.

english_verse: So I thought it over and said to the leaders and officials, “How can you charge your own people interest?” Then I called a public meeting and accused the leaders
translation_verse: Na líti etemila ammɔ kasusu kɔlɛ kɔlɛ. Mmɔ na líti kɔtɔ bɔdu líte mina bakutine ku mina benengu. Na lɛ́su-ma nnini, “Kuvonsia kɔni mɔɔlɛ́ mɛni kɔ́si-mii kudɔ!” Ɔmmɔ ɔsu lɛ́lɔ bekyuli bammɔ ƒui na búduo litemi lɛmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: by saying, “We have tried to buy back all of our people who were sold into exile. But here you are, selling more of them for us to buy back!” The officials and leaders did not say a word, because they knew this was true.
translation_verse: Na lɛ́su-ma nnini, “Ama bani na béye-ma béte bekyuli bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ ni, bɔ́bla kalɛ na bɔkana, na bɔ́ƒɔ-ma bɔ́siku bekyuli bammɔ kudɔ. Nsu amii binye bina banwani lɛlɔ kalɛ na beti lɛlɔ beye bete-mii, na amii lɛnɔ bɛsɔku-ma biye bite-bu.” Na benengu bammɔ bába lɛsɛ, ka beeebo kulɛla na basu ɔsu.

english_verse: I continued, “What you have done is wrong! We must honor our God by the way we live, so the Gentiles can't find fault with us.
translation_verse: Amu na lísie anumi na lɛ́su-ma nnini, “Lɛla lɛni na bɛɛbla mmɔ lɛɛɛdia munu munu! Na dɛ ɔsu na útalɛka bɛbla ala na Katɔti ulu lɛlɔ, kalɛ na Unwoti ulanyonu-bu ulakya bula bekisine bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ enu kemmo?

english_verse: My relatives, my friends, and I are also lending money and grain, but we must no longer demand payment in return.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu ami ku mina banwani bani búti egulabi ku edula ebi búvo búte-ma mmɔ ƒui ni, nsu ɔlɛka bɔda kevonsia bute bɔya.

english_verse: The leaders answered, “We will do whatever you say and return their property, without asking to be repaid.” So I made the leaders promise in front of the priests to give back the property.
translation_verse: Amu benengu bammɔ básu banini, “Bɔdubɔsɔku bana ala ƒui bute-ma. Bɔsɔ baláƒɔ lɛla biala bulásiku ɔdi biala kudɔ. Na lɛla biala ásu-bu ni, bɔdubɔdi-ni lɛlɔ.” Amu na ami Nehemia lɛ́lɔ mina bakpane ƒui ku mina bakutine ƒui, na lɛ́ya na bákpali Katɔti bése kenye kalɛ na badi bana linyese lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then I emptied my pockets and said, “If you don't keep your promise, that's what God will do to you. He will empty out everything you own, even taking away your houses.” The people answered, “We will keep our promise.” Then they praised the Lord and did as they had promised. Nehemiah Is Generous
translation_verse: Amu na lídie kɔdi kɔni nda-mi kavobi na lɛ́kuna-ku na lɛ́su nnini, “Lɛni na Katɔti ɔdubo bɔkuna bina akɔ ɔdi biala ɔni naaadi nwuna linyese lɛlɔ.” Na lɛ́sɔ lɛ́su nnini, “Katɔti ɔdubɔƒɔ bina kɔduli ku bina lɛla biala lise-mii ku lɛla lɛni nébu-mii.” Na ukyuli biala ɔni nése mmɔ ɔ́su ɔnii, “Ɔsia lɛni!” Na bana ƒui bémwi Unwoti. Na bekyuli bammɔ bábla aani kalɛ na básu.

english_verse: Each governor before me had been a burden to the people by making them pay for his food and wine and by demanding forty silver coins a day. Even their officials had been a burden to the people. But I respected God, and I didn't think it was right to be so hard on them.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si akwa leevu-anyɔ ani na lɛ́kya Ɔga Artasasta kudɔ na údie-mi ka ńtaanu Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ úti úbedu nwuna akwa avlaatɛ-inyɔ lɛlɔ ni, ami iye mina banwani ɔdi biala útadi adila ani beete Yudaƒuɔ lɛlɔ ɔnune kudii. Nsu bekyuli bani bátɔ-mi na kabla kamɛni udu kenye ni, ama béti etila bonwu básia bekyuli bammɔ lɛlɔ, na baaƒɔ́ sika ɔƒualadi akyami aavlene ku adila ku ntɛ taasiku bekyuli bammɔ kudɔ. Na lɛni kani na bana kama basiakune lɛnɔ bataabla. Nsu na Katɔti bɔyia kemmo ni, ami ńtabla ɔbladu ɔmmɔ udu kudii.

english_verse: I spent all my time getting the wall rebuilt and did not buy any property. Everyone working for me did the same thing.
translation_verse: Mmomu ami líti lɛlɔ líse líte awodu ammɔ bɔtu. Na mina bekyuli bani ƒui bábla kabla béte-mi ni, ami iye ama ɔdi biala útawia kalɔ útete lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Each day one ox, six of the best sheep, and lots of chickens were prepared. Then every ten days, a large supply of wine was brought in. I knew what a heavy burden this would have been for the people, and so I did not ask for my food allowance as governor.
translation_verse: Na limeyi ndi limeyi ni, mɔɔdú ɔmantɛ akɔ unwi ku baƒonu bani nélie lɛmwi ɛku ku bakɔkɔ badi teeti taanwa. Na limeyi leevudi biala lɛlɔ ni, muute-ma ntɛ udu biala. Nsu ɔmɛni kama ƒui ni, ńtasu bekyuli bani mɔɔnu lɛlɔ kudii nnii bete-mi adila ani ɔlɛka beteete Yudaƒuɔ lɛlɔ ɔnune. Ɔsika bemomo na ala ani baawia lɛnɔ émomo.

english_verse: I pray that God will bless me for everything I have done for my people.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́kpali katɔ lɛ́su nnini, “O Unwoti Katɔti, nyimo-mi ku kɔnyana bɔnu na ala ani ƒui lɛ́bla líte bekyuli bamɛni ɔsu.”

english_verse: Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem, and our other enemies learned that I had completely rebuilt the wall. All I lacked was hanging the doors in the gates.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Sanbalat ku Tobia ku Arabini ɔni baalɔ Gesem ku bula bekisine bakladi bénu ka lɛ́sɔku awodu ammɔ lɛ́tu ɔni na ńtada kuƒi kɔdi ńtakya ina ka uwi ɔmmɔ ńtakya tɔ kɔyakun kɔmmɔ lɛpunu ni,

english_verse: Then Sanballat and Geshem sent a message, asking me to meet with them in one of the villages in Ono Valley. I knew they were planning to harm me in some way.
translation_verse: Sanbalat ku Gesem béti kenye kamɛni bémene-mi. Na aka ndi ka ni, “Bo na abu ku-ɔ bɔsa na Ono akpaklɔ ani nwi ƒiaa mmɔ kemmo unwi.” Nsu lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka lɛkwɛ likpidi na baakya.

english_verse: So I sent messengers to tell them, “My work is too important to stop now and go there. I can't afford to slow down the work just to visit with you.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ami Nehemia lɛ́tala batalane badi lɛ́kya bekyuli bammɔ ka batásu-ma banini, “Linye kabla kadi lɛlɔ kpakplaa, anwuɔsu naaakana bubo. Bi ɔsu na ɔlɛka lɛda kabla kamɛni bɔbla lɛya na lɛtɔlɔ libo-mii kudɔ?”

english_verse: They invited me four times, but each time I refused to go.
translation_verse: Na Sanbalat bene béti kenye kamɛni bémene-mi kune sɔɔn. Na uwi biala ni, kenye kenwi kani na ami lídie.

english_verse: Finally, Sanballat sent an official to me with an unsealed letter,
translation_verse: Na kɔlɔndi ni, Sanbalat ɔ́tala nwuna ukyuli ɔni mɔɔgyumana-nwu na ɔda kakunkɛ kani bátakalɛ-ka kenye

english_verse: which said: A rumor is going around among the nations that you and the other Jews are rebuilding the wall and planning to rebel, because you want to be their king. And Geshem says it's true!
translation_verse: na etemila ani ńkya-ka kemmo anya ndi amɛni, “Búnu bɔ́siku kadi bekyuli pii ku Gasmu kudɔ ka aasu ani sɔsɔ ɔdi ka awɔ ku Yudaƒuɔ bɛɛyɔ́ ka bɛda Israel batɔnkune bidie liboku lɛlɔ na ásɔku Yerusalem awodu aatu. Na kalɛ buunú baayɔ́ beti-ɔ babla bana ɔga.

english_verse: You even have prophets in Jerusalem, claiming you are now the king of Judah. You know the Persian king will hear about this, so let's get together and talk it over.
translation_verse: Ɔni na édie kenye bediene ka bátaakɔ litemi lɛmmɔ lɛsa na Yerusalem ka awɔ ndi Yudaƒuɔ ɔga. Ɔƒɛni litemi lɛmɛni lɛkana lidu Yudaƒuɔ ɔga kudɔ, anwuɔsu bo na buti kasusu bɔsala.”

english_verse: I sent a message back to Sanballat, saying, “None of this is true! You are making it all up.”
translation_verse: Amu na líti kenye kamɛni límene-nwu nnini, “Ala ani ƒui na ásu mɛni eeese lɛni. Na mɔɔsu-ɔ ka awɔ ɔlati nábla lili kemmo kasusu asa na énweni ɔku ɔmɛni émene-mi.”

english_verse: Our enemies were trying to frighten us and to keep us from our work. But I asked God to give me strength.
translation_verse: Na liƒu na baayɔ́ ka bakya-bu ku kasusu ka enu aƒɛ kabla bablane bammɔ, na kabla kammɔ kelebo kawɔlɔkɔ. Nsu ɔƒɛni lɛ́kpali Katɔti muuvele-nwu ka ɔkya-mi ɔlɔkplu.

english_verse: One day I went to visit Shemaiah. He wasn't supposed to leave his house, but he said, “Let's hurry to the holy place of the temple and hide there. We will lock the temple doors, because your enemies are planning to kill you tonight.”
translation_verse: Amu na limeyi lɛdi lísie Semaia ɔni ndi Delaia ubidi na ɔdi Mehetabel uwɔ kaduli, na bákalɛ-nwu bákya nwuna ɔtɔ. Na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ya na busie Katɔti kakpakɔ bɔsala, na bɔkalɛ lɛlɔ bɔda nwuna ɔtɔ kemmo. Ɔsika báwia-a badu. Na usien ɔmɛni kani badubo na babadu-ɔ.”

english_verse: I answered, “Why should someone like me have to run and hide in the temple to save my life? I won't go!”
translation_verse: Amu na lídie kenye nnini, “Lɛɛɛdi ɔnana ɔni udu mɔɔyia, na ukeli utabɛ. Munuu aakali ka si líkeli ńtábɛ Katɔti kakpakɔ na ndubɔƒɔ mina ngba? Lɛɛɛdubo bukeli kudii.”

english_verse: Suddenly I realized that God had not given Shemaiah this message. But Tobiah and Sanballat had paid him to trick me
translation_verse: Ka lílie líti litemi lɛmɛni kasusu ni, lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka ɔɔɔdi Katɔti nétemi éte Semai, mmomu Sanbalat ku Tobia náwia egulabi adi éte-nwu.

english_verse: and to frighten me into doing something wrong, because they wanted to ruin my good name.
translation_verse: Lɛla lɛdi geen na báwia béte ukyuli ɔmɛni ka úbayila-mi kalɛ na lɛbla likpidi. Si bunu na línu litemi lɛmɛni ni, nka badubo-mi lɛnyi bubile na baláƒɔ-mi baladi.

english_verse: Then I asked God to punish Tobiah and Sanballat for what they had done. I prayed that God would punish the prophet Noadiah and the other prophets who, together with her, had tried to frighten me. The Work Is Finished
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́kpali katɔ lɛ́su nnini, “O mina Katɔti, nyimo Tobia ku Sanbalat ɔ́si lɛla lɛni bábla mɛni ɔsu. Na enyimo Kenye Udiene Noadia ku Katɔti kenye bediene bakladi bani naayɔ́ ka baƒɔ-mi badi lɛnɔ.” Nehemia Ɔ́tu Awoduku Ammɔ Ɔ́wɔlɔ

english_verse: On the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, the wall was completely rebuilt. It had taken
translation_verse: Na bátu awodu ammɔ báwɔlɔ na kɔbuli limeyi aavlanyɔ-ɛlɔ lɛlɔ. Na emeyi liti ku inyɔ na béti bátu-nya.

english_verse: When our enemies in the surrounding nations learned that the work was finished, they felt helpless, because they knew that our God had helped us rebuild the wall.
translation_verse: Ka bula bekisine ƒui bénu etemila amɛni ni, liƒu lɛ́da ama ku kadi bamba bekyuli bani ƒui nde-bu. Na ama bani nánu báti ka bula Katɔti kɔnu kɔkya kabla kani bɔ́bla mmɔ kemmo ni, enu áƒɛ-ma.

english_verse: All this time the Jewish leaders and Tobiah had been writing letters back and forth.
translation_verse: Emeyi ammɔ kemmo lɛnɔ ni, bakutine pii bani nási Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ béteenweni lɛku pii teemine Tobia. Na Tobia lɛnɔ úteenweni teemine-ma.

english_verse: Many people in Judah were loyal to Tobiah for two reasons: Shecaniah son of Arah was his father-in-law, and Tobiah's son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
translation_verse: Ɔsika Yudaƒuɔ pii bése kenye béte-nwu. Na nwuna aasi ndi Arah ubidi Sekania. Na Tobia ɔmɛni ubidi ɔnanabi Yohanan úti Berekia ubidi Mesulam ubidi ulekubi.

english_verse: The people would always tell me about the good things Tobiah had done, and then they would tell Tobiah everything I had said. So Tobiah kept sending letters, trying to frighten me.
translation_verse: Na lɛnɔ ni, bekyuli bése anumi baasu-mi kabla kabuni kani na Tobia ɔ́ɔbla, na báasu mina lɛlɔ etemila ku ala ani lɛ́su lɛnɔ taatina-nwu. Na Tobia anwu ni, únweni lɛku ka nka ubakya-mi liƒu.

english_verse: Although Jerusalem covered a large area, not many people lived there, and no new houses had been built.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni Yerusalem ɔma Unengudi ɔmɛni ubomo, nsu bekyuli bani nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo beeemomo. Lɛni ɔsu ni, bátasɔku kɔduli pii bátatu tɔ.

english_verse: kilograms of gold,
translation_verse: Paros kaba kadi

english_verse: This is a list of how many returned from the families of Levites:
translation_verse: Bagyumanane bani nási Salum kaba ku Ater kaba ku Talmon kaba ku Akub kaba ku Hatita kaba ku Sobai kaba kadi

english_verse: Here are the names of Solomon's servants whose descendants returned: Sotai, Sophereth, Perida, Jaala, Darkon, Giddel, Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth Hazzebaim, and Amon.
translation_verse: ku Seƒatia kaba ku Hatil kaba ku Pokeret-Hasebaim kaba ku Amon kaba.

english_verse: The families of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai could not prove they were priests. The ancestor of the family of Barzillai had married the daughter of Barzillai from Gilead and had taken his wife's family name. But the records of these three families could not be found, and none of them were allowed to serve as priests.
translation_verse: Bakpane bamɛni ndi bekyuli bani báwia bana anyi na kɔduli kɔkunkɛ kemmo, nsu bétenu bana anyi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bátabu-ma aani bakpane. Mmomu bánu-ma aani bekyuli bani beesé lɛlɔ.

english_verse: In fact, the governor told them, “You cannot eat the food offered to God until he lets us know if you really are priests.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu, Israelƒuɔ ɔtɔnkune úbo-ma ɔda ka batadi adila ani nse kedee ntulo utédu ka bakɛ ɔkpane ɔni mɔɔbla kabla na ɔɔda ala ani baalɔ Urim ku Tumim ɔni kalɔ ndi ɔnii Bukeye ku Litemi Geen.

english_verse: There were
translation_verse: ku baƒlumu

english_verse: Many people gave gifts to help pay for the materials to rebuild the temple. The governor himself gave
translation_verse: Na ka béti bekyuli bakladi ala ani béte básala ni, béyi sika ugyiedi atabi

english_verse: And so, by the seventh month, priests, Levites, temple guards, musicians, workers, and many of the ordinary people had settled in the towns of Judah.
translation_verse: Na bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ ku kɔyakun lɛlɔ banune ku lɛnu batune ku kakpakɔ kabla bablane ku Israelƒuɔ bakladi ama ni, bésie bétélie bana lɛma kemmo.

english_verse: On the first day of the seventh month, the people came together in the open area in front of the Water Gate. Then they asked Ezra, who was a teacher of the Law of Moses, to read to them from this Law that the Lord had given his people. Ezra the priest came with the Law and stood before the crowd of men, women, and the children who were old enough to understand.
translation_verse: Na ɔni na uteedu kɔbuli maatɛdi kawɔlɔkɔ ni, ɔdi biala ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie nwuna ɔma. Na limeyi lideedi na kɔbuli kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ ƒui bása na Yerusalem na kesii kani balɔ banii Ntu Kayakun. Na básu Ɔkpane Esra ɔni ndi ɔku unwenine ka udie Mose Ɔda Bubo Ɔku ɔni Unwoti úti úte Israelƒuɔ uboku. Anwuɔsu Esra úsie na útéti ɔda bubo ɔku ɔmmɔ úboku na kesii kani na básala béli. Na banana ku beleku ku banamu bani beenú ala kalɔ násala mmɔ.

english_verse: From early morning till noon, he read the Law of Moses to them, and they listened carefully.
translation_verse: Na kayakun kammɔ kenye ni, Esra ɔ́ka ɔku ɔmmɔ úte bekyuli bammɔ ɔ́si lɛdigye utédu ɔƒiiwi uwi. Na bekyuli bammɔ bése atu na bénu kaduɛ.

english_verse: Ezra stood on a high wooden platform that had been built for this occasion. Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah were standing to his right, while Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hash Baddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam were standing to his left.
translation_verse: Na Esra ɔ́kɔ únye kugyiikɛ kɔni na bekyuli bammɔ bátu béte kasala kammɔ lɛlɔ. Na Matitia ku Sema ku Anaia ku Uria ku Hilkia ku Maaseia bénye-nwu kɔdianu. Na Pedaia ku Misae ku Malkia ku Hasum ku Hasbadana ku Sakaria ku Mesulam bénye-nwu kɔmii kakɛ.

english_verse: Ezra was up on the high platform, where he could be seen by everyone, and when he opened the book, all the people stood up.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ɔdi biala ɔɔnu-nwu, na kugyiikɛ kɔni lɛlɔ na ɔ́kɔ unye mmɔ ɔsu. Na uwi ɔni na úbimi ɔku ɔmmɔ kani bekyuli bammɔ ƒui báta bénye kɔnakunwi.

english_verse: Ezra praised the great Lord God, and they lifted their hands, shouting “Amen! Amen!” Then they bowed with their faces to the ground and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Amu na Esra ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bɛya na bumwi Unwoti Katɔti ɔni nébomo!” Amu na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bátalaku bana enu katɔ na básu banini, “Ɔsia lɛni! Ɔsia lɛni!” Na bálɛ akɔnkɔ na béti anumi bébi kalɔ.

english_verse: The people started crying when God's Law was read to them. Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and teacher, and the Levites who had been teaching the people all said, “This is a special day for the Lord your God. So don't be sad and don't cry!”
translation_verse: Ka bekyuli bammɔ bénu ala ani na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔwia bɔsiku-ma kudɔ ni, ɔ́bla-ma kalɛ kadi na bése kalɔ beewulo. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Israelƒuɔ ɔtɔnkune Nehemia ku Ɔkpane Esra ɔni ndi Ɔku Unwenine ku Lewiƒuɔ bani nkya muudie ɔda bubo etemila ani báka mmɔ kalɔ básu-ma banini, “Ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛdi limeyi kedee lite Unwoti, bina Katɔti. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bitewulo na bitadu kɔnyana.”

english_verse: Nehemiah told the people, “Enjoy your good food and wine and share some with those who didn't have anything to bring. Don't be sad! This is a special day for the Lord, and he will make you happy and strong.”
translation_verse: Na Nehemia ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔlɛka biteesie kaduli, na bitánwa adila kaduɛ na bite ɔkpanadi ɔni neeebo ɔdi. Ɔsika ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛdi limeyi kedee lite Unwoti. Bitadu kɔnyana, ɔsika Unwoti lɛlɔyɔ lɛdubute-mii lɛlɔkplu!”

english_verse: The Levites encouraged the people by saying, “This is a sacred day, so don't worry or mourn!”
translation_verse: Na Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ bákɛ bekyuli bammɔ lɛlɔ baasia-ma kɔnu ka betewulo limeyi kedee lɛmɛni udu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: When the people returned to their homes, they celebrated by eating and drinking and by sharing their food with those in need, because they had understood what had been read to them. Celebrating the Festival of Shelters
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bátɔlɔ bésie kɔduli bátánwa, na bádi na báni na béte bakpanadi lɛnɔ. Ɔsika ɔda bubo etemila ani báka bátina-ma mmɔ ni, bénu-nya kalɔ. Limeyi Kadikɔ Kevo Bɔtu

english_verse: On the second day of the seventh month, the leaders of all the family groups came together with the priests and the Levites, so Ezra could teach them the Law
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛni nsia ni, kɔduɔti biala ku bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bésie Esra kudɔ ka bátátɛya ɔda bubo etemila ammɔ.

english_verse: that the Lord had given to Moses. They learned from the Law that the people of Israel were to live in shelters when they celebrated the festival in the seventh month of the year.
translation_verse: Na mmɔ na bánu báti ka ɔda bubo etemila ani Unwoti úti ɔ́siaku Mose lɛlɔ ni, úbo Israel ƒui ɔda ka si baadi limeyi na kɔbuli maatɛdi kemmo ni, na bataatu nvuo betélie-nya kemmo.

english_verse: They also learned that they were to go into the woods and gather branches of leafy trees such as olives, myrtles, and palms for making these shelters.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu béti ɔda bubo bɔmɛni béte-ma ka bataakɔ-ni lɛsa na Yerusalem ku lɛma libendi ku libliidi ƒui na basu-ma banii bakɔ besie abi lɛlɔ na batada like ku egyii kɔgba na beti babla nvuo aani kalɛ na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔɔsu.

english_verse: So the people gathered branches and made shelters on the flat roofs of their houses, in their yards, in the courtyard of the temple, and in the open areas around the Water Gate and Ephraim Gate.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bekyuli bammɔ báta na bátáwia egyii kɔgba na bátu nvuo adi bálɛ bana kɔduli lɛsa eli ku kɔduli amadɔ ku Katɔti kakpakɔ amadɔ ku kesii kani kadi beelie taasiaku Ntu Kayakun ku Eƒraim Kayakun amadɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Everyone who had returned from Babylonia built shelters. They lived in them and joyfully celebrated the Festival of Shelters for the first time since the days of Joshua son of Nun.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani ƒui na kekpo béƒie-ma na bénwini bébo ni, bátu nvuo amɛni na bélie-nya kemmo. Ɔmɛni ndi lɛla lideedi lɛni na bábla ɔ́si Nun ubidi Yosua uwi. Na ɔdi biala ɔ́kɛ kubiti geen.

english_verse: On each of the first seven days of the festival, Ezra read to the people from God's Law. Then on the eighth day, everyone gathered for worship, just as the Law had said they must.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si limeyi lɛmmɔ bɔdi, limeyi lideedi útédu limeyi likplodi lɛlɔ bataaka Unwoti bubo etemila ammɔ adi kakɛ. Na bádi emeyi ammɔ emeyi maatɛ. Na limeyi maanedi lɛlɔ ni, básala na bádi limeyi lɛmmɔ báwɔlɔ aani kalɛ ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔɔtina.

english_verse: On the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month, the people of Israel went without eating, and they dressed in sackcloth and threw dirt on their heads to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Na limeyi aavlanyɔ-ine na kɔbuli kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ kani kemmo ni, Israelƒuɔ básala lisu na bényimi kenye, na béti adikpi adi bényimi lɛlɔ, na béti ntɔ báwɛɛ bana eli.

english_verse: They refused to let foreigners join them, as they met to confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ geen bámami lɛlɔ bédie báƒɔ bani nkya-ma akɔ kudɔ. Na béténye sɛsɛɛ, na bévele bana ekpidi ani bábla, na bévele béte bana bati kuuku likyulikpi lɛni bábla lɛnɔ.

english_verse: For three hours they stood and listened to the Law of the Lord their God, and then for the next three hours they confessed their sins and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Na bénye mmɔ kani báka Unwoti ɔda bubo ɔku ɔ́si lɛdɔ ɛtɛ sɔɔn. Na básɔ béti lɛdɔ ɛtɛ lɛnɔ beevele bana ekpidi, na baakɔliku bana Unwoti Katɔti lɛnyi katɔ.

english_verse: Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the special platform for the Levites and prayed aloud to the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Na Lewiƒuɔ ku Yesua ku Bani ku Kadmiel ku Sabania ku Buni ku Serebia ku Bani ku Kenani bákɔ bénye kugyiikɛ kɔni Israelƒuɔ bátu bálɛ mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na bákpali bana Unwoti Katɔti lɛnyi momoomo.

english_verse: Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said: “Stand and shout praises to your Lord, the eternal God! Praise his wonderful name, though he is greater than words can express.” The People Pray
translation_verse: Na Lewiƒuɔ ku Yesua ku Kadmiel ku Bani ku Hasabnia ku Serebia ku Hodia ku Sebnia ku Petahia básu Israelƒuɔ ƒui banii, “Bɛta binye na bimwi bina Unwoti Katɔti ɔni nli ngba ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ƒui! “Na buute ƒula lɛnyi bonwu lɛmmɔ kusɛ kusɛ. Na ƒula lɛnyi lɛ́kɔ litulo lɛnyi biala.

english_verse: You alone are the Lord, Creator of the heavens and all the stars, Creator of the earth and those who live on it, Creator of the ocean and all its creatures. You are the source of life, praised by the stars that fill the heavens.
translation_verse: Awɔ lɛti ndi Unwoti. Na awɔ nédie katɔ ku katɔ katɔ ƒui muedi, ku ala ani nkya-nya kemmo. Na awɔ kani nédie kalɔ ku ala ani ƒui nkya-ka ƒui kemmo ku ɛpu ku ala ani ƒui nkya-nwu kemmo. Na awɔ muute lɛla biala ngba, na ala ani nkya katɔ eeboku lili kalɔ teete-ɔ.

english_verse: You are the Lord our God, the one who chose Abram— you brought him from Ur in Babylonia and named him Abraham.
translation_verse: “Na awɔ ndi Unwoti Katɔti na áƒuna Abram na áda-nwu édie ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Ur ɔni nkya Kaldea kalɛkɛ, na ásia-nwu lɛnyi anii Abraham.

english_verse: Because he was faithful, you made an agreement to give his descendants the land of the Canaanites and Hittites, of the Amorites and Perizzites, and of the Jebusites and Girgashites. Now you have kept your promise, just as you always do.
translation_verse: Awɔ nánu ka nwuna kayi kése siin. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu ényimiku-nwu na éti Kanaanƒuɔ ku Hetiƒuɔ ku Girgasiƒuɔ kalɔ éte nwuna kaba bekyuli. Na ádi ƒula linyese lɛlɔ, ɔsika ese siin.

english_verse: When our ancestors were in Egypt, you saw their suffering; when they were at the Red Sea, you heard their cry for help.
translation_verse: “Na ánu bula bati kuuku lɛbibo na énu bana kɔvanu na Ɛpugyie kɔtu.

english_verse: You knew that the King of Egypt and his officials and his nation had mistreated your people. So you worked fearsome miracles against the Egyptians and earned a reputation that still remains.
translation_verse: Na ábla akɔla lidu lidu asiaku Ƒarao ku nwuna kabla bablane ku nwuna bekyuli bani ƒui nli-nwu kalɔ kemmo. Ɔsika ánu áti tati tati ɔni na Hetiƒuɔ béti bábla ƒula bekyuli kalala. Na awɔ nábla lɛnyi éte ƒula lɛlɔ. Na lɛnyi lɛmmɔ lise líbedu ɔmwi kadi.

english_verse: You divided the deep sea, and your people walked through on dry land. But you tossed their enemies in, and they sank down like a heavy stone.
translation_verse: Awɔ néle ɛpu kemmo inyɔ na bánu báti na básia-nwu kemmo bávi aani kalɔ kani nákwii. Nsu bani nábi ásiaku-ma ni, áya na ɛpu lɛmmɔ lɛ́nyina-ma aani kalɛ na lɛtabi lɛɛnyi ntu kalɔ.

english_verse: Each day you led your people with a thick cloud, and at night you showed the way with a flaming fire.
translation_verse: Na si ƒula bekyuli bakɛ ɔƒiiwi ni, eeti liƒlukutu teetile ɔƒɛ. Na si bákɛ usien aayá na lɛgyavonku bonwu liite-ma bukeye na ɔɔtina-ma ulu.

english_verse: At Sinai you came down from heaven, and you gave your people good laws and teachings that are fair and honest.
translation_verse: “Na awɔ náyu ébelie Sinai Kɔbi lili, na étemi éte-ma. Na éte-ma ɔda bubo lidu lidu bɔni ndia na buse siin.

english_verse: You commanded them to respect your holy Sabbath, and you instructed your servant Moses to teach them your laws.
translation_verse: Na áya na báti ƒula ɔda bubo lidu lidu bɔni na éti ásiaku Mose lɛlɔ éte-ma.

english_verse: When they were hungry, you sent bread from heaven, and when they were thirsty, you let water flow from a rock. Then you commanded them to capture the land that you had solemnly promised. *
translation_verse: Na ka kɔka kɔɔda-ma ni, éte-ma adila ásiku katɔ. Na ka ntukwɛ ɔɔda-ma ni, áya na ntu bɔ́bwɛ bɔlɛ lɛtakpɛ bonwu kemmo. Na ásu-ma ka béteesie bététi kalɔ kani átalaku kɔnu katɔ na ése kenye ka eeti-ka eete-ma.

english_verse: Our stubborn ancestors refused to obey— they forgot about the miracles you had worked for them, and they were determined to return to Egypt and become slaves again.
translation_verse: “Nsu bula bati kuuku bamɛni béti tati tati ku atuɔkplu na bátadi ƒula ɔda bubo lɛlɔ.

english_verse: not even when they made an idol shaped like a calf and insulted you by claiming, “This is the god who rescued us from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ábla ala amɛni ina ka ama alati béti bana ala bávɔ ɔmantɛ akɔ bálɛ na básu banii, ‘Bina Katɔti ɔni nédie-mii na ɔ́kpanku-mii ɔlɛku Egyipte mɛni,’ iye ɔni na bétemi ɔkɔ etemila pii béwi-ɔ.

english_verse: Because of your great mercy, you never abandoned them in the desert. And you always guided them with a cloud by day and a fire at night.
translation_verse: “Na ɔ́si ƒula kɔnyana bonwu kɔni na ébo ɔsu ni, étenwini kama átakya-ma na ketele kemmo mmɔ. Na si ƒula bekyuli bakɛ ɔƒiiwi ni, eeti liƒlukutu teetile-ma ɔƒɛ. Na si bákɛ usien aayá lɛgyavonku bonwu liite-ma bukeye na ɔɔtina-ma ulu.

english_verse: Your gentle Spirit instructed them, and you gave them manna to eat and water to drink.
translation_verse: Na éte-ma ƒula Kɔyu kɔbuni kɔmmɔ ka kɔ́da-ma. Na átada ƒula manna étedie-ma kenye kemmo. Na éte-ma ntu na béti bádu bana ntukwɛ.

english_verse: You took good care of them, and for forty years they never lacked a thing. Their clothes didn't wear out, and their feet were never swollen.
translation_verse: Na akwa aavlene sɔɔn áda-ma na ketele kemmo, na bátayaki kulɛla. Na bana adala lɛnɔ átabuɛ iye ɔdi lɛgba lɛ́ta líƒu.

english_verse: You let them conquer kings and take their land, including King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan.
translation_verse: “Na áya békpo bádi bagadine ku lɛma pii lɛlɔ ku kɔlɔ kɔni ani alati libo ɔmii. Na békpo bádi Ɔga Sihon ɔni mɔɔdi Hesbon kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na básɔ békpo bádi Ɔga Basan ɔni mɔɔdi Og kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You brought them into the land that you had promised their ancestors, and you blessed their nation with people that outnumbered the stars in the sky.
translation_verse: Na áya bana bebi bananabi bemomo aani katɔ ayabi. Na ákpanku-ma éboku kalɔ kani na ásu bana bati ése ka adubuti ka ete-ma.

english_verse: Then their descendants conquered the land. You helped them defeat the kings and nations and treat their enemies however they wished.
translation_verse: Na bana bebi bananabi béteti kalɔ kammɔ. Na ábɔku Kanaanƒuɔ bani nli kalɔ kammɔ. Na éti Kanaanƒuɔ bammɔ ákya-ma enu kemmo. Na békpo bádi bana baga ku bekyuli bani ƒui nli kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ. Na bábla-ma kalala kani námanku.

english_verse: They captured strong cities and rich farmland; they took furnished houses, as well as cisterns, vineyards, olive orchards, and numerous fruit trees. They ate till they were satisfied, and they celebrated your abundant blessings.
translation_verse: Na békpo bádi lɛma libendi ku kɔlɔ kɔni néyii ku lɛmwi. Na béti kɔduli kɔni ala abuni éyi-ku kemmo. Na béti abiɔ ani béku bése ku ntɛ mmo ku nnɔmii mmo ku adingyii mmo pii. Na bádi na bémo na béle lɛmwi. Na bákɛ ebiti na ƒula lɛbuni bonwu lɛni na ábla ɔsu.

english_verse: In spite of this, they rebelled and disobeyed your laws. They killed your prophets, who warned them to turn back to you, and they cursed your name.
translation_verse: “Nsu báyu atuɔkplu na báta bénye-ɔ lɛlɔ. Na béti ƒula ɔda bubo bábala bana kama. Na bádu ƒula kenye bediene bani bákya-ma ɔkplu ka nka benwini bebo-ɔ kudɔ. Na bétemi enyekpi ani mɔɔda lɛƒu béwi-ɔ.

english_verse: So you handed them over to their enemies, who treated them terribly. But in their sufferings, they begged you to help. From heaven you listened to their prayers and because of your great mercy, you sent leaders to rescue them.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu éti-ma éte bana bekisine, na bábla-ma kalala. Nsu na bana lɛbibo kemmo ni, béwulo bákpali-ɔ na énu-ma bɔ́kpali na kesii kani akya na katɔ mmɔ. Na ƒula kɔnyana bonwu bɔnu kemmo ni, édie ukyuli ɔni ndubukpo bɔƒɔ-ma. Na úbekpo ɔ́ƒɔ-ma ɔ́lɛku bana bekisine enu kemmo.

english_verse: But when they were at peace, they would turn against you, and you would hand them over to their enemies. Then they would beg for help, and because you are merciful, you rescued them over and over again.
translation_verse: “Nsu uwi ɔni na bákɛ bɔnwuna blii ni, basɔ bábla likpidi na ƒula anumi. Amu na awɔ lɛnɔ ányonu-ma éte bana bekisine kalɛ na badi-ma lɛlɔ. Amu ka básɔ béwulo bákpali-ɔ ni, énu-ma kɔvanu na kalɔ mmɔ. Na ƒula kɔnyana bɔnu kemmo ni, eedie ukyuli ɔni ndubukpo ɔƒɔ-ma si báƒiɔ-ɔ uwi ndi uwi.

english_verse: For years, you were patient, and your Spirit warned them with messages spoken by your prophets. Still they refused to listen, and you handed them over to their enemies.
translation_verse: Na ákɛku-ma kayi akwa pii. Na átala ƒula kɔyu ákya ƒula kenye bediene ka basu-ma ɔkplu bɔkya etemila. Nsu ɔmɛni kama ƒui ni, bétenu ƒula litemi. Anwuɔsu ányonu-ma éte bana liku bekyuli.

english_verse: But you are merciful and kind, and so you never forgot them or let them be destroyed.
translation_verse: Nsu na ƒula kɔnyana bɔnu bɔni ebo ɔsu, átaya na bádi-ma lɛlɔ iye étenwini kama átakya-ma. Ɔsika adi Katɔti ɔni mɔɔnu kɔnyana na ebo lɛƒɔndia.

english_verse: Our God, you are powerful, fearsome, and faithful, always true to your word. So please keep in mind the terrible sufferings of our people, kings, leaders, priests, and prophets, from the time Assyria ruled until this very day.
translation_verse: “Ɔƒɛni, o bula Katɔti ɔni na edu na ebomo, na eeti bɔyɔ taadi bunyimi lɛlɔ ni, buvele bɔda-a bɔnii tabu lɛbibo lɛni mɔɔlɛ́ mɛni aani lɛla lɛni nse bliisuɛ na ƒula anumi. Na tabu lɛbibo lɛni mɔɔlɛ́ abu ku bula baga ku bula batɔnkune ku bula bakpane ku kenye bediene ku bula bati ku ƒula bekyuli ƒui lɛlɔ úti ɔ́si Asiriaƒuɔ baga uwi úbedu ɔmwi kadi aani lɛla blii.

english_verse: You have always been fair when you punished us for our sins.
translation_verse: Na ala amɛni ƒui bɔlɛ kemmo ni, édie atina ka aabla ala ulu lɛlɔ. Na abu mmomu ni, bula ɔdi naaadia.

english_verse: Our kings and leaders, our priests and ancestors have never obeyed your commands or heeded your warnings.
translation_verse: Na bula baga ku bula batɔnkune ku bula bakpane ku bula bati ƒui ɔdi biala útasiaku ƒula ɔda bubo kama iye bese atu bete-nwu.

english_verse: You blessed them with a kingdom and with an abundance of rich, fertile land, but they refused to worship you or turn from their evil.
translation_verse: Ina ɔmwi ɔni bakya bana lɛgadi kemmo na baakɛ́ ƒula ebiti bonwu na kalɔ kani kewi ƒiaa na kélie lɛmwi na aka na éti éte-ma mmɔ lɛlɔ ni, bátasiaku-ɔ iye benwini kama bakya bana ekpidi.

english_verse: Its plentiful harvest is taken by kings you placed over us because of our sins. Our suffering is unbearable, because they do as they wish to us and our livestock. The People Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Ɔ́si bula ekpidi ɔsu ni, baga bamba bani na édie ka bataadi-bu lɛlɔ ni, ama mɔɔdi edula ammɔ. Na baga bammɔ mɔɔdi abu ku bula ɔmantɛ bakɔ lɛlɔ kalɛ biala baayɔ́. Na buuvele-ɔ ka bɔkya ɔgbankpi bonwu kemmo. Bekyuli Bammɔ Bényimi-ku Katɔti

english_verse: And so, a firm agreement was made that had the official approval of the leaders, the Levites, and priests.
translation_verse: “Ɔ́si ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, buunyimiku-ɔ na kakunkɛ lɛlɔ, na bula batɔnkune ku bula Lewiƒuɔ ku bula bakpane bakya kɔnu kalɔ.”

english_verse: As governor, I signed the agreement together with Zedekiah and the following priests:
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani nákya bunyimi bɔmmɔ kɔnu kalɔ ndi bamɛni. Kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔnune Nehemia ku Hakalia ubidi Sedekia

english_verse: Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah, Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah, Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch, Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah, Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch, Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin, Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah.
translation_verse: ku Maasia ku Bilga ku Semaia. Bamɛni ndi bakpane bani nákya kɔnu kalɔ.

english_verse: The Levites who signed were: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui from the clan of Henadad, Kadmiel,
translation_verse: Na Lewiƒuɔ ndi bamɛni. Asania ubidi Yesua ku Binui ɔni ɔdi Henadad ubidi unwi ku Kadmiel

english_verse: Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,
translation_verse: ku Mika ku Rehob ku Hasabia

english_verse: Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,
translation_verse: ku Sukur ku Serebia ku Sebania

english_verse: Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.
translation_verse: ku Hodia ku Bani ku Beninu.

english_verse: The leaders who signed were: Parosh, Pahath Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
translation_verse: Bekyuli bammɔ batɔnkune ndi bamɛni. Paros ku Pahat-Moab ku Elam ku Satu ku Bani

english_verse: Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,
translation_verse: ku Buni ku Asgad ku Bebai

english_verse: Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,
translation_verse: ku Adonia ku Bigwai ku Adin

english_verse: Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,
translation_verse: ku Ater ku Hesekia ku Asur

english_verse: Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,
translation_verse: ku Hodia ku Hasum ku Besai

english_verse: Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai,
translation_verse: ku Hariƒ ku Anatot ku Nebai

english_verse: Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,
translation_verse: ku Magpias ku Mesulam ku Hesir

english_verse: Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,
translation_verse: ku Mesesabel ku Sadok ku Yadua

english_verse: Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,
translation_verse: ku Pelatia ku Hanan ku Anaia

english_verse: Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,
translation_verse: ku Hosea ku Hanania ku Hasub

english_verse: Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,
translation_verse: ku Halohes ku Pilha ku Sobek

english_verse: Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,
translation_verse: ku Rehum ku Hasabna ku Maaseia

english_verse: Ahiah, Hanan, Anan,
translation_verse: ku Ahia ku Hanan ku Anan

english_verse: Malluch, Harim, and Baanah. The Agreement
translation_verse: ku Maluk ku Harim ku Baana.

english_verse: All of us, including priests, Levites, temple guards, singers, temple workers and leaders, together with our wives and children, have separated ourselves from the foreigners in this land and now enter into an agreement with a complete understanding of what we are doing. And so, we now place ourselves under the curse of the Lord our God, if we fail to obey his laws and teachings that were given to us by his servant Moses.
translation_verse: buse kenye bɔɔsála ku bula batɔnkune ka ewida asiaku-bu si bɔ́ta búnye ɔda bubo bɔmɛni lɛlɔ. Na bɔɔsu ka bɔdubɔdi Katɔti ɔda bubo bɔni na úti ɔ́siaku nwuna kabla ɔblane Mose lɛlɔ. Na lɛla biala na Unwoti ɔni ndi bula Katɔti úbo-bu ɔda ni, bɔdubɔdi-nwu lɛlɔ kalɛ na Katɔti ɔɔwia.

english_verse: We won't let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
translation_verse: Na buláya na bula bebi beetí iye belieku baƒɔ bani nkya-bu akɔ.

english_verse: We won't buy goods or grain on the Sabbath or on any other sacred day, not even from foreigners. Every seven years we will let our fields rest, and we will cancel all debts.
translation_verse: Na si bula ala beyene beti bana ala iye edula ebi bebeye bete-bu lɛnwuna limeyi iye limeyi kedee lɛdi lɛlɔ ni, buléye bulásiku-ma kudɔ. Na lɛkwa maatɛdi biala lɛlɔ ni, bulatuma kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ kalɛ na kakɛ bɔnwuna. Na kayu biala na báda-bu na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, bɔdubuti bɔkyiɛ.

english_verse: Once a year we will each donate a small amount of silver to the temple of our God.
translation_verse: Lɛkwa biala ni, ukyuli biala ɔdubuyi sika ɔƒualadi atabi na buti bubunku kakpakɔ lɛlɔ bɔnu.

english_verse: This is to pay for the sacred bread, as well as for the daily sacrifices and special sacrifices such as those offered on the Sabbath and during the New Moon Festival and the other festivals. It will also pay for the sacrifices to forgive our sins and for all expenses connected with the worship of God in the temple.
translation_verse: Na bɔdubo buteete ala ani badubuti bakpa, na anya ndi bodobodo kedee ku edula ebi ani badubuti bataakpa limeyi ndi limeyi ku bebuo bani badubuti babla bɔkyula akpala limeyi ndi limeyi ku akpala ani badubutaawia lɛnwuna limeyi biala ku kɔbuli kɔwɔdi limeyi bɔdi ku emeyi adi mene bɔdi lɛnɔ. Na bɔdubuteete ala ani beetí baabla akpala kedee ku akpala ani meedie Israelƒuɔ ekpidi ku lɛla biala na kakpakɔ kammɔ kadubɔwia.

english_verse: We have decided that the families of priests, Levites, and ordinary people will supply firewood for the temple each year, so that sacrifices can be offered on the altar, just as the Lord our God has commanded.
translation_verse: Na abu ku bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bɔdubutaatu egulabi teenwini lɛkwa biala teeti taawia kaba kani ɔlɛka bawia ekyweni ani badubuti bɔbla bɔkyula akpala teeti teete bula Unwoti Katɔti aani kalɛ na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔɔsu.

english_verse: Each year we will bring to the temple the first part of our harvest of grain and fruit.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa biala ni, bɔdubuteeti bula edula ebi edeedi ku bula adingyii ebi edeedi teesienku kakpakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: We will bring our first-born sons and the first-born males of our herds and flocks and offer them to the priests who serve in the temple, because this is what is written in God's Law.
translation_verse: Na bula bebi bananabi bani na bula akɔ ɔdi biala ɔdubɔwɔ ni, bɔdubuti-nwu busienku ɔkpane ɔni nkya mmɔ na uti-nwu ɔkya Katɔti enu kemmo. Na lɛnɔ ni, bula ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu ku bese ku bebuo bakladi bebi bedeedi bani badubɔwɔ ni, bɔdubuti-ma bɔkya Unwoti enu kemmo.

english_verse: To the priests in the temple of our God, we will bring the bread dough from the first harvest, together with our best fruit, and an offering of new wine and olive oil. We will bring ten percent of our grain harvest to those Levites who are responsible for collecting it in our towns.
translation_verse: Na bɔdubuti bula ɔlaaƒɔ ɔni bɔ́kɛ bɔ́siku bula edula ebi ku adingyii ebi ku nnɔmii ku ntɛ bɔwɔdi busienku kakpakɔ ɔkpane ɔni nkya mmɔ lɛkwa biala na beti babla akpala. Na bɔdubuti bula ala lɛkpa leevudi busienku Lewini ɔni mɔɔví bula akpaklɔ taaƒɔ lɛkpa leevudi lɛmmɔ na likpo biala lɛni na bɔɔbla kabla.

english_verse: A priest from the family of Aaron must be there when we give this to the Levites. Then the Levites will put one tenth of this part in the temple storeroom,
translation_verse: Na bakpane bani nási Aaron kaba kemmo ku Lewiƒuɔ ɔlɛka basiaku lɛlɔ asa na bataaƒɔ bekyuli bammɔ lɛkpa leevudi. Na kakpakɔ kammɔ ala ni, Lewiƒuɔ badubuti ala buyi bɔmmɔ ana lɛkpa leevudi beteesienku Katɔti kakpakɔ kavumi kemmo.

english_verse: which is also the place for the sacred objects used by the priests, the temple guards, and the singers. Levites and everyone else must bring their gifts of grain, wine, and olive oil to this room. We will not neglect the temple of our God.
translation_verse: Israelƒuɔ ku Lewiƒuɔ ndubo buteeti edula ebi ku ntɛ ku nnɔmii bɔni na bekyuli bammɔ béyi teesienku kakpakɔ kammɔ ala kesekɔ na kesii kani na kakpakɔ kammɔ akyami eesé.
