Mmɔ ndi kesii kani na kakpakɔ kammɔ bakpane ku bagyumanane ku lɛnu batune bani mɔɔbla kabla uwi ɔmmɔ belie. Na buléni bula Katɔti Kaduli bulése.

english_verse: The nation's leaders and their families settled in Jerusalem. But there was room for only one out of every ten of the remaining families, and so they asked God to show them who would live there.
translation_verse: Batɔnkune bammɔ bétélie Yerusalem, na bekyuli bammɔ bátu egulabi bánu na bédie kaduli kenwi bekyuli bálɛku kɔduli leevu kemmo, na bétélie Yerusalem ɔma kedee ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na bekyuli bakladi bétélie lɛma lɛkladi kemmo.

english_verse: Then everyone else asked God to bless those who were willing to live in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na bani nátuna ka badubusie betélie Yerusalem ni, bakladi bémwi-ma.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple workers, and the descendants of Solomon's servants lived on their own property in the towns of Judah. But the leaders of the province lived in Jerusalem with their families. The Judah Tribe
translation_verse: Na Yuda lɛma libendi ku libliidi lɛkladi kemmo ni, Israelƒuɔ bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ ku kakpakɔ kabla bablane ku Salomo kabla bablane kaba bétéduo kɔduli kɔni na ama alati bátu na bana lɛma.

english_verse: Joel son of Zichri was their leader, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command. Priests
translation_verse: Na Sikri ubidi Yoel ndi bana lɛlɔ ɔnune. Na Senua ubidi Yuda mɔɔnu ɔma ɔmmɔ kakɛ kanyɔdi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Four priests settled in Jerusalem. The first was Jedaiah; he was the son of Joiarib and the uncle of Jachin.
translation_verse: Na bani nási bakpane kemmo ndi bamɛni. Yedaia, ɔni ndi Yoiarib ubidi ku Yakin

english_verse: The second priest to settle there was Seraiah son of Hilkiah. His ancestors were Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub, who had been a high priest.
translation_verse: ku Seraia ɔni ndi Hilkia ubidi, ɔni ndi Mesulam ubidi, ɔni ndi Sadok ubidi, ɔni ndi Meraiot ubidi, ɔni ndi Ahitub ɔni ndi Katɔti kakpakɔ lɛlɔ ɔnune unengu

english_verse: from his clan who served in the temple. The third priest to settle there was Adaiah son of Jeroham. His ancestors were Pelaliah, Amzi, Zechariah, Pashhur, and Malchijah.
translation_verse: . Na Adaia ɔni ndi Yeroham ubidi, ɔni ndi Pelalia ubidi, ɔni ndi Pashur ubidi, ɔni ndi Malkia ubidi

english_verse: clan leaders among his relatives. The fourth priest to settle there was Amashsai son of Azarel. His ancestors were Ahzai, Meshillemoth, and Immer.
translation_verse: . Na Amasai ɔni ndi Asarel ubidi, ɔni ndi Ahsai ubidi, ɔni ndi Mesilimot ubidi, ɔni ndi Imer ubidi

english_verse: brave warriors from their clans, and their leader was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim. Levites
translation_verse: . Na bana lɛlɔ ɔnune ndi Hagedolim ubidi Sabdiel.

english_verse: Several Levites settled in Jerusalem. First, there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub. His ancestors were Azrikam, Hashabiah, and Bunni.
translation_verse: Na bani nási Lewiƒuɔ kemmo ndi bamɛni. Semaia ɔni ndi Hasub ubidi, ɔni ndi Asrikam ubidi, ɔni ndi Hasabia ubidi, ɔni ndi Buni ubidi

english_verse: Next, there were Shabbethai and Jozabad, the Levite leaders in charge of the work outside the temple.
translation_verse: ku Sabetai ku Yosabad bani mɔɔnu Katɔti kakpakɔ keyi kakɛ kabla lɛlɔ. Na badi Lewiƒuɔ benengu

english_verse: Then there was Mattaniah son of Mica. His ancestors were Zabdi and Asaph. Mattaniah led the temple choir in the prayer of praise. Bakbukiah, who also settled in Jerusalem, was his assistant. Finally, there was Abda son of Shammua; his grandfather was Galal, and his great-grandfather was Jeduthun.
translation_verse: ku Matania ɔni ndi Mika ubidi, ɔni ndi Sabdi ubidi, ɔni ndi Asaƒ ubidi ɔni mɔɔtɔnku linugya lɛkpa ku Katɔti bɔkpali ku Bakbukia ɔni nsia unyɔdi na nwuna banwani kemmo ku Abda ɔni ndi Samua ubidi, ɔni ndi Gilai ubidi, ɔni ndi Yedutun ubidi.

english_verse: One hundred seventy-two temple guards settled in Jerusalem; their leaders were Akkub and Talmon.
translation_verse: Na kɔyakun lɛlɔ banune ndi Akub ku Talmon ku bana banwani, na bana bumomo bɔdi

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, lived on their own property in the other towns of Judah.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ ku bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bakladi bétélie bana bati kɔlɔ lɛlɔ na lɛma libendi ku libliidi na Yuda kalɛkɛ kemmo.

english_verse: But the temple workers lived in the section of Jerusalem known as Ophel, and the two men in charge of them were Ziha and Gishpa.
translation_verse: Na kakpakɔ kabla kablane bélie Yerusalem na kesii kani baalɔ banii Oƒel, na bakya Siha ku Gispa kalɔ baabla Katɔti kabla.

english_verse: Uzzi son of Bani was the leader of the Levites in Jerusalem. His grandfather was Hashabiah, his great-grandfather was Mattaniah, and his great-great-grandfather was Mica. He belonged to the Asaph clan that was in charge of the music for the temple services,
translation_verse: Na unengu ɔni nkya mɔɔnu Lewiƒuɔ bani nkya Yerusalem lɛlɔ ni, baalɔ-nwu banii Usi na ɔti ndi Bani, na ɔdi Hasabia uwɔ, na nwuna kaba bekyuli badi ndi Matania ku Mika. Na ɔ́si Asaƒ kaba kemmo. Na kaba kamɛni mɔɔnu kakpakɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: though the daily choice of music and musicians was decided by royal decree of the Persian king.
translation_verse: Na lɛnu batune ama ni, ɔga ɔmmɔ mɔɔtina kɔdua biala uwi ɔni na bana uwi údu ka batɔnku ɔnu bɔtu na Unwoti kakpakɔ limeyi biala.

english_verse: The people of Israel were represented at the Persian court by Pethahiah son of Meshezabel from the Zerah clan of the Judah tribe. The People in the Other Towns and Villages
translation_verse: Na Mesesabel ubidi Petahia ɔni nási Serah ɔtɔ na ɔ́si Yuda kaba kemmo ama mɔɔtɛ Israelƒuɔ bani nkya mmɔ etemila.

english_verse: Some of the people of Judah lived in the following towns near their farms: Kiriath-Arba, Dibon, Jekabzeel,
translation_verse: Na bekyuli pii bani nli lɛma lɛni nde bana mmo ndi bekyuli bani nási Yuda kaba kemmo. Na belie Kiriat-Arba ku Dibon ku Yekabseel ku akpaklɔ ani nde lɛma libendi lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: Enrimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth,
translation_verse: ku En-Rimon ku Sora ku Yarmut

english_verse: Zanoah, Adullam, Lachish, and Azekah. In fact, they settled the towns from Beersheba in the south to Hinnom Valley in the north.
translation_verse: ku Sanoa ku Adulam ku akpaklɔ ani náka ámana-ma ku Lakis ku bana mmo bɔni nde-ma ku Aseka ku nwuna akpaklɔ. Na bekyuli bani nási Yuda belie Beer-Seba ɔmii kada kakɛ útédu Hinom Kɔwɛ kakɛ.

english_verse: The people of Benjamin lived in the towns of Geba, Michmash, Aija, Bethel with its nearby villages,
translation_verse: Na Benyamin kaba bekyuli belie ɔ́si Geba katɔ kakɛ útédu Mikmas ku Aia ku Betel ku nwuna akpaklɔ ani náka ámana-ma

english_verse: Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
translation_verse: ku Anatot ku Nob ku Anania

english_verse: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
translation_verse: ku Hasor ku Rama ku Gitaim

english_verse: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
translation_verse: ku Hadia ku Seboim ku Nebalat

english_verse: Lod, and Ono, as well as in Craft Valley.
translation_verse: ku Lod ku Ono ku bekyuli bani mɔɔnwí ligyii.

english_verse: Several groups of Levites from the territory of Judah were sent to live among the people of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Na Lewiƒuɔ bani nási Yuda kakɛ ni, bésie bétélie Benyamin kɔdua bekyuli akɔ.

english_verse: Many priests and Levites had returned from Babylonia with Zerubbabel and Joshua as their leaders. Those priests were Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
translation_verse: Na bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bani nénwini bébo ku Sealtiel ubidi Serubabel ku ɔkpane unengudi Yesua ama ndi bamɛni. Seraia ku Yeremia ku Esra

english_verse: Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
translation_verse: ku Amaria ku Maluk ku Hatus

english_verse: Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
translation_verse: ku Sekania ku Rehum ku Meremot

english_verse: Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
translation_verse: ku Ido ku Gineton ku Abia

english_verse: Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
translation_verse: ku Miamin ku Maadia ku Bilga

english_verse: Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
translation_verse: ku Semaia ku Yoiarib ku Yedaia

english_verse: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and another Jedaiah. These were the leading priests and their assistants during the time of Joshua.
translation_verse: ku Salu ku Amok ku Hilkia ku Yedaia. Na ama ndi bakpane ƒui batɔnkune na Yesua uwi.

english_verse: The Levites who returned were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. They and their assistants were responsible for the songs of praise,
translation_verse: Na Lewiƒuɔ ndi bamɛni. Yesua ku Binui ku Kadmiel ku Serebia ku Yuda ku Matania ni, ama ku bana banwani mɔɔtɔnku linugya lɛnu bɔtu.

english_verse: while Bakbukiah and Unno, together with their assistants, were responsible for the choral responses. Descendants of Joshua the High Priest
translation_verse: Na Bakbukia ku Una ku bana banwani muunye-ma anumi taaƒɔ lɛnu lɛni baatu teete-ma. Ɔkpane Unengudi Yesua Kaba Kemmo Bebi

english_verse: Joshua was the father of Joiakim, the grandfather of Eliashib, and the great-grandfather of Joiada.
translation_verse: Na Yesua ɔ́wɔ Yoiakim, na Yoiakim ɔ́wɔ Eliasib, na Eliasib ɔwɔ Yoiada,

english_verse: Joiada was the father of Jonathan and the grandfather of Jaddua. Leaders of the Priestly Clans
translation_verse: na Yoiada ɔ́wɔ Yonatan, na Yonatan ɔ́wɔ Yadua.

english_verse: When Joiakim was high priest, the following priests were leaders of their clans: Meraiah of the Seraiah clan, Hananiah of Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Na Yoiakim uwi ni, bekyuli bamɛni ndi Lewiƒuɔ kɔduli benengu. Na Seraia kaduli ni, Meraia. Na Yeremia ni, Hanania.

english_verse: Meshullam of Ezra, Jehohanan of Amariah,
translation_verse: Na Esra ni, Mesulam. Na Amaria ni, Yehohanan.

english_verse: Jonathan of Malluchi, Joseph of Shebaniah,
translation_verse: Na Maluki ni, Yonatan. Na Sebania ni, Yoseƒ.

english_verse: Adna of Harim, Helkai of Meraioth,
translation_verse: Na Harim ni, Adna. Na Meraiot ni, Helkai.

english_verse: Zechariah of Iddo, Meshullam of Ginnethon,
translation_verse: Na Ido ni, Sakaria. Na Gineton ni, Mesulam.

english_verse: Zichri of Abijah, Piltai of Moadiah,
translation_verse: Na Abia ni, Sikri.

english_verse: Shammua of Bilgah, Jehonathan of Shemaiah,
translation_verse: Na Bilga ni, Samua. Na Semaia ni, Yehonatan.

english_verse: Mattenai of Joiarib, Uzzi of Jedaiah,
translation_verse: Na Yoiarib ni, Matenai. Na Yedaia ni, Usi.

english_verse: Kallai of Sallai, Eber of Amok,
translation_verse: Na Salai ni, Kalai. Na Amok ni, Eber.

english_verse: Hashabiah of Hilkiah, and Nethanel of Jedaiah. The Priestly and Levite Families
translation_verse: Na Hilkia ni, Hasabia. Na Yedaia ni, Netanel.

english_verse: During the time of the high priests Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and including the time that Darius was king of Persia, a record was kept of the heads of the Levite and priestly families.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Eliasib ku Yoiada ku Yohanan ku Yadua badi Lewiƒuɔ kɔdua batɔnkune ni, bénweni ama ku bakpane anyi bákya ɔku kemmo uwi ɔni na Persiaƒuɔ Ɔga Dario ɔɔdi lɛga.

english_verse: However, no official record was kept of the heads of the Levite clans after the death of Johanan, the grandson of Eliashib.
translation_verse: Na béteenweni adua batɔnkune ku Lewi kaba bekyuli anyi úti útédu Eliasib uwɔ Yohanan uwi.

english_verse: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their assistants organized two choirs of Levites to offer praises to God, just as King David, the man of God, had commanded.
translation_verse: Na Lewiƒuɔ batɔnkune ndi Haabia ku Serebia ku Kasmiel ubidi Yusua ku bana banwani bani muunye-ma anumi na beedie linugya lɛnu atɔ asia aani kalɛ na Katɔti ukyuli Dawid ɔ́tina.

english_verse: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were responsible for guarding the storerooms near the temple gates.
translation_verse: Na Matania ku Bakbukia ku Obadia ku Mesulam ku Talmon ku Akub mɔɔgyumana kɔyakun. Na basɔ baagyumana ala kesekɔ kani nde kɔyakun kɔmmɔ.

english_verse: All of these men lived during the time of Joiakim and during the time that I was governor and Ezra, a teacher of the Law of Moses, was priest. Nehemiah Dedicates the City Wall
translation_verse: Na bamɛni nábla kabla béte Yosadak ku ubidi Yesua ku ubidi Yoiakim. Na bábla kabla na uwi ɔni na Nehemia ɔdi kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ɔnune, na Ɔkpane Esra ɔdi ɔku unwenine. Béti Yerusalem Awodu Bákya Katɔti Enu Kemmo

english_verse: When the city wall was dedicated, Levites from everywhere in Judah were invited to join in the celebration with songs of praise and with the music of cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na badubo Yerusalem awodu ani bátu mmɔ buti bɔkya Katɔti enu kemmo ni, bávi bálɔ Lewiƒuɔ bani nli ekpo ekpo ƒui ka bebo Yerusalem. Báwia-ma ka babadiku-ma limeyi lɛmmɔ ku ebiti, na batu linungya lɛnu na beti agyala beteedie lɛnu.

english_verse: The Levite singers lived in villages around Jerusalem, and so they came from there, as well as from the villages around Netophah, Beth-Gilgal, Geba, and Azmaveth.
translation_verse: ku Bet-Gilgal ku Geba ku Asmawet amadɔ ƒui. Ɔsika lɛnu batune bamɛni ni, báda akpaklɔ na belie-nya kemmo na Yerusalem amadɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: The priests and Levites held special ceremonies to make themselves holy, and then they did the same for the rest of the people and for the gates and walls of the city.
translation_verse: Amu ka bakpane bammɔ ku Lewiƒuɔ bábla sɛɛn bɔbla ɔdi béte bana lɛlɔ ni, bábla lɛni kani béte bekyuli bammɔ ku kɔyakun kɔmmɔ ku awodu ammɔ.

english_verse: I brought the leaders of Judah to the top of the city wall and put them in charge of the two groups that were to march around on top of the wall, singing praises to God. One group marched to the right in the direction of Garbage Gate.
translation_verse: Amu na ami Nehemia lɛ́ya na Yudaƒuɔ batɔnkune bákɔ bésie awodu ammɔ eli. Na lídie lɛnu bediene esu bonwu akpa anyɔ bani ndubo buteesie taamana Yerusalem awodu ammɔ na beteeti linugya teete Katɔti. Na lisu lideedi bésie kɔdianu kakɛ na béti anumi bátina Ruben Kayakun.

english_verse: Hoshaiah and half of the leaders followed them.
translation_verse: Na Hosaia ɔ́kpɛ lɛnu bediene bammɔ kama. Na Yuda benengu kakɛ lɛnɔ bákpɛ-ma kama.

english_verse: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,
translation_verse: ku Yuda ku Benyamin ku Semaia ku Yeremia

english_verse: and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played musical instruments like those that had been played by David, the man of God. And they marched behind Ezra, the teacher of the Law.
translation_verse: ku banwani bani nási ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo. Na ama ndi Semaia ku Asarel ku Milalai ku Gilalai ku Maai ku Natanael ku Yuda ku Hanani. Bekyuli bamɛni nti agyala ani na Katɔti ukyuli Ɔga Dawid ɔ́tina ka bataagya. Na Ɔku Unwenine Esra ɔtɔ-ma anumi.

english_verse: When they reached Fountain Gate, they climbed the steps to David's City and went past his palace, before stopping at the Water Gate near the eastern wall of the city.
translation_verse: Na ka bédu Ntu Kalɛkɔ Kayakun ni, bátásia ulu ɔni ntɛ úsie Dawid Ɔma na bákɛ Dawid kaduli katɔ kakɛ, na bésie bétédu Ntu Kayakun na Yerusalem ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall,
translation_verse: Na lɛnu bediene lɛkpa linyɔdi bákɛ awodu ammɔ kɔmii kakɛ. Na ami Nehemia ku bekyuli kakɛ bakladi bɔsiaku-ma. Na bɔ́kɛ Bodobodo Ayu Katutaasia kudɔ, na búbedu lɛwoduku lɛni nabɛbɛ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Ephraim Gate, Old Gate, Fish Gate, Hananel Tower, Hundred Tower, and on to Sheep Gate. Finally, we stopped at Gate of the Guard,
translation_verse: Na ka bɔ́si mmɔ ni, bútásia Eƒraim Kayakun ku Kayakun Kakukudi ku Kɔbɛ Kayakun ku Hananel Katutaasia ku Eti Anyɔ Katutaasia na bútédu Baƒonu Kayakun na búdi búnye na kakpakɔ mmɔ na bɔ́wɔlɔ.

english_verse: where we stood in front of the temple with the other group, praising God. In the group with me were half of the leaders,
translation_verse: Amu na esu akpa anyɔ ani nkya mɔɔgyá Katɔti enu mmɔ ni, bésie béténye bana kunyekɔ na kakpakɔ mmɔ. Na ami ku batɔnkune bammɔ kakɛ kadi búsie bútákya-ma kudɔ.

english_verse: as well as the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, who were blowing trumpets.
translation_verse: Na bakpane ndi bamɛni. Eliakim ku Maaseia ku Miniamin ku Mikaia ku Elioenai ku Sakaria ku Hanania. Na bada bana kɔkpɛɛ.

english_verse: Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer also stood there, as Jezrahiah led the singers.
translation_verse: Na bakpane bakladi ndi Maaseia ku Semala ku Eleasar ku Usi ku Yehohanan ku Malkia ku Elam ku Eser. Na lɛnu bediene bani na Yisrahia ntɔnku-ma bákpɛ-ma kama na beedie lɛnu momoomo.

english_verse: God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem. Preparation for Worship
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛmmɔ ni, bábla akpala enengudi béte Katɔti. Na lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́-ma, ɔsika Katɔti ebiti áƒɔ-ma lɛlɔ kemmo geen! Na beleku ku bebi lɛnɔ béduo lɛlɔyɔ lɛmmɔ kemmo. Na kudu kɔni na bédie mmɔ ni, kúsie kútédu ɔgyu kakaaka. Kakpakɔ Kammɔ Etela Lɛlɔ Banune

english_verse: On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites. Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, bédie bekyuli ka bátaanu kakpakɔ kammɔ etela kesekɔ lɛlɔ. Na etela ammɔ adi ndi etela lɛkpa leevudi ku edula ebi edeedi ku adingyii ebi edeedi. Na bekyuli bani na bédie mɛni mɔɔví taaƒɔ ala ammɔ na mmo bɔni nde lɛma libendi, na ama muudie bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ ɔdi téteete-ma aani kalɛ na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔɔtina. Na bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bani nkya Yuda kalɛkɛ ƒui lɛlɔ lɛɛda bekyuli bammɔ ebiti.

english_verse: when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon.
translation_verse: Ɔsika baabla lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi ku ɔdi bamba ƒui aani kalɛ na Katɔti úbo-ma ɔda. Na kakpakɔ lɛnu batune ku bagyumanane lɛnɔ baabla bana kabla ulu lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na ɔda bubo bɔni na Dawid ku ubidi Salomo bénweni bése.

english_verse: In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si Dawid ku lɛnu ɔnwine Asaƒ uwi ni, bekyuli bákya bani mɔɔtɔnku lɛnu bediene na baatina-ma bumwi lɛnu ku linugya lɛnu lɛni beeti teemwi Katɔti.

english_verse: During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔ́si Serubabel ku Nehemia uwi ni, Israelƒuɔ ƒui beete etela ani na beeti taanu kakpakɔ lɛnu batune ku bagyumanane lɛlɔ limeyi biala. Na beeti akpala adi teesienku Lewiƒuɔ bakladi lɛnɔ. Na Lewiƒuɔ lɛnɔ beedie Aaron kaba kemmo bebi kadikɔ teete-ma kalɛ na ɔ́manku.

english_verse: On that day when the Law of Moses was read aloud to everyone, it was discovered that Ammonites and Moabites were forbidden to belong to the people of God.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo na báka Mose ɔda bubo ɔku momoomo, na ukyuli biala únu. Mmɔ na bánu ka bénweni bákya ka Amonni biala iye Moabni biala útalɛka baƒɔ-nwu bakya Katɔti bekyuli akɔ.

english_verse: This was because they had refused to give food and water to Israel and had hired Balaam to call down a curse on them. However, our God turned the curse into a blessing.
translation_verse: Ɔsika bekyuli bammɔ béteti adila ku ntu bɔdi bátasiaku Israelƒuɔ. Mmomu buti béteti Bileam ka úbewida-ma. Nsu Bula Katɔti únwini ewida ammɔ ɔ́bla kusɛ kusɛ.

english_verse: Following the reading of the Law of Moses, the people of Israel started sending away anyone who had any foreign ancestors. Nehemiah Makes Other Changes
translation_verse: Na ka bekyuli bammɔ bénu ɔda bubo bɔmɛni ni, báda baƒɔ bani ƒui nkya-ma akɔ bédie bényine sɛsɛɛ.

english_verse: The priest Eliashib was a relative of Tobiah and had earlier been put in charge of the temple storerooms.
translation_verse: Na asa na ɔmɛni ábalɛ ni, ɔkpane Eliasib béti bése ka utaanu Unwoti Katɔti ala kesekɔ ɔtɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́si kukuuku ƒui ni, ɔkpane ɔmɛni ɔkpana ndi Tobia.

english_verse: So he let Tobiah live in one of these rooms, where all kinds of things had been stored—the grain offerings, incense, utensils for the temple, as well as the tenth of the grain, wine, and olive oil that had been given for the use of the Levites, singers, and temple guards, and the gifts for the priests.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu úte Tobia ɔtɔ ubendi ɔni na nka béteeti edula ebi akpala ku oloƒui ku kakpakɔ kabla ala ku etela lɛkpa leevudi lɛni na bekyuli bammɔ beeyi ku ntɛ ku nnɔ bɔni beete Lewiƒuɔ ku kakpakɔ lɛnu batune ku bagyumanane teese.

english_verse: This happened in the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes ruled Babylonia. I was away from Jerusalem at the time, because I was visiting him. Later I received permission from the king
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔni na ala amɛni ƒui aalɛ́ ni, na ami Nehemia liiibo Yerusalem. Na lɛkwa avlaatɛ-linyɔdi lɛlɔ ɔni na Ɔga Artasasta ɔɔdi lɛga na Babilon ni, línwini lísie ɔga ɔmmɔ kudɔ. Na uwi ɔdi kemmo ni, nwuna kudɔ na lívele kuƒi,

english_verse: to return to Jerusalem. Only then did I find out that Eliashib had done this terrible thing of letting Tobiah have a room in the temple.
translation_verse: na lɛ́tɔlɔ lísie Yerusalem. Mɛni na línu ɔbladu ukpidi ɔni na Eliasib ɔ́kya útaabla na údie ɔtɔ unwi úte Tobia na Unwoti Kaduli na uli-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture.
translation_verse: Na ka ńtánu ni, livo líƒi-mi geen, na lɛ́la Tobia ala ƒui líbo líwi keyi.

english_verse: Then I ordered the room to be cleaned and the temple utensils, the grain offerings, and the incense to be brought back into the room.
translation_verse: Na mmɔ kani lɛ́ya na bábla ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ sɛɛn bɔbla ɔdi. Na lɛ́sɔku Katɔti Kaduli ala ƒui ku edula ebi akpala ku oloƒui ńtése Katɔti ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: I also found out that the temple singers and several other Levites had returned to work on their farms, because they had not been given their share of the harvest.
translation_verse: Na lɛ́sɔ línu ka kadikɔ kani ɔlɛka beti bete Lewiƒuɔ béteti bétete-ma. Na Lewiƒuɔ ku kakpakɔ lɛnu batune bani kabla uwi nédu ni, básɔ bénwini bésie bana akpaklɔ.

english_verse: I called the leaders together and angrily asked them, “Why is the temple neglected?” Then I told them to start doing their jobs.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu lɛ́lɔ benengu bammɔ na lɛ́dɔnku-ma na líye-ma nnini, “Bi ɔsu ba béni Unwoti Kaduli bése lɛni?” Amu na lɛ́lɔ Lewiƒuɔ ku lɛnu batune bani nénwini bésie bana akpaklɔ na lɛ́su-ma nnii ɔdi biala ɔsɔ unwini usie uténye nwuna kabla kenye na kakpakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom.
translation_verse: Amu na Israelƒuɔ bése kalɔ beeti bana etela lɛkpa leevudi ku ntɛ bɔwɔdi ku nnɔ teesienku kakpakɔ ala kesekɔ.

english_verse: Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
translation_verse: Na lɛ́ya na bekyuli bamɛni baanu kakpakɔ ala kesekɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ. Na lɛ́ƒɔ lɛ́di ka bekyuli bamɛni badubo bɔbla bana kabla ulu lɛlɔ na beteete kabla bablane bammɔ ala kalɛ na ɔ́manku. Na bekyuli bammɔ ndi Ɔkpane Selemia ku Ɔku Unwenine Sadok ku Pedaia ɔni nási Lewiƒuɔ kaba kemmo. Na Hanan ɔni ndi Sakur ubidi na ɔdi Matania uwɔ ni, anwu ndi bana ubunkune.

english_verse: I pray that my God will remember these good things that I have done for his temple and for those who worship there. The Sabbath
translation_verse: Amu na ami Nehemia muuvele Katɔti nnii, “Mina Katɔti, nyimo-mi na kabla kabuni kani lɛ́bla na ƒula kaduli, na taya na kabla keeke.”

english_verse: I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, lɛ́nu bekyuli ka baabla ntɛ na lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ na Yuda. Na badi lɛnɔ bákya beeti bana edula ku ntɛ ku adingyii ebi ku ala bamba na bényimi básia bana bebuo ala betine kama. Na líbo-ma ɔda kpakplaa ka ɔdi úteti nwuna lɛla lɛdi utéye lɛnwunameyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Na banana badi bási Tiro ɔma unengudi na belie Yerusalem na béti kɔkpaku ku ala eyedi lidu lidu pii béboku Yerusalem ka beti bebeye bete bula bekyuli na lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath!
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́dɔnku Yudaƒuɔ benengu bammɔ. Na lɛ́su-ma nnii, “Bi likyulikpi ala benye baabla mɛni? Na bɛɛyá na lɛnwunameyi lɛmɛni lɛɛlɛ́ ɔbu?

english_verse: Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
translation_verse: Lɛni kani na bina bati kuuku bábla ɔsu na Katɔti ɔ́ni-ma kɔtu. Na ɔ́ya na Yerusalem ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni ɔ́yii udu. Na bɛsɔ binye kpakplaa ka Katɔti kɔnyi kɔsɔ kɔyu kubo abu Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ ɔkɛnku ɔbu ɔni na biléte lɛnwunameyi ɔsu.”

english_verse: I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed on the eve of the Sabbath and not to be opened until after the Sabbath had ended. Then I put some of my own men in charge of the gates to make certain that nothing was brought in on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu líbo-ma ɔda ka bataakalɛ Yerusalem kɔyakun ƒui limeyi biala useyi ɔni na lɛnwunameyi liise kalɔ. Na batalɛmi-ku wetédu ka badi lɛnwunameyi lɛmmɔ bawɔlɔ. Na lídie mina bekyuli badi ka bataagyumana kɔyakun kɔmmɔ kalɛ na ukyuli ɔdi uleti lɛla lɛdi uleduoku ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Once or twice some merchants spent the night outside Jerusalem with their goods.
translation_verse: Na kunwi iye kunyɔ ni, kuye badine beeti bana ala teeboku Yerusalem na baatɛ ɔma ɔmmɔ kɔyakun kama usien umodi ƒui.

english_verse: But I warned them, “If you do this again, I'll have you arrested.” From then on, they did not come on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Nsu líye-ma kpakplaa nnii, “Bi ɔsi na bíbo bíbatɛ awodu amɛni kudɔ usien ɔmɛni? Si lɛ́sɔ lɛ́nu-mii lɛni ndubuƒie-mii!” Na ɔ́si limeyi lɛmmɔ kama ni, kuye badine bammɔ básɔ bétebo mmɔ kudii na lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I ordered the Levites to make themselves holy and to guard the gates on the Sabbath, so that it would be kept holy. God is truly merciful, and I pray that he will treat me with kindness and bless me for doing this. Mixed Marriages
translation_verse: Mmɔ na líbo Lewiƒuɔ bammɔ ɔda ka ɔdi biala utábla lɛlɔ sɛɛn na beteesie batágyumana kɔyakun kɔmmɔ kalɛ beeti ɔbu beete lɛnwunameyi. Amu na lívele Katɔti nnii, “Mɛni lɛnɔ ni, nyimo-mi na anu-mi kɔnyana ɔ́si ƒula bɔyɔ bonwu bɔni ebo ɔsu.”

english_verse: I discovered that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo lɛnɔ ni, lɛ́nu Yudaƒuɔ banana badi ka béti Asdod ku Amon ku Moab beleku.

english_verse: About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language.
translation_verse: Na bebi bani na báwɔ kakɛ beenú Asdod lɛdi ku lɛma lɛkladi adi. Nsu belenu Yudaƒuɔ lɛdi.

english_verse: So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise: In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na lɛ́dɔnku-ma na líwida-ma, na líbo bananabi bammɔ badi na lɛ́ni-ma linwini. Na lɛ́ya na bése kenye na Unwoti lɛnyi kemmo banii, “Bɔsɔ buleti bula bebi belekubi bulete kadi bamba banana na beti-ma. Na bula bananabi lɛnɔ ni, beleti kadi bamba belekubi. Na abu lɛnɔ buleti ɔdi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: God dearly loved King Solomon of Israel and made him the greatest king on earth, but Solomon's foreign wives led him into sin.
translation_verse: “Na kadi bamba beleku buti bɔmɛni udu ɔsu na Ɔga Salomo ɔ́bla likpidi. Na ɔdi ɔga ɔni na nwuna lɛgadi lítulo kadi bamba bagadine ƒui. Na ɔdi ɔga ɔni na Katɔti ɔ́yɔ-nwu litemi, na ɔ́ya na ɔ́di Israel ƒui lɛlɔ. Nsu ɔ́bla likpidi lɛmɛni udu.

english_verse: So we will obey you and not rebel against our God by marrying foreign women.
translation_verse: Na muuye-mii nnii ɔlɛka bɔsiaku lɛla lɛmɛni udu kama na bɔda bɔvia Katɔti litemi na buteeti kadi bamba beleku?”

english_verse: Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane Unengudi Eliasib ubidi Yoiada bebi bammɔ kemmo unwi úti Horonni Sanbalat ubidi ulekubi. Ɔmɛni ɔsu lɛ́bɔku-nwu lɛ́lɛku Yerusalem.

english_verse: I pray that God will punish them for breaking their priestly vows and disgracing the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: O mina Katɔti, nyimi-ma. Ɔsika bébile bana bakpane kabla ku bunyimi bɔni na bakpane ku Lewiƒuɔ bényimiku-ɔ.

english_verse: Then I made sure that the people were free from every foreign influence, and I assigned duties for the priests and Levites.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu lɛ́ya na Lewiƒuɔ ku bakpane ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bámami lɛlɔ bédie kadi bamba ɔdi ablala ƒui kudɔ. Na lɛ́bla ɔda bubo líte ɔdi biala kalɛ na ɔdi biala ɔnu nwuna kabla kani ɔlɛka ɔbla ɔti.

english_verse: I also arranged for the people to bring firewood to the altar each day and for them to bring the first part of their harvest to the temple. I pray that God will bless me for the good I have done.
translation_verse: Na lɛ́ya béyi kugyiikɛ kɔni beeti taakyula akpala na béti béboku nwuna uwi lɛlɔ. Na básɔ béyi bana edula ebi edeedi ani na báƒɛ ku adingyii ebi edeedi ani béde na béti béboku bábabla akpala na uwi lɛlɔ. Amu na lívele Katɔti ka unyimo-mi na nwuna kɔnyana bɔnu kemmo.

english_verse: King Xerxes of Persia lived in his capital city of Susa and ruled
translation_verse: Na ɔma unengudi ɔni baalɔ Susa mmɔ na úse nwuna lɛga kadikɔ liboku.

english_verse: During the third year of his rule, Xerxes gave a big dinner for all his officials and officers. The governors and leaders of the provinces were also invited, and even the commanders of the Persian and Median armies came.
translation_verse: Na nwuna lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa lɛtɛdi kemmo ni, Ɔga Ahasweros ɔ́lɔ nwuna benengu pii badi ku lɛku batine úboku limeyi bɔdi adila kadikɔ bonwu kadi. Na ɔ́lɔ aban bagadine ku bana benengu bani nási kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ kemmo lɛnɔ úboku. Na ɔ́lɔ Persia ku Midian bekpone benengu lɛnɔ ɔnii bebo.

english_verse: At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens.
translation_verse: Uwi útetu na ɔmmɔ kama asa na Ɔga Ahasweros ɔ́sɔ ɔ́lɔ bekyuli ƒui úboku kadikɔ kammɔ udu na Susa ɔma kemmo. Na ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ɔ́bla aani emeyi maatɛ ɔni na baadi na baaní na ɔga ɔmmɔ adingyii kemo egyii kalɔ, na ɔɔɔkɛ ukyuli ɔni udu na adi.

english_verse: The area was decorated with blue and white cotton curtains tied back with purple linen cords that ran through silver rings fastened to marble columns. Couches of gold and silver rested on pavement that had all kinds of designs made from costly bright-colored stones and marble and mother-of-pearl.
translation_verse: Na bákya kadikɔ kammɔ akya ku aduni abuni aƒualadi ku egyiedi. Na béti linwo lɛni náƒɔ kuye litulo ƒui bávili sika ɔƒualadi asikpɛɛ ani ndanku kesii kani bene na asɛɛ ebi ani náƒɔ kuye geen ada aduni ammɔ lɛlɔ. Na bése sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi eboku bése kesii kani na bákya asɛɛ ebi ku ketu kemmo atabi aƒualadi ani muukeye kalɔ ku akya bun bun.

english_verse: The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous
translation_verse: Na lɛɛƒɛɛ lɛni na benengu bammɔ bada baaní ntɛ ƒui ɔdi biala ku kalɛ na bábla-nwu. Na bɔni kani na ɔga ɔmmɔ unye ɔɔní ala taalɛku teeboku kalɛ kalɛ.

english_verse: and said to them, “Drink all you want!” Then he told his servants, “Keep their cups full.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Amii bitaani-mu kalɛ na bɛdubɔkana.” Na ɔ́su nwuna kabla bablane lɛnɔ ɔnini, “Biteeyile-ma lɛɛƒɛɛ ku atu.”

english_verse: While the men were enjoying themselves, Queen Vashti gave the women a big dinner inside the royal palace.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni uwi ɔni na unye ɔɔbla ɔmɛni teete banana bɔmmɔ ni, ulekudi beleku ɔga ɔni baalɔ Wasti lɛnɔ úse kadikɔ kammɔ udu kani úte beleku na ɔga kesii mmɔ.

english_verse: By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas,
translation_verse: Na limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ ni, ntɛ pii bɔmmɔ bɔ́ɔta bɔ́sia Ɔga Ahasweros anumi, na lɛlɔ lɛnɔ lɛɛyɔ́-nwu geen, anwuɔsu ɔ́tala nwuna kabla bablane maatɛ badi bani ndi Mehuman ku Bitsa ku Harbona ku Bigta ku Abagta ku Setar ku Karkas ɔnii

english_verse: to bring Queen Vashti to him. The king wanted her to wear her crown and let his people and his officials see how beautiful she was.
translation_verse: batálɔ ulekudi Beleku Ɔga Wasti beboku-nwu. Na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́yɔ ka nka ulekudi uti nwuna beleku kagabwa ubi na ɔlɛ ubo, na nwuna bekyuli bani na ɔ́lɔ mmɔ banu kalɛ na ɔɔdia bɔnu.

english_verse: The king's servants told Queen Vashti what he had said, but she refused to go to him, and this made him terribly angry.
translation_verse: Kabla bablane bammɔ bátásu ɔga uleku Wasti kenye kammɔ, nsu úni na útasiaku-ma na ubo kesii kani na ɔga ɔɔlɔ-nwu. Anwuɔsu Ɔga Ahasweros ɔ́kɛku ulekudi kɔnyi kpakplaa.

english_verse: The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
translation_verse: Na bani nde-nwu geen mmɔ ndi benengu maatɛ bani baalɔ Kasena ku Seta ku Admata ku Tarsis ku Meres ku Masena ku Memukan. Bekyuli bamɛni mɔɔdi kasusu na Persia ku Media kalɔ kammɔ ku kana lɛga kadikɔ ala lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The king said to them, “Queen Vashti refused to come to me when I sent my servants for her. What does the law say I should do about that?”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́lɔ-ma na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Lɛni na lɛ́lɔ mina ulekudi Beleku Ɔga Wasti nnii ubo na úni. Bi na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔɔtina ka lɛbla-nwu?”

english_verse: Then Memucan told the king and the officials: Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Memukan ɔ́su ɔga ku benengu bakladi bammɔ ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdi awɔ lɛti na ƒ'ulekudi Beleku Ɔga Wasti ɔmɛni ɔ́kya kɔƒa. Mmomu údumi ƒula lɛga kadikɔ benengu bani ƒui na álɔ ásiku kɔlɔ ekpo ekpo ƒui éboku mɛni lɛnɔ ku kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ ƒui bekyuli.

english_verse: The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?”
translation_verse: Na beleku bammɔ ƒui badubunu ɔmɛni na bakɛ kenyekɔ. Ɔkɛnku ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, uleku biala ɔdubuse kalɔ utaanu ɔgyani anumi. Na si ɔɔtɛmiku-nwu ɔdubɔsu-nwu ɔnini, ‘Ɔga Ahasweros muedi ɔ́lɔ ulekudi Beleku Ɔga Wasti na úni útesie!’

english_verse: Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
translation_verse: Na si bɛɛbu bɛnii ɔkɔ litemi mɔɔsu ni, bula benengu bani nása mɛni beleku badubunu lɛla lɛni na beleku ɔga ɔmɛni ɔ́bla, na bɛdubɔnu ka ama lɛnɔ badubuseku-bu udu ɔmɛni kalɔ asa na kadi kadubugye muedi.

english_verse: Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu si ami ku-mii kasusu kadubɔbla unwi ni, na ɔga ɔya na bunyimi ɔda bubo kpakplaa bɔdi, na basɔ balavumana-mu lɛnɔ kudii. Na bakɔ-mu lɛsa bete kadi ƒui banii Beleku Ɔga Wasti ɔsɔ uuubo kuƒi na ɔsɔ ɔda ɔlɛ bula ɔga anumi kudii lɛnɔ ɔ́si ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ. Na ɔga ɔƒɔ-nwu kenyekɔ kammɔ ute uleku bamba ɔni na ɔdia utulo-nwu ƒui.

english_verse: When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
translation_verse: Na si búte-ma bɔti bɔmɛni na kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo bɔ́vi ni, beleku bammɔ badubo lɛlɔ kalɔ buteeboku teete bana bagya ɔ́si banamu lɛlɔ útédu benengudi lɛlɔ ina dɛ na kɔnu kemmo kadia uleku ɔmmɔ.”

english_verse: King Xerxes and his officials liked what Memucan had said,
translation_verse: Ɔga Ahasweros ku nwuna benengu bammɔ báƒɔ lɛla lɛmɛni enu anyɔ.

english_verse: and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔ́ya na bénweni ɔku ɔmmɔ na adi ani ƒui na akya kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ƒui, na béti bémene-ma bákɔ lɛsa bávi ka kaduli biala kemmo ni, ɔnana ndi beleku bammɔ ku bebi ƒui lɛlɔ ɔdine.

english_verse: After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her.
translation_verse: Kama ni, kɔnyi kúbayɔ Ɔga Ahasweros, nsu ɔ́mu ɔkya ɔɔbla kasusu na Beleku Ɔga Wasti lɛla lɛni na ɔ́bla mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́kali lɛla lɛni na ɔ́ya na bákɔ lɛsa bávi na kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo lɛlɔ ɔkɛnku anwu ɔsu.

english_verse: Then the king's personal servants said: Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na kabla bablane bani nkya Ɔga Ahasweros kaduli geen básu-nwu banini, “Ɔga ɔbune, ya na ƒula benengu basia kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ ƒui anu na baƒuna beleku babuni bani mɔɔdia bɔnu geen bete-ɔ.

english_verse: You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments.
translation_verse: Akana na edie batɔnkune na kalɛkɛ biala kemmo na bakpanku beleku bammɔ beboku Hegai ƒula kabla ɔblane ɔni mɔɔnu ƒula beleku lɛlɔ teete-ɔ mmɔ, na basɔ bakya kesii kani na ƒula beleku baakya na Susa ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo. Anwu ndubɔnu ka báklibi-ma kaduɛ na bákya-ma akya kalɛ na bataadia bɔnu geen ka ɔmmɔ kabla na ɔɔbla ɔsu.

english_verse: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
translation_verse: Na awɔ ɔlati aƒuna bana akɔ ugblebi ɔni na aayɔ́, na eti-nwu abla beleku ɔga na Wasti kenye.” Na kenye kamɛni káda-nwu ebiti geen sɔsɔ.

english_verse: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Na Susa ɔma unengudi kemmo na ɔga kesii mmɔ ni, Yudani ɔdi baalɔ banii Mordekai ɔ́kya. Na ɔti baalɔ Yairo, na Yairo ɔti baalɔ Simei, na Simei ɔti baalɔ Kis, na ɔ́si Benyamin kɔdua kemmo.

english_verse: Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Mordekai ɔmɛni lɛnɔ ubunku bekyuli bani na Ɔga Nebukadnesar úƒie ɔ́tɔlɔku Yerusalem úsienku Babilon uwi ɔni na úƒie Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga Yekonia.

english_verse: Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died.
translation_verse: Na Mordekai ubo ɔnwani ulekubi ɔni mɔɔdia bɔnu geen ɔdi na baalɔ-nwu Hadasa, na nwuna lɛnyi linyɔdi baalɔ Ester. Ulekubi ɔmɛni ɔdi Mordekai uni ɔnwani ɔnana ubidi, nsu anwu nánu-nwu lɛlɔ, ɔsika ulekubi ɔmmɔ bawɔne béyile bukpi, anwuɔsu únwini aani ubidi.

english_verse: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Ɔga Ahasweros úte bɔti ka bavi baƒuna belekubi bani mɔɔdia bɔnu geen bésienku Susa ni, na Ester lɛnɔ ɔ́kya-ma akɔ. Na béti-nwu bésienku ɔga kesii na Hegai ɔɔnu-ma lɛlɔ na beleku kakyakɔ kammɔ.

english_verse: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si limeyi lideedi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ kani na Ester ala éƒie Hegai kayi, ɔsu úse kalɔ ɔɔklibi-nwu kɔnakunwi na ɔɔkya-nwu akya ani udu naaabɔ. Uute-nwu adila abuni geen na ɔɔdi, na Hegai ɔ́wia belekubi kabla bablane maatɛ úte-nwu, na úte-ma lɛtɔ lɛni mɔɔdia bɔnu teetulo ƒui na ɔga kesii mmɔ na bakya.

english_verse: Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him.
translation_verse: Nsu Mordekai ɔ́ɔgyu ɔ́tɔ na ɔ́su Ester ɔnii utaya na bati banii Yudani na ɔdi kudi kudii. Na anwu lɛnɔ únu úte-nwu.

english_verse: He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
translation_verse: Mordekai ɔɔyɔ́ ɔti lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́ku ubidi Ester ɔsu ni, limeyi ndi limeyi uusié taasɔ na beleku bammɔ kakyakɔ anumi mmɔ na ɔɔwia unu lɛla lɛni nsɔ ndubo bɔlɛ.

english_verse: The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes.
translation_verse: Lɛkwa limodi na beeti taaklibi beleku bammɔ asa na bada balɛ ɔga anumi ɔdi biala ku ƒula limeyi. Na abuli aku edeedi ni, nnɔmii bɔni mɔɔbla lɛlɔ suɛlɛ suɛlɛ na baalɔ-mu mira, na baawɛɛ-ma. Na abuli aku ani nsɔ nsia na bawɛɛ-ma ugyulo ƒɛƒɛɛ lidu lidu.

english_verse: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
translation_verse: Si limeyi lɛni na údu ka uleku ɔdi usie ɔga kudɔ na nwuna kesii mmɔ ni, anwu ɔlati mɔɔsu lɛla lɛni na ɔɔyɔ́ ka uti ɔda asa na usie na badubuti-ni bete-nwu.

english_verse: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
translation_verse: Useyi uwi na uleku ɔni na ƒula uwi údu ka esie ɔga kudɔ ésela na atákya mmɔ útálɛ kadi bugye ɔtanta. Na si ási mmɔ ni, badubɔkpanku-ɔ besienku ɔga basɔnɔ lɛlɔ ɔnune ɔni baalɔ Sasgas na atákya basɔnɔ bammɔ kakyakɔ mmɔ na aka kese bun. Na si ƒula lɛlɔ lɛ́da ɔga ebiti ni, anwu na ɔdubɔya na basɔ baalɔ-ɔ bete-nwu.

english_verse: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
translation_verse: Ka Ahasweros ɔ́nu Ester ni, ɔ́da-nwu kayi geen útulo beleku bammɔ ƒui na nwuna kayi kásia-nwu lɛlɔ kɔnakunwi útulo begblebi bakladi ƒui. Anwuɔsu úti kagabwa kammɔ úbi-nwu lili na ɔ́bla-nwu beleku ɔga na Wasti kenye.

english_verse: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Ɔga Ahasweros ɔ́lɔ nwuna benengu ku lɛku batine ɔ́siku kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo úboku limeyi bonwu lɛdi kadikɔ úti ɔ́kya Ester ebiti, na úte bekyuli ala geen, na ɔ́su lɛnɔ ka ɔdi utabla kabla kadi limeyi lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
translation_verse: Na begblebi bammɔ bɔsɔ bɔsa kunyɔdi ni, na Mordekai ɔkya ɔga kabla bablane benengu akɔ na uunye ɔga kesii ɔban kayakun.

english_verse: He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ ƒui ni, Ester útaya na ɔdi ɔti kesii kani na ɔ́si aani kalɛ na Mordekai ɔ́su-nwu kalɛ. Ɔsika ɔ́mu uunú-nwu litemi aani kalɛ kani na útaabla ɔ́si lɛnamu uwi.

english_verse: Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Nkyuli inyɔ badi na baalɔ Bigtana ku Teres lɛnɔ bátaabla ɔga kabla na ama mɔɔgyumana ɔga kayakun. Nsu nkyuli inyɔ bamɛni bébeti kasusu kekpidi kadi na Ɔga Ahasweros lɛlɔ ka badu-nwu.

english_verse: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
translation_verse: Na Mordekai úbanu ɔmɛni ɔ́ti, na ɔ́su Beleku Ɔga Ester ɔnii ɔya na ɔga ɔti.

english_verse: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_verse: Ka báwia litemi lɛmmɔ kalɔ laa na bánu ka sɔsɔ na ɔdi ni, ɔga ɔ́ya na bátákya-ma abuli limɔ báƒala akpa lɛlɔ na békpi. Na ɔga ɔ́ya na bénweni ala ani nálɛ ƒui bákya nwuna ɔku ɔni kemmo na baakya ala alɛdi kemmo bése.

english_verse: Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag,
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Ɔga Ahasweros ɔ́kɔliku Haman ɔni ndi Hamedata ubidi ɔnanabi kenyekɔ, na únwini nwuna benengu bani muubunku-nwu ƒui unengu na nwuna lɛga kadikɔ. Na Haman ɔmɛni ɔ́si Ɔga Agag kaba kemmo.

english_verse: and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai.
translation_verse: Na ɔga úbo ɔda ka bakladi bani na bakya-nwu kalɔ ƒui bataakya Haman lili kalɔ na balɛ akɔnkɔ lɛnɔ kalɔ si ɔ́si ɔɔví aani bana unengu kalɛ. Nsu Mordekai kani néni na ulábla lɛni si ɔ́nu-nwu.

english_verse: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
translation_verse: Limeyi ndi limeyi ni, baatɛmiku-nwu ka nka unwini kasusu, nsu útenu kalɔ. Anwuɔsu bésie bátásu Haman lɛla lɛni na Mordekai ɔɔbla na banu si dɛ na badubo-nwu bɔbla.

english_verse: Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him.
translation_verse: Haman úti kɔnyi kpakplaa ka únu kenye kamɛni ka Mordekai úni ɔnii ulalɛ akɔnkɔ kalɔ ulete-nwu ɔbu.

english_verse: And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
translation_verse: Ka únu lɛnɔ ka Yudani na Mordekai ɔdi ɔsu ni, ɔ́lɛ ugyii ka badu Yudaƒuɔ ƒui na ɔɔɔdi Mordekai kani, ɔsika ɔmmɔ ulálɛ kɔsia kɔdi na kɔlɔ kɔni ƒui lɛlɔ na Ɔga Ahasweros ɔɔdi mmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmɛni kemmo ni, Ahasweros úuduo nwuna lɛkwa aavlanyɔdi kemmo ka ɔɔdi lɛga. Na bana kɔbuli kudeedi kɔni baalɔ Nisan kemmo ni, Benengu badi bábatu egulabi banu na Haman anumi na bati uwi ɔni na ɔ́manku ka badu Yudaƒuɔ bammɔ. Na egulabi ammɔ átina ka kɔbuli leevu-kunyɔdi kɔni baalɔ Ada na ɔlɛka babla lɛla lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: Then Haman went to the king and said: Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them!
translation_verse: Amu na Haman útásu Ɔga Ahasweros ɔnini, “Kadi bekyuli badi básala bakya ƒula kɔlɔ kɔni lɛlɔ na aadi bekyuli ƒui akɔ. Na bebo ɔdi ɔdi na baabla na ɔ́vumanaku bekyuli bakladi ƒui ɔdi, na baládi ƒula ɔda bubo lɛnɔ lɛlɔ. Na lɛla lɛmɛni lɛɛɛdububoku kɔsia biala na ƒula lɛga kadikɔ. Anwuɔsu ɔlɛka bɔyila-ma udu kalɛ na lɛga kadikɔ kammɔ kenye kaduɛ.

english_verse: Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
translation_verse: Mɔɔnu ka ɔdia ka ebo ɔda na bɔdu-ma. Na muusé kenye lite-ɔ ka si úbo úte lɛni ni, ndubɔkɛ sika ɔƒualadi pii lɛkya ƒula lɛga kadikɔ kavumi kemmo.”

english_verse: The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him,
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, Ahasweros úti nwuna ɔyikun kakwɛnimi kani mɔɔtina ka ɔ́sia lɛla lɛdi kɔnu ka babla-ni úte Haman ɔni ndi Hamedata ubidi ɔni nási Ɔga Agag kaba kemmo, ɔni muukisi Yudaƒuɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: “Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Ahasweros ɔ́su Haman ɔnini, “Bekyuli bammɔ ku bana sika ƒui ɔkya-a enu kemmo, anwuɔsu bla-ma lɛla lɛni na ánu ka lɛ́manku.”

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
translation_verse: Na bana kɔbuli kudeedi kɔni ndi Nisan limeyi leevu-lɛtɛdi lɛlɔ ni, Haman ɔ́lɔ ɔga lɛku benwenine ƒui, na úbo-ma ɔda ɔnii benweni lɛku na kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ ƒui adi butemi ku bunweni kemmo. Anwuɔsu bénweni-ni na ɔga lɛnyi kemmo na bétu-ni kɔnu bɔsia likpose kakwɛnimi na béti bémene kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ badine ku aban bagadine benengu ƒui na Ahasweros lɛga kadikɔ ƒui.

english_verse: The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
translation_verse: Batu na bátala ku kɔnu kɔnu na bele lɛku lɛmmɔ bávi. Na ala ani nkya lɛku lɛmmɔ kemmo aatina ka ɔlɛka badu Yudaƒuɔ ƒui, banana ku beleku ku bana bebi ƒui banamu ku benengu, na bayila-ma udu na limeyi linwi pɛ lɛlɔ lɛni ndi kɔbuli leevu-kunyɔdi limeyi leevu-lɛtɛdi lɛlɔ, na beti-ma ala ƒui.

english_verse: King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_verse: Ɔga Ahasweros ɔ́ya na bákɔ litemi lɛmɛni lɛsa na kesii biala, na ɔ́lɛ lɛni na Susa ɔma unengudi kemmo lɛnɔ. Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Ɔga Ahasweros ku Haman bétélie kalɔ na báni ntɛ. Nsu litemi lɛmɛni lɛ́bla Susa ɔma bekyuli dɛye dɛye, na lɛsɛ lɛ́ƒɔ-nwu kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping.
translation_verse: Ka Mordekai únu ɔku ɔmmɔ kenye ni, ɔ́ni nwuna awu ɔni na ɔkya ɔ́bwɛ, na úti adikpi ɔ́sabla, na ɔ́kpi ntɔ anumi, na ɔkɛ uuwulo momoomo taavi na Susa ɔma ɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo.

english_verse: But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace.
translation_verse: Nsu útakana ɔga kesii buduo, ɔsika kuƒi kuuubo ka adala ammɔ udu eduoku mmɔ. Anwuɔsu kayakun kenye kani na ɔ́wɔ.

english_verse: In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
translation_verse: Na kalɛkɛ biala lɛlɔ na báka ɔku ɔmmɔ ni, Yudaƒuɔ bani nkya mmɔ keku kani na beewulo na baaƒɛ́ enu, na badi béti adikpi bényimi na báyu béwi ntɔ akɔ.

english_verse: When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Ester kabla bablane belekubi ku ɔga kabla ɔblane ɔni mɔɔnu Ester lɛlɔ básu-nwu kalɛ na Mordekai ɔɔbla ni, kayi kákpulu Ester, na lɛla lɛmmɔ líkpoku-nwu geen. Anwuɔsu ɔ́wia adala adi úte ɔnii besienku-nwu na ɔda, na ɔɔɔdi ammɔ udu kemmo na ɔlɛka ɔkya. Nsu Mordekai úni ɔnii uláƒɔ-nya.

english_verse: Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ester ɔ́lɔ Hatak ɔga beleku lɛlɔ banune akɔ unwi ɔni mɔɔnu-nwu lɛlɔ ɔnii usie na utéye unu lɛla lɛni geen mɔɔbla Mordekai, na ubasu-nwu.

english_verse: Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate,
translation_verse: Hatak úsie útásiaku Mordekai na ɔma kemmo kaduli kani nwi ɔga kesii anumi mmɔ.

english_verse: and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Mordekai ɔ́sɔku ɔ́su-nwu lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́ ku kayu kani na Haman ɔnii ɔdubɔƒɔ akya ɔga kavumi kemmo si bákana na bádu Yudaƒuɔ ƒui bédie.

english_verse: Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
translation_verse: Mordekai údie ɔku ɔni na bénweni banii badu Yudaƒuɔ mmɔ ɔdi úte Hatak ɔnii uti usienku Ester, na udie lɛla biala kalɔ ute-nwu na ɔkya ɔkplu na usie ɔga anumi, na utévele na ama Yudaƒuɔ lili.

english_verse: Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Hatak únwini úsie na útásu Ester lɛla lɛni na Mordekai ɔ́su-nwu.

english_verse: there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
translation_verse: “Ɔga benengu bammɔ ƒui ku bagadine bani na bakya kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ƒui bagyi ka ukyuli ɔni na adubɔda bɔlɛ-nwu lɛlɔ na ɔɔɔdi anwu násu ɔnii balɔ-ɔ beboku ni, ɔnana na adi o-o uleku na adi o-o ni, bɔdu na badubo-ɔ. Na si kuli kɔ́dia-a na úti nwuna sika ugyiedi ɔgagyii ɔ́kywɛ-ɔ ni, na anwu na adubulie ngba. Ɔƒɛni ni, ɔ́ɔbla aani emeyi avlaatɛ mɛni ka bálɔ-mi na lísie-nwu kudɔ.”

english_verse: When Mordecai was told what Esther had said,
translation_verse: Ka Mordekai únu Ester kenye kamɛni ni,

english_verse: he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace.
translation_verse: ɔ́sɔku ɔtu ɔmmɔ kani ɔ́kya Ester ɔnini, “Takali anii ka akya ɔga kesii ɔsu ni, baaadubo awɔ lɛla lɛdi bɔbla na awɔ kani ndubɔlɛ ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni kemmo.

english_verse: If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
translation_verse: Na si átakana na abla lɛla lɛdi na uwi ɔmɛni udu kemmo ni, kebunku kadubɔsi kesii bamba kudɔ kete Yudaƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui na bakɛ bɔƒɔ, nsu awɔ ku ƒula bati ku bina ɔtɔ kemmo bɛdubo udu bɔyii ƒui. Ɔma ngyi lɛla lɛni ɔsu na ákɛ kuƒi ka éduo likpo lɛmɛni udu uwi ɔmɛni kemmo?”

english_verse: Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying,
translation_verse: Amu na Ester údie kenye ɔnii batásu Mordekai ɔnini,

english_verse: “Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
translation_verse: “Sala Yudaƒuɔ bani ƒui nkya Susa ɔma kemmo lisu, na binyimi kenye emeyi atɛ usien ku ɔƒɛ na ami ɔsu, na ɔdi utadi lɛla lɛdi. Ami ku mina beleku kabla bablane bani mɔɔnu-mi lɛlɔ lɛnɔ bɔdubɔbla lɛni kani. Na si bɔ́wɔlɔ ɔmɛni ni, ndubusie ɔga kudɔ ina ka kuƒi kuuubo lɛni. Na si kukpi na ɔdi ka likpi lɛnɔ ni, na likpi ƒaa.”

english_verse: Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
translation_verse: Mordekai lɛnɔ úsie na útábla lɛni kani sɔsɔ.

english_verse: Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛtɛdi lɛlɔ ni, Ester ɔ́da nwuna beleku ɔga adala na úsie unye kaduli kemmo na ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na ɔga uulie nwuna lɛgaboku lɛlɔ taanu keyi teemene anumi.

english_verse: He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her. When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na ɔga ɔ́nu Uleku Ɔga Ester úmene ni, ɔ́da-nwu kayi kɔnakunwi, na únene nwuna sika ugyiedi ɔgagyii ɔ́tina-nwu. Anwuɔsu Ester úsie útétuku ɔgagyii ɔmmɔ lili.

english_verse: the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Amu na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Mina Uleku Ɔga Ester, bi nébo? Su-mi lɛla lɛni na aawia, ina mina lɛga kadikɔ kakɛ kenwi na aawia muedi ndubute-ɔ.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ester údie kenye ɔnini, “O mina ɔga ɔbune, si ɔdia ute-ɔ ni, mɔɔyɔ́ ka awɔ ku Haman bibo kadikɔ kani na lɛ́ɛklibi líse-mii ɔmwi limeyi lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.” The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner,
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnii, “Ya na Haman ɔklibi lɛlɔ pla, kalɛ na bɔbla lɛla lɛni na Ester ɔɔwia!” Na anwu ku Haman bébo kadikɔ kani na Ester ɔ́klibi úse-ma.

english_verse: and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Na ɔni na béboku ntɛ bɔdi na badaku bɔni ni, ɔga ɔ́sɔ úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ndi lɛla lɛni na ébo ebevele-mi. Su-mi lɛla lɛni na aawia, ina mina lɛga kadikɔ kakɛ kenwi na aawia muedi ndubute-ɔ.”

english_verse: Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.” Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
translation_verse: mɔɔyɔ́ ka mbalɔ awɔ ku Haman na bibo kadikɔ bamba kani na ndubɔklibi lise-mii kɔnaadi. Na si ɔdubɔyɔ-ɔ kaƒɔ ƒaa na mmɔ ni, ndubɔsu-ɔ lɛla lɛni na mɔɔwia.”

english_verse: Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry,
translation_verse: Ka Haman ɔ́ta ntɛ bɔmmɔ kanikɔ mmɔ ni, lɛlɔyɔ lɛkya-nwu lɛlɔ kemmo kaduɛ, ɔsika ntɛ bɔmmɔ bɔsia-nwu anumi. Nsu uwi ɔni na ɔ́nu Mordekai na ɔban kayakun ka ulie na ulábla lɛla lɛdi ulatina ka uute-nwu ɔbu ɔdi ɔsu ni, kɔnyi kɔ́kɔ-nwu geen.

english_verse: but he did not say a thing. When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh
translation_verse: Nsu útasu lɛla lɛdi. Amu ka Haman útéduo kaduli ni, ɔ́lɔ nwuna bakpana ku ulekudi Sares ɔ́sala,

english_verse: and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him.
translation_verse: na úse kalɔ ɔɔkun lɛmɛnɛ na nwuna lɛkɛ pii lɛni na ubo lɛlɔ ku bebi bananabi lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́su-ma kesii kani na ɔga úti-nwu útése, na nwuna kenyekɔ kenye ku kalɛ na bakladi baakya-nwu lili kalɔ, na baalɛ akɔnkɔ kalɔ taabu-nwu.

english_verse: Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su ɔ́sia ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdi ɔmmɔ lɛti mmomu na bekyuli ƒui akɔ ni, ami kani na Beleku Ɔga Ester ɔ́lɛ lɛnimi úbunku ɔga ka bubo bubadiku-nwu. Na kɔnaadi kani na ɔdi.

english_verse: But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui ulayɔ-mi tɔ kaƒɔ na uwi ɔni na Yudani Mordekai ɔmmɔ mmu muulie ɔga kayakun kammɔ kenye ɔsu.”

english_verse: That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king.
translation_verse: Usien ɔmmɔ ni, Ɔga Ahasweros útakana bɔlɛɛ. Anwuɔsu ɔ́ya na bálɔ nwuna kabla ɔblane ɔdi béte-nwu, na unye ɔɔká ala ani ƒui náalɛ na nwuna lɛga bɔdi uwi na nwuna lɛga kadikɔ teete-nwu.

english_verse: When the servant read how Mordecai had kept Bigthana and Teresh from killing the king,
translation_verse: Na ka kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ ɔ́ka kalɛ na Mordekai ɔ́bla asa na Bigtana ku Teres bátakana-nwu bɔdu ni,

english_verse: the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?” “Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
translation_verse: úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ndi lɛla lɛni na bénweni ka ani na béti bágya Mordekai enu?” Amu na kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Mina Ɔbune, bátabla lɛla lɛdi.”

english_verse: About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo kani ni, Haman úbo ɔnii ubasu ɔga na ɔya na bakya Mordekai ɔbuli limɔ baƒala akpa ku ɔta bonwu ɔni na ɔ́tu únyene mmɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́ɔnu-nwu úmene, anwuɔsu ɔ́kpali úye ɔnini, “Awɔ ɔma na ɔdi nnye mmɔ?”

english_verse: The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.” “Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
translation_verse: Amu na kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ údie kenye ka Haman na ɔdi. Mmɔ na ɔga ɔsu-nwu ɔnini, “Su-nwu anii ami nnii ubo.”

english_verse: When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?” Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor.
translation_verse: Ka Haman úduo-nwu kudɔ mmɔ ni, ɔga ɔmmɔ úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi na ɔdi ka lɛbla lite ukyuli ɔni na mɔɔkali ka lɛkɔliku katɔ na lite-nwu ɔbu?” Ɔ́bla Haman kasusu ka ukyuli bamba ɔdi ɔsɔ uuubo na ɔga ɔmmɔ wakali ɔnii ɔɔkɔliku katɔ utulo anwu Haman.

english_verse: So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu údie kenye ɔnini, “Si aayɔ́ ka akɔliku ukyuli ɔdi katɔ bɔdi ni,

english_verse: get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress.
translation_verse: amu tala na betéti ƒula awu bonwu ɔbunidi ku ƒula ɔpɔnkɔ ku lɛduni lɛni na eebi lili na lɛ́ƒɔ kuye geen mmɔ beboku.

english_verse: Tell one of your highest officials to place your robe on this man and lead him through the streets on your horse, while someone shouts, ‘This is how the king honors a man!’ ”
translation_verse: Na aya na ƒula kabla ɔblane ɔni na ubo kenyekɔ utulo ƒui uti awu ɔbunidi bonwu ɔmɛni ɔkya ukyuli ɔmmɔ, na ɔkɔ ulie ƒula ɔpɔnkɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ, na batɔnku-nwu na ɔvi ɔma ɔmmɔ lɛblɔnu ƒui lɛlɔ ɔsa, na ukyuli ɔdi utaava taasu ɔnini, ‘Lɛni na baabla teete ukyuli ɔni na ɔga ɔ́kɔliku katɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani na ɔga ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Babla na atábla lɛla lɛni na ásu mɛni na tayiƒala lɛdi tese. Sie na atáƒɔ awu ɔmmɔ ku ɔpɔnkɔ ɔmmɔ na eti atákya Yudani Mordekai na ɔban kenye na abla-nwu ala ani ƒui na ásu mɛni!”

english_verse: Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
translation_verse: Haman úsie útáƒɔ ala amɛni ƒui úboku na úbakya Mordekai awu ɔbunidi ɔmmɔ, na ɔ́tɔnku Mordekai ɔ́siaku ulu biala lɛlɔ na ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo, na ulie ɔpɔnkɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ, na Haman ɔɔva taasu ɔnini, “Lɛni na baabla teete ukyuli ɔni na ɔga ɔ́kɔliku katɔ!”

english_verse: Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Mordekai ɔ́sɔ únwini úsie nwuna kabla kablakɔ na ɔga kesii ɔban kenye mmɔ. Nsu Haman úkeli ɔ́tɔlɔ ku kɔƒa ku kɔƒa úsie kaduli.

english_verse: Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.”
translation_verse: Na útásɔku ala ani nálɛ mɛni ƒui ɔ́su ulekudi ku nwuna bakpana. Amu na nwuna bakpana ku ulekudi básu-nwu banini, “Si anii Yudani na Mordekai ɔdi bɔdi ni, na agyi anii adubo bɔnɔ geen! Na si étewi lɛlɔ adubɔyii udu muedi.”

english_verse: They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_verse: Na bétedie tɔ kenye na lɛla lɛni na baasu kemmo asa ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔtu úbeduo, na ɔ́lɔ Haman ɔnii ɔga ɔnii ubo na beteesie kadikɔ kani na beleku ɔga ɔ́lɔ-ma mmɔ.

english_verse: The king and Haman were dining with Esther
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ ku Haman bésie na bátádi ku Beleku Ɔga Ester.

english_verse: and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
translation_verse: Na ka basɔ badaku ntɛ bɔni kunyɔdi ni, ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ úye Uleku Ɔga Ester ɔnini, “Bi na aawia ka lɛbla lite-ɔ. Su-mi na ndubute-ɔ útédu mina lɛga kadikɔ kakɛ kenwi muedi ƒaa.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want,
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ulekudi beleku ɔga údie kenye ɔnini, “Mina ɔbune, si ɔ́yɔ-ɔ kaƒɔ ƒaa ka abla lɛla lɛni na muuvele-ɔ ku lɛlɔ kalɔ buboku ete-mi ni, na anu-mi kɔnyana kalɛ na baládu-mi ku mina kadi bekyuli lɛnɔ.

english_verse: because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
translation_verse: Ɔsika béti ami ku mina kadi bekyuli ƒui béye kalɛ na badu-bu na bayila-bu udu ƒui kede kede. Na si nka buye na banii beeti-bu beye na bunwini kabla bablane kani ni, nka lɛɛɛdubo nnii mbete-ɔ lɛƒɛda lɛdi, ɔsika ɔmmɔ lɛti uláya na mbada lɛlɛ awɔ mina ɔga anumi.”

english_verse: “Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
translation_verse: Kɔnakunwi ni, Ɔga Ahasweros úye Beleku Ɔga Ester ɔnini, “Ɔma nábla ɔtɔtɔ ɔmmɔ udu? Ntele ukyuli ɔmmɔ?”

english_verse: Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!” Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
translation_verse: Amu na Ester údie kenye ɔnini, “Ukisine ukpidi kati kati ɔmmɔ ndi Haman ɔni nli-ɔ kudɔ mɛni.” Mmɔ kani na liƒu bonwu líƒie Haman na Ɔga Ahasweros ku Beleku Ɔga Ester anumi mmɔ.

english_verse: The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden. Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
translation_verse: Mmɔ mmɔ ni, ɔga ɔ́ta nwuna keliekɔ ku kɔnyi na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie nwuna kevoma kemo kani nkya kaduli mmɔ. Nsu ka Haman ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka ɔga ɔ́ɔbla nwuna kasusu na lɛla lɛni na ɔdubo-nwu bɔbla lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, ɔ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ ulie kama ɔnii uukpi Uleku Ɔga Ester kɔtɔ kalɛ na ɔga uládu-nwu.

english_verse: Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!” As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head.
translation_verse: Na ɔni kani na Haman ɔɔyu ɔɔlɛ akɔnkɔ na liboku lɛni kemmo na beleku ɔga ɔmmɔ ukpo kudɔ kani na Ɔga Ahasweros ɔ́si úbeduo. Mmɔ kani na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́va ku lɛdi momoomo ɔnini, “Buƒie muedi na asɔ adubo mina uleku buƒie na mina anumi mɛni na ami ɔlati kaduli?” Ɔga ɔmmɔ útawɔlɔ tɔ kenye kammɔ bɔsu asa na nwuna beleku lɛlɔ banune báka bámana Haman, na béti ala bébi-nwu lili.

english_verse: At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani na ɔga ɔmmɔ údie lɛdi úte-ma ɔnini, “Bɛgyunku-nwu na bitákya-nwu ɔbuli limɔ bɛƒala mmɔ!” Anwuɔsu béti-nwu na bátaƒala-nwu na anwu ɔlati ugyii lɛlɔ. Na ɔga ɔmmɔ kɔnyi kɔ́yɔ-nwu na kaƒɔ lɛnɔ kába-nwu.

english_verse: Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛmmɔ kani ni, Ɔga Ahasweros úti Haman Yudaƒuɔ ukisine ɔmmɔ kaduli ku ala ani na nse-nwu ƒui úte ulekudi Beleku Ɔga Ester. Na ka Ester ɔ́su ɔga ɔmmɔ ka nwuna lɛlɔ ukyuli na Mordekai ɔdi ɔsu ni, ɔga ɔmmɔ úti-nwu ɔ́bla nwuna unengu na nwuna kaduli.

english_verse: and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
translation_verse: Na ɔga ɔmmɔ údie nwuna kakwɛnimi kani na ɔ́ƒɔ ɔ́siku Haman kudɔ úte Mordekai. Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Ester úti Mordekai únyene Haman ala ƒui kenye.

english_verse: Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!”
translation_verse: Ester ɔ́sɔ úsie Ɔga Ahasweros kudɔ na ɔmmɔ kama, na útayu úwi-nwu lɛgba kalɔ ku keku na úvele-nwu ɔnini, “Buvele geen na nda-a mɔɔyɔ́ ka abla lɛla lɛdi asiku Haman, Ɔga Agag kaba kemmo ubi, ɔmmɔ kasusu kekpidi kani na úboku na Yudaƒuɔ kadi bekyuli lɛlɔ mmɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: King Xerxes held out the golden scepter to Esther,
translation_verse: Amu ka ɔga ɔmmɔ únene nwuna sika ugyiedi ɔgagyii ɔ́tina Ester ni, ɔ́ta úbenye-nwu anumi.

english_verse: and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed,
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔga ɔbune, si ɔɔyɔ́-ɔ kaƒɔ na aayɔ́-mi geen na ánu lɛnɔ ka ɔdia ni, na ete kati kpakplaa na etile kenye kani na Hamedata ubidi Haman ɔni ndi Ɔga Agag kaba kemmo ubi ɔ́su ɔ́siku Yudaƒuɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ, kalɛ na basɔ baladi litemi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ na badu-ma na kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo.

english_verse: and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
translation_verse: Ɔsika lɛɛɛdubo bɔkana bulie bɔnu na ɔgbankpi bonwu ɔmɛni udu ubo mina kadi bekyuli lɛlɔ na bakyula-ma ƒui.”

english_verse: King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews.
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Ahasweros ɔ́su Beleku Ɔga Ester ku Mordekai ɔni nnye mmɔ ɔnini, “Kasusu kekpidi kani na Haman úti na Yudaƒuɔ lɛlɔ ɔsu na lɛ́ya na bákya-nwu ɔbuli limɔ na báƒala-nwu, na líti nwuna kaduli ku ala ƒui líte Beleku Ɔga Ester.

english_verse: I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu nweni lɛla lɛni na ánu ka lɛ́manku Yudaƒuɔ na etu ɔku ɔmmɔ kɔnu ku mina kakwɛnimi kani mɔɔtina ka ami ɔga nákya ɔku ɔmmɔ kɔnu. Na ukyuli biala ulakana lɛla lɛni na nkya ɔku ɔmmɔ kemmo bɔvumana.”

english_verse: They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
translation_verse: Mordekai ɔ́ya na bénweni lɛku lɛmmɔ na Ɔga Ahasweros lɛnyi kemmo, na bétu ɔku ɔmmɔ ku nwuna kakwɛnimi. Na batu bani ngyi kalɛ na beelie bapɔnkɔ bani na bátumini béte ɔga, na beekeli usi momoomo geen na ɔ́ya na béti lɛku lɛmmɔ bésienku kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth. After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Mordekai ɔ́da lɛlɔ na ɔ́vi ɔ́lɛ ɔ́si ɔga kesii mmɔ. Na ɔda agala ani ndi lɛwu lɛƒualadi ku ligyiedi, na ubi sika ugyiedi kagabwa lili na ɔkya awu ɔbunidi ɔni náƒɔ kuye geen. Na kudu kúwi na Susa ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo.

english_verse: and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
translation_verse: Na kenye kani na Yudaƒuɔ bénu mmɔ únwini-ma lɛlɔyɔ ku ebiti geen aani si lɛlɔ na báadi muedi.

english_verse: In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_verse: Na geen geen na kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ lɛma linengudi ƒui kemmo ni, Yudaƒuɔ badi limeyi ku ebiti geen na kadi bamba bekyuli badi muedi béti lɛlɔ bénwini Yudaƒuɔ, ɔsika baayia-ma geen.

english_verse: The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around,
translation_verse: Kɔbuli kɔtɛdi limeyi leevu-lɛtɛdi lɛni lɛlɔ na ɔlɛka ala amɛni alɛ lídu. Na nka Yudaƒuɔ bekisine bákali ka nka bekpo na badi Yudaƒuɔ bamɛni lɛlɔ na bakya-ma kalɔ. Nsu ala ammɔ ƒui ébo énwini na Yudaƒuɔ mmomu nádi bana bekisine lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
translation_verse: Na kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ lɛma linengudi kemmo ƒui na Ɔga Ahasweros lɛga kadikɔ ni, Yudaƒuɔ bammɔ básala lɛlɔ na báklibi lɛlɔ benye bete bana ukisine biala na mata mebo ɔnii ubékpo-ma, nsu ɔdi útakana-ma bɔni bude na bana lɛlɔ liƒu bonwu lɛni náda bekyuli ɔsu.

english_verse: The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews.
translation_verse: Na geen ni, kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ bakutine ku benengu ku bagadine ku batɔnkune ku aban kenye benyene ƒui ni, bénwini benye Mordekai kama, ɔsika baayia-nwu geen.

english_verse: Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
translation_verse: Mordekai únwini ukyuli unengudi geen na úbaƒɔ lɛnyi na kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo ɔni na bɔkɔ kani na nwuna ɔyikun ɔɔkɔ́ katɔ uwi biala.

english_verse: The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yudaƒuɔ békpo bana bekisine na bádu-ma geen na báblaku bana bekisine kalɛ na baayɔ́.

english_verse: Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani ƒui na bádu na Susa ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo ƒui ni, bésie bátásu ɔga ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́su Beleku Ɔga Ester ɔnini, “Na Susa ɔma unengudi kemmo ni, Yudaƒuɔ bammɔ bádu nkyuli eti leevu, na bádu Haman bebi bammɔ lɛnɔ ƒui. Na kalɛ na bábla na kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ lɛma linengudi lɛkladi kemmo na lɛɛɛgyi. Bi lɛnɔ na asɔ aawia iye evele-mi na lɛbla lite-ɔ?”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Ester údie kenye ɔnini, “Si ɔdi-ɔ lɛƒɔyɔ ni, na ete kuƒi na Yudaƒuɔ bani na bakya Susa bekpo kɔnaadi lɛnɔ aani kalɛ na békpo ɔmwi na aya na bakya Haman bebi leevu bammɔ ɔbuli limɔ baƒala akpa ku ɔta bonwu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔga ɔmmɔ údie lɛdi ɔnii babla lɛni na ɔ́ya na bébo ɔda na Susa ɔma kemmo, na báƒala Haman bebi leevu bammɔ.

english_verse: Then on the fourteenth day of Adar the Jews of the city got together and killed
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Yudaƒuɔ bani na Susa básɔ bása kɔbuli kɔtɛdi limeyi leevu-linedi lɛlɔ na bádu nkyuli eti aku na Susa mmɔ, nsu béteti lɛla bamba biala betenwini bana lɛdi.

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed
translation_verse: Kɔbuli kɔtɛdi limeyi leevu-lɛtɛdi lɛlɔ na ala amɛni álɛ. Na limeyi leevu-linedi lɛlɔ ni, bánwuna na bádi limeyi na ɔbla lɛlɔyɔ limeyi geen úte-ma.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth.
translation_verse: Nsu Yudaƒuɔ bani na bakya Susa ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo ama ni, békpo limeyi leevu-lɛtɛdi ku leevu-linedi na limeyi leevu-lɛlɔndi lɛlɔ, mmomu na bánwuna na bádi limeyi.

english_verse: This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other. The Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni náya na Yudaƒuɔ lɛma libliidi kemmo ni, kɔbuli kɔtɛdi limeyi leevu-linedi na ama baadi limeyi lɛmmɔ aani lɛlɔyɔ limeyi na beete bekyuli ala.

english_verse: Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces
