translation_verse: Na Mordekai únweni ala amɛni ƒui úse na úte Yudaƒuɔ bani na bakya Ɔga Ahasweros kalɛkɛ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ bɔti na ɔlɔgyu ku ekpo ani na ede ƒui ɔnii

english_verse: and told them: Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,
translation_verse: bataadi kɔbuli kɔtɛdi limeyi leevu-linedi ku leevu-lɛlɔndi aani bɔnwuna limeyi lɛkwa biala

english_verse: the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
translation_verse: ku limeyi lɛni na Yudaƒuɔ békpo bana bekisine, na bákɛ bɔnwuna básiku-ma enu kemmo. Úte-ma bɔti ka badi limeyi lɛmmɔ ku ebiti na bete bana banwani etela ku adila, na batayiƒala bawabane.

english_verse: They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration. The Reason for the Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bádi Mordekai litemi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ na emeyi amɛni énwini limeyi bɔdi emeyi éte Yudaƒuɔ ƒui lɛkwa ndi lɛkwa.

english_verse: Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ na Hamedata ubidi Haman ɔni ndi Ɔga Agag kaba kemmo ukyuli ɔni muukisi Yudaƒuɔ mmɔ únyimi ɔda bubo bɔdi ka badu Yudaƒuɔ ƒui. Na ɔ́tu egulabi adi na ɔ́nu ɔ́ti uwi ɔni na ɔlɛka badu Yudaƒuɔ bammɔ.

english_verse: Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged.
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔni na Yudaƒuɔ lɛlɔ kelisa kekpidi kamɛni litemi líbeduo Ɔga Ahasweros kɔtu kemmo ɔkɛnku Beleku Ɔga Ester lɛlɔ ni, ɔ́ya na bénweni ɔku bamba bébile Haman lɛla lɛni na únyimi kemmo, na likpidi lɛmmɔ línwini líbo Haman ku nwuna bebi lɛlɔ mmomu ɔni na bákya-ma ɔbuli limɔ anwu ku nwuna bebi na báƒala-ma.

english_verse: Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na baalɔ emeyi amɛni bɔdi banii Egulabi Bɔtu Emeyi ɔ́si ɔku ɔni na Mordekai úbenweni ku ala ani nébo ábalɛ na ɔmmɔ kama ɔsu.

english_verse: Now every year the Jews set aside these two days for having parties and celebrating, just as they were told to do.
translation_verse: Na Yudaƒuɔ ƒui bálɛ-nwu ugyii ka ama Yudaƒuɔ ku bana kaba kemmo bebi ku bekyuli bani néti lɛlɔ bénwini Yudaƒuɔ bataadi emeyi amɛni na uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na Mordekai úbo-ma ɔda.

english_verse: Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast.
translation_verse: Na Abihail ubidi ɔni ndi Beleku Ɔga Ester ku Mordekai ɔmɛni básala bénweni ɔku bamba básia ɔni na Mordekai ɔ́ka bunweni ɔ́siku emeyi amɛni bɔdi lɛlɔ, béti baatina ka Ester na nwuna kenyekɔ kenye ɔ́sia litemi lɛmmɔ kɔnu.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
translation_verse: Na bátina kalɛ na ɔlɛka bataadi emeyi amɛni kalɛ kani na ama ku bana kaba kemmo bebi baadi emeyi bamba ku kenye bunyimi ku kɔnyana buwulo emeyi. Na ɔmɛni ɔdi lɛla lɛni na Ester ku Mordekai bébo Yudaƒuɔ ƒui ɔda.

english_verse: These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_verse: Na bénweni Ester lɛla lɛni na únyimi mɛni bákya ɔku kemmo bése.

english_verse: King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea.
translation_verse: Ɔga Ahasweros únyimi úte nwuna lɛga kadikɔ bekyuli bɔmmɔ ƒui ku bani na ɛpu ɔvi na baaƒɔ nwuna kalɔ kemmo bɔkya kayu kadi teete-nwu.

english_verse: All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai.
translation_verse: Na ala ebendi ani ƒui na Ɔga Ahasweros ɔ́bla ni, bénweni-nya bákya Media ku Persia bagadine lɛku kemmo bése. Na ala ani na bénweni bése mɛni lɛnɔ adi ɔbu ɔni na Ahasweros úte Mordekai ku kalɛ na ɔ́kɔliku-nwu katɔ.

english_verse: Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_verse: Na ɔga ɔmmɔ kama ni, Mordekai kenyekɔ ndi kenengudi ƒui kani na kasɔ kasia na nwuna lɛga kadikɔ mmɔ. Na Mordekai ɔmɛni ɔdi Yudaƒuɔ ɔtɔnkune ɔni na ɔ́ƒɔ lɛnyi geen, ɔsika ɔ́da-ma geen na ɔɔtɛmi teete ɔga muedi na bana kenye si lɛla lɛdi líbo.

english_verse: Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
translation_verse: Ɔnana ɔdi ɔ́kya Us kalɔ lɛlɔ na baalɔ-nwu Hiob. Útaayia Katɔti geen, anwuɔsu ɔ́da lɛlɔ siin ɔni na lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-nwu na Katɔti anumi, ɔsika ɔɔdi nwuna etemila ƒui lɛlɔ kaduɛ.

english_verse: the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti úye Satan ɔnini, “Wɛ na ási na ébo aalɛ́ mɛni?” Mmɔ na Satan údie kenye ɔnini, “Bɔkɛ kani na nkɛ mɔɔví kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Nwuna bebi bammɔ béteesie lɛlɔ kudɔ taatádi emeyi na bana kɔduli. Na baalɔ bana banwani belekubi lɛnɔ na baasiaku-ma teesie emeyi amɛni udu kadikɔ taatáni na badi.

english_verse: After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God. Angels, the Lord, and Satan
translation_verse: Uwi biala na bádi limeyi báwɔlɔ lɛni ni, Hiob ɔɔta ɔtanta tutuutu na ɔɔsia kama taalɔ-ma taasala, na babla lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi na ɔdi biala lili, ku kasusu ka ɔdi ɔdubɔƒiɔ Katɔti ɔsu. Na ɔmɛni únwini lɛla lɛni na ɔɔbla bɔbla bɔbla. Kayaa Bayikune Lidu Ku Satan Bébo Katɔti Anumi

english_verse: One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Limeyi linwi ni, kayaa bayikune lidu ƒui bébo Katɔti anumi, na Satan lɛnɔ ɔkya-ma akɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́sɔ úye-nwu ɔnini, “Na dɛ, ka ésie ni, ánu mina kabla ɔblane Hiob? Ukyuli biala uuubo nwuna kalɛ na kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Ɔdi ukyuli ɔni na ɔɔyia-mi na ɔɔbu-mi lɛnɔ geen, anwuɔsu use siin, ɔsika ulayɔ ɔnii ɔɔbla lɛla lɛdi ɔƒiɔ-mi.”

english_verse: “You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere.
translation_verse: Ɔɔɔdi awɔ nágyi ɔba ákya-nwu, na aagyumana nwuna bebi ku ala ani ƒui na ubo? Na ɔɔɔdi awɔ náya na kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiaku-nwu, na ala ani ƒui na ɔɔbla aatɛ teete-nwu, na bumomo kani na nwuna bebuo beemomo na báaƒɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui munuu?

english_verse: Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Na si aawia-mi ɔkɔ ni, na ayila ala ani ƒui na ubo udu, na anu si ulata ulenye-ɔ anumi na utaakywɛ-ɔ animi teewida-a uwi biala.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.” Then Satan left. Job Loses Everything
translation_verse: Mmɔ mmɔ ni, Katɔti ɔ́su Satan ɔnini, “Ɔdia, amu líte-ɔ kuƒi na nwuna ala ƒui lɛlɔ, mmomu ƒula lɛnimi litetuku-nwu ɔlɔna lɛlɔ kesii biala anii aabla-nwu lɛla lɛdi.” Amu na Satan ɔ́gyu Katɔti anumi mmɔ ɔ́tɔlɔ. Satan Úbile Hiob Akɛla Ku Bebi, Na Ɔ́yila-ma Udu

english_verse: Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son,
translation_verse: Limeyi linwi ni, Hiob bebi bananabi bammɔ ku bana banwani belekubi básɔ badaku limeyi lɛdi bɔdi na bana ɔnwani unengudi kesii.

english_verse: when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ɔtalane ɔdi úbo Hiob kudɔ na úbasu-nwu ɔnini, “Bɔ́bala ƒula ɔmantɛ bakɔ bana kɔgba na benye beegúlu kalɔ, na bebuo ala betine bammɔ benye baadi bana kudɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Nsu búdu bɔti ni, Sabaƒuɔ badi bábwɛ bálɛ na békpoku-bu, na bádu ƒula kabla bablane ƒui, na bála bebuo bammɔ ƒui békeliku bátɔlɔku. Na ami kani nébu na líbo nnii mbasu-ɔ!”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Kabla ɔblane ɔmɛni útawɔlɔ tɔ kenye kamɛni bɔsu asa na ɔbamba ɔ́da úbalɛ ɔnini, “Katɔti ɔ́ya na katɔ kábwɛ ogya na úbewi ƒula baƒonu ku bana badane lɛlɔ na bákywi ƒui na ami kani nébu na líbo nnii mbasu-ɔ!”

english_verse: Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Lɛni kani na kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ útawɔlɔ tɔ asa na ɔbambadi ɔdi ɔ́da úbalɛ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Kaldeaƒuɔ bekpone kasala akpa atɛ badi bébo na bébeyu-bu bátu, na békpoku-bu na bádu ƒula kabla bablane ƒui. Na bétiku ƒula bebuo ala betine ku keƒu bammɔ bátɔlɔku na ami kani nébu na líbo mbasu-ɔ.”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son,
translation_verse: Kenye kamɛni bɔsu kemmo ni, kabla ɔblane unedi ɔ́da úbalɛ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ka ƒula bebi badaku bana limeyi bɔdi na bana ɔnwani unengudi kesii ni,

english_verse: when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa ɔdi úbekpo kɔnakunwi ɔ́si kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ kakɛ, na ɔ́tuaku kaduli kammɔ lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ ƒui. Na ɔ́ƒɛ ɔmmɔ úbi-ma lɛlɔ na bana ƒui békpi. Na ami kani nákana ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ kemmo bɔlɛ na líbo mbasu-ɔ.”

english_verse: When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God
translation_verse: Hiob ɔ́ta únye kɔnakunwi ka únu kenye kamɛni. Na ɔ́ni nwuna awu ɔ́bwɛ na úkpeyi lili, na ɔ́yu úbi kalɔ úmwi Unwoti.

english_verse: and said: “We bring nothing at birth; we take nothing with us at death. The Lord alone gives and takes. Praise the name of the Lord!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Kasɔngya na mina uni ɔ́wɔ-mi ɔ́lɛku nwuna kaƒɔ kemmo, na kasɔngya kani na ndubɔsɔ linwini. Unwoti néte, na Unwoti násɔ ɔ́ƒɔ. Bemwi Unwoti lɛnyi!”

english_verse: In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_verse: Na ɔmɛni ƒui kemmo ni, Hiob útasu lɛla lɛdi na ɔta unye Unwoti lɛlɔ iye ɔdu Unwoti kɔtɔ kɔdi.

english_verse: When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi lɛ́sɔ lídu na kayaa bayikune lidu bammɔ básɔ bébo Unwoti kudɔ na Satan lɛnɔ ɔkya-ma akɔ.

english_verse: and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti úye-nwu ɔnini, Wɛ na ási ébo aalɛ́ mɛni? Mmɔ na Satan údie kenye ɔnini, “Bɔkɛ kani na nkɛ mɔɔví kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́sɔ úye-nwu ɔnini, “Na dɛ, ka ésie ni, ánu mina kabla ɔblane Hiob? Ukyuli biala uuubo nwuna kalɛ na kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Ɔdi ukyuli ɔni na ɔɔyia-mi na ɔɔbu-mi lɛnɔ geen, anwuɔsu use siin, ɔsika ulayɔ ɔnii ɔɔbla lɛla lɛdi ɔƒiɔ-mi. Na ina ka útabla lɛla lɛdi asa na énye-mi lɛlɔ anii nte-ɔ kuƒi na ekpoku-nwu muedi ni, ɔmu unye nwuna kenyekɔ na ɔɔdi mina litemi lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Nsu si banii énene kɔnu ɔƒaani na ákya-nwu ɔlɔna ɔlɛ ɔdi ni, adubɔnu ka ɔdubo-ɔ animi butaakywɛɛ na uteewida-a anumi ku anumi.”

english_verse: “All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su Satan ɔnini, “Ɔdia lɛ́nyonu-nwu lɛ́kya-a lɛkɔkɔ akana na ekpoku-nwu ɔlɔna ku ɔlɛ biala kalɛ na aayɔ́, mmomu tadu-nwu.”

english_verse: Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Satan ɔ́gyu lɛgba na ɔ́tɔlɔ Unwoti kudɔ mmɔ na útáya na ɔlɛ kpakplaa úbo Hiob ɔni na nwuna lɛlɔ ƒui línwini alɛbi sɔɔn ɔ́si lɛgba kalɔ útédu lili.

english_verse: Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu kebu na Hiob úsie ulie ku kɔnyana. Na ɔda kubuikɛ kɔdi uukuo nwuna alɛbi na ntɔ akɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
translation_verse: Amu ka ulekudi ɔ́da úbalɛ ni, úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi? Bɔsiaku na amu asiaku Unwoti kama? Wida-nwu na ekpi!”

english_verse: Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God. Job's Three Friends
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Hiob údie kenye ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na aatɛmi aani uleku ɔdɔlɔdi? Uwi ɔni na Unwoti úte-bu ala abuni ni, bɔ́ƒɔ-nya. Na si ɔƒaani anwu úte-bu lɛbibo ni, útalɛka bɔƒɔ ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ?” Na ɔmɛni kemmo ƒui ni, Hiob útasu lɛla lɛdi na ɔƒiɔ Unwoti. Hiob Bakpana Ɛtɛ Bébo-nwu Kudɔ

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmɛni kemmo ni, Hiob bakpana ɛtɛ badi bénu ka Hiob uuƒi. Na bése limeyi ka babasa na Hiob kudɔ na bewuloku-nwu kɔnyana na basia-nwu kɔnu. Ama ndi Eliƒas ɔni nási Teman ku Bildad ɔni nási Suhi ku Soƒar ɔni nási Naama.

english_verse: When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Ka bakɛ ɔgyu bésela na bánu-nwu bémene ni, béteyile-nwu bɔnu bɔti banii anwu na ɔdi mmɔ. Na litemi lɛmmɔ lɛ́bla-ma kɔnyana, anwuɔsu báni bana lɛwu bábwɛ na báma ɔtumu béwi eli na beewulo momoomo na anwu ɔsu.

english_verse: For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_verse: Ɔni na bédu-nwu kudɔ ni, báyu béwi kalɔ mmɔ na bélie-nwu kudɔ emeyi maatɛ usien ku ɔƒɛ. Na ɔdi útasu-nwu lɛla lɛdi ka bánu kalɛ na uubó abi ɔsu.

english_verse: Finally, Job cursed the day of his birth
translation_verse: Kawɔlɔkɔ na emeyi ammɔ kama ni, Hiob ɔ́kpali Unwoti na úwida limeyi lɛni na báwɔ-nwu.

english_verse: by saying to God:
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su ɔnini,

english_verse: Blot out the day of my birth and the night when my parents created a son.
translation_verse: “Unwoti, nine limeyi lɛni na báwɔ-mi die emeyi ƒui kemmo, ku usien ɔni na básu ka mina bawɔne báwɔ ɔnanabi.

english_verse: Erase that night from the calendar and conceal it with darkness.
translation_verse: Liƒlukutu suu lɛƒɔ limeyi lɛmmɔ, na basɔ bataka-ni batakya lɛkwa emeyi kemmo, iye kɔbuli kɔdi emeyi akɔ.

english_verse: Don't let children be created or joyful shouts be heard ever again in that night.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛsɔ litanu ubi ɔdi, iye bete mmo na bebo lɛlɔyɔ kudu kɔdi lɛnɔ kudii.

english_verse: Let those with magic powers place a curse on that day.
translation_verse: Ya na bevone ƒui bakanti bakya limeyi lɛmmɔ ku ewida.

english_verse: Darken its morning stars and remove all hope of light,
translation_verse: Ayabi ani mɔɔtu limeyi lɛmmɔ ɔtanta ƒui abla suu, na lɛla lɛla litatina ka bukeye bɔdi bɔkya limeyi lɛmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Why was I accepted and allowed to nurse at my mother's breast?
translation_verse: Bi ɔsu na bágyu-mi básia lɛgba na ɔɔbla ku ɔni na bete-mi lɛnyii?

english_verse: Now I would be at peace in the silent world below
translation_verse: Kesii kani na lídu ɔƒɛni amu ni, ndubo bɔyu butéduo kubiɔ na lɛtɛ kpoo ntaanwuna.

english_verse: with kings and their advisors whose palaces lie in ruins,
translation_verse: Na ndubusie ntátɛ baga ku bana benengu bani nátu baga kɔkyakɔ bonwu bonwu na kɔ́bwɛ kudɔ,

english_verse: and with rulers once rich with silver and gold.
translation_verse: iye bagabi bani nákɛ sika ugyiedi na básala sika ɔƒualadi béyile bana lɛtɔ dii kudɔ.

english_verse: I wish I had been born dead and then buried, never to see the light of day.
translation_verse: Bi ɔsu na ńtekpi na ntu kemmo mmɔ uwi ɔni na báwɔ-mi, na nsɔ muumónku ngba bulie na lɛnu ɔƒɛ kadi bukeye?

english_verse: In the world of the dead, the wicked and the weary rest without a worry. *
translation_verse: Na kekpine mmɔ ni, balalane basɔ belekpoku bekyuli. Na bekyuli bani muususu lɛlɔ basɔ beletu lɛlɔ, na baakɛ́ bɔnwuna.

english_verse: where captives and slaves are free at last. Why Does God Let Me Live?
translation_verse: Mmɔ kadi ukyuli biala kesiekɔ na bekyuli babune bani kabla na baabla ku bani mɔɔbla-ma kabla ƒui baakɛ́ bɔnwuna.

english_verse: Why does God let me live when life is miserable and so bitter?
translation_verse: “Bi ɔsu na muulie ntaanu bukeye na mina lɛbibo kemmo, na use aani si ngba ala abuni eebo teete bani naaadaku ngba lɛda?

english_verse: I keep longing for death more than I would seek a valuable treasure.
translation_verse: Na nli mɔɔwia kukpi aani kalɛ na ukyuli ɔɔwia lɛkɛ taanɔ na kúbulo kɔnii kulebo na kubeeti-mi?

english_verse: Nothing could make me happier than to be in the grave.
translation_verse: Ɔsika lɛla biala lɛsɔ liiibo na lɛdubute-mi lɛlɔyɔ butulo kaƒiɔtɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Why do I go on living when God has me surrounded, and I can't see the road?
translation_verse: Mina ngba bɔsɔ bulie ɔƒɛni kalɔ ndi bi, ka Unwoti ɔ́ya na ala áka-mi ákya na nsɔ naaanu ulu nwaa ɔdi lɛlɔ naaasia?

english_verse: Moaning and groaning are my food and drink,
translation_verse: Edumo ku lɛnwuna bubo sɔɔn nénwini-mi adila ɔƒɛni amu.

english_verse: and my worst fears have all come true.
translation_verse: Na lɛla lɛni geen na mɔɔyia nálɛku-mi. Na lɛla lɛni mɔɔgyú-mi ɔtɔtɔ ni, ani nébo-mi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I have no peace or rest— only troubles and worries.
translation_verse: Liiibo atu bɔyɔ iye lɛlɔ buwi bɔdi. Na lɛbibo ku lɛƒɛda kani náƒɔ-mi keliela kemmo uwi ƒui.”

english_verse: Please be patient and listen to what I have to say. *
translation_verse: “Hiob, kɛ kayi na enu lɛla lɛni na ndubo-ɔ bɔsu, ɔsika kesii kani na éedu ni, ukyuli ɔdi uuubo na wakana bɔsɔ bulie kpoo.

english_verse: You respect God and live right, so don't lose hope!
translation_verse: Kalɛ na aayia Unwoti, na aabla ala ulu lɛlɔ siin ni, utalɛka aya na ɔmmɔ lɛti ute-ɔ lɛnunsia lɛdi?

english_verse: and then they are swept away by the angry breath of God.
translation_verse: Unwoti kɔnyi kuubo-ma lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa uukpó taayila lɛla lɛdi udu.

english_verse: They may roar and growl like powerful lions. But when God breaks their teeth,
translation_verse: Balalane baakwanyi na beebó adi aani bagyata, nsu Unwoti ɔɔƒɛ-ma anyi ƒui.

english_verse: they starve, and their children are scattered. A Secret Was Told to Me
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu beekpi ka basɔ beeebo lɛla lɛni na beƒie, anwuɔsu na bana bebi beegyingya.

english_verse: A secret was told to me in a faint whisper—
translation_verse: “Mina kɔtu kúnu lɛbɛla litemi lɛdi, na kabɛnsɛ butemi bɔdi kemmo.

english_verse: I was overcome by sleep, but disturbed by dreams;
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na nka lɛlɛɛ líiti-mi líselaku ɔgyu ƒui ni, kɔna kemmo liƒu ala bɔnu bɔmɛni bɔ́gyila-mi.

english_verse: and my hair stood on end, as a wind blew past my face.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́bla aani kɔyu kɔdi návi-mi anumi, ɔni na mina lɛlɔ linwini ƒui lɛ́ta línye-mi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: It stopped and stood still. Then a form appeared— a shapeless form. And from the silence, I heard a voice say,
translation_verse: Lɛla lɛmmɔ lísie lítédi línye-mi anumi geen, nsu naaanu lɛla lɛni na lɛdi taati. Ɔ́bla blii kani na línu butemi bɔdi lɛ́siku kesii kani na nka kese diin mmɔ ɔnini,

english_verse: He finds fault with his servants and even with his angels.
translation_verse: Unwoti ulánu nwuna batu bani na bakya-nwu kudɔ na katɔ mmɔ muedi ka bese sɛɛn. Mmomu uudie-ma bɔƒiɔ.

english_verse: Humans are formed from clay and are fragile as moths, so what chance do you have?
translation_verse: Na dɛ na ɔdubo buse bute ukyuli ɔni na lɛti na béti bávɔ-nwu na ɔtumu kani na ɔdi? Bakana na banya-nwu babwɛ aani agyangbaala!

english_verse: Born after daybreak, you die before nightfall and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si usien utátaalɛ kadi bugye ni, baanya-ma taabwɛ. Na baaadaku-ma lɛda na báyii udu ƒui.

english_verse: Your tent pegs are pulled up, and you leave this life, having gained no wisdom.”
translation_verse: Buse aani kevo kani na bálɛ na básɔ báda-ka bágyu ku kana akpa bédie kana kenyekɔ. Nsu bɔɔɔdubo Unwoti kasusu kalɔ bunu.’ ”

english_verse: Job, call out for help and see if an angel comes!
translation_verse: “Si aayɔ́ na akpali emene ɔƒaani na anu si ukyuli ɔdi ɔdubɔƒɔ ute-ɔ. Kayaa ɔyikune ɔmani na adubɔkpali ɔƒaani?

english_verse: Envy and jealousy will kill a stupid fool.
translation_verse: Lɛnungyie ku kogyulo kɔnyi buti bɔɔdú ukyuli.

english_verse: I have seen fools take root. But God sends a curse, suddenly uprooting them
translation_verse: Lɛ́ɛnu dii kalɛ na badɔlɔdi beedie lidu, nsu si Unwoti úti kɔnyi ni, ɔɔgyú-ma teedie bana kenyekɔ kɔnakunwi.

english_verse: and leaving their children helpless in court.
translation_verse: Na nwuna bebi basɔ balákɛ ukyuli ɔni medie-ma kenye na litemi katɛkɔ.

english_verse: Our suffering isn't caused by the failure of crops;
translation_verse: Ɔgbankpi ulakwɛ taasi kalɔ kemmo aani livo. Na lɛbibo lɛnɔ liláta taalɛ ɔtumu akɔ aani ligyiitu.

english_verse: it's all part of life, like sparks shooting skyward.
translation_verse: Mmomu sɔsɔ na ɔdi ka bɔwɔ na báwɔ ukyuli ku lɛbibo aani kalɛ na ogya etenku adanku agyakpabi.

english_verse: Job, if I were you, I would ask God for help.
translation_verse: “Na si ami ndi awɔ ni, nka ndubunwini anumi lɛsia Unwoti lɛlɔ mmomu. Na lɛda mina litemi lɛva-nwu anumi.

english_verse: His miracles are marvelous, more than we can count.
translation_verse: Ɔsika ɔɔbla akɔla ala budie taatina ani kalɔ na bulakana bunu iye bɔti-nya bɔka muedi.

english_verse: God sends showers on earth and waters the fields.
translation_verse: Ɔɔyá na ɔnantu ɔɔna na edula mmo bɔɔƒɔ́ ntu.

english_verse: He protects the sorrowful and lifts up those who have been disgraced. *
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔɔtalaku bekyuli bani néboku lɛlɔ kalɔ katɔ na ɔɔyá lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ bekyuli bani muuwulo kɔnyana.

english_verse: in their own evil schemes, and their wisdom fails.
translation_verse: Bana kayawi lɛnunda ƒui lɛɛwɔ́ ulu. Na bana ablala eenwíni kɔkpagyuɛ na kuudie-ma.

english_verse: God rescues the needy from the words of the wicked and the fist of the mighty.
translation_verse: Unwoti uudie bani mɔɔyaki ala na belikplune kuwii kenye na ɔɔƒɔ́-ma taasiku belikplune bayikune bammɔ enu kemmo.

english_verse: The poor are filled with hope, and injustice is silenced. Consider Yourself Fortunate
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bawabane baakɛ́ lɛnunsia. Na etemila ani na balatɛ teete-ma ulu lɛlɔ siin kenye keekúlo.

english_verse: Consider yourself fortunate if God All-Powerful chooses to correct you.
translation_verse: “Lɛlɔ lɛdubɔyɔ ukyuli ɔni na Unwoti ɔɔní kɔtu na uleni nwuna bɔdɔnku, ka úti-nwu ɔɔsiaku ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: He may cause injury and pain, but he will bandage and heal your cuts and bruises.
translation_verse: Ɔsika si ina ɔ́ya na ɔ́ƒɔ ɔlɛ ni, anwu kani ndubo-nwu bɔmana.

english_verse: God will protect you from harm, no matter how often trouble may strike.
translation_verse: “Ɔdubudie-ɔ na ɔgbankpi biala kemmo ina dɛ na lɛɛlɛ́ku-ɔ taasia kama.

english_verse: In times of war and famine, God will keep you safe.
translation_verse: Na si kɔka nébo o-o, iye kekpo kadi o-o ni, Unwoti ɔdubudie-ɔ na ɔna ƒui kemmo.

english_verse: You will be sheltered, without fear of hurtful words or any other weapon.
translation_verse: Na ɔdubudie-ɔ na ɔkɔ banyine linyemi lɛni na bada beebó bekyuli, na baakya-ma ɔlɛ kudɔ ɔni na asɔ alayia ɔgbankpi ɔdi si úbo.

english_verse: You will laugh at the threat of destruction and famine. And you won't be afraid of wild animals—
translation_verse: Adubunye na ama si uwi ɔni na kɔka iye kekpo kébo. Na asɔ alayia beƒiebuo badi.

english_verse: they will no longer be fierce, and your rocky fields will become friendly.
translation_verse: Ɔɔɔdi atakpɛ akɔ na asɔ adubo bɔtuma. Na beƒiebuo lɛnɔ basɔ belékpoku-ɔ.

english_verse: You will have more descendants than there are blades of grass on the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Ƒula bebi ku bawɔ badubumomo geen betulo livo lɛni muuwi kalɔ.

english_verse: You will live a very long life, and your body will be strong until the day you die.
translation_verse: Adubulie abi lɛlɔ geen ku ɔyikun aani kalɛ edula eenye kemo taabi teegyie asa na baƒɛ-nya.

english_verse: Our experience has proven these things to be true, so listen and learn.
translation_verse: “Hiob, bɔ́ɔnu ala amɛni ƒui bɔ́ti, na bɔgyi ka litemi geen na lɛdi. Anwuɔsu nu lɛla lɛni mɔɔsu-ɔ, na eti ete lɛlɔ kasusu.”

english_verse: It's impossible to weigh my misery and grief!
translation_verse: “Uuuse kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ka akɔku mina lɛbibo ku ɔlɛ ɔni na muunú anu.

english_verse: They outweigh the sand along the beach, and that's why I have spoken without thinking first.
translation_verse: Ɔsika ubo unu utulo ɛpu kɔnwinimi. Na ɔmmɔ geen náya na mɔɔtɛmi aani si kasusu na ńteti.

english_verse: The fearsome arrows of God All-Powerful have filled my soul with their poison.
translation_verse: Unwoti úbo nwuna atula ɔ́lɛ-mi, na ugyulo ɔmmɔ ɔkɛ ɔ́vi-mi lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui. Na nwuna liƒu akɔla budie taatina bonwu enye-mi anumi aani bekpone.

english_verse: Do oxen and wild donkeys cry out in distress unless they are hungry?
translation_verse: Ebuo ala utine ulénye taava ukpludi si ɔ́kɛ livo ɔɔkun, iye ɔmantɛ akɔ si unye ɔɔkun livo.

english_verse: What is food without salt? What is more tasteless than the white of an egg?
translation_verse: Ukyuli ulati adila ekpludi emini si mma buuubo. Lɛni kani na lɛvala lɛna lɛƒualadi liláyu emini.

english_verse: That's how my food tastes, and my appetite is gone. *
translation_verse: Lɛni na mina adila ƒui ani mɔɔdi ese-mi. Na liiibo ɔkwɛ emini liiite adila biala.

english_verse: Then I would be comforted, knowing that in all of my pain I have never disobeyed God.
translation_verse: Na si bɔbla na ɔbla ɔmɛni ute-mi ni, nka ndubɔƒulu ku ebiti ina ka muunú ɔlɛ na mina lɛlɔ kemmo. Ɔsika ngyi ka Unwoti use kedee, na ńtata ńtenye nwuna litemi lɛdi lɛlɔ kudii.

english_verse: I am not strong as stone or bronze,
translation_verse: Lɛtabi na mina ɔlɔna ɔdi? Munuu lɛbualagyie?

english_verse: and I have finally reached the end of my rope. My Friends, I Am Desperate
translation_verse: Bubo na mbo ɔyikun ɔdi na ndubɔkana lɛlɔ bubunku ka lɛbuni biala líkeli-mi, na lɛla lɛla lɛsɔ lilátɛ-mi mɛni?

english_verse: My friends, I am desperate, and you should help me, even if I no longer respect God All-Powerful. *
translation_verse: “Na lɛbibo lɛmɛni udu kemmo ni, amii mina bakpana na ɔlɛka bibunku-mi, ina úbo úte ka nnye Unwoti anumi mɔɔtɛmi ku kayi.

english_verse: like streams that swell with melting snow,
translation_verse: Bise aani utukwalɛ ɔni mɔɔƒɔ́ ntu taagba ku kudu.

english_verse: then suddenly disappear in the summer heat.
translation_verse: Nsu si kaƒɛndi kédu ni, ntu bɔmmɔ bɔɔkwii ƒui kɔnakunwi.

english_verse: I am like a caravan, lost in the desert while searching for water.
translation_verse: Na kaatɔ́lɔ beyedine bani nkɛ ku bana kɛɛkɛ ku etila, na baada ulu taava taatáwia ntu taayi udu.

english_verse: just as I am with you. Only one look at my suffering, and you run away scared. What Have I Done Wrong?
translation_verse: Lɛni geen na bise bite-mi aani utukwalɛ ɔni nákwii mɛni, na ɔ́tɔlɔ beyedine bammɔ útákya kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ kemmo na báyii udu.

english_verse: Have I ever asked any of you to give me a gift
translation_verse: Buvele na lívele bina ɔdi lɛla lɛdi nnii bite-mi bɛsiku bina lɛlakɛ kemmo, iye bite ɔdi lɛla lɛdi na ami ɔsu?

english_verse: or to purchase my freedom from brutal enemies?
translation_verse: Munuu bɔsu na lɛ́su-mii nnii, bikpo bɛƒɔ-mi na mina ukisine ɔdi lɛkɔkɔ?

english_verse: What have I done wrong? Show me, and I will keep quiet.
translation_verse: “Ɔdia, ndububile kenye kpoo na bɛtina-mi lɛla lɛdi, na bidie mina bɔƒiɔ bɛtina-mi.

english_verse: Here I am desperate, and you consider my words as worthless as wind.
translation_verse: Bɔkali na bɛɛkali ka bɛklibi-mi na mina bɔtɛmi kemmo ka lɛ́yila lɛnunsia na enu áƒɛ-mi ɔsu, na bɛɛnu bɛnii etemila keeke na mɔɔtɛmi?

english_verse: Why, you would sell an orphan or your own neighbor!
translation_verse: Mɔɔnu ka bɛdubɔkana na bɛtu egulabi na ukpinebi lili, na bɛsɔ bɛdi-nwu kuye, ina ka ɔdi bina ɔkpana ubidi!

english_verse: Look me straight in the eye; I won't lie to you.
translation_verse: “Na ɔƒaani ni, binwini bitaanu-mi ligeen, ɔsika lɛɛɛdubo ɔkɔ bɔnyi bɔtɔlɔ-mii.

english_verse: Stop accusing me falsely; my reputation is at stake.
translation_verse: Bɛda-mi kalala kɔtɔ bɔdu bɛya, ɔsika mina kenyekɔ ku lɛnyi lɛni na lɛ́ƒɔ ƒui mɔɔyii udu mɛni.

english_verse: I know right from wrong, and I am not telling lies.
translation_verse: Bɔnu na bɛɛnu bɛnii ɔkɔ na mɔɔnyi, iye lɛɛɛgyi lɛbuni ku likpidi kavumana?

english_verse: We are slaves in search of shade; we are laborers longing for our wages.
translation_verse: Na útavumanaku kabla ɔblane ɔni na unye ɔgya useyi uwi ɔyuli, iye ɔtumane ɔni na unye ɔgya nwuna lɛyuƒɔla.

english_verse: God has made my days drag on and my nights miserable.
translation_verse: Nsɔ lɛɛɛgyi lili ku lɛgba liiite mina emeyi, na usien lɛnɔ lɛbibo ku kɔnyana buwulo sɔɔn kani na bɔdi-mi.

english_verse: I pray for night to end, but it stretches out while I toss and turn.
translation_verse: Si líduo lɛ́tɛ ni, ndubukpoku lɛlɔ laa asa na kadi kegye, na usien ɔmmɔ úne-mi na kadi kelegye-mi pla.

english_verse: My parched skin is covered with worms, dirt, and sores,
translation_verse: Mina ɔlɔna úbie na beklubi báƒɔ-nwu ƒui, na únwini alɛbi alɛbi sɔɔn ku eƒula ani mɔɔlɛ́ ntu uwi biala.

english_verse: and my days are running out quicker than the thread of a fast-moving needle. Don't Forget!
translation_verse: “Na bɔsa kani mina ngba bɔda aani kalɛ na uleku ɔɔtu unwo ku kedetila.

english_verse: I beg you, God, don't forget! My life is just a breath, and trouble lies ahead.
translation_verse: O Unwoti, tayiƒala ka mina ngba buse aanii kalɛ na banwuna ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ukplodi. Na mina anumi asɔ aaadubo ebiti adi bɔnu kudii.

english_verse: I will vanish from sight, and no one, including you, will ever see me again.
translation_verse: Ndubo bɔyii bɔkya, na awɔ iye ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ ɔɔɔdubo-mi bɔnu lɛnɔ kudii.

english_verse: I will disappear in the grave or vanish from sight like a passing cloud.
translation_verse: Kalɛ na liƒlukutu lɛɛyii taakya ni, lɛni kani na ndubo kubiɔ buduo na nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo bunwini bubo.

english_verse: Never will I return home; soon I will be forgotten.
translation_verse: Nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo mina kaduli bunwini bubo, na uwi ɔsɔ uletu asa na bekyuli badubo-mi bɔyiƒala.

english_verse: And so, I cry out to you in agony and distress.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu na lɛɛɛdubo kenye bubile bɔsɔ bulie kpoo, mmomu ndubo-ɔ bɔkpali na lɛsu-ɔ ala ani muukpóku-mi.

english_verse: Am I the sea or a sea monster? Is that why you imprison me?
translation_verse: Unwoti, ɛpu ɔni na ásia ubili iye liƒu kebweyi kani na ébo lɛkpu ése na ndi ɔsu na ábala-mi ƒui lɛni yoo?

english_verse: but you torture me with terrible dreams. *
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔmmɔ na eedie liƒu ala taatina-mi na kɔna kemmo, na ulaya na mɔɔkana bɔlɛɛ.

english_verse: I'd rather choke to death than live in this body.
translation_verse: Na nka mɔɔwia ka mina ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔsa-mi kɔnakunwi na likpi, utulo si nli ngba muunú ɔlɛ ɔmɛni.

english_verse: What makes you so concerned about us humans?
translation_verse: “Bi ɔsu na bekyuli lɛlɔ lɛ́ƒɔ-ɔ kuye na aasia bana ablala anu lɛni?

english_verse: Why do you test us from sunrise to sunset?
translation_verse: Na bi ɔsu na enye aakɔ́ku-bu taanu ɔ́si ɔtanta útálɛ useyi lɛni?

english_verse: Won't you look away just long enough for me to swallow?
translation_verse: Bi ɔsu na ƒula anumi alɛ-mi lɛlɔ uwi biala, na anii elédie anumi na ina lisuo muedi na ɔdia-mi bubweli?

english_verse: Why do you watch us so closely? What's it to you, if I sin? Why am I your target and such a heavy burden?
translation_verse: Si bɔƒiɔ bɔdi na lɛ́ƒiɔ-ɔ ni, bi ndi bɔƒiɔ bɔmmɔ, na elédie alatina-mi ka aanu ukyuli ablala kemmo uwi ndi uwi. Bi ɔsu na édie ami lɛti ése na ƒula anumi alɛ-mi lɛlɔ lɛni aani si etila ebendi na línwini líte-ɔ?

english_verse: Why do you refuse to forgive? Soon you won't find me, because I'll be dead.
translation_verse: Na bi ɔsu na eléti mina alaekpidi alakyiɛ-mi na anu-mi kɔnyana? Úbu blii kani na badubo-mi lɛti bubi ɔni na adubɔwia-mi anɔ na asɔ alanu-mi.”

english_verse: How long will you talk and keep saying nothing?
translation_verse: “Áawɔlɔ ƒula ala ekpludi ani na enye aaká gyɔlɔɔ mmɔ?

english_verse: Does God All-Powerful stand in the way of justice?
translation_verse: Bɔbu na aabu anii Unwoti ɔɔnu litemi geen taatu-ni teenwini na uƒu lɛla lɛbuni lɛdi ɔkya?

english_verse: He made your children pay for their sins.
translation_verse: Alaekpidi ani na ƒula bebi bábla ni, nwuna kɔtu na ɔ́ni-ma.

english_verse: So why don't you turn to him
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bunwini na ɔlɛka enwini, na ekpi Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui kɔtɔ.

english_verse: and start living right? Then he will decide to rescue and restore you to your place of honor.
translation_verse: Na si adi ukyuli ɔni na nse siin sɔsɔ na lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-a ni, ɔƒɛni muedi Unwoti ɔdubɔta na ubebunku-ɔ na ɔya na asɔ enwini eténye ƒula kenyekɔ kani mbo ɔbu mmɔ.

english_verse: Your future will be brighter by far than your past. Our Ancestors Were Wise
translation_verse: Na akɛla ani ƒui na ákɛ ábavi ni, aaadubo-nya bɔbu, ɔsika Unwoti ɔdubute-ɔ ala ani ntulo ammɔ ƒui uwi ɔni mebo.

english_verse: Our ancestors were wise, so learn from them.
translation_verse: “Ye nu ɔ́si bula bati kuuku uwi ƒui na ati lɛla lɛni na bátɛya,

english_verse: Our own time has been short, like a fading shadow, and we know very little.
translation_verse: ɔsika abu bútetu tɔ uwi ɔdi, na kamaaku mɛni kani na báwɔ-bu na bɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛdi. Bula ngba emeyi ƒui ese aani ɔyuli ɔni mɔɔyii taakya.

english_verse: But they will instruct you with great understanding.
translation_verse: Na bula bati kuuku bammɔ ama bebo lɛlati na badubɔkana na batina-a lɛla.

english_verse: Papyrus reeds grow healthy only in a swamp,
translation_verse: Ketudɔ alakpi alakwɛ kesii kani naaadi lɛba taalɛ lili.

english_verse: and if the water dries up, they die sooner than grass.
translation_verse: Lɛni kani na si lɛba lɛ́kwii ni, alakpi ani muunye mmɔ aaka livo bamba bukpi taayii udu.

english_verse: Such is the hopeless future of all who turn from God
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani mɔɔyiƒala Unwoti Katɔti na beedie-nwu atu ni, lɛni na bana kawɔlɔkɔ kaabla ka báyila bana lɛnunsia ɔsu.

english_verse: and trust in something as frail as a spider's web—
translation_verse: Na lɛla bamba biala lɛlɔ na ukyuli úti anu ɔ́sia ni, nina ɔkplu útedu anasi kɔgbu na Unwoti anumi.

english_verse: they take hold and fall because it's so flimsy.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu si ukyuli ébo áda lɛla lɛmɛni udu lɛlɔ ni, bubuli kani na adubo bubuli.

english_verse: Sinful people are like plants with spreading roots and plenty of sun and water.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bamɛni udu bese aani kugyii kɔni nákɛ ntu ku ɔƒɛ. Kúdie evete na kúgyingya kɔ́ƒɔ kemo kammɔ kesi kesii.

english_verse: They wrap their roots tightly around rocks.
translation_verse: Na kuubó kuna ligyiitu taabala atakpɛ ani nkya mmɔ taamana.

english_verse: But once they are pulled up, they have no more place;
translation_verse: Nsu si bámami-ku na mmɔ ni, asɔ alanu mmɔ aláti anii kugyii kɔdi kúnye mmɔ dii muedi.

english_verse: their life slips away, and other plants grow there.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bekpidi ebiti ƒui kawɔlɔkɔ na kadi mmɔ, na bekyuli bamba mɔɔƒɔ́-ma kunyekɔ.

english_verse: We know God doesn't reject an innocent person or help a sinner.
translation_verse: “Nsu Unwoti ulédie bekyuli bani mɔɔdi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ siin atu kudii. Na lɛni kani na ɔɔɔdubo bekyuli bekpidi lɛnɔ kebunku kadi bute kudii.

english_verse: And so, he will make you happy and give you something to smile about.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Unwoti ɔdubɔya na asɔ ama ku ebiti, na ebo lɛlɔyɔ kudu momoomo ete-nwu.

english_verse: But your evil enemies will be put to shame and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Na ɔdubɔya na kɔƒa kukpo ƒula bekisine, na balalane kɔduli ƒui kɔyii udu, na basɔ balanu bana ɔdi.”

english_verse: What you say is true. No human is innocent in the sight of God.
translation_verse: “Sɔsɔ litemi na ásu ka ukyuli ɔyawine ɔdi ɔɔɔdubo bɔkana na use siin na Unwoti anumi kudii.

english_verse: Not once in a thousand times could we win our case if we took him to court.
translation_verse: Si ina litemi na banii batɛ ni, ukyuli ɔyawine ulakana Unwoti litemi linwi kenye budie na etemila apim kemmo.

english_verse: God is wise and powerful— who could possibly oppose him and win?
translation_verse: Nwuna lɛnunda kemmo kágyu, na nwuna ɔyikun uuubo bɔka. Ɔma náta únye Unwoti lɛlɔ dii na úse-nwu buɛɛ?

english_verse: When God becomes angry, he can move mountains before they even know it.
translation_verse: “Nwuna kɔnyi kulákada teese asa na ɔɔgyú abi enengudi ana kenyekɔ na ɔyila-nya udu.

english_verse: God can shake the earth loose from its foundations
translation_verse: Ɔɔkana na ɔkunku kalɔ kammɔ ƒui na kanyonu lɛlɔ útálɛ kana ɔka lɛlɔ muedi.

english_verse: or command the sun and stars to hold back their light.
translation_verse: Na ɔɔbɔku ɔƒɛ na uledie nwuna bukeye, na ɔɔbala ayabi bukeye kenye.

english_verse: God alone stretched out the sky, stepped on the sea,
translation_verse: Anwu lɛti nédie katɔ na úbimi-ka ɔ́ƒala kayaa, na ɔ́kɔliku nwuna ɔgba ɔ́nya ɛpu ɔni mɔɔnwanɛ lɛlɔ mmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and set the stars in place— the Big Dipper and Orion, the Pleiades and the stars in the southern sky.
translation_verse: Anwu nédie ayabi esu esu ani nkya kayaa, ɔgbini ku akpewe, akɔkɔ ku bebi, ku esu esu ani násala na kada kakɛ.

english_verse: Of all the miracles God works, we cannot understand a one.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔdi ɔɔɔdubo Unwoti ablala kalɔ bunu. Na ɔdi lɛnɔ ulakana nwuna akɔla budie taatina bɔka.

english_verse: God walks right past me, without making a sound.
translation_verse: Unwoti uusié taavi-mi kudɔ suɛlɛ suɛlɛ, na ɔɔtɔ-mi anumi nsu naaanu-nwu.

english_verse: And if he grabs something, who can stop him or raise a question?
translation_verse: Si úkpeli lɛla lɛdi ɔ́ƒɔ na ukyuli enu kemmo ni, ɔma ndubo bɔnwanɛku-nwu, iye uye-nwu ɔnii, ‘Bi na aabla?’

english_verse: When God showed his anger, the servants of the sea monster fell at his feet.
translation_verse: Si Unwoti údie nwuna kɔnyi keyi ni, ɔsɔ ulanu kama. Na Rahab ku nwuna batu muedi ƒui béboku bana eli kalɔ na báyu bátɛ-nwu lɛgba kalɔ.

english_verse: How, then, could I possibly argue my case with God? Though I Am Innocent
translation_verse: “Na dɛ na ndubɔkana na lɛkyaku Unwoti unyeƒi. Bi na ndubo bɔkana bɔsu?

english_verse: Even though I am innocent, I can only beg for mercy.
translation_verse: Ina ka ngyi ka ńtaƒiɔ ni, kɔtɔ kani na ɔlɛka likpi mina litemi ɔtɛne na ɔnu-mi kɔnyana.

english_verse: And if God came into court when I called him, he would not hear my case.
translation_verse: Ina lɛ́lɔ-nwu katɛ na úbo litemi katɛkɔ mmɔ ni, Unwoti ɔɔɔdubo-mi litemi bunu.

english_verse: He would strike me with a storm and increase my injuries for no reason at all.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa na ɔdubo bɔya na uteebo-mi taavinku. Na ɔya na lɛsɔ lɛƒɔ lɛlɛ lidu lɛsia lɛlɔ ƒui, ina ka ńtaƒiɔ-nwu.

english_verse: Before I could get my breath, my miseries would multiply.
translation_verse: Ɔɔɔdubo-mi bɔnwuna bɔdi bute, mmomu lɛbibo lɛdubɔƒɔ-mi ngba ƒui ku ɔdu.

english_verse: God is much stronger than I am, and who would call me into court to give me justice?
translation_verse: Si banii nkpoku-nwu ku ɔyikun ni, ubo ɔyikun utulo-mi ƒui. Na si litemi bɔtɛ na bɔdi ni, ɔma ndubɔlɔ-nwu katɛ?

english_verse: Even if I were innocent, God would prove me wrong.
translation_verse: Si ina ńtaƒiɔ ni, mina kenye etemila ndubo-mi budie bute na adu-mi kɔtɔ.

english_verse: I am not guilty, but I no longer care what happens to me.
translation_verse: “Mɔɔnu ka lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-mi, na lɛɛɛdaku-ni ku lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́ku-mi, ɔsika mina ngba bumodi bɔmmɔ bɔ́bɔ-mi.

english_verse: What difference does it make? God destroys the innocent along with the guilty.
translation_verse: Kavumana kadi keeebo-nwu kemmo ka likpidi bablane o-o lɛbuni bablane o-o ni, Unwoti ɔdubo bana ƒui udu bɔyila.

english_verse: When a good person dies a sudden death, God sits back and laughs.
translation_verse: Si ɔgbankpi ɔdi úyu ukyuli ɔbuni ɔdi ɔ́tu na úkpi kɔnakunwi ni, bɔma kani na Unwoti ɔɔmá.

english_verse: And who else but God blindfolds the judges, then lets the wicked take over the earth? My Life Is Speeding By
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔmmɔ kani mɔɔyá na litemi batɛne baatɛ litemi likpidi. Na ɔɔyá na belikplune mmomu baaƒɔ́ lɛla biala teebo kayi na baadi lɛlɔ. Na si ɔɔɔdi anwu ni, na ɔma nábla ɔmɛni?

english_verse: My life is speeding by, without a hope of happiness.
translation_verse: “Usi kani na mina ngba bɔkɛ búsela, ɔni na ebiti ina blii suɛ eeebo-mu kemmo.

english_verse: Each day passes swifter than a sailing ship or an eagle swooping down.
translation_verse: Lɛni na bɔkɛ aani kalɛ na ntu buuti livete taatɔlɔku, iye aani kalɛ na kasangbii kaatu taayu teebeƒie lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: Sometimes I try to be cheerful and to stop complaining,
translation_verse: Mɔɔkya ɔkplu nnii mɔɔyiƒala mina lɛbibo ku ɔlɛ bunu, na lɛda ala bɔka lɛya na ntaama.

english_verse: but my sufferings frighten me, because I know that God still considers me guilty.
translation_verse: Nsu mina lɛbibo lɛɛkya-mi liƒu, ɔsika ngyi ka aaadubo-mi ubo bute.

english_verse: So what's the use of trying to prove my innocence?
translation_verse: Na ka áadu-mi kɔtɔ kuuku ni, bi bukpo na nsɔ nteekpo lɛnɔ?

english_verse: Even if I washed myself with the strongest soap,
translation_verse: Ina lɛ́kpi na lɛ́ƒɔ mina enu na eekeye dɛ ni,

english_verse: God would throw me into a pit of stinking slime, leaving me disgusting to my clothes.
translation_verse: adubo-mi buƒwimi butákya ubu ɔni kemmo na alakpi eesé lɛlɔ geen kemmo, ɔni na mina adala muedi aláyɔ ka asɔ ama-mi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: God isn't a mere human like me. I can't put him on trial.
translation_verse: “Unwoti ɔɔɔdi ukyuli mina kalɛ na busie litemi katɛkɔ na ami ku-nwu butáni lɛla lɛdi bunene.

english_verse: Who could possibly judge between the two of us?
translation_verse: Na nka mɔɔwia ka ukyuli ɔdi uduo-bu ntɛ na ɔsia-bu kɔnu,

english_verse: Can someone snatch away the stick God carries to frighten me?
translation_verse: na ɔƒɔ kegyiimi kani na ɔda uubó-mi, kalɛ na nwuna lɛlɔ liƒu lɛsɔ lilakya-mi kemmo.

english_verse: Then I could speak up without fear of him, but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na nka lɛ́yɔ ka lɛsu-nwu lɛla lɛni na mɔɔyɔ́ ka naaayia-nwu ɔsu. Nsu kalɛ na use ɔƒaani ni, naaakana bɔbla.”

english_verse: I am sick of life! And from my deep despair, I complain to you, my God.
translation_verse: “Unwoti, lɛ́ɛnɔ ku mina ngba ɔƒɛni amu. Anwuɔsu na mɔɔkpali-ɔ taasiku mina kayi kemmo ƒui, ɔsika lɛ́yila lɛnunsia biala.

english_verse: Don't just condemn me! Point out my sin.
translation_verse: Katɔti, buvele, tadu-mi kɔtɔ. Mmomu su-mi lɛla lɛni na lɛ́bla-a na eedie-mi bɔƒiɔ.

english_verse: Why do you take such delight in destroying those you created and in smiling on sinners?
translation_verse: Bɔyɔ na ɔɔyɔ́-ɔ kaƒɔ kalɛ na ala étulo ami ƒula ukyuli ɔni nsiaku-ɔ mɛni, na aatuna ku balalane kɔkwɛ kɔni na baakya ku bana ablala?

english_verse: Do you look at things the way we humans do?
translation_verse: Kalɛ na abu bekyuli bayawine bɔɔnu ala ni, lɛni kani na awɔ lɛnɔ aanu-nya?

english_verse: Is your life as short as ours?
translation_verse: Buse na ƒula ngba buse aani ukyuli ɔyawine bɔdi kalɛ?

english_verse: Is that why you are so quick to find fault with me?
translation_verse: Na bi ɔsu na use-mi aani enye eenweni mina alaekpidi teese atɔ asia lɛni, na ƒula anu asia mina bɔƒiɔ biala lɛlɔ lɛni?

english_verse: You know I am innocent, but who can defend me against you?
translation_verse: Agyi ka ńtaƒiɔ-ɔ, na ukyuli ɔdi lɛnɔ uuubo na wakana-mi budie bɔsiku ƒula enu kemmo.

english_verse: Will you now destroy someone you created?
translation_verse: “Awɔ ɔlati néti ƒula enu ávɔ-mi. Bunwini na adubo bunwini na ayila-mi ngba ɔƒɛni?

english_verse: Remember that you molded me like a piece of clay. So don't turn me back into dust once again.
translation_verse: Kali nu ka awɔ návɔ-mi aani kalɛ na beeti lɛvɔti taavɔ lɛla lɛdi. Na butu na adubɔsɔ etu-mi abwɛ na linwini lɛti?

english_verse: As cheese is made from milk, you created my body from a tiny drop.
translation_verse: Kalɛ na baasála ɔlaaƒɔ ku ntu na uunwíni kana ni, lɛni na ɔkɛnku mina ɔti lɛlɔ na ávɔ-mi ákya mina uni kaƒɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Then you tied my bones together with muscles and covered them with flesh and skin.
translation_verse: Awɔ návɔ-mi ekubi ku kɔbuli, na éte-mi ɔlɔna ku ɔku ɔni mma-mi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You, the source of my life, showered me with kindness and watched over me. You Have Not Explained
translation_verse: Éte-mi ngba, na lɛƒɔndia lɛni na aabla-mi uwi ndi uwi lilávumana. Na aanu-mi lɛlɔ na aagyumana-mi kɔyu.

english_verse: You have not explained all of your mysteries,
translation_verse: “Nsu ábɛla ala ani mɔɔlɛ́ku-mi mɛni ákya ƒula lili kemmo na lɛɛɛgyi.

english_verse: but you catch and punish me each time I sin.
translation_verse: Si lɛ́bla lɛla lɛdi lɛ́ƒiɔ-ɔ ni, agyi ana ƒui, na aaadubo-mi atu budie lɛni, mmomu adubɔni-mi kɔtu.

english_verse: No matter how hard I try, you keep hunting me down like a powerful lion.
translation_verse: Na uwi biala na lɛ́bla kasusu nnii mɔɔtalaku lɛlɔ blii ni, na eebó-mi taava kalɔ ku ƒula ɔyikun ala bɔbla aani kalɛ na gyata ɔɔtú ebuo teeƒie.

english_verse: Why did you let me be born? I would rather have died before birth
translation_verse: “O Katɔti, bi ɔsu geen na áya na báwɔ-mi, na átaya na likpi asa na ukyuli ɔdi uti nwuna lɛnumi muedi ɔnu-mi?

english_verse: and been carried to the grave without ever breathing.
translation_verse: Nka kawɔkɔ mmɔ kani na aya na bagyu-mi batákya kaƒiɔtɔ na ukyuli ɔdi uláti ɔnii lɛ́kya dii.

english_verse: I have only a few days left. Why don't you leave me alone? Let me find some relief, *
translation_verse: Emeyi alɛɛ nébu-mi, anwuɔsu ya na lɛkɛ bɔnwuna na ebiti blii adi ada-mi,

english_verse: Your words have silenced others and made them ashamed; now it is only right for you to be put to shame.
translation_verse: Aabu ka ala ani na enye aaká mɛni adubɔya na bekyuli bebile kenye? Na baladɔnku-ɔ banii aatɛmi enyekpi yoo?

english_verse: You claim to be innocent and argue that your beliefs are acceptable to God.
translation_verse: Ákana na ásu Katɔti anini, ‘Bɔƒiɔ bɔdi buuubo-mi kayi kemmo, na nse siin na ƒula anumi.’

english_verse: and let you know that wisdom has many different sides. You would then discover that God has punished you less than you deserve.
translation_verse: Na ɔsu-ɔ ka lɛnunda lɛɛɛdi unwi, na abɛla lɛnɔ akya-nwu kemmo. Ɔlɛka ɔbla-a nwaa ka bɔyiƒala muedi na Unwoti ɔ́yiƒala ƒula ekpidi adi bene.

english_verse: They are higher than the heavens and deeper than the grave. So what can you do when you know so little,
translation_verse: Nwuna lɛnunda lɛ́kuku líbo lɛ́vi katɔ ƒui. Na lɛnunda lɛmmɔ kemmo lɛnɔ kágyu ketulo kekpine ƒui. Na bi na adubɔkana na ati na amɛni ƒui lɛlɔ?

english_verse: and these mysteries outreach the earth and the ocean?
translation_verse: Lɛnunda lɛmɛni líne líbo lɛ́vi kalɔ kammɔ ƒui, na lɛ́bɛbɛ litulo ɛpu ƒui.

english_verse: If God puts you in prison or drags you to court, what can you do?
translation_verse: “Si banii Katɔti ɔ́ya na bákya-a ɔtɔ iye úti-ɔ úsienku litemi lɛdi katɛkɔ ni, ɔma ndubɔkana na ɔta unye-nwu lɛlɔ?

english_verse: God has the wisdom to know when someone is worthless and sinful,
translation_verse: Geen geen ni, Unwoti ɔɔnu bekyuli bekpidi taati, na ulénye likpidi kama, mmomu uudie-ni keyi.

english_verse: but it's easier to tame a wild donkey than to make a fool wise. Surrender Your Heart to God
translation_verse: Use kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ka atumini ebuo ala utine na unu litemi ukyuli kalɛ, utulo ka atina ɔdɔlɔdi ala na unwini ɔnundane.

english_verse: Surrender your heart to God, turn to him in prayer,
translation_verse: “Nyonu ƒula lɛlɔ ƒui te Unwoti, na akpali-nwu evele ala ani muukpóku-ɔ.

english_verse: and give up your sins— even those you do in secret.
translation_verse: Na edie ƒula alaekpidi ƒui atu, ku ani na ábla na bɔbɛ kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: Then you won't be ashamed; you will be confident and fearless.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na kɔƒa kɔsɔ kulékpo-ɔ, na kayi kelie-ɔ kalɔ na enye kpakplaa na asɔ alayia lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Your troubles will go away like water beneath a bridge,
translation_verse: Na ala ani muukpóku-ɔ ƒui ni, adubo-nya bɔyiƒala aani ntu nágba bɔ́tɔlɔ.

english_verse: and your darkest night will be brighter than noon.
translation_verse: Na ƒula ngba emeyi kemmo adubukeye butulo ɔƒiiwi. Na kasuudikɔ kammɔ kabla nwaa aani ɔtanta kadi bugye.

english_verse: You will rest safe and secure, filled with hope and emptied of worry.
translation_verse: Adubulie kalɔ kpi ku lɛnunsia na anu aka amana lɛlɔ na akɛ bɔnwuna ƒaa.

english_verse: You will sleep without fear and be greatly respected.
translation_verse: Adubo bɔtɛ bɔlɛɛ na lɛla lɛdi lɛsɔ lilakya-a liƒu. Na bekyuli pii badububo bebeye-ɔ kebunku.

english_verse: But those who are evil will go blind and lose their way. Their only escape is death!
translation_verse: Nsu balalane ama badubɔnu ulu banɔ, na balákɛ kebunku ku kekelikɔ kadi. Na lɛla linwi lɛni kani na badubɔsia anu ndi ka kukpi kubeti-ma.”

english_verse: Job said to his friends:
translation_verse: Hiob údie kenye ɔnini,

english_verse: You think you are so great, with all the answers.
translation_verse: “Sɔsɔ na ɔdi, bɛɛnu ka amii kani ndi amii. Na si bíkpi ni, bíti lɛnunda bɛ́tɔlɔku!

english_verse: But I know as much as you do, and so does everyone else.
translation_verse: Nsu ni, ami lɛnɔ mbo kasusu aani bina kalɛ, na ńtasɔ liiitulo-mii. Ɔma naaagyi ala ani na bɛɛsu mɛni ƒui?

english_verse: I have always lived right, and God answered my prayers; now friends make fun of me.
translation_verse: “Ɔƒɛni amu lɛ́ta línwini lɛmala líte mina bakpana, ina ka lɛ́kpali Unwoti na únu úte-mi. Ndi lɛmala, ina ka nda lɛlɔ siin na bɔƒiɔ buuubo-mi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: It's easy to condemn those who are suffering, when you have no troubles.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani nli ƒaa ni, ama mɔɔpii lilikpi ala. Na baanu bani muugyile teebuli aani lɛla lɛni na ama báƒɔ béboku.

english_verse: Robbers and other godless people live safely at home and say, “God is in our hands!” If You Want To Learn
translation_verse: Kasusu kelekpoku beyune ku bakantankpine na bana kakyakɔ. Na bani mɔɔkya Unwoti kɔnyi ni, bɔyia bɔdi buuubo-ma kemmo, ɔsika bada bana baƒiɔ enu kemmo kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english_verse: If you want to learn, then go and ask the wild animals and the birds,
translation_verse: “Nsu si aawia lɛla ati ni, na esie lɛku kemmo bebuo ku kayaa baasɛ kudɔ, na badubɔtina-a ala.

english_verse: Any of them can tell you what the Lord has done.
translation_verse: Bana ƒui bagyi ka Unwoti Katɔti nábla ala amɛni ƒui.

english_verse: We hear with our ears, taste with our tongues,
translation_verse: Atu na buuti teenu, na unyemi na buuti taati adila emini.

english_verse: and gain some wisdom from those who have lived a long time.
translation_verse: Benengu bani néelie bétu uwi kudɔ na bɔɔkɛ́ lɛnunda, na bana ala bɔtina mɔɔyá na buunú ala kalɔ.

english_verse: But God is the real source of wisdom and strength.
translation_verse: “Nsu ɔna ƒui kawɔlɔkɔ ni, Katɔti ndi lɛnunda ku ɔyikun ƒui kasikɔ. Na anwu mɔɔtina-bu kasiakɔ ku ala kalɔ bunu.

english_verse: just as he rules over liars and those they lie to.
translation_verse: Katɔti ubo ɔyikun na ɔɔdi bekyuli ƒui lɛlɔ. Ɔɔdi ɔkɔ banyine bani mɔɔtɔ́lɔ bekyuli ku bani na baatɔ́lɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: God removes priests and others who have great power—
translation_verse: Ɔɔbɔku bakpane teedie bana kunyekɔ. Na bayikune bani náƒɔ lɛnyi ni, uukpeli-ma taava kalɔ.

english_verse: God strikes their rulers senseless, then leaves them to roam through barren deserts,
translation_verse: Ɔɔbla na bana bɔtɔnkune benwini badɔlɔdi na babla susuusu, na bayii lɛla biala bɔbla ulu.

english_verse: None of you are smarter than I am; there's nothing you know that I don't.
translation_verse: Na ala ani na bɛgyi ni, ami lɛnɔ ngyi-nya, na bitakali bɛnii lɛ́sɔ na bina kudɔ.

english_verse: But I prefer to argue my case with God All-Powerful—
translation_verse: Nsu mɔɔwia ka ami ku Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔmmɔ bɔtɛmi, na ami ku-nwu bɔni litemi lɛmmɔ bɔnu.

english_verse: you are merely useless doctors, who treat me with lies.
translation_verse: Ɔkɔ ɔlɛ babwine na bina ƒui bɛdi. Na ɔkɔ etemila ani neeebo kɔsia kani na binye bɛɛká taasu-mi.

english_verse: The wisest thing you can do is to keep quiet
translation_verse: Si bíbile kenye bilie kpoo muedi ni, bekyuli badubɔnu-mii aani banundane mmomu!

english_verse: and listen to my argument.
translation_verse: “Bise atu na binu mina unyeƒi ɔni na mɔɔkya.

english_verse: Are you telling lies for God
translation_verse: Bɔnyi na bɛdubo ɔkɔ bɔnyi bɛnii Katɔti kenye na biidie?

english_verse: and not telling the whole truth when you argue his case?
translation_verse: Bɔkana na bɛdubɔkana na bɛtu-nwu litemi binwini na bɛsu ka nwuna litemi geen kenye na biidie na litemi katɛkɔ?

english_verse: If he took you to court, could you fool him, just as you fool others?
translation_verse: Na si banii ɔlɔ-mii katɛ ni, bɛdubɔkana anwu lɛnɔ bɔtɔlɔ kalɛ na bɛɛtɔ́lɔ bekyuli bamba?

english_verse: If you were secretly unfair, he would correct you,
translation_verse: Ina dɛ na bɛɛnu bekyuli anumi taabla ala ni, ɔdubo bɔnu bɔti na ɔdɔnku-mii.

english_verse: and his glorious splendor would make you terrified.
translation_verse: Nwuna bukeye ku nwuna lɛlɔ liƒu bulákya-mii bɔyia?

english_verse: Your wisdom and arguments will blow away like dust. Be Quiet While I Speak
translation_verse: Bina lɛnunda ku agba ani na biibó ƒui adi ɔtumu, na uuubo kɔsia kɔdi, ɔsika unyeƒi ukpludi kani na ɔdi.

english_verse: Be quiet while I speak, and we'll see what happens.
translation_verse: “Bibile kenye kpoo na binu lɛla lɛni na mɔɔsu. Ɔmmɔ kama na bitaasu lɛla lɛni na amii lɛnɔ bɛgyi.

english_verse: I will be responsible for what happens to me.
translation_verse: Lɛ́tuna ka liti mina ngba lɛkpa ƒaa.

english_verse: God may kill me, but still I will trust him and offer my defense.
translation_verse: Ina bɔdu na ɔnii wadu-mi muedi ni, nwuna lɛlɔ kani na mina anu asia. Na anwu na ndubudie ala ani muukpóku-mi lɛsu.

english_verse: This may be what saves me, because no guilty person would come to his court.
translation_verse: Na ɔƒɛni kalɛ mina kayi buse bɔmmɔ ndubunwini mina ngba bɔƒɔ, ɔsika ukyuli ukpidi ɔdi uuubo na ɔdubuse kayi ɔda ɔlɛ Unwoti anumi ku lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: I have prepared my case well, and I am certain to win.
translation_verse: Lɛ́klibi lɛlɔ líte mina litemi kaduɛ, na ngyi ka mbo ubo.

english_verse: If you can prove me guilty, I will give up and die. Job Prays I Ask Only Two Things
translation_verse: Na si úbo úte ka mina likpidi lɛ́lɛ keyi ka lɛ́ƒiɔ na ńtati bɔbla ni, ndububile kenye kpoo na likpi ƒaa.

english_verse: I ask only two things of you, my God, and I will no longer hide from you—
translation_verse: “Mmomu ni, O Unwoti, alakpa anyɔ adi kani na muuvele-ɔ na abla-nya ete-mi asa na mbenye-ɔ anumi.

english_verse: Then speak, and I will reply; or else let me speak, and you reply.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama na alɔ-mi katɛ na lidie kenye, iye na aya na liye-ɔ mina litemi na edie kenye.

english_verse: Please point out my sins, so I will know them.
translation_verse: Buvele, die mina alaekpidi ani na lɛ́bla keyi. Na atina-mi bɔƒiɔ bɔmmɔ na lɛnu lɛti.

english_verse: Why have you turned your back and count me your enemy?
translation_verse: Bi ɔsu na énwini kama ákya-mi, na bi ɔsu na éti-mi énwini ukisine?

english_verse: Do you really enjoy frightening a fallen leaf?
translation_verse: Bɔyɔ na ɔɔyɔ́-ɔ kaƒɔ ka eteebo-mi taavinku aani kalɛ na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ uubó livete lɛnudi?

english_verse: Why do you accuse me of horrible crimes and make me pay for sins I did in my youth?
translation_verse: Mɔɔnu ka enye aadú-mi kɔtɔ geen ku kɔnyi na aadá-mi kenye ku ekpidi ani na lɛ́bla ɔ́si mina lɛnamu uwi ƒui.

english_verse: You have tied my feet down and keep me surrounded;
translation_verse: Na ébo-mi lɛkpu ése, na aanu mina kɔnyakɔ ƒui teese likpo.

english_verse: I am rotting away like cloth eaten by worms.
translation_verse: “Na mina ngba bɔyii udu aani kalɛ na lɛla lɛdi liibun, iye kalɛ na kubweyi kuubile adala.”

english_verse: Life is short and sorrowful for every living soul.
translation_verse: “Ngba buse klukui bute ɔyawine biala, na nwuna ngba bɔmmɔ lɛnɔ bɔdanku lɛbibo.

english_verse: We are flowers that fade and shadows that vanish.
translation_verse: Uubimi aani kugyii anwula, na ɔɔnú na ɔmmɔ kama. Na use lɛnɔ aani ɔyuli ɔni mɔɔyii taakya.

english_verse: And so, I ask you, God, why pick on me?
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na líye Katɔti si ami ɔmɛni udu na ɔlɛka uti anumi ɔlɛ na ɔtɛku-mi litemi kpakplaa lɛmɛni.

english_verse: There's no way a human can be completely pure.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔɔɔdubo ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ bɔkana bɔsia na ɔbla lɛlɔ kedee ƒui ɔwɔlɔ.

english_verse: Our time on earth is brief; the number of our days is already decided by you.
translation_verse: Áakɔku bula ngba emeyi bumomo ése, na agyi abuli bumomo ani na bɔdubo bulie, ɔni na ɔdi ulébo ulávi kesii kani na éte-nwu áwɔ.

english_verse: Why don't you leave us alone and let us find some happiness while we toil and labor? When a Tree Is Chopped Down
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu, da atu die ukyuli lɛlɔ, kalɛ na ɔdi lɛla lɛni na ɔdubɔkɛ aani kabla ɔblane kalɛ.

english_verse: When a tree is chopped down, there is always the hope that it will sprout again.
translation_verse: “Kugyii muedi si báda-ku ni, kubo lɛnunsia ka kɔdubo bɔsɔ bɔta ɔwɔdi.

english_verse: Its roots and stump may rot,
translation_verse: Ina ka ligyukui lɛmmɔ lɛɛkwii na ligyiitu lɛmmɔ liitu uwi ni,

english_verse: but at the touch of water, it sprouts once again.
translation_verse: uwi ɔni na ɔnantu ɔ́nya úbo kebi úwi-nwu lɛlɔ ni, ɔɔta kɔgba kɔwɔdi.

english_verse: Humans are different— we die, and that's the end.
translation_verse: Nsu bayawine ama ni, beeese lɛni. Si bɔnwuna bukplodi bɔ́lɛ-ma kemmo ni, na bana ɔdi ɔ́sa.

english_verse: We are like streams and lakes after the water has gone;
translation_verse: Na baasɔ taatɛ ukpludi aani ketu iye lɛba lɛni na ntu bɔ́kwii-ni kemmo.

english_verse: we fall into the sleep of death, never to rise again, until the sky disappears.
translation_verse: Si bekyuli ama bánya bálɛɛ kukpi lɛlɛɛ linwi lɛmɛni ni, ɔ́sa. Bɔta bɔsɔ buuubo-ma lɛlɔ wetédu ka kayaa muedi kayii kákya.

english_verse: Please hide me, God, deep in the ground— and when you are angry no more, remember to rescue me. Will We Humans Live Again?
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu ni, O Unwoti, bɛla-mi kya kaƒiɔtɔ kemmo na ese uwi ɔni na adubɔsɔ enyimo-mi si ƒula kɔnyi kɔ́yɔ-ɔ.

english_verse: Will we humans live again? I would gladly suffer and wait for my time.
translation_verse: Bulie na bekyuli badubɔsɔ benwini bebelie ngba sɔsɔ? Ndubunye nteebo abi na linye kabla kamɛni lɛlɔ ƒaa wetédu uwi ɔni na adubɔvumana-mi.

english_verse: My Creator, you would want me; you would call out, and I would answer.
translation_verse: Unwoti, ngyi ka adubo-mi bɔwia aani ƒula ubi. Adubɔkpali-mi, na lɛtuna-a.

english_verse: You would take care of me, but not count my sins—
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, ngyi ka adubo-mi lɛlɔ bɔnu, na asɔ alasia mina alaekpidi anu.

english_verse: you would put them in a bag, tie it tight, and toss them away.
translation_verse: Adubuti ala ebi mina ekpidi na etile-nya kenye. Na adubuti mina bɔƒiɔ akya koƒo kemmo na enyimi-mu kenye.

english_verse: But in the real world, mountains tumble, and rocks crumble;
translation_verse: “Nsu kalɛ na abi ku atakpɛ muedi aakunku na aayii udu na ana kenyekɔ,

english_verse: streams wear away stones and wash away soil. And you destroy our hopes!
translation_verse: na ntu bɔɔyu teewi lɛtabi lɛlɔ na lɛɛtu ubu, na ntu bɔmmɔ buukú kalɔ ni, lɛni geen na eete kuƒi ka ukyuli lɛnunsia ƒui lɛɛyii udu!

english_verse: You change the way we look, then send us away, wiped out forever.
translation_verse: Ƒula ɔyikun ɔɔdi-nwu lɛlɔ na nwuna enu aaƒɛ. Aayá na nwuna udu ɔɔvumana na ɔɔtɔlɔ-ɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: We never live to know if our children are praised or disgraced.
translation_verse: Na ulélie taanu si anyi buni na nwuna bebi baaƒɔ́ iye kɔƒa na baadi.

english_verse: We feel no pain but our own, and when we mourn, it's only for ourselves.
translation_verse: Anwu ɔlati lɛbibo ku kɔnyana kɔni na uuwulo kani na ɔgyi, na lɛla bamba lɛsɔ lɛɛɛkɛ-nwu.”

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman said: *
translation_verse: Eliƒas ɔni nási Teman mmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su ɔnini,

english_verse: Job, if you had any sense,
translation_verse: “Ɔnundane ɔdi ulátɛmi lɛni aani kalɛ na enye aatɛmi kɔtɛ keeke mɛni.

english_verse: you would stop spreading all of this hot air.
translation_verse: Etemila ani neeebo kalɔ kani na enye aaká.

english_verse: Your words are enough to make others turn from God and lead them to doubt.
translation_verse: Geen ni, ala ani mɔɔlɛ́-ɔ kenye ni, bɔsu na ada bekyuli anii basɔ batabu Unwoti na bakya-nwu lili kalɔ.

english_verse: And your sinful, scheming mind is the source of all you say.
translation_verse: Na ƒula ekpidi pii ani na aabla ni, anya náya na éti kasusu kani ɔsu na aasu kenye kamɛni udu.

english_verse: I am not here as your judge; your own words are witnesses against you.
translation_verse: Awɔ ɔlati ƒula kenye mɔɔdú-ɔ kɔtɔ, na ɔɔɔdi mina kadi. Na ƒula unyemi muudie-ɔ keyi.

english_verse: Were you the first human? Are you older than the hills?
translation_verse: “Awɔ ndi ukyuli udeedi ɔni na báka bɔwɔ? Munuu awɔ ntɔ abi ani nnye mɛni na bɔɔnu?

english_verse: Have you ever been present when God's council meets? Do you alone have wisdom?
translation_verse: Éenye Katɔti kasusu kadi ketikɔ dii, munuu aanu lɛlɔ aani ɔnundane unengudi utulo ƒui na bekyuli akɔ?

english_verse: We have the benefit of wisdom older than your father.
translation_verse: Benengu eli ƒuala geen bakya-bu akɔ bani mɔɔkya-bu kasusu, na bábi lɛlɔ betulo ƒ'ɔti ƒui.

english_verse: And you have been offered comforting words from God. Isn't this enough?
translation_verse: Bi ɔsu na Unwoti litemi lilaƒɔ-ɔ anu na kaƒɔ kayɔ-ɔ, ka ani na búti bɔɔsia-a kɔnu?

english_verse: Your emotions are out of control, making you look fierce;
translation_verse: Bi ɔsu na ƒula kayi kaatɔ́lɔ-ɔ, na éƒu eli ku kɔnyi,

english_verse: that's why you attack God with everything you say.
translation_verse: na livo liiƒí-ɔ na Katɔti lɛlɔ, na aatɛmiku-nwu kalɛ kalɛ na aayɔ́?

english_verse: and neither are angels— not in the sight of God. If God doesn't trust his angels,
translation_verse: Katɔti batu muedi beeese sɛɛn na Unwoti anumi na katɔ kesii kani na bakya mmɔ.

english_verse: what chance do humans have? We are so terribly evil that we thirst for sin. Just Listen to What I Know
translation_verse: Na dɛ na ukyuli anwu ɔdubɔbla sɛɛn? Likpidi lɛ́ƒɔ-nwu lɛlɔ kemmo, na lɛɛda-nwu ɔkwɛ aani utukwɛ kalɛ.

english_verse: Just listen to what I know, and you will learn
translation_verse: “Hiob, se atu na enu lɛla lɛni na lɛ́ɛnu na línu lɛnɔ dii.

english_verse: Those who gained such insights also gained the land, and they were not influenced by foreign teachings.
translation_verse: Baƒɔ badi bátakya-ma akɔ, anwuɔsu ukyuli ɔdi uuubo na ɔdubunwini-ma kasusu na Katɔti lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But suffering is in store each day for those who sin.
translation_verse: Balalane bani mɔɔbla bana bakpana ulikplu ni, abi kani na beelie teebo bana ngba emeyi ƒui kemmo.

english_verse: They scrounge around for food, all the while dreading the approaching darkness.
translation_verse: Na baasia kesi kesii taavi taawia bana lɛdila na beeye lɛlɔ kesii kani na badubɔkɛ-nya. Na begbini ndubo-ma ɔlɔna bɔkun si békpi.

english_verse: They are overcome with despair, like frightened soldiers facing a fearsome king in battle.
translation_verse: Ɔgbankpi ɔ́bɛla lɛlɔ unye ɔgya-ma, na liƒu bonwu líƒie-ma aani ɔga ɔyikune ɔdi ndubo ubekpoku-ma.

english_verse: This is because they rebelled against God All-Powerful
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani muunene enu taakya Katɔti na baadi lɛmɛnɛ taakya-nwu ni, lɛni na ɔɔbla-ma.

english_verse: and have attacked him with their weapons.
translation_verse: Báta ku usi ku lɛla tabu, na béti agyumanala ka betékpoku Katɔti.

english_verse: They may be rich and fat,
translation_verse: “Ina dɛ na bebo akɛla na bélie lɛmwi muedi ni,

english_verse: but they will live in the ruins of deserted towns.
translation_verse: lɛtɔ ɔgbɔnɔ kemmo na badubo bebelie na lɛma lɛni nábwɛ kemmo.

english_verse: Their property and wealth will shrink and disappear.
translation_verse: Na bana akɛla adububo kalɔ na ayii udu.

english_verse: They won't escape the darkness, and the blazing breath of God will set their future aflame. *
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛ ɔdubɔsa ɔkya-ma, na ogya ɔdubɔkyula-ma. Na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni mɔɔlɛ́ taasi Katɔti kenye kemmo ɔdubɔkpala-ma ɔtɔlɔku.

english_verse: They have put their trust in something worthless; now they will become worthless
translation_verse: Na si bana kɔdɔlɔ kɔ́ya na béti anu básia ala keeke lɛlɔ ni, lɛla lɛni neeebo kɔsia na badubo bɔkɛ.

english_verse: Or like vineyards or orchards whose blossoms and unripe fruit drop to the ground.
translation_verse: Badubo bɔbla aani egyii ani néwiile ana ebi ekuni na étegyie asa na ánu. Badubo buse aani anwula ani na átakya ebi asa na ánu.

english_verse: Yes, the godless and the greedy will have nothing but flames feasting on their homes,
translation_verse: Bekyuli bekpidi bamɛni udu ni, bedinkɔ kani na badubo bunwini. Na ogya ndubo-ma kɔduli bɔkyula.

english_verse: because they are the parents of trouble and vicious lies.
translation_verse: Ɔsika likpidi kasusu kani na beelie teeti, na likpidi lɛmmɔ kani na badubo bɔwɔ ka nina kaƒɔ na bada ɔsu.”

english_verse: If I were in your place, it would be easy to criticize or to give advice.
translation_verse: Si banii bɔ́vumana kunyekɔ na bise aani kalɛ na nse mɛni ni, nka ndubɔsu litulo-mii na lɛkunku lili lɛkya-mii.

english_verse: But I would offer hope and comfort instead.
translation_verse: Nsu mina etemila ni, adubɔkya-mii ɔkplu, na ala ani na ndubɔsu aya na kaƒɔ kaba-mii buɛɛ.

english_verse: If I speak, or if I don't, I hurt all the same. My torment continues.
translation_verse: “Na bi na lɛ́su o-o, bi na ńtasu o-o ni, mina ɔlɛ bunu buláƒana.

english_verse: God has worn me down and destroyed my family;
translation_verse: O Unwoti, áya na mina ɔyikun ɔ́sa na lɛ́bla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ, na áyila mina kaduli bekyuli ƒui udu.

english_verse: my shriveled up skin proves that I am his prisoner.
translation_verse: Áya na mina ɔlɔna ɔ́kwii ɔma-mi ekubi lɛlɔ, na ébo-mi lɛkpu aani ƒula ɔtɔntɛne.

english_verse: God is my hateful enemy, glaring at me and attacking with his sharp teeth.
translation_verse: Unwoti úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya-mi na ɔ́duli-mi ɔ́va kalɔ. Na unye ɔɔnu-mi ɔnusɛ aani nwuna ukisine kalɛ.

english_verse: Everyone is against me; they sneer and slap my face.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bébimi kenye baanu-mi taapii-mi. Na básala baatu etemila taalɛ-mi na baaƒiɛmi-mi kɔnu utugya.

english_verse: And God is the one who handed me over to this merciless mob. Everything Was Going Well
translation_verse: Katɔti údie-mi atu na ɔ́nyonu-mi ɔ́kya bekyuli bekpidi enu kemmo.

english_verse: Everything was going well, until God grabbed my neck and shook me to pieces. God set me up as the target
translation_verse: Nka lɛla lɛdi lilekpoku-mi, nsu Katɔti ɔ́da-mi na ɔ́mana-mi ɔkwɛ na ɔ́kunku-mi na úbo-mi útáva. Na úti anumi ɔ́lɛ-mi ka ɔdu-mi.

english_verse: for his arrows, and without showing mercy, he slashed my stomach open, spilling out my insides.
translation_verse: Uubó nwuna atula taalɛ-mi taasiku lɛƒɛnyi ƒui lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́ƒuala-mi ɔƒɛnyi na ubugya ɔɔyu teewi kalɔ.

english_verse: God never stops attacking,
translation_verse: Katɔti útada-mi bukpoku útaya uwi ɔdi.

english_verse: and so, in my sorrow I dress in sackcloth and sit in the dust.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu na líti kɔnyana ala lɛ́da na mina lɛbibo ku lɛƒɛda kemmo, na líbo nli ɔtumu akɔ na mɛni.

english_verse: My face is red with tears, and dark shadows circle my eyes,
translation_verse: Líwulo laa na mina anumi egyie na éƒu.

english_verse: If I should die, I beg the earth not to cover my cry for justice.
translation_verse: “Muuvele geen nnii si úbo úte ka líkpi ni, kalɔ ketebi mina ubugya ku kɔvanu lɛti!

english_verse: Even now, God in heaven is both my witness and my protector.
translation_verse: Ngyi nwaa ka ukyuli ɔni ndubudie-mi kenye ɔkya katɔ, na anwu ndi-mi ubunkune.

english_verse: My friends have rejected me, but God is the one I beg
translation_verse: Mina ɔkpana ndi ukyuli ɔni muuvele teete-mi uwi ɔni na muuwulo taakpali Katɔti.

english_verse: to show that I am right, just as a friend should.
translation_verse: Na uudie taatina Katɔti ka ńtabla lɛla lɛdi aani kalɛ na ukyuli uuvele teete nwuna ɔkpana.

english_verse: Because in only a few years, I will be dead and gone.
translation_verse: “Ɔsika akwa alɛɛ kani nébu-mi na likpi, na nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo bunwini bubo lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: My hopes have died, my time is up, and the grave is ready.
translation_verse: “Lɛlɔ lítu mina kɔyu. Na mina emeyi lɛnɔ áda liku. Kaƒiɔtɔ kani nébu-mi ɔƒaani, na nsɔ liiibo lɛnunsia lɛdi.

english_verse: All I can see are angry crowds, making fun of me.
translation_verse: Bekyuli benye bámana-mi baamá-mi. Na mina anumi aanu-ma ƒui.

english_verse: If you, Lord, don't help, who will pay the price for my release?
translation_verse: “Unwoti, si awɔ átanu-mi kɔnyana na ebunku-mi ni, ɔma ndubɔkana na ɔƒɔ kayu kadi na mina lili na udie-mi?

english_verse: My friends won't really listen, all because of you, and so you must be the one to prove them wrong.
translation_verse: Awɔ náya na bana kasusu kékpi na bébulo ala kalɔ bunu. Anwuɔsu adubo-ma likpidi keyi budie na bekyuli banu kalɛ na báƒiɔ.

english_verse: They have condemned me, just to benefit themselves; now blind their children.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔví nwuna ɔkpana kalɔ kalɛ na ɔkɛ bɔdi ni, nwuna bebi anumi adubɔbwɛ.

english_verse: You, God, are the reason I am insulted and spit on.
translation_verse: “Unwoti, awɔ geen ɔsu na línwini ukyuli ɔni na beedumi taama, na beetuo lisuo lɛnɔ teewi-mi.

english_verse: I am almost blind with grief; my body is a mere shadow.
translation_verse: Mina kɔnyana buwulo bɔ́ya na anumi ábla-mi ƒluƒlu, na ami ukyuli umodi ɔmmɔ ƒui nkɛ aani kɔyu kɔyu.

english_verse: People who are truly good would feel so alarmed, that they would become angry with my worthless friends.
translation_verse: Nsu bekyuli bani nse siin bánu ɔmɛni na bana kayi kékpoku-ma, na bátatuna ku bani ɔbladu neeebo kɔsia kɔdi mɛni.

english_verse: They would do the right thing and because they did, they would grow stronger.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani nse siin beenye bana ala siin bɔbla lɛlɔ, na bana ɔyikun ɔɔkɔ́ katɔ teebu uwi biala.

english_verse: But none of my friends show any sense.
translation_verse: “Nsu mina bakpana, amii bilátina ka bina kasusu kese nwaa lɛni.

english_verse: My life is drawing to an end; hope has disappeared.
translation_verse: Mina ngba búudu kawɔlɔkɔ, na lɛ́yila lɛnunsia biala na kasusu kani na nda ku mina kayi lɛyɔla biala lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But all my friends can do is offer empty hopes.
translation_verse: Na kayi kekpludi kani na bagyi ukyuli buse, na si bánu usien ni, banii kadi bugye bɔdi.

english_verse: I could tell the world below to prepare me a bed.
translation_verse: Ami mina lɛnunsia ƒui ɔƒaani ni, ani ndi kekpine kesii kani na ndubusie ntátɛ kpoo na kasuudikɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Then I could greet the grave as my father and say to the worms, “Hello, mother and sisters!”
translation_verse: Ndubuti kaƒiɔtɔ linwini mina ɔti, na liti beklubi bammɔ linwini mina uni ku banwani belekubi.

english_verse: Will it keep me company in the world of the dead?
translation_verse: Na lɛnunsia lɛmmɔ lɛdubo-mi bɔsiaku na bɔdubusie butéduo kekpine kesii kani na lísela mmɔ?”

english_verse: Or do you think that we are dumb animals?
translation_verse: Na tabu anii abu bani nlie-ɔ kudɔ mɛni ni, buse aani bebuo bani neeebo kasusu.

english_verse: The lamps of sinful people soon are snuffed out,
translation_verse: “Bunine na Unwoti uunine balalane asogya ɔni na bátu bada, na ɔsɔ ulédie unyemi na ukeye.

english_verse: Their powerful legs become weak, and they stumble on schemes of their own doing. *
translation_verse: Na lɛgba lɛni na nka úteetu kalɔ ni, ɔƒɛni amu akɔnkɔ ammɔ áyɔ. Na kɔkwɛ kɔni na anwu ɔlati ɔ́kya úse ni, aku na ɔdubo butulo bubuli.

english_verse: Before they know it,
translation_verse: Na anwu ɔlati ɔɔnya teetéduo kakpagyuɛ kemmo.

english_verse: they are trapped in a net,
translation_verse: Keedie-nwu na kebo-nwu lɛkpu na lɛlɔ bunwini bɔdi bɔsɔ bulakya-nwu.

english_verse: Terror strikes and pursues from every side.
translation_verse: “Na ulákɛ bɔnwuna na liƒu ala ani ndubo-nwu butaayila na ataabɔku-nwu lɛnɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: Those sinners are dragged from the safety of their tents to die a gruesome death.
translation_verse: Na badubo-nwu bɔkpɛ bɔlɛku nwuna kevo kani kemmo na nka uli ƒaa kudeedi mmɔ, na betiku-nwu na utásiaku kukpi liƒu ala ƒui unengu.

english_verse: Then their tents and possessions are burned to ashes,
translation_verse: “Ɔmmɔ kama na bakyula nwuna kevo ku ala ani ƒui na ɔ́da úse mmɔ, na enwini ntɔ.

english_verse: and they are left like trees, dried up from the roots.
translation_verse: Ɔdubukpi ku lidu ku lidu, na ɔkwii unye aani kugyii kɔkwiidi ku kɔgba.

english_verse: thrown far from the light into a world of darkness,
translation_verse: Badubo-nwu bɔbɔku bɔlɛku bukeye kemmo butákya kasuudikɔ, na bayila-nwu udu kede kede na kayawi.

english_verse: without any children to carry on their name.
translation_verse: Na ubi iye uwɔ ɔdi ulakya-nwu kama na wakɔliku nwuna lɛnyi katɔ.

english_verse: Such is the fate of sinners and their families who don't know God.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔni na naaayia Katɔti ni, kakyakɔ kammɔ ndu kani námanku-nwu.”

english_verse: How long will you torture me with your words?
translation_verse: “Bi ɔsu na biikpóku-mi na bɛɛkya-mi ɔlɛ lɛlɔ ku bina atɛ lɛni?

english_verse: Isn't ten times enough for you to accuse me? Aren't you ashamed?
translation_verse: Leevudi mɛni ka binye bɛɛdú-mi kɔtɔ taasia kama, na biidumi-mi teewi-mi anumi kalɔ.

english_verse: Even if I have sinned, you haven't been harmed.
translation_verse: Na si sɔsɔ na ɔdi ka ami náƒiɔ ni, mina litemi na lɛdi.

english_verse: You boast of your goodness, claiming I am suffering because I am guilty.
translation_verse: Bitakali bɛnii amii bɛdia bitulo-mi bɛ́gya ɔsu na bɛɛnu bɛnii mina ekpidi ɔsu na muubó abi.

english_verse: But God is the one at fault for finding fault with me.
translation_verse: Mɔɔyá na bɛti ka Katɔti mmomu náƒiɔ-mi na ɔɔní-mi kɔtu ɔnii lɛ́bla likpidi.

english_verse: Though I pray to be rescued from this torment, no whisper of justice answers me.
translation_verse: “Ina ka muuwulo ni, ami na báƒiɔ. Na ka mɔɔkpali lɛnɔ ni, Katɔti úni, na ulátɛ mina litemi ulu lɛlɔ ulete-mi.

english_verse: God has me trapped with a wall of darkness
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔ́bala-mi ulu na naaakɛ́ kasiakɔ. Na ɔ́ya na mina ulu ɔ́bla suu.

english_verse: and attacks with fierce anger, as though I were his enemy.
translation_verse: Úti kɔnyi ɔ́kya-mi kati kati, na ɔɔká-mi takya nwuna bekisine akɔ.

english_verse: His entire army advances, then surrounds my tent. I Am Forgotten *
translation_verse: Ɔ́ya na nwuna bekpone báta bebekpoku-mi. Na báka bámana mina kevo.

english_verse: God has turned relatives and friends against me,
translation_verse: “Katɔti ɔ́ya na mina lɛlɔ bekyuli ƒui béni-mi, na línwini ɔƒɔ líte mina bekyuli batidi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: and I am forgotten.
translation_verse: Na banwa ku bakpana bammɔ ƒui báda-mi bése.

english_verse: and when I call my servants, they pay no attention.
translation_verse: Na ɔmwi si lɛ́kpali mina kabla ɔblane iye lívele-nwu dɛ muedi ni, ulákpete-mi.

english_verse: My breath disgusts my wife; everyone in my family turns away.
translation_verse: Mina ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni mɔɔlɛ́-mi kenye muedi uunwenyi mina uleku, na muusé mina banwani bananabi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Young children can't stand me, and when I come near, they make fun.
translation_verse: Na ku banamu wɛlɛwɛlɛ muedi baanu-mi taama, na beekeli-mi si bánu-mi.

english_verse: My best friends and loved ones have turned from me.
translation_verse: Mina bakpana geen ƒui muedi ku mina bayɔne béni-mi, na baláwia-mi balanu kunyɔ.

english_verse: I am skin and bones— just barely alive.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ekubi ekubi kani na ndi nkɛ, na ɔɔɔdi ngba na basɔ baalɔ ɔmɛni.

english_verse: My friends, I beg you for pity! God has made me his target.
translation_verse: “Bɛkɛ bɛnu-mi kɔnyana blii o-o, mina bakpana! Katɔti néti nwuna anumi ɔ́lɛ-mi na úbo-mi útáva lɛni.

english_verse: Hasn't he already done enough? Why do you join the attack?
translation_verse: Bi ɔsu na amii lɛnɔ bɛsiaku-mi biikpóku-mi aani Katɔti kalɛ? Bɛnyonu-mi!

english_verse: I wish that my words could be written down
