english_verse: I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me.
translation_verse: Ala amɛni ƒui na lɛ́nu laa kpoo na lɛ́su ka ndubɔda anu na lɛnu lɛla lɛni ɔsu na ala amɛni ese lɛni lɛti, nsu útulo-mi.

english_verse: So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na lɛ́bla kasusu nnii mɔɔtɛya lɛla biala na makana kalɛ na lɛda anu na lɛti lɛla lɛni na ngba bumodi bɔmmɔ bɔdanku. Na lɛti kɔdɔlɔ ku libuokpi lɛni udu nkya likyulikpi bulie taabla lɛnɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for.
translation_verse: Lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka uleku ukpidi ubo ɔdu utulo kukpi. Na úbimi enu ku kayi ƒui úse aani kakpagyuɛ ka uƒie ukyuli. Na ɔnana ɔni mɔɔdi Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ ni, ɔkana na ukeli-nwu. Nsu ukyuli ɔni na uládi-ni lɛlɔ ni, ɔdubo-nwu buƒie aani kakpagyuɛ na ɔyii udu kede kede.

english_verse: With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together,
translation_verse: Ala ɔtinane ɔnini, “Lɛ́sia mina lɛnunda lɛni ƒui na mbo lɛlɔ nnii mɔɔnu kalɛ na ala amɛni ámanku lɛlɔ.

english_verse: but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman.
translation_verse: Nsu lítuku laa lɛ́nɔ. Mmomu lɛ́nu ka na nkyuli apim unwi kemmo ni, bakana na bakɛ ɔnana ɔbuni unwi nsu beleku ama lítuku lɛ́nɔ na ńtakɛ ɔdi na bɔka bɔmɛni kemmo.

english_verse: I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
translation_verse: Lɛla linwi nábla-mi nwaa ƒui ndi ka Katɔti ɔ́bla-bu na nka bɔdi bekyuli siin, nsu búbavumana kasusu bɔ́sia ala bamba pii lɛlɔ na búƒu bula kasusu.”

english_verse: Who is smart enough to explain everything? Wisdom makes you cheerful and gives you a smile. Obey the King
translation_verse: Ɔma mbo lɛlati lɛni na ɔkana lɛla biala kalɔ budie? Lɛnunda lɛɛbla ukyuli anumi nwaa na anumi aaƒɛnimi-nwu.

english_verse: If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise.
translation_verse: Si énye Katɔti anumi ése kenye ka adubɔdi ɔga ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ni, amu mɔɔsu-ɔ kpakplaa nnii di ƒula linyese lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind.
translation_verse: Tababla na akyaku ɔga unyeƒi si ɔ́ɔlɛ nwuna lɛla lɛdi ugyii iye ata enye-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?”
translation_verse: Ɔga litemi lɛdi ɔda bubo na ɔdi ɔɔɔdubo bɔta kalɛ kalɛ na uye-nwu ɔnii bi ɔsu na ɔɔbla lɛla lɛdi na ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it.
translation_verse: Si aabu ɔga ni, eleduo ɔgbankpi kemmo. Anwuɔsu sia anu na ati lɛla lɛni na abla ku uwi ɔni na abla-ni.

english_verse: Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything,
translation_verse: Ngba bulie bubo ukyuli ɔkplu geen nsu lɛla biala bɔbla bubo kalɛ na abla-ni asiaku ku uwi ku kesii kani na babla-ni,

english_verse: though no one can tell the future.
translation_verse: ina ka ukyuli ɔdi ɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛni mebo uwi ɔni ndubo.

english_verse: We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔdi ulakana ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ulu bɔtina iye ɔti nwuna likpimeyi. Na kama busie lɛnɔ buuubo si kekpo kálɛ. Lɛni kani na ɔdi ulakana na wabɛ na nwuna likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla kama.

english_verse: I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another? Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
translation_verse: Lɛ́nu ɔmɛni ƒui lɛ́ti na líti-nwu kasusu kpakplaa na ala ani mɔɔlɛ́ kayawi kamɛni kemmo lɛlɔ. Dɛ na ɔ́bla na ukyuli ɔdi anwu ɔɔkɛ́ ɔyikun ɔdi utulo bakladi na anu ka ɔɔbla kalala?

english_verse: I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense.
translation_verse: Lɛnɔ ni, lɛ́nu kalɛ na baavá bekyuli bekpidi ku ɔbu, nsu Katɔti bekyuli bávi bálɛ ɔma kedee ɔmmɔ kemmo na báyiƒala-ma. Na ɔmɛni lɛnɔ uuubo kalɔ bunu bɔdi.

english_verse: When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime.
translation_verse: Si bɔ́nu kalɛ na bekyuli bekpidi benye baabla likyulikpi ala taasia kama na balakɛ lɛtuni lɛdi ni, na ɔɔbla-bu aani abu lɛnɔ buse kalɔ buteelie ngba bɔmmɔ udu.

english_verse: They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying: Everyone who lives right and respects God will prosper,
translation_verse: Bɔɔnu kalɛ na bekyuli bekpidi bani muulie taabla ekpidi liti liti taasia kama beelie ngba na uwi uutu ina ka nka básu banii bekyuli bani mɔɔsiaku Katɔti kama siin na baabu-nwu na ala adubo bɔtɛku.

english_verse: but no one who sins and rejects God will prosper or live very long.
translation_verse: Na ɔɔɔdi bani muuní-nwu na baabla ekpidi na ala adubo bɔtɛku.

english_verse: There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens.
translation_verse: Lɛla bamba lɛnɔ lɛkya lɛni neeebo kalɔ budie bɔdi. Bekyuli babuni na baabla kalala aani bekyuli bekpidi. Na bekpidi mmomu na baatu lili aani bekyuli babuni.

english_verse: So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na mɔɔtí nwaa ka lɛla bamba lɛdi liiibo liiite ukyuli na ɔbla utulo ka ɔdi adila na ɔni na ebiti ada-nwu asa na ɔkana kayawi kemmo bɔsia bɔlɛ aani lɛla lɛni na Katɔti úte-bu.

english_verse: Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world.
translation_verse: Mɔɔtɛ usien ku ɔƒɛ lɛlɛɛ talɛɛ talɛɛ na muuti kasusu taasiku ala ani ƒui mɔɔlɛ́ na kalɔ kamɛni kemmo lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_verse: Lɛ́nu ala ani ƒui na Katɔti ɔ́bla na lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka ukyuli biala uuubo na wakana-nya kalɔ bunu iye ɔnu lɛla lɛni na ɔ́bla ɔti nwaa kudi kudii ina dɛ na ɔnii ɔ́da anu.

english_verse: I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad.
translation_verse: Ka lɛ́bla kasusu lɛ́siku ala amɛni ƒui lɛlɔ ni, línu kalɔ ka Katɔti ubo ɔyikun na ukyuli biala lɛlɔ, ku abu bani náda anu na bɔsiaku-nwu kama siin lɛnɔ lɛlɔ. Lɛla biala udu lɛkana na lɛlɛku bula akɔ ɔdi biala. Na bulakana bɔti si ngba bɔdubɔtɛku-bu iye bɔdububieku-bu.

english_verse: But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
translation_verse: Lɛlakpa linwi lɛmmɔ kani udu ndubo bɔlɛku bula ƒui na kawɔlɔkɔ. Bɔsiaku na bɔsiaku-nwu kama siin na bɔɔbu-nwu o-o, bɔbu na bulabu-nwu o-o ni, kawɔlɔkɔ kenwi kammɔ kani nse nte-bu. Akpala na bɔɔkyula teete-nwu o-o, bɔkyula na bulakyula adi teete-nwu o-o, si bɔɔdi bula linyese lɛlɔ o-o, buladi-ni lɛlɔ o-o ni, kawɔlɔkɔ kammɔ kani na kadi.

english_verse: It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die.
translation_verse: Nka ubo ɔkplu na ɔɔɔdia ka kɔnyana litemi lɛmɛni udu lɛlɛku bekyuli babuni ku bekpidi ɔsala. Bula ngba uliewi ƒui ni, bɔdi bekyuli bani na bɔ́sɔ na bɔ́dɔlɔ lɛnɔ. Ɔmɛni kemmo kani na bɔɔkya laa na buti bukpi.

english_verse: As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion.
translation_verse: Nsu si bulie ngba bɔdi ni, bɔdubo anumi butaanu ka lɛbuni lɛdi lɛdububo. Ɔsika si ina akpewe ɔni nkya ngba ɔdia utulo gyata ukpine!

english_verse: We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten.
translation_verse: Bayawine bagyi ka badubo bukpi nsu bekpine ama basɔ balasia lɛla lɛdi anu, ɔsika basɔ baaagyi lɛla lɛdi. Na basɔ beeebo lɛyuƒɔla lɛdi lɛnɔ. Na ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ ulényimo-ma muedi.

english_verse: Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
translation_verse: Bana bekyuli bɔyɔ ku bekyuli bukisi ku bana lɛnungyie ƒui ni, békpi bátɔlɔku-ni ɔni bana kɔnu kɔsɔ kulakya kayawi kamɛni lɛla lɛdi bɔbla kemmo.

english_verse: So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do.
translation_verse: Di adila na ani na akya lɛlɔ kubiti, ɔsika Katɔti nése ɔmɛni úse úte ukyuli ɔ́si kukuuku.

english_verse: Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best.
translation_verse: Tada lɛlɔ tese kalɛ kalɛ mmomu da lɛlɔ na egyeli lili na aklibi lɛlɔ kaduɛ.

english_verse: Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth.
translation_verse: Ngba bútene, na ka aayɔ́ ƒ'ulekudi ɔsu ni, bitesie bitaya lɛlɔ. Ɔmɛni na ɔ́lɛka bɛbla na uwi ɔni kemmo na bɛkya kayawi kamɛni kemmo biisusu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
translation_verse: Kabla biala na ɔdi aabla ni, nye-ka lɛlɔ kpakplaa. Ɔsika uwi uletu asa na adubo-ka bɔda búwi na atɔlɔ etéduo kekpine, kesii kani na ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ ulabla kabla kadi iye ulie uteeti kasusu kadi iye ɔti lɛla lɛdi muedi.

english_verse: Here is something else I have learned: The fastest runners and the greatest heroes don't always win races and battles. Wisdom, intelligence, and skill don't always make you healthy, rich, or popular. We each have our own share of misfortune.
translation_verse: Lɛ́nu lɛla bamba lɛnɔ lɛ́ti na kayawi. Ɔɔɔdi bekyuli bani ngyi usi bukeli kaduɛ kani muukeli taadi lɛlɔ. Na ɔɔɔdi bekpone bani ngyi kekpo lɛlɔ ala kani muukpó taadi lɛlɔ. Lɛni kani na ɔɔɔdi banundane kani mɔɔkɛ́ adila abuni taadi. Na ɔɔɔdi bani kasusu kemmo nse nwaa kani muunwíni balakɛne iye bani ngyi bana kabla kadi lɛlɔ ala mɔɔƒɔ́ lɛnyi. Mmomu uwi ku lilidia kuƒi kubunku.

english_verse: None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap. Better To Be Wise than Foolish
translation_verse: Na lɛnɔ ni, ukyuli ɔdi ɔɔɔgyi uwi ɔni na nwuna uwi ɔdubo ubedu. Kalɛ na kabɛ keeduo agyakuo kemmo iye aasɛ ɔɔnú kamia ni, lɛni na uwi ukpidi uubo taabasiaku bekyuli aani kalɛ na baanú kakpagyuɛ.

english_verse: Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me.
translation_verse: Na kayawi mɛni ni, lɛ́nu lɛnunda udu bamba ɔdi lɛnɔ lɛ́ti ɔni néte-mi kasusu geen.

english_verse: It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls.
translation_verse: Úbebo úte uwi ɔdi kemmo, ka ɔma unengudi ɔdi na nkyuli ɛlɛɛ badi kani nkya-nwu kemmo ni, ɔga ɔdi ɔ́ta ka ubekpo ɔma ɔmmɔ. Anwuɔsu nwuna bekpone bábaka bámana-nwu na bábla kunyekɔ ƒui bése ku kɔbɛkɔ kunengudi kesii kani na badubunye na bekpo badi ɔma ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten.
translation_verse: Na ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ɔwabane ɔdi ɔ́kya na ɔ́da anu geen. Na anwu náƒɔ ɔma ɔmmɔ úse na nwuna lɛnunda ɔsu. Nsu útaƒɔ uwi asa na báyiƒala ɔnana ɔmɛni.

english_verse: Words of wisdom spoken softly make much more sense than the shouts of a ruler to a crowd of fools.
translation_verse: Banundane kabɛnsɛ kani baatɛmi ni, kadia kétulo badɔlɔdi batɔnkune kɔvanu.

english_verse: Wisdom is more powerful than weapons, yet one mistake can destroy all the good you have done.
translation_verse: Si ukyuli ubo lɛnunda ni, ɔdia utulo si ada ekpola. Nsu ukyuli ukpidi unwi ɔɔkana na ubile ala abuni pii.

english_verse: A few dead flies in perfume make all of it stink, and a little foolishness outweighs a lot of wisdom.
translation_verse: Kalɛ na si balɔlɔ békpi bákya nnɔmii ƒɛƒɛɛ kemmo na ɔɔyá na nnɔmii bɔmmɔ ɔnyi ɔɔbla buɛ buɛ ni, lɛni na kɔdɔlɔ kɔɔyá na lɛnunda ku ɔbu ɔɔyii udu.

english_verse: Sensible thoughts lead you to do right; foolish thoughts lead you to do wrong.
translation_verse: Banundane kayi kaatɔnku-ma na baabla ala abuni. Lɛni kani na badɔlɔdi kayi kaatɔnku-ma na baabla likpidi.

english_verse: Fools show their stupidity by the way they live; it's easy to see they have no sense.
translation_verse: Si ina ɔgbami na ɔdɔlɔdi ɔkɛ muedi ni, nwuna busie lɛti lɛti bɔɔtina-a kalɛ na ɔ́dɔlɔ.

english_verse: Don't give up your job when your boss gets angry. If you stay calm, you'll be forgiven.
translation_verse: Si ƒula ɔtɔnkune ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi ɔ́kya-a ni, teni ƒula kabla na ada-ka ewi. Ɔsika lɛlɔ kalɔ buboku buɛɛ uutile na uuboku kɔnyi ku ala pii kalɔ.

english_verse: they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
translation_verse: Lɛ́nu ka bekyuli bani nkya bekyuli kudɔ baabla-ma kabla mmomu nlie bapɔnkɔ kama na bagabi bakɛ lɛgba aani ama mmomu ndi kabla bablane.

english_verse: If you dig a pit, you might fall in; if you break down a wall, a snake might bite you.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani muukú libu teese bana bakpana ni, ama alati mɔɔnú-ni kemmo. Lɛni kani na bekyuli bani mɔɔbwɛ kɔwodu taawia kasiakɔ ni, balakpi mɔɔdu-ma.

english_verse: You could even get hurt by chiseling a stone or chopping a log.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔni na atabi na aabwɛ ni, akana na aƒɔ ɔlɛ na ana bɔbwɛ kemmo. Na si egyii lɛnɔ na aabwɛ ni, ɔgbankpi ɔkana na ɔsiaku-ɔ.

english_verse: If you don't sharpen your ax, it will be harder to use; if you are wise, you'll know what to do.
translation_verse: Oloma ɔni neeebo ɔbi ni, amu ntu ébeyi ku ɔyikun momoomo. Nsu si agyi-nwu kemmo ni, adubɔbwɛ lɛla lɛni na aayɔ́ abwɛ.

english_verse: The power to charm a snake does you no good if it bites you anyway.
translation_verse: Si kɔlakpi kɔ́ɔdu ukyuli kɔ́wɔlɔ asa na ukyuli ɔni ngyi bɔkanti ɔnii ɔɔbala-ku bɔdu ni, kekeeke na ɔdi.

english_verse: If you talk sensibly, you will have friends; if you talk foolishly, you will destroy yourself.
translation_verse: Ɔnundane etemila ani mɔɔlɛ́-nwu kenye aatina lɛƒɔndia. Nsu ɔdɔlɔdi etemila mɔɔyila-nwu udu.

english_verse: Fools begin with nonsense, and their stupid chatter ends with disaster.
translation_verse: Badɔlɔdi balabla kasusu si baatɛmi. Na ɔmmɔ muuboku-ma ɔgbankpi na kawɔlɔkɔ.

english_verse: They never tire of talking, but none of us really know what the future will bring.
translation_verse: Na badɔlɔdi bammɔ beemomo atɛ nsu bula ɔdi ɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛni masia. Lɛni kani na bɔɔɔgyi lɛla lɛni ndubo kama.

english_verse: Fools wear themselves out— they don't know enough to find their way home.
translation_verse: Ɔdɔlɔdi kabla ni, lɛlɔ butu bukpludi na bɔdi, ɔsika ɔɔɔgyi ulu ɔni na ɔsia uduo ɔma.

english_verse: A country is in for trouble when its ruler is childish, and its leaders party all day long.
translation_verse: Kalɔ kani ɔtɔnkune mɔɔbla anamula na bɔdi ku bɔni emeyi bɔdi kani na nwuna benengu belie bete ni, bɔbuɛ na beete kalɔ kammɔ.

english_verse: But a nation will prosper when its ruler is mature, and its leaders don't party too much.
translation_verse: Nsu kalɔ kani ɔtɔnkune ndi ukyuli ɔni náni ɔ́kɔ na nwuna benengu baládi taani kani ni, kalɔ kammɔ keesié anumi.

english_verse: Eating and drinking make you feel happy, and money can buy everything you need.
translation_verse: Bɔdi ku bɔni bɔɔyá na lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́ ukyuli geen nsu egulabi mɔɔbla lɛla biala.

english_verse: Don't let yourself think about cursing the king; don't curse the rich, not even in secret. A little bird might hear and tell everything.
translation_verse: Tabɛ takya ƒula ɔtɔ kemmo na ataalɔ ɔga iye ɔlakɛne ɔdi lɛnyi eteedumi na eteewida-nwu. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ aasɛ blii ɔdi úveyi ɔɔví eli na ɔdubuti-ɔ litemi utásu-ma.

english_verse: Be generous, and someday you will be rewarded.
translation_verse: Taabla lɛƒɔndia na adubɔkɛ ƒula lɛyuƒɔla limeyi lɛdi.

english_verse: Share what you have with seven or eight others, because you never know when disaster may strike.
translation_verse: Le lɛla lɛni na ákɛ te nkyuli maatɛ ku maane ƒaa, ɔsika aaagyi limeyi lɛni na ayaki adi adububo ebeyu-ɔ atu.

english_verse: Rain clouds always bring rain; trees always stay wherever they fall.
translation_verse: Si ɔnantu ava bonwu bonwu asia kayaa ni, aana ɔnantu. Na kesii biala na kugyii kɔ́ƒɛ kúsie ni, mmɔ kani na kɔɔtɛ.

english_verse: If you worry about the weather and don't plant seeds, you won't harvest a crop.
translation_verse: Si áyia ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni muukpó ni, alakana edula bɔkya, lɛni kani na si ánu ɔnantu ava na alakana edula bɔƒɛ.

english_verse: No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
translation_verse: Kalɛ na ukyuli ɔɔɔgyi kesii kani na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ uukpó teesie iye kalɛ na kaƒɔ keenwíni ubi na uleku kaƒɔ kemmo ni, lɛni kani na ukyuli ɔdi ulakana Katɔti kalɔ bunu kalɛ na ɔɔbla ala. Anwu nábla ala ƒui.

english_verse: Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce. Youth and Old Age
translation_verse: Nye kabla lɛlɔ kpakplaa na akya edula lɛdigye ku useyi uwi ka aaagyi ani geen ndubo bɔdia iye si ana ƒui madia.

english_verse: Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun.
translation_verse: Lɛla lɛdi liládia bɔnu teetulo ɔtanta ɔƒɛ ɔni nátu ɔdubo.

english_verse: Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
translation_verse: Ina dɛ na élie ábi lɛlɔ ni, ya na lɛlɔ lɛyɔ-ɔ na ƒula ngba emeyi ƒui kemmo. Ɔsika ɔƒɛ ɔdubo ubasa ɔkya-a na asɔ akya lɛdisa lɛmmɔ kemmo na uwi utu. Na kalɔ bunu bɔdi buuubo ɔmɛni kemmo. Bɔlɛ Úte Bakloƒu

english_verse: Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
translation_verse: Lɛlɔ lɛyɔ-ɔ na ƒula lɛkloƒu uwi na enu ngba emini. Na teni lɛbuni biala na ánu iye ƒula kayi kaayɔ́ tete lɛlɔ. Nsu tayiƒala ka Katɔti ɔdubɔtɛku-ɔ litemi na lɛla biala lɛni na ábla lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_verse: Taya na kasusu kekpoku-ɔ na ulu biala lɛlɔ na akya lɛlɔ ɔlɛ, ɔsika lɛkloƒu uwi ala abuni ammɔ adubo abavi ɔƒɛni kani.

english_verse: Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
translation_verse: Taakali ƒula udiene lɛlɔ taanu uwi biala na ƒula lɛkloƒu uwi! Ɔsika uwi ɔdubo ɔni na kayawi ala adubukpi-ɔ ɔkwɛ na etila ani nsia-a lɛlɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: Someday the light of the sun and the moon and the stars will all seem dim to you. Rain clouds will remain over your head.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔdubo ɔni na ɔƒɛ ku kɔbuli ku ayabi bukeye ƒui bɔdubɔbla-a suu. Na kayaa kadubɔbla-a aani ɔnantu kadi na ƒula eli.

english_verse: Your body will grow feeble, your teeth will decay, and your eyesight fail.
translation_verse: Ƒula lɛlɔ ekpo adubɔyɔ na abla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ. Na ƒula kenye anyi ese kalɔ atayii udu. Na ƒula anumi asɔ alanu nwaa.

english_verse: The noisy grinding of grain and the voices of singers will be shut out by your deaf ears, but even the song of a bird will keep you awake.
translation_verse: Ƒula atu asɔ aaadubo buteenu kaduɛ na ina kukɔ mɔɔkɔ́ ala muedi asɔ elénu. Nsu aasɛ ɔnu budie muedi bɔdubɔya na ekeyi lɛlɔ agyinya.

english_verse: You will be afraid to climb up a hill or walk down a road. Your hair will turn as white as almond blossoms. You will feel lifeless and drag along like an old grasshopper. We each go to our eternal home, and the streets here are filled with those who mourn.
translation_verse: Adubo butaayia ina lɛbinkpo na aakɔ́ iye bɔyu na ada ulu ɔni nénwini ɔ́yu. Ƒula lili linwini lɛdubɔta lɛƒuala aani kɔdingyii anwula ƒuala ƒuala. Na adubɔkɛ ataakpɛ lɛgba kalɔ aani kɔɔgyu kɔni náabi na ɔɔyɔ́ ɔvumana livuo. Bula ƒui bɔdubɔsɔ bunwini busie bula kasikɔ na bekyuli bani muuwulo-bu baƒɔ lɛblɔnu lɛmmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The silver cord snaps, the golden bowl breaks; the water pitcher is smashed, and the pulley at the well is shattered.
translation_verse: Nyimo ƒula Udiene asa na lɛkun lɛni nda-a aani ɔkun mmɔ ukulo iye sika ugyiedi lɛkyami lɛni náƒɔ-ɔ kuye mmɔ lɛbwɛ, iye ƒula ketubui kabwɛ iye ɔbuli ɔni na eeti taani ntu taalɛku libiɔ kemmo mmɔ ukulo.

english_verse: So our bodies return to the earth, and the life-giving breath returns to God.
translation_verse: Lɛni na bula ɔlɔna ɔɔsɔ teenwini teesie kalɔ kemmo na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni nkya-bu lɛlɔ kemmo uute-bu ngba mmɔ ɔsɔ uunwíni teesie Katɔti kudɔ.

english_verse: Nothing makes sense. I have seen it all— nothing makes sense. Respect and Obey God
translation_verse: Ami lɛ́ɛnu lɛ́ti ka lɛla lɛdi liiibo kalɔ bunu bɔdi.

english_verse: I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied.
translation_verse: Ndi ala ɔtinane ɔni muunú ala kalɔ geen na lɛ́da anu na lɛ́sala agba adi na líduo mu kemmo kaduɛ.

english_verse: Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama lɛ́kya ɔkplu na lídie-mu kalɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kalɛ na ɔ́manku.

english_verse: Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together.
translation_verse: Lɛnunda etemila ese aani ugyii ɔni na umonsene uuti taakpanku nwuna bebuo. Asugba amɛni ási Katɔti ɔlati kudɔ na ese kɔbuɛlɛ ani na beeti taakana ligyii taadanku lɛlɔ.

english_verse: My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these. There is no end to books, and too much study will wear you out.
translation_verse: Ubi, mɔɔlɛ-ɔ kpakplaa nnii die ala bɔtina bamba biala atu na eti bɔmɛni kani. Lɛku liiibo kawɔlɔkɔ. Na ala ƒui bulie taatɛya lɛnɔ ɔɔyá na ukyuli ɔɔyii udu.

english_verse: Everything you were taught can be put into a few words: Respect and obey God! This is what life is all about.
translation_verse: Ala ani ƒui na bátina-a ni, akana na asala-nya akya etemila klo klo amɛni kemmo anini, “Di Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ na abu-nwu. Lɛla lɛni ƒui na ngba bumodi bɔmmɔ bɔdanku kani na lɛdi mmɔ.”

english_verse: God will judge everything we do, even what is done in secret, whether good or bad.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔdubɔtɛku-bu litemi na lɛla biala na ukyuli ɔ́bla lɛlɔ ina bɔbɛ na ábɛ ábla-nya na adi likpidi iye lɛbuni.

english_verse: This is Solomon's most beautiful song. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Salomo lɛnu ƒui ɔnu ɔni na ɔ́nwi na bɔdubo bunu mɛni.

english_verse: Kiss me tenderly! Your love is better than wine,
translation_verse: Bo na abakya-mi kɔgbu na ada-mi amana lɛlɔ. Ɔsika ƒula bɔyɔ bɔɔyɔ́ kayi teetulo ntɛ.

english_verse: and you smell so sweet. All the young women adore you; the very mention of your name is like spreading perfume. *
translation_verse: Ebo ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔdi ɔni na si línu ka ɔdi ɔ́kpali-ɔ lɛnyi ni, na ɔnyi ɔmmɔ kani na muunú. Na unyeƒi ɔdi uuubo-nwu kemmo ka ɔmmɔ ɔsu geen na begblebi ƒui baayɔ́-ɔ!

english_verse: Hurry, my king! Let's hurry. Take me to your home. The Young Women Speak: We are happy for you! And we praise your love even more than wine. She Speaks: Young women of Jerusalem, it is only right that you should adore him.
translation_verse: Kpanku-mi da na bɔtɔlɔ pla! Na awɔ ɔga eti-mi eduoku ƒula kɔtɔma. Lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́-bu na ƒula lɛlɔ. Na kalɛ na aayɔ́ bekyuli ubo emini utulo ntɛ mini mini. Ɔdia geen ka bemwi-ɔ.

english_verse: My skin is dark and beautiful, like a tent in the desert or like Solomon's curtains.
translation_verse: Yerusalem beleku, ɔlɔgyii otondi na ɔdi-mi, nsu mɔɔdia bɔnu geen. Na nse aani kevo kani na bátu bényene Kedar ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo iye Salomo kayakun aduni abuni ammɔ adi.

english_verse: Don't stare at me just because the sun has darkened my skin. My brothers were angry with me; they made me work in the vineyard, and so I neglected my complexion.
translation_verse: Bitanu-mi ɔnusɛ bɛnii lɛ́sɔ ka ɔƒɛ ɔ́ya na mina ɔlɔgyii ɔdi otondi ɔsu. Mina benibi bananabi béti kɔnyi bákya-mi na báya na mɔɔbla kabla na adingyii kemo na lídie mina ɔlɔna atu na nsɔ lɛɛɛdaku-nwu lɛda.

english_verse: My dearest, if you don't know, just follow the path of the sheep. Then feed your young goats near the shepherds' tents.
translation_verse: Beleku babuni ƒui ɔbuni, bɔsu na ada anii aaagyi kesii kammɔ? Amu ni, Ɔyɔne, siaku baƒonu bammɔ agyobi kanyakɔ na etiku ƒula bese na batádi na baƒonu badane nvo anumi.

english_verse: You move as gracefully as the pony that leads the chariot of the king.
translation_verse: Aanya kalɔ ligblebi kemmo aani ɔpɔnkɔ ɔni mɔɔní Ɔga Ƒarao kɛɛkɛ.

english_verse: Earrings add to your beauty, and you wear a necklace of precious stones.
translation_verse: Asɛɛ ebi ani nkya-a atu ku kɔsɛɛ kɔni na akya ɔkwɛ áya na ƒula litugya liikeye na aadia bɔnu geen.

english_verse: Let's make you some jewelry of gold, woven with silver. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Nsu bɔdubɔvɔ sika ugyiedi asɛɛ ebi ani na akya atu bute-ɔ na bɔkya-nwu bɔdia ku sika ɔƒualadi.

english_verse: My king, while you were on your couch, my aroma was a magic charm.
translation_verse: Mina ɔga, uwi ɔni na elie kadikɔ na ƒula liboku kemmo ni, mina ugyulo ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ɔnyi ɔ́ƒɔ ntɛ mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: My darling, you are perfume between my breasts;
translation_verse: Mina ɔyɔne use ute-mi aani ugyulo ɔni baalɔ nard ɔsii na ɔtɛ-mi anyii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: you are flower blossoms from the gardens of En-Gedi. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Na úlieku egyii anwula abuni ani muudie ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ taasiku egyiibi kemo na kesii kani baalɔ En-Gedi.

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— your eyes are those of a dove. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ɔbuni, ése álɛ ligblebi na aadia bɔnu geen. Na ƒula anumi eekeyi aani lɛmangbɛ.

english_verse: My love, you are handsome, truly handsome— the fresh green grass will be our wedding bed
translation_verse: Ɔyɔne, lɛni na álɛ lɛkloƒu geen ɔni na balásu. Livo lɛwɔdi lɛni mɔɔlɛ́ wɔwɔɔwɔ, mmɔ ndubɔbla bula katɛnkɔ si búti lɛlɔ.

english_verse: in the shade of cedar and cypress trees.
translation_verse: Kesii kani na bɔkya ni, egyii enengudi ani nnye mmɔ ákya ɔyuli.

english_verse: I am merely a rose from the land of Sharon, a lily from the valley. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Buse na mina ligblebi lise aani eveteli ku anwula gyie gyie ani nálɛ enye sɛsɛɛ na Saron kalɔ lɛlɔ, na nsɔ nse aani eveteli ku anwula ƒuala ƒuala na ɔkwalɛ ɔdi kemmo.

english_verse: My darling, when compared with other young women, you are a lily among thorns. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ɔbuni, si banii beti-ɔ bakɔku begblebi bamba ni, ese aani eveteli ku anwula ƒuala ƒuala ani nédie lɛlɔ sɛsɛɛ na liyu alakpi akɔ.

english_verse: And you, my love, are an apple tree among trees of the forest. Your shade brought me pleasure; your fruit was sweet.
translation_verse: Na awɔ ni, mina Ɔyɔne, lɛni na álɛ salalaa aani kɔdingyii na lɛku kemmo egyii akɔ si béti-ɔ bákɔku banana bamba. Na ƒula ɔyuli ɔni na ákya-mi ɔ́ya na lɛ́nwuna buɛɛ. Na ƒula ebi ani na éte-mi na lɛ́di áyu-mi emini geen.

english_verse: You led me to your banquet room and showered me with love.
translation_verse: Átɔnku-mi éduoku ƒula ɔtɔ bonwu ɔni kemmo na aadi ƒula limeyi bɔdi adila. Na mmɔ nédie ƒula bɔyɔ átina-mi.

english_verse: Refresh and strengthen me with raisins and apples. I am hungry for love!
translation_verse: Te-mi ƒula egyiibi buni lidu lidu lɛmmɔ na asɔku-mi abla ɔwɔdi na lɛkɛ ɔyikun ɔwɔdi, ɔsika ƒula bɔyɔ kɔka kɔɔda-mi na lɛ́bla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: Put your left hand under my head and embrace me with your right arm.
translation_verse: Ti ƒula kɔmiinu kɔnu kya-mi lili kalɔ na eti ƒula kɔdianu kɔnu abala-mi kayi.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles never to awaken love before it is ready. Winter Is Past She Speaks:
translation_verse: Yerusalem begblebi, muubó-mii ɔda ɔkɛnku bakwa ku bete ɔyikun lɛlɔ, na bise-mi kenye ka bɛɛɛdubo busie butágyila tɔ bɔyɔ wetédu ka uwi údu ka ulu ɔ́lɛmi úte bɔyɔ bɔmmɔ alati.

english_verse: I hear the voice of the one I love, as he comes leaping over mountains and hills
translation_verse: Muunú mina ɔyɔne kɔku ka ɔ́si ɔdubo na ɔkɛ ɔɔba agyu taavia abi ku abinkpo.

english_verse: like a deer or a gazelle. Now he stands outside our wall, looking through the window
translation_verse: Ɔkɛ aani akwa iye kete ɔdubo. Na ɔƒaani ni, unye kowodu kama na ɔɔnu taavinku ƒansili.

english_verse: Winter is past, the rain has stopped;
translation_verse: Nu, ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ku ɔnantu uwi ɔ́ɔvi,

english_verse: flowers cover the earth, it's time to sing. The cooing of doves is heard in our land.
translation_verse: na egyii anwula lidu áƒɔ kayawi ƒui, na ɔdi lɛlɔyɔ uwi ute ala ƒui ku lɛnu budie. Na beenú bamangbɛ kudu bɔbla na aku kemmo.

english_verse: Fig trees are bearing fruit, while blossoms on grapevines fill the air with perfume. My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
translation_verse: Anwingyie eesé kalɔ ku bɔnwu na egyiibi anwula ɔnyi ɔmmɔ ɔɔƒɔ́ kayaa ƒui aani ugyulo ƒɛƒɛɛ. Ɔbuni, mɔɔyɔ́-ɔ geen! Anwuɔsu ya na bula inyɔ bɔtɔlɔ.”

english_verse: You are my dove hiding among the rocks on the side of a cliff. Let me see how lovely you are! Let me hear the sound of your melodious voice.
translation_verse: Ese ete-mi aani mina lɛmangbɛ lɛni nábɛla lɛlɔ ɔkya atabi ubu kemmo na lɛtakpɛ bonwu lɛni nƒa kemmo. Nwini na aya na lɛsɔ lɛnu ƒula bɔdia! Na aya na linu ƒula lɛdi mini mini lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: Our vineyards are in blossom; we must catch the little foxes that destroy the vineyards. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Bula adingyii ebi kemo kani na búse éwi anwula, anwuɔsu ɔlɛka buƒie beƒukutu bani nkya muubile kemo kammɔ edula.

english_verse: My darling, I am yours, and you are mine, as you feed your sheep among the lilies.
translation_verse: Mina Ɔyɔne, awɔ ɔni mɔɔnyuɛ ƒula baƒonu na eveteli ani nédie anwula akɔ, awɔ mbo-mi na ami lɛnɔ mbo-ɔ.

english_verse: Pretend to be a young deer dancing on mountain slopes until daylight comes and shadows fade away.
translation_verse: Bla lɛlɔ aani akwa ɔkɔdi ɔni nnye abi lɛlɔ ɔɔƒulu ku lɛlɔyɔ úti útédu uwi ɔni na kadi kadubugye na ala ɔyuli ɔ́yii ɔkya.

english_verse: While in bed at night, I reached for the one I love with heart and soul. I looked for him, but he wasn't there.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bɔtɛ usien ni, lísienku kɔnu nnii muutúku mina ɔyɔne ɔni na mɔɔyɔ́ ku mina kayi ku kɔyu ƒui. Nsu ɔɔɔtɛ, anwuɔsu líbo kɔnu lɛ́nɔ na ńtanu-nwu.

english_verse: So I searched through the town for the one I love. I looked on every street, but he wasn't there.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu lɛ́ta ńtávi ɔma kemmo lɛ́wia-nwu na lɛblɔnu ƒui lɛlɔ, nsu ńtanu-nwu.

english_verse: I even asked the guards patrolling the town, “Have you seen the one I love so much?”
translation_verse: Líye bagyumane bani nkɛ mɔɔkɔ́ taayu na ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo muedi nnini, “Bɛ́nu ukyuli ɔni na mɔɔyɔ́ ku mina kayi ku kɔyu ƒui mmɔ?”

english_verse: Right after that, I found him. I held him and would not let go until I had taken him to the home of my mother.
translation_verse: Nsu mina mmɔ bɔgyu ku tagyu kani na lɛ́nu-nwu na lɛ́tu lɛ́da-nwu, na ńtanyonu-nwu úti útédu uwi ɔni na lɛ́kpanku-nwu lísienku mina uni kaduli, na búduo ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na báwɔ-mi.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles, never to awaken love before it is ready. The Groom and the Wedding Party Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Yerusalem begblebi, muubó-mii ɔda ɔkɛnku bakwa ku bete ɔyikun lɛlɔ, na bise-mi kenye ka bɛɛɛdubo busie butágyila tɔ bɔyɔ wetédu ka uwi údu ka ulu ɔ́lɛmi úte bɔyɔ bɔmmɔ alati.

english_verse: What do we see approaching from the desert like a cloud of smoke? With it comes the sweet smell of spices, including myrrh and frankincense.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔmani na bɔɔnu ka ɔ́si kalɔ kakwiidi lɛlɔ ɔdubo mɛni aani liƒlukutu uyɔ ɔdi udu? Uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔdanku nard ugyulo ku oloƒui ku kutu akyala ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔnyi.

english_verse: It is King Solomon carried on a throne, surrounded by sixty of Israel's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Bɛnu! Salomo na ɔdi na badanku badububoku na uli nwuna lɛgaboku lɛlɔ, na Israelƒuɔ bekpone benengudi ƒui liti ku leevu báka bámana-nwu.

english_verse: Each of them wears a sword. They are experts at fighting, even in the dark.
translation_verse: Kewii kama ɔdi biala ligu. Na badi bekyuli bani na kekpo káma-ma enu ɔni na usien muedi benye kagyumana bete lɛla biala.

english_verse: The throne is made of trees from Lebanon.
translation_verse: Lebanon egyii na béti bánwi lɛga boku lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: Its posts are silver, the back is gold, and the seat is covered with purple cloth. You women of Jerusalem have taken great care to furnish the inside.
translation_verse: Liboku lɛmmɔ lɛgba lɛdi sika ɔƒualadi na nina kama kekpokɔ kadi sika ugyiedi. Na liboku lɛmmɔ alati egu keliekɔ geen ni, kɔdi kugyiedi kɔni náƒɔ kuye geen na béti bébi keliekɔ kammɔ. Na kalɛ na ayu eduo liboku lɛmmɔ kemmo alati na elie kalɔ ni, Yerusalemƒuɔ beleku bése béwi lɛlɔ buɛɛ geen bákya-ni bɔdia.

english_verse: Now come and see the crown given to Solomon by his mother on his happy wedding day.
translation_verse: Bɛlɛ bibo amii Sion belekubi na bibanu kagabwa kani na Salomo uni úte-nwu na nwuna uleku buti limeyi bɔdi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— as you look through your veil, your eyes are those of a dove. Your hair tosses about as gracefully as goats coming down from Gilead.
translation_verse: Ɔbuni, ése álɛ ligblebi geen si mɔɔnu-ɔ taavinku ƒula lɛduni lɛni mbi-ɔ anumi mmɔ kemmo. Ƒula anumi eekeye aani lɛmangbɛ. Na ƒula linwini liibó ɔƒɛƒɛɛ aani kalɛ na bese pii baasí taayu Gilead abi.

english_verse: Your teeth are whiter than sheep freshly washed; they match perfectly, not one is missing.
translation_verse: Na ƒula kenye anyi ása-a kenye kemmo na eekeye ƒututuu aani koƒonu kɔni na bákpila-ku ntu ɔƒɛni kani.

english_verse: Your neck is more graceful than the tower of David, decorated with thousands of warriors' shields.
translation_verse: Ƒula limɔ lɛ́lɛ sɛsɛɛ ku aka ku bɔdia aani Salomo katutaasia kagyumanakɔ kani na ɔ́tu. Na agyumanala ani mɔɔgyumana bekpone mpim mpim ada-a limɔ.

english_verse: Your breasts are perfect; they are twin deer feeding among lilies.
translation_verse: Ƒula anyii ani nnye-ɔ kayi ése aadia bɔnu aani bakwa bakɔdi inyɔ bani na benye baadi na eveteli ku anwula ƒualaƒuala akɔ.

english_verse: I will hasten to those hills sprinkled with sweet perfume and stay there till sunrise.
translation_verse: Ndubɔbabla lɛkɔ lisie abi ani lɛlɔ na kutu akyala ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔ́ƒɔ mmɔ ƒui asa na kadi kada kebewi nwaa.

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely in every way.
translation_verse: Ɔbuni, álɛ ligblebi na ulu biala lɛlɔ.

english_verse: My bride, together we will leave Lebanon! We will say goodbye to the peaks of Mount Amana, Senir, and Hermon, where lions and leopards live in the caves.
translation_verse: Mina uleku uveledi, ami ku awɔ ƒui bɔdubo bɔtɔlɔ Lebanon mɛni! Na bɔdubuƒwimi enu na bɔsu Amana ku Senir ku Hermon abi kesii kani bagyata ku bebuoƒuala bakya atakpɛ ubu kemmo bɔnii bɔ́tɔlɔ.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, you have stolen my heart! With one glance from your eyes and the glow of your necklace, you have stolen my heart.
translation_verse: Ami ɔlati mina uleku uveledi, ƒula anumi ani na ánu-mi lɛti pɛ áda-mi kayi geen! Na sika asɛɛ ani na akya ɔkwɛ bukeye bɔ́ya na mina kayi kénwini kasia-a lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Your love is sweeter than wine; the smell of your perfume is more fragrant than spices.
translation_verse: Ƒula bɔyɔ bɔɔyu kayi teetulo ntɛ. Na ƒula ugyulo ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni na áwɛɛ ɔnyi utulo kutu akyala ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni na uudie.

english_verse: Your lips are a honeycomb; milk and honey flow from your tongue. Your dress has the aroma of cedar trees from Lebanon.
translation_verse: Ƒula enyekuli ese aani uwɔ kɔtakɛ, na bebuo anyii ntu ku uwɔ mɔɔyu taasi ƒula unyemi lɛlɔ. Na ƒula adala eedie ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ aani Lebanon egyii ani muudie ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, you are a garden, a fountain closed off to all others.
translation_verse: Ami ɔlati mina uleku uveledi, ese aani kevoma kemo iye libiɔ lɛgyumanadi lɛni na ukyuli bamba ɔdi ulakana bɔta budu kalɛ kalɛ.

english_verse: Your arms are vines, covered with delicious fruits and all sorts of spices— henna, nard,
translation_verse: Na aanwu egyiibi mini mini ku kutu akyala ku ugyulo ebi pii ani baabla ugyulo ɔni baalɔ hena ku nard,

english_verse: You are a spring in the garden, a fountain of pure water, and a refreshing stream from Mount Lebanon. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Libiɔ lɛni mɔɔyu ntu buni geen na adi na kevoma kemo kammɔ kemmo. Na álɛ ási Lebanon abi lɛlɔ na adi ntu bɔni mɔɔyu kayi geen.

english_verse: Let the north wind blow, the south wind too! Let them spread the aroma of my garden, so the one I love may enter and taste its delicious fruits.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ukpo ɔsi katɔ ku kada kakɛ ƒui na ugyingya mina ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni muudie taasiku mina kemo kammɔ kemmo na ɔƒɔ kesi kesii. Na mina ɔyɔne uduo-mi lɛlɔ aani kemo kalɛ na utu egyiibi mini mini ammɔ unyemi ɔnu kalɛ na mbo emini sɔsɔ.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, I come to my garden and enjoy its spices. I eat my honeycomb and honey; I drink my wine and milk. Their Friends Speak: Eat and drink until you are drunk with love. Another Dream She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ami ɔlati mina uleku uveledi, líbo-ɔ kudɔ aani ami ɔlati mina kemo na mbadi ala mini mini ammɔ. Ndubɔƒiɔ mina uwɔ kɔtakɛ na lɛni uwɔ ɔmmɔ. Ndubɔni mina ntɛ ku mina bebuo anyii ntu bɔmmɔ. Mina bakpana, bɛdi na bɛni utédu uwi ɔni na bɔyɔ bɔmmɔ búmo-mii.

english_verse: I was asleep, but dreaming: The one I love was at the door, knocking and saying, “My darling, my very own, my flawless dove, open the door for me! My head is drenched with evening dew.”
translation_verse: Ntɛ mɔɔlɛɛ, nsu mina kayi kenye kagyumana, na muugyé kɔna ka mina ɔyɔne úbo únye kayakun uubó-mi kɔnu taasu-mi ɔnini, “Mina kayi ku ɔyɔne, mina lɛmangbɛ ɔni na lɛla lɛdi lítebie-nwu lɛlɔ, lɛmi kayakun te-mi! Amii ani náyu usien umodi ɔmmɔ áƒɔ-mi lili.”

english_verse: But I had already undressed and bathed my feet. Should I dress again and get my feet dirty?
translation_verse: Nka lɛ́ɛƒɔ lɛgba na lídie mina adala ƒui líse. Buti na nsɔ ndubo mina adala buti bɔkya, na aba asɔ etuku-mi lɛgba?

english_verse: Then my darling's hand reached to open the latch, and my heart stood still.
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani na lɛ́ti ka mina ɔyɔne ɔ́kya kɔnu kegbuta kama na údie ugyii ɔni na líti lɛ́bala kayakun mmɔ, na ɔ́bla-mi aani mina utu ɔ́da bubo ɔ́ya.

english_verse: When I rose to open the door, my hands and my fingers dripped with perfume.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na lɛ́ta lɛ́da kayakun kalɛmikɔ kammɔ nnii mɔɔlɛmi ɔtɔ lite mina ɔyɔne ni, ugyulo nnɔmii ƒɛƒɛɛ kani mɔɔyu-mi kɔnu ku animi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: And I yearned for him while he spoke to me, but when I opened the door, my darling had disappeared. I searched and shouted, but I could not find him— there was no answer.
translation_verse: Na ka unye ɔɔtɛmiku-mi ni, ɔ́bla-mi aani mina utu ɔ́da bubo ɔ́ya. Nsu ka lɛ́lɛmi ɔtɔ ni, mina ɔyɔne ɔ́yii-mi anumi kɔnakunwi na lɛ́sɔ ńtanu-nwu. Lɛni na ɔ́bla aani mina utu bɔnu na ɔ́nu úduo-mi kaƒɔ ɔni na lɛ́wia-nwu laa na mɔɔva taakpali-nwu taanɔ.

english_verse: Then I was found by the guards patrolling the town and guarding the wall. They beat me up and stripped off my robe.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na usien bagyumanane bani nkɛ mɔɔkɔ́ taayu ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo bénu-mi kɔku. Na béƒie-mi na bébo-mi na bákya-mi ɔlɛ lɛlɔ na bédie-mi kɔdi kɔni na mbi-mi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, if you find the one I love, please say to him, “She is weak with desire.” Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Yerusalem begblebi, mɔɔsu-mii kpakplaa nnii si bɛ́nu mina ɔyɔne ni, bɛsu-nwu bɛnii nwuna bɔyɔ bɔɔda-mi na lɛ́bla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: Most beautiful of women, why is the one you love more special than others? Why do you ask us to tell him how you feel? She Speaks:
translation_verse: O begblebi ƒui ugblebi, bi ɔsu na ƒula ɔyɔne lɛlɔ libo-ɔ kubiti lɛni utulo ukyuli bamba biala? Na bi ɔsu na aatala-bu akya-nwu anii bɔsu-nwu kalɛ na ƒula kayi kaabla-a na nwuna lɛlɔ?

english_verse: He is handsome and healthy, the most outstanding among ten thousand.
translation_verse: Na nkyuli mpim leevu akɔ ni, anwu nálɛ-mi lɛkloƒu utulo na ɔɔdia bɔnu na ubo ɔlɔkplu geen.

english_verse: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy, black as a raven.
translation_verse: Nwuna lili lɛ́ƒɔ-mi kuye litulo sika ugyiedi ɔni ndia utulo ƒui. Na linwini ƒuku ƒuku liwi-nwu lili na lise totonto aani aasɛ otondi.

english_verse: His eyes are a pair of doves bathing in a stream flowing with milk.
translation_verse: Na uukeye aani lɛmangbɛ lɛni nákpi ntu, na unye libiɔ kɔtu aani sika ugyiedi asɛɛ, na béti báklibi-nwu, na nwuna anumi ebi eekeye aani bebuo anyi ntu.

english_verse: His arms are branches of gold covered with jewels; his body is ivory decorated with sapphires.
translation_verse: Na nwuna enu ese aani kugyii kɔgba kɔni na béti sika ugyiedi bákya-nwu bɔdia ku asɛɛ ani na áƒɔ kuye. Na nwuna ɔlɔgyii umodi use aani atu ɔtunkpɛ.

english_verse: His legs are columns of marble on feet of gold. He stands there majestic like Mount Lebanon and its choice cedar trees.
translation_verse: Na nwuna lɛgba lise aani ɔtɔ akpa ani lɛlɔ na bámana atabi ani náƒɔ kuye na eekeye geen na enye sika ugyiedi atabi lɛlɔ. Na unye lɛgadi kemmo aani Lebanon Kɔbi ku kuna egyii kpakplaa ani nálɛ lili enye bonwu bonwu.

english_verse: His kisses are sweet. I desire him so much! Young women of Jerusalem, he is my lover and friend.
translation_verse: Kalɛ na ɔɔkya-mi kɔgbu ɔɔyu-mi kayi geen, na mɔɔwia-nwu lɛni uwi biala kemmo!

english_verse: My bride, my very own, I come to my garden and enjoy its spices. I eat my honeycomb and honey; I drink my wine and milk. Their Friends Speak: Eat and drink until you are drunk with love. Another Dream She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ami ɔlati mina uleku uveledi, líbo-ɔ kudɔ aani ami ɔlati mina kemo na mbadi ala mini mini ammɔ. Ndubɔƒiɔ mina uwɔ kɔtakɛ na lɛni uwɔ ɔmmɔ. Ndubɔni mina ntɛ ku mina bebuo anyii ntu bɔmmɔ. Mina bakpana, bɛdi na bɛni utédu uwi ɔni na bɔyɔ bɔmmɔ búmo-mii.

english_verse: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy, black as a raven.
translation_verse: Nwuna lili lɛ́ƒɔ-mi kuye litulo sika ugyiedi ɔni ndia utulo ƒui. Na linwini ƒuku ƒuku liwi-nwu lili na lise totonto aani aasɛ otondi.

english_verse: His eyes are a pair of doves bathing in a stream flowing with milk.
translation_verse: Na uukeye aani lɛmangbɛ lɛni nákpi ntu, na unye libiɔ kɔtu aani sika ugyiedi asɛɛ, na béti báklibi-nwu, na nwuna anumi ebi eekeye aani bebuo anyi ntu.

english_verse: His arms are branches of gold covered with jewels; his body is ivory decorated with sapphires.
translation_verse: Na nwuna enu ese aani kugyii kɔgba kɔni na béti sika ugyiedi bákya-nwu bɔdia ku asɛɛ ani na áƒɔ kuye. Na nwuna ɔlɔgyii umodi use aani atu ɔtunkpɛ.

english_verse: His legs are columns of marble on feet of gold. He stands there majestic like Mount Lebanon and its choice cedar trees.
translation_verse: Na nwuna lɛgba lise aani ɔtɔ akpa ani lɛlɔ na bámana atabi ani náƒɔ kuye na eekeye geen na enye sika ugyiedi atabi lɛlɔ. Na unye lɛgadi kemmo aani Lebanon Kɔbi ku kuna egyii kpakplaa ani nálɛ lili enye bonwu bonwu.

english_verse: His kisses are sweet. I desire him so much! Young women of Jerusalem, he is my lover and friend.
translation_verse: Kalɛ na ɔɔkya-mi kɔgbu ɔɔyu-mi kayi geen, na mɔɔwia-nwu lɛni uwi biala kemmo!

english_verse: My bride, my very own, I come to my garden and enjoy its spices. I eat my honeycomb and honey; I drink my wine and milk. Their Friends Speak: Eat and drink until you are drunk with love. Another Dream She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ami ɔlati mina uleku uveledi, líbo-ɔ kudɔ aani ami ɔlati mina kemo na mbadi ala mini mini ammɔ. Ndubɔƒiɔ mina uwɔ kɔtakɛ na lɛni uwɔ ɔmmɔ. Ndubɔni mina ntɛ ku mina bebuo anyii ntu bɔmmɔ. Mina bakpana, bɛdi na bɛni utédu uwi ɔni na bɔyɔ bɔmmɔ búmo-mii.

english_verse: I was asleep, but dreaming: The one I love was at the door, knocking and saying, “My darling, my very own, my flawless dove, open the door for me! My head is drenched with evening dew.”
translation_verse: Ntɛ mɔɔlɛɛ, nsu mina kayi kenye kagyumana, na muugyé kɔna ka mina ɔyɔne úbo únye kayakun uubó-mi kɔnu taasu-mi ɔnini, “Mina kayi ku ɔyɔne, mina lɛmangbɛ ɔni na lɛla lɛdi lítebie-nwu lɛlɔ, lɛmi kayakun te-mi! Amii ani náyu usien umodi ɔmmɔ áƒɔ-mi lili.”

english_verse: But I had already undressed and bathed my feet. Should I dress again and get my feet dirty?
translation_verse: Nka lɛ́ɛƒɔ lɛgba na lídie mina adala ƒui líse. Buti na nsɔ ndubo mina adala buti bɔkya, na aba asɔ etuku-mi lɛgba?

english_verse: Then my darling's hand reached to open the latch, and my heart stood still.
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani na lɛ́ti ka mina ɔyɔne ɔ́kya kɔnu kegbuta kama na údie ugyii ɔni na líti lɛ́bala kayakun mmɔ, na ɔ́bla-mi aani mina utu ɔ́da bubo ɔ́ya.

english_verse: When I rose to open the door, my hands and my fingers dripped with perfume.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na lɛ́ta lɛ́da kayakun kalɛmikɔ kammɔ nnii mɔɔlɛmi ɔtɔ lite mina ɔyɔne ni, ugyulo nnɔmii ƒɛƒɛɛ kani mɔɔyu-mi kɔnu ku animi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: And I yearned for him while he spoke to me, but when I opened the door, my darling had disappeared. I searched and shouted, but I could not find him— there was no answer.

english_verse: Then I was found by the guards patrolling the town and guarding the wall. They beat me up and stripped off my robe.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, if you find the one I love, please say to him, “She is weak with desire.” Their Friends Speak:

english_verse: But I had already undressed and bathed my feet. Should I dress again and get my feet dirty?

english_verse: Then I was found by the guards patrolling the town and guarding the wall. They beat me up and stripped off my robe.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, if you find the one I love, please say to him, “She is weak with desire.” Their Friends Speak:

english_verse: I am his, and he is mine, as he feeds his sheep among the lilies. He Speaks:

english_verse: My dearest, the cities of Tirzah and Jerusalem are not as lovely as you. Your charms are more powerful than all of the stars in the heavens.
translation_verse: Mina kayi, Tirsa ku Yerusalem lɛma linengudi ƒui liládia bɔnu aani awɔ. Na kalɛ na ƒula bɔdia bɔɔda-mi kayi utulo ayabi ani nkya katɔ ƒui bukeye.

english_verse: Turn away your eyes— they make me melt. Your hair tosses about as gracefully as goats coming down from Gilead.
translation_verse: Na si áda ƒula anumi édie-mi lɛlɔ uwi klukwii ɔdi kani na use-mi aani ogya lɛlɔ na básia-mi na mɔɔyɛlɛ. Ƒula lili linwini liibó ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ku lɛlɔyɔ aani bese pii badi náyu bási Gilead kɔbi lɛlɔ badubo ku ebiti.

english_verse: Your teeth are whiter than sheep freshly washed; they match perfectly, not one is missing.
translation_verse: Ƒula kenye anyi ása-a kenye na eekeye aani koƒonu kɔni na bákpila-ku ntu ɔƒɛni kani.

english_verse: What if I could have sixty queens, eighty wives, and thousands of others!
translation_verse: Ina beleku baga liti ku leevu iye basɔnɔ liti ku avlaatɛ iye begblebi bani na balakana-ma bɔka nébo benye-mi anumi muedi ni, neeeti bana ɔdi naaakɔku-ɔ!

english_verse: You would be my only choice, my flawless dove, the favorite child of your mother. The young women, the queens, and all the others tell how excited you are as they sing your praises:
translation_verse: Awɔ kani na ndubo bɔƒuna. Awɔ ndi mina lɛmangbɛ lɛni na lɛla lɛdi lítebie-ɔ kesii kadi. Ƒula uwele ɔ́ƒuna-a ɔ́wɔ geen. Ƒula bɔdia búnwini ɔnu na begblebi ku beleku baga ku bakladi ƒui beedie teemwi kalɛ na ese.

english_verse: “You are as majestic as the morning sky— glorious as the moon— blinding as the sun! Your charms are more powerful than all the stars above.” She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ése álɛ ligblebi ku bukeye aani kalɛ na ɔtanta kayaa kese. Na eekeye aani kɔbuli. Na aatu anumi aani ɔƒɛ bukeye! Na ƒula bɔdia bɔɔda kayi teetulo ayabi ani nkya kayaa ƒui.

english_verse: I went down to see if blossoms were on the walnut trees, grapevines, and fruit trees.
translation_verse: Líse adingyii kemo kadi na ɔkwalɛ nnii ntánu si egyii ammɔ aata evete iye adi adaku anwula buwi.

english_verse: But in my imagination I was suddenly riding on a glorious chariot. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Nsu kawɔlɔkɔ ni, mina kasusu kéti-mi kátɔlɔku késienku ɔgyu, na ɔ́bla aani si bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ɔni muukeye ɔdi kemmo na nlie.

english_verse: Dance! Dance! Beautiful woman from Shulam, let us see you dance! She Speaks: Why do you want to see this woman from Shulam dancing with the others?
translation_verse: Begblebi ƒui ugblebi, awɔ ɔni nási Sulam, bimi lɛlɔ na atɔ atina-bu na bɔnu! Bi ɔsu na bɛɛyɔ́ bɛnu ami Sulam uleku bɔtɔ na bakpana akɔ?

translation_verse: Begblebi ƒui ugblebi, su-bu kesii kani na ƒula ɔyɔne úsie, na bɔsia-nwu kama bute-ɔ.

english_verse: My darling has gone down to his garden of spices, where he will feed his sheep and gather lilies.
translation_verse: Mina ɔyɔne úsie nwuna kutu akyala ƒɛƒɛɛ kevoma kemo. Mmɔ na úsie útéte nwuna baƒonu adila na ɔƒɛ egyii anwula ƒɛƒɛɛ ƒuala ƒuala adi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: I am his, and he is mine, as he feeds his sheep among the lilies. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Anwu ɔdi na ndi na anwu lɛnɔ ɔdi mina ɔdi uwi ɔni na ɔkya mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: My dearest, the cities of Tirzah and Jerusalem are not as lovely as you. Your charms are more powerful than all of the stars in the heavens.
translation_verse: Mina kayi, Tirsa ku Yerusalem lɛma linengudi ƒui liládia bɔnu aani awɔ. Na kalɛ na ƒula bɔdia bɔɔda-mi kayi utulo ayabi ani nkya katɔ ƒui bukeye.

english_verse: Turn away your eyes— they make me melt. Your hair tosses about as gracefully as goats coming down from Gilead.
translation_verse: Na si áda ƒula anumi édie-mi lɛlɔ uwi klukwii ɔdi kani na use-mi aani ogya lɛlɔ na básia-mi na mɔɔyɛlɛ. Ƒula lili linwini liibó ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ku lɛlɔyɔ aani bese pii badi náyu bási Gilead kɔbi lɛlɔ badubo ku ebiti.

english_verse: Your teeth are whiter than sheep freshly washed; they match perfectly, not one is missing.
translation_verse: Ƒula kenye anyi ása-a kenye na eekeye aani koƒonu kɔni na bákpila-ku ntu ɔƒɛni kani.

english_verse: What if I could have sixty queens, eighty wives, and thousands of others!
translation_verse: Ina beleku baga liti ku leevu iye basɔnɔ liti ku avlaatɛ iye begblebi bani na balakana-ma bɔka nébo benye-mi anumi muedi ni, neeeti bana ɔdi naaakɔku-ɔ!

english_verse: You would be my only choice, my flawless dove, the favorite child of your mother. The young women, the queens, and all the others tell how excited you are as they sing your praises:
translation_verse: Awɔ kani na ndubo bɔƒuna. Awɔ ndi mina lɛmangbɛ lɛni na lɛla lɛdi lítebie-ɔ kesii kadi. Ƒula uwele ɔ́ƒuna-a ɔ́wɔ geen. Ƒula bɔdia búnwini ɔnu na begblebi ku beleku baga ku bakladi ƒui beedie teemwi kalɛ na ese.

english_verse: “You are as majestic as the morning sky— glorious as the moon— blinding as the sun! Your charms are more powerful than all the stars above.” She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ése álɛ ligblebi ku bukeye aani kalɛ na ɔtanta kayaa kese. Na eekeye aani kɔbuli. Na aatu anumi aani ɔƒɛ bukeye! Na ƒula bɔdia bɔɔda kayi teetulo ayabi ani nkya kayaa ƒui.

english_verse: I went down to see if blossoms were on the walnut trees, grapevines, and fruit trees.
translation_verse: Líse adingyii kemo kadi na ɔkwalɛ nnii ntánu si egyii ammɔ aata evete iye adi adaku anwula buwi.

english_verse: But in my imagination I was suddenly riding on a glorious chariot. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Nsu kawɔlɔkɔ ni, mina kasusu kéti-mi kátɔlɔku késienku ɔgyu, na ɔ́bla aani si bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ɔni muukeye ɔdi kemmo na nlie.

english_verse: Dance! Dance! Beautiful woman from Shulam, let us see you dance! She Speaks: Why do you want to see this woman from Shulam dancing with the others?
translation_verse: Begblebi ƒui ugblebi, awɔ ɔni nási Sulam, bimi lɛlɔ na atɔ atina-bu na bɔnu! Bi ɔsu na bɛɛyɔ́ bɛnu ami Sulam uleku bɔtɔ na bakpana akɔ?

english_verse: You are a princess, and your feet are graceful in their sandals. Your thighs are works of art, each one a jewel;
translation_verse: Uleku ɔga ubi na adi, na ƒula lɛgba lɛɛdia bɔnu na ƒula lɛgbanvuo kemmo. Na ƒula ebuli aadia bɔnu aani si ɔvɔne ɔdi néti sika ugyiedi na ɔ́nwi-nya ɔ́lɛku-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: your navel is a wine glass filled to overflowing. Your body is full and slender like a bundle of wheat bound together by lilies.
translation_verse: Ƒula lɛkun lise aani ntɛ ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔni na béyile ku ntɛ. Na ƒula ɔlɔgyii úyi ɔ́lɛ munu munu na use salalaa aani ɔmukɔ ɔni na bényimi ku anwula ƒuala ƒuala limu lɛdi.

english_verse: Your breasts are like twins of a deer.
translation_verse: Na ƒula anyii ani nnye-ɔ kayi ese aani bakwa inyɔ bani nnye básala kesii kadi.

english_verse: Your neck is like ivory, and your eyes sparkle like the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath-Rabbim. Your nose is beautiful like Mount Lebanon above the city of Damascus.
translation_verse: Na ƒula limɔ lise aani atu ɔtunkpɛ. Na ƒula anumi ebi eekeye aani Hesbon libiɔ ntu na Bat-Rabin ɔma ɔban kenye. Na ƒula enwu aadia bɔnu aani Lebanon Kɔbi kɔni nákɔ kɔ́lɛ na Damasko ɔma unengudi.

english_verse: Your head is held high like Mount Carmel; your hair is so lovely it holds a king prisoner.
translation_verse: Ƒula lili linye ligeen katɔ katɔ aani Karmel Kɔbi. Na ƒula lili linwini lɛɛdia bɔnu geen, na ɔmmɔ lɛti muedi ɔkana na uƒie ɔga umodi unwini ƒula kabla ɔblane.

english_verse: You are very beautiful, so desirable!
translation_verse: Ése álɛ ligblebi na aadia bɔnu na aada ukyuli biala ɔkwɛ!

english_verse: You are tall and slender like a palm tree, and your breasts are full.
translation_verse: Ákuku na ese salalaa aani kubo, na ƒula kayi anyii ani nlɛ-ɔ kayi éyi álɛ munu munu.

english_verse: I will climb that tree and cling to its branches. I will discover that your breasts are clusters of grapes, and that your breath is the aroma of apples.
translation_verse: Ndubɔkɔ kugyii kɔmmɔ na ntébo lɛda nwuna kɔgba kɔmmɔ. Na liƒie anyii ammɔ lɛda na lɛnu kalɛ na ese aani akutu lɛboyo. Na ƒula ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni na aanwuna taalɛku enwu kemmo ɔnyi use ƒɛƒɛɛ aani adingyii ebi abuni ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni na eedie.

english_verse: Kissing you is more delicious than drinking the finest wine. How wonderful and tasty! She Speaks:
translation_verse: Si ukyuli ɔ́kya-a kɔgbu ni, ɔɔyu kayi teetulo si áni ntɛ bɔni ndia ntulo ƒui. Bi nsɔ nse mini mini na ɔdia lɛni?

english_verse: My darling, I am yours, and you desire me.
translation_verse: Mina Ɔyɔne, awɔ ɔdi na ndi, na mɔɔnu kalɛ na mɔɔda-a ɔkwɛ geen.

english_verse: Let's stroll through the fields and sleep in the villages.
translation_verse: Ya na bɔvi ɔgbami busie kemo na butátɛ akpaklɔ ammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: At dawn let's slip out and see if grapevines and fruit trees are covered with blossoms. When we are there, I will give you my love.
translation_verse: Na aya na buyile bɔlɛ ɔtanta tutuutu butánu si adingyii ammɔ éewi anwula. Na si uwi ɔni na búdu mmɔ ni, ndubudie mina kayi bɔyɔ lɛtina-a na mmɔ.

english_verse: Perfume from the magic flower fills the air, my darling. Right at our doorstep I have stored up for you all kinds of tasty fruits.
translation_verse: Egyii anwula ani ɔnyi ƒɛƒɛɛ mɔɔda ukyuli enwu aani kuvo áƒɔ kayaa ƒui. Ɔyɔne, lɛ́ɛsala adingyii ebi abuni lidu lidu líse bula ɔtɔ kayakun líse-ɔ.

english_verse: If you were my brother, I could kiss you whenever we happen to meet, and no one would say I did wrong.
translation_verse: Si banii mina ɔnwani ɔnanabi na adi ni, nka ndubɔkana na lɛkya-a kɔgbu uwi biala na ukyuli ɔdi ulasu ɔnii lɛ́ƒiɔ.

english_verse: I could take you to the home of my mother, who taught me all I know. I would give you delicious wine and fruit juice as well.
translation_verse: Na ndubɔkana na lɛkpanku-ɔ lisienku mina uni ɔni nátina-mi lɛla biala lɛni na ngyi kesii. Na ndubute-ɔ ntɛ bɔni mbo emini geen ku adingyii ebi ntu lɛnɔ na ani.

english_verse: Put your left hand under my head and embrace me with your right arm.
translation_verse: Ti ƒula kɔmii kɔnu kya-mi lili kalɔ na eti ƒula kɔdianu kɔnu abala-mi kayi.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me never to awaken love before it is ready. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Yerusalem begblebi, muubó-mii ɔda ɔkɛnku bakwa ku bete ɔ yikun lɛlɔ, na bise-mi kenye ka bɛɛɛdubo busie butágyila tɔ bɔyɔ wetédu ka uwi údu ka ulu ɔ́lɛmi úte bɔyɔ bɔmmɔ alati.

english_verse: Who is this young woman coming in from the desert and leaning on the shoulder of the one she loves? She Speaks: I stirred up your passions under the apple tree where you were born.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔmani ndi uleku ɔni nási kalɔ kakwiidi lɛlɔ ɔdubo mɛni na ɔ́kada úkpo nwuna ɔyɔne lɛmangba lɛlɔ lɛni? Lɛ́gyila mina bɔyɔ na kɔdingyii kɔni kalɔ na báda-a kaƒɔ na báwɔ-ɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Always keep me in your heart and wear this bracelet to remember me by. The passion of love bursting into flame is more powerful than death, stronger than the grave.
translation_verse: Mɔɔwia ka ami kani mina lɛlɔ litemi lɛkya-a kayi kemmo uwi ndi uwi, na akya kakwɛnimi kamɛni kɔnu na eti eteenyimo-mi. Bɔyɔ kogyulo bukpo kɔni mɔɔda ogya kubo ɔkplu kutulo kukpi na kutulo kaƒiɔtɔ.

english_verse: Love cannot be drowned by oceans or floods. It cannot be bought— any offer would be scorned no matter how great. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Ɛpu muedi iye ketu kadi buyi bulakana bɔyɔ buƒie na wanyina-mu wakya ntu kalɔ na ɔɔɔdi lɛla lɛni na beye lɛnɔ si ina bi kayu na ukyuli ɔdi ɔnii waƒɔ.

english_verse: We have a little sister whose breasts are not yet formed. If someone asks to marry her, what should we do?
translation_verse: Bubo ɔnwani ulekubi ɔni anyibɛɛ nátalɛ tɔ. Na si ukyuli ɔdi ɔnii ɔɔwia-nwu uti ni, bi na ɔlɛka bɔbla?

english_verse: She isn't a wall that we can defend behind a silver shield. Neither is she a room that we can protect behind a wooden door. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Si banii kowodu na kɔdi ni, nka badubɔtu sika ɔƒualadi kɔgyumanakɔ bunyene-nwu lɛlɔ. Na si kayakun na kadi lɛnɔ ni, nka sida kugyii kpakplaa na bɔdubɔnwi bɔbala-ka.

english_verse: I am a wall around a city, my breasts are towers, and just looking at me brings him great pleasure.
translation_verse: Nse aani kowodu na lɛ́ka lɛ́mana ɔma unengudi. Na mina kayi anyii adi kagumanakɔ kete-nwu. Na mina bɔnu kplu kplu muedi búdu-nwu ɔkwɛ.

english_verse: Solomon has a vineyard at Baal-Hamon, which he rents to others for a thousand pieces of silver each.
translation_verse: Salomo ubo adingyii kemo kadi na kesii kani baalɔ banii Baal-Hamon. Na uusé-ka ɔkpa teete bekyuli taaƒɔ sika ɔƒualadi ebi apim unwi taasiku ukyuli biala kudɔ.

english_verse: My vineyard is mine alone! Solomon can keep his silver and the others can keep their share of the profits. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Nsu mina adingyii kemo ni, ami lɛti kadi na kadi. O Salomo, nwuna sika ɔƒualadi apim unwi ɔdi ƒula ɔdi. Na bani mɔɔnu-ka lɛlɔ ni, bana ɔdi ndi sika ɔƒualadi koƒo kunwi.

english_verse: You are in the garden with friends all around. Let me hear your voice! She Speaks:
translation_verse: Mina kayi, awɔ ku ƒula bakpana nkya adingyii kemo kammɔ kemmo, ya na lɛsɔ linu-ɔ lɛdi!

english_verse: Hurry to me, my darling! Run faster than a deer to mountains of spices.
translation_verse: Ɔyɔne, babla na ebo-mi kudɔ mɛni! Keli momoomo tulo kalɛ na akwa uukeli bo kɔbi lɛlɔ kesii kani na kutu akyala ƒɛƒɛɛ akya mɛni.

english_verse: I am Isaiah, the son of Amoz. And this is the message that I was given about Judah and Jerusalem when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah: A Guilty Nation
translation_verse: Yesaia ɔni ndi Amos ubidi ɔ́nu kɔyu kemmo ala budie taatina adi na adanku Yuda ku Yerusalem. Útaanu ala amɛni na uwi ɔni na Usia ku Yutan ku Ahas ku Hesekia bélie bádi lɛga na ɔdi biala uwi kemmo na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ. Katɔti Ɔ́su Yudaƒuɔ Batuɔkplune Kenye Kadi

english_verse: The Lord has said, “Listen, heaven and earth! The children I raised have turned against me.
translation_verse: Binu, amii bani nkya katɔ ƒui! Na bise atu, amii kalɔ lɛlɔ bekyuli! Ɔsika Unwoti ɔ́su kenye kadi ɔnini, “Lɛ́tumini bebi na lɛ́da-ma na bábi lɛlɔ, nsu báta bénye-mi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Israel, you are a sinful nation loaded down with guilt. You are wicked and corrupt and have turned from the Lord, the holy God of Israel.
translation_verse: O kadi bekyuli bekpidi, bana ekpidi énwini etila na aayu-ma unu. Badi alaekpidi bablane kasala, bebi bekpidi bani muusé lɛlɔ! Béni na bédie Unwoti atu, na béni Israel Ɔlatidi Kedee ɔmmɔ, na bénwini kama bákya-nwu.

english_verse: Why be punished more? Why not give up your sin? Your head is badly bruised, and you are weak all over.
translation_verse: Bi ɔsu na binye bɛɛwia lɛbibo teete lɛlɔ lɛni? Bi ɔsi na bɛdubɔta binye-mi lɛlɔ lɛni biteesie uwi ƒui? Bilánu ka bise aani bekyuli bani na bébo-ma eli bábwɛ na biinú ɔlɛ na bina kayi kemmo.

english_verse: From your head to your toes there isn't a healthy spot. Bruises, cuts, and open sores go without care or oil to ease the pain. A Country in Ruins
translation_verse: Ɔ́si bina lɛgba kalɔ útédu lili ni, ɔlɛ ɔda-mii na bɛ́ƒɔ alɛbi ƒui, na akpanabi asia-mii lɛlɔ, na bina alɛbi eenwenyi, na biiibo evogyii na binyimi-ni.

english_verse: Your country lies in ruins; your towns are in ashes. Foreigners and strangers take and destroy your land while you watch.
translation_verse: Bina kɔlɔ ƒui kɔ́yii udu na kuwi ukpludi. Na bákyula-mii lɛma linengudi ƒui. Na binye bɛɛnu baƒɔ bammɔ na béti-mii mmo ku lɛla biala bénwini bana lɛdi na bébile lɛla biala.

english_verse: Enemies surround Jerusalem, alone like a hut in a vineyard or in a cucumber field.
translation_verse: Sion, lídie-ɔ atu aani kevo kani na bányonu bákya eƒu akɔ. Na útavumana ku ɔma unengudi ɔni bekpone báka bákya.

english_verse: Zion would have disappeared like Sodom and Gomorrah, if the Lord All-Powerful had not let a few of its people survive. Justice, Not Sacrifices
translation_verse: Si Blɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui útebu bula ɛlɛɛ badi útese kama ni, bɔdubo udu bɔyii aani kalɛ na Sodom ku Gomora lɛma lɛ́yii udu.

english_verse: You are no better than the leaders and people of Sodom and Gomorrah! So listen to the Lord God:
translation_verse: Amii bani nse aani Sodom batɔnkune, bise atu na binu Unwoti lɛla lɛni na ɔɔsu, binu bula Katɔti ɔda bubo, amii bani nse aani Gomora kadi bekyuli!

english_verse: “Your sacrifices mean nothing to me. I am sick of your offerings of rams and choice cattle; I don't like the blood of bulls or lambs or goats.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Bina akpala pii ani na biiboku-mi alaƒɔ-mi anu. Límo-nya na aaba-mi ɔkwɛ! Bi mɔɔka-nya? Na bina baƒonu ku bebuo bamba ƒui lɛmwi ni, naaawia-ni naaanu. Bina ɔmantɛ bakɔ ku baƒonu ku bese bammɔ ubugya uusé-mi lɛlɔ na naaawia-nwu naaanu.

english_verse: “Who asked you to bring all this when you come to worship me? Stay out of my temple!
translation_verse: Si bɛ́da bɛ́lɛ-mi anumi ku ala ammɔ na bɛnii mina kakpakɔ na bíbo ni, ɔma névele-mii ɔnii biboku-nwu ala ammɔ, na bɛɛkɔ́-mi kaduli taayu?

english_verse: Your sacrifices are worthless, and your incense disgusting. I can't stand the evil you do on your New Moon Festivals or on your Sabbaths and other times of worship.
translation_verse: Bɛsɔ biteboku-mi akpala ani neeebo kɔsia kɔdi! Bina oloƒui ɔni bɛɛkyula ƒui uusé-mi. Na bina emeyi buni ani bɛɛdi ƒui átamanku-mi. Kɔbuli kɔwɔdi bɔlɛ ku lɛnwunameyi ku emeyi aƒunadi ani na biilie kɔka ku bina emeyi buni ani bɛɛsála lɛlɔ taadi ƒui adi likpidi ku ɔkɔ ala sɔɔn. Nsɔ naaawia-mii naaablaku lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: I hate your New Moon Festivals and all others as well. They are a heavy burden I am tired of carrying.
translation_verse: Muukisi kɔbuli kɔwɔdi bɔlɛ ku bina emeyi buni ani bɛɛdi ku bina akpala ƒui na naaawia-nya naaanu, ɔsika énwini-mi etila na lɛ́ɛnɔ-nya buti.

english_verse: and learn to live right. See that justice is done. Defend widows and orphans and help the oppressed.” An Invitation from the Lord
translation_verse: Bɛtɛya lɛbuni bɔbla. Na bɛbla ala ulu lɛlɔ siin. Bibunku bekyuli bani na beekpóku, na bikpo bite bekpinebi, na bɛya na bekpinele bakɛ bana kadikɔ.”

english_verse: If you willingly obey me, the best crops in the land will be yours.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni si bɛdubunu-mi litemi na binu kalɔ na libunku-mii ni, bɛdubɔkɛ ala pii bɛdi.

english_verse: But if you turn against me, your enemies will kill you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Condemns Jerusalem
translation_verse: Nsu si bɛ́ta bínye-mi lɛlɔ ni, bina bekisine badubo-mii bɔyila ku udu. Yerusalem Kadi Bekyuli Béni Ka Badi Unwoti Litemi Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Jerusalem, you are like an unfaithful wife. Once your judges were honest and your people lived right; now you are a city full of murderers.
translation_verse: “Bɛnu kalɛ na Yerusalem ɔma ɔni kemmo na balawia ala basa basa balanu ɔƒɛni amu úbenwini aani ɔyalɛ ɔni kudɔ banana lidu lidu beeduo taalɛ. Ɔma ɔni kemmo na nka bátaadi mina etemila lɛlɔ ulu lɛlɔ ku ala bɔbla siin ni, ɔƒɛni amu bekyuli badune néyi-nwu kemmo tɛɛ.

english_verse: Your leaders have rejected me to become friends of crooks; your rulers are looking for gifts and bribes. Widows and orphans never get a fair trial.
translation_verse: Na ɔma umodi ɔmmɔ batɔnkune bénwini bekyuli bani mɔɔta teenye-mi lɛlɔ, na baadiku beyune kɔkpana, na baaƒɔ́ ala na bɔbɛ kemmo taasiku bekyuli kudɔ. Béni ka bekpo bete bekpinebi. Na bekpinele litemi ani lɛɛɛkɛ-ma munu munu.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the mighty ruler of Israel, and I make you a promise: You are now my enemy, and I will show my anger by taking revenge on you.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, ɔni ndi Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ ɔdine Ɔyikune ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Ndubo-mii atu budie aani mina bekisine na mina livoƒi libo-mii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I will punish you terribly and burn away everything that makes you unfit to worship me.
translation_verse: Ndubo-mii bina likpidi kasi budie geen na ndubo-mii bɔnwamana na lidie eku ana ƒui bina lɛlɔ ku bina bɔsɔ ƒui kaduɛ.

english_verse: Jerusalem, I will choose judges and advisors like those you had before. Your new name will be “Justice and Faithfulness.” The Lord Will Save Jerusalem
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, ndubute-mii litemi batɛne babuni ku kasusu betine aani bani nákya-mii akɔ kuuku. Na bekyuli badubɔsɔ balɔ Yerusalem banii Ɔma unengudi ɔni kemmo baatɛ litemi geen ku Ɔma unengudi ɔni bekyuli mɔɔdi etemila lɛlɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Jerusalem, you will be saved by showing justice; Zion's people who turn to me will be saved by doing right.
translation_verse: Ka Unwoti Katɔti ɔɔtɛ litemi ulu lɛlɔ na use siin ɔsu ni, alaekpidi bablane bani nkya Sion na bana ekpidi éduo-ma na bénwini kayi, badubɔkɛ bɔƒɔ.

english_verse: But those rebellious sinners who turn against me, the Lord, will all disappear.
translation_verse: Na bani na ekpidi kani na beli baabla ni, ɔdubo-ma udu bɔyila ƒui, ɔsika béni na banii belebo Unwoti kudɔ.

english_verse: You will be like a grove of trees dying in a drought.
translation_verse: Na bɛdubo bɔyuɛ na biwiile evete aani kemo kani egyii nátakɛ ntu.

english_verse: Your strongest leaders will be like dry wood set on fire by their idols. No one will be able to help, as they all go up in flames.
translation_verse: Na bina bayikune ƒui badubɔyii aani kalɛ na keti kaakywí na ɔdi ulakana bunine.”

english_verse: This is the message I was given about Judah and Jerusalem:
translation_verse: Ala ani ndubo mɛni na Amos ubidi Yesaia ɔ́nu ɔkɛnku Yuda ku Yerusalem lɛlɔ.

english_verse: In the future, the mountain with the Lord's temple will be the highest of all. It will reach above the hills; every nation will rush to it.
translation_verse: Na uwi ukplodi kemmo ni, kɔbi kɔni lɛlɔ na Katɔti kakpakɔ kenye ndubɔbla kɔbi kɔni náƒɔ kuye kutulo abi ƒui akɔ. Kɔdubɔkuku kɔvia abi ƒui eli, na kadi bekyuli ƒui badubukeli besie mmɔ.

english_verse: Many people will come and say, “Let's go to the mountain of the Lord God of Jacob and worship in his temple.” The Lord will teach us his Law from Jerusalem, and we will obey him.
translation_verse: Bekyuli badubɔsi kɔlɔ pii lɛlɔ bebo na babasu banini, “Bɛya na bɔkɔ busie Unwoti Katɔti kɔbi lili na Yakob Katɔti kakpakɔ, na ɔtina-bu nwuna lilu na bɔsia-ni lɛlɔ.” Ɔsika Sion mmɔ na badubɔtina-bu ala, na bunu Unwoti litemi bɔsiku Yerusalem.

english_verse: He will settle arguments between nations. They will pound their swords and their spears into rakes and shovels; they will never make war or attack one another.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔdubɔtɛ litemi na ɔklibi kadi ku kadi unyeƒi ɔni nkya-ma ntɛ. Na bana kuwii ƒui ni, ama alati badubuti-ku bakywɛ anwami bonwu ani muunwíni kalɔ. Na beti bana atula bakywɛ asaaka. Na kadi ku kadi basɔ balata kekpo, na basɔ balatumini bekyuli belete kekpo lɛnɔ.

english_verse: People of Israel, let's live by the light of the Lord. Following Sinful Customs
translation_verse: Israel kadi bekyuli, bibo na bɔsia Unwoti bukeye kemmo. Katɔti Ɔ́su Bekyuli Úse Ka Ɔdubɔtɛku-ma Litemi

english_verse: Our Lord, you have deserted your people, Israel, because they follow customs of nations from the east. They worship Philistine gods and are close friends of foreigners.
translation_verse: Unwoti úni Israel kadi bekyuli, ɔsika bábla unwi ku ɔƒɛ katukɔ kadi bamba bekyuli bani na evo ala bɔbla bɔ́ƒɔ-ma lɛlɔ kemmo, na beebó like aani Ƒilistiƒuɔ kalɛ. Na baakya kadi bamba bekyuli lɛnɔ kɔgbu.

english_verse: They have endless treasures of silver and gold; they have countless horses and war chariots.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bebo akɛla lidu lidu aani sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ku bapɔnkɔ ku bana kɛɛkɛ pii.

english_verse: Everywhere in the country they worship the idols they have made.
translation_verse: Baƒiɔ béyi kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ. Na bekyuli bammɔ baakya eli kalɔ taakpa ala ani na béti bana enu bábla béte lɛlɔ.

english_verse: And so, all of them will be ashamed and disgraced. Don't forgive them! A Day of Judgment
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Unwoti ɔdububoku bekyuli ƒui kalɔ. Na ukyuli biala ɔyila nwuna kenyekɔ. Teti takyiɛ-ma!

english_verse: Every one of you, go hide among the rocks and in the ground, because the Lord is fearsome, marvelous, and glorious.
translation_verse: Bikeli bitéduo atakpɛ libu. Na bɛbɛla bina lɛlɔ bɛsiku Unwoti ɔni mɔɔda liƒu, na nwuna lɛgadi liikeye kudɔ.

english_verse: When the Lord comes, everyone who is proud will be made humble, and the Lord alone will be honored.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛmmɔ ni, bekyuli bekpidi bani mɔɔnu bekyuli ɔnusɛ bɔdubɔkya lili kalɔ, na lɛlɔ katɔ bɔkɔliku biala bɔdububo kalɔ.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful has chosen a day when those who are proud and conceited will be put down.
translation_verse: Unwoti ubo nwuna limeyi na lɛsia ulu lɛdubo lite bani mɔɔkun lɛmɛnɛ na baanu lɛlɔ katɔ katɔ. Na ɔdububoku lɛlɔ katɔ bɔkɔli biala kalɔ limeyi lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: The tall and towering cedars of Lebanon will be destroyed. So will the oak trees of Bashan,
translation_verse: Na Lebanon egyii kpakplaa enengudi ammɔ ƒui ɔdubukulo-nya uwi kalɔ ku Basan adi kpakplaa ammɔ.

english_verse: all high mountains and hills,
translation_verse: Na ɔdubɔbwɛ abi ku abinkpo ƒui uwi kalɔ.

english_verse: all the seagoing ships, and every beautiful boat.
translation_verse: Na ɔbwɛ beyedine lɛkɔlɔ libendi ƒui ku lɛkɔlɔ libliidi lɛni nnye lɛkɔlɔ kalɛlɛkɔ.

english_verse: When that day comes, everyone who is proud will be put down. Only the Lord will be honored.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli atuɔkplu ku lɛlɔ katɔ bɔkɔliku ƒui ɔdububoku-mu kalɔ. Na Unwoti lɛnyi kani ndubɔkɔ katɔ limeyi lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: Idols will be gone for good.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔdubɔyila baƒiɔ biala udu.

english_verse: You had better hide in caves and holes— the Lord will be fearsome, marvelous, and glorious when he comes to terrify people on earth.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Katɔti ɔdubɔta unye ɔnii ɔɔkunku kalɔ kammɔ ni, nwuna bekisine badubɔkpɛ na bekeli beduo ubu. Na babɛ na libu kemmo na atakpɛ akɔ, na Unwoti bɔyia ku kalɛ na uukeye ɔsu.

english_verse: On that day everyone will throw to the moles and bats their idols of silver and gold they made to worship.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛmmɔ ni, sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi baƒiɔ bani na bávɔ bése lɛlɔ baakpá ni, badububo-nwu bewi baƒiamu ku bagyina.

english_verse: The Lord will be fearsome, marvelous, and glorious when he comes to terrify people on earth— they will hide in caves and in the hills.
translation_verse: Badubo bukeli butéduo atabi libu bonwu kemmo, na batábɛ atabi yayaaya ammɔ kɔka, na bekeli Unwoti kɔnyi limeyi lɛmmɔ ku nwuna lɛgadi lɛni muukeye na limeyi lɛni na ɔdubɔta unye ɔnii ɔɔkunku kayawi.

english_verse: Stop trusting the power of humans. They are all going to die, so how can they help?
translation_verse: Bɛsɔ bitasia ukyuli ɔyawine anu ka ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kani na nkya-nwu enwu. Bi kɔsia na ɔdubɔlɛ ute-mii?

english_verse: The mighty Lord All-Powerful is going to take away from Jerusalem and Judah everything you need— your bread and water, *
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔni ndi Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔdubutile kebunku biala kuƒi, na ɔdubɔya na adila ku ntu bɔsɔ bulédu Yerusalem ku Yuda bekyuli,

english_verse: soldiers and heroes, judges and prophets, leaders and army officers,
translation_verse: kadi bayikune ku bekpone, litemi batɛne ku kenye bediene, ku bani muubó like ku benengu ƒui,

english_verse: officials and advisors, fortunetellers and others who tell the future.
translation_verse: ku bekpone esu batɔnkune ku bekyuli babune ku kasusu bakyane ku enu kabla lidu bablane ku bani mɔɔkanti taakya ala.

english_verse: He will let children and babies become your rulers.
translation_verse: Na bakloƒu na ɔdubɔya na bataanu-ma lɛlɔ, na ɔya na banamu keeke bataadi-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You will each be cruel to friends and neighbors. Young people will insult their elders; no one will show respect to those who deserve it.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli badubo lɛlɔ butaanya taakya, na banwani ku bakpana beteekpoku lɛlɔ. Bakɔdi badubɔta benye benengu lɛlɔ, na bani na nka balábu-ma kadi akɔ badubɔta benye bekyuli babune lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Some of you will grab hold of a relative and say, “You still have a coat. Be our leader and rule this pile of ruins.”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ ni, ɔnwa ɔdubɔta na ɔsu ɔnwani na ɔti kaduli ɔnini, “Ka awɔ ebo ala adadi ɔsu ni, awɔ nwini bula ɔtɔnkune na anu kalɛ na aklibi ala ani nébie mɛni!”

english_verse: But the answer will be, “I can't do you any good. Don't make me your leader. There's no food or clothing left in my house.”
translation_verse: Nsu ɔdubudie kenye ɔnini, “Oowo! Lɛɛɛdubo bɔkana kebunku kadi bute, ɔsika liiibo adila iye adala adi na mina kaduli, anwuɔsu tabla-mi ɔtɔnkune tete bekyuli bammɔ.”

english_verse: Jerusalem and Judah, you rebelled against your glorious Lord— your words and your actions, made you stumble and fall.
translation_verse: Yerusalem ku Yuda lɛma ƒui lɛdubo bubie na ala ƒui eƒu akya, ɔsika bana etemila áta énye Unwoti lɛlɔ, na béni ka babu anwu ɔni muukeye na bana akɔ.

english_verse: The look on your faces shows that you are sinful as Sodom, and you don't try to hide it. You are in for trouble, and you have brought it all on yourselves. The Wrong Kind of Leaders
translation_verse: Na bana anumi lɛlɔ muedi adubɔnu bana bɔƒiɔ ati. Na anumi ku anumi na baabla ekpidi ammɔ, aani Sodom kadi bekyuli kalɛ na balábɛla-nya muedi. Bɔbuɛ ute-ma! Ama alati néti bana ɔgbankpi kɔtu bɔni béboku lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Tell those who obey God, “You're very fortunate— you will be rewarded for what you have done.”
translation_verse: Su bekyuli bani nse siin anii, ɔdubɔtɛ ute-ma ɔsika badubɔdi bana kabla ebi.

english_verse: Tell those who disobey, “You're in big trouble— what you did to others will come back to you.”
translation_verse: Bɔbuɛ ute likyulikpi ala bablane! Ɔgbankpi ɔ́ɔda ɔ́lɛ-ma lɛlɔ! Bana enu kabla lɛyuƒɔla badubo bɔƒɔ.

english_verse: Though you are God's people, you are ruled and abused by women and children. You are confused by leaders who guide you down the wrong path.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani ablala nse aani banamu mɔɔnya mina bekyuli taakya, na beleku baadi-ma lɛlɔ. O mina kadi bekyuli, bina batɔnkune bákpanku-mii bésela batáyila. Bákpanku-mii bálɛku ulu geen ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Lord is ready to accuse and judge all nations.
translation_verse: Katɔti úusie ulie kalɔ na litemi katɛkɔ, na ɔdubo bekyuli ƒui litemi bɔtɛku.

english_verse: He will even judge you rulers and leaders of his own nation. You destroyed his vineyard and filled your houses by robbing the poor.
translation_verse: Ɔdubɔtɛku nwuna kadi benengu ku batɔnkune litemi ɔnini, “Amii nébile Yerusalem ɔni nse aani mina adingyii ebi kemo. Na bíyile bina kɔduli ku ala ani na bíƒie bɛ́ƒɔ bawabane kudɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says, “You have crushed my people and rubbed in the dirt the faces of the poor.” The Women of Jerusalem
translation_verse: Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔnini, “Ulu ɔmani udu na bɛ́kɛ, na bɛɛkɔ́ mina bekyuli bawabane kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ lɛni binwini ɔtumu?” Katɔti Ɔ́lɛ Yerusalem Beleku Kpakplaa

english_verse: The Lord says: The women of Jerusalem are proud and strut around, winking shamelessly. They wear anklets that jingle and call attention to the way they walk.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Yerusalem beleku balábu. Bákpa bana amɔ bakɛ beesé anumi teete banana, na bana enwu eti kayaa, na ala ani nda-ma akɔnkɔ ku anikpo aabla kɔku na beebó lɛlɔ kudu. Katɔti ɔdubɔni-ma kɔtu.

english_verse: But I, the Lord, will cover their heads with sores, and I will uncover their private parts.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔdubɔya na bana eli alɛ alɛlɛbi na bana eli apa na linwini lɛsɔ lilákwɛ.”

english_verse: When that day comes, I will take away from those women all the fine jewelry they wear on their ankles, heads, necks, ears, arms, noses, fingers, and on their clothes. I will remove their veils, their belts, their perfume, their magic charms, their royal robes, and all their fancy dresses, hats, and purses.
translation_verse: ku bana kɔnu kɔni baanu lɛlɔ ku lɛwu kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ gyɔlɔɔ ku ala ani beeti taakya bana eli bɔdia ku aduni ani beebi eli ku amangba mmɔ ƒui ɔdubo-nya budie.
