One day, Zedekiah sent Jehucal and the priest Zephaniah to talk with me. At that time, I was free to go wherever I wanted, because I had not yet been put in prison. Jehucal and Zephaniah said, “Jeremiah, please pray to the Lord our God for us.”
translation_verse: Kama kama ni, Babilonƒuɔ bekpone bébekpo Yerusalem, nsu bébenwini kama ka bénu ka Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ɔni baalɔ Apres na basɔ baalɔ-nwu Hopra ɔ́tɔnku Egyipteƒuɔ bekpone na béti básia kakɛ kammɔ bésela ɔsu. Limeyi lɛdi ni, Sedekia ɔ́tala Selemia ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Yehukal ku Maaseia ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Seƒania na ɔdi ɔkpane ɔnii bebo na ami ku-ma bɔtɛmi. Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, na mbo bɔnwuna, ɔsika bátakya-mi tɔ ɔtɔ na lɛkana na lisie kesii biala na mɔɔyɔ́. Mmɔ na Yukal ku Seƒania bábasu-mi banini, “Yeremia, buvele, kpali Unwoti bula Katɔti na bula lili.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message: Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnii nsɔku-ma nnwiniku ku kenye kamɛni ɔnini, “Sedekia, aawia ka Yeremia uvele ami Unwoti Israel Katɔti na lɛsu-mii lɛla ndubo bɔlɛ. Anwuɔsu ndubo-mii bɔsu. Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ku nwuna bekpone bébo bábaƒɔ-mii ngba. Nsu uwi uletu badubɔsɔ benwini besie bana kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Babilonƒuɔ badubɔsɔ benwini bebo na bebekpo Yerusalem. Na ɔƒaani ni, badubo ɔma ɔmmɔ bɔka bɔkya na batu ogya bakya lɛla biala.

english_verse: Don't fool yourselves into thinking that the Babylonians will leave as they did before.
translation_verse: Utabla-mii aani Babilonƒuɔ bammɔ badubɔsɔ benwini aani kudeedi kalɛ na bise lɛlɔ lisusu.

english_verse: Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire. Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
translation_verse: Ina bɛ́di-ma lɛlɔ muedi ni, bekpone bani náƒɔ ɔlɛ, nsu bétekpi mmɔ badubo na bɔsi bana adi nvo kemmo bebo na batu ogya Yerusalem ɔma umodi ɔmmɔ.” Béƒie Yeremia Bákya Ɔtɔ

english_verse: The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us.
translation_verse: Ka Egyipteƒuɔ bébo banii bebebunku-bu na bekpo bete-bu ɔsu ni, Babilonƒuɔ básɔ bénwini.

english_verse: So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu lɛ́bla kasusu ka mɔɔtɔlɔ Yerusalem linwini lisie Benyamin kɔdua kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ na ami lɛnɔ ntáƒɔ mina ɔtɔ kemmo kalɔ kadikɔ kani medu-mi.

english_verse: I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
translation_verse: Ulu ɔmmɔ na ndaku bɔyu ɔ́si Yerusalem na nkɛ kesii kani baalɔ Benyamin Ɔban Kenye uwi ɔni na Selemia ubidi ɔnanabi ɔni baalɔ Iriya na ɔdi Hanania uwɔ na ɔsɔ ɔdi ɔban ɔmmɔ bagyumane lɛlɔ ɔnune údi-mi únyene. Mmɔ na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Yeremia, mɔɔyá-a na ati ka búƒie-ɔ, ɔsika ábla unwi ku Babilonƒuɔ na ésela atásiaku-ma.”

english_verse: “I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials.
translation_verse: Amu na lídie kenye nnini, “Ɔɔɔdi bana kudɔ na lísela ntáblaku-ma unwi!” Nsu Iriya útete-mi kuƒi kɔdi munu munu, mmomu úti-mi úsienku ɔga benengu bammɔ.

english_verse: They were angry and ordered the soldiers to beat me. Then I was taken to the house that belonged to Jonathan, one of the king's officials. It had been turned into a prison, and I was kept in a basement room. After I had spent a long time there,
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bédie lɛdi béte bekpone bammɔ na bébo-mi, ɔsika béti kɔnyi bákya-mi. Ɔmmɔ kama béti-mi bésienku ɔga benengu bammɔ akɔ unwi ɔni baalɔ banii Yonatan kesii, ɔsika nwuna kaduli na béti bénwini bekyuli ɔtɔ kakyakɔ. Na béti-mi bákya ɔtɔ ɔdi na kalɔ kemmo. Uwi ɔni na bákya-mi ɔtɔ mmɔ na ɔ́ɔƒɔ uwi gyɔlɔɔ ni,

english_verse: King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?” “Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
translation_verse: Ɔga Sedekia ɔ́ya na bábɛ bédie-mi béboku-nwu kudɔ na úye-mi buɛɛ ɔnini, “Adanku kenye kadi ásiku Unwoti kudɔ ete-bu?” Amu na lídie kenye nnini, “Bula ɔga ɔbune, ɛɛn, ndanku kenye kadi. Unwoti ɔdubo bɔya na Babilonƒuɔ ɔga uƒie-ɔ ɔtɔlɔku.”

english_verse: Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation?
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, líye-nwu nnini, “Ɔga ɔbune, bi na lɛ́bla ɔsu na áya na bákya-mi ɔtɔ? Bɔbla na lɛ́bla likpidi bonwu lɛdi lɛ́ta línye-ɔ lɛlɔ iye ƒula benengu bammɔ ɔdi lɛlɔ iye kalɔ kammɔ ɔda bubo bɔdi lɛlɔ?

english_verse: Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem?
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔ kenye bediene bani nátɔlɔ-ɔ banii Babilonƒuɔ baaadubo Yerusalem bukpo kudii ni, ákya bana ɔdi ɔtɔ?

english_verse: Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
translation_verse: Buvele nda-a, tasɔku-mi tatákya ɔtɔ na Yonatan kesii mmɔ. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, ndubo bukpi.”

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Ɔga Sedekia ɔ́ya na béti-mi bátákya ɔtɔ na ɔga kesii kaduli bagyumanane bammɔ enu kemmo, na ɔ́su bekpone bammɔ ɔnii bataasíku bodobodo na bodobodo keƒikɔ mmɔ teeboku-mi limeyi ndi limeyi wetédu ka adila ása ɔma bonwu ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: One day, Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jehucal, and Pashhur heard me tell the people of Judah
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, Matan ubidi Seƒatia ku Pasur ubidi Gedalia ku Selemia ubidi Yehukal ku Milkiya ubidi ɔni baalɔ Pasur bénu ka mɔɔsu Yudaƒuɔ ka

english_verse: that the Lord had said, “If you stay here in Jerusalem, you will die in battle or from disease or hunger, and the Babylonian army will capture the city anyway. But if you surrender to the Babylonians, they will let you live.”
translation_verse: Unwoti násu ɔnini, “Kekpo kadubo-mii buƒie si bɛ́sɔ bɛkya Yerusalem mɛni iye kɔka kɔdu-mii iye lɛlɛ likpidi libo-mii na bikpi. Na Babilonƒuɔ badubo-mii bɔka bɔkya na beti ɔma ɔmmɔ ku lɛla biala benwini bana ɔdi. Nsu si bíboku lɛlɔ kalɔ bíte-ma na bɛ́nyonu lɛlɔ bíte-ma ni, badubɔya na bilie ngba.”

english_verse: So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bana ine bammɔ bésie ɔga kudɔ na bátásu-nwu banini, “Ɔdi ka adu Yeremia, ɔsika ɔɔkya bekpone bammɔ ku bekyuli ƒui liƒu, na ɔ́ya na baayia ɔni na basɔ beeebo lɛnunsia lɛdi munu munu. Ulebunku bula kadi bekyuli na ulu biala lɛlɔ, mmomu uubile-ma na ɔɔkya-ma ɔlɛ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Zedekiah replied, “Do what you want with him. I can't stop you.”
translation_verse: Amu na Sedekia ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bɛbla-nwu lɛla lɛni na bɛɛyɔ́, ɔsika lɛɛɛdubo-mii bɔkana bɔbala.”

english_verse: Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
translation_verse: Amu na básɔku-mi bésienku ɔga kesii kaduli kemmo kesii kani na bagyumanane bammɔ bakya mmɔ, na báyula-mi bákya libiɔ lɛdi kemmo ku kɔbuli, na libiɔ lɛmmɔ lɛdi ɔga ɔmmɔ ubidi ɔni baalɔ Milkiya libiɔ. Nsu ntu bɔdi buuubo-ni kemmo.

english_verse: Ebedmelech from Ethiopia was an official at the palace, and he heard what they had done to me. So he went to speak with King Zedekiah, who was holding court at Benjamin Gate.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔmmɔ ni, benengu bammɔ akɔ unwi ɔ́kya ɔga kesii mmɔ ɔni nási Kus kalɔ lɛlɔ na baalɔ-nwu Ebedmelek. Ɔnana ɔmɛni nésie Ɔga Sedekia kudɔ uwi ɔni na uli Benyamin Ɔban Kenye mmɔ ɔɔbla nwuna kabla na útásu-nwu lɛla lɛni na bekyuli bamɛni bábla-mi.

english_verse: Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
translation_verse: Ebedmelek ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ɔga Ɔbune, kenye udiene na Yeremia ɔdi, na kalɛ na bekyuli bammɔ béti-nwu bátákya libiɔ kemmo mmɔ ɔɔɔdi munu munu báƒiɔ. Ɔƒɛni si adila ása na Yerusalem ni, agyi anii Yeremia ɔdubo bukpi na mmɔ.”

english_verse: Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well.
translation_verse: Ebedmelek ku bekpone bammɔ bésie ɔga kesii kaduli mmɔ na bátáwia adikpi adi na egulabi kesekɔ ɔtɔ ɔlɔndi kemmo na úbo kabuli ɔ́da-nya lɛlɔ na ɔ́yula ɔ́kya libiɔ lɛmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did,
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ti adikpi amɛni kya ƒula kanwa kalɛ na kɔbuli kɔmɛni kulamana-a.” Anwuɔsu ka lɛ́bla lɛni lɛ́wɔlɔ ni,

english_verse: the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards. King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
translation_verse: bekpone bammɔ báni-mi bálɛku libiɔ lɛmɛni kemmo. Na ka ɔ́si uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, báda-mi bákya ɔga kesii kaduli kemmo mmɔ na bagyumanane bammɔ akɔ. Ɔga Sedekia Úye Yeremia Ala Adi Únu

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
translation_verse: Ɔga Sedekia ɔ́ya na bákpanku-mi béboku-nwu kudɔ na kakpakɔ ɔkɛ nwuna kayakun kani nábɛ mmɔ kemmo na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Mɔɔwia ka liye-ɔ ala adi na lɛti litemi geen lɛmmɔ.”

english_verse: “Why?” I replied. “You won't listen, and you might even have me killed!”
translation_verse: Amu na lídie kenye nnini, “Bi na aawia ati? Ngyi ka si lɛ́su-ɔ muedi ni, aaadubo bunu na bɔwia na adubɔwia ka badu-mi mmomu!”

english_verse: He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na úse kenye ɔnini, “Lɛ́kpali Unwoti, ala ƒui Udiene ɔni nli ngba uwi ƒui, ka lɛɛɛdubo bɔya na badu-ɔ, na ɔdi biala lɛnɔ ulénu lɛla lɛni na bɔɔsu na ɔdi lɛnɔ uládu-ɔ.”

english_verse: Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́su-nwu nnii Unwoti ɔnini, “Sedekia, ami ndi Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, Israel Katɔti. Na muusé kenye ka si bɛ́kya lili kalɔ bíte Ɔga Nebukadnesar na bɛ́nyonu lɛlɔ bíte nwuna benengu ni, baaadubo awɔ ku ƒula kaduli bekyuli ƒui ɔdi biala bɔdu. Na balakyula Yerusalem lɛnɔ.

english_verse: But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
translation_verse: Nsu si bíni na bɛnii bilakya-ma lili kalɔ bɔdi ni, ndubo bɔya na Babilonƒuɔ bekpone baka ɔma ɔmmɔ bakya na beti lɛla biala benwini bana lɛdi. Na beƒie-mii lɛnɔ na binwini-ma batɔntɛne.”

english_verse: Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Sedekia údie kenye ɔnini, “Naaakana lili kalɔ bɔkya bute Babilonƒuɔ bani na ama ku Yudaƒuɔ báabla benwi mɛni na beleti-mi belete-ma na babla-mi kalala, ɔsika Yudaƒuɔ bammɔ lɛlɔ libo-mi liƒu geen na mɔɔyia ka badubo-mi bususu kalɛ udu naaadia bɔnu.”

english_verse: I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́su-nwu nnini, “Lɛ́su-ɔ ka si adubunu Unwoti litemi ni, Babilonƒuɔ baaadubo-ɔ buti bɔkya Yudaƒuɔ enu kemmo, mmomu adubulie ƒaa na ala adianku-ɔ kaduɛ.

english_verse: But the Lord has shown me that if you refuse to obey,
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti údie ɔ́tina-mi ka si ébulo na étenu-nwu litemi bɔdi ni,

english_verse: then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you: Friends you trusted led you astray. Now you're trapped in mud, and those friends you trusted have all turned away.
translation_verse: badubo ƒula beleku bani na ɔga kesii mmɔ ƒui buƒie na benwini batɔntɛne bete Nebukadnesar benengu. Na beleku bammɔ badubɔsu-ɔ banini, ‘Bakpana bani lɛlɔ na asia anu ni, ama nákpanku-ɔ bátáyila aanu-ɔ náaƒɔ lɛlɔ akya aba kemmo na bakpana bammɔ bénwini na báda-a bese.’

english_verse: The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
translation_verse: Babilonƒuɔ bekpone badubo ƒula beleku ku bebi ƒui buti bunwini bekyuli beƒiedi na beti-ɔ benwini ɔtɔntɛne bete Ɔga Nebukadnesar. Na bakyula Yerusalem bewi kalɔ kputu kputu.”

english_verse: Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life.
translation_verse: Amu na Sedekia ɔnini, “Yeremia, si ánu ka ásɔku lɛla lɛni na ami ku-ɔ bɔsu mɛni asu ukyuli ɔni ni, bakana na badu-ɔ.

english_verse: And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them.
translation_verse: Na ngyi nwaa ka si mina benengu bammɔ báti bula kelisa kamɛni lɛlɔ litemi ni, badubo-ɔ buye lɛla lɛni na ami ku-ɔ bɔ́su. Na ɔƒɛni kalɛ badubɔwia ulu ka badu-ɔ muedi si átasu-ma lɛla lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu si béye-ɔ ni, na asu-ma ka buvele na ada-mi anii nsɔ ntasɔku-ɔ ntesienku Yonatan kaduli, ɔsika si ásɔ énwini ésie mmɔ ni, adubukpi.”

english_verse: The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
translation_verse: Na sɔsɔ ni, benengu bammɔ bánya bébo bébeye-mi bɔsa bɔni na ami ku ɔga bɔsa mmɔ kalɔ bénu. Na lɛ́su-ma lɛla lɛni kani na ɔga ɔ́su-mi mmɔ kani pɛpɛɛpɛ. Anwuɔsu ɔdi ɔ́sɔ úteye-mi lɛla lɛdi útasiku bula bɔsa bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ kudii lɛnɔ ka ɔdi útenu-bu kɔtɔ kɔmmɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_verse: Amu na bábala-mi bákya ɔga kesii kaduli bagyumanane bammɔ kudɔ mmɔ útédu limeyi lɛni na kekpo kéƒie Yerusalem.

english_verse: When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Ɔga Sedekia ku nwuna bekpone bánu ka kekpo kéƒie Yerusalem ƒui ni, báwia ka bekeli balɛ ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo usien ɔmmɔ kani. Na bésie ɔga kevoma kemo kesii kani na bátábɛ básia ɔban ɔni nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ awodu anyɔ kɔsa mmɔ na béti eli bátina Yordan Ketu kɔwɛ kemmo.

english_verse: to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen.
translation_verse: Ebedmelek ɔni ndi Kusni ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Ami ndi Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, Israel Katɔti. Na mɔɔlɛ ɔdi biala kpakplaa ka ndubo bɔya na ɔgbankpi ubo ɔma ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na ɔɔɔdi keyi kayɔdi ku kubiti. Na ɔƒaani ni, uwi ɔsɔ uletu ndubo lɛla lɛni na lɛ́su bɔbla na ɔdi biala ɔnu ka lɛ́lɛ sɔsɔ.

english_verse: “Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
translation_verse: “Wia Yeremia na agyumana-nwu kɔkɔɔkɔ na abla lɛla biala na weye-ɔ ete-nwu.”

english_verse: But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty,
translation_verse: Nsu Babilonƒuɔ bekpone bábi básiaku-ma na bétéƒie-ma na Yeriko ɔma kudɔ na bákpanku Ɔga Sedekia bésienku ɔma ɔnii baalɔ Ribla na Hamat kalɛkɛ kemmo. Mmɔ na Nebukadnesar ɔ́tɛku-nwu litemi na ɔ́du-nwu kɔtɔ ka nwuna litemi lɛɛɛdia.

english_verse: and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families.
translation_verse: Na Ribla mmɔ ni, bádu Sedekia bebi bananabi ku nwuna benengu uwi ɔni na anwu ɔlati unye ɔɔnu.

english_verse: Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Na bátu-nwu anumi bédie evuo kemmo na bákya-nwu ɔbuli báni-nwu bésienku Babilon.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ƒui ni, na Babilonƒuɔ bekpone báakyula kɔduli kɔni nkya Yerusalem ƒui úbunku ɔga kesii lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ƒui. Na báƒɛ ɔma unengudi awodu ammɔ ƒui béwi kalɔ.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Babilonƒuɔ bagyumanane lɛlɔ ɔnune unengu ƒui ɔni baalɔ Nebusaradan ɔ́ya na bákpanku bekyuli bani ƒui nébu bakya Yerusalem mmɔ ku bani néeti lɛlɔ béte-nwu ƒui bátɔlɔku aani bekyuli beƒiedi kalɛ úsienku Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani ndi bawabane geen na beeebo lɛla lɛla kani nébu bakya Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ. Na Nebusaradan ɔmɛni úte-ma kɔlɔ ku mmo bɔdi.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar had given the following orders to Nebuzaradan:
translation_verse: Amu na Nebukadnesar úbo Nebusaradan ɔda ɔmɛni ɔnini,

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, Nebushazban, Nergal Sharezer, and the other officers of King Nebuchadnezzar
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Nebusaradan ku Nebusasban ku Nergal-Saresa ku Ɔga Nebukadnesar benengu bamba ƒui

english_verse: sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah. The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
translation_verse: bémene bana bekpone badi banii babakpanku-mi basiku ɔga kesii bagyumanane kaduli kesii kani na nka nkya mmɔ beboku. Na béti-mi bákya Ahikam ubidi Gedalia ɔni ndi Saƒan uwɔ kɔnu banii uti-mi usienku mina kaduli. Na béte-mi kuƒi ka lɛ́sɔ nkya bekyuli bani nébu kudɔ na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ. Unwoti Úse Kenye Ka Ɔdubo Ebedmelek Bɔgyumana

english_verse: While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na ndi ɔtɔntɛne na nkya ɔga kesii bagyumane kaduli mmɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔni nsu

english_verse: But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Nsu ka áƒɔ-mi ádi na ƒula anu asia-mi lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, ndubo-ɔ bɔgyumana bɔsiku Yudaƒuɔ benengu enu kemmo. Na si uwi ɔni na ɔgbankpi ɔ́bwɛ úwi Yuda lɛlɔ ni, ndubudie-ɔ na lɛya na elie ngba. Ami Unwoti násu.”

english_verse: I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free.
translation_verse: Ami ku bekyuli bani nási Yuda ku Yerusalem ƒui na bébo kɔgba na bákpanku baatɔlɔku béselaku Babilon. Na Nebusaradan ndi unengu ɔni mɔɔnu bagyumanane bani ndanku-bu mmɔ lɛlɔ. Ka bédi-bu bényene Rama ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na bédie-mi kɔgba kemmo na béte-mi bɔnwuna.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan said: Jeremiah, the Lord your God warned your people that he would bring disaster on this land.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Nebusaradan ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Yeremia, Unwoti, ƒula Katɔti, ɔ́lɛ ƒula kadi bekyuli kpakplaa ɔ́siku ɔgbankpi ɔni na ɔdubo bɔya na ɔlɛku-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But they continued to rebel against him, and now he has punished them just as he threatened.
translation_verse: Nsu beni na benye baabla ala ani mɔɔta teenye-nwu lɛlɔ uwi biala. Na ɔƒaani ni, ɔ́ni-ma kɔtu aani kalɛ na ubo-ma lɛnimi enwu úse.

english_verse: Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish.
translation_verse: Ɔmwi ni, lɛ́da kɔgba kɔmɛni muudie-ɔ enu taatina ka líte-ɔ bɔnwuna! Si aayɔ́ ni, akana na asiaku-mi na busie Babilon na ndubɔnu ka bánu-ɔ lɛlɔ kaduɛ kalɛ na ɔ́manku. Na si mɛni lɛnɔ na anii aasɔ akya ni, ebo kuƒi ka esie kesii biala na aayɔ́.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar has chosen Gedaliah to rule Judah. You can live near Gedaliah, and he will provide for you, or you can live anywhere else you choose. Nebuzaradan gave me a supply of food, then let me leave.
translation_verse: Gedalia na Ɔga Nebukadnesar ɔ́ƒuna ka utaadi Yuda kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ. Akana na elie ede-nwu na ɔdubute-ɔ lɛla biala lɛni na adubɔwia iye akana na elie kesii biala na aayɔ́.” Amu na Nebusaradan úte-mi adila ku ala ani ƒui na ndubɔyaki, na ɔ́nyonu-mi na lɛ́tɔlɔ.

english_verse: I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah. The Harvest Is Brought In
translation_verse: Na lɛ́bla kasusu ka ndubɔsɔ lɛkya mina kadi bekyuli kudɔ na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ, na lilie Mispa ɔma kemmo na lilie lide Gedalia. Báƒɛ Edula Básiku Mmo Béboku

english_verse: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, together with Johanan and Jonathan, the two sons of Kareah, had been officers in Judah's army. And so had Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah from Maacah. They and their troops had been stationed outside Jerusalem and had not been captured. They heard that Gedaliah had been chosen to rule Judah, and that the poorest men, women, and children had not been taken away to Babylonia. So they went to Mizpah and met with their new ruler.
translation_verse: Netania ubidi ɔni baalɔ Ismael ku Karea bebi bananabi inyɔ bani ndi Yonatan ku Yohanan ni, ama nádi Yudaƒuɔ bekpone benengu. Na lɛni kani na Tanhumet ubidi Seraia ku Netoƒani ɔni baalɔ Eƒai bebi bananabi ku Yasania ɔni nási Maaka. Ama ku bana bekpone ni, bana kakyakɔ keeebo Yerusalem ɔma kemmo, anwuɔsu kekpo kéteƒie ama. Na bénu ka Gedalia ndi ukyuli ɔni na báƒuna ka utaadi Yuda lɛlɔ na bawabane bani mɔɔyaki ala teetulo ƒui banana ku beleku ku banamu ama béteti-ma bátatɔlɔku bétesienku Babilon. Anwuɔsu bésie Mispa mmɔ banii batánu bana lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔwɔdi.

english_verse: Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Amu na Gedalia ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Liti mina litemi muute-mii ɔni na utalɛka bɛyia Babilonƒuɔ kabla bablane bammɔ. Mmomu bɛsɔ bɛkya kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ na bɛsiaku Babilonƒuɔ Ɔga Nebukadnesar na lɛla biala lɛdubuse kaduɛ lite-mii.

english_verse: I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
translation_verse: Ami ndubulie mɛni na ntaaƒɔ Babilonƒuɔ benengu bani ndubo mɛni buteebo. Nsu amii ni, bɛsɔ binwini bisie bina lɛma kemmo na bitaƒɛ edula biboku na bɛbla ntɛ na bidie nnɔ bɔdi lɛnɔ biboku na buse lɛlɛ kama.”

english_verse: Earlier, when the Babylonians had invaded Judah, many of the Jews escaped to Moab, Ammon, Edom, and several other countries. But these Jews heard that the king of Babylonia had appointed Gedaliah as ruler of Judah, and that only a few people were left there. So the Jews in these other countries came back to Judah and helped with the grape and fruit harvest, which was especially large that year. Gedaliah Is Murdered
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Babilonƒuɔ báka Yuda bukpo ni, Yudaƒuɔ pii békeli bésie Moab ku Amon ku Edom abi lɛlɔ ku kɔlɔ bamba pii lɛnɔ kemmo. Nsu Yudaƒuɔ bamɛni bénu ka Gedalia na Babilonƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́ƒuna úse ka utaadi Yuda kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ, nsu nkyuli ɛlɛɛ kani nébu bakya kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bekyuli bamɛni bénwini bébo banii bebebunku na bede egyiibi ani nánwu kaduɛ mmɔ na lɛkwa lɛmmɔ kemmo utulo akwa bamba ƒui. Bekyuli Badi Bádu Gedalia

english_verse: One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, Yohanan ɔ́sala banana bamba bani na anwu ku-ma ƒui nádi Yuda kalɔ bekpone benengu na bébo Gedalia kudɔ na Mispa ɔma kemmo.

english_verse: They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!” Gedaliah refused to believe them,
translation_verse: Mmɔ na básu-nwu banini, “Gedalia, búbo bubete-ɔ kati na enye kagyumana ka Amon Ɔga Baalis útétiku Ismael na kayu kenye ɔnii ubadu-ɔ!” Nsu Gedalia útaƒɔ-ma kenye kammɔ útadi.

english_verse: so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yohanan ɔ́bɛ úbo Gedalia kudɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ya na lɛdu Ismael lɛbɛla na ukyuli ɔdi ɔɔɔdubo bɔti ukyuli ɔni nádu-nwu. Ɔsika nkyuli ɛlɛɛ bani nébu na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mɛni beeemomo na ƒula lɛlɔ kani na bana lɛlɔ bɔnu bɔsia. Na si banii bádu-ɔ ɔƒɛni ni, badubo-ma bɔbɔku bugyingya ƒui iye badu-ma muedi.”

english_verse: Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_verse: Amu na Gedalia údie kenye ɔnini, “Tadu Ismael! Ɔsika lɛla lɛni na ásu ásiku-nwu lɛlɔ lilakana na wabla litemi geen.”

english_verse: But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Nsu na kɔbuli maatɛdi kemmo ni, Netania ubidi Ismael ɔni ndi Elisama uwɔ úbo Mispa ɔma kemmo na ɔdanku nwuna bekpone leevu badi. Ismael ɔmɛni ɔdi ɔga kesii ukyuli na ɔ́di ɔga lɛlɔ benengu akɔ unwi. Na básiaku anwu ku nwuna bekpone bammɔ ka babadiku Gedalia na nwuna kesii.

english_verse: During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Kadikɔ mmɔ na Ismael ku nwuna bekpone bammɔ bádu Gedalia ɔni na nka Babilon ɔga ɔ́ƒuna ka utaanu Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
translation_verse: Na bádu Yudaƒuɔ bani nkya Gedalia kudɔ mmɔ ku Babilonƒuɔ bekpone bani lɛnɔ nkya mmɔ.

english_verse: Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah.
translation_verse: Amu na Ismael ɔ́sia ɔ́lɛ ɔma ɔban kenye útásiaku-ma na ɔ́bla lɛlɔ aani si buwulo na ɔda na ɔ́su bekyuli bamɛni ɔnii basia Mispa ɔma kemmo na badu Gedalia ɔni mɔɔnu Yuda kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔni na béduo Mispa ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo kani na ɔ́ya na nwuna bekpone bammɔ bádu-ma na bebo-ma bákya abiɔ kemmo.

english_verse: He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field.
translation_verse: Na bana akɔ leevu badi ama ni, utaya na badu-ma, ɔsika básu-nwu banii bebo antabi edula ebi lidu lidu ku uwɔ ku nnɔ bɔni na bábɛla bákya alakpi akɔ kesii kadi na badubuti bete-nwu ɔsu.

english_verse: The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
translation_verse: Na abiɔ ani kemmo na úbo bekpine bamɛni ɔ́kya ni, Yudaƒuɔ Ɔga ɔni baalɔ Asa néku-nya kalɛ na bataaƒɔ ɔnantu ntu teewi-mu kemmo, ɔsika ɔɔyia Israelƒuɔ Ɔga Baasa ɔdubɔka Mispa ɔma ɔmmɔ ɔkya limeyi na basɔ balákɛ ntu kedukɔ na nwuna ɔma bekyuli balákɛ ntu bɔni na bani.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Ɔga Nebukadnesar bagyumanane unengu ɔni ndi Nebusaradan ɔ́da Ɔga Sedekia ku nwuna bebi belekubi ku bekyuli bamba pii ɔ́ka Mispa ɔnii Gedalia utaanu-ma lɛlɔ. Nsu bekyuli bamɛni na Ismael ɔ́kpanku ɔ́tɔlɔku úselaku Amon na Yordan Ketu ɔvi aani nwuna bekyuli beƒiedi.

english_verse: Johanan and the other army officers heard what Ishmael had done.
translation_verse: Kama ƒui ni, Yohanan ku bekpone benengu bamba bénu lɛla lɛni na Ismael ɔ́bla.

english_verse: So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ama ku bana bekpone báta básia Ismael kama na bátásiaku-nwu na ubu bonwu ɔdi kɔtu kesii kani baalɔ Gibeon.

english_verse: and turned around and ran toward Johanan.
translation_verse: na bénwini békeli badubo Yohanan ku nwuna badi kudɔ.

english_verse: But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon. Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
translation_verse: Nsu Ismael ku nwuna badi maane békeli na bátɔlɔ bésie Amon. Yohanan Ɔ́bla Kasusu Ka Utiku Bekyuli Bammɔ Usienku Egyipte

english_verse: Johanan and the officers had rescued the women, children, and royal officials that Ishmael had taken prisoner after killing Gedaliah. Johanan led the people from Gibeon
translation_verse: Yohanan ku bekpone benengu bakladi bédie beleku ku banamu bammɔ ku ɔga kesii benengu bani ƒui na nka béƒie baatɔlɔku mmɔ na Gedalia bɔdu kama. Na Yohanan ɔ́sɔku-ma únwiniku ɔ́siku Gibeon mmɔ.

english_verse: toward Egypt. They wanted to go there, because they were afraid of what the Babylonians would do when they found out that Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, the ruler appointed by King Nebuchadnezzar. The People Ask Jeremiah To Pray for Them On the way to Egypt, we stopped at the town of Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Na béti bésela Egyipte kakɛ. Na báyɔ ka besie mmɔ, ɔsika baayia na baaagyi lɛla lɛni na Babilonƒuɔ badubɔsu banii baabla si bénu ka Ismael ɔ́du Gedalia ɔni na Ɔga Nebukadnesar ɔ́ƒuna ka utaanu Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ. Uwi ɔni na bɔkɛ ulu búsela Egyipte ni, búdi búnye Gerut Kimham, ɔma ɔni nde Betlehem mmɔ.

english_verse: Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Karea ubidi Yohanan ku Hosaia ubidi Yesenia ku bekpone bamba bakladi ƒui na kasala kammɔ kemmo bébo-mi kudɔ,

english_verse: and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left.
translation_verse: na básu-mi banini, “Buvele, kpali Unwoti, ƒula Katɔti, na bula lili te-bu. Agyi ka nka bekyuli bakya Yuda kalɔ mɛni kuuku, nsu bula ɛlɛɛ kani nébu ɔƒɛni aani kalɛ na awɔ ɔla aanu.

english_verse: Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ye Unwoti kesii kani na ɔɔwia ka buteesie ku lɛla lɛni na ɔɔyɔ́ ka bɔbla.”

english_verse: “All right,” I answered, “I will pray to the Lord your God, and I will tell you everything he says.”
translation_verse: Amu na lídie kenye nnini, “Ɔdia, ndubo Unwoti bina Katɔti bɔkpali na livele, na lɛla biala na ɔ́su-mi ni, ndubɔya na bɛti.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord himself will be our witness that we promise to do whatever he says,
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ama lɛnɔ báƒɔ banini, “Unwoti ɔlati ndubo-bu kenye budie ka búse kenye ka lɛla biala na ɔ́su-bu ni, bɔdubɔbla bɔsiaku lɛni kani.

english_verse: even if it isn't what we want to do. We will obey the Lord so that all will go well for us.”
translation_verse: Ina ɔɔɔdi bula lɛƒɔyɔ muedi ni, bɔdubunu-nwu litemi na bɔdi-ni lɛlɔ kalɛ na ala asɔ adianku-bu.”

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for
translation_verse: Emeyi leevu kama ni, Unwoti úte-mi bɔti na lɛla lɛni na

english_verse: Johanan, the officers, and the other people. So I called them together
translation_verse: lɛsu Yohanan ku bekpone benengu ku bekyuli bakladi bammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu lɛ́lɔ-ma ƒui lɛ́sala,

english_verse: and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said: You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do.
translation_verse: na lɛ́su-ma ka Unwoti, Israel Katɔti ɔnini, “Bɛ́su Yeremia bɛnii ɔkpali-mi na uye-mi lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka bɛbla.

english_verse: I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you.
translation_verse: Nsu muute-mii bɔbuɛ, ɔsika bina ɔbladu náya na ɔdi ka lɛni-mii kɔtu kɔmmɔ udu. Na mɔɔsu-mii ɔƒaani nnii bɛsɔ bilie Yuda mɛni kani na ndubɔsɔku-mii lɛlɛ aani kalɛ na baalɛ lɛla lɛdi na lɛnu-mii lɛlɔ na bɛbi lɛlɔ. Na ɔɔɔdi ɔni na lɛgyingya-mii iye lɛgyu-mii lidie bina kenyekɔ ku ligyiitu.

english_verse: Don't be afraid of the King of Babylonia. I will protect you from him,
translation_verse: Bitayia Babilon ɔga, ɔsika ndububo-mii bɔgyumana bɔsiku nwuna bukpoku kudɔ.

english_verse: and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
translation_verse: Na ndububo-nwu lɛlɔ bunye muedi na ɔsɔku bina mmo ute-mii.

english_verse: But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God.
translation_verse: “Ɔƒɛni kalɛ ɔdubo-mii bɔbla kalɛ kadi na bɛsu bɛnini, ‘Bɔɔɔdubo Unwoti bula Katɔti litemi lɛmɛni bunu na bɔsɔ bɔkya Yuda mɛni.

english_verse: We are going to Egypt, where there is plenty of food and no danger of war.”
translation_verse: Bɔ́tɔlɔ búsela Egyipte kesii kani na adila akya kaduɛ na kekpo ɔgbankpi ɔdi uuubo.’

english_verse: People of Judah, you survived when the Babylonian army attacked. Now you are planning to move to Egypt, and if you do go, this is what will happen.
translation_verse: Yuda kadi bekyuli, uwi ɔni na kekpo kamɛni kébo na bina bekisine békpo-mii ni, bítekpi bilie ngba. Na ɔƒɛni amu binye bɛɛbla kasusu ka biteesie Egyipte. Na mɔɔyá na bɛti lɛla lɛni ndubo-mii bɔlɛku si bísie mmɔ.

english_verse: You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
translation_verse: Kekpo ku kɔka ku lɛlɛ na bɛɛyia na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ mɛni, nsu ala amɛni adubo-mii bɔsiaku buteesie Egyipte mmɔ na abadu-mii. Na ɔgbankpi ɔni na ndubɔya na ubo-mii lɛlɔ na mmɔ ni, ɔdi biala ɔɔɔdubo-nwu kemmo bɔlɛ.

english_verse: I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word. Jeremiah Gives a Warning
translation_verse: “Ami Unwoti néti kɔnyi lɛ́kya Yerusalemƒuɔ na lɛ́ni-ma kɔtu. Na si bísie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, ndubo kɔnyi buti bɔkya-mii na lɛni-mii kɔtu lɛni kani na bɛsɔ bɛɛɛdubo bina ɔma bɔnu limeyi lɛdi. Liƒu bonwu lɛdubo bekyuli bɔda na lɛla lɛni lɛ́bla ɔsu. Na badubo bina lɛnyi bɔlɔ aani ewida bakya bekyuli.” Yeremia Úbo Bekyuli Bammɔ Ɔda Kpakplaa

english_verse: I told the people: You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt.
translation_verse: Lɛ́su bekyuli bammɔ nnini, “Amii bíkeli ɔgbankpi ɔni nálɛku Yuda, nsu ɔƒɛni amu ni, Unwoti uubó-mii ɔda ɔnii bitanya Egyipte ɔgba.

english_verse: You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake,
translation_verse: Bɛ́su-mi bɛnii nkpali Unwoti bula Katɔti na livele-nwu na ɔtina-mii lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka bɛbla na bíse kenye ka bɛdubɔdi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ. Nsu ɔmmɔ ɔdi-mii bɔƒiɔ bubendi.

english_verse: because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him.
translation_verse: Ɔsika ɔni na lɛ́su-mii lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔwia ka bɛbla ni, bíni na bɛnii bilenu-nwu litemi.

english_verse: And so, you will die in Egypt from war, hunger, and disease.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na kekpo ku kɔka ku ɔlɛ ɔdubo-mii bɔdu na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: I told the people everything the Lord had told me.
translation_verse: Lɛ́su bekyuli bammɔ lɛla biala na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi.

english_verse: But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt.
translation_verse: Nsu Hosaia ubidi Asaria ku Karea ubidi Yohanan ku batuɔkplune bamba básu-mi banini, “Ɔkɔ na aanyi! Unwoti ɔdi útasu-ɔ ɔnii su-bu anii butesie Egyipte.

english_verse: Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
translation_verse: Bɔgyi Neria ubidi Baruk násu-ɔ ɔnii su-bu lɛni, ɔsika ɔɔwia ka Babilonƒuɔ bebeƒie-bu kalɛ na bakpanku-bu besienku Babilon iye badu-bu muedi.”

english_verse: Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command.
translation_verse: Yohanan ku bekpone benengu bamba ku bekyuli bakladi ƒui béni ka basɔ bakya Yuda ina ka Unwoti úbo-ma ɔda.

english_verse: So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Yohanan ku benengu bammɔ bátɔnku-bu na buti bɔ́yu ulu bésela Egyipte. Na bekyuli bani ƒui náyu ulu ɔmmɔ ndi bekyuli bani negyingya bakya kɔlɔ ƒui lɛlɔ na básɔ bénwini bébo ka nka bebelie Yuda.

english_verse: Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
translation_verse: Ami ku Baruk nkɛ ku bekyuli bamba bani na nka bulie Gekalia kudɔ ɔni na Nebusaradan, Babilonƒuɔ bagyumanane unengu ɔmmɔ, ɔ́su-nwu kpakplaa ka utaanu abu ku ɔga bebi belekubi bammɔ ku banana ɛlɛɛ badi ku beleku ku banamu bammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes,
translation_verse: Bekyuli bammɔ bétenu Unwoti litemi na bátɔlɔ bésie Egyipte na bétéli kesii kani baalɔ banii Taƒanes.

english_verse: when the Lord told me:
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini,

english_verse: Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
translation_verse: “Yeremia, ti atabi adi sienku aban ɔgadine ɔmmɔ kaduli kayakun na Taƒanes mmɔ na eku-nya akya atimbɔ aƒidi ani na béti bákya ulu mmɔ kalɔ na Yudaƒuɔ bammɔ anumi.

english_verse: Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama na asu-ma ka ami Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, Israel Katɔti, nátala nnii balɔ mina kabla ɔblane Nebukadnesar ɔni nási Babilon. Ndubo-nwu bɔkpanku buboku mɛni na ubatu nwuna lɛga kadikɔ na use nwuna lɛgaboku mɛni na ɔdi lɛlɔ na kesii kani na éku atabi ani na lɛsu-ɔ mɛni ákya kalɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: He will attack Egypt and kill many of its people; others will die of disease or be dragged away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Ɔdubo ubekpo Egyipte na ɔdu bekyuli pii na ɔlɛ ɔdu bana akɔ badi iye bakya-ma lɛbuli batɔlɔku aani bekyuli beƒiedi.

english_verse: I will let him set Egypt's temples on fire, and he will either burn or carry off their idols. He will destroy the sacred monuments at the temple of the sun-god. Then Nebuchadnezzar will pick the land clean, just like a shepherd picking the lice off his clothes. And he will return safely home.
translation_verse: Ndubo bɔya na ɔtu ogya ɔkya Egyipteƒuɔ baƒiɔ akpabi na ɔkyula iye uti baƒiɔ bavɔdi ku anwidi ammɔ ɔtɔlɔku. Na lɛya na ubile bana ekpo ani bábla na ese-ma kedee ute bana ɔƒɛ baƒiɔ mmɔ. “Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Nebukadnesar ɔdubo kalɔ kemodi kammɔ bɔgyu buɛɛ bɔtɔlɔku aani kalɛ na baami kebweyi na adala lɛlɔ na lɛla lɛdi lilabla-nwu.”

english_verse: The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnii ntɛmiku Yudaƒuɔ bani nkya Migdol ku Taƒanes ku Memƒis lɛma kemmo na Egyipte kalɔ katɔ kakɛ ku bani na bakya kalɔ kammɔ kada kakɛ na lɛsu-ma nnini,

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today,
translation_verse: “Ami ndi Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, Israel Katɔti. Na bɛ́nu kalɛ na lɛ́yila Yerusalem udu ku lɛma lɛni nkya Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔmwi ni, lɛma lɛmmɔ lɛ́bwɛ na liwi ukpludi,

english_verse: because the people of Judah made me angry by worshiping gods that had never helped them or their ancestors.
translation_verse: ɔsika Yudaƒuɔ bákya-mi kɔnyi na ɔni na bakya baakpá baƒiɔ bani nétebunku bana bati kuuku badi kudii ɔsu.

english_verse: Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning,
translation_verse: Mɔɔyá na mina kabla bablane kenye bedie beebo taabatɛmiku-ma taasia kama uwi ndi uwi kalɛ na nkisi bana ablala ani muusé lɛlɔ mmɔ. Na bébo-ma ɔda kpakplaa ka bada bana alaekpidi bɔbla baya.

english_verse: but they refused to listen and would not stop worshiping other gods.
translation_verse: Nsu béni na bétenu na banii balada bana baƒiɔ bɔkpa lɛnɔ baláya.

english_verse: Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
translation_verse: Kawɔlɔkɔ ni, mina kɔnyi kɔ́bwɛ kúwi-ma lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na ketu keeyi taabwɛ na keeƒie bekyuli. Na ɔmwi ni, Yerusalem ku Yuda lɛma liwi ukpludi aani kebu alakpi.

english_verse: Why do you now insist on heading for another disaster? A disaster that will destroy not only you, but also your children and babies.
translation_verse: “Na ɔƒaani ni, bi ɔsu na binye kpakplaa bɛnii bɛsɔ biiti lɛlɔ bitákya ɔgbankpi ɔbambadi kemmo? Ɔgbankpi ɔni na ɔɔɔdi amii lɛti ndubo-nwu kemmo buduo mmomu ku bina beleku ku bebi ku banamu ƒui?

english_verse: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Bina baƒiɔ bani na bɛɛkpá ku kalɛ na bɛɛkyula oloƒui teete baƒiɔ bamba ɔ́si ɔni na bɛ́si Egyipte bíbo mɛni ɔ́ya na lɛ́kɛ kɔnyi geen. Na bɛdubo kukpi kɔni muusé lɛlɔ bukpi. Na kadi bamba bekyuli badubo-mii lɛnyi bɔlɔ bewida bekyuli banii ɔlɛku-ma kalɛ na ɔ́lɛku-mii.

english_verse: When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni kemmo na bilie Yerusalem ku Yuda ni, bɛ́siaku bina bati kuuku ɔbladu kama na bɛɛbla likpidi aani bina baga ku beleku baga kalɛ.

english_verse: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Na úti úbedu ku ɔƒɛni muedi ni, bina lɛlɔ katɔ bɔkɔliku ɔsu bilakana na biti ɔbu bite-mi na bitaadi ɔda bubo ku ala ani na lɛtina bina bati kuuku lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have decided to wipe you out with disasters.
translation_verse: “Ami Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui lɛ́lɛ ugyii ka ndubɔya na ɔgbankpi lidu libo-mii lɛlɔ na lɛyila-mii lidie ƒui.

english_verse: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Bina ɛlɛɛ bani kani nébu na Yuda na bɛ́lɛ ugyii ka biteesie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu ogya ogya kukpi na bɛdubo bukpi na kekpokɔ na kɔka lɛnɔ kɔdu-mii. Na bina lɛnyi na kɔlɔ bamba bekyuli badubo bɔkpali buwida bɔkya bekyuli.

english_verse: I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you.
translation_verse: Kekpo ku kɔka ku lɛlɛ lidu na líti lɛ́ni Yerusalemƒuɔ kɔtu na lɛni kani na ndubo amii lɛnɔ bɔbla.

english_verse: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
translation_verse: Bina ɔdi ɔɔɔdubo bubu bulie ngba. Bɛdubɔbla kasusu ka bɛdubɔsɔ binwini bisie Yuda kalɔ limeyi lɛdi, nsu bina ɛlɛɛ bani ndubo kukpi bukeli kani ndubɔkana na benwini besie mmɔ.” Bekyuli Bammɔ Béni Ka Bakpa Unwoti

english_verse: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
translation_verse: Yudaƒuɔ lisu bonwu lɛdi bani nákya Egyipte kalɔ kammɔ katɔ ku kada kakɛ ƒui benye beenú asa na mɔɔsu ala ani na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi. Na banana bammɔ ketulodikɔ na kasalakɔ kammɔ bagyi ka bana beleku baakyula oloƒui teete baƒiɔ bamba. Anwuɔsu ama ku bana beleku ƒui báva ku lɛdi momoomo banini,

english_verse: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
translation_verse: “Yeremia, bi nkɛ-bu si Unwoti lɛnyi kemmo na enye aatɛmi? Buni geen na búni bɔnii bulenu-ɔ litemi!

english_verse: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
translation_verse: Astarot ɔni ndi kayaa uleku ɔga baƒiɔ na abu búse kenye ka bɔdubɔkpa. Na ɔmmɔ geen na bɔdubo bɔbla. Bɔdubo oloƒui bɔkyula bute-nwu na buwi ntɛ kalɔ bɔkpa-nwu kalɛ kani na bula bati kuuku ku baga ku bula batɔnkune bábla uwi ɔni na bɔ́kya Yerusalem ku Yuda lɛma bamba kemmo. Lɛni na bɔ́bla na adila ákya-bu kaduɛ uwi ɔmmɔ na ala ádianku-bu na likpidi lɛdi lítalɛku-bu kudii.

english_verse: But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔni kani na bɔ́da oloƒui bɔkyula teete-nwu bɔ́ya na bɔ́da ntɛ kalɔ buwi teete-nwu lɛnɔ bɔ́ya kani na búse kakɔ buukpi na kekpokɔ na kɔka lɛnɔ kɔɔdú-bu.”

english_verse: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
translation_verse: Amu na beleku bammɔ lɛnɔ básu banini, “Bɔ́kya Yuda na bútaakpa Kayaa Uleku Ɔga na buteeti ntɛ ku bodobodo sɛsɛɛ ɔdi udu na béƒi-nwu na nwuna udu kenye taakpa teete-nwu. Na bula bagya lɛnɔ bagyi ɔmɛni na bátunaku-bu lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: Then I told the crowd:
translation_verse: Mmɔ na lɛ́su kasalakɔ kammɔ nnini,

english_verse: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
translation_verse: “Bilakali ka Unwoti ɔ́ti ka lɛni na amii ku bina bati kuuku ku bina batɔnkune ku baga ku bekyuli bakladi ƒui bítaakyula oloƒui teete baƒiɔ bamba na Yerusalem ku Yuda kesii biala?

english_verse: And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na útulo-nwu na ɔ́nɔ bɔnu ni, úwida bina kalɔ na káta kénwini ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kalɛ udu na kese ɔmwi na bɛɛnu mɛni.

english_verse: This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni úbo-mii lɛlɔ, ɔsika bɛ́kpa baƒiɔ bamba na bɛ́ta bínye Unwoti lɛlɔ na bíni bɛnii bilenu-nwu litemi na bɛsiaku nwuna ɔda bubo ku ala ani na ɔɔtina lɛlɔ ɔsu.”

english_verse: Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́su banana bammɔ ku bana beleku ka Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔnini, “Na Egyipte mɛni lɛnɔ ni, bɛmu binye bina linyese lɛlɔ ka bɛdubo bina lɛla lɛni na bɛɛlɔ bɛnii Kayaa Uleku Ɔga bɔkpa na bɛkyula oloƒui ku ntɛ akpala bite-nwu.

english_verse: Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name.
translation_verse: Bɛdi bina linyese lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ! Nsu mɔɔyá na bɛti lɛla lɛni ndubo-mii bɔlɛku. Ka ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti ɔsu ni, líse kenye ka kenye biala kadi kasɔ keeebo na bɛdubuse na mina lɛnyi kemmo na menu mete-mii.

english_verse: Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death.
translation_verse: Na ɔni na ntaanu-mii lɛlɔ kenye ni, ndubɔwia ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na masia mani-mii kɔtu mmomu. Na bina badi bɛdubo bukpi na kekpokɔ na kɔka lɛnɔ kɔdu badi.

english_verse: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
translation_verse: Bina ɛlɛɛ kani ndubɔlɛ ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni kemmo na basɔ benwini besie Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔdubɔya na amii bani ƒui nésie Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ bɛti ka si ami lɛ́su nnii lɛla lɛdi lɛdubo bɔlɛ ni, ɔ́bla bi ɔ́bla dɛ ni, lɛla lɛmmɔ lɛdubɔlɛ lɛni kani. Ina bi na amii bɛ́su.

english_verse: And here is how you will know that I will keep my threats to punish you in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na ɔmɛni na bɛdubuti bɛnu bɛti ka ngba liƒu akyala ani na mɔɔsu ka adubɔlɛku-mii na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ mɛni adubo bɔlɛ lɛni sɔsɔ.

english_verse: I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
translation_verse: Ndubo Egyipteƒuɔ Ɔga Hoƒre bɔnyonu bute nwuna bekisine na badu-nwu aani kalɛ na lɛ́nyonu Ɔga Sedekia líte Babilonƒuɔ Ɔga Nebukadnesar na ɔ́du-nwu.”

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him.
translation_verse: Na Ɔga Yehoiakim lɛga bɔdi na Yuda lɛkwa linedi kemmo ni, Baruk únweni lɛla biala na lɛ́su-nwu.

english_verse: Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnii nsu Baruk ɔnini,

english_verse: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
translation_verse: “Enye eewulo kɔnyana na aadú ami Unwoti kɔtɔ na ƒula lɛbibo ku kɔnyana kɔni kemmo na akya ɔsu, ku kalɛ na lɛlɔ lítu-ɔ na alakɛ bɔnwuna bɔdi.

english_verse: But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted.
translation_verse: Nsu na kayawi kamɛni kemmo ni, ndaku bɔbuɛ lɛtɔ lɛni ƒui na lɛ́tu, na mɔɔgyú ala ani ƒui na lɛ́lɛ.

english_verse: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ndubo bɔya na ɔgbankpi utaalɛ kesii biala. Anwuɔsu tabla kasusu na ala ebendi adi bɔbla lɛlɔ ete lɛlɔ. Nsu muusé kenye ka ndubo-ɔ bɔgyumana na elekpi na ɔmɛni kemmo. Ami Unwoti násu.”

english_verse: The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world. What the Lord Says about Egypt
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔɔsu-mi ala ani na lɛsu kadi bamba bekyuli bakladi lɛlɔ bɔsu bɔsu. Unwoti Ɔ́su Lɛla Lɛdi Ɔ́siku Egyipte Lɛlɔ

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Yehoiakim ɔɔdi lɛga na Yuda lɛkwa linedi kemmo ni, Babilonƒuɔ Ɔga Nebukadnesar ɔ́di Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ɔni baalɔ Neko lɛlɔ na kekpokɔ na ɔma unengudi ɔni baalɔ Karkemis na mmɔ ude Euƒrate Ketu. Na lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnii nsu nsiku Egyipteƒuɔ bekpone lɛlɔ na bɛdubo bunu mɛni.

english_verse: It's time to go into battle! So grab your shields,
translation_verse: “Uwi údu ka bɛta kekpo, anwuɔsu bikeyi bina agyumanala,

english_verse: saddle your horses, and polish your spears. Put on your helmets and armor, then take your positions.
translation_verse: na bɛbala bina bapɔnkɔ ekpola, na bisusu bina atula nnɔ. Biti bina kekpo kɔbwa bibi eli na bɛda kekpo adala bamba lɛnɔ ƒui na biténye bina kɔgyumanakɔ.

english_verse: I can see the battle now— you are defeated and running away, never once looking back. Terror is all around.
translation_verse: Ami ndaku kekpo kammɔ bɔnu kalɛ na kaaví na báadi-mii lɛlɔ kuuku na bíkeli bɛɛtɔlɔ na kama bunwini bɔnu buuubo ina kunwi. Liƒu bonwu lɛ́ka lɛ́mana-mii lɛƒɛnyi ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You are strong and run fast, but you can't escape. You fall in battle near the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Bibo lɛlɔ ɔkplu na beekeli usi momoomo, nsu bilakana bukeli bɔtɔlɔ bina bekisine kudɔ. Kekpo kéƒie-mii na Euƒrate Ketu kɔtu.

english_verse: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
translation_verse: “Kadi kamani bekyuli nákɔ badubo mɛni lɛni aani kalɛ na Nil Ketu keeyi taavia nwuna utubili?

english_verse: It is Egypt, rising with a roar like a raging river and saying, “I'll flood the earth, destroying cities, and killing everyone in them.”
translation_verse: Egyipte na ɔdi mɔɔkɔ́ lɛni aani kalɛ na ketu keeyi ku kɔku momoomo na ɔɔsu ɔnini, ‘Ndubuyi na lɛƒɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui na lɛbwɛ lɛma linengudi na lɛdu bekyuli bani ƒui nkya-ni kemmo.’

english_verse: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: “Egyipte, awɔ sie anumi na asu ƒula bekpone ku bana lɛkɛɛkɛ lɛni bada ƒui anii bikpo-ma kpakplaa. Na edie lɛdi ete ƒula bekpone akpa ammɔ anii babwɛ balɛ ku Kus bekpone ku Libia badi lɛnɔ bani nda agyumanala ku Lida bekpone bani nda kɔtaminta ku atula ƒui.

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful will win this battle and take revenge on his enemies. His sword will eat them and drink their blood until it is full. They will be killed in the north near the Euphrates River, as a sacrifice to the Lord.
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔdubo lɛlɔ bɔdi na kekpo kamɛni kemmo na udie nwuna bekisine kasi. Nwuna kewii kadubɔkɛ bɔdi na ɔni ubugya umo kaduɛ. Badubɔdu bekyuli bammɔ na kalɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ na Euƒrate Ketu kudɔ aani akpala bete Unwoti.

english_verse: Egypt, no medicine can heal you, not even the soothing lotion from Gilead.
translation_verse: “Egyipte, kuvo kɔdi kɔɔɔdubo-ɔ bɔkana bɔbwi, na Gilead nnɔmii bɔni mɔɔyala ɔlɔna buɛɛ mmɔ muedi bɔɔɔdubo-ɔ kebunku kadi bute.

english_verse: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
translation_verse: Kadi bekyuli ƒui badubo ƒula keku kani na eewulo bunu. Ɔsika bagyi ka ádi kɔƒa. Ƒula bekpone ƒui bebi kalɔ ɔni na beebuli teebo bana bakpana lɛlɔ.” Bébo Egyipte Ɔda Kpakplaa Ɔdi

english_verse: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Babilonƒuɔ Ɔga Nebukadnesar ɔkɛ ulu ka ubekpo Egyipteƒuɔ ni, Unwoti úbo-mi ɔda kpakplaa ɔdi ɔkɛnku Egyipte ɔma biala lɛlɔ, na bani ɔdi ntulo ƒui ndi Migdol ku Mimƒie ku Taƒanes lɛma lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́su-mi ɔnii nsu-ma ɔnini, “Bɛklibi lɛlɔ na binye kagyumana bite lɛlɔ! Bukpi kani na bekyuli beekpi na bina kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ kesii biala na kekpokɔ.

english_verse: I have struck down your mighty god Apis and chased him away.
translation_verse: Bina baƒiɔ benengudi bani ndi Apis ni, líibo-ma lɛ́ƒiɛmi kalɔ na lɛ́bɔku-nwu na úkeli ɔ́tɔlɔ.

english_verse: Your soldiers stumble over each other and say, “Get up! The enemy will kill us, unless we can escape to our own land.”
translation_verse: Na ƒula bekpone ni, bubuli kani na beebuli teebo bana bakpana lɛlɔ na baasu lɛlɔ banini, ‘Ta nye! Amu ntu bukeli na bukele búsie bula kalɔ lɛlɔ amu bekisine badubo-bu bɔdu.’

english_verse: Give the king of Egypt this new name, “Talks-Big-Does-Nothing.”
translation_verse: Sia Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga lɛnyi lɛwɔdi lɛmɛni anini, ‘Kenye Kétulo-nwu na Ulakana Lɛla Lɛla.’

english_verse: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
translation_verse: “Egyipte, ami Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui ndi Ɔga geen. Na ɔni na nli ngba mɛni bɔdi ni, bekisine bani muukpó-mii badubo-mii lɛlɔ bɔdi na bakuku betulo-mii aani kalɛ na Tabor Kɔbi kɔ́kuku kútulo abi ani náka ámana-nwu ƒui, iye kalɛ na Karmel Kɔbi kunye kangyaa na ɛpu kɔtu.

english_verse: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
translation_verse: Badubo-ɔ bɔkpanku bɔtɔlɔku aani ukyuli uƒiedi, anwuɔsu bo ala alɛɛ ani na adubuti ada ulu obo. Ƒula ɔma unengudi Memƒis ɔdubo buwi ukpludi ka ɔ́bwɛ úbie ɔsu.

english_verse: An enemy from the north will attack you, beautiful Egypt, like a fly biting a cow.
translation_verse: “Egyipte ɔbuni, ukisine ɔdi ɔdubɔsi katɔ kakɛ ubekpo-ɔ aani kalɛ na alɔlɔ ɔɔdu ɔmantɛ akɔ.

english_verse: The foreign soldiers you hired will turn and run. But they are doomed, like well-fed calves being led to the butcher. *
translation_verse: Na baƒɔ bekpone bani na átáƒɔ kayu kenye badubo bunwini na bekeli batɔlɔ. Nsu ama ɔdi lɛnɔ ɔ́sa aani ɔmantɛ bakɔ bebi bani na bányuɛ-ma na bélie lɛmwi na bákpanku-ma béselaku kadukɔ.

english_verse: The enemy army will go forward like a swarm of locusts. Your troops will feel helpless, like a snake in a forest
translation_verse: Bekisine bekpone lisu bonwu lɛdi badubɔgyu batɔ aani baalɔlɔ kalɛ. Na bina bekpone badubo bɔnu ka beeebo kablakɔ kadi na bana bekisine bammɔ kudɔ aani kalɛ na kɔlakpi kɔɔkya lɛku kemmo.

english_verse: when men with axes start chopping down trees. It can only hiss and try to escape.
translation_verse: Na si egyii badane ku bana kɔdadi bése kalɔ baaƒɛ egyii ammɔ teewi kalɔ ni, uƒiomu kani na baavwi na baawia kasiakɔ.

english_verse: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
translation_verse: Kɔƒa kɔdubo bina bekyuli bukpo na bana bekisine bani nási katɔ kakɛ mmɔ beƒie-ma.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
translation_verse: “Ami ndi Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, Israel Katɔti. Na uwi ɔsɔ uletu asa na ndubɔni Tebes baƒiɔ bani baalɔ Amon ku Egyipte baƒiɔ bamba biala na bakya kɔtu. Na ndubɔni Egyipteƒuɔ baga ku bana bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ku bani ƒui néti bana anu básia Egyipteƒuɔ ɔyikun lɛlɔ kɔtu.

english_verse: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
translation_verse: Na ndubo-ma bɔnyonu bɔ́kya Ɔga Nebukadnesar ku nwuna bekpone enu kemmo. Nsu muusé kenye lɛnɔ ka limeyi lɛdi ni, Egyipte ɔdubo bekyuli bɔsɔ bɔkɛ na belie mɛni aani kalɛ na bákya kuuku. Ami Unwoti násu. Unwoti Ɔdubo Israel Bɔkpanku Buboku Ɔma

english_verse: Israel, don't be afraid. Someday I will bring you home from foreign lands. You and your descendants will live in peace and safety, with nothing to fear.
translation_verse: “Limeyi lɛdi ni, ndubo-mii bɔkpanku bɔsiku baƒɔ kɔlɔ kɔni lɛlɔ na bɛkya búboku ɔma. Na amii ku bina bebi ku bawɔ ƒui bilie na atu bɔyɔ kemmo ɔni na bɛsɔ bilayia lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: So don't be afraid, even though now you deserve to be punished and have been scattered among other nations. But when I destroy them, I will protect you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bɛsɔ bitayia ina bɛ́manku ka bani-mii kɔtɔ na bégyingya-mii bákya baƒɔ kɔlɔ lɛnɔ lɛlɔ ɔƒɛni. Nsu si uwi ɔni na lɛ́yila-ma udu ni, ndubo-mii bɔgyumana. Ami Unwoti násu.”

english_verse: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
translation_verse: Asa na Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ɔdubukpo Gasa ɔma ni, Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnii nsu Ƒilistiƒuɔ ɔnini,

english_verse: I, the Lord, tell you that your land will be flooded with an army from the north. It will destroy your towns and sweep you away, moaning and screaming.
translation_verse: “Ami Unwoti mɔɔsu-mii nnii bekisine bekpone badubɔsi katɔ kakɛ na babaƒɔ bina kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui. Na badubo bina lɛma bɔbwɛ na bakpala-mii batɔlɔku na anu ka keku ku kɔvanu kɔda.

english_verse: When you hear the thunder of horses and chariots, your courage will vanish, and parents will even abandon their own children.
translation_verse: Si uwi ɔni na bínu ka bapɔnkɔ ku kɛɛkɛ kɔku kɔ́bwɛ kɔdubo ni, bina ɔtɔtɔ ɔdubɔgyu-mii na bawɔne badubɔda ama alati bana bebi bewi.

english_verse: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
translation_verse: Na amii baƒɔ bekeline bani nási Kreta, bina uwi údu na ndubo-mii udu bɔyila. Na bina akɔ ɔdi ɔsɔ ulébu na uteebunku Tiro ku Sidon lɛma linengudi lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: The Anakim who survive in Gaza and Ashkelon will mourn for you by shaving their heads and sitting in silence.
translation_verse: Na bablani bani na baalɔ-ma Anakƒuɔ bani nébu belie ngba na Gasa ku Askelon ni, badubo bana eli bukpeyi na basɔ belie kpoo beteewulo-mii kɔnyana.

english_verse: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
translation_verse: “Biiye bɛnii uwi ɛlɛ na ndubo-mii bukpo butálɛ ku mina kewii na bɛdubɔsu-mi bɛnii nsɔku-ka nkya livuo kemmo na lite-mii bɔnwuna.

english_verse: But how can my sword rest, when I have commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the seacoast?
translation_verse: Nsu dɛ na mina kewii kadubo bɔnwuna si lídie lɛdi líte-ka ka ukpo Askelonƒuɔ ku bani ƒui nli ɛpu kɔtu?”

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
translation_verse: Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, Israel Katɔti, ɔ́su-mi ɔnii nsu Moab kadi bekyuli ɔnini, “Nebo ɔma ɔdi ɔ́sa. Na badubo Kiriataim buƒie bɔƒɔ na bakya-nwu kɔƒa. Na nwuna awodu bonwu ani mɔɔgyumana ɔma ɔmmɔ muedi adubo bɔbwɛ.

english_verse: No one honors you, Moab. In Heshbon, enemies make plans to end your life. My sword will leave only silence in your town named “Quiet.”
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́sɔ ulabu awɔ Moab lɛnɔ. Na bekisine benye baabla kakwɛ na Hesbon ɔma kemmo kalɛ na babla na bada-a ngba liku. Mina kewii kabla kadubo bɔya na basia ƒula ɔma lɛnyi banii ‘Bɔba Diin.’

english_verse: The people of Horonaim will cry for help, as their town is attacked and destroyed.
translation_verse: Horonaim kadi bekyuli badubo butaava ku keku ka bebebunku-ma uwi ɔnii na beekpóku ɔma ɔmmɔ na bakyula-nwu.

english_verse: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
translation_verse: Badubo Moab butu bugyingya! Na ƒula bebi badubo buteewulo.

english_verse: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
translation_verse: Na badubo buteewulo si bakɛ ulu bákɔ bésela Lihuti. Na bataatɛmi taasiku ɔgbankpi ɔni nálɛku-ma lɛlɔ si báyu bésela Horonaim.

english_verse: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
translation_verse: Bikeli bɛlɛ na bɛƒɔ bina lili ngba! Na biti bina anumi bɛtina ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ kemmo aani alakpi akɔ ebuo ala utine.

english_verse: You thought you could be saved by your power and wealth, but you will be captured along with your god Chemosh, his priests, and officials.
translation_verse: Bɛ́bu bɛnii bina lɛkɛ ku ɔyikun ɔni na bibo ɔdubɔkana na ɔƒɔ-mii ngba, nsu badubo-mii buƒie ƒui ku bina Kemos baƒiɔ bammɔ ku bana bakpane ku nwuna benengu bammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Not one of your towns will escape destruction. I have told your enemies, “Wipe out the valley and the flatlands of Moab.
translation_verse: “Bina ɔma ɔdi biala ɔɔɔdubo bubu na balabwɛ-nwu. Ɔsika lɛ́su bina bekisine nnini, ‘Bɛkpala Moab Kɔwɛ kɔmmɔ kemmo ku kalɔ ƒiaa kammɔ ƒui bekyuli bidie-ka lɛlɔ.’

english_verse: Spread salt on the ground to kill the crops. Leave its towns in ruins, with no one living there.
translation_verse: Na bɛgyingya mma biwi kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛla na edula ammɔ ƒui ekpi. Na bɛbwɛ lɛma lɛmmɔ ƒui biwi kakɔ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ na ɔdi ɔsɔ utebu utelie mmɔ.

english_verse: I want you to kill the Moabites, and if you let them escape, I will put a curse on you.”
translation_verse: “Mɔɔwia ka bɛdu Moabƒuɔ ƒui. Na si bɛ́ya na bana ɔdi úkeli ni, ndubo-mii buwida.

english_verse: Moab, you are like wine left to settle undisturbed, never poured from jar to jar. And so, your nation continues to prosper and improve.
translation_verse: “Moab lɛni bise aani ntɛ bɔni na báda bése na búlie kalɔ, ɔsika belewilimi-mu taasia kama, anwuɔsu na bina ablala aakɔ́-mi katɔ uwi ndi uwi.

english_verse: But now, I will send enemies to pour out the wine and smash the jars!
translation_verse: Nsu ɔƒaani ni, ndubuti bekisine limene-mii na bewilimi ntɛ bɔɔmɔ na babwɛ kutubui kɔmmɔ!

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed, because your god Chemosh cannot save you, just as Bethel could not help the Israelites.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na kɔƒa kɔdubo-mii bukpo, ɔsika bina Kemos baƒiɔ baaadu-mii bɔkana bɔƒɔ aani kalɛ na Betel útakana na ɔƒɔ Israelƒuɔ.

english_verse: You claim that your soldiers are strong and brave.
translation_verse: “Bɛɛsu ka bina bekpone bebo ɔkplu na bebo kayi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
translation_verse: Nsu ami ndi Unwoti Ɔga Ɔyikune Ƒui na muusé kenye ka bina bekisine badubo-mii lɛlɔ bɔdi. Na bina bekpone bani ndia ntulo ƒui badubukpi na kekpokɔ.

english_verse: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
translation_verse: Uwi ɔsɔ uletu asa na ɔgbankpi ɔdubɔlɛku Moab!

english_verse: I will order the nearby nations to mourn for you and say, “Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others, but now its glorious power has been shattered.”
translation_verse: Ndubo lɛdi budie bute kɔlɔ kɔni na amadɔ na bewulo-mii kɔnyana basu banini, ‘Ɔɔɔdi kɔnyana litemi na lɛdi mɛni ka Moab ɔni na nka ɔ́di bekyuli bamba lɛlɔ ni, nsu ɔƒɛni amu nwuna ɔyikun ɔni muukeye mmɔ ƒui ɔ́yii udu.’

english_verse: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
translation_verse: “Amii bekyuli bani nkya Moab ɔma unengudi ɔni baalɔ Dibon, bekyuli basɔ baaadubo-mii bɔbu. Anwuɔsu bɛɛnu bina liboku na lɛti akɔ mmɔ. Bina bekisine badubo bina awodu bubo bɔƒɛ si uwi ɔni na beekpóku-mii.

english_verse: You people of Aroer, go wait beside the road, and when refugees run by, ask them, “What happened?”
translation_verse: Na amii Aroer ɔma bekyuli bisie na biténye ulu kɔtu na biye baƒɔ bekeline si uwi ɔni na baaví bɛnini, ‘Bi nálɛku-mii asa na bɛkɛ ku usi lɛni?’

english_verse: They will answer, “Moab has been defeated! Weep with us in shame. Tell everyone at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.”
translation_verse: “Na badubudie kenye banini, ‘Moab lɛlɔ na bekisine bádi! Anwuɔsu biteewuloku-bu bula kɔƒa keku. Na bɛsu bekyuli bani ƒui na bakya Arnon Ketu ka bákyula Moab na ɔ́yii udu.’

english_verse: I will punish every town that belongs to Moab, but especially Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath,
translation_verse: Ɔma biala na ɔdi Moab ɔma ni, ndubo-nwu kɔtu bɔni. Nsu bani ɔdi utulo ƒui ndi Holon ku Yasa ku Meƒat ku

english_verse: Dibon, Nebo, Beth-Diblathaim,
translation_verse: Dibon ku Nebo ku Bet-Diblataim,

english_verse: Kerioth, and Bozrah.
translation_verse: ku Keriot ku Bosra.

english_verse: My decision is final— your army will be crushed, and your power broken.
translation_verse: Lɛla lɛni na ami lɛ́lɛ ugyii kani ndubɔbla likplodi ƒui. Na ani ndi ka badubo bina bekpone lɛlɔ bɔdi. Na bábwɛ-mii ɔyikun na bɛyii udu ƒui.

english_verse: People of Moab, you claim to be stronger than I am. Now I will tell other nations to make you drunk and to laugh while you collapse in your own vomit.
translation_verse: Moab kadi bekyuli, bɛɛsu taatina ka bibo ɔyikun bitulo-mi. Nsu ɔƒɛni ni, ndubo kadi bamba bekyuli bɔsu na bete-mii ntɛ na bɛni bikpi. Na bataama-mi si uwi ɔni na ntɛ bɔmmɔ bútulo-mii na biibuli taatɛ amii alati bina kɔdala kemmo.

english_verse: You made fun of my people and treated them like criminals caught in the act.
translation_verse: Lɛni na bɛ́kya mina bekyuli lɛlɔ lɛma na bɛɛbla-ma aani bakantankpine bani na béƒie na bana likyulikpi lɛdi bɔbla kemmo.

english_verse: Now you must leave your towns and live like doves in the shelter of cliffs and canyons.
translation_verse: Ɔƒaani ni, bɛdubo bina lɛma bɔda buwi na bitábla kɔkyakɔ na atakpɛ lɛkɔkɔ ku kɔka kemmo na bitélie mmɔ aani babloduma.

english_verse: I know about your pride, and how you strut and boast.
translation_verse: “Ngyi kalɛ na bɛɛtalaku lɛlɔ katɔ na bígyingya enu bɛɛkun lɛmɛnɛ taavi.

english_verse: But I also know bragging will never save you.
translation_verse: Nsu ami lɛnɔ ngyi ka kɔnu kayi butu taakun lɛmɛnɛ likpludi ulaƒɔ-mii.

english_verse: So I will cry and mourn for Moab and its town of Kir-Heres.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ndubo keku ku kɔnyana buwulo bute Moab ku nwuna Kir-Heres ɔma.

english_verse: People of Sibmah, you were like a vineyard heavy with grapes, and with branches reaching north to the town of Jazer and west to the Dead Sea. But you have been destroyed, and so I will weep for you, as the people of Jazer weep for the vineyards.
translation_verse: Amii Sibma kadi bekyuli, bíse aani adingyii mmo bɔni egyiibi nánwu kpasa kpasa. Na adingyii ammɔ édie kɔgba gyɔlɔɔ gyɔlɔɔ ésie kalɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ kútédu Yasar. Na kúsie ɔƒɛ kanukɔ lɛnɔ kútédu Ɛpugyie ɔmmɔ. Nsu ɔƒaamu báyila-mii udu, anwuɔsu ndubo-mii buwulo aani kalɛ na Yasar kadi bekyuli béwulo bana adingyii mmo.

english_verse: Harvest celebrations are gone from the orchards and farms of Moab. I have silenced the shouts of people making wine.
translation_verse: Edula bɔƒɛ taasiku mmo emeyi bɔdi bɔ́sa na Moab kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔƒaamu na lɛlɔyɔ kɔku bɔbla na ntɛ kediekɔ lɛnɔ kenye kékulo.

english_verse: Weeping from Heshbon can be heard as far as Elealeh and Jahaz; cries from Zoar are heard in Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
translation_verse: “Na beenú Hesbon keku buwulo na ɔgyu kakaaka útédu Eleale ku Yahas. Na kɔvanu kɔɔsí Soar ɔma kemmo na beenú na Horonaim ku Eglat-Selesia. Na Nimrim Ketu muedi kákwii.

english_verse: I will get rid of anyone who burns incense to the gods of Moab or offers sacrifices at their shrines. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala ɔni mɔɔkyula oloƒui teete Moab baƒiɔ badi iye uti akpala adi úsie utákpa na nwuna ɔƒiɔtɔ ɔdi ni, ndubo-nwu udu bɔyila. Ami Unwoti násu.

english_verse: In my heart I moan for Moab, like a funeral song played on a flute. I mourn for the people of the town of Kir-Heres, because their wealth is gone. *
translation_verse: “Muunú ɔlɛ geen teete Moabƒuɔ na mina kayi kemmo aani kalɛ na ɔɔbla ukyuli si beedie ɔkwanu na lɛtoloyii lɛlɔ. Na muuwulo Kir-Heres kɔnyana, ɔsika nwuna lɛkɔ ƒui lɛ́yii udu.

english_verse: Moab lies broken! Listen to its people cry as they turn away in shame. Other nations are horrified at what happened, but still they mock her.
translation_verse: Aanu Moab nábwɛ uwi kalɔ! Na nwuna bekyuli keku kada ɔni na básɔ beenwíni ku kɔƒa. Liƒu bonwu líƒie bekyuli ka bánu ɔmɛni, nsu ina amu benye baamá-ma.

english_verse: Moab, an enemy swoops down like an eagle spreading its wings over your land.
translation_verse: “Moab, aanu ka ukisine ɔdi úveyi ɔɔví kayaa na ɔ́tu ɔdubo aani kɔdigbo aasɛ na úgyingya avwi úbi ƒula kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Your cities and fortresses will be captured, and your warriors as fearful as women giving birth.
translation_verse: Badubo ƒula ɔma ku awodu ani mɔɔgyumana-a buƒie bɔƒɔ na ƒula kudɔ na liƒu liƒie ƒula bekpone.

english_verse: You are finished as a nation, because you dared oppose me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Amii ɔdi ɔ́sa aani kadi bekyuli kalɛ, ɔsika bɛ́wia bɛnii bɛɛta binye bɛsiaku-mi ami Unwoti.

english_verse: Terror, pits, and traps are waiting for you.
translation_verse: Agyala ku libu bonwu ku kɔkpagyuɛ kunye kɔgya-mii na bina kasiakɔ.

english_verse: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; and if you crawl out of the pit, you'll get caught in a trap. The time has come for you to be punished. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: “Si liƒu lɛ́da-mii na bɛnii biikeli, bɛdubɔnu biduo ubu. Na si bɛ́kpɛ buɛɛ buɛɛ bɛnii bɛɛlɛ́ ubu ɔmmɔ kemmo lɛnɔ ni, kɔkpagyuɛ kɔdubo-mii budie. Uwi ɔmmɔ nédu ka bani-mii kɔtu.

english_verse: Near the city of Heshbon, where Sihon once ruled, tired refugees stand in shadows cast by the flames of their burning city. Soon, the towns on other hilltops, where those warlike people live, will also go up in smoke.
translation_verse: “Na Hesbon ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kɔmadɔ kesii kani na Sihon ɔ́di lɛlɔ dii ni, baƒɔ bekeline bani na lɛlɔ lítu-ma benye kasuudikɔ kesii kani na ogya ɔni mɔɔkyula bana ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ bukeye bɔ́kya ɔyuli. Na uwi uletu asa na bekyuli bani nli abi bamba eli na badi bekpone mmɔ lɛnɔ lɛma lɛdubuse kalɔ ku bɔkywi.

english_verse: People of Moab, you worshiped Chemosh, your god, but now you are done for, and your children are prisoners in a foreign country.
translation_verse: “Moab kadi bekyuli, bɛ́siaku bina Kemos baƒiɔ. Nsu ɔƒaani ni, bɛ́wɔlɔ, amii ɔdi ɔ́sa na bina bebi bénwini bekyuli beƒiedi na kadi bamba bekyuli kɔlɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: “Nsu limeyi lɛdi ni, ndubɔsɔku ƒula bekyuli liboku ɔma. Ami Unwoti násu.”

english_verse: The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon: The people of Israel have plenty of children to inherit their lands. So why have you worshipers of the god Milcom taken over towns and land belonging to the tribe of Gad?
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́su ɔ́siku Amon lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Israel kadi bekyuli bebo bebi ku bawɔ bani nádi nwuna kalɔ. Na bi ɔsu na amii bani mɔɔkpá Molek baƒiɔ néti Gad kɔdua lɛma ku kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ bínwini amii kɔdi?

english_verse: Someday I will send an army to attack you in Rabbah, your capital city. It will be left in ruins, and the surrounding villages will lie in ashes. You took some of Israel's land, but on that day Israel will take yours!
translation_verse: Ndubo bekpone badi buti bumene-mii limeyi lɛdi na bebekpo-mii na bina ɔma unengudi ɔni ndi Raba na babwɛ-nwu ƒui kede kede. Na badubo lɛma lɛkladi lɛni na amadɔ bɔkyula bunwini ntɔ. Bɛ́ƒɔ Israelƒuɔ kalɔ kadi, nsu limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, Israel ɔdubɔƒɔ awɔ kadi!

english_verse: Cry, people of Heshbon; your town will become a pile of rubble. You will turn here and there, but your path will be blocked. Put on sackcloth and mourn, you citizens of Rabbah, because the idol you worship will be taken to a foreign country, along with its priests and temple officials.
translation_verse: “Amii Hesbon bekyuli, biteewulo! Bina ɔma ɔdubunwini kebu alakpi, ɔsika bábwɛ Ai na ɔ́yii udu. Bɛdubo buteekeli taaka taamana bɛnii bɛɛwia katamikukɔ, nsu ala adubo-mii bɔbala na lɛƒɛnyi ƒui lɛlɔ. Bɛdubo bunwini, ɔsika bina kɔsiakɔ ƒui kɔdubo buti na bilákɛ kasiakɔ kadi. Na amii Rabaƒuɔ, biti kɔnyana ala bɛda na biteewulo kɔnyana, ɔsika badubo bina baƒiɔ Milkom bani na bɛɛkpá buti bɔtɔlɔku busienku ɔlɔgyu kakaaka na kaƒɔ. Na betiku bina bakpane ku bina benengu bammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: You rebellious Ammonites trust your wealth and ask, “Who could attack us?” But I warn you not to boast when your strength is fading.
translation_verse: Amii batuɔkplune Amonƒuɔ bani mɔɔta teenye-mi lɛlɔ. Bina lɛkɛ lɛlɔ kani na bɛsia anu na biiye bɛnini, ‘Ɔma ndubo bɔkana na ukpoku-bu?’ Nsu ami mɔɔlɛ-mii kpakplaa nnii bɛda lɛlɔ katɔ bɔtalaku bɛya. Ɔsika uwi ɔni na bina ɔyikun ɔdubuse kalɔ uteebo kalɔ ni,

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send neighboring nations to strike you with terror. You will be scattered, with no one to care for your refugees.
translation_verse: ami, Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, ndubɔya na kadi bekyuli bani na bina adɔ badububo na bebekpo-mii geen ku ogya na ɔɔɔdubo-mii buse buɛɛ. Mmomu badubo-mii bugyingya kalɛ kalɛ na bɛɛɛdubo ukyuli ɔdi bɔkɛ na ɔnu-mii lɛlɔ iye ubunku bina baƒɔ bekeline.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Edom
translation_verse: “Nsu limeyi lɛdi ni, ndubɔsɔku-mii liboku bina ɔma. Ami Unwoti násu.” Unwoti Ɔ́su Lɛla Lɛdi Ɔ́siku Edomƒuɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: People who harvest grapes leave some for the poor. Thieves who break in at night take only what they want.
