translation_verse: Si beyune bábwɛ béduo kaduli kadi usien ni, lɛla lɛni na baawia kani na beeti. Na si bekyuli béde egyiibi adi ni, ana ƒui alasa bɔla na egyii kalɔ.

english_verse: But I will take everything that belongs to you, people of Edom, and I will uncover every place where you try to hide. Then you will die, and so will your children, relatives, and neighbors.
translation_verse: Nsu ami ndubo lɛla biala na lɛdi Edomƒuɔ lɛdi bɔda buti na libimi-mii ala na kesi kesii na bɛdubɔkali bɛnii bɛɛbɛ́ bɛkya. Na bɛdubo bukpi ƒui ku bina lɛlɔ bekyuli ku badukɛne ƒui.

english_verse: But I can be trusted to care for your orphans and widows.
translation_verse: Nsu bɛƒɔ-mi bɛdi ka ndubɔnu bina bekpinebi ku bekpinele ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape?
translation_verse: “Na kadi bani bekyuli na útalɛka nka bani-ma kɔtu muedi ni, badubo mina kɔnyi bɔni aani kalɛ na baaní lɛla lɛdi na ɔɔƒɛɛ kemmo na bebo abi. Anwuɔsu bina ɔdi ulakana bulekeli.

english_verse: I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
translation_verse: Ami Unwoti nnye mina lɛnyi kenye muusé kenye ka bina ɔma unengudi ɔni baalɔ Bosra ku bina lɛma lɛkladi ƒui badubo ɔgbankpi kpakplaa ɔmɛni kemmo buduo, na badubo lɛma lɛmmɔ ƒui bɔbwɛ búwi kalɔ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ. Na badubuti-mii lɛnyi muedi bewida bekyuli banii ɔdubɔlɛku-ma aani bina kalɛ kani.

english_verse: I have sent a messenger to command the nations to prepare for war against you people of Edom.
translation_verse: Lɛ́ɛtala ɔtu ɔdi nnii ute kadi bekyuli bammɔ bɔti na baklibi lɛlɔ na bebekpo amii Edomƒuɔ.

english_verse: Your nation will be small, yet hated by other nations.
translation_verse: “Ndubo-mii bɔbla na bɛsɔ na kadi ƒui akɔ na balabu-mii balakya lɛla lɛdi akɔ.

english_verse: Pride tricks you into thinking that other nations look at you with fear. You live along the cliffs and high in the mountains like the eagles, but I am the Lord, and I will bring you down.
translation_verse: Bina lɛlɔ katɔ bɔtalaku mɔɔtɔ́lɔ-mii bɔnii kadi bekyuli bamba ƒui baanu-mii ku bɔyia. Bilie atakpɛ ku abi eli aani kɔdigbo baasɛ kalɛ, nsu ami Unwoti ndubo-mii kalɔ buboku ƒui.

english_verse: as bad as the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and towns nearby. The towns of Edom will be empty.
translation_verse: Lɛ́kyula Sodom ku Gomora ku lɛma lɛni na lide-ma ƒui. Na lɛni kani na ndubo Babilon lɛnɔ bɔkyula kede kede. Na ukyuli biala ɔdi ɔsɔ ɔɔɔdubo mmɔ bulie.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: “Ndubo awɔ Edom bukpoku aani kalɛ na gyata ɔɔsí lɛku kemmo teebekpoku baƒonu bani nnye kadikɔ na Yordan kɔtu. Na ulaƒɔ uwi ɔdi asa na baƒonu bammɔ beekeli taatɔlɔ na bada kalɔ kammɔ bese ukpludi. Ɔma na ndubo bɔƒuna na ukpoku-ɔ? Ami ɔlati ndubo-ɔ bukpoku! Ɔsika ɔdi ulakana-mi bunye bɔsiaku na kekpokɔ iye ɔbɔku-mi na likeli lɛtɔlɔ.

english_verse: Listen to my plans for you, people of Edom. Your children will be dragged off and your country destroyed.
translation_verse: “Bise atu na binu lɛla lɛni na lɛ́ɛlɛ ugyii líse na amii Edom bekyuli lɛlɔ. Badubo bina bebi ɔbuli bɔkya bɔni bɔtɔlɔku na babwɛ bina kalɔ kemodi kammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will reach the Red Sea and cause the earth to shake.
translation_verse: Na ala ani na badubo bubile mmɔ kɔku kɔdubusie kutédu Ɛpugyie kɔtu ƒui. Na kɔku kɔmmɔ kɔdubɔya na kalɔ kammɔ kakunku.

english_verse: An enemy will swoop down to attack you, like an eagle spreading its wings and circling over Bozrah. Your warriors will be as fearful as women giving birth. What the Lord Says about Damascus
translation_verse: Ukisine ɔdi ɔdubɔtu ɔsi kayaa ubebi-mii lɛlɔ na ukpoku-mii aani kɔdigbo aasɛ na ɔdubugyingya nwuna avwi ubi Bosra ɔma na utaaka taamana-nwu. Na liƒu bonwu lɛdubuƒie ƒula bekpone ƒui.” Unwoti Ɔ́su Lɛla Lɛdi Ɔ́siku Damasko Lɛlɔ

english_verse: The Lord says about Damascus: The towns of Hamath and Arpad have heard your bad news. They have lost hope, and worries roll over them like ocean waves.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́su ɔ́siku Damasko lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Hama ku Aprad lɛma linengudi lɛmmɔ línu ƒula kenye kekpidi kani nébo-ɔ mmɔ na báyila bana lɛnunsia ƒui na lɛƒɛda lɛ́ƒɔ-ma lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui aani kalɛ na ɛpu avlɔvɔ eebi lɛla lɛdi lɛlɔ ƒui.

english_verse: You people of Damascus have lost your courage, and in panic you turn to run, gripped by fear and pain.
translation_verse: Ɔtɔtɔ ɔ́gyu amii Damaskoƒuɔ na bínwini ku liƒu bíkeli bɛɛtɔlɔ. Na bɔyia ku ɔlɛ bunu sɔɔn kemmo.

english_verse: Once I was pleased with your famous city. But now I warn you, “Escape while you still can!”
translation_verse: Uwi ɔdi návi kemmo ni, na nka lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ-mi na bina ɔma unengudi ɔni náƒɔ lɛnyi mmɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu ɔƒɛni amu ni, mɔɔlɛ-mii kpakplaa nnii bikeli uwi ɔni na bɛmu bibo kuƒi kɔdi mɛni!

english_verse: Soon, even your best soldiers will lie dead in your streets. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ɔsika uwi ɔsɔ uletu asa na bina bekpone babuni ƒui muedi badubɔdu-ma bewi lɛblɔnu lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ. Ami Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui násu kenye kamɛni.

english_verse: I will set fire to your city walls and burn down the fortresses King Benhadad built. Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
translation_verse: Ndubo ogya bɔtu bɔkya bina awodu na lɛkyula bina kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa kɔni na Ɔga Benhadad ɔ́tu mmɔ.” Nebukadnesar Ku Ketele Kalɔ Kakwiidi Bekyuli Lɛlɔ Kɔtɛ

english_verse: Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia: Listen, you people of Kedar and the other tribes of the eastern desert. I have told Nebuchadnezzar to attack and destroy you.
translation_verse: Binu lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su ɔ́siku Kedar kɔdua bekyuli ku akpaklɔ lɛma lɛni na ketele kalɔ kakwiidi kammɔ lɛlɔ na Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ. “Amii Kedarƒuɔ, ku adua bamba ani na akya kalɔ kakwiidi kani néti kése ɔƒɛ katukɔ mmɔ binu. Lɛ́ɛsu Nebukadnesar nnii ukpoku-mii na ɔyila-mii udu ƒui.

english_verse: Run and hide, you people of the desert who live in villages! Nebuchadnezzar has big plans for you.
translation_verse: Amii kalɔ kakwiidi akpaklɔ lɛma kemmo bekyuli ƒui, bikeli bitábɛ! Nebukadnesar ɔdanku kasusu bonwu kadi udu na bina lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You have no city walls and no neighbors to help, yet you think you're safe— so I told him to attack.
translation_verse: Biiibo awodu ani mɔɔgyumana-mii na biiibo badukɛne bebunkune badi lɛnɔ. Nsu use-mii aani bibo bɔƒɔ bɔdi, anwuɔsu lɛ́su-nwu nnii ukpo-mii.

english_verse: Then your camels and large herds will be yours no longer. People of the Arabian Desert, disaster will strike you from every side, and you will be scattered everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Na mmɔ na bɛdubɔyila bina bebuo ala betine ku bebuo bamba pii badubo-mii enu bɔlɛ na lɛla lɛdi lɛsɔ lilabla bina ɔdi. Amii bani na Arabia kalɔ kakwiidi kemmo mmɔ ƒui ɔgbankpi ɔdubo-mii lɛlɔ ɔ́si lɛƒɛnyi ƒui lɛlɔ, na badubo-mii bugyingya bɔkya kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Only jackals will live where your villages once stood. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Elam
translation_verse: Na kesii kani na bina akpaklɔ ammɔ ákya ƒui adubunwini beƒukutu keliekɔ. Ami Unwoti násu.”

english_verse: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say: People of Elam, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will kill the archers who make your army strong.
translation_verse: Ka Ɔga Sedekia úbelie liboku lɛlɔ aani Yudaƒuɔ ɔga ni, uwi útetu ɔdi asa na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi kenye kadi ɔnii nsu Elamƒuɔ ɔnini, “Elam kadi bekyuli, ami Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui ndubo ƒula kɔtaminta bebone bani ɔsu na ƒula bekpone bebo ɔyikun mmɔ bɔdu.

english_verse: Enemies will attack from all directions, and you will be led captive to every nation on earth.
translation_verse: Na bekisine badubo-ɔ bukpoku bɔsiku lɛƒɛnyi ƒui lɛlɔ na kekpo keƒie-ɔ na bakpanku ƒula bekyuli batakya kalɔ kadi ƒui bekyuli akɔ.

english_verse: Their armies will crush and kill you, and you will face the disaster that my anger brings.
translation_verse: Na bekpone bammɔ badubo-mii bususu na badu-mii ƒui. Na bɛdubɔsiaku ɔgbankpi ɔni na mina kɔnyi kɔdanku ƒui.

english_verse: Your king and his officials will die, and I will rule in their place. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Na ƒula ɔga ku nwuna benengu ƒui badubo bukpi. Na lilie ntaadi lɛlɔ na bana kenye. Ami Unwoti násu.

english_verse: But I promise that someday I will bring your people back to their land.
translation_verse: “Nsu líse kenye ka limeyi lɛdi ni, ndubo-mii bɔsɔku buboku bina ɔma.”

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: Announce what will happen and don't leave anything out.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnii nsu Babilonƒuɔ bammɔ nnini, “Su-ma lɛla lɛni ndubo bɔlɛ na tada lɛdi tedie-nwu kemmo.

english_verse: Raise the signal flags; shout so all nations can hear— Babylon will be captured! Marduk, Babylon's god, will be ashamed and terrified, and his idols broken.
translation_verse: Lɛ kati bute aƒlaga na ava momoomo kalɛ na kadi bekyuli ƒui benu anini, ‘Badubo Babilon buƒie enu enu! Na kɔƒa kɔdubo bana Marduk baƒiɔ bammɔ bukpo na liƒu liƒie-nwu geen na bebo ala ani na bávɔ béte-nwu bɔbwɛ buwi kalɔ ƒui.

english_verse: The attack on the Babylonians will come from the north; they and their animals will run, leaving the land empty. Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
translation_verse: Na Babilonƒuɔ bukpoku bɔmmɔ bɔdubɔsi katɔ kakɛ. Na ama ku bana bebuo ƒui badubo bukeli bɔtɔlɔ na bada ɔma ɔmmɔ bewi ukpludi.’ ” Israel Ku Yordan Badubɔsɔ Benwini Besie Bana Kalɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: The Lord said: People of Israel and Judah, when these things happen you will weep, and together you will return to your land and worship me, the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Amii Israel ku Yuda kadi bekyuli, uwi ɔni na ala amɛni adubɔlɛ ni, bɛdubo buwulo na bɛsɔ binwini bisie kalɔ lɛlɔ na bɛkpa-mi bina Unwoti ku Katɔti.

english_verse: You will ask the way to Zion and then come and join with me in making an agreement you won't break or forget.
translation_verse: Bɛdubo Sion ɔma ulu buye na bibo bibasalaku-mi na bunyimi lɛla lɛwɔdi lɛni na bɛsɔ bilayiƒala.

english_verse: My people, you are lost sheep abandoned in the mountains by their shepherds. You don't even remember your resting place.
translation_verse: Mina kadi bekyuli, bise aani baƒonu bani na bana lɛlɔ banune bányonu bákya abi lɛlɔ. Na kesii kani na bɛɛtɛ taanwuna muedi bɛ́yiƒala mmɔ.

english_verse: I am your true pastureland, the one who gave hope to your ancestors. But you abandoned me, so when your enemies found you, they felt no guilt as they gobbled you up.
translation_verse: Ndi bebuo kadikɔ kabuni nte-mii kani na bina bati kuuku básia anu. Nsu bíni-mi, anwuɔsu bina bekisine lɛnɔ bákɛ-mii béƒie aani kalɛ na baaduli ebuo teebweli na bana kayi kátadu-ma kɔtɔ kɔdi.

english_verse: Escape from Babylonia, my people. Get out of that country! Don't wait for anyone else.
translation_verse: “Mina kadi bekyuli, bikeli Babilonƒuɔ na bɛlɛ bana kalɔ kemmo! Bitenye bitagya ukyuli ɔdi.

english_verse: In the north I am bringing great nations together. They will attack Babylon and capture it. The arrows they shoot are like the best soldiers, always finding their target.
translation_verse: Ndubɔsala kadi bayikune lɛsiku kalɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ liboku na bebekpoku Babilonƒuɔ na beƒie-ma enu enu. Kalɛ na beebó kɔtaminta use aani bekpone babuni ƒui kɔtaminta bubo kalɛ na belebo taaƒiɔ.

english_verse: Babylonia will be conquered, and its enemies will carry off everything they want. Babylon Will Be Disgraced The Lord said:
translation_verse: Badubo Babilon lɛlɔ bɔdi na nwuna bekisine beti lɛla biala na baawia batɔlɔku.” Kɔƒa Kɔdubo Babilon Bukpo

english_verse: People of Babylonia, you were glad to rob my people. You had a good time, making more noise than horses and jumping around like calves threshing grain.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ-mii ka bíyu mina bekyuli. Bítuku lɛlɔ ku kudu momoomo aani bapɔnkɔ na bɛɛƒulu taavi ɔmantɛ bakɔ bakɔdi bani muuwila edula ebi.

english_verse: The city of Babylon was like a mother to you. But it will be disgraced and become nothing but a barren desert.
translation_verse: Ƒula ɔma unengudi ɔni na aayɔ́ aani ƒula uwele ɔdubo kɔƒa bɔdi na unwini aani kalɔ kakwiidi kani nsɔ neeebo lɛblakula.

english_verse: My anger will destroy Babylon, and no one will live there. Everyone who passes by will be shocked to see what has happened.
translation_verse: Mina kɔnyi kɔdubo Babilon bɔkyula na ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ ulelie mmɔ. Na liƒu lɛdubɔda ukyuli biala ɔni ndubɔsia mmɔ ɔvi na lɛla lɛni ndubɔlɛ mmɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: Babylon has rebelled against me. Archers, take your places. Shoot all your arrows at Babylon.
translation_verse: Babilon ɔ́ta únye-mi lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu atula bebone binye bina kunyekɔ kpakplaa na bibo bina atula bibo bina kɔtaminta bɛlɛ Babilon.

english_verse: Attack from every side! Babylon surrenders! The enemy tears down its walls and towers. I am taking my revenge by doing to Babylon what it did to other cities.
translation_verse: Bikpo-ma na lɛƒɛnyi lɛlɔ! Babilon úte lili! Bekisine bammɔ báƒɛ-ma awodu ƒui béwi kalɔ ku bana kɔgyumanakɔ kɔmmɔ ƒui. Lɛla lɛni na Babilonƒuɔ bábla lɛma linengudi bamba ni, ami lɛnɔ muudie-ma kasi kammɔ.

english_verse: There is no one in Babylonia to plant or harvest crops. Even foreigners who lived there have left for their homelands, afraid of the enemy armies.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ uuubo Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ na ɔkya edula adi iye ɔƒɛ adi lɛnɔ. Na baƒɔ bani ƒui nkya mmɔ bátɔlɔ bésie bana lɛma na bekisine bammɔ bɔyia ɔsu.

english_verse: Israel is a flock of sheep scattered by hungry lions. The king of Assyria first gobbled Israel up. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, crunched on Israel's bones.
translation_verse: Israelƒuɔ bese aani baƒonu lisu lɛni na bagyata bani na kɔka kɔɔda bábɔku bégyingya. Na Asiria ɔga náka-ma bɔduli kɔkɛ kɔkɛ lɛni asa na Babilon Ɔga Nebukadnesar úbabwɛ-ma ku ekubi ƒui.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, punished the king of Assyria, and I will also punish the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: “Ami Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, Israel Katɔti, lɛ́ni Asiria kɔtu na ndubo Babilon lɛnɔ kɔtu bɔni.

english_verse: But I will bring Israel back to its own land. The people will be like sheep eating their fill on Mount Carmel and in Bashan, in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
translation_verse: Nsu ndubɔsɔku Israel liboku nwuna kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na badubuse aani baƒonu bani ndubunye badi bemo na Karmel Kɔbi lɛlɔ na Basan kalɛkɛ kani nkya Eƒraim ku Gilead abi lɛlɔ kalɔ kemmo.

english_verse: I will rescue a few people from Israel and Judah. I will forgive them so completely that their sin and guilt will disappear, never to be found. The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
translation_verse: Ndubudie Israelƒuɔ ku Yudaƒuɔ nkyuli ɛlɛɛ badi na ndubuti bana ekpidi lɛkyiɛ-ma ɔni na ɔdi ɔsɔ ulanu ekpidi bɔƒiɔ biala bɔdi ka bɔkya-ma lɛlɔ.” Unwoti Údie Lɛdi Úte Babilon Bekisine

english_verse: The Lord said: I have told the enemies of Babylonia, “Attack the people of Merathaim and Pekod. Kill them all! Destroy their possessions!”
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Lɛ́ɛsu Babilonƒuɔ bekisine nnini, ‘Bikpoku Merataim ku Pekod kadi bekyuli. Bɛdu bana ƒui! Na bibile bana ala ani nse-ma ƒui!’

english_verse: Sounds of war and the noise of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Bɛdubunu ka kekpo ku ala bubile kudu kɔda.

english_verse: Babylonia was a hammer pounding every country, but now it lies broken. What a shock to the nations of the world!
translation_verse: Babilon nse aani lɛbuala lɛni na bada baawɔ́ kɔlɔ ƒui bekyuli. Nsu ɔƒɛni amu lɛbuala lɛmmɔ lɛ́ƒɛ. Na nwuna kalɔ bubo bɔmɛni bɔ́bla kalɔ kemodi kammɔ ƒui kalɛ kadi!

english_verse: Babylonia challenged me, the Lord God All-Powerful, but that nation doesn't know it is caught in a trap that I set.
translation_verse: Babilon ɔ́kyaku ami Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui unyeƒi. Nsu kalɔ lɛlɔ bekyuli bammɔ baaagyi banii ɔ́ɔnu mina kakpagyuɛ kani na lɛ́kywɛ-nwu.

english_verse: I've brought out my weapons, and with them I will put a curse on Babylonia.
translation_verse: Lídie mina ekpola keyi na anya na ndubuti lɛbla na ewida asiaku Babilon.

english_verse: Come from far away, you enemies of Babylon! Pile up the grain from its storehouses, and destroy it completely, along with everything else.
translation_verse: Amii Babilon bekisine bɛsi ɔlɔgyu kakaaka ƒui bibo! Na bɛsala bana antabi edula udu ƒui bɛsiku bana linwu kemmo na bɛkyula-nya ku ala bamba biala na bebo ƒui.

english_verse: Kill the soldiers of Babylonia, because the time has come for them to be punished.
translation_verse: Uwi údu ka bani Babilon bekpone bammɔ kɔtu, anwuɔsu bɛdu-ma ƒui.

english_verse: The Babylonian army destroyed my temple, but soon I will take revenge. Then refugees from Babylon will tell about it in Zion.
translation_verse: Babilonƒuɔ nébile mina kakpakɔ, nsu uwi ɔsɔ uletu asa na ndubudie-ma kasi. Na bekeline bani nási Babilon mmɔ bésie Sion alati ndubo kenye budie na litemi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Attack Babylon, enemy archers; set up camp around the city, and don't let anyone escape. It challenged me, the holy God, so do to it what it did to other cities. Proud Babylon Will Fall
translation_verse: “Bikpoku Babilon amii nwuna bekisine atula bebone. Na bɛbla kakyakɔ bɛmana ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ. Na bitaya na ɔdi biala ukeli ɔtɔlɔ. Babilon ɔ́ta na únye ɔ́siaku ami Katɔti kedee. Anwuɔsu ala ani na ɔ́bla lɛma linengudi bamba ni, amii lɛnɔ bɛbla-nwu lɛni kani. Babilon Ɔdubo Kalɔ Bubo Na Nwuna Lɛlɔ Katɔ Bɔtalaku Ɔsu

english_verse: People of Babylon, I, the Lord, promise that even your best soldiers will lie dead in the streets.
translation_verse: “Ami Unwoti nése kenye ka amii Babilonƒuɔ bekpone babuni ƒui muedi badubo bukpi buwi bina lɛblɔnu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Babylon, you should be named, “The Proud One.” But the time has come when I, the Lord All-Powerful, will punish you.
translation_verse: Babilon, ɔlɛka basia-a lɛnyi banii, ‘Lɛlɔ Katɔ Ɔtalane.’ Nsu uwi údu na ami Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui lɛni-ɔ kɔtu.

english_verse: You are proud, but you will stumble and fall, and no one will help you up. I will set your villages on fire, and everything around you will go up in flames.
translation_verse: Aatalaku lɛlɔ katɔ, nsu adubo butulo na ebuli na ɔdi biala ɔɔɔdubo-ɔ bubunku na ata. Na ndubɔya na batu ogya bakya ƒula akpaklɔ lɛma ƒui. Na lɛla biala náka lɛ́mana-a lɛdubo butaada ogya.

english_verse: You Babylonians were cruel to Israel and Judah. You took them captive, and now you refuse to let them go.
translation_verse: “Babilonƒuɔ bábla Israel ku Yuda kalala. Bɛ́kpanku-ma bɛ́tɔlɔku aani bekyuli beƒiedi na bíni bɛnii bɛɛɛdubo-ma kuƒi bute na benwini batɔlɔ.

english_verse: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, will rescue and protect them. I will bring peace to their land and trouble to yours.
translation_verse: Nsu ami Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui ndubo-ma budie na lɛya na bakɛ keyi buɛɛ na bana kalɔ kemmo na bukpoku bubo amii lɛlɔ mmomu.

english_verse: I have declared war on you, your officials, and advisors.
translation_verse: “Líte ulu ka kekpo kekpo amii ku bina benengu ku bina kasusu bakyane ƒui.

english_verse: This war will prove that your prophets are liars and fools. And it will frighten your warriors.
translation_verse: Na kekpo kamɛni ndubɔya na bɛti ka bina kenye bediene badi ɔkɔ banyine ku badɔlɔdi. Na kekpo kammɔ kadubo bina bekpone liƒu bɔda geen.

english_verse: Then your chariot horses and the foreigners in your army will refuse to go into battle, and the enemy will carry away everything you treasure.
translation_verse: Na bina bapɔnkɔ bani mɔɔní bina kɛɛkɛ ku baƒɔ bani na bakya bina bekpone akɔ badubuni na belésie kekpokɔ. Na bekisine badubuti bina akɛla biala na bibo batɔlɔku.

english_verse: Your rivers and canals will dry up. All of this will happen, because your land is full of idols, and they have made fools of you.
translation_verse: Na bina ntukpa ku ntu bɔni na bɛ́bwɛ ulu bíte ka butaavi ƒui bɔdubo bɔkwii. Na ala amɛni ƒui adubɔlɛ lɛni na baƒiɔ ala ani náƒɔ bina kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui na ábla-mii bɔdɔlɔdi ɔsu.

english_verse: Never again will people live in your land— only desert animals, jackals, and unclean birds.
translation_verse: “Na ka ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ni, bekyuli basɔ baaadubo ƒula kalɔ lɛlɔ bulie, amu ntu beƒukutu ku ketele kakɔ kakwiidi bebuo ku baasɛ bani muusé lɛlɔ kani.

english_verse: I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns, and I will destroy Babylon just as completely. No one will live there again. Babylonia Is Invaded The Lord said:
translation_verse: Lɛ́kyula Sodom ku Gomora ku lɛma lɛni na lide-ma ƒui. Na lɛni kani na ndubo Babilon lɛnɔ bɔkyula kede kede. Na ukyuli biala ɔdi ɔsɔ ɔɔɔdubo mmɔ bulie. Békpo Babilon Na Bádi-nwu Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Far to the north, a nation and its allies have been awakened. They are powerful and ready for war.
translation_verse: “Bɛnu! Ɔ́si ɔgyu kakaaka na kalɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ ni, kadi bekyuli bayikune badi ku baga pii báata bátu akpagya na benye kagyumana ka bebekpo.

english_verse: Bows and arrows and swords are in their hands. The soldiers are cruel and show no pity. The hoofbeats of their horses echo like ocean waves crashing against the shore. The army has lined up for battle and is coming to attack you, people of Babylonia!
translation_verse: Bada kɔtaminta ku atula ku kuwii. Na bekpone bammɔ bebo kalala na balanu kɔnyana lɛnɔ. Na bana bapɔnkɔ bɔnya kɔku kɔda momoomo aani kalɔ na ɛpu uubó teebewi ketudɔ. Bekpone bammɔ benye sininii badubo bebekpoku Babilonƒuɔ!

english_verse: Ever since your king heard about this army, he has been weak with fear; he twists and turns in pain like a woman giving birth.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si ɔni na bina ɔga únu kekpo kamɛni kɔku kani na kɔyɔ ku liƒu líƒie-nwu. Na uususu lɛlɔ na uulii lɛlɔ aani ɔƒɔndane ɔni ntɛ kɔwɔ.

english_verse: Babylonia, I will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Ndubo awɔ Babilon bukpoku aani kalɛ na gyata ɔɔsí lɛku kemmo teebekpoku baƒonu bani nnye kadikɔ na Yordan kɔtu. Na ulaƒɔ uwi ɔdi asa na baƒonu bammɔ beekeli taatɔlɔ na bada kalɔ kammɔ bese ukpludi. Ɔma na ndubo bɔƒuna na ukpoku-ɔ? Ami ɔlati ndubo-ɔ bukpoku! Ɔsika ɔdi ulakana-mi bunye bɔsiaku na kekpokɔ iye ɔbɔku-mi na likeli lɛtɔlɔ.

english_verse: Listen to my plans for you, people of Babylonia. Your children will be dragged off, and your country destroyed.
translation_verse: Bise atu na binu lɛla lɛni na lɛ́ɛlɛ ugyii líse na amii Babilon bekyuli lɛlɔ. Badubo bina bebi ɔbuli bɔkya bɔni bɔtɔlɔku na babwɛ bina kalɔ kemodi kammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will be heard among the nations, and the earth will shake.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli badubunu kɔku na kadi bekyuli ƒui akɔ na kalɔ kammɔ kakunku.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, am sending a wind to destroy the people of Babylonia and Babylon, its capital.
translation_verse: “Ami Unwoti ndubuti kɔyu kɔni muubile ala aani ɔƒɛƒɛɛ limene na ubayila amii Babilonƒuɔ udu ku bina ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Foreign soldiers will come from every direction, and when the disaster is over, Babylonia will be empty and worthless.
translation_verse: Bekpone bani na badi baƒɔ badubɔsi lɛƒɛnyi ƒui lɛlɔ bebo. Na si uwi ɔni na ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ kenye kávi ni, Babilon ɔdubɔsɔ uwi ukpludi ɔni na ɔsɔ uuubo lɛla lɛdi bɔbla lɛnɔ.

english_verse: I will tell these soldiers, “Attack quickly, before the Babylonians can string their bows or put on their armor. Kill their best soldiers and destroy their army!”
translation_verse: Na ndubɔsu bekpone bammɔ nnini, ‘Bikpo-ma kɔnakunwi asa na Babilonƒuɔ bataabu bana kɔtaminta iye bakya bana ekpola. Na bɛdu bana bekpone babuni bammɔ ƒui!’

english_verse: Their troops will fall wounded in the streets of Babylon.
translation_verse: Bana bekpone lisu lɛmmɔ ƒui badubo bubuli bubi Babilon lɛblɔnu lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ na baƒɔ lɛlɛ ƒui.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel and Judah is guilty. But I, the Lord All-Powerful, their holy God, have not abandoned them.
translation_verse: Ukyuli biala na Israel ku Yuda ƒui bábla ekpidi na báƒiɔ, nsu ami bana Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui lɛɛɛdubo-ma buni.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon! Run for your lives! If you stay, you will be killed when I take revenge on the city and punish it for its sins.
translation_verse: Bɛvi bɛlɛ Babilon! Na bɛƒɔ bina lili ngba! Nsu si bɛ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ bɛkya mɛni bɔdi ni, bɛdubo bukpi si uwi ɔni na muudie ɔma ɔmmɔ kasi na mɔɔní-nwu kɔtu na nwuna ekpidi ani na ɔ́bla ɔsu.

english_verse: Babylon was my golden cup, filled with the wine of my anger. The nations of the world got drunk on this wine and went insane.
translation_verse: Babilon úse úte-mi aani sika ugyiedi ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔni kemmo na mina kɔnyi kúyi tɛtɛɛtɛ. Na kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui kadi bekyuli báni ntɛ bɔmmɔ békpi na basɔ beleti kasusu kadi.

english_verse: But suddenly, Babylon will fall and be destroyed. I, the Lord, told the foreigners who lived there, “Weep for the city! Get medicine for its wounds; maybe they will heal.”
translation_verse: Nsu uwi uletu asa na Babilon ɔdubo bubuli na ɔyii udu. Ami Unwoti násu baƒɔ bani nkya mmɔ nnini, ‘Biwulo bite ɔma ɔmɛni! Na bɛƒɔ kuvo bɛsia-ma alɛbi ani nsia-ma lɛlɔ. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ lɛdubɔsa-ma.’

english_verse: The foreigners answered, “We have already tried to treat Babylon's wounds, but they would not heal. Come on, let's all go home to our own countries. Nothing is left in Babylonia; everything is destroyed.”
translation_verse: “Baƒɔ bammɔ bédie kenye banini, ‘Bɔ́ɔsia-ma alɛbi ammɔ kuvo, nsu ébulo bɔsa. Bibo na bula ƒui bɔtɔlɔ buteesie bula ɔma. Lɛla biala lɛsɔ liiibo Babilon. Ala ana ƒui áyii udu.’

english_verse: I, the Lord, want Babylon destroyed, because its army destroyed my temple. So, you kings of Media, sharpen your arrows and pick up your shields.
translation_verse: “Ami Unwoti mɔɔwia ka bayila Babilon udu, ɔsika nwuna bekpone báyila mina kadi bekyuli udu. Na bébile mina kakpakɔ. Anwuɔsu amii Media baga bɛdɔ bina atula na bɛgyu bina agyumanala bɛda.

english_verse: People of Babylon, you live along the Euphrates River and are surrounded by canals. You are rich, but now the time has come for you to die.
translation_verse: Amii Babilon bekyuli, amii nli Euƒrate Ketu amadɔ na ntu bɔni na bɛ́bwɛ ulu bíte bɔ́ka bɔ́mana-mii. Na bibo lɛkɛ, nsu ɔƒaamu bina uwi údu ka bikpi.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, swear by my own life that enemy soldiers will fill your streets like a swarm of locusts. They will shout and celebrate their victory. A Hymn of Praise (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Ami Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui nkɛnku ami ɔlati mina lɛlɔ líse kenye ka bekisine bekpone badubɔƒɔ ƒula lɛblɔnu lɛlɔ aani baalɔlɔ. Na badubo kudu buteebo taakɛ lɛlɔyɔ ka bádi-mii lɛlɔ ɔsu.” Linugya Ɔnu Bɔtu

english_verse: The waters in the heavens roar at his command. He makes clouds appear; he sends the wind from his storehouse and makes lightning flash in the rain.
translation_verse: Eedie lɛdi teete ntu bɔni na áya na bɔƒa kayaa na buudu ku kɔku bonwu. Na liƒlukutu lɛɛdá taalɛ kayaa. Aayá na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔɔsí ƒula kesii kani na áklibi ala ése teebekpo. Na kayaa kemodi kaabwɛ ogya si ɔnantu ɔɔna.

english_verse: God used his wisdom and power to create the earth and spread out the heavens.
translation_verse: Katɔti úti nwuna lɛnunda ku ɔyikun na údie kalɔ ku kayaa ala ƒui.

english_verse: People who make idols are stupid! They will be disappointed, because their false gods cannot breathe.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani mɔɔnwí na baavɔ́ ala teese lɛlɔ aani baƒiɔ bádɔlɔ! Badubo bana lɛnunsia bɔyila na enu aƒɛ-ma, ɔsika bana ɔkɔ bɔnyi baƒiɔ bammɔ balakana bɔnwuna.

english_verse: Idols are merely a joke, and when the time is right, they will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Baƒiɔ badi aƒiankula ku amala na si uwi ɔbuni úbo ubedu ni, badubo-ma udu bɔyila ƒui.

english_verse: But the Lord, Israel's God, is all-powerful. He created everything, and he chose Israel to be his very own. God's Hammer The Lord said:
translation_verse: Nsu awɔ Israel Katɔti ni, eeese lɛni. Awɔ nédie ala ƒui na áƒuna Israel kadi bekyuli na badi awɔ badi geen. Ƒula lɛnyi ndi Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui. Katɔti Lɛbuala Lɛni Na Uubó Ala

english_verse: Babylonia, you were my hammer; I used you to pound nations and break kingdoms,
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Babilon, awɔ na lɛ́da aani lɛbuala lɛni na muubó ala, na awɔ na líti ńtaawɔ kadi ƒui bekyuli na lɛ́bwɛ lɛga kɔdikɔ.

english_verse: as well as men and women, young and old,
translation_verse: Na banana ku beleku banamu ku benengu ƒui lɛni kani na lɛ́bla-ma.

english_verse: shepherds and their flocks, farmers and their oxen, and governors and leaders.
translation_verse: Baƒonu badane ku bana bebuo lɛnɔ ku bemonsene ku bana bebuo bani mɔɔtuma teete-ma lɛnɔ bátalɛ-nwu kemmo ku aban bagadine ku bana benengu ƒui.

english_verse: But now, my people will watch, while I repay you for what you did to Zion.
translation_verse: “Nsu ɔƒaani ni, mina bekyuli badubunye banu uwi ɔni na muudie-mii kasi na kalɛ na bɛ́bla Sion kenye.

english_verse: You destroyed the nations and seem strong as a mountain, but I am your enemy. I might even grab you and roll you off a cliff. When I am finished, you'll only be a pile of scorched bricks.
translation_verse: Bɛ́yila kadi bekyuli pii udu na kalɛ na bɛɛnu lɛlɔ ka bibo ɔyikun aani kɔbi ɔsu. Nsu ami nénwini bina ukisine ɔƒaamu. Na lɛkana na liƒie-mii na libo-mii lɛsiku atakpɛ lili mbaƒiɛmi kalɔ. Na si uwi ɔni na lɛ́wɔlɔ ala ani ƒui na nnii mɔɔbla ni, bɛdubunwini aani atimbɔ ani na bébo béwi na ɔƒɛ úƒi-nya.

english_verse: Your stone blocks won't be reused for cornerstones or foundations, and I promise that forever you will be a desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Nations Will Attack Babylon The Lord said:
translation_verse: Na bina atabi ani na bɛ́nwi bíse mmɔ ni, ɔdi ɔsɔ uleti-nwu ulenyimi kowodu likpo iye beti bakya kowodu ɔka kalɔ. Na muusé kenye ka ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela uwi ƒui ni, bɛdubunwini aani kalɔ kakwiidi. Ami Unwoti násu.” Kadi Bekyuli Badubo Babilon Bukpoku

english_verse: Signal the nations to get ready to attack. Raise a flag and blow a trumpet. Send for the armies of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Choose a commander; let the cavalry attack like a swarm of locusts.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Bite kalɔ bekyuli bɔti na benye kagyumana kalɛ na betékpo. Na bɛkɔliku kati bute aƒlaga katɔ na bɛvwi lise. Na bɛtala na betétiku bekpone basiku Ararat ku Mini ku Askenas. Na bɛƒuna bekpone ɔtɔnkune na bɛya na bekpone bani nkɛ lɛgba batɔ kekpo aani baalɔlɔ lisu bonwu kalɛ.

english_verse: Tell the kings and governors, the leaders and the people of the kingdoms of the Medes to prepare for war!
translation_verse: Bɛsu baga ku aban bagadine bammɔ ku batɔnkune ku Medes lɛga kɔdikɔ bekyuli bammɔ ƒui bɛnii baklibi lɛlɔ bete kekpo!

english_verse: The earth twists and turns in torment, because I have decided to make Babylonia a desert where no one can live, and I won't change my mind.
translation_verse: Kalɔ kemodi kammɔ kakya lɛbibo kemmo na kenye kelii na keesusu lɛlɔ. Ɔsika lɛ́ɛlɛ ugyii ka lɛya na Babilon unwini kalɔ kakwiidi kesii kani na ukyuli biala ɔsɔ ulakana bulie na nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo mina kasusu bɔvumana.

english_verse: The Babylonian soldiers have lost their strength and courage. They stay in their fortresses, unable to fight, while the enemy breaks through the city gates, then sets their homes on fire.
translation_verse: Babilonƒuɔ bekpone báyila bana ɔyikun ku ɔtɔtɔ na báƒɔ lɛlɔ bakya bana kagyumanakɔ lɛtɔ kemmo na balakana na bekpo uwi ɔni na bana bekisine baabwɛ bana ɔma awodu taasia ɔban kenye teeduo-ma lɛlɔ na baatu ogya taakya bana kɔduli.

english_verse: One messenger after another announces to the king, “Babylon has been captured!
translation_verse: Na batu basiaku lɛlɔ atɔ asia na beete kati ka bádi Babilon lɛlɔ na béƒie-nwu báƒɔ!

english_verse: The enemy now controls the river crossings! The marshes are on fire! Your army has panicked!”
translation_verse: Na kesii kani ndi ketu kaviakɔ mmɔ ni, bekisine mɔɔdi mmɔ lɛlɔ! Na bátu ogya bákya ketu alakpi kangyaa ani nse na ƒula bekpone bágyini benye.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I make this promise— “Soon Babylon will be leveled and packed down like a threshing place at harvest time.” Babylonia Will Pay!
translation_verse: “Ami ndi Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, Israel Katɔti, na ami muusé kenye kamɛni nnii uwi ɔsɔ uletu asa na badubutu Babilon babwɛ bewi kalɔ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ na mmɔ kabla tataata aani kakpa kesii kani na beewiile kamu teewi. Babilon Ɔdubo Kayu Bɔƒɔ!

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem say, “King Nebuchadnezzar made us panic. That monster stuffed himself with us and our treasures, leaving us empty— he gobbled up what he wanted and spit out the rest.
translation_verse: “Yerusalem, bɛsu bɛnini, ‘Ɔga Nebukadnesar ɔ́ya na bɔ́gyini. Liƒu kebweyi kammɔ kéti-bu ku bula akɛla kése lɛlɔ lɛmwi na abu bɔ́sɔ bɔkya ukpludi. Úti-bu ala ani na ɔɔwia úbweli na útuo akladi úwi.

english_verse: The people of Babylonia harmed some of us and killed others. Now, Lord, make them pay!” The Lord Will Take Revenge on Babylon
translation_verse: Na Babilonƒuɔ bákya abu badi ɔlɛ na bádu bakladi. Na ɔƒɛni ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na báƒɔ kayu kammɔ!’ Unwoti Ɔdubo Babilon Kasi Budie

english_verse: My people, I am on your side, and I will take revenge on Babylon. I will cut off its water supply, and its stream will dry up.
translation_verse: “Mina kadi bekyuli, nnye nte-mii na bina kakɛ na ndubo Babilon kasi budie. Ndubo-ma kuƒi butile na basɔ balákɛ ntu kedukɔ, ɔsika bana ketu kadubo bɔkwii.

english_verse: Babylon will be a pile of rubble where only jackals live, and everyone will be afraid to walk among the ruins.
translation_verse: Babilon ɔdubunwini kebu alakpi ɔlɛ lisu kesii kani na beƒukutu kani ndubo mmɔ bulie. Bekyuli badubo-ma bɔma, nsu badubo bɔyia lɛnɔ ka besie bavi kebu alakpi ammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The Babylonians roar and growl like young lions.
translation_verse: Babilonƒuɔ badubo butaakwanyi na beteebo adi aani bagyata bebi.

english_verse: And since they are hungry, I will give them a banquet. They will celebrate, get drunk, then fall asleep, never to wake up!
translation_verse: Na ka kɔka mɔɔda-ma ɔsu ni, ndubute-ma na badi na bakɛ lɛlɔyɔ na ɔmmɔ kama na lɛya na balɛɛ lɛlɛɛ linwi na basɔ balata!

english_verse: I will lead them away to die, like sheep, lambs, and goats being led to the butcher.
translation_verse: Ndubo-ma bɔtɔnku na betékpi aani baƒonu ku bese bani na béti béselaku bekyuli bani mɔɔdú-ma teeye.

english_verse: All nations now praise Babylon, but when it is captured, those same nations will be horrified.
translation_verse: “Ɔƒaamu kadi bekyuli ƒui bimwi Babilon. Nsu si uwi ɔni na béƒie-nwu báwɔlɔ ni, liƒu lɛdubo kadi bekyuli bammɔ kani bɔda geen.

english_verse: Babylon's enemies will rise like ocean waves and flood the city.
translation_verse: Na Babilonƒuɔ bekisine badubo bɔta aani ɛpu avlɔvɔ na baƒɔ ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: Horrible destruction will strike the nearby towns. The land will become a barren desert, where no one can live or even travel.
translation_verse: Na ala bubile kpakplaa bɔdubuse kalɔ na lɛma lɛni na adɔ kemmo. Na kalɔ kammɔ ƒui kadubo bunwini kalɔ kakwiidi kesii kani na ukyuli ɔdi ulakana bulie iye besie bavi kemmo muedi.

english_verse: I will punish Marduk, the god of Babylon, and make him vomit out everything he gobbled up. Then nations will no longer bring him gifts, and Babylon's walls will crumble. The Lord Offers Hope to His People
translation_verse: Na ndubo Babilonƒuɔ baƒiɔ bani baalɔ Marduk kɔtu bɔni geen na lɛya na ɔdala lɛla biala na ɔ́ƒɔ úbweli. Na kadi bekyuli badi basɔ beleboku-nwu etela adi. Na Babilon awodu adubo bɔƒɛ búwi kalɔ. Unwoti Ɔ́ya Na Nwuna Kadi Bekyuli Bákɛ Lɛnunsia

english_verse: Get out of Babylon, my people, and run for your lives, before I strike the city in my anger!
translation_verse: “Mina kadi bekyuli, bɛvi bɛlɛ Babilon ɔma kemmo na bɛƒɔ bina lili ngba asa na lise kalɔ ntaabwɛ ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ na mina kɔnyi kemmo!

english_verse: Don't be afraid or lose hope, though year after year there are rumors of leaders fighting for control in the city of Babylon.
translation_verse: Bɛsɔ bitayia na bɛyila lɛnunsia lɛnɔ ina ka atɛ keeke ada lɛkwa ndi lɛkwa banii bɔtɔnkune baata teenye teekpoku lɛlɔ na ɔni madi lɛlɔ na Babilon ɔsu.

english_verse: The time will come when I will punish Babylon's false gods. Everyone there will die, and the whole nation will be disgraced,
translation_verse: Uwi ɔdubo ɔni na ndubo ɔkɔ baƒiɔ bani nkya Babilon kɔtu bɔni. Na ukyuli biala ɔni na ɔkya mmɔ ɔdubo bukpi na kɔƒa kukpo ɔma umodi ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: when an army attacks from the north and brings destruction. Then the earth and the heavens and everything in them will celebrate.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bekpone badubɔta basi katɔ kakɛ bebebile ala ni, katɔ ku kalɔ ku ana ala ani nkya-nya kemmo ƒui badubɔkɛ lɛlɔyɔ.

english_verse: Babylon must be overthrown, because it slaughtered the people of Israel and of many other nations.
translation_verse: “Ɔlɛka bekpeli Babilon bebo, ɔsika ɔ́du Israel ku kadi bamba bekyuli pii.

english_verse: My people, you escaped death when Jerusalem fell. Now you live far from home, but you should trust me and think about Jerusalem. Leave Babylon! Don't stay!
translation_verse: Mina kadi bekyuli, bíkeli kukpi uwi ɔni na Yerusalem úbuli. Na ɔƒaani ni, bɛdubɔkya ɔgyu kakaaka bɔsiku bina ɔma, nsu bɛƒɔ-mi bɛdi na bina kasusu kasia Yerusalem lɛlɔ. Bɛtɔlɔ Babilon! Na bitakya mmɔ!

english_verse: You feel ashamed and disgraced, because foreigners have entered my sacred temple.
translation_verse: “Kɔƒa kuukpó-mii na bɛɛnu bɛnii bina anumi éwi kalɔ ka baƒɔ béduo mina kakpakɔ kedee ɔsu.

english_verse: Although Babylon's walls reach to the sky, the army I send will destroy that city. I, the Lord, have spoken. Babylon Will Be Destroyed The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ina ka bátu Babilon awodu bákɔliku katɔ katɔ kakaaka muedi ni, bekpone bani na ndubo bumene badubo ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ bɔbwɛ ƒui. Ami Unwoti násu.”

english_verse: Listen to the cries for help coming from Babylon. Everywhere in the country the sounds of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Binu kɔvanu kɔni nda Babilon kesii biala na beevele ka bekyuli bebunku-ma ka baabwɛ ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: The shouts of the enemy, like crashing ocean waves, will drown out Babylon's cries as I level the city.
translation_verse: Nsu bekisine bammɔ bɔkwanyi bɔni nse aani kalɛ na ɛpu uubó momoomo ɔdubɔyila Babilonƒuɔ buvele kɔvanu kɔmmɔ uwi ɔni baabwɛ ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ teewi kalɔ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: An enemy will attack and destroy Babylon. Its soldiers will be captured and their weapons broken, because I am a God who takes revenge against nations for what they do.
translation_verse: Ukisine ɔdi ɔdubo ubekpo Babilon na ɔyila-nwu udu. Na badubuƒie nwuna bekpone na baƒɛ bana ekpola, ɔsika ami ndi Katɔti ɔni muudie kadi biala bekyuli kasi na ala ani na bábla ɔsu.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the true King, promise that the officials and advisors, the governors and leaders, and the soldiers of Babylon will get drunk, fall asleep, and never wake up.
translation_verse: Ami Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔni ndi Ɔga geen ɔmmɔ, muusé kenye ka Babilon benengu ku bana kasusu bakyane ku aban bagadine ku batɔnkune bammɔ ƒui badubo bɔlɛɛ aani ntɛ mɔɔda-ma na basɔ baaadubo bɔtɔ kudii.

english_verse: The thick walls of that city will be torn down, and its huge gates burned. Everything that nation worked so hard to gain will go up in smoke. Jeremiah Gives Seraiah a Scroll
translation_verse: “Na badubɔƒɛ bana awodu bonwu bonwu ammɔ ƒui bewi kalɔ na batu ogya bakya lɛban kɔyakun kɔmmɔ. Na ala ani ƒui na bábla kabla ku lɛnungyie bákɛ ƒui badubo-nya bɔkyula na uyɔ utaakɔ ka teesie katɔ.” Yeremia Úti Ebuo Ɔku Kakunkɛ Kadi Úte Seraia

english_verse: During Zedekiah's fourth year as king of Judah, he went to Babylon. And Baruch's brother Seraiah went along as the officer in charge of arranging for places to stay overnight.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa linedi kemmo uwi ɔni na Sedekia ɔɔdi lɛga na Yuda ni, úsie Babilon anwu ku Baruk ɔnwani Seraia ɔni ndi Neria ubidi na ɔdi Maseya uwɔ ɔni Yeremia ɔ́su ka ubunku na ɔnu ɔga keduokɔ ala lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Before they left, I wrote on a scroll all the terrible things that would happen to Babylon.
translation_verse: Asa na badubɔyu ulu ni, línweni ɔgbankpi ala ani ndubɔlɛku Babilon lɛ́sia kakunkɛ kadi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I gave the scroll to Seraiah and said: When you get to Babylon, read this scroll aloud,
translation_verse: Na líti-ka líte Seraia na lɛ́su-nwu nnini, “Si bíduo Babilon ni, na aka ɔku ɔmɛni momoomo ete bekyuli bammɔ na benu.

english_verse: then pray, “Our Lord, you promised to destroy this place and make it into a desert where no people or animals will ever live.”
translation_verse: Na akpali Unwoti evele anini, ‘Bula Unwoti, ése kenye ka adubɔkyula likpo lɛmɛni na ɔ́ta unwini kalɔ kakwiidi kani lɛlɔ na ukyuli ɔdi iye bebuo lɛnɔ basɔ belelie kudii.’

english_verse: When you finish praying, tie the scroll to a rock and throw it in the Euphrates River. Then say,
translation_verse: Si áwɔlɔ Katɔti bɔkpali lɛni ni, na ebo ɔku ɔmmɔ ada lɛtakpɛ lɛdi lɛlɔ na ebo atákya Euƒrate Ketu kemmo na asu anini,

english_verse: “This is how Babylon will sink when the Lord destroys it. Everyone in the city will die, and it won't have the strength to rise again.” The End of Jeremiah's Writing Jeremiah's writing ends here.
translation_verse: ‘Lɛni na Babilon ɔdubo bɔnyi busie kalɔ kalɔ si uwi ɔni Unwoti ɔdubo kalɔ kammɔ bɔkyula. Na ukyuli biala na ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo ɔdubo bukpi balákɛ ɔyikun ɔni na basɔ benwini bebo ngba.’ ” Yeremia ala ani na únweni ni, édu kawɔlɔkɔ.

english_verse: Next, Nebuzaradan arrested Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah his assistant, and three temple officials.
translation_verse: Ɔni mbuku ni, bekpone unengu ɔmmɔ úƒie ɔkpane unengu Seraia ku nwuna ɔmansiane Seƒania ku kakpakɔ kabla bablane bani náƒɔ lɛnyii ɔ́tɔlɔku.

english_verse: then his eyes were poked out. He was put in chains, then dragged off to Babylon and kept in prison until he died.
translation_verse: Na bátu-nwu anumi bédie evuo kemmo na bákya-nwu ɔbuli báni-nwu bésienku Babilon bátákya-nwu ɔtɔ útédu uwi ɔni na úkpi.

english_verse: meters around. They were hollow, but the bronze was about
translation_verse: Báka ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ bákya útédu lɛkwa leevu-unwidi ka Sedekia ɔɔdi lɛga na Yerusalem.

english_verse: After a year and a half, all the food in Jerusalem was gone. Then on the ninth day of the fourth month,
translation_verse: Na kɔbuli kunedi limeyi yaalenwi kemmo ni, uwi ɔmmɔ na kɔka kɔmmɔ kenye kébo kaayu ɔkplu geen ute bekyuli bammɔ kalɛ bakɛ lɛla lɛdi muedi badi.

english_verse: the Babylonian troops broke through the city wall. That same night, Zedekiah and his soldiers tried to escape through the gate near the royal garden, even though they knew the enemy had the city surrounded. They headed toward the Jordan River valley,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bekpone bammɔ báƒɛ awodu ammɔ na bana ƒui báwia kasiakɔ na békeli bátɔlɔ usien ɔmmɔ. Na ina ka Babilonƒuɔ báka bámana ɔma ɔmmɔ ni, bakɛ bagadine ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kaƒɔkɔ na bátásia kayakun kani na awodu anyɔ ammɔ ása na bakɛ mmɔ báda bálɛ Yordan Ketu kɔwɛ kemmo.

english_verse: Zedekiah was taken to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial and found him guilty.
translation_verse: Béti Sedekia bésienku ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Ribla na Hamat kalɔ lɛlɔ kesii kani na Nebukadnesar ɔ́tɛku-nwu litemi na ɔ́du-nwu kɔtɔ.

english_verse: Zedekiah's sons and the officials of Judah were killed while he watched,
translation_verse: Na Ribla mmɔ ni, bádu Sedekia bebi bananabi ku nwuna benengu uwi ɔni na anwu ɔlati unye ɔɔnu.

english_verse: Jerusalem was captured during Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king of Babylonia. About a month later, Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guards arrived in Jerusalem. His name was Nebuzaradan,
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa leevu-yaalenwi na kɔbuli kɔlɔndi na limeyi leevudi na Babilonƒuɔ Ɔga Nebukadnesar lɛga bɔdi kemmo ni, Nebusaradan ɔni ndi Ɔga Nebukadnesar kasusu ɔkyane ku bekpone ɔtɔnkune útéduo Yerusalem.

english_verse: and he burned down the Lord's temple, the king's palace, and every important building in the city, as well as all the houses.
translation_verse: Unengu ɔmɛni ɔ́kyula Katɔti kakpakɔ kammɔ na ɔ́kyula ɔga kesii ku lɛtɔ linengudi lɛni náƒɔ lɛnyi mmɔ ƒui ku bekyuli kɔduli lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Then he ordered the Babylonian soldiers to break down the walls around Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na Nebusaradan ɔmɛni ɔ́kpanku Babilonƒuɔ bekpone ƒui na bátáƒɛ Yerusalem awodu ɔba.

english_verse: He led away the people left in the city, including everyone who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar, the rest of the skilled workers, and even some of the poor people of Judah.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama bekpone unengu ɔmɛni úti bekyuli bani nébu na ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo ku bakladi bani ngyi enu kabla kɔkwɛ ku bani na bátuna ka babla Babilonƒuɔ Ɔga kabla ɔ́tɔlɔku úsienku Babilon.

english_verse: Only the very poorest were left behind to work the vineyards and the fields.
translation_verse: Na bawabane bani na ayaki ada geen kani na bébu bákya na bataanu egyiibi mmo ku mmo geen bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan ordered his soldiers to go to the temple and take everything made of gold or silver, including bowls, fire pans, sprinkling bowls, pans, lampstands, dishes for incense, and the cups for wine offerings. The Babylonian soldiers took all the bronze things used for worship at the temple, including the pans for hot ashes, and the shovels, lamp snuffers, sprinkling bowls, and dishes for incense. The soldiers also took everything else made of bronze, including the two columns that stood in front of the temple, the large bowl called the Sea, the twelve bulls that held it up, and the movable stands. The soldiers broke these things into pieces so they could take them to Babylonia. There was so much bronze that it could not be weighed.
translation_verse: Bekpone bammɔ béti lɛla biala na béti abuala egyiedi bábla na ese kakpakɔ mmɔ ku abuala egyiedi ammɔ lɛta inyɔ bɔdi nlɛ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ anumi mmɔ lɛnɔ ku lɛkyami bonwu lɛni baalɔ ɛpu na bábla-ni básia ɔmantɛ bakɔ udu leevu-inyɔ badi lɛlɔ. Na ala amɛni ƒui enye lɛgba lɛni náya na bakana ala ammɔ ƒui bɔni busienku kesii bamba lɛlɔ. Bekpone bamɛni bébo ala amɛni ƒui bábwɛ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ kalɛ na bakana-nya buti bɔtɔlɔku busienku Babilon. Na abuala ammɔ emomo ɔni na balakana-nya unu bɔti.

english_verse: people. In his eighteenth year as king, he took
translation_verse: . Na lɛkwa leevu-maanedi kemmo ni, úƒie nkyuli

english_verse: from Jerusalem. In his twenty-third year as king, his officer Nebuzaradan took
translation_verse: ɔ́siku Yerusalem. Na lɛkwa aavlanyɔ-lɛtɛdi kemmo ni, úƒie nkyuli

english_verse: Evil Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there.
translation_verse: Ewil-Merodak ɔ́nu ɔga ɔmmɔ kɔnyana na úte-nwu kenyekɔ kani nákɔ na kebo ɔbu ketulo baga bakladi bani béƒie bátakya Babilon mmɔ kadi.

english_verse: Jehoiachin was allowed to wear regular clothes instead of a prison uniform, and he even ate at the king's table every day.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu béte Yekonia kuƒi ka ɔ́vumana nwuna batɔntɛne adala. Na utaadiku Babilonƒuɔ ɔga ɔmmɔ na kadikɔ kenwi utédu uwi ɔni ukpi.

english_verse: As long as Jehoiachin lived, he was paid a daily allowance to buy whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Na limeyi ndi limeyi ni, beete Ɔga Yekonia egulabi adi na uuti teeye ala ani na ɔɔwia. Na bábla ɔmɛni na nwuna ngba bulie kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: Jerusalem, once so crowded, lies deserted and lonely. This city that was known all over the world is now like a widow. This queen of the nations has been made a slave.
translation_verse: Aanu kalɛ na ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ uwi ukpludi. Ɔma ɔni na nka bekyuli báƒɔ-nwu kemmo pii dii, ɔƒɛni amu ɔ́ta ɔ́bla aani ukpinele. Nka anwu náƒɔ lɛnyi dii na kadi bekyuli akɔ. Anwu ɔni na nka úse aani beleku ɔga na kɔlɔ kɔni na amadɔ mmɔ ƒui akɔ ɔƒɛni amu únwini bekyuli bamba kabla ɔblane.

english_verse: Each night, bitter tears flood her cheeks. None of her former lovers are there to offer comfort; her friends have betrayed her and are now her enemies.
translation_verse: Keku kani nda usien umodi. Na imii bɔɔgbá-nwu anumi ƒui. Na útakɛ ukyuli ɔni na ɔsia-nwu kɔnu na nwuna bayɔne ƒui akɔ. Mmomu bénwini-nwu bekisine ɔƒaamu.

english_verse: The people of Judah are slaves, suffering in a foreign land, with no rest from sorrow. Their enemies captured them and were terribly cruel.
translation_verse: Kekpo kéƒie Yuda kátɔlɔku késinku kalɔ bamba, na únwini bekyuli bamba kabla ɔblane ku lɛbibo. Kadi bamba bekyuli akɔ na ɔkya na útakɛ kanwunakɔ kadi. Na bekyuli bani nsia beekpóku-nwu báavi báda-nwu na kesii kani na úmii ɔkya.

english_verse: The roads to Zion mourn because no one travels there to celebrate the festivals. The city gates are deserted; priests are weeping. Young women are raped; Zion is in sorrow!
translation_verse: Lilu lɛni ntɛ lísela Sion ƒui lɛtɛ kɔka ku kɔnyana ɔsika ukyuli ɔdi ɔsɔ ulásia-ni lɛlɔ na besie batádi bana emeyi buni adi. Nwuna ɔma unegudi lɛban kɔyakun ƒui kuse ukpludi. Na bakpane bammɔ beewulo teedumo. Banana bamba beebo teebeƒie-nwu badagyaa taatɔlɔku. Na kɔnyana ku ɔdu kati kati náƒɔ ɔma ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Enemies now rule the city and live as they please. The Lord has punished Jerusalem because of her awful sins; he has let her people be dragged away.
translation_verse: Nwuna bekisine nénwini ɔma ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ badine, na bekisine bammɔ belie-nwu ƒaa. Ekpidi bonwu ani na ɔɔbla ɔsu na Unwoti ɔ́ya na lɛbibo lɛmmɔ udu líbo-nwu lɛlɔ, na ɔ́ya na bekisine béƒie nwuna bebi bátɔlɔku na béténwini bana bekisine kalɔ bakyane.

english_verse: Zion's glory has disappeared. Her leaders are like deer that cannot find pasture; they are hunted down till their strength is gone.
translation_verse: Kalɛ na Sion uukeye ɔ́yii udu, na nwuna batɔnkune báta bábla aani bakwa bani nsɔ naaakɛ́ taadi, anwuɔsu basɔ beeebo ɔyikun na bekeli na bagbini bammɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: Her people recall the good life that once was theirs; now they suffer and are scattered. No one was there to protect them from their enemies who sneered when their city was taken.
translation_verse: Na nwuna lɛbibo ku ala ani muukpóku-nwu kemmo ni, Yerusalem ɔɔkali taanu akɛla ani nése-nwu na uwi ɔni nábavi dii kemmo, na ɔƒɛni amu ɔkɛ kɔlɔ ƒui lɛlɔ ɔɔví. Uwi ɔni na úduo nwuna bekisine enu ni, útakɛ ukyuli ɔni nebunku-nwu na bekisine bammɔ benye baanu-nwu na beedumi-nwu taama na nwuna ɔgbankpi ɔsu.

english_verse: Jerusalem's horrible sins have made the city a joke. Those who once admired her now hate her instead— she has been disgraced; she groans and turns away.
translation_verse: Ekpidi bonwu ani na Yerusalem ɔ́bla ɔsu bekyuli béti ɔma ɔmmɔ bénwini lɛmala. Na bekyuli bani na nka baabu ɔma ɔmmɔ beekisi-nwu ɔƒaamu, ɔsika údie lɛlɔ kasɔngya na únwini anumi ku kɔƒa ku keku ku edumo.

english_verse: Her sins had made her filthy, but she wasn't worried about what could happen. And when Jerusalem fell, it was so tragic. No one gave her comfort when she cried out, “Help! I'm in trouble, Lord! The enemy has won.”
translation_verse: Nwuna ekpidi énwini ala éduo-nwu adala na uleti kasusu lɛla lɛni ndubo-nwu bɔlɛku na uwi ɔni ntɔ-nwu anumi adubo lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu Yerusalem kalɔ bubo bɔdi kɔnyana litemi bonwu, na ukyuli ɔdi uuubo na ɔsia-nwu kɔnu uwi ɔni na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Unwoti, nu kalɛ na mina bekisine bádi-mi lɛlɔ na muubó abi na anu-mi kɔnyana.”

english_verse: Zion's treasures were stolen. Jerusalem saw foreigners enter her place of worship, though the Lord had forbidden them to belong to his people.
translation_verse: Béyu Sion akɛla ƒui békeliku, na unye ɔɔnu uwi ɔni na kadi bamba bekyuli béduo nwuna kakpakɔ ina ka ɔdi ekisila bubile ka bekyuli bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ beduo mmɔ.

english_verse: Everyone in the city groans while searching for food; they trade their valuables for barely enough scraps to stay alive. Jerusalem Speaks: Jerusalem shouts to the Lord, “Please look and see how miserable I am!”
translation_verse: “Budumo sɔɔn na mina bekyuli beedumo taawia bana limeyi lɛdila. Na beeti bana ala ani náƒɔ-ma kuye teeye, na basɔku beye lɛla blii lɛni kani na badi belie ngba.” Yerusalem Ɔ́tɛmiku Unwoti Yerusalem ɔ́kpali Unwoti ɔnini, “Buvele, nwini nu-mi na anu kalɛ na lɛ́yii udu.”

english_verse: No passerby even cares. Why doesn't someone notice my terrible sufferings? You were fiercely angry, Lord, and you punished me worst of all.
translation_verse: “Amii bani mɔɔví, bɛɛɛdaku-ni? Bɛnu si ɔdi ɔsɔ uubó bula abi amɛni udu. Lɛbibo lɛni kemmo na Unwoti ɔ́ya na líduo na nwuna kɔnyi kpakplaa ɔsu.

english_verse: From heaven you sent a fire that burned in my bones; you set a trap for my feet and made me turn back. All day long you leave me in shock from constant pain.
translation_verse: “Áya na ogya ɔ́si katɔ úbo na ɔɔkyula-mi teeduo-mi ekubi kemmo. Ákywɛ-mi kakpagyuɛ, na nsɔ naaakɛ́ kavikɔ. Na áya na ɔtɔtɔ ɔɔgyú-mi limeyi limodi na ɔlɛ ɔni na muunú uwi biala ɔsu.

english_verse: You have tied my sins around my neck, and they weigh so heavily that my strength is gone. You have put me in the power of enemies too strong for me.
translation_verse: “Ébo mina ekpidi áda-mi ɔkwɛ, na aayu-mi unu, na mina ɔyikun ɔ́sa. Áya na mina bekisine bákɛ ɔyikun na mina lɛlɔ, na bákɔ-mi básɔ ɔni na bebo ɔyikun bétulo-mi.

english_verse: You, Lord, have turned back my warriors and crushed my young heroes. Judah was a woman untouched, but you let her be trampled like grapes in a wine pit.
translation_verse: “Awɔ Unwoti, éni mina bekpone na édie bekpone bamba ákya-mi ka babayila mina bakloƒu bekpone udu. Yuda use aani uleku ɔni na nka bétetuku-nwu kudii, nsu anwu nénwini ukyuli ɔni na baanya teesusu aani kalɛ na baamana egyiibi ntu teewi ntɛ kewikɔ.

english_verse: Because of this, I mourn, and tears flood my eyes. No one is here to comfort or to encourage me; we have lost the war— my people are suffering. The Prophet Speaks:
translation_verse: “Ɔmɛni ɔsu kɔnyana kani na muuwulo, na imii bɔ́ƒɔ-mi anumi uwi ƒui. Na ukyuli ɔdi uuubo na ɔsia-mi kɔnu iye ɔkya-mi ogya lɛnɔ. Kekpo kádi-mi lɛlɔ na mina bekyuli beebó abi.” Kenye Udiene Údie Kenye Kadi

english_verse: Zion reaches out her hands, but no one offers comfort. The Lord has turned the neighboring nations against Jacob's descendants. Jerusalem is merely a filthy rag to her neighbors. Jerusalem Speaks:
translation_verse: Sion údie enu na ɔɔwia ubunkune nsu útakɛ kɔnu ɔsiane. Unwoti ɔ́ya na kadi bekyuli bani náka bámana Sion báta bénye Yakob bebi ku bawɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Yerusalem únwini aani lɛla lɛni muusé lɛlɔ na nwuna liku bekyuli ƒui anumi. Yerusalem Ɔ́tɛmiku Unwoti

english_verse: The Lord was right, but I refused to obey him. Now I ask all of you to look at my sufferings— even my young people have been dragged away.
translation_verse: “Unwoti ablala ƒui ese siin. Na ami mmomu, néni na neeenu-nwu litemi. Na ɔƒaani ni, mɔɔsu-mii nnii binwini bɛnu abi ani na muubó. Béƒie-mi bakloƒu ku begblebi ƒui bátɔlɔku bésienku kaƒɔ.

english_verse: I called out to my lovers, but they betrayed me. My priests and my leaders died while searching the city for scraps of food.
translation_verse: “Lɛ́lɔ mina bebunkune bakpana nsu bákya-mi kakya. Mina bakpane ku kadi batɔnkune békpi uwi ɔni na bakya baawia adila ani na badi.

english_verse: Won't you look and see how upset I am, our Lord? My stomach is in knots, and my heart is broken because I betrayed you. In the streets and at home, my people are slaughtered.
translation_verse: “Unwoti, elenwini alanu kalɛ na lɛla lɛmɛni liikpóku-mi? Kaƒɔ kébo-mi likpo na kayi kaakpulu-bu, ɔsika lɛ́lɛ-ɔ kama na ńtenu ƒula litemi. Bádu bekyuli na lɛblɔnu lɛlɔ ku kɔduli kemmo lɛnɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Everyone heard my groaning, but no one offered comfort. My enemies know of the trouble that you have brought on me, and it makes them glad. Hurry and punish them, as you have promised.
translation_verse: “Ukyuli biala únu kalɛ na muudumo, nsu ukyuli biala uuubo na ɔsia-mi kɔnu. Na mina bekisine lɛnɔ bánu lɛbibo lɛni kemmo na éti-mi ákya báti. Na ɔmɛni ɔ́ya na baakɛ́ ebiti na mina lɛlɔ geen. Buvele, babla na ebo abáni-ma kɔtu na kenye kani na ése-mi ése kenye.

english_verse: Don't let their evil deeds escape your sight. Punish them as much as you have punished me because of my sins. I never stop groaning— I've lost all hope!
translation_verse: “Taya na bana ekpidi ani baabla avi-ɔ anumi. Mmomu ni-ma kɔtu kpakplaa geen aani kalɛ kani na áni ami lɛnɔ kɔtu na mina ekpidi ɔsu. Lɛ́yila lɛnunsia biala, na naaada budumo taaya lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord was angry! So he disgraced Zion though it was Israel's pride and his own place of rest. In his anger he threw Zion down from heaven to earth.
translation_verse: Unwoti úti kɔnyi! Anwuɔsu na ɔ́kya Sion kɔƒa. Na nwuna kɔnyi kemmo ni, úbo Sion ɔni ndi Israel bukeye ɔ́va kalɔ. Na ɔ́sɔ úteti mmɔ ka ɔdi nwuna lɛgba kanyakɔ.

english_verse: The Lord had no mercy! He destroyed the homes of Jacob's descendants. In his anger he tore down every walled city in Judah; he toppled the nation together with its leaders, leaving them in shame.
translation_verse: Unwoti útanu Israel lɛma lɛmmɔ kɔnyana munu munu, mmomu ɔ́bwɛ-ni na ɔ́yila kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa kɔmmɔ ƒui udu. Na úboku bagadine ku lɛgakadikɔ kɔmmɔ ƒui kalɔ ɔkɛnku nwuna kɔnyi ɔsu.

english_verse: The Lord was so furiously angry that he wiped out the whole army of Israel by not supporting them when the enemy attacked. He was like a raging fire that swallowed up the descendants of Jacob.
translation_verse: Unwoti úti kɔnyi kpakplaa geen ɔ́kya Israel na ɔ́yila nwuna ɔyikun na bekisine bammɔ bésusu-nwu na ɔ́sɔ útekpo útete-nwu Mmomu únwini aani ogya ɔni muubile ala, na ɔ́kyula Israel kaba kemmo bebi bammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: He attacked like an enemy with a bow and arrows, killing our loved ones. He has burned to the ground the homes on Mount Zion.
translation_verse: Úbo nwuna kɔtaminta atula ɔ́lɛ-nwu aani ukisine kalɛ. Na ɔ́du nwuna bayɔne, na ɔ́kyula kɔduli kɔni ƒui nkya Sion Kɔbi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Lord was like an enemy! He left Israel in ruins with its palaces and fortresses destroyed, and with everyone in Judah moaning and weeping.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́bla lɛlɔ aani ukisine, na ɔ́da Israel úwi aani ɔma ɔni nábwɛ, na nwuna baga lɛgbanya ku ɔma kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa ƒui kɔ́bwɛ. Na ukyuli biala uuwulo keku na Yuda kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ ku kɔnyana.

english_verse: He shattered his temple like a hut in a garden; he completely wiped out his meeting place, and did away with festivals and Sabbaths in the city of Zion. In his fierce anger he rejected our king and priests.
translation_verse: Ɔ́ya na bábwɛ Katɔti kakpakɔ kammɔ béwi kalɔ aani kalɛ na kevoma kemo ɔban ɔɔbwɛ teewi kalɔ. Na úbile lɛla biala na kesii kani na uubo taabasiaku-bu mmɔ. Na ɔ́ya na bɔ́da emeyi buni ku Lɛnwunameyi bɔdi bɔ́ya na Sion ɔma kemmo. Ɔkɛnku nwuna kɔnyi kpakplaa kɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, úni bula baga ku bakpane ƒui.

english_verse: The Lord abandoned his altar and his temple; he let Zion's enemies capture her fortresses. Noisy shouts were heard from the temple, as if it were a time of celebration.
translation_verse: Unwoti údie nwuna lɛkpabi ku kakpakɔ kammɔ ƒui atu, na ɔ́ya na Sion bekisine bábaƒɛ awodu ku libili lɛmmɔ ƒui. Lɛsɛ ku kɔvanu kɔku kani na eenú yoo taasiku kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo aani si limeyi lɛdi na baadi.

english_verse: The Lord had decided to tear down the walls of Zion stone by stone. So he started destroying and did not stop until walls and fortresses mourned and trembled.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́lɛ ugyii ka ɔƒɛ Sion awodu uwi kalɔ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ɔni na lɛtabi lɛdi lɛsɔ lilasia ɔkpanadi lɛlɔ, na úubo kabuli úte kabla kammɔ kalɔ buse ɔni na lɛla lɛdi lɛsɔ liletile kuƒi kɔmmɔ. Na awodu ammɔ ku libili lɛmmɔ ƒui lɛɛƒɛ teewi kalɔ ku kɔnyana aani kalɛ na ukyuli uuwulo kɔnyana na lɛlɔ lɛɛtɔ́-nwu.

english_verse: Zion's gates have fallen facedown on the ground; the bars that locked the gates are smashed to pieces. Her king and royal family are prisoners in foreign lands. Her priests don't teach, and her prophets don't have a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Sion lɛban kɔyakun ƒui kɔ́ƒɛ kúbi anumi kalɔ, na abuala ani mɔɔbala kɔyakun kɔmmɔ kenye ƒui kɔ́ƒɛ eku eku. Na nwuna baga ku bagadine bammɔ ƒui bénwini bekyuli beƒiedi na bakya kɔlɔ bamba kemmo. Nwuna bakpane basɔ balátina ala, na nwuna kenye bediene bammɔ lɛnɔ basɔ balakɛ linyesia lɛdi taasiku Unwoti kudɔ.

english_verse: Zion's leaders are silent. They just sit on the ground, tossing dirt on their heads and wearing sackcloth. Her young women can do nothing but stare at the ground.
translation_verse: Sion batɔnkune ƒui bába lɛsɛ kpoo, na beli kalɔ kplu beebó ɔtumu teewi lɛlɔ, na benyimi adikpi. Na nwuna begblebi basɔ beeebo lɛla lɛdi, na babla utulo ka benye bataanu kalɔ kpoo.

english_verse: My eyes are red from crying, my stomach is in knots, and I feel sick all over. My people are being wiped out, and children lie helpless in the streets of the city.
translation_verse: Mina anumi asɔ alanu na keku ɔsu, na mina kaƒɔ kébo-mi likpo na ɔ́ya na mina lɛlɔ ekpo ƒui aadu-mi. Ɔdu ɔ́ƒɔ-mi lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui, ɔsika mina bekyuli báyii udu na bebi ku bebiwɔ báƒɔ lɛlɔ bewi ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ lɛblɔnu ƒui lɛlɔ beekpi ku kɔnyana ɔni na lɛblala liiibo.

english_verse: A child begs its mother for food and drink, then blacks out like a wounded soldier lying in the street. The child slowly dies in its mother's arms.
translation_verse: Bebi beewulo kɔka teeye bana beni adila, na ɔmmɔ kama na bayuɛ aani bekpone bani na báƒɔ ɔlɛ batɛ lɛblɔnu lɛlɔ, na baayula na bana beni enu kemmo.

english_verse: Zion, how can I comfort you? How great is your pain? Lovely city of Jerusalem, how can I heal your wounds, gaping as wide as the sea?
translation_verse: Sion, dɛ na ndubɔkana-a kɔnu bɔsia na ƒula lɛbibo bonwu lɛmɛni kemmo? O Yerusalem, ɔma unengudi ɔbuni, bi na ndubɔkana na lɛsu lɛsiku-ɔ lɛlɔ? Na dɛ na ndubɔkana-a budie bɔlɛku kesii kani gbion aani ɛpu mɛni kemmo?

english_verse: Your prophets deceived you with false visions and lying messages— they should have warned you to leave your sins and be saved from disaster.
translation_verse: Ƒula kenye bediene bátɔlɔ-ɔ ku ɔkɔ kɔyu kemmo ala bɔnu ku linyesia lɛni naaadi litemi geen. Bétedie ƒula bɔƒiɔ bátatina-a, na enwini ƒula ekpidi kama na akɛ bɔƒɔ. Mmomu bányi ɔkɔ na bátɔlɔ-ɔ bátáyila.

english_verse: Those who pass by shake their heads and sneer as they make fun and shout, “What a lovely city you were, the happiest on earth, but look at you now!”
translation_verse: Belusiene bani mɔɔsia mmɔ taavi baakunku eli na bapii, na beedumi-ɔ taama-a banini, “Ɔma ɔbuni ɔni na bátaalɔ banii bɔdia ku bɔdia na adi kadi ƒui lɛlɔyɔ na ɔdi mɛni ɔƒɛni?”

english_verse: Zion, your enemies curse you and snarl like wild animals, while shouting, “This is the day we've waited for! At last, we've got you!”
translation_verse: Sion, ƒula bekisine beedumi-ɔ taama banii “Útakɛ-ɔ kaduɛ, lɛni geen na bɔɔwia ɔ́si kukuuku ka bubile-ɔ na bɔyila-a udu. Na ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni na bɔ́kɛ-ɔ sɔsɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord has done everything that he had planned and threatened long ago. He destroyed you without mercy and let your enemies boast about their powerful forces.
translation_verse: Lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su úse kuuku ka wabla ni, ɔ́bla-ni lɛni kani, na ɔ́yila-a udu ɔni na útanu-ɔ kanyana, na ɔ́ya na ƒula bekisine baakun lɛmɛnɛ ka bana ɔyikun udu ɔdi ɔsɔ uuubo.

english_verse: Zion, deep in your heart you cried out to the Lord. Now let your tears overflow your walls day and night. Don't ever lose hope or let your tears stop.
translation_verse: Sion, wulo keku momoomo na ákpali Unwoti. Biwulo imii usien ku ɔƒɛ na bɔgba bɔvia bina awodu muedi. Na enu ataƒɛ-mii na bitada buwulo lɛnɔ bitaya.

english_verse: Get up and pray for help all through the night. Pour out your feelings to the Lord, as you would pour water out of a jug. Beg him to save your people, who are starving to death at every street crossing. Jerusalem Speaks:
translation_verse: Bɛta bilie usien umodi, na biteevele Unwoti bɛnii ubunku-mii. Na bidie bina ala ani muukpóku-mii ƒui bɛva-nwu anumi aani kalɛ na beewilimi ntu teedie lɛbo kemmo. Bivele-nwu na udie bina bekyuli bani nwi lɛblɔnu ƒui lɛlɔ na kɔka kɔɔdú-ma na baayɔ́ bekpi. Yerusalem Údie Lɛlɔ Kenye

english_verse: Think about it, Lord! Have you ever been this cruel to anyone before? Is it right for mothers to eat their children, or for priests and prophets to be killed in your temple?
translation_verse: Unwoti! Awɔ ɔlati, bu ɔmɛni nu anii áabla bekyuli badi ulikplu ɔmɛni udu dii! Na ɔdia ka bebi beni beƒie ama alati bebi bataakun? Munuu bɔdia na ɔdia ka badu ƒula bakpane ku kenye bediene na ƒula kakpakɔ ɔtɔ kemmo?

english_verse: My people, both young and old, lie dead in the streets. Because you were angry, my young men and women were brutally slaughtered.
translation_verse: Benengu ku banamu ƒui békpi bewi lɛblɔnu lɛlɔ ɔni na badi mina bekyuli. Na ɔkɛnku ƒula kɔnyi ɔsu ni, bekisine bébeyi mina bakloƒu ku begblebi ƒui bádu kalala kemmo.

english_verse: When you were angry, Lord, you invited my enemies like guests for a party. No one survived that day; enemies killed my children, my own little ones.
translation_verse: Unwoti kɔnyi kɔni na ákɛ ɔ́kya-bu ɔ́ya na ásɔku mina bekisine mmomu éboku ƒula kadikɔ aani ƒula bekyuli babune kalɛ. Na bekisine bamɛni bádu mina bebi benengudi ku bebliidi ƒui, na bana ɔdi útebu limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I have suffered much because God was angry.
translation_verse: Ɔkɛnku kɔnyi kɔni na Katɔti úti ɔsu, líbo abi geen.

english_verse: He chased me into a dark place, where no light could enter.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́bɔku-mi útákya kesii kani na bukeye bɔdi bulakana buduo.

english_verse: I am the only one he punishes over and over again, without ever stopping.
translation_verse: Na limeyi ndi limeyi ni, ami lɛti kani na unye ɔɔní kɔtu taasia kama.

english_verse: God caused my skin and flesh to waste away, and he crushed my bones.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔ́ya na mina ɔlɔna ɔ́yii udu, na mina ekubi ese aani bɔbwɛ na ada kɔkɛ kɔkɛ.

english_verse: He attacked and surrounded me with hardships and trouble;
translation_verse: Ɔ́ta únye-mi lɛlɔ, na ɔ́ya na ɔgbankpi ku lɛbibo lɛ́ka lɛ́mana-mi.

english_verse: he forced me to sit in the dark like someone long dead.
translation_verse: Ɔ́ya na lɛ́sɔ nli kasuudikɔ mmɔ aani ukyuli ɔni na úkpi kukuuku ƒui.

english_verse: God built a fence around me that I cannot climb over, and he chained me down.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔ́gyi ɔban ɔ́kya-mi ɔni na naaakana bɔkɔ bɔvia-nwu, na úbo-mi kɔgba úse liku linwi.

english_verse: Even when I shouted and prayed for help, he refused to listen.
translation_verse: Na ina uwi ɔni na mɔɔva taakpali-nwu nnii ubunku-mi muedi ni, úni na útakpete-mi.

english_verse: God put big rocks in my way and made me follow a crooked path.
translation_verse: Katɔti úti atakpɛ bonwu bonwu ɔ́bala-mi ulu lɛlɔ, na mina kasiakɔ kábla gontii.

english_verse: God was like a bear or a lion waiting in ambush for me;
translation_verse: Na ɔɔtú-mi aani kalɛ na gyata uubi ulu lɛlɔ taatu ebuo ɔni na uƒie.

english_verse: he dragged me from the road, then tore me to shreds.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́tu úbada-mi, na ɔ́ni-mi ɔtɔlɔku ulu lɛlɔ útáduli-mi kɔkɛ kɔkɛ.

english_verse: God took careful aim and shot his arrows
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔ́nu mina ligeen, na úbo nwuna atula úbalɛ-mi,

english_verse: straight through my heart.
translation_verse: na áƒuaala-mi kayi álɛ.

english_verse: I am a joke to everyone— no one ever stops making fun of me.
translation_verse: Lɛ́ta línwini lɛƒiankula líte ukyuli biala, na baláda-mi lɛlɔ lɛma bɔkya taaya.

english_verse: God has turned my life sour.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔ́ya na mina ngba búnwini ɔdu ɔdu búte-mi.

english_verse: He made me eat gravel and rubbed me in the dirt.
translation_verse: Ɔ́bla aani si ɔtumu lɛ́kpi nkɛ, na atabi na úte-mi ɔnii ntaanwanta na ɔƒɛ-mi anyi.

english_verse: I cannot find peace or remember happiness.
translation_verse: Liiibo bɔnwuna bɔdi na mina lɛlɔ kemmo na nsɔ neeenyimo ebiti adi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: I tell myself, “I am finished! I can't count on the Lord to do anything for me.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu lɛ́su mina lɛlɔ nnini, “Ɔƒaamu ami ɔdi ɔ́sa! Nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo ulu bɔnu nnii Unwoti ɔdubɔbla lɛla lɛdi ute-mi.”

english_verse: Just thinking of my troubles and my lonely wandering makes me miserable.
translation_verse: Na si nnye mɔɔbla kasusu taasiku mina lɛbibo ku kalɛ na ami lɛti nkɛ mɔɔka taamana ni, ɔɔyá na mina lɛlɔ lɛɛbla-mi kɔnyana geen.

english_verse: That's all I ever think about, and I am depressed.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ kani na mina kasusu kasia uwi ndi uwi na ɔɔyá na kayi kaakpulu-mi geen.

english_verse: Then I remember something that fills me with hope.
translation_verse: Nsu muunyimo lɛla linwi lɛni mɔɔyá na nsɔ mɔɔkɛ́ kayi.

english_verse: The Lord's kindness never fails! If he had not been merciful, we would have been destroyed.
translation_verse: Unwoti uleni lɛƒɔndia bɔbla kudii! Ɔsika si ɔɔɔdi nwuna kɔnyana kɔni na ɔ́nu-bu ɔsu ni, nka bɔ́yii ku udu.

english_verse: The Lord can always be trusted to show mercy each morning.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔdi ukyuli ɔni lɛlɔ na basia anu ka ɔdubɔnu-bu kɔnyana ɔtanta biala.

english_verse: Deep in my heart I say, “The Lord is all I need; I can depend on him!”
translation_verse: Na mina kayi ɔkwalɛ kemmo ƒui ni, mɔɔsu lɛlɔ geen nnini, “Unwoti kani ndi ukyuli ɔni mɔɔwia. Na nwuna lɛlɔ kani na ndubukpo kama!”

english_verse: The Lord is kind to everyone who trusts and obeys him.
translation_verse: Ukyuli biala ɔni néti nwuna anu ɔ́sia Unwoti lɛlɔ na uunú-nwu litemi ni, Unwoti ɔɔbla-nwu lɛƒɔndia.

english_verse: It is good to wait patiently for the Lord to save us.
translation_verse: Ɔdia geen ka bɔkɛ kayi na bunye butaanu Unwoti anumi na udie-bu.

english_verse: When we are young, it is good to struggle hard
translation_verse: Ɔdia ka bɔbla kagyoklo kaduɛ uwi ɔni na bɔ́si bɔɔkɔ́.

english_verse: Being rubbed in the dirt can teach us a lesson;
translation_verse: Si éboku lɛlɔ kalɔ buɛɛ ni, adubɔkɛ lɛla lɛni na asia anu.

english_verse: we can also learn from insults and hard knocks.
translation_verse: Lɛni kani na adubɔtɛya ala si bekyuli beedumi-ɔ na bana ebola éduo-ɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The Lord won't always reject us!
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔɔɔdubo-bu buni uwi ƒui!

english_verse: He causes a lot of suffering, but he also has pity because of his great love.
translation_verse: Ɔɔyá na buubó abi geen, nsu lɛni kani na ɔɔnu kɔnyana, ɔsika ubo bɔyɔ ute-bu uwi ndi uwi.

english_verse: The Lord doesn't enjoy sending grief or pain.
translation_verse: Lɛlɔ lilayɔ Unwoti ka ɔya na buteebo abi na buteenu ɔlɛ lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Don't trample prisoners under your feet
translation_verse: Bɛsɔ bitataakɔ taanya batɔntɛne eli teesusu.

english_verse: or cheat anyone out of what is rightfully theirs. God Most High sees everything,
translation_verse: Na bitebulo ukyuli kuƒi bute ka ɔbla ala ulu lɛlɔ. Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔɔnu lɛla biala.

english_verse: and he knows when you refuse to give someone a fair trial.
translation_verse: Na ɔgyi uwi ɔni na ɔdi úni ka ɔtɛ ukyuli ɔbambadi litemi siin.

english_verse: No one can do anything without the Lord's approval.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔdi ulakana lɛla lɛdi bɔbla si Unwoti útete-nwu kuƒi kɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Good and bad each happen at the command of God Most High.
translation_verse: Lɛbuni lɛdi o-o likpidi lɛdi o-o ni, Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui muudie lɛdi asa na uubo-nwu kemmo lɛni.

english_verse: We're still alive! We shouldn't complain when we are being punished for our sins.
translation_verse: Ka bɔmu bulie ngba ɔsu ni, utalɛ ka buteeni lɛla lɛdi si báni-bu kɔtu na bula ekpidi ɔsu.

english_verse: Instead, we should think about the way we are living, and turn back to the Lord.
translation_verse: Mmomu ɔlɛka bɔsia anu kalɛ na bɔti ngba bulie bɔmmɔ, na bunwini bubo Unwoti kudɔ.

english_verse: When we lift our hands in prayer to God in heaven, we should offer him our hearts and say,
translation_verse: Na si bɔ́kɔliku enu katɔ bɔɔkpali Katɔti ni, ɔlɛka buti bula kayi lɛnɔ bute-nwu na bɔsu bɔnini,

english_verse: “We've sinned! We've rebelled against you, and you haven't forgiven us!
translation_verse: “Bɔ́bla alaekpidi bɔ́ƒiɔ, na bɔ́ta búnye-ɔ lɛlɔ, na éteti tɔ átakyiɛ-bu!

english_verse: Anger is written all over you, as you pursue and slaughter us without showing pity.
translation_verse: “Kɔnyi kɔ́ƒɔ-ɔ lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui na asiaku-bu aadú-bu ɔni na kɔnyana bɔnu bɔdi buuubo.

english_verse: You are behind a wall of clouds that blocks out our prayers.
translation_verse: Ábɛla lɛlɔ ákya liƒlukutu lɛdi kama, na liitile ulu ka bula bɔkpali budu-ɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: You allowed nations to treat us like garbage;
translation_verse: Áya na kadi bamba bekyuli bada-bu beebó teewi aani kebu alakpi.

english_verse: our enemies curse us.
translation_verse: “Na bula bekisine beewida-bu.

english_verse: We are terrified and trapped, caught and crushed.”
translation_verse: Bákywɛ-bu kɔkpagyuɛ na liƒu bonwu kemmo kani na bulie, na báka-bu bákya beesusu, na bayila-bu udu.”

english_verse: My people are destroyed! Tears flood my eyes,
translation_verse: Báyila mina bekyuli udu! Na imii sɔɔn nda-mi anumi.

english_verse: and they won't stop
translation_verse: Na balada baláya lɛnɔ úti útédu

english_verse: until the Lord looks down from heaven and helps.
translation_verse: uwi ɔni na Unwoti únwini ɔ́nu-bu ɔ́siku katɔ mmɔ na úbunku-bu.

english_verse: I am horrified when I see what enemies have done to the young women of our city.
translation_verse: Ɔtɔtɔ ukpidi ɔɔgyú-mi si lɛ́nu ala ani udu na bekisine bábla bula ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ begblebi.

english_verse: No one had reason to hate me, but I was hunted down like a bird.
translation_verse: Ńtabla lɛla lɛni na ukyuli ɔdi ɔsu ɔnii anwuɔsu na ɔlɛka ukisi-mi. Nsu basiaku-mi baabwi-mi aani aasɛ ka badu-mi.

english_verse: Then they tried to kill me by tossing me into a pit and throwing stones at me.
translation_verse: Na baawia lɛnɔ ka bedi-mi bakya libiɔ kemmo na bebo-mi atabi na likpi.

english_verse: Water covered my head— I thought I was gone.
translation_verse: Ntu búyi bɔ́via-mi lili, na lɛ́bu nnii mina kawɔlɔkɔ na kadi mmɔ.

english_verse: From the bottom of the pit, I prayed to you, Lord.
translation_verse: Nsu ubu kemmo mmɔ nkya na lɛ́kpali awɔ mina Unwoti.

english_verse: I begged you to listen. “Help!” I shouted. “Save me!” You answered my prayer
translation_verse: Lívele-ɔ nnii enu-mi bɔkpali na ebunku-mi ku kɔvanu na lɛ́su nnini, “Bunku-mi! Ƒɔ-mi!” Na énu éte-mi sɔsɔ.

english_verse: and came when I was in need. You told me, “Don't worry!”
translation_verse: Ébo uwi ɔni geen lɛlɔ na mɔɔwia-a kebunku, na ásu-mi anini, “Da bɔyia ya!”

english_verse: You rescued me and saved my life.
translation_verse: Édie-mi na áƒɔ-mi ngba.

english_verse: You saw them abuse me, Lord, so make things right.
translation_verse: Unwoti, ánu ala ani udu na mina bekisine bábla-mi, anwuɔsu tɛ litemi lɛmmɔ na edie lɛla biala atina siin.

english_verse: You know every plot they have made against me.
translation_verse: Agyi likpidi lɛni lili na bása na mina lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Yes, you know their insults and their evil plans.
translation_verse: Sɔsɔ na ɔdi ka agyi kalɛ na beedumi-mi ku kɔkwɛ kukpidi kɔni na baakya-mi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: All day long they attack with words and whispers.
translation_verse: Baatɛmiku lɛlɔ kabɛnsɛ, na bada kenye etemila beekpóku-mi limeyi limodi.

english_verse: No matter what they are doing, they keep on mocking me.
translation_verse: Bebo uwi ina bi kabla lɛlɔ na benye ka bedumi na bataakya-mi lɛlɔ lɛma.

english_verse: Pay them back for everything they have done, Lord!
translation_verse: Unwoti, ƒɔ-ma lɛla biala na bábla-mi kayu!

english_verse: Put your curse on them and make them suffer.
translation_verse: Ya na ƒula ewida asiaku-ma na aya na bebo abi geen.

english_verse: Get angry and go after them until not a trace is left under the heavens.
translation_verse: Bɔku-ma die kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ kede kede na ƒula kɔnyi kemmo útédu ka basɔ balanu bana ɔdi.

english_verse: The purest gold is ruined and has lost its shine; jewels from the temple lie scattered in the streets.
translation_verse: Bébile sika ugyiedi ɔni náƒɔ kuye útulo ƒui na ɔsɔ ulékeye kalɛ na uukeye. Na bégyingya Katɔti kakpakɔ asɛɛ ebi ani náƒɔ kuye mmɔ béwi kuyeya na lɛblɔnu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: These are Zion's people, worth more than purest gold; yet they are counted worthless like dishes of clay.
translation_verse: Na Sion bebi bani na nka báƒɔ kuye betulo sika ugyiedi ni, bekyuli baanu-ma aani lɛvɔti akyami ani naaadi ku lɛla.

english_verse: Even jackals nurse their young, but my people are like ostriches that abandon their own.
translation_verse: Beƒiebuo muedi baanyuɛ bana bebi, nsu mina bekyuli bese aani aasɛ bonwu ɔdi ɔni muudie nwuna bebi atu.

english_verse: Babies are so thirsty that their tongues are stuck to the roof of the mouth. Children go begging for food, but no one gives them any.
translation_verse: Utukwɛ ɔ́du bebiwɔ ɔni na bana linyemi lɛ́du lɛ́ma bana kenye kemmo. Na banamu bakɛ beevele adila, nsu ukyuli ɔdi ulete-ma.

english_verse: All who ate expensive foods lie starving in the streets; those who grew up in luxury now sit on trash heaps.
translation_verse: Na bani mɔɔdi balakɛne adila ku lɛmwi ku lɛmwi muedi ni, batɛ beekpi ku kɔka na lɛblɔnu lɛlɔ. Na bani nási bákɔ na kɔduli kɔbuni kemmo na baaagyi ayaki adi ni, ɔƒɛni amu beli kɔwaba kemmo.

english_verse: My nation was punished worse than the people of Sodom, whose city was destroyed in a flash without the help of human hands.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́ni mina kalɔ bekyuli kɔtu útulo kalɛ na ɔ́ni Sodom ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ bekyuli kɔtu, na ɔ́ya na bábwɛ-ma ɔma uwi klukwii ɔdi kemmo kani, na ɔdi uuubo na ubunku-nwu.

english_verse: The leaders of Jerusalem were purer than snow and whiter than milk; their bodies were healthy and glowed like jewels.
translation_verse: Yerusalem batɔnkune bétebie na beekeye aani etubankɛ iye aani si nnɔmii báwɛɛ. Na bebo ɔlɔkplu na baadia bɔnu aani asɛɛ ebi ani náƒɔ kuye na aatu anumi.

english_verse: Now they are blacker than tar, and no one recognizes them; their skin clings to their bones and is drier than firewood.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔƒaani ni, bana ɔlɔgyii ɔ́nwu tonto aani kɔma nnɔ batondi bɔni na beewi ulu. Na ukyuli biala ulánu-ma taati. Ɔsika bana ɔlɔna ɔ́kwii ɔma-ma ekubi lɛlɔ, na ɔ́kwii útulo kekyweni.

english_verse: Being killed with a sword is better than slowly starving to death.
translation_verse: Si bádu ukyuli ku kewii ni, ɔdia utulo ka kɔka kutaada-a na ukpi.

english_verse: Life in the city is so bad that loving mothers have boiled and eaten their own children.
