translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Ƒilistiƒuɔ balalane bamɛni béedie bana bekisine kasi básia kama kɔlɛ kɔlɛ na báwia ka bayila bana bekisine bammɔ udu kede kede.

english_verse: Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast.
translation_verse: Na ɔƒaani ni, uwi údu ka ami lɛnɔ liti Ƒilistiƒuɔ aani mina bekisine kalɛ na lɛdu bana ɔdi biala na bana lɛma lɛni nwi ɛpu kɔtu mmɔ bene ƒui.

english_verse: In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ndubo-ma kasi budie na mina kɔnyi kpakplaa kemmo na uwi ɔmmɔ na badubɔnu bɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
translation_verse: Ka béƒie abu ku Ɔga Yekonia bátɔlɔku bésienku Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ akwa leevu-unwi kama kɔbuli kudeedi limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ni, Unwoti ɔ́tɛmiku-mi na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, Tiro ɔma unengudi bekyuli bátɔ ku lɛlɔyɔ lɛnu budie ka bekisine békpo Yerusalem na badi-nwu lɛlɔ na baasu banini, ‘Yerusalem úbuli! Uwi ɔni návi ni, badi kadi bekyuli bani na bebo ɔkplu geen na mmɔ kadi kuye kadikɔ kenengudi geen lɛnɔ. Na ɔƒaani ni, ɔmmɔ ɔ́yii udu na úbo kalɔ. Na abu ndubo-ma kenye bɔƒɔ ɔƒaamu.’

english_verse: Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore.
translation_verse: “Na ɔnu ɔni na Tiroƒuɔ bédie mɛni ɔsu ni, mɔɔlɛ-ma kpakplaa nnini, ‘Ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti na ɔƒaani línwini bina ukisine! Na ndubɔya na kadi bamba bekyuli bunbun bebo na bebekpo-mii aani kalɛ na ɛpu uubó teebewi utubli.

english_verse: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
translation_verse: Na badubo bina awodu ani na bɛ́tu bɛ́mana bina lɛma bubo bɔbwɛ na baƒɛ bina kɔgyumakɔ kɔni na bɛ́tu bínyene ƒui bewi kalɔ. Na ndubo bɔya na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔkpala lɛla biala ɔtɔlɔku ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na kebu atakpɛ ani kani ndubo butaatina.

english_verse: where fishermen can dry their nets along the coast. I promise that you will be robbed
translation_verse: Na mmɔ na lɛsawu bewine badubo bana lɛsawu ɔƒɛ buteewi na ɛpu kɔtu kɔtu mmɔ. Na líse kenye ka badubo-mii ala ƒui buƒie bɔƒɔ bɔtɔlɔku.

english_verse: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani nkya bina lɛma lɛni Mma Ɛpu kɔtu kemmo ƒui ni, badubo-ma bɔdu. Na mmɔ na bɛdubo bɔnu bɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti.’

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: “Babilonƒuɔ Ɔga Nebukadnesar ndi ɔga ɔni mbo ɔyikun utulo ƒui na kayawi. Na anwu kani mbo bapɔnkɔ ku bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ku bekpone bapɔnkɔ beliene utulo ƒui.

english_verse: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
translation_verse: Ɔdubo bina lɛma lɛni nkya ɛpu kɔtu kɔtu bɔka bukpoku na ɔdu bekyuli bani nli mmɔ bene ƒui. Na ɔmmɔ kama na ɔsia kenyekɔ ubili ku kagyumanakɔ kpakplaa na ɔkuku utédu awodu ammɔ eli ɔka ɔmana-mii.

english_verse: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
translation_verse: Na ɔdubudie lɛdi ute nwuna bekpone badi na beti egyiiku ku abuala eku na baƒɛ-mii awodu ammɔ ku kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa kɔmmɔ ƒui bewi kalɔ.

english_verse: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
translation_verse: Na ɔtumu ɔni ndubo butaata taakɔ katɔ na bapɔnkɔ bammɔ bumomo ku bana lɛgba lɛni na beetú kalɔ ɔsu ɔdubɔbla aani kalɛ na liƒlukutu bonwu lɛɛƒɔ́ kayaa. Na bapɔnkɔ kɛɛkɛ ku bapɔnkɔ beliene bammɔ kɔku kɔni na badubo butaabla si báni beedé ɔma ɔdubɔya na awodu ammɔ muedi ataakunku. Na ɔni ntulo ƒui ndi uwi ɔni na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔlati uuduo ɔma ɔni na bábwɛ béwi kalɔ mmɔ ku lɛmɛnɛ bɔkun.

english_verse: His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground.
translation_verse: Nwuna bekpone badubo ɔma ɔmmɔ bɔkɔ bɔyu na bataadu bekyuli teewi kalɔ na kɔmii ku kɔdianu ƒui na baƒɛ awodu ani eli na bínyimi kpakplaa mmɔ ƒui bewi kalɔ.

english_verse: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
translation_verse: “Bekpone bammɔ badubo bina ala ani náƒɔ-mii kuye mmɔ ƒui buyu bɔtɔlɔku. Na bebo-mii lɛtɔ lɛbuni lɛmmɔ ƒui babwɛ. Na egyiiku ku atabi ani nébu ewi kalɔ mmɔ ƒui badubo-nya bubo buwi ɛpu kemmo.

english_verse: You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps,
translation_verse: Na bɛsɔ bɛɛɛdubo lɛla lɛdi bɔnu na ɔdia na biteedie lɛnu na bitaagya lɛbentaa ku agyala adi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
translation_verse: Ɔsika ndubo-mii udu bɔyila na bɛbla aani lɛtakpɛ lɛni lɛlɔ na asawu bewine beewi bana lɛsawu ɔƒɛ. Na bɛsɔ bɛɛɛdubo bɔkana na bɛsɔku bina ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ bɛtu lɛnɔ. Ami Unwoti nése kenye lɛni.

english_verse: The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death.
translation_verse: “Na lɛlɔ lɛdubo bekyuli bani nkya ɛpu ɔmmɔ katɔ kakɛ ku kada kakɛ ƒui butaatɔ ku liƒu si beenú bina kɔvanu ku edumo ku kalɛ na badubo bina kukpi kɔku buteenu.

english_verse: The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear
translation_verse: Baga badubo bɔta bana agaboku lɛlɔ na bedie bana agala abuni lidu lɛmmɔ bewi na bayu belie ɔtuma akɔ na bataatɔ kpakpaakpa ku liƒu. Na ɔtɔtɔ ukpidi geen ɔdubɔgyu-ma si bénu kalɛ na ƒula bekisine badi-ɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and sing this funeral song: “The great city beside the sea is destroyed! Its people once ruled the coast and terrified everyone there.
translation_verse: Na badubudie ɔkwanu bete-ɔ banini, ‘Bábwɛ ɛpu kɔtu ɔma bonwu ɔmmɔ! Nka nwuna bekyuli nádi ɛpu kɔtu mmɔ bekyuli ƒui lɛlɔ dii ɔni na bana lɛlɔ libo ukyuli biala liƒu geen.

english_verse: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
translation_verse: Nsu ɔƒaani ni, Tiro ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔ́bwɛ ƒui kede kede na ɛpu kɔtɔ bekyuli baanu-nwu teemene ku liƒu ku bɔyia na bana lɛlɔ lɛɛtɔ́ sɛsɛɛsɛ.’

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will turn you into a ghost-town. The ocean depths will rise over you
translation_verse: “Ami Unwoti ndubo ɔma ɔmmɔ bɔbla aani kalɛ na ukpine kɔyu kuse. Na lɛya na ɛpu ɔmmɔ ɔyila-a ɔkya nwuna ɔkwalɛ ɔni nágyu geen kemmo

english_verse: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
translation_verse: na bɛyii bɛkya kekpine kesii kani na bati kuuku bani lɛma na bábwɛ bésie bákya ɔ́si kukuuku uwi ƒui. Mmɔ na bɛdubo bɔkya na bɛsɔ bilabla ɔma bonwu ɔni na bekyuli badubɔƒɔ-nwu kemmo pii kudii.

english_verse: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Kukpi buɛ na bɛdubo bukpi! Na bekyuli badubɔsi bebo babataawia bina ɔma ɔmmɔ, nsu baaadubo-nwu bɔnu. Ami Unwoti násu.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre,
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, die ɔkwanu na Tiro lili.

english_verse: the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me: Tyre, you brag about your perfect beauty,
translation_verse: Ɔdi ɔma unengudi ɔni na nka uwi ɛpu kɔtu na útaadiku kadi bekyuli bamba bani na ɛpu kɔtu mmɔ kuye. Na aya na bati anii kenye kamɛni kási-mi kudɔ nnini, ‘Tiro aakun lɛmɛnɛ na ƒula bɔdia bɔni na aanu ka adia geen ɔsu.

english_verse: and your control of the sea. You are a ship built to perfection.
translation_verse: Na ɛpu ɔmmɔ ɔkya-a kalɔ na aadi-nwu lɛlɔ. Na ese aani ɔkɔlɔ bonwu ɔni na bánwi na ɔdia geen.

english_verse: Builders used cypress trees from Mount Hermon to make your planks and a cedar tree from Lebanon for your tall mast.
translation_verse: Ƒula banwine béti egyii abuni kpakplaa ani na básiku Hermon Kɔbi lɛlɔ bánwi ƒula kɔnyakɔ kugyikɛ na béti egyii ani na básiku Lebanon bábla eƒulo ligyii kangyaa lɛni mɔɔƒɔ́ ɔƒɛƒɛɛ teete-ɔ.

english_verse: Oak trees from Bashan were shaped into oars; pine trees from Cyprus were cut for your deck, which was then decorated with strips of ivory.
translation_verse: Na béti egyii kpakplaa udu bamba básiku Basan abi lɛlɔ bánwi ɔkɔlɔ likuni bonwu lɛni na beeti taaka-a. Na básiku ligyii lɛni nálɛ ƒia ƒia na Kipro kalɔ lɛlɔ basia-a ɔtɔ kalɔ ubili kuliekɔ kuliekɔ na béti ɔtunkpɛ básia kukulo kukulo bákya-a akya abuni.

english_verse: The builders used fancy linen from Egypt for your sails, so everyone could see you. Blue and purple cloth from Cyprus was used to shade your deck.
translation_verse: Ƒula banwine béti adi kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ani náƒɔ kuye geen básiku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ bédi ƒula eƒulo ammɔ kalɛ na bekyuli banu-ɔ ɔsiku ɔgyu kakaaka ƒui. Adi ani náƒɔ kuye geen ku kunweni lidu lidu na básiku Kipro na béti bébi kuliekɔ kɔni na bási ubili mɛni kevo na ɔ́kya-nwu ɔyuli.

english_verse: Men from Sidon and Arvad did the rowing, and your own skilled workers were the captains.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na banana bani nási Sidon ku Arvad mɔɔka ɔkɔlɔ ku likuni bonwu bonwu lɛmɛni. Na benengu bani mɔɔnu kabla bablane bamɛni lɛlɔ ndi ƒula banwine bani nánwi-ɔ kaduɛ mɛni.

english_verse: Experienced men from Byblos repaired any damages. Sailors from all over shopped at the stores in your port.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani ngyi ɔkɔlɔ lɛlɔ ala kabla kaduɛ na bási Biblos ni, ama mɔɔklibi-ɔ si lɛla lɛdi líbie-ɔ lɛlɔ. Na beyedine baasí ekpo ekpo teebo teebeye ƒula eyedila na ƒula kalɛlɛkɔ.

english_verse: Brave soldiers from Persia, Lydia, and Libya served in your navy, protecting you with shields and helmets, and making you famous.
translation_verse: “ ‘Bekpone bani mbo kayi geen na bási Persia ku Lidia ku Libia mɔɔbla kabla aani ƒula ketu lɛlɔ bekpone na baagyumana-a ku kekpo agyumanala ku kekpo kɔbwa na báya na aaƒɔ́ lɛnyi teesie ɔgyu sɔsɔ.

english_verse: Your guards came from Arvad and Cilicia, and men from Gamad stood watch in your towers. With their weapons hung on your walls, your beauty was complete.
translation_verse: Ƒula bagyumanane bamɛni bási Arvad ku Kilikia. Na bekyuli bani na bási Gamad muunye ƒula kɔgyumanakɔ kpakplaa kɔmmɔ taasia anu na béti bana ekpola báƒala ƒula awodu lɛlɔ na ƒula bɔdia búdu bɔ́wɔlɔ.

english_verse: Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products.
translation_verse: “ ‘Beyedine bani nási Tarsis baadi sika ɔƒualadi ku abuala kpakplaa ku abuala ani baanwamana kuye teete-ɔ kalɛ na eti-nya abla kabla lidu.

english_verse: The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze,
translation_verse: “ ‘Na Grikiƒuɔ ku Tubal ku Mesek bekyuli beeyé bekyuli teeboku-ɔ ku abuala egyiedi.

english_verse: and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na bekyuli bani nási Bet-Togarma baadiku-ɔ kuye teeboku-ɔ bapɔnkɔ bani mɔɔtuma ku bani muusié kekpokɔ ku bebuo ala betine.

english_verse: You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods.
translation_verse: “ ‘Awɔ ku Dedanƒuɔ bɛɛdi kuye taasala. Na kadi bekyuli bani nli ɛpu kɔtu mmɔ bene ƒui bɛɛdi kuye na beeyé batu ɔtunkpɛ teete-ɔ ku egyii atonwudi kpakplaa adi udu teeti taavumanaku ala ani na awɔ ebo.

english_verse: Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na Yuda ku Israelƒuɔ béti kakpa edula ku egyiibi lidu béboku-ɔ ku uwɔ ku nnɔ ku kutu akyala lidu bábavumanaku ƒula eyedila.

english_verse: The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na ka Damaskoƒuɔ bánu ala ani na ebo ɔsu ni, ama lɛnɔ béti ntɛ bɔni na bɔ́si Helbon ku bebuo linwini lɛni na básiku Saha béboku-ɔ.

english_verse: Vedan and Javan near Uzal traded you iron and spices.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na Vedan ku Yavan bani nde Usal béboku-ɔ abuala ku kutu akyala.

english_verse: The people of Dedan supplied you with saddle blankets,
translation_verse: “ ‘Dedanƒuɔ béti kuntu ɔni na baasia bapɔnkɔ lɛlɔ teelie-nwu lɛlɔ mmɔ béboku-ɔ.

english_verse: while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na Arabiaƒuɔ ku Kedar lɛlɔ badine béboku-ɔ baƒonubi ku baƒonu ku bese.

english_verse: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products.
translation_verse: “ ‘Beyedine bani na bási Seeba ku Raama béti kutu akyala abuni geen ku atabi ani na áƒɔ kuye geen ku sika ugyiedi bábavumana ku ƒula eyedila ani na ebo.

english_verse: You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad,
translation_verse: “ ‘Lɛni kani na awɔ ku bekyuli bani na bási lɛma linengudi lɛni ndi Haran ku Kane ku Eden ku Seeba ku Asur ku Kilmad bɛ́di kuye bɛ́sala.

english_verse: and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope.
translation_verse: Na ama béte-ɔ adi ani na áƒɔ kuye geen na bédi-nya atu bákya akya lidu lidu ku ani muukeye ku lɛbuli lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go. You were like a ship loaded with heavy cargo
translation_verse: “ ‘Lɛkɔlɔ libendi geen muuti-ɔ ala kesii biala na lɛɛyɔ́ ka lisie. Na awɔ ɔlati ɔmmɔ ese aani ɔkɔlɔ ɔni na bétile-nwu ala pii geen,

english_verse: and sailing across the sea, but you were wrecked by strong eastern winds.
translation_verse: na asia ntu anumi ésela na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa úbebo-ɔ ɔ́bwɛ.

english_verse: The shouts of your drowning crew were heard on the shore.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bénu kɔvanu kɔni na bekyuli bani nkya-a kemmo baabla ka ketu keeti-ma na ɛpu utubli ƒui.

english_verse: Every ship is deserted; rowers and sailors and captains all stand on shore,
translation_verse: Lɛkɔlɔ bamba bakane ku bani na bakya-ni kemmo ku lɛkɔlɔ lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ banune ƒui bálɛ bana lɛkɔlɔ kemmo bésie benye utubli,

english_verse: mourning for you. They show their sorrow by putting dust on their heads and rolling in ashes;
translation_verse: na beewulo teete-ɔ ku kɔnyana na ƒula ɔgbankpi ɔsu na baakpí ɔtumu teebo lɛti teewi lili taatina kalɛ na lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́ku-ɔ liikpóku-ma.

english_verse: they shave their heads and dress in sackcloth as they cry in despair.
translation_verse: Békpeyi bana eli na bada kɔnyana buwulo adala na beewulo ku kɔnyana ka basɔ beeebo lɛnunsia lɛdi ɔsu.

english_verse: In their grief they sing a funeral song for you: “Tyre, you were greater than all other cities. But now you lie in silence at the bottom of the sea.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na bana kɔnyana kemmo ni, bédie ɔkwanu béte-ɔ banini, “Tiro, nka awɔ náƒɔ lɛnyi étulo lɛma linengudi lɛkladi ƒui. Nsu ɔƒɛni amu ni, ƒula kenye kába mana mana na atɛ ɛpu kalɔ ƒui.”

english_verse: “Nations that received your merchandise were always pleased; kings everywhere got rich from your costly goods.
translation_verse: Ebiti átaada kadi bani bekyuli nákɛ ƒula eyedila béye. Na baga ƒui na kesi kesii bénwini balakɛne na ƒula ala ani náƒɔ bekyuli kuye geen ɔsu.

english_verse: But now you are wrecked in the deep sea, with your cargo and crew scattered everywhere.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔƒaani ni, aanu-ɔ nábwɛ ewi ɛpu kalɔ na ƒula eyedila ku kabla lidu bablane ƒui bégyingya bakya kesi kesii na ɛpu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: People living along the coast are shocked at the news. Their rulers are horrified, and terror is written across their faces.
translation_verse: Ɔtɔtɔ buɛ ɔ́gyu bekyuli bani ƒui na beli ɛpu ɔmmɔ kɔtu mmɔ na liƒu líƒie-ma na ɔɔtina na bana anumi lɛnɔ kɔnakunwi.

english_verse: The merchants of the world can't believe what happened. Your death was gruesome, and you are gone forever.”
translation_verse: Kayawi beyedine ƒui balakana na bɔƒɔ lɛla lɛni udu nálɛku-mii mɛni udu badi. Ƒula kukpi litemi lɛdi lɛyiala geen. Na awɔ ɔdi ɔ́sa ƒui kede kede.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying: You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human.
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, su Tiro ɔga anini, ‘Aatalaku lɛlɔ katɔ taavili na aawia ka bekyuli banu-ɔ aani kayaa ɔyikune ɔdi na adi na Tiro ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔdi ƒula lɛga kadikɔ, nsu ukyuli keeke kani na adi.

english_verse: You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
translation_verse: Aabu ka áda anu etulo Daniel na agyi lɛla biala.

english_verse: Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver.
translation_verse: Sɔsɔ ƒula lɛnunda lɛ́ya na énwini ɔlakɛne, ɔsika ebo sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi geen na ƒula egulabi kesekɔ.

english_verse: You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
translation_verse: Agyi egulabi bɔbla kɔkwɛ lilu geen sɔsɔ na ala lɛnɔ emomo-ɔ geen, nsu ƒula akɛla áya na aatina lɛlɔ na asɔ alabu lɛla lɛdi!

english_verse: You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God,
translation_verse: “ ‘Éti lɛlɔ aakɔ́ku kayaa ɔyikune ɔdi, anwuɔsu ɔƒaani ni, ami Unwoti Katɔti

english_verse: will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get.
translation_verse: ndubo-ɔ buti bɔkya bekisine balalane enu kemmo na bayila-a udu ku ƒula akɛla ani na ƒui na ábla kabla kpakplaa ákɛ mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
translation_verse: Ƒula bekisine badubo-ɔ bɔdu kalala kemmo na ɛpu kalɔ ndubunwini ƒula kaƒiɔtɔ.

english_verse: When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human.
translation_verse: Na si uwi ɔni na úbo úte ka enye asiaku ƒula bekisine adubɔsɔ asu anii kayaa ɔyikune ɔdi na adi? Badubo-ɔ bukpoku na ebo abi aani ukyuli ɔyawine bamba kalɛ.

english_verse: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
translation_verse: Baƒɔ ndubo bebekpoku na badu-ɔ na adubukpi aani bekyuli bani naaakya liili kalɔ teete-mi kalɛ. Ami Unwoti násu.’ ” Bédie Ɔkwanu Béte Tiro Ɔga

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying: At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking.
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, die ɔkwanu te Tiro ɔga na asu-nwu anii ami nnini, ‘Na uwi ɔdi návi kemmo ni, na adia geen áwɔlɔ na ebo kasusu geen na aadia bɔnu lɛnɔ.

english_verse: You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born.
translation_verse: Na Eden Ɔban kemmo na ákya na áda sika ugyiedi adala ani na béti sika ugyiedi atabi ani mbo bukeye lidu lidu bábla na aadia bɔnu geen. Na ala amɛni ƒui ese ete-ɔ ɔ́si limeyi lɛni na báwɔ-ɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
translation_verse: Na lɛ́ya na ngba kebweyi kadi mbo avwi ɔɔgyumana-a kaduli na mina kɔbi kedee lɛlɔ kesii kani na eesié atabi ani muukeye aani sika ugyiedi na aatu anumi akɔ.

english_verse: You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na ɔ́si uwi ɔni na báwɔ-ɔ mmɔ ni, átaabla ala ƒui ulu lɛlɔ, nsu nwuna kama ni, ése kalɔ aabla ulikplu ala.

english_verse: You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
translation_verse: Átaadiku kadi bamba bekyuli kuye na énwini ɔlalane na likyulikpi lɛ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui. Anwuɔsu línye-ɔ lɛlɔ na lɛ́bɔku-ɔ lɛ́lɛ mina kɔbi kedee lɛlɔ mmɔ. Na ngba kebweyi kani na nka kátaagyumana-a mmɔ ɔlati nábɔku-ɔ ɔ́lɛku sika atabi ani náƒɔ kuye akɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you.
translation_verse: Ƒula bɔdia bɔni na aadia bɔnu nátɔlɔ na énwini ukyuli ɔni na asɔ alábu lɛla lɛdi na aatina lɛlɔ. Na ka ƒula lɛnyi lísie ɔgyu ɔsu ni, ese kalɔ aabla adɔlɔla. Anwuɔsu na líkpeli-ɔ lɛ́va kalɔ na baga babambadi baamá-a.

english_verse: You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood,
translation_verse: Ánya beyedine bamba ákya ɔni náya na bina kɔkpakɔ kɔmmɔ ƒui kuusé lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu na lɛ́kya ƒula ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ogya na ntɔ sɔɔn kani na ukyuli biala ɔɔnu na kesii kani na nka ƒula ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ uwi mmɔ.

english_verse: and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever. Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
translation_verse: Kadi bamba bekyuli bánu ɔmɛni na liƒu bonwu líƒie-ma. Ƒula kɔtu bɔbi bɔɔtɛ kalɔ munu munu na awɔ áyii udu ƒui kede kede.’ ” Unwoti Ɔ́tɛku Sidon Litemi Na Israel Ɔ́kɛ Atu Bɔyɔ

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, du Sidon ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ bekyuli kɔtɔ

english_verse: and tell its people: I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy.
translation_verse: na asu-ma anini, ‘Ami Unwoti Katɔti línwini bina ukisine! Na bekyuli badubo-mi bumwi si lɛ́ni-mii kɔtu na banu-mi bati kalɛ na nse kedee.

english_verse: I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ndubo bɔya na lɛlɛ likpidi libo-mii na lɛkyula-mii. Na lɛya na bekisine bebekpo-mii na baka bamana-mii na badu-mii na bɛnu bɛti ka sɔsɔ ami ndi Unwoti.

english_verse: When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. A Blessing for Israel
translation_verse: Na su uwi ɔni na ala amɛni álɛ ni, Israel badukɛne basɔ balabla bekyuli bekpidi bani ndubukpoku-ma na ɔbla-ma aani si liyu alakpi akɔ na bakya. Na Israelƒuɔ badubo bɔnu bɔti ka ami Unwoti Katɔti nábla ala amɛni.’ ” Unwoti Úte Israel Kusɛ Kusɛ

english_verse: The Lord God said: Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob.
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti ɔnini, “Limeyi lɛdi ni, ndubo Israel bekyuli bɔsala bɔsiku kadi bamba bekyuli akɔ kesii kani na bégyingya bakya ɔƒɛni na kadi biala bekyuli banu kalɛ na nse kedee. Na Israelƒuɔ badubɔsɔ bebelie ɔmii ɔni na líti líte mina kabla ɔblane Yakob kemmo.

english_verse: They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Badubo bulie ku keyi buɛɛ na atu ayɔ-ma na ama alati batu bana lɛtɔ na besie bana adingyii mmo. Basɔ baaadubo ɔgbankpi kemmo bɔkya, ɔsika ndubo bana bekisine kpakplaa bammɔ kɔtu bɔni. Na Israelƒuɔ badubo bɔnu bɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti bana Katɔti.”

english_verse: Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na béti Ɔga Yekonia ku abu bakladi bátɔlɔku bésienku Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ aani batɔntɛne kalɛ akwa leevu kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́tɛmiku-mi na kɔbuli leevudi limeyi leevu-linyɔdi lɛlɔ na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, du Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga kɔtɔ na asu anwu ku nwuna bekyuli anii

english_verse: that I am saying: King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy!
translation_verse: ami nnini, ‘Awɔ Egyipte ɔga, ábla lɛlɔ aani odenge bonwu ɔdi na ɔtɛ ketu kemmo. Na átaabla lɛlɔ aani si Nil Ketu bonwu kammɔ ƒui ɔwɔ kadi na kadi na awɔ nábla-ka éte lɛlɔ. Nsu ɔƒaani ni, ami Unwoti Katɔti línwini ƒula ukisine!

english_verse: I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body.
translation_verse: Ndubo ɔdaliwa bubo bɔda-a kenye na lɛni-ɔ lidie ntu bɔmmɔ kemmo na ƒula bebunkune bani lɛnɔ nse aani kɔbɛ mmɔ ƒui badu bada-a ɔlɔna ku akpa ammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh.
translation_verse: Na ndububo awɔ ku kɔbɛ kɔmmɔ ƒui liwi kalɔ kakwiidi kpakplaa lɛlɔ na bɛƒɔ lɛlɔ bɛtɛ mmɔ ɔni na ukyuli biala ɔɔɔdubo-ɔ bɔva, mmomu bebuo ku baasɛ ndubo-ɔ ɔlɔna bɔkun.

english_verse: Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord. You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala na Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔdubo bɔnu bɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti. “ ‘Awɔ ku ƒula kadi bekyuli bíni bɛnii bilebunku Israelƒuɔ, mmomu buse bise aani ugyii ɔni nábwɛ únwini kegyiikɛ.

english_verse: When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bébo kɔnu báda-mii ka nka bibunku-ma ni, bɔƒɛ na bɛ́ƒɛ kemmo inyɔ na kakɛ kammɔ kátu-ma kɔnu na bálɛ bétébo na bébuli.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ami Unwoti Katɔti ndubo bekpone buti bumene na bebekpo awɔ Egyipte ɔga. Na badubo ƒula bekyuli ku bebuo bɔdu

english_verse: until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things. You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it.
translation_verse: utédu uwi ɔni na ƒula kalɔ kadubunwini kalɔ kekpludi kani nákwii na kasɔ kaladia lɛla lɛdi bɔbla. Mmɔ na adubɔti ka ami nábla ala amɛni. “ ‘Aasu taatina aani ka awɔ nábla Nil Ketu kammɔ na awɔ mɔɔdi-ka lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Na ɔƒaani ni, lɛ́ta muunye awɔ ku ƒula ketu kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Na ƒula kalɔ kammɔ ƒui kadubunwini kalɔ kekpludi kani lɛlɔ nsɔ neeebo kɔsia kɔdi ɔ́si Migdol ɔma na kɔtɔ kakɛ útédu Aswan na kada kakɛ ɔ́vi útédu Kus ɔmii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔyawine iye ebuo ɔdi muedi ulése kayi ɔnii ɔɔsia Egyipte kalɔ kemmo mmɔ ɔlɛ, ɔsika na akwa aavlene kemmo ƒui ni, lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛdubo bɔtina aani si ngba lɛla lɛdi lɛkya kalɔ kammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: It will be the most barren place on earth. Every city in Egypt will lie in ruins during those
translation_verse: Kalɔ kammɔ ndubɔbla kalɔ kekpludi ƒui utulo na kayawi ɔni na lɛla lɛla lɛɛɛdubo bɔdi na kana kemmo. Na ɔma unengudi biala na Egyipte kalɔ kammɔ ƒui kemmo ɔdubo bɔbwɛ na ɔyii udu akwa aavlene sɔɔn.

english_verse: They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom
translation_verse: Badubɔsɔ bebelie liku linwi na Egyipte bana kalɔ kammɔ kemmo na kada kakɛ, nsu lɛga kadikɔ kammɔ kasɔ kaaadubo ɔyikun bɔkɛ geen lɛni.

english_verse: and won't ever be strong enough to rule nations, as they did in the past.
translation_verse: Na basɔ baaadubo bekyuli lɛlɔ bɔdi aani kalɛ na bátaabla uwi ɔni návi kemmo.

english_verse: My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
translation_verse: Mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ basɔ baaadubo-mii anu bɔsia na beti lɛlɔ bekpo-mii lɛlɔ. Na geen si banii Israelƒuɔ bammɔ benyimo lɛla lɛni nábla amii Egyipteƒuɔ ni, nka ama alati badubo bɔnu bɔti bɔƒiɔ bɔni na báaƒiɔ si bénwini bébo-mii kudɔ banii baawia kebunku kadi basiku-mii kudɔ. Na Israelƒuɔ badubo bɔnu bɔti ka ami Unwoti Katɔti nábla ala amɛni.’ ” Babilonƒuɔ Ɔga Nebukadnesar Ɔdubɔdi Egyipte Kalɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: Ka béti Ɔga Yekonia ku abu bakladi bátɔlɔku bésienku Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ aani batɔntɛne akwa aavlanyɔ-maatɛ kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́tɛmiku-mi na kɔbuli kudeedi limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ. Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini,

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city.
translation_verse: “Babilonƒuɔ Ɔga Nebukadnesar úkpo Tiro ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ. Na únye bekpone bammɔ lɛlɔ na béti etila bonwu pii ani náya na bana eli ápa na bana lɛlɔ lɛ́ƒɔ ɔlɛ geen na amangba ku ekpo bamba pii lɛnɔ. Nsu Ɔga Nebukadnesar ku nwuna bekpone bátakana na beƒie Tiro ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ baƒɔ.

english_verse: So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔƒaani ni, ndubuti Egyipte kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛkya-nwu enu na beti bana akɛla ani náƒɔ-ma kuye geen mmɔ ƒui batɔlɔku na uti ɔƒɔ nwuna bekpone bammɔ kayu.

english_verse: Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Egyipte kalɔ kammɔ na ndubuti lɛƒɔ-nwu kayu, ɔsika anwu ku nwuna bekpone bákya bátaabla-mi kabla na baadi mina litemi lɛlɔ. Ami Unwoti Katɔti násu.

english_verse: Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: “Esekiel, si uwi ɔni na lɛ́ya na bádi Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ báwɔlɔ ni, ndubɔya na Israelƒuɔ bakɛ ɔyikun na lɛya na ndubute-ɔ ɔyikun ɔni na atɛmi ete-ma. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na bati ka ami Unwoti nábla ala amɛni.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying: Cry out in despair,
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, su Egyipteƒuɔ anii ami nnini, ‘Biteewulo kɔnyana ka bɛsɔ biiibo lɛnunsia lɛdi ɔsu,

english_verse: because you will soon be punished! That will be a time of darkness and doom for all nations.
translation_verse: ɔsika bɛdubo bina kɔtu bɔni bɔƒɔ uwi klukui kemmo! Na uwi ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla lɛdisa bonwu ku udu bɔyii ute kadi bekyuli ƒui.

english_verse: Your own nation of Egypt will be attacked, and Ethiopia will suffer. You will be killed in battle, and your land will be robbed and left in ruins.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli badubo bina Egyipte kalɔ kammɔ alati bukpoku na Kus ɔdubo abi bubo. Na badubo-mii bɔdi na kekpokɔ. Na badubudie ala abuni ƒui balɛku bina kalɔ kemmo na kasɔ kewi ukpludi na kebie lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Soldiers hired from Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Arabia, Kub, as well as from Israel, will die in that battle.
translation_verse: Na bekpone bani na bɛ́ƒɔ bɛ́siku Kus ku Libia ku Lidia ku Arabia kalɔ lɛlɔ na kayu kenye ku Israel badi ƒui badubo bukpi na kekpo kammɔ.

english_verse: All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Badubo bina kadi bamba bekpone bani nnye nte-mii bɔdu na bina ɔyikun ɔni na bibo ƒui kenye kekulo na bɛyii udu. Na bekyuli badubo bukpi ɔ́si Migdol na katɔ kakɛ útédu Aswan na kada kakɛ ami Unwoti násu.

english_verse: Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin.
translation_verse: “ ‘Bina Egyipte kalɔ ndubo bunwini ɔmii ɔni na bekyuli badubuni bese ƒui na kalɔ lɛlɔ na lɛma linengudi lɛmmɔ ƒui lɛsɔ liwi ukpludi ɔni na lɛla lɛla lɛsɔ lilakya-ni kemmo.

english_verse: I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ndubo ogya bɔtu bɔkya bina kalɔ kemodi kammɔ ƒui na ukyuli biala ɔni menye ɔnii uukpó ute kalɔ kammɔ ɔdubo bukpi. Na bɛdubo bɔnu bɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti.

english_verse: On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na limeyi lɛni kani lɛlɔ na ndubo Egyipte kalɔ bɔkyula ni, limeyi lɛmmɔ kani lɛlɔ na ndubɔtala ukyuli lɛkya Kus kalɔ lɛlɔ bekyuli na batákɔ lɛsa bete-ma ka ama lɛnɔ bana bɔkywi bɔsia ulu bɔdubo. Baakali ka ama belie-nwu ƒaa, nsu liƒu ala adubɔlɛku-ma.

english_verse: Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army.
translation_verse: “ ‘Bina Egyipteƒuɔ bekpone bebo ɔkplu geen, nsu ndubo Babilon Ɔga Nebukadnesar bɔtala bɔkya-mii na ubo ubadi-mii lɛlɔ ƒui kede kede.

english_verse: He and his cruel troops will invade and destroy your land and leave your dead bodies piled everywhere.
translation_verse: Anwu ku nwuna bekpone balalane badubo bebekpo-mii na bayila-mii udu na beƒie-mii ala ƒui baƒɔ na bina bekyuli bekpi bewi lisu na kesi kesii.

english_verse: I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
translation_verse: “ ‘Ndubo bɔya na Nil Ketu bonwu kammɔ kakwii na liti kalɔ kammɔ liye lite bekyuli bekpidi badi. Na ndubɔya na bekyuli basi kaƒɔ bebo bababla na kalɔ kemodi kammɔ kenwini kalɔ kakwiidi kani kemmo na lɛla lɛdi lɛsɔ liladia. Ami Unwoti násu.’ ” Egyipteƒuɔ Lɛma Linengudi Lɛni Lɛlɔ Na Baakun Lɛmɛnɛ Lɛdubo Bubie

english_verse: All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land.
translation_verse: “ ‘Baƒiɔ ku ala ani ƒui amii Egyipteƒuɔ bɛ́bla bíse bíte lɛlɔ bɛɛkpá na Memƒis ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, badubo-nya bubo bɔbwɛ. Na bana akɔ ɔdi ɔsɔ ulebu na utaadi kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ. Na liƒu bonwu lɛdubɔƒɔ kalɔ kammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The city of Pathros will be left in ruins, and Zoan will be burned to the ground. Thebes, your capital city, will also be destroyed!
translation_verse: Na Patros ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔdubo bubie na ɔsɔ uwi ukpludi. Na badubo Soan ɔma ɔmmɔ ƒui bɔkyula buwi kalɔ. Na bina ɔma unengudi Tebes lɛnɔ badubo-nwu bɔbwɛ!

english_verse: The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
translation_verse: Mine kɔnyi ablala kpakplaa adubo bɔlɛku Pelusum ɔma unengudi ɔni na bátu awodu bámana mmɔ. Na badubo bekpone bani ƒui nnye Tebes mmɔ baagyumana bɔdu.

english_verse: I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ndubo ogya bɔtu bɔkya Egyipte kalɔ kemodi kammɔ ƒui! Na Pelusum ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔdubo buteedumo ku kɔnyana. Tebes ɔdubo bubuli na liƒu bonwu liƒie Memƒis kadi bekyuli na bataabla gyuma gyuma uwi biala.

english_verse: The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner.
translation_verse: Bekpone bakɔdi bani ƒui nkya Heliopoli ku Bubastis ƒui badubo bukpi na kekpokɔ na beƒie bekyuli bakladi batɔlɔku aani batɔntɛne.

english_verse: You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity.
translation_verse: Ɔyikun ɔni na bina kalɔ kebo ni, anwuɔsu na bɛɛkun lɛmɛnɛ na bɛɛkɔliku lɛlɔ katɔ lɛni. Nsu si uwi ɔni na líbile-nwu bubile na líkulo bina lɛmɛnɛ bɔkun kenye ni, Taƒanes ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ƒui ɔdubo bɔbla suu. Na liƒlukutu suu lɛdi lɛdubɔƒɔ kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ ku kɔnyana uwi ɔni na bákpanku-mii baalɛ́ku aani bekyuli beƒiedi kalɛ.

english_verse: When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord. Egypt's King Is Powerless
translation_verse: Na si uwi ɔni na lɛ́wɔlɔ Egyipteƒuɔ kɔtu kɔmɛni udu bɔni bɔwɔlɔ lɛni ni, bɛdubɔnu bɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti.’ ” Ɔyiku Ɔ́lɛ Egyipteƒuɔ Ɔga Lɛkɔkɔ

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: Na akwa leevu-unwi kama uwi ɔni na béƒie Ɔga Yekonia ku abu bakladi bátɔlɔku bésienku Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ aani batɔntɛne kalɛ ni, Unwoti ɔ́tɛmiku-mi na kɔbuli kudeedi limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword.
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, ami Unwoti lɛ́di Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga lɛlɔ! Lɛ́ƒɛ-nwu kɔnu ɔni na ukyuli biala útenyimi-ku iye bakya-nwu kɔnu kɔmmɔ lɛdiku lɛdi kalɛ na kuyile-nwu bɔsa na kɔsɔ kɔyu-nwu ɔkplu na ɔkana kewii kadi bɔda.

english_verse: So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu su-nwu anii línwini-nwu ukisine unengudi ƒui. Na ndubo-nwu enu ananyɔ ammɔ kɔbuni ku kukpidi ƒui bɔƒɛ! Na nwuna kewii kadubo bɔlɛ-nwu enu bubo kalɔ úsela uwi ƒui.

english_verse: and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
translation_verse: Na ndubo Egyipteƒuɔ bugyingya bɔkya kayawi kemodi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na ndubo Babilonƒuɔ ɔga ɔyikun bɔkya bubu na liti mina kewii lite-nwu na uti-ka ukpo Egyipteƒuɔ. Na lɛya na Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ɔyikun ɔyii udu na uteedumo na lɛlɛ lɛni na ɔ́ƒɔ ɔsu. Na ɔdubunu ɔlɛ geen útédu ka ukpi na Babilonƒuɔ ɔga anumi. Na kalɔ lɛlɔ bekyuli ƒui badubɔnu ka ami ndi Unwoti.

english_verse: I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
translation_verse: Ndubo Egyipteƒuɔ lɛlɔ bunye na bakya bekyuli bamba kalɔ aani bekyuli beƒiedi na baƒɔ kalɔ lɛlɔ na banu bati ka ami Unwoti náni-ma kɔtu.’ ”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
translation_verse: Na akwa leevu-unwi kama uwi ɔni na béƒie Ɔga Yekonia ku abu bakladi bátɔlɔku bésienku Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ aani batɔntɛne kalɛ ni, Unwoti ɔ́tɛmiku-mi na kɔbuli kɔtɛdi limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying: You are more powerful than anyone on earth. Now listen to this.
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, su Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ku nwuna bekyuli anini, ‘Bibo ɔyikun bitulo ukyuli bamba biala ka kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔƒaani ni, bise atu na binu.

english_verse: There was once a cedar tree in Lebanon with large, strong branches reaching to the sky.
translation_verse: Dii uwi ɔdi návi kemmo ni, kugyii kpakplaa kɔdi kúnye Lebanon kalɔ. Na kubo kɔgba kunengudi kpakplaa kɔni nálɛ kúsie kayaa ƒui.

english_verse: This tree had plenty of water to help it grow tall, and nearby streams watered the other trees in the forest.
translation_verse: Na kugyii kɔmɛni kubo ntu pii geen ɔni náya na kɔɔlɛ́ lili kaduɛ. Na ntukpa bɔni amadɔ muute lɛku kemmo egyii akladi anya ntu asa na aalɛ́ lili.

english_verse: But this tree towered over those other trees, and its branches grew long and thick.
translation_verse: Nsu kugyii kunengudi kɔmɛni aku kɔ́lɛ lili kangyaa ƒui kutulo akladi na kuna kɔgba kúbo na kúne lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Birds built nests in its branches, and animals were born beneath it. People from all nations lived in the shade of this strong tree.
translation_verse: Baasɛ bábla ayu bákya-ku kɔgba akɔ. Na bebuo bamba lɛnɔ beebo taabawɔ kuna kalɔ. Na kadi bekyuli beelie kuna ɔyuli kalɔ.

english_verse: It had beautiful, long branches, and its roots found water deep in the soil.
translation_verse: Kuna kɔgba kɔɔdia bɔnu geen na kuna ligyiitu lɛnɔ líduo lísie kalɔ kemmo ɔgyu na kɔɔkɛ́ ntu kaduɛ na lɛti lɛti lɛmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: None of the cedar trees in my garden of Eden were as beautiful as this tree; no tree of any kind had such long branches.
translation_verse: Na egyii kpakplaa ani ƒui nákya mina ɔban kemmo na Eden muedi kɔdi kuládia bɔnu lɛni. Na kugyii kɔdi udu uuubo na kuna kɔgba kúne aani kugyii kɔmɛni ɔdi.

english_verse: I, the Lord, gave this tree its beauty, and I helped the branches grow strong. All other trees in Eden wanted to be just like it.
translation_verse: Ami Unwoti nábla na kugyii kɔmɛni kɔdia bɔnu lɛni. Na ami kani mɔɔyá na kuna kɔgba kɔɔlɛ́ lili lɛni na egyii bamba ani na ɔban ɔmmɔ kemmo aakɔ́ku-ku kalɛ na anya lɛnɔ alɛ kugyii kɔmɛni.

english_verse: King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree: The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na awɔ Egyipte ɔga, se kɔtu na enu lɛla lɛni na ami Unwoti Katɔti mɔɔsu-ɔ. Kugyii kɔmmɔ kɔ́kuku ɔni na kuna kɔgba kúsie kayaa geen, anwuɔsu kɔɔkun lɛmɛnɛ na kɔɔtina lɛlɔ.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ami Unwoti Katɔti ndubo kugyii kɔmmɔ buni na liti-ku lɛkya ɔƒɔ lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔdi kalɔ na ɔni-ku kɔtu na kuna kalala ala bɔbla ɔsu.

english_verse: Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else.
translation_verse: Baƒɔ balalane badubo-ku bɔda bɔva kalɔ na kɔsɔ kɔtɛ kesii kani na kɔ́yu mmɔ kani. Na kuna kugyigba eku ku ntɛ bɔni náƒɛ-ku kɔdubo bugyingya buwi kɔbi kɔmmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ ku kɔwɛ kɔmmɔ kemmo. Na bekyuli bani ƒui na nka belie-ku ɔyuli kalɔ badubo bɔtɔlɔ busie kesii bamba.

english_verse: Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
translation_verse: Na baasɛ badubɔbla kɔkyakɔ na ugyiigba ɔmmɔ kemmo, na bebuo bamba bataanya taavi-ku kɔgba akɔ.

english_verse: Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Na kugyii kɔdi kɔsɔ kɔɔɔdubo lili bɔlɛ na kɔkuku aani kugyii kɔmɛni udu kudii ina bi ntu nkya-ku. Kugyii biala kɔdubo bukpi aani kalɛ kani na ukyuli uukpi na kuduo kalɔ kemmo na kekpine.

english_verse: On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither.
translation_verse: “ ‘Limeyi lɛni na Asiria úbo kalɔ lɛni ni, ami Unwoti Katɔti lɛ́su ntukpa bunengudi ku bubliidi ƒui na béwulo-nwu. Anwuɔsu ntukpa ku abiɔ ani nkya kalɔ kemmo ƒui áda bɔgba áya. Na Lebanon abi lɛlɔ ƒui ábla suu na átina kalɛ na kɔnyana kɔda-ma. Na lɛku kemmo egyii ƒui éwiile evete.

english_verse: This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble. The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls.
translation_verse: Kugyii kɔmɛni kɔ́ƒɛ kúwi kalɔ na kúduo kekpine. Na bekyuli ƒui bánu na lɛlɔ lɛ́tɔ-ma. Na ɔban kemmo egyii ku Lebanon egyii aƒunadi abuni ani nkya kekpine mmɔ ánu ɔmɛni na lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ-nya na kugyii kɔmɛni bukpi ɔsu.

english_verse: Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani ƒui nákɛ katamikukɔ na kuna kalɔ lɛnɔ béduo kekpine na bátáblaku-ma unwi na mmɔ.

english_verse: King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ala amɛni ƒui adubo awɔ Egyipte ɔga ku ƒula bekyuli bɔbla! Bise aani egyii amɛni, na bɛ́kuku na bibo ɔkplu lɛnɔ geen na kalɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu ɔƒaani ni, badubo-mii bɔda bɔva kalɔ aani kalɛ kani na ɔ́lɛku ɔban kemmo egyii ammɔ na ékpi. Na bɛdubo kekpine buduo na bitáblaku bani nkya kekpine mmɔ unwi. Ama bábla ulikplu na bátayia Unwoti na batábu lɛla lɛdi lɛnɔ. Anwuɔsu békpi kukpi buɛ kɔmmɔ udu. Ami Unwoti Katɔti násu.’ ”

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
translation_verse: Na akwa leevu-anyɔ kama uwi ɔni na béƒie Ɔga Yekonia ku abu bakladi bátɔlɔku bésienku Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ aani batɔntɛne kalɛ ni, Unwoti ɔ́tɛmiku-mi na kɔbuli leevu-kunyɔdi kuna limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying: You act like a lion roaming the earth; but you are nothing more than a crocodile in a river, churning up muddy water with your feet.
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, du Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga kɔtɔ na asu-nwu anii ami nnini, ‘Aabla ala aani gyata ɔni nkɛ mɔɔví kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu buse kani na ese odenge na ketu kemmo ɔni muubwile aba ntu ku nwuna lɛgba na bɔɔbla avlɔvɔ taakɔliku katɔ.

english_verse: King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore.
translation_verse: Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga, se kɔtu na enu lɛla lɛni na mɔɔsu-ɔ. Ami Unwoti Katɔti ndubo-ɔ buƒie bɔkya mina asawu kemmo na lɛya na baƒɔ lisu lɛdi bani-ɔ bebewi utuvi.

english_verse: I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh.
translation_verse: Ndubo-mii bubo butáva kalɔ kekpludi lɛlɔ na baasɛ ku bebuo babaduli bina ɔlɔna bakun.

english_verse: I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys,
translation_verse: Na lɛgyingya bina ɔlɔna ɔni ndubo buteebu mmɔ lɛkya abi ammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ ku kɔwɛ kɔmmɔ lɛnɔ kemmo.

english_verse: and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams.
translation_verse: Na bina ubugya ɔdubo bɔgba butéyile ntukpa bɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo.

english_verse: I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining.
translation_verse: Ndubo bɔya na liƒlukutu litile kayaa kammɔ ku ayabi ƒui anumi kalɛ na ɔƒɛ ku kɔbuli ƒui kɔsɔ kulekeye.

english_verse: The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Kayaa ƒui kadubo bɔbla tonwu tonwu. Na bina kalɔ kemodi kammɔ kabla suu. Ami Unwoti násu.

english_verse: Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na ɔƒɛ ɔdubo baƒɔ bani kɔku na bítenu kudii bɔda si lɛ́su-ma kalɛ na líti lɛ́kyula-mii.

english_verse: They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
translation_verse: Badubo bɔyia geen si uwi ɔni na lɛ́di-mii lɛlɔ lɛ́wɔlɔ na muuƒwimi mina kewii taavinku kayaa taatina kalɛ na líti lɛ́du-mii. Na liƒu bonwu litaada-ma na lɛlɔ lɛnɔ litaatɔ-ma ka baaagyi lɛla lɛni ndubo-ma bɔlɛku ɔsu.

english_verse: The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt!
translation_verse: “ ‘Babilon ɔga ɔdubo ubekpo awɔ Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga!

english_verse: Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed.
translation_verse: Na bekpone bani mbo kalala betulo ƒui na kayawi kamɛni kemmo ndubo babadu ƒula bekpone na bayila-mii udu ƒui ku ala ani lɛlɔ na bɛɛkun lɛmɛnɛ mmɔ.

english_verse: I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water.
translation_verse: Na lɛdu bina bebuo bani ƒui muunye ketudɔ mmɔ taadi di. Na bekyuli ku bebuo ƒui ɔdi ɔsɔ ɔɔɔdubo bubu na bataabla aba taakya ntu bɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Etudɔ mmɔ adubɔbla kpoo na ntu bɔmmɔ bɔtɛ kede kede.

english_verse: Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: “ ‘Egyipte kalɔ kadubo bubie na kasɔ katɛ ukpludi ɔni na lɛla lɛdi lɛsɔ lilakya ngba na kana kemmo. Na awɔ ku ƒula bekyuli ƒui bɛdubɔnu bɛti ka ami ndi Unwoti.’

english_verse: This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. A Sad Ending for Egypt
translation_verse: “Ɔmɛni ndi bɔlɛ kpakplaa bɔni na muute-mii. Na amu ndi ɔkwanu ɔni na badubo budie bute bina bekpine. Ami Unwoti Katɔti násu.” Egyipte Ngba Bɔ́wɔlɔ Ku Kɔnyana

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of that same month, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Kɔbuli kɔmmɔ kani limeyi lɛlɔndi ni, Unwoti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations.
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, teewulo kɔnyana na Egyipteƒuɔ ɔsu. Na adu-ma kukpi kɔtɔ na edie-ma atu na betéduo kekpine kesii kani na badubɔva ama lɛnɔ bebunku kadi bamba bekyuli bani lɛnɔ mbo ɔyikun ɔmmɔ udu.

english_verse: Say to them: You may be more beautiful than the people of other nations, but you will also die and join the godless in the world below.
translation_verse: Na asu-ma anii, ‘Bɛkana na bɛdia bitulo bekyuli bamba, nsu amii lɛnɔ bɛdubo kekpine mmɔ buduo butébunku bani ƒui naaabu Unwoti mmɔ.

english_verse: You cannot escape! The enemy's sword is ready to slaughter every one of you.
translation_verse: Bilakana ɔmɛni bukeli! Ɔsika ukisine kewii kenye kagya-mii kukuuku ka katu bina ɔdi biala kadu.

english_verse: Brave military leaders killed in battle will gladly welcome you and your allies into the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Bekpone bani na bebo kayi geen asa na bádu-ma na bakya kekpine mmɔ badubo-mii eduo bute na baƒɔ-mii ku ebiti.’

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: “Asiriaƒuɔ kɔƒiɔtɔ kɔkya mmɔ. Ama nákya bekyuli liƒu dii, nsu bádu-ma na kekpokɔ na batɛ kekpine mmɔ na kɔƒiɔtɔ kalɔ kalɔ ƒui kesii kani mɔɔyila ukyuli ɔbu biala mmɔ.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
translation_verse: “Elamƒuɔ bekpone kɔƒiɔtɔ lɛnɔ kakya mmɔ. Bekpone bani kɔƒiɔtɔ na bánu mmɔ lɛti ɔ́ya na bágyini. Nka bekpone bamɛni nákya bekyuli bɔyia geen dii na bátataayia Unwoti lɛnɔ. Ɔƒɛni amu batɛ kekpine kpoo bebunku babambadi bani lɛnɔ na bádu na kekpokɔ na bana anumi éwi kalɔ na kɔƒa kuukpó-ma.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle.
translation_verse: “Bekpone bani nási Mesek ku Tubal kɔƒiɔtɔ lɛnɔ kɔkya mmɔ. Bekyuli bamɛni ƒui bátataabu Unwoti na bákya bekyuli liƒu geen lɛnɔ, nsu békpi na kekpokɔ.

english_verse: They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
translation_verse: Na bátava-ma na bakɔliku-ma lɛnyi katɔ aani bekyuli bani nékpo na ɔma lili na báƒɔ lɛnyi kalɛ na báva-ma ku bana ekpola.

english_verse: You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
translation_verse: “Badubo amii Egyipteƒuɔ lɛlɔ bɔdi buɛ buɛ na badubo amii lɛnɔ bava bubunku bekyuli bani nékpi na kekpokɔ na udu ɔmɛni kemmo.

english_verse: The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: “Edomƒuɔ baga ku bana batɔnkune kɔƒiɔtɔ kɔkya mmɔ. Bekyuli bamɛni lɛnɔ bákɛ ɔyikun dii úbavi. Na ɔƒaani ni, batɛ kekpine bebunku bekpone babambadi bani lɛnɔ nátaabu Unwoti na békpi na kekpokɔ.

english_verse: The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: “Batɔnkune bani nási kalɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ ku Sidonƒuɔ ƒui kɔƒiɔtɔ kɔkya mmɔ. Bana bekpone kpakplaa bani nákya bádi liƒu lɛla béte bana bekisine dii, nsu ɔƒɛni amu batɛ kekpine ku kɔƒa bebunku bani na bádu na kekpokɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: The Lord God says: When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering.
translation_verse: “Unwoti Katɔti ɔnii si bina Egyipteƒuɔ ɔga ɔ́nu kɔƒiɔtɔ kɔmɛni ni, kubiti kɔdubɔda anwu ku nwuna bekpone ka ɔɔɔdi ama lɛti muubó abi amɛni udu.

english_verse: I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ami nátala-nwu nnii usie na utákya kayawi ƒui liƒu, nsu anwu ku nwuna bekpone ƒui badubo bukpi na bava ama lɛnɔ bebunku bani ƒui na balayia Unwoti na batɛ kekpine mmɔ. Ami Unwoti Katɔti násu.”

english_verse: and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming.
translation_verse: Na ute-ma bɔti si uwi ɔni na ɔ́nu ka ɔgbankpi ɔdi ɔdubo na bana bekisine ɔsu na ɔlɛ-ma lɛƒiɔ.

english_verse: Their past sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they have done right.
translation_verse: Ndubuti alaekpidi ani ƒui na bábla bábavi lɛkyiɛ-ma. Na ka bábla lɛbuni ɔsu ni, badubulie ngba.

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
translation_verse: Na akwa leevu-anyɔ kama uwi ɔni na béƒie Ɔga Yekonia ku abu bakladi aani batɔntɛne kalɛ bésienku Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, bekyuli bani muukeli kekpo akɔ unwi ɔ́si Yerusalem úbo-mi kudɔ na kɔbuli leevudi limeyi lɛlɔndi lɛlɔ. Úbasu-mi ka Yerusalem úbuli.

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying: Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, tɛmiku ƒula bekyuli kpakplaa na asu-ma anini, ‘Ɔkana na ubo ute ka ami Unwoti lɛ́tala bekisine badi limeyi lɛdi ka bebekpo kalɔ kadi. Na kadi bekyuli bammɔ lɛnɔ báƒuna ukyuli ɔdi banii unye-ma kagyumana na utaanu ala taasu-ma.

english_verse: If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
translation_verse: Si banii ukyuli ɔmmɔ úte bekyuli bamɛni bɔti na béni na bátadi-mu lɛlɔ ni, badubo-ma bɔdu na kekpokɔ. Nsu ɔdi ama alati bɔƒiɔ, ɔsika nka bakana na bekeli ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ si bunu na nka bénu bɔlɛ bɔmmɔ.

english_verse: But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Nsu si ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnu ala taasu-ma mmɔ lɛnɔ néni na útete-ma bɔti ni, bekisine badubo bebekpo na badu alaekpidi bablane badi na kalɔ kammɔ kemmo, na ami Unwoti ndubuti bekyuli bammɔ kukpi etila lɛsia ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.’

english_verse: Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me.
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ami náƒuna-a nnii enye Israel kadi bekyuli kagyumana na ataanu ala taasu-ma. Anwuɔsu nu lɛla lɛni mɔɔsu-ɔ kaduɛ na alɛ-ma kpakplaa ete-mi.

english_verse: When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Si lɛ́su balalane nnii badubo bukpi na bana ekpidi ɔsu ni, ɔlɛka atɛmiku-ma kpakplaa anii benwini kama bakya bana ekpidi. Nsu si ébulo na átasu-ma ɔmɛni ni, bana kukpi kɔsia-a lili.

english_verse: If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent. The Lord Is Always Fair (Ezekiel
translation_verse: Na si álɛ-ma kpakplaa na ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na bámu benye ekpidi ammɔ bɔbla lɛlɔ ni, badubo bukpi na bana ekpidi ɔsu, nsu awɔ édie lɛlɔ na lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-a.”

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Si bekyuli babuni bése kalɔ baabla alaekpidi ni, badubo bukpi na ekpidi ammɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.”
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, bekyuli bani nkya-a kudɔ na Babilon mmɔ ni, baatɛmi-ɔ lɛlɔ kɔtɛ si bása na ɔma ɔmmɔ awodu ani bátu bámana-nwu kudɔ iye bana lɛtɔ kɔyakun. Na baasu banini, ‘Bɛya na buye Esekiel bunu lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ubo ute-bu ɔmwi.’

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, Israelƒuɔ bakya baakya unyeƒi banii bana ekpidi ani na bábla kɔtu kɔni na ɔlɛka lɛni-ma ni, kútulo-ma buti. Na basɔ beeebo lɛnunsia lɛdi ka badubɔsɔ bakana ngba bulie lɛnɔ. Na ami mmomu na baadú kɔtɔ.

english_verse: Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
translation_verse: Su-ma anii kede kede nwaa ni, ami Unwoti Katɔti ɔni na nli ngba uwi ƒui mɛni ni, naaawia ukyuli ukpidi kukpi. Mmomu lɛlɔ mɔɔyɔ́-mi ka lɛnu ka ɔvumana udu na ɔ́da likpidi bɔbla ɔ́ya. Anwuɔsu si Israelƒuɔ baayɔ́ ka belie ngba bɔdi ni, ɔlɛka bada ekpidi bɔbla baya na benwini bebo-mi kudɔ.

english_verse: Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
translation_verse: “Na asu-ma anii si ukyuli ɔbuni use kalɔ ku likpidi bɔbla ni, ala abuni ani ƒui na ɔ́ɔbla úbavi alakana-nwu bɔƒɔ na ulákɛ kɔtu bɔni. Na aya na bati anii lɛni kani na si ukyuli ukpidi ɔ́da alaekpidi bɔbla ɔ́ya na ɔɔbla lɛbuni ni, ndubuti alaekpidi ani ƒui na ɔ́bla úbavi lɛkyiɛ-nwu kede kede. Na nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo-nwu kɔtu bɔni.

english_verse: Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
translation_verse: “Biti-nwu bɛnii líse bekyuli babuni kenye ka ndubɔya na belie ngba na ɔmmɔ kama na bése kalɔ baabla alaekpidi na bebo lɛnunsia ka lɛbuni lɛni na bábla bábavi ɔsu ni, badubɔkɛ bɔƒɔ. Mɔɔsu-mii nwaa ka ɔ́bla bi ɔ́bla dɛ ni, bekyuli bamɛni badubo bukpi na bana ekpidi ɔsu. Na bekyuli bayiƒala lɛbuni lɛni na bábla bábavi.

english_verse: Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right.
translation_verse: “Biti-nwu bɛnii líbo balalane ɔda ka badubo bukpi na bana ekpidi ani na baabla ɔsu na báda-nya bɔbla báya na baabla lɛbuni.

english_verse: For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live.
translation_verse: Bɛya buti-nwu bɔnii bánu báti ka basɔku ala ani na báƒɔ bekyuli kudɔ bényene kama na lɛla lɛni na bévo básiku-ma kudɔ ɔsu béte balati iye básɔku bekyuli ala ani na béyu bétése balati. Ɔmmɔ kama báda udunkpi biala báya na baadi mina litemi lɛlɔ na baabla lɛbuni ni, badubulie ngba.

english_verse: Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair.
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ƒula kadi bekyuli baadú-mi kɔtɔ ka naaabla ala teete-ma ulu lɛlɔ. Nsu ama mmomu naaabla ala ulu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Na si bekyuli bekpidi bése kalɔ baabla lɛbuni ni, badubɔƒɔ bana ngba balɛku kɔtu bɔni kemmo.

english_verse: But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done. The News of Jerusalem's Fall
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui kama ni, Israelƒuɔ ama baanu ka ami naaabla ala teete-ma na ulu lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu su-ma kpakplaa anii ndubo-ma kɔtu bɔni na bana ekpidi ani na bábla ɔsu.” Básu Ka Yerusalem Ɔdubo Bubuli

english_verse: The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak. What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛni useyi uwi asa na ukyuli ɔmɛni ɔdububo-mi kudɔ ni, Unwoti ɔyikun ɔ́ƒɔ-mi lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui. Anwuɔsu asa na kadi keteegye uwi ɔni na ɔnana ɔmɛni úubo ɔkya ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na lɛ́sɔ lɛ́kana na mɔɔtɛmi taasu nwuna ala. Israelƒuɔ Béye Lɛla Lɛni Ndubɔlɛku Bekyuli Bani Nébu Na Israel

english_verse: Then the Lord said:
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́su ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, bekyuli bani nébu bakya lɛma lɛni bábwɛ na Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ beeye banini, ‘Ukyuli unwi kani na Abraham ɔdi asa na Unwoti úti Israel kalɔ kamɛni ƒui úte-nwu. Na abu bumomo, anwuɔsu ɔlɛka kalɔ kammɔ kenwini abu kadi.’

english_verse: So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying: How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu ni, Esekiel, su-ma anii ami nnini, ‘Bi ɔsu na bɛɛkali ka kalɔ kamu kadi amii kadi ka bɛɛkun lɛna lɛni kemmo na ubugya ɔmu ɔkya na bɛɛkpá baƒiɔ na bɛɛdú bekyuli?

english_verse: and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
translation_verse: Na kalala ala bɔbla bɔ́ƒɔ kalɔ kammɔ ƒui kemmo na bagya ku bele baalɛ́ lɛlɔ kama muedi. Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui kama biitú kɔnu kayi bɛnii kalɔ kammɔ kadi amii kadi!

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na ɔni na ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti na nli ngba uwi ƒui mɛni ni, amii bani nébu bɛkya lɛma lɛni na bábwɛ kemmo mɛni ni, bɛdubo bukpi na kekpokɔ. Na amii bani nkya akpaklɔ ni, beƒiebuo badubo-mii buƒie. Na bani nábɛ bakya atakpɛ libu kemmo ku bani nli atakpɛ eli ƒui ni, ɔlɛ buɛ ndubo-mii bɔdu.

english_verse: I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them.
translation_verse: Ndubo bɔya na lɛla biala lɛyii udu na kalɔ kammɔ ƒui kemmo ka kalɔ kammɔ kasɔ kewi ukpludi na libile ɔyikun ɔni na bɛɛnu ka bibo ɔsu na bɛɛkun lɛmɛnɛ. Abi lɛlɔ muedi livo lilenye na ɔdi ulabla kasusu ɔnii ɔɔsia mmɔ ɔlɛ usie kesii kadi.

english_verse: I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord. The People Listen, but Don't Change The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ndubo-mii kɔtu bɔni na bina ekpidi ani na bɛɛbla ɔsu, na lɛya bina kalɔ kammɔ ƒui kenweni kalɔ kakwiidi kani nsɔ naaadia lɛla lɛdi. Na mmɔ na bɛdubɔnu bɛti ka ami ndi Unwoti.’ Israelƒuɔ Beenú Nsu Balavumana Udu

english_verse: So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bana ƒui beebo teebenu lɛla lɛni na adubɔsu, nsu béni na balabla taasiaku kalɛ na ásu-ma. Ama baasu ka basiaku-mi kama siin, nsu baanya bana bakpana taakya na beeyu bana egulabi.

english_verse: They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
translation_verse: Bɔnu kani na baanu-ɔ aani ukyuli ɔni muudie bɔyɔ lɛnu taagya ala. Na beenú, nsu balabla lɛla lɛla taasiaku lɛla lɛni na aasu-ma lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
translation_verse: “Na uwi ɔsɔ uletu asa na ndubo-ma kɔtɔ bɔni aani kalɛ na ásu-ma ése, na badubɔnu bati ka kenye udiene ɔdi ɔ́kya-ma akɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them: I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep.
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, Israel batɔnkune bese aani baƒonu badane bani mɔɔnu mina baƒonu bani ndi Israel kadi bekyuli lɛlɔ. Nsu mɔɔwia ka lɛdu bɔtɔnkune bamɛni kɔtɔ na lɛsu-ma nnini, ‘Ami Unwoti Katɔti mɔɔsu amii Israel baƒonu badane nnii bɛdubo udu bɔyii na amii ɔdi ɔsa! Bɛɛnu amii alati lɛlɔ na bíni mina baƒonu lɛlɔ bɔnu.

english_verse: You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock!
translation_verse: Bɛɛní bana anyi ntu na biiti bana linwini teedi adi teete lɛlɔ. Na bɛɛdú babuni bani nélie lɛmwi taakun, nsu bíni na bilanu baƒonu lisu lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ!

english_verse: You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep.
translation_verse: Bíni bani nse kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ bɔgyumana na bɛbwi bani muuƒi iye binyimi-ma lɛlɛ lɛni na báƒɔ. Biidie-ma atu na baakɛ taavi kalɛ kalɛ na bilasia bani náyii ulu kama. Bɛɛbla-ma ulikplu na bɛɛɛdaku-ma lɛda.

english_verse: They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals.
translation_verse: Báyii ulu bakɛ kesi kesii na ka bátakɛ ɔdane ɔdi ɔsu ni, beƒiebuo békpoku-ma na béƒie-ma taakun.

english_verse: So my sheep were scattered across the earth. They roamed on hills and mountains, without anyone even bothering to look for them.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu mina baƒonu bégyingya bakya kalɔ lɛlɔ kesii biala. Bakɛ abi lɛlɔ ku abinkpo ƒui lɛlɔ na bátakɛ ukyuli ɔni nawia-ma kama ulu.

english_verse: Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na ɔƒaani ni, binu lɛla lɛni na ami Unwoti Katɔti mɔɔsu amii baƒonu badane bammɔ. Beƒiebuo békpoku mina baƒonu na béƒie-ma bákun, ɔsika bíni-ma lɛlɔ bɔnu. Na bítatásia bani na báyii lɛnɔ kama kudii. Na amii bɛɛdi teemo, nsu bítete mina baƒonu ama adila.

english_verse: So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ami Unwoti ndubo-mii kɔtu bɔni! Na likpo lɛƒɔ-ma ƒui na bina enu kemmo, na nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo bɔya na bɛbla bana badane ɔƒaamu iye bɛdu ɔdi lɛnɔ bɛkun. Ami Unwoti násu.’ ” Unwoti Ndi Baƒonu Ɔdane Buni

english_verse: The Lord God then said: I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Unwoti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “ ‘Ndubo mina baƒonu kama bɔsia na ami ɔlati lɛnu-ma lɛlɔ

english_verse: just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them
translation_verse: aani kalɛ na baƒonu ɔdane ɔɔsia baƒonu bani náyii kama. Ɔ́si kɔnyana limeyi suu lɛni kani na bégyingya-ma bákya kalɔ lɛlɔ kadi bekyuli akɔ ni, uwi ɔmmɔ kani lɛlɔ na mina baƒonu báyii. Nsu ndubo bukpo bɔƒɔ-ma ƒui

english_verse: and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields.
translation_verse: na lɛkpanku-ma lɛsiku baƒɔ kɔlɔ kɔni lɛlɔ na bégyingya bakya ƒui lɛsɔku liboku. Ami ndubɔbla bana ɔdane na lɛya na badi na Israelƒuɔ abi ku awɛ kemmo kesii kani na kadi kalɔ kabuni lɛlɔ.

english_verse: They will be safe as they feed on grassy meadows and green hills.
translation_verse: Badubo bɔdi bɔvi ƒaa na lɛla lɛdi lilékpoku-ma na kesii kani na kadi adila abuni kakyakɔ.

english_verse: I promise to take care of them and keep them safe,
translation_verse: Líse kenye ka ndubo-ma lɛlɔ bɔnu na lɛda-ma kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english_verse: to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right. Judgment on the Strong Sheep
translation_verse: Na ndubɔsia bani náyii ku bani négyingya bakya lɛnɔ kama na linyimi bani náƒɔ lɛlɔ alɛbi na bani lɛgyumana bani nse kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ. Na bani nélie lɛmwi na bebo ɔlɔkplu ni, ndubɔdu ama, ɔsika lɛla lɛni ndi lɛbuni na mɔɔbla uwi biala.’ ” Katɔti Ɔdubɔdu Bekyuli Bekpidi Kɔtɔ

english_verse: The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel: I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak.
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su Israelƒuɔ bani nse aani nwuna baƒonu ɔnini, “Ndubo-mii anu bɔsia geen unwi unwi na lɛnu bani ndi baƒonu bani mbo ɔlɔkplu ku bani nse kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: Some of you eat the greenest grass, then trample down what's left when you finish. Others drink clean water, then step in the water to make the rest of it muddy.
translation_verse: Bina badi bɛɛkun livo lɛbuni geen na bɛɛnya taavi lɛkladi lɛlɔ si uwi ɔni na bɛ́wɔlɔ. Na bina badi bɛɛní ntu bɔbuni, na si bɛ́wɔlɔ na bɛkya bɔkladi lɛgba na bɔbla aba aba.

english_verse: That means my other sheep have nothing fit to eat or drink.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ ɔɔtina ka mina baƒonu bakladi ama balakɛ ntu bɔbuni taani.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will separate you strong sheep from the weak.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu ami Unwoti Katɔti ndubo-mii kemmo bule na bani mbo ɔlɔkplu bakya bunwu, na bani nse kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ lɛnɔ bakya bunwu.

english_verse: You strong ones have used your powerful horns to chase off those that are weak,
translation_verse: Ɔsika amii bani lɛlɔ mbo ɔkplu bɛɛtu bani nse kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ku bina ese kpakplaa kalɛ na adila edu amii lɛti.

english_verse: but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
translation_verse: Nsu ndubo bukpo bɔƒɔ-ma ƒui kalɛ na bilátaabla-ma lɛla lɛni naaadia. Na ndubɔƒuna-ma lɛsiku-mii kudɔ na lɛdu-mii kɔtɔ.

english_verse: After that, I will give you a shepherd from the family of my servant King David. All of you, both strong and weak, will have the same shepherd, and he will take good care of you.
translation_verse: “Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, ndubute-mii baƒonu ɔdane buni ɔni ndubɔsi mina kabla ɔblane ɔni ndi Ɔga Dawid ɔtɔ kemmo na bina ƒui bani mbo ɔlɔkplu ku bani na bese kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ƒui bakɛ ɔdane unwi pɛ na ɔnu-mii lɛlɔ kaduɛ.

english_verse: He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Anwu ndubɔbla bina ɔtɔnkune na ami lɛbla bina Katɔti. Ami Unwoti násu. Uwi Ɔbuni Ɔdubo Ute Unwoti Baƒonu

english_verse: The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace. I will chase away every wild animal from the desert and the forest, so my sheep will not be afraid.
translation_verse: “Israel kadi bekyuli ndi mina baƒonu. Na líse kenye kpakplaa ka badubuli na atu bɔyɔ kemmo. Na ndubo eƒiebuo biala bɔbɔku bɔtɔlɔku kalɔ kakwiidi ku lɛku lɛmmɔ kemmo na basɔ baaadubo bɔyia.

english_verse: They will live around my holy mountain, and I will bless them by sending more than enough rain
translation_verse: Badubulie bamana mina kɔbi kedee lɛlɔ. Na ndubo-ma kusɛ kusɛ bute na ɔnantu ɔna ute-ma utulo kalɛ na baawia muedi.

english_verse: to make their trees produce fruit and their crops to grow. I will set them free from slavery and let them live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Na bana adingyii adubo bɔnwu kaduɛ na edula lɛnɔ adia-ma. Ndubo bɔya na bakɛ bɔnwuna ƒaa na belie bana kalɔ lɛlɔ ku atu bɔyɔ na basɔ balabla ukyuli bamba kabla. Na badubɔnu bati ka ami ndi Unwoti.

english_verse: Foreign nations will never again rob them, and wild animals will no longer kill and eat them. They will have nothing to fear.
translation_verse: Kadi bamba bekyuli basɔ baaadubo-ma buyu. Na beƒiebuo lɛnɔ basɔ beleƒie-ma balakun. Na basɔ baaadubo lɛla lɛdi lɛnɔ bɔyia.

english_verse: I will make their fields produce large amounts of crops, so they will never again go hungry or be laughed at by foreigners.
translation_verse: Ndubo bɔya na baƒɛ edula abuni geen balɛku bana mmo kalɛ na kɔka kɔsɔ kulada-ma iye baƒɔ bani na bana adɔ basɔ baláma-ma.

english_verse: Then everyone will know that I protect my people Israel. I, the Lord, make this promise.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala ɔdubɔnu ka mɔɔgyumana mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ. Ami Unwoti nése kenye kamɛni.

english_verse: They are my sheep; I am their God, and I take care of them.
translation_verse: Mina baƒonu na badi na ami ndi bana Katɔti. Na mɔɔnu-ma lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Edom
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, du Edom kadi bekyuli kukpi kɔtɔ

english_verse: and say to them: I, the Lord God, am now your enemy! And I will turn your nation into an empty wasteland,
translation_verse: na asu-ma anini, ‘Ami Unwoti Katɔti ɔƒɛni amu línwini-mii ukisine! Na ndububo bina kalɔ bunwini bɔbla kalɔ kebiedi kani kemmo na lɛla lɛdi lɛsɔ lilakya.

english_verse: leaving your towns in ruins. Your land will be a desert, and then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Na bina lɛma lɛbwɛ liwi ukpludi na mmɔ kenwini kalɔ kakwiidi. Na bɛdubɔnu bɛti ka ami ndi Unwoti.

english_verse: People of Edom, not only have you been Israel's longtime enemy, you simply watched when disaster wiped out its people as punishment for their sins.
translation_verse: “ ‘Amii Edom kadi bekyuli ni, ɔɔɔdi bekisine kani na bɛdi bite Israelƒuɔ ɔ́si kukuuku, mmomu lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ-mii na bínye bɛ́nu uwi ɔni na ɔgbankpi úbo-ma lɛlɔ na baadú-ma ƒui ku kuwii teewi kalɔ aani bana lɛtuni na ekpidi ani na bábla ɔsu.

english_verse: And so, as surely as I am the living Lord God, you are guilty of murder and must be put to death.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu geen ni, muudie-mii bɔƒiɔ ka bɛ́du ukyuli na ɔlɛka badu amii lɛnɔ.
