english_verse: I will destroy your nation and kill anyone who travels through it.
translation_verse: Ndubo bina kalɔ bubile na kayii udu na badu ukyuli biala ɔni masia-ka kemmo lɛnɔ malɛ.

english_verse: Dead bodies will cover your mountains and fill up your valleys,
translation_verse: Bekpine badubɔƒɔ bina abi lɛlɔ ku awɛ kemmo ƒui tɛɛ.

english_verse: and your land will lie in ruins forever. No one will live in your towns ever again. You will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Na bina kɔlɔ kɔdubɔsɔ kuwi ukpludi uwi ƒui. Na ukyuli biala ɔdi usɔ ulakya bina lɛma lɛmmɔ kemmo kudii. Na bɛdubɔnu bɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti.

english_verse: You thought the nations of Judah and Israel belonged to you, and that you could take over their territory. But I am their God,
translation_verse: “ ‘Bɛ́bu bɛnii Yuda ku Israel kadi bekyuli kɔlɔ kúnwini amii kɔdi na bɛkana biti bana kɔlɛkɛ kɔmmɔ binwini amii ɔdi uwi biala kemmo. Nsu ami ndi bana Katɔti.

english_verse: and as surely as I live, I will punish you for treating my people with anger and hatred. Then they will know that I, the Lord, am punishing you!
translation_verse: Na mɔɔsu-mii geen nnii ɔni na nli uwi ƒui mɛni ni, ndubɔnu ka lɛ́ni-mii kɔtu na kalɛ na bɛ́bla-ma na kɔnyi kemmo na bíkisi-ma lɛnɔ ɔsu. Na badubɔnu ka ami mɔɔní-mii kɔtu lɛni.

english_verse: And you will finally realize that I heard you laugh at their destruction and say their land was yours to take.
translation_verse: Na amii alati bɛdubo bɔnu bɔti ka línu kalɛ na binye bɛɛlɛ́-ma uwi ɔni na bana ɔgbankpi úbo-ma lɛlɔ na bɛɛsu ka bana kɔlɔ kɔdubunwini amii kɔdi na biti-ku.

english_verse: You even insulted me, but I heard it all.
translation_verse: Na bidumi ami ɔlati muedi na línu ɔnaƒui kede kede.

english_verse: Everyone on earth will celebrate when I destroy you,
translation_verse: “ ‘Lɛlɔ lɛdubo ukyuli biala bɔyɔ si uwi ɔni na lɛ́yila-mii udu lɛ́wɔlɔ

english_verse: just as you celebrated when Israel was destroyed. Your nation of Edom will be nothing but a wasteland. Then everyone will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: kalɛ kani na lɛlɔ lɛ́yɔ-mii uwi ɔni na báyila Israel udu. Na bina Edom kalɔ ƒui kadubo bubie na kasɔ kewi ukpludi lɛla biala tadia tadia. Na ukyuli biala ɔdubɔnu ɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the mountains of Israel
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, kɔ lɛsa te Israel abi lɛlɔ badi ƒui anii

english_verse: that I, the Lord God, am saying: Your enemies sneered and said that you mountains belonged to them.
translation_verse: ami Unwoti Katɔti mɔɔsu-ma nnini, ‘Ƒula bekisine bápii-ɔ, na básu ka ƒula abi ammɔ ƒui adi ama adi.

english_verse: They ruined and crushed you from every side, and foreign nations captured and made fun of you.
translation_verse: Bébile-mii na békpo-mii bádi-mii lɛlɔ ɔ́si lɛƒɛnyi ƒui lɛlɔ. Na kadi bamba bekyuli bani ndi baƒɔ béƒie-mii na baamá-mii.

english_verse: So all you mountains and hills, streams and valleys, listen to what I will do. Your towns may now lie in ruins, and nations may laugh and insult you.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu amii abi ammɔ ƒui ku abinkpo ku ntukpa ku awɛ ammɔ ƒui, binu lɛla lɛni na ndubo bɔbla. Bekyuli bakana na bataama amii lɛma lɛni nabwɛ liwi ukpludi ɔƒɛni na beteedumi-mii.

english_verse: But in my fierce anger, I will turn against those nations, and especially the Edomites, because they laughed at you the loudest and took over your pasturelands.
translation_verse: Nsu ndubo kadi bekyuli bammɔ lɛlɔ bɔta bunye ku kɔnyi kpakplaa geen, na bani ɔdi ntulo ndi Edomƒuɔ, ɔsika ama náma-mii bétulo ƒui na báda-mii bebuo kadikɔ kɔlɔ lɛnɔ béti.

english_verse: You have suffered long enough, and, I, the Lord God, am very angry! Nations have insulted you,
translation_verse: Bíibo abi na uwi útu geen na ami Unwoti Katɔti lɛ́kɛ kɔnyi geen! Na kadi bamba bekyuli lɛnɔ bédumi-mii.

english_verse: so I will now insult and disgrace them. That is my solemn promise.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ami lɛnɔ líse kenye kpakplaa ka ndubo-ma budu-mi na lɛkya-ma kɔƒa.

english_verse: Trees will grow on you mountains of Israel and produce fruit for my people, because they will soon come home.
translation_verse: “ ‘Egyii adubɔkwɛ abi ammɔ lɛlɔ na anwu ebi kaduɛ ete mina kadi bekyuli na bakɛ badi, ɔsika badubo ɔma uwi klukwii kemmo.

english_verse: I will take care of you by plowing your soil and planting crops on your fertile slopes.
translation_verse: Ndubo bɔya na bɛtu kalɔ kabuni kani nwi káyu abi ɔkwalɛ mmɔ binwini ƒui na bɛkya edula na liti lɛnu-mii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The people of Israel will return and rebuild your ruined towns and live in them.
translation_verse: Israel kadi bekyuli badubɔsɔ benwini bebo na bɛsɔku bina lɛma lɛni nábwɛ bɛda na bilie-mi kemmo.

english_verse: Children will be born, and animals will give birth to their young. You will no longer be deserted as you are now, but you will be covered with people and treated better than ever. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Bɛdubɔwɔ bebi na bina bebuo lɛnɔ bawɔ. Na nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo-mii atu budie aani kalɛ na use ɔƒɛni. Mmomu bɛdubo bumomo geen na lɛda-mii kaduɛ litulo kudeedi ƒui na bɛnu bɛti ka ami ndi Unwoti.

english_verse: I will bring my people Israel home, and they will live on you mountains, because you belong to them, and your fertile slopes will never again let them starve.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ndubɔkpanku mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ liboku ɔma na bebelie bana abi ani ndi bana adi lɛlɔ. Na badubɔtuma na kɔlɔ kɔbuni kɔni néti kɔ́yu ɔkwalɛ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ, na kɔka kɔsɔ kuládu-ma kudii.

english_verse: It's true that you have been accused of not producing enough food and of letting your people starve.
translation_verse: Sɔsɔ na ɔdi ka Israelƒuɔ baakya unyeƒi taasu ka adila aladia-mii lɛlɔ na kɔka kɔɔdú-ma na beekpi.

english_verse: But I, the Lord, promise that you won't hear other nations laugh and sneer at you ever again. From now on, you will always produce plenty of food for your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Lord Will Be Honored
translation_verse: Nsu ami Unwoti muusé kenye ka adila adubɔdia na amii abi amɛni lɛlɔ ɔƒaamu ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela uwi ƒui. Na kadi bamba bekyuli akɔ ɔdi ɔsɔ ulasu ulásiku-mii lɛlɔ ɔnii biládia adila na bataapii taama. Mmomu bɛdubo adila butaadia geen na Israel kadi bekyuli bakɛ-nya adila pii geen. Ami Unwoti Katɔti násu.’ ” Bekyuli Badubo Unwoti Bɔbu

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, when the people of Israel were living in their own country, they made the land unclean by the way they behaved, just as a woman's monthly period makes her unclean.
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ beli ama alati kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, bébile kalɔ kammɔ ekisila na kasɔ keeese sɛɛn na bana ala ɔbladu ɔsu kalɛ kani na si uleku ɔ́lɛ ɔtɔ na uubile ekisila pii na ɔsɔ uuuse sɛɛn kalɛ.

english_verse: They committed murders and worshiped idols, which made the land even worse. So in my anger, I punished my people
translation_verse: Bádu bekyuli na bákpa baƒiɔ na ɔ́ya na kalɔ kammɔ kásɔ kébie kétulo ƒui. Anwuɔsu líti kɔnyi geen na lɛ́ni mina kadi bekyuli kɔtu,

english_verse: and scattered them throughout the nations, just as they deserved.
translation_verse: na lɛ́ya na bégyingya bakya kadi bamba bekyuli kɔlɔ ƒui lɛlɔ kalɛ kani na ɔ́manku ka lɛbla-ma.

english_verse: Wherever they went, my name was disgraced, because foreigners insulted my people by saying I had forced them out of their own land.
translation_verse: Kesi kesii na bakɛ ni, mina lɛnyi kani na baakya kɔƒa. Ɔsika baƒɔ bani na badi kadi bamba bekyuli beedumi-ma taasu ka ami nábɔku mina kadi bekyuli lɛ́lɛku bana kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I care what those foreigners think of me,
translation_verse: “Mɔɔbla kasusu na ala ani na baƒɔ bammɔ baasu taasiku-mi lɛlɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: so tell the Israelites that I am saying: You have disgraced my holy name among the nations where you now live. So you don't deserve what I'm going to do for you. I will lead you home to bring honor to my name
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu su Israelƒuɔ lɛla lɛni na mɔɔsu-ɔ mɛni anini, ‘Bɛ́kya-mi lɛnyi lɛni muukeye kɔƒa na kadi bamba bekyuli bani akɔ na bili mɛni akɔ. Anwuɔsu bítamanku lɛla lɛni na mɔɔwia ka lɛbla lite-mii mɛni munu munu. Ndubo-mii bɔkpanku busienku ɔma na bekyuli babu-mi lɛnyi.

english_verse: and to show foreign nations that I am holy. Then they will know that I am the Lord God. I have spoken.
translation_verse: Na kadi bamba bekyuli banu kalɛ na mina lɛnyi liikeye. Na bɛnu bɛti ka ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti. Ami násu.

english_verse: I will gather you from the foreign nations and bring you home.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ndubo-mii bɔkpanku bɔsiku kadi bamba bekyuli akɔ na lɛsala-mii liboku bina ɔma.

english_verse: I will sprinkle you with clean water, and you will be clean and acceptable to me. I will wash away everything that makes you unclean, and I will remove your disgusting idols.
translation_verse: Ndubo ntu bɔni nse sɛɛn bɔkuna buwi-mii lɛlɔ na bina lɛlɔ lɛbla sɛɛn na lɛƒɔ-mii. Ndubo-mii ntu bɔkpila na bɛlɛ sɛɛn bɛsiku lɛla biala náya na biisé lɛlɔ kudɔ ku baƒiɔ ala anu ƒui muusé lɛlɔ mmɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: I will take away your stubborn heart and give you a new heart and a desire to be faithful. You will have only pure thoughts,
translation_verse: Ndubɔda bina kayi kani neeenu litemi mmɔ lidie-mii lɛlɔ kemmo na lite-mii kayi kawɔdi ku udu ɔni mɔɔtina ka bɛsɔ bilálɛ-mi kama. Na kasusu kabuni sɔɔn na bɛdubo buteeti ɔƒaamu.

english_verse: because I will put my Spirit in you and make you eager to obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ɔsika ndubuti mina kɔyu lite-mii na lɛya na mina litemi lɛlɔ bɔdi ku ala ani mɔɔtina-mii kama bɔsia kɔka kutaada-mii.

english_verse: You will once again live in the land I gave your ancestors; you will be my people, and I will be your God.
translation_verse: Na bɛdubɔsɔ binwini bibelie ɔmii ɔni na líte bina bati lɛlɔ na binwini mina kadi bekyuli na ami lɛbla bina Katɔti.

english_verse: I will protect you from anything that makes you unclean. Your fields will overflow with grain, and no one will starve.
translation_verse: Na ndubo-mii bɔgyumana bɔsiku ala ani ƒui mɔɔyá na biisé lɛlɔ kudɔ. Na bina mmo bɔdubɔdi edula pii na kɔka kɔsɔ kuládu ɔdi.

english_verse: Your trees will be filled with fruit, and crops will grow in your fields, so that you will never again feel ashamed for not having enough food.
translation_verse: Bina adingyii adubɔnwu ebi pii na bina edula ani na bɛ́kya lɛnɔ adia geen, na kɔƒa kɔsɔ kɔɔɔdubo-mii bukpo kudii ka biiibo adila ani bɛdi ɔsu.

english_verse: You will remember your evil ways and hate yourselves for what you've done.
translation_verse: Bɛdubo bina ngba bukpidi bɔni na bílie bíbavi bunyimo na kɔƒa kukpo-mii geen na ala ani na bɛ́bla lɛlɔ.

english_verse: People of Israel, I'm not doing these things for your sake. You sinned against me, and you must suffer shame and disgrace for what you have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Israel kadi bekyuli, ɔɔɔdi amii ɔsu na mɔɔbla ala amɛni, ɔsika bɛ́bla alaekpidi bítuloku lɛlɔ. Na ɔlɛka nka bina anumi ewi kalɔ na kɔƒa kukpo-mii lɛnɔ geen na ala ani na bɛ́bla ɔsu. Ami Unwoti násu.’

english_verse: After I have made you clean, I will let you rebuild your ruined towns and let you live in them.
translation_verse: “Na su-ma anini, ‘Uwi ɔni na lɛ́bla-mii sɛɛn lɛ́wɔlɔ ni, ndubɔya na bɛsɔku bina lɛma lɛni nábwɛ bɛtu na bilie-ni kemmo.

english_verse: Your land will be plowed again, and nobody will be able to see that it was once barren.
translation_verse: Bɛsɔ bɛdubo bina kalɔ bɔtuma na ɔdi ulakana bɔnu bɔti ka nka kébie dii na kasɔ kaládi lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: Instead, they will say that it looks as beautiful as the garden of Eden. They won't see towns lying in ruins, but they will see your strong cities filled with people.
translation_verse: Mmomu bɔsu na badubo banii kaadia bɔnu aani kalɛ na Eden ɔban kemmo kése dii. Na bekyuli balanu ka lɛma lɛmmɔ lɛ́bwɛ liwi, mmomu badubɔnu lɛma lɛni bátu bényene kpakplaa na bekyuli báƒɔ-mi kemmo tɛɛ.

english_verse: Then the nearby nations that survive will know that I am the one who rebuilt the ruined places and replanted the barren fields. I, the Lord, make this promise.
translation_verse: Na kadi bamba bekyuli bani nébu beli na bina amadɔ badubɔnu ka ami násɔku lɛma lɛmmɔ lɛ́tu na lɛ́sɔku mmo bɔni nébie na buládia lɛla lɛdi mmɔ lɛnɔ lɛ́bla bɔwɔdi na bɔɔdia edula. Ami Unwoti nése kenye kamɛni.

english_verse: I will once again answer your prayers, and I will let your nation grow until you are like a large flock of sheep.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ndubɔsɔ linu-mii bɔkpali ɔƒaamu na lɛbla lɛla lɛni na bɛdubuvele-mi lite-mii na bina kadi bekyuli basɔ bemomo aani baƒonu lisu bonwu kalɛ.

english_verse: The towns that now lie in ruins will be filled with people, just as Jerusalem was once filled with sheep to be offered as sacrifices during a festival. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Na lɛma lɛni ƒui náyii udu na lɛ́bwɛ liwi kalɔ ɔƒɛni ni, bekyuli badubɔƒɔ-ni kemmo aani kalɛ na Yerusalem úse dii uwi ɔni na bebuo báƒɔ-nwu kemmo tɛɛ úte akpala bɔbla na limeyi kadikɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Some time later, I felt the Lord's power take control of me, and his Spirit carried me to a valley full of bones.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔdi kama ni, lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka Unwoti ɔyikun ɔ́ƒɔ-mi lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui na nwuna Kɔyu kúti-mi kúsienku kɔwɛ kɔdi kemmo na kesii kadi na bekyuli ekubi éyii tɛtɛɛtɛ mmɔ.

english_verse: The Lord showed me all around, and everywhere I looked I saw bones that were dried out.
translation_verse: Unwoti úti-mi ɔ́vinku mmɔ bene ƒui. Na ka lɛ́sia anumi lɛ́nu ni, lɛ́nu ka bekyuli ekubi akwiidi áƒɔ kesi kesii.

english_verse: He said, “Ezekiel, son of man, can these bones come back to life?” I replied, “Lord God, only you can answer that.”
translation_verse: Na úye-mi ɔnini, “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, ekubi amɛni adubɔsɔ akana na enwini ebo ngba?” Mmɔ na lídie kenye nnini, “Unwoti Katɔti, awɔ lɛti kani ndubɔkana lɛmɛni ani kenye budie.”

english_verse: He then told me to say: Dry bones, listen to what the Lord is saying to you,
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Su ekubi akwiidi ammɔ anii, ‘Binu lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔɔsu-mii!

english_verse: “I, the Lord God, will put breath in you, and once again you will live.
translation_verse: Ami Unwoti Katɔti ndubuti ɔƒɛƒɛɛ lɛkya-mii kemmo na bɛsɔ bibelie ngba.

english_verse: I will wrap you with muscles and skin and breathe life into you. Then you will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na ndubɔya na ɔlɔna ku nti ɔsɔ ubama-mii lɛlɔ na lɛnwuna ngba ɔƒɛƒɛɛ lɛnya-mii lɛlɔ kemmo. Na bɛdubɔnu bɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti.’ ”

english_verse: I did what the Lord said, but before I finished speaking, I heard a rattling noise. The bones were coming together!
translation_verse: Lɛ́bla lɛla lɛni na Unwoti ɔ́su-mi. Na asa na ndubɔwɔlɔ ni, líse kalɔ muunú kɔku kɔdi aani kalɛ na ala adi eekuonku lɛlɔ. Na lɛ́nu ka ekubi ammɔ aasála lɛlɔ!

english_verse: I saw muscles and skin cover the bones, but they had no life in them.
translation_verse: Na lɛ́nu ka ɔlɔna ku nti ɔɔma ekubi ammɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu ngba buuubo-ma tɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, now say to the wind, “The Lord God commands you to blow from every direction and to breathe life into these dead bodies, so they can live again.”
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su ɔnini, “Esekiel, ɔƒaani ni, su ɔƒɛƒɛɛ anini, ‘Unwoti uudie lɛdi teete-ɔ ɔnii kpo si lɛƒɛnyi ƒui lɛlɔ na anwuna ngba ɔƒɛƒɛɛ akya bekpine bamɛni kemmo kalɛ na basɔ benwini bebelie ngba.’ ”

english_verse: As soon as I said this, the wind blew among the bodies, and they came back to life! They all stood up, and there were enough to make a large army.
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani ka lɛ́su lɛni lɛ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔƒɛ úkpo ɔ́vi bekyuli bamɛni kemmo na bénwini bébo ngba! Na bana ƒui báta bénye na bemomo geen kalɛ na babla bekpone lisu bonwu lɛdi.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, the people of Israel are like dead bones. They complain that they are dried up and that they have no hope for the future.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama Unwoti ɔ́su ɔnini, “Esekiel, Israel kadi bekyuli bese aani bekpine. Baadɔ taasu banii bákwii bakɛ aadi bekpine ekubi na basɔ beeebo ngba lɛnunsia lɛdi bete uwi ɔni ndubo.

english_verse: So tell them, “I, the Lord God, promise to open your graves and set you free. I will bring you back to Israel,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu su-ma anini, ‘Ami Unwoti Katɔti muusé kenye ka ndubɔlɛmi bina kɔƒiɔtɔ na lite-mii bɔnwuna. Na ndubɔsɔku-mii liboku Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and when that happens, you will realize that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Na si uwi ɔni na ɔmɛni ɔ́lɛ lɛni ni, na bɛnu bɛti ka ami ndi Unwoti.

english_verse: My Spirit will give you breath, and you will live again. I will bring you home, and you will know that I have kept my promise. I, the Lord, have spoken.” Judah and Israel Together Again
translation_verse: Mina Kɔyu kɔdubɔya na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔsɔ uduo-mii lɛlɔ kemmo na bɛsɔ bibelie ngba. Ami Unwoti násu. Ndubɔsɔku-mii liboku bina ɔma na bɛti ka lɛ́di mina linyese lɛlɔ. Ami Unwoti násu.’ ” Yuda Ku Israel Básɔ Básala

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, get a stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Judah.” Then get another stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Israel.”
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, wia ugyii ɔdi na enweni asia-nwu lɛlɔ anini, ‘Yuda lɛga kadikɔ.’ Na asɔ awia ugyii bamba na enweni asia-nwu lɛlɔ anini, ‘Israel lɛga kadikɔ.’

english_verse: Hold these two sticks end to end, so they look like one stick.
translation_verse: Ti ligyii inyɔ bɔmɛni eli danku lɛlɔ na ɔbla aani ugyii unwi.

english_verse: And when your people ask you what this means,
translation_verse: Na si ƒula bekyuli béye-ɔ lɛla lɛmɛni kalɔ ni,

english_verse: tell them that I, the Lord, will join together the stick of Israel and the stick of Judah. I will hold them in my hand, and they will become one.
translation_verse: na asu-ma anii, ‘Ami Unwoti ndubo Israel ku Yuda ligyii inyɔ bɔmɛni bɔsala bɔda mina kɔnu kemmo na bana inyɔ benwini bekyuli benwi.’

english_verse: Hold these two sticks where they can be seen by everyone
translation_verse: “Da ligyii inyɔ bɔmɛni na kesii kani na ukyuli biala ɔnu-ni

english_verse: and then say: I, the Lord God, will gather the people of Israel and bring them home from the foreign nations where they now live.
translation_verse: na asu-ma anii, ‘Ami Unwoti Katɔti ndubo Israel bekyuli bɔsala na lɛkpanku-ma baƒɔ kɔlɔ lɛlɔ kesii kani na belie ɔƒɛni liboku ɔma.

english_verse: I will make them into one nation and let them once again live in the land of Israel. Only one king will rule them, and they will never again be divided into two nations.
translation_verse: Ndubo-ma bɔbla na benwini kalɔ kenwi kadi bekyuli na belie Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔga unwi kani ndubo-ma lɛlɔ bɔdi na bɔsɔ baaadubo lɛlɔ kemmo bule bɔbla kɔlɔ akpa anyɔ kudii.

english_verse: They will no longer worship idols and do things that make them unacceptable to me. I will wash away their sin and make them clean, and I will protect them from everything that makes them unclean. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Basɔ baaadubo baƒiɔ bɔkpa na bataabla ala ani ndubɔya na naaakana-ma bɔƒɔ aani mina bekyuli. Ndubɔƒɔ bana ekpidi lidie-ma lɛlɔ ƒui na babla sɛɛn. Na ndubo-ma bɔgyumana bɔsiku lɛla biala na mɔɔyá na beesé-mi lɛlɔ kudɔ. Na benwini mina bekyuli na ami lɛnɔ linwini bana Katɔti.

english_verse: Their king will always come from the family of my servant King David and will care for them like a shepherd. The people of Israel will faithfully obey my laws. They and their descendants will live in the land I gave my servant Jacob, just as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na ɔga biala na badubɔƒuna ɔdubɔsi mina kabla ɔblane Dawid ɔtɔ kemmo, na ɔdubo-ma lɛlɔ bɔnu aani baƒonu ɔdane buni kalɛ. Israel kadi bekyuli badubɔdi mina litemi lɛlɔ siin na basɔ balálɛ-mi kama. Na ama ku bana bawɔ bawɔ badubulie ɔmii ɔni na líte mina kabla ɔblane Yakob kemmo aani kalɛ kani na bana banana bábla.

english_verse: I solemnly promise to bless the people of Israel with unending peace. I will protect them and let them become a powerful nation. My temple will stand in Israel for all time,
translation_verse: Na líse kenye kpakplaa ka ndubute Israel kusɛ kusɛ na belie ku keyi buɛɛ kani udu nsɔ naaadubo bɔsa lɛnɔ kudii. Ndubo-ma bɔgyumana na lɛya na babla kadi bekyuli bani ndubɔkɛ ɔyikun geen. Na mina kakpakɔ kadubunye Israel uwi ndi uwi.

english_verse: and I will live among my people and be their God.
translation_verse: Ndubulie mina kadi bekyuli akɔ na lɛbla bana Katɔti.

english_verse: Every nation on earth will know that my temple is in Israel and that I have chosen the Israelites to be my people.
translation_verse: “ ‘Kalɔ lɛlɔ kadi biala bekyuli badubɔnu ka mina kakpakɔ kenye Israel, na ami náƒuna-ma ka babla mina kadi bekyuli.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog, that wicked ruler of the kingdoms of Meshech and Tubal in the land of Magog. Tell him:
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, Ɔga Gog ɔlalane ɔni mɔɔdi Mesek ku Tubal lɛga kadikɔ kani nkya Magog kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ ni, du-nwu kukpi kɔtɔ. Na asu-nwu anini,

english_verse: I, the Lord God, am your enemy,
translation_verse: ‘Ami Unwoti Katɔti ndi-ɔ ukisine.

english_verse: and I will make you powerless! I will put a hook in your jaw and drag away both you and your large army. You command cavalry troops that wear heavy armor and carry shields and swords.
translation_verse: Na ndubo ƒula ɔyikun ƒui udu bɔyila na liti ɔdaliwa lɛkya-a ɔnungla na lɛni awɔ ku ƒula bekpone lisu bonwu lɛmmɔ. Awɔ muudie lɛdi teete bekpone bapɔnkɔ beliene bani nkya ekpola bonwu bonwu na bada kekpo agyumanala ku kuwii na bana enu kemmo.

english_verse: Your army includes soldiers from Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya,
translation_verse: Na ebo bekpone ásiku Persia ku Kus ku Libia kɔlɔ kemmo.

english_verse: as well as from Gomer and Beth-Togarmah in the north. Your army is enormous!
translation_verse: Na badi lɛnɔ bási Goma ku Bet-Togarma na kalɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ ɔni na sɔsɔ ƒula bekpone bemomo geen.

english_verse: So keep your troops prepared to fight,
translation_verse: “ ‘Anwuɔsu bunku ƒula bekpone na baklibi lɛlɔ na bekpo.

english_verse: because in a few years, I will command you to invade Israel, a country that was ruined by war. It was deserted for a long time, but its people have returned from the foreign nations where they once lived. The Israelites now live in peace in the mountains of their own land.
translation_verse: Ɔsika na akwa alɛɛ adi kama ni, ndubo lɛdi budie bute-ɔ na etékpo Israel kadi bekyuli bani na kekpo kábwɛ-ma lɛma ƒui. Báyii udu na bekyuli bédie-ma atu uwi gyɔlɔɔ ɔdi mɛni. Nsu bekyuli bammɔ bási baƒɔ kɔlɔ kɔni lɛlɔ na bélie dii mmɔ bénwini bébo ɔma bébo beli bana kalɔ lɛlɔ. Beli ku keyi buɛɛ na ama alati bana kalɔ kemmo na abi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But you and your army will attack them like a fierce thunderstorm and surround them like a cloud.
translation_verse: Nsu awɔ ku ƒula bekpone lisu bonwu lɛmmɔ bɛdubo-ma bukpo aani kalɛ na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa ɔɔkya ligede na bɛka bɛmana-ma aani liƒlukutu bonwu lɛdi.

english_verse: When that day comes, I know that you will have an evil plan
translation_verse: “ ‘Si limeyi lɛmmɔ lídu ni, ngyi ka bɛdubo kasusu kekpidi bɔbla

english_verse: to take advantage of Israel, that weak and peaceful country where people live safely inside towns that have no walls or gates or locks.
translation_verse: bɛnii bɛdubɔkɛ kadi bani bekyuli nse kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ na beli ku atu bɔyɔ mmɔ lɛlɔ kɔsia. Ɔsika beli lɛma lɛni na bátatu awodu bátamana-ni na bakya-ni ɔban kɔyakun bonwu na babala-ni.

english_verse: You will rob the people in towns that were once a pile of rubble. These people lived as prisoners in foreign nations, but they have returned to Israel, the most important place in the world, and they own livestock and property.
translation_verse: Na bɛdubo bekyuli bani na bábwɛ-ma lɛma béwi aani kebu alakpi dii mmɔ buyu. Bekyuli bamɛni bélie kaƒɔ aani batɔntɛne kalɛ, nsu básɔ bénwini bébo Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ kesii kani náƒɔ kuye ketulo na kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ, na bebo bebuo ku akɛla bamba lɛnɔ.

english_verse: The people of Sheba and Dedan, along with merchants from villages in southern Spain, will be your allies. They will want some of the silver and gold, as well as the livestock and property that your army takes from Israel.
translation_verse: Na Seeba ku Dedan kadi bekyuli ku beyedine bani nási akpaklɔ ani nde mmɔ badubo-mii kama bunye na bebunku-mii. Ɔsika badubɔyɔ ka ama lɛnɔ bakɛ sika ɔƒualadi ku ugyiedi ku bebuo ku bana akɛla bamba ani na bebo na bekpone bamɛni badubo buƒie bɔƒɔ Israelƒuɔ kudɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: you will lead your powerful cavalry from your kingdom in the north.
translation_verse: Na awɔ ndubo ƒula bekpone kpakplaa bamɛni bɔtɔnku bɔsiku ƒula lɛga kadikɔ na katɔ mmɔ buboku.

english_verse: You will attack my people like a storm-cloud that covers their land. I will let you invade my country Israel, so that every nation on earth will know that I, the Lord, am holy. Judgment on Gog
translation_verse: Na adubo mina bekyuli bukpo aani liƒlukutu ku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ bonwu ɔni muutile kayaa. Na ndubo kuƒi bute na ekpo mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ kalɛ na kadi ƒui bekyuli na kalɔ lɛlɔ banu bati ka ami Unwoti nse kedee.’ ” Unwoti Ɔ́tɛku Ɔga Gog Litemi

english_verse: The Lord said to Gog: Long ago, I ordered my prophets to warn the people of Israel that someday I would send an enemy to attack them. You, Gog, are that enemy, and that day is coming.
translation_verse: “Unwoti ɔ́su Ɔga Gog ɔnini, “ ‘Kukuuku ni, mbo kenye bediene pii bani na lɛ́ya na básu mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ kpakplaa ka limeyi lɛdi ni, ndubo ukisine ɔdi budie bɔkya-ma. Na awɔ Gog ndi ukisine ɔmmɔ. Na limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛnɔ lɛ́ɛsi lɛdubo.

english_verse: When you invade Israel, I will become furious,
translation_verse: Si uwi ɔni na ékpo Israelƒuɔ bammɔ áwɔlɔ ni, ndubo kɔnyi bɔkɛ geen.

english_verse: and in my anger I will send a terrible earthquake to shake Israel.
translation_verse: Na ndubo bɔya na kalɔ bɔkunku kpakplaa bɔdi bubo na bubakunku Israel kalɔ kammɔ na mina kɔnyi kɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Every living thing on earth will tremble in fear of me—every fish and bird, every wild animal and reptile, and every human. Mountains will crumble, cliffs will fall, and cities will collapse.
translation_verse: Na lɛlɔ lɛdubo ngba lɛla biala nkya kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ bɔtɔ ku bɔyia geen na ami ɔsu, kɔbɛ ku baasɛ ku alakpi akɔ bebuo ku bebuo bani mɔɔkpɛ́ kaƒɔ kalɔ ku bekyuli bayawine ƒui. Abi adubo butaabwɛ teegyingya na atakpɛ ataamami na lɛma linengudi ala ataaƒɛ teewi kalɔ.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will make the mountains of Israel turn against you. Your troops will be so terrified that they will attack each other.
translation_verse: Ami Unwoti ndubɔya na Israel abi aƒɛ ebi-ɔ lɛlɔ. Na liƒu lɛni ndubo ƒula bekpone bɔda ɔsu badubo bunwini bunye bana lɛlɔ lɛlɔ beteekpoku bana bakpana ku kuwii.

english_verse: I will strike you with diseases and punish you with death. You and your army will be pounded with rainstorms, hailstones, and burning sulfur.
translation_verse: Ndubo bɔya na ɔlɛ buɛ ubo-mii na kukpi na ndubuti lɛni-mii kɔtu. Na ɔnantu ku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa ku etubankɛ ku ogya aƒɛ ku ɔnyi gbagbangba ndubo butaayu-mii lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na baawɛ́ lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: I will do these things to show the world that I, the Lord, am holy.
translation_verse: Ndubo ɔmɛni bɔbla liti lɛtina kayawi ƒui ka ami Unwoti nse kedee.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog and tell him: You are the ruler of Meshech and Tubal, but I, the Lord, am your enemy!
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, du Ɔga Gog kukpi kɔtɔ na asu-nwu anini, “ ‘Awɔ mɔɔdi Mesek ku Tubal lɛlɔ, nsu ami Unwoti ndi-ɔ ukisine!

english_verse: I will turn you around and drag you from the north until you reach the mountains of Israel.
translation_verse: Ndubo-mii bɔtɔnku kama kama na lɛkpɛ-mii lɛsiku katɔ mmɔ liboku Israel abi kudɔ.

english_verse: I will knock the bow out of your left hand and the arrows out of your right hand,
translation_verse: Ndubo ƒula kataminta bubo bɔlɛku-ɔ kɔmiinu kɔnu kemmo na libo atula ammɔ lɛnɔ lɛlɛku ƒula kɔdianu kɔnu kemmo.

english_verse: and you and your army will die on those mountains. Then birds and wild animals will eat the flesh
translation_verse: Na awɔ ku ƒula bekpone ƒui bɛdubo bukpi na abi ammɔ lɛlɔ. Na baasɛ bakun bina bekpine

english_verse: of your dead bodies left lying in open fields. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: bani ndubo bukpi buwi alakpi akɔ kesi kesii mmɔ. Ami Unwoti násu.

english_verse: I will set fire to the land of Magog and to those nations along the seacoast that think they are so secure, and they will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ndubɔya na batu ogya bakya Magog ku kadi bani nli ɛpu kɔtu na baakali ka beli ƒaa na lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-ma mmɔ. Na badubɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti.

english_verse: My people Israel will know me, and they will no longer disgrace my holy name. Everyone on earth will know that I am the holy Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: “ ‘Mina kadi bekyuli badubo-mi bɔti na basɔ balakya-mi lɛnyi kɔƒa. Na badubɔti ka ami ndi Israelƒuɔ Ukyuli Kedee.

english_verse: The day is coming when these things will happen, just as I have promised.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛsia ulu lɛdubo lɛni na ala amɛni adubo bɔlɛ kalɛ kani na líse kenye.

english_verse: When that day comes, the people in the towns of Israel will collect the weapons of their dead enemies. They will use these shields, bows and arrows, spears, and clubs as firewood, and there will be enough to last for seven years.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na si limeyi lɛmmɔ lídu ni, Israelƒuɔ badubo bana bekisine bani nebekpi-ma kudɔ mmɔ ekpola bɔla na bana lɛma lɛni kemmo na beli mmɔ. Na kɔtaminta ku atula lidu ku kekpo agyumanala ani bada mmɔ ku bana ligyii buti butaakya ogya. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔbla bana ekyweni akwa maatɛ sɔɔn.

english_verse: They will burn these weapons instead of gathering sticks or chopping down trees. That's how the Israelites will take revenge on those who robbed and abused them. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Burial of Gog The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ekpola amɛni na badubo butaakyula na egyii ani na ɔlɛka bada iye ekyweni ani na bawia bavi kenye. Lɛni na Israelƒuɔ badubo bekyuli bani néyu-ma na bédumi-ma bábla-ma kalala udu biala kasi budie. Ami Unwoti násu. Báva Ɔga Gog

english_verse: After Gog has been destroyed, I will bury him and his army in Israel, in Travelers' Valley, east of the Dead Sea. That graveyard will be so large that it will block the way of anyone who tries to walk through the valley, which will then be known as “The Valley of Gog's Army.”
translation_verse: “ ‘Si báyila Ɔga Gog udu báwɔlɔ ni, ndubɔya na bava-nwu na nwuna bekpone akɔ na Israel mmɔ na kesii kani baalɔ banii Belusiene Kɔwɛ si éti ésela Ɛpugyie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na bekyuli kavakɔ kammɔ kadubo bubomo ɔni na kadubutile ukyuli biala masu ɔnii ɔɔsia mmɔ ɔvi ulu. Anwuɔsu na badubɔlɔ mmɔ ɔmmɔ kama banii Gog ku nwuna bekpone kɔwɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites will spend seven months burying dead bodies and cleaning up their land.
translation_verse: “ ‘Abuli maatɛ na Israelƒuɔ badubo buti bɔva bekpine bammɔ na babla bana kalɔ kammɔ sɛɛn.

english_verse: Everyone will help with the burial, and they will be honored for this on the day the brightness of my glory is seen.
translation_verse: Na kalɔ kammɔ ukyuli biala ɔdubo bubunku na bekyuli bammɔ bɔva kemmo. Na limeyi lɛni na badubɔnu mina bukeye ni, ɔdubɔbla limeyi lɛni na ɔdi biala ɔdubɔkɛ ɔbu.

english_verse: After those seven months, the people will appoint a group of men to look for any dead bodies left unburied. This must be done for seven months to make sure that the land is no longer unclean.
translation_verse: “ ‘Si abuli maatɛ ammɔ ávi áwɔlɔ ni, mina kadi bekyuli bammɔ badubo bekyuli badi bɔƒuna na bavi banu si bekpine badi básɔ bébu bakya kesii kadi na bátava ama. Na badubɔbla ɔmɛni abuli maatɛ bamba kalɛ na bati nwaa ka ukpine ɔdi útaƒɔ lɛlɔ ɔɔɔtɛ kesii kadi na ubile ekisila adi na kalɔ kammɔ kalabla sɛɛn.

english_verse: Whenever they find a human bone, they will set up a marker next to it. Then the gravediggers will bury it in “The Valley of Gog's Army”
translation_verse: Na kesii biala na bánu ukyuli likubi ni, badubɔbla likposela bese mmɔ. Na ɔmmɔ kama na beyitaƒu bebeti-nwu batáva na Belusiene Kɔwɛ kemmo mmɔ

english_verse: near the town of “Gog's Army.” After that, the land will be pure again.
translation_verse: na ude kesii kani na badubo lɛnyi bɔsia banii Gog Bekpone Ɔma. Na kalɔ kammɔ kadubɔsɔ kabla sɛɛn na ɔmmɔ kama.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to hold a feast on Israel's mountains and offer sacrifices there. So invite all the birds and wild animals to come from every direction and eat the meat of sacrifices and drink the blood. The birds and animals
translation_verse: “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, ndubo limeyi bɔdi na Israel abi lɛlɔ na lɛbla akpala na mmɔ. Anwuɔsu ya na baasɛ ku bebuo ku alakpi akɔ bebuo na basi lɛƒɛnyi ƒui bebo na babakun akpala lɛna na bani ubugya lɛnɔ.

english_verse: will feast on the bodies of warriors and foreign rulers that I will sacrifice like sheep, goats, and bulls.
translation_verse: Badubo bekpone ku baƒɔ lɛlɔ badine lɛna bɔkun. Bekyuli bammɔ na ndubo bɔdu bɔbla akpala aani kalɛ na baadú baƒonu ku bese ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ taabla akpala.

english_verse: I want the birds and animals to eat until they are full and drink until they are drunk.
translation_verse: Mɔɔwia ka baasɛ bammɔ bakun lɛna bemo na bani ubugya lɛnɔ na udu-ma ɔkwɛ aani kalɛ na baaní ntɛ teekpi.

english_verse: They will come to my table and stuff themselves with the flesh of horses and warriors of every kind. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Israel Will Be Restored The Lord said:
translation_verse: Badubo babadi mina kadikɔ na bakun bapɔnkɔ lɛna ku bekpone lidu lidu lɛna beyile eƒi. Ami Unwoti násu.” Israel Ɔdubɔsɔ Unwini Ubenye Nwuna Kenyekɔ Kuuku

english_verse: When I punish the nations of the earth, they will see the brightness of my glory.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Si lɛ́ni kalɔ lɛlɔ kadi bekyuli kɔtu ni, badubɔnu kalɛ na muukeye.

english_verse: The people of Israel will know from then on that I am the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si uwi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ lɛnɔ ni, Israelƒuɔ badubɔnu bɔti ka ami ndi Unwoti, bana Katɔti.

english_verse: Foreign nations will realize that the Israelites were forced to leave their own land because they sinned against me. I turned my back on my people and let enemies attack and kill them.
translation_verse: Na baƒɔ lɛnɔ badubɔnu bati ka bunye na bénye Israelƒuɔ lɛlɔ na bábɔku-ma bálɛku bana kalɔ lɛlɔ ka bábla ekpidi báƒiɔ-mi ɔsu. Línwini kama lɛ́kya-ma na bana bekisine békpoku-ma na bádu-ma.

english_verse: Their lives were wicked and corrupt, and they deserved to be punished.
translation_verse: Ulikplu ku bubie lidu lidu lɛ́ƒɔ-ma keliela kemmo, anwuɔsu na bámanku ka lɛni-ma kɔtu.

english_verse: Now I will show mercy to the people of Israel and bring them back from the nations where they are living. They are Jacob's descendants, so I will bless them and show that I am holy.
translation_verse: “Ɔƒaani ni, ndubo Israelƒuɔ kɔnyana bɔnu na lɛkpanku-ma lɛsiku baƒɔ lɛma lɛni kemmo na bákya mmɔ lɛsɔku liboku bana kalɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔsika Yakob bebi ku bawɔ na badi, anwuɔsu ndubute-ma kusɛ kusɛ na lɛtina-ma ka nse kedee.

english_verse: They will live safely in their own land, but will be ashamed when they remember their evil ways and how they disgraced me.
translation_verse: Na badubo bulie ku keyi buɛɛ na ama alati kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na kɔƒa kukpo-ma si bényimo alaekpidi ani na bábla bábavi na bákya-mi kɔƒa.

english_verse: Foreign nations will watch as I take the Israelites from enemy lands and bring them back home, and those nations will see that I am holy.
translation_verse: Kadi bamba bekyuli bani ndi baƒɔ badubunye banu kalɛ na ndubɔƒɔ Israelƒuɔ lɛlɛku bana bekisine enu kemmo lɛsɔku liboku bana ɔma. Na kadi bammɔ bekyuli badubɔnu ka nse kedee.

english_verse: My people will realize that I, the Lord their God, sent them away as prisoners and now will bring them back to their own land.
translation_verse: “Mina bekyuli badubɔnu bati ka ami Unwoti, bana Katɔti, nábɔku-ma lɛ́lɛku bana kalɔ lɛlɔ aani batɔntɛne kalɛ. Na ɔƒaani ndubɔsɔku-ma liboku ama alati bana kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Never again will I turn my back on the people of Israel, and my Spirit will live in them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo kama bunwini bɔkya mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ kudii, na mina Kɔyu kɔdubo bulieku-ma. Ami Unwoti násu.”

english_verse: He measured the entrance room at the far end of the passageway, and it was ten meters wide.
translation_verse: Na ɔtɔ ɔni na ulu ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ kammɔ ni, ɔ́kɔku anwu lɛnɔ na ubo lɛgba avlaatɛ-ine bɔbɛbɛ.

english_verse: In my vision the Lord took me closer, and I saw a man who was sparkling like polished bronze. He was standing near one of the gates and was holding a tape measure in one hand and a measuring stick in the other.
translation_verse: Na mina ala bɔnu bɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Unwoti ɔ́ya na lɛ́ni líde suɛlɛ suɛlɛ geen na lɛ́nu ɔnana ɔdi na unye na uukeye aani lɛbuala ligyiedi lɛni na békuo na liikeye taatu anumi geen. Na unye ɔban kayakun kenwi kadi kenye na ɔda kadii ku ugyii ɔni na baakɔ́ku ala na kɔnu kɔni ku kɔni.

english_verse: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay close attention to everything I'm going to show you—that's why you've been brought here. Listen carefully, because you must tell the people of Israel what you see.” The East Gate
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, sia anu kaduɛ na anu ala ani na ndubo-ɔ bɔtina mɛni, ɔsika anya ɔsu na béti-ɔ béboku mɛni. Se atu kaduɛ, ɔsika ala ani ƒui na ánu ni, adubo-nya bɔsɔku bɔsu Israelƒuɔ.” Ɔban Kayakun Kani Nésie Ɔƒɛ Katukɔ Litemi

english_verse: Then he went to the east gate, where he walked up steps that led to a long passageway. On each side of this passageway were three guardrooms, which were three meters square, and they were separated by walls two and a half meters thick. The man measured the distance between the opening of the gate and the first guardroom, and it was three meters, the thickness of the outer wall. At the far end of this passageway, I saw an entrance room that faced the courtyard of the temple itself. There was also a distance of three meters between the last guardroom and the entrance room
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama úsie ɔban ɔni nkya ɔƒɛ katukɔ na ɔ́kɔ libili lɛdi útédu ulu ɔdi na ɔtɛ úsela anumi ƒui. Na ulu ɔmɛni kɔmii ku kɔdianu ni, bátu lɛtɔ ɛtɛ ɛtɛ lɛni kemmo na beenye taagyumana bényene. Na lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ bunene ku bɔbɛbɛ ƒui bubo lɛgba leevu leevu. Na awodu ani bugbigbli ntulo lɛgba maane líle lɛtɔ lɛmɛni lɛ́siku ɔkpanadi kudɔ. Ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku kalɛ na bagyumanane ɔtɔ udeedi ɔ́gyunku ɔban ɔmmɔ kenye na ubo lɛgba leevu. Na bɔgyunku bɔmmɔ búlieku kowodu kɔmadi kɔmmɔ bugbigbli bɔni ndi lɛgba leevu. Amu na ulu ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ na kama kama ƒui ni, lɛ́nu ɔtɔ ɔdi kayakun ka kéti anumi kéboku kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔlati kaduli. Na bagyumane ɔtɔ ukplodi ku ɔtɔ kayakun kamɛni ntɛ bɔgyu lɛnɔ bɔdi lɛgba leevu

english_verse: at the end of the passageway. The man measured this room: It was four meters from the doorway to the opposite wall, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one meter.
translation_verse: na ulu ɔmɛni kawɔlɔkɔ mmɔ. Ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ, na ɔ́si nwuna kayakun úsie kowodu kɔni na ɔvi unyɔdi ntɛ ɔdi lɛgba leevu-ɛtɛ. Na ɔ́si kayakun kammɔ útédu awodu anyɔ ani na nwuna lɛƒɛnyi inyɔ lɛmmɔ ɔdi lɛgba ɛtɛ ɛtɛ.

english_verse: The three guardrooms on each side of the passageway were the same size, and the walls that separated them were the same thickness.
translation_verse: Bagyumane lɛtɔ ɛtɛ ɛtɛ lɛni na linye ulu ɔmɛni lɛvi inyɔ bɔmmɔ bɔkɔku ku udu ɔdi unwi. Na awodu ani néle lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ lɛ́siku ɔkpanadi kudɔ lɛnɔ bɔdi bugbigbli bunwi pɛ.

english_verse: Next, the man measured the width of the passageway, and it was six and a half meters, but the two doors of the gate were only five meters wide.
translation_verse: Kama ni, ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku ulu ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ lɛbɛbɛ na ubo lɛgba aavlanyɔ-inyɔ, nsu ɔban kɔyaku inyɔ kɔmmɔ ƒui bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba leevu-ɛku kani.

english_verse: The man measured the distance from the back wall of one of these rooms to the same spot in the room directly across the passageway, and it was twelve and a half meters.
translation_verse: Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɔku ɔ́si bagyumanane ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kowodu kɔmadi ɔ́via ulu úsie ɔtɔ ɔni na ulu ɔvi unyɔdi kowodu kɔmadi na ubo lɛgba aavlene-inyɔ.

english_verse: Finally, he measured the total length of the passageway, from the outer wall to the entrance room, and it was
translation_verse: Kawɔlɔkɔ ni, ɔ́kɔku ulu ɔmmɔ ƒui bune ɔ́si kowodu kɔmadi kɔmmɔ útédu ɔtɔ ɔni kayakun néti anumi kéboku kakpakɔ kaduli geen mmɔ, na ulu ɔmmɔ ubo lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ.

english_verse: The three walls in the guardrooms had small windows in them, just like the ones in the entrance room. The walls along the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. The Outer Courtyard
translation_verse: Bédie ƒansili na bagyumanane lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ awodu ƒui kemmo ku awodu ani nkya lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ntɛ kemmo aani kalɛ na use na ɔtɔ ɔni nnye ulu ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ mmɔ kemmo kalɛ. Na bánwi ala na ebo udu kenye béti bákya awodu ani na ulu ɔmmɔ lɛvi inyɔ bɔmmɔ akya. Búsie Kaduli Kedeedi Kemmo

english_verse: In fact, everything along the passageway was also the same size, including the guardrooms, the walls separating them, the entrance room at the far end, and the windows. This gate, like the others, was
translation_verse: Na geen ni, lɛla biala na lɛkya ulu lɛlɔ lílieku ekpo edeedi adi. Na bagyumane lɛtɔ ku awodu ani nkya lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ntɛ ku ɔtɔ ɔni nnye ulu ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ na adubɔvia-nwu eduo ɔban ɔmmɔ kemmo ku lɛƒansili ƒui lise aani lideedi lɛdi kalɛ. Na ɔban ɔmmɔ ɔlati bune bubo lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ, na bɔbɛbɛ lɛnɔ bubo lɛgba aavlene-inyɔ.

english_verse: This was known as the lower sidewalk, and it was
translation_verse: Na mmɔ ndi ɔkwalɛ lɛgba kasiakɔ ka mmɔ kébo kánu ɔsu. Na nwuna bɔbɛbɛ ɔdi lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ.

english_verse: I saw the gates that led to the inner courtyard of the temple and noticed that they were higher than those leading to the outer courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gates, and it was
translation_verse: Lɛ́nu kayakun kɔni na baasia teeduo kakpakɔ kaduli geen geen kemmo. Na lɛ́nu ka aku kɔ́kuku kutulo kɔyakun kɔni na baasia teeduo kaduli kedeedi kemmo. Ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku ɔ́si kaduli kedeedi kɔyakun kenye útédu kaduli kebliidi kayakun kenye na ubo lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ. Bákɔku Kayakun Kani Nkya Katɔ Kakɛ

english_verse: Next, the man measured the north gate that led to the outer courtyard.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɔku kayakun kani nkya katɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: This gate also had three guardrooms on each side of a passageway. The measurements of these rooms, the walls between them, and the entrance room at the far end of the passageway were exactly the same as those of the east gate. The north gate was also
translation_verse: Kayakun kamɛni lɛnɔ kebo bagyumane lɛtɔ ɛtɛ na ulu ɔni ntɛ úsela lɛlɔ. Lɛtɔ lɛmɛni bɔkɔku ku awodu ani nkya lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ntɛ ku ɔban kayakun kani nkya ulu ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ ƒui lɛnɔ use aani kalɛ kani na use na ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔban kayakun. Na ulu ɔni ntɛ úsie ɔban kayakun kani na katɔ kakɛ mmɔ lɛnɔ ɔdi lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ bune ku lɛgba aavlene-inyɔ bɔbɛbɛ.

english_verse: and the windows, the entrance room, and the carvings of palm trees were just like those in the east gate. The entrance room also faced the courtyard of the temple and had seven steps leading up to it.
translation_verse: Na lɛƒansili ku ɔban awodu ku ala ani na bánwi na ebo udu kenye béti bákya awodu ammɔ bɔdia ni, ese aani kalɛ na use na ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔban kayakun mmɔ kemmo kalɛ. Kɔnyakɔ libili maatɛ na adubɔkɔ etédu ɔban ɔmɛni kenye na ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na adubɔsia eduo unye kakpakɔ kaduli geen kammɔ.

english_verse: Directly across the outer courtyard was a gate that led to the inner courtyard, just as there was for the east gate. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was
translation_verse: Na ulu ɔtɛ ɔ́si mmɔ úsie kakpakɔ kaduli geen geen kemmo kɔnakunwi aani kalɛ na ɔtɛ ɔ́si ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔban kayakun úsie mmɔ. Ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku kayakun kani na anumi mɛni úti úsie kayakun kamaadi na lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ. Búsie Kayakun Kadani

english_verse: The man then took me to the south gate. He measured the walls and the entrance room of this gate, and the measurements were exactly the same as those of the other two gates.
translation_verse: Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpanku-mi na búsie na kayakun kani ka kada kakɛ. Na ɔ́kɔku awodu ku ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kayakun úlieku kɔyakun kudeedi kɔni na ɔ́ka bɔkɔku pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Seven steps led up to the gate; the entrance room was at the far end of the passageway and faced the courtyard of the temple. Carvings of palm trees decorated the walls along the passageway.
translation_verse: Kɔnyakɔ libili maatɛ na adubɔkɔ etédu ɔban ɔmɛni kenye na ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na adubɔsia eduo unye ulu ɔmmɔ kawɔlɔkɔ lili ƒui. Na ɔtɔ anumi aatina kakpakɔ kaduli geen kammɔ. Na bánwi ala na ebo udu kenye béti bákya awodu ammɔ akya na ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: And directly across the outer courtyard was a gate on the south side of the inner courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was also
translation_verse: Na si ánu ávia kaduli kedeedi kamɛni úsie kakpakɔ kaduli geen kani nkya kemmo kada kakɛ ni, ɔban kayakun kadi kenye. Na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku kuƒi kɔni nkya ɔban kayakun kani na anumi mɛni ku kani kemmo ntɛ na ubo lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ. Kasiakɔ Katɛ Lɛban Lɛmmɔ Kenye Líduo Kakpakɔ Kaduli Geen

english_verse: We then went into the inner courtyard, through the gate on the south side of the temple. The man measured the gate, and it was the same size as the gates in the outer wall.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, bɔ́sia ɔban kayakun kani na kakpakɔ kada kakɛ mmɔ bútéduo kaduli kani na kemmo. Na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɔku ɔban kayakun kammɔ na kélie ku kɔni na kaduli kedeedi awodu kemmo.

english_verse: The entrance room of this gate faced the outer courtyard, and carvings of palm trees decorated the walls of the passageway. Eight steps led up to this gate.
translation_verse: Na ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na adubɔsia mɛni eduo ɔban ɔmmɔ kemmo anumi aatina kaduli kedeedi kammɔ na ala ani na bánwi aani ebo udu na béti bákya kasiakɔ kammɔ ulu akya. Na libili maane násia úsie ɔban ɔmmɔ kenye.

english_verse: Next, we went through the east gate to the inner courtyard. The man measured this gate, and it was the same size as the others.
translation_verse: Ka bɔ́si mmɔ ni, bɔ́sia ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔban kemmo bútéduo kaduli kani na kemmo mmɔ kemmo na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku mmɔ lɛnɔ. Na mɛni lɛnɔ úlieku kudeedi.

english_verse: The guardrooms, the walls separating them, and its entrance room had the same measurements as the other gates. The guardrooms and the entrance room had windows, and the gate was
translation_verse: Bagyumanane lɛtɔ ku awodu ani nkya lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ntɛ ku ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na adubɔsia eduo ƒui bɔkɔku bɔdi unwi aani budeedi kalɛ. Na lɛƒansili lɛkya lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ƒui kemmo. Na ɔban ɔmmɔ bune bɔdi lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ. Na nwuna bɔbɛbɛ bubo lɛgba aavlene-inyɔ.

english_verse: The entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and the walls in the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate.
translation_verse: Na ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na adubɔsia eduo mmɔ anumi aatina kaduli kedeedi kammɔ. Na bánwi ala na ebo udu kenye bákya awodu ani na ulu lɛlɔ. Na libili maatɛ násia úsie ɔban ɔmmɔ kenye.

english_verse: Then the man took me to the north gate. He measured it, and it was the same size as the others,
translation_verse: Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpanku-mi úsienku ɔban ɔni na katɔ kakɛ. Na ɔ́kɔku ɔban ɔmmɔ na bɔkɔku bunwi pɛ kani na ɔdi ku lɛkladi.

english_verse: including the guardrooms, the walls separating them, and the entrance room. There were also windows in this gate. It was
translation_verse: Bagyumane lɛtɔ ku awodu ani nkya lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ ntɛ ku ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na baasia teeduo mmɔ ƒui ni, lɛƒansili lɛkya ɔna ƒui lɛlɔ. Nwuna bune bɔdi lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ. Na nwuna bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba aavlene-inyɔ.

english_verse: and like the other inner gates, its entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and its walls were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate. The Rooms for Sacrificing Animals
translation_verse: Na ɔban ɔmɛni lɛnɔ aani lɛni nkya kaduli kani na kemmo mmɔ kalɛ ni, nwuna anumi aatina kaduli kedeedi na bánwi ala aani ebo udu bákya awodu ani na ulu lɛlɔ mmɔ akya. Libili maane nsia útédu ɔban ɔmmɔ kenye. Lɛ́nu Ɔtɔ Ɔni Kemmo Na Baadú Bebuo Taakpa

english_verse: Inside the entrance room of the north gate, I saw four tables, two on each side of the room, where the animals to be sacrificed were killed. Just outside this room was a small building used for washing the animals before they were offered as sacrifices to please the Lord or sacrifices for sin or sacrifices to make things right.
translation_verse: Na ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na adubɔsia eduo ɔban ɔmmɔ kemmo na katɔ kakɛ mmɔ ni, lɛ́nu ka ala kasiakɔ ine bɔlɛ. Inyɔ na ɔƒɛnyi unwi na inyɔ lɛnɔ na ɔƒɛnyi ɔkladi. Na nwuna lɛlɔ na baadú bebuo bani na baakyula taabla akpala. Na ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kamadɔ ni, ɔtɔ blii ɔdi unye ɔni kemmo na baakpila bebuo bamɛni asa na badu-ma bakyula ƒui bete Unwoti na ɔƒɔ-nwu anu iye bakpa babla ekpidi lili buvele akpala.

english_verse: Four more tables were in the outer courtyard, two on each side of the steps leading into the entrance room.
translation_verse: Ala kɔsiakɔ ine bamba linye kaduli kedeedi kammɔ libili lɛni násia lísie ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na baasia teeduo mmɔ.

english_verse: So there was a total of eight tables, four inside and four outside, where the animals were killed,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ala kɔsiakɔ kɔmmɔ ƒui kubo maane. Ine na keyi na ine lɛnɔ na ɔtɔ kemmo kesii kani na baadú bebuo mmɔ

english_verse: The man then took me to the inner courtyard, where I saw two buildings, one beside the inner gate on the north and the other beside the inner gate on the south.
translation_verse: Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpanku-mi na bútéduo kaduli kani nkya kemmo mmɔ kemmo. Mmɔ ni, lɛ́nu lɛtɔ inyɔ na unwi unye ɔban ɔni na kaduli kani na kemmo mmɔ katɔ kakɛ, na ɔkladi unye kaduli kani na kemmo mmɔ kada kakɛ.

english_verse: He said, “The building beside the north gate belongs to the priests who serve in the temple,
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ɔtɔ ɔni na aanu ka unye ɔban ɔni na katɔ kakɛ mmɔ kɔmadɔ ni, anwu ndi bakpane bani mɔɔbla kabla na kakpakɔ ɔdi.

english_verse: and the building beside the south gate belongs to those who serve at the altar. All of them are descendants of Zadok and are the only Levites allowed to serve as the Lord's priests.” The Inner Courtyard and the Temple
translation_verse: Na ɔni nnye ɔban ɔni kada kakɛ mmɔ kamadɔ ni, mmɔ ndi bekyuli bani muubunku kabla na lɛkpabi lɛlɔ lɛnɔ ɔdi. Na bana ƒui Sadok bebi ku bawɔ bani ndi Lewiƒuɔ bani kani na Unwoti úte kuƒi ka babla Unwoti bakpane.” Lɛ́nu Kakpakɔ Kaduli Geen Ku Kakpakɔ Kammɔ

english_verse: We walked to the porch of the temple, and the man measured the doorway of the porch: It was seven meters long, two and a half meters wide, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one and a half meters.
translation_verse: Búsie bútédu kakpakɔ lɛgbanya kemmo na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɔku kayakun kammɔ na nwuna bune bɔdi lɛgba aavlanyɔ-ine. Na bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba maane. Na ɔ́si kayakun mmɔ úsie kowodu kɔmmɔ kudɔ ubo lɛgba ɛlɔ ɛlɔ ɔvi ɔni ku ɔni.

english_verse: The porch itself was ten meters by six meters, with steps leading up to it. There was a column on each side of these steps.
translation_verse: Na lɛgbanya mmɔ geen anwu ubo lɛgba avlaatɛ-ine bune na bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba aavlanyɔ. Na básia libili bétédu mmɔ. Na atabi akpa anyɔ enye libili lɛmɛni ɔdi biala ɔvi ɔni ku ɔni.

english_verse: Next we went into the main room of the temple. The man measured the doorway of this room: It was
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama bútéduo kakpakɔ ɔtɔ geen kemmo na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔku ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kayakun. Na bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba leevu,

english_verse: with carvings of winged creatures and had a carving of a palm tree between the creatures. Each winged creature had two faces: A human face looking at the palm tree on one side, and a lion's face looking at the palm tree on the other side. These designs were carved into the paneling all the way around the two rooms.
translation_verse: ku ala ani na bánwi na bebweyi badi mbo avwi udu kenye na bánwi ebo udu bényene-ma ntɛ. Na bebweyi bani mbo avwi mɛni bebo anumi lɛtɔtɔ ku kama. Ukyuli anumi aanu ebo ani bényene mmɔ kakɛ kenwi na gyata anumi lɛnɔ aanu ebo ani nnye ɔvi unyɔdi. Na bánwi ala amɛni bákya ligyii lɛkanadi lɛmmɔ kemmo na awodu ammɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́ka ɔ́ma lɛtɔ inyɔ lɛmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: and the nearest buildings ten meters away.
translation_verse: Na ɔtɔ ɔni nákpɛ úde kakpakɔ kamɛni bɔgyu bɔdi lɛgba avlaatɛ-ine.

english_verse: The walls of the temple were thicker at the bottom than at the top, which meant that the storage rooms on the top level were wider than those on the bottom level. Steps led from the bottom level, through the middle level, and into the top level.
translation_verse: Kakpakɔ awodu ammɔ égbigbli na kalɔ kakɛ utulo katɔ kakɛ, anwuɔsu ala kusekɔ kɔni nkya katɔ kemmo kúwi kutulo kɔni nkya kada kakɛ. Na ubo kɔnyakɔ kanyakɔ ɔ́si bamana budeedi ku unyɔdi útédu ɔtɛdi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The temple rested on a stone base three meters high, which also served as the foundation for the storage rooms.
translation_verse: Kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔlati kenye atabi ɔka ɔni nákuku lɛgba leevu lɛlɔ. Na ɔmmɔ kani ndi ɔka ute ala kusekɔ lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ lɛnɔ.

english_verse: The outside walls of the storage rooms were two and a half meters thick; there was nothing between these walls
translation_verse: Ala kusekɔ lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ awodu amadi égbigbli lɛgba maane na lɛla lɛdi liiibo awodu ammɔ ntɛ.

english_verse: One door led into the storage rooms on the north side of the temple, and another door led to those on the south side. The stone base extended two and a half meters beyond the outside wall of the storage rooms. The West Building and the Measurements of the Temple
translation_verse: Kayakun kenwi kani na adubɔsia étéduo ala kusekɔ kɔni nkya kusie kakpakɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ kemmo. Na kabambadi lɛnɔ kakya késie ala kusekɔ kɔni nkya kakpakɔ kammɔ kada kakɛ kemmo. Na lɛtabi ɔka ɔni lɛlɔ na kakpakɔ kammɔ kenye kábɛbɛ kávia késie kama lɛgba maane úbo ɔ́vi ala kusekɔ awodu amadi ammɔ.

english_verse: The distance across the front of the temple, including the open space on either side, was also
translation_verse: Kalɔ ƒiaa kani nwi kakpakɔ kaduli geen kammɔ anumi ku lɛƒɛnyi ƒui bɔkɔku lɛnɔ bubo lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ.

english_verse: were paneled with wood all the way from the floor to the windows, while the doorways, the small windows, and the three side rooms were trimmed in wood.
translation_verse: ligyii sɔɔn na bákana bámana awodu ammɔ lɛlɔ ku kalɔ ƒui útédu ƒansili. Na kayakun ku lɛƒansili wɛlɛ wɛlɛ lɛmmɔ ku lɛtɔ lɛni na lɛƒɛnyi ni, baakana na beebi-ni ligyii lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: The paneling stopped just above the doorway. These walls were decorated
translation_verse: Na kalɛ na béti ligyii bákana bámana awodu ammɔ lɛlɔ ni, kayakun katɔ kani na ɔ́wɔ. Na bákya awodu ammɔ akya geen

english_verse: The doorframe to the temple's main room was in the shape of a rectangle. The Wooden Altar In front of the doorway to the most holy place was something that looked like
translation_verse: Na kakpakɔ kammɔ kayakun ugyii ɔni bákya kesii kani geen ndi ɔtɔ keliekɔ ni, nwuna bɔnu kemmo use aani adaka gyɔlɔɔ ɔni mbo lɛƒɛnyi ine. Bábla Ugyii Lɛkpabi Na kayakun kani néti késela kakpakɔ katɔma kedee kemmo ni, lɛla lɛdi linye na ɔɔtina aani

english_verse: a wooden altar. It was one and a half meters high and one meter square, and its corners, its base, and its sides were made of wood. The man said, “This is a reminder that the Lord is constantly watching over his temple.” The Doors in the Temple
translation_verse: ugyii lɛkpabi. Ɔ́kuku lɛgba ɛlɔ na nwuna bune ku bɔbɛbɛ ƒui bɔdi lɛgba ine ine. Na akpa ani nda nwuna lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ na ɔda kalɔ aani ɔka ni, ligyii na béti bábla-ni. Mmɔ na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ɔmɛni mɔɔtina ka Unwoti ɔɔsia nwuna kakpakɔ kammɔ anu uwi ndi uwi.” Kakpakɔ Kɔkalɛkɔ

english_verse: Both the doorway to the main room of the temple and the doorway to the most holy place had two doors,
translation_verse: Kakpakɔ ɔtɔ geen ɔmmɔ ku kakpakɔ katɔma kedee ƒui ni, ubo kɔlɛmikɔ lɛvi inyɔ.

english_verse: and each door had two sections that could fold open.
translation_verse: Na kɔlɛmikɔ kɔmɛni kubo ntɛ bule ɔni na bakana na báƒɛ-nwu basia ɔkpanadi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The doors to the main room were decorated with carvings of winged creatures and palm trees just like those on the walls, and there was a wooden covering over the porch just outside these doors.
translation_verse: Na ɔtɔ keliekɔ geen kammɔ kɔlɛmikɔ kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, bánwi bebweyi ku avwi ku ebo udu básia aani kalɛ na bábla na awodu ammɔ lɛlɔ na ɔtɔ kemmo. Na asa na adubuduo ɔtɔ kemmo kayakun anumi kesii kani ndi lɛgbanya mɛni ni, ligyii na béti bébi mmɔ.

english_verse: The walls on each side of this porch had small windows and were also decorated with carvings of palm trees.
translation_verse: Na lɛgbanya awodu ammɔ ni, lɛƒansili lɛkya na bánwi bebweyi ku avwi bammɔ ku ebo udu bákya ani lɛnɔ akya.

english_verse: After the man and I left the temple and walked back to the outer courtyard, he showed me a set of rooms on the north side of the west building. This set of rooms was
translation_verse: Kama ƒui uwi ɔni na bɔ́tɔlɔ kakpakɔ kesii mmɔ búnwini búbo kaduli kedeedi kammɔ kemmo ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́tina-mi lɛtɔ lɛdi nnye lisu na ɔtɔ ɔni nnye ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kudɔ katɔ kakɛ, na lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ bune ɔdi lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ na bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ-ɛlɔ.

english_verse: and at the east end of this wall was the door leading from the courtyard to these rooms. There was also a set of rooms on the south side of the west building.
translation_verse: Na ɔtɔ ɔmɛni ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ ni, kayakun kadi kakya na ulu ɔtɛ ɔ́si kaduli kamɛni kemmo útéduo lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ kemmo. Na lɛtɔ lisu lɛdi lɛnɔ lɛkya ɔtɔ ɔni nnye ɔƒɛ kanukɔ mmɔ kada kakɛ.

english_verse: with doors that opened toward the north, and in front of them was a walkway five meters wide and
translation_verse: Na bálɛmi lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ kɔyakun béwi úti úsie katɔ kakɛ na lɛgba kasiakɔ katɛ kɔyakun kɔmmɔ anumi na kábɛbɛ lɛgba leevu-maatɛ na úne lɛgba eti atɛ ku aavlanyɔ.

english_verse: The rooms on the top level were narrower than those on the middle level, and the rooms on the middle level were narrower than those on the bottom level.
translation_verse: Lɛtɔ lɛtɔdi kemmo lise blii suɛ litulo lɛni nkya ntɛntɛ. Na lɛni ntɛntɛ mmɔ lɛdi lɛnɔ lɛsɔ lise blii suɛ litulo lɛni na kalɔ.

english_verse: The rooms on the bottom level supported those on the two upper levels, and so these rooms did not have columns like other buildings in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Lɛtɔ lɛni nkya kalɔ nda lɛni nkya ntɛ ku katɔ lɛdi ƒui, anwuɔsu akpa abambadi adi asɔ aaada lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ aani kalɛ na use lɛtɔ lɛbambadi lɛni nnye kaduli kemmo mmɔ.

english_verse: To the north was a privacy wall
translation_verse: Na katɔ kakɛ ƒui ɔtɔ ɔdi údie lɛlɔ na úne lɛgba liti ku avlaatɛ.

english_verse: These rooms were exactly like those on the north side, and they also had a walkway in front of them.
translation_verse: Lɛtɔ lɛmɛni lise aani lɛni nkya katɔ kakɛ mmɔ udu na ani lɛnɔ libo lɛgba kasiakɔ na nina anumi.

english_verse: The door to these rooms was at the east end of the wall that stood in front of them.
translation_verse: Na kayakun kani na baasia teesie lɛtɔ lɛmɛni kemmo ɔkya ɔtɔ nnye anumi mmɔ na nwuna kowodu kúti kúsie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kalɛ mmɔ.

english_verse: The man then said to me: These rooms on the north and south sides of the temple are the sacred rooms where the Lord's priests will eat the most holy offerings. These offerings include the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices for sin, and the sacrifices to make things right.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Lɛtɔ lɛni na nkya kakpakɔ kammɔ katɔ kakɛ ku kada kakɛ ni, ani bédie bése sɛsɛɛ béte Unwoti bakpane badubɔdi akpala ani nse kedee etulo ƒui mmɔ. Na akpala amɛni ndi antabi udu akpala ku ekpidi lili buvele akpala ku unwi bɔbla akpala.

english_verse: When the priests are ready to leave the temple, they must go through these rooms before they return to the outer courtyard. They must leave their sacred clothes in these rooms and put on regular clothes before going anywhere near other people. The Size of the Temple Area
translation_verse: Si uwi ɔni na bakpane báklibi lɛlɔ ka balɛ kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo ni, lɛtɔ lɛmɛni kemmo na ɔlɛka basia asa na benwini besie kaduli kammɔ kemmo. Na bana adala ani na bábla bése sɛsɛɛ ute kabla kammɔ ni, mɛni na ɔlɛka bedie adala ammɔ bese na beti adala bamba bada asa na ama ku bekyuli bamba bataasala ku lɛlɔ.” Bánu Kakpakɔ Kaduli Geen Bubomo

english_verse: After the man had finished measuring the buildings inside the temple area, he took me back through the east gate and measured the wall around this area.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́wɔlɔ lɛtɔ lɛni nkya kakpakɔ kaduli geen mmɔ bɔkɔku ni, ɔ́kpanku-mi na bɔ́sɔ bútásia ɔban kayaku kani nkya ɔƒɛ katukɔ mmɔ na útákɔku kowodu kɔni náka kɔ́mana mɛni.

english_verse: He used his measuring stick to measure the east side of this wall; it was
translation_verse: Na úti nwuna ugyii lɛkɔkula na ɔ́kɔku kowodu kɔmɛni kakɛ kani nésie ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ na kúne lɛgba eti maane ku aavlene.

english_verse: Then he measured the north side, the south side, and the west side of the wall, and they were each
translation_verse: Lɛni kani na ɔ́kɔku katɔ kakɛ ku kada kakɛ ku ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ, na ekpo amɛni ƒui ɔdi biala bune bɔdi lɛgba eti maane ku aavlene.

english_verse: and so the temple area was a perfect square. The wall around this area separated what was sacred from what was ordinary.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu kakpakɔ kaduli geen kammɔ katɛ lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Na kowodu kɔni náka kɔ́mana mɛni ɔɔtina ka béle ala ani na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ bete Unwoti ku ala aƒuƒuɛdi ntɛ.

english_verse: The man took me back to the east gate of the temple,
translation_verse: Ɔnana ɔmmɔ útiku-mi na bɔ́sɔ búnwini búsie kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: meters high, was the place where sacrifices were burned, and the four corners of the top section looked like the horns of a bull. The steps leading up to the altar were on the east side. The Dedication of the Altar
translation_verse: Mmɔ na lɛ́nu Israel Unwoti Katɔti bukeye ka bɔ́si ɔƒɛ katukɔ bɔdubo. Na línu kɔku kɔdi aani kalɛ na ɛpu ɔɔbla kɔku bonwu, na Unwoti bukeye bɔmɛni bɔ́ya na lɛla biala nkya amadɔ liikeye taatu anumi.

english_verse: This vision was like the one I had seen when God came to destroy Jerusalem and like the one I had seen near the Chebar River. I immediately bowed with my face to the ground,
translation_verse: Kɔyu kemmo ala bɔnu bɔmɛni búlieku bɔni na lɛ́nu uwi ɔni na Katɔti úbo úbakyula Yerusalem na ɔyila-nwu udu ku uwi ɔni na lɛ́nu na Keba Ketu kudɔ.

english_verse: and the Lord's glory came through the east gate and into the temple.
translation_verse: Katɔti bukeye bɔmɛni bɔ́sia kakpakɔ ɔban kayakun na ɔƒɛ katukɔ mmɔ na búbeduo kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit lifted me to my feet and carried me to the inner courtyard, where I saw that the Lord's glory had filled the temple.
translation_verse: Katɔti Kɔyu kɔ́ya na lɛ́ta línye mina lɛgba lɛlɔ na kútiku-mi kúsienku kakpakɔ kaduli geen kani nkya kemmo ƒui na mmɔ, na lɛ́nu ka Unwoti bukeye bɔ́ƒɔ kakpakɔ kemmo mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: But if the people and their kings stop worshiping other gods and tear down those memorials, I will live among them forever.
translation_verse: Nsu si bekyuli bamɛni báda baƒiɔ bɔkpa báya na bábwɛ ala ani na bávɔ na bánwi bése baanu mmɔ ni, ndubulieku-ma uwi ƒui.

english_verse: The people of Israel must suffer shame for sinning against me, so tell them about my holy temple. Let them think about it,
translation_verse: Ɔlɛka kɔƒa kukpo Israelƒuɔ na bebo abi na bana ekpidi ani na bábla ɔsu. Anwuɔsu tɛmiku-ma siku mina kakpakɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: then if they are truly sorry, describe for them the design and shape of the temple, the gates, the measurements, and how the buildings are arranged. Explain the regulations about worshiping there, then write down these things, so they can study and obey them.
translation_verse: Na si bana ekpidi éduo-ma sɔsɔ ni, na asɔku lɛla biala na ánu na kakpakɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ku lɛban lɛmmɔ ku kalɛ na bákɔku lɛla biala ku kalɛ na bényene lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ. Na edie ɔda bubo bɔni ndanku kalɛ na ɔlɛka bakpa na mmɔ na enweni lɛla biala ese kalɛ na batɛya kaduɛ na badi ala ammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The temple area on my holy mountain must be kept sacred! This is the most important law about the temple. The Altar
translation_verse: “Na mina kakpakɔ kaduli geen kani na kɔbi lɛlɔ mmɔ ni, ɔlɛka bada mmɔ edu aani lɛla lɛni na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ béte-mi! Ɔmɛni ndi ɔda bubo bɔni náƒɛ kuye butulo ƒui ɔ́siku mina kakpakɔ lɛlɔ. Kalɛ Na Unwoti Lɛkpabi Lise

english_verse: Each day for the next seven days, you must offer a goat and a bull and a ram as sacrifices for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: “Emeyi maatɛ ani nsia kadi biala megye ni, ɔlɛka bɛdu ese ku akɔ ku koƒonu bete-mi aani alaekpidi lili buvele akpala. Na ɔlɛka bɛnu ka bátasɔ kesii kadi.

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, after the altar is built, it must be dedicated by offering sacrifices on it and by splattering it with blood. Here is what you must do:
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti ɔnini, “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, si uwi ɔni na bátu lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ báwɔlɔ ni, ɔlɛka bakyula akpala nwuna lɛlɔ na bewi-ni ubugya na bedie-ni sɛsɛɛ basɔku bakya-mi lɛkɔkɔ. Na ndubɔtina-a ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na adubo ala ammɔ bɔbla.

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe from the family of Zadok the priest are the only ones who may serve in my temple—this is my law. So give them a young bull to slaughter as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Ɔnana ɔni baalɔ Sadok bebi ku bawɔ bani nási Lewi kɔdua kemmo ni, ama kani na ɔlɛka babla kabla na mina kakpakɔ aani kalɛ na mina ɔda bubo bɔɔtina. Anwuɔsu ti ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔkɔdi te-ma na badu bakyula babla alaekpidi lili buvele akpala.

english_verse: Take some of the animal's blood and smear it on the four corners of the altar, some on the corners of the middle section, and some more on the rim around its edge. That will purify the altar and make it fit for offering sacrifices to me.
translation_verse: Na eti ubugya ɔmmɔ ɔdi ákwaa lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ ekpo ene ammɔ. Na aya na ubugya ɔmmɔ ɔdi ususu lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ bule bɔni ntɛntɛ mmɔ ekpo ammɔ. Na ɔdi lɛnɔ ususu atabi kɔlɛkɛ kɔni na bátu bámana mmɔ. Ɔmmɔ ndubɔya na lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛbla sɛɛn kalɛ na bataabla akpala nwuna lɛlɔ teete-mi.

english_verse: Then take the body of the bull outside the temple area and burn it at the special place.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama na beti ebuo ɔmmɔ balɛku kakpakɔ kaduli geen mmɔ na batákyula-nwu na kesii kani na báƒuna bése.

english_verse: The next day, a goat that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice for sin. Purify the altar with its blood, just as you did with the blood of the bull.
translation_verse: “Kadi kegye ni, na beti ketukpa kani na kátasɔ kesii kadi na ɔ́manku batádu babla ekpidi lili buvele akpala. Na beti nwuna ubugya bakwaa lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ babla-ni sɛɛn aani kalɛ na bábla akɔ ɔkɔdi ɔmmɔ ɔdi.

english_verse: Then choose a young bull and a young ram that have nothing wrong with them,
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama na báƒuna akɔ ɔkɔdi ku koƒonu kɔgyani kɔkɔdi bani na bátasɔ kesi kesii

english_verse: and bring them to my temple. The priests will sprinkle salt on them and offer them as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: na biti-ma biboku mina kakpakɔ. Ɔkpane ɔdubuti mma ɔkuna uwi-ma lɛlɔ na beti-ma babla kɔnu bɔsia akpala bete-mi na ɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ.

english_verse: The priests will purify the altar during those days, so that it will be acceptable to me and ready to use.
translation_verse: Emeyi ammɔ kemmo ni, ɔkpane ɔdubo lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ bɔbla sɛɛn kalɛ na ɔmanku ute ka bakpa na nwuna lɛlɔ bete-mi.

english_verse: From then on, the priests will use this altar to offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices to ask my blessing. Then I will be pleased with the people of Israel. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔkpane ɔdubo akpala butaabla na lɛkpabi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ na ɔyɔ-ni kaƒɔ na uvele kusɛ kusɛ ɔsiku-mi kudɔ ɔni ndi unwi bɔbla akpala. Ami Unwoti násu.”

english_verse: The man took me back to the outer courtyard, near the east gate of the temple area. I saw that the doors to this gate were closed.
translation_verse: Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔsɔku-mi úboku kaduli kedeedi kesii kani nde kakpakɔ kammɔ ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na lɛ́nu ka bákalɛ ɔban ɔmɛni kɔyakun kɔlɛmikɔ ƒui bényene.

english_verse: The Lord said: I, the Lord God of Israel, came through this gate, so it must remain closed forever! No one must ever use it.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Ɔban ɔmɛni kayakun na ami Unwoti Israel Katɔti lɛ́sia líbo. Anwuɔsu ɔlɛka bakalɛ-nwu benyene usela uwi ƒui! Na ukyuli ɔni ɔsɔ utasia mmɔ uteduo iye ɔlɛ lɛnɔ.

english_verse: The ruler of Israel may come here to eat a sacrificial meal that has been offered to me, but he must use only the entrance room of this gate. People Who Are Not Allowed in the Temple
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔdi Israel lɛlɔ ɔkana na ɔsia ɔban ɔmɛni kemmo ɔtɔ kayakun uduo ubadi akpala ani na bábla béte-mi adila kedee na mmɔ kani na ɔdubɔkana na ɔsia.” Bétete Bekyuli Badi Kuƒi Ka Beduo Kakpakɔ Kemmo

english_verse: Then the man took me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I saw that the brightness of the Lord's glory had filled the temple, and I immediately bowed with my face to the ground.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔnana ɔmmɔ útiku-mi na bútásia ɔban kayakun kani na katɔ kakɛ na kakpakɔ anumi mmɔ. Na lɛ́nu kalɛ na Unwoti uukeye na bukeye bɔmmɔ bɔ́ƒɔ kakpakɔ mmɔ ƒui. Kɔnakunwi ni, líbo kalɔ na líti mina anumi líbi kalɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to give you the laws for my temple. So pay attention and listen carefully to what kind of people are allowed to come in the temple, and what kind are not.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, ndubo-ɔ ɔda bubo bɔni ndanku mina kakpakɔ bute. Anwuɔsu nu kaduɛ na ati bekyuli bani udu líte kuƒi ka beduo kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo ku bani na ńtete kuƒi. Ami Unwoti Katɔti muubó-mii ɔda kpakplaa ka bɛda bina likyulikpi ngba bulie bɛya.

english_verse: Tell those rebellious people of Israel: I, the Lord God, command you to stop your evil ways!
translation_verse: Su Israel kadi bekyuli bani náta bénye-mi lɛlɔ mmɔ anii ami Unwoti Katɔti muubó-ma ɔda ka bada bana likyulikpi ala bɔbla baya.

english_verse: My temple has been disgraced, because you have let godless, stubborn foreigners come here when sacrifices are being offered to me. You have sinned and have broken our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: Bɛ́kya mina kakpakɔ kammɔ kɔƒa na uwi ɔni na bɛ́ya na baƒɔ bani na balabu-mi na bebo atuɔkplu bébeduo mmɔ uwi ɔni na baabla akpala teete-mi. Bɛ́ƒiɔ-mi na bíbile lɛla kedee lɛni na línyimiku-mii.

english_verse: Instead of following the proper ways to worship me, you have put foreigners in charge of worship at my temple.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na ɔlɛka bɛsia ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ bɛkpa-mi ni, baƒɔ mmomu na bíti bínyene kenye ka bataanu lɛkpa lɛmmɔ lɛlɛ na mina kakpakɔ.

english_verse: And so I, the Lord God, say that no godless foreigner who disobeys me will be allowed in my temple. This includes any foreigner living in Israel. The Levites Are Punished The Lord said:
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na ami Unwoti Katɔti mɔɔsu nnii naaawia ɔƒɔ biala na ulábu-mi na ɔdi mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ka uduo mina kakpakɔ. Na ɔmɛni ɔdanku baƒɔ bani nli Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ.” Unwoti Ɔ́ni Lewiƒuɔ Kɔtu

english_verse: Some of the Levites turned their backs on me and joined the other people of Israel in worshiping idols. So these Levites must be punished!
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Lewiƒuɔ bani bénwini kama bákya-mi na basiaku bana kadi bekyuli badi na baakpá baƒiɔ. Anwuɔsu ɔdi ka bani Lewiƒuɔ bamɛni kɔtu!

english_verse: They will still be allowed to serve me as temple workers by guarding the gates and by killing the animals to be sacrificed and by helping the worshipers.
translation_verse: Ndubɔsɔ lite-ma kuƒi na bataabla kabla teete-mi na mina kakpakɔ aani kayakun bɔgyumana ku bebuo bani na badubuti bakpa-mi bɔdu na beteebunku bakpane bammɔ.

english_verse: But because these Levites served the people of Israel when they worshiped idols, I, the Lord God, promise that the Levites will be punished. They did not stop the Israelites from sinning,
translation_verse: Nsu ka Lewiƒuɔ bamɛni bébunku Israelƒuɔ na bákpa baƒiɔ ɔsu ni, ami Unwoti Katɔti líse kenye kpakplaa ka bani Lewiƒuɔ kɔtu, ɔsika bátabala Israelƒuɔ na benwini na baƒiɔ bɔkpa kama.

english_verse: and now I will no longer let the Levites serve as my priests or come near anything sacred to me. They must suffer shame and disgrace for their disgusting sins.
translation_verse: Ka ɔ́si ɔƒɛni ni, nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo bɔya na Lewiƒuɔ badi mina bakpane iye bani bede mina ala ani nse kedee muedi. Ɔsika ɔdi ka kɔƒa kukpo-ma na anumi ewi-ma kalɔ na bebo abi lɛnɔ na ekpidi ani na bábla na eesé lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: They will be responsible for all the hard work that must be done in the temple. Rules for Priests The Lord said:
translation_verse: Na kabla kpakplaa biala na ɔlɛka babla na kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo ni, ama ndubo-ka bɔbla.” Béte Bakpane Bammɔ Ɔda Bubo Bɔdi

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe who are descendants of Zadok the priest were faithful to me, even when the rest of the Israelites turned away. And so, these priests will continue to serve as my priests and to offer the fat and the blood of sacrifices.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Lewi kɔdua bebi bani ndi bakpane na bási Sadok ɔtɔ kemmo ni, bátalɛmi kama uwi ɔni na Israelƒuɔ bénwini kama bákya-mi. Anwuɔsu ama kani ndubo bakpane kabla butaabla teete-mi. Na ama ndubo bebuo ubugya ku lɛmwi buteeti taakpa-mi.

english_verse: They will come into my temple, where they will offer sacrifices at my altar and lead others in worship.
translation_verse: Ama ndubuduo mina kakpakɔ na babla akpala bete-mi na batɔnku bakladi na lɛkpa lɛmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: When they come to the inner courtyard, they must wear their linen priestly clothes. My priests must never wear anything made of wool when they are on duty in this courtyard or in the temple.
translation_verse: “Si uwi ɔni na bébeduo mina kakpakɔ kaduli geen kani nkya kemmo ƒui ni, ɔdi ka banu ka bada ɔkpane adala ani ndi kugyii evuo awu kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ mmɔ. Útalɛ ka mina ɔkpane ɔdi ɔkya awu ɔni béti unwo iye bebuo linwini bábla uwi ɔni na unye mina kabla kadi lɛlɔ na kaduli kamɛni kemmo iye kakpakɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Even their turbans and underwear must be made of linen to keep my priests from sweating when they work.
translation_verse: Bana lɛdiku lɛni na beebi lili ku awu ɔlɔndi ɔni nda-ma kavobi muedi ɔlɛka ɔbla awu kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ ɔmmɔ udu kalɛ ewulu asɔ alatuku-ma si baabla kabla.

english_verse: And before they leave to join the other people in the outer courtyard, they must take off their priestly clothes, then place them in the sacred rooms and put on their regular clothes. That way, no one will touch their sacred clothes and be harmed.
translation_verse: Na asa na badubɔlɛ kakpakɔ mmɔ lɛnɔ ni, ɔdi bedie ɔkpane adala ammɔ bese likpo kedee lɛni na báklibi bése na lɛtɔ lɛmmɔ kemmo na beti ama alati adala bada asa na basɔ batásalaku bana bekyuli na kaduli kemmo mmɔ. Si bábla lɛni ni, ukyuli bamba ɔdi ulétuku adala ammɔ na weboku ɔgbankpi nwuna lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Priests must never shave their heads when they are mourning. But they must keep their hair properly trimmed and not let it grow too long.
translation_verse: “Ɔɔɔdi ka bakpane bekpeyi bana lili linwini si beewulo kɔnyana. Nsu ɔlɛka bada bana linwini edu na lileyi lilagya.

english_verse: They must not drink wine before going to the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Útalɛ ka bani ntɛ asa na besie kakpakɔ kaduli geen kemmo mmɔ.

english_verse: A priest must not marry a divorced woman; he can marry only a virgin from Israel or the widow of another priest.
translation_verse: “Útalɛ ka ɔkpane uti uleku ɔni na ukyuli ɔdi úuti ɔ́nyonu. Adagyaa kani na ɔdi uti ɔsiku Israel kadi bekyuli akɔ iye ɔkpane bamba ukpinele.

english_verse: Priests must teach my people the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary, and between what is clean and what is unclean.
translation_verse: “Ɔdi ka bakpane bammɔ batina bekyuli kavumana kani nkya ala ani nse kedee ku ala keeke ntɛ. Na batina-ma ala ani nse sɛɛn ku ani neeese sɛɛn ntɛ.

english_verse: They will make decisions in difficult legal cases, according to my own laws. They must also observe the religious festivals my Law requires and must always respect the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Na badubɔbla kabla aani litemi batɛne na baklibi unyeƒi biala basiaku mina bunyimi lɛlɔ. Na ama alati badubɔbla basiaku mina litemi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ na batɔnku bekyuli na mina emeyi buni bɔdi lɛlɔ, na babla mina lɛnwunameyi lɛnɔ kedee.

english_verse: Touching a dead body will make a person unclean. So a priest must not go near a dead body, unless it is one of his parents or children, or his brother or unmarried sister.
translation_verse: “Si ukyuli ɔdi útuku ukpine ni, úbile lɛlɔ likisi na ɔsɔ uuuse sɛɛn. Anwuɔsu utalɛ ka bakpane bani bede bekpine si ɔɔɔdi nwuna bawɔne iye bebi iye banwani bananabi iye belekubi bani neeelie kɔgya kani.

english_verse: If a priest touches a dead body, he is unclean and must go through a ceremony to make himself clean. Then seven days later,
translation_verse: Si ɔkpane ɔdi útuku ukpine ni, úbile lɛlɔ likisi na ɔsɔ uuuse sɛɛn. Na ɔlɛka ɔbla lɛlɔ bɔbla sɛɛn ɔdi. Na emeyi maatɛ kama ni,

english_verse: he must go to the inner courtyard of the temple and offer a sacrifice for sin. After that, he may once again serve as my priest. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: ɔdi ka usie kakpakɔ kaduli geen kani nkya kemmo ƒui na utábla likpidi lili buvele akpala. Na ɔmmɔ kama asa na ɔsɔ ɔkana na utaabla mina kabla aani ɔkpane kalɛ. Ami Unwoti Katɔti násu.

english_verse: I myself will provide for my priests, and so they won't receive any land of their own.
translation_verse: “Ami ɔlati ndubo mina bakpane lɛlɔ butaanu, anwuɔsu beeebo kadikɔ kalɔ kadi bele bete-ma.

english_verse: Instead, they will receive part of the grain sacrifices, as well as part of the sacrifices for sin and sacrifices to make things right. They will also be given everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me.
