translation_verse: Na lɛla lɛni na badubule bete-ma kenye ni, antabi udu etela ani na bekyuli badubuti babakpa bete-mi ku ekpidi lili buvele akpala ani na bekyuli badubɔbla unwi bɔbla akpala ni, badubɔƒɔ ana kakɛ kadi. Na lɛla biala na Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ na bábla-ni kedee bése sɛsɛɛ béte-mi ni, ɔdi bana lɛdi.

english_verse: The first part of every harvest will belong to the priests. They will also receive part of all special gifts and offerings the Israelites bring to me. And whenever any of my people bake bread, they will give their first loaf as an offering to the priests, and I will bless the homes of the people when they do this.
translation_verse: Na edula edeedi biala na báƒɛ lɛnɔ adi bakpane bammɔ. Na ala ani na ukyuli ɔdi úse kenye na adi etela ni, ama lɛnɔ badubɔkɛ kakɛ kadi. Lɛni kani si bodobodo na mina kadi bekyuli akɔ ɔdi úƒi ni, na uti udeedi uboku bakpane bammɔ, na ndubute ukyuli ɔmmɔ kusɛ kusɛ anwu ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ƒui si bábla ɔmɛni.

english_verse: Priests must not eat any bird or animal that dies a natural death or that has been killed by a wild animal.
translation_verse: “Bakpane beeebo kuƒi ka bakun aasɛ iye ebuo ɔni na anwu alati nékpi nwuna kukpi iye eƒiebuo.”

english_verse: So from now on, you must use honest weights and measures.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ni, biti unu ku bumomo akɔkula abuni bitaakɔku ala teete bekyuli.

english_verse: The Festival of Shelters will begin on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and will continue for seven days. On each day of this festival, the ruler will provide the same number of animals that he did each day during Passover, as well as the same amount of grain and olive oil for the sacrifices.
translation_verse: “Nvo kemmo bɔkya emeyi bɔdi bɔdubuse kalɔ na kɔbuli maatɛdi kɔni baalɔ na Hebri kemmo banii Tisri iye Etanim limeyi leevu-lɛlɔndi lɛlɔ. Na badubɔdi limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛni laa emeyi maatɛ. Na bebuo bani kani na úboku ku atabi ku ɔlaaƒɔ ku nnɔ bumomo bɔmmɔ kani na ɔdi ka uboku na beti babla akpala ammɔ.”

english_verse: The regions west and east of my sacred land and the city of Jerusalem will belong to the ruler of Israel. He will be given the region between the western edge of my land and the Mediterranean Sea, and between the eastern edge of my land and the Jordan River. This will mean that the length of his property will be the same as the sections of land given to the tribes. This property will belong to every ruler of Israel, so they will always be fair to my people and will let them live peacefully in the land given to their tribes. Israel's Rulers Must Be Honest
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Ɔmii ɔni nwi mina ɔmii ɔni na bídie bíse sɛsɛɛ mmɔ ɔƒɛ katukɔ ku ɔƒɛ kanukɔ ku Yerusalem ƒui ɔdubɔbla Israel lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔdi. Na ɔ́si mina kalɔ kawɔlɔkɔ na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ útédu Mediterenia Ɛpu ntɛ ku ɔmii ɔni nwi ɔ́si mina kalɔ kammɔ kawɔlɔkɔ na ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ útédu Yordan Ketu ntɛ ƒui ɔdubɔbla anwu ɔdi. Na ɔɔtina ka kalɔ kammɔ bune ɔdubɔbla aani kesii kani na béte adua ammɔ ƒui. “Na kese kamɛni kadubɔbla lɛlɔ ɔdine biala ɔni melie madi Israel lɛlɔ ɔdi.” Ɔlɛka Israel Lɛlɔ Badine Basu Litemi Geen Lɛmmɔ

english_verse: The Lord God said: You leaders of Israel have cheated and abused my people long enough! I want you to stop sinning and start doing what is right and fair. You must never again force my people off their own land. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti ɔnini, “Amii Israel batɔnkune, bíiyu na bɛ́nya mina kadi bekyuli bɛ́kya uwi útu! Na mɔɔwia ka bɛda ekpidi bɔbla bɛya na bise kalɔ bitaabla ala siin taasiaku ulu lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́sɔ útalɛka binye mina bekyuli lɛlɔ na bɛbɔku-ma na bavi balɛ bana kalɔ lɛlɔ. Ami Unwoti násu.

english_verse: The ephah will be the standard dry measure, and the bath will be the standard liquid measure. Their size will be based on the homer, which will equal ten ephahs or ten baths.
translation_verse: Na biti anta lɛkyami bɔkɔku binwini lɛla lɛni biti bitaakɔku edula ebi teete bekyuli. Na ɔsii keyile kenwini lɛla lɛni na biti bitaakɔku nnɔ ku ala ani na beedú taakɔku ala ammɔ udu teete bekyuli. Na ala amɛni ƒui akana na akɔ etédu kangyi keyile.

english_verse: The same ceremony must also be done on the seventh day of the month, so that anyone who sins accidentally or without knowing it will be forgiven, and so that my temple will remain holy.
translation_verse: “Na ɔdi ka babla limeyi bɔdi ablala amɛni na kɔbuli kɔmmɔ limeyi maatɛdi lɛnɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔya na si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́bla likpidi lɛdi na tati tati kemmo iye likpidi lɛmmɔ líyu-nwu lɛ́tu ni, na liti lɛkyiɛ-nwu kalɛ na kakpakɔ kammɔ kedee.

english_verse: Leaders of Israel, the people must bring you one sixtieth of their grain harvests as offerings to me.
translation_verse: “Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune, bɛya na bekyuli bammɔ bele bana anta ani na bákɛ akpa liti ku leevu na beti lɛkpa linwi beboku-mi aani bana etela.

english_verse: They will also bring one percent of their olive oil. These things will be measured according to the bath, and ten baths is the same as one homer or one cor.
translation_verse: Na bele nnɔ bɔni na bákɛ lɛnɔ akpa eti anyɔ na beti lɛkpa linwi beboku-mi. Na nnɔ ɔsii unengudi ɔni na baakɔ́ku ala na badubuti bakɔku bumomo bɔmɛni beboku-mi.

english_verse: The people of Israel will bring you these offerings.
translation_verse: “Israel kadi bekyuli ndubuti etela amɛni beboku-ɔ.

english_verse: But during New Moon Festivals, Sabbath celebrations, and other religious feasts, you leaders will be responsible for providing animals for the sacrifices, as well as the grain and wine. All these will be used for the sacrifices for sin, the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices to please me, and those to ask my blessing. I will be pleased and will forgive the sins of my people. The Festivals (Exodus
translation_verse: Nsu kɔbuli kɔwɔdi bɔlɛ emeyi bɔdi ku Lɛnwunameyi ku emeyi kedee bamba bɔdi ni, amii batɔnkune bammɔ na ɔlɛka bite bebuo bani na badubuti babla akpala ammɔ. Na amii kani ndubute kamu ku antabi udu biala ku ntɛ bɔni na badubuti babla akpala ammɔ. Na ala amɛni ƒui na badubuti babla adila bɔsia lɛkpabi lɛlɔ teete-mi ku ekpidi lili buvele ku unwi bɔbla akpala ku kalɛ na bevele kusɛ kusɛ basiku-mi kudɔ. Na ɔmɛni ɔdubɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ na liti mina bekyuli ekpidi lɛkyiɛ-ma.” Kalɛ Na Ɔlɛka Badi Emeyi Buni

english_verse: Each day of the festival he is to bring seven bulls and seven rams as sacrifices to please me, and he must bring a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Na limeyi biala na emeyi amɛni bɔdi kemmo ni, ɔdi ka uboku ɔmantɛ bakɔ maatɛ ku baƒonu maatɛ na beti babla akpala ani ndubɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ. Na uboku ese lɛnɔ na beti-nwu babla ekpidi lili buvele akpala. Na ɔdi ka banu ka bebuo bamɛni ƒui ɔdi útasɔ na kesii kadi.

english_verse: The Lord God said: On the first day of the first month, a young bull that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to purify the temple.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Na kɔbuli kudeedi kɔni baalɔ Abib iye Nisan na Hebri lɛdi kemmo limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka beti ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔkɔdi ɔni na útasɔ kesii kadi badu babla akpala na babla kakpakɔ kammɔ sɛɛn.

english_verse: The priest will take some blood from this sacrifice and smear it on the doorposts of the temple, as well as on the four corners of the altar and on the doorposts of the gates that lead into the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Na ɔkpane ɔmmɔ uti ebuo ɔmmɔ ubugya ɔdi ɔkwaa kakpakɔ kammɔ kɔyakun ligyii lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ku lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ ƒui. Na ɔkwaa ɔban kɔyakun kɔni na baasia teeduo kakpakɔ kaduli geen kani nkya-ka kemmo mmɔ ligyii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, and continuing for seven days, everyone will celebrate Passover and eat bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: “Na ɔ́si kɔbuli kudeedi kɔmɛni limeyi leevu-linedi lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛka ukyuli biala use kalɔ ku Kukpi Lili Bɔvia limeyi bɔdi utálɛ limeyi maatɛdi lɛlɔ. Na bodobodo ɔni kemmo na bátakya bɔnyii na ukyuli biala ɔdubɔdi.

english_verse: On the first day, the ruler will bring a bull to offer as a sacrifice for his sins and for the sins of the people.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ni, ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ ɔdubuti ɔmantɛ akɔ uboku na bakpa aani anwu ɔlati ekpidi lili buvele ku bekyuli bammɔ ƒui ekpidi lili buvele.

english_verse: He will also provide nine kilograms of grain and three liters of olive oil to be offered with each bull and each ram.
translation_verse: Na ɔdi ka uboku edula ebi ɔlaaƒɔ akyami aani leevu ku nnɔ lɛsii ine na beti bakpa ku ɔmantɛ akɔ unwi ku koƒonu kunwi biala.

english_verse: The Lord said: The east gate of the inner courtyard must remain closed during the six working days of each week. But on the Sabbath and on the first day of the month, this gate will be opened.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Na emeyi aku ani na bekyuli badubuti babla bana kabla na uyolu unwi kemmo ƒui ni, ɔdi ka bakalɛ kakpakɔ geen ɔban kayakun kani nésie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Nsu na Lɛnwunameyi ku limeyi lideedi na kɔbuli kemmo ni, ɔdi ka bakɛmi-ka bewi.

english_verse: Israel's ruler will go from the outer courtyard into the entrance room of this gate and stand in the doorway while the priest offers sacrifices to ask my blessing and sacrifices to please me. The ruler will bow with his face to the ground to show that he has worshiped me. Then he will leave, and the gate will remain open until evening.
translation_verse: Na Israel ɔtɔnkune ɔdubɔsi kaduli kedeedi kemmo na ɔsia uduo ɔtɔ ɔni kemmo na baasia teeduo ɔban ɔmɛni kemmo. Na ubenye kayakun na uwi ɔni na ɔkpane unye ɔɔbla akpala teevele mina kusɛ kusɛ ku unwi bɔbla ute bekyuli bammɔ. Uwi ɔmmɔ ni, ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔyu ubi anumi kalɔ ɔtina kalɛ na ɔɔkya lili kalɔ teete-mi, na ɔmmɔ kama na ɔtɔlɔ mmɔ na kayakun kammɔ kasɔ kewi lɛni utédu useyi uwi.

english_verse: Each Sabbath and on the first day of each month, the people of Israel must also come to the east gate and worship me.
translation_verse: “Na Lɛnwunameyi biala lɛlɔ ku kɔbuli biala limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ni, ɔdi ka Israel kadi bekyuli bebo ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔban kenye mmɔ na babakya lili kalɔ bete-mi na mmɔ.

english_verse: On the Sabbath, the ruler will bring six lambs and one ram to be offered as sacrifices to please me. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: Na Lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ ni, ɔtɔnkune ɔdi ka uboku baƒonu bakɔdi ɛku ku koƒonu kɔgyani na beti babla akpala ani ndubɔyɔ-mi kaƒɔ bete-mi. Na bebuo bammɔ batasɔ na kesii kadi.

english_verse: With the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Na ɔdi uti antabi akyami aani leevu ubunku koƒonu kɔgyani kɔmmɔ. Na baƒonu bakɔdi bammɔ ama ni, ɔkana na uboku kalɛ na anwu ɔlati ɔɔyɔ́.

english_verse: The ruler is to bring six lambs, a bull, and a ram to be offered as sacrifices at the New Moon Festival. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: “Ɔƒɛni si kɔbuli kɔwɔdi kɔ́sia ni, ɔdi ka ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ uboku baƒonu bakɔdi ɛku ku ɔmantɛ akɔ ku koƒonu kɔgyani na beti babla limeyi bɔdi akpala ammɔ. Na bebuo bammɔ batasɔ na kesii kadi.

english_verse: With the bull and the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Na ɔmantɛ akɔ iye koƒonu kɔgyani ni, ɔdi ka uti antabi akyami leevu ɔsia ku lɛlɔ uboku-mi. Na baƒonu bakɔdi ama ni, ɔkana na uboku kalɛ na ɔɔyɔ́. Na ɔdi ka uti nnɔ lɛsii ine ubunku antabi akyami leevu biala lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The ruler must come through the entrance room of the east gate and leave the same way.
translation_verse: “Si ɔga úbo ubakpa-mi ni, ɔban kayakun kani na ɔ́sia úduo ni, mmɔ kani na ɔdubɔsia ɔlɛ.

english_verse: When my people come to worship me during any festival, they must always leave by the opposite gate from which they came: Those who come in the north gate must leave by the south gate, and those who come in the south gate must leave by the north gate.
translation_verse: Nsu si mina kadi bekyuli bébo bábakpa-mi na limeyi bɔdi biala kemmo ni, ɔdi ka basia kayakun bamba batɔlɔ na ɔɔɔdi kani na básia béduo. Anwuɔsu si kayakun katɔdi na ásia éduo ni, ɔdi ka asia kadani alɛ. Na si kadani lɛnɔ na ásia éduo ni, ɔdi ka asia katɔdi alɛ.

english_verse: Their ruler will come in at the same time they do and leave at the same time they leave.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni kani na bekyuli bammɔ ƒui beeduo ni, uwi ɔmmɔ kani na bana ɔtɔnkune lɛnɔ uduo. Lɛni kani na ɔlɛka basiaku lɛlɔ balɛ uwi unwi.

english_verse: At all other festivals and celebrations, nine kilograms of grain will be offered with a bull, and nine kilograms will be offered with a ram. The worshipers can offer as much grain as they want with each lamb. Three liters of olive oil must be offered with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: “Na emeyi bamba biala bɔdi kemmo ni, ɔdi ka antabi akyami leevu na beti bebunku ɔmantɛ akɔ ɔmmɔ. Na beti akyami leevu ammɔ kani bebunku koƒonu kɔgyani akpala lɛnɔ. Nsu bekyuli bani nébo bababla akpala ammɔ bakana na beti antabi akyami ani na baayɔ́ bebunku baƒonu bakɔdi bammɔ ɔdi biala anwu lɛlɔ. Na beti nnɔ lɛsii ine bebunku antabi akyami leevu biala lɛlɔ.

english_verse: If the ruler voluntarily offers a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, the east gate of the inner courtyard will be opened for him. He will offer his sacrifices just as he does on each Sabbath; then he will leave, and the gate will be closed.
translation_verse: “Na si kaƒɔ ƒaa etela na ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ úti úboku ɔnii ubabla unwi bɔbla akpala iye uvele-mi na lite-nwu kusɛ kusɛ ni, badubɔlɛmi kakpakɔ geen kaduli ɔban kayakun kani na ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ bete-nwu. Na ɔdubɔbla nwuna akpala aani kalɛ kani na ɔɔbla na Lɛnwunameyi biala lɛlɔ. Na si ɔ́tɔlɔ ni, na bakalɛ kayakun kammɔ.

english_verse: Each morning a year-old lamb that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to please me.
translation_verse: “Na ɔtanta biala ni, koƒonu kɔkɔdi kɔni na kútasɔ na ɔdi ka beti bakpa bete-mi na kaƒɔ kayɔ-mi.

english_verse: Along with it, two kilograms of fine flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice. This law will never change—
translation_verse: Na ɔdi ka beti ɔlaaƒɔ akɔkɔ leevu bebunku nnɔ ɔsii unwi. Na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bulavumana úti úsela uwi ƒui.

english_verse: The Lord God said: If the ruler of Israel gives some of his land to one of his children, it will belong to the ruler's child as part of the family property.
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti ɔnini, “Si Israel ɔtɔnkune ɔdi úti nwuna kalɔ kakɛ kadi úte ubidi ɔdi ni, kalɔ kammɔ kadubunwini ubidi kadi na kabla ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo kese.

english_verse: But if the ruler gives some of his land to one of his servants, the land will belong to the servant until the Year of Celebration, when it will be returned to the ruler. Only the ruler's children can keep what is given to them.
translation_verse: Nsu si ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ úti nwuna kalɔ kakɛ kadi úte nwuna kabla ɔblane ni, kadubunwini kabla ɔblane ɔmmɔ kadi butédu uwi ɔni na baadi bɔnwuna bɔkɛ lɛkwa limeyi, na kalɔ kammɔ kadubɔsɔ kenwini kesie ɔlati ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ kudɔ. Ɔsika ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ ubidi geen kani na mbo kuƒi ka uti ɔmii ɔni na béte-nwu unwini anwu ɔdi ƒui.

english_verse: The ruler must never abuse my people by taking land from them. Any land he gives his children must already belong to him. The Sacred Kitchens
translation_verse: “Ɔtɔnkune ɔdi utetile mina bekyuli bana kalɔ lɛlati bɔdi kuƒi na uƒie-ma kalɔ ɔƒɔ. Na kalɔ biala na ɔdubute ubidi ni, ɔti nwaa ka anwu ɔlati kadi na kadi ɔ́si kukuuku.” Bátina-mi Akpala Kanwakɔ Kedee

english_verse: The man who was showing me the temple then took me back to the inner courtyard. We walked to the south side of the courtyard and stopped at the door to the sacred rooms that belonged to the priests. He showed me more rooms at the western edge of the courtyard
translation_verse: Ɔnana ɔni mɔɔtina-mi kakpakɔ ala mɛni ni, ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kpanku-mi úsienku kakpakɔ kaduli geen kemmo. Na búti bɔ́sia kaduli kammɔ kada kakɛ na bútédi búnye lɛtɔ lɛni na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ béte bakpane mmɔ kayakun. Mmɔ na ɔ́tina-mi lɛtɔ pii úbu na kakpakɔ kaduli kammɔ ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ

english_verse: We went back to the outer courtyard and walked past the four corners.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama búnwini búsie kaduli kedeedi kemmo na bɔ́sia bɔvi lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Around the inside of these smaller courtyards was a low wall of stones, and against the wall were places to build fires.
translation_verse: Na béti atabi bátu kowodu klukwii kɔdi bámana kɔduli kɔmɛni ɔdi biala kɔmadɔ kɔmadɔ. Na bálɛ asi bámana awodu amɛni lɛlɔ kudɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: The man said, “These are the kitchens where the temple workers will boil the meat that worshipers offer as sacrifices.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔnana ɔmɛni ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Mmɔ na kakpakɔ kabla bebunkune beeƒulo lɛna lɛni na bekyuli bani nébo babakpa Katɔti béboku.”

english_verse: The man took me back to the temple, where I saw a stream flowing from under the entrance. It began in the south part of the temple, where it ran past the altar and continued east through the courtyard.
translation_verse: Ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kpanku-mi na búnwini búsie kakpakɔ kemmo mmɔ. Na mmɔ na lɛ́nu ketu blii kadi ka kaagbá taasi kayakun kammɔ kalɔ. Kése kalɔ kási kakpakɔ kammɔ kada kakɛ na ɔ́gba ɔkɛ lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ na ɔ́gba ɔkɛ kaduli kammɔ kemmo úsela ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: We walked out of the temple area through the north gate and went around to the east gate. I saw the small stream of water flowing east from the south side of the gate.
translation_verse: Bɔ́gyu bɔ́tɔlɔ kakpakɔ amadɔ mmɔ na bɔkɛ bútávi ɔban kayakun katɔdi kudɔ na bɔ́ka bɔ́mana bútédu ɔban kayakun kani na ɔƒɛ katukɔ. Na lɛ́nu ka ketu blii kammɔ kágba késela ɔƒɛ kanukɔ ɔ́si ɔban kayakun kani na kada kakɛ mmɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay attention to what you've seen.” We walked to the riverbank,
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Esekiel, ɔyawine ubi, se atu na enu lɛla lɛdi asiku ala ani na ánu lɛlɔ.” Bɔ́sia búsie ketu kammɔ kɔtu.

english_verse: where I saw dozens of trees on each side.
translation_verse: Na ntánu egyii pii ka enye ketu ɔvi ɔnanyɔ.

english_verse: The man said: This water flows eastward to the Jordan River valley and empties into the Dead Sea, where it turns the salt water into fresh water.
translation_verse: Na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ntu bɔmɛni bɔ́gba bɔkɛ ɔƒɛ kanukɔ mɛni búsela Yordan Ketu ɔkwalɛ kemmo na bɔdubo kenye buti butákya Ɛpugyie kemmo kesii kani na ɔdubo mma ntu bɔmmɔ bunwini bɔbla ntu bɔbuni mamaama bɔni mɔɔdia bɔni.

english_verse: Wherever this water flows, there will be all kinds of animals and fish, because it will bring life and fresh water to the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Na kesi kesii na ntu bɔmɛni bɔ́gba bɔkɛ ni, ketu kemmo lɛna ku kɔbɛ lidu lidu badubo mmɔ bɔkya. Ɔsika ɔdubo ngba ku ntu bɔbuni bɔni mɔɔdia bɔni buti buboku Ɛpugyie kemmo.

english_verse: From En-Gedi to Eneglaim, people will fish in the sea and dry their nets along the coast. There will be as many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea as there are in the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Engedi útédu Eneglaim ɔma bekyuli badubo kɔbɛ buteedie na mmɔ na bakula bana lɛsawu na ɛpu kɔtu mmɔ. Na kɔbɛ lidu pii kɔdubɔkya Ɛpugyie kemmo aani kalɛ na kɔkya Mediterenia Ɛpu kemmo.

english_verse: But the marshes along the shore will remain salty, so that people can use the salt from them.
translation_verse: Nsu lɛba lɛni ndubɔkya ɛpu amadɔ mmɔ ani ni, mma bɔdubɔkya-ni kemmo kalɛ na bekyuli bakɛ-mu bedie.

english_verse: Fruit trees will grow all along this river and produce fresh fruit every month. The leaves will never dry out, because they will always have water from the stream that flows from the temple, and they will be used for healing people. The Borders of the Land
translation_verse: Adingyii pii adubɔkwɛ ketu kamɛni kɔtu na ataanwu ebi kɔbuli biala. Na evete ammɔ aaadubo bɔkwii bɔnu kudii, ɔsika adubo ntu butaakɛ uwi biala taasiku ketu kani mɔɔgbá taasi kakpakɔ kudɔ mmɔ na bekyuli badubuti evete ammɔ babwi bekyuli.” Básia Kalɔ Kammɔ Lɛmii

english_verse: The Lord God said to the people of Israel: When the land is divided among the twelve tribes of Israel, the Joseph tribe will receive two shares. Divide the land equally, because I promised your ancestors that this land would someday belong to their descendants. These are the borders of the land:
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́su Israel kadi bekyuli ɔnini, “Si uwi ɔni na béle kalɔ kammɔ béte Israel adua leevu-anyɔ ammɔ ni, Yoseƒ kɔdua bekyuli badubɔƒɔ bule akpa anyɔ. Na ka éle kalɔ kammɔ likeke, ɔsika ami nése ƒula bati kukuuku kenye ka ndubuti kalɔ kamɛni lite bana. Na ndubɔtina-a kalɔ kammɔ lɛmii.

english_verse: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean Sea, then continue eastward to Hethlon, to Lebo-Hamath, then across to Zedad,
translation_verse: “Ɔmii ɔni na katɔ kakɛ ɔdubuse kalɔ ɔsi Mediterenia Ɛpu kudɔ na uti usie ɔƒɛ katukɔ utédu Hetlon ɔma. Na ɔkɛ Lebo Hamat ɔ́via Sedad.

english_verse: Berothah, and Sibraim, which is on the border between the two kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The border will end at Hazer-Hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛ Berota ku Sibraim lɛma lɛni nwi Damasko ku Hamat lɛgakadikɔ kalɔ ɔmii lɛlɔ. Na utáwɔlɔ na Hasa-Hatikon ɔni nkya Hauran ɔmii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: So the northern border will run between the Mediterranean Sea and Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔmii ɔni na katɔ kakɛ ɔmii ɔdubɔvi Mediterenia Ɛpu ku Hasar-Enan ɔni nkya Damasko ku Hamat ɔmii lɛlɔ ntɛ.

english_verse: The eastern border will begin on the border between the two kingdoms of Hauran and Damascus. It will run south along the Jordan River, which separates the territories of Gilead and Israel, and it will end at the Dead Sea near the town of Tamar.
translation_verse: “Na ɔmii ɔni na ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ ɔmii ɔdubuse kalɔ ɔsi ɔmii ɔni nkya Damasko ku Hauran lɛga kadikɔ kalɔ ɔmii lɛlɔ. Na ɔdubuti ɔyu kada kakɛ na ɔkɛ Yordan Ketu kani néle Gilead ku Israel kɔlɛkɛ. Na ɔdubusie útáwɔlɔ na Ɛpugyie na kesii kani nde Tama ɔma.

english_verse: The southern border will begin at Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and will end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: “Na ɔmii ɔni na kada kakɛ ɔdubuse kalɔ ɔsi Tama na ɔkɛ kada kada na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ útédu abiɔ ani na Meriba-Kades. Na ɔdubɔsia Egyipteƒuɔ ɔmii lɛlɔ utédu Mediterenia Ɛpu.

english_verse: The western border will run north along the Mediterranean Sea to a point just west of Lebo-Hamath.
translation_verse: “Na ɔmii ɔni na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ ɔdubuse kalɔ ɔsi Mediterenia Ɛpu utédu kesii kani mma Hamat na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ.

english_verse: That is the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: “Kalɔ kani nkya ntɛ bɔmɛni na badubo bule bute Israel adua ammɔ.

english_verse: It will belong to the Israelites and to any foreigners living among them whose children were born in Israel. These foreigners must be treated like any other Israelite citizen, and they will receive
translation_verse: Kadubo Israelƒuɔ kadi bunwini ku baƒɔ bani ƒui nkya-ma kudɔ na báwɔ béte Israelƒuɔ. Ɔdi ka banu baƒɔ bamɛni aani Israelƒuɔ bebi na bada-ma lɛni kani na bele kalɔ kammɔ

english_verse: a share of the land given to the tribe where they live. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: kakɛ kadi bete-ma na kɔdua kɔni kemmo na bakya. Ami Unwoti Katɔti násu.”

english_verse: Each tribe will receive a section of land that runs from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. The northern border of Israel will run along the towns of Hethlon and Lebo-Hamath, and will end at Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between the kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The tribes will receive their share of land in the following order, from north to south: Dan, Asher, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, Reuben, and Judah. The Special Section of Land The Lord said:
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Kalɔ kani nwi kási Israel kalɔ ɔmii ɔni ntɛ ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ ɔ́yu útédu Mediterenia Ɛpu na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ ni, kɔdua biala bekyuli badubo kalɔ kammɔ bule lɛkpa lɛdi bɔkɛ. Na ɔmii ɔni ntɛ katɔ kakɛ ɔdubɔsia Hetlon ku Hamat lɛma na útáwɔlɔ na Hasar-Enan ɔni nkya Damasko ku Hamat lɛga kadikɔ kalɔ ntɛ ɔmii lɛlɔ. Na ndubɔtina-a ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na badubo kalɔ kammɔ bule bute adua ammɔ, Dan ku Aser ku Naƒtali ku Manase ku Eƒraim ku Ruben ku Yuda. Na ɔdubɔsi katɔ útédu kada.” Bédie Kalɔ Kadi Bése Sɛsɛɛ

english_verse: South of Judah's territory will be a special section of land. Its length will be twelve and a half kilometers, and its width will run from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. My temple will be located in this section of land.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Na Yuda kalɛkɛ kada kakɛ ni, mmɔ na mina kalɔ kani badubudie bese sɛsɛɛ kadubo bɔkya. Na kana bune ɔdi lɛma ntɛ eluku bɔkɔku maane. Na nwuna bɔbɛbɛ ɔdubɔsi Israel ɔmii ɔni nkya ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ úsie ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ útédu Mediterenia Ɛpu. Na mmɔ lɛnɔ na badubo mina kakpakɔ bɔtu.

english_verse: An area in the center of this land will belong to me. It will be twelve and a half kilometers long and ten kilometers wide.
translation_verse: “Kesii kadi na kalɔ kamɛni ntɛntɛ kadubɔbla mina ɔdi. Na kadubo bune eluku maane na kabɛbɛ eluku aku.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will give half of my sacred land to the priests. Their share will be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide, and my temple will be right in the middle.
translation_verse: “Ami Unwoti ndubo mina kalɔ kani na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ mɛni kakɛ buti bute bakpane. Na bana kakɛ kani medu-ma kadubune eluku maane úsie eluku atɛ bɔbɛbɛ. Na mina kakpakɔ kadubo ntɛntɛ bunye.

english_verse: Only priests who are descendants of Zadok will receive a share of this sacred land, because they remained faithful to me when the Levites and the rest of the Israelites started sinning.
translation_verse: Na bakpane bani nási Sadok ɔtɔ kemmo lɛti pɛ ndubo kadikɔ bɔkɛ na kalɔ kamɛni bule kemmo. Ɔsika ama kani násiaku-mi kama siin na bátalɛ-mi kama uwi ɔni na Lewiƒuɔ ku Israelƒuɔ bakladi bése kalɔ baabla ekpidi.

english_verse: The land belonging to the priests will be the most sacred area and will lie south of the area that belongs to the Levites.
translation_verse: Na bakpane kalɔ kamɛni kadubɔbla kedee ketulo ƒui na kadubɔkya Lewiƒuɔ kalɔ kada kakɛ.

english_verse: I will give the other half of my sacred land to the Levites. Their share will also be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide,
translation_verse: “Mina kalɔ kakɛ kakladi kani na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ mɛni ni, ndubuti-ka lite Lewiƒuɔ. Na kana bune bɔdi eluku maane na bɔbɛbɛ bɔdi eluku atɛ.

english_verse: and they must never sell or trade any of this land—it is the best land and belongs to me.
translation_verse: Na útalɛka beti kakɛ kadi beye iye beti-ka badi kuye. Ɔsika kalɔ kammɔ ndi kalɔ kabuni ƒui, na kadi mina kadi.

english_verse: South of my sacred land will be a section twelve and a half kilometers long and three kilometers wide. It will not be sacred, but will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem, together with its houses and pastureland.
translation_verse: “Na mina kalɔ kada kakɛ mmɔ lɛnɔ ɔdubɔbla eluku maane úsie eluku anyɔ bɔbɛbɛ ɔdubɔbla Israelƒuɔ ƒui ɔdi, na mmɔ na Yerusalem ɔma unengudi ɔdubo bɔkya ku bebuo kadikɔ ku bana lɛtɔ ƒui, nsu mmɔ ɔɔɔdi kesii kani na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ mɛni.

english_verse: The city will be a square: Each side will be two kilometers long,
translation_verse: Ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ lɛƒɛnyi ine bɔmmɔ ƒui bɔkɔku bɔdubo bulie. Na ɔƒɛnyi biala ɔdubo bɔbla liluku linwi ku kakɛ.

english_verse: The land on the east and west sides of the city limits will be farmland for the people of Jerusalem; both sections will be five kilometers long and three kilometers wide.
translation_verse: Na kalɔ kani nwi ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ ku ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ ɔ́si ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔmii lɛlɔ ɔdubo bunwini katumakɔ ute Yerusalem kadi bekyuli.

english_verse: People from the city will farm the land, no matter which tribe they belong to.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani nkya ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni kemmo ɔdi biala ɔkana na ɔtuma kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ na ɔɔɔda kɔdua kɔni ukyuli na ɔdi.

english_verse: And so the center of this special section of land will be for my sacred land, as well as for the city and its property. The land will be a square, twelve and a half kilometers on each side.
translation_verse: “Na kalɔ kamɛni ntɛntɛ na mina kalɔ kani bédie bése-mi sɛsɛɛ mmɔ kakya. Na kadi ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kadi ku kese. Na kana bune ku bɔbɛbɛ ƒui bɔdubɔbla unwi ɔni ndi eluku maane ɔƒɛnyi biala.

english_verse: The regions east and west of this square of land will belong to the ruler of Israel. His property will run east to the Jordan River and west to the Mediterranean Sea. In the very center of his property will be my sacred land, as well as the temple,
translation_verse: “Na kalɔ kani nwi ntɛ bɔmɛni kama kakɛ úsie ɔƒɛ katukɔ ku kanukɔ kadi Israel ɔtɔnkune kalɔ. Na nwuna kadikɔ kamɛni kakɛ késie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ útédu Yordan Ketu. Na ɔkɛ útédu Mediterenia na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ kakɛ. Na nwuna kalɔ kamɛni ntɛntɛ na mina kalɔ kani na bédie bése sɛsɛɛ mmɔ ku mina kakpakɔ kakya.

english_verse: together with the share belonging to the Levites and the city of Jerusalem. The northern border of the ruler's property will be the land that belongs to Judah, and the southern border will be the land that belongs to Benjamin. The Division of Land among Tribes in the South The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Na kadanku kesii kani ndi Lewiƒuɔ kadi ku kesii kani na Yerusalem ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ uwi. Na Israel lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔmɛni kalɔ ɔmii ɔni nkya katɔ kakɛ ni, mmɔ ndi Yuda kalɔ. Na nwuna ɔmii ɔni nkya kada kakɛ ni, mmɔ ndi Benyamin kalɔ.” Béle Kalɔ Béte Adua Ani Nka Kad Kakɛ

english_verse: South of this special section will be the land that belongs to the rest of Israel's tribes. Each tribe will receive a section of land that runs from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. The tribes will receive their share of land in the following order, from north to south: Benjamin, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, and Gad.
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti ɔnini, “Kalɔ kamɛni kada kakɛ ni, mmɔ ndi kalɔ kani na béti béte Israelƒuɔ adua akladi. Na kɔdua biala ɔdubɔƒɔ kalɔ kani nási ɔmii ɔni ntɛ ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔ́yu úsie ɔƒɔ kanukɔ útédu Mediterenia Ɛpu. Na ndubɔtina-a kalɛ na badubule kalɔ kammɔ ɔ́si katɔ útédu kada. Na ulu ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na badubo kalɔ kammɔ bɔƒɔ, Benyamin ku Simeon ku Isakar ku Sebulon ku Gad.

english_verse: Gad's southern border is also the southern border of Israel. It will begin at the town of Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: “Na Gad kalɔ ɔmii na kada kakɛ kani ndi Israel kalɔ kawɔlɔkɔ ɔmii. Na ɔdubuse kalɔ ɔsi Tama ɔma na ɔkɛ kada kada na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ útédu abiɔ ani nka Meriba-Kades. Na ɔkɛ útásia Egyipteƒuɔ ɔmii lɛlɔ na útáwɔlɔ na Mediterenia Ɛpu.

english_verse: That's how the land of Israel will be divided among the twelve tribes. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Gates of Jerusalem The Lord said:
translation_verse: “Lɛni na badubo kalɔ kammɔ bule bute Israelƒuɔ adua leevu-anyɔ ammɔ. Ami Unwoti Katɔti násu.” Yerusalem Ubo Ɔban Kɔyakun

english_verse: In the third year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia attacked Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na lɛkwa lɛtɛdi lɛni kemmo na Yehoiakim ɔɔdi lɛga na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, Babilonƒuɔ Ɔga Nebukadnesar úsie útékpo Yerusalem.

english_verse: The Lord let Nebuchadnezzar capture Jehoiakim and take away some of the things used in God's temple. And when the king returned to Babylonia, he put these things in the temple of his own god.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́ya na ɔ́di lɛlɔ na úƒie Yehoiakim ɔ́tɔlɔku, na úti ala adi bene ani beeti taabla kabla na Katɔti kakpakɔ lɛnɔ ɔ́tɔlɔku. Na uwi ɔni na Babilon ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ únwini úsie Babilon ni, úti ala ammɔ útése ɔtɔ na nwuna baƒiɔ kakpakɔ.

english_verse: One day the king ordered Ashpenaz, his highest palace official, to choose some young men from the royal family of Judah and from other leading Jewish families.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, ɔga ɔmɛni údie lɛdi úte nwuna kesii benengu ƒui ɔtɔnkune ɔni baalɔ banii Aspenas ɔnii ɔƒuna bakloƒu badi ɔsiku Israel bagadine ɔtɔ ku Yudaƒuɔ benengu bammɔ lɛnɔ akɔ.

english_verse: The king said, “They must be healthy, handsome, smart, wise, educated, and fit to serve in the royal palace. Teach them how to speak and write our language
translation_verse: Na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Nu ka bekyuli bammɔ bebo ɔlɔkplu kaduɛ na baadia bɔnu, na báda anu na bebo ababla, na badi bakutine lɛnɔ na bámanku ka babla kabla na ɔga kesii. Na atina-ma kalɛ na baatɛmi bula lɛdi ku bunweni lɛnɔ.

english_verse: and give them the same food and wine that I am served. Train them for three years, and then they can become court officials.”
translation_verse: Na eteete-ma adila ku ntɛ bɔni kani na beete-mi. Na atumini-ma akwa atɛ kalɛ na bakana na benwini litemi katɛkɔ kabla bablane.”

english_verse: Four of the young Jews chosen were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, all from the tribe of Judah.
translation_verse: Amu na báƒuna Yudaƒuɔ bakloƒu badi bani ndi Daniel ku Hanania ku Misael ku Asaria. Na bana ƒui bási Yuda kɔdua kemmo.

english_verse: But the king's chief official gave them Babylonian names: Daniel became Belteshazzar, Hananiah became Shadrach, Mishael became Meshach, and Azariah became Abednego.
translation_verse: Na unengu ɔmmɔ ɔ́sia-ma Babilonƒuɔ anyi. Na Daniel únwini Beltesasar, na Hanania únwini Sadrak, na Misael únwini Mesak, na Asaria únwini Abednego.

english_verse: Daniel made up his mind to eat and drink only what God had approved for his people to eat. And he asked the king's chief official for permission not to eat the food and wine served in the royal palace.
translation_verse: Nsu Daniel ɔ́bla kasusu ka lɛla lɛni kani na Katɔti úte kuƒi ka nwuna kadi bekyuli badi ni, ani kani na anwu ɔdubo bɔdi. Anwuɔsu úvele unengu ɔmmɔ kuƒi ka betete-nwu adila ku ntɛ bɔni na beete bekyuli bani nkya ɔga kesii mmɔ na baadi.

english_verse: God had made the official friendly and kind to Daniel.
translation_verse: Katɔti lɛnɔ ɔ́ya na ukyuli ɔmɛni ɔ́bla buɛɛ ɔkya Daniel aani ɔkpana kalɛ na ɔ́bla-nwu lɛƒɔndia.

english_verse: But the man still told him, “The king has decided what you must eat and drink. And I am afraid he will kill me, if you eat something else and end up looking worse than the other young men.”
translation_verse: Nsu unengu ɔmmɔ ɔ́ya na Daniel ɔ́ti ɔnini, “Ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔlati nálɛ ugyii lɛla lɛni na ɔdi ka beteete-mii na bitaadi na bitaani lɛnɔ úse. Anwuɔsu mɔɔyia ka ɔdubɔya na badu-mi si ɔƒɛni kalɛ amii bilakɛ lɛlɔ aani bina bakpana bakladi kalɛ na ala ani na ɔ́su mmɔ tadi tadi ɔsu.”

english_verse: The king's official had put a guard in charge of Daniel and his three friends. So Daniel said to the guard,
translation_verse: Ɔga ɔtalane unengu ɔmɛni ɔ́wia bagyumane úte Daniel ku nwuna bakpana ɛtɛ bakladi bammɔ. Anwuɔsu Daniel ɔ́su ɔgyumanane ɔmmɔ ɔnini,

english_verse: “For the next ten days, let us have only vegetables and water at mealtime.
translation_verse: “Na emeyi leevu ani ndubo kemmo mɛni ni, kɔku-bu nu. Si údu ɔdiwi ni, ya na beteete-bu lɛkpuna ku nwuna lɛlɔ akyala na butaadi, na butaani ntu.

english_verse: When the ten days are up, compare how we look with the other young men, and decide what to do with us.”
translation_verse: Na si uwi ɔni na emeyi leevu ammɔ édu ni, na eti-bu akɔku bakloƒu bakladi, na awɔ ɔlati anu kalɛ na adubɔbla-bu.”

english_verse: The guard agreed to do what Daniel had asked.
translation_verse: Ɔgyumanane ɔmɛni únu lɛla lɛni na Daniel ɔ́su, na ɔbla bana lɛƒɔyɔ úte-ma na emeyi leevu ammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Ten days later, Daniel and his friends looked healthier and better than the young men who had been served food from the royal palace.
translation_verse: Emeyi leevu kama ni, Daniel ku nwuna bakpana bákɛ lɛlɔ na baadia bɔnu teetulo bakloƒu bakladi bani na beete adila ani na beete ɔga kesii bekyuli bammɔ.

english_verse: After this, the guard let them eat vegetables instead of the rich food and wine.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si ɔmmɔ kama ni, lɛkpuna ala ammɔ kani na ɔ́ya na Daniel ku nwuna bakpana baadi, na adila abuni ku ntɛ bɔni na beete bakladi kenye.

english_verse: God made the four young men smart and wise. They read a lot of books and became well educated. Daniel could also tell the meaning of dreams and visions.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔ́ya na bakloƒu ine bamɛni báda anu na bebo ababla sɔsɔ. Báka lɛku pii na bénwini bakutine geen. Na Daniel anwu ɔɔkana na uudie ana kalɔ muedi ku kɔyu kemmo ala bɔnu taati ku ana kalɔ budie.

english_verse: At the end of the three-year period set by King Nebuchadnezzar, his chief palace official brought all the young men to him.
translation_verse: Amu ka uwi údu ka ɔga kabla ɔblane unengu ɔmɛni ɔ́kpanku bakloƒu bammɔ ƒui úboku ɔga anumi ni, úti-ma útényene Ɔga Nebukadnesar anumi.

english_verse: The king interviewed them and discovered that none of the others were as outstanding as Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they were given positions in the royal court.
translation_verse: Na ɔga ɔmmɔ úye-ma kenye kemmo etemila únu, na ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka ɔdi uuubo kenye ogya aani Daniel ku Hanania ku Misael ku Asaria. Anwuɔsu béte-ma kabla na ɔga litemi katɛkɔ.

english_verse: From then on, whenever the king asked for advice, he found their wisdom was ten times better than that of any of his other advisors and magicians.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si uwi ɔmmɔ úsela ni, si ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔɔwia kasusu na lɛla lɛdi lɛlɔ ni, nwuna bevone ku kasusu betine ƒui ɔdi ɔsɔ uledu bakloƒu ine bamɛni ɔdi munu munu!

english_verse: Daniel served there until the first year of King Cyrus.
translation_verse: Na Daniel ɔ́bla kabla na mmɔ úti útédu Ɔga Kores lɛga bɔdi uwi lɛkwa lideedi kemmo.

english_verse: During the second year that Nebuchadnezzar was king, he had such horrible nightmares that he could not sleep.
translation_verse: Na Nebukadnesar lɛga bɔdi lɛkwa linyɔdi kemmo ni, úteegye ana ani mɔɔda liƒu geen na ulákana bɔlɛɛ.

english_verse: So he called in his counselors, advisors, magicians, and wise men,
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔ́lɔ nwuna kasusu bakyane ku bevone ku kelisa benengu ku banundane ƒui ɔ́sala.

english_verse: and said, “I am disturbed by a dream that I don't understand, and I want you to explain it.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Kayi keekpóku-mi geen na kɔna kɔni lígye, na neeenu-ku kalɔ. Anwuɔsu mɔɔwia ka bidie-ku kalɔ bite-mi.”

english_verse: They answered in Aramaic, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever! We are your servants. Please tell us your dream, and we will explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Amu na bédie kenye na Siria lɛdi kemmo banini, “Bula Ɔga Ɔbune, bɔɔwia ka elie ngba uwi ƒui! Ƒula kabla bablane na bɔdi, anwuɔsu su-bu ƒula kɔna kɔni na égye na budie kuna kalɔ bute-ɔ.”

english_verse: But the king replied, “No! I have made up my mind. If you don't tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be chopped to pieces and your houses will be torn down.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔga ɔmmɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Oowo! Lɛ́ɛbla mina kasusu líse ka si bítasu-mi kɔna kɔni na lígye ku kuna kalɔ budie ni, ndubɔya na bekulo-mii eku eku bewi kalɔ na babwɛ-mii kɔduli lɛnɔ ƒui.

english_verse: However, if you do tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be greatly rewarded and highly honored. Now tell me the dream and explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Mmomu si bɛ́kana na bɛ́su-mi kɔna kɔmmɔ ku kuna kalɔ budie ni, bɛdubo lɛyuƒɔla bonwu bɔkɛ na bekyuli bete-mii ɔbu geen. Anwuɔsu ɔƒaani ni, bɛsu-mi kɔna kɔmmɔ ku kuna kalɔ budie.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” they said, “if you will only tell us your dream, we will interpret it for you.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bákpali ɔga ɔmmɔ banini, “Bula Ɔga Ɔbune, si banii bɔsu na adubɔsu-bu kɔna kɔni na égye ni, nka bɔdubo-ku kalɔ budie bute-ɔ.”

english_verse: because you know what's going to happen if you don't come up with the answer. You've decided to make up a bunch of lies, hoping I might change my mind. Now tell me the dream, and that will prove that you can interpret it.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ngyi ka lɛkwɛ kani na binye bɛɛkya na bɛkɛ kuƒi kɔdi. Ɔsika bɛgyi geen ka lɛla lɛni na lɛ́su ni, lɛ́lɛ ugyii ka ndubo-ni bɔbla si bítakana kenye kabuni kadi budie bɔsiku lɛla lɛni na lɛ́su-mii lɛlɔ. Bɛ́ɛsa lili ka bɛnyi ɔkɔ bonwu ɔdi bɛtina-mi ku kasusu ka ndubo mina kasusu bɔvumana. Bɛsu-mi mina kɔna kɔni na lígye ku kuna kalɔ budie ɔƒaani.”

english_verse: His advisors explained, “Your Majesty, you are demanding the impossible! No king, not even the most famous and powerful, has ever ordered his advisors, magicians, or wise men to do such a thing.
translation_verse: Amu na nwuna kasusu bakyane bédie kalɔ banini, “Bula Ɔga Ɔbune, aawia lɛla lɛni na libo ɔkplu litulo kalɛ na ukyuli ɔkana bɔbla taasiku-bu kudɔ! Ɔga ɔdi uuubo ina dɛ na ɔ́ƒɔ lɛnyi na ubo ɔyikun geen muedi na udie lɛdi ɔsu nwuna kasusu bakyane iye bevone ku banundane ɔdi ɔnii ɔbla lɛmɛni udu.

english_verse: It can't be done, except by the gods, and they don't live here on earth.”
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ulatɛ bɔbla amu ntu baƒiɔ bayikune bani nkya kayaa, na beeelie-bu kudɔ na kalɔ lɛlɔ mɛni.”

english_verse: This made the king so angry that he gave orders for every wise man in Babylonia to be put to death, including Daniel and his three friends. God Tells Nebuchadnezzar's Dream to Daniel
translation_verse: Lɛla lɛmɛni lɛ́bla ɔga ɔmmɔ kɔnyi geen na údie lɛdi ɔnii badu banundane ƒui na Babilon kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu bátala badi ka betétiku Daniel ku nwuna bakpana ɛtɛ bakladi bammɔ lɛnɔ batádu. Katɔti Ɔ́su Daniel Kɔna Kɔni Na Nebukadnesar Úgye

english_verse: Arioch was the king's official in charge of putting the wise men to death. He was on his way to have it done, when Daniel very wisely went to him
translation_verse: Na Ariok ndi ɔga ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ bagyumanane ɔtɔnkune ɔni nnye bekyuli bammɔ bɔdu kabla kenye. Na nka úuti ala ɔdaku ulu bɔyu utánu ka babla kabla kamɛni sɔsɔ, asa na Daniel ɔ́tɛmiku-nwu na lɛnunda kemmo.

english_verse: and asked, “Why did the king give such cruel orders?” After Arioch explained what had happened,
translation_verse: Na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na ɔga úte kalala ɔda bubo bɔmɛni udu?” Na ka Ariok údie lɛla lɛni nálɛ kalɔ ɔ́wɔlɔ ni,

english_verse: Daniel rushed off and said to the king, “If you will just give me some time, I'll explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Daniel ɔ́babla úsie ɔga ɔmmɔ kudɔ na útasu-nwu ɔnini, “Si nka adubute-mi uwi klukui ɔdi ni, ndubudie ƒula kɔna kalɔ lite-ɔ.”

english_verse: Daniel returned home and told his three friends.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Daniel únwini úsie kaduli na útásu nwuna bakpana ɛtɛ bammɔ lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́.

english_verse: Then he said, “Pray that the God who rules from heaven will be merciful and explain this mystery, so that we and the others won't be put to death.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bivele na Katɔti ɔni mɔɔdi lɛlɔ ɔ́si katɔ kakaaka udie abɛla amɛni keyi kalɛ na baládu-bu ku bekyuli bakladi.”

english_verse: In a vision one night, Daniel was shown the dream and its meaning. Then he praised the God who rules from heaven:
translation_verse: Usien ɔmmɔ ni, Katɔti údie ɔga ɔmɛni kɔna kɔmmɔ ɔ́tina Daniel na kɔyu kemmo ala bɔnu kemmo ku kuna kalɔ budie. Anwuɔsu úmwi Katɔti ɔni nli mɔɔdi lɛlɔ ɔ́si katɔ kakaaka ƒui ɔ́su ɔnini,

english_verse: “Our God, your name will be praised forever and forever. You are all-powerful, and you know everything.
translation_verse: “Bula Katɔti, bemwi ƒula lɛnyi kedee ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ƒui. Awɔ ndi ɔyikune ƒui na agyi lɛla biala.

english_verse: You control human events— you give rulers their power and take it away, and you are the source of wisdom and knowledge.
translation_verse: Awɔ mɔɔdi bayawine ablala ƒui lɛlɔ na eete lɛlɔ badine ɔyikun na aasɔ taaƒɔ-nwu bana kudɔ. Na awɔ ndi lɛnunda ku lɛlati biala kasikɔ.

english_verse: “You explain deep mysteries, because even the dark is light to you.
translation_verse: Awɔ muudie abɛla ani kemmo nágyu kalɔ, ɔsika kesii kani nse suu ƒui muedi ni, ɔdi bukeye ute awɔ.

english_verse: You are the God who was worshiped by my ancestors. Now I thank you and praise you for making me wise and telling me the king's dream, together with its meaning.” Daniel Interprets the Dream
translation_verse: Awɔ ndi Katɔti ɔni na mina bati kukuuku bákpa. Ɔƒɛni ni, mɔɔgyá-a enu, na muumwi-ɔ. Ɔsika ábla-mi ɔnundane geen na ásu-mi kɔna kɔni na ɔga úgye ku kuna kalɔ budie.” Daniel Údie Kɔna Kɔmmɔ Kalɔ

english_verse: Daniel went back to Arioch, the official in charge of executing the wise men. Daniel said, “Don't kill those men! Take me to the king, and I will explain the meaning of his dream.”
translation_verse: Amu na Daniel úsie Ariok ɔni ndi unengu ɔni na nka ɔdubɔnu na badu banundane bammɔ kudɔ, na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Tadu bekyuli bammɔ! Kpanku-mi sienku ɔga ɔmmɔ kudɔ. Na ndubɔsu-nwu nwuna kɔna kɔmmɔ ku kuna kalɔ.”

english_verse: Arioch rushed Daniel to the king and announced, “Your Majesty, I have found out that one of the men brought here from Judah can explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Usi usi na Ariok ɔkɛnku Daniel úsienku ɔga ɔmmɔ kudɔ na útébo kudu ɔnini, “Bula Ɔga Ɔbune, ḿbakɛ Yudaƒuɔ bani na bákpanku béboku mɛni akɔ unwi ka ɔdubɔkana na udie ƒula kɔna kɔmmɔ kalɔ.”

english_verse: The king asked Daniel, “Can you tell me my dream and what it means?”
translation_verse: Ɔga ɔmmɔ úye Daniel ɔni basɔ baalɔ banii Beltesasar ɔnini, “Adubɔkana-mi kɔna kɔni na lígye bɔsu na edie-ku kalɔ lɛnɔ ete-mi?”

english_verse: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, not even the smartest person in all the world can do what you are demanding.
translation_verse: Amu na Daniel údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔga Ɔbune, ɔnundane unengudi ƒui na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ muedi ulakana lɛla lɛni na aawia mɛni bɔbla.

english_verse: But the God who rules from heaven can explain mysteries. And while you were sleeping, he showed you what will happen in the future.
translation_verse: Nsu Katɔti ɔni nli mɔɔdi ala ƒui lɛlɔ ɔ́siku katɔ kakaaka ɔdubɔkana na udie abɛla amɛni keyi. Na uwi ɔni na atɛ alɛɛ ni, ɔ́tina-a ala ani ndubo abalɛ uwi ɔni ndubo.

english_verse: However, you must realize that these mysteries weren't explained to me because I am smarter than everyone else. Instead, it was done so that you would understand what you have seen.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔyɔ́ ka anu ati ka ɔɔɔdi ɔni na ami náda anu ntulo bekyuli bakladi ƒui ɔsu na údie ala amɛni ɔ́tina-mi. Mmomu ɔ́bla ɔmɛni kalɛ na enu ala ani na ánu kalɔ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, what you saw standing in front of you was a huge and terrifying statue, shining brightly.
translation_verse: “Ɔga Ɔbune, lɛla lɛni na ánu ka linye-ɔ anumi ni, ɔdi ukyuli ɔvɔdi bonwu ɔni mɔɔda liƒu na uukeye.

english_verse: Its head was made of gold, its chest and arms were silver, and from its waist down to its knees, it was bronze.
translation_verse: Na nwuna lili lɛdi sika ugyiedi na nwuna kayi ku enu adi sika ɔƒualadi. Na ɔ́si nwuna kavobi ɔ́yu úbo akɔnkɔ ɔdi abuala egyiedi.

english_verse: From there to its ankles it was iron, and its feet were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́si mmɔ úbo nwuna anikpo ni, ɔdi abuala kpakplaa sɔɔn na nwuna ɔgba ɔkladi ku kanintɔ ƒui kadi abuala kpakplaa ku lɛti kasala.

english_verse: As you watched, a stone was cut from a mountain—but not by human hands. The stone struck the feet, completely shattering the iron and clay.
translation_verse: “Ɔƒɛni uwi ɔni na enye aanu ni, ánu ka lɛtabi lɛdi na bánwi básiku abi lɛlɔ, na ɔɔɔdi ukyuli ɔyawine nánwi-ni lɛ́si líbayu ukyuli ɔvɔdi ɔmɛni lɛgba na úbo abuala ku lɛti lɛmmɔ úgyingya.

english_verse: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed and blown away without a trace, like husks of wheat at threshing time. But the stone became a tremendous mountain that covered the entire earth.
translation_verse: Na mmɔ ni, abuala kpakplaa ammɔ ku lɛti ku abuala egyiedi ku sika ɔƒualadi ku sika ugyiedi ɔmmɔ ƒui ni, ɔƒɛƒɛɛ úƒwi-nya ɔ́tɔlɔku ƒui kede kede ɔni na asɔ alanu nwuna kesii kadi aani kalɛ na beeƒi kamu aƒata teedie kamu ebi kemmo taatɔlɔku na kakpa. Nsu lɛtabi lɛmmɔ ani libenwini kɔbi bonwu kɔdi na kɔ́ƒɔ kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: That was the dream, and now I'll tell you what it means.
translation_verse: “Kɔna kɔni na égye kɔdi mmɔ, na ɔƒɛni na ndubo-ku kalɔ budie bute-ɔ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you are the greatest of kings, and God has highly honored you with power
translation_verse: Ɔga Ɔbune, awɔ ndi ɔga unengudi ƒui ɔmmɔ na Katɔti úte-ɔ ɔyikun sɔsɔ, na ɔ́ya na bekyuli baabu-ɔ.

english_verse: over all humans, animals, and birds. You are the head of gold.
translation_verse: Na aadi bekyuli ku bebuo ku baasɛ ƒui lɛlɔ. Na awɔ ndi sika ugyiedi lili lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: After you are gone, another kingdom will rule, but it won't be as strong. Then it will be followed by a kingdom of bronze that will rule the whole world.
translation_verse: Na si uwi ɔni na ƒula uwi ɔ́sa ni, lɛga kadikɔ bamba kadubo-ɔ kama bɔsia, nsu lɛga kadikɔ kammɔ kaaadubo ɔkplu bɔyu aani ƒula kadi. Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, lɛga kadikɔ bamba lɛnɔ kasɔ kadubo kani ndi abuala egyiedi kadi, na ɔdubo kayawi ƒui lɛlɔ bɔdi.

english_verse: Next, a kingdom of iron will come to power, crushing and shattering everything.
translation_verse: Na kawɔlɔkɔ ni, lɛga kadikɔ kani ndi abuala kpakplaa kadi kadubo na ubetu kayawi kammɔ ɔbwɛ na ugyingya lɛla biala.

english_verse: This fourth kingdom will be divided—it will be both strong and brittle, just as you saw that the feet and toes were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: “Lɛga kadikɔ kenedi kamɛni kadubo lɛlɔ bule akpa akpa, na badi bayu ɔkplu, na badi lɛnɔ babla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ aani kalɛ kani na ánu ka lɛgba ku lɛgba animi ammɔ adi lɛti ku abuala kasala.

english_verse: This kingdom will be the result of a marriage between kingdoms, but it will crumble, just as iron and clay don't stick together.
translation_verse: Na lɛga kadikɔ kamɛni kadubuse lɛni na beleku ku banana lɛlɔ buti taasiku lɛga kɔdikɔ bamba ɔsu, na kadubo bɔbwɛ kalɛ kani na lɛti ku abuala alasala taada lɛlɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: During the time of those kings, the God who rules from heaven will set up an eternal kingdom that will never fall. It will be like the stone that was cut from the mountain, but not by human hands—the stone that crushed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. Your Majesty, in your dream the great God has told you what is going to happen, and you can trust this interpretation. Daniel Is Promoted
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na baga bammɔ badubo bekyuli lɛlɔ butaadi ni, Katɔti ɔni mɔɔdi lɛla biala lɛlɔ ɔ́siku katɔ kakaaka mmɔ ɔdubudie lɛga kadikɔ bamba kadi use kani ndubunye kete uwi ƒui na kelebo kawɔlɔkɔ kudii. Na kadubɔbla aani lɛtabi lɛni na bánwi básiku kɔbi lɛlɔ mmɔ, na ɔɔɔdi ukyuli nánwi-ni. Lɛtabi lɛmɛni nábwɛ abuala kpakplaa ku abuala egyiedi ku lɛti ku sika ɔƒualadi ku sika ugyiedi ɔmmɔ ƒui. Ɔga Ɔbune, na ƒula kɔna kemmo ni, Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔ́su-ɔ lɛla lɛni ndubo libalɛ na ɔdi ka aƒɔ kalɔ budie bɔmɛni adi.” Ɔga Ɔmmɔ Ɔ́kɔli Daniel Kenyekɔ Katɔ

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar bowed low to the ground and worshiped Daniel. Then he gave orders for incense to be burned and a sacrifice of grain to be offered in honor of Daniel.
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Nebukadnesar úboku lɛlɔ kalɔ na ɔ́kya Daniel lili kalɔ, na úmwi-nwu na údie lɛdi úte nwuna kabla bablane ɔnii beti oloƒui beboku na bakyula, na babla edula ebi etela lɛkpa beti bete Daniel ɔbu.

english_verse: The king said, “Now I know that your God is above all other gods and kings, because he gave you the power to explain this mystery.”
translation_verse: Na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔƒɛni na lɛ́ti ka ƒula Katɔti utulo baƒiɔ bayikune bani ƒui nkya. Ɔsika anwu néte-ɔ ɔyikun na édie abɛla amɛni kalɔ.”

english_verse: The king then presented Daniel with a lot of gifts; he promoted him to governor of Babylon Province and put him in charge of the other wise men.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔga ɔmmɔ úte Daniel ala pii na ɔ́kɔliku-nwu kenyekɔ, na únwini aban ɔgadine unengu na Babilon kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ, na úti-nwu únwini banundane bakladi ƒui lɛlɔ ɔnune.

english_verse: At Daniel's request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to high positions in Babylon Province, and he let Daniel stay on as a palace official.
translation_verse: Na Daniel úye kuƒi na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɔliku Daniel bakpana ɛtɛ bani ndi Sadrak ku Mesak ku Abednego lɛnɔ kunyekɔ útése kunyekɔ kunengudi na Babilon kalɛkɛ kammɔ kemmo. Na Daniel anwu ni, únwini ɔga kesii unengu geen.

english_verse: and the king's high officials, governors, and advisors all crowded around them. The men were not burned, their hair wasn't scorched, and their clothes didn't even smell like smoke.
translation_verse: na ɔga bakutine bammɔ ku aban bagadine benengu ku ɔga kasusu bakyane bammɔ ƒui bábasa lisu na bana kudɔ mmɔ. Na bánu ka nkyuli ɛtɛ bammɔ kesii kadi kátakywi iye ogya útekeyi bana lili linwini na belénwenyi uyɔ lɛnɔ.

english_verse: So all of them came and stood in front of it.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bana ƒui bébo na bébenye lɛtabi lɛmmɔ anumi.

english_verse: and he commanded his governors, advisors, treasurers, judges, and his other officials to come from everywhere in his kingdom to the dedication of the statue.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́lɔ nwuna kadi benengu ƒui ɔ́siku nwuna lɛga kadikɔ kesii biala úbasala. Na ama ndi aban bagadine benengu ku nwuna kasusu bakyane ku egulabi lɛlɔ banune ku litemi batɛne ku nwuna bakutine benengu ɔnii bebedie lɛtabi lɛmɛni keyi batina kadi ƒui.

english_verse: Then an official stood up and announced: People of every nation and race, now listen to the king's command!
translation_verse: Amu na ɔkutine unengu ɔdi ɔ́ta únye na úte bɔti ɔnii, “Amii bani nási kadi ƒui akɔ ku adi ƒui batɛmine bíbo mɛni, binu ɔda bubo bɔni na bula ɔga úte ka badi-mu lɛlɔ!

english_verse: Trumpets, flutes, harps, and all other kinds of musical instruments will soon start playing. When you hear the music, you must bow down and worship the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
translation_verse: Kɔkpɛɛ ku atoloyii ku lɛbentaa lidu lɛdubo kalɔ buse ku bɔku uwi klukwii kemmo. Na si uwi ɔni na ala amɛni ése kalɔ ni, ɔlɛka ɔdi biala ɔkya lili kalɔ na umwi sika ugyiedi baƒiɔ lɛtabi lɛni na bula Ɔga Nebukadnesar ɔ́ya na bátu bényene mmɔ.

english_verse: Anyone who refuses will at once be thrown into a flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Ukyuli biala ɔni meni lili kalɔ bɔkya bute-nwu ni, badubo-nwu buƒwimi bɔkya lɛgyavonku kemmo.”

english_verse: As soon as the people heard the music, they bowed down and worshiped the gold statue that the king had set up.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu uwi ɔni kani na bekyuli bamɛni bénu lɛnu ku agyala ammɔ kani na bana ƒui bákya lili kalɔ na beemwi lɛtabi lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: Some Babylonians used this as a chance to accuse the Jews to King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Babilonƒuɔ badi bákɛ kasiakɔ na ɔmɛni lɛlɔ ka badu Yudaƒuɔ bamɛni kɔtɔ bete Ɔga Nebukadnesar.

english_verse: They said, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever!
translation_verse: Na básu-nwu banini, “Bula Ɔga Ɔbune, bɔɔwia ka elie ngba uwi ƒui!

english_verse: You commanded everyone to bow down and worship the gold statue when the music played.
translation_verse: Ébo-bu ɔda anii ukyuli biala ɔkya lili kalɔ ute ƒula sika ugyiedi baƒiɔ lɛtabi lɛmɛni si uwi ɔni na agyala amɛni ése kalɔ aaku.

english_verse: And you said that anyone who did not bow down and worship it would be thrown into a flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Na ásu lɛnɔ ka ukyuli biala néni na útabla lɛni ni, badubo-nwu bubo bɔkya lɛgyavonku kemmo.

english_verse: Sir, you appointed three men to high positions in Babylon Province, but they have disobeyed you. Those Jews, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, refuse to worship your gods and the statue you have set up.”
translation_verse: Ati, áƒuna nkyuli ɛtɛ badi na kesii kani na káƒɔ kuye sɔsɔ na Babilonƒuɔ kalɛkɛ kani lɛlɔ na aadi. Ama ndi Sadrak ku Mesak ku Abednego. Nsu ni, bédie atu na ƒula litemi lɛlɔ, na balákya lili kalɔ teete ƒula baƒiɔ iye ƒula sika ugyiedi lɛtabi lɛni na bátu bényene mmɔ.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar was furious. So he sent for the three young men and said,
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Ɔga Nebukadnesar ɔ́kɛ kɔnyi geen, na ɔ́ya na bététiku-ma béboku.

english_verse: “I hear that you refuse to worship my gods and the gold statue I have set up.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Línu ka bíni na bítakya lili kalɔ bítete mina baƒiɔ iye sika ugyiedi lɛtabi lɛni na lɛ́ya na bátu bényene mmɔ.

english_verse: Now I am going to give you one more chance. If you bow down and worship the statue when you hear the music, everything will be all right. But if you don't, you will at once be thrown into a flaming furnace. No god can save you from me.”
translation_verse: Ɔƒaani ni, ndubɔya na bedie lɛnu na bagya agyala bete-mii. Na si bɛ́kya lili kalɔ bímwi mina lɛtabi lɛni na lɛ́tu ni, lɛla biala lɛdubo buse buɛɛ bute-mii na ɔsa. Nsu si bíni na bítabla lɛni ni, badubo-mii bubo bɔkya lɛgyavonku kemmo, na baƒiɔ badi baaadubo-mii bɔkana bɔƒɔ bɔsiku mina enu kemmo.”

english_verse: The three men replied, “Your Majesty, we don't need to defend ourselves.
translation_verse: Amu na Sadrak ku Mesak ku Abednego bédie kenye banini, “Ɔga Ɔbune, abu bulawia ka bukpo budie lɛlɔ na litemi lɛmɛni kemmo.

english_verse: The God we worship can save us from you and your flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔni na abu bɔɔkya lili kalɔ teete ni, ɔkana na ɔƒɔ-bu ɔsiku ƒula lɛgyavonku lɛmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: But even if he doesn't, we still won't worship your gods and the gold statue you have set up.”
translation_verse: Nsu si ina útabla lɛni muedi ni, abu bɔmu bunye kpakplaa ka bulakya lili kalɔ bulete ƒula baƒiɔ sika ugyiedi lɛtabi lɛni na átu ényene mmɔ.”

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar's face twisted with anger at the three men. And he ordered the furnace to be heated seven times hotter than usual.
translation_verse: Amu ka básu lɛni ni, Nebukadnesar ɔ́nyina anumi geen ku kɔnyi ɔ́kya nkyuli ɛtɛ bamɛni. Na ɔ́su nwuna kabla bablane ɔnii basɔ babla lɛgyavonku lɛmmɔ na lɛƒɔ ogya libu akpa maatɛ.

english_verse: Next, he commanded some of his strongest soldiers to tie up the men and throw them into the flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama údie lɛdi úte nwuna bekpone bayikune geen ɔnii benyimi-ma kpakplaa na bebo-ma bakya ogya ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The king wanted it done at that very moment. So the soldiers tied up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and threw them into the flaming furnace with all of their clothes still on, including their turbans. The fire was so hot that flames leaped out and killed the soldiers.
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́yɔ ka babla lɛni kɔnakunwi ɔsu ni, mmɔ kani na bekpone bammɔ bényimi Sadrak ku Mesak ku Abednego na bébo-ma bákya lɛgyavonku lɛmmɔ kemmo ku bana adala ani na bada ku aduni ani na beebi eli ƒui. Na ogya ɔmmɔ bɔbi ɔsu ni, liwulu likpidi líkeyi bekpone bammɔ na békpi.

english_verse: Suddenly the king jumped up and shouted, “Weren't only three men tied up and thrown into the fire?” “Yes, Your Majesty,” his officers answered.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́ƒulu na ɔ́va ku lɛdi momoomo ɔnini, “Ɔɔɔdi nkyuli ɛtɛ kani na bébo bákya lɛgyavonku lɛmmɔ kemmo, iye?” Na bekyuli bammɔ lɛnɔ bédie kenye banini, “Ɛɛn, Ɔga Ɔbune.”

english_verse: “But I see four men walking around in the fire,” the king replied. “None of them is tied up or harmed, and the fourth one looks like a god.”
translation_verse: Na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Nsu nkyuli ine na mɔɔnu ka bakɛ beesié taavi na ogya ɔmmɔ kemmo, na bétenyimi bana ɔdi. Ɔdi lɛnɔ ulátina ka ogya ɔmmɔ ɔ́kyula-nwu na ɔ́ƒɔ ɔlɛ. Na si aanu ukyuli unedi ɔmmɔ ni, ɔ́lɛ aani kayaa ɔtu na ɔdi.”

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar went closer to the flaming furnace and said to the three young men, “You servants of the Most High God, come out at once!” They came out,
translation_verse: Amu na Nebukadnesar ɔ́ni úde ogya ɔmmɔ na ɔ́va ɔ́kpali bakloƒu ɛtɛ bammɔ ɔnini, “Sadrak ku Mesak ku Abednego, amii Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui kabla bablane, bɛvi bɛlɛ mmɔ bibo ɔƒaani!” Amu na bana ɛtɛ bammɔ bávi bálɛ ogya ɔmmɔ kemmo,

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar said: Praise their God for sending an angel to rescue his servants! They trusted their God and refused to obey my commands. Yes, they chose to die rather than to worship or serve any god except their own.
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Nebukadnesar ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bemwi bakloƒu bamɛni Katɔti ka úmene nwuna katɔ batu na bébedie nwuna kabla bablane! Báƒɔ bana Katɔti bádi, na béni ka badi mina ɔda bubo lɛlɔ. Sɔsɔ ni, báƒuna ka bekpi betulo ka bemwi iye bakya lili kalɔ bete baƒiɔ badi amu ntu bana Katɔti lɛti.

english_verse: And I won't allow people of any nation or race to say anything against their God. Anyone who does will be chopped up and their houses will be torn down, because no other god has such great power to save.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔsu geen ka lɛɛɛdubo kuƒi bute na bekyuli bani nási kadi ƒui akɔ ku adi ƒui batɛmine akɔ ɔdi ɔsu lɛla lɛdi iye ɔtɛmi uwi-ma. Si ɔdi ɔ́bla lɛni ni, ndubɔya na bekulo-nwu eku eku na babwɛ-nwu kaduli kɔkɛ kɔkɛ. Ɔsika baƒiɔ bayikune badi beeebo ɔyikun ɔni na baƒɔ ukyuli ɔdi ngba lɛni.”

english_verse: After this happened, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to even higher positions in Babylon Province.
translation_verse: Na ala amɛni bɔlɛ bɔwɔlɔ kama ni, ɔga ɔ́sɔ ɔ́ƒuna Sadrak ku Mesak ku Abednego útényene kesii kani na kásɔ kákuku ketulo ƒui na Babilon lɛga kadikɔ kalɛkɛ kammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar sent the following letter to the people of all nations and races on the earth: Greetings to all of you!
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔ́si Ɔga Nebukadnesar kudɔ. Úte kadi ƒui bekyuli ku adi ƒui batɛmine bani nli kayawi kammɔ kemmo. Muugyele amii bekyuli ƒui ku kusɛ kusɛ ka ala ƒui atɛ ete-mii!

english_verse: I am glad to tell about the wonderful miracles God Most High has done for me.
translation_verse: Na ɔdi-mi lɛlɔyɔ pii ka lɛsu-mii ala ebendi ani na Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔ́bla úte-mi.

english_verse: His miracles are mighty and marvelous. He will rule forever, and his kingdom will never end.
translation_verse: Nwuna akɔla budie taatina ébomo geen, Na nwuna ablala etulo bɔsu! Nwuna lɛgakadikɔ kese késela uwi ƒui Na ɔdubo lɛlɔ butaadi ɔ́si kaba úsie kaba.

english_verse: I was enjoying a time of peace and prosperity,
translation_verse: Nka nlie-nwu ƒaa ku atu bɔyɔ na lɛla lɛdi lɛnɔ lilekpoku-mi.

english_verse: when suddenly I had some horrifying dreams and visions.
translation_verse: Lígye kɔna kɔdi na kɔɔda liƒu geen ku kɔyu kemmo ala adi bene bɔnu.

english_verse: Then I commanded every wise man in Babylonia to appear in my court, so they could explain the meaning of my dream.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu lɛ́lɔ banundane bani nkya Babilon kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui nnii bebo mina kesii na bebedie kɔna kɔmɛni kalɔ bete-mi.

english_verse: After they arrived, I told them my dream, but they were not able to say what it meant.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bevone ku bekebone ku ayabi kemmo ala banune ku bani mɔɔkanti mmɔ bébeduo ni, lɛ́sɔku mina kɔna lɛ́su-ma, nsu ɔdi útakana na udie-ku kalɔ ute-mi.

english_verse: Finally, a young man named Daniel came in, and I told him the dream. The holy gods had given him special powers, and I had renamed him Belteshazzar after my own god.
translation_verse: Kawɔlɔkɔ ni, okloƒu ɔdi na baalɔ banii Daniel ɔni na lɛ́sia mina baƒiɔ lɛnyi nnii Beltesasar úbo úbeduo na lɛ́sɔku kɔna kɔmɛni lɛ́su-nwu. Na baƒiɔ bayikune bani nse kedee ɔyikun ɔsiaku-nwu.

english_verse: I said, “Belteshazzar, not only are you the wisest of all advisors and counselors, but the holy gods have given you special powers to solve the most difficult mysteries. So listen to what I dreamed and tell me what it means:
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́su-nwu nnini, “Beltesasar, ɔɔɔdi anu kani na áda etulo mina kasusu bakyane ku kelisa benengu bammɔ, mmomu baƒiɔ bayikune kedee bammɔ béte-ɔ ɔyikun sɛsɛɛ ɔni na aakana na eeti taakɛ ala ani na ebo ɔkplu geen muedi kakwɛ, na aakana-nya, na eedie akɔla ala budie taatina abɛdi muedi kalɔ. Anwuɔsu se kɔtu na enu mina kɔna kɔni na lígye na edie-ku kalɔ ete-mi.

english_verse: In my sleep I saw a very tall tree in the center of the world.
translation_verse: Na mina kɔna bugye kemmo ni, lɛ́nu kugyii kangyaa kɔdi ka kunye kayawi kammɔ ntɛntɛ.

english_verse: It grew stronger and higher, until it reached to heaven and could be seen from anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Kɔ́kuku na kubo ɔkplu geen kutulo egyii ƒui, na kútétuku kayaa katɔ katɔ ƒui, na ukyuli biala ɔɔkana-ku bɔnu na kayawi ƒui.

english_verse: It was covered with leaves and heavy with fruit— enough for all nations. Wild animals enjoyed its shade, birds nested in its branches, and all creatures on earth lived on its fruit.
translation_verse: Evete áƒɔ-ku lili na kɔ́nwu ebi bonwu bonwu lɛnɔ pii na adubudu kayawi bekyuli ƒui bɔdi. Na alakpi akɔ bebweyi bákɛ ɔyuli na kuna kalɔ na baasɛ lɛnɔ bábla ayu bákya-ku kɔgba akɔ. Na kuna ebi ammɔ na kayawi ala ediedi ƒui aadi.

english_verse: “While I was in bed, having this vision, a holy angel came down from heaven
translation_verse: “Na uwi ɔni na ntɛ muugyé kɔna kɔmɛni ni, Katɔti ɔtu kedee ɔdi na lɛ́nu ka ɔ́yu ɔ́si katɔ ɔdubo.

english_verse: and shouted: ‘Chop down the tree and cut off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Make the animals leave its shade and send the birds flying from its branches.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́va ku lɛdi momoomo ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Da kugyii kɔmmɔ va kalɔ na ekulo-ku kɔgba ƒui na ekpeli-ku evete na egyingya kuna ebi ammɔ akya. Na aya na bebuo bammɔ batɔlɔ-ku kalɔ. Na baasɛ bammɔ beveyi batɔlɔ kuna kɔgba akɔ.

english_verse: But leave its stump and roots in the ground, surrounded by grass and held by chains of iron and bronze. ‘Make sure that this ruler lives like the animals out in the open fields, unprotected from the dew.
translation_verse: Nsu ya na ligyukui lɛmmɔ lɛsɔ linye na kuna ligyiitu lɛda kalɔ na lɛku kemmo alakpi akɔ mmɔ. Ti abuala kpakplaa ku abuala egyiedi na ebo-nwu lɛkpu. “ ‘Sia anu na ɔnantu ku amii aƒɔ-nwu lɛlɔ ƒui na ulie ngba aani bebuo bamba kalɛ na alakpi akɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Give him the mind of a wild animal for seven long years.
translation_verse: Na ete-nwu alakpi akɔ bebuo kasusu na ɔkya udu ɔmmɔ kemmo akwa maatɛ.

english_verse: This punishment is given at the command of the holy angels. It will show to all who live that God Most High controls all kingdoms and chooses for their rulers persons of humble birth.’
translation_verse: “ ‘Na Katɔti batu kedee bammɔ nédie lɛdi asa na lɛtuni lɛmmɔ líbo ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔmmɔ ɔdubunwini ala bɔtɛya ute bekyuli bani ƒui nli ngba ka Unwoti Katɔti Ɔni Ntulo Ƒui mɔɔdi lɛga kadikɔ biala lɛlɔ, na anwu kani mɔɔƒuna ɔtɔnkune ɔni na uuubo kenyekɔ bonwu kadi na bekyuli anumi na uunwíni ɔga.’

english_verse: “Daniel, that was the dream that none of the wise men in my kingdom were able to understand. But I am sure that you will understand what it means, because the holy gods have given you some special powers.”
translation_verse: “Kɔna kɔmɛni ndi kɔni na ami Ɔga Nebukadnesar lígye, na banundane bammɔ ɔdi útakana-ku kalɔ budie. Nsu lɛ́ƒɔ lɛ́di ka baƒiɔ kedee béte awɔ, Beltesasar, ɔyikun sɛsɛɛ, na adubɔkana na edie kɔna kɔmɛni kalɔ.” Daniel Údie Kɔna Kɔmmɔ Kalɔ

english_verse: For a while, Daniel was terribly confused and worried by what he was thinking. But I said, “Don't be bothered either by the dream or by what it means.” Daniel replied: Your Majesty, I wish the dream had been against your enemies.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi klukui ɔdi kemmo ni, Daniel kasusu kéƒu-nwu na kayi lɛnɔ kákpulu-nwu na kasusu kani na ɔɔbla taasiku kɔna kɔmɛni lɛlɔ ɔsu. Nsu Ɔga ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Beltesasar kasusu ketekpoku-ɔ, na kayi lɛnɔ katakpulu-ɔ na kɔna kɔmɛni ɔsu, iye lɛla lɛni na kuna kalɔ budie bɔdanku lɛlɔ.” Mmɔ na Daniel údie kenye ɔnini, “Ɔga Ɔbune, si nka ƒula bekisine lɛlɔ na égye kɔna kɔmɛni udu ni, nka kaƒɔ kadubɔyɔ-mi!

english_verse: You saw a tree that grew so big and strong that it reached up to heaven and could be seen from anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Ánu kugyii kɔni na kúbomo na kɔ́kuku kútédu kayaa katɔ ƒui na ukyuli biala ɔɔkana-ku bɔnu na kayawi ƒui.

english_verse: Its leaves were beautiful, and it produced enough fruit for all living creatures; animals lived in its shade, and birds nested in its branches.
translation_verse: Na kuna evete lɛnɔ aadia bɔnu na kɔ́nwu ebi pii na adubudu kayawi ala ediedi ƒui bɔdi. Na bebuo baatɛ-ku ɔyuli kalɔ na baasɛ lɛnɔ bábla ayu bákya-ku kɔgba akɔ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, that tree is you. Your glorious reputation has reached heaven, and your kingdom covers the earth.
translation_verse: Ɔga Ɔbune, awɔ ndi kugyii kɔmmɔ. Na kalɛ na áƒɔ lɛnyi ni, ákɔ ésie katɔ katɔ ƒui, na ƒula lɛga kadikɔ káƒɔ kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then you saw a holy angel come down from heaven and say, “Chop down the tree and destroy it! But leave its stump and roots in the ground, fastened there by a chain of iron and bronze. Let it stay for seven years out in the field with the wild animals, unprotected from the dew.”
translation_verse: “Na ɔmmɔ kama ánu Katɔti ɔtu kedee ɔdi ka ɔ́yu ɔ́si katɔ úbo na ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Bɛda kugyii kɔmmɔ bɛva kalɔ na bɛyila-ku udu! Nsu kuna ligyukui ani liteenye na nwuna ligyiitu lɛda kalɔ. Na beti abuala kpakplaa ku abuala egyiedi bebo-nwu lɛkpu na lɛku kemmo alakpi akɔ mmɔ. Na ɔ́sɔ unye mmɔ akwa maatɛ ku alakpi akɔ bebuo bamba na kayaa amii aƒɔ-nwu lɛlɔ ƒui.’

english_verse: Your Majesty, God Most High has sent you this message, and it means
translation_verse: “Ɔga Ɔbune, Katɔti Ɔni Ntulo Ƒui néti linyesia lɛmɛni úmene-ɔ ɔkɛnku kɔna kɔni na égye lɛlɔ, na kuna kalɔ budie ndi ɔmɛni.

english_verse: that you will be forced to live with the wild animals, far away from humans. You will eat grass like a wild animal and live outdoors for seven years, until you learn that God Most High controls all earthly kingdoms and chooses their rulers.
translation_verse: Badubo-ɔ bɔbɔku budie bekyuli bayawine akɔ, na awɔ ku alakpi akɔ bebuo bɛsala bilie liku linwi. Na adubo livo bɔkun aani bebuo bammɔ kalɛ. Na ɔnantu ku amii eteewi-ɔ akwa maatɛ úti útédu uwi ɔni na adubɔnu ati ka Katɔti Ɔni Ntulo Ƒui mɔɔdi kayawi lɛga kadikɔ biala lɛlɔ, na uuti-ka teete ukyuli ɔni na ɔɔyɔ́.

english_verse: But he gave orders not to disturb the stump and roots. This is to show that you will be king once again, after you learn that the God who rules from heaven is in control.
translation_verse: Nsu úbo ɔda ɔnii batabla ligyukui lɛmmɔ iye ligyiitu lɛmmɔ lɛla lɛdi biala. Ɔmɛni ɔɔtina ka adubɔsɔ enwini abadi lɛlɔ aani ɔga kalɛ si uwi ɔni na ánu áti ka Katɔti mɔɔdi lɛla biala lɛlɔ taasiku katɔ kesii kani na ulie mmɔ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, please be willing to do what I say. Turn from your sins and start living right; have mercy on those who are mistreated. Then all will go well with you for a long time. The Rest of Nebuchadnezzar's Letter about His Second Dream
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu, Ɔga Ɔbune, buvele, nu kalɔ na abla lɛla lɛni na ndubo-ɔ bɔsu mɛni. Da ƒula ekpidi ani na aabla ya na enwini kama akya-nya na ataabla lɛbuni. Na ataanu bekyuli bani na ala eekpóku kɔnyana, na ɔƒaalɛ lɛla biala lɛdubɔtɛ lite-ɔ.” Nebukadnesar Kɔna Kunyɔdi Kúbo Kúte Lɛni

english_verse: About twelve months later, I was walking on the flat roof of my royal palace and admiring the beautiful city of Babylon, when these things started happening to me. I was saying to myself, “Just look at this wonderful capital city that I have built by my own power and for my own glory!”
translation_verse: Ɔbla aani abuli leevu-anyɔ kama ni, Ɔga Nebukadnesar ɔkɛ uusié taavi na nwuna lɛsa katɔ na ɔɔnu Babilon ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ bɔdia asa na ala amɛni ése kalɔ aalɛ́ku-nwu. Na ɔ́su lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Bɛnu, ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni ɔɔdia bɔnu ku ala enengudi ani na ami ɔlati líti mina ɔyikun lɛ́tu kalɛ na mina lɛnyi liteekeye!”

english_verse: But before I could finish speaking, a voice from heaven interrupted: King Nebuchadnezzar, this kingdom is no longer yours.
translation_verse: Nsu asa na útaawɔlɔ ala amɛni bɔsu ni, lɛdi lɛdi lɛ́si katɔ na líkulo-nwu kenye lɛnini, “Ɔga Nebukadnesar, lɛga kadikɔ kammɔ kasɔ kaaadi awɔ kadi.

english_verse: You will be forced to live with the wild animals, away from people. For seven years you will eat grass, as though you were an ox, until you learn that God Most High is in control of all earthly kingdoms and that he is the one who chooses their rulers.
translation_verse: Badubo-ɔ bɔbɔku na eteesie atákya alakpi akɔ ku bebuo bammɔ na alɛ bekyuli akɔ. Na livo na adubo bɔkun akwa maatɛ aani ɔmantɛ akɔ úti útédu uwi ɔni na adubɔnu ati ka Katɔti Ɔni Ntulo Ƒui mɔɔdi kayawi lɛga kadikɔ biala lɛlɔ, na anwu mɔɔƒuna bana lɛlɔ ɔdine lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: This was no sooner said than done—I was forced to live like a wild animal; I ate grass and was unprotected from the dew. As time went by, my hair grew longer than eagle feathers, and my fingernails looked like the claws of a bird.
translation_verse: Na lɛdi lɛmmɔ kenye kamɛni kátawɔlɔ tɔ asa na bábɔku-nwu bálɛku na úse kalɔ ɔɔkun livo na ɔkɛ amii lɛlɔ ɔɔví aani alakpi akɔ bebuo kalɛ. Na kalɛ na emeyi ammɔ eebo ni, lɛni kani na nwuna linwini liine aani kɔdigbo aasɛ agya, na nwuna aƒiɔ lɛnɔ eene gyɔlɔɔ aani aasɛ lɛgba aƒiɔ.

english_verse: Finally, I prayed to God in heaven, and my mind was healed. Then I said: “I praise and honor God Most High. God lives forever, and his kingdom will never end.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni bése kawɔlɔkɔ ni, lɛ́kpali Katɔti lívele-nwu na mina kasusu kásɔ kénwini kébo-mi na ɔ́bla-mi nwaa. Mmɔ na lɛ́su nnini, “Muumwi Katɔti Ɔni Ntulo Ƒui, na mɔɔbu-nwu. Anwu nli ngba uwi ƒui.” Nwuna lɛga kadikɔ kese késela uwi ƒui. Na kadubuse ɔ́si kaba úsie kaba.

english_verse: To him the nations are far less than nothing; God controls the stars in the sky and everyone on this earth. When God does something, we cannot change it or even ask why.”
translation_verse: Kalɔ lɛlɔ kadi bekyuli ƒui baaadi lɛla lɛdi na nwuna anumi. Lɛla lɛni mɔɔyɔ́-nwu kaƒɔ na ɔɔbla Ɔɔdi ayabi ku kayaa kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ. Na ɔɔdi ukyuli biala lɛlɔ na kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na si Katɔti ɔ́bla lɛla lɛdi ni, bulakana-nwu bɔbala iye buye bɔnii, “Bi ndi lɛla lɛni na ábla mɛni?”

english_verse: At that time my mind was healed, and once again I became the ruler of my glorious kingdom. My advisors and officials returned to me, and I had greater power than ever before.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni kemmo kani na mina kasusu kásɔ kénwini kébo-mi nwaa ni, bekyuli bése kalɔ baabu-mi na muukeye kalɛ na mina lɛgakadikɔ lɛnɔ kekeye. Na ɔmɛni kama ni, mina kasusu bakyane ku kelisa benengu ƒui básɔ bénwini bábasia-mi kama, na básɔku-mi bése liboku lɛlɔ mina ɔyikun ku kenyekɔ kásɔ kákɔ katɔ kétulo kudeedi ƒui.

english_verse: That's why I say: “Praise and honor the King who rules from heaven! Everything he does is honest and fair, and he can shatter the power of those who are proud.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na lɛ́su nnii bemwi Katɔti ɔni nli mɔɔdi lɛlɔ ɔ́si katɔ ƒui ku ɔbu! Ɔsika lɛla biala na ɔ́bla lɛdia na lɛkɛ ulu lɛlɔ siin, na bani ƒui mɔɔkɔliku lɛlɔ katɔ ni, uuboku-ma kalɔ.

english_verse: One evening, King Belshazzar gave a great banquet for a thousand of his highest officials, and he drank wine with them.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi useyi uwi ni, Ɔga Belsasar use adila kadikɔ bonwu kadi úte nwuna bakutine benengu mpim mpim, na anwu ku-ma báni ntɛ básala.

english_verse: He got drunk and ordered his servants to bring in the gold and silver cups his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem. Belshazzar wanted the cups, so that he and all his wives and officials could drink from them.
translation_verse: Ntɛ búbo bɔɔda-nwu na ɔ́tala nwuna kabla bablane ɔnii besie na betéti sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi lɛɛƒɛɛ lɛni na ɔti Nebukadnesar ɔ́da úti na Katɔti kakpakɔ na Yerusalem mmɔ beboku. Na ɔɔwia lɛɛƒɛɛ lɛmmɔ kalɛ na anwu ku nwuna beleku ku benengu bani na ɔ́lɔ úboku kadikɔ mmɔ bani ntɛ na nina kemmo.

english_verse: When the gold cups were brought in, everyone at the banquet drank from them and praised their idols made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
translation_verse: Amu ka béti lɛɛƒɛɛ lɛmmɔ béboku ni, ukyuli biala ɔni nkya adila ammɔ kadikɔ mmɔ ɔ́ni ntɛ na lɛɛƒɛɛ lɛmmɔ kemmo na beemwi baƒiɔ bani na béti sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi ku abuala egyiedi ku atabi ku egyiiku bávɔ iye bánwi mmɔ.

english_verse: Suddenly a human hand was seen writing on the plaster wall of the palace. The hand was just behind the lampstand, and the king could see it writing.
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani ni, ukyuli lɛnuku lɛdi lɛ́da lɛ́lɛ na bánu ka uunweni ala adi taasia kɔwodu kɔmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: He was so frightened that his face turned pale, his knees started shaking, and his legs became weak.
translation_verse: Ɔga ɔmɛni ɔ́yia geen na nwuna anumi ávumana ábla aani ɔlɛne kukuuku ɔdi, na akɔnkɔ aatɔ́-nwu, na nwuna lɛgba ƒui lɛ́bla kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: The king called in his advisors, who claimed they could talk with the spirits of the dead and understand the meanings found in the stars. He told them, “The man who can read this writing and tell me what it means will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. He will wear robes of royal purple and a gold chain around his neck.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpali nwuna bevone bani mɔɔtɛmiku bekpine ayu ku ama bani mɔɔnu ayabi na beebó like ɔnii bebo. Na ɔ́su banundane bamɛni ɔnini, “Ukyuli ɔni ndubɔkana ala amɛni bɔka na udie-nya kalɔ ute-mi ni, ɔdubunwini ukyuli ɔtɛdi ɔni ndubɔkɛ kenyekɔ ku ɔyikun butulo ƒui na mina lɛga kadikɔ. Na ɔdubo awu ɔni náƒɔ kuye geen butaakya na ɔkya sika ugyiedi kɔsɛɛ ɔkwɛ.”

english_verse: All of King Belshazzar's highest officials came in, but not one of them could read the writing or tell what it meant,
translation_verse: Ɔga Belsasar banundane bammɔ ƒui bébo, nsu ɔdi útakana na udie lɛla lɛni na lɛnuku lɛmmɔ línweni mmɔ kalɔ iye ɔkana bɔka muedi.

english_verse: and they were completely puzzled. Now the king was more afraid than ever before, and his face turned white as a ghost.
translation_verse: Na lɛla lɛmmɔ líkpoku-ma na béƒu benye, anwuɔsu ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́yia úbu na nwuna anumi ábla aani ukpine anumi.

english_verse: When the queen heard the king and his officials talking, she came in and said: Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! Don't be afraid or look so pale.
translation_verse: Amu uwi ɔni na nwuna uleku ɔga únu lɛla lɛni na ɔga ɔmmɔ ku nwuna banundane badaku ni, úbo úbeduo-ma kudɔ mmɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔga Ɔbune, mɔɔwia ka elie ngba uwi ƒui! Na tayia na ƒula anumi abla ƒuƒuu lɛni.

english_verse: In your kingdom there is a man who has been given special powers by the holy gods. When your father Nebuchadnezzar was king, this man was known to be as smart, intelligent, and wise as the gods themselves.
