english_verse: Of all nations on earth, you are the only one I have chosen. That's why I will punish you because of your sins. The Work of a Prophet
translation_verse: Amii kani na lɛ́ƒuna na kayawi kadi bekyuli ƒui akɔ, anwuɔsu na ndubo-mii kɔtu bɔni na bina alaekpidi ɔsu.” Kakɛ Na Katɔti Kenye Udiene Ɔɔbla Kabla

english_verse: Can two people walk together without agreeing to meet?
translation_verse: Nkyuli inyɔ belesie taasala na bana kasusu kalábla kenwi.

english_verse: Does a lion roar in the forest unless it has caught a victim? Does it growl in its den unless it is eating?
translation_verse: Gyata ulakwanyi na lɛku kemmo si úteƒie tɔ ebuo. Lɛni kani gyata ɔkɔdi ulebo lɛdi na nwuna lɛtakpɛ ubu kemmo si útakɛ lɛla lɛdi ulákun.

english_verse: How can anyone catch a bird without using a net? Does a trap spring shut unless something is caught?
translation_verse: Aasɛ ulenu buƒie si átakywɛ-nwu kamia. Na lɛni kani na kakpagyuɛ kaláta keeke si lɛla lɛdi lítanu-ka kemmo.

english_verse: Isn't the whole city frightened when the trumpet signals an attack? Isn't the Lord the one who brings disaster on a city?
translation_verse: Lɛlɔ lɛɛtɔ́ ukyuli biala na ɔma kemmo si bávwi kekpo lise. Na ɔgbankpi ulalɛ na ɔma ɔdi kemmo si Unwoti útatuna.

english_verse: Whatever the Lord God plans to do, he tells his servants, the prophets.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti ulábla lɛla lɛdi ntu ɔ́ka nwuna kenye udiene bɔsu.

english_verse: Everyone is terrified when a lion roars— and ordinary people become prophets when the Lord God speaks. Samaria Is Doomed
translation_verse: Liƒu lɛɛda ukyuli biala si gyata ɔɔkwanyi. Na si Katɔti ɔ́su lɛla lɛdi ni, usi na ukyuli biala ɔkɛ na ɔdubo-ni lɛsa bɔkɔ. Katɔti Ɔdubo Samaria Udu Bɔyila

english_verse: Here is a message for the leaders of Philistia and Egypt— tell everyone to come together on the hills of Samaria. Let them see the injustice and the lawlessness in that city.
translation_verse: Bɛkɔ litemi lɛmɛni lɛsa bite batɔnkune bani na beli kɔgyumanakɔ kɔni na bátu na Asiria ku Egyipte kɔlɔ lɛlɔ bɛnii, “Bɛsala lɛlɔ na Samaria abi eli na bɛnu ɔda bubo lɛlɔ tadi ku ekpidi lidu bamba lɛni udu na bekyuli baabla na mmɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord has said that they don't even know how to do right. They have become rich from violence and robbery.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Bekyuli bamɛni baaagyi kalɛ na baabla lɛbuni. Béyu bekyuli, na béƒie ani báƒɔ ɔkplu kemmo bénwini bana lɛlakɛ.”

english_verse: And so the Lord God has sworn that they will be surrounded. Enemies will break through their defenses and steal their treasures.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu na Unwoti úse kenye ka badubɔka-ma bakya na bekisine babwɛ bavi bana kɔgyumanakɔ na beduo beyu bana akɛla ani na bebo mmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: The Lord has promised that only a few from Samaria will escape with their lives and with some broken pieces of their beds and couches. It will be like when a shepherd rescues two leg bones and part of a sheep's ear from the jaws of a lion. The Altars at Bethel
translation_verse: Kalɛ na si gyata úƒie koƒonu na kakɛ blii kani na baƒonu ɔdane ɔɔnu taaƒɔ́ ni, lɛni geen na ɔdubo bɔlɛku Samariaƒuɔ, na bana ɛlɛɛ kani ndubo bukeli na bakɛ ngba ku bana ala ekuku ani na badububile bebu.

english_verse: The Lord God All-Powerful told me to speak this message against Jacob's descendants:
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui néte-mi kenye kamɛni ɔnii nkɔ-ka lɛsa na liti libo-mii ɔda, amii Yakob kaba kemmo bebi ɔnini,

english_verse: When I, the Lord, punish Israel for their sins, I will destroy the altars at Bethel. Even the corners of the altar will be left in the dirt.
translation_verse: “Na limeyi lɛni lɛlɔ na ndubo Israelƒuɔ kɔtu bɔni na bana ekpidi ɔsu ni, ndubo Betel akpabi ammɔ ƒui bɔbwɛ na lɛƒɛ ese ani na bálɛ akpabi ammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui lɛva kalɔ na ɔtumu akɔ.

english_verse: I will tear down winter homes and summer homes. Houses decorated with ivory and all other mansions will be gone forever. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Ndubo bina kɔyɔ ku kaƒɛndi uwi lɛtɔ ƒui bɔbwɛ buwi kalɔ. Na bina lɛtɔ lɛni na bíti ɔtunkpɛ bɛ́kya-ni bɔdia ku lɛgbanya libendi lɛmmɔ ƒui ndubo-ni bɔbwɛ ƒui. Ami Unwoti násu!”

english_verse: You women of Samaria are fat cows! You mistreat and abuse the poor and needy, then you say to your husbands, “Bring us more drinks!”
translation_verse: “Amii Samariaƒuɔ beleku bise atu na binu! Bise aani Basan ɔmantɛ bakɔ bani nélie lɛmwi, ɔsika bana balati bánu-ma lɛlɔ kaduɛ. Biláda bawabane edu munu munu. Na bani mɔɔyaki ala ni, bísusu-ma geen kalɛ na bakpa bayii bakya. Na bɛɛwia ka bina bagya beteete-mii ntɛ na bitaani uwi biala.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, have sworn by my own name that your time is coming. Not one of you will be left— you will be taken away by sharp hooks.
translation_verse: Ami Unwoti nkɛnku mina lɛnyi lɛni nse kedee lɛlɔ líse kenye ka uwi ɔdi ɔdubo ɔni na badubo-mii ɔbuli enwu bɔkya aani ɔdaa na bani-mii batɔlɔku na ɔdi ulébu.

english_verse: You will be dragged through holes in your city walls, and you will be thrown toward Harmon. I, the Lord, have spoken! Israel Refuses To Obey The Lord said:
translation_verse: Badubo-mii bɔni bɔvinku bina ɔma unengudi awodu eƒi ani ntɛ-nya kemmo na ɔdi ulébu. Na bebo-mii batáva Harmon kakɛ. Ami Unwoti násu! Israel Úni Ka Unwini Ubo Katɔti Kudɔ

english_verse: Bring offerings to show me how thankful you are. Gladly bring more offerings than I have demanded. You really love to do this. I, the Lord God, have spoken! How the Lord Warned Israel
translation_verse: “Amii biti bina etela lidu bitátina na bitaakun lɛmɛnɛ ɔsika ɔmmɔ udu kani na bɛgyi na bɛɛyɔ́ ka bitaabla. Ami Unwoti násu!

english_verse: I, the Lord, took away the food from every town and village, but still you rejected me.
translation_verse: “Ami náya na kɔka kúbo na lɛma lɛmmɔ ƒui kemmo. Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui bitenwini, mmomu bɛ́mu bíni-mi.

english_verse: Three months before harvest, I kept back the rain. Sometimes I would let it fall on one town or field but not on another, and pastures dried up.
translation_verse: “Lɛ́ya na ɔnantu lɛnɔ ɔ́da bɔna ɔ́ya uwi ɔni kemmo na nka bina edula aawia ɔnantu geen, na bɔna kani na lɛ́ya na ɔɔna egyu egyu, na lɛma lɛmmɔ kemmo na ekpo akladi ákwii.

english_verse: People from two or three towns would go to a town that still had water, but it wasn't enough. Even then you rejected me. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Bekyuli baata bana lɛma teesie lɛma bamba taatáwia ntu, na kesii kani na badubɔkɛ bɔdi bani, nsu buledu-ma. Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui bítenwini. Ami Unwoti násu.

english_verse: I dried up your grain fields; your gardens and vineyards turned brown. Locusts ate your fig trees and olive orchards, but even then you rejected me. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: “Lɛ́ya na bina edula ƒui ku adingyii mmo bɔ́kwii na lɛla biala lɛ́bla ƒuƒuu linye. Baalɔlɔ bádi bina anwingyie ku nnɔ egyii mmo ƒui. Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui bítenwini. Ami Unwoti násu.

english_verse: I did terrible things to you, just as I did to Egypt— I killed your young men in war; I let your horses be stolen, and I made your camp stink with dead bodies. Even then you rejected me. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: “Lɛ́ya na ɔgbankpi ala enengudi álɛku-mii aani kalɛ na lɛ́ya na álɛku Egyipteƒuɔ, na bina bakloƒu lɛnɔ békpi na kekpokɔ. Lɛ́ya na béyu bina bapɔnkɔ, na bina bekyuli pii békpi na beenwenyi na bina kuliekɔ. Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui bítenwini. Ami Unwoti násu!

english_verse: I destroyed many of you, just as I did the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. You were a burning stick I rescued from the fire. But even then you rejected me. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: “Lɛ́yila bina bekyuli pii udu aani kalɛ na lɛ́bla Sodom ku Gomora. Bɔkywi na nka bina ɛlɛɛ bani nébu bɛda aani ugyii na ogya kemmo asa na lídie-mii. Nsu ɔmɛni ƒui bítenwini. Ami Unwoti násu!

english_verse: Now, Israel, I myself will deal with you. Get ready to face your God!
translation_verse: “Ɔƒɛni amu ami ku-mii alati ndubo bɔsa. Anwuɔsu ni, Israel, bɛklibi lɛlɔ na amii ku ami bina Unwoti anumi abla enwi!

english_verse: I created the mountains and the wind. I let humans know what I am thinking. I bring darkness at dawn and step over hills. I am the Lord God All-Powerful!
translation_verse: “Ami nédie abi ku ɔƒɛƒɛɛ. Na ami mɔɔyá na bekyuli baatí mina kasusu. Na ami mɔɔyá na ɔƒɛ kadi kaasá. Na mɔɔkɔ́ taayu abi ammɔ ƒui eli ku kesi kesii. Ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔmmɔ!”

english_verse: Listen, nation of Israel, to my mournful message:
translation_verse: Israel kadi bekyuli, bise atu na binu kɔnyana ɔnu ɔni na muudie teete-mii.

english_verse: You, dearest Israel, have fallen, never to rise again— you lie deserted in your own land, with no one to help you up.
translation_verse: “Awɔ ɔni nse aani adagyaa ni, ébuli, na asɔ aaadubo bɔkana bɔta bunye ligeen kudii. Aanu-ɔ ntɛ enukplu ɔni na asɔ eeebo lɛla lɛdi bɔbla, na eeebo ukyuli ɔni mebunku-ɔ lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord God has warned, “From every ten soldiers only one will be left; from a thousand troops, only a hundred will survive.”
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti ɔnii, “Bina bekpone leevu biala kemmo ni, unwi pɛ kani ndubo bubu. Na bana apim unwi biala kemmo ni, eti anyɔ kani ndubo bubu.”

english_verse: The Lord keeps saying, “Israel, turn back to me and you will live!
translation_verse: Unwoti unye ɔɔsu uwi biala ɔnini, “Israel, bɛwia ami Unwoti kama ulu na bɛkɛ ngba bilie!

english_verse: Don't go to Gilgal or Bethel or even to Beersheba. Gilgal will be dragged away, and Bethel will end up as nothing.”
translation_verse: Na bitesie Gilgal iye Betel iye Beer-Seba. Ɔsika Gilgal ku nwuna bekyuli bammɔ ƒui kekpo kadubo kebeƒie-ma na beti-ma batɔlɔku. Na bayila Betel udu kede kede na ɔsɔ uladi lɛla lɛdi.”

english_verse: Turn back to the Lord, you descendants of Joseph, and you will live. If you don't, the Lord will attack like fire. Bethel will burn to the ground, and no one can save it.
translation_verse: Bɛwia Unwoti kama ulu na bilie ngba! Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, Unwoti ɔdubo ubakyula-mii aani ogya kalɛ. Na Betel ɔdubo bɔkywi kputu kputu buwi kalɔ ɔni na ukyuli ɔdi ulakana-nwu bunine.

english_verse: You people are doomed! You twist the truth and trample on justice.
translation_verse: Amii bani mɔɔtu litemi geen teenwini na biiƒú ala taakya na bilábla ala ulu lɛlɔ siin ni, amii ɔdi ɔ́sa.

english_verse: But the Lord created the stars and put them in place. He turns darkness to dawn and daylight to darkness; he scoops up the ocean and empties it on the earth.
translation_verse: Unwoti nábla ayabi lidu ɔ́kya katɔ, na enye ana kunyekɔ. Ɔɔyá na usien uugyé kadi nwaa na ɔƒɛ kadi nwaa kaasá teenwini usien. Na uudie ntu na ɛpu kemmo teewi kalɔ lɛlɔ. Nwuna lɛnyi ndi Unwoti.

english_verse: God destroys mighty soldiers and strong fortresses. Choose Good Instead of Evil! The Lord said:
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔɔyila bekpone bayikune udu na ɔɔbwɛ lɛma kɔgyumanakɔ kɔni na bátu bényene.

english_verse: you abuse the poor and demand heavy taxes from them. You have built expensive homes, but you won't enjoy them; you have planted vineyards, but you will get no wine.
translation_verse: Na bɛɛnya bawabane taakya na bɛɛƒɔ́ eyi bonwu bonwu ku edula na bana kudɔ. Bɛ́tu lɛtɔ libendi bíte lɛlɔ, nsu bɛɛɛdubo-ni kemmo bulie. Na bíse adingyii mmo, nsu bɛɛɛdubo ntɛ bɔkɛ bɔsiku egyiibi ammɔ kemmo.

english_verse: I am the Lord, and I know your terrible sins. You cheat honest people and take bribes; you rob the poor of justice.
translation_verse: Ami ndi Unwoti na ngyi bina ekpidi enengudi ani na bɛɛbla. Bɛɛƒɔ́ ala bɔbɛ kemmo na bɛɛyila bawabane bani nse siin lili, na biládi etemila lɛlɔ siin teete-ma.

english_verse: Times are so evil that anyone with good sense will keep quiet.
translation_verse: Likpidi líse lɛ́ƒɔ uwi ɔmmɔ geen ɔni na ukyuli ɔni na ubo lɛbuni bɔbla kasusu dɛ muedi ɔlɛka ubile kenye na ɔsɔ ulie kpoo.

english_verse: If you really want to live, you must stop doing wrong and start doing right. I, the Lord God All-Powerful, will then be on your side, just as you claim I am.
translation_verse: Nsu si ngba na bɛɛwia bilie bɔdi ni, ɔlɛka bɛda likpidi bɔbla bɛya na bise kalɔ bitaabla lɛbuni. Mmɔ asa na ami Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui ndubɔkana na lilieku-mii aani kalɛ na amii alati bɛɛsu.

english_verse: Choose good instead of evil! See that justice is done. Maybe I, the Lord All-Powerful, will be kind to what's left of your people. Judgment Is Coming
translation_verse: Bini likpidi na bɛyɔ lɛbuni bɔbla. Na bɛya na litemi geen kama bɔsia bɔkya bina etemila katɛkɔ. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔdubɔnu Yoseƒ kaba kemmo bebi bani nébu kanyana.

english_verse: This is what the Lord has sworn: Noisy crying will be heard in every town and street. Even farmers will be told to mourn for the dead, together with those who are paid to mourn.
translation_verse: Ɔsika Unwoti úuse kenye ɔnini, “Keku buwulo bɔdubɔƒɔ lɛblɔnu lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ƒui na kɔnyana ku ɔlɛ bunu geen bɔdubɔkya kesi kesii. Na bemonsene bani kabla naaaƒɔ anu muedi badubɔlɔ-ma na bebebunku bani na báƒɔ lɛkwanu budie enu na bebewulo bekpine bammɔ bava.

english_verse: Your vineyards will be filled with crying and weeping, because I will punish you. I, the Lord, have spoken! When the Lord Judges
translation_verse: Bina adingyii mmo bɔmmɔ kemmo muedi keku sɔɔn na bɛdubunu ka kada, ɔsika lɛni na lɛ́su ka ndububo mbani-mii kɔtu. Ami Unwoti násu!”

english_verse: You look forward to the day when the Lord comes to judge. But you are in for trouble! It won't be a time of sunshine; all will be darkness.
translation_verse: Binye bɛɛnu ulu teete limeyi lɛni na Unwoti webo wabatɛku bekyuli litemi, nsu bɔbuɛ na muute-mii! Ɔsika limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛɛɛdubo buse buɛɛ na ɔƒɛ ɔɔɔdubo bɔlɛ munu munu. Bɔbla na ɔdubo suu geen.

english_verse: You will run from a lion, only to meet a bear. You will escape to your house, rest your hand on the wall, and be bitten by a snake.
translation_verse: Bɛdubukeli gyata na bitéduo kegidi enu kemmo. Na bɛdubukeli bitéduo bina kɔduli, nsu awodu eli ani na bɛdubuti enu bɛsia bɛnii bɛɛnwuna ni, mmɔ na balakpi badubo-mii bɔdu.

english_verse: The day when the Lord judges will be dark, very dark, without a ray of light. What the Lord Demands
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛni na Unwoti ɔdubulie kalɔ ɔnii litemi na ɔɔtɛ ni, ɔdubo bɔbla suu geen na bukeye bɔdi bulakya kesi kesii munu munu.

english_verse: I, the Lord, hate and despise your religious celebrations and your times of worship.
translation_verse: “Ami Unwoti nkisi na líni bina emeyi bɔdi ku bina bɔkpa bumodi bɔmmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: No more of your noisy songs! I won't listen when you play your harps.
translation_verse: Nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo-mii atu bɔkywɛɛ si uwi ɔni na bɛɛgyá bina lɛbentaa.

english_verse: But let justice and fairness flow like a river that never runs dry.
translation_verse: Mmomu bɛya na litemi lɛlɔ bɔdi ku ala bɔbla ulu lɛlɔ siin unwini aani ketu na kataagba na bina keliela kemmo na kasɔ katakwii kudii.

english_verse: Israel, for forty years you wandered in the desert, without bringing offerings or sacrifices to me.
translation_verse: “Israelƒuɔ, ɔɔɔdi ami na bíti bebuo ku baƒonu bɛ́bla akpala bíte akwa aavlene ani na bɛ́kya ketele kemmo mmɔ.

english_verse: Now you will have to carry the two idols you made— Sakkuth, the one you call king, and Kaiwan, the one you built in the shape of a star.
translation_verse: Mmomu bɛ́gyu Molek lɛbi ku Romƒa ayabi ani ndi baƒiɔ bani na bɛ́vɔ bíse bɛnii bitaakpa bíti.

english_verse: I will force you to march as captives beyond Damascus. I, the Lord God All-Powerful, have spoken!
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ndubɔya na beƒie-mii besienku ɔgyu kakaaka na Damasko kama ngye ƒui. Ami Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui násu!”

english_verse: Do you rulers in Jerusalem and in the city of Samaria feel safe and at ease? Everyone bows down to you, and you think you are better than any other nation. But you are in for trouble!
translation_verse: Bɔbuɛ ute amii bani nli-nwu ƒaa na Sion ku amii bani nli kɔbi lili na Samaria na bɛɛkali ka bɛ́gyi ɔban bɛ́mana bina lɛlɔ. Amii ndi lɛlɔ badine na Israel kalɔ kani náƒɔ lɛnyi ketulo mmɔ. Na Israel kadi bekyuli beebo-mii kudɔ teebevele-mii ala na beebó kalɔ teegyele-mii!

english_verse: Look what happened to the cities of Calneh, powerful Hamath, and Gath in Philistia. Are you greater than any of those kingdoms?
translation_verse: Bisie Kalne ku Hamat ɔma ɔni náƒɔ lɛnyi mmɔ na bitánu Gat lɛnɔ na Ƒilisti kalɔ lɛlɔ na bɛnu si bana lɛga kadikɔ kédu Yuda ku Israel lɛga kadikɔ.

english_verse: You are cruel, and you forget the coming day of judgment.
translation_verse: Bɛ́yiƒala ka kalɛ na bilie bɛɛdi bekyuli lɛlɔ kalala kemmo ndubo bɔya Unwoti uyile bubo bubatɛku-mii litemi.

english_verse: You rich people lounge around on beds with ivory posts, while dining on the meat of your lambs and calves.
translation_verse: Amii balakɛne, biwi bina atɛla mɔmɔɔmɔ ani na béti ɔtunkpɛ bánwi nina ligyii lɛlɔ ku eboku bonwu bonwu kemmo, na baadú baƒonu ku ɔmantɛ bakɔ bebi bakɔdi bani nélie lɛmwi teeboku-mii na bɛɛdi taaní!

english_verse: You sing foolish songs to the music of harps, and you make up new tunes, just as David used to do.
translation_verse: Na bɛ́nwi kɔdɔlɔ lɛnu na bɛɛgyá teedie teete lɛlɔ na bina lɛbentaa lɛlɔ. Na bɛɛvumana lɛnu lɛmmɔ adi aani kalɛ na Ɔga Dawid útaabla.

english_verse: You drink all the wine you want and wear expensive perfume, but you don't care about the ruin of your nation.
translation_verse: Na si ntɛ bɔkya wɛ bɛdubo bɔya na beti-mu beboku-mii na bɛni-mu ɔdivo kemmo bɛsia kama. Na bɛɛwɛɛ ligyulo ƒɛƒɛɛ lidu lidu lɛni náƒɔ kuye na bɛɛɛdaku-ni si bɔbwɛ Israel kalɔ kemodi kammɔ kaabwɛ.

english_verse: So you will be the first to be dragged off as captives; your good times will end.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu amii ndubɔdi bekyuli bedeedi bani na kekpo kadubo buƒie bɔtɔlɔku na bina ebiti ku lɛlɔyɔ kenye kekulo.

english_verse: The Lord God All-Powerful has sworn by his own name: “You descendants of Jacob make me angry by your pride, and I hate your fortresses. And so I will surrender your city and possessions to your enemies.”
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔ́kpali anwu ɔlati lɛnyi úse kenye ɔnini, “Amii Yakob kaba kemmo bebi, bɛɛkya-mi kɔnyi geen na bina lɛlɔ katɔ bɔkɔliku ɔsu, na muukisi bina ɔma agbanya ani na bɛ́tu bínyene mmɔ ƒui. Anwuɔsu ndubo-mii atu budie na lɛnyonu-mii ku bina ɔma lɛkya bina bekisine enu kemmo ku bina akɛla ƒui.”

english_verse: If only ten of you survive by hiding in a house you will still die.
translation_verse: Na si nkyuli leevu nébu na kaduli kadi kemmo ni, ama lɛnɔ badubo bukpi.

english_verse: As you carry out a corpse to prepare it for burial, your relative in the house will ask, “Are there others?” You will answer, “No!” Then your relative will reply, “Be quiet! Don't dare mention the name of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na si ukyuli ɔni nékpi mmɔ lɛlɔ ukyuli ɔni nálɛ ka ɔbla-nwu bɔva ala kalɛ na baabla úbo ɔnii ubeti ukyuli ɔmmɔ ni, ɔdubɔkpali na uye unu si ukyuli ɔdi úbu na ɔkya katɔma kesii kadi. Na ukyuli ɔni nányonu ukpine ɔmmɔ ɔɔkya-nwu lɛkɔkɔ ɔdubɔsu-nwu ɔnini, “Oowo, enu! Ba lɛsɛ kpoo, utalɛka bakpali Unwoti lɛnyi mɛni.”

english_verse: At the Lord's command, houses great and small will be smashed to pieces.
translation_verse: Ɔsika si Unwoti údie lɛdi ni, kaduli kenengudi o-o kebliidi o-o ni, ɔdubo-ku bugyingya ƒui kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ.

english_verse: Horses can't gallop on rocks; oceans can't be plowed. But you have turned justice and fairness into bitter poison.
translation_verse: Nka ɔpɔnkɔ ulakɛ taaƒulu na atakpɛ lɛlɔ, na ɔmantɛ bakɔ balada bana anwami bonwu bonwu ammɔ teegulu ɛpu anumi. Nsu amii bɛ́tu litemi geen lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ bɔdi bínwini ugyulo ukpidi, na bíti lɛbuni bɔbla bínwini likpila.

english_verse: But the Lord God All-Powerful will send a nation to attack you people of Israel. They will capture Lebo-Hamath in the north, Arabah Creek in the south, and everything in between.
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui ɔnini, “Ndubo bɔya na kadi badi bekyuli bata bebékpo-ku amii Israelƒuɔ na badi-mii lɛlɔ na beƒie bina ala ƒui baƒɔ ɔ́si Hamat na katɔ kakɛ útédu Araba Ɔkwalɛ na kada kakɛ ku lɛla biala na lɛkya ekpo anyɔ amɛni ntɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord God showed me that he is going to send locusts to attack your crops. It will happen after the king has already been given his share of the grain and before the rest of the grain has been harvested.
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti údie ɔ́tina-mi na kɔyu kemmo ka ɔdubuti baalɔlɔ umene na bebile edula ammɔ ƒui si uwi ɔni na báƒɛ ɔga ɔmmɔ ɔdi béte-nwu báwɔlɔ, na livo lɛwɔdi lɛ́sɔ líse kalɔ lɛɛlɛ́.

english_verse: In my vision the locusts ate every crop in the land, and I said to the Lord, “Please forgive your nation. It's so weak. How can it survive?”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na nnye mɔɔnu na baalɔlɔ bammɔ bádi lɛla biala bédie báwɔlɔ ni, lívele-nwu nnini, “Unwoti Ɔyikune Ƒui, nu-ma kɔnyana na eti akyiɛ-ma! Dɛ na Yakob kaba kemmo bebi badubɔbla asa na belie ngba? Bana ɛlɛɛ kani badi na beeebo ɔyikun ɔdi!”

english_verse: Then the Lord felt sorry and answered, “I won't let it be destroyed.” A Vision of Fire
translation_verse: Na lɛla lɛmɛni líkpoku Unwoti ɔlati, anwuɔsu enu áƒɛ-nwu ka ɔbla lɛla lɛni na ɔ́su. Na ɔnini, “Nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo bɔya na ubo-nwu kemmo lɛni.”

english_verse: The Lord showed me that he is going to send a ball of fire to burn up everything on earth, including the ocean.
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti údie ɔ́tina-mi na kɔyu kemmo ka ɔdubɔya na ogya bonwu ɔdi ubo na ubakyula ɛpu ɔmmɔ na ɔkyula kalɔ kammɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Again the Lord felt sorry and answered, “I won't let it be destroyed.” A Vision of a Measuring Line
translation_verse: Na lɛla lɛmɛni líkpoku Unwoti ɔlati, anwuɔsu enu áƒɛ-nwu ka ɔbla lɛla lɛni na ɔ́su. Na ɔnini, “Nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo bɔya na anwu lɛnɔ ubo-nwu kemmo lɛni.”

english_verse: The Lord showed me a vision of himself standing beside a wall and holding a string with a weight tied to the end of it. The string and weight had been used to measure the straightness of the wall.
translation_verse: Unwoti údie lɛla bamba ɔ́tina na kɔyu kemmo. Na lɛ́nu ka unye kowodu kɔdi kudɔ na ɔda kabuli kadi kɔnu kani mɔɔtina kowodu bunye.

english_verse: Then he asked, “Amos, what do you see?” “A measuring line,” I answered. The Lord said, “I'm using this measuring line to show that my people Israel don't measure up, and I won't forgive them any more.
translation_verse: Ɔ́kpali-mi úye ɔnini, “Amos, bi na aanu?” Amu na lídie kenye nnini, “Kabuli kani mɔɔtina kowodu bunye.” Mmɔ na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Kabuli kamɛni na líti mɔɔkɔ́ku mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ taatina ka baaakɛ ligeen, mmomu bese aani kowodu kɔni nábu na nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo-ma buti bɔkyiɛ.

english_verse: Their sacred places will be destroyed, and I will send war against the nation of King Jeroboam.” Amos and Amaziah
translation_verse: Na ndubɔbwɛ Isak kaba kemmo bebi baƒiɔ kɔkpakɔ kɔmmɔ ƒui na lɛbwɛ Israelƒuɔ kɔkpakɔ kedee kɔmmɔ ƒui. Na lɛbwɛ Ɔga Yeroboam lɛga kadikɔ kammɔ.” Amos Ku Amasia Lɛlɔ Litemi

english_verse: Amaziah the priest at Bethel sent this message to King Jeroboam of Israel, “Amos is plotting against you in the very heart of Israel. Our nation cannot put up with his message for very long.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Amasia ɔni ndi ɔkpane unengudi na Betel ɔ́tala na bátásu Yeroboam, Israelƒuɔ ɔga, ɔnini, “Amos unye ɔɔví-ɔ kalɔ momoomo ɔni na ɔɔɔdia na awɔ ɔlati ƒula kalɔ kemmo na Israel kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na mɔɔnu ka ɔmmɔ ɔdubo kalɔ kammɔ ƒui bubile na bekyuli bammɔ lɛnɔ balakana-nwu lɛlɔ bɔta búnye na beni lɛla lɛni na ɔɔsu.

english_verse: Here is what he is saying: ‘Jeroboam will be put to death, and the people will be taken to a foreign country.’ ”
translation_verse: Na nwuna kenye ndi ɔnini, ‘Badubo Ɔga Yeroboam bɔdu na beƒie kalɔ kammɔ bekyuli batɔlɔku besienku kaƒɔ na kekpo kemmo.’ ”

english_verse: Then Amaziah told me, “Amos, take your visions and get out! Go back to Judah and earn your living there as a prophet.
translation_verse: Kama ni, ɔkpane unengudi Amasia ɔmɛni úbasu-mi ɔnini, “Amos, ti ala na avi alɛ mɛni! Na eteesie Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ na atátaabla ƒula kenye budie kabla na mmɔ na akɛ ƒula lɛdila.

english_verse: Don't do any more preaching at Bethel. The king worships here at our national temple.”
translation_verse: Sɔ tasu ƒula kenye kadi na mɛni, ɔsika mɛni kadi kakpakɔ ute ɔga ku nwuna lɛga kadikɔ bekyuli bammɔ ƒui.”

english_verse: I answered: I'm not a prophet! And I wasn't trained to be a prophet. I am a shepherd, and I take care of fig trees.
translation_verse: Amu na lídie kenye nnini, “Lɛɛɛdi Katɔti Kenye Udiene ɔni mɔɔbla kabla taaƒɔ egulabi adi. Baƒonu ɔdane na ndi na mɔɔnu adingyii lɛnɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord told me to leave my herds and preach to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti nábakpanku-mi na bebuo lɛlɔ kanukɔ mmɔ, na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Sie na atásu mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ mina kenye.’

english_verse: Now, listen to what the Lord says about you: Your wife will become a prostitute in the city, your sons and daughters will be killed in war, and your land will be divided among others. You will die in a country of foreigners, and the people of Israel will be dragged from their homeland.
translation_verse: “Unwoti ɔnini, ‘Ƒ'ulekudi ɔdubo ɔsɔnɔdine ɔyalɛ ubendi bunwini na ɔma unengudi ɔmɛni kemmo. Na ƒula bebi bananabi ku belekubi ƒui kuwii kenye na badubo bɔtɛ. Bekyuli badubo kalɔ kani ndi awɔ ɔlati kadi mɛni bɔkɔku na bele-ka bete lɛlɔ. Na kaƒɔ, na kadi bamba kalɔ lɛlɔ na adubo bukpi. Na kekpo kadubo Israelƒuɔ bukpo na beƒie-ma batɔlɔku bana lɛma ƒui.’ ”

english_verse: and asked, “Amos, what do you see?” “A basket of ripe fruit,” I replied. Then he said, “This is the end for my people Israel. I won't forgive them again.
translation_verse: Amu na úye-mi ɔnini, “Amos, bi na aanu?” Mmɔ na lídie kenye nnini, “Mɔɔnu kagyigyɛ ku egyiibi egyiedi ani nánu mmɔ.” Amu na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Mina kadi bekyuli Israelƒuɔ bani nánu bási kugyii lɛlɔ kawɔlɔkɔ na kadi mmɔ. Nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo lɛla lɛdi buti bɔkyiɛ-ma.”

english_verse: Instead of singing in the temple, they will cry and weep. Dead bodies will be everywhere. So keep silent! I, the Lord, have spoken!” Israel Is Doomed The Lord said:
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Na limeyi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, lɛnu lɛni na beedie na kakpakɔ mmɔ ƒui lɛdubo bunwini keku ku kɔnyana buwulo sɔɔn na bekpine badubɔƒɔ kesi kesii. Anwuɔsu awɔ bile kenye na asɔ elie kpoo ataanu!” Unwoti Ɔdubo Israelƒuɔ Kɔtu Bɔni Na Bana Ekpidi Pii Ɔsu

english_verse: You say to yourselves, “How much longer before the end of the New Moon Festival? When will the Sabbath be over? Our wheat is ready, and we want to sell it now. We can't wait to cheat and charge high prices for the grain we sell. We will use dishonest scales
translation_verse: Biiye bɛnii, ‘Bi ɔsu na emeyi alasa bɔdi na buse kalɔ buteeye bula antabi, na lɛnwunameyi lɛnɔ lilavi pla na ɔdia na butaadi bula kakpa kuye? Ɔƒɛni na bɔɔwia ka butaadi kuye kɔmmɔ na bɔsia ala kuye kalɛ na ala ammɔ aƒɔ-bu kuye. Na bɔƒana akɔkula ammɔ lɛnɔ kalɛ na bɔnya-ma bɔkya na bɔkɛ kɔsia kaduɛ.

english_verse: and mix dust in the grain. Those who are needy and poor don't have any money. We will make them our slaves for the price of a pair of sandals.”
translation_verse: Na bɔsala antabi ammɔ ku ebiedi ƒui bɔkya buye. Na bani mɔɔyaki ala ku bawabane bani neeebo egulabi na baƒɔ bana kɔyu kɔni na bada ni, bɔdubɔƒɔ-ma buye na lɛgbanvuo kayu kenye na benwini-bu kabla bablane.’ ”

english_verse: I, the Lord, won't forget any of this, though you take great pride in your ancestor Jacob.
translation_verse: Unwoti úse kenye ɔkɛnku kalɛ na Israelƒuɔ baabu-nwu kenye ɔnini, “Lɛɛɛdubo ala ani udu na bábla mɛni bɔyiƒala.

english_verse: Your country will tremble, and you will mourn. It will be like the Nile River that rises and overflows, then sinks back down.
translation_verse: Ndubo bɔya na kayawi kemodi kammɔ katɔ kpakpaakpa na bekyuli bani mebu melie-ka kemmo bewulo kɔnyana na bataata teebo aani kalɛ na Nil Ketu keeƒuƒuo taakɔ taasɔ taayu.

english_verse: On that day, I, the Lord God, will make the sun go down at noon, and I will turn daylight into darkness.
translation_verse: “Na limeyi lɛdubo lɛni na ndubɔya na ɔƒɛ ɔda bukeye ɔya ɔƒiiwi ketee na kalɔ kammɔ kabla suu.

english_verse: Your festivals and joyful singing will turn into sorrow. You will wear sackcloth and shave your heads, as you would at the death of your only son. It will be a horrible day.
translation_verse: Na bina emeyi buni ani na bɛɛdi ƒui ndubɔya na enwini keku ku kɔnyana buwulo sɔɔn. Na bina adala adubunwini adikpi ekuku na bikpeyi eli bɛkɛ bitaavi. Na ɔdubɔbla aani si ubi unwi pɛ ɔni na ukyuli ɔdi ubo náyii-nwu na uuwulo. Na limeyi limodi lɛmmɔ lɛdubɔbla ɔdu kati kati sɔɔn limeyi.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, also promise you a terrible shortage, but not of food and water. You will hunger and thirst to hear my message.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Emeyi adubo ani na kɔka kpakplaa geen kɔdubo na kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui. Nsu ɔɔɔdi adila iye ntu kɔka. Mmomu mina litemi bunu kɔka, ɔsika bɛdubɔwia kpakplaa ka binu kenye kadi bɛsiku-mi kudɔ, nsu bilénu lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: You will search everywhere— from north to south, from east to west. You will go all over the earth, seeking a message from me, the Lord. But you won't find one.
translation_verse: Bɛdubo bɔka bɔmana bɛnii bɛɛwia-mi kenye kadi binu ɔ́si katɔ útédu ɔƒɛ katukɔ na ɔsɔ ɔsi kada kakɛ útédu ɔƒɛ kanukɔ, nsu ukpludi na bɛkɛ bɛɛkɔ́ taayu na bilanu lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: Your beautiful young women and your young men will faint from thirst.
translation_verse: Na bakloƒu ku begblebi bayikune muedi badubo bubuli si uwi ɔmmɔ údu na kɔka kɔmmɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: You made promises to the goddess Ashimah at Samaria; you made vows to other gods at the shrines of Dan and Beersheba. So now you will fall and never get up.
translation_verse: Na bani mɔɔbla kɔƒa ala taakpali Samaria baƒiɔ, bani nkya Dan ku Beer-Seba teese kenye ni, badubo bubuli ɔni na basɔ balakana bɔta lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: I saw a vision of the Lord standing by the temple altar, and he said, “Shake the columns until the tops fall loose, and the doorposts crumble. Then make the pieces fall on the people below. I will take a sword and kill anyone who escapes.
translation_verse: Lɛ́nu ka Unwoti unye lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Kunku akpa enengudi ammɔ momoomo útédu ka ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ɔ́kunku útálɛ kowodu kalɔ ƒui. Na lɛsa limodi lɛmmɔ ligyingya na lɛta lɛmmɔ lɛƒɛ libayu bekyuli bammɔ lɛlɔ. Na si badi bébu ni, ndubo-ma bɔdu ku kuwii. Na ina ukyuli unwi muedi ulébu na ɔdi lɛnɔ ulakana bukeli.

english_verse: “If they dig deep into the earth or climb to the sky, I'll reach out and get them.
translation_verse: Si béku ubu na béduo bésie kalɔ kemmo ƒui dɛ muedi ni, ndubɔnu-ma lidie lɛsiku mmɔ. Na si bɔkɔ na bákɔ bésie katɔ katɔ kakaaka lɛnɔ ni, mina kɔnu kɔda-ma na mmɔ lɛnɔ na liboku-ma kalɔ.

english_verse: If they escape to the peaks of Mount Carmel, I'll search and find them. And if they hide from me at the bottom of the ocean, I'll command a sea monster to bite them.
translation_verse: Si ina Karmel Kɔbi lili na bésie bátábɛ muedi ni, ndubo-ma bɔwia bɔnu na liƒie-ma. Si béduo ɛpu kalɔ ƒui lɛnɔ ni, ndubo liƒu kebweyi kammɔ ɔda bubo na ɔdu-ma na mmɔ.

english_verse: I'll send a sword to kill them, wherever their enemies drag them off as captives. I'm determined to hurt them, not to help them.” His Name Is the Lord
translation_verse: Si bana bekisine nábɔku-ma bátákya kaƒɔ ɔgyu dɛ muedi ni, ndubɔya na kuwii kɔtu-ma kɔdu na mmɔ. Mina anumi adubɔlɛ-ma lɛlɔ geen ute likpidi lɛni ndubɔlɛku-ma, na ɔɔɔdi lɛbuni lɛdi munu munu.”

english_verse: When the Lord God All-Powerful touches the earth, it melts, and its people mourn. God makes the earth rise and then fall, just like the Nile River.
translation_verse: Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui ndi anwu ɔni na si útuku kalɔ kammɔ ni, kaayɛɛlɛ, na bekyuli bani na beli-ka kemmo ƒui beewulo kɔnyana. Na kalɔ kammɔ kaata taawɔ aani kalɛ na Nil Ketu keeƒuƒuo taakɔ taayu.

english_verse: He built his palace in the heavens and let its foundations rest on the earth. He scoops up the ocean and empties it on the earth. His name is the Lord. The Lord Is God
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔmmɔ nátu nwuna lɛgadi kesii ɔ́kya katɔ kakaaka ƒui, na kana ɔka ndi kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ. Na ɔɔyá na ntu bɔɔsí ɛpu kemmo teebewi kalɔ lɛlɔ. Anwu ndi Unwoti.

english_verse: Israel, I am the Lord God, and the Ethiopians are no less important to me than you are. I brought you out of Egypt, but I also brought the Philistines from Crete and the Arameans from Kir.
translation_verse: “Israelƒuɔ, ami ndi Unwoti Katɔti, na buse na Kusiƒuɔ bese bete-mi aani bina kalɛ. Ɔsika kalɛ na lɛ́kpanku-mii lɛ́siku Egyipte kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, lɛni kani na lɛ́kpanku Ƒilistiƒuɔ lɛ́siku Kaƒtor. Na lɛ́kpanku Siriaƒuɔ lɛ́siku Kir.

english_verse: My eyes have seen what a sinful nation you are, and I'll wipe you out. But I will leave a few of Jacob's descendants. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Ami ɔlati néti mina anumi lɛ́nu ekpidi ani udu na amii kadi kamɛni bekyuli bɛɛbla. Anwuɔsu na ndubo bina ƒui udu bɔyila na kalɔ kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ, na kebu Yakob kaba kemmo bebi ɛlɛɛ badi kani. Ami Unwoti násu!

english_verse: At my command, all of you will be sifted like grain. Israelites who remain faithful will be scattered among the nations. And the others will be trapped like trash in a sifter.
translation_verse: “Ndubo ɔda bubo na bekyuli begyingya-mii bakya kayawi aani kalɛ na baatanyi ɔlaaƒɔ teedie atago, na atago ebi ammɔ ina unwi uleduo ɔlaaƒɔ ɔbuni ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Some of you are evil, and you deny that you will ever get caught. But you will be killed. The Lord's Promise to Israel
translation_verse: Bina badi bɛdi bekyuli bekpidi geen, na bɛɛsu bɛnii, ‘Ɔgbankpi ɔdi ɔɔɔdubo-bu bɔsiaku.’ Nsu bina ƒui bɛdubo bukpi na kuwii kenye. Unwoti Ɔdubɔsɔku Israel Unyene Nwuna Kenyekɔ

english_verse: In the future, I will rebuild David's fallen kingdom. I will build it from its ruins and set it up again, just as it used to be.
translation_verse: “Nwuna kama ni, ndubɔsɔ libo na mbasɔku Dawid lɛga kadikɔ lise na lɛklibi ala ani néebie mmɔ, na asɔ atɛ kaduɛ.

english_verse: Then you will capture Edom and the other nations that are mine. I, the Lord, have spoken, and my words will come true.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Edom bekyuli bani nébu ku kadi ƒui bekyuli bani na lɛ́lɔ aani mina badi badubɔwia-mi kama ulu. Lɛni na Unwoti ɔni mɔɔbla ala amɛni ƒui ɔ́su úse.

english_verse: You will have such a harvest that you won't be able to bring in all of your wheat before plowing time. You will have grapes left over from season to season; your fruitful vineyards will cover the mountains.
translation_verse: “Bɛdubo edula bɔƒɛ ɔni na bilakana-nya ƒui bɔlɛku buboku ɔma asa na wasɔ wedu edula ɔkyawi. Egyiibi pii adububu-mii ɔ́si edula ɔƒɛwi útédu edula ɔƒɛwi bamba. Na adingyii ani mɔɔnwu uwi ndi uwi mmɔ adubɔƒɔ abi ammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui.

english_verse: I'll make Israel prosper again. You will rebuild your towns and live in them. You will drink wine from your own vineyards and eat the fruit you grow.
translation_verse: Ndubɔya na ala asɔ adianku Israel. Na bɛsɔku bina lɛma bɛtu na bilie-ni kemmo. Na bɛdubɔkɛ ntɛ buni bɔni bɔsiku bina adingyii mmo egyiibi ani muudie-mii ntɛ kemmo. Na bɛdi amii alati adingyii ebi ani na bɛ́tuma.

english_verse: I'll plant your roots deep in the land I have given you, and you won't ever be uprooted again. I, the Lord God, have spoken!
translation_verse: Ndubɔya na bidie lidu bisie ɔgyu aani kugyii kalɛ na bina kalɔ kani kemmo na bilie, na ɔdi ɔsɔ ulágyu-mii uledie bina kenyekɔ. Ami Unwoti Katɔti násu!”

english_verse: The Lord God gave Obadiah a message about Edom, and this is what we heard: “I, the Lord, have sent a messenger with orders for the nations to attack Edom.”
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́su kenye kadi ɔ́siku Edomƒuɔ lɛlɔ na údie ɔ́tina Obadia ɔnini, “Ami Unwoti lɛ́tala ɔtu ɔdi ku kenye kadi, na líbo ɔda ka kadi bekyuli ƒui betékpo Edom.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Edom: I will make you the weakest and most despised nation.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔ́su Edomƒuɔ ɔnini, “Ndubo-mii bɔbla na bɛsɔ na kadi ƒui akɔ na balabu-mii balakya lɛla lɛdi akɔ.

english_verse: You live in a mountain fortress, because your pride makes you feel safe from attack, but you are mistaken.
translation_verse: Lɛmɛnɛ likpludi kani na bilie bɛɛkun na abi eli, na atakpɛ akɔ kesii kani na bɛɛkali bɛnii bɛ́kɛ kagyumanakɔ mmɔ na bɛɛsu bɛnii, ‘Ukyuli ɔdi ulakana-bu bɔni bɔsiku mɛni buboku kalɔ na ɔdi-bu lɛlɔ.’

english_verse: I will still bring you down, even if you fly higher than an eagle or nest among the stars. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: “Nsu ina dɛ na bíveyi bɛ́kɔ katɔ katɔ aani kɔdigbo aasɛ na bɛ́bla bina ayu na ayabi lɛlɔ muedi ni, ndubo-mii kalɔ buboku. Ami Unwoti násu!

english_verse: If thieves break in at night, they steal only what they want. And people who harvest grapes always leave some unpicked. But, Edom, you are doomed!
translation_verse: “Si beyune bábwɛ béduo kaduli kadi usien ni, lɛla lɛni na baawia kani na beeti. Na si bekyuli béde egyiibi adi ni, ana ƒui alasa bɔla na egyii kalɔ.

english_verse: Everything you treasure most will be taken from you.
translation_verse: Ƒula akɛla ani náƒɔ-ɔ kuye geen mmɔ ƒui badubo-nya buti bɔtɔlɔku kede kede.

english_verse: Your allies can't be trusted. They will force you out of your own country. And your best friends will trick and trap you, even before you know it.
translation_verse: Ƒula bebunkune bani na benye-ɔ kama baaadi bekyuli bani na basia lɛnu. Budi na bédi-ɔ bálɛku ƒula ɔma bétédu ɔmii lɛlɔ. Na ƒula bakpana bammɔ bálɛ-ɔ kama na básia lɛlɔ bákɛ bana kɔsia. Ama bani na awɔ ku-ma bɛɛsála taadi. Na baakya-a lɛlɔ lɛma teeye banii wɛ na nwuna lɛnunda ƒui lɛkya.”

english_verse: Edom, when this happens, I, the Lord, will destroy all your marvelous wisdom.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Si limeyi lɛmmɔ lídu ni, ndubo-ɔ udu bɔyila na lɛdu ƒula banundane ƒui ku bana kɔkwɛ ƒui.

english_verse: Warriors from the city of Teman will be terrified, and you descendants of Esau will be wiped out. The Lord Condemns Edom's Cruelty
translation_verse: Liƒu bonwu lɛdubo Teman ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ bekpone buƒie, na badubɔdu amii Edomƒuɔ ƒui.

english_verse: You were cruel to your relatives, the descendants of Jacob. Now you will be destroyed, disgraced forever.
translation_verse: Bɛ́bla bina lɛlɔ bekyuli bani ndi Yakob kaba kemmo bebi kalala. Anwuɔsu ɔƒaani ni, bɛdubo kɔƒa bɔdi uwi ƒui na badi-mii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You stood there and watched as foreigners entered Jerusalem and took what they wanted. In fact, you were no better than those foreigners.
translation_verse: Bínye bɛ́nu uwi ɔni na kadi bamba bekyuli béduo Yerusalem na béti ala ani ƒui na baayɔ́ bátɔlɔku. Na bátu egulabi bánu na Yerusalem lɛlɔ. Na geen ni, bina ɔbladu ɔ́tina ka bítavumanaku baƒɔ bammɔ.

english_verse: Why did you celebrate when such a dreadful disaster struck your relatives? Why were you so pleased when everyone in Judah was suffering?
translation_verse: Bi ɔsu na lɛlɔ lɛɛyɔ́-mii si ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni udu ɔ́lɛku bina lɛlɔ bekyuli? Na bi ɔsu na ebiti aada-mii lɛni si Yudani biala uubó abi amɛni udu?

english_verse: They are my people, and you were cruel to them. You went through their towns, sneering and stealing whatever was left.
translation_verse: Mina bekyuli na badi, nsu amii bɛɛbla-ma kalala. Bításia-ma lɛma kemmo ƒui bɛ́vi na bɛɛpii-ma taama. Na bíyu ala akladi ani nébu na bana lɛma kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: In their time of torment, you ambushed refugees and handed them over to their attackers. The Lord Will Judge the Nations
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bakya lɛbibo kemmo ni, utalɛ ka bílie bani muukeli ulu lɛlɔ na bíƒie-ma bíte bana bekisine bani muukpó-ma.

english_verse: The day is coming when I, the Lord, will judge the nations. And, Edom, you will pay in full for what you have done.
translation_verse: “Limeyi lɛdubo lɛni na ami Unwoti ndubɔtɛku kadi ƒui litemi. Na amii Edomƒuɔ ni, bɛdubɔƒɔ kayu kani ƒui na bɛda na bina ablala kenye.

english_verse: I forced the people of Judah to drink the wine of my anger on my sacred mountain. Soon the neighboring nations must drink their fill— then vanish without a trace. Victory for Israel
translation_verse: Línye Yudaƒuɔ lɛlɔ na báni mina kɔnyi aani ntɛ na mina kɔbi kedee lɛlɔ. Na uwi uletu kadi bamba bekyuli lɛnɔ badubɔkɛ ama ɔdi na bayii ku udu ku udu ɔni na basɔ belénu bana ɔdi kɔku lɛnɔ kudii.

english_verse: The Lord's people who escape will go to Mount Zion, and it will be holy. Then Jacob's descendants will capture the land of those who took their land.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti bekyuli bani ndubɔlɛ ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ kemmo badubulie Sion Kɔbi kedee lɛlɔ. Na Yakob kaba kemmo bebi bammɔ badubɔsɔ baƒɔ bana kalɔ kani na nka kadi bana ɔdi mmɔ basiku bekyuli bani néƒie-ka báƒɔ mmɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: Israel will be a fire, and Edom will be straw going up in flames. The Lord has spoken!
translation_verse: Na Israel ɔdubunwini aani ogya na ɔkyula Edom ɔni na ndubɔbla aani lɛtɔ lɛni ndubɔda ogya. Ami Unwoti násu!”

english_verse: The people of Israel who live in the Southern Desert will take the land of Edom. Those who live in the hills will capture Philistia, Ephraim, and Samaria. And the tribe of Benjamin will conquer Gilead.
translation_verse: Na Israelƒuɔ bani na beli Negev kalɔ kemmo badubuti Edomƒuɔ abi lɛlɔ kɔlɔ kɔmmɔ. Na bani na beli abi lɛlɔ lɛnɔ beti Ƒilistiƒuɔ ku Eƒraim ku Samariaƒuɔ kɔlɔ. Na Benyamin kɔdua beti Gileadƒuɔ kɔlɔ.

english_verse: Those who return from captivity will control Phoenicia as far as Zarephath. Captives from Jerusalem who were taken to Sepharad will capture the towns of the Southern Desert.
translation_verse: Na bani na kekpo kéƒie asa na básɔ bénwini bébo lɛnɔ beti Kanaanƒuɔ kalɔ útálɛ Sareƒat. Na bekyuli bani na béƒie básiku Yerusalem na béti-ma bésienku Seƒarad ni, badubɔdi lɛma lɛni nkya Negev mmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Those the Lord has saved will live on Mount Zion and rule over Edom. Then the kingdom will belong to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na bani Unwoti ɔ́ƒɔ mmɔ badubɔkya Sion Kɔbi lɛlɔ na badi Edom lɛlɔ. Na lɛga kadikɔ kammɔ ƒui kenwini Unwoti kadi.

english_verse: One day the Lord told Jonah, the son of Amittai,
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́su Yona, Amitai ubidi, kenye kadi ɔnii,

english_verse: to go to the great city of Nineveh and say to the people, “The Lord has seen your terrible sins. You are doomed!”
translation_verse: “Ta na esie ɔma unengudi ɔni baalɔ banii Niniwe, na atákɔ lɛsa ete-ma ka ami Unwoti mɔɔnu kalɛ na ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli baabla likyulikpi ala.”

english_verse: Instead, Jonah ran from the Lord. He went to the seaport of Joppa and found a ship that was going to Spain. So he paid his fare, then got on the ship and sailed away to escape.
translation_verse: Nsu ka Yona ulayɔ ka usie ɔsu ni, úkeli úsie Yopa ɔnii utéti ɔkɔlɔ ubendi na mmɔ na uteesie kalɔ kani baalɔ banii Tarsis. Amu na ɔ́ƒɔ kayu na úduo ɔkɔlɔ ubendi ɔmmɔ kemmo na básia ntu anumi bésela Tarsis kalɔ lɛlɔ likpo lɛni na watábɛ Unwoti.

english_verse: But the Lord made a strong wind blow, and such a bad storm came up that the ship was about to be broken to pieces.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́ya na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ubendi ɔdi úkpo na ɛpu lɛlɔ. Na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ɔ́yu ɔkplu geen ɔni na ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ ɔ́ya bɔbwɛ muedi.

english_verse: The sailors were frightened, and they all started praying to their gods. They even threw the ship's cargo overboard to make the ship lighter. All this time, Jonah was down below deck, sound asleep.
translation_verse: Na liƒu libendi lɛ́da bekyuli bani ƒui nkya ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo na ɔdi biala ɔɔva momoomo taakpali nwuna unwoti. Na kalɛ na ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ walɛ unu ɔsu ni, béƒwimi bana etila ani ƒui nkya ɔkɔlɔ ubendi ɔmmɔ kemmo bákya ɛpu kemmo. Nsu uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, Yona ɔ́yu úsie ɔkɔlɔ ubendi ɔmmɔ kalɔ ɔtɔ unwi kemmo útátɛ ɔlɛɛ geen.

english_verse: The ship's captain went to him and said, “How can you sleep at a time like this? Get up and pray to your God! Maybe he will have pity on us and keep us from drowning.”
translation_verse: Amu na unengu ɔni mɔɔka ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ útánu Yona ka ɔtɛ ɔlɛɛ, na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na atɛ alɛɛ lɛni? Ta pla na akpali ƒula Katɔti na eye kebunku. Ɔƒɛni kalɛ ɔdubɔnu bu kɔnyana na ɔƒɔ-bu ngba.”

english_verse: Finally, the sailors got together and said, “Let's ask our gods to show us who caused all this trouble.” It turned out to be Jonah.
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bani ƒui nkya ɔkɔlɔ ubendi ɔmmɔ kemmo básala eli lisu na básu banini, “Bɔdubo egulabi bɔtu bɔnu ukyuli ɔni lɛlɔ ɔsu na bɔɔkɛ́ ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni udu.” Na ka bátu-ni, Yona lɛnyi nálɛ.

english_verse: They started asking him, “Are you the one who brought all this trouble on us? What business are you in? Where do you come from? What is your country? Who are your people?”
translation_verse: Amu na básu-nwu banini, “Ɔƒɛni su-bu, ɔma ɔsu na bɔɔkɛ́ ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni udu! Na bi ndi ƒula kalabla? Na wɛ na asi? Kalɔ kamani na asi? Kadi ukyuli ɔmani na adi?”

english_verse: Jonah answered, “I'm a Hebrew, and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Yona údie kenye ɔnini, “Hebrini na ndi. Na mɔɔkpali Unwoti Katɔti ɔni nkya katɔ. Na anwu nédie kalɔ ku ɛpu.”

english_verse: When the sailors heard this, they were frightened, because Jonah had already told them he was running from the Lord. Then they said, “Do you know what you have done?”
translation_verse: Liƒu lɛ́da bekyuli bani ƒui nkya ɔkɔlɔ ubendi ɔmmɔ kemmo, ɔsika Yona ɔ́ɔsu-ma úbavi ka Unwoti na uukeli. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu béye-nwu banini, “Bi ndi ƒula kabla?”

english_verse: The storm kept getting worse, until finally the sailors asked him, “What should we do with you to make the sea calm down?”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmɛni ƒui kemmo ni, na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ bukpo bɔɔkɔ́ katɔ teebu, ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo bekyuli béye-nwu banini, “Bi na ɔlɛka bɔbla-a ɔƒɛni asa na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ɔda ɔya?”

english_verse: Jonah told them, “Throw me into the sea, and it will calm down. I'm the cause of this terrible storm.”
translation_verse: Amu na Yona ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ngyi ka mina bɔƒiɔ ɔsu na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ubendi ɔmɛni udu uukpó. Anwuɔsu bibo-mi bɛkya ɛpu kemmo na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔda bukpo bɔya.”

english_verse: The sailors tried their best to row to the shore. But they could not do it, and the storm kept getting worse every minute.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo bekyuli bákya ɔkplu ka basɔku ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ besienku ketudɔ. Nsu uwi ɔmmɔ geen na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔ́nyi anyi úbu. Ɔmɛni ɔsu bátakana.

english_verse: So they prayed to the Lord, “Please don't let us drown for taking this man's life. Don't hold us guilty for killing an innocent man. All of this happened because you wanted it to.”
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu béwulo bákpali Unwoti banini, “Unwoti, buuvele-ɔ, teti ukyuli ɔmɛni kukpi tani-bu kɔtu si búbo-nwu bɔ́kya ɛpu kemmo. O Unwoti, awɔ mɔɔbla lɛla lɛni na aayɔ́.”

english_verse: Then they threw Jonah overboard, and the sea calmed down.
translation_verse: Amu na bágyu Yona na béƒwimi-nwu bákya ɛpu kemmo. Na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ɔ́da bukpo ɔ́ya kɔnakunwi.

english_verse: The sailors were so terrified that they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made all kinds of promises.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔ́ya na ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo bekyuli ƒui báyia Unwoti, na béti enugya akpala béte-nwu na bése kenye lɛnɔ béte-nwu.

english_verse: The Lord sent a big fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti údie lɛdi na kabɛ kebendi kadi kébweli Yona. Na Yona úlie kabɛ kammɔ kaƒɔ kemmo usien ku ɔƒɛ, emeyi atɛ.

english_verse: From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the Lord his God:
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na Yona ɔkya kabɛ kamɛni kaƒɔ kemmo na ɛpu ntu kalɔ ni, ɔ́kpali nwuna Unwoti Katɔti na ɔ́su ɔnini,

english_verse: When I was in trouble, Lord, I prayed to you, and you listened to me. From deep in the world of the dead, I begged for your help, and you answered my prayer.
translation_verse: “Na mina kɔnyana buwulo kemmo ni, O Unwoti, lɛ́kpali-ɔ na énu-mi bɔkpali. Na líwulo lívele ƒula kebunku ɔ́siku kekpine, na énu-mi bɔkpali.

english_verse: You threw me down to the bottom of the sea. The water was churning all around; I was completely covered by your mighty waves.
translation_verse: Édie-mi ákya ɛpu ntu kalɔ kalɔ ƒui likpo lɛni ntu bɔ́ka bɔ́mana-mi, na ɛpu únwini avlɔvɔ na eebó-mi teesienku lɛƒɛnyi lɛni ƒui.

english_verse: I thought I was swept away from your sight, never again to see your holy temple.
translation_verse: Lɛ́bu nnii áyila-mi udu ƒui na ƒula anumi, na nsɔ lɛɛɛdubo ƒula kakpakɔ kedee bɔnu kudii.

english_verse: I was almost drowned by the swirling waters that surrounded me. Seaweed had wrapped around my head.
translation_verse: Ɛpu ntu búƒie-mi na ɛpu ntu kemmo, na alakpi lɛnɔ ákwɛ aka amana-mi lɛlɔ ƒui.

english_verse: I had sunk down deep below the mountains beneath the sea. I knew that forever, I would be a prisoner there. But, you, Lord God, rescued me from that pit.
translation_verse: Lɛ́yu lísie ɛpu ntu kalɔ kalɔ na abi enengudi ƒui kalɔ kesii kani na lɛ́bu nnii bébo-mi lɛkpu bákya uwi ƒui. Nsu awɔ Unwoti mina Katɔti áda-mi édie éboku ngba.

english_verse: When my life was slipping away, I remembered you— and in your holy temple you heard my prayer.
translation_verse: “Uwi ɔni na lɛ́bu nnii mina ngba bɔ́sa ƒui ni, lɛ́kpali-ɔ, na awɔ mina Unwoti énu mina bɔkpali na ƒula kakpakɔ kedee mmɔ.

english_verse: All who worship worthless idols turn from the God who offers them mercy.
translation_verse: Bani mɔɔkpá baƒiɔ ku bani neeebo kɔsia kɔdi bénwini kama bákya awɔ ɔni mɔɔbla-ma lɛƒɔndia.

english_verse: But with shouts of praise, I will offer a sacrifice to you, my Lord. I will keep my promise, because you are the one with power to save.
translation_verse: Nsu ami ndubɔtu lɛnu limwi-ɔ na liti akpala lite-ɔ na lɛdi mina linyese lɛlɔ! Ɔsika ngba bɔƒɔ bɔɔsí Unwoti kudɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord commanded the fish to vomit up Jonah on the shore. And it did.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti údie lɛdi ka kabɛ kammɔ kadala Yona úbewi ketudɔ. Na úbo lɛni.

english_verse: Once again the Lord told Jonah
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tɛmi úte Yona ɔnini,

english_verse: to go to that great city of Nineveh and preach his message of doom.
translation_verse: “Ta na esie Niniwe, ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo, na atákɔ mina lɛsa lɛni lɛ́su-ɔ ete ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli ka ndubo ɔma ɔmmɔ bɔkyula.”

english_verse: Jonah obeyed the Lord and went to Nineveh. The city was so big that it took three days just to walk through it.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu Yona únu Unwoti litemi na ɔ́ta úsie Niniwe ɔma ubendi ɔmmɔ kemmo na úti emeyi atɛ usie ɔ́vi ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: After walking for a day, Jonah warned the people, “Forty days from now, Nineveh will be destroyed!”
translation_verse: Yona úse kalɔ uusié taavi ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo limeyi limodi, na uute-ma bɔti ka, “Badubɔkyula Niniwe ɔma udu ƒui na emeyi aavlene kama.”

english_verse: They believed God's message and set a time when they would go without eating to show their sorrow. Then everyone in the city, no matter who they were, dressed in sackcloth.
translation_verse: Niniweƒuɔ ƒui báƒɔ litemi lɛmɛni bádi. Ɔmɛni ɔsu bábla kasusu ka ɔ́si benengu útálɛ banamu ƒui ni, badubunyimi kenye na bényimi adikpi beti batina ka bana ekpidi éduo-ma.

english_verse: When the king of Nineveh heard what was happening, he also dressed in sackcloth; he left the royal palace and sat in dust.
translation_verse: Lebo lɛni na Niniweƒuɔ ɔga únu litemi lɛmmɔ ni, ɔ́ta ɔ́lɛ nwuna lɛga kadikɔ ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo na údie nwuna agala uwi, na únyimi adikpi na ɔ́sɔ úlie ntɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: When God saw that the people had stopped doing evil things, he had pity and did not destroy them as he had planned.
translation_verse: Ka Katɔti ɔ́nu kalɛ na bávumana na báda bana likyulikpi báya ɔsu ni, ɔ́vumana nwuna kasusu na ɔ́sɔ útani-ma kɔtu aani kalɛ na ɔ́su use kalɛ.

english_verse: Jonah was really upset and angry.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛ ɔ́da Yona, na úti kɔnyi geen.

english_verse: So he prayed: Our Lord, I knew from the very beginning that you wouldn't destroy Nineveh. That's why I left my own country and headed for Spain. You are a kind and merciful God, and you are very patient. You always show love, and you don't like to punish anyone.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔ́kpali Katɔti ɔnini, “Unwoti ɔɔɔdi ɔmɛni na lɛ́su nnii aaadubo ɔma ɔmɛni bɔkyula iye ɔ́si ɔni nkya ɔma. Ɔmɛni ɔsu na lɛ́kya ɔkplu ka likeli lisie Tarsis! Ngyi ka awɔ adi kɔnyana ɔnune Katɔti na ebo kayi buɛɛ uwi ndi uwi, na aakana tavumana ƒula kasusu uwi biala kemmo kalɛ na aláni ukyuli kɔtu lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Now let me die! I'd be better off dead.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ni, Unwoti, ya-mi likpi. Si líkpi ɔdia-mi utulo ka lilie ngba.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “What right do you have to be angry?”
translation_verse: Unwoti údie kenye ɔnini, “Bi ɔyikun na ebo ɔsu na eeti kɔnyi?”

english_verse: Jonah then left through the east gate of the city and made a shelter to protect himself from the sun. He sat under the shelter, waiting to see what would happen to Nineveh.
translation_verse: Yona ɔ́vi ɔlɛ ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na útélie ɔƒɛ katukɔ kakɛ. Na ɔ́tu kevo kadi ute lɛlɔ na uli-ka kemmo ɔɔnu lɛla lɛni malɛ na ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The Lord made a vine grow up to shade Jonah's head and protect him from the sun. Jonah was very happy to have the vine,
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti Katɔti ɔ́ya na kabuli kadi kákwɛ na Yona keliekɔ mmɔ na kátu kébi mmɔ, na uute-nwu ɔyuli ɔni nwuna kalɔ kese buɛɛ. Kubiti kɔ́da Yona geen na kabuli kammɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: but early the next morning the Lord sent a worm to chew on the vine, and the vine dried up.
translation_verse: Nsu lɛdigye ni, Katɔti ɔ́ya na beklubi báyalɛ kabuli kammɔ békulo na káyɛyɛ.

english_verse: During the day the Lord sent a scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, making him feel faint. Jonah was ready to die, and he shouted, “I wish I were dead!”
translation_verse: Ka kadi kammɔ kaata ni, Katɔti ɔ́ya na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni náƒɔ ogya úkpo ɔ́si ɔƒɛ katukɔ úbewi Yona lɛlɔ, na ɔ́ya na ɔƒɛ ɔmmɔ kenye lɛnɔ káyu ɔkplu. Anwuɔsu anumi ánwu-nwu kɔnakunwi, na ɔɔyɔ́ ka ukpi muedi. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu Yona ɔkya ɔɔdɔ na ɔɔká ala ɔnini, “Si líkpi muedi ni, nka ɔdia-mi utulo ɔni na nli ngba mɛni.”

english_verse: But the Lord asked, “Jonah, do you have the right to be angry about the vine?” “Yes, I do,” he answered, “and I'm angry enough to die.”
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ɔyikun na ebo ɔsu na eeti kɔnyi akya kabuli kammɔ?” Yona údie kenye ɔnini, “Mbo kuƒi ka liti kɔnyi kɔni nédu ka líkpi muedi.”

english_verse: But the Lord said: You are concerned about a vine that you did not plant or take care of, a vine that grew up in one night and died the next.
translation_verse: Amu na Unwoti ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Kabuli kani nákwɛ usien uwi na káyii kákya lɛdigye na ɔɔɔdi awɔ náva kebii kammɔ ni, uukpóku-ɔ ka kékpi.

english_verse: I am Micah from Moresheth. And this is the message about Samaria and Jerusalem that the Lord gave to me when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah. Judgment on Samaria
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́su Mika Moresetni kenye kadi, na ala amɛni adanku Samaria ku Yerusalem lɛma linengudi lɛmmɔ na uwi ɔni na Yuda baga Yotam ku Ahas ku Hesekia bélie bádi lɛga ɔdi biala ku nwuna uwi kemmo.

english_verse: Listen, all of you! Earth and everything on it, pay close attention. The Lord God accuses you from his holy temple.
translation_verse: Amii kalɔ lɛlɔ bekyuli ƒui binu! Bise atu kaduɛ na binu, ɔsika Unwoti Katɔti uudie-mii bɔƒiɔ taasiku nwuna keliekɔ kedee na nwuna kakpakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: And he will come down to crush underfoot every pagan altar.
translation_verse: Na ɔdubo bɔsi bubo bubanya bɔvi abi ku abinkpo ammɔ ƒui eli.

english_verse: Mountains will melt beneath his feet like wax beside a fire. Valleys will vanish like water rushing down a ravine.
translation_verse: Abi ƒui adubo bɔyɛɛlɛ aani kalɛ na kɔma kɔɔyɛɛlɛ na ogya kudɔ. Na lɛbonka libendi lɛyii lɛkya aani kalɛ na ntu bɔɔgbá taayu ɔkwalɛ ɔdi taatɔlɔ.

english_verse: This will happen because of the terrible sins of Israel, the descendants of Jacob. Samaria has led Israel to sin, and pagan altars at Jerusalem have made Judah sin.
translation_verse: Yakob kaba kemmo bebi bábla ekpidi pii ɔ́si kalɛ na Samariaƒuɔ bátɔnku-ma ɔsu. Lɛni kani na Yerusalemƒuɔ aƒiodu akpabi ani na bátu áya na Yuda ɔ́bla likpidi.

english_verse: So the Lord will leave Samaria in ruins— merely an empty field where vineyards are planted. He will scatter its stones and destroy its foundations.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na Unwoti ɔdubunye ɔnu na Samaria ɔyii udu na lɛla biala libie lɛbla aani kebu alakpi. Na ɔdubɔta ɔbla aani kesii kani na bálɛ adingyii. Na ɔdubugyingya nwuna lɛtɔ atabi ƒui na ɔgbala-nya utákya ɔkwalɛ na ugyingya awodu ammɔ ɔka ɔni nkya kalɔ kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: Samaria's idols will be smashed, and the wages of temple prostitutes will be destroyed by fire. Silver and gold from those idols will then be used by foreigners as payment for prostitutes. Judah Is Doomed
translation_verse: Badubo Samaria baƒiɔ ƒui bubo bɔbwɛ. Na ogya ɔkyula ala ani na bákɛ básiku bana kakpakɔ na nwuna bayalɛ kabla kammɔ kudɔ. Na baƒɔ bani nse aani bana kalɛ kani bebeti bana akɛla ammɔ ƒui na beti betéte bana lɛƒiɔkpa bayalɛ, ɔsika bayalɛ kudɔ na ala ammɔ ási.

english_verse: Because of this tragedy, I go barefoot and naked. My crying and weeping sound like howling wolves or ostriches.
translation_verse: Ɔgbankpi ɔmɛni ɔsu na nkɛ lɛgbakplu ku kasɔngya. Na biinú mina kɔvanu aani ebuoƒuala ɔni nkɛ mɔɔkwanyi ku keku kani muuwulo teedumo aani likuku.

english_verse: Depart naked and ashamed, you people of Shaphir. The town of Bethezel mourns because no one from Zaanan went out to help.
translation_verse: Na amii Saƒirƒuɔ, bɛvi bɛtɔlɔ ku kasɔngya ku kɔƒa. Na ka bekisine báka Sanaanƒuɔ bákya ɔsu ni, ɔdi ɔɔɔdubo bɔkana bɔlɛ. Na keku ku kɔvanu kɔni nkya Bet-Esel ɔsu ni, bɛgyi bɛnii mmɔ kaaadi kaatamikukɔ kadi.

english_verse: Everyone in Maroth hoped for the best, but the Lord sent disaster down on Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Marotƒuɔ benye bagya Unwoti anumi momoomo ka bakɛ bɔƒɔ bɔdi, ɔsika ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ úudu Yerusalem kabanye suɛlɛ suɛlɛ.

english_verse: Get the war chariots ready, you people of Lachish. You led Jerusalem into sin, just as Israel did.
translation_verse: Amii Lakisƒuɔ, bɛbala bapɔnkɔ bammɔ ku kekpo kɛɛkɛ lɛmmɔ. Amii násiku kalala ala amɛni na Israel bíboku bíbatina Yerusalemƒuɔ.

english_verse: Now you will have to give a going-away gift to Moresheth. Israel's kings will discover that they cannot trust the town of Achzib.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ ɔsu bɛdubute Moreset Gat bɔkada etela na begyingyaku lɛlɔ. Na Israelƒuɔ baga badubɔnu bati ka Aksib ɔɔɔdi katamikukɔ kani na basia lɛnu ka badubɔkɛ bɔƒɔ.

english_verse: People of Mareshah, the Lord will send someone to capture your town. Then Israel's glorious king will be forced to hide in Adullam Cave.
translation_verse: Amii Maresaƒuɔ kadi bekyuli, Unwoti ɔdubo ukisine ɔdi bɔtala bɔkya-mii na ubékpo-mii na uƒie ɔma ɔmmɔ ɔƒɔ. Na Israel batɔnkune ƒui badubukeli na bátábɛ Adulam atakpɛ libu kemmo.

english_verse: Judah, shave your head as bald as a vulture and start mourning. Your precious children will be dragged off to a foreign country.
translation_verse: Bikpeyi bina eli bitédu aani ka bɔpa na ápa aani begbini na biteewulo kɔnyana na bina bebi bani na bɛɛyɔ́ geen ɔsu. Ɔsika badubo-ma buƒie bɔtɔlɔku ƒui buteesienku kaƒɔ ɔgyu kakaaka.

english_verse: Doomed! You're doomed! At night you lie in bed, making evil plans. And when morning comes, you do what you've planned because you have the power.
translation_verse: Bɔbuɛ muute amii bani na likpidi kɔkwɛ kani na bɛɛkya na bɛɛtɛ bina atɛla lɛlɔ teeti likpidi kasusu uwi biala. Na si kadi kégye na bɛɛnu ka bɛ́bla lɛla lɛmmɔ, ɔsika bɛɛnu ka bibo ɔyikun.

english_verse: You grab any field or house that you want; you cheat families out of homes and land.
translation_verse: Biiƒie mmo ku lɛtɔ lɛni na bɛɛwia taaƒɔ. Bɛɛnya bekyuli taakya na bɛɛƒɔ́ bana kɔduli ku kalɔ.

english_verse: But here is what the Lord says: “I am planning trouble for you. Your necks will be caught in a noose, and you will be disgraced in this time of disaster.”
translation_verse: Nsu Unwoti ɔ́lɛ ugyii ka ɔbla lɛla lɛdi, na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Lɛ́klibi ɔgbankpi líse-mii. Na ɔbuli ɔdubo-mii amɔ bɔda, na bɔdi kɔƒa ɔgbankpi uwi ɔmɛni kemmo.

english_verse: When that happens, this sorrowful song will be sung about you: “Ruined! Completely ruined! The Lord has taken our land and given it to traitors.”
translation_verse: Si uwi ɔni na ala amɛni álɛ ni, bekyuli badubo-mii kenye bunye na batu kɔnyana ɔnu ɔmɛni basiku-mii lɛlɔ banini, ‘Bɔ́yii udu! Bɔ́yii udu kede kede! Unwoti ɔ́ƒɔ-bu kalɔ úte bula bekisine.’ ”

english_verse: And so you will never again own property among the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bɛsɔ bɛɛɛdubo kadikɔ kadi bɔkɛ na Unwoti bekyuli akɔ si uwi ɔni na beele kalɔ kammɔ teete-ma.

english_verse: “Enough of your preaching!” That's what you tell me. “We won't be disgraced, so stop preaching!”
translation_verse: Na si mɔɔsu-mii lɛla lɛdi ni, bɛsɔ bitasu bɛnii lɛsa na mɔɔkɔ́ teewi-mii ndubɔya na kɔƒa kukpo-mii. Bitasu bɛnii Katɔti uláya na kɔƒa kukpo-mii.

english_verse: Descendants of Jacob, is it right for you to claim that the Lord did what he did because he was angry? Doesn't he always bless those who do right?
translation_verse: Bɛɛbu bɛnii ɔmɛni ɔɔdia bunu si beeye banini, “Unwoti uuti kɔnyi na ɔbla ala amɛni udu, na uléwi lɛlɔ na ɔkɛ kayi?” Iye Unwoti uléte bekyuli bani mɔɔbla ala ulu lɛlɔ kusɛ kusɛ uwi ndi uwi?

english_verse: My people, you have turned against one another! You have even stolen clothes right off the backs of innocent neighbors who pass by in peace.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Bɛ́da mina bekyuli aani bekisine kalɛ. Na bɛɛbla ala aani si bibo ɔyikun ka bɛbla lɛla biala. Na use aani ama bani nási kekpokɔ na bédie-ma adala ani na bakya ɔni na baaagyi beeese.

english_verse: You take over lovely homes that belong to the women of my nation. Then you cheat their children out of the inheritance that comes from the Lord.
translation_verse: Bíƒie kɔduli kɔbuni kɔni na kɔdi mina kalɔ lɛlɔ beleku bɛ́ƒɔ. Na bɛ́bɔku bana bebi bɛ́lɛku bana kɔlɔ kemmo na bíti-ma kɔdikɔ kɔni na Unwoti úte-ma bínwini bina kɔdi.

english_verse: Get out of here, you crooks! You'll find no rest here. You're not fit to belong to the Lord's people, and you will be destroyed.
translation_verse: “Bɛvi bɛlɛ mɛni, amii bekyuli bekpidi, ɔsika bɛɛɛdubo bɔnwuna bɔdi bɔkɛ na mɛni, na bítamanku lɛnɔ ka bɛbla Unwoti bekyuli. Na bɛdubo udu bɔyii lɛnɔ.

english_verse: The only prophet you want is a liar who will say, “Drink and get drunk!” A Promise of Hope
translation_verse: Kenye Udiene ɔni kani na bɛɛwia ndi ɔkɔ ɔnyine ɔni masu-mii ɔnii bɛdi na bɛni ntɛ bikpi!

english_verse: I, the Lord, promise to bring together the people of Israel who have survived. I will gather them, just as a shepherd brings sheep together, and there will be many.
translation_verse: “Ami Unwoti lise kenye ka ndubɔkpanku Israelƒuɔ bani nébu liboku mbasala aani kalɛ na baƒonu ɔdane ɔɔsála nwuna baƒonu na beemomo.

english_verse: I will break down the gate and lead them out— then I will be their king.
translation_verse: Ndubo kayakun kammɔ bubo bɔbwɛ na lɛkpanku-ma lɛlɛku na linwini-ma ɔga.”

english_verse: Listen to me, you rulers of Israel! You know right from wrong,
translation_verse: Binu amii Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune! Ɔlɛka bɛti likpidi ku lɛbuni kavumana.

english_verse: but you prefer to do evil instead of what is right. You skin my people alive. You strip off their flesh,
translation_verse: Nsu bɛ́ƒuna ka bitaabla likpidi bitulo lɛbuni. Na use aani kalɛ na beedie bekyuli ɔku ku ngba ku ngba. Na baanwí bana ɔlɔna taamami ekubi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: break their bones, cook it all in a pot, and gulp it down.
translation_verse: Na beebó bana ekubi taaƒɛ na baasála ɔna ƒui teeƒulo na libui linwi kemmo taaduli teebweli.

english_verse: Someday you will beg the Lord to help you, but he will turn away because of your sins.
translation_verse: Bɛdubo Unwoti buvele limeyi linwi bɛnii ubunku-mii, nsu ɔdubo kama bunwini bɔkya-mii na ulénu bina bɔkpali na bina ekpidi ɔsu.

english_verse: You lying prophets promise security for anyone who gives you food, but disaster for anyone who refuses to feed you. Here is what the Lord says to you prophets:
translation_verse: “Na amii ɔkɔ kenye bediene biisé bekyuli bani muute-mii adila na bɛɛdi kenye ka badubulie kpi na lɛla lɛdi lilékpoku-ma. Na bani na balakɛ lɛla lɛdi teete-mii ama ni, bɛɛsu-ma ka ɔgbankpi ɔdubɔsiaku-ma. Binu lɛla lɛni na ami Unwoti mɔɔsu-mii.

english_verse: “You will live in the dark, far from the sight of the sun, with no message from me.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛ ɔdubo-mii bɔsa bɔkya na bɛsɔ bilanu bukeye iye binu kenye kadi bɛsiku-mi kudɔ lɛnɔ.

english_verse: You prophets and fortunetellers will all be disgraced, with no message from me.”
translation_verse: Amii kenye bediene ku like bebone ƒui ni, kɔƒa kɔdubo-mii bukpo na bɛsɔ bɛɛɛdubo kenye kadi bunu bɔsiku-mi kudɔ.”

english_verse: But the Lord has filled me with power and his Spirit. I have been given the courage to speak about justice and to tell you people of Israel that you have sinned.
translation_verse: Nsu ami ni, Katɔti Kɔyu kɔ́ƒɔ-mi lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui na úte-mi ɔyikun ka lɛtɛmi lɛsiku litemi geen lɛlɔ bɔdi ulu lɛlɔ siin. Na lidie lɛtina amii Israelƒuɔ kalɛ na bina ekpidi ese.

english_verse: So listen to my message, you rulers of Israel! You hate justice and twist the truth.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu binu kenye kani na nda líboku amii Israelƒuɔ batɔnkune! Bikisi litemi lɛlɔ bɔdi ulu siin lɛlɔ na biinwíni litemi geen lɛmmɔ taalɛ.

english_verse: You make cruelty and murder a way of life in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na bɛ́ya na bekyuli béti kalala bɔbla ku bekyuli bɔdu bénwini ngba bɔni na bekyuli belie ɔƒaamu na Yerusalem.

english_verse: You leaders accept bribes for dishonest decisions. You priests and prophets teach and preach, but only for money. Then you say, “The Lord is on our side. No harm will come to us.”
translation_verse: Na amii batɔnkune bammɔ bɛɛƒɔ́ ala na bɔbɛ kemmo na bɛɛsia kasusu kekpidi kɔnu. Amii bakpane ku kenye bediene ƒui sika ɔsu kani na bɛɛtina ala na bɛɛsu Katɔti litemi lɛmmɔ. Na ɔmɛni ƒui kama bɛɛsu bɛnini, “Unwoti unye-bu kama na likpidi lɛdi lɛɛɛdubo-bu bɔlɛku.”

english_verse: And so, because of you, Jerusalem will be plowed under and left in ruins. Thorns will cover the mountain where the temple now stands.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na amii ɔsu ni, bekisine badubo Yerusalem bɔtu bunwini bubi aani kalɛ na beeti anwami teegulu kalɔ na ɔma ɔmmɔ ubie ɔyii udu. Na liyu alakpi kani ndubo bɔkwɛ bɔƒɔ abi ammɔ lɛlɔ kesii kani na kakpakɔ kammɔ kenye ɔƒɛni.

english_verse: In the future, the mountain with the Lord's temple will be the highest of all. It will reach above the hills, and every nation will rush to it.
translation_verse: Na uwi ukplodi kemmo ni, kɔbi kɔni lɛlɔ na Katɔti kakpakɔ kenye ndubɔbla kɔbi kɔni náƒɔ kuye kutulo abi ƒui akɔ. Kɔdubɔkuku kɔvia abi ƒui eli na kadi bekyuli ƒui badubukeli besie mmɔ.

english_verse: People of many nations will come and say, “Let's go up to the mountain of the Lord God of Jacob and worship in his temple.” The Lord will teach us his Law from Jerusalem, and we will obey him.
translation_verse: Kadi bekyuli badubɔsi kɔlɔ pii lɛlɔ bebo na babasu banini, “Bɛya na bɔkɔ busie Unwoti, Yakob Katɔti, kɔbi lili na nwuna kakpakɔ na ɔtina-bu nwuna lilu na bɔsia-ni lɛlɔ.” Ɔsika Sion mmɔ na badubɔtina-bu ala na bunu Unwoti litemi bɔsiku Yerusalem.

english_verse: He will settle arguments between distant and powerful nations. They will pound their swords and their spears into rakes and shovels; they will never again make war or attack one another.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔdubɔtɛ litemi na ɔklibi kadi ku kadi bayikune bani nkya ƒui unyeƒi ɔni nkya-ma ntɛ. Na bana kuwii ƒui ni, ama alati badubuti-ku bakywɛ anwami bonwu ani muunwíni kalɔ. Na beti bana atula bakywɛ asaaka. Na kadi ku kadi basɔ balata kekpo, na basɔ balatumini bekyuli belete kekpo lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Everyone will find rest beneath their own fig trees or grape vines, and they will live in peace. This is a solemn promise of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli biala ɔdubulie nwuna adingyii kalɔ ɔkɛ bɔnwuna ƒaa na bakɛ keyi buɛɛ. Kenye kpakplaa kamɛni na Unwoti Katɔti Ɔyikune Ƒui úse nwuna bekyuli.

english_verse: Others may follow their gods, but we will always follow the Lord our God. The Lord Will Lead His People Home
translation_verse: Kadi bamba bekyuli badubɔsiaku bana baƒiɔ, nsu abu amu bɔdubɔsiaku bula Unwoti Katɔti uwi ndi uwi.

english_verse: The Lord said: At that time I will gather my people— the lame and the outcasts, and all others into whose lives I have brought sorrow.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ndubo mina bekyuli bani na kekpo kéƒie na béti-ma bátɔlɔku ku bani na lɛbibo líduo-ma keliela kemmo ƒui bɔsala.

english_verse: Then the lame and the outcasts will belong to my people and become a strong nation. I, the Lord, will rule them from Mount Zion forever.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani nébu mɛni na badi balɛne na bani na béƒie bátɔlɔku mɛni kemmo ni, badubunwini mina bekyuli na lɛya na benwini kadi bani na bebo ɔkplu. Na ami Unwoti ndubo Sion Kɔbi lɛlɔ mmɔ bulie na Yerusalem, na ntaadi-ma lɛlɔ úsela uwi ƒui.

english_verse: Mount Zion in Jerusalem, guardian of my people, you will rule again.
translation_verse: Sion Kɔbi na Yerusalem, awɔ ndi mina bekyuli lɛlɔ ɔnune na adubɔsɔ adi lɛga na mina bekyuli lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Jerusalem, why are you crying? Don't you have a king? Have your advisors gone? Are you suffering like a woman in childbirth?
translation_verse: “Yerusalem, bi lɛsɛ na bɛɛní? Eeebo ɔga! Na ƒula kasusu bakyane nɔɔ? Bana ƒui bása bukpi? Bi muubo-ɔ lɛlɔ lɛni aani kalɛ na kawɔƒɔ keeƒie ukyuli?

english_verse: Keep on groaning with pain, you people of Jerusalem! If you escape from your city to the countryside, you will still be taken as prisoners to Babylonia. But later I will rescue you from your enemies.
translation_verse: “Amii Yerusalemƒuɔ, biteedumo ku ɔlɛ bunu! Si bíkeli bina ɔma unengudi kemmo bísie alakpi akɔ muedi ni, badububo-mii bɔnu buƒie bɔsiku mmɔ busienku Babilon. Nsu kama kama ƒui ni, ndubo mbaƒɔ-mii lɛsiku bina bekisine kudɔ.

english_verse: Zion, because of your sins you are surrounded by many nations who say, “We can hardly wait to see you disgraced.”
translation_verse: “Sion, ƒula ekpidi ɔsu na kadi bekyuli pii báka bámana-a na banini, ‘Ɔmɛni anwu buletu uwi bɛya na bɔnu ka bana anumi éwi kalɔ.’

english_verse: But they don't know that I, the Lord, have gathered them here to grind them like grain.
translation_verse: “Nsu bekyuli bamɛni baaagyi lɛla lɛni na ami Unwoti mɔɔkali. Ndubo-ma bɔkɔ kpɛtɛ kpɛtɛ aani kalɛ na baakɔ́ antabi.

english_verse: Smash them to pieces, Zion! I'll let you be like a bull with iron horns and bronze hoofs. Crush those nations and bring their wealth to me, the Lord of the earth.
translation_verse: “Sion, bibo-ma bɛbwɛ biwi kalɔ kɔkɛ kɔkɛ. Ndubo-mii bɔbla aani akɔ ɔgyani ɔni mbo abuala ese na ɔkya abuala egyiedi lɛgbanvuo. Bikpo kadi bammɔ ƒui na biƒie-ma akɛla ƒui bɛƒɔ biboku ami kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ Unwoti.”

english_verse: Jerusalem, enemy troops have surrounded you; they have struck Israel's ruler in the face with a stick.
translation_verse: Yerusalemƒuɔ, bekpone bekisine báka bámana-a na báƒiɛmi Israel ɔtɔnkune ugyii anumi.

english_verse: Bethlehem Ephrath, you are one of the smallest towns in the nation of Judah. But the Lord will choose one of your people to rule the nation— someone whose family goes back to ancient times.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔnini, “Awɔ Betlehem na Eƒrata kalɛkɛ kemmo, awɔ ndi ɔma blii suɛ ntulo na Yuda kalɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu uuuse lɛni, ɔsika ƒula kemmo na ɔtɔnkune ubendi ɔdubɔlɛ ɔsi na watɔnku mina kaduli bekyuli Israelƒuɔ wete-mi. Na ɔdubɔbla ukyuli ɔni na nwuna kaba kése kalɔ kási kukuuku na ala kalɔ kesekɔ ƒui.”

english_verse: The Lord will abandon Israel only until this ruler is born, and the rest of his family returns to Israel.
translation_verse: Na Unwoti ɔdubudie Israel atu wetédu uwi ɔni na uleku ɔni nda kɔƒɔ ɔdubɔwɔ lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔmɛni, na nwuna badi bakladi basɔ benwini bebo Israel.

english_verse: Like a shepherd taking care of his sheep, this ruler will lead and care for his people by the power and glorious name of the Lord his God. His people will live securely, and the whole earth will know his true greatness,
translation_verse: Na lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔmɛni ɔdubɔtɔnku nwuna bekyuli ɔkɛnku Unwoti nwuna Katɔti ɔni lɛnyi muukeye lɛlɔ. Na ɔdubɔnu-ma lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na baƒonu ɔdane ɔɔnu nwuna baƒonu lɛlɔ. Na nwuna bekyuli badubulie ku atu bɔyɔ, na lɛla lɛdi lilékpoku-ma. Na kayawi kadi bekyuli ƒui badubɔnu kalɛ geen na úbomo.

english_verse: because he will bring peace. Assyria Will Be Defeated Let Assyria attack our country and our palaces. We will counterattack, led by a number of rulers
translation_verse: Ɔsika anwu ɔmmɔ geen ndanku keyi buɛɛ ku atu bɔyɔ bammɔ. Si Asiriaƒuɔ békpo-bu kalɛ kalɛ na bébile-bu kalɔ ku bula baga kesii dɛ ni, abu lɛnɔ bula batɔnkune baƒunadi badi badubɔtɔnku-bu na bɔdubukpoku-ma budie kasi.

english_verse: whose strong army will defeat the nation of Assyria. Yes, our leaders will rescue us, if those Assyrians dare to invade our land. The Survivors Will Be Safe
translation_verse: Batɔnkune bamɛni bekpone kpakplaa badubunye na badi Asiriaƒuɔ lɛlɔ na baƒɔ-bu na bana lɛkɔkɔ si bákali ka bakɔ-bu basɔ na beti-bu kalɔ.

english_verse: A few of Jacob's descendants survived and are scattered among the nations. But the Lord will let them cover the earth like dew and rain that refreshes the soil.
translation_verse: Yakob kaba kemmo bebi ɛlɛɛ badi bébu na bégyingya bákya kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui kadi bekyuli akɔ. Nsu Unwoti ɔdubɔya na benwini aani amii ani mɔɔyu teewi ala lɛlɔ iye ɔnantu ɔni mɔɔna na kalɔ kaayɔ́. Na ɔɔɔdubo bɔsi bekyuli kudɔ, mmomu ɔdubɔsi Unwoti ɔlati kudɔ.

english_verse: At present they are scattered, but later they will attack, as though they were fierce lions pouncing on sheep. Their enemies will be torn to shreds, with no one to save them;
translation_verse: Ɔƒaani ni, bekyuli négyingya-ma bákya kalɔ ekpo ekpo ƒui. Nsu kama ni, badubɔta na bekpo bana bekisine aani kalɛ na gyata ɔni néti kɔnyi geen ɔɔta teetéƒie koƒonu. Na begyingya bana bekisine bammɔ kɔkɛ kɔkɛ ɔni na ukyuli ɔdi ulakana-ma bɔƒɔ.

english_verse: they will be helpless, completely destroyed. Idols Will Be Destroyed in Israel
translation_verse: Bekisine bamɛni balakana lɛlɔ bɔnwanɛ ulu biala lɛlɔ, mmomu badubɔyila-ma udu ƒui kede kede.

english_verse: as well as your cities and your fortresses.
translation_verse: Na bina lɛma linengudi ku ɔma kɔgyumanakɔ kɔni na bɛ́tu ƒui ndubo-ku bubile.

english_verse: I will stop you from telling fortunes and practicing witchcraft.
translation_verse: Na bina kabɔ ala bɔbla ku like lɛni na biibó ƒui ndubutile ɔmmɔ bene ƒui ulu.

english_verse: You will no longer worship the idols or stone images you have made— I will destroy them,
translation_verse: “Na atabi ku egyii ala ani na bɛ́nwi bíse lɛlɔ bɛɛkpá mmɔ ni, ndubo-nya bɔbwɛ ƒui na bɛsɔ bɛɛɛdubo-nya bɔkpa lɛnɔ.

english_verse: together with the sacred poles and even your towns.
translation_verse: Na lɛbwɛ bina baƒiɔ ligyii ku bina lɛma lɛnɔ muedi.

english_verse: I will become furious and take revenge on the nations that refuse to obey me.
translation_verse: “Ndubo kɔnyi buti geen, na lɛni kadi bani bekyuli néni banii baaadubo-mi litemi bunu kɔtu na lidie-ma kasi na bana ɔbladu kenye.”

english_verse: The Lord said to his people: Come and present your case to the hills and mountains.
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔ́su nwuna bekyuli ɔnini, “Bɛlɛ bibo na bɛda bina etemila bɛva na bunu na abinkpo ku abi enengudi ƒui anumi.

english_verse: Israel, I am bringing charges against you— I call upon the mountains and the earth's firm foundation to be my witnesses.
translation_verse: Israel, ndubudie bina bɔƒiɔ keyi lɛtina na abi ku kayawi kammɔ ɔ́si kalɔ kesekɔ ƒui na bidie lɛla lɛmmɔ kenye.

english_verse: My people, have I wronged you in any way at all? Please tell me.
translation_verse: “Mina kadi bekyuli, bɛsu na linu si lɛ́ƒiɔ-mii na ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ?

english_verse: I rescued you from Egypt, where you were slaves. I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Lɛ́ƒɔ-mii lɛ́siku Egyipteƒuɔ enu kemmo kesii kani na nka bɛkya bɛɛbla-ma kabla. Na lɛ́tala Mose ku Aaron ku Miriam nnii batɔnku-mii.

english_verse: Don't forget the evil plans of King Balak of Moab or what Balaam son of Beor said to him. Remember how I, the Lord, saved you many times on your way from Acacia to Gilgal. True Obedience
translation_verse: “Bitayiƒala kasusu kekpidi kani na Moabƒuɔ Ɔga Balak ɔ́bla ɔ́siku-mii lɛlɔ iye lɛla lɛni na Beor ubidi Bileam ɔ́su-nwu ku kalɛ na údie kenye. Na binyimo akɔla ala budie taatina ala ani na ami Unwoti lɛ́bla ɔ́si bina keliekɔ na Sitim mmɔ úsie Gilgal.”

english_verse: What offering should I bring when I bow down to worship the Lord God Most High? Should I try to please him by sacrificing calves a year old?
translation_verse: Na bana akɔ ɔdi ɔdubɔkana na uye ɔnini, “Unwoti, bi na ndubuti liboku mbakpa awɔ ɔni na ƒula lɛnyi lɛ́kɔ katɔ kakaaka mɛni si uwi ɔni na líbo nnii mbakya-a lili kalɔ? Ɔmantɛ bakɔ bakɔdi bani náƒɔ lɛkwa linwi na bélie lɛmwi na baadia bɔnu teetulo ƒui na muuti liboku?

english_verse: Will thousands of sheep or rivers of olive oil make God satisfied with me? Should I sacrifice to the Lord my first-born child as payment for my terrible sins?
translation_verse: Baƒonu mpim mpim ndubɔda-a kubiti? Munuu nnɔmii ƒɛƒɛɛ na muuti liboku na butaagba aani ketu na ɔdubɔƒɔ-ɔ anu? Munuu mina ubi ɔnanabi udeedi na ndubuti lɛkpa-a na mina ekpidi bonwu lili na ɔƒɔ-ɔ anu?”

english_verse: The Lord God has told us what is right and what he demands: “See that justice is done, let mercy be your first concern, and humbly obey your God.” Cheating and Violence
translation_verse: Unwoti ɔlati ɔ́su-bu lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka bɔbla. Na lɛla lɛni na ɔɔwia ɔsiku-bu kudɔ ndi ka bɔbla ala ulu lɛlɔ, na butaayɔ bekyuli ku lɛƒɔndia, na buboku lɛlɔ kalɔ buɛɛ, na bɔsiaku-nwu kama siin.

english_verse: I am the Lord, and you are wise to respect my power to punish. So listen to my message for the city of Jerusalem:
translation_verse: Bise atu na binu, ɔsika Unwoti ɔɔtɛmiku amii bani ƒui na bɛkya ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo na ubo ɔyikun ɔni na ɔni bekyuli kɔtu. Na bekyuli bani mɔɔyia awɔ Unwoti ni, bebo lɛnunda.

english_verse: But I, the Lord, will punish you for cheating with weights and with measures.
translation_verse: Nsu ami Unwoti ndubo-mii kɔtu bɔni na akɔkula ekpidi ani na bɛda bɛɛkya ala na bɛɛkɔ́ku ala unu lɛnɔ na biiyú-ma mɛni ɔsu.

english_verse: You rich people are violent, and everyone tells lies.
translation_verse: “Amii balakɛne bibo kalala na bina akɔ ɔdi biala ɔɔnyi ɔkɔ.

english_verse: Because of your sins, I will wound you and leave you ruined and defenseless.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu na líse kalɔ mɔɔkyula-mii na bɛyii udu na bina ekpidi ɔsu.

english_verse: You will eat, but still be hungry; you will store up goods, but lose everything— I, the Lord, will let it all be captured in war.
