translation_verse: Usien ɔmmɔ ni, Paulo ɔ́nu budie bɔtina bɔdi na kɔna kemmo. Na kɔna kɔmɛni kemmo ni, ɔ́nu ɔnana ɔdi ɔni nási Makedonia na unye uuvele-nwu ɔnini, “Via bo Makedonia mɛni na ebebunku-bu o-o!”

english_verse: After Paul had seen the vision, we began looking for a way to go to Macedonia. We were sure that God had called us to preach the good news there. Lydia Becomes a Follower of the Lord
translation_verse: Amu na budie bɔtina bɔmɛni ɔsu ni, bɔ́klibi lɛlɔ na bɔ́tɔlɔ búsie Makedonia. Ɔsika ɔmɛni ɔɔtina-bu ka Blɔti ɔɔwia ka ɔtala-bu na busie butásu litemi buni lɛmɛni na mmɔ. Lidia Úti Lɛlɔ Úte Katɔti Na Ƒilipi

english_verse: We sailed straight from Troas to Samothrace, and the next day we arrived in Neapolis.
translation_verse: Amu na bútélie ɔkɔlɔ ɔdi kemmo na Troa, na bɔ́via búsie Samotrake. Na ka kadi kégye ni, búsie bútéduo Neapoli.

english_verse: From there we went to Philippi, which is a Roman colony in the first district of Macedonia. We spent several days in Philippi.
translation_verse: Ka bɔ́si mmɔ ni, bútéduo Ƒilipi ɔni ndi Makedonia ɔma udeedi. Na mmɔ lɛnɔ ɔdi Romaƒuɔ kalɛkɛ. Na búlie mmɔ emeyi adi.

english_verse: Then on the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to a place by the river, where we thought there would be a Jewish meeting place for prayer. We sat down and talked with the women who came.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛnwunameyi lɛlɔ ni, bɔ́vi bɔ́lɛ ɔma ɔmɛni kemmo na búsie ketu kadi kudɔ na kesii kani na bɔ́kali ka mmɔ na bekyuli beesié taatákpali katɔ. Na búlie mmɔ bɔ́su beleku bani nébo mmɔ Blɔti litemi.

english_verse: One of them was Lydia, who was from the city of Thyatira and sold expensive purple cloth. She was a worshiper of the Lord God, and he made her willing to accept what Paul was saying.
translation_verse: Na bana kemmo unwi baalɔ banii Lidia. Uuyé adi egyiedi na Tiatira, na ɔdi ukyuli ɔni mɔɔbu Katɔti geen. Na uwi ɔni na ɔkya uunú bula butemi bɔmɛni ni, Blɔti úbimi-nwu kasusu na ɔ́ƒɔ etemila ani na Paulo ɔ́su mɛni ƒui.

english_verse: Then after she and her family were baptized, she kept on begging us, “If you think I really do have faith in the Lord, come stay in my home.” Finally, we accepted her invitation. Paul and Silas Are Put in Jail
translation_verse: Amu ka anwu ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ƒui báƒɔ ntu bɔkpila ɔdi ni, úvele-bu ɔnini, “Si bɛ́tuna bɛnii ndi ɔƒɔtaadine geen nte Blɔti ni, na bibeduo-mi kudɔ.” Na ɔ́ni litemi lɛmɛni úneneku-bu útédu ka búsie bútéduo-nwu kudɔ. Bákya Paulo Ku Silas Aban Ɔtɔ

english_verse: One day on our way to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl. She had a spirit in her that gave her the power to tell the future. By doing this she made a lot of money for her owners.
translation_verse: Amu na limeyi lɛdi uwi ɔni na búsela butákpali katɔ ni, bɔ́siaku ugblebi ɔdi ɔni lɛlɔ na kɔyu kukpidi kulie na uubó like. Na ɔɔbla egulabi kaduɛ teete nwuna benwoti.

english_verse: The girl followed Paul and the rest of us, and she kept yelling, “These men are servants of the Most High God! They are telling you how to be saved.”
translation_verse: Amu na ugblebi ɔmɛni ɔ́siaku abu ku Paulo kama na ɔɔva taasu ɔnini, “Bekyuli bamɛni badi Katɔti kabla bablane, na bébo mɛni bani babatina-mii ngba bɔƒɔ ulu!”

english_verse: This went on for several days. Finally, Paul got so upset that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ, I order you to leave this girl alone!” At once the evil spirit left her.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛla lɛmɛni lísie anumi emeyi pii. Na ka Paulo ɔ́nɔ bɔnu ni, únwini na ɔ́su kɔyu kɔni nsiaku ugblebi ɔmɛni ɔnini, “Mɔɔbɔku-ɔ na Yesu Kristo lɛnyi kemmo nnii vi lɛ-nwu lɛlɔ!” Na kɔnakunwi ni, kɔyu kukpidi kɔmɛni kɔ́vi kɔ́lɛ-nwu lɛlɔ kemmo!

english_verse: When the girl's owners realized they had lost all chances for making more money, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them into court.
translation_verse: Amu ka nwuna benwoti bánu ka bana lɛlakɛ lɛ́yii ɔsu ni, béƒie Paulo ku Silas na báni-ma bésienku litemi katɛkɔ benengu na kuyentɛ.

english_verse: They told the officials, “These Jews are upsetting our city!
translation_verse: Na básu na kuye mmɔ banini, “Bekyuli bamɛni badi Yudaƒuɔ, na bakya beebile bula ɔma.

english_verse: They are telling us to do things we Romans are not allowed to do.”
translation_verse: Bakya baatina bekyuli ala ani na muunye teetile Romaƒuɔ ɔda bubo lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: The crowd joined in the attack on Paul and Silas. Then the officials tore the clothes off the two men and ordered them to be beaten with a whip.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli pii bábaka bámana-ma, na benye beedí Paulo ku Silas teete lɛlɔ. Na litemi batɛne bamɛni báya na báni-ma lɛwu bábwɛ, na béte kuƒi banii bebo-ma kugyiimi.

english_verse: After they had been badly beaten, they were put in jail, and the jailer was told to guard them carefully.
translation_verse: Amu ka ebola éduo-ma lɛlɔ kaduɛ ni, béti-ma bátákya aban ɔtɔ. Na básu ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnu ama bani ntɛ ɔtɔ mmɔ lɛlɔ banii ɔda Paulo ku Silas kaduɛ.

english_verse: The jailer did as he was told. He put them deep inside the jail and chained their feet to heavy blocks of wood.
translation_verse: Na ka bébo-nwu ɔda lɛni ɔsu ni, úti-ma útákya kasuudikɔ ƒui na bébo-ma kɔgba.

english_verse: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing praises to God, while the other prisoners listened.
translation_verse: Amu na usientɛ uwi ɔni na Paulo ku Silas bakya baakpali katɔ na beedie lɛnu teete Katɔti ni, bani ntɛ ɔtɔ mmɔ bakya beenú.

english_verse: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the jail to its foundations. The doors opened, and the chains fell from all the prisoners.
translation_verse: Kɔnakunwi ni, kalɔ kákunku momoomo, na ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ ƒui lɛnɔ ɔ́kunku ɔni na ɔtɔ kɔyakun ƒui kɔ́lɛmi, na kɔgba kɔni bébo báda batɔntɛne bammɔ ƒui kɔ́ƒɛ.

english_verse: When the jailer woke up and saw that the doors were open, he thought that the prisoners had escaped. He pulled out his sword and was about to kill himself.
translation_verse: Amu na bana lɛlɔ ɔnune úkeyi lɛlɔ ɔ́gyinya na ɔ́nu ka ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kɔyakun ƒui kɔ́lɛmi kuwi. Na ka ɔ́kali ɔnii ɔtɔ batɛne bammɔ ƒui békeli ɔsu ni, ɔ́kpa nwuna kewii ɔnii ɔɔdú lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The jailer asked for a torch and went into the jail. He was shaking all over as he knelt down in front of Paul and Silas.
translation_verse: Amu na ukyuli ɔmɛni ɔ́lɔ ɔnii beti ukpo beboku. Na lɛlɔ bɔtɔ kemmo ni, úbalɛ akɔnkɔ na Paulo ku Silas anumi.

english_verse: After he had led them out of the jail, he asked, “What must I do to be saved?”
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́da-ma údie ɔtɔ ɔmɛni kemmo ni, úye-ma ɔnini, “Ati bene, bi na ɔlɛka lɛbla asa na lɛkɛ bɔƒɔ?”

english_verse: They replied, “Have faith in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved! This is also true for everyone who lives in your home.”
translation_verse: Amu na básu-nwu banini, “Ƒɔ Blɔti Yesu Kristo di, na adubɔkɛ bɔƒɔ, awɔ ku ƒula kaduli bekyuli ƒui.”

english_verse: Then Paul and Silas told him and everyone else in his house about the Lord.
translation_verse: Na bésie bátásu anwu ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ƒui Blɔti lɛlɔ litemi buni lɛmɛni.

english_verse: While it was still night, the jailer took them to a place where he could wash their cuts and bruises. Then he and everyone in his home were baptized.
translation_verse: Na usien ɔmmɔ kani na ɔ́mana-ma alɛbi ani nsia-ma lɛlɔ, na anwu ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ƒui báƒɔ ntu bɔkpila ɔdi.

english_verse: They were very glad they had put their faith in God. After this, the jailer took Paul and Silas to his home and gave them something to eat.
translation_verse: Amu na béduo ɔtɔ na úte-ma lɛla lɛdi bádi. Na nwuna kaduli bekyuli ƒui bákɛ ebiti geen, ɔsika báƒɔ Katɔti bádi.

english_verse: The next morning the officials sent some police with orders for the jailer to let Paul and Silas go.
translation_verse: Amu na kadi kégye ni, ɔma ɔmmɔ litemi batɛne bátala beƒiene banii bátásu ukyuli ɔni mɔɔnu batɔntɛne lɛlɔ mmɔ banii, “Nyonu baƒɔ bammɔ na beteesie.”

english_verse: The jailer told Paul, “The officials have ordered me to set you free. Now you can leave in peace.”
translation_verse: Amu na bana lɛlɔ ɔnune ɔmɛni ɔ́su Paulo ku Silas ɔnini, “Litemi batɛne banii nnyonu-mii na biteesie. Anwuɔsu biteesie ku keyi buɛɛ.”

english_verse: But Paul told the police, “We are Roman citizens, and the Roman officials had us beaten in public without giving us a trial. They threw us into jail. Now do they think they can secretly send us away? No, they cannot! They will have to come here themselves and let us out.”
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo ɔ́su beƒiene bammɔ ɔnini, “Bébo-bu na bekyuli ƒui anumi ɔni bátatɛku-bu litemi lɛdi asa na béti-bu bátákya aban ɔtɔ kemmo. Nsu ni, Romaƒuɔ na bɔdi! Na ɔƒɛni na baawia ka bɔbɛ bɔtɔlɔ? Kudii! Ya ama alati bebo bebedie-bu!”

english_verse: When the police told the officials that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, the officials were afraid.
translation_verse: Amu na beƒiene bamɛni bénwini bésie bátásu litemi batɛne kenye kamɛni. Na ka bénu ka Paulo ku Silas badi Romaƒuɔ ni, liƒu lɛ́da-ma geen!

english_verse: So they came and apologized. They led them out of the jail and asked them to please leave town.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu bésie bétékpi-ma kɔtɔ, na bákpanku-ma bálɛku aban ɔtɔ. Na bévele-ma banii batɔlɔ ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo na beteesie likpo bamba.

english_verse: But Paul and Silas went straight to the home of Lydia, where they saw the Lord's followers and encouraged them. Then they left.
translation_verse: Amu na Silas ku Paulo bátɔlɔ bésie Lidia kesii. Na mmɔ na bátánu baƒɔtaadine bakladi. Na básɔ bákya-ma ogya bébu asa na bátɔlɔ ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: After Paul and his friends had traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they went on to Thessalonica. A synagogue was in that city.
translation_verse: Amu ka bésie bátásia Amƒipoli ku Apolonia ni, bétédu Tesalonika. Na mɛni na Yudaƒuɔ kasalakɔ kadi kákya.

english_verse: So as usual, Paul went there to worship, and on three Sabbaths he spoke to the people. He used the Scriptures
translation_verse: Amu na aani kalɛ na Paulo ɔɔyɔ́ bɔbla ni, úsie mmɔ ɔnii utétemi ute-ma na kasalakɔ mmɔ. Na anwunameyi atɛ sɔɔn ni, útaatina Bunweni Kedee Ɔku kemmo etemila.

english_verse: to show them that the Messiah had to suffer, but that he would rise from death. Paul also told them that Jesus is the Messiah he was preaching about.
translation_verse: Na uudie lɛbibo lɛni na básu bése ka Kristo ɔdubo bɔnu ku kalɛ na ɔsɔ ɔdubɔta na ulie ngba ɔni na ɔsɔ ulekpi. Paulo ɔ́su-ma ɔnii, “Ukyuli ɔni lɛlɔ litemi mɔɔsu-mii mɛni ndi Yesu ɔni ndi Ukyuli Ɔƒunadi ɔmmɔ.”

english_verse: Some of them believed what Paul had said, and they became followers with Paul and Silas. Some Gentiles and many important women also believed the message.
translation_verse: Etemila ani na údie kalɔ ɔ́tina-ma mɛni énwini bekyuli bamɛni badi kasusu, na báƒɔ bádi na básiaku Paulo ku Silas. Na Grikiƒuɔ bani nda lɛlɔ na Katɔti bɔyia kemmo pii ku beleku bani lɛlɔ mbo ɔbu pii lɛnɔ bénwini kayi na ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders were jealous and got some troublemakers who hung around the marketplace to start a riot in the city. They wanted to drag Paul and Silas out to the mob, and so they went straight to Jason's home.
translation_verse: Nsu anumi égyie Yudaƒuɔ batɔnkune na bana lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu bátáwia bekyuli basa basa badi na ɔma kemmo banii batákya ɔma bekyuli ogya. Na básala otogyi bákya lɛsɛ lɛmɛni na bésie bátáka bámana Yason kaduli banii betéƒie Paulo ku Silas besienku ɔma ɔmmɔ kasalakɔ.

english_verse: But when they did not find them there, they dragged out Jason and some of the Lord's followers. They took them to the city authorities and shouted, “Paul and Silas have been upsetting things everywhere. Now they have come here,
translation_verse: Nsu ka bátanu-ma ɔsu ni, béƒie Yason ku baƒɔtaadine badi na báni-ma bésienku kasalakɔ. Mmɔ na baava taasu banini, “Bekyuli badi bakɛ baakya lɛsɛ likpo biala, na bébo mɛni lɛnɔ baakya lɛsɛ lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. All of them break the laws of the Roman Emperor by claiming that someone named Jesus is king.”
translation_verse: Na anwu Yason lɛnɔ ɔ́ƒɔ-ma ɔ́kya nwuna kaduli. Na bekyuli bammɔ báta bénye Ɔga Unengudi Kaesare ɔda bubo lɛlɔ. Na baatina ka ɔnana ɔni baalɔ Yesu ndi Ɔga!”

english_verse: The officials and the people were upset when they heard this.
translation_verse: Amu ka bénu ɔmɛni ni, ɔƒɛ ɔ́da otogyi ɔmmɔ ku ɔma benengu.

english_verse: So they made Jason and the other followers pay bail before letting them go. People in Berea Welcome the Message
translation_verse: Na báya na Yason ku nwuna badi báƒɔ kɔtu bɔni kayu asa na bányonu-ma. Paulo Ku Silas Bátɔlɔ Bésie Beroia

english_verse: That same night the Lord's followers sent Paul and Silas on to Berea, and after they arrived, they went to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Nsu usien ɔmmɔ kani ni, baƒɔtaadine bani nkya ɔma ɔmmɔ bétiku Paulo ku Silas békeliku bésienku Beroia. Na ka bétéduo mmɔ ni, bésie Yudaƒuɔ kasalakɔ batásu litemi buni lɛmɛni.

english_verse: The people in Berea were much nicer than those in Thessalonica, and they gladly accepted the message. Day after day they studied the Scriptures to see if these things were true.
translation_verse: Na Beroiaƒuɔ ni, bana kasusu kébimi kétulo Tesalonikaƒuɔ kadi. Na bése atu na bénu bana butemi. Na limeyi ndi limeyi ni, bátaawia Bunweni Kedee Ɔku kemmo etemila taanu si Paulo ala ani na ɔ́su adi sɔsɔ.

english_verse: Many of them put their faith in the Lord, including some important Greek women and several men.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bana akɔ pii báƒɔ bádi. Grikiƒuɔ beleku bani lɛlɔ mbo ɔbu pii bénwini kayi ku banana pii lɛnɔ.

english_verse: When the Jewish leaders in Thessalonica heard that Paul had been preaching God's message in Berea, they went there and caused trouble by turning the crowds against Paul.
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔni na Yudaƒuɔ bani nkya Tesalonika bénu ka Paulo ɔkya ɔɔsu litemi buni na Beroia ni, bávi bésie mmɔ bátákya kadɔ na ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: At once the followers sent Paul down to the coast, but Silas and Timothy stayed in Berea.
translation_verse: Nsu baƒɔtaadine bani nkya mmɔ ni, báta kɔnakunwi na bétiku Paulo bésienku ɛpu kudɔ. Na Silas ku Timoteo báƒɔ lɛlɔ bákya kama.

english_verse: Some men went with Paul as far as Athens, and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible. Paul in Athens
translation_verse: Ama bani nsiaku Paulo mmɔ béti-nwu bétédu Atene. Na mmɔ na ama básɔ bénwini na Paulo ɔ́sia-ma kenye ɔnii batásu Silas ku Timoteo na bekeli babasiaku-nwu. Paulo Ɔkya Atene

english_verse: He went to the synagogue to speak to the Jews and to anyone who worshiped with them. Day after day he also spoke to everyone he met in the market.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu úsie útátɛmiku Yudaƒuɔ ku bekyuli bamba lɛnɔ na bana kasalakɔ. Na limeyi ndi limeyi ni, útaatɛmiku bani lɛnɔ na ɔ́nu na kuye.

english_verse: Some of them were Epicureans and some were Stoics, and they started arguing with him. People were asking, “What is this know-it-all trying to say?” Some even said, “Paul must be preaching about foreign gods! That's what he means when he talks about Jesus and about people rising from death.”
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔdi ni, anwu ku bekyuli lisu lɛdi bani ndi Epikuroƒuɔ ku Stoaƒuɔ bani nlie nte kayawi lɛnunda bákya ku Paulo unyeƒi na básu banini, “Bi na ɔnana ɔmɛni uutemi taasu?” Amu na babambadi lɛnɔ básu banini, “Use aani kalɔ bamba baƒiɔ badi lɛlɔ kɔtɛ na ɔɔtɛmi.” Na bekyuli bammɔ básu lɛni ɔsika bénu ka Paulo ɔ́su litemi buni ɔ́siku Yesu ku nwuna bɔsɔ taata lɛlɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: They brought Paul before a council called the Areopagus, and said, “Tell us what your new teaching is all about.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, béti-nwu bésienku kesii kani na baatɛ etemila na Areopago benengu kasalakɔ, na básu banini, “Bɔwia bɔti lɛla lɛni na ala awɔdi ani na aatina mɛni adanku.

english_verse: We have heard you say some strange things, and we want to know what you mean.”
translation_verse: Ɔsika ala ani na aasu ni, eeese-bu nwaa. Anwuɔsu bɔɔyɔ́ bunu-nya kalɔ.”

english_verse: More than anything else the people of Athens and the foreigners living there loved to hear and to talk about anything new.
translation_verse: Na Ateneƒuɔ ƒui ku baƒɔ bani nkya kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui ni, bebo kɔnu bete kɔtɛ keeke ku ala awɔdi bugyeli.

english_verse: So Paul stood up in front of the council and said: People of Athens, I see that you are very religious.
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo ɔ́ta únye kasalakɔ bekyuli bammɔ anumi, na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Na ulu biala lɛlɔ ni, lɛ́nu ka amii Ateneƒuɔ ni, bɛɛsia lɛkpa anu geen.

english_verse: As I was going through your city and looking at the things you worship, I found an altar with the words, “To an Unknown God.” You worship this God, but you don't really know him. So I want to tell you about him.
translation_verse: Ɔsika ɔni na nkɛ mɔɔví na lɛ́nu bina kɔkpakɔ ni, lɛ́nu lɛkpatabi lɛdi lɛlɔ ka bénweni básia-ni lɛlɔ banii, ‘Amɛni búti buute Bula Ɔti ɔni na bɔɔɔgyi.’ Na Ati ɔni na bɛɛɛgyi asa na bɛɛkpá-nwu mɛni ni, nwuna lɛlɔ litemi mɔɔyɔ́ ka lɛsu-mii ɔƒɛni.

english_verse: This God made the world and everything in it. He is Lord of heaven and earth, and he doesn't live in temples built by human hands.
translation_verse: “Ati ɔmɛni ndi ala ƒui Ɔti ɔni nédie katɔ ku kalɔ ku ala ani nkya-nya kemmo ƒui. Na ulélie ɔtɔ ɔni na ukyuli ɔyawine enu ábla kemmo.

english_verse: He doesn't need help from anyone. He gives life, breath, and everything else to all people.
translation_verse: Na ulawia bɔdi lɛnɔ taasiku bayawine enu kabla kadi lɛnɔ kemmo, ɔsika anwu ɔlati muute ukyuli biala ngba ku lɛkɛ.

english_verse: From one person God made all nations who live on earth, and he decided when and where every nation would be.
translation_verse: Údie bayawine ƒui ɔ́siku ukyuli unwi lɛlɔ ɔnii bulie aani ubugya unwi bebi na kayawi ƒui lɛlɔ. Anwu ɔlati nése uwi ku kadikɔ úse úte ɔdi biala.

english_verse: God has done all this, so that we will look for him and reach out and find him. He isn't far from any of us,
translation_verse: Na bula Ɔti ɔ́bla ɔmɛni úte abu bekyuli kalɛ na bɔwia-nwu kama ulu na bɔnu-nwu, ina ka nka utagyunku-bu.

english_verse: and he gives us the power to live, to move, and to be who we are. “We are his children,” just as some of your poets have said.
translation_verse: Ɔsika aani kalɛ na bina agyangba bediene básu ni, ‘Anwu nli na buli, na bɔdubɔsiaku-nwu na bɔtɛ bɔlɛɛ.’ Na básu lɛnɔ banini, ‘Bɔdi nwuna kaba.’

english_verse: Since we are God's children, we must not think that he is like an idol made out of gold or silver or stone. He isn't like anything that humans have thought up and made.
translation_verse: “Na ka bɔdi Katɔti bebi ɔsu ni, utalɛka bɔkali bɔnii Katɔti ɔmɛni use aani lɛla lɛni na abu bayawine néti enu bɔ́bla aani sika ugyiedi iye ɔƒualadi iye ugyii iye lɛtabi iye ala anwidi lɛnɔ kalɛ.

english_verse: In the past, God forgave all this because people did not know what they were doing. But now he says that everyone everywhere must turn to him.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si kalɔ kesekɔ úti úbedu uwi ɔmɛni kemmo ni, Katɔti útani bekyuli kɔtu ɔsika bátati-nwu. Nsu ɔƒaani ni, úbo-bu ɔda ɔnii bɔda anumi budie ala amɛni bene lɛlɔ na bunwini anumi buboku-nwu kudɔ.

english_verse: He has set a day when he will judge the world's people with fairness. And he has chosen the man Jesus to do the judging for him. God has given proof of this to all of us by raising Jesus from death.
translation_verse: Ɔsika anwu údie limeyi lɛdi úse lɛni lɛlɔ na ukyuli ɔni na ɔ́ƒuna úse wabatɛku-bu litemi ɔ́si bula ɔbladu lɛlɔ. Na údie Ukyuli Ɔƒunadi ɔmɛni ɔ́tina-bu nwaa ɔ́si ɔni na ɔ́gyila-nwu ɔ́siku kekpine na ɔ́sɔ úbo úbelie ngba.”

english_verse: As soon as the people heard Paul say a man had been raised from death, some of them started laughing. Others said, “We will hear you talk about this some other time.”
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔni na bénu ka Paulo ɔ́tɛmi ɔ́siku bɔsɔ taata lɛlɔ ni, bana akɔ badi báma-nwu. Na badi lɛnɔ básu banini, “Bɔsɔ bɔɔyɔ́ ka bunu etemila adi bɔsiku ukyuli bɔsɔ taata lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: When Paul left the council meeting,
translation_verse: Amu ka úbo úte lɛni ni, Paulo ɔ́tɔlɔ-ma kudɔ.

english_verse: some of the men put their faith in the Lord and went with Paul. One of them was a council member named Dionysius. A woman named Damaris and several others also put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Nsu bekyuli badi bábasiaku-nwu na bénwini baƒɔtaadine. Na bana akɔ ɔdi ndi Areopago unengu ɔni baalɔ Dionisio ku uleku ɔni baalɔ Damari ku badi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Paul left Athens and went to Corinth,
translation_verse: Amu na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Paulo ɔ́tɔlɔ Atene úsie Korinto.

english_verse: where he met Aquila, a Jewish man from Pontus. Not long before this, Aquila had come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Emperor Claudius had ordered the Jewish people to leave Rome. Paul went to see Aquila and Priscilla
translation_verse: Mmɔ na útánu Yudani ɔni baalɔ Akwila, na báwɔ-nwu na Ponto. Anwu ku ulekudi Priskila bási Italia bébo mmɔ uwi útetu tɔ, ɔsika kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔni baalɔ Klaudio ɔ́su ka Yudaƒuɔ ƒui balɛ Roma. Paulo úsie útanu-ma,

english_verse: and found out they were tent makers. Paul was also a tent maker, so he stayed with them, and they worked together.
translation_verse: na ɔ́kya-ma kudɔ úteebunku-ma na bebuo lɛku bɔka kabla kani na anwu lɛnɔ ɔɔbla taadi kemmo.

english_verse: Every Sabbath, Paul went to the synagogue. He spoke to Jews and Gentiles and tried to win them over.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛnwunameyi biala ni, Paulo uusié Yudaƒuɔ kasalakɔ teetédie ala kalɔ teete Yudaƒuɔ ku Grikiƒuɔ ƒui kalɛ benwini kayi.

english_verse: But after Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, he spent all his time preaching to the Jews about Jesus the Messiah.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na Silas ku Timoteo bási Makedonia bébo ni, Paulo ɔ́kɛ uwi kaduɛ úti úte litemi buni bɔsu ku kalɔ budie taatina Yudaƒuɔ ka ni, Yesu ndi Ukyuli Ɔƒunadi ɔmmɔ geen.

english_verse: Finally, they turned against him and insulted him. So he shook the dust from his clothes and told them, “Whatever happens to you will be your own fault! I am not to blame. From now on I am going to preach to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Amu uwi ɔni na Yudaƒuɔ bamɛni báta bénye-nwu lɛlɔ na beetemi enyekpi taasiku Yesu lɛlɔ ni, Paulo úveli enu úwi-ma, na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Si bɛ́yii ni, mina kɔnu, mina ɔgba uuubo-nwu kemmo. Ɔ́si ɔƒaani ni, lísela bekyuli bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ kudɔ ntásu-ma litemi buni lɛmɛni.”

english_verse: Paul then moved into the house of a man named Titius Justus, who worshiped God and lived next door to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́gyu-ma kudɔ ni, ɔ́tɔlɔ útákya ɔnana ɔdi ɔni naaadi Yudani na baalɔ-nwu banii Tito Yusto kudɔ ɔni mɔɔbu Blɔti na ulie Yudaƒuɔ kasalakɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: Crispus was the leader of the synagogue. He and everyone in his family put their faith in the Lord. Many others in Corinth also heard the message, and all the people who had faith in the Lord were baptized.
translation_verse: Amu na kasalakɔ kammɔ unengu ɔni baalɔ Krispo ku nwuna kaduli bekyuli ƒui báƒɔ Blɔti bádi, na bákpila-ma ntu. Lɛni kani na bákpila babambadi bani náƒɔ bádi lɛnɔ ntu na Korinto mmɔ.

english_verse: One night, Paul had a vision, and in it the Lord said, “Don't be afraid to keep on preaching. Don't stop!
translation_verse: Amu na limeyi lɛdi usientɛ ni, Blɔti ɔ́su Paulo na kɔna kemmo ɔnini, “Tayia! Na tada litemi lɛmɛni bɔsu taya.

english_verse: I am with you, and you won't be harmed. Many people in this city belong to me.”
translation_verse: Ɔsika nsiaku-ɔ, na ukyuli ɔdi ulákana-a likpidi lɛdi bɔbla. Bekyuli pii bakya ɔma ɔmɛni kemmo bani ndi mina badi.”

english_verse: Paul stayed on in Corinth for a year and a half, teaching God's message to the people.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Paulo úlie ɔma ɔmɛni kemmo lɛkwa linwi ku kakɛ ɔ́su Blɔti litemi lɛmɛni ɔ́tina bekyuli.

english_verse: While Gallio was governor of Achaia, some of the Jewish leaders got together and grabbed Paul. They brought him into court
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔni na bése Galio Roma aban lɛga na Akaia kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, Yudaƒuɔ badi bábla lɛkpa lɛdi na bánwi litemi bámana Paulo lɛlɔ na béƒie-nwu bésienku litemi katɛkɔ.

english_verse: and said, “This man is trying to make our people worship God in a way that is against our Law!”
translation_verse: Amu na básu ɔga ɔmmɔ banini, “Ukyuli ɔmɛni uunwíni bekyuli kasusu ɔnii bataakpa Katɔti na ulu ɔni náta únye bula ɔda bubo lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Even before Paul could speak, Gallio said, “If you were charging this man with a crime or some other wrong, I would have to listen to you.
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔni kani na Paulo úse kalɔ ɔnii uteedie kenye ni, aban lɛga ɔdine Galio ɔmɛni útemi na ɔ́su Yudaƒuɔ bamɛni ɔnini, “Amii Yudaƒuɔ binu! Si litemi lɛni bɛda bíboku mɛni lɛdi bɔƒiɔ bubendi bɔdi ni, ndubɔkɛ kayi na linu bina litemi.

english_verse: But since this concerns only words, names, and your own law, you will have to take care of it yourselves. I refuse to judge such matters.”
translation_verse: Nsu ka unyeƒi ukpludi na bɛɛkya na bina etemila ku ɔda bubo lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, amii alati bitásu-ni. Ɔɔɔdi ami mabla litemi ɔtɛne mete-mii na ala amɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Then he sent them out of the court.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ɔ́bɔku-ma ɔ́lɛku nwuna litemi katɛkɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: The crowd grabbed Sosthenes, the Jewish leader, and beat him up in front of the court. But none of this mattered to Gallio. Paul Returns to Antioch in Syria
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli lisu lɛmɛni béƒie Sostene ɔni ndi bana kasalakɔ kammɔ ɔtɔnkune na bétébo-nwu na litemi katɛkɔ kamɛni kudɔ. Nsu Galio útakpete-ma. Paulo Únwini Úsie Antiokia

english_verse: After Paul had stayed for a while with the Lord's followers in Corinth, he told them goodbye and sailed on to Syria with Aquila and Priscilla. But before he left, he had his head shaved at Cenchreae because he had made a promise to God.
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo úlie Korinto ɔma ɔmɛni kemmo emeyi pii. Na nwuna kama ni, ɔ́kada baƒɔtaadine bamɛni na anwu ku Akwila ku Priskila básia ntu anumi bésie Siria. Nsu asa na watɔlɔ ni, Paulo ɔ́ya na békpeyi-nwu lili na Kenkrea na Yudaƒuɔ ɔdi lɛlɔ ɔ́si kenye kani na úse ɔsu.

english_verse: The three of them arrived in Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He then went into the synagogue to talk with the people there.
translation_verse: Ka úbayu na Eƒeso ni, ɔ́da Priskila ku Akwila ɔ́kya ɔkɔlɔ kemmo mmɔ. Nsu anwu ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Yudaƒuɔ kasalakɔ ɔnii utéduoku Yudaƒuɔ bammɔ ala adi kemmo.

english_verse: They asked him to stay longer, but he refused.
translation_verse: Amu na bévele-nwu banii ulie-ma kudɔ ubu, nsu ɔ́nu ka uuubo uwi.

english_verse: He told them goodbye and said, “If God lets me, I will come back.”
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ka ɔɔtɔlɔ ni, ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Si Blɔti ɔ́tuna ni, ndubɔsɔ linwini libo-mii kudɔ.” Na ɔ́sɔ útéduo ɔkɔlɔ kemmo na ɔ́tɔlɔ Eƒeso.

english_verse: Paul sailed to Caesarea, where he greeted the church. Then he went on to Antioch.
translation_verse: Na ka útéduo Kaesarea ni, ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Yerusalem na útákya baƒɔtaadine bammɔ kenye. Na ɔ́sɔ úbavi ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Antiokia.

english_verse: After staying there for a while, he left and visited several places in Galatia and Phrygia. He helped the followers there to become stronger in their faith. Apollos in Ephesus
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́kya mmɔ uwi ɔdi ni, ɔ́sɔ ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie útásia Galatia ku Ƒrigia kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na uwi ɔmɛni ƒui ni, ɔkɛ ɔɔví taanu baƒɔtaadine bani nkya mmɔ bene, na ɔɔkya-ma ɔkplu. Apolo Úsie Eƒeso Ku Korinto

english_verse: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. Apollos had been born in the city of Alexandria. He was a very good speaker and knew a lot about the Scriptures.
translation_verse: Amu na Yudani ɔdi úbo Eƒeso. Anwu baalɔ Apolo, na báwɔ-nwu na Aleksandria. Ɔdi ukyuli ɔni na kenye káda-nwu, na ɔgyi Bunweni Kedee Ɔku kemmo etemila lɛnɔ.

english_verse: He also knew much about the Lord's Way, and he spoke about it with great excitement. What he taught about Jesus was right, but all he knew was John's message about baptism.
translation_verse: Na ina ka únu Blɔti lɛlɔ litemi na uutemi ku ogya na ɔ́tɛmi ɔ́siku Yesu lɛlɔ na ulu geen ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, Yohane ntu bɔkpila lɛlɔ ala kani na ɔgyi.

english_verse: Apollos started speaking bravely in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him to their home and helped him understand God's Way even better.
translation_verse: Amu ka unye uutemi ku kayi buse na kasalakɔ mmɔ na Priskila ku Akwila bénu ni, bákpanku-nwu bésienku kaduli na bédie Blɔti etemila kemmo bátina-nwu kaduɛ bébu.

english_verse: Apollos decided to travel through Achaia. So the Lord's followers wrote letters, encouraging the followers there to welcome him. After Apollos arrived in Achaia, he was a great help to everyone who had put their faith in the Lord Jesus because of God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Amu na ka Apolo ɔ́bla kasusu ka usie Akaia ni, Eƒesoƒuɔ baƒɔtaadine bébebunku-nwu na bénweni ɔku béte baƒɔtaadine bani nkya Akaia mmɔ banii si úbeduo mmɔ ni, na baƒɔ-nwu kaduɛ. Na uwi ɔni na útéduo mmɔ ni, úbunku bekyuli pii bani nébenwini kayi na Blɔti kɔnyana bɔnu ɔsu.

english_verse: He got into fierce arguments with the Jewish people, and in public he used the Scriptures to prove that Jesus is the Messiah.
translation_verse: Na nwuna etemila ammɔ ádi Yudaƒuɔ lɛlɔ, ɔsika úti Bunweni Kedee Ɔku kemmo etemila údie ɔ́tina nwaa ka Yesu ndi Ukyuli Ɔƒunadi ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled across the hill country to Ephesus, where he met some of the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Amu uwi ɔni na Apolo ɔkya Korinto ni, Paulo lɛnɔ útávi lɛgba ulu ɔtɔdi, na útédu Eƒeso. Mmɔ na útánu baƒɔtaadine badi.

english_verse: He asked them, “When you put your faith in Jesus, were you given the Holy Spirit?” “No!” they answered. “We have never even heard of the Holy Spirit.”
translation_verse: Amu na úye-ma ɔnini, “Ɔ́si uwi ɔni na bɛ́ƒɔ bɛ́di ni, bɛ́ɛƒɔ Katɔti Kɔyu?” Amu bédie kenye banini, “Oowo! Bi ndi Katɔti Kɔyu? Bútenu-ku tɔ lɛla lɛdi.”

english_verse: “Then why were you baptized?” Paul asked. They answered, “Because of what John taught.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́sɔ úye-ma ɔnini, “Na bina ntu bɔkpila kalɔ ndi dɛ?” Na básu-nwu banini, “Amu ndi Yohane ntu bɔkpila lɛsa lɛni na ɔ́kɔ.”

english_verse: Paul replied, “John baptized people so they would turn to God. But he also told them someone else was coming, and they should put their faith in him. Jesus is the one that John was talking about.”
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo údie kalɔ ɔ́tina-ma ɔnini, “Yohane ɔ́kpila bekyuli bani nénwini kama bákya bana ekpidi ntu. Na ɔ́su-ma ɔnii baƒɔ ukyuli ɔni ndubɔsia anwu Yohane kama badi. Na ukyuli ɔmmɔ ndi Yesu Kristo.”

english_verse: After the people heard Paul say this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Amu ka bánya bénu litemi lɛmɛni ni, báya na ɔ́kpila-ma ntu na Blɔti Yesu lɛnyi kemmo.

english_verse: Then Paul placed his hands on them. The Holy Spirit was given to them, and they spoke unknown languages and prophesied.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Paulo úti enu ɔ́sia-ma lɛlɔ ni, Katɔti Kɔyu kɔ́ƒɔ-ma lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui, na bésie kalɔ ku adi lidu lidu butemi na bédie Blɔti ala kenye.

english_verse: There were about twelve men in this group.
translation_verse: Amu na bana bumomo bɔ́bla aani banana leevu-inyɔ.

english_verse: For three months Paul went to the synagogue and talked bravely with the people about God's kingdom. He tried to win them over,
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo úteesie Yudaƒuɔ kasalakɔ taatátɛmi ku ogya abuli atɛ, na uudie ala kalɔ taatina-ma. Na uunwíni bana kasusu teesienku Blɔti lɛga kadikɔ ala lɛlɔ.

english_verse: but some of them were stubborn and refused to believe. In front of everyone they said terrible things about God's Way. Paul left and took the followers with him to the lecture hall of Tyrannus. He spoke there every day
translation_verse: Nsu badi ama bétenu nwuna litemi buni lɛmɛni, na báta bénye Blɔti lilu ku ala bɔtina lɛlɔ na kadi ƒui anumi. Anwuɔsu Paulo ɔ́tɔlɔ-ma kudɔ. Na útiku bani náƒɔ bádi úsienku Tirano lɛgbanya kemmo. Na mmɔ na útaatɛmiku-ma limeyi ndi limeyi.

english_verse: for two years, until every Jew and Gentile in Asia had heard the Lord's message. The Sons of Sceva
translation_verse: Amu na akwa anyɔ kemmo ni, lɛni na ɔ́tina-ma ala. Na litemi buni lɛmɛni lígyingya lɛ́kya Asia kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ mmɔ ƒui. Na ama bani ndi Yudaƒuɔ ku Helaƒuɔ lɛnɔ bénu-ni. Skeva Bebi Maatɛ Báwia Ɔyikun

english_verse: God gave Paul the power to work great miracles.
translation_verse: Amu na Blɔti úte Paulo ɔyikun ɔni na úti ɔ́bla akɔla budie taatina.

english_verse: People even took handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul's body, and they carried them to everyone who was sick. All of the sick people were healed, and the evil spirits went out.
translation_verse: Na si béti nwuna adala adi bétuku ɔlɛne ɔdi muedi ni, aabwi-nwu, na asɔ aagyá ayu ekpidi lɛnɔ taalɛku bekyuli bani kemmo na eli.

english_verse: Some Jewish men started going around trying to force out evil spirits by using the name of the Lord Jesus. They said to the spirits, “Come out in the name of that same Jesus that Paul preaches about!”
translation_verse: Amu na Yudaƒuɔ bevone badi bani nkɛ mɔɔví ekpo ekpo ni, básusu banii beeti Yesu lɛnyi bataabɔku ayu ekpidi. Na baasu banii, “Bɔɔbɔku-ɔ na Yesu ɔni lɛlɔ na Paulo ɔkɛ uutemi taasiku bɔnii vi lɛ ukyuli ɔmɛni kemmo!”

english_verse: Seven sons of a high priest named Sceva were doing this,
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bani nátaabla udu ɔmɛni ndi bakloƒu maatɛ bani ndi Yudani ɔkpane unengu ɔdi ɔni baalɔ Skeva bebi.

english_verse: when an evil spirit said to them, “I know Jesus! And I have heard about Paul. But who are you?”
translation_verse: Nsu ka bátásu kɔyu kukpidi kɔdi lɛni ni, kɔ́su-ma kɔnini, “Ami ngyi Yesu, na ngyi Paulo lɛnɔ. Nsu amii ni, lɛɛɛgyi-mii! Ɔma bene bɛdi?”

english_verse: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and beat them up. They ran out of the house, naked and bruised.
translation_verse: Amu na ukyuli ɔni lɛlɔ na kɔyu kukpidi kɔmɛni kulie ni, úbo-ma! Na báƒɔ lɛlɛ geen, na békeli bálɛ kaduli kammɔ ku kasɔngya!

english_verse: When the Jews and Gentiles in Ephesus heard about this, they were so frightened that they praised the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Lɛla lɛni nálɛ mɛni lígyingya na líyi Eƒeso ƒui ɔni na Yudaƒuɔ ku ɔma ɔmmɔ bekyuli ƒui bénu. Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, liƒu lɛ́da-ma geen, na Blɔti Yesu lɛnyi lɛ́sɔ lɛ́ƒɔ kuye líbu.

english_verse: Many who were followers now started telling everyone about the evil things they had been doing.
translation_verse: Amu na bani nénwini kayi ni, bébo bébedie bana lɛlɔ kalɔ na bekyuli anumi.

english_verse: Some who had been practicing witchcraft even brought their books and burned them in public. These books were worth about
translation_verse: Amu na bana akɔ bani náƒɛ evo béti bana evo lɛku ku lɛsɛbɛ béboku na bákyula-nya na bekyuli anumi. Lɛku lɛmmɔ ƒui kuye kɔdubɔbla aani sika ɔƒualadi mpim liti.

english_verse: So the Lord's message spread and became even more powerful. The Riot in Ephesus
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔɔtina kalɛ na Blɔti litemi lígyingya ku ɔyikun, na lɛ́ƒɔ mmɔ ƒui. Bukpoku Bɔdi Búbo Eƒeso

english_verse: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama ni, Katɔti Kɔyu kúdie kɔ́tina Paulo ɔnii ɔvi usie Makedonia ku Akaia asa na usie Yerusalem. Na Paulo ɔ́su ɔnini, “Si líduo mmɔ ni, ɔlɛka lɛvi lisie Roma lɛnɔ.”

english_verse: So he sent his two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But he stayed on in Asia for a while.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́tala nwuna bebunkune inyɔ, Timoteo ku Erasto, na bágyu batɔ-nwu na Makedonia. Na anwu ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kya kama na Asia mmɔ uwi blii ɔdi.

english_verse: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, lɛƒɛda bonwu lɛdi líbebo na Eƒeso na Kristo bɔƒɔtaadi ulu ɔmmɔ kama bɔsiaku ɔsu.

english_verse: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni úse kalɔ ɔ́si ukyuli ɔni baalɔ Demetrio ɔni muuti sika ɔƒualadi taakywɛ kakpakɔ ala. Na anwu ku nwuna bebunkune beeyé-nya teete bekyuli bani muubo taabakpa bana baƒiɔ bani baalɔ Artemi. Na ala amɛni buye eete-ma kɔsia geen.

english_verse: Demetrius brought together everyone who was in the same business and said: Friends, you know we make a good living at this.
translation_verse: Limeyi lɛdi ni, Demetrio ɔ́lɔ bakywɛne bamɛni ƒui ɔ́sala na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Banwa, bɛgyi ka bɔɔkɛ́ kɔsia geen na bula kabla kamɛni ɔsu.

english_verse: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
translation_verse: Na biinú na bɛɛnu kede kede kalɛ na Paulo ɔkya uuwi bula kabla kamɛni anumi kalɔ, na uunwíni bekyuli pii kasusu ɔnii baƒiɔ ala ani na bɔɔbla ƒui aaadi ala ani na bakya lili kalɔ bete! Ɔmɛni ɔsu na bula liyedi líbo kalɔ! Na ɔɔɔdi Eƒeso mɛni lɛti na ɔmɛni ɔdaku bɔlɛ. Mmomu ɔkya na Asia kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ ƒui!

english_verse: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
translation_verse: Nsu ɔɔɔdi bula kabla lɛti ndubɔyii udu! Geen geen ni, bula uni baƒiɔ benengudi Artemi lɛnyi ku nwuna ɔbu ɔdubɔyii na Asia mɛni ƒui!”

english_verse: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Amu ka bénu Demetrio butemi bɔmɛni ni, ɔƒɛ ɔ́da-ma na bákɛ kɔnyi pii na báva momoomo básu banini, “Eƒesoƒuɔ Uni Artemi ndi baƒiɔ benengudi ƒui!”

english_verse: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
translation_verse: Na kɔvanu kɔmmɔ kúgyingya kɔ́kya ɔma ɔmmɔ ƒui kemmo. Anwuɔsu bása lisu na bétéƒie Paulo basiakune inyɔ badi bani baalɔ Gaio ku Aristarko na bási Makedonia. Na béti-ma bésienku ɔma ɔmmɔ kasalakɔ.

english_verse: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo lɛnɔ ɔ́yɔ ka nka usie mmɔ, nsu Kristoƒuɔ bakladi bátatunaku-nwu.

english_verse: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
translation_verse: Amu na kalɛkɛ kammɔ benengu bani lɛnɔ ndi Paulo bakpana ni, bátala ɔtu bákya-nwu na bévele-nwu banii utakya lɛlɔ mmɔ munu munu!

english_verse: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, ɔtɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo ƒui kéyi ku lɛsɛ. Na bekyuli bani nábasa mmɔ ni, ɔdi biala ku lɛla lɛni na ɔɔsu. Na bana pii muedi baaagyi lɛla lɛni ɔsu na bébo mmɔ.

english_verse: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
translation_verse: Amu na bédi Aleksandro bétényene lɛtɔtɔ banii udie lɛla lɛni mɔɔlɛ́ mɛni kalɔ. Amu na Aleksandro ɔ́kɔliku enu katɔ na ɔ́bala-ma ɔnii baba lɛsɛ na ɔsu-ma lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Amu ka bekyuli bamɛni báti ka Yudani na ɔdi ni, básɔ bése kalɔ baaní lɛsɛ ku kɔvanu laa na ɔ́ƒɔ lɛdɔ bubo kunyɔ uwi. Na baasu banini, “Eƒesoƒuɔ Uni Artemi ndi baƒiɔ benengudi ƒui!”

english_verse: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
translation_verse: Uwi útu asa na aban unengu ɔdi ɔ́kana-ma bɔbala, na ɔ́tɛmi ɔ́su ɔnini, “Eƒesoƒuɔ, bina akɔ ɔdi biala ɔgyi ka Eƒeso mɛni ndi baƒiɔ benengudi Artemi keliekɔ. Na baƒiɔ lɛtabi kedee lɛni nási katɔ líbayu ni, bula lɛkɔkɔ na lɛkya.

english_verse: No one can deny this, and so you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
translation_verse: Na ukyuli ɔdi ulakana litemi lɛmɛni ɔkɔ bɔsia. Anwuɔsu bɛkɛ kayi buɛɛ na bitabla lɛla lɛdi ku kɔnyi.

english_verse: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
translation_verse: Ɔsika bekyuli bani na bíƒie bíboku mɛni ni, béteyu bula kakpakɔ lɛla lɛdi na bétebile bula Artemi baƒiɔ lɛnyi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: If Demetrius and his workers have a case against these men, we have courts and judges. Let them take their complaints there.
translation_verse: Nsu si Demetrio ku nwuna bakywɛne bánu ka bebo litemi lɛdi ku ukyuli ɔdi ni, litemi batɛne bakya mɛni. Na bubo emeyi ani lɛlɔ na baatɛ etemila. Bakana bedie bana bɔƒiɔ batina-ma na mmɔ. Bɛya na buwi lɛlɔ na bɔsia ulu ɔbuni lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
translation_verse: Nsu si lɛla bamba na bɛɛwia bɛti ni, bɛya na bɔda bɔlɛ kadi benengu anumi.

english_verse: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
translation_verse: Ɔsika ɔmɛni use aani si bɔ́ta bunye aban lɛlɔ. Na si Romaƒuɔ bekpone bébo bábanu ɔmwi limeyi lɛmɛni ablala ni, bulakana kenye budie, na badubɔni-bu kɔtu.”

english_verse: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́su ala amɛni ni, ɔ́bɔku-ma na bana ƒui bégyingya.

english_verse: When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na lɛsɛ lɛmmɔ líbo kalɔ ni, Paulo ɔ́lɔ baƒɔtaadine bamɛni ɔ́sala. Na ka ɔ́kya-ma ɔkplu na bana bɔƒɔtaadi kemmo ɔ́wɔlɔ ni, úye ulu na ɔ́kada-ma na ɔ́tɔlɔ úsie Makedonia.

english_verse: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
translation_verse: Na nwuna ulu busie kemmo ni, Paulo ɔ́vi ekutɛ ammɔ ƒui na ɔ́su-ma Blɔti etemila pii úti ɔ́kya-ma ogya útédu Akaia.

english_verse: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́kya aani abuli atɛ. Uwi ɔni na ɔɔklibi lɛlɔ ka watɔlɔ wesie Siria ni, ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka Yudaƒuɔ bakya baawia nwuna ngba na ulu ɔdi lɛlɔ. Anwuɔsu ɔ́bla nwuna kasusu ɔnii ɔsɔ ɔɔsia usie Makedonia.

english_verse: With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na úsela ni, anwu ku bekyuli pii nkɛ. Na bekyuli bamɛni ndi Sopater ɔni nási Beroia na ɔdi Piro ubidi ku Aristarko ku Sekundo bani nási Tesalonika ku Gaio ɔni nási Derbe ku Tihiko ku Troƒimo bani nási Asia kalɛkɛ ku Timoteo.

english_verse: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
translation_verse: Ama nágyu bátɔ-bu béténye ɔma ɔni baalɔ banii Troa bágya-bu.

english_verse: After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week. Paul's Last Visit to Troas
translation_verse: Amu ka Yudaƒuɔ emeyi ani na bɔɔdi Bodobodo Ɔni Néteƒu Limeyi ávi ni, búti ɔkɔlɔ na Ƒilipi, na bútásiaku-ma na Troa emeyi alɔ kama. Na búlie mmɔ emeyi maatɛ. Paulo Úsie Troa Kukplodi

english_verse: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
translation_verse: Amu na Kwasida limeyi lideedi lɛlɔ ni, bɔ́sala lɛlɔ lisu bɔnii bɔɔdi Blɔti adila. Na ka Paulo ɔdubo bɔtɔlɔ kadi kegye ɔsu ni, útemi laa útédu usientɛ.

english_verse: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
translation_verse: Na bátu likpo pii bése ɔtɔ ɔtɔdi ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
translation_verse: Amu ka Paulo útemi úsela laa ni, lɛlɛɛ líti okloƒu ɔni baalɔ Eutiko uwi ɔni na ulie katɔ ƒansili lɛlɔ. Mmɔ na ɔ́ƒami ɔ́si katu taasia ɔtɔ ɔtɛdi lɛlɔ mmɔ úbayu kalɔ. Na bani nátása-nwu kudɔ ni, bánu ka úkpi.

english_verse: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
translation_verse: Nsu ka Paulo ɔ́yu úbo kalɔ ni, ɔ́kpɛ-nwu uboku lɛlɔ na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bitebo kudu! Ɔkya ngba!”

english_verse: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
translation_verse: Amu na bana ƒui básɔ bénwini bésie katɔ mmɔ bátádi Blɔti adila. Na básɔ bátɛmiku lɛlɔ útédu lɛdigye asa na Paulo ɔ́tɔlɔ.

english_verse: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
translation_verse: Nsu ka okloƒu ɔni na bágyila mmɔ ɔ́sɔ ɔkya-ma akɔ ɔsu ni, kayi káyɔ-ma. Paulo Ɔ́si Troa Úsie Mileto

english_verse: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo ɔ́sia lɛgba ulu úsie Aso. Nsu abu bani na abu ku-nwu bɔkɛ ni, búti ɔkɔlɔ bɔ́gyu bɔ́tɔ-nwu kalɛ na butása mmɔ na buti-nwu aani kalɛ na ɔ́su.

english_verse: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
translation_verse: Amu ka úbo úbanu-bu na Aso mmɔ ni, abu ku-nwu ƒui bɔ́tɔlɔ búsie Mitilene.

english_verse: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
translation_verse: Na kadi kégye ni, bútéduo Kio. Amu na limeyi lɛni nsɔ nsia lɛmmɔ kama ni, bútéduo Samo. Amu na limeyi lɛtɛdi ni, búsie bútéduo Mileto.

english_verse: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
translation_verse: Paulo ɔ́ya na búbo bɔ́vi Eƒeso, ɔsika útayɔ ka ɔdi uwi gyɔlɔɔ ɔdi na Asia kalɔ mmɔ. Na ɔ́lɛ ugyii ka si ɔ́kana ni, na uduo Yerusalem na Pentekoste limeyi lɛlɔ. Paulo Ɔ́kada Eƒeso Baƒɔtaadine Benengu

english_verse: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
translation_verse: Amu ka bútédu Mileto ni, ɔ́tala batu ɔ́kya Eƒesoƒuɔ baƒɔtaadine benengu ɔnii bebo babanu-nwu na mmɔ.

english_verse: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
translation_verse: Amu ka bébo ni, ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Banwa, bina ƒui bɛgyi ka ńtalɛ-mii kama kudii ɔ́si limeyi lideedi lɛni na lɛ́ka Asia kalɔ lɛlɔ mɛni bubo úti úbedu ɔƒaani.

english_verse: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
translation_verse: Bɛ́nu kalɛ na lɛ́siaku Blɔti na lɛlɔ kalɔ buboku kemmo, ina ka líbo abi ku keku ɔ́si ɔni na Yudaƒuɔ báwia ka badu-mi ɔsu.

english_verse: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
translation_verse: Bɛɛnu-mi kaƒɔ. Lɛɛɛdi ulikplune. Na Blɔti ala ani ƒui ngyi na nwuna lɛlɔ ni, anya na lɛtina-mii, na ńteti ɔdi ńtabla-mii. Lɛ́tina Blɔti litemi lɛmɛni na kadi ƒui anumi ku bina kɔduli.

english_verse: I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Na kesi kesii na lísie ni, lɛ́su Yudaƒuɔ ku Helaƒuɔ ƒui kpakplaa ka bada ekpidi bɔbla baya na benwini besie Katɔti kudɔ, na baƒɔ Blɔti Yesu Kristo badi.

english_verse: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
translation_verse: “Na ɔƒaani ni, Katɔti Kɔyu kɔɔsu-mi ka nteesie Yerusalem, ɔni na lɛɛɛgyi lɛla lɛni malɛku-mi mmɔ.

english_verse: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nsu na lɛma lɛni ƒui kemmo na mɔɔví ni, Katɔti Kɔyu kɔɔyá na mɔɔtí ka ndubɔtɛ ɔtɔ ku lɛbibo.

english_verse: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Nsu ɔmmɔ ɔɔɔdi-mi lɛla lɛdi. Ɔsika si ńtakana na lɛbla lɛla lɛni na Blɔti Yesu ɔ́tala-mi ɔnii mbabla ni, mina ngba buuubo-mi kɔsia kɔdi. Lɛla lɛni na Yesu ɔ́tala-mi ɔnii mbabla ndi ka lɛsu bekyuli Blɔti litemi buni ku kalɛ na Katɔti ɔɔnu-bu kɔnyana.

english_verse: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
translation_verse: “Na ni, amii bani ƒui nénu mina ala bɔtina ɔ́si Blɔti lɛga kadikɔ ala lɛlɔ ni, bɔsɔ bulasa kudii.

english_verse: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu muute-mii bɔti ka ni, si ɔdi ɔ́yila nwuna ngba ulu ni, beleti ukyuli ɔmmɔ kɔtɔ bɔdu balasia-mi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
translation_verse: Sɔsɔ ni, ńteti Katɔti lɛga kadikɔ ulu lɛla lɛdi ńtabla-mii.

english_verse: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, binye lɛlɔ kagyumana. Katɔti Kɔyu nábla-mii batɔnkune ɔnii bɛda nwuna bebi bani na Katɔti úti úte-mii bɔda kɔkɔɔkɔ. Bɛda-ma kaduɛ, ɔsika Katɔti úwi Ubidi ubugya kalɔ úti udie-ma lili.

english_verse: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
translation_verse: Na ngyi kede kede ka si lɛ́tɔlɔ-mii kudɔ ni, bekyuli badubo bɔta bukpoku-mii na begyingya-mii aani kalɛ na begiti beekpóku baƒonu.

english_verse: Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Na bina akɔ muedi ni, badi badubo litemi geen lɛmmɔ bɔda bɔnyonu na bakpanku bekyuli pii basiaku bana ɔkɔ ala bɔtina kama.

english_verse: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
translation_verse: Binye kagyumana na bɛkali bɛnu kalɛ na líti keku buwulo lɛ́lɛ-mii na lɛ́tina-mii ala usien ku ɔƒɛ na akwa atɛ ani na lɛ́kya-mii kudɔ kemmo.

english_verse: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
translation_verse: “Na ɔƒaani ni, líti-mii mɔɔkya Blɔti lɛkɔkɔ nnii ɔnu-mii lɛlɔ. Na nwuna litemi lɛni muubunku bekyuli mɛni lɛkya bina bɔƒɔtaadi ɔkplu kalɛ na wabla-mii katɔ ala badine aani bani na ɔ́ƒuna úte nwuna lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
translation_verse: Anumi étegyie-mi na ɔkpanadi sika ugyiedi iye ɔƒualadi iye lɛwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
translation_verse: Amii alati bɛgyi ka mina enu amɛni líti lɛ́bla kabla kani na ńtaadi ku kani na ńteeti taanu bekyuli bani nsiaku-mi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
translation_verse: Lɛ́bla ala amɛni ƒui líti lɛ́tina-mii kalɛ na buteebunku bawabane, na binyimo litemi lɛni na Blɔti Yesu ɔ́su ɔnini, ‘Bute bɔdia butulo bɔƒɔ.’ ”

english_verse: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Paulo ɔ́wɔlɔ butemi bɔmɛni ni, ɔ́lɛ akɔnkɔ na ama ku-nwu bákpali katɔ.

english_verse: Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him.
translation_verse: Na bana ƒui bátu báda-nwu na beewulo ɔ́si bana lɛlɔ bɔkada bɔmɛni ɔsu.

english_verse: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_verse: Na lɛla lɛni nábla-ma ɔkwɛnu útulo ndi ɔni na ɔ́su-ma ɔnii basɔ baaadubo-nwu bɔnu ɔsu. Amu na básiaku-nwu na béti-nwu bétése ɔkɔlɔ kudɔ na ketu kenye mmɔ.

english_verse: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na bɔ́kada lɛlɔ bɔ́wɔlɔ ni, bútéduo ɔkɔlɔ kemmo na bɔ́via búsie Ko. Amu na kadi kégye ni, bútéduo Rodo na bɔkɛ mmɔ bɔ́vi búsie Patara.

english_verse: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
translation_verse: Na mmɔ na bútéti ɔkɔlɔ ɔdi ɔni nésela Ƒoinike, na bɔ́tɔlɔ.

english_verse: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
translation_verse: Amu na bɔ́nu Kipro kalɔ, na bɔ́da mmɔ bɔ́va na búti bɔ́yu kada kakɛ búsie bútáyu Tiro. Na bútásia kesii kani na badubudie ala ani nkya ɔkɔlɔ ɔmɛni kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na búlie-ma kudɔ bɔ́wɔlɔ na búsela ni, baƒɔtaadine bamɛni ku bana beleku ku bebi ƒui béti-bu bétésie ɛpu kɔtu, na bula ƒui bɔ́lɛ akɔnkɔ na bɔ́kpali katɔ.

english_verse: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
translation_verse: Amu na bɔ́kada lɛlɔ na bɔ́gyu bútéduo ɔkɔlɔ kemmo, na ama lɛnɔ bénwini bésie bana kɔduli.

english_verse: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
translation_verse: Amu ka bɔ́ta Tiro ni, bútédi búnye Ptolemai. Mmɔ na bútégyele baƒɔtaadine bani nkya mmɔ, na búlie-ma kudɔ limeyi linwi.

english_verse: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
translation_verse: Amu ka kadi kégye ni, bɔ́ta mmɔ búsie Kaesarea. Na bútéduo Litemi Buni Lɛsa Ɔkɔne Ƒilipo kesii. Anwu ndi bebunkune maatɛ bani na bédie na Yerusalem akɔ unwi.

english_verse: and he had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
translation_verse: Na ubo bebi begblebi ine bani neeelie agya na badi Katɔti kenye bediene.

english_verse: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
translation_verse: Amu na búlie mmɔ emeyi pii adi. Na uwi ɔni na bɔkya mmɔ ni, Katɔti kenye udiene ɔdi ɔni baalɔ Agabo ɔ́si Yudea úbo mmɔ.

english_verse: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Amu ka úbo-bu kudɔ ni, ɔ́ƒɛnimi kabuli kani nda Paulo kavobi na únyimi anwu ɔlati enu ku lɛgba na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Katɔti Kɔyu kɔɔsu ka lɛni na Yudaƒuɔ badubunyimi ukyuli ɔni mbo kabuli kamɛni na Yerusalem na beti-nwu bakya ama bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ lɛlɔ badine enu kemmo.”

english_verse: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amu ka búnu etemila amɛni ni, abu ku bekyuli bani nkya mmɔ ƒui búvele Paulo bɔnii utesie Yerusalem.

english_verse: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔ́su-bu ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na biiwulo na bɛɛƒɛ-mi enu lɛni? Ami lɛ́tuna ka benyimi-mi na Yerusalem, na likpi lite Blɔti Yesu lɛnyi.”

english_verse: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na bɔ́nu bɔ́ti ka bulakana-nwu kasusu bunwini ni, bɔ́da-nwu bɔ́nyonu na bɔ́su bɔnini, “Babla Unwoti lɛƒɔyɔ.”

english_verse: Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amu na emeyi adi kama ni, bɔ́sala bula ala ƒui lisu na bɔ́tɔlɔ búsie Yerusalem.

english_verse: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
translation_verse: Na Kaesarea baƒɔtaadine badi básiaku-bu. Na bákpanku Kiproni unengu ɔni baalɔ banii Mnason bada banii butéduo-nwu kudɔ na mmɔ. Na unengu ɔmɛni ɔdi ɔƒɔtaadine ɔ́si kukuuku.

english_verse: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
translation_verse: Amu ka búduo Yerusalem ni, baƒɔtaadine bani nkya mmɔ báƒɔ-bu kaduɛ. Paulo Úsie Útánu Yakobo

english_verse: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
translation_verse: Na ka kadi kégye ni, Paulo útiku-bu na búsie bútánu Yakobo ku Yerusalem baƒɔtaadine benengu.

english_verse: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Na ka búgyele-ma bɔ́wɔlɔ ni, Paulo ɔ́su-ma ala ani ƒui na Katɔti ɔ́bla ɔ́kɛnku-nwu lɛlɔ na bekyuli bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ akɔ.

english_verse: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, bana ƒui bémwi Blɔti. Amu na básu-nwu banini, “Ɔnwa ɔyɔne, agyi lɛla lɛni nálɛ Yerusalem mɛni. Yudaƒuɔ mpim mpim badi bakya bani náƒɔ bádi na bada Mose ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ kpakplaa.

english_verse: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
translation_verse: Badi básu-ma ka awɔ nátina Yudaƒuɔ bani nkya ekpo ekpo anii batasiaku Mose ɔda bubo ku bula ɔdi bɔbla kama, na ásu lɛnɔ ka betekulo bana bebi ago lɛnɔ.

english_verse: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu bi na ɔlɛka bɔbla ɔƒaani? Bɔgyi ka badubutiku lɛlɔ na bebo. Ɔsika badubunu ka ébo-bu kudɔ mɛni.”

english_verse: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
translation_verse: Amu na béte-nwu kasusu kadi banini, “Bubo nkyuli ine badi na bula ɔma mɛni, bani nése kenye.

english_verse: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ti-ma sienku Yudaƒuɔ kakpakɔ mmɔ na ebunku-ma na bana lili bukpeyi kayu bɔƒɔ. Ɔmɛni ndubɔya na ukyuli biala ɔnu ka ɔkɔ na bányi básia-a, na awɔ lɛnɔ ada Mose ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ kaduɛ.

english_verse: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Na ama bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ na bénwini baƒɔtaadine ni, búnweni-ma ɔku na bɔ́su-ma ka ni, bada ala ani na béti bákpa béte baƒiɔ bɔdi baya ku ubugya bɔni baya, na batakun bebuo bani na bélii-ma amɔ bádu, na batadi kɔsɔnɔ.”

english_verse: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ka kadi kégye ni, Paulo útiku banana bammɔ na bésie batábla lɛlɔ buveli ɔdi ɔmmɔ. Nwuna kama úsie Yudaƒuɔ kakpakɔ na útéte bakpane bɔti emeyi ani kama asa na lɛlɔ buveli ɔdi ɔmmɔ webo kawɔlɔkɔ kalɛ na beti etela beboku na babla akpala na bana lili. Béƒie Paulo Na Yudaƒuɔ Kakpakɔ

english_verse: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
translation_verse: Amu ka kébu blii na emeyi maatɛ ammɔ edu ni, Yudaƒuɔ badi bási Asia kalɛkɛ bábanu Paulo na Yudaƒuɔ kakpakɔ mmɔ. Amu na bátásala bekyuli badi lisu na bétéƒie-nwu.

english_verse: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Na bákya baava taasu banini, “Israelƒuɔ banana, bibebunku-bu o-o! Ɔnana ɔmɛni nkɛ mɔɔsu bekyuli ƒui taavi na kesi kesii ku mɛni lɛnɔ ɔnii batadi bula Yudaƒuɔ ɔda bubo lɛlɔ. Na lɛnɔ ni, uuti Grikiƒuɔ teeduoku Yudaƒuɔ kakpakɔ ɔni mɔɔtina ka bula Yudaƒuɔ kakpakɔ kammɔ keesé lɛlɔ!”

english_verse: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
translation_verse: Básu lɛni ɔsika uwi ɔdi kemmo ni, bánu ka Paulo ku Troƒimo ɔni ndi Eƒesoni bakɛ na Yerusalem. Anwuɔsu bákali banii útiku-nwu úsienku Yudaƒuɔ kakpakɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
translation_verse: Amu na bɔva bɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, bekyuli ƒui béƒu na báta ku lɛsɛ na békeli bátása kakpakɔ mmɔ. Badi báni Paulo bálɛku kakpakɔ na bákalɛ kɔyakun ƒui.

english_verse: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
translation_verse: Amu uwi ɔni na báwia ka badu-nwu ni, Romaƒuɔ bekpone unengu ɔdi únu ka Yerusalemƒuɔ ƒui báta baakya lɛsɛ.

english_verse: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
translation_verse: Kɔnakunwi ni, útiku bekpone badi na bésie lɛsɛ kanikɔ mmɔ. Amu ka lɛsɛ bakyane bammɔ bánu bekpone bamɛni ni, báda Paulo bubo báya.

english_verse: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
translation_verse: Mmɔ kani na bekpone bamɛni unengu ɔ́ya na béƒie Paulo na béti kɔgba inyɔ bébo báda-nwu. Amu na úye únu ukyuli ɔni na ɔnana ɔmmɔ ɔdi ku lɛla lɛni na ɔ́bla.

english_verse: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bamɛni kemmo ɔdi biala ɔɔsu litemi bamba. Na ka bekpone unengu ɔmɛni ulenu litemi ƒeelee lɛdi ulasiku-ma kudɔ ɔsu ni, ɔ́ya béti Paulo batákya bekpone ɔtɔ kemmo.

english_verse: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
translation_verse: Nsu uwi ɔni na báwia ka beti-nwu bakya ɔtɔ kemmo ni, Paulo ɔ́su bekpone unengu ɔmɛni ɔnini, “Mɔɔyɔ́ ka lɛtɛmiku-ɔ blii.” Amu na bekpone unengu ɔmɛni úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi! Eenú Griki butemi?”

english_verse: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo údie kenye ɔnini, “Yudani na ndi. Báwɔ-mi na Tarso na Kilikia kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔma ɔmmɔ ni, ɔɔɔdi ɔma ubliidi na ɔdi. Anwuɔsu, buvele, ya na lɛtɛmiku bekyuli bammɔ.”

english_verse: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_verse: Amu na unengu ɔmɛni ɔ́tuna ɔnii Paulo ɔtɛmiku-ma. Na Paulo úbenye kayakun ubili kakɔkɔ mmɔ na ɔ́kɔliku kɔnu katɔ na ɔ́bala bekyuli lisu lɛmɛni. Na ka báda lɛsɛ báya ni, útemi úte-ma na Yudaƒuɔ butemi kemmo ɔnini,

english_verse: “My friends and leaders of our nation, listen as I explain what happened!”
translation_verse: “Ati bene ku banwa, agoo! Bɛya na lidie lɛlɔ kenye na binu.”

english_verse: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na bénu ka Yudaƒuɔ lɛdi kemmo na uutemi ni, básɔ bába lɛsɛ bébu.

english_verse: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
translation_verse: Na Paulo ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Yudani na ndi, na báwɔ-mi na Tarso na Kilikia kalɔ lɛlɔ. Nsu ni, Yerusalem mɛni na lísie sukuu. Gamaliel kalɔ na lɛ́kya lɛ́tɛya ala. Bátina-mi bula bati ɔda bubo ala ku bana ɔdi ƒui kaduɛ geen. Na líti mina kayi ƒui líte Katɔti aani kalɛ kani na amii lɛnɔ bɛɛbla.

english_verse: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si uwi ɔmmɔ ni, líse kalɔ muukpóku bekyuli bani nsiaku Kristo baƒɔtaadine ulu lɛlɔ, na mɔɔyá na baadú-ma. Na líƒie banana ku beleku lɛ́kya aban ɔtɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
translation_verse: Ɔkpane unengudi ku kasalakɔ unengu biala ɔdubudie lɛla lɛni mɔɔsu mɛni kenye, ɔsika béteenweni lɛku teete-mi banii ntátaabla ala amɛni. Na uwi ɔni na lísela Damasko ni, béte-mi ɔyikun ka si lɛ́nu baƒɔtaadine bani nkya mmɔ ni, na liƒie-ma, na linyimi-ma liboku Yerusalem na bani-ma kɔtu. Paulo Ɔ́su Nwuna Kayi Bunwini Lɛlɔ Litemi

english_verse: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
translation_verse: “Uwi ɔni na nkɛ lísela na úbu blii na liduo Damasko ni, ɔbla aani ɔƒiiwi lɛdɔ leevu-inyɔ kemmo ni, kɔnakunwi bukeye bɔni mbo ɔkplu bɔdi bɔ́si katɔ búbewi-mi!

english_verse: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
translation_verse: Amu na líbuli lɛ́tɛ kalɔ na línu ka lɛdi lɛdi lɛɛsu-mi lɛnini, ‘Saulo, Saulo, bi ɔsu na eekpóku-mi lɛni?’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
translation_verse: “Amu na líye nnini, ‘Ati, ɔma na adi?’ “Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Ami ndi Yesu Nasareni ɔni na eekpóku kpakplaa.’

english_verse: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani na ami ku-ma bɔkɛ ni, bánu bukeye bɔmɛni, nsu bétenu ukyuli ɔni na ami ku-nwu bɔɔtɛmi mmɔ lɛdi.

english_verse: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
translation_verse: “Na líye-nwu nnini, ‘Blɔti, bi na ɔlɛka lɛbla?’ “Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Ta, na eteesie Damasko. Mmɔ na ndubɔtina-a lɛla lɛni na lɛ́ƒuna líte-ɔ ka abla.’

english_verse: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
translation_verse: Bukeye bubendi bɔmɛni bɔ́bwɛ-mi anumi ɔni na bekyuli bani na ami ku-ma bɔ́kɛ mɛni náda-mi kɔnu asa na bɔ́tɔlɔ bútéduo Damasko.

english_verse: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
translation_verse: “Na mmɔ ni, ɔnana ɔdi ɔkya ɔni baalɔ Anania. Ɔdi ukyuli ɔni mɔɔkya lili kalɔ teete Katɔti geen, na ɔsiaku bula ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ lɛnɔ. Na Yudaƒuɔ bani nkya mmɔ ƒui baabu-nwu kaduɛ.

english_verse: He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!” At once I could see.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔmɛni úbo úbenye-mi kudɔ na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Ɔnwa Saulo, bimi anumi!’ Na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo kani ni, mina anumi ábla nwaa na lɛ́nu-nwu!

english_verse: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Bula bati kuuku Katɔti náƒuna-a kalɛ na anu nwuna lɛyɔla ati, na anu nwuna Ukyuli Ɔƒunadi Kedee ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ ati, na eteenu-nwu lɛdi.

english_verse: You must tell everyone what you have seen and heard.
translation_verse: Ɔlɛka eti linyesia lɛmɛni esienku kesi kesii na asu bekyuli ƒui lɛla lɛni na ánu ku ani na énu ƒui.

english_verse: What are you waiting for? Get up! Be baptized, and wash away your sins by praying to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na ɔƒaani ni, lɛla lɛdi lɛ́sɔ lítebu. Ta, na aƒɔ ntu bɔkpila ɔdi. Na akpali Blɔti lɛnyi, na ɔdubɔƒɔ ƒula ekpidi udie-ɔ lɛlɔ.’ Katɔti Ɔ́tala Paulo Na Bani Naaadi Yudaƒuɔ Kudɔ

english_verse: After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision
translation_verse: “Ɔmɛni kama ni, línwini lísie Yerusalem. Na ka nkya kakpakɔ mɔɔkpali katɔ ni, ɔ́bla-mi aani si bɔlɛɛ na nda, na lɛ́nu budie taatina bɔdi.

english_verse: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ na Blɔti ɔlati ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Babla na avi alɛ Yerusalem, ɔsika mɛni bekyuli belénu-ɔ litemi lɛni na aasu taasiku-mi lɛlɔ.’

english_verse: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
translation_verse: “Nsu lídie kenye nnini, ‘Blɔti, bana ƒui bagyi ka ami ńteeƒie ama bani náƒɔ-ɔ badi na ńteebo-ma.

english_verse: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na badubɔdu Steƒano ni, ami lɛnɔ lɛ́tuna, na bédie bana lɛwu béte-mi, na nda-ni asa na beebó-nwu atabi.’

english_verse: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: “Nsu Blɔti ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Ta, na eteesie ɔgyu kakaaka na kesii kani mɔɔtala-a na bekyuli bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ akɔ!’ ”

english_verse: The crowd listened until Paul said this. Then they started shouting, “Get rid of this man! He doesn't deserve to live.”
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔmɛni ƒui ni, bekyuli bamɛni benye kpoo beenú-nwu litemi. Nsu uwi ɔni na ɔ́su lɛla likplodi lɛmɛni ni, bana ƒui báva momoomo básu banini, “Aa! Bɛyila-nwu udu! Bɛtɔlɔku-nwu ƒui!”

english_verse: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
translation_verse: Amu na báva momoomo na bése kalɔ baakuna bana lɛwu, na beebo ɔtumu lɛnɔ taakɔliku katɔ na kɔnyi ɔsu.

english_verse: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
translation_verse: Na bekpone ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ ɔ́ya na béti-nwu béduoku ɔtɔ kemmo ɔnii betébo-nwu na ɔwia ɔti lɛla lɛni ɔsu na Yudaƒuɔ bamɛni baakywɛ-nwu anumi lɛni.

english_verse: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na benye beenyimi-nwu ni, Paulo úye Romaƒuɔ bekpone unengu ɔdi ɔnini, “Ulu ɔtɛ ka bebo Romani ubi ɔni na batatɛku-nwu tɔ litemi?”

english_verse: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
translation_verse: Amu na unengu ɔmɛni úsie bana ɔtɔnkune kudɔ na útéye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi ɔdi na bɛɛbla mɛni? Ɔnana ɔmɛni ni, Romani na ɔdi!”

english_verse: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bekpone ɔtɔnkune ɔmɛni úsie Paulo kudɔ na útéye-nwu ɔnini, “Anii bi? Romani na adi?” Amu na Paulo údie kenye ɔnini, “Romani geen na ndi!”

english_verse: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔtɔnkune ɔmɛni ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ami lɛnɔ Romani na ndi. Na ami líbo kayu pim asa na línwini Romani!” Amu na Paulo ɔ́sɔ údie kenye ɔnini, “Ami ni, mina bawɔne ƒui badi Romaƒuɔ.”

english_verse: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
translation_verse: Mmɔ mmɔ ka bekyuli bani na nka benye kagyumana ka bebo-nwu mɛni bénu ka Romani na ɔdi ni, bana ƒui békeyi lɛlɔ na bákpɛ bésie kama. Amu ka bana ɔtɔnkune ɔ́ti ka Romani na ɔdi ni, ɔtɔtɔ ɔ́gyu-nwu na liƒu lɛ́da-nwu geen, ɔsika anwu néte kuƒi na bébo-nwu kɔgba. Béti Paulo Béboku Litemi Batɛne Anumi

english_verse: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
translation_verse: Amu ka kadi kégye na bekpone ɔtɔnkune ɔmɛni ɔɔwia ɔti lɛla lɛni nébo asa na baadá Paulo kenye ni, ɔ́lɔ Yudaƒuɔ bakpane benengu ku bana litemi batɛne ƒui na bábasala lisu. Na ɔ́ya na báƒɛnimi Paulo na bétiku-nwu béboku-ma anumi banii beeduo nwuna litemi kemmo.

english_verse: Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
translation_verse: Amu ka Paulo ɔ́tɛ anu na ɔ́nu Yudaƒuɔ litemi batɛne bani nása bélie litemi katɛkɔ mmɔ kpoo ni, ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Banwa, mina kayi kaladu-mi kɔtɔ kɔdi na Katɔti anumi úbedu ɔmwi kadi kamɛni lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
translation_verse: Amu ka Anania ɔni ndi Yudaƒuɔ ɔkpane unengudi na bana akɔ mmɔ únu Paulo kenye kamɛni ni, údie lɛdi úte bani nnye Paulo kudɔ mmɔ na báƒiɛmi-nwu ɔtugya.

english_verse: Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
translation_verse: Mmɔ mmɔ ni, Paulo ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Katɔti ɔdubɔƒiɛmi-ɔ ɔsia! Atɔnku akwadi na adi! Bi litemi ɔtɛne udu na adi mɛni? Ɔda bubo bɔni lɛlɔ na akɛ átɛku-mi litemi ni, amu kani lɛlɔ na áta enye uwi ɔni na áya na báƒiɛmi-mi kɔnu!”

english_verse: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
translation_verse: Amu na ama bani nnye Paulo kudɔ mmɔ béye-nwu banini, “Ɔkpane unengudi na eedumi lɛni?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Paulo údie kenye ɔnini, “Banwa, ńtati nnii anwu ndi ɔkpane unengudi, nka ńtasu-nwu lɛni. Ɔsika Bunweni Kedee Ɔku ɔ́su ɔnii, ‘Bitetemi lɛla likpidi lɛdi na bina batɔnkune lɛlɔ.’ ”

english_verse: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka ni, bekyuli bani nábasa mmɔ akɔ badi badi lɛkpa lɛni baalɔ Sadukiƒuɔ, na badi lɛnɔ badi Ƒarisiƒuɔ. Anwuɔsu ɔ́va momoomo ɔnini, “Banwa, Ƒarisini na ndi! Na Ƒarisini náwɔ-mi! Na baatɛku-mi litemi mɛni ɔmwi ɔni na lɛ́ƒɔ bekpine bɔsɔ taata lɛ́di ɔsu!”

english_verse: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
translation_verse: Amu ka Paulo ɔ́nya ɔ́su litemi lɛmɛni ni, mmɔ kani na kadɔ kéduo akpa anyɔ amɛni ntɛ, na béle lɛlɔ kemmo.

english_verse: The Sadducees do not believe in angels or spirits or that the dead will rise to life. But the Pharisees believe in all of these,
translation_verse: Ɔsika ama Sadukiƒuɔ baasu banii ukpine ɔsɔ ulata, na Katɔti batu beeebo, na ayu lɛnɔ eeebo. Nsu Ƒarisiƒuɔ ni, ama baaƒɔ́ ala amɛni ƒui taadi.

english_verse: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
translation_verse: Mɛni na owogyo ɔdi úbeduo-ma akɔ. Na ɔda bubo ala batinane bani ndi Ƒarisiƒuɔ bénye Paulo litemi lɛmmɔ kama banii lɛdi litemi geen. Na báva momoomo básu banini, “Bútanu lɛla likpidi lɛdi na nwuna lɛlɔ! Na si kɔyu kɔdi iye Katɔti ɔtu ɔdi nétemiku-nwu ni, bitaya na bukpoku Katɔti!”

english_verse: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
translation_verse: Mɛni ni, bɔva bɔmɛni bɔ́sɔ bɔ́kɔ katɔ búbu. Na bekyuli bamɛni ƒui bada Paulo na baaní-nwu teenene. Na ka bekpone ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ ɔɔyia ka badubɔni-nwu baduli ɔsu ni, ɔ́su nwuna bekpone ɔnii beti-nwu beboku aban ɔtɔ kemmo.

english_verse: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
translation_verse: Amu na limeyi lɛmmɔ usientɛ ni, Blɔti úbenye Paulo kudɔ na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Paulo, kya ɔkplu. Kalɛ na ásu mina lɛlɔ litemi mɛni na Yerusalem ni, lɛni kani na adubɔsu-ni na Roma lɛnɔ.” Yudaƒuɔ Bása Lili Ka Badu Paulo

english_verse: The next morning more than
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bamɛni badubɔbla aani nkyuli aavlene ku kama.

english_verse: Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul.
translation_verse: Amu na básɔ bésie bakpane benengu ku bana batɔnkune kudɔ na bátásu-ma banini, “Búse kenye ka buladi na buláni si bútadu Paulo.

english_verse: You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu amii ku litemi batɛne bɛsu bekpone ɔtɔnkune na ɔsɔ utédie Paulo uboku kasalakɔ mɛni. Bɛbla aani si bɛɛwia ka biye-nwu etemila adi bibu. Na si béti-nwu badububoku ni, na bɔdubɔdu-nwu na ulu.”

english_verse: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
translation_verse: Nsu ka Paulo ɔnwani ulekubi ubidi ɔnanabi únu ala ani na básu mɛni ƒui ɔsu ni, úkeli úsie aban ɔtɔ mmɔ na útásu Paulo lɛla lɛni na básu.

english_verse: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
