translation_verse: Amu na Paulo ɔ́lɔ bekpone bani nnye mmɔ kemmo unwi na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Tiku ɔnamu ɔmɛni teesienku bina ɔtɔnkune kudɔ. Ɔ́da litemi kpakplaa lɛdi na ɔsu-nwu.”

english_verse: The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ni, ukpone ɔmmɔ útiku ubi ɔmɛni úsienku ɔtɔnkune ɔmmɔ kudɔ. Na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Paulo ɔni na bákya ɔtɔ mɛni nálɔ-mi na ɔ́su-mi ɔnii ntiku ubi ɔmɛni mboku-ɔ kudɔ na ubasu-ɔ litemi lɛdi.”

english_verse: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
translation_verse: Amu na bekpone ɔtɔnkune ɔmɛni ɔda ubi ɔmɛni kɔnu na útiku-nwu úsienku kɔƒɛlɛ na úye-nwu ɔnini, “Bi na aawia ka asu-mi?”

english_verse: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Yudaƒuɔ badi bása kenye ku bana benengu banii bebevele-ɔ na biti Paulo biboku kasalakɔ mmɔ kɔnaadi ku kasusu ka beye-nwu etemila adi.

english_verse: The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.” Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
translation_verse: Bekpone Ɔtɔnkune ɔmɛni ɔ́bala-nwu ɔnini, “Taya na ukyuli ɔdi biala ɔsɔ unu litemi lɛni na ásu-mi mɛni munu munu!” Béti Paulo Bésienku Ɔga Ƒelike Kudɔ

english_verse: Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
translation_verse: Bite Paulo ɔpɔnkɔ ɔdi na ulie-nwu kama na bitiku-nwu buɛɛ bisienku Aban Ɔgadine Ƒelike.”

english_verse: The commander wrote a letter that said:
translation_verse: Amu na únweni ɔku ɔdi úte kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔmmɔ ɔnini,

english_verse: Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
translation_verse: Ɔku ɔmɛni ɔ́si ami Klaudio Lisia kudɔ na liti muute awɔ Ɔgadine Ɔbune Ƒelike ku kegye.

english_verse: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
translation_verse: Yudaƒuɔ béƒie ukyuli ɔmɛni na nka bɔdu banii baadú-nwu asa na ami lɛ́ya bekpone bátáƒɔ-nwu, ɔsika línu ka Romani ubi na ɔdi ɔsu.

english_verse: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
translation_verse: Amu na líti-nwu lísienku bana kasalakɔ kalɛ na bunu lɛla lɛni na ɔ́bla.

english_verse: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
translation_verse: Lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka ala ani badaku mɛni adi ama Yudaƒuɔ ɔda bubo ala ɔni na ɔɔɔdi bɔƒiɔ bɔni na bakya-nwu ɔtɔ iye badu-nwu.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na básu-mi ka baabla-nwu lɛlɔ kasusu ka badubo-nwu bɔdu ni, lɛ́bu lili kemmo nnii muuti-nwu liboku-ɔ na lɛsu ama bani na anwu ku-ma bákɛ litemi ka beti nwuna bɔƒiɔ beboku-ɔ anumi.

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu usien ɔmmɔ kani ni, bekpone bamɛni bétiku Paulo bésienku Antipatri.

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: Amu ka kadi kégye ni, bekpone bani nkɛ lɛgba básɔ bénwini bésie aban ɔtɔ mmɔ, na báya na bapɔnkɔ beliene bákpanku Paulo bésienku Kaesarea.

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: Ka bétéduo ni, béti Paulo ku ɔku ɔni na béte-ma mmɔ ƒui béte aban ɔgadine ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: Amu uwi ɔni na ɔɔká ɔku ɔmɛni ni, úye Paulo kesii kani na ɔ́si. Ka ɔ́nu ɔ́ti ka Paulo ɔ́si Kilikia ɔ́su ni,

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ndubuduo ƒula litemi lɛmɛni kemmo na linu-ni kaduɛ si uwi ɔni na awɔ ku bekyuli bani ndaku lɛsɛ mmɔ bébo.” Amu na ɔ́sɔ údie lɛdi ɔ́su nwuna bekpone bani nnye ɔnii beti Paulo batákya ɔtɔ ɔni na Ɔga Herode ɔ́tu kemmo na bataagyumana-nwu.

english_verse: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
translation_verse: Emeyi alɔ kama ni, Ɔkpane Unengudi Anania ku Yudaƒuɔ batɔnkune badi ku litemi ɔtɛne ɔni baalɔ banii Tertulo bésie Kaesarea. Bébo Ƒelike kudɔ banii bebedie Paulo bɔƒiɔ ƒui batina.

english_verse: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
translation_verse: Amu ka bákpali Paulo ni, Tertulo úse kalɔ uudie kenye ɔnini, “Bula Ɔbune, uwi pii na ɔdi mɛni ka bɔ́kɛ keyi buɛɛ na ƒula lɛnunda ku lɛlati lɛni na éti atɔnku-bu ɔsu. Na bɔ́nu ka kavumana pii lɛnɔ kébo bula kalɔ kemodi kammɔ ƒui kemmo.

english_verse: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔdi lɛla lɛni náƒɔ abu Yudaƒuɔ ƒui anu.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: Na muuvele-ɔ nnii se atu na enu etemila ani na ndubo bɔsu bɔsiku ɔnana ɔmɛni lɛlɔ.

english_verse: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
translation_verse: “Ɔsika bɔ́nu-nwu bɔ́ti ka lɛsɛ ɔkyane na ɔdi, na ɔkɛ ɔɔví uwi ndi uwi uunwíni Yudaƒuɔ kasusu na kesi kesii na kayawi kamɛni ƒui ɔnii bataabla basa basa na bata benye aban lɛlɔ. Na anwu ndi lɛkpa lɛni na baalɔ banii Nasareƒuɔ ɔtɔnkune.

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su ɔnii ntu Romaƒuɔ ɔda bubo na badubuti batɛku-nwu litemi na ƒula anumi. Anwuɔsu akana na eye-nwu enu si etemila ani na bɔ́su mɛni adi ɔkɔ.”

english_verse: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
translation_verse: Amu na Yudaƒuɔ bammɔ ƒui bása kenye na linyeda lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ banii ala ani ƒui na Tertulo ɔ́su ƒui adi sɔsɔ. Paulo Údie Nwuna Litemi Kenye Na Ƒelike Anumi

english_verse: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
translation_verse: Nsu ka aban ɔgadine ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpali Paulo ɔnii ɔtɛmi ni, Paulo úse kalɔ ɔnini, “Ati, ngyi ka awɔ kani mɔɔtɛ Yudaƒuɔ etemila na akwa pii amɛni kemmo. Na ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔɔda-mi kubiti ka lɛsu na lidie mina lɛlɔ kenye na ƒula anumi.

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: Adubɔnu ati ka ɔbla aani emeyi leevu-anyɔ kani mɛni ka líbo Yerusalem nnii muubo mbakpa na Yudaƒuɔ kakpakɔ.

english_verse: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
translation_verse: Na ɔdi útanu-mi ka mɔɔkyaku ɔdi unyeƒi iye lɛsɛ na Yudaƒuɔ kakpakɔ mmɔ iye na Yudaƒuɔ kasalakɔ kadi lɛnɔ iye ɔgbami kesi kesii na ɔma kemmo.

english_verse: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bamɛni ɔdi ulakana lɛla lɛdi ugyii bɔlɛ geen na bɔnu bɔti ka etemila ani na básu básiku-mi lɛlɔ mɛni ni, sɔsɔ na adi.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Nsu ni, lɛlakpa linwi lɛni na lɛ́tunaku-ma ndi ɔnii nsiaku bɔƒɔtaadi ulu ɔni na baasu banii ɔdi lɛkpa lɛni náta linye-ma lɛlɔ. Na lɛ́ƒɔ Mose ɔda bubo ƒui lɛ́di kpakplaa ku ala ani na bénweni bákya kenye bediene lɛku kemmo.

english_verse: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
translation_verse: Mbo lɛnunsia aani kalɛ na ama lɛnɔ bebo lɛnunsia ka bekyuli babuni ku bekpidi ƒui básɔ badubɔta bɔlɛ kekpine.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́si ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, mɔɔkya ɔkplu ka lɛbla mina kasusu kemmo nwaa na Katɔti ku bayawine ƒui anumi.

english_verse: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: “Akwa pii mɛni ni, liiibo Yerusalem. Na ɔƒɛni lísie nnii muuti bawabane etela lite mina badi na lɛbla akpala lɛnɔ lite Katɔti.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na lɛ́bla lɛlɔ buveli ɔdi ɔmmɔ lɛ́wɔlɔ ni, Yudaƒuɔ badi bábanu-mi na kakpakɔ mmɔ. Na ɔɔɔdi ami ku otogyi ɔdi nkɛ. Na ńtakya unyeƒi ɔdi lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: Na nka Yudaƒuɔ bani nási Asia kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, ama na nka ɔlɛka bebo ƒula anumi. Na si ami ku-ma bubo lɛla lɛdi ni, na basu.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Iye bekyuli bani nlie mɛni ni, ɔlɛka basu lɛla likpidi lɛni na lɛ́bla uwi ɔni na Yudaƒuɔ litemi batɛne benengu bakya baatɛku-mi litemi.

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: Munuu ɔdi uwi ɔni na lɛ́tala lɛdi katɔ lɛ́su nnii, Líbo kasalakɔ mɛni nnii mbedie lɛlɔ kenye lɛsu ka lɛ́ƒɔ lɛ́di ka bekpine basɔ badubɔta ɔsu na bɛɛtɛku-mi litemi?”

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ƒelike ɔni ngyi bɔƒɔtaadi ulu ɔmɛni etemila kaduɛ ni, ɔ́su Yudaƒuɔ bamɛni ɔnini, “Binye bɛgya utédu uwi ɔni na Lisia webo asa na likulo litemi lɛmɛni.”

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: Na ɔ́ya bétiku Paulo bátákya ɔtɔ. Nsu ɔ́su nwuna lɛlɔ banune bammɔ ɔnii bada-nwu buɛɛ, na bete nwuna bakpana kuƒi si badi bebo-nwu kudɔ banii babanu-nwu iye beboku-nwu etela adi. Paulo Ɔ́su Ƒelike Ku Drusila Nwuna Litemi

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Amu na emeyi klukui adi kama ni, Ƒelike ku ulekudi Drusila ɔni ndi Yudani bébo na ɔ́ya-nwu bétédie Paulo béboku, na ɔ́su-ma litemi ɔ́siku Yesu Kristo bɔƒɔtaadi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na ulie uudie ala kalɔ taasiku bɔƒɔtaadi ngba buni bulie ku lɛlɔ bɔti bɔda ku litemi bɔtɛ bɔni ndubo diɛdi lɛlɔ ni, liƒu geen lɛ́da Ƒelike. Na mɛni na Ƒelike ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Ta, na eteesie. Na si lɛkɛ kɔnu kaduɛ ni, ndubɔya na balɔ-ɔ bete-mi.”

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
translation_verse: Na ka ɔ́kali ɔnii Paulo wasu ɔnii ɔɔwia lɛla lɛdi ususu-nwu kenye ɔsu ni, ɔɔtala na baalɔ-nwu uwi ndi uwi na anwu ku-nwu baatɛmiku lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: Amu na akwa anyɔ kama ni, bédie Ƒelike na béti Porkio Ƒesto bébesie-nwu keliekɔ. Nsu ka Ƒelike ɔɔwia ka Yudaƒuɔ bataayɔ-nwu litemi ɔsu ni, ɔ́ya na Paulo ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kya ɔtɔ katɛnkɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amu ka Ƒesto útéduo nwuna kalɛkɛ kani lɛlɔ na ɔdubo bɔdi emeyi atɛ kama ni, ɔ́si Kaesarea úsie Yerusalem.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: Mmɔ na bakpane benengu ku Yudaƒuɔ benengu básu-nwu Paulo lɛlɔ litemi. Na bévele-nwu banii

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
translation_verse: utétiku Paulo uboku Yerusalem. Na bana kasusu ndi ka nka betélie-nwu ulu. Na si ɔ́si ɔɔví ni, na badu-nwu.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: Nsu Ƒesto ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Ɔtɔntɛne na Paulo ɔdi na Kaesarea. Na ami lɛnɔ ndubo mmɔ busie uwi klukui.

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bɛya na bina benengu bebo mmɔ na bebedie nwuna bɔƒiɔ batina.”

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Amu na emeyi maane iye leevu kama ni, Ƒesto únwini úsie Kaesarea. Na limeyi lɛni na útéduo mmɔ kadi kégye ni, ɔ́lɔ Paulo litemi lɛmɛni.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Amu ka Paulo úbeduo litemi katɛkɔ mmɔ ni, Yudaƒuɔ bani nási Yerusalem bébenye bámana na bánwi etemila pii básia-nwu ani kalɔ na bátakana budie.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
translation_verse: Paulo údie nwuna kenye na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ńtaƒiɔ Yudaƒuɔ iye Yudaƒuɔ kakpakɔ iye Ɔga Unengudi Kaesare ɔda bubo bɔdi lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Amu ka Ƒesto ɔɔwia ka Yudaƒuɔ bataayɔ-nwu litemi ɔsu ni, úye Paulo ɔnini, “Aayɔ́ ka esie Yerusalem na ntátɛku-ɔ litemi mmɔ?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Oowo. Béte-mi kuƒi ka kalɔ kamɛni ƒui lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔlatidi ɔtɛku-mi litemi. Awɔ agyi geen ka ńtaƒiɔ.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: Si lɛ́bla lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka badu-mi ni, ndubɔtuna na badu-mi! Nsu si ńtaƒiɔ ni, útalɛka awɔ iye ukyuli bamba uti-mi ute bekyuli bamɛni ɔnii badu-mi. Anwuɔsu lɛ́da mina litemi mɔɔvá Ɔga Unengudi Kaesare anumi!”

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama ni, Ƒesto ku nwuna litemi batɛne bammɔ básu-nwu banini, “Ka éti ƒula litemi átáva Kaesare anumi ɔsu ni, Kaesare kudɔ na adubusie.” Ɔga Agripa Ku Berenike Bénu Paulo Litemi

english_verse: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
translation_verse: Amu na emeyi adi kama ni, Ɔga Agripa ku ɔnwani ulekubi ɔni baalɔ Berenike bébo Ƒesto kudɔ na Kaesarea banii babanu-nwu na begyele-nwu.

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: Bákya mmɔ emeyi pii na Ƒesto úti Paulo litemi ɔ́su ɔga ɔmɛni ɔnini, “Ɔnana ɔdi ɔtɛ ɔtɔ mɛni, na Ƒelike úti nwuna litemi úte-mi.

english_verse: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
translation_verse: Ka lísie Yerusalem ni, bakpane benengu ku bana batɔnkune básu-mi etemila básiku-nwu lɛlɔ, na básu-mi ka nte kuƒi na badu-nwu.

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: “Na lídie kalɔ lɛ́tina-ma uwi klukui kemmo ka Romaƒuɔ ɔda bubo uléte kuƒi ka badu ukyuli kɔtɔ asa na batɛku-nwu litemi. Ɔlɛka bete-nwu kuƒi na anwu ku bekyuli bani nákɛ litemi basa asa na basu-ni.

english_verse: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bébo mɛni na litemi lɛmɛni ɔsu ni, ami lɛnɔ ńtada-ni ńtese. Limeyi lɛmmɔ kadi kégye kani ni, lɛ́ya na bétiku ɔnana ɔmɛni béboku.

english_verse: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
translation_verse: Nsu ni, etemila ani na básu básiku-nwu lɛlɔ ni, ávumanaku ani na lɛ́kali ka anya na badubo bɔsu.

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: Ala ani na básu mɛni akɛnku bana bɔkpa lɛlɔ ku ukyuli ɔni baalɔ Yesu na úkpi lɛlɔ, nsu Paulo ɔmu unye ɔɔsu ka uli ngba!

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: Ɔ́bla-mi basaa na ńtati kalɛ na likulo litemi lɛmɛni. Anwuɔsu líye Paulo si ɔɔwia ka litiku-nwu lisienku Yerusalem na utédie etemila amɛni kenye na Yerusalem mmɔ.

english_verse: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Amu na Ɔga Agripa ɔ́su Ƒesto ɔnini, “Mɔɔwia ka ami ɔlati linu nwuna litemi.” Amu na Ƒesto ɔ́su-nwu ɔnini, “Adubunu litemi lɛmɛni kɔnaadi!” Paulo Unye Agripa Anumi

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: Amu ka kadi kégye ni, Ɔga Agripa ku Berenike bakɛ lɛgadi kemmo bébeduo litemi katɛkɔ mmɔ. Na bekpone benengu ku ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo benengu básiaku-ma kama. Na Ƒesto úte ɔyikun na bédie Paulo béboku.

english_verse: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
translation_verse: Na Ƒesto ɔ́su ɔnini, “Ɔga Agripa ku amii bani nábasa mɛni, ɔnana ɔmɛni ndi ukyuli ɔni na Yudaƒuɔ bani nkya Yerusalem ku Kaesarea mɛni lɛnɔ baawia badu!

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Nsu nka mina kasusu kemmo ni, útabla lɛla lɛni na ɔlɛka badu-nwu. Nsu anwu lɛnɔ ɔnii ɔɔƒɔ́ nwuna litemi ute bula ɔga unengudi. Na ami lɛnɔ ńtebulo.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Nsu ni, bi na ɔlɛka linweni lite ɔga unengudi ɔmɛni? Ɔsika ni, útaƒiɔ geen. Anwuɔsu na líti-nwu líboku-mii ku awɔ Ɔga Agripa geen ka atɛku-nwu litemi na atina-mi litemi lɛni na menweni masiku-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: Ɔsika ni, ɔɔɔdia ka liti ɔtɔntɛne ɔdi lisienku kalɔ kamɛni ƒui lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔni na ńtedie likpidi lɛni na ɔ́bla kalɔ ntatina-nwu.”

english_verse: Agrippa told Paul, “You may now speak for yourself.” Paul stretched out his hand and said:
translation_verse: Amu na Agripa ɔ́su Paulo ɔnini, “Kuƒi kɔtɛ ka ataasu ƒula litemi.” Anwuɔsu Paulo ɔ́gya enu na ɔ́tɛmi údie lɛlɔ ɔnini,

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: “Bula Ɔga Ɔbune Agripa, lili lɛ́dia-mi ka ndubo mina litemi bɔda bɔva ƒula anumi na lɛla lɛni ɔsu na Yudaƒuɔ báda-mi kenye lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
translation_verse: Ɔsika ngyi ka awɔ agyi Yudaƒuɔ ɔda bubo ku bana ɔdi ƒui kaduɛ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, ntɛ na awɔ ɔsu. Kɛ kayi na enu mina litemi.

english_verse: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
translation_verse: Lɛni kani na líti lílie ɔni na si nka budie na badubudie-mi kenye na litemi geen bɔsu kemmo ni, nka bagyi ka ami ndi Ƒarisini ɔni mɔɔdi Yudaƒuɔ ɔda bubo ɔdi lɛlɔ teetulo.

english_verse: Now I am on trial because I believe the promise God made to our people long ago.
translation_verse: Na lɛla lɛni ɔsu geen na béti etemila amɛni baasia-mi lili ndi ɔni na ami nnye mɔɔnu ulu ku lɛnunsia teete kenye kani na Katɔti ɔ́su bula bati kuuku úse ɔsu.

english_verse: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
translation_verse: Israelƒuɔ kaba kani ndi leevu-inyɔ mɛni ƒui baakya ɔkplu usien ku ɔƒɛ ka ama lɛnɔ bakɛ lɛnunsia lɛni na ami mbo mɛni. Bula Ɔga Ɔbune, ɔmɛni ɔsu na Yudaƒuɔ baadá-mi kenye.

english_verse: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
translation_verse: Bi ɔsu na ɔɔyu-mii ɔkplu ka bɛƒɔ bɛdi ka Katɔti ɔɔgyila bekpine?

english_verse: I once thought that I should do everything I could to oppose Jesus from Nazareth.
translation_verse: “Líti lɛ́sia lɛlɔ nnii ntaabla Yesu ɔni ndi Nasareni basiakune kalala.

english_verse: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
translation_verse: Yudaƒuɔ bakpane benengu béte-mi ɔyikun na líƒie bekyuli kedee pii lɛ́kya ɔtɔ na Yerusalem. Na bana akɔ bani na bádu lɛnɔ ni, ɔdi-mi lɛƒɔyɔ.

english_verse: I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
translation_verse: Lɛ́siaku-ma na líkpoku-ma lɛni laa útédu lɛma bamba na ɔgyu kemmo muedi. Na lɛ́ya na baabla-ma kalala na Yudaƒuɔ kɔsakɔ ƒui. Na línye-ma lɛlɔ na beetemi kɔbɔ ala taasiku Yesu lɛlɔ. Paulo Ɔ́su Kalɛ Na Ɔ́bla Na Ɔ́siaku Yesu Kama

english_verse: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
translation_verse: “Kasusu kamɛni udu kani lɛlɔ na líti lísela Damasko na ɔyikun ɔni na bakpane benengu béte-mi kenye.

english_verse: About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me.
translation_verse: Bula Ɔbune, ɔni na nkɛ ulu ɔƒiiwi lísela ni, lɛ́nu ka bukeye bɔni muukeye teetulo ɔƒɛ búkeye bɔ́si katɔ bɔ́mana ami ku bani nkɛ.

english_verse: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
translation_verse: Mmɔ ka bula ƒui búbuli ni, línu lɛdi lɛdi ka lɛɛtɛmi na Hebri lɛdi kemmo taasu lɛnini, ‘Saulo, Saulo, bi ɔsu na eekpóku-mi lɛni? Si aata liyu ni, ƒula lɛlɔ kani na aadú.’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I asked. Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to.
translation_verse: “Amu na líye-nwu nnini, ‘Ati, ɔma na adi?’ “Na lɛdi lɛmmɔ lɛ́su lɛnini, ‘Ami ndi Yesu ɔni na eekpóku kpakplaa.

english_verse: Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
translation_verse: Ɔƒaani ni, ta nye! Ɔsika lídie lɛlɔ lɛ́tina-a kalɛ na meti-ɔ mabla mina kabla ɔblane ku mina kenye udiene. Adubɔsu kayawi ƒui lɛla lɛni na ánu mɛni ku ala ani na ndubo buteedie taatina-a.

english_verse: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
translation_verse: Na kesii kani na mɔɔtala-a ni, ndubɔgyumana-a na ƒula kadi bekyuli akɔ ku kadi bamba lɛnɔ akɔ.

english_verse: I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
translation_verse: Na ndubɔya-a na etébimi-ma anumi na balɛ Satan ɔyikun kemmo na kasuudikɔ mmɔ bebo Katɔti ɔyikun ku bukeye kemmo. Na Katɔti ɔdubuti bana ekpidi ɔkyiɛ-ma na wabla-ma katɔ ala badine aani bani na ɔ́ƒuna úte nwuna lɛlɔ ka báƒɔ-mi bádi ɔsu.’ Paulo Ɔ́su Nwuna Kabla Lɛlɔ Litemi

english_verse: King Agrippa, I obeyed this vision from heaven.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu ni, Ati Agripa, ńtada atu ńtedie budie bɔtina bɔni na lɛ́nu lɛ́siku katɔ mmɔ lɛlɔ!

english_verse: First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
translation_verse: Lɛ́ka litemi buni bɔsu bute Damaskoƒuɔ ku Yerusalemƒuɔ ku Yudaƒuɔ ƒui ku bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ lɛnɔ nnii benwini kama bakya bana ekpidi na beti anumi besienku Katɔti kudɔ, na bataabla ala ani mɔɔtina ka bávumana sɔsɔ.

english_verse: That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu na Yudaƒuɔ bamɛni bébeƒie-mi na Yudaƒuɔ kakpakɔ ɔni na nnye mɔɔsu etemila amɛni. Na báwia ka nka badu-mi.

english_verse: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
translation_verse: Nsu ni, Katɔti údie-mi na bana enu kemmo. Anwuɔsu na mmu nli ngba muudie ɔmɛni kenye taatina amii benengu ku bekyuli ƒui lɛnɔ. Lɛla lɛni na mɔɔsu mɛni ni, ani kani na Katɔti kenye bediene ku Mose bene ƒui básu ka lɛdubɔlɛ.

english_verse: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Na ani ndi ka Mesia ɔni ndi Ukyuli Ɔƒunadi ɔdubo ubebo abi. Na anwu ndubɔbla ukyuli udeedi ɔni maka bɔta bɔlɛ bekpine akɔ, na ɔdubuti bukeye uboku Yudaƒuɔ ku bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ ƒui.”

english_verse: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
translation_verse: Kɔnakunwi ni, Ƒesto ɔ́va ɔ́su ɔnini, “Paulo, eekpi libuo! Ƒula ala bɔtɛya pii búbile-ɔ lili kemmo!”

english_verse: But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense.
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo údie kenye ɔnini, “Ƒesto Ɔbune, neeekpi libuo. Biteti litemi lɛmɛni bitakya bɔƒia. Litemi geen na mɔɔsu.

english_verse: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
translation_verse: Sɔsɔ ni, Ɔga Agripa ɔgyi etemila ani na mɔɔsu mɛni. Anwuɔsu muutemiku-nwu ku kayi ƒaa. Lɛ́ƒɔ lɛ́di kede kede ka bátabla ala amɛni bátabɛ-nwu.

english_verse: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
translation_verse: Ati Agripa, áƒɔ Katɔti kenye bediene bamɛni ádi? Ngyi ka áƒɔ-ma ádi.”

english_verse: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
translation_verse: Amu na Agripa úye Paulo ɔnini, “Aawia ka linwini Kristoni uwi klukui ɔmɛni kemmo?”

english_verse: Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo údie kenye ɔnini, “Uwi klukui iye uwi gyɔlɔɔ ni, mɔɔkpali katɔ nnii ɔmwi ni, amii bani nkya mɛni ƒui binwini aani kalɛ na ami lɛnɔ nse. Nsu ɔɔɔdi aani kalɛ na kɔgba kɔmɛni kɔ́da-mi kalɛ!”

english_verse: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔga ɔmɛni ku aban ɔgadine ku Berenike ku bekyuli bakladi ƒui báta.

english_verse: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
translation_verse: Na ka bávi bálɛ mmɔ ni, bátɛmi básiku Paulo litemi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ básu banini, “Ukyuli ɔmɛni útabla lɛla lɛni na badu-nwu iye bakya-nwu ɔtɔ.”

english_verse: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_verse: Amu na Agripa ɔ́su Ƒesto ɔnini, “Nka bɔkana bɔnyonu-nwu si ɔɔɔdi ka úti litemi lɛmɛni ɔ́siaku Kaesare lɛlɔ ɔsu.”

english_verse: When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na bálɛ ugyii ka ɔdi ka busie Italia ni, béti Paulo ku batɔntɛne bakladi bákya bekpone unengu ɔni baalɔ Yulio enu kemmo. Ɔdi aban bagyumanane lɛkpa linwi lɛni baalɔ Ɔga Unengudi Bekpone Lɛkpa.

english_verse: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
translation_verse: Amu na búti ɔkɔlɔ ɔni nási Adramitio na úsela Asia kalɛkɛ. Na abu ku Makedoniani ɔni baalɔ Aristarko na ɔ́si Tesalonika nlie ɔkɔlɔ ɔmɛni kemmo.

english_verse: The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Amu na nwuna kadi kégye ni, bútédi búnye Sidon Ketudɔ. Amu na Yulio úte Paulo kuƒi ku kaƒɔ ƒaa ɔnii uteesie ɔma kemmo na utánu nwuna bakpana kalɛ na bete-nwu ala ani na weti wesie ulu.

english_verse: When we left Sidon, the winds were blowing against us, and we sailed close to the island of Cyprus to be safe from the wind.
translation_verse: Na ka bɔ́sɔ bɔ́ta mmɔ ni, na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ kenye ɔkplu ɔsu ni, bɔ́sia Kipro kada kakɛ kesii kani na bɔ́bɛ ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia.
translation_verse: Amu ka bɔ́via mmɔ ni, bútásia Kilikia ku Pamƒilia Ketudɔ, na bútédi búnye ɔma ɔni baalɔ Mira na Likia kalɛkɛ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
translation_verse: Mɛni na ɔgyumanane ɔni ntɔnku-bu ɔ́nu ɔkɔlɔ ɔdi ɔni nási Aleksandria na úsela Italia kalɔ lɛlɔ. Na úti bula ƒui ɔ́kya ɔkɔlɔ ɔmɛni kemmo.

english_verse: We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind.
translation_verse: Na emeyi pii kemmo ni, ulu busie bɔmmɔ bɔ́yu-bu ɔkplu asa na bɔ́kana Knido ɔma kudɔ budu. Na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa ɔni muukpó mmɔ ɔsu ni, bútakana na bɔvi ligeen. Anwuɔsu ka búdu Salmone ni, búdeyi bútávi Kreta kɔmadɔ kesii kani na kalɔ kammɔ kétile ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ kenye ɔkplu.

english_verse: We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
translation_verse: Na ɔkplu kemmo na bɔkɛ utubili kudɔ kudɔ búbedu kesii kani baalɔ Ɔkɔlɔ Kenyekɔ ɔni na útagyunku ɔma ɔni baalɔ Lasea.

english_verse: By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past.
translation_verse: Amu ka bɔ́ɔdi emeyi pii na bula ulu busie bɔmɛni kemmo ɔsu ni, Kɔka Bulie Uwi ɔ́vi. Na ntu lɛlɔ bɔvi na uwi ɔmɛni kemmo ɔdubo ɔkplu bɔyu. Ɔmɛni ɔsu na Paulo ɔ́lɛ-ma ɔnini,

english_verse: Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.”
translation_verse: “Ati bene, lɛ́nu lɛ́ti ka bula ulu busie ɔ́si ɔƒɛni bɔdubo ɔkplu bɔyu, ɔsika ɔkɔlɔ ɔmɛni ɔdubuduo ɔgbankpi kemmo, na ala pii ku bekyuli lɛnɔ badubo bɔyii.”

english_verse: But Julius listened to the captain of the ship and its owner, rather than to Paul.
translation_verse: Nsu bekpone unengu ɔmɛni ɔ́ƒɔ ɔkɔlɔ ɔtɔnkune ku ɔkɔlɔ ɔlati bɔlɛ útulo lɛla lɛni na Paulo ɔ́su.

english_verse: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there. The Storm at Sea
translation_verse: Amu ka kalɛlɛkɔ kammɔ kaaadia bunye gyɔlɔɔ na kɔyɔ uwi ɔni ndubo ɔsu ni, ulu besiene bamɛni ketulodikɔ béte kasusu ka besie betédu Ƒoinike. Mmɔ na badubɔkana bɔkya kɔyɔ uwi. Ɔsika Ƒoinike ɔdi ɔma na Kreta kalɔ lɛlɔ ɔni mbo lɛkɔlɔ kalɛlɛkɔ kani muutile ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kenye na ɔƒɛ kanukɔ. Ɔƒɛƒɛɛ Ukpidi Úkpo Na Ɛpu Lɛlɔ

english_verse: When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo kani na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔbuni ɔdi úse kalɔ uukpó ɔ́si kada kakɛ, na ɔ́bla aani si ulu busie bɔmmɔ bɔdubɔdia. Anwuɔsu báklibi lɛlɔ na bátɔlɔ bátásia Kreta kɔmadɔ.

english_verse: days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing.
translation_verse: Nsu kɔnakunwi ni, ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ukpidi ɔdi úkpo ɔ́si kɔmii kakɛ ɔ́vi Kreta.

english_verse: The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
translation_verse: Na úbo ɔkɔlɔ ɔmɛni ɔ́kɔli. Bawia ka nka basɔ benwini ɔkɔlɔ ɔmɛni anumi besienku ketudɔ, nsu bátákana. Anwuɔsu bányonu-nwu na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ údi-nwu úsela.

english_verse: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
translation_verse: Amu kama kama ni, bútákɛ kabɛkɔ blii kadi na ntuntɛ kalɔ kani baalɔ Klauda kama kakɛ. Na ɔkplu kemmo asa na bɔ́kana ɔkɔlɔ blii ɔni bɔda na unengudi ɔmmɔ kemmo bunyimi bɔda lɛla lɛdi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
translation_verse: Amu ka bébo-nwu báda ni, béti lɛbuli báda ɔkɔlɔ ubendi lɛnɔ, ɔsika baayia ka ɔƒɛƒɛɛ webo-nwu wesienku kɔnwinimi kekpidikɔ na Libia ketudɔ. Anwuɔsu báyula adi ani nƒa ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ katɔ ƒui. Ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ kani nda-nwu mɔɔvínku.

english_verse: The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard.
translation_verse: Kadi kégye ka ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ útada bukpo útaya ɔsu ni, bése kalɔ beedie ɔkɔlɔ ɔmɛni kemmo etila teebo taakya ntu kemmo.

english_verse: Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear.
translation_verse: Na limeyi lɛtɛdi lɛlɔ ni, bébo ɔkɔlɔ lɛlɔ ala pii lɛnɔ bávaakun.

english_verse: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ bonwu ɔmɛni úkpo laa emeyi pii ɔni na básɔ bátanu ɔƒɛ iye ayabi kudii. Na bula akɔ ɔdi ɔsɔ uuubo ngba bɔkɛ lɛnunsia lɛdi!

english_verse: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
translation_verse: Amu ka bésie liluku gyɔlɔɔ na bátakɛ uwi bátadi ni, Paulo ɔ́ta únye-ma anumi na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Banwa, si búnu na nka bínu-mi litemi ni, nka bútata Kreta na ala amɛni ƒui ataalɛku-bu.

english_verse: But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔsu-mii kede kede ka ni, ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ ɔdubɔyii udu bɔdi, nsu bina akɔ ɔdi biala ulekpi!

english_verse: I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel
translation_verse: Ɔsika kamaadi usien ni, Katɔti ɔni mbo-mi na anwu na mɔɔkpá ni, nwuna ɔtu ɔdi úbenye-mi kudɔ.

english_verse: to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, ‘Paulo, sɔ tayia. Ɔlɛka atɛ ƒula litemi na Kaesare anumi! Katɔti lɛƒɔndia ɔsu ni, únu ƒula buvele na ɔ́nu-ɔ kɔnyana ɔnii awɔ ku belusiene bammɔ ƒui ɔdi ulekpi.’

english_verse: Cheer up! I am sure that God will do exactly what he promised.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu banana, bɛkɛ kayi! Mɔɔƒɔ́ Katɔti taadi ka ni, lɛla lɛdi biala lɛdubo bɔsia aani kalɛ na ɔ́su.

english_verse: But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
translation_verse: Nsu ni, ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔdububo-bu utáva ntuntɛ kalɔ kadi lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu békulo abuli ani nda abuala ani bébo báda ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ, na báƒɛnimi ugyii ɔni nda ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ kama na ɔɔtina ɔkɔlɔ kavinkɔ. Na bákɔliku ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ adi katɔ kalɛ na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ubo-ma usienku ɛpu kɔtu.

english_verse: The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship.
translation_verse: Amu ka ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ kabla bablane báwia ka bekeli ɔsu ni, béti ɔkɔlɔ ubliidi ɔmmɔ na bákya lɛkwɛ banii nka batánu ɔkɔlɔ ubendi ɔmmɔ lɛtɔtɔ na bakya abuala ku unu ɔmmɔ adi.

english_verse: The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
translation_verse: Amu ka baayia ka ɔƒɛƒɛɛ webo ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ watáƒiɛmi atakpɛ adi lɛlɔ ɔsu ni, báyula abuala ene ani mbo unu geen adi bákya ntu kalɔ na bébo-nya báda ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ kalɛ na udi unye. Na benye baanu anumi kpakplaa ka kadi keyile bugye.

english_verse: But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.”
translation_verse: Nsu ni, Paulo ɔ́su bekpone ku bana ɔtɔnkune ɔnini, “Si bina ƒui bítasɔ bítakya ɔkɔlɔ ɔmɛni kemmo ni, bɛdubukpi.”

english_verse: The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bekpone bamɛni békulo ɔkɔlɔ ubliidi ɔmɛni kɔbuli kɔni nda-nwu, na bányonu-nwu bákya ntu bɔmɛni kemmo.

english_verse: I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu buvele nda-mii, bɛdi lɛla lɛdi na bɛkɛ ɔyikun kalɛ na bilekpi. Ɔsika alɔlɔ muedi ulelie ɔdi lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some.
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo úti bodobodo ɔdi, na ka ɔ́gya Katɔti enu na bana ƒui anumi mmɔ ni, ɔ́ƒɛ ɔdi na úti ɔ́di.

english_verse: They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something.
translation_verse: Kɔnakunwi ni, ɔdi biala ɔ́kɛ kayi na bana ƒui bése kalɔ baadi.

english_verse: and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter. The Shipwreck
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na bádi báwɔlɔ ni, bekyuli bammɔ básɔ bédie etila akladi ƒui na ɔkɔlɔ ɔmɛni kemmo béwi ntu kemmo, na ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ ɔ́bla ƒaaƒaa. Ɔkɔlɔ Ɔmmɔ Ɔ́bwɛ

english_verse: Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
translation_verse: Uwi ɔni na kadi kégye nwaa ni, bátanu ɛpu kɔtu mɛni bétese likpo. Nsu bánu kalɛlɛkɔ kadi na ɛpu kɔtu mɛni kesii kani na nka kadia kalɛ na basia mmɔ balɛ. Anwuɔsu báwia ka nka si ɔdia muedi ni, na beti ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ anumi batákya mmɔ.

english_verse: But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
translation_verse: Amu ka bésela lɛtɔtɔ ni, ɔkɔlɔ ɔmmɔ útányi kɔnwinimi kemmo ɔni na ɔsɔ ulakana lɛtɔtɔ busie. Na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ lɛnɔ úbo kama kakɛ úgyingya ƒui kede kede.

english_verse: The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping.
translation_verse: Ka bekpone bamɛni bákali bani batɔntɛne bammɔ badubo bukeli ɔsu ni, bábla kasusu ka bebo-ma badu.

english_verse: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
translation_verse: Nsu ka bana ɔtɔnkune ɔmɛni ɔɔwia ka ɔƒɔ Paulo ngba ɔsu ni, útatunaku-ma. Anwuɔsu údie ɔ́su ɔnii si bani makana ni, baba lɛgyu beduo ntu kemmo na bakpi beteesie ketudɔ.

english_verse: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
translation_verse: Na bakladi bani mebu ƒui lɛnɔ ni, beti kugyiikɛ ku ala abambadi ani meti-ma masia ntu anumi metédu ketudɔ. Ɔmɛni ɔsu bétéduo ketudɔ mmɔ, na ɔdi biala útekpi.

english_verse: When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
translation_verse: Na ka bɔ́lɛ ɔgbankpi ɔmmɔ kemmo ni, búbati ka mmɔ ndi ntuntɛ kalɔ kani na baalɔ Malta.

english_verse: The local people were very friendly, and they welcomed us by building a fire, because it was rainy and cold.
translation_verse: Amu na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ bekyuli báƒɔ-bu kaduɛ. Ka ɔnantu ku kɔyɔ uwi na ɔdi ɔsu ni, básala-bu ogya bonwu ɔdi na ketudɔ mmɔ na béte-bu eduo.

english_verse: After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand.
translation_verse: Amu ka Paulo ɔnii uudie ekyweni adi ɔkya ogya ɔmɛni kemmo ni, kɔlakpi kɔdi kɔ́vi kɔ́lɛ ekyweni amɛni akɔ ɔ́si ogya liwulu lɛmmɔ ɔsu, na kúbaka kɔ́mana Paulo kɔnu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
translation_verse: Amu ka kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ bekyuli bánu ka kɔlakpi kɔmɛni kɔ́ƒa-nwu kɔnu lɛlɔ ni, básu lɛlɔ banini, “Bekyuli ɔdune na ukyuli ɔmɛni ɔdi. Anwuɔsu baƒiɔ baláya-nwu wakɛ ngba ina ka úkeli ɛpu kemmo kukpi.”

english_verse: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
translation_verse: Nsu Paulo úƒwimi kɔlakpi kɔmɛni ɔ́kya ogya ɔmɛni kemmo, na kútabla-nwu lɛla lɛdi.

english_verse: The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
translation_verse: Amu na bekyuli bamɛni benye baanu, na bákali ka ɔdubuƒu iye ɔlɛ ubo ukpi kɔnakunwi. Amu ka bénye bánu laa na ɔmɛni ɔdi útebo lɛni ni, bábavumana bana bɔkali na nwuna lɛlɔ na básu banii baƒiɔ badi.

english_verse: The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days.
translation_verse: Amu na kesii kani na búbenye mɛni ni, ude kalɔ kammɔ Ɔga Publio kesii. Na ɔga ɔmɛni lɛnɔ ɔ́ƒɔ-bu ku kubiti, na ɔ́nu-bu lɛlɔ emeyi atɛ ƒui.

english_verse: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
translation_verse: Amu uwi ɔmɛni kemmo kani ni, Publio ɔti uuƒi. Na nwuna lɛlɔ lɛ́ƒɔ ogya, na ɔɔnyi kaƒɔ lɛnɔ. Na ka Paulo útéduo-nwu kudɔ na ɔ́kpali katɔ na úti enu ɔ́sia-nwu lɛlɔ ni, ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ ɔ́ba-nwu.

english_verse: After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed.
translation_verse: Ka bénu ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ bɔbwi ni, balɛne bani nkya kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui bálɛ bébo, na Paulo ɔ́bwi-ma.

english_verse: The people were very respectful to us, and when we sailed, they gave us everything we needed. From Malta to Rome
translation_verse: Na ablala amɛni ɔsu ni, bébete-bu etela pii. Na ɔni na uwi údu ka bɔtɔlɔ mmɔ ni, béti etela ani ƒui bɔdubuti bɔda ulu béboku-bu. Básia Malta Bésie Roma

english_verse: Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.”
translation_verse: Bɔ́kya mmɔ abuli atɛ asa na bɔ́tɔlɔ. Na bula bɔtɔlɔ kemmo ni, búlie ɔkɔlɔ ɔni baalɔ banii Nta Baƒiɔ ɔni nási Aleksandria úbenye kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ na kɔyɔ uwi ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
translation_verse: Ka bɔ́ta mmɔ ni, ɔma udeedi ɔni búdi búnye ndi Sirakusa. Na búlie mmɔ lɛnɔ emeyi atɛ.

english_verse: From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli.
translation_verse: Ka bɔ́si mmɔ ni, bɔ́tu búnwini bútédu Regio. Na nwuna kadi kégye ni, ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔbuni ɔdi úkpo ɔ́si bula kama ɔni nébunku-bu, na útiku-bu na búbeduo Puteoli limeyi linyɔdi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
translation_verse: Na mmɔ na bútánu baƒɔtaadine badi, na bévele-bu banii bulie-ma kudɔ emeyi maatɛ. Na ɔmɛni kama ka bɔ́ta mmɔ ni, bútéduo Roma.

english_verse: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
translation_verse: Na ka banwa bani nkya Roma lɛnɔ bénu ka bɔ́si bɔdubo ɔsu ni, badi bási ɔgyu bábasiaku-bu na Apia Kuye. Na badi lɛnɔ bábasiaku-bu na likpo lɛni baalɔ Kuduokɔ Ɛtɛ. Ka Paulo ɔ́nu-ma ni, ɔ́gya Katɔti enu, na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́kɛ kayi úbu. Bédu Roma

english_verse: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
translation_verse: Amu na uwi ɔni na bútéduo Roma ni, béte Paulo kuƒi banii utélie kesii kani na ɔɔyɔ́. Na báya na bekpone bamɛni kemmo unwi útaagyumana-nwu.

english_verse: Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said: My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.
translation_verse: Amu na emeyi atɛ kama ni, Paulo ɔ́lɔ Yudaƒuɔ batɔnkune bani nkya mmɔ ƒui ɔ́sala. Ka bása ni, ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Banwa, Yudaƒuɔ bani nkya Yerusalem néƒie-mi na béti-mi béte Romaƒuɔ aban banii ɔtɛku-mi litemi ina ka ńtaƒiɔ ukyuli ɔdi iye bula bati kuuku ɔdi ala bɔbla bɔdi.

english_verse: They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death.
translation_verse: Romaƒuɔ bamɛni bátɛku-mi litemi na báwia ka nka banyonu-mi. Ɔsika ni, bátanu lɛla lɛni lɛlɔ benye badu-mi kɔtɔ aani kalɛ na Yudaƒuɔ batɔnkune bani néƒie-mi báwia.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders disagreed, so I asked to be tried by the Emperor. But I don't have anything to say against my own nation.
translation_verse: Na uwi ɔni na Yudaƒuɔ bamɛni bénye bétile lɛla lɛmɛni ni, ɔ́ya na lɛ́su-ma nnii betiku-mi na lisie ntánu Ɔga Unengudi Kaesare ɔlati. Ɔsika mɔɔwia ka unu-mi lɛla lɛni mɔɔsu kalɔ, na ɔɔɔdi bɔyɔ na lɛ́yɔ ka lɛda mina kadi bekyuli kenye.

english_verse: I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu na lɛ́lɔ-mii. Ɔsika Ukyuli Ɔƒunadi ɔni lɛlɔ na Israelƒuɔ basia anu ni, nwuna lɛlɔ na mbo bɔƒɔtaadi ɔsu na kɔgba kɔmɛni kɔda-mi lɛni.”

english_verse: The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you.
translation_verse: Amu na básu-nwu banini, “Abu ni, bútenu tɔ lɛla lɛdi bútasiku-ɔ lɛlɔ. Na bútaƒɔ ɔku iye linyesia likpidi lɛdi na ƒula lɛlɔ bútasiku banwa bani nási Yudea bebo mɛni ɔdi kudɔ.

english_verse: But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
translation_verse: Nsu bɔɔwia ka bunu lɛla lɛdi bɔsiku lɛla lɛni na áƒɔ ádi mɛni lɛlɔ. Ɔsika sɔsɔ ni, balásu lɛla lɛbuni lɛdi taasiku lɛkpa lɛmɛni lɛlɔ na kesi kesii.”

english_verse: They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
translation_verse: Amu na bése limeyi lɛdi bese, na bekyuli pii bébo-nwu kudɔ. Mmɔ na ɔ́tɛmi úte-ma ɔ́siku Katɔti lɛga kadikɔ lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́lɔ-ma kasusu úsienku kesii kani na Mose ku Katɔti kenye bediene bénweni ala bése básiku Yesu lɛlɔ. Na ɔ́tɛmiku-ma ɔ́si ɔtanta útédu useyi uwi.

english_verse: Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not.
translation_verse: Na bana akɔ bekyuli badi báƒɔ-nwu bádi, nsu badi lɛnɔ bátaƒɔ-nwu bátadi.

english_verse: Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Amu na etemila amɛni ébenwini unyeƒi na bana akɔ. Na bégyingya uwi ɔni na Paulo ɔ́su-ma litemi likplodi lɛmɛni ɔnini, “Ɔdi litemi geen ka Katɔti Kɔyu kɔ́sia Yesaia lɛlɔ na ɔ́su bula bati kuuku ɔnini,

english_verse: to tell our ancestors, ‘Go to these people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.
translation_verse: “ ‘Sie tásu Yudaƒuɔ anii, “Bɛdubunu na bilénu kalɔ, na bɛdubɔnu na bilanu biláti.”

english_verse: All of you have stubborn hearts. Your ears are stopped up, and your eyes are covered. You cannot see or hear or understand. If you could, you would turn to me, and I would heal you.’ ”
translation_verse: Ɔsika bekyuli bamɛni kɔyi kútili, na bebo atu ɔkplu na bébile bana anumi lɛnɔ. Si ɔɔɔdi lɛni ni, nka bana anumi adubɔnu, na bana atu lɛnɔ adubunu, na bana kɔyi lɛnɔ kɔdubɔbla nwaa na benwini bebo-mi kudɔ na lɛbwi-ma.’ ”

english_verse: Paul said, “You may be sure that God wants to save the Gentiles! And they will listen.”
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo ɔ́wɔlɔ-ma bɔtɛmiku ɔnini, “Ɔlɛka lɛsu-mii na bɛti ka ni, bekyuli bɔƒɔ litemi lɛmɛni ni, béeti-ni béselaku bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ. Na ama ni, badubɔƒɔ-ni!”

english_verse: For two years Paul stayed in a rented house and welcomed everyone who came to see him.
translation_verse: Amu na Paulo ɔ́kya mmɔ akwa anyɔ na kaduli kani na úvo kemmo, na útaaƒɔ bekyuli bani ƒui muubo-nwu kudɔ.

english_verse: He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
translation_verse: Ɔ́kɔ Katɔti lɛga kadikɔ lɛsa ku kayi buse úte-ma, na ɔ́tina-ma ala ani nkɛnku Yesu Kristo lɛlɔ. Na ukyuli ukyuli útetile-nwu kuƒi.

english_verse: From Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus. God chose me to be an apostle, and he appointed me to preach the good news
translation_verse: Ami Paulo, ɔni ndi Yesu Kristo kabla ɔblane na ndi ɔtalane ɔni na Katɔti ɔ́ƒuna ka lɛkɔ-nwu litemi buni lɛsa ni, ami muunweni ɔku ɔmɛni.

english_verse: that he promised long ago by what his prophets said in the holy Scriptures.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti litemi buni lɛni na ɔ́su nwuna kenye bediene úse ka ɔdubudie keyi ni, bénweni-ni bákya Bunweni Kedee Ɔku kemmo.

english_verse: This good news is about his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ! As a human, he was from the family of David. But the Holy Spirit proved that Jesus is the powerful Son of God, because he was raised from death.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛnku Katɔti Kɔyu lɛlɔ ni, Katɔti údie-nwu ɔ́tina bekyuli ku ɔyikun bonwu ka ɔdi ubidi ɔni na ɔ́gyila ɔ́lɛku bekpine akɔ.

english_verse: Jesus was kind to me and chose me to be an apostle, so that people of all nations would obey and have faith.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɛnku Kristo lɛlɔ ni, Katɔti ɔ́nu-bu kɔnyana na úti-bu ɔ́bla batalane úte Kristo kalɛ na bɔya na kadi ƒui bekyuli baƒɔ badi na babla nwuna lɛyɔla.

english_verse: You are some of those people chosen by Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: Na amii lɛnɔ ni, Katɔti ɔ́lɔ-mii ɔnii bibebunku Yesu Kristo badi bammɔ.

english_verse: This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people. I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! A Prayer of Thanks
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu na muunweni ɔku ɔmɛni lite amii bani ƒui nkya Roma na Katɔti ɔɔyɔ́-mii, na ɔ́lɔ-mii ka bɛbla nwuna badi. Katɔti ku Blɔti Yesu Kristo lɛƒɔndia ku keyi buɛɛ kasiaku-mii. Paulo Ɔ́yɔ Ka Ubo Ubanu-ma

english_verse: First, I thank God in the name of Jesus Christ for all of you. I do this because people everywhere in the world are talking about your faith.
translation_verse: Kudeedi ni, nkɛnku Yesu Kristo lɛlɔ mɔɔgyá mina Katɔti enu na bina ƒui lili, ɔsika kayawi bekyuli ƒui beenú kalɛ na bɛ́ƒɔ Kristo bɛ́di.

english_verse: God has seen how I never stop praying for you, while I serve him with all my heart and tell the good news about his Son.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔni kabla na mɔɔbla ku mina kayi ƒui na litemi buni lɛni lɛsa mɔɔkɔ́ ɔkɛnku ubidi lɛlɔ ni, ani ndubudie-mi kenye ɔ́si kalɛ na naaayiƒala-mii uwi biala kemmo si mɔɔkpali katɔ.

english_verse: In all my prayers, I ask God to make it possible for me to visit you.
translation_verse: Na uwi biala na mɔɔkpali Katɔti ni, muuvele Katɔti nnii si ɔdi-nwu lɛƒɔyɔ ni, na lɛkɛ kuƒi na libo mbanu-mii uwi ɔmɛni kemmo.

english_verse: I want to see you and share with you the same blessings that God's Spirit has given me. Then you will grow stronger in your faith.
translation_verse: Anumi égyie-mi geen ka libo mbanu-mii na libunku-mii na kɔyu kemmo ɔkɛnku Katɔti kɔnyana bɔnu ɔsu na bɛkɛ ɔkplu.

english_verse: What I am saying is that we can encourage each other by the faith that is ours.
translation_verse: Lɛla lɛni mɔɔsu mɛni ndi ka bɔdubɔkya lɛlɔ ogya na uwi ɔmɛni kemmo. Ɔsika bina bɔƒɔtaadi bɔdubo-mi ogya bɔkya, na ami bɔdi lɛnɔ bɔkya-mii ogya.

english_verse: My friends, I want you to know that I have often planned to come for a visit. But something has always kept me from doing it. I want to win followers to Christ in Rome, as I have done in many other places.
translation_verse: Banwa, bɛti ka lɛ́bla kasusu uwi pii kemmo ka libo-mii kudɔ nka, nsu lɛla lɛdi lítile-mi kuƒi. Mɔɔyɔ́ ka lɛya na bekyuli baƒɔ Kristo badi na bina akɔ aani kalɛ na lɛ́bla na bekyuli bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ akɔ.

english_verse: It doesn't matter if people are civilized and educated, or if they are uncivilized and uneducated. I must tell the good news to everyone. That's why I am eager to visit all of you in Rome. The Power of the Good News
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu na anumi égyie-mi geen ka lɛsu amii bani nkya Roma lɛnɔ litemi buni lɛmɛni. Ɔyikun Ɔni Na Litemi Buni Lɛmɛni Libo

english_verse: I am proud of the good news! It is God's powerful way of saving all people who have faith, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Litemi buni lɛmmɔ lilekpo-mi kɔƒa, ɔsika lɛdi Katɔti ɔyikun ɔni mɔɔyá na ukyuli biala ɔni mɔɔƒɔ́ taadi ɔɔkɛ́ ngba bɔƒɔ. Na Yudaƒuɔ ndi bedeedi bani ndubunu asa na bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ basia.

english_verse: The good news tells how God accepts everyone who has faith, but only those who have faith. It is just as the Scriptures say, “The people God accepts because of their faith will live.” Everyone Is Guilty
translation_verse: Na litemi buni lɛmɛni muudie ulu siin ɔni mɔɔyɔ́ Katɔti kaƒɔ taatina. Na ulu siin ɔmɛni ɔkɛnku bɔƒɔtaadi lɛlɔ ɔ́si kalɔ kesekɔ útédu kawɔlɔkɔ. Na lɛni na bénweni na Bunweni Kedee Ɔku kemmo banini, “Bani mɔɔsiaku-mi kama siin ni, badubulie ngba na bana bɔƒɔtaadi kemmo.” Katɔti Ɔɔkɛ́ Kɔnyi Na Likpidi Udu Biala Lɛlɔ

english_verse: From heaven God shows how angry he is with all the wicked and evil things that sinful people do to crush the truth.
translation_verse: Katɔti uudie nwuna kɔnyi keyi taasiku katɔ na ala ani mɔɔta teenye-nwu lɛlɔ ku likyulikpi ala bɔbla bɔni muutile bekyuli kuƒi ka bati Katɔti litemi geen lɛmmɔ.

english_verse: They know everything that can be known about God, because God has shown it all to them.
translation_verse: Uuti kɔnyi ɔsika bekyuli baanu Katɔti ala ani na ɔ́bla ƒui nwaa. Na Katɔti ɔlati nédie-nya nwaa ɔ́tina-ma.

english_verse: God's eternal power and character cannot be seen. But from the beginning of creation, God has shown what these are like by all he has made. That's why those people don't have any excuse.
translation_verse: Ɔsika ɔ́si uwi ɔni na Katɔti údie kayawi ni, ala ani ƒui na ɔ́bla ɔ́kya kayawi lɛlɔ muudie Katɔti ɔni na bulánu ku bula anumi ɔyikun ku nwuna udu keyi. Anwuɔsu ukyuli biala ɔsɔ ulakana bɔsu ɔnii útaƒɔ Katɔti útadi.

english_verse: They know about God, but they don't honor him or even thank him. Their thoughts are useless, and their stupid minds are in the dark.
translation_verse: Ɔsika ina ka bekyuli bagyi Katɔti ni, beléte-nwu ɔbu ɔni námanku-nwu aani Katɔti kalɛ. Na balagya-nwu enu lɛnɔ. Mmomu bana kasusu kéƒu na baabla adɔlɔla. Na lɛdisa lɛ́ƒɔ-ma.

english_verse: They claim to be wise, but they are fools.
translation_verse: Na baanu lɛlɔ aani bekyuli bani na báda anu, nsu bénwini badɔlɔdi.

english_verse: They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
translation_verse: Na báda Katɔti ɔni nli ngba uwi ƒui bɔkpa báya, na beemwi ala abambadi ani muukpi mmomu. Bábla ala amɛni aani ukyuli iye baasɛ iye bebuo iye bebuo bani mɔɔkpɛ́ kalɔ aani balakpi udu. Na bése-ma béte lɛlɔ aani baƒiɔ.

english_verse: So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ni, Katɔti ɔ́nyonu-ma, na baabla lɛyalɛ ala ani mɔɔyá na beesé lɛlɔ. Na baabla kɔƒa ala na bana akɔ.

english_verse: They gave up the truth about God for a lie, and they worshiped God's creation instead of God, who will be praised forever. Amen.
translation_verse: Na bávumana Katɔti litemi geen lɛmmɔ ku ɔkɔ bɔnyi. Na baakpá ala ani na Katɔti údie. Nsu ɔlɛka bakpa Katɔti ɔlati ɔni námanku bumwi uwi ƒui. Ɔsia lɛni.

english_verse: God let them follow their own evil desires. Women no longer wanted to have sex in a natural way, and they did things with each other that were not natural.
translation_verse: Ala amɛni bɔbla ɔsu na Katɔti ɔ́nyonu bekyuli, na baabla ala ani mɔɔda bana ɔlɔna ɔkwɛ ani muukpó kɔƒa. Na beleku muedi báda banana bése na baaƒuƒwɛ lɛlɔ na aƒiankpi kemmo.

english_verse: Men behaved in the same way. They stopped wanting to have sex with women and had strong desires for sex with other men. They did shameful things with each other, and what has happened to them is punishment for their foolish deeds.
translation_verse: Na lɛni kani na banana lɛnɔ báda beleku bése na baabla kɔƒa ala, na beesié lɛlɔ kudɔ aani ɔnana ku uleku kalɛ. Na ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, Katɔti ɔ́ni-ma kɔtu kɔni námanku-ma ɔ́si bana udu ukpidi ɔni na bábla ɔsu.

english_verse: Since these people refused even to think about God, he let their useless minds rule over them. That's why they do all sorts of indecent things.
translation_verse: Na ka bése béni banii balatɛya lɛla lɛni na ɔdi ka bati ɔsu ni, Katɔti ɔ́nyonu-ma, na likyulikpi lɛ́ƒɔ-ma kasusu kemmo. Na baabla ala ani na utalɛka babla.

english_verse: They are evil, wicked, and greedy, as well as mean in every possible way. They want what others have, and they murder, argue, cheat, and are hard to get along with. They gossip,
translation_verse: Na likyulikpi ala bɔbla bɔ́ƒɔ-ma lɛlɔ kemmo ƒui. Na anya ndi alaekpidi bɔbla ku ɔdivo ku kalala. Na lɛnungyie na bekyuli bamba ala lɛlɔ ku ukyuli bɔdu ku kekpo ku ɔkɔ bɔnyi ku lɛlɔ bule ati ati bɔ́ƒɔ-ma lɛlɔ kemmo. Na beeti lɛlɔ kasusu kekpidi. Na beekeyi atɛ.

english_verse: say cruel things about others, and hate God. They are proud, conceited, and boastful, always thinking up new ways to do evil. These people don't respect their parents.
translation_verse: Na beetemi enyekpi na bana bakpana lɛlɔ. Badi bekyuli bani muukisi Katɔti. Beedumi lɛlɔ, na baatina lɛlɔ, na baakun lɛmɛnɛ. Na baawia likpidi lilu lɛbambadi pii. Na balábu bana bawɔne.

english_verse: They are stupid, unreliable, and don't have any love or pity for others.
translation_verse: Badi bekyuli bani naaagyi lɛbuni ku likpidi kavumana. Na baládi bana ala ani na básu lɛlɔ. Na lɛla lɛdi lilakywi-ma kaƒɔ. Na balánu ukyuli kɔnyana.

english_verse: They know God has said that anyone who acts this way deserves to die. But they keep on doing evil things, and they even encourage others to do them.
translation_verse: Bagyi ka Katɔti úbo-bu ɔda siin ka bekyuli bani nlie ngba bɔmɛni udu ni, Katɔti ɔdubɔdu-ma kukpi kɔtɔ. Nsu ni, benye momoomo na baabla alaekpidi amɛni. Na ɔɔɔdi ɔmɛni lɛti, mmomu beeti ɔbu teete bekyuli bani lɛnɔ mɔɔbla ala amɛni.

english_verse: Some of you accuse others of doing wrong. But there is no excuse for what you do. When you judge others, you condemn yourselves, because you are guilty of doing the very same things.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ni, si awɔ ɔdi aatɛku ukyuli litemi na aadú-ma kɔtɔ ni, eeebo kenye kadi na eedie. Na ulu biala lɛlɔ na ádu ƒula bakpana kɔtɔ ni, ƒula lɛlɔ na aadú kɔtɔ. Ɔsika ala ani na bábla ni, ana udu kani na awɔ lɛnɔ aabla.

english_verse: We know that God is right to judge everyone who behaves in this way.
translation_verse: Bula ƒui bɔgyi ka Katɔti lɛti pɛ mbo kuƒi kɔni na ɔtɛku bekyuli bani mɔɔbla ala amɛni udu litemi.

english_verse: Do you really think God won't punish you, when you behave exactly like the people you accuse?
translation_verse: Na si awɔ aani ukyuli ɔyawine kani aabla ala amɛni udu na aadú bekyuli bamba kɔtɔ ni, aakali anii adubukeli Katɔti litemi bɔtɛ?

english_verse: You surely don't think much of God's wonderful goodness or of his patience and willingness to put up with you. Don't you know that the reason God is good to you is because he wants you to turn to him?
translation_verse: Munuu bɛɛbu bɛnii keeke na Katɔti ɔɔbla-bu kaƒɔbuni na ɔɔkɛ́ kayi na uuwiku-bu lɛlɔ? Bɛti geen ka ni, Katɔti ɔɔbla-bu lɛƒɔndia lɛmɛni ɔsika ɔɔwia ka ubunku-bu na bunwini kayi.

english_verse: But you are stubborn and refuse to turn to God. So you are making things even worse for yourselves on that day when he will show how angry he is and will judge the world with fairness.
translation_verse: Na ka bina atu ebo ɔkplu na bítenwini kayi ɔsu ni, Katɔti ɔdubo-mii kɔtu bɔni geen na limeyi lɛni na údie úse lɛlɔ ka ɔdubɔtɛku bayawine ƒui litemi na nwuna ulu siin lɛlɔ.

english_verse: God will reward each of us for what we have done.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti ɔdubɔƒɔ ukyuli biala kayu na nwuna kabla kani na ɔ́bla kenye.

english_verse: He will give eternal life to everyone who has patiently done what is good in the hope of receiving glory, honor, and life that lasts forever.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani mɔɔkya lɛbuni bɔbla ɔkplu na basiaku bukeye ku bumwi ku ngba bɔnii nsɔ naaadubo bɔsa kudii kama ni, Katɔti ɔdubɔya na bakɛ ngba ƒui bɔmmɔ.

english_verse: But he will show how angry and furious he can be with every selfish person who rejects the truth and wants to do evil.
translation_verse: Nsu bekyuli bani mɔɔwia ama lɛti lɛkɛ na beení litemi geen lɛmmɔ na basiaku alaekpidi bɔbla kama ni, Katɔti ɔdubo kɔnyi bɔkɛ na bana lɛlɔ na ɔni-ma kɔtu geen.

english_verse: All who are wicked will be punished with trouble and suffering. It doesn't matter if they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani ƒui mɔɔbla ekpidi ni, badubo abi bubo na balákɛ bɔnwuna bɔdi. Yudaƒuɔ ndi bedeedi na kɔtu bɔni bɔmɛni kemmo, na bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ basia.

english_verse: But all who do right will be rewarded with glory, honor, and peace, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Nsu ama bani mɔɔbla ala abuni ni, Katɔti ɔdubute-ma bukeye ku ɔbu ku keyi buɛɛ. Yudaƒuɔ ndi bedeedi bani ndubɔkɛ ala amɛni, na bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ basia.

english_verse: God doesn't have any favorites!
translation_verse: Ɔsika Katɔti ulánu anumi lɛlɔ taatɛ litemi.

english_verse: Those people who don't know about God's Law will still be punished for what they do wrong. And the Law will be used to judge everyone who knows what it says.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani ƒui nábla ekpidi na baaagyi Mose ɔda bubo ni, badubo bukpi bɔyii. Nsu Katɔti ulatɛku-ma litemi na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na bani na bakya Mose ɔda bubo bɔmɛni kalɔ na bábla ekpidi ni, ɔkɛnku ɔda bubo bɔmɛni lɛlɔ na Katɔti ɔdubɔtɛku-ma litemi.

english_verse: This proves that the conscience is like a law written in the human heart. And it will show whether we are forgiven or condemned,
translation_verse: Na ɔɔtina ka Katɔti úti ala ani nkya Mose ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔɔtina ɔ́kya-ma kayi kemmo. Na bana kayi lɛnɔ kaatina-ma geen ka ɔmɛni use lɛni. Na uwi ɔdi ni, bana kasusu kaadú-ma kɔtɔ iye keete-ma ubo.

english_verse: when God appoints Jesus Christ to judge everyone's secret thoughts, just as my message says. The Jews and the Law
translation_verse: Na litemi buni lɛni lɛsa na mɔɔkɔ́ ni, lɛɛtina ka Katɔti ɔdubɔya na Yesu Kristo ɔtɛku bekyuli litemi ɔ́siku ala ani nábɛ akya-ma kasusu kemmo ƒui lɛlɔ. Mose Ɔda Bubo Bɔɔsu Ala Taasiku Yudaƒuɔ Lɛlɔ

english_verse: Some of you call yourselves Jews. You trust in the Law and take pride in God.
translation_verse: Na amii bani mɔɔsu bɛnii bɛdi Yudaƒuɔ ni, bíti lɛlɔ bíkpo Mose ɔda bubo lɛlɔ, na bɛɛkun lɛmɛnɛ ka bibo kɔna ku Katɔti.

english_verse: By reading the Scriptures you learn how God wants you to behave, and you discover what is right.
translation_verse: Bɛɛsu lɛnɔ bɛnii bɛgyi lɛla lɛni mɔɔyɔ́ Katɔti kaƒɔ, na bɛ́tɛya ala abuni ani na ɔdi ka bɛƒuna na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for all who are in the dark.
translation_verse: Na bɛ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ bɛ́di ka bɛdi lɛnumi bite banumbwɛne, na bɛdi bukeye bite bekyuli bani nkya lɛdisa kemmo.

english_verse: And since there is knowledge and truth in God's Law, you think you can instruct fools and teach young people.
translation_verse: Na bɛɛsu ka amii mɔɔlɛ badɔlɔdi, na bɛɛtina banamu bakɔdi ala. Na bɛ́ƒɔ bɛ́di geen ka ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bunye bute lɛlati ku litemi geen ƒui.

english_verse: But how can you teach others when you refuse to learn? You preach it is wrong to steal. But do you steal?
translation_verse: Nsu amii bani mɔɔtina bekyuli bamba ala ni, bɛɛtina bina lɛlɔ ala ammɔ? Bɛɛkɔ́ Katɔti litemi buni lɛsa teete bekyuli bɛnii beteyu, nsu amii alati nɔɔ? Bileyu?

english_verse: You say people should be faithful in marriage. But are you faithful? You hate idols, yet you rob their temples.
translation_verse: Bɛɛsu bekyuli bɛnii batadi kɔsɔnɔ, nsu amii alati nɔɔ? Biladi kɔsɔnɔ? Bɛɛta teenye baƒiɔ lɛlɔ kpakplaa, nsu bileyu bana kakpakɔ kammɔ ala?

english_verse: You take pride in the Law, but you disobey the Law and bring shame to God.
translation_verse: Bɛda Katɔti ɔda bubo bɛɛkun lɛmɛnɛ, nsu bɛɛɛgyi ka kɔƒa kuukpó Katɔti ka biládi ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔsu?

english_verse: It is just as the Scriptures tell us, “You have made foreigners say insulting things about God.”
translation_verse: Na Bunweni Kedee Ɔku kemmo ni, básu banii, “Amii Yudaƒuɔ udunkpi náya na bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ baalɔ Katɔti lɛnyikpi.”

english_verse: Being circumcised is worthwhile, if you obey the Law. But if you don't obey the Law, you are no better off than people who are not circumcised.
translation_verse: Na si bɛɛdi ɔda bubo bɔmɛni lɛlɔ ni, bina lego bukulo bɔdi lɛla lɛni na libo kɔsia. Nsu si biládi ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ni, na lego bukulo ɔdi ɔni na bɛ́bla ɔdi lɛla keeke.

english_verse: In fact, if they obey the Law, they are as good as anyone who is circumcised.
translation_verse: Na si ukyuli ɔni naaadi Yudani na útekulo lego ɔɔdi ɔda bubo bɔmɛni lɛlɔ ni, Katɔti ɔɔnu-nwu aani ukyuli ɔni nékulo lego.

english_verse: So everyone who obeys the Law, but has never been circumcised, will condemn you. Even though you are circumcised and have the Law, you still don't obey its teachings.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔdi ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ nsu útekulo lego ni, ɔdubɔdu-mii kɔtɔ ina ka amii na béte ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ na bíkulo ago lɛnɔ nsu biládi-mu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Just because you live like a Jew and are circumcised doesn't make you a real Jew.
translation_verse: Ɔɔɔdi ɔlɔna lɛlɔ na bɔɔnu Yudani geen taati. Na lego bukulo geen bɔmmɔ ni, buuunye buuute ɔlɔna lɛlɔ kabla kani na bekyuli baanu taati na ukyuli lɛlɔ kani.

english_verse: To be a real Jew you must obey the Law. True circumcision is something that happens deep in your heart, not something done to your body. And besides, you should want praise from God and not from humans.
translation_verse: Mmomu ukyuli ɔni ndi Yudani geen ndi ukyuli ɔni mɔɔtina na nwuna ablala kemmo ka úti nwuna kayi úte Katɔti. Na ɔɔɔkɛnku ɔlɔna ɔni na békulo na ɔda bubo ɔdi kenye lɛlɔ. Mmomu ɔkɛnku Katɔti Kɔyu lɛlɔ. Na ɔɔɔdi ukyuli ɔyawine mɔɔkɔliku ukyuli ɔmmɔ lɛnyi katɔ, mmomu Katɔti.

english_verse: What good is it to be a Jew? What good is it to be circumcised?
translation_verse: Na si use lɛni ni, kɔsia kɔmani na Yudani ɔni na békulo lego ubo utulo bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ?

english_verse: It is good in a lot of ways! First of all, God's messages were spoken to the Jews.
translation_verse: Na lilu pii lɛlɔ ni, ɔdanku ala abuni. Kudeedi ni, Yudaƒuɔ enu kemmo na Katɔti úti nwuna Bunweni Kedee ɔ́kya.

english_verse: It is true that some of them did not believe the message. But does this mean that God cannot be trusted, just because they did not have faith?
translation_verse: Nsu si úbo úte ka badi bátaƒɔ bátadi nɔɔ? Aaƒɔ́ taadi ka Katɔti uladi nwuna etemila lɛlɔ?

english_verse: No, indeed! God tells the truth, even if everyone else is a liar. The Scriptures say about God, “Your words will be proven true, and in court you will win your case.”
translation_verse: Kudii! Ina ukyuli biala ɔdi ɔkɔ ɔnyine muedi ni, bɛya bɔti ka Katɔti ɔɔdi nwuna litemi lɛlɔ. Lɛni na bénweni na Bunweni Kedee Ɔku kemmo banini, “Lɛla biala lɛɛtina ka ƒula kenye etemila adi litemi geen. Na aatɛku bekyuli ƒui litemi ulu siin lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: If our evil deeds show how right God is, then what can we say? Is it wrong for God to become angry and punish us? What a foolish thing to ask.
translation_verse: Bɔsu na bɔdubɔsu bɔnii bula ekpidi ani na bɔɔbla mɔɔyá na bekyuli baanu Katɔti lɛbuni lɛni na ɔɔbla taati? Na ɔmmɔ ɔsu ni, bɔdubɔsu bɔnii Katɔti ulábla kaduɛ si ɔɔní-bu kɔtu? Kudii! Nsu lɛni na badi baakali!

english_verse: But the answer is, “No.” Otherwise, how could God judge the world?
translation_verse: Na si buse na use aani kalɛ na baakali ni, bi lɛlɔ na Katɔti ɔdubunye ɔtɛku bayawine ƒui litemi?

english_verse: Since your lies bring great honor to God by showing how truthful he is, you may ask why God still says you are a sinner.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔdi ɔkana na uye ɔnini, “Nsu si mina ala ani na naaabla ulu lɛlɔ mɔɔyá na Katɔti litemi geen lɛmmɔ liigyingya na beemwi-nwu ni, bi ɔsu na bɛɛdú-mi kɔtɔ ka ukyuli ukpidi na ndi?”

english_verse: You might as well say, “Let's do something evil, so that something good will come of it!” Some people even claim that we are saying this. But God is fair and will judge them as well. No One Is Good
translation_verse: Si búti-nwu lɛni ni, bɔkana bɔsu bɔnii, “Bɛya na butaabla likpidi kalɛ na lɛla lɛbuni lɛlɛ lɛsiku-nwu kemmo.” Bekyuli bani meti-nwu lɛni ni, bámanku ka Katɔti ɔdu-ma kɔtɔ. Nsu lɛni na bekyuli badi beedumi-bu, na baasu taatina ka abu násu lɛni. Bekyuli Ƒui Bábla Likpidi

english_verse: What does all this mean? Does it mean that we Jews are better off than the Gentiles? No, it doesn't! Jews, as well as Gentiles, are ruled by sin, just as I have said.
translation_verse: Na ɔƒɛni ni, bi na bɔkana bɔsu na abu Yudaƒuɔ lɛlɔ? Bubo kenyekɔ kabuni butulo bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ? Kudii! Ɔsika lɛ́ɛtina ḿbavi ka likpidi lɛ́ƒɔ Yudaƒuɔ ku bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ ƒui lɛnɔ lɛlɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Not one of them understands or even searches for God.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔdi biala uuubo ɔni mɔɔnu lɛbuni taati. Na ɔdi lɛnɔ uláwia Katɔti kama ulu.

english_verse: They have all turned away and are worthless. There isn't one person who does right.
translation_verse: Bekyuli ƒui bénwini kama bákya Katɔti, na bana ƒui báƒiɔ. Na ukyuli ɔdi uuubo ɔni mɔɔbla lɛbuni. Ina unwi pɛ muedi!

english_verse: Their words are like an open pit, and their tongues are good only for telling lies. Each word is as deadly as the fangs of a snake,
translation_verse: Bana inye buse aani kɔƒiɔtɔ kɔni nálɛmi kuwi. Na bana linyemi lɛɛta na ɔkɔ bɔnyi lɛlɔ. Na bana inye bɔɔdú bekyuli aani kɔlakpi bɔdu kalɛ.

english_verse: and they say nothing but bitter curses.
translation_verse: Na ewida ku ɔdu úyi-ma kenye kemmo tɛ.

english_verse: These people quickly become violent.
translation_verse: Lɛgba lɛɛta-ma pla pla na bekyuli bɔdu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Wherever they go, they leave ruin and destruction.
translation_verse: Bana ngba búbie na beebó abi geen.

english_verse: They don't know how to live in peace.
translation_verse: Na baaagyi lɛla lɛdi na keyi buɛɛ ngba bulie lɛlɔ.

english_verse: They don't even fear God.”
translation_verse: Na bana ɔbladu ulátina ka baayia Katɔti.”

english_verse: We know that everything in the Law was written for those who are under its power. The Law says these things to stop anyone from making excuses and to let God show that the whole world is guilty.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni ni, bɔgyi ka ala ani ƒui básu na Mose ɔda bubo ɔku kemmo adanku bekyuli bani nkya ɔda bubo bɔmɛni kalɔ. Na ɔyawine ɔdi ulakana kenye kadi budie na Katɔti litemi bɔtɛ kemmo. Ɔsika Katɔti ɔdubɔtɛku kayawi ƒui litemi.

english_verse: God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin. God's Way of Accepting People
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu ni, ɔɔɔdi ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ kama bɔsiaku mɔɔyá na ukyuli ɔbla siin na Katɔti anumi. Mmomu ni, ɔda bubo bɔmɛni bɔɔyá na bekyuli baatí ka baabla likpidi. Katɔti Ku Bayawine Baabla Unwi Na Kristo Bɔƒɔtaadi Kemmo

english_verse: Now we see how God does make us acceptable to him. The Law and the Prophets tell how we become acceptable, and it isn't by obeying the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Nsu ulu ɔni lɛlɔ na Katɔti údie ɔ́tina ka bekyuli baasia taabla siin ni, ɔɔɔkɛnku ɔda bubo lɛlɔ. Na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ ku kenye bediene bédie ɔmɛni bátina nwaa.

english_verse: God treats everyone alike. He accepts people only because they have faith in Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔɔyá na bekyuli baabla siin si báƒɔ Yesu Kristo bádi. Ɔɔbla ɔmɛni teete bekyuli bani ƒui náƒɔ Kristo bádi. Na ulákya kavumana kadi na bekyuli bammɔ ntɛ.

english_verse: All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory.
translation_verse: Bekyuli ƒui bábla likpidi, na bátamanku ka bakɛ Katɔti lɛgadi bukeye.

english_verse: But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins.
translation_verse: Nsu ni, Katɔti ɔkɛnku Kristo Yesu ɔni náƒɔ bula lili kayu lɛlɔ ɔ́ya na bɔɔbla siin na nwuna lɛƒɔndia ɔsu.

english_verse: What is left for us to brag about? Not a thing! Is it because we obeyed some law? No! It is because of faith.
translation_verse: Na bi lɛlɔ na bɔdubɔkana lɛmɛnɛ bɔkun ka ani na bɔ́bla asa na bɔ́kɛ bɔƒɔ? Ku lɛla! Ɔsika ukyuli ulábla siin ka ɔɔdi ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔsu. Mmomu ɔkɛnku bɔƒɔtaadi lɛlɔ kani na Katɔti ɔɔklibi abu ku-nwu ntɛ.

english_verse: We see that people are acceptable to God because they have faith, and not because they obey the Law.
translation_verse: Ɔsika bɔgyi nwaa ka ni, ɔkɛnku bɔƒɔtaadi lɛlɔ kani na ukyuli ɔɔbla siin na Katɔti anumi, na ɔɔɔdi nwuna ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ lɛlɔ bɔdi ɔsu.

english_verse: Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is!
translation_verse: Munuu ni, Yudaƒuɔ lɛti pɛ ɔdi na Katɔti ɔdi? Na ɔɔɔdi bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ ama ɔdi? Ɛɛn, ɔdi ama lɛnɔ ɔdi.

english_verse: There is only one God, and he accepts Gentiles as well as Jews, simply because of their faith.
translation_verse: Ɔsika Katɔti unwi pɛ kani nkya na anwu ndubɔbla na Yudaƒuɔ baabla siin ɔkɛnku bɔƒɔtaadi lɛlɔ. Lɛni kani na ɔdubɔbla bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ lɛnɔ na babla siin ɔkɛnku bɔƒɔtaadi bɔmmɔ kani lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu bi na ɔmɛni ɔɔtina? Ɔɔtina ka bɔ́da ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ buse ka bɔƒɔtaadi bɔ́ƒɔ-mu kenye ɔsu? Kudii! Mmomu lɛla lɛni na ɔda bubo bɔmmɔ bɔdanku geen na bɔɔkɔliku katɔ.

english_verse: Well then, what can we say about our ancestor Abraham?
translation_verse: Bi ndi lɛla lɛni na bɔdubɔsu ka bula ɔti kuuku Abraham ɔ́nu ɔ́ti na litemi lɛmɛni lɛlɔ?

english_verse: If he became acceptable to God because of what he did, then he would have something to brag about. But he would never be able to brag about it to God.
translation_verse: Si ɔkɛnku kabla lɛlɔ na Katɔti ɔ́nu ka Abraham use siin ni, na ubo kenyekɔ ka ɔkun lɛmɛnɛ. Nsu uuubo kenyekɔ kammɔ na Katɔti anumi, ɔsika ɔɔɔdi Abraham kabla na ɔ́nu.

english_verse: The Scriptures say, “God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.”
translation_verse: Ɔsika na Bunweni Kedee Ɔku kemmo ni, básu banini, “Abraham ɔ́ƒɔ Katɔti ɔ́di. Ɔmmɔ ɔsu na Katɔti ɔ́bu-nwu aani ukyuli ɔni use siin.”

english_verse: Money paid to workers isn't a gift. It is something they earn by working.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔni mɔɔbla kabla ni, ulábu nwuna lɛyuƒɔla aani litela, mmomu ɔdi lɛla lɛni námanku-nwu na nwuna kabla kenye.

english_verse: But you cannot make God accept you because of something you do. God accepts sinners only because they have faith in him.
