english_verse: This is what you must write to the angel of the church in Sardis: I have the seven spirits of God and the seven stars. Listen to what I say. I know what you are doing. Everyone may think you are alive, but you are dead.
translation_verse: Ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Nweni te Sardi baƒɔtaadine lɛkpa ɔtu anii, “Lɛni na ukyuli ɔni mɔɔdi ayu maatɛ ani mɔɔbla Katɔti kabla na nwuna lɛga boku anumi lɛlɔ na ɔda ayabi maatɛ ammɔ na nwuna kɔdianu ɔɔsu.

english_verse: Wake up! You have only a little strength left, and it is almost gone. So try to become stronger. I have found that you are not completely obeying God.
translation_verse: Ngyi kalɛ na bɛɛbla bina kabla, na ngyi lɛnɔ ka bekyuli baanu-mii ka bili ngba, nsu bíkpi na kɔyu kemmo! Anwuɔsu bɛgyinya na bɛkya lɛla lɛni nébu lise-mii ogya kalɛ na bilekpi ƒui! Ɔsika lɛ́nu ka lɛla lɛni na bɛɛbla ni, lítedu tɔ lítawɔlɔ na Katɔti anumi.

english_verse: Remember the teaching you were given and heard. Hold firmly to it and turn from your sins. If you don't wake up, I will come when you least expect it, just as a thief does.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, binyimo lɛla lɛni na bátina-mii na bínu lɛnɔ, na bɛda-ni kaduɛ na bina ekpidi eduo-mii na binwini kama bɛkya-nya. Nsu si bítagyinya ni, ndubo-mii kudɔ aani uyune kalɛ na biláti uwi ɔni kemmo na meti mada malɛ-mii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: A few of you in Sardis have not dirtied your clothes with sin. You will walk with me in white clothes, because you are worthy.
translation_verse: Nsu bibo nkyuli ɛlɛɛ badi na Sardi mmɔ bani nétebile bana adala. Na ami ku-ma bɔdubɔda ala aƒualadi na bɔkɛ butaavi, ɔsika bámanku ka babla lɛni.

english_verse: Everyone who wins the victory will wear white clothes. Their names will not be erased from the book of life, and I will tell my Father and his angels that they are my followers.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔni madi ekpidi lɛlɔ ni, ɔdubɔda ala aƒualadi aani bana kalɛ. Na lɛɛɛdubo-ma anyi bɔda budie ngba ɔku kemmo. Na ndubudie-ma kenye na mina Ɔti ku Katɔti batu ƒui anumi ka badi ami badi.

english_verse: If you have ears, listen to what the Spirit says to the churches. The Letter to Philadelphia
translation_verse: “Si bibo atu ni, na binu lɛla lɛni na Katɔti Kɔyu kɔɔsu baƒɔtaadine akpa ammɔ.” Ɔku Ɔni Na Únweni Úte Ƒiladelƒia Baƒɔtaadine Lɛkpa

english_verse: This is what you must write to the angel of the church in Philadelphia: I am the one who is holy and true, and I have the keys that belonged to David. When I open a door, no one can close it. And when I close a door, no one can open it. Listen to what I say.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Nweni te Ƒiladelƒia baƒɔtaadine lɛkpa ɔtu anii, “Lɛni na anwu ɔni nse kedee na nwuna litemi lɛdi litemi geen ɔɔsu. Anwu nda Ɔga Dawid ɔyikun ɔni na si ɔ́lɛmi kayakun kadi ni, ɔdi ɔsɔ ulakana-ka bɔkalɛ. Na si ɔ́kalɛ-ka ni, ɔdi ulakana-ka bɔlɛmi.

english_verse: I know everything you have done. And I have placed before you an open door no one can close. You were not very strong, but you obeyed my message and did not deny you are my followers.
translation_verse: Ngyi kalɛ na bɛɛbla bina kabla na ngyi ka bibo ɔyikun blii ɔdi. Bɛ́siaku mina ala bɔtina kama na bɛ́di mina etemila lɛnɔ lɛlɔ ulu lɛlɔ. Lɛ́lɛmi kayakun kadi líte-mii na bina anumi na ukyuli biala ulakana-ka bɔkalɛ.

english_verse: Now you will see what I will do with those people who belong to Satan's group. They claim to be God's people, but they are liars. I will make them come and kneel down at your feet. Then they will know that I love you.
translation_verse: Bɛnu! Ɔkɔ banyine bani násala bewi Satan ku nwuna badi kasalakɔ ngye na baalɔ-ma Yudaƒuɔ nsu baaadi Yudaƒuɔ ni, ndubɔya na balɛ akɔnkɔ na ƒula lɛgba akɔ. Na bana ƒui badubɔsu banii mɔɔyɔ́-ɔ.

english_verse: You obeyed my message and endured. So I will protect you from the time of testing everyone in all the world must go through.
translation_verse: Na ka bɛ́di mina ɔda ɔni na líbo-mii lɛlɔ, na bínye kpakplaa na bɛ́siaku ala ani ƒui muukpóku-mii ɔsu ni, ndubɔda-mii lidie lɛbibo lɛni mebo kayawi ƒui lɛlɔ libakɔku bekyuli bani nlie kalɔ lɛlɔ lɛnu kemmo.

english_verse: I am coming soon. So hold firmly to what you have, and no one will take away the crown you will be given as your reward.
translation_verse: “Ndubo uwi klukui kemmo. Anwuɔsu bɛda lɛla lɛni nse-mii kaduɛ kalɛ na ukyuli ɔdi uláƒɔ bina lɛyuƒɔla ulásiku-mii enu kemmo.

english_verse: Everyone who wins the victory will be made into a pillar in the temple of my God, and they will stay there forever. I will write on each of them the name of my God and the name of his city. It is the new Jerusalem my God will send down from heaven. I will also write on them my own new name.
translation_verse: Ndubo ukyuli ɔni madi lɛlɔ bɔbla aani lɛkpa na mina Katɔti kakpakɔ ɔni na lɛsɔ lilágyu mmɔ kudii. Ndubo mina Katɔti lɛnyi ku nwuna ɔma kedee ɔmmɔ lɛnyi bunweni bɔsia-nwu lɛlɔ. Na ɔdi Yerusalem ɔwɔdi ɔni mayu masi katɔ na Katɔti kudɔ. Na ndubo ami ɔlati lɛnyi lɛwɔdi lɛnɔ bunweni bɔsia-nwu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: If you have ears, listen to what the Spirit says to the churches. The Letter to Laodicea
translation_verse: Si bibo atu ni, na binu lɛla lɛni na Katɔti Kɔyu kɔɔsu baƒɔtaadine akpa ammɔ.” Ɔku Ɔni Na Únweni Úte Laodikea Baƒɔtaadine Lɛkpa

english_verse: This is what you must write to the angel of the church in Laodicea: I am the one called Amen! I am the faithful and true witness and the source of God's creation. Listen to what I say.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́sɔ ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Nweni te Laodikea baƒɔtaadine ɔtu anii, “Lɛni na anwu ɔni mɔɔyá na lɛla biala lɛɛsia lɛni ɔɔsu. Na ɔdi Katɔti kenye udiene geen ɔni mɔɔbla ala ulu lɛlɔ, na anwu mɔɔdi Katɔti ala ani ƒui na údie lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I know everything you have done, and you are not cold or hot. I wish you were either one or the other.
translation_verse: Ngyi lɛla lɛni na bɛ́bla na ngyi ka bítaba na bítaƒɔ ogya lɛnɔ. Nsu nka mɔɔyɔ́ si bɛ́ƒuna linwi.

english_verse: But since you are lukewarm and neither cold nor hot, I will spit you out of my mouth.
translation_verse: Nsu ka buse kani na bise gugungu na bítaba iye bítaƒɔ ogya lɛnɔ ɔsu ni, ndubo-mii butuo bɔlɛku mina kenye kemmo!

english_verse: You claim to be rich and successful and to have everything you need. But you don't know how bad off you really are. You are pitiful, poor, blind, and naked.
translation_verse: Bɛɛsu bɛnii, ‘Mbo ala na ɔdianku-mi, na mbo ala ani ƒui na mɔɔwia.’ Nsu bɛɛɛgyi bɛnii biisé lɛlɔ na bina lɛlɔ libo kɔnyana, na biiibo lɛla lɛdi, na anumi ábwɛ-mii, na bɛkɛ kasɔngya.

english_verse: Buy your gold from me. It has been refined in a fire, and it will make you rich. Buy white clothes from me. Wear them and you can cover up your shameful nakedness. Buy medicine for your eyes, so you will be able to see.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu mɔɔlɛ-mii kpakplaa nnii bibo na bibeye sika ugyiedi ɔni bábla kede kede na ogya kemmo na mina kudɔ na binwini balakɛne. Na bibeye adiƒuala ani na binyimi na bekyuli basɔ balanu bina kasɔngya ku kɔƒa. Na biye kuvo bɛkya anumi na bitaanu kaduɛ.

english_verse: I correct and punish everyone I love. So make up your minds to turn away from your sins.
translation_verse: “Bekyuli bani na mɔɔyɔ́ ni, ama na mɔɔdɔnku na mɔɔní-ma kɔtu. Anwuɔsu bɛsia lɛlɔ anu kpakplaa na binwini kama bɛkya bina ekpidi.

english_verse: Listen! I am standing and knocking at your door. If you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in and we will eat together.
translation_verse: Binu! Nnye kayakun muubó kɔnu. Na si ukyuli ɔdi únu-mi lɛdi na ɔ́lɛmi úte-mi ni, ndubuduo-nwu kudɔ na ami ku-nwu bɔsala bɔdi.

english_verse: Everyone who wins the victory will sit with me on my throne, just as I won the victory and sat with my Father on his throne.
translation_verse: “Anwu ɔni madi ekpidi lɛlɔ ni, ndubute-nwu kuƒi na ulie-mi kudɔ na lɛgaboku lɛlɔ aani kalɛ na lɛ́di lɛlɔ na nli mina Ɔti kudɔ na lɛgaboku lɛlɔ.

english_verse: If you have ears, listen to what the Spirit says to the churches.
translation_verse: Si bibo atu ni, na binu lɛla lɛni na Katɔti Kɔyu kɔɔsu baƒɔtaadine akpa ammɔ.”

english_verse: After this, I looked and saw a door that opened into heaven. Then the voice that had spoken to me at first and that sounded like a trumpet said, “Come up here! I will show you what must happen next.”
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama ni, Katɔti údie kɔyu kemmo ala adi ɔ́tina-mi. Na lɛ́nu kayakun kadi ka bálɛmi-ka na katɔ. Amu na lɛdi lɛni na lɛ́ka bunu aani kakpɛɛ ni, línu ka lɛsɔ lɛɛtɛmiku-mi lɛnini, “Bo katɔ kakɛ mɛni na lɛtina-a lɛla lɛni ndubo bɔlɛ na ɔmɛni kama.”

english_verse: Right then the Spirit took control of me, and there in heaven I saw a throne and someone sitting on it.
translation_verse: Kɔnakunwi ni, Kɔyu kɔmmɔ kúti-mi kɔ́kɔliku katɔ. Ka mɔɔnu ni, lɛgaboku lɛdi lise na Katɔti ulie liboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The one who was sitting there sparkled like precious stones of jasper and carnelian. A rainbow that looked like an emerald surrounded the throne.
translation_verse: Na uukeye kede kede! Na bukeye bɔmmɔ buse aani aseebi egyiedi ku aƒualadi ani náƒɔ kuye. Na bukeye bonwu bɔdi bɔ́ka bɔ́mana lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ ƒui aani evete awɔdi bukeye.

english_verse: Twenty-four other thrones were in a circle around that throne. And on each of these thrones there was an elder dressed in white clothes and wearing a gold crown.
translation_verse: Na agaboku aavlanyɔ-ene áka ámana lɛgaboku lɛmɛni. Na benengu aavlanyɔ-ine lɛnɔ belie-nya lɛlɔ. Na bebi adiƒuala lɛlɔ, na sika ugyiedi kɔgabwa kubi-ma eli.

english_verse: Flashes of lightning and roars of thunder came out from the throne in the center of the circle. Seven torches, which are the seven spirits of God, were burning in front of the throne.
translation_verse: Na ogya ɔɔbwɛ ku bukeye geen taasi lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ kudɔ! Na muunú adi adi ku ɔnantu budu kɔku na mmɔ. Na lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ anumi ni, lɛsogya maatɛ lɛɛda. Na ani ndi Katɔti Kɔyu kɔni mbo ɔyikun maatɛ ɔni nnye Katɔti lɛgaboku anumi.

english_verse: Also in front of the throne was something that looked like a glass sea, clear as crystal. Around the throne in the center were four living creatures covered front and back with eyes.
translation_verse: Na kesii kani na lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɛ anumi ni, ɔdi kalɔ kani nwi aani ɛpu na use kede kede aani asogya. Na lɛgaboku lɛmɛni amadɔ ni, ngba batu ine badi udu benye lɛƒɛnyi lɛna ƒui. Na anumi áka ámana-ma lɛlɔ lɛtɔtɔ ku kama ƒui.

english_verse: The first creature was like a lion, the second one was like a bull, the third one had the face of a human, and the fourth was like a flying eagle.
translation_verse: Ngba ɔtu udeedi ɔ́lɛ gyata. Na unyɔdi ɔ́lɛ akɔ. Na ɔtɛdi ɔ́lɛ ukyuli. Na unedi ɔ́lɛ kɔdigbo aasɛ ɔni muuveyi.

english_verse: Each of the four living creatures had six wings, and their bodies were covered with eyes. Day and night they never stopped singing, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord, the all-powerful God, who was and is and is coming!”
translation_verse: Na ngba batu ine bamɛni ƒui bebo avwi aku aku, na anumi akya avwi amɛni kemmo ku kama. Usien ku ɔƒɛ ni, baláda bɔsu taaya banini, “Kedee, kedee, kedee ndi Blɔti ɔni mbo ɔyikun ƒui, ɔni nélie, na uli, na ɔdubo bulie.”

english_verse: The living creatures kept praising, honoring, and thanking the one who sits on the throne and who lives forever and ever.
translation_verse: Ngba batu bammɔ beeti bumwi ku ɔbu ku linugya teete anwu ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ na uli ngba úsela ƒui. Na uwi biala na baabla lɛni ni,

english_verse: “Our Lord and God, you are worthy to receive glory, honor, and power. You created all things, and by your decision they are and were created.”
translation_verse: “Blɔti ku bula Katɔti! Awɔ námanku éte bumwi ku ɔbu ku ɔyikun. Ɔsika awɔ nédie ala ani ƒui, na áya na ana ƒui eli ngba na ƒula lɛƒɔyɔ kenye.”

english_verse: In the right hand of the one sitting on the throne I saw a scroll that had writing on the inside and on the outside. And it was sealed in seven places.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́nu ka anwu ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔda kakunkɛ kadi na nwuna kɔdianu, na bénweni ala ani ndubo abalɛ básia-ka anumi ku kama. Na báƒɛ-ka, na béti kɔma bábala-nwu kenye ekpo maatɛ kalɛ na ukyuli keeke ulakana bubimi.

english_verse: I saw a mighty angel ask with a loud voice, “Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals?”
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, lɛ́nu Katɔti ɔtu ɔyikune ɔdi ɔni násu ku lɛdi momoomo ɔnini, “Ɔma námanku ka ɔmami kɔma kɔmɛni na ɔƒɛnimi kakunkɛ kammɔ?”

english_verse: No one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or look inside it.
translation_verse: Nsu ukyuli ɔdi uuubo katɔ iye kalɔ lɛlɔ iye kekpine muedi ɔni makana kakunkɛ kamɛni bɔƒɛnimi na wanu ɔku ɔmmɔ kemmo.

english_verse: I cried hard because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or look inside it.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, líwulo geen ɔsika bátakana ukyuli ɔdi bɔkɛ na ɔkana ɔku ɔmɛni bɔƒɛnimi bɔka.

english_verse: Then one of the elders said to me, “Stop crying and look! The one who is called both the ‘Lion from the Tribe of Judah’ and ‘King David's Great Descendant’ has won the victory. He will open the scroll and its seven seals.”
translation_verse: Amu na benengu bammɔ akɔ unwi ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Sɔ tewulo. Nu! Yesu ɔni baalɔ banii Gyata ɔni nási Yuda kaba kemmo na ɔdi Dawid Kugyii Ugyiitu ni, ɔ́di lɛlɔ. Anwu námanku ka ɔƒɛnimi kɔma kɔni na béti bábala ekpo maatɛ ammɔ.”

english_verse: Then I looked and saw a Lamb standing in the center of the throne surrounded by the four living creatures and the elders. The Lamb looked as if it had once been killed. It had seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God, sent out to all the earth.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, lɛ́nu ka Katɔti Koƒonu Ubi ɔdi unye agaboku ammɔ lɛlɔ. Na ngba batu ine bammɔ ku benengu aavlanyɔ-ine bammɔ báka bámana-nwu. Na ɔɔtina aani si bɔkpa na béti-nwu bákpa. Ese maatɛ alɛ Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ lili, na ubo anumi maatɛ. Na alakpa maatɛ amɛni adi Katɔti Kɔyu kɔni mbo ɔyikun maatɛ kɔni na Katɔti ɔ́tala ɔ́kya kayawi ƒui.

english_verse: The Lamb went over and took the scroll from the right hand of the one who sat on the throne.
translation_verse: Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ úsie na útáƒɔ kakunkɛ kammɔ ɔ́siku anwu ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ kɔnu kemmo.

english_verse: Then they sang a new song, “You are worthy to receive the scroll and open its seals, because you were killed. And with your own blood you bought for God people from every tribe, language, nation, and race.
translation_verse: Bédie ɔnu ɔwɔdi ɔdi banini, “Awɔ námanku ka aƒɔ kakunkɛ kammɔ na amami kɔma kɔmmɔ. Ɔsika awɔ na bádu. Na ɔkɛnku ƒula ubugya akpala ɔsu ni, áƒɔ bekyuli lili kayu, na ásɔku-ma éte Katɔti. Awɔ náƒɔ-ma ásiku kadi ƒui bekyuli ku adi lidu biala batɛmine ku bekyuli lidu ƒui akɔ na kalɔ biala lɛlɔ.

english_verse: You let them become kings and serve God as priests, and they will rule on earth.”
translation_verse: Awɔ nábla-ma bénwini baga ku bakpane bani mɔɔkpanku bekyuli teeboku bula Katɔti. Na badubɔdi lɛga na kalɔ lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: As I looked, I heard the voices of a large number of angels around the throne and the voices of the living creatures and of the elders. There were millions and millions of them,
translation_verse: Ka lɛ́sɔ lɛ́nu ni, lɛ́nu katɔ batu mpim ɛlɛ ɛlɛ ku mpim leevu akpa leevu alɛ alɛ ka bénye bámana lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ ku ngba batu ine ku benengu bammɔ.

english_verse: and they were saying in a loud voice, “The Lamb who was killed is worthy to receive power, riches, wisdom, strength, honor, glory, and praise.”
translation_verse: Na katɔ batu bamɛni bédie ɔnu ku lɛdi momoomo banini, “Awɔ ndi Koƒonu Ubi ɔni na béti bákpa. Na ámanku éte ɔyikun ku lɛlakɛ ku lɛnunda ku ɔlɔkplu ku ɔbu ku bumwi ku linugya.”

english_verse: Then I heard all beings in heaven and on the earth and under the earth and in the sea offer praise. Together, all of them were saying, “Praise, honor, glory, and strength forever and ever to the one who sits on the throne and to the Lamb!”
translation_verse: Na línu ka ala ani ƒui na Katɔti údie na katɔ ku kalɔ ku kekpine ku ɛpu ku kayawi beedie ɔnu banini, “Linugya ku ɔbu ku bumwi ku ɔyikun na beete anwu ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛlɔ ku Koƒonu Ubi ka ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ƒui.”

english_verse: The four living creatures said “Amen,” while the elders knelt down and worshiped.
translation_verse: Amu na ngba batu ine bammɔ bédie kenye banini, “Ɔsia lɛni.” Na benengu bammɔ báyu bébi kalɔ na beemwi-nwu.

english_verse: At the same time I saw the Lamb open the first of the seven seals, I heard one of the four living creatures shout with a voice like thunder. It said, “Come out!”
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́nu ka Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami kɔma kɔni nda kakunkɛ kani mɔɔtina ala ani ndubo abalɛ mmɔ ekpo maatɛ ammɔ akɔ unwi. Na línu ka ngba batu bammɔ akɔ unwi ɔ́su ku lɛdi momoomo lɛni náku aani ɔnantu budu ɔnini, “Bo!”

english_verse: Then I saw a white horse. Its rider carried a bow and was given a crown. He had already won some victories, and he went out to win more.
translation_verse: Na lɛ́nu ɔpɔnkɔ ɔƒualadi ɔdi ka unye. Ukyuli ɔni nlie ɔpɔnkɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔ́da kataminta na béti kagabwa kadi béte-nwu. Ukyuli ɔmɛni ulie ɔpɔnkɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ aani ukpone lɛlɔ ɔdine ɔni nésela utádi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: When the Lamb opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature say, “Come out!”
translation_verse: Na ɔmmɔ kama ni, Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami kɔma likpo linyɔdi na línu ka ngba batu bammɔ akɔ unyɔdi ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bo!”

english_verse: Then another horse came out. It was fiery red. And its rider was given the power to take away all peace from the earth, so people would slaughter one another. He was also given a big sword.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na ɔpɔnkɔ ɔbambadi ɔni négyie aani ogya kalɛ ɔ́da ɔ́lɛ. Na Katɔti úti ɔyikun úte ukyuli ɔni nlie ɔpɔnkɔ ɔmɛni lɛlɔ ɔnii uti kekpo uboku kalɔ lɛlɔ ƒui kalɛ na bekyuli badu lɛlɔ. Na úte-nwu kewii bonwu kadi.

english_verse: When the Lamb opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, “Come out!” Then I saw a black horse, and its rider had a balance scale in one hand.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama ni, Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami kɔma likpo lɛtɛdi. Mmɔ ni, línu ka ngba batu bammɔ akɔ ɔtɛdi ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bo!” Na ka mɔɔnu ni, lɛ́nu ɔpɔnkɔ totonto ɔdi ka unye. Na ukyuli ɔni nlie ɔpɔnkɔ ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔda kakpagyuɛ kani na baakɔ́ku ala unu taanu.

english_verse: I heard what sounded like a voice from somewhere among the four living creatures. It said, “A liter of wheat will cost you a whole day's wages! Three liters of barley will cost you a day's wages too. But don't ruin the olive oil or the wine.”
translation_verse: Línu ka kɔku kɔdi kɔ́si ngba batu ine bammɔ kudɔ aani ukyuli butemi, na lɛdi lɛmmɔ lɛ́su lɛnini, “Ya na kamu kalaku kenwi kuye kɔkɔ kutédu limeyi lɛyuƒɔla, na antabi kɔlaku ɛtɛ kuye lɛnɔ kɔkɔ kutédu limeyi lɛyuƒɔla. Nsu tavumana nnɔ iye ntɛ bɔmmɔ kuye!”

english_verse: When the Lamb opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature say, “Come out!”
translation_verse: Amu na Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami kɔma likpo linedi. Na línu ka ngba batu bammɔ akɔ unedi ɔ́su ɔnini, “Bo!”

english_verse: Then I saw a pale green horse. Its rider was named Death, and Death's Kingdom followed close behind. They were given power over one fourth of the earth, and they could kill its people with swords, famines, diseases, and wild animals.
translation_verse: Na mmɔ ni, lɛ́nu ka ɔpɔnkɔ ƒuƒuu ɔdi unye aani ɔlɛne. Na básia ukyuli ɔni nlie-nwu lɛlɔ lɛnyi banii Kukpi. Na ukyuli bamba ɔkpɛ-nwu kama ɔni baalɔ Kekpine. Béte-ma ɔyikun ka badu kalɔ lɛkpa linedi bekyuli ƒui. Na kekpo ku kɔka ku ɔlɛ ku beƒiebuo ndubɔdu-ma.

english_verse: When the Lamb opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of everyone who had been killed for speaking God's message and telling about their faith.
translation_verse: Amu na Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami likpo lɛlɔndi. Na lɛ́nu ayu adi na katɔ ka enye lɛbi lɛni lɛlɔ na baakpá mmɔ kalɔ. Badi bekyuli bani ƒui na bádu ayu ka básu Katɔti litemi buni ɔsu. Ama ndi bani nédie ala ammɔ kenye na ulu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: They shouted, “Master, you are holy and faithful! How long will it be before you judge and punish the people of this earth who killed us?”
translation_verse: Ayu amɛni áva ku lɛdi momoomo anini, “Blɔti, ala ƒui lɛlɔ ɔdine, awɔ nse kedee na ƒula etemila lɛnɔ adi litemi geen. Uwi ɛlɛ sɔɔn na adubunye etédu asa na bekyuli bani nádu-bu na kalɔ kamɛni lɛlɔ ni, atɛku-ma litemi na ani-ma kɔtu?”

english_verse: Then each of those who had been killed was given a white robe and told to rest for a little while. They had to wait until the complete number of the Lord's other servants and followers would be killed.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na úte bekyuli bamɛni ɔdi biala awu ɔƒualadi, na ɔ́su-ma ɔnii bakɛ kayi betédu uwi ɔni na kayawi bekyuli bádu bana kabla bablane bakpana bammɔ aani kalɛ na bádu ama lɛnɔ. Ɔsika bana bumomo bútedu bútawɔlɔ tɔ.

english_verse: When I saw the Lamb open the sixth seal, I looked and saw a great earthquake. The sun turned as dark as sackcloth, and the moon became red as blood.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama ni, lɛ́nu ka Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami kɔma likpo lɛkundi. Na kayawi kemodi kákunku kpakplaa, na ɔƒɛ ɔ́da bukeye ɔ́ya, na ala ƒui ábla suu. Na kɔbuli kumodi kɔmmɔ kɔ́vumana kɔ́bla aani ubugya.

english_verse: The stars in the sky fell to earth, just like figs shaken loose by a windstorm.
translation_verse: Ayabi ánu ébo kalɔ aani kalɛ na kugyii ebi aanú na ɔƒɛƒɛɛ kpakplaa kemmo.

english_verse: Then the sky was rolled up like a scroll, and all mountains and islands were moved from their places.
translation_verse: Kayaa káyii aani kalɛ na baaƒɛ ebuo ɔku. Na bágyu abi ku ntuntɛ kalɔ ƒui na ana kenyekɔ.

english_verse: The kings of the earth, its famous people, and its military leaders hid in caves or behind rocks on the mountains. They hid there together with the rich and the powerful and with all the slaves and free people.
translation_verse: Amu na kalɔ lɛlɔ baga ƒui ku bekyuli bani mbo kenyekɔ ku bekpone batɔnkune ku balakɛne ku bayikune ku bekyuli bamba lidu ƒui bani mɔɔbla bekyuli bamba kabla ku bani mɔɔbla ama alati kabla ƒui bábala lɛlɔ na libu ku atakpɛ kalɔ na abi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then they shouted to the mountains and the rocks, “Fall on us! Hide us from the one who sits on the throne and from the anger of the Lamb.
translation_verse: Bákpali abi ku atakpɛ ammɔ banii, “Bibo na bibebi-bu lɛlɔ na bɛbala-bu kalɛ na anwu ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ulanu-bu, na Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ uláni-bu kɔtu!

english_verse: That terrible day has come! God and the Lamb will show their anger, and who can face it?”
translation_verse: Ɔsika Katɔti ku Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ kɔnyi kpakplaa limeyi lídu! Na ɔma makana kɔnyi kɔmmɔ kenye bunye?”

english_verse: After this I saw four angels. Each one was standing on one of the earth's four corners. The angels held back the four winds, so that no wind would blow on the earth or on the sea or on any tree. These angels had also been given the power to harm the earth and the sea. Then I saw another angel come up from where the sun rises in the east, and he was ready to put the mark of the living God on people. He shouted to the four angels,
translation_verse: Katɔti úte-ma ɔyikun ka babla kalɔ ku ɛpu kalala na beti bani bekyuli kɔtu. Nsu lɛ́nu Katɔti ɔtu ɔbambadi ɔdi ka ɔ́si ɔƒɛ katukɔ ɔdubo na ɔda lɛla lɛni na Katɔti ɔni nli ngba ɔdubuti use bekyuli likpo. Na ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpali batu ine ku lɛdi momoomo,

english_verse: “Don't harm the earth or the sea or any tree! Wait until I have marked the foreheads of the servants of our God.”
translation_verse: na ɔ́su-ma ɔnini, “Bitabla kalɔ iye ɛpu iye egyii adi kalala weti wetédu lebo lɛni na búse Katɔti kabla bablane likpo ku likposela lɛmɛni na bana atɛntɛ.”

english_verse: After this, I saw a large crowd with more people than could be counted. They were from every race, tribe, nation, and language, and they stood before the throne and before the Lamb. They wore white robes and held palm branches in their hands,
translation_verse: Na ɔmɛni kama ni, lɛ́nu ka bekyuli pii badi benye mmɔ bani na ukyuli ɔdi ulakana bɔka! Bekyuli bamɛni bási kalɔ biala kemmo ku kadi biala akɔ ku bekyuli lidu lidu ƒui akɔ ku adi lidu biala kemmo ka bénye lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ ku Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ anumi, na bákya lɛwu lɛƒualadi na bada like.

english_verse: as they shouted, “Our God, who sits upon the throne, has the power to save his people, and so does the Lamb.”
translation_verse: Na básu ku lɛdi momoomo banini, “Ngba bɔƒɔ bɔɔsí bula Katɔti ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛlɔ ku Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ kudɔ.”

english_verse: One of the elders asked me, “Do you know who these people are that are dressed in white robes? Do you know where they come from?”
translation_verse: Amu na benengu bammɔ akɔ unwi úye-mi ɔnini, “Ɔma bene ndi bekyuli bani nkya lɛwu lɛƒualadi mɛni lɛni? Na wɛ na bási?”

english_verse: “Sir,” I answered, “you must know.” Then he told me: “These are the ones who have gone through the great suffering. They have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb and have made them white.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́su-nwu nnini, “Ati, lɛɛɛgyi-ma. Awɔ ngyi bekyuli bamɛni.” Amu na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Bekyuli bamɛni ndi bani nénye lɛbibo bonwu lɛmmɔ kenye, na bálɛ-nwu kemmo. Bábla sɛɛn na Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ubugya ɔsu, aani kalɛ na baaƒɔ lɛwu na lɛɛƒuala.

english_verse: And so they stand before the throne of God and worship him in his temple day and night. The one who sits on the throne will spread his tent over them.
translation_verse: “Anwuɔsu na benye Katɔti lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ anumi na baabla-nwu kabla usien ku ɔƒɛ na nwuna kakpakɔ. Ka anwu ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔkya-ma akɔ ɔsu ni, ɔdubo-ma bɔgyumana.

english_verse: They will never hunger or thirst again, and they won't be troubled by the sun or any scorching heat.
translation_verse: Na kɔka iye utukwɛ ɔsɔ uladu-ma kudii. Na ɔƒɛ iye liwulu lɛdi lɛsɔ lileƒi-ma.

english_verse: “The Lamb in the center of the throne will be their shepherd. He will lead them to streams of life-giving water, and God will wipe all tears from their eyes.”
translation_verse: Ɔsika Koƒonu Ubi ɔni nlie lɛgaboku lɛlɔ na mmɔ ni, anwu ndubɔda-ma aani baƒonu ɔdane buni. Na ɔdubo-ma bɔtɔnku busienku abiɔ ani kemmo na ntu bɔni muute ngba buwi uwi biala. Na Katɔti lɛnɔ ɔdubo-ma imii buni.”

english_verse: When the Lamb opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.
translation_verse: Lebo lɛni na Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ ɔ́mami kɔma likpo maatɛdi ni, katɔ mmɔ ƒui kábla diin, na ɔdubɔbla aani ɔdɔ bubo kakɛ kemmo.

english_verse: I noticed that the seven angels who stood before God were each given a trumpet.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́nu Katɔti batu maatɛ bani muunye Katɔti anumi, na úte-ma kɔkpɛɛ maatɛ.

english_verse: Another angel, who had a gold container for incense, came and stood at the altar. This one was given a lot of incense to offer with the prayers of God's people on the gold altar in front of the throne.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti ɔtu ɔbambadi ɔ́da ɔ́lɛ ɔni nda sika ugyiedi libwi lɛni kemmo na baakyula oloƒui, na úbenye lɛkpabi lɛmmɔ kudɔ. Béte-nwu oloƒui pii kalɛ na ɔkyula-nwu na sika ugyiedi lɛkpabi lɛni nnye lɛgaboku lɛmmɔ anumi lɛlɔ. Na oloƒui ɔmmɔ ku Katɔti bekyuli ƒui katɔ bɔkpali bɔbla akpala enwi.

english_verse: Then the smoke of the incense, together with the prayers of God's people, went up to God from the hand of the angel.
translation_verse: Oloƒui ɔni mɔɔkywí mmɔ uyɔ ku Katɔti bekyuli bammɔ katɔ bɔkpali ƒui bɔ́kɔ búsie Katɔti kudɔ ɔ́si Katɔti ɔtu ɔmmɔ enu kemmo.

english_verse: After this, the angel filled the incense container with fire from the altar and threw it on the earth. Thunder roared, lightning flashed, and the earth shook. The Trumpets
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama ni, Katɔti ɔtu ɔmmɔ úti oloƒui libui lɛmmɔ na úyile-ni ku ogya ɔni na údie na lɛbi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ, na úbo éwi kalɔ lɛlɔ na kayawi. Mmɔ ni, línu ɔnantu budu kudu ku kɔku bonwu, na kayaa kaabwɛ ogya, na kalɔ kaakunku. Katɔti Batu Bɔmmɔ Bávwi Bana Kɔkpɛɛ

english_verse: The seven angels now got ready to blow their trumpets.
translation_verse: Amu na batu maatɛ bani nda kɔkpɛɛ maatɛ kɔmmɔ báklibi lɛlɔ kalɛ na bavwi bana kɔkpɛɛ.

english_verse: When the first angel blew his trumpet, hail and fire mixed with blood were thrown down on the earth. A third of the earth, a third of the trees, and a third of all green plants were burned.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔtu udeedi ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Mmɔ kani ni, etubankɛ ku ogya ɔni násalaku ubugya ɔ́bwɛ úbewi kalɔ lɛlɔ na kalɔ kemodi ku egyii lɛkpa lɛtɛdi lɛ́kywi. Na livo ƒui lɛ́kywi.

english_verse: When the second angel blew his trumpet, something like a great fiery mountain was thrown into the sea. A third of the sea turned to blood,
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama ni, Katɔti ɔtu unyɔdi lɛnɔ ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Amu na úbo lɛla lɛni nálɛ aani kɔbi kɔni mɔɔda ku ogya útákya ɛpu kemmo. Na ɛpu lɛkpa lɛtɛdi ƒui línwini ubugya.

english_verse: a third of the living creatures in the sea died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.
translation_verse: Na ketu kemmo bebweyi lɛkpa lɛtɛdi ƒui békpi. Na lɛkɔlɔ linengudi ƒui lɛkpa lɛtɛdi lɛ́kywi.

english_verse: When the third angel blew his trumpet, a great star fell from heaven. It was burning like a torch, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on a third of the springs of water.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔtu ɔtɛdi ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Amu na lɛyabi bonwu lɛdi lɛni mɔɔda aani ogya lɛ́lɛ líbo lɛ́si kayaa na lɛ́yu ntukpa ƒui lɛkpa lɛtɛdi ku abiɔ ƒui lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The name of the star was Bitter, and a third of the water turned bitter. Many people died because the water was so bitter.
translation_verse: Lɛyabi lɛmmɔ lɛnyi ndi Ɔdu Kati Kati. Ntu lɛkpa lɛtɛdi lɛmmɔ ƒui lɛ́yu ɔdu, na bekyuli pii badi békpi na ntu bɔmmɔ ɔdu ɔsu.

english_verse: When the fourth angel blew his trumpet, a third of the sun, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars were struck. They each lost a third of their light. So during a third of the day there was no light, and a third of the night was also without light.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔtu unedi ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Na lɛla lɛdi lɛ́yila ɔƒɛ ku kɔbuli ku ayabi lɛkpa lɛtɛdi bukeye. Anwuɔsu usien ku ɔƒɛ limeyi lɛkpa lɛtɛdi lɛ́sɔ lítanu bukeye.

english_verse: Then I looked and saw a lone eagle flying across the sky. It was shouting, “Trouble, trouble, trouble to everyone who lives on earth! The other three angels are now going to blow their trumpets.”
translation_verse: Amu ka nnye mɔɔnu budie bɔtina bɔmɛni ni, lɛ́nu kɔdigbo aasɛ ɔdi ɔni néveyi ɔkɛ kayaa kakaaka, na ɔ́su ku lɛdi momoomo ɔnini, “Si uwi ɔni na Katɔti batu ɛtɛ bani nébu mɛni bávwi bana kɔkpɛɛ ni, muute bekyuli bani ƒui nli kalɔ lɛlɔ bɔbuɛ, bɔbuɛ, bɔbuɛ kɔtɛ!”

english_verse: When the fifth angel blew his trumpet, I saw a star fall from the sky to earth. It was given the key to the tunnel that leads down to the deep pit.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔtu ɔlɔndi ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Na lɛ́nu ɔtu ɔdi ka ɔ́nu ɔ́si katɔ aani lɛyabi úbayu kalɔ. Na Katɔti úte-nwu ɔyikun ɔni mɔɔbala kasuudikɔ ubu bonwu ɔmmɔ kenye.

english_verse: As it opened the tunnel, smoke poured out like the smoke of a great furnace. The sun and the air turned dark because of the smoke.
translation_verse: Ɔtu ɔmɛni ɔ́lɛmi ubu bonwu ɔmɛni na uyɔ ɔ́lɛ ubu ɔmmɔ kemmo aani uyɔ ɔni mɔɔlɛ́ taasi lɛgyavonku bonwu lɛdi kemmo. Na ɔƒɛ bukeye ku kayaa kábla suu na uyɔ ɔmmɔ ɔsu.

english_verse: Locusts came out of the smoke and covered the earth. They were given the same power that scorpions have.
translation_verse: Baalɔlɔ bani muubile edula badi báyu bási uyɔ ɔmmɔ kemmo bébo kalɔ, na Katɔti úte-ma ɔyikun aani ɔni na batamlukpa bebo kalɛ.

english_verse: The locusts were told not to harm the grass on the earth or any plant or any tree. They were to punish only those people who did not have God's mark on their foreheads.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́su baalɔlɔ bammɔ ka batabla livete iye livo iye kugyii kɔdi kalala ntu bekyuli bani na Katɔti útese likpo na bana atɛntɛ.

english_verse: The locusts were allowed to make them suffer for five months, but not to kill them. The suffering they caused was like the sting of a scorpion.
translation_verse: Útete baalɔlɔ bammɔ ulu ka baya na ukyuli ɔdi ukpi, nsu babla-ma kalala na bebo abi na benu ɔlɛ abuli alɔ. Na ɔlɛ bunu ɔni nkya lɛbibo lɛmɛni kemmo ni, buse aani kalɛ na katamlukpa kaata.

english_verse: In those days people will want to die, but they will not be able to. They will hope for death, but it will escape from them.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni na abuli alɔ ammɔ kemmo ni, badubo kukpi bɔwia, nsu balákɛ-ku. Badubɔwia banii beekpi, nsu kukpi kɔdubo-ma bukeli.

english_verse: These locusts looked like horses ready for battle. On their heads they wore something like gold crowns, and they had human faces.
translation_verse: Baalɔlɔ bammɔ bɔnu buse aani bapɔnkɔ bani nnye kagyumana bete kekpo. Na kɔbwa kɔni nálɛ sika ugyiedi kɔgabwa kubi-ma eli. Na bana anumi álɛ bekyuli anumi.

english_verse: Their hair was like a woman's long hair, and their teeth were like those of a lion.
translation_verse: Bana lili linwini lise gyɔlɔɔ, na bana kenye kemmo anyi ese aani gyata anyi.

english_verse: On their chests they wore armor made of iron. Their wings roared like an army of horse-drawn chariots rushing into battle.
translation_verse: Na béti ala ani nse aani abuala lɛwu lɛni mɔɔgyumana kayi bákya. Na kɔku kɔni na bana avwi aabla ni, aaku aani kɛɛkɛ pii ɔni bapɔnkɔ báni béselaku kekpokɔ.

english_verse: Their tails were like a scorpion's tail with a stinger that had the power to hurt someone for five months.
translation_verse: Baalɔlɔ bamɛni bebo lɛka ku akpɛlɛ aani batamlukpa kalɛ na bana lɛka lɛmɛni kemmo, na bebo ɔyikun ɔni na badubo buti bɔbla bekyuli kalala abuli alɔ.

english_verse: Their king was the angel in charge of the deep pit. In Hebrew his name was Abaddon, and in Greek it was Apollyon.
translation_verse: Bebo ɔga ɔni ndi ɔtu ɔni mɔɔnu kasuudikɔ ubu bonwu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Ɔtu ɔmmɔ lɛnyi na Hebri lɛdi kemmo ndi Abadon. Na Griki lɛdi kemmo ni, nwuna lɛnyi ndi Apolion ɔni kalɔ ndi Ɔkyulane.

english_verse: The first horrible thing has now happened! But wait. Two more horrible things will happen soon.
translation_verse: Bɔbuɛ lɛla lideedi lɛ́vi. Na alakpa anyɔ ani ndanku bɔbwɛ inyɔ bɔni nébu ni, adubo bɔlɛ.

english_verse: Then the sixth angel blew his trumpet. I heard a voice speak from the four corners of the gold altar that stands in the presence of God.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔtu ɔkundi ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Na línu lɛdi lɛdi ka lɛ́si sika ugyiedi lɛbi lɛni nnye Katɔti anumi ekpo ene ammɔ lɛlɔ lɛdubo.

english_verse: The voice spoke to this angel and said, “Release the four angels who are tied up beside the great Euphrates River.”
translation_verse: Lɛdi lɛmmɔ lɛ́su Katɔti ɔtu ɔkundi ɔmmɔ ɔnini, “Táƒɛnimi batu ine bani na bényimi bése Euƒrate Ketu bonwu kudɔ!”

english_verse: The four angels had been prepared for this very hour and day and month and year. Now they were set free to kill a third of all people.
translation_verse: Amu na báƒɛnimi batu ine bamɛni bani na bényimi-ma bése mmɔ bete ka báƒɛnimi-ma na ɔdɔ ɔmɛni lɛlɔ na limeyi lɛmɛni kemmo na kɔbuli kɔmɛni kemmo na lɛkwa lɛmɛni tutuutu kemmo kalɛ na badu bayawine ƒui lɛkpa lɛtɛdi.

english_verse: In my vision their riders wore fiery-red, dark-blue, and yellow armor on their chests. The heads of the horses looked like lions, with fire and smoke and sulfur coming out of their mouths.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni na lɛla lɛni bédie bátina-mi mɛni kemmo ni, lɛ́nu bekpone pii bani nlie bapɔnkɔ lɛlɔ bésela kekpokɔ. Na básu-mi bana bumomo ɔni ndi bekyuli bɔka etili eti ene. Na abuala lɛwu lɛni mɔɔgyumana-ma kayi mmɔ égyie aani ogya, na eekeye aani ɛpu ku ogya atabi. Bapɔnkɔ bammɔ eli ese aani bagyata eli, na ogya ku uyɔ ku agyakpabi aalɛ́ taasi-ma inye kemmo.

english_verse: One third of all people were killed by the three terrible troubles caused by the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur.
translation_verse: Na alakpa atɛ ani ndanku kukpi na ási bapɔnkɔ bamɛni inye kemmo ɔsu ni, bekyuli lɛkpa lɛtɛdi sɔɔn békpi.

english_verse: The horses had powerful mouths, and their tails were like poisonous snakes that bite and hurt.
translation_verse: Ɔsika bapɔnkɔ bammɔ ɔyikun ɔkya bana inye ku lɛka kemmo. Bana lɛka libo eli aani balakpi kalɛ, na beeti taadu bekyuli.

english_verse: The people who lived through these terrible troubles did not turn away from the idols they had made, and they did not stop worshiping demons. They kept on worshiping idols that were made of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood. Not one of these idols could see, hear, or walk.
translation_verse: Bekyuli bakladi bani ƒui nétekpi na alakpa atɛ ani ndanku kukpi mmɔ kemmo ni, béténwini kama bátákya ala ani na ama alati béti bana enu bábla bése béte lɛlɔ ka bataakpa. Ala amɛni adanku ayu ekpidi ku bana baƒiɔ bani na béti sika ugyiedi ku ɔƒualadi bávɔ ku kalɔ kemmo abuala ku atabi ku egyii ani na bánwi. Nsu ala amɛni ƒui ni, alánu na elenu na elesie muedi!

english_verse: No one stopped murdering or practicing witchcraft or being immoral or stealing.
translation_verse: Bétenwini kayi na bana bekyuli bɔdu ku evo ala bɔbla kudɔ iye kɔsɔnɔ ala bɔbla ku kuyu kudɔ.

english_verse: I saw another powerful angel come down from heaven. This one was covered with a cloud, and a rainbow was over his head. His face was like the sun, his legs were like columns of fire,
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́nu Katɔti ɔtu ɔyikune ɔbambadi ka ɔ́si katɔ ɔɔyu. Na ɔ́ka ɔ́mana-nwu aani kɔdi, na bukeye bɔ́ka bɔ́mana-nwu lili. Nwuna anumi eekeye aani ɔƒɛ kalɛ, na nwuna lɛgba lise aani akpa ani nnye kalɔ na aada aani ogya.

english_verse: and with his hand he held a little scroll that had been unrolled. He stood there with his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land.
translation_verse: Kakunkɛ blii suɛ kadi kébimi kakya-nwu kɔnu. Na úti nwuna kɔdianu ɔgba únyene ɛpu lɛlɔ, na úti kɔmiinu ɔgba únyene kalɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Then he shouted with a voice that sounded like a growling lion. Thunder roared seven times.
translation_verse: Amu na údie lɛdi momoomo aani gyata kalɛ. Na ka ɔ́va ni, kayaa kábwɛ ogya ku kɔku bonwu maatɛ!

english_verse: After the thunder stopped, I was about to write what it had said. But a voice from heaven shouted, “Keep it secret! Don't write these things.”
translation_verse: Ka línu kɔku bonwu kɔmɛni ni, líse kalɔ nnii muunweni lɛla lɛni na línu. Nsu lɛdi lɛdi lɛ́si katɔ na lɛ́su-mi lɛnini, “Ɔlɛka abɛla lɛla lɛni na énu na kɔku bonwu kɔmmɔ kemmo ese, na tenweni-nya.”

english_verse: The angel I had seen standing on the sea and the land then held his right hand up toward heaven.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́nu ka ɔtu ɔni nnye kalɔ ku ɛpu lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔ́talaku kɔdianu kɔnu katɔ.

english_verse: He made a promise in the name of God who lives forever and who created heaven, earth, the sea, and every living creature. The angel said, “You won't have to wait any longer.
translation_verse: Na ɔ́kpali ala ɔ́lɔ Katɔti lɛnyi. Ɔ́lɔ Anwu ɔni nli ngba ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ƒui ɔni nédie katɔ ku kalɔ ku ɛpu ku ala ani nkya-nya kemmo ƒui. Na ɔ́su ɔnini, “Katɔti ɔsɔ ulebile uwi!

english_verse: God told his secret plans to his servants the prophets, and it will all happen by the time the seventh angel sounds his trumpet.”
translation_verse: Kabla kabɛdi kani na ɔ́su nwuna kenye bediene bani ndi nwuna kabla bablane ka kadubɔlɛ ni, kadubo kete lɛni si Katɔti ɔtu maatɛdi ɔmmɔ ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ.”

english_verse: Once again the voice from heaven spoke to me. It said, “Go and take the open scroll from the hand of the angel standing on the sea and the land.”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, lɛdi lɛni nátɛmiku-mi lɛ́si-ku katɔ mmɔ lɛ́sɔ lɛ́su-mi lɛnini, “Sie na atáƒɔ kakunkɛ kani nkya Katɔti ɔtu ɔni nnye ɛpu ku kalɔ lɛlɔ mmɔ kɔnu kemmo.”

english_verse: When I went over to ask the angel for the little scroll, the angel said, “Take the scroll and eat it! Your stomach will turn sour, but the taste in your mouth will be sweet as honey.”
translation_verse: Amu na lísie ɔtu ɔmmɔ kudɔ na lɛ́su-nwu nnii uti kakunkɛ kammɔ ute-mi. Amu na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ƒɔ, na eti-ka akun! Mɔɔsu-ɔ ka ɔdubo ɔdu bɔyu na ƒula kaƒɔ kemmo, nsu ɔdubɔyu-ɔ emini aani uwɔ na ƒula kenye kemmo.”

english_verse: I took the little scroll from the hand of the angel and ate it. The taste was sweet as honey, but my stomach turned sour.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́ƒɔ kakunkɛ kammɔ, na lɛ́kun. Na ɔ́yu-mi emini na kenye kemmo. Nsu ka líbweli-ka lɛ́wɔlɔ ni, ɔ́yu ɔdu na mina kaƒɔ kemmo.

english_verse: Then some voices said, “Keep on telling what will happen to the people of many nations, races, and languages, and also to kings.”
translation_verse: Nwuna kama ni, ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Ɔlɛka asɔ esie anumi eteedie Katɔti litemi lɛni ndanku bekyuli lidu lidu na kalɔ pii lɛlɔ ku adi lidu lidu batɛmine ku baga pii lɛlɔ ete bekyuli.”

english_verse: But don't measure the courtyard outside the temple building. Leave it out. It has been given to those people who don't know God, and they will trample all over the holy city for
translation_verse: Nsu takɔku keyi, ɔsika béti mmɔ béte bekyuli bani naaadi Yudaƒuɔ. Badubo mmɔ ku ɔma ɔmmɔ ƒui lɛgba butu bɔvi abuli aavlene-anyɔ.

english_verse: These two witnesses are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand in the presence of the Lord who rules the earth.
translation_verse: Ɔkya Bunweni Kedee Ɔku kemmo ka nnɔ egyii anyɔ ku sika ugyiedi ligyii inyɔ lɛni lɛlɔ na asogya ɔsia ni, linye Kayawi Ƒui Unwoti anumi na katɔ. Na akpa anyɔ amɛni enye ete Katɔti kenye bediene inyɔ bamɛni.

english_verse: Any enemy who tries to harm them will be destroyed by the fire that comes out of their mouths.
translation_verse: Si ukyuli ɔdi ɔ́kya ɔkplu ɔnii ɔɔbla-ma kalala ni, ogya ɔdubo bɔlɛ bɔsi bana kenye kemmo na ɔkyula bekisine bammɔ. Na ukyuli biala ɔni mɔɔwia ɔnii ɔɔbla-ma kalala ni, ulu ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ kani na ɔdubɔsia ukpi.

english_verse: They have the power to lock up the sky and to keep rain from falling while they are prophesying. And whenever they want to, they can turn water to blood and cause all kinds of terrible troubles on earth.
translation_verse: Bebo ɔyikun ka betile ɔnantu na ɔsɔ ulana na uwi ɔni kemmo na beedie Katɔti kenye mmɔ. Na bebo ɔyikun lɛnɔ na ntukpa ƒui lɛlɔ kalɛ na baya na bunwini ubugya. Na bebo ɔyikun lɛnɔ na baya na lɛlɛ lidu lidu libo kayawi ƒui lɛlɔ uwi biala na baayɔ́.

english_verse: After the two witnesses have finished preaching God's message, the beast that lives in the deep pit will come up and fight against them. It will win the battle and kill them.
translation_verse: Ɔƒɛni si bédie Katɔti kenye báwɔlɔ ni, eƒiebuo ɔni nási ɔɔlɛ́ kasuudikɔ ubu bonwu ɔmmɔ kemmo ɔdubukpoku-ma na ɔdi-ma lɛlɔ na ɔdu-ma lɛnɔ.

english_verse: Their bodies will be left lying in the streets of the same great city where their Lord was nailed to a cross. And this city is spiritually like the city of Sodom or the country of Egypt.
translation_verse: Bana ɔlɔna ɔdubɔtɛ lɛblɔnu lɛlɔ na ɔma unengudi ɔni baalɔ na lɛsugba kemmo banii Egyipte iye Sodom. Mmɔ na bákana Blɔti bámana ugyii lɛlɔ.

english_verse: For three and a half days the people of every nation, tribe, language, and race will stare at the bodies of these two witnesses and refuse to let them be buried.
translation_verse: Ama bani nási bekyuli ku kadi ku adi lidu ƒui akɔ ku kalɔ ƒui lɛlɔ ni, badubo bekyuli bamɛni ɔlɔna bɔnu emeyi atɛ ku kakɛ sɔɔn. Nsu badubuni na baláva-ma.

english_verse: Everyone on earth will celebrate and be happy. They will give gifts to each other, because of what happened to the two prophets who caused them so much trouble.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani nlie kalɔ lɛlɔ badubo kubiti bɔkɛ na nkyuli inyɔ bammɔ kukpi ɔsu. Badubo limeyi bɔdi na bete lɛlɔ ala, ɔsika kenye bediene inyɔ bammɔ béti lɛbibo pii béboku kayawi bekyuli lɛlɔ.

english_verse: But three and a half days later, God will breathe life into their bodies. They will stand up, and everyone who sees them will be terrified.
translation_verse: Na emeyi atɛ ku kakɛ kama ni, ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔni muute ngba ɔ́si Katɔti kudɔ úbo na úduo-ma lɛlɔ kemmo na báta bénye. Na bani ƒui nánu-ma ni, liƒu lɛ́da-ma.

english_verse: The witnesses then heard a loud voice from heaven, saying, “Come up here.” And while their enemies were watching, they were taken up to heaven in a cloud.
translation_verse: Mmɔ na kenye bediene inyɔ bammɔ bénu lɛdi bonwu lɛdi ka lɛ́si katɔ na lɛ́su-ma lɛnini, “Bibo katɔ mɛni!” Ka bana bekisine baanu ni, bákɔ bésie katɔ na kemmo.

english_verse: At that same moment there was a terrible earthquake that destroyed a tenth of the city. Seven thousand people were killed, and the rest were frightened and praised the God who rules in heaven.
translation_verse: Kɔnakunwi ni, kalɔ bɔkunku kpakplaa bɔdi bɔ́lɛ na ɔma ɔmmɔ lɛkpa leevudi lɛ́bwɛ, na bekyuli mpim maatɛ békpi. Liƒu pim líƒie bekyuli bakladi, na bákɔliku Ati ɔni nkya katɔ lɛnyi katɔ!

english_verse: The second horrible thing has now happened! And the third one will be here soon. The Seventh Trumpet
translation_verse: Bɔbuɛ lɛla linyɔdi lɛ́vi, na lɛtɛdi lɛdubo lɛmmɔ kama bɔsia uwi klukui. Bávwi Kakpɛɛ Maatɛdi

english_verse: At the sound of the seventh trumpet, loud voices were heard in heaven. They said, “Now the kingdom of this world belongs to our Lord and to his Chosen One! And he will rule forever and ever!”
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, Katɔti ɔtu maatɛdi ɔ́vwi nwuna kakpɛɛ. Na línu ka bekyuli pii báva na katɔ mmɔ básu banini, “Kayawi lɛga kadikɔ ƒui kénwini bula Unwoti Katɔti ku nwuna Ukyuli Ɔƒunadi kadi! Na ɔdubo lɛlɔ bɔdi ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ƒui!”

english_verse: They said, “Lord God All-Powerful, you are and you were, and we thank you. You used your great power and started ruling.
translation_verse: Na baasu banini, “Blɔti ɔni mbo ɔyikun ƒui, ɔni nli na úlie, bɔɔgyá-a enu, ɔsika áƒɔ ƒula ɔyikun ubendi na ése kalɔ aadi lɛlɔ!

english_verse: When the nations got angry, you became angry too! Now the time has come for the dead to be judged. It is time for you to reward your servants the prophets and all your people who honor your name, no matter who they are. It is time to destroy everyone who has destroyed the earth.”
translation_verse: Bekyuli bani ƒui nátaƒɔ-ɔ bátadi ni, béti kɔnyi. Anwuɔsu ƒula kɔtu bɔni kúbo-ma lɛlɔ. Ɔsika uwi údu ka atɛku bekyuli bekpine litemi. Ɔdi uwi ɔni na adubɔƒɔ kayu kabuni ete ƒula kabla bablane ku kenye bediene ku ƒula bekyuli ƒui. Na benengu ku banamu bani ƒui mɔɔbu-ɔ ni, adubɔƒɔ-ma kayu kabuni. Na adubɔkyula bekyuli bekpidi bani nádu ƒula bekyuli na kalɔ lɛlɔ!”

english_verse: The door to God's temple in heaven was then opened, and the sacred chest could be seen inside the temple. I saw lightning and heard roars of thunder. The earth trembled and huge hailstones fell to the ground.
translation_verse: Amu na bálɛmi Katɔti kakpakɔ kedee, na bánu Bunyimi Adaka kedee ka use mmɔ. Na kayaa kábwɛ ogya ku kɔku bonwu. Na katɔ keedu taasia kama. Kalɔ kákunku, na etubankɛ áyu pii!

english_verse: She was about to give birth, and she was crying because of the great pain.
translation_verse: Ɔda kaƒɔ. Na ka uwi údu ka ɔwɔ ni, ɔ́va momoomo ka uunú ɔlɛ ɔsu.

english_verse: Something else appeared in the sky. It was a huge red dragon with seven heads and ten horns, and a crown on each of its seven heads.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́nu akɔla ala bɔnu bɔbambadi lɛnɔ! Liƒu kɔlakpi bonwu kɔdi négyie geen kɔ́da kɔ́lɛ kayaa. Na kubo eli maatɛ ku ese leevu. Na kagabwa kebi-ku lili biala lɛlɔ.

english_verse: With its tail, it dragged a third of the stars from the sky and threw them down to the earth. Then the dragon turned toward the woman, because it wanted to eat her child as soon as it was born.
translation_verse: Na kútiku kayaa ayabi lɛkpa lɛtɛdi ƒui ku nwuna ɔka úbo úbewi kalɔ lɛlɔ. Kunye uleku ɔmmɔ lɛtɔtɔ kalɛ na kuti ubi ɔni na uleku ɔmmɔ wawɔ ɔkun si ɔ́nya ɔ́wɔ-nwu.

english_verse: The woman gave birth to a son, who would rule all nations with an iron rod. The boy was snatched away. He was taken to God and placed on his throne.
translation_verse: Na uleku ɔmmɔ ɔ́wɔ ɔnanabi ɔni madi kayawi ƒui lɛlɔ ku ɔyikun kpakplaa. Nsu Katɔti Kɔyu kúkpeli ubi ɔmmɔ kɔ́ƒɔ na kúti-nwu kúsienku Katɔti na nwuna lɛgaboku anumi.

english_verse: The woman ran into the desert to a place that God had prepared for her. There she would be taken care of for
translation_verse: Na uleku ɔmmɔ úkeli úsie ketele kemmo likpo lɛni na Katɔti ɔ́klibi úse-nwu. Mmɔ na badubo-nwu lɛlɔ bɔnu emeyi apim unwi eti alɔ ku leevu.

english_verse: A war broke out in heaven. Michael and his angels were fighting against the dragon and its angels.
translation_verse: Amu na kekpo kálɛ na katɔ. Na Katɔti ɔtu unengudi ɔni ndi Mikael ɔ́tɔnku Katɔti batu bakladi na báta, na ama ku liƒu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ ku kuna batu lɛnɔ békpo.

english_verse: But the dragon lost the battle. It and its angels were forced out of their places in heaven
translation_verse: Nsu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kútakana-ma kenye bunye. Anwuɔsu básɔ bátakɛ keliekɔ kadi na katɔ mmɔ.

english_verse: and were thrown down to the earth. Yes, that old snake and his angels were thrown out of heaven! That snake, who fools everyone on earth, is known as the devil and Satan.
translation_verse: Na bábɔku liƒu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ béboku kalɔ. Aku ndi kɔlakpi kɔkukudi bonwu kɔni baalɔ ukisine ɔmmɔ iye Satan, na ɔɔtɔ́lɔ kayawi kemodi ƒui. Bábɔku anwu ku nwuna batu ƒui bábava kalɔ lɛlɔ mɛni.

english_verse: Then I heard a voice from heaven shout, “Our God has shown his saving power, and his kingdom has come! God's own Chosen One has shown his authority. Satan accused our people in the presence of God day and night. Now he has been thrown out!
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama línu lɛdi bonwu lɛdi na katɔ na lɛɛsu lɛnini, “Ɔƒɛni na Katɔti ngba bɔƒɔ ku nwuna ɔyikun ku lɛgadi lɛ́da lɛ́lɛ. Na nwuna Ukyuli Ɔƒunadi ɔmmɔ kenyekɔ lɛnɔ káda kálɛ. Ɔsika bábɔku baƒɔtaadine ukisine ɔmmɔ bálɛku katɔ mmɔ. Anwu muunye bula Katɔti anumi usien ku ɔƒɛ taawia baƒɔtaadine bammɔ litemi.

english_verse: “Our people defeated Satan because of the blood of the Lamb and the message of God. They were willing to give up their lives.
translation_verse: Bula banwani bádi-nwu lɛlɔ ɔkɛnku Koƒonu Ubi ubugya lɛlɔ ku litemi geen lɛni kenye bédie lɛlɔ. Ɔsika bénye kagyumana ka beti bana ngba bakpa.

english_verse: “The heavens should rejoice, together with everyone who lives there. But pity the earth and the sea, because the devil was thrown down to the earth. He knows his time is short, and he is very angry.”
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu lɛlɔ lɛyɔ amii bani nkya katɔ mmɔ ƒui! Nsu muute kalɔ ku ɛpu ala ƒui bɔbuɛ! Ɔsika Satan ɔ́ɔda ɔ́lɛ-mii lɛlɔ. Na úti kɔnyi geen, ɔsika ɔgyi ka uwi klukui kani nébu-nwu.”

english_verse: When the dragon realized it had been thrown down to the earth, it tried to make trouble for the woman who had given birth to a son.
translation_verse: Lebo lɛni na liƒu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kɔ́nu kɔ́ti ka bábɔku-nwu bábava kalɔ lɛlɔ ni, úse kalɔ ɔ́bi ɔ́siaku uleku ɔni náwɔ ubi ɔnanabi ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: But the woman was given two wings like those of a huge eagle, so she could fly into the desert. There she would escape from the snake and be taken care of for a time, two times, and half a time.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti úte uleku ɔmmɔ aasɛ bonwu avwi kalɛ na uveyi uteesie nwuna keliekɔ na ketele kemmo. Mmɔ na badubo-nwu bɔgyumana akwa atɛ ku kakɛ ɔsiku kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kudɔ.

english_verse: The snake then spewed out water like a river to sweep the woman away.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kútuo ntu pii bɔdi bɔ́lɛku nwuna kenye kemmo kalɛ na bɔgba butéƒie uleku ɔmmɔ na butiku-nwu bɔtɔlɔku.

english_verse: But the earth helped her and swallowed the water that had come from the dragon's mouth.
translation_verse: Nsu kalɔ kébunku uleku ɔmmɔ na kébimi kenye na káni ntu bɔni nálɛ bɔ́si kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kenye kemmo ƒui.

english_verse: This made the dragon terribly angry with the woman. So it started a war against the rest of her children. They are the people who obey God and are faithful to what Jesus did and taught.
translation_verse: Mmɔ ni, kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kúti kɔnyi kɔ́kya uleku ɔmmɔ geen, na kɔ́gyu kɔ́tɔlɔ kúsie kútékpoku nwuna bawɔ bakladi bani muunú Katɔti litemi na beedie Yesu kenye.

english_verse: The dragon stood on the beach beside the sea.
translation_verse: Amu na kɔlakpi kukpidi kɔmmɔ kɔ́ƒɔ lɛlɔ kɔkya ɛpu kɔtu mmɔ.

english_verse: I looked and saw a beast coming up from the sea. This one had ten horns and seven heads, and a crown was on each of its ten horns. On each of its heads were names that were an insult to God.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama lɛ́nu eƒiebuo ɔdi ka ɔ́lɛ ɔ́si ɛpu kemmo ɔ́kɔ ɔɔlɛ́. Ubo eli maatɛ na ese leevu alɛ-nwu eli ammɔ lɛlɔ. Na lise biala lɛlɔ ni, kagabwa kebi. Na nwuna lili biala lɛlɔ ni, lɛnyi lɛdi lɛsia lɛni muudumi Katɔti.

english_verse: The beast I saw had the body of a leopard, the feet of a bear, and the mouth of a lion. The dragon handed over its own power and throne and great authority to this beast.
translation_verse: Eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ use aani ebuoƒuala, na nwuna lɛgba lise aani kegiti lɛgba, na nwuna kenye kese aani gyata kenye. Liƒu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kúti kuna ɔyikun kúte eƒiebuo ɔmɛni ku kuna lɛgaboku ku kenyekɔ kenengudi.

english_verse: One of its heads seemed to have been fatally wounded, but now it was well. Everyone on earth marveled at this beast,
translation_verse: Eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ lili linwi lɛ́tina aani si ɔ́ƒɔ ɔlɛ ɔni na ɔlɛka ukpi nka. Nsu ɔlɛ ɔmmɔ ɔ́ɔsa. Ɔmɛni ɔ́bla kayawi bekyuli ƒui dɛye dɛye, na basiaku eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ kama.

english_verse: and they worshiped the dragon who had given its authority to the beast. They also worshiped the beast and said, “No one is like this beast! No one can fight against it.”
translation_verse: Bekyuli bátaalɛ akɔnkɔ teete kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ, ɔsika kúte eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ kenyekɔ kenengudi. Na bátaalɛ akɔnkɔ teete eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ lɛnɔ. Na baasu banii, “Ɔma nse aani eƒiebuo ɔmɛni? Na ɔma makana-nwu bukpoku? Ɔdi uuubo!”

english_verse: The beast was allowed to brag and claim to be God, and for
translation_verse: Eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɛ ɔyikun na ɔ́di ala lɛlɔ abuli aavlene-anyɔ, na ɔ́talaku lɛlɔ katɔ, na údumi Katɔti geen.

english_verse: It was allowed to fight against God's people and defeat them. It was also given authority over the people of every tribe, nation, language, and race.
translation_verse: Ɔ́kɛ ɔyikun ka ukpo Katɔti bekyuli na ɔdi-ma lɛlɔ. Kaba biala ku bekyuli lidu ku adi ƒui ku ama bani nási kalɔ biala lɛlɔ béduo nwuna lɛlɔ bɔdi kalɔ.

english_verse: The beast was worshiped by everyone whose name wasn't written before the time of creation in the book of the Lamb who was killed.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bani ƒui nlie kalɔ lɛlɔ badubɔlɛ akɔnkɔ bete-nwu, ntu bekyuli bani anyi na bénweni bákya ngba ɔku kemmo bése asa na Katɔti údie kayawi. Ngba ɔku ɔmmɔ ɔdi Koƒonu Ubi ɔni na béti bákpa ɔdi.

english_verse: If you have ears, then listen!
translation_verse: Si bibo atu ni, na binu!

english_verse: If you are doomed to be captured, you will be captured. If you are doomed to be killed by a sword, you will be killed by a sword. This means God's people must learn to endure and be faithful!
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔni na badubo buƒie ni, badubuƒie-nwu. Na ukyuli ɔni lɛnɔ na badubo bɔdu na ɔkɛɛ kenye lɛnɔ ni, badubo-nwu bɔdu. Ɔmɛni ɔsu ni, amii Katɔti bekyuli ɔlɛka binye lɛbibo biala kenye kpakplaa na bɛsiaku Blɔti ulu lɛlɔ.

english_verse: I now saw another beast. This one came out of the ground. It had two horns like a lamb, but spoke like a dragon.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́nu eƒiebuo ɔbambadi ɔni nálɛ ɔ́si kalɔ kemmo. Ese anyɔ alɛ-nwu lili aani koƒonubi, nsu ɔ́talaku lɛlɔ katɔ aani liƒu kɔlakpi kɔni muuƒwi.

english_verse: It worked for the beast whose fatal wound had been healed. And it used all its authority to force the earth and its people to worship that beast.
translation_verse: Únye eƒiebuo udeedi ɔmmɔ kenye útaabla nwuna kabla. Na únye kayawi kammɔ ƒui lɛlɔ beliene lɛlɔ ka balɛ akɔnkɔ bete eƒiebuo udeedi ɔni ɔlɛ nása mmɔ.

english_verse: It worked mighty miracles, and while people watched, it even made fire come down from the sky.
translation_verse: Eƒiebuo unyɔdi ɔmɛni údie akɔla ɔ́tina-ma, na ɔ́ya na ogya muedi ɔ́si katɔ úbo kalɔ lɛlɔ na ukyuli biala anumi.

english_verse: This second beast fooled people on earth by working miracles for the first one. Then it talked them into making an idol in the form of the beast that did not die after being wounded by a sword.
translation_verse: Ɔ́tɔlɔ bekyuli bani ƒui nlie kalɔ lɛlɔ na nwuna akɔla bɔbla ani na ɔ́bla ɔkɛnku eƒiebuo udeedi ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔsu. Ɔ́ya na bekyuli bammɔ bése baƒiɔ badi béte lɛlɔ, na bávɔ-ma na bese aani eƒiebuo udeedi ɔni náƒɔ ɔlɛ ka bébeyi-nwu ɔkɛɛ nsu ɔmu uli ngba.

english_verse: It was allowed to put breath into the idol, so it could speak. Everyone who refused to worship the idol of the beast was put to death.
translation_verse: Eƒiebuo unyɔdi ɔmmɔ ɔ́kɛ ɔyikun ka ɔnwuna ngba ɔƒɛƒɛɛ ɔkya eƒiebuo baƒiɔ bani na bése béte lɛlɔ mmɔ kemmo kalɛ na ɔkana butemi, na ɔya na badu bekyuli bani ƒui naaadubo akɔnkɔ bɔlɛ bute-nwu.

english_verse: All people were forced to put a mark on their right hand or forehead. Whether they were powerful or weak, rich or poor, free people or slaves,
translation_verse: Na eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ únye bekyuli ƒui lɛlɔ, banamu ku benengu, balakɛne ku bawabane ku bekyuli bani mɔɔbla bekyuli bamba kabla ku bani mɔɔbla ama alati kabla ka bese-ma likpo na bana kɔdianu kɔnu lɛlɔ iye bana atɛntɛ.

english_verse: they all had to have this mark, or else they could not buy or sell anything. This mark stood for the name of the beast and for the number of its name.
translation_verse: Ukyuli ɔdi biala ulakana na weye lɛla lɛdi wasiku ɔdi kudɔ iye uye lɛla lɛdi ute ukyuli bamba lɛnɔ si uuubo likpose lɛmmɔ. Na likpose lɛmmɔ nnye nte eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ lɛnyi iye bumomo bɔka bɔni nnye lɛnyi lɛmɛni kenye.

english_verse: You need wisdom to understand the number of the beast! But if you are smart enough, you can figure this out. Its number is
translation_verse: Ntu ebo lɛnunda asa na ala amɛni adubɔbla-a nwaa. Ukyuli ɔni makana ni, ɔwia bumomo bɔni nnye eƒiebuo ɔmɛni lɛnyi kenye kalɔ unu. Ɔsika bumomo bɔmɛni bɔdi bɔka bɔni nnye nte ukyuli lɛnyi. Na bumomo bɔmmɔ ndi

english_verse: Then I heard a sound from heaven that was like a roaring flood or loud thunder or even like the music of harps.
translation_verse: Amu na línu lɛdi bonwu lɛdi lɛni nse aani ntu bɔni mɔɔgbá taayu lɛtakpɛ bonwu lɛdi lɛlɔ na lɛ́sɔ lɛ́lɛ aani si katɔ muudu ku kɔku bonwu. Lɛnɔ ni, use aani ɔnu na bagyane baagyá na lɛbentaa lɛlɔ.

english_verse: And a new song was being sung in front of God's throne and in front of the four living creatures and the elders. No one could learn that song, except the
translation_verse: Na nkyuli mpim eti anyɔ ku aavlene-ine bamɛni badi bekyuli bani na bédie básiku kayawi na bákɛ ngba bɔƒɔ. Na bana ƒui benye lɛgaboku ku Katɔti ngba batu ine bammɔ anumi ku benengu bammɔ anumi. Na béteedie ɔnu ɔwɔdi ɔni na ama lɛti pɛ kani nákana-nwu bɔtɛya.

english_verse: All of these are pure virgins, and they follow the Lamb wherever he leads. They have been rescued to be presented to God and the Lamb as the most precious people on earth.
translation_verse: Ama ndi bekyuli bani náda lɛlɔ sɛɛn. Na bana lɛlɔ lilese lɛlɔ na lɛsɔnɔdi ala lɛlɔ ɔsu. Ama mɔɔsiaku Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ likpo biala na úsela. Ama na bédie bálɛku bayawine ƒui akɔ. Na ama ndi bekyuli bedeedi bani na béti béte Katɔti ku Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ.

english_verse: They never tell lies, and they are innocent. The Messages of the Three Angels
translation_verse: Likpidi lɛɛɛma bekyuli bamɛni lɛlɔ, na ɔkɔ lɛla lɛdi lɛɛɛda-ma. Yohane Ɔ́nu Katɔ Batu Ine Badi

english_verse: I saw another angel. This one was flying across the sky and had the eternal good news to announce to the people of every race, tribe, language, and nation on earth.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama lɛ́nu Katɔti ɔtu ɔbambadi ɔdi ka úveyi ɔɔví kayaa katɔ katɔ ku litemi buni lɛni nse nte uwi biala. Litemi lɛmmɔ lɛsa na úbo úbakɔ ute bekyuli bani nlie kayawi kamɛni lɛlɔ. Na ama ndi kalɔ biala lɛlɔ bekyuli ku kaba biala ku adi ƒui batɛmine ku bekyuli lidu ƒui.

english_verse: The angel shouted, “Worship and honor God! The time has come for him to judge everyone. Kneel down before the one who created heaven and earth, the oceans, and every stream.”
translation_verse: Ɔ́su ku lɛdi bonwu ɔnini, “Bɛbu Katɔti na bɛkɔliku-nwu lɛnyi katɔ! Ɔsika nwuna uwi údu ka ɔtɛku bayawine ƒui litemi. Bimwi anwu ɔni nábla katɔ ku kalɔ ku ɛpu ku ntukpa ƒui!”

english_verse: A second angel followed and said, “The great city of Babylon has fallen! This is the city that made all nations drunk and immoral. Now God is angry, and Babylon has fallen.”
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔtu unyɔdi ɔsia udeedi kama na ɔɔva momoomo ɔnini, “Úbuli! Babilon bonwu ɔmmɔ úbuli geen! Kayawi bekyuli ƒui báni ɔma ɔmmɔ alaekpidi bɔbla békpi aani ntɛ. Na ɔ́tɔlɔ-ma aani kalɛ na ɔyalɛ ɔɔtɔ́lɔ bekyuli taatákya likpidi kemmo.”

english_verse: Finally, a third angel came and shouted: Here is what will happen if you worship the beast and the idol and have the mark of the beast on your hand or forehead.
translation_verse: Katɔti ɔtu ɔbambadi ɔsia bammɔ kama na ɔɔva ku lɛdi momoomo ɔnini, “Bekyuli bani mɔɔlɛ akɔnkɔ teete eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ ku nwuna baƒiɔ bani na bávɔ béte lɛlɔ ni, ama náƒɔ eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ likpose na bana atɛntɛ iye kɔnu.

english_verse: You will have to drink the wine that God gives to everyone who makes him angry. You will feel his mighty anger, and you will be tortured with fire and burning sulfur, while the holy angels and the Lamb look on.
translation_verse: Ama na Katɔti ɔdubɔya na bani nwuna kɔnyi lɛbibo ɔɔƒɛɛ ku ɔdu kati kati! Ogya ku ogya atabi adubo-ma bɔkyula na Katɔti batu kedee ku Koƒonu Ubi anumi.

english_verse: If you worship the beast and the idol and accept the mark of its name, you will be tortured day and night. The smoke from your torture will go up forever and ever, and you will never be able to rest.
translation_verse: Na ogya ɔni mɔɔkyula-ma uyɔ ɔdubɔkɔ uteesie katɔ uwi ƒui. Na usien ku ɔƒɛ ni, bekyuli bamɛni balákɛ bɔnwuna! Ɔsika ama mɔɔlɛ akɔnkɔ teete eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ ku nwuna baƒiɔ, na báƒɔ nwuna lɛnyi likpose.

english_verse: God's people must learn to endure. They must also obey his commands and have faith in Jesus.
translation_verse: “Ɔmɛni ɔsu ɔlɛka amii Katɔti bekyuli bani mɔɔdi Katɔti litemi lɛlɔ na bɛsiaku Yesu kama ulu lɛlɔ ni, binye lɛbibo kenye kpakplaa.”

english_verse: Then I heard a voice from heaven say, “Put this in writing. From now on, the Lord will bless everyone who has faith in him when they die.” The Spirit answered, “Yes, they will rest from their hard work, and they will be rewarded for what they have done.” The Earth Is Harvested
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama línu lɛdi lɛdi ka lɛ́si katɔ na lɛɛsu lɛnini, “Nweni ala amɛni. Bekyuli bani na lɛlɔ lɛdubɔyɔ-ma ndi bani ndubukpi ka básiaku Blɔti kama ɔ́si ɔƒɛni úsela ɔsu.” Na Katɔti Kɔyu kɔɔtuna kɔnini, “Ɛɛn, badubɔkɛ bɔnwuna! Na badubɔkɛ bana kabla kɔsia!” Baasála Kayawi Bekyuli

english_verse: I looked and saw a bright cloud, and someone who seemed to be the Son of Man was sitting on the cloud. He wore a gold crown on his head and held a sharp sickle in his hand.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, lɛ́nu ƒututuu ɔdi. Na lɛ́nu ka ukyuli ɔni nálɛ Ukyuli Ɔyawine Ubi ulie ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ, na sika ugyiedi kagabwa kebi-nwu lili. Na ɔda lɛsaka.

english_verse: An angel came out of the temple and shouted, “Start cutting with your sickle! Harvest season is here, and all crops on earth are ripe.”
translation_verse: Amu na ɔtu ɔbambadi ɔ́lɛ ɔ́si kakpakɔ mmɔ na ɔ́va ku lɛdi momoomo ɔɔsu ukyuli ɔni nlie ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ ɔnini, “Awɔ, sala Katɔti bekyuli lɛku kayawi aani kalɛ na beeti lɛsaka taanwa edula. Ɔsika uwi údu ka basala-ma bete-nwu.”

english_verse: The one on the cloud swung his sickle and harvested the crops.
translation_verse: Amu na ukyuli ɔni nlie lɛlɔ mmɔ ɔ́sala-ma na kalɔ kammɔ lɛlɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Another angel with a sharp sickle then came out of the temple in heaven.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama lɛ́sɔ lɛ́nu Katɔti ɔtu ɔbambadi ka ɔ́si Katɔti kakpakɔ mmɔ ɔ́yu úbo, na anwu lɛnɔ ɔ́da asɔsɔ ɔni mbo ɔbi.

english_verse: After this, an angel with power over fire came from the altar and shouted to the angel who had the sickle. He said, “All grapes on earth are ripe! Harvest them with your sharp sickle.”
translation_verse: Na ɔtu ɔbambadi lɛnɔ ɔ́si Katɔti lɛbi lɛmmɔ kudɔ úbo. Na anwu ndi ɔni mɔɔdi ogya lɛlɔ. Ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́va ku lɛdi momoomo na ɔ́su Katɔti ɔtu ɔni nda asɔsɔ mmɔ ɔnini, “Awɔ, sala bekyuli bekpidi lɛku kayawi aani kalɛ na beeti asɔsɔ ɔni mbo ɔbi teede egyiibi. Ɔsika uwi údu ka basala-ma.”

english_verse: The angel swung his sickle on earth and cut off its grapes. He threw them into a pit where they were trampled on as a sign of God's anger.
translation_verse: Anwuɔsu Katɔti ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́sala bekyuli bammɔ na kayawi lɛlɔ, na úti-ma útéwi kesii kani na Katɔti ɔdubɔni-ma kɔtu aani ebi ani béde béwi ntɛ kablakɔ.

english_verse: The pit was outside the city, and when the grapes were mashed, blood flowed out. The blood turned into a river that was about
translation_verse: Na ɔ́ni-ma kɔtu na ɔma ɔmmɔ kabanye aani kalɛ na baamana ntu teedie ebi ammɔ kemmo. Na ubugya ɔ́gba ɔ́si mmɔ, na ɔ́ƒɔ kalɛkɛ kammɔ ƒui. Na ubugya ɔmmɔ bɔgyu ɔdubudu ukyuli limɔ.

english_verse: After this, I looked at the sky and saw something else that was strange and important. Seven angels were bringing the seven last terrible troubles. When these are ended, God will no longer be angry.
translation_verse: Na lɛ́sɔ lɛ́nu akɔla budie taatina bonwu bɔbambadi na katɔ bɔni nábla-mi kalɛ kadi. Lɛ́nu batu maatɛ ka bada lɛbibo maatɛ lɛni ndi lɛbibo maatɛ likplodi. Ɔsika ɔmɛni kemmo na Katɔti kɔnyi kúdu kɔ́wɔlɔ.

english_verse: Then I saw something that looked like a glass sea mixed with fire, and people were standing on it. They were the ones who had defeated the beast and the idol and the number that tells the name of the beast. God had given them harps,
translation_verse: Na lɛ́nu kalɔ kani nwi aani ɛpu na use kede kede aani asogya kani kemmo na ogya ɔɔda. Na ɛpu ɔmmɔ amadɔ ni, bekyuli benye beedie lɛnu na baagyá lɛbentaa lɛni na Katɔti úte-ma. Ama nádi eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ ku nwuna baƒiɔ ku bumomo bɔni nnye nte nwuna lɛnyi lɛlɔ.

english_verse: and they were singing the song his servant Moses and the Lamb had sung. They were singing, “Lord God All-Powerful, you have done great and marvelous things. You are the ruler of all nations, and you do what is right and fair.
translation_verse: Na lɛnu lɛni na beedie mmɔ ni, lɛdi Mose ɔni ndi Katɔti kabla ɔblane ku Koƒonu Ubi ɔmmɔ lɛnu. Na beedie banini, “Blɔti ɔni mbo ɔyikun ƒui, ƒula ala bɔbla ébomo, na bulakana-nya kalɔ bunu. Na ƒula ablala ese siin, na ƒula etemila adi litemi geen. Awɔ ndi Uwi Ƒui Ɔga.

english_verse: Lord, who doesn't honor and praise your name? You alone are holy, and all nations will come and worship you, because you have shown that you judge with fairness.”
translation_verse: Ɔma makana-a anumi bunye na ulayia awɔ Blɔti, na uleti bumwi ulete ƒula lɛnyi? Ɔsika awɔ lɛti nse kedee, na kalɔ ƒui bekyuli badubo babakya-a lili kalɔ. Ɔsika bédie bátina ka aabla lɛla biala ulu siin lɛlɔ.”

english_verse: After this, I noticed something else in heaven. The sacred tent used for a temple was open.
translation_verse: Ɔmɛni kama ni, lɛ́nu ka bálɛmi kakpakɔ kedee na katɔ. Na adaka ɔni kemmo na Katɔti bunyimi bɔkya ni, use mmɔ.

english_verse: And the seven angels who were bringing the terrible troubles were coming out of it. They were dressed in robes of pure white linen and wore belts made of pure gold.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti batu maatɛ bani nda lɛbibo maatɛ bammɔ bálɛ bási Katɔti kakpakɔ mmɔ. Na bakya lɛwu lɛƒualadi lɛni muukeye na sika ugyiedi kɔbuli kɔ́da kɔ́mana-ma kayi.

english_verse: One of the four living creatures gave each of the seven angels a bowl made of gold. These bowls were filled with the anger of God who lives forever and ever.
translation_verse: Amu na ngba batu ine bammɔ kemmo unwi úti sika ugyiedi kɔlaku kɔni na Katɔti ɔni nli ngba uwi ƒui kɔnyi kúyi úte batu maatɛ bammɔ.

english_verse: The temple quickly filled with smoke from the glory and power of God. No one could enter it until the seven angels had finished pouring out the seven last troubles.
translation_verse: Na Katɔti kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo kéyi ku uyɔ ɔni nási Katɔti ɔyikun ku bukeye kemmo. Na ukyuli biala ulakana kakpakɔ kammɔ kemmo buduo, amu ntu batu maatɛ bammɔ béti lɛbibo maatɛ lɛmmɔ béboku kayawi báwɔlɔ.

english_verse: From the temple I heard a voice shout to the seven angels, “Go and empty the seven bowls of God's anger on the earth.”
translation_verse: Amu na línu lɛdi bonwu lɛdi ka lɛɛtɛmi taasiku Katɔti kakpakɔ mmɔ úte batu maatɛ bammɔ ɔnini, “Bisie na bitéwilimi Katɔti kɔnyi kɔlaku maatɛ kɔmmɔ biwi kayawi lɛlɔ!”

english_verse: The first angel emptied his bowl on the earth. At once ugly and painful sores broke out on everyone who had the mark of the beast and worshiped the idol.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔtu udeedi úsie na útéwilimi nwuna kalaku úwi kayawi lɛlɔ. Ɔmmɔ ɔ́ya na alɛbi álɛ éwi bekyuli bani mbo eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ likpose na baalɛ akɔnkɔ teete nwuna baƒiɔ mmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The second angel emptied his bowl on the sea. At once the sea turned into blood like that of a dead person, and every living thing in the sea died.
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔtu unyɔdi úwilimi nwuna kalaku úwi ɛpu kemmo, na ntu bɔmmɔ búnwini ubugya aani ɔni nkya ukpine. Na lɛla biala lɛni mbo ngba na lɛkya ɛpu kemmo mmɔ líkpi.

english_verse: The third angel emptied his bowl into the rivers and streams. At once they turned to blood.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔtu ɔtɛdi úwilimi nwuna kalaku úwi ntukpa ku abiɔ ƒui kemmo na búnwini ubugya.

english_verse: Then I heard the angel, who has power over water, say, “You have always been, and you always will be the holy God. You had the right to judge in this way.
translation_verse: Amu na línu ka ɔtu ɔni mɔɔnu ntukpa lɛlɔ ɔ́su ɔnini, “Awɔ ɔni nli na élie ni, awɔ nse kedee. Ɔsika átɛ etemila amɛni ƒui na ulu siin lɛlɔ.

english_verse: They poured out the blood of your people and your prophets. So you gave them blood to drink as they deserve!”
translation_verse: Bekyuli bamɛni nádu ƒula bekyuli ku kenye bediene. Anwuɔsu na éte-ma ubugya ukpidi ɔmɛni na báni. Lɛla lɛni námanku-ma na baaƒɔ́!”

english_verse: After this, I heard the altar shout, “Yes, Lord God All-Powerful, your judgments are honest and fair.”
translation_verse: Amu na línu lɛdi lɛni nási Katɔti lɛbi lɛmmɔ kudɔ ka lɛ́su lɛnini, “Blɔti ɔni mbo ɔyikun ƒui, ƒula litemi bɔtɛ buse siin, na ƒula etemila adi litemi geen.”

english_verse: The fourth angel emptied his bowl on the sun, and it began to scorch people like fire.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔtu unedi úwilimi nwuna kalaku úwi ɔƒɛ lɛlɔ na béte kuƒi ka nwuna ogya ɔkyula bekyuli.

english_verse: Everyone was scorched by its great heat, and all of them cursed the name of God who had power over these terrible troubles. But no one turned to God and praised him.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bákywi ɔ́si ogya liwulu kpakplaa lɛmmɔ ɔsu. Na béwida Katɔti lɛnyi, ɔsika nwuna ɔyikun ɔsu na lɛbibo lɛmɛni líbo-ma lɛlɔ. Nsu ɔmɛni kama ƒui ni, bétenwini kama bátakya bana ekpidi na bemwi Katɔti.

english_verse: The fifth angel emptied his bowl on the throne of the beast. At once darkness covered its kingdom, and its people began biting their tongues in pain.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔtu ɔlɔndi úwilimi lɛla lɛni nkya nwuna kalaku kemmo úwi eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ lɛgaboku lɛlɔ. Na kalɔ kani lɛlɔ na eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ ɔɔdi lɛga ƒui kábla suu kɔnakunwi! Na bekyuli baadu anyi na lɛbibo ɔsu.

english_verse: And because of their painful sores, they cursed the God who rules in heaven. But still they did not stop doing evil things.
translation_verse: Na bekyuli bammɔ béwida Katɔti, ɔsika bana alɛbi áya na beenú ɔlɛ geen! Nsu bátada bana alaekpidi bɔbla bátaya.

english_verse: The sixth angel emptied his bowl on the great Euphrates River, and it completely dried up to make a road for the kings from the east.
translation_verse: Ɔmmɔ kama ni, ɔtu ɔkundi úwilimi lɛla lɛni nkya nwuna kalaku kemmo úwi Euƒrate Ketu kebendi kammɔ kemmo. Na ketu kammɔ kákwii kalɛ na baga bani nási ɔƒɛ katukɔ bakɛ kavinkɔ.

english_verse: An evil spirit that looked like a frog came out of the mouth of the dragon. One also came out of the mouth of the beast, and another out of the mouth of the false prophet.
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́nu ayu ekpidi atɛ ani nálɛ aani bapɔtɔlɔ ka bási baalɛ́ liƒu kɔlakpi kɔmmɔ kenye ku eƒiebuo udeedi ɔmmɔ kenye ku eƒiebuo unyɔdi ɔni baalɔ ɔkɔ kenye udiene kenye kemmo.

english_verse: These evil spirits had the power to work miracles. They went to every king on earth, to bring them together for a war against God All-Powerful. But that will be the day of God's great victory.
translation_verse: Ayu ammɔ ndi ukisine ayu ekpidi ani muudie akɔla taatina. Na ayu atɛ amɛni muusié kayawi baga ƒui kudɔ kalɛ na basala lɛlɔ na bekpo Katɔti bekyuli na Katɔti ɔni ndi Ɔyikune Ƒui limeyi linengudi lɛmmɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: Remember Christ says, “When I come, it will surprise you like a thief! But God will bless you, if you are awake and ready. Then you won't have to walk around naked and be ashamed.”
translation_verse: “Binu! Ami Yesu ndubo bɔda bɔlɛ-mii lɛlɔ kɔnakunwi aani uyune kalɛ! Lɛlɔ lɛdubɔyɔ ukyuli ɔni nnye kagyumana na ɔda adala ani mɔɔtina ka use siin uwi biala kemmo, kalɛ na ulakɛ kasɔngya ku kɔƒa na kadi akɔ!”

english_verse: Those armies came together in a place that in Hebrew is called Armagedon.
translation_verse: Amu na ayu ekpidi ammɔ ásala baga bammɔ na likpo lɛni baalɔ na Hebri kemmo bani Armagedon.

english_verse: As soon as the seventh angel emptied his bowl in the air, a loud voice from the throne in the temple shouted, “It's done!”
translation_verse: Amu na Katɔti ɔtu maatɛdi úwilimi lɛla lɛni nkya nwuna kalaku kemmo úwi kayaa. Na lɛdi bonwu lɛdi lɛ́ku lɛ́si lɛgaboku kudɔ na Katɔti kakpakɔ mmɔ, na lɛɛsu lɛnini, “Ɔ́sa!”

english_verse: There were flashes of lightning, roars of thunder, and the worst earthquake in all history.
translation_verse: Na kayaa kábwɛ ogya ku kɔku bonwu, na katɔ keedu taasia kama! Na kalɔ kaakunku ɔni na kalɔ bɔkunku bɔmmɔ udu bútalɛ kudii ɔ́si uwi ɔni na Katɔti údie ukyuli!

english_verse: The great city of Babylon split into three parts, and the cities of other nations fell. So God made Babylon drink from the wine cup filled with his anger.
translation_verse: Na ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ɔ́bwɛ úle akpa atɛ, na lɛma linengudi lɛkladi lɛni nkya kayawi ekpo ƒui lɛ́bwɛ ƒui. Mmɔ ni, Katɔti únyimo Babilon ɔma unengudi ɔmmɔ ekpidi na ɔ́ya na ɔ́ni nwuna kɔnyi lɛbibo ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔmmɔ ƒui.

english_verse: Every island ran away, and the mountains disappeared.
translation_verse: Na ntuntɛ kɔlɔ ku abi ani ƒui nkya ni, áyii ákya.

english_verse: One of the seven angels who had emptied the bowls came over and said to me, “Come on! I will show you how God will punish that shameless prostitute who sits on many oceans.
translation_verse: Amu na batu maatɛ bani nda kɔlaku kɔmmɔ kemmo unwi úbo-mi kudɔ na ɔ́su-mi ɔnini, “Bo, na lɛtina-a kalɛ na badubo ɔyalɛ ɔni náƒɔ lɛnyi mmɔ kɔtu bɔni. Anwu ndi ɔma unengudi ɔni na bátu bényene ntukpa pii kudɔ.

english_verse: Every king on earth has slept with her, and her shameless ways are like wine that has made everyone on earth drunk.”
translation_verse: Na kayawi baga bákya béteesie teesie ɔma ɔmmɔ kemmo aani kalɛ na banana beesié ɔyalɛ kudɔ. Na ɔma ɔmmɔ ekpidi bɔbla bɔ́ƒɔ kayawi bekyuli lɛlɔ kemmo aani kalɛ na baaní ntɛ teekpi.”

english_verse: With the help of the Spirit, the angel took me into a desert, where I saw a woman sitting on a red beast. The beast was covered with names that were an insult to God, and it had seven heads and ten horns.
translation_verse: Ɔtu ɔmmɔ ɔ́kpanku-mi úsienku ketele kemmo na kɔyu kemmo. Mmɔ na lɛ́nu uleku ɔdi ka ulie eƒiebuo ugyiedi lɛlɔ. Na bénweni anyikpi ani muudumi Katɔti ƒui básia eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ lɛlɔ. Na eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ mbo eli maatɛ ku ese leevu.

english_verse: The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet robes, and she wore jewelry made of gold, precious stones, and pearls. In her hand she held a gold cup filled with the filthy and nasty things she had done.
translation_verse: Uleku ɔmmɔ unyimi adi otondi ku egyiedi na úti sika ugyiedi ku asɛɛ ku aseebi ɔ́klibi lɛlɔ. Na ɔda sika ugyiedi ɔɔƒɛɛ ɔdi ɔni kemmo na ala ani na Katɔti ukisi na eesé lɛlɔ éyi tɛtɛɛtɛ ɔkɛnku nwuna lɛyalɛ ala bɔbla ɔsu.

english_verse: On her forehead a mysterious name was written: I AM THE GREAT CITY OF BABYLON, THE MOTHER OF EVERY IMMORAL AND FILTHY THING ON EARTH.
translation_verse: Na nwuna lɛtɛntɛ ni, bénweni lɛsugba lɛnyi lɛdi básia. Babilon, Ɔma Unengudi. Bayalɛ Ƒui Uni Ku Ekisila Ƒui Uni.

english_verse: I could tell that the woman was drunk on the blood of God's people who had given their lives for Jesus. This surprising sight amazed me,
translation_verse: Amu na lɛ́nu ka uleku ɔmmɔ úkpi ntɛ na Katɔti bekyuli bani ubugya na ɔ́ni ku bani na ɔ́du ɔsika benye Yesu kama kpakplaa ɔsu. Uwi ɔni na lɛ́nu-nwu ni, ɔ́bla-mi kalɛ kadi.

english_verse: and the angel said: Why are you so amazed? I will explain the mystery about this woman and about the beast she is sitting on, with its seven heads and ten horns.
translation_verse: Amu na ɔtu ɔmmɔ úye-mi ɔnini, “Bi ɔsu na ɔ́bla-a kalɛ kadi? Ndubudie lɛsugba lɛmɛni kalɔ lite-ɔ. Lɛkɛnku uleku ɔmmɔ ku eƒiebuo ɔni lɛlɔ na uleku ɔmmɔ ulie mmɔ lɛlɔ. Na eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ mbo eli maatɛ, na ese leevu alɛ eli ammɔ lɛlɔ.

english_verse: The beast you saw is one that used to be and no longer is. It will come back from the deep pit, but only to be destroyed. Everyone on earth whose names were not written in the book of life before the time of creation will be amazed. They will see this beast that used to be and no longer is, but will be once more.
translation_verse: Eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ ni, úlie ngba dii, nsu ɔsɔ uuubo. Na ɔdubo bɔlɛ bɔsi kasuudikɔ ubu bonwu ɔmmɔ kemmo, na usie na Katɔti ɔyila-nwu udu ƒui. Na bekyuli bani nli kayawi lɛlɔ na bétenweni-ma anyi bátakya ngba ɔku kemmo asa na Katɔti údie kayawi ni, ɔdubo-ma bɔbla kalɛ kadi si banu eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ. Ɔsika úlie ngba dii, nsu ɔsɔ uuubo, na ɔsɔ ɔdubo bɔda bɔlɛ.

english_verse: Anyone with wisdom can figure this out. The seven heads that the woman is sitting on stand for seven hills. These heads are also seven kings.
translation_verse: “Asa na ukyuli wenu lɛsugba lɛmɛni kalɔ ni, amu ntu ubo lɛnunda. Eƒiebuo eli maatɛ ku uleku ɔyalɛ ɔmmɔ benye bete ɔma ɔni bátu bálɛ abi maatɛ lɛlɔ. Na eli ammɔ lɛnɔ enye ete baga maatɛ badi.

english_verse: Five of the kings are dead. One is ruling now, and the other one has not yet come. But when he does, he will rule for only a little while.
translation_verse: Baga ɛlɔ bádi lɛga bávi, na unwi ɔmu ɔɔdi lɛga, na ɔkladi anwu útadi tɔ lɛga. Nsu si úbo ni, ɔdubo lɛga bɔdi uwi klukui ɔdi kani.

english_verse: You also saw a beast that used to be and no longer is. That beast is one of the seven kings who will return as the eighth king, but only to be destroyed.
translation_verse: Eƒiebuo ɔni nélie ngba dii nsu ɔsɔ uuubo mmɔ ni, anwu ndi ɔga maanedi. Na nwuna udu use aani baga maatɛ bammɔ kalɛ, na ɔdubo busie na Katɔti ɔyila-nwu udu ƒui.

english_verse: The ten horns you saw are ten more kings, who have not yet come into power, and they will rule with the beast for only a short time.
translation_verse: “Na ese leevu ani na ánu mmɔ ni, adi baga leevu bani nétese tɔ kalɔ ku lɛga bɔdi. Nsu badubo-ma kuƒi bute uwi klukui na badi lɛga ku eƒiebuo ɔmmɔ.
